title: Dual structure of environmental performance: an empirical analysis of the decoupling between ESG ratings and substantive environmental performance
source: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether evaluation-based environmental performance measured by ESG ratings aligns with, or diverges from, substantive environmental performance measured by carbon and energy intensity. Design/methodology/a
content: Purpose This study aims to examine whether evaluation-based environmental performance measured by ESG ratings aligns with, or diverges from, substantive environmental performance measured by carbon and energy intensity. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 104 South Korean firms covered by the Korea Institute of Corporate Governance and Sustainability ESG evaluation with continuous data availability between 2017 and 2023, this study examines the relationship between evaluation-based and substantive environmental performance. The sample is constructed by matching these firms to those subject to mandatory greenhouse gas disclosure under Korea’s Emissions Trading Scheme or Target Management System, resulting in a sample concentrated in emission- and energy-intensive firms, predominantly in manufacturing sectors. ESG ratings appear to be largely associated with institutional signaling activities, including participation in global initiatives such as RE100 and the UN Global Compact, as well as environmental disclosure practices. By contrast, substantive environmental performance appears to be less related to symbolic actions and more closely associated with internal operational factors. Corporate governance characteristics and institutional investor ownership show limited association with either dimension, suggesting that firms may respond more strongly to ESG evaluation criteria than to monitoring mechanisms. Findings This study provides evidence consistent with a dual structure of environmental performance that reflects a distinction between external legitimacy-seeking behavior and internal capability-building. By distinguishing evaluation-based from substantive performance, the findings refine the application of institutional theory and the resource-based view and raise questions about whether ESG ratings adequately capture firms’ decarbonization capacity in export-oriented economies. Originality/value The results suggest that reliance on ESG ratings alone may overestimate firms’ environmental capabilities; the observed divergence is consistent with a potential greenwashing risk, although greenwashing itself is not directly measured. Policymakers, investors and regulators may benefit from adopting a dual-track evaluation approach that assesses both strategic signaling and operational substance to better align sustainability assessments with emissions reduction outcomes. This conclusion is scoped to carbon-intensive, export-oriented firms subject to mandatory emissions disclosure and may not generalize to sectors with different institutional exposure.

title: Attaining carbon neutrality in supply chains by leveraging green dynamic and transactional capabilities
summary: Purpose Carbon neutrality has become a core strategic imperative for manufacturing firms facing resource constraints and mounting net-zero pressures. Drawing on the dynamic capability view (DCV) and transaction cost economics (TCE), this st
content: Purpose Carbon neutrality has become a core strategic imperative for manufacturing firms facing resource constraints and mounting net-zero pressures. Drawing on the dynamic capability view (DCV) and transaction cost economics (TCE), this study examines how green dynamic capabilities (environmental sensing, resource seizing, and resource reconfiguring) interact with green transactional capability to enable carbon neutral supply chain (CNSC) practices. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 254 manufacturing managers across four emissions-intensive sectors in India were analyzed using structural equation modelling. Findings Resource seizing and reconfiguring capabilities are directly associated with both green transactional capability and CNSC outcomes, while mediating the effect of environmental sensing. Green transactional capability emerged as a key driver of supply chain decarbonization. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-country design limits causal inference and generalizability; future research should employ longitudinal and multi-economy designs. Practical implications Managers should prioritize resource seizing and reconfiguring over sensing alone, embedding green knowledge into supplier contracts and process workflows, while policymakers should advance decarbonization through standardized carbon reporting frameworks and fiscal incentives for green capability development. Social implications This study demonstrates how manufacturing firms in emerging economies can systematically achieve carbon neutrality across Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions, supporting the global transition toward low-carbon industrial ecosystems. Originality/value This study validates green transactional capability as a distinct mediating mechanism between internal dynamic capabilities and CNSC outcomes; integrates DCV and TCE into a unified framework; and advances capability-driven decarbonization understanding in an emerging economy marked by institutional voids and supply base heterogeneity.

title: Accelerating the Systemic Digital Transition of Urban Logistics and Planning: the Disco Urban Freight Data Space
summary: The Urban Freight Data Space (UFDS) is a core asset designed, demonstrated, and deployed in DISCO [1] (GA 101103954). It aims to accelerate the digital transition of urban logistics and the Physical Internet, enabling solutions that drive t
content: The Urban Freight Data Space (UFDS) is a core asset designed, demonstrated, and deployed in DISCO [1] (GA 101103954). It aims to accelerate the digital transition of urban logistics and the Physical Internet, enabling solutions that drive the decarbonisation of logistics in cities. Cities can connect and exchange information with logistics players, providing a trustworthy way to integrate valuable city data into logistics operations. UFDS supports this transition by enabling seamless interoperability across commercial and open systems, and establishing clear, open governance to promote data democracy and high-value, data-driven services. An integrated Data Pipeline connects internal and external data sources, standardises and anonymises diverse datasets, ensuring they are shareable across the data space. This approach supports stakeholder onboarding and scalability. UFDS is built on three core principles: leveraging open-source and existing technologies, offering an intuitive user interface, and using mature, secure components to ensure stability and reliability. Its architecture provides a scalable model that any city can replicate, empowering them to harness data for more efficient and integrated urban freight systems. A proof of concept is available, featuring: 3 data types (access rules, parking occupancy, real estate locations); 7 onboarded cities (5 from DISCO, 2 external); 4 connected applications.

title: Adsorption of Paracetamol, Ibuprofen, and Diclofenac on a Carbonaceous Material Derived from Rhus tripartita
summary: This work demonstrated that Rhus tripartita stem , a Tunisian biomass, is a good lignocellulosic precursor for developing a non-activated biochar that efficiently removes paracetamol (PCT), ibuprofen (IBU), and diclofenac (DCF) in a multico
content: This work demonstrated that Rhus tripartita stem , a Tunisian biomass, is a good lignocellulosic precursor for developing a non-activated biochar that efficiently removes paracetamol (PCT), ibuprofen (IBU), and diclofenac (DCF) in a multicomponent real hospital wastewater matrix. Characterization techniques showed that Rhus tripartita biochar (RtB) is a predominantly carbonaceous, chemically heterogeneous material with a disordered aromatic framework, oxygen-containing surface groups, hierarchical porosity, and a minor inorganic fraction. The adsorption study in synthetic solutions showed that all three pharmaceuticals had the highest measured removal at pH 7.0: 97.5 ± 2.0% for DCF, 92.7 ± 2.0% for IBU, and 97.3 ± 2.0% for PCT. The measured kinetic profiles approached practical plateaus within the experimental time window, and Langmuir yielded the lowest BIC in 11 of the 12 adsorbate-temperature datasets, with Liu preferred only for PCT at 298 K. Thermodynamic analysis indicated favorable and exothermic adsorption and, together with the pH response and surface characterization, supported predominantly non-covalent interactions. Ethanol desorption reached 100%, but adsorption-capacity retention after six cycles was adsorbate-dependent: 85.2% for DCF, 50.5% for PCT, and 40.0% for IBU. The most important finding was that the Rhus tripartita biochar (RtB) performance in single-solute systems translated to a chemically complex matrix. In the real effluent treatment, TOC, NPOC, TN, TS, and COD decreased by 47.0%, 53.9%, 55.2%, 78.4%, and 75.7%, respectively, while DCF, IBU, PCT, and all other monitored pharmaceuticals were not detected after treatment.

title: Charting new horizons in non-sacrificial electroflotation: Fundamentals, advances, and applications across water and biomass processing
summary: Electrocoagulation–flotation (ECF) has emerged as a promising technology for wastewater treatment and the recovery of valuable resources from liquid streams. While sacrificial ECF systems have been extensively studied, non-sacrificial elect
content: Electrocoagulation–flotation (ECF) has emerged as a promising technology for wastewater treatment and the recovery of valuable resources from liquid streams. While sacrificial ECF systems have been extensively studied, non-sacrificial electroflotation (NS-EF) systems involving coagulation or flocculation have received comparatively less attention, with a clear lack of consolidated literature addressing these systems. This review first highlights the key mechanistic differences between sacrificial ECF and NS-EF and then outlines the unique potential of non-sacrificial configurations. The factors affecting NS-EF system performance are elaborated, followed by a critical discussion of recent modifications and strategies to improve overall performance, including advances in electrode materials, reactor configurations, and system design. These developments are assessed in terms of recovery efficiency, operational cost, and energy consumption. The current status of NS-EF across diverse application scenarios is subsequently examined. The final part of this review presents the future perspectives to guide ongoing efforts toward the rational development and optimization of separation and purification applications using NS-EF systems.

title: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements
summary: Atmospheric CO 2 exchanges in agroecosystems are strongly controlled by plant phenology, management and microclimatic conditions; yet obtaining finely resolved flux estimates across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes remains challenging.
content: Atmospheric CO 2 exchanges in agroecosystems are strongly controlled by plant phenology, management and microclimatic conditions; yet obtaining finely resolved flux estimates across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes remains challenging. This study evaluates the ability of a single Eddy Covariance (EC) system combined with wind-sector partitioning and Random Forest (RF) modelling to estimate the annual Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE) of adjacent fields (wheat, mixed-grain, permanent grassland) in the Marais poitevin wetland (French Atlantic coast). Fluxes were measured over the period 1 February 2023–31 January 2024 and attributed to eight wind sectors, each used as a proxy for the corresponding field or landscape feature that dominates its footprint. Two modelling strategies were compared (i) a single global RF trained on all sectors and (ii) sector-specific RFs trained separately for each wind sector. RF models globally showed good overall performance ( R 2 ≈0.20–0.94 depending on sector and period), but this apparent equivalence broke down once fluxes were reconstructed over the full annual cycle: the sector-specific approach then better reproduced phenological dynamics and management-driven flux reversals (harvest, senescence) than the global model, which compressed inter-sector variability by up to 70 %. Annual NEE estimated from the sector-specific models indicated that the mixed-grain field acted as net source (+151 g C m −2 yr −1 ), whereas the permanent grassland and the wheat field acted as net sinks (−145 and −308 g C m −2 yr −1 , respectively). A light-response-curve partitioning of these reconstructed fluxes into gross primary production (GPP) and ecosystem respiration (Reco) revealed contrasting phenological signatures behind different land-covers. Methodology and associated limitations/uncertainties due to flux measurement and modelling, footprint attribution and sector delineation, and the limited one-year observation period are particularly addressed. This study highlights the novelty and practical value of coupling a single EC system with wind-sector partitioning and machine learning approaches to resolve carbon fluxes at the field scale within heterogeneous agricultural landscapes. This integrated approach provides an alternative to traditional multi-tower setups, offering new opportunities to monitor spatial carbon dynamics and management effects in real agricultural mosaics. Beyond methodological innovation, this work provides one of the first field-scale, uncertainty-resolved carbon flux datasets for a mosaic of contrasting agricultural land covers monitored by a single EC tower, offering a transferable framework to better constrain the terrestrial carbon balance of retro-littoral wet and agricultural landscapes.

title: Species-resolved inventory of forest biogenic volatile organic emissions across China with MEGAN v3.2
summary: Biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) are important precursors of secondary organic aerosols and tropospheric ozone, yet their emissions are commonly modelled at the plant functional type (PFT) level, which obscures substantial inters
content: Biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) are important precursors of secondary organic aerosols and tropospheric ozone, yet their emissions are commonly modelled at the plant functional type (PFT) level, which obscures substantial interspecies variability. This limitation is particularly acute for China, where high forest diversity and ambitious afforestation initiatives are expected to reshape national BVOC budgets. Here, we present a species-resolved BVOC emissions inventory for China covering 234 tree species (Liu et al., 2026). The inventory was developed within the Model of Emissions of Gases and Aerosols from Nature (MEGAN) v3.2 modeling framework, with refined inputs comprising species-specific emission factors and high-resolution forest composition data for China. Total forest BVOC emissions were estimated at 10.26 Tg of compound mass in 2019, with summer emissions accounting for about 50 % of the annual total and a clear decreasing gradient from southern to northern China. Emissions were highly concentrated among a limited number of species: the five largest contributors, Pinus massoniana , Quercus liaotungensis , Phyllostachys edulis , Cunninghamia lanceolata , and Quercus variabilis accounted for 41.7 % of total emissions while occupying only 25.4 % of forest area. At the compound-class level, Quercus liaotungensis dominated isoprene emissions, whereas Pinus massoniana was the leading contributor to monoterpene emissions. Applying this species-resolved framework to two future afforestation scenarios with identical planted areas but contrasting species composition, we found that BVOC emissions may increase by 4.65 Tg yr −1 with the biomass-maximization tree species and by 5.10 Tg yr −1 under the most environmental-suitability species. Notably, the dominant component of additional BVOC emissions shifts from isoprene under biomass maximization (BIO) to monoterpenes under highest environmental suitability (HIGH). These results demonstrate the importance of incorporating species-specific emission traits into BVOC models and suggest that future afforestation strategies could substantially reshape both the magnitude and chemical composition of biogenic emissions, with implications for atmospheric chemistry and air quality depending on species selection.

title: Scenario-based life cycle assessment of beef production in Colombia: intensive silvopastoral transition scenarios under uncertainty
summary: Introduction Beef production in Colombia is associated with high methane emissions, low land-use efficiency, and pressure on forested landscapes. This study evaluates whether silvopastoral intensification can reduce product-level greenhouse
content: Introduction Beef production in Colombia is associated with high methane emissions, low land-use efficiency, and pressure on forested landscapes. This study evaluates whether silvopastoral intensification can reduce product-level greenhouse-gas intensity while explicitly distinguishing such reductions from territorial emissions and land-use effects. Methods A scenario-based life cycle assessment combined with Monte Carlo simulation was developed to compare an extensive reference cattle system (BAU-F) with moderate (SSPi-M) and intensive (SSPi-I) silvopastoral configurations. The cradle-to-farm-gate model used 1 kg of live-weight gain (LWG) as the functional unit and represented biological dependence among stocking rate, animal productivity, methane emissions, manure, and nitrogen excretion. Production-related greenhouse-gas emissions were quantified separately from land-use-change burdens and carbon-sequestration credits, which were evaluated through structural sensitivity analyses. Results Across 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations, mean greenhouse-gas intensities were 13.88 kg CO 2 eq kg −1 LWG for BAU-F, 8.49 for SSPi-M, and 7.10 for SSPi-I, corresponding to modeled reductions of 38.84% and 48.82%, respectively. These reductions were driven primarily by higher productivity rather than lower territorial emissions. Mean production-related emissions increased from 1,464 kg CO 2 eq ha −1 yr −1 in BAU-F to 2,920 and 5,795 in SSPi-M and SSPi-I, respectively. Structural analyses showed that land-use-change and carbon-sequestration assumptions materially affected absolute net footprints, while the lower product-level intensity of the silvopastoral configurations persisted under conservative accounting and productivity assumptions. Discussion Silvopastoral systems can substantially improve the greenhouse-gas and land-use efficiency of Colombian beef production, but lower emissions per kilogram do not necessarily imply lower emissions per hectare or lower sector-wide emissions. Credible mitigation therefore requires productivity gains to be coupled with control of herd expansion, prevention of new pasture conversion, and verifiable carbon-stock monitoring.

title: 4D Aviation Emission Inventory Data of China estimated with QAR data in 2023 (4D-AEID-2023)
summary: Accurate aviation emission inventories provide the fundamental basis for environmental impact assessment, yet existing estimates typically rely on idealized trajectory assumptions and generic aircraft performance models. Here, we present a
content: Accurate aviation emission inventories provide the fundamental basis for environmental impact assessment, yet existing estimates typically rely on idealized trajectory assumptions and generic aircraft performance models. Here, we present a high-resolution, four-dimensional aviation emission inventory for purely domestic civil aviation flights within mainland China in 2023, built directly from onboard Quick Access Recorder (QAR) measurements covering 4.52 million flights (∼96.8 % of national commercial movements). Integrating 1 Hz per-engine fuel-flow measurements with observed flight trajectories, ambient temperature and pressure, and specific humidity profiles via the Boeing Fuel Flow Method 2 and atmospheric corrections, this dataset yields temporally and spatially explicit emission estimates for CO 2 , NO x , SO 2 , PM, CO, and HC. In 2023, domestic civil aviation consumed 23.7 Mt of fuel, emitting 74.6 Mt CO 2 , 311.84 kt NO x , 73.5 kt CO, 6.02 kt HC, 23.69 kt SO 2 , and 2.00 kt PM. Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and Shapley variance decomposition demonstrate that physical observations constrain activity and fuel-flow uncertainties, narrowing the coefficients of variation (CV) to 1.5 %–20.0 % across pollutants and revealing that residual inventory variance is now dominated by emission-index parameterizations. At the process level, 1 Hz resolution successfully resolves transient operational dynamics obscured by phase-averaged models; for instance, low-power ground taxiing accounts for 21.9 % of total HC and 23.3 % of total CO emissions. Spatially, emissions are highly concentrated, with the top 10 % of 0.1 ° ×0.1 ° grid cells accounting for 76.7 % of national CO 2 emissions and exhibiting strong spatial clustering (Global Moran's I =0.4227, p <0.05) along trunk corridors and terminal areas. Ultimately, this dataset provides a robust empirical baseline for improving total emission estimates and offers a physical foundation for regional and near-airport air-quality assessments. The dataset is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23334964 (Lu et al., 2026).

title: Axion-induced Casimir interaction between graphene plates
summary: Axion dark matter may induce observable electromagnetic effects in resonant cavity systems, and potentially lead to modifications of the Casimir interaction. In this context, graphene represents a particularly attractive platform owing to i
content: Axion dark matter may induce observable electromagnetic effects in resonant cavity systems, and potentially lead to modifications of the Casimir interaction. In this context, graphene represents a particularly attractive platform owing to its distinctive and tunable electromagnetic properties, and the fact that its electromagnetic response can be modeled microscopically from first principles within quantum field theory. The electromagnetic response induced by axion dark matter is investigated in a planar cavity geometry consisting of parallel graphene interfaces in the presence of a homogeneous external magnetic field, incorporating finite temperature, chemical potential and dissipation effects through the graphene conductivity. Closed analytical expressions are obtained for the induced electric field and the resulting pressure exerted on the interfaces. The pressure exhibits resonant enhancement, at a series of plate separations satisfying d n = 2 π n − ϕ ( r ) m a , where m a is the axion mass and the phase ϕ ( r ) is determined by the reflection coefficient r , which depends on the graphene conductivity evaluated at the axion frequency ω = m a . The resonant structure is strongly influenced by the graphene chemical potential and damping parameter. In particular, increased doping, for example via a gate voltage, sharpens the resonances and amplifies the axion-induced signal. By comparing the resonantly enhanced signal with the conventional Casimir background, the parametric regimes in which the effect could become experimentally relevant are identified, with the strongest sensitivity obtained for highly doped low-dissipation graphene configurations operated near resonance. These results demonstrate that graphene-based Casimir-type configurations may provide a sensitive framework for probing axion-induced electromagnetic phenomena and highlight the interplay between axion electrodynamics, cavity resonances, and material properties in low-dimensional systems.

title: Analyzing the Impact of Travel Time on the Driving Assignment Strategies of Heavy Duty Trucks
summary: One of the major global source of carbon dioxide (CO $$_2$$ 2 ) emissions is the transport sector, particularly heavy-duty trucks (HDTs). The deployment of plug-in hybrid HDTs is a challenging yet a sustainable solution to achieve climate n
content: One of the major global source of carbon dioxide (CO $$_2$$ 2 ) emissions is the transport sector, particularly heavy-duty trucks (HDTs). The deployment of plug-in hybrid HDTs is a challenging yet a sustainable solution to achieve climate neutrality. Optimal driving assignment strategies are known to extend the potential electric range and reduce CO $$_2$$ 2 emissions. This work incorporates travel time, a critical metric in logistics, as a primary variable in the analysis. For that, an integrated framework that uses topographical data, an accurate energy consumption model and an optimization algorithm is employed. Nine real scenarios selected from the busiest freight route in Spain are studied. Specifically, the 640 km Cádiz–Madrid corridor is analyzed using the three different available battery capacities (30/60/90 kWh) of the SCANIA PHE Euro 6 (9-L engine), and three different traffic road conditions reflected on the HDT speed (60/80/100% of nominal speed). Results show that the proposed methodology reduces over 43% of the CO $$_2$$ 2 compared to a diesel internal combustion engine, with less than 9% extra travel time. Compared to the state of the art, the proposed tri-objective formulation preserves efficiency gains and elucidates feasible solutions within established time delivery constraints. This framework analyzes how battery capacity and traffic shape the emissions–time trade-off.

title: Unlocking Data-Driven Transport and Logistics: Challenges, Opportunities, and Insights from European Initiatives
summary: European transport and logistics sectors are undergoing a transformative shift driven by the increasing adoption of data-driven solutions. This paper explores challenges and opportunities associated with implementing data-sharing frameworks
content: European transport and logistics sectors are undergoing a transformative shift driven by the increasing adoption of data-driven solutions. This paper explores challenges and opportunities associated with implementing data-sharing frameworks and interoperable systems, drawing insights from European initiatives such as KEYSTONE and HOLOGISTICS projects and DTLF group. Fragmented data ecosystems and associated sociotechnical barriers, such as lack of inter-organisational trust and concerns over data sovereignty, significant barriers to realising the full potential of data-driven transport. However, innovations like federated platforms, real-time data utilisation and collaborative frameworks have demonstrated their ability to enhance operational efficiency, reduce environmental impact and improve resilience across multimodal transport networks. This paper presents valuable lessons learned, highlighting practical outcomes, including reduced times, optimised resource allocation, and emissions reductions. It also offers policy recommendations and a technological roadmap to address remaining barriers, scale solutions, and align with European Union’s strategic objectives for sustainability and digital integration, particularly in support of EU’s Green Deal and climate neutrality targets for 2050, also in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. By addressing these challenges and leveraging emerging technologies, Europe’s transport and logistics sectors can achieve cleaner, more resilient, and connected mobility systems, setting a global benchmark for sustainable innovation.

title: The illusion of clean energy: unveiling biohazardous PFAS risks from lithium-ion batteries
summary: The sharp rise of CO 2 and other greenhouse gases has accelerated the global push toward clean energy technologies, with lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) emerging as a cornerstone of this transition. From powering smartphones and laptops to dri
content: The sharp rise of CO 2 and other greenhouse gases has accelerated the global push toward clean energy technologies, with lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) emerging as a cornerstone of this transition. From powering smartphones and laptops to driving the rapid adoption of electric vehicles, LIBs are celebrated for enabling cleaner air and reducing CO 2 emissions. Yet beneath this promise lies a troubling paradox: these same batteries rely on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a class of highly persistent “ forever chemicals ” in their manufacturing. This dependence risks transforming a climate solution into a new source of pollution during production, operation, or end-of-life recycling. Without careful oversight, the pursuit of lower greenhouse gas emissions could inadvertently substitute one form of pollution for another, compounding global environmental challenges. This perspective highlights the overlooked risks, pathways of exposure, and regulatory blind spots surrounding the use of PFAS in LIBs.

title: Site engineering of spinel electrocatalysts for water oxidation: from bulk modulation to confined interfaces
summary: Spinel oxides (AB2O4) have emerged as widely studied non-noble-metal electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction owing to their structural plasticity, versatile cationic valence states, and cost-effectiveness. To circumvent the high
content: Spinel oxides (AB2O4) have emerged as widely studied non-noble-metal electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction owing to their structural plasticity, versatile cationic valence states, and cost-effectiveness. To circumvent the high activation barriers of multi-step proton-coupled electron transfer and improve catalytic efficiency, current research has shifted toward advanced site engineering to precisely orchestrate the catalytic active centers. This review presents a structured framework that organizes site-engineering strategies into three complementary dimensions. At the bulk level, strategic cation substitution, high-entropy-oxide engineering, and defect engineering deeply remodel the d-orbital configurations and metal-oxygen covalency, which can alter lattice-oxygen reactivity and may help reduce activity limitations under selected conditions. At the surface level, we examine high-energy-facet exposure, lattice-strain effects, and operando reconstruction, which may generate catalytically relevant oxyhydroxide species in selected systems and influence interfacial kinetics. Finally, built-in electric fields at coupled interfaces can promote charge redistribution, while genuine spatial confinement and molecular-level control over the solid-liquid microenvironment can improve interfacial transport and intermediate regulation. By synthesizing these multi-scale strategies, this review proposes an organizing framework for the rational design of next-generation, highly efficient electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction.

title: A study on pricing decisions in dual-channel fresh agricultural product supply chains considering risk aversion and blockchain technology
summary: Pricing decisions in the fresh agricultural produce supply chain face multiple challenges, including product perishability, information asymmetry, and market demand uncertainty. The dual-channel sales model and blockchain technology offer n
content: Pricing decisions in the fresh agricultural produce supply chain face multiple challenges, including product perishability, information asymmetry, and market demand uncertainty. The dual-channel sales model and blockchain technology offer new opportunities to enhance consumer trust and operational efficiency. This paper constructs a Stackelberg game model for a dual-channel fresh agricultural product supply chain comprising producers and retailers, in which producers determine wholesale prices, online direct-sales prices, and the level of preservation efforts, while retailers determine offline retail prices. A mean-variance utility function is used to characterize the degree of risk aversion among participants. Under two scenarios—with and without blockchain—the study derives equilibrium decisions for four risk-aversion combinations: both producers and retailers are risk-neutral; only producers are risk-averse; only retailers are risk-averse; and both are risk-averse. Theoretical derivations are validated through numerical simulations. The study found that risk aversion among fresh agricultural product producers has a significant suppressing effect on wholesale prices, online prices, and the level of freshness preservation efforts, and this effect holds true in both scenarios—with and without blockchain technology. The impact of retailers' risk aversion is moderated by the level of consumers' freshness preferences: when preferences are high, their risk aversion leads to increases in all decision variables; conversely, when preferences are low, it causes offline prices to decrease; The combined effects of risk aversion follow a consistent pattern: decision levels are lowest when only fresh agricultural product producers exhibit risk aversion, intermediate when both parties are risk-averse, and highest when only retailers are risk-averse; the introduction of blockchain technology can increase supply chain members' profits and channel demand, but the level of preservation effort consistently decreases as unit blockchain costs rise, while whether pricing decisions follow this cost increase depends on a specific threshold; There is a critical threshold for the variable cost per unit of blockchain; only when the cost is below this threshold can blockchain adopters achieve a Pareto improvement.

title: Exploring the Future of Urban Logistics Through Physical Internet Implementation Using Delphi
summary: E-commerce growth has intensified urban delivery demands while cities pursue environmental neutrality. This creates tension between consumer expectations for rapid deliveries and CO 2 reduction goals, as faster services typically decrease l
content: E-commerce growth has intensified urban delivery demands while cities pursue environmental neutrality. This creates tension between consumer expectations for rapid deliveries and CO 2 reduction goals, as faster services typically decrease load factors and increase emissions. While the Physical Internet paradigm holds significant academic promise for improving efficiency and reducing environmental impact, its practical implementation faces considerable barriers that contribute to a currently vague outlook on the widespread adoption of the PI. To navigate this uncertainty and better delineate future pathways, this study employed a structured three-phase methodology: (1) PI dimensions were identified through literature review, with each dimension presenting two options (optimistic and pessimistic scenarios); (2) DISCO experts voted on the most plausible options for each dimension by 2050, and these votes were analysed and used to generate nine archetypes; (3) these archetypes were then shared with 23 experts from industry and academia through a Delphi approach to identify the most plausible urban logistics PI scenarios. Results reveal optimism about technological advancements and futuristic logistics solutions, but significant hesitation regarding collaborative business models persists. This research provides expert and stakeholder insights to guide companies and city authorities in making informed investments and developing strategic initiatives for sustainable urban logistics transformation.

title: Freight Traffic Avoidance in Austria–Key Factors and a Network for Sharing Best Practices
summary: Freight transport is a major source of GHG emissions, and avoidance measures are increasingly recognized as critical for sustainable mobility. Within the Avoid-Shift-Improve framework, avoidance is often seen as the most effective but also
content: Freight transport is a major source of GHG emissions, and avoidance measures are increasingly recognized as critical for sustainable mobility. Within the Avoid-Shift-Improve framework, avoidance is often seen as the most effective but also the most difficult strategy to implement. This paper addresses this gap by developing an Actors-and-Competences Map (ACM) that identifies relevant Austrian avoidance actors, their competences, and inter-organizational relations in the field of traffic avoidance. The ACM, based on systematic data collection, participatory validation, and digital visualization, provides an empirical foundation for analyzing actors and practices. Empirical analysis of 163 best-practice cases shows that measures reducing vehicle kilometres (e.g., logistics collaborations, intermodal ride-sharing, car-go-bike delivery) are well represented. Strategies targeting transport performance (tonne-kilometres) are also widespread, with urban hubs, distribution centres, and route optimisation playing central roles. By contrast, volume-reduction measures remain rare, though digital tools, additive manufacturing, and circular economy models offer untapped potential. The study highlights concrete mechanisms to accelerate sustainable freight transitions. This project was funded by the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) as part of the Innovation Network for Traffic Avoidance project under the grant number FO999899483.

title: Reparations in the context of the international climate funds: a climate justice comparison
summary: With momentum for climate reparations continuing to grow, the newly established Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) is seen by some as an avenue for reparations in effect, if not in name. However, whether the FRLD constitutes a me
content: With momentum for climate reparations continuing to grow, the newly established Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) is seen by some as an avenue for reparations in effect, if not in name. However, whether the FRLD constitutes a mechanism for climate reparations is not universally agreed. This article explores what a funding mechanism for climate reparations might entail in practice. To do this, I identify five qualities of a functional climate reparations fund: just governance; link between responsibility, sources of funding, and recipients; appropriate funding modality; appropriate and accessible delivery; and political feasibility and durability. I then compare these qualities to the experiences of climate funds already established under the UNFCCC’s Financial Mechanism to assess the extent to which they exhibit these qualities in practice, finding a consistent pattern of justice shortcomings across the funds. Although the FRLD falls short of reparative ideals, in broadening conceptualisations of the kinds of climate funds that are possible, its realisation nevertheless represents a significant milestone in the pursuit of climate justice.

title: The Economic Cost Of “Clean Air”: Evidence From The Air Pollution Prevention And Control Action Plan In China
summary: The Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan (APPCAP) is considered China’s largest initiative to combat air pollution. Despite its effectiveness in reducing haze pollution, there is limited empirical evidence on its economic impact
content: The Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan (APPCAP) is considered China’s largest initiative to combat air pollution. Despite its effectiveness in reducing haze pollution, there is limited empirical evidence on its economic impact. Employing a continuous difference-in-differences design, this paper evaluates the effect of the APPCAP on economic output between 2009 and 2017. The findings suggest that the APPCAP leads to reductions in economic output in cities with stricter environmental regulations, with these effects resulting from the suppression of innovation and the tightening of financing constraints. Furthermore, this study reveals that the negative impacts on economic output are more pronounced in environmentally focused cities, economically less developed regions, and resource-poor areas. This study contributes to measuring the economic cost of clean air, while also providing insights into the economic consequences of environmental governance.

title: An Enhanced NSGA-III for Low-Carbon Multimodal Path Optimization in Port Transportation
source: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
summary: Driven by the carbon-neutrality target, port transportation requires routing methods that jointly optimize economic efficiency, carbon emissions, and network robustness. Existing studies mainly rely on static carbon constraints and conventi
content: Driven by the carbon-neutrality target, port transportation requires routing methods that jointly optimize economic efficiency, carbon emissions, and network robustness. Existing studies mainly rely on static carbon constraints and conventional evolutionary strategies, which often suffer from poor adaptability and limited Pareto diversity in large-scale multimodal transport networks. To address these issues, this paper proposes an enhanced low-carbon port path optimization framework (LCPPO-E) based on an improved NSGA-III. The main algorithmic innovations include a congestion-aware dual-layer chromosome encoding mechanism, an adaptive reference-point update strategy guided by population distribution, and an external elite archive with self-tuning crossover-mutation coordination. A tri-objective optimization model is constructed to minimize total transport cost, carbon emission intensity, and node congestion risk simultaneously. Shanghai Port container transport data are used for validation. Experimental results show that, compared with the traditional cost-minimization model, the proposed method reduces carbon emission intensity by 21.3% and node congestion rate by 28.6%, while increasing total cost by only 5.1%. In comparison with GA, PSO, NSGA-II, and standard NSGA-III, the proposed algorithm achieves the best comprehensive performance, with a hypervolume improvement of 6.1% over standard NSGA-III and an increase in multimodal transport share to 41.8%. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in solving low-carbon and resilient port routing problems.

title: Re-examining the relationship between artificial intelligence development and urban per capita carbon emissions within a government–market–public framework
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) development may be associated with urban emissions through technological applications and interactions among government, market, and public actors, yet city-level evidence remains limited. This study develops a
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) development may be associated with urban emissions through technological applications and interactions among government, market, and public actors, yet city-level evidence remains limited. This study develops a government–market–public (GMP) framework using panel data for 279 Chinese cities from 2013 to 2021. A city-level AI development index combines government policy support, AI-related firms and patents, and public attention. Two-way fixed-effects models with city-clustered standard errors assess its association with urban per capita carbon emissions, supplemented by sensitivity, spatial, pathway-consistency, and heterogeneity analyses. AI development is negatively associated with urban per capita carbon emissions in the baseline model and under alternative controls, lagged controls, province-by-year fixed effects, most leave-one-out tests, and the spatial model. The relationship is not sustained with city-specific linear trends or first differences, and a significant lead term complicates its temporal interpretation. Spatial estimates show a significant local association but no significant cross-city spillover. GMP regressions yield exploratory patterns involving government intervention, population agglomeration, and household income rather than verified transmission processes. Interaction tests indicate stronger negative associations in coastal cities and provincial capitals or centrally administered municipalities; city-size results remain exploratory. Overall, the findings reveal a context-dependent and specification-sensitive relationship between AI development and lower urban per capita carbon emissions.

title: Hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to formic acid over HZSM-5 zeolites modified with single-atom Rh and Mg
summary: Direct hydrogenation of CO 2 to formic acid represents a promising strategy for carbon capture and utilization. For the first time, commercially available HZSM-5 zeolites (Si/Al ~ 15–18) were systematically studied as heterogeneous catalyst
content: Direct hydrogenation of CO 2 to formic acid represents a promising strategy for carbon capture and utilization. For the first time, commercially available HZSM-5 zeolites (Si/Al ~ 15–18) were systematically studied as heterogeneous catalysts for this reaction under mild conditions. In a water-triethylamine medium at 60–150°C, all catalysts exhibited nearly 100% formic acid selectivity, with yields strongly governed by acidity and mesoporosity. Bimetallic Rh-Mg catalysts demonstrated a pronounced synergistic effect, yielding up to 5100 µmol·g –1 at 150°C, which is 7–17% higher than Rh alone and 1.6–3.7 times higher than Mg alone. The synergy originates from the close proximity of Rh and Mg, where adjacent Mg cations promote CO 2 adsorption and stabilizes intermediate formate species, preventing their decomposition at elevated temperatures. Controlled desilication further improved mesoporosity and active-site accessibility, increasing the yield to 5600 µmol·g –1 . Notably, retaining polyvinylpyrrolidone on the catalyst surface eliminated the requirement for an external amine, as it acts as a built‑in base. The optimized Rh-Mg/PVP/HZ des catalyst achieved the highest yield of 5780 µmol·g –1 .

title: Uneven Progress in Urban Air Quality: Evidence From the Greater Bay Area and Implications for Metropolitan Management
source: Journal of Urban Development and Management
summary: Improving urban air quality requires attention to both regional trends and persistent differences between cities. This study examines how these patterns inform urban environmental management across the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay
content: Improving urban air quality requires attention to both regional trends and persistent differences between cities. This study examines how these patterns inform urban environmental management across the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area. Official observations from 23 monitoring stations across 11 cities during 2019–2025 were analysed using city comparisons, a continuity-screened sample of 18 stations, and monthly regressions with seasonal controls and heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent covariance estimates. Economic associations were examined using matched air quality and gross domestic product (GDP) per capita data for 2024. Across all stations, annual mean concentrations of particulate matter (PM$_{10}$ and PM$_{2.5}$) and nitrogen dioxide (NO$_2$) declined by 18.4%, 23.8% and 25.0%, respectively, with reductions recorded in every city. However, the between-city coefficient of variation (CV) for PM$_{10}$ increased from 0.126 to 0.153, and the correlation between the 2019 and 2025 city rankings was 0.835. Monthly models estimated an annual PM$_{2.5}$ decline of 5.50%, whereas the ozone (O$_3$) trend was −0.12% per year, with a 95% confidence interval of −3.21% to 3.07%. Higher GDP per capita was associated with lower PM$_{2.5}$ in 2024, but the relationship varied across pollutants. The official dust-adjusted PM$_{10}$ mean for 2025 matched the reported 2024 value, removing the apparent rebound at the published precision. These findings show that regional improvement alone provides an incomplete assessment of urban air quality progress. Urban environmental management requires pollutant-specific monitoring, continued assessment of intercity disparities and coordinated evaluation of exceptional pollution episodes. The study provides a reproducible basis for identifying monitoring priorities across cities and distinguishing regional fluctuations from persistent local conditions.

title: European Green Deal and climate change regulations: The Bulgarian perspective
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study aims to map the legal framework and critically evaluate the transposition of EU regulations concerning climate change mitigation and the green energy transition in Bulgaria. It focuses
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study aims to map the legal framework and critically evaluate the transposition of EU regulations concerning climate change mitigation and the green energy transition in Bulgaria. It focuses on the institutional implementation deficits against the relevant European Green Deal legal benchmarks. The methodological approach incorporates both contemporary legal research methods and interdisciplinary analytical tools. The paper draws primarily on European policies for sustainable development, EU primary law, enacted climate change directives and regulations, and scholarly literature and research reports on relevant themes. The green transition in Bulgaria involves not simply the transposition of EU directives but the production of an autonomous national legal architecture having the formal capacity and legal credibility to drive the transformation from within. While Bulgaria has gradually aligned its national legislation with EU climate and energy law, the legislative action has been reactive and inefficiently attached to a coherent national vision of the energy sector. Transposition steps often occurred under direct pressure from the European Commission's infringement proceedings and financial sanctions imposed by the Court of Justice of the European Union. Based on its findings, the paper outlines recommendations for strengthening Bulgarian legal architecture in conformity with its obligations under the European Green Deal. Bulgaria should strengthen its climate governance by introducing legally binding national carbon budgets under the Climate Change Mitigation Act, supported by independent scientific oversight. Key measures include establishing an independent climate advisory body, adopting a coal phase-out law with mandatory transition commitments, and fully transposing RED III.AcknowledgmentThis work was financially supported by thе UNWE Research Programme.

title: China’s carbon neutrality strengthens its photovoltaic potential: Co-benefits for climate action and energy security
summary: Solar photovoltaic (PV) power is central to China’s carbon neutrality strategy, but the extent to which mitigation reshapes the climate resource base for PV generation remains uncertain. Here we combine Earth system simulations with a 0.1°-
content: Solar photovoltaic (PV) power is central to China’s carbon neutrality strategy, but the extent to which mitigation reshapes the climate resource base for PV generation remains uncertain. Here we combine Earth system simulations with a 0.1°-resolution deep learning downscaling framework to quantify changes in China’s meteorological PV potential under divergent emission pathways. We find that the carbon-neutral SSP2-com pathway not only stabilizes but actively strengthens national meteorological PV potential by century’s end (+0.27% relative to 1981−2010 baseline), whereas high emissions trigger a persistent decline (−0.49%). Crucially, stringent mitigation induces a fundamental spatial restructuring: it shields premium solar resources in western China from severe depletion (e.g. Tibet: −0.42% under SSP2-com versus −1.23% under SSP3-7.0), while substantially boosting meteorological PV potential in historically resource-constrained eastern provinces (e.g. Guizhou: +1.05%, Hunan: +1.04%, Jiangxi: +0.97%, Fujian: +1.07%). This asymmetric response reduces interprovincial disparities in solar resource availability. Factor-separation analyses attribute most changes to shortwave radiation rather than temperature or wind speed, consistent with aerosol-related brightening under stringent mitigation. Our findings reveal that carbon neutrality functions not merely as a climate corrective but as a potential driver of energy security, potentially contributing to a solar landscape with greater spatial equity and resilience.

title: Household Satisfaction and Compensation Preferences under the Grain-for-Green Program: Evidence from Guyuan on China’s Loess Plateau
summary: Household evaluations provide important evidence for diagnosing problems in ecological compensation programs. However, concerns about payment standards need to be distinguished from overall dissatisfaction before policy responses are design
content: Household evaluations provide important evidence for diagnosing problems in ecological compensation programs. However, concerns about payment standards need to be distinguished from overall dissatisfaction before policy responses are designed. Taking Guyuan on China’s Loess Plateau as a case study, this research used a 2024 convenience survey of 1,650 Grain-for-Green households to examine compensation evaluations and preferences. Descriptive analysis and multivariable Logit models (n = 1,601 complete cases) were combined with locality-clustered uncertainty estimation, multiple-comparison correction and sensitivity analyses. The results show that (1) 39.7% of surveyed households were satisfied, 32.4% were neutral and 27.9% were dissatisfied, with substantial differences across sampled counties and districts. (2) Low payment standards were reported by 1,588 households (96.2%); nevertheless, 71.6% of this group were satisfied or neutral overall. Concern about payment amounts therefore did not necessarily indicate overall dissatisfaction. (3) Jingyuan households had higher odds of dissatisfaction than Longde households (OR = 23.31), while respondents who were not very familiar with policy had higher odds than those who were very familiar (OR = 11.82). Both contrasts retained statistical support after multiple-comparison correction and exclusion of Pengyang, and the familiarity contrast persisted in locality fixed-effect models. These estimates did not establish a monotonic familiarity gradient. Evidence for individual maintenance depended on model specification and multiplicity correction, while total income category showed no clear common linear association. (4) Among households’ preferred compensation arrangements, cash payments were the most frequently selected option (86.0%); employment opportunities (28.5%) and vocational training (19.9%) were also preferred. This study provides empirical evidence for distinguishing payment-specific concerns from overall evaluations and identifying priorities for local investigation before compensation arrangements are redesigned.

title: Elucidating the Iron Effect in Alkaline Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Structural Transformation, Dynamic Synergy, and Industrial Realities
summary: Electrochemical water splitting is critical for carbon neutrality, but its efficiency is significantly limited by the kinetically slow oxygen evolution reaction (OER). While earth-abundant 3d transition-metal catalysts are promising alterna
content: Electrochemical water splitting is critical for carbon neutrality, but its efficiency is significantly limited by the kinetically slow oxygen evolution reaction (OER). While earth-abundant 3d transition-metal catalysts are promising alternatives, their exceptional performance is strongly associated with the prominent Fe effect. The electrocatalysis community remains divided by prolonged scientific discussion regarding whether Fe functions as a direct active site or a passive electronic spectator. Moving beyond conventional material classifications (e.g., oxides, sulfides, phosphides, nitrides, etc.), we propose a unified paradigm: these diverse matrices fundamentally act as pre-catalysts, while Fe universally directs their dynamic surface reconstruction into catalytically active (oxy)hydroxide phases. Synthesizing operando and theoretical evidence, we elucidate the true active site as a dynamic, highly flexible dual-metal synergistic interface. Crucially, we identify a critical gap: the significant disconnect between idealized lab-scale testing and demanding industrial conditions. We demonstrate how Fe-induced porosity unexpectedly becomes a significant mass-transfer limitation under extreme industrial gas evolution. To bridge this gap, we outline a practical roadmap advocating for standardized industrial-condition testing, extreme-environment operando techniques, heterointerface engineering against Fe leaching, and artificial intelligence-driven materials discovery. This Review provides a comprehensive framework for designing industrially robust OER electrocatalysts.

title: AI-Enabled Governance Systems for Sustainable Development: From Goals to Ecosystems
summary: Demonstrating how modular, AI-enabled governance systems can transform sustainability from fragmented commitments into coherent action, this book presents an integrated governance ecosystem spanning policy coherence, corporate transformatio
content: Demonstrating how modular, AI-enabled governance systems can transform sustainability from fragmented commitments into coherent action, this book presents an integrated governance ecosystem spanning policy coherence, corporate transformation, territorial governance, and sustainable finance and trade. Arguing that sustainability can no longer be treated as a collection of aspirational targets, the book shows how meaningful change depends on operationalising sustainability through modular governance functions that can be adapted across governments, businesses, territories, financial institutions, and international trade. Grounded in five years of applied research, system design, and pilot implementations across Europe and Africa, it moves beyond abstract debate to demonstrate how sustainability can be embedded within everyday governance and decision-making. The book introduces new approaches for measuring policy effort, applying AI-enabled coherence diagnostics, embedding ESG across corporate functions, strengthening territorial governance through interoperable data systems, supporting participatory yet accountable local governance, and aligning finance and trade with long-term sustainability and competitiveness. Through comparative analysis and practical illustrations, it contrasts outcome-based monitoring with effort-based benchmarking, fragmented governance structures with AI-enabled coherence, and compliance-driven reporting with continuous organisational transformation. Rather than treating sustainability as a checklist of goals, the book presents it as an actionable governance ecosystem capable of translating strategic ambition into operational reality. Written for students, researchers, and practitioners of sustainability and governance, the book will also be of interest to policymakers, business leaders, investors, and professionals working in ESG, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), sustainable finance, public policy, and digital governance.

title: Unveiling hidden risks in the decoupling of carbon emissions from building growth: evidence from China
summary: Balancing economic growth with carbon reduction has become a critical challenge for China’s building sector under its carbon peaking and neutrality goals. However, conventional decoupling assessments mainly focus on relative changes between
content: Balancing economic growth with carbon reduction has become a critical challenge for China’s building sector under its carbon peaking and neutrality goals. However, conventional decoupling assessments mainly focus on relative changes between emissions and economic output and may overlook hidden risks associated with continued absolute emission growth. This study integrates the Tapio decoupling index with the Crisis Resolution Degree model to develop a continuous decoupling quality index (DQ). Using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces during 2006–2022, spatial analysis and interpretable machine learning approaches are employed to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution and nonlinear drivers of DQ. The results show that the average DQ increased by 14.22%, and healthy states accounted for more than 50% of provincial observations in the final phase. DQ exhibited stage-specific spatial clustering and neighborhood-conditioned transitions, with high-DQ neighboring regions facilitating upward transitions, whereas low-DQ neighboring regions increasing the likelihood of downward transitions. Carbon emission intensity and material structure were identified as the dominant factors influencing DQ, with approximate turning points at 2.85 t CO₂/10 4 CNY and 23.5%, respectively. Furthermore, the interaction between carbon emission intensity and material structure showed the strongest synergistic effect among the examined factors. These findings provide a new perspective for uncovering hidden risks behind apparent decoupling and supporting differentiated low-carbon transition pathways in the building sector.

title: Regiospecific Sila‐Matteson Homologative Arylation of Biased ( N ‐Oxide) Azines
summary: The judicious selection of silicon-as a Lewis acid-able to generate penta- and hexavalent hypercoordinated ate complexes is herein presented as a strategy to realize conceptually novel homologative arylations. Chemically stable aryl- equipp
content: The judicious selection of silicon-as a Lewis acid-able to generate penta- and hexavalent hypercoordinated ate complexes is herein presented as a strategy to realize conceptually novel homologative arylations. Chemically stable aryl- equipped C1-silanes, conveniently activated with the same biased (N-oxide) substrate in the presence of fluoride, furnish-upon fine-tuning of consecutive [1,2]-transposition events-benzyl-like nucleophilic elements which are precisely transferred at the C2-position of azines. These benzyl synthons originate from combining an aryl residue and the homologating methylene fragment. The regioselective logic is levered on the unique capability of silicon to undergo two controllable expansive-contractive modifications of its coordinative sphere. Compared to single rearrangements accomplished with labile C1-donors on boron manifolds-retained in the final products (Matteson-like)-the silicon approach directly gathers heteroatom-free azines, thus documenting high versatility for rapid and predictable functionalization.

title: Brazilian Intergovernmental Fiscal Relations: Tax Assignment and Tax Sharing
summary: This chapter analyses Brazil’s intergovernmental fiscal relations, focusing on the constitutional allocation of taxing powers and tax sharing mechanisms across the country’s three-tier federation. It maps the tax assignment system under the
content: This chapter analyses Brazil’s intergovernmental fiscal relations, focusing on the constitutional allocation of taxing powers and tax sharing mechanisms across the country’s three-tier federation. It maps the tax assignment system under the 1988 Constitution, covering federal, state, and municipal levies, and examines the coordination instruments governing overlapping tax bases. Special attention is devoted to Brazil’s historically fragmented multi-level consumption tax system and to its replacement by a destination-based dual Value Added Tax through the landmark Constitutional Amendment 132 of 2023. The chapter also examines federal and subnational tax sharing arrangements, including the participation funds and innovative ecological and performance-based transfer criteria. A critical assessment identifies persistent vertical fiscal imbalances, horizontal disparities, and ineffective equalization mechanisms. The chapter concludes with comparative insights, highlighting Brazil’s tax reform as a pioneering experiment with broader lessons for fiscal federalism.

title: Regional emissions in post-transition Central Europe: An overview on greenhouse gas emissions per capita in the Visegrád regions since the 1990s
summary: Air pollution, particularly greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, is among the forms of environmental degradation most consistently measured using harmonized international methodologies. This study analyzes long-term trends and regional dispariti
content: Air pollution, particularly greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, is among the forms of environmental degradation most consistently measured using harmonized international methodologies. This study analyzes long-term trends and regional disparities in per capita GHG emissions, expressed in tons of CO2 equivalent, across the NUTS 2 regions of the four Visegrád (V4) countries – Czechia, Hungary,Poland and Slovakia – over the period 1990–2024. Although the collapse of the former socialist heavy industry reduced emissions, increased integration into the global economy introduced new environmental pressures. The findings of the linear trend tests indicate that the predominant trend during the period under scrutiny exhibited a significant decline in GHG emissions per capita. Nevertheless, seven of the 37 regions experienced statistically significant increases, and eight exhibited no significant trends, implying persistent regional heterogeneity. The results of the firstdifference panel regression underpin that reductions in regional emissions remainedsensitive to economic fluctuations.

title: Spectrally Adaptive Electrochromic Windows for Year‐Round Photothermal Management
summary: Advanced glazing systems harness natural resources to minimize carbon emissions generated by traditional heating and cooling infrastructure, providing sustainable alternatives for indoor photothermal management. However, achieving independe
content: Advanced glazing systems harness natural resources to minimize carbon emissions generated by traditional heating and cooling infrastructure, providing sustainable alternatives for indoor photothermal management. However, achieving independent modulation across multiple spectral bands remains a critical challenge for them, which leads to undesirable radiative heat loss or gain throughout the year. Here, we present a spectrally adaptive electrochromic window to optimally utilize both solar and thermal radiation in diverse climates. Featuring indium‐free wideband transparent electrodes, this window integrates 65% solar modulation with a low mid‐wave infrared emissivity of 0.26. Its asymmetric heat‐emission structure enables the secondary heat radiation from the solar‐heated window to radiate toward outer space for cooling, while preserving superior solar transmission and heat insulation for indoor heating. Field experiments demonstrate that, compared to the conventional window, our design breaks the limitations on its maximum thermal modulating power, raising the internal temperature by 6.9°C in winter and exhibiting an extra temperature reduction of 7.6°C in summer. Simulations show that the window would save up to 38% of annual energy consumption relative to commercial glass. This photonic approach offers a scalable solution toward carbon neutrality, paving the way for a more sustainable and resilient urban development.

title: Blockchain–Quantum Computing Integration for Smart City Pollution Management: A Comprehensive Framework for Multi-Pollutant Mitigation, Traceability, and Environmental Sustainability
summary: Rapid urbanization and industrial expansion have exacerbated multi-domain environmental degradation, encompassing greenhouse gas emissions, air particulate pollution, aquatic contamination, solid waste accumulation, and soil toxicity. Tradi
content: Rapid urbanization and industrial expansion have exacerbated multi-domain environmental degradation, encompassing greenhouse gas emissions, air particulate pollution, aquatic contamination, solid waste accumulation, and soil toxicity. Traditional environmental management systems suffer from centralized data vulnerabilities, severe computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional telemetry, and lack of immutable regulatory traceability. This manuscript presents a conceptual architecture and comprehensive narrative literature review exploring the theoretical integration of blockchain technology and quantum computing for smart city pollution management. Specifically, this study examines how decentralized cryptographic ledgers, quantum machine learning (QML), and quantum optimization algorithms can be coupled with 6G wireless communication infrastructures to automate real-time multi-pollutant mitigation. Furthermore, this work explicitly broadens the analysis of blockchain's established environmental applications—including pollution-data traceability, emissions monitoring, electronic waste tracking, supply-chain transparency, and regulatory compliance—while critically assessing how blockchain capabilities directly complement quantum computing in overcoming urban pollution challenges. The investigation is structured as a systematic narrative synthesis examining literature across databases including IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink. The primary findings indicate that while quantum algorithms offer theoretical quadratic-to-exponential speedups for specific combinatorial optimization and molecular simulation problems under ideal fault-tolerant assumptions, current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware constraints necessitate hybrid classical-quantum workflows. Moreover, blockchain smart contracts combined with quantum-resistant lattice-based cryptography can secure environmental telemetry against emerging quantum decryption threats while providing immutable audit trails.

title: Activating N = O Bond Cleavage Via Geometrically Matched Co‐C Atomic Pairs for Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Electrosynthesis
summary: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO 3 − ) to ammonia (NH 3 ) is an attractive synthesis route, yet its efficiency is fundamentally limited by sluggish N = O bond cleavage due to insufficient N = O bond stretching and slow electron
content: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO 3 − ) to ammonia (NH 3 ) is an attractive synthesis route, yet its efficiency is fundamentally limited by sluggish N = O bond cleavage due to insufficient N = O bond stretching and slow electron transfer. Here, we report that cobalt oxide supported on oxygen‐functionalized carbon felt (CoO/O‐CF) overcomes these limitations. In this catalyst, the Co–C atomic pairs exhibit an interatomic distance that geometrically matches the O–O spacing in NO 3 − , stabilizing an O‐bridged bidentate adsorption configuration. Characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that this geometry concomitantly elongates the N = O bonds and enhances electron donation from active sites to their antibonding orbitals, accelerating N = O bond cleavage. Consequently, CoO/O‐CF delivers a high NH 3 yield rate of 16.8 mmol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 93.2% at –0.7 V vs. RHE in neutral wastewater. The outstanding performance of CoO/O‐CF surpasses that of previously reported state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Furthermore, CoO/O‐CF operates as a high‐performance cathode in a Zn‐NO 3 − battery, achieving simultaneous NH 3 electrosynthesis and energy output with a power density of 13.98 mW cm −2 . This work reveals how geometric correspondence in atomic pairs can be leveraged to activate challenging oxyanions, offering a promising design paradigm for advanced electrocatalysis in sustainable nitrogen cycling.

title: Constitutional Environmental Rights: Albania and Italy in Comparative Perspective
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
summary: The relationship between formal constitutional recognition and effective implementation remains contested and empirically underexplored, particularly in post-communist legal systems and EU candidate states. While existing comparative enviro
content: The relationship between formal constitutional recognition and effective implementation remains contested and empirically underexplored, particularly in post-communist legal systems and EU candidate states. While existing comparative environmental law scholarship addresses either single jurisdictions or broad regional surveys, the specific normative-institutional comparison between Albania and Italy two Adriatic neighbours at different stages of EU integration remains unexplored. This gap is particularly significant given Albania's EU accession process under Chapter 27 of the acquis communautaire and Italy's landmark 2022 constitutional reform. This article presents a systematic comparative legal analysis of constitutional environmental rights in Albania (Articles 56 and 59, Constitution of the Republic of Albania, 1998) and Italy (Articles 9 and 41, as amended by Constitutional Law No. 1/2022, 2022). Employing a twelve-dimensional analytical matrix developed through a modified functionalist approach (Zweigert & Kötz, 1998) the study integrates formal-normative, institutional, and outcome-oriented dimensions weighted by their relevance to rights effectiveness. On a weighted scale of 10, Albania scores 5.60 and Italy 8.18, yielding a mean gap of 2.58 points. The most pronounced divergences concern jurisprudential development (−4.5), institutional capacity (−3.5), and judicial access (−3.0). Critically, the smallest gap (−1.0) appears at the level of formal constitutional recognition, establishing that Albania's implementation deficit is structural rather than textual a pattern the article conceptualizes as an "implementation gap" within the literature on aspirational constitutionalism. A four-phase Normative Convergence Model (2025–2035) and five priority reform pillars are proposed for Albania, with implications for both comparative environmental constitutionalism theory and EU accession policy. title: The properties of wool fabrics modified by poly(vinyl alcohol) acetals
summary: Wool fabrics suffer from inherent drawbacks such as felting propensity, energy-intensive dyeing requirements (typically necessitating boiling conditions), and relatively lower mechanical strength and pilling resistance compared with synthet
content: Wool fabrics suffer from inherent drawbacks such as felting propensity, energy-intensive dyeing requirements (typically necessitating boiling conditions), and relatively lower mechanical strength and pilling resistance compared with synthetic fibers, limiting their use in high-performance textiles. To address these issues, a dual-crosslinked polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) acetal (GE-PVA), crosslinked simultaneously through acetal and ester covalent bonds using glyoxylic acid and ethyl glyoxylate, was prepared and applied to wool fabric through an impregnation, padding and curing process. Characterization included attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), zeta-potential analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), while hydrophilicity, antibacterial activity, mechanical properties, felting shrinkage, and pilling resistance were systematically evaluated. The partially crosslinked PVA-based coating was deposited on untreated wool fibers to prepare the GE-PVA-modified wool fabric (GE-PVA@WF), and was fully crosslinked during curing, thereby enhancing the hydrophilicity of the fabric. The modified fabrics showed a 99.97% inhibition rate against Staphylococcus aureus (maintained at 99.78% after 50 washing cycles). Moreover, the felting shrinkage rate was reduced by up to 85.8%; pilling resistance reached Grade 5; and the breaking strength reached 248.2% of that of the blank wool fabric. Under moist conditions (30% moisture regain), the relative increase in effective thermal conductivity was smaller for the coated fabric (172%) than for the untreated wool (279%). A system-level assessment of thermophysiological comfort was outside the scope of this work. This strategy provides multifunctional wool fabrics integrating hydrophilicity, antibacterial activity, antifelting performance, and mechanical strength, holding significant potential for textile and apparel applications.

title: Effect of Normal Saline and Balanced Salt Solution on Resuscitation of Patients with Peritonitis: A Prospective Randomized Study
summary: Background: This study aimed to evaluate differences in metabolic parameters following resuscitation with either normal saline or Plasmalyte A in patients undergoing surgery for perforated peritonitis.Methods: In this prospective, randomize
content: Background: This study aimed to evaluate differences in metabolic parameters following resuscitation with either normal saline or Plasmalyte A in patients undergoing surgery for perforated peritonitis.Methods: In this prospective, randomized study, 50 adult patients (≥18 years) of either gender presenting with peritonitis and undergoing emergency exploratory laparotomy were enrolled. Patients were randomly allocated into two groups of 25 each: Group A received Plasmalyte A for resuscitation; Group B received normal saline for resuscitation. We recorded baseline measurements, including blood pressure, heart rate, SpO2, and arterial blood gases (ABG). We then assessed these parameters one hour after fluid resuscitation, preoperatively, intraoperatively (at incision), and postoperatively.Results: The mean age in Group A was 38.56 ± 17.18 years, and in Group B, 39.80 ± 15.93 years (p = 0.792). Group B showed a notable intraoperative decrease in mean arterial pressure (MAP) (73.21 ± 6.95 mmHg) compared with the preoperative period (79.38 ± 7.35 mmHg). Group B also showed a significant intraoperative drop in pH (p < 0.001) and a corresponding increase in intraoperative and postoperative PCO2 levels compared with Group A. Group B also showed a persistent increase in serum sodium levels throughout the study period.Conclusion: Compared to normal saline, Plasmalyte A offers superior preservation of metabolic stability in patients undergoing large-volume resuscitation. Consequently, it is highly recommended as the crystalloid of choice in these clinical settings.

title: A race at all costs? Economic and environmental effects of geoeconomic rivalry in clean energy technologies
summary: Major economies are increasingly protecting their domestic clean-technology industries from one another. We ask what happens if this protection becomes reciprocal and escalates. Using regulatory, fiscal, or trade policies to protect and pro
content: Major economies are increasingly protecting their domestic clean-technology industries from one another. We ask what happens if this protection becomes reciprocal and escalates. Using regulatory, fiscal, or trade policies to protect and promote the interests of national industries against external competition may increase the cost of transformation and delay the diffusion of key low-carbon technologies. But how large are these effects? And do these measures actually help to achieve the objective of strengthening domestic industrial competitiveness and resilience of domestic industries?
