Employing a macroeconomic model, we assess scenarios with varying stringency of protectionism in which the five leading industrial economies symmetrically impose import tariffs on clean energy technologies and their upstream value chains and recycle the revenues into subsidies for domestic producers. We find that this reciprocal tariff escalation may double the mitigation cost for some regions in the most stringent case. Its environmental effects are small as reduced economic growth compensates for less efficient climate action. We also show that protective tariffs are hardly effective where major economies deploy them symmetrically. Only under the most stringent assumptions can we observe some limited success in boosting domestic competitiveness of green industries. Our analysis provides a first quantification of the economic and environmental costs of the geoeconomic turn in decarbonisation. Going beyond the modelled effects, we discuss the risk that sharply rising transition costs erode domestic support for climate policy and international cooperation, and we underline the need for collaborative governance to contain escalating geoeconomic rivalry.

title: Towards a standardised baseline methodology to support the EU carbon farming certification in agricultural mineral soils
summary: Carbon farming refers to management practices aimed at increasing biogenic carbon pools or reduce their emissions. However, methodologies for the accreditation of carbon farming projects vary in their implementation and scientific rigor, ha
content: Carbon farming refers to management practices aimed at increasing biogenic carbon pools or reduce their emissions. However, methodologies for the accreditation of carbon farming projects vary in their implementation and scientific rigor, hampering an effective voluntary carbon market. The European Union’s regulation for Carbon Removal and Carbon Farming (CRCF) includes the standardised baseline concept to calculate emissions/removals under the “additionality” principle. We present a proof of concept model ensemble, based on LUCAS soil data and process-based modelling results, that supports standardised baseline development across European agricultural mineral soils. Across the test areas, estimates of soil organic carbon (SOC) change differed both in their magnitude and sign, depending on the models and input data used. Harmonizing and aligning model inputs allowed a better convergence of results from different models, while model ensemble was suggested to be the best approach for less biased estimates. The standard deviation associated with the ensemble quantified to what extent different approaches diverge. Future work could expand the standardised baseline methodology with: i.) parcel-level agricultural activity data, ii.) assessing different configurations of model ensembles and their effect on the additionality of SOC emissions/removals.

title: Climate suitability of East Asian mangroves for nature-based solutions is limited by climate extremes
summary: Mangroves represent distinctive coastal ecosystems that offer ecological benefits, notably through their high carbon sequestration rates. However, their resilience to extreme climate events remains uncertain. Here, we investigated the respo
content: Mangroves represent distinctive coastal ecosystems that offer ecological benefits, notably through their high carbon sequestration rates. However, their resilience to extreme climate events remains uncertain. Here, we investigated the response of mangroves in East Asia to climate variability by employing the remote-sensing derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) as a proxy for canopy greenness. A bootstrapping-based statistical framework was applied to identify vegetation responses associated with extreme climate events and quantify lagged climatic effects. We found East Asian mangrove NDVI variability was strongly influenced by preceding winter temperature and seasonal solar radiation, with distinct lagged responses on seasonal time scales across latitudinal zones. These findings were extrapolated to future projections by the Earth system modelling to assess future climate suitability for existing mangroves and for areas of potential thermal suitability in East Asia, particularly China, South Korea and Japan. While shifts in wintertime isotherms suggest a northward shift in the thermal range of mangroves under global warming, low solar radiation events associated with aerosol emissions under the high-emission SSP3-7.0 scenario could constrain future climatic suitability for mangroves. This study highlights that both temperature-driven opportunities and solar radiation constraints should be integrated into practical planning for future conservation, restoration, and migration as nature-based climate solutions.

title: An equitable framework for verifying airline contrail mitigation
source: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
summary: Aviation’s non-CO 2 effects, particularly contrails, contribute radiative forcing potentially 1.7 times as large as cumulative CO 2 emissions since 1940. The EU’s 2025 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification framework requires European airl
content: Aviation’s non-CO 2 effects, particularly contrails, contribute radiative forcing potentially 1.7 times as large as cumulative CO 2 emissions since 1940. The EU’s 2025 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification framework requires European airlines to report these effects through the NEATS tool, and COM(2026) 616 is the first legislative proposal to act on them. The proposal sets a direction on how contrail avoidance could be encouraged: through incentive-based measures that reward capability and reporting. Starting from this direction, we ask how such an incentive could encourage operators to actually attempt avoidance, in a way that is fair to them and leads to verifiable reductions in warming. We propose a framework built on three trajectories per flight: a cost-optimal plan (FP 0 ), a contrail-optimized plan (FP 1 ), and the executed trajectory (EXF) from ADS-B data. FP 0 and FP 1 assessed against forecast weather establish whether avoidance was possible and attempted, and EXF against ERA5 reanalysis establishes whether it was achieved. A decision matrix then grants a per-flight incentive that covers the cost of an avoidance attempt and adds a reward when avoidance is verified. Using data from a European airline, we show that the framework distinguishes genuine mitigation from inaction, adding outcome verification to an incentive built on capability.

title: Transition 1point5, the platform for French academic research laboratories engaged in their environmental transition
summary: This article presents an analysis, quantitative and qualitative, of the actions shared by French laboratories on the Transition 1point5 platform. This is an open-source web application, developed by the French research group GDR Labos 1poin
content: This article presents an analysis, quantitative and qualitative, of the actions shared by French laboratories on the Transition 1point5 platform. This is an open-source web application, developed by the French research group GDR Labos 1point5, that allows volunteer French laboratories to share the measures -the actions - they have taken to reduce their environmental footprint. We present the analysis of the 274 actions shared by 69 laboratories on the platform on 11 June 2025, addressing the following questions. What measures are research laboratories implementing to adopt sustainable practices? Is there a single transition path that applies to all laboratories? What role do awareness-raising initiatives play in this process? Can participatory workshops add value to the transition process? Have laboratories undergoing transition effectively reduced their GHG (greenhouse gases) emissions? The main result of this study is that, rather than a single transition pathway, the platform’s laboratories employ various approaches depending on their specific characteristics. These approaches share common features, such as the use of awareness-raising activities, the creation of working groups dedicated to environmental issues, and increasingly participatory workshops to discuss and implement transition actions. Another key finding is that it is too early to measure the effectiveness of the implemented measures in terms of laboratories’ GHG (greenhouse gas) reductions, since most of the laboratories only implemented their actions in 2024 or early 2025. Nevertheless, the platform provides valuable insights into how research laboratories are engaging in the transition, revealing organizational processes and demonstrating that another way to do research is explored.

title: Rock burst prevention and control method for irregular section coal pillars under thick hard roof with multiple mining disturbances
summary: Regarding the prevention and control of rock bursts in irregular coal pillars in thick coal seams, with the No. 5316 working face of Shandong Mine as the engineering background, a combination of on-site investigation, theoretical analysis,
content: Regarding the prevention and control of rock bursts in irregular coal pillars in thick coal seams, with the No. 5316 working face of Shandong Mine as the engineering background, a combination of on-site investigation, theoretical analysis, numerical simulation and on-site industrial tests was adopted to systematically study the stress and impact instability evolution law of irregular coal pillars in working faces with thick and hard roofs. The rock burst risk in the irregular coal pillar area under mining influence was systematically evaluated, and a coal pillar rock burst prevention and control method coordinating overlying strata structure optimization and stress control was proposed. The results show that the expressions of vertical stress and horizontal stress borne by coal pillars with different widths are derived, and the evolution law of stress in irregular coal pillars is studied through examples; the stability of irregular coal pillars under mining disturbance is systematically analyzed, and the energy-induced mechanism of impact instability of coal pillars is discussed and analyzed. Based on the Dempster-Shafer evidence Theory, an overall evaluation method for coal pillar rock burst risk is proposed, which integrates monitoring information from microseismic, online stress and drill cuttings methods within the same time window, and the early warning values for rock burst risk in irregular coal pillars are determined. In combination with the characteristics of rock burst risk areas in irregular coal pillars, a coal pillar rock burst prevention and control method that coordinates the optimization of overlying strata structure of thick and hard roof with stress control is proposed. The results of on-site industrial tests show that after the implementation of comprehensive prevention and control measures, there were no abnormal conditions in stress and working resistance of hydraulic supports in the irregular coal pillar area during the mining process of the working face. The rock burst prevention and control effect is good, which ensures the safe and efficient mining of the working face.

title: Business and Human Rights
summary: This is not a book about sustainable business. Moving far beyond greenwashing, Business and Human Rights: From Knowledge to Responsibility applies a pioneering transdisciplinary lens (integrating international law, environmental science, an
content: This is not a book about sustainable business. Moving far beyond greenwashing, Business and Human Rights: From Knowledge to Responsibility applies a pioneering transdisciplinary lens (integrating international law, environmental science, and Doughnut Economics) to expose the structural cost externalisation of global capitalism. Part I establishes the normative framework toward binding corporate accountability. Part II details global violations across five continents, exposing forced labour, toxic concealment, and land grabbing. The volume culminates in a searing critique of the modern governance laboratory, dissecting how corporate capital and military technology converge to profit from systemised occupation and institutional impunity. Rejecting passive neutrality, this textbook serves as both a rigorous analytical tool and an ethical catalyst. It maps a resilient web of scholar-activists and social movements, charting a concrete path for organised resistance against systems of oppression and exploitation.

title: Strategies for regulating atom economy over iron-based catalysts in catalytic syngas conversion
summary: As key evaluation metrics for direct catalytic syngas conversion, hydrogen atom economy (HAE) and carbon atom economy (CAE) can accurately quantify the different atom flows during the main and side reactions, providing insights for rational
content: As key evaluation metrics for direct catalytic syngas conversion, hydrogen atom economy (HAE) and carbon atom economy (CAE) can accurately quantify the different atom flows during the main and side reactions, providing insights for rational catalyst design. This work reviewed the active phase types, structural evolution patterns, and regulatory mechanisms for syngas conversion on iron-based catalysts. Accordingly, this work detailed the optimization pathways of carbon and hydrogen atom economies and analyzed their coupling and tradeoffs. Furthermore, this work emphasized that balancing HAE and CAE is crucial for improving atom utilization efficiency in iron-based catalytic syngas conversion. The appropriate application of interdisciplinary strategies could open up new perspectives for the efficient regulation of atom economy and provide novel insights for developing high-performance catalytic systems.

title: In-depth evaluation of the electron beam-induced damage on the accuracy of EDS quantification of zeolite
summary: Electron-beam induced damage can significantly compromise the reliability of quantitative scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis of zeolites. We examined how irradiation mode, probe current, acquisition t
content: Electron-beam induced damage can significantly compromise the reliability of quantitative scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis of zeolites. We examined how irradiation mode, probe current, acquisition time, and raster area affected the quantitative results and surface condition of HEU-type zeolite. Point analysis produced a crater at the irradiated center and spindle-shaped surface damage highlighted by electric charging, accompanied by decreases in analytical Total, and Na and Al concentrations. At a total electron dose of 30 nC, raster scanning over 2 × 3 µ m area kept Total close to the expected value, whereas point analysis yielded substantially lower Total values due to beam damage, despite a small charge-balance error. The choice of raster area depends on the purpose of analysis: the smallest (2 × 3 µ m) raster analysis is effective for obtaining local compositional information, while larger areas (>16 × 24 µ m) analysis is useful when further textural observations are necessary after analysis because it produces virtually no surface alterations. A heat-diffusion simulation assuming the incident electron-beam energy as the input heat source predicted a lower temperature rise for raster irradiation than for point irradiation. However, the calculated thermal response was approximately four orders of magnitude faster than the observed timescale of surface damage propagation, indicating the need to consider other factors such as charge accumulation, cation migration, and possible Joule heating within the sample, and the thermal insulation caused by nano-cracks.

title: Modeling Climate Change Policy Diffusion
summary: This study analyzes the diffusion dynamics of carbon neutrality policies in the large-scale event management sector in China. Understanding how such policies diffuse from the central to provincial governments is critical for building instit
content: This study analyzes the diffusion dynamics of carbon neutrality policies in the large-scale event management sector in China. Understanding how such policies diffuse from the central to provincial governments is critical for building institutional resilience against escalating environmental risks. This chapter, therefore, enhances understanding of the dynamics of the diffusion of climate policies in the context of managing the transition. The results show that internal diffusion mechanisms dominate the diffusion process and provincial digital governing capability is the most significant factor driving policy adoption. The findings suggest that the strategic focus of the central government on promoting climate policy innovation should shift from traditional economic incentives to subnational institutional capacity, and digital governance capability has become an essential requirement for subnational governments to participate in climate action in China. This study confirms the key managerial importance of subnational digital governance capability in climate policy innovation. This study employs a two-stage theoretical framework covering the period 2019–2023. The Bass diffusion model is used to test policy diffusion pattern and the event history model is used to analyze determinants that influence provincial governments’ policy adoption. The two-stage model overcomes the limitations of traditional policy diffusion research that relies on a single explanatory pathway. The findings also provide an analytical example of transition in China’s climate governance research from qualitative description to quantitative estimation.

title: Phase-wise variation in soil quality under shifting cultivation in the tropical highland red soils of the Eastern Ghats, India
summary: Shifting cultivation (ShC) is a prominent land-use pattern in the tropical highlands of the Eastern Ghats. Although ecologically important, the phase-wise ecological and pedological footprint of ShC, particularly its association with soil q
content: Shifting cultivation (ShC) is a prominent land-use pattern in the tropical highlands of the Eastern Ghats. Although ecologically important, the phase-wise ecological and pedological footprint of ShC, particularly its association with soil quality, has received less attention. This study investigated variation in soil nutrient status and soil quality across different cultivation phases of shifting cultivation in the red soils of the Eastern Ghats. In total, 16 independent composite topsoil samples representing post-slash-and-burn (SB), short fallow (SF), long fallow (LF), and secondary cultivation (SC) phases were analysed, while settled agricultural (SA) soils without a history of SC were included as a reference agricultural system. The study represents a space-for-time observational comparison of cultivation-history phases. Soil physicochemical properties were evaluated and integrated into a Soil Quality Index (SQI). A highly significant difference among cultivation phases was observed for soil physicochemical properties (MANOVA, F = 29.71, p < 0.001). SQI values were 0.389 ± 0.016 (poor) for SB, 0.503 ± 0.007 (moderate) for SF, 0.912 ± 0.027 (very good) for LF, 0.642 ± 0.038 (good) for SC, and 0.695 ± 0.023 (good) for SA, following the order SB < SF < SC < SA < LF. The PCA exhibited clear multivariate differentiation among the sampled cultivation-history phases. Overall, the findings indicate clear associations between cultivation history and soil nutrient status including quality indicators. Long-fallow sites in this study (≥ 10 years) were associated with higher nutrient status and improved soil quality indicators; however, this period should not be interpreted as a universal threshold for soil recovery.

title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BOx catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
summary: The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BO x inv
content: The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BO x inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal Co F/H-1.0 @BO x catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BO x -Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

title: Multivariate Optimization of the Synthesis of ZnCl 2 -Activated Biochar Functionalized with Bimetallic Au-Ag Nanoparticles for Catalytic Application in the Reduction of p-Nitrophenol
summary: The valorization of agro-industrial residues to produce carbonaceous materials offers a sustainable route for developing heterogeneous catalysts. In this study, passion fruit peel was used as a precursor for ZnCl 2 -activated biochar, whose
content: The valorization of agro-industrial residues to produce carbonaceous materials offers a sustainable route for developing heterogeneous catalysts. In this study, passion fruit peel was used as a precursor for ZnCl 2 -activated biochar, whose synthesis was optimized using a Central Composite Rotatable Design (CCRD), considering carbonization temperature, residence time, and impregnation ratio. The optimized conditions were 525 °C, 60 min, and a biomass-to-ZnCl 2 impregnation ratio of 2.0 (w/w). The resulting optimized biochar (BC-OT) exhibited a high specific surface area of 1411.64 m 2 g -1 . Pyrolysis promoted carbon enrichment, reduced the H/C and O/C ratios to 0.338 and 0.381. BC-OT showed a point of zero charge (pH PZC ) of 6.53 and a lactonic group content of 1.50 mmol g -1 . The biochar was subsequently functionalized with Au and Ag nanoparticles (NPs) and applied as a heterogeneous catalyst for the NaBH 4 -mediated reduction of p -nitrophenol. For Au 0.5 -Ag 0.5 NPs/BC-OT, EDS confirmed the presence of Au and Ag, while HRTEM revealed nanoparticles with an average diameter of 7.4 ± 3.4 nm. Lattice fringes and SAED patterns showed interplanar spacings consistent with face-centered cubic Au and/or Ag domains and wurtzite ZnO. Among the evaluated materials, 50:50 Ag:Au exhibited the highest apparent rate constant ( k app ) of (15.18 ± 2.27) × 10⁻³ s⁻¹, outperforming the monometallic catalysts and the non-functionalized support. The catalyst remained active over four reuse cycles. These results demonstrate the potential of passion fruit peel as a renewable precursor for porous carbonaceous supports containing Au-Ag nanoparticles for the catalytic reduction of nitroaromatic compounds.

title: Review of Characteristics and Performance Assessment of Urban Rail Transit Station Areas under Stock-Oriented Development Stage
source: COTA International Conference of Transportation Professionals (CICTP)
summary: Starting from the definition and scope of urban rail transit station areas, this article reviews the classic characteristics and sinicization development of rail station areas under the transit-oriented development (TOD) model and extracts
content: Starting from the definition and scope of urban rail transit station areas, this article reviews the classic characteristics and sinicization development of rail station areas under the transit-oriented development (TOD) model and extracts five characteristic trends of rail transit station areas include: Relying more on public transportation to solve urban problems, paying more attention to slow-traffic systems, emphasizing urban spatial governance and high-quality development, paying more attention to refined design from a human perspective, and paying more attention to green and carbon reduction. Taking the Beijing’s Station as an example, this paper constructs a TOD efficiency evaluation system for urban rail transit stations that includes convenient travel, composite diversity, efficient intensification, shared vitality, pleasant space, and Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality Goals. This system provides guidance for problem diagnosis and renewal and promotes high-quality spatial development of urban rail transit areas.

title: Most US dairy farmers do not identify with sustainability language, despite using sustainable practices
summary: Voluntary agricultural conservation programs and incentive delivery often use abstract terminology (e.g., ‘regenerative’, ‘climate-smart’) to frame public and private incentive programs, direct technical assistance, and track environmental
content: Voluntary agricultural conservation programs and incentive delivery often use abstract terminology (e.g., ‘regenerative’, ‘climate-smart’) to frame public and private incentive programs, direct technical assistance, and track environmental progress. However, deploying programs that center these concepts without precise definitions—or an evaluation of farmer awareness—introduces operational uncertainty that can compromise access, implementation, and the baseline metrics used to evaluate ecological ‘success’. Using the US dairy sector as a case study, we surveyed over 900 farmers to assess the relationship between sustainability framing and on-farm behavior. We reveal a substantial decoupling between institutional language and actual practice adoption. While 79% of farmers report using at least one sustainable management practice, the vast majority are unfamiliar with the institutional terminology used to describe and fund them. Furthermore, engagement with climate-related terms did not consistently predict management behavior. These patterns suggest that sustainability terminology is not a neutral descriptor of practice, but encodes distinct framings of conservation. Ecological, stewardship-oriented terms such as ‘regenerative’ and ‘nature-based’ were positively associated with the soil-health and forage practices farmers most commonly used, whereas climate- and market-oriented terms such as ‘climate-smart’ and ‘carbon market’ showed weak or negative associations with those same practices. Adopters of capital-intensive manure technologies, the practices with the clearest greenhouse gas mitigation potential, showed no positive association with any term we examined. These confinement-oriented operations are therefore among the least likely to identify with sustainability language, despite implementing practices with substantial documented mitigation potential. Associations with grazing practices were partly attributable to certified organic operations, which are required to graze. Because the terminology embedded in conservation program eligibility, outreach, and technical assistance may affect whether farmers perceive programs as relevant to them, these language choices can shape who participates, independent of what farmers may already be doing on the ground. Conservation programs may reach more of the practitioners already advancing this work by building outreach and program design from farmers’ existing soil-health and stewardship vocabulary rather than from externally derived frames.

title: REDEFINING GREEN ECONOMY BASED ON ISLAMIC ETHICS AS A JUST AND INCLUSIVE FOUNDATION FOR SUSTAINABILITY
source: Count Journal of Accounting Business and Management
summary: The concept of green economy has been widely promoted as a solution to the environmental crisis. However, dominant definitions remain technocratic and growth-oriented, often neglecting ethical, distributive, and spiritual dimensions. This s
content: The concept of green economy has been widely promoted as a solution to the environmental crisis. However, dominant definitions remain technocratic and growth-oriented, often neglecting ethical, distributive, and spiritual dimensions. This study aims to critically reconstruct the definition of green economy by integrating ecological justice and Islamic environmental ethics. Employing a systematic literature review of 43 peer-reviewed articles from 2015–2025, this conceptual research identifies epistemological gaps in prevailing definitions and synthesizes alternative frameworks rooted in spiritual and ethical principles. The findings reveal that current models emphasize carbon reduction, circular economy, and green finance but often fail to address structural inequalities, greenwashing, and global epistemic injustice. As an alternative, the study proposes a redefinition of green economy as a system based on ecological balance, social justice, and human spiritual responsibility as khalifah (steward of the earth), grounded in values such as tauhid, mizan, and maslahah. This reconceptualization offers a holistic approach that reframes green transition not only as a technical project but as a moral and collective imperative. The proposed framework has implications for addressing greenflation and designing inclusive, context-sensitive green policies, especially in the global south.

title: A common human anticodon polymorphism in an alanine-like tRNA gene predicts alanine incorporation at valine codons
summary: Transfer RNA identity is determined by elements recognized by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases. In alanine, serine, and leucine tRNAs the principal identity elements lie outside the anticodon, so an anticodon substitution may uncouple aminoacylat
content: Transfer RNA identity is determined by elements recognized by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases. In alanine, serine, and leucine tRNAs the principal identity elements lie outside the anticodon, so an anticodon substitution may uncouple aminoacylation specificity from codon recognition. Screening 431 human tRNA genes identified one candidate: tRNA-Val-AAC-6-1 on chromosome 6, which retains G3:U70, the major alanine identity element, but carries a valine anticodon. Sequence and isotype-model assignment support alanine-like identity: 88.9% maximum identity to alanine genes against 64.4% to valine genes. The anticodon polymorphism rs1233572 (chr6:28,735,467 T > C) distinguishes AGC, specifying alanine on about 61% of sampled chromosomes, from AAC, specifying valine on approximately 39% and ranging across nine cohorts from 13% in African ancestry groups to 60% in Finnish participants. Four primate species support AGC as ancestral. Under pooled Hardy–Weinberg expectations, the estimated AGC/AGC, AGC/AAC, and AAC/AAC frequencies are 37.2%, 47.6%, and 15.2%. The variant alters anticodon position 35, which separates the alanine and valine anticodon families in the analyzed gene set and is a principal valyl-tRNA synthetase determinant, while every alanine determinant is left intact and the retained acceptor-stem G:U pairs oppose valine charging. The AAC allele is therefore predicted to be partitioned between two synthetases rather than captured by one, and that partition sets the rate of alanine delivery to valine codons. Across the queried genes, common anticodon variation was confined to loci where it creates no conflict between the amino acid accepted and the synthetase's requirement.

title: Regional trajectories of carbon stock and carbon pools in China’s Harvested Wood Products
summary: Harvested wood products (HWP) can reduce climate change by retaining biogenic carbon in products and substituting materials and energy carriers associated with higher emissions. China currently hosts around one third of the global HWP carbo
content: Harvested wood products (HWP) can reduce climate change by retaining biogenic carbon in products and substituting materials and energy carriers associated with higher emissions. China currently hosts around one third of the global HWP carbon sink, measuring at -110 MtCO 2 yr − 1 , yet recent studies suggest that the sink is saturated, raising critical questions about its long-term sequestration potential. Previous forward-looking assessment have only assessed the development of the HWP carbon flux at the national scale, leaving unresolved how this transition is distributed among provinces and how accounting choices affects the regional attribution of carbon. Here we show that China’s HWP sink declines across all scenarios and accounting approaches, reflecting structural saturation driven by slowing growth in HWP production and consumption. By 2060, the national HWP sink is projected to decline by 30.5% to 91.5% from current levels, while its spatial distribution varies strongly with the selected accounting framework. Consumption-based accounting increases the national HWP carbon stock but does not fundamentally alter the long-term decline of the sink. Production-based accounting concentrates HWP carbon stocks in a few industrial processing provinces, whereas consumption-based accounting reallocates carbon towards highly populated regions, highlighting a mismatch between the physical carbon flows and accounting-based attribution. Stronger bioenergy demand may further accelerate the sink decline, while increased material use delays, but does not prevent, saturation. These findings reveal a fundamental distinction between the national HWP dynamics and provincial attribution of HWP fluxes. National assessment along may obscure substantial differences in where carbon storage occurs and where mitigation responsibilities are assigned.

title: Physiological Adaptation of Comammox Nitrospira to Acidic pH Suppresses N2O Production
summary: Nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas, is a major byproduct of microbial nitrification, yet how environmental pH governs N2O production by complete ammonia oxidizers (comammox) remains poorly understood. We conducted controlled cultu
content: Nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas, is a major byproduct of microbial nitrification, yet how environmental pH governs N2O production by complete ammonia oxidizers (comammox) remains poorly understood. We conducted controlled culture experiments with comammox Nitrospira inopinata at pH 6.5, 7.5, and 8.5. Under mild acidification (pH 6.5), nitrification activity was largely maintained, but cellular growth declined sharply, and both N2O yield and extracellular hydroxylamine (NH2OH) accumulation fell substantially relative to neutral conditions. Strikingly, this reduced growth was accompanied by pronounced transcriptional upregulation of core nitrification, stress response, and pH homeostasis genes, whereas carbon fixation genes remained largely unchanged. This decoupling of growth from gene expression indicates that acid-stressed cells reallocate energy away from biosynthesis toward cellular maintenance and proton extrusion, tightening intracellular handling of NH2OH and limiting its extracellular release. Isotopomer analysis (site preference ∼28–36‰) confirmed that NH2OH-driven chemistry remained the dominant N2O source across all pH conditions, and complementary abiotic assays indicated that chemical N2O formation was likely influenced by the diminished NH2OH pool. These results establish that comammox suppresses, rather than enhances, N2O production under mild acidification, opposite to the response reported for canonical ammonia-oxidizing microbes. This distinctive trait carries important implications for predicting nitrification-derived N2O fluxes and refining greenhouse-gas budgets in acidifying ecosystems.

title: Supercritical Fluids: Fundamentals and Engineering Applications
summary: Supercritical Fluids: Fundamentals and Engineering Applications explores the development of supercritical fluids in energy sectors and their application in energy conversion systems, chemical, power, and material industries. Looking beyond
content: Supercritical Fluids: Fundamentals and Engineering Applications explores the development of supercritical fluids in energy sectors and their application in energy conversion systems, chemical, power, and material industries. Looking beyond a conventional chemical-focused approach, the book provides critical support to a broad spectrum of professional fields and lays a solid foundation for the industrial application and technological innovation of supercritical fluid technologies. It begins with the basic physical laws and thermophysical basis of supercritical fluids in energy sectors before building on these principles to discuss basic heat transfer, flow properties, and the governing laws of flow and transportation of heat, mass, and energy conversions. Through the presentation of experimental evidence, numerical models, and industrial case studies, readers will gain insight into the unique physical mechanisms underlying supercritical fluid phenomena and their practical implications for energy efficiency, carbon neutrality, and technological innovation. This book is a valuable resource for professional engineers in energy sectors as well as graduate students and researchers studying supercritical fluids, energy conversion, and environmentally friendly systems.

title: Visualizing Microporosity Generated by Polyanion Vacancies in Single Crystals of (NH 4 ) 4 [SiW 12 O 40 ]
summary: Ammonium or cesium salts of the Keggin‐type polyoxometalates such as (NH 4 ) 3 [PMo 12 O 40 ], Cs 3 [PW 12 O 40 ], Cs 4 [PVMo 11 O 40 ] and (NH 4 ) 4 [SiW 12 O 40 ] possess microporosity arising from intercrystallite space or polyanion vaca
content: Ammonium or cesium salts of the Keggin‐type polyoxometalates such as (NH 4 ) 3 [PMo 12 O 40 ], Cs 3 [PW 12 O 40 ], Cs 4 [PVMo 11 O 40 ] and (NH 4 ) 4 [SiW 12 O 40 ] possess microporosity arising from intercrystallite space or polyanion vacancies within the single crystals. Herein, we present the first crystallographic evidence of polyanion vacancy in the single crystals of (NH 4 ) 4 [SiW 12 O 40 ], confirming Schlögl's structural model of intrinsic microporosity in tetravalent Keggin anions. The single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction patterns show sharp Bragg reflections and weak reflections with non‐integer hkl and are indicative of a correlated, short‐range vacancy order and the formation of vacancy clusters. The powder x‐ray diffraction pattern and high‐angle annular dark‐field image revealed that the vacant sites are parallel to the {111} planes and are clustered, forming regions with a high concentration of defects. The crystallographic evidence of polyanion vacancy was corroborated with nitrogen gas and water vapor sorption isotherms and crystal density measurements. The micropores adsorb water vapor at a low relative pressure, facilitating proton conduction at low relative humidity.

title: Neutralité carbone : une meilleure qualité de l’air améliore la santé publique et fait économiser des millions d’euros
summary: Limiter l’emploi des énergies fossiles n’a pas seulement un effet positif sur le climat : cela permet aussi d’améliorer la santé publique, en réduisant la quantité de particules fines et de dioxyde d’azote dans l’atmosphère.
content: Limiter l’emploi des énergies fossiles n’a pas seulement un effet positif sur le climat : cela permet aussi d’améliorer la santé publique, en réduisant la quantité de particules fines et de dioxyde d’azote dans l’atmosphère.

title: Study on Corrosion and Scaling Risks and Prevention/Control Measures of Water Injection Systems in Middle East Oilfields
summary: To address the severe scaling and corrosion challenges in water injection systems of high-salinity and acidic oilfields in the Middle East, a combined approach of laboratory experiments, software simulation, and machine learning was employe
content: To address the severe scaling and corrosion challenges in water injection systems of high-salinity and acidic oilfields in the Middle East, a combined approach of laboratory experiments, software simulation, and machine learning was employed to systematically investigate the scaling characteristics, corrosion behavior, and performance of corrosion inhibitors. CaSO4, CaCO3, and SrSO4 were identified as the dominant scale types. The effects of temperature, calcium ion concentration, CO2 partial pressure, and chloride ion concentration on scaling and corrosion were elucidated, and a high-accuracy machine-learning scale-prediction model was established. It achieves favorable prediction performance for three scale types (CaCO3, CaSO4, and SrSO4) on the test set, with coefficients of determination R2 all no less than 0.93, which enables rapid on-site scale-formation risk identification. The mechanism by which elevated calcium ion concentration aggravates localized corrosion was clarified. When the scale layer is incomplete, an increase in Ca2+ causes uneven distribution of the scale layer and the formation of microgalvanic couples, accelerating the initiation and propagation of localized corrosion. For example, the localized corrosion rate of L80 steel can reach 2.555 mm/y when the concentration of Ca2+ is 20000 mg/L. The multiscale inhibition mechanism of an imidazoline quaternary ammonium salt corrosion inhibitor was explored, and a prevention-control strategy combining water quality ion regulation and corrosion inhibitor injection was proposed. Controlling the Ca2+ content in water below 6000 mg/L and SO2–4 content below 1000 mg/L can effectively reduce the scaling risk of CaSO4. Injecting 100 ppm of No.3 corrosion inhibitor can realize both scale control and localized corrosion suppression, with a corrosion inhibition efficiency of over 94%. The research outcomes can directly guide the mitigation of scaling and corrosion in water injection systems of high-salinity and acidic oilfields in the Middle East, with expected reductions in pipeline perforation accidents and significant extensions of equipment service life.

title: Energy crisis management in small isolated energy systems
summary: The oil crises of the 1970s led governments to adopt immediate measures to limit fuel consumption, such as rationing, driving bans and speed limits, and to create new institutions including the International Energy Agency (IEA) and strategi
content: The oil crises of the 1970s led governments to adopt immediate measures to limit fuel consumption, such as rationing, driving bans and speed limits, and to create new institutions including the International Energy Agency (IEA) and strategic oil reserves. The 2022–2024 energy crisis triggered by the war in Ukraine shifted the European Union towards a different mix of responses centered on energy savings, diversification of suppliers, accelerated deployment of renewables and storage, and extensive financial support for consumers and businesses. Building on lessons from these episodes, this paper develops a structured framework for short-term energy crisis management in small, isolated, import-dependent energy systems. The ongoing 2026 war in Iran and the associated disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz constitute the largest oil-market shock to date and a major challenge for security of supply in both oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG). Several countries have already implemented measures such as fuel rationing, four-day working weeks, teleworking, restrictions on air-conditioning and strengthened energy-saving campaigns. Focusing on Cyprus as a case study, the paper proposes a coherent set of immediate policy packages organized into three crisis-intensity scenarios (mild, medium, extreme). These scenarios link global crisis patterns to pre-defined national response measures, allowing interventions to toughen automatically as conditions worsen while maintaining protection for vulnerable consumers and critical infrastructure.

title: Online Routing for Shared E-Bikes under Distributed Scheduling and Retrieval
source: COTA International Conference of Transportation Professionals (CICTP)
summary: Driven by carbon-peak and carbon-neutrality goals, shared e-bikes have grown rapidly owing to their economic viability and low-carbon advantages. Nevertheless, high demand uncertainty and imperfect operational decisions often lead to elevat
content: Driven by carbon-peak and carbon-neutrality goals, shared e-bikes have grown rapidly owing to their economic viability and low-carbon advantages. Nevertheless, high demand uncertainty and imperfect operational decisions often lead to elevated costs and reduced system efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper investigates distributed scheduling and problem for shared e-bikes under demand uncertainty. An online vehicle routing framework is developed based on online algorithms and competitive analysis, with the objective of minimizing total operational cost. The proposed model provides theoretical performance guarantees and offers practical insights for improving the efficiency of shared e‑bike operations in dynamic and information‑limited environments.

title: Limited Intrinsic CO2/CH4 Selectivity in Imine-Linked COF-LZU-1: Evidence from PBE-D3 Adsorption Energetics and Binary-Mixture Monte Carlo Simulations
summary: Imine-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely proposed for CO2/CH4 separation, yet the intrinsic selectivity of the archetypal framework COF-LZU1 has not been quantified against a transparent baseline. Here, periodic PBE-D3 cal
content: Imine-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely proposed for CO2/CH4 separation, yet the intrinsic selectivity of the archetypal framework COF-LZU1 has not been quantified against a transparent baseline. Here, periodic PBE-D3 calculations and grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations are combined to test whether pristine COF-LZU1 discriminates between CO2 and CH4. At three positions spanning the 1.8 nm channel, relaxed PBE-D3 adsorption energies are −3.10, −3.66, and −8.90 kJ mol-1 for CO2 and −3.13, −3.63, and −8.76 kJ mol-1 for CH4; CO2 binds more strongly than CH4 by at most 0.14 kJ mol-1, at the confined site near the imine linkage. Consistently, GCMC simulations of equimolar mixtures (TraPPE, DREIDING, DDEC6 charges, Ewald electrostatics, 14 Å cutoff with analytic tail corrections) give low selectivities of 1.15–1.71 between 273 and 323 K and 0.1–10 bar, and 1.20–1.38 at 298 K, rising with pressure and falling with temperature. At 223 K and 7–10 bar, CO2 fills about 80% of the pore volume and the selectivity reaches about 11, a pore-filling effect and not intrinsic discrimination. Replacing EPM2 CO2, a 12 Å cutoff, and no tail corrections by the final force-field set raises the selectivity by 7–27%, so selectivities near unity are force-field sensitive. The weak simulated selectivity, together with the near-equal DFT binding energies, defines a baseline that functionalization, for example with Ag+, must overcome.

title: A Nucleic Acid Mimetic Hexaplex Assembly Stabilized by the Synergistic Association of Non-Canonical Recognition Units and Peptide Backbones
summary: Two modes of self-assembly, backbone-backbone hydrogen bonding and base-base hydrogen bonding with stacking interactions, are brought together in a class of nucleic acid mimetic peptides that form hexameric water-soluble supramolecular asse
content: Two modes of self-assembly, backbone-backbone hydrogen bonding and base-base hydrogen bonding with stacking interactions, are brought together in a class of nucleic acid mimetic peptides that form hexameric water-soluble supramolecular assemblies. These oligodipeptides contain dimeric repeats of glutamic acid (Glu) and a diaminobutyric acid (Dab) that is covalently linked to either melamine or cyanuric acid (Mel Dab and Cy Dab ). Molecular models predict that these oligomers will form assemblies with a core of stacked, hydrogen-bonded Mel-Cy hexads that are sheathed by the six peptide backbones, creating a structure comparable to a six-stranded β-barrel. Experimental analyses confirm that such assemblies are formed upon mixing of the octapeptides (Mel Dab -Glu) 4 and (Cy Dab -Glu) 4 . This assembly exhibits high thermal stability with pH-dependent apparent melting temperatures greater than 100°C. The chemical structure and assembly properties of these peptides support the hypothesis that compounds of similar form may have served as ancestors to RNA (i.e., proto-RNA) in the emergence of life on Earth.

title: Impact of shea production on economic growth and carbon emissions in Ghana
summary: Using annual data on shea export volume (tons) , gross domestic product per capita, carbon emissions per capita, and the proportion of the population with access to electricity from 2003-2022, the study used an Autoregressive Distributed La
content: Using annual data on shea export volume (tons) , gross domestic product per capita, carbon emissions per capita, and the proportion of the population with access to electricity from 2003-2022, the study used an Autoregressive Distributed Lag model to estimate the long- and short-run relationships among these variables. T he study finds a long-run stable equilibrium for economic growth , with about 62% of deviations from equilibrium corrected each year. Similarly, a 1% increase in shea production exports is associated with a 0.12% increase in economic growth. These findings highlight that the shea value chain is crucial to economic growth and development. Also, a 1% increase in carbon emissions per capita significantly boost s long-run economic growth by 2.6% . Thus, Ghana’s economic cycle is still linked to the carbon-based economy and is consistent with the early stages of the Environmental Kuznets Curve. A 1% increase in population access to electricity boosts economic growth by 1.26% in the short term . Finally, the study indicates that the time trend negatively affect s economic growth and that structural issues may affect growth even after controlling for other factors. Hence, the research concludes that growing shea production positively affects economic growth but, in the context of a wider growth-emissions nexus, carbon-intensive growth remains . Therefore, policymakers should ensure that efforts to enhance shea productivity, upgrade processes, and improve access to energy support rural income and national production. At the same time, policymakers should develop complementary environmental policies to separate growth from emissions .

title: Robustness-oriented RF-RFE-TCN framework for PEMFC degradation and remaining useful life prediction
summary: Introduction Accurate proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) prognosis requires evaluation beyond low errors on familiar operating records. We assess the reliability, robustness, and transferability of a previously explored random‐fores
content: Introduction Accurate proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) prognosis requires evaluation beyond low errors on familiar operating records. We assess the reliability, robustness, and transferability of a previously explored random‐forest recursive feature elimination–temporal convolutional network (RF‐RFE‐TCN) pipeline for voltage degradation and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. Methods Particle swarm optimization tunes the network architecture. Feature selection and standardization are fitted to training data only, with a fixed 24‐step input history and chronological evaluation. Voltage forecasts are mapped to threshold‐based RUL, while Monte Carlo dropout provides prediction intervals. Synthetic perturbation and cross‐regime transfer tests characterize sensitivity to changing conditions. Result The test mean absolute errors (MAEs) are 0.0452 V (FC1) and 0.0478 V (FC2). Under the reported synthetic perturbations, R 2 ranges from 0.91 to 0.95 and MAE from 0.05 to 0.07 V. Relative to the 0.045 V FC1 reference error, direct high‐to‐low‐load and FC1‐to‐FC2 transfer increase MAE to 0.068 and 0.082 V, respectively. Discussion These findings support leakage-controlled and uncertainty‐aware evaluation while highlighting the limits of direct transfer. The predictor uses physically motivated inputs but lacks explicit electrochemical constraints; independently varied thermal, humidity, stoichiometric, and load‐cycling regimes require further validation.

title: Paleodietary Stable Isotope Analysis of the Pre‐Hispanic Indigenous Population of La Palma (Canary Islands)
summary: We study the stable isotopes of the indigenous population (4th–15th century ad ) on individuals from cave burials of the island of La Palma. This approach allows for the study of dietary patterns depending on sites and areas. Further, the i
content: We study the stable isotopes of the indigenous population (4th–15th century ad ) on individuals from cave burials of the island of La Palma. This approach allows for the study of dietary patterns depending on sites and areas. Further, the isotopic analysis was augmented by use of food percentage reconstruction software (FRUITS), which allowed for a visualization of the amount of potential food sources used by the islanders. The results of this paper suggest that the population of La Palma relied greatly on plant food sources, with mild differences in food sources between individuals and between the eastern and western areas of the island.

title: Avances recientes en la optimización de Ciclos Rankine Orgánicos alimentados por biomasa residual: revisión sistemática y bibliométrica
summary: La creciente demanda energética mundial y las restricciones ambientales asociadas al uso de combustibles fósiles han impulsado el desarrollo de tecnologías sostenibles capaces de aprovechar fuentes renovables y residuos energéticos. Entre e
content: La creciente demanda energética mundial y las restricciones ambientales asociadas al uso de combustibles fósiles han impulsado el desarrollo de tecnologías sostenibles capaces de aprovechar fuentes renovables y residuos energéticos. Entre estas tecnologías, los Ciclos Rankine Orgánicos (ORC, Organic Rankine Cycle) alimentados por biomasa residual han demostrado ser una solución eficiente para la conversión de calor de baja y media temperatura en electricidad. El presente artículo desarrolla una revisión sistemática y bibliométrica global sobre los avances recientes en la optimización de sistemas ORC impulsados por biomasa residual, considerando configuraciones termodinámicas, fluidos de trabajo, estrategias de optimización energética y exergética, algoritmos de inteligencia artificial, integración híbrida y análisis tecnoeconómicos. La metodología se fundamentó en el protocolo PRISMA utilizando bases de datos Scopus y Web of Science. Los resultados muestran un incremento significativo de publicaciones relacionadas con ORC-biomasa durante la última década, destacándose China, Italia, Estados Unidos e India como los principales países productores. Asimismo, las configuraciones regenerativas, supercríticas y multietapa presentan mejoras sustanciales en eficiencia térmica y destrucción de exergía. Los fluidos orgánicos de nueva generación, especialmente hidrofluoroolefinas y mezclas zeotrópicas, evidencian ventajas ambientales y energéticas relevantes. Finalmente, se concluye que la integración de algoritmos de optimización multiobjetivo, inteligencia artificial y enfoques híbridos constituye la principal tendencia futura para incrementar la sostenibilidad y viabilidad comercial de los ORC alimentados con biomasa residual.

title: Climate-aware photovoltaic technology selection using hybrid BWM–CRITIC, MARCOS, and explainable surrogate modeling
summary: Selecting photovoltaic (PV) technology for a specific location requires consideration of both local operating conditions and technology-specific characteristics. This study proposes a climate-aware Multi-criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) fram
content: Selecting photovoltaic (PV) technology for a specific location requires consideration of both local operating conditions and technology-specific characteristics. This study proposes a climate-aware Multi-criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework integrating the Best–Worst Method (BWM), Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC), and Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to COmpromise Solution (MARCOS) for PV technology selection. Ten years of hourly NASA POWER data (2015–2024) for Kütahya, Türkiye, were combined with commercial module specifications to evaluate Mono-PERC, TOPCon, heterojunction (HJT), bifacial n-TOPCon, and CdTe technologies. Four criteria were considered: expected energy production, temperature performance, long-term reliability, and low-irradiance performance. BWM represented literature-supported engineering priorities, whereas CRITIC quantified the discriminatory information contained in the decision matrix. Under the reference hybrid weighting scheme, MARCOS ranked HJT first with a utility of 0.6877, followed by bifacial n-TOPCon (0.6832) and TOPCon (0.6761). Robustness was examined through weighting sensitivity, TOPSIS, and VIKOR comparisons, leave-one-criterion-out analysis, and 60,000 Monte Carlo realizations across three perturbation levels. Under the ± 5% reference scenario, HJT had a 53.90% probability of ranking first, while HJT, bifacial n-TOPCon, and TOPCon remained among the top three in 98.32%, 97.45%, and 91.14% of realizations, respectively. A Random Forest surrogate achieved a held-out R 2 of 0.9435, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified expected energy production as the dominant contributor to surrogate-predicted MARCOS utility. Overall, the results support a robust leading group rather than an unequivocal single-technology winner and demonstrate the importance of combining site-specific climatic information, engineering priorities, and uncertainty analysis in PV technology selection.

title: From savings to capital: tax incentives for Europe’s retail investors
source: London School of Economics and Political Science Theses Online (London School of Economics and Political Science)
summary: The EU published the Savings and Investment Union (SIU) strategy in 2025, marking a renewed effort to build on the Capital Markets Union agenda it brought to life a decade earlier. However, progress on the SIU’s objectives has remained unev
content: The EU published the Savings and Investment Union (SIU) strategy in 2025, marking a renewed effort to build on the Capital Markets Union agenda it brought to life a decade earlier. However, progress on the SIU’s objectives has remained uneven, despite recent developments in its operationalisation. In particular, European retail investment markets remain fragmented, with considerable differences in participation between member states. Accordingly, there is an urgent need to direct retail investors’ savings more efficiently towards deeper European capital markets, especially in light of Europe’s competitiveness challenges, fast-moving geopolitical context and pressing climate concerns. While taxation has been absent from discussions on the SIU’s development, tax incentives for retail investors could be a powerful driver in efforts to create more integrated European capital markets.

title: Beyond the managerial zero-sum perspective: how exemplar organizations support freight transport decarbonization adoption
summary: Decarbonizing freight transportation, although it has existed for years, has not resulted in a significant reduction in sectoral greenhouse gas emissions. One reason for this is the competitive nature of freight transport, with cost minimiz
content: Decarbonizing freight transportation, although it has existed for years, has not resulted in a significant reduction in sectoral greenhouse gas emissions. One reason for this is the competitive nature of freight transport, with cost minimization as a driving goal, and rejection of low-carbon investments. Nevertheless, evolving regulatory forces, customer demand, and competitive pressures may make familiar technology unusable soon. Some shippers, carriers, and logistics service providers do understand this situation and seriously decarbonize transportation. To this end, we investigate these exemplar organizations utilizing expert interviews and an adjusted grounded-theory approach. Findings show that exemplar organizations continue to rely on a business case for decarbonization, but broaden this business case by incorporating longer-term competitiveness, organizational capabilities, managerial values, and environmental considerations. Theoretically, developed propositions set the stage for further research. Practically, we provide a blueprint on how practitioners can move beyond their managerial zero-sum perspective in transport decarbonization.

title: Evaluasi Kecukupan Ruang Terbuka Hijau Terhadap Emisi CO2 Berbasis SIG dan Analisis Ketidakpastian di Kota Bogor
source: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
summary: Penilaian kecukupan ruang terbuka hijau sebagai penyerap karbon dioksida di Indonesia umumnya membandingkan emisi dengan daya serap vegetasi, tetapi jarang menguji kepekaan hasilnya terhadap koefisien serapan dan definisi ruang terbuka hija
content: Penilaian kecukupan ruang terbuka hijau sebagai penyerap karbon dioksida di Indonesia umumnya membandingkan emisi dengan daya serap vegetasi, tetapi jarang menguji kepekaan hasilnya terhadap koefisien serapan dan definisi ruang terbuka hijau. Penelitian ini bertujuan menyusun neraca emisi dan serapan karbon dioksida pada enam kecamatan di Kota Bogor serta menilai kekokohan status kecukupan ruang terbuka hijau. Emisi dari sektor transportasi, gas minyak cair rumah tangga, dan peternakan dihitung dengan pendekatan tingkat dasar IPCC, lalu diintegrasikan dengan tiga skenario luas ruang terbuka hijau, empat koefisien serapan dari literatur, dan simulasi Monte Carlo sebanyak 20.000 kali dalam Sistem Informasi Geografis. Total emisi ketiga sektor sebesar 341.885 ton setara karbon dioksida per tahun atau 0,30 ton per jiwa, dengan transportasi sebagai penyumbang terbesar (71,4%). Dengan koefisien berbasis ekologi, ruang terbuka hijau eksisting hanya menyerap 4,2–12,4% emisi tiap kecamatan, dan netralisasi penuh memerlukan ruang terbuka hijau seluas dua hingga empat kali luas kecamatan. Sebaliknya, koefisien serapan tinggi yang lazim dipakai dalam studi nasional membalik kesimpulan menjadi cukup di seluruh kecamatan. Koefisien serapan menjelaskan hampir seluruh variasi hasil, jauh melebihi pengaruh luas ruang terbuka hijau dan besaran emisi. Ruang terbuka hijau Kota Bogor karenanya perlu diposisikan sebagai pelengkap, bukan pengganti, mitigasi emisi di sektor transportasi dan energi rumah tangga.

title: Accuracy- versus efficiency-driven artificial intelligence use: Purpose matters, yet user dehumanization persists.
summary: Building on prior studies that have documented the dehumanization of the users of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, that is, the tendency for observers to attribute less humanness to individuals who use AI than to those who do not, t
content: Building on prior studies that have documented the dehumanization of the users of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, that is, the tendency for observers to attribute less humanness to individuals who use AI than to those who do not, the present research examines whether and how different AI use purposes (i.e., accuracy- vs. efficiency-driven use) influence this effect. We conducted four preregistered studies (total N = 1,270) spanning diverse professional domains. We observed that accuracy-driven AI use negatively predicted the dehumanization of AI users, whereas efficiency-driven AI use positively predicted such dehumanization (Study 1). Furthermore, accuracy-driven AI users elicited less dehumanization than their efficiency-driven counterparts did, a pattern that proved robust across both intuitive assessments of dehumanization (Study 2) and deliberative ratings of humanness traits (Studies 3 and 4). However, both accuracy- and efficiency-driven AI users were significantly dehumanized compared with non-AI users (Study 4), demonstrating that while purpose matters, AI user dehumanization persists. These findings extend the literature on the social cost of AI and offer novel insights into how human–AI interaction shapes interpersonal dynamics .

title: Do Boilerplate Green Narratives Affect Responsible Investment Decisions? Evidence From ESG Mutual Funds in China
summary: This paper employs natural language processing to measure boilerplate in green narratives and examines its effects on responsible investment decisions in China. We find that green narrative boilerplate discourages investment by responsible
content: This paper employs natural language processing to measure boilerplate in green narratives and examines its effects on responsible investment decisions in China. We find that green narrative boilerplate discourages investment by responsible investors. This may be because boilerplate reduces the effective information available to investors and raises suspicions of poor environmental performance. The negative association is stronger among firms with higher overall information transparency, lower media coverage, and more intense product‐market competition. Boilerplate primarily affects investment selection rather than post‐investment holdings. Our findings offer implications for improving environmental disclosure and the efficiency of responsible investment.

title: Closing the Energy Efficiency Gap: Unlocking Private-Sector Investment in Poland and Romania
summary: This report examines the persistent gap between the significant potential for energy-efficiency improvements and actual private-sector investment in Europe, drawing on detailed analysis of Poland and Romania. It finds that stronger energy e
content: This report examines the persistent gap between the significant potential for energy-efficiency improvements and actual private-sector investment in Europe, drawing on detailed analysis of Poland and Romania. It finds that stronger energy efficiency can improve firms’ competitiveness, energy security, and emissions performance, but investment remains constrained by limited firm capabilities, weak pipelines of bankable projects, low borrower demand, restrictive investment criteria, financing gaps, and poorly targeted or administered public support. The analysis shows that moving underperforming firms to median sector-level energy efficiency could reduce energy consumption and emissions by an estimated 38 to 44 percent, while increasing profitability by only 2 to 6 percent, highlighting the large social and environmental benefits relative to private returns. SMEs face particular challenges in identifying, assessing, and financing energy-efficiency opportunities, while commercial-bank lending for such projects remains limited. Based on findings from Poland and Romania, the report recommends strengthening regulatory governance, redesigning public financial support toward more predictable and repayable instruments, improving energy audits and follow-through, using green public procurement to stimulate demand, mobilizing private capital through green lending and risk-sharing mechanisms, and strengthening firms’ technical capabilities and awareness. Together, these measures can help make energy efficiency a scalable and investable business proposition while directing public resources toward sectors and market failures where they can deliver the greatest economic, energy-security, and emissions benefits.

title: Selective Lanthanide-Binding Peptides: Molecular Insights into Binding Affinity and Selectivity
summary: Rare earth elements (REEs), including the lanthanides, are essential to clean-energy technologies, semiconductors, electric vehicles, turbines, and other advanced materials that exploit their luminescent, magnetic, and catalytic properties.
content: Rare earth elements (REEs), including the lanthanides, are essential to clean-energy technologies, semiconductors, electric vehicles, turbines, and other advanced materials that exploit their luminescent, magnetic, and catalytic properties. Current REE separation methods, however, suffer from poor selectivity, high solvent use, and environmental burden, which motivates greener and more selective strategies. Here we combine fluorescence binding measurements, molecular dynamics, enhanced-sampling calculations, descriptor analysis, and machine learning to determine how lanthanide-binding tag (LBT) peptides discriminate among trivalent REE cations in aqueous solution. The peptides operate in two binding regimes. For larger, lighter REEs, affinity is governed primarily by ion size, solvation, solvent accessibility, and non-bonded electrostatic interactions in a loosely coordinated binding pocket. For smaller, heavier REEs, the pocket contracts, and steric crowding, ligand–ligand electrostatic repulsion, and backbone torsional strain increasingly oppose further stabilization. Correlation analyses with sequence-derived, solvation, ligation, and conformational descriptors support this dichotomy. Analysis of selected LBT1-derived variants yields design rules: terminal charge tunes absolute affinity, ligating-residue geometry controls productive electrostatic coordination, a gatekeeper residue regulates water access and steric closure, and terminal residue hydrophobicity modulates amphiphilicity while preserving lanthanide-size sensitivity. Finally, classifiers trained on 37,041 sequences predict coarse Tb3+ affinity classes from a few bioinformatic descriptors, including disorder propensity, charge, amphiphilicity, and hydrophobicity, whereas predicting relative affinity across the full lanthanide series remains sensitive to solvation and binding-pocket remodeling. These results provide a molecular framework for engineering peptides for selective REE recovery and separation.

title: Effect of B40 Biodiesel on the Performance and Emissions of Fishing-Vessel Diesel Engines and Its Implications for Operating Costs
summary: Background: Indonesia's B40 mandate (40% palm oil-based fatty acid methyl ester [FAME] blended with petroleum diesel), which took effect in January 2025, extends to fishing fleets that operate older engines and purchase subsidized fuel at a
content: Background: Indonesia's B40 mandate (40% palm oil-based fatty acid methyl ester [FAME] blended with petroleum diesel), which took effect in January 2025, extends to fishing fleets that operate older engines and purchase subsidized fuel at a fixed price. However, no study has systematically traced how the blend's fuel properties affect engine behavior and, consequently, fishers' operating costs. Objective: This study develops and evaluates a closed-form model linking B40 fuel properties to engine performance, exhaust emissions, and trip operating costs across three classes of Indonesian fishing vessels (≤5, 5–10, and 10–30 gross tonnage [GT]). Methods: A secondary-data modeling approach combines ideal-mixture fuel-property relationships, a Willans-line engine model based on the ISO 8178 E5 marine engine test cycle, exponential emission-response functions, and a trip-level cost function. Uncertainty is propagated through 20,000 Latin hypercube simulation draws, with sensitivity assessed using Sobol indices. Results: Under the stated model assumptions, B40 reduces volumetric energy content by 3.46%, resulting in a modeled 4.6% increase in fuel volume consumed per trip (90% simulation interval: 2.7–6.6%) and a 2.4–3.0% increase in operating costs. All 20,000 simulation draws yield a positive change in operating costs. Fossil-derived tank-to-wake CO₂ emissions decrease by 37.2%, while modeled CO, HC, and PM emissions decrease by approximately 21–23%. Modeled NOₓ emissions increase by 4.9%, although the simulation interval encompasses both a slight decrease and an increase. Cost neutrality requires an estimated compensatory adjustment of Rp347–364 per liter. Conclusion: At the assumed fixed retail fuel price, B40 imposes an additional modeled cost burden, which is described in this study as an implicit levy solely as an economic metaphor rather than as an official tax or government-imposed charge. The findings underscore the need for field-based engine-efficiency measurements and further policy assessments of potential targeted compensation as Indonesia considers adopting higher biodiesel blends.

title: Engineering Electrical Double Layers for Accelerated Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
summary: Improving the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline media is central to advancing efficient anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). Alkaline HER activity depends on the interplay between hydrogen and hydroxide adsorption
content: Improving the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline media is central to advancing efficient anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). Alkaline HER activity depends on the interplay between hydrogen and hydroxide adsorption energetics and the surrounding interfacial environment. Within this environment, water structure, ion distributions, and local electric fields modulate the activation free‐energy barriers for water activation, proton transfer, hydrogen adsorption, and OH − removal. This review examines how the electrical double layer (EDL) influences these interfacial processes in alkaline HER. Fundamental concepts, including the potential of zero charge, the potential of maximum entropy, and cation solvation, are first introduced to provide a basis for understanding how EDL structure influences alkaline HER. Experimental and computational studies are then summarized to examine the effects of surface charge, cation identity, and electrolyte composition and concentration on interfacial water structure, hydrogen‐bond connectivity, and local electric fields. On the basis of this understanding, recent EDL engineering strategies are reviewed, together with their relevance to practical AEMWE operation. Finally, key interfacial design principles and remaining challenges are discussed to guide the integration of EDL regulation with catalyst and electrode development toward more efficient and durable alkaline water electrolysis.

title: CbSDI for Ecological Sustainability and Smart Urban Development in Kigali: An Integrated Approach to Building Resilient Cities
summary: Urbanization presents pressing challenges for sustainability, requiring cities to balance equity, economic growth, and environmental preservation. Kigali, Rwanda’s capital, has emerged as a model for integrating ecological sustainability wi
content: Urbanization presents pressing challenges for sustainability, requiring cities to balance equity, economic growth, and environmental preservation. Kigali, Rwanda’s capital, has emerged as a model for integrating ecological sustainability with smart city development. This study examines Kigali’s initiatives in green infrastructure, biodiversity conservation, waste management, renewable energy, and sustainable transportation, highlighting their role in enhancing resilience and livability. Projects such as the Nyandungu Urban Eco-Park, car-free zones, and solar energy installations demonstrate the city’s commitment to harmonizing urban growth with environmental protection. Smart city approaches, including ICT-enabled transportation systems and real-time environmental monitoring, further optimize resource use and reduce ecological impacts. The findings reveal that Kigali’s strategies supported by government commitment, collaborative partnerships, and innovative technologies have significantly advanced ecological restoration and sustainable urban planning. However, challenges remain, including limited resources, infrastructure gaps, and socio-economic inequalities. A SWOT analysis underscores opportunities in green investment, circular economy practices, and international collaboration, while identifying threats such as climate change, land scarcity, and technological dependencies. Overall, Kigali’s experience illustrates how developing cities can leverage nature-based solutions and smart technologies to achieve ecological sustainability. The research concludes that continued investment in green infrastructure, renewable energy, and sustainable mobility, alongside long-term impact assessments, will be critical for scaling Kigali’s model to other urban contexts. By prioritizing environmental health and social well-being, Kigali sets a benchmark for resilient, inclusive, and sustainable cities.

title: Intention to Use Social Media for Travel Planning among Tourists Who Have Visited Terengganu
source: Research in Management of Technology and Business
summary: The research paper reports on the use of social media by foreign tourists coming to Terengganu, Malaysia, as a case study. The researchers were trying to know the factors that trigger the intention of tourists to use social media for the pu
content: The research paper reports on the use of social media by foreign tourists coming to Terengganu, Malaysia, as a case study. The researchers were trying to know the factors that trigger the intention of tourists to use social media for the purpose of travel planning and decision-making. The quick growth of digital technology has completely changed the tourism business, and one of the major reasons for this change is that eventually, tourists have started to count on social media more for destination info, sharing experiences and trip planning. But quite a few research are done in Terengganu on the adoption of social media by tourists which however are still in limited numbers. The present study makes use of a quantitative method where a structured questionnaire was used for data collection through surveys of local tourists. The total number of valid responses received was 228, and the data were analysed by using the SPSS software package. To investigate the interplay between compatibility, enjoyment, e-trust, expertise and intention to use social media, descriptive analysis, reliability and correlation analyses were performed. The results showed that the four factors were positively and significantly associated with the tourists intention to use social media platforms, revealing that when the platforms are aligned with the travel habits of the tourists, provide fun, are considered as trustworthy and once users feel confident in their own skill levels they are more likely to adopt social media. The research overall suggests that social media has a pivotal role in driving travel behaviour of tourists in Terengganu and that it also is a good way for destination planning and getting involved with the audience.

title: INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AGREEMENTS AND THEIR IMPLEMENTATION IN THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN
source: American Journal of Interdisciplinary Research and Development
summary: This article compares Uzbekistan’s implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Convention on Biological Diversity and the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification through a review of legislation, official reports and project recor
