title: An acoustic fuzzy decision analytics framework for prioritizing artificial intelligence investments in hospitals
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer significant opportunities for hospitals in terms of improving the quality of healthcare services. However, the limited financial resources of hospitals necessitate a strategic prioritization a
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer significant opportunities for hospitals in terms of improving the quality of healthcare services. However, the limited financial resources of hospitals necessitate a strategic prioritization among different AI investment alternatives. Previous studies have extensively examined the relative importance of evaluation criteria and addressed uncertainty and hesitation in expert judgments through various multi-criteria decision-making and fuzzy set approaches. Building on this established literature, the present study focuses on incorporating acoustic characteristics of expert responses, including response latency, vocal fluctuations, and energy-related indicators, into the representation of fuzzy decision information. This approach provides an additional dimension for modeling expert evaluations in the context of hospital AI investment prioritization. Hospitals must evaluate AI applications with different clinical and operational functions, implementation requirements, and expected benefits, making investment prioritization a complex decision-making problem under limited resources. The integration of acoustic characteristics of expert responses into an established multi-criteria decision-making framework provides an additional perspective for addressing this problem. The aim of this study is to prioritize the most suitable AI investment strategies for hospitals and to develop an innovative decision support model that considers behavioral uncertainties in expert evaluations. In this context, the Acoustic Fuzzy Sets (AFS) approach, which analyzes not only the verbal evaluations of experts but also their acoustic characteristics such as response time, voice vibration, and tone change, is proposed. The Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method is employed to calculate the importance weights of the criteria, while the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) approach is used to rank the strategies. The robustness of the proposed framework was examined through comparative analyses with different multi-criteria decision-making methods and Monte Carlo-based sensitivity analyses. The analysis results show that operational efficiency is the most important evaluation criterion in AI investment decisions in hospitals. Among the alternatives, robotic process automation for hospital management processes was determined to be the most suitable investment option. This study offers an innovative methodological contribution to the multi-criteria decision-making literature by proposing an acoustic fuzzy sets approach that analyzes behavioral uncertainties in expert evaluations through voice biometrics.

title: Pseudomagnetic focusing of valley-polarized beams in strained graphene
summary: In addition to spin, the low-energy charge carriers in graphene have two inequivalent valley flavors K and K ′ related by time-reversal symmetry, which can potentially serve as carriers for additional information. One promising route of con
content: In addition to spin, the low-energy charge carriers in graphene have two inequivalent valley flavors K and K ′ related by time-reversal symmetry, which can potentially serve as carriers for additional information. One promising route of controlling the valley degree of freedom relies on strain-induced pseudomagnetic fields, which couple with opposite signs to the two valleys. In this work, we theoretically investigate quantum transport in strained graphene devices that host tailored pseudomagnetic field profiles for valley manipulation. We focus on experimentally feasible geometries and propose transverse pseudomagnetic focusing in a bent graphene ribbon as an efficient method for generating valley-polarized currents, even in presence of disorder. Our work highlights pseudomagneto-transport in graphene as a viable tool for valleytronic applications.

title: Valorizing Arundo donax and polyethylene terephthalate waste into sustainable hydrochar-bitumen mastics via hydrothermal co-liquefaction
summary: As the demand for sustainable pavement materials grows, this study evaluates hydrochar, a solid by-product of the hydrothermal co-liquefaction (co-HTL) of Arundo donax biomass and polyethylene terephthalate (PET), as an alternative filler i
content: As the demand for sustainable pavement materials grows, this study evaluates hydrochar, a solid by-product of the hydrothermal co-liquefaction (co-HTL) of Arundo donax biomass and polyethylene terephthalate (PET), as an alternative filler in bitumen mastics. The effects of biomass-to-PET ratio, co-HTL temperature, and residence time on hydrochar characteristics and mastic chemo-mechanical performance are investigated. Results reveal that hydrochar improves high-temperature deformation resistance and elastic recovery, with the maximum recovery reaching 8.07 times that of mineral mastics. However, hydrochar mastics show inferior low-temperature relaxation and fatigue resistance, with fatigue life reduced by more than 50%, limiting their suitability for cold climates and heavily trafficked pavements. Increasing the biomass-to-PET ratio enhances high-temperature performance but reduces low-temperature flexibility and fatigue life, whereas higher co-HTL temperatures improve thermal cracking and fatigue resistance. The mastic containing 345–30–0.5B hydrochar exhibits the best fatigue and relaxation performance, while the 250–30–0.5B sample presents the highest rutting resistance. Hydrochar introduces more aromatic, polar, and oxygen-containing structures into the bitumen, strengthening hydrochar-bitumen interactions. Chemo-mechanical correlations further suggest that bitumen rich in aromatic rings, long-chain hydrocarbons, and carbonyl groups may improve the low-temperature relaxation and fatigue performance of hydrochar mastics.

title: Upgrading Concepts for the Implementation of Sustainable DTG Fuels
summary: Die Dekarbonisierung des Verkehrssektors ist ein zentraler Pfeiler des Klimaschutzes. Trotz rascher Fortschritte bei der Elektrifizierung werden Kraftstoffe allerdings, insbesondere in der Luft- und Seeschifffahrt, weiterhin eine wichtige R
content: Die Dekarbonisierung des Verkehrssektors ist ein zentraler Pfeiler des Klimaschutzes. Trotz rascher Fortschritte bei der Elektrifizierung werden Kraftstoffe allerdings, insbesondere in der Luft- und Seeschifffahrt, weiterhin eine wichtige Rolle spielen. Außerdem, da ein Großteil der Fahrzeugflotte nach wie vor auf Verbrennungsmotoren basiert. Treibhausgasneutrale synthetische Kohlenwasserstoffe, die durch methanol-to-gasoline (MTG) und dimethyl ether-to-gasoline (DTG) hergestellt werden, stellen aufgrund ihrer Kompatibilität mit bestehenden Motoren und Kraftstoffinfrastrukturen eine vielversprechende Lösung dar. Allerdings enthält dieses Benzin aromatenreiches Schwerbenzin, das sich durch einen erhöhten Durolgehalt, geringe Flüchtigkeit und erhöhte Emissionen auszeichnet. Die Aufbereitung und Integration dieser Fraktionen stellt eine zentrale Herausforderung für den großtechnischen Einsatz synthetischer Kraftstoffe dar. Diese Dissertation befasst sich mit dieser Fragestellung, indem zwei auf Hydroprocessing basierende Konzepte für die Verwertung von Schwerbenzin entwickelt werden. Für den ersten Ansatz wird das Hydroprocessing von bioliq-Schwerbenzin unter Verwendung bifunktioneller Pt/Zeolith-Katalysatoren (Pt/HZSM-5, Pt/SAPO-11 und Pt/Mordenit) in einem Laborfestbettreaktor untersucht. Katalysator- und prozessbedingte Auswirkungen auf Oktanzahlen und Flüchtigkeitsparameter werden systematisch analysiert. Die Experimente zeigen eine ausgeprägte Abhängigkeit der Motoroktanzahl von der Wahl des Katalysators, wobei die Reihenfolge Pt/HZSM-5 > Pt/SAPO-11 > Pt/Mordenit gilt, was auf eine formselektive Isomerisierung zurückzuführen ist. Erhöhte Reaktionstemperaturen verstärken das Cracken, was zu einem deutlichen Anstieg der wichtigsten Flüchtigkeitsparameter führt. Um die europäische Benzinnorm EN 228 erfüllen zu können, wird ein weiterführendes Blending-Konzept entwickelt, um verbleibende Volatilitätsdefizite durch die Einbeziehung von Oxygenaten (Methanol, Ethanol, MTBE und ETBE) und einem Benzindestillat aus hydrogekrackten Fischer-Tropsch-Wachsen zu beheben. Blending-Versuche zeigen, dass Oxygenate deutliche und teilweise nichtlineare Auswirkungen auf die Destillationskurve haben. Methanol ist besonders wirksam bei der Erhöhung der Flüchtigkeit im unteren Siedebereich, während MTBE und ETBE ein gleichmäßigeres Siedeverhalten ermöglichen. Es wird eine nahezu normkonformes Benzin erhalten, wobei Formulierungen auf Methanol-/ETBE-Basis die besten Ergebnisse in Bezug auf Flüchtigkeit und Oktanzahl erzielen. In einem zweiten Ansatz wird eine Raffinerieintegration untersucht, indem aromatenreiches bioliq-Schwerbenzin unter industriellen Hydrotreating-Bedingungen gemeinsam mit fossilem Mitteldestillat hydroprocessed wird. Langzeitversuche werden durchgeführt, um die Isomerisierungsselektivität und wichtige petrochemische Parameter zu bewerten. title: Mn-regulated quaternary molten alloys for CO2-free hydrogen production via methane pyrolysis
summary: Methane pyrolysis offers a route to low-carbon hydrogen by converting CH 4 into H 2 and solid carbon without direct CO 2 formation, but efficient catalysts must activate strong C H bonds while remaining tolerant to continuous carbon formati
content: Methane pyrolysis offers a route to low-carbon hydrogen by converting CH 4 into H 2 and solid carbon without direct CO 2 formation, but efficient catalysts must activate strong C H bonds while remaining tolerant to continuous carbon formation. Liquid alloys provide a dynamic, carbon-tolerant reaction medium, yet the compositional rules that govern active liquid environments remain insufficiently defined. Here, we screened eight elements as fourth-metal regulators in NiMo-Bi molten alloys and combined melting-point prediction with compositional screening. Among the 29 catalysts evaluated, Ni 12 Mo 4 Mn 4 -Bi was identified as the most effective catalyst in this series. The catalyst operated from 350 to 1050 °C with an apparent activation energy of 77.51 kJ mol −1 , potentially reflecting contributions from gas–liquid mass transfer. At 800 °C, Ni 12 Mo 4 Mn 4 -Bi achieved 23.67% CH 4 conversion, 99.98% H 2 selectivity, and a H 2 production rate of 0.5845 mL H 2 g cat − 1 min − 1 , with continuous operation demonstrated for 260 h, accompanied by a slight decline in catalytic performance. Increasing the active-metal loading from Ni 7.6 Mo 2.6 -Bi to Ni 12 Mo 4 -Bi raised the hydrogen production rate 4.86-fold, from 0.0929 to 0.4515 mL H 2 g cat − 1 min − 1 . Adding Mn to the matched Ni 12 Mo 4 -Bi baseline further increased the rate by 29%, yielding a total 6.29-fold gain over Ni 7.6 Mo 2.6 -Bi. Structural characterization and theoretical simulations show that Mn promotes the dispersion of Ni and Mo in the Bi-rich liquid, tunes their electronic environment, and strengthens C H bond polarization in adsorbed CH 4 . Analysis of the solid carbon also revealed catalyst-dependent structures, as Ni 7.6 Mo 2.6 -Bi and Ni 12 Mo 4 Mn 4 -Bi produced mainly amorphous carbon, while Ni 12 Mo 4 Cu 4 -Bi produced a small fraction of carbon nanotubes. These findings provide an effective method for designing carbon-tolerant molten alloy catalysts for CO 2 -free hydrogen production from methane pyrolysis.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL CRIME AS A BARRIER TO SUSTAINABILITY TRANSITIONS
summary: Environmental crime represents a significant barrier to the global sustainability transition by compromising environmental integrity, economic stability, and social well-being. The study assesses the multifaceted impacts of illegal activiti
content: Environmental crime represents a significant barrier to the global sustainability transition by compromising environmental integrity, economic stability, and social well-being. The study assesses the multifaceted impacts of illegal activities, including wildlife trafficking, illegal logging, pollution, and illicit waste disposal, on sustainable development pathways. Utilizing interdisciplinary perspectives from environmental economics, criminology, and sustainability science, the analysis explores how environmental crime disrupts resource efficiency, weakens institutional frameworks, and erodes public trust in governance systems. Drawing on case studies from the European Union, the analysis places particular emphasis on regulatory gaps, corruption, and transnational networks that enable these activities, thereby complicating enforcement and policy implementation. The study highlights the economic consequences of environmental degradation, including biodiversity loss, diminished ecosystem services, and long-term financial burdens on governments and communities. The research findings indicate that addressing environmental crime is essential for effective and equitable sustainable development, necessitating coordinated action among policymakers, businesses, and civil society to mitigate risks and strengthen resilience. Strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing cross-border cooperation, and leveraging technological innovations such as environmental monitoring systems are essential for effective prevention and enforcement. Furthermore, integrating anti-crime measures into sustainability strategies can enhance policy coherence and reinforce long-term economic and environmental resilience.

title: Green finance, institutional quality, and climate resilience in the Global South: Evidence from a panel of developing economies
summary: Climate finance commitments have escalated under successive COP frameworks. Yet adaptive capacity deficits across the Global South remain persistent and, in many contexts, are widening. This study examines whether, and under what governance
content: Climate finance commitments have escalated under successive COP frameworks. Yet adaptive capacity deficits across the Global South remain persistent and, in many contexts, are widening. This study examines whether, and under what governance conditions green finance translates into tangible improvements in climate resilience across developing economies. It positions institutional quality as the critical moderating variable that conditions the relationship between Green Finance and Climate Resilience. Using a balanced panel of 3,190 country-year observations across six sub-regional groupings of the Global South spanning 1995–2023, the study deploys various technique: panel fixed-effects regression, quantile and threshold regression and four principal findings emerge. First, Institutional Quality is the dominant, distributional-invariant determinant of Climate resilience with its effect remaining stable across quantile of the resilience distribution. Second, Green Finance exerts a negative unconditional effect on resilience that intensifies monotonically across higher readiness quantiles. Third, the interaction term is negative and significant throughout escalating threefold across quantiles and confirming that green finance effectiveness diminishes as institutional quality increases. Fourth, North Africa and the Middle East is the only region in which green finance exerts a positive and significant effect on resilience while Sub-Saharan Africa records the most strongly negative effect. This study advances an Institutional Primacy Thesis in climate finance, providing the first comprehensive multi-method empirical evidence across the full vulnerability distribution of the Global South.

title: Biochar/persulfate-modified biogas slurry mitigates soil N2O emissions: Roles of organic components and microbial nitrogen-cycling potentials
summary: Biogas slurry is a liquid fertilizer with a low C/N ratio, a high ammonia nitrogen concentration, and a high moisture content. Compared with the addition of mineral fertilizer, the application of biogas slurry may further promote soil nitro
content: Biogas slurry is a liquid fertilizer with a low C/N ratio, a high ammonia nitrogen concentration, and a high moisture content. Compared with the addition of mineral fertilizer, the application of biogas slurry may further promote soil nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions. This study used biochar and persulfate to modify organic components in biogas slurry, and assessed the effects of modified biogas slurry (MBS) on N 2 O emissions from purple soil and cabbage growth in a 52-day pot experiment. Compared to raw biogas slurry (BS), MBS application in low-fertility purple soil significantly reduced cumulative N 2 O emissions by 19.15% while increasing cabbage biomass by 31.88%. In the MBS treatment, the relative abundances of the denitrifying bacteria Nocardiopsis , nocardioides and Lysobacter in topsoil decreased by 42.82%, 29.33%, and 60.52%, respectively, while Sphingomonas in the rhizosphere increased by 27.32%. Compared with BS, the application of MBS significantly promoted the genetic potentials for nitrate reduction (+41.05%) and nitrate respiration (+216.67%), whereas the abundance of the nrfA/H encoding the nitrate dissimilatory reduction process increased by 50.82%. Additionally, MBS application was associated with greater stability of the soil bacterial co-occurrence network and shifts in putative keystone taxa, including Streptomyces , Microvirga , Paenibacillus , and Gemmatimonas , which may be linked to the observed reduction in N 2 O emissions. Overall, MBS application showed potential to mitigate N 2 O emissions from low-fertility purple soils under short-term controlled greenhouse conditions. This reduction was associated with lower abundances of denitrification-related genes and greater genetic potential for alternative nitrate reduction pathways. This study provides preliminary evidence for improving the environmental friendliness of biogas slurry for agriculture.

title: Study on the Impression of “Solid Wood Quality” with Image-based and Physical Evaluations
source: Journal of the Society of Materials Science Japan
summary: Utilizing wood contributes to carbon neutrality, and prioritizing solid wood maximizes this benefit by reducing processing load and ensuring long-term carbon storage. However, because engineered wood often prevails in the market due to its
content: Utilizing wood contributes to carbon neutrality, and prioritizing solid wood maximizes this benefit by reducing processing load and ensuring long-term carbon storage. However, because engineered wood often prevails in the market due to its cost-effectiveness and usability, appealing to the sensory perception of "solid wood quality" is essential for motivating consumer choice. This study investigated how impression evaluations vary based on surface material (real wood vs. color-copied grain pattern) and veneer thickness (0.2–4.0 mm) using six wood plates. Impression evaluation was conducted with 26 participants under three conditions: digital image observation on a display, physical visual observation, and visual–tactile observation. Factor analysis of semantic differential evaluations using eight evaluation terms identified three key factors that explained approximately 50% of the whole evaluation and define the structure of "solid wood quality": preference, roughness, and warmth. The results showed that, while color-copied and real wood were indistinguishable in digital images, real wood was rated significantly higher in physical observations, highlighting its importance. Regarding thickness, a general correlation with "solid wood quality" was not found. However, specifically in the visual–tactile condition, the preference factor score was significantly higher for thicknesses exceeding 4.0 mm compared to those under 0.5 mm, although ANOVA revealed no significant main effects of roughness or warmth factors on thickness. These findings suggest that the preference for solid wood is not primarily driven by visual appearance or surface properties of warmth or roughness, but rather by other sensory characteristics.

title: Framing, filtering, and friction: the domestic mechanics of the Belt and Road Initiative
summary: This chapter analyses the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) between 2020 and 2026 through the lens of the political processing of global challenges. Drawing on strategic documents – including China’s 15th Five-Year Plan – and comparative case
content: This chapter analyses the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) between 2020 and 2026 through the lens of the political processing of global challenges. Drawing on strategic documents – including China’s 15th Five-Year Plan – and comparative case studies from Kazakhstan and Serbia, the study is anchored in the framework of global governance and the domestic filtering of norms. It examines how global standards of the Green and Digital Silk Roads enter national policy arenas, arguing that domestic institutional and political filters shape implementation outcomes. The findings reveal that the BRI is not a monolithic instrument of Chinese hegemony, but a dynamic, fragmented process actively co-created by partner states. Rather than simple compliance, local elites employ strategies of selective implementation and symbolic alignment to reinforce domestic political legitimacy and regime stability.

title: China’s 15th Five-Year Plan: green transition, technological innovation, and the legal roadmap to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060
source: Review of Crime Peace and Society
summary: China’s 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), the first national planning framework operating fully within the 2060 carbon neutrality horizon, has been widely read as a shift from climate target-setting to institutional operationalization. This
content: China’s 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), the first national planning framework operating fully within the 2060 carbon neutrality horizon, has been widely read as a shift from climate target-setting to institutional operationalization. This article tests that reading by drawing on ecological modernization theory and the emerging Chinese doctrine of foreign-related rule of law (涉外法治); it analyses three interlocking mechanisms: the administrative transition from energy dual control (能耗双控) to carbon emission dual control (碳排放双控); the expansion of the national Emissions Trading System to the steel, cement, and aluminum sectors from 2025 and the planned move to absolute caps by 2027; and a new blended-finance architecture built around the National Low-Carbon Transition Fund. The analysis finds that the institutional advance is real but narrower than the terminology suggests; yet the plan removes the binding energy-intensity target and elevates carbon intensity to binding status, while setting no economy-wide absolute emissions cap, so the total emissions limb of dual control remains aspirational outside the ETS. More consequentially, the revision of the carbon-intensity accounting methodology that produced a reported 17.7% reduction for the 14th FYP, against independent estimates closer to 12%, carries forward into the new target; under the revised methodology, a 17% intensity reduction across 2026-2030 is compatible with absolute emissions continuing to rise. The article’s principal contribution is analytical rather than terminological. It proposes climate-related foreign-related law (气候涉外法治) as a bounded analytical category, defined by three cumulative criteria, and shows that China’s ETS reforms, carbon accounting standards, and green Belt and Road investment norms satisfy these criteria in ways that ordinary accounts of domestic implementation do not capture. The category is offered as a framework for examining how planning-based legal systems simultaneously absorb, resist, and export international climate obligations.

title: Securitisation of EU ETS 2 in the European Parliament
summary: The European Union (EU) is one of the signatories of the 2015 Paris Agreement, which sets the ambitious goal of limiting the increase in the global average temperature on Earth to 1.5 °C. In order to fulfil this commitment, the organisation
content: The European Union (EU) is one of the signatories of the 2015 Paris Agreement, which sets the ambitious goal of limiting the increase in the global average temperature on Earth to 1.5 °C. In order to fulfil this commitment, the organisation has adopted a comprehensive strategy for green transformation – the European Green Deal (EGD). One of its most significant elements is the new Emission Trading System (ETS 2), which constitutes a supplement to the European Union Emission Trading System (EU ETS) that has been in operation since 2005. Similarly to other components of the green agenda, the issue of the new emissions trading system has generated considerable controversy among actors and stakeholders within the EU. The aim of this chapter is to examine the narrative following the topic of ETS 2 in one of the organisation’s legislative institutions – the European Parliament. In order to analyse and frame this issue, securitisation theory will be applied, together with the following research methods and techniques: institutional-legal analysis, comparative analysis, and the textual analysis of academic literature and documents.

title: Political Processing of Global Challenges
summary: This edited volume examines how global challenges are politically interpreted, institutionally mediated and translated into policy responses at national, regional and international levels. It develops the concept of political processing thr
content: This edited volume examines how global challenges are politically interpreted, institutionally mediated and translated into policy responses at national, regional and international levels. It develops the concept of political processing through three interconnected thematic axes: the interpretation and framing of global challenges, global governance and the domestic filtering of norms, and national policy responses, implementation and legitimation. Drawing on interdisciplinary perspectives from political science, international relations and public policy studies, the volume brings together eleven chapters addressing climate governance, economic sanctions, technological sovereignty, artificial intelligence, military innovation, nuclear waste management, agricultural policy, public health and migration. Through diverse regional and national case studies, the authors explore how institutional arrangements, political interests, strategic narratives and administrative capacities shape responses to transboundary pressures. Particular attention is paid to securitisation, norm localisation, selective implementation and the divergence between formal commitments and policy outcomes. The volume provides an analytical framework for understanding the political mediation of contemporary global challenges and the complex relationship between global governance and domestic policy-making.

title: Political shield against carbon risk: Evidence from Chinese stock markets
summary: As China accelerates its transition toward a carbon-neutral economy, regulatory pressure on high-emission firms is intensifying. The country's two-tier economic structure of state-owned and private enterprises makes political connections cr
content: As China accelerates its transition toward a carbon-neutral economy, regulatory pressure on high-emission firms is intensifying. The country's two-tier economic structure of state-owned and private enterprises makes political connections crucial in determining how these risks are priced. We examine how political connections affect carbon risk pricing in the Chinese stock market. Our results suggest that political connections, either through state ownership or corporate leaders’ prior government experience, reduce stocks' sensitivity to carbon emission performance. This effect arises from both explicit channels, including green subsidies and administrative penalties, and implicit channels, including preferential tax treatment, selective regulatory enforcement, and green credit. Based on the Fama-French 5-factor model, the political shield lowers the carbon risk premium that investors demand from state-owned firms by 0.38% to 0.69% monthly, relative to private firm stocks.

title: Degradation problems in energy conversion materials and devices: Efficiency-durability trade-off, interfacial instability, and mitigation strategies
summary: The transition toward carbon-neutral, sustainable energy systems has intensified the demand for highly durable, efficient energy-conversion materials and devices. However, their practical use is constrained by degradation processes that sim
content: The transition toward carbon-neutral, sustainable energy systems has intensified the demand for highly durable, efficient energy-conversion materials and devices. However, their practical use is constrained by degradation processes that simultaneously degrade their durability and efficiency. This article provides a critical and comprehensive overview of degradation pathways across diverse energy conversion technologies, including fuel cells, photovoltaics, electrolyzers, photothermal systems, and thermoelectric systems. Particular emphasis has been placed on the intrinsic efficiency-durability trade-off, where energy materials engineered for high performance and activity often exhibit limited long-term stability under operating conditions. The review systematically presents multiscale degradation pathways in these systems, encompassing interfacial degradation, electrochemical corrosion, nanostructural evolution, mechanical and thermal stress, environmental instability, and chemical instability. These degradation processes adversely affect heat, mass, and charge transport, leading to progressive performance decay and eventual device failure. This also highlights the role of interfaces as critical, vulnerable components that control the functionality of energy devices. Several mitigation strategies, such as interface stabilization, advanced encapsulation, defect engineering, self-healing materials, and operando diagnostic techniques, have been explored in this article. This review underscores the need to adopt a holistic design philosophy that integrates material sustainability, durability, efficiency, and scalability. This also highlights the urgent need to refine performance metrics in energy conversion materials and devices by integrating life-cycle considerations and efficiency retention under defined operating conditions. This review provides forward-looking frameworks for designing high-performing, durable, economically viable, environmentally sustainable, and scalable energy conversion technologies.

title: GC×GC–MS analysis of volatile components extracted by spinning cone column from Forsythia suspensa and its antimicrobial assessment
summary: Forsythia suspensa is a traditional medicinal plant rich in volatile bioactive compounds with important pharmacological and application value. In this study, volatile compounds from F. suspensa were extracted using spinning cone column (SCC
content: Forsythia suspensa is a traditional medicinal plant rich in volatile bioactive compounds with important pharmacological and application value. In this study, volatile compounds from F. suspensa were extracted using spinning cone column (SCC) technology for the first time. The compounds were qualitatively characterized using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) and comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC×GC–MS), as well as quantified using the area normalization method. The antibacterial activity of the resulting essential oil against six pathogenic microorganisms was evaluated using the broth microdilution method. The essential oil yield obtained through SCC extraction reached 2.16%. A total of 38 compounds were identified from the essential oil, with β-pinene, 4-terpinenol, sabinene, and α-pinene as the major constituents. The GC×GC–MS analysis enabled the detection of 90 compounds, including those identified by GC–MS, and revealed additional bioactive compounds, such as guaiacol, myrtenal, citronellol, carvacrol, and α-bisabolol, that were not detected by GC–MS. The antimicrobial assays demonstrated that the essential oil exhibited antimicrobial activity against susceptible test microorganisms, with minimum inhibitory concentration values ranging from 31.3 μg/mL to 62.5 μg/mL. These findings highlighted the potential of SCC technology for extracting F. suspensa essential oil and demonstrated the value of GC×GC–MS for comprehensive characterization of its volatile constituents, providing a basis for further investigation of its antibacterial potential.

title: A New 6-deoxy-talopyranoside derivative with antibacterial and radical-scavenging activities from Streptomyces sp. HDSJ4
summary: Chemical investigation of the secondary metabolites from a Streptomyces sp. strain yielded two compounds (1 and 2), including an undescribed 6-deoxy-talopyranoside derivative, designated strepyranin A (1). The structure of strepyranin A was
content: Chemical investigation of the secondary metabolites from a Streptomyces sp. strain yielded two compounds (1 and 2), including an undescribed 6-deoxy-talopyranoside derivative, designated strepyranin A (1). The structure of strepyranin A was unambiguously established based on comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including 1D and 2D NMR spectra, together with HRESIMS data. Compound 1 was assayed for its antibacterial and radical-scavenging activities. Bioassays revealed that strepyranin A (1) exhibited weak antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Streptococcus pneumoniae, with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values of 64 μg/mL and 128 μg/mL, respectively, and moderate DPPH radical-scavenging activity with an RSA of 36.4%.

title: Asperpolyols A and B, two novel hydroxy polyunsaturated fatty acids, isolated from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus versicolor M7
summary: Asperpolyols A ((4E,8E,12E,16E)-3,7,11,15-tetrahydroxy-4,6,8,10,12,14,16-heptamethyloctadeca-4,8,12,16-tetraenoic acid) and B ((4E,8E,12E,16E)-3,7,11,15-tetrahydroxy-4,6,8,10,12,14,16-heptamethyloctadeca-4,8,12,16-tetraen-oic acid), two new
content: Asperpolyols A ((4E,8E,12E,16E)-3,7,11,15-tetrahydroxy-4,6,8,10,12,14,16-heptamethyloctadeca-4,8,12,16-tetraenoic acid) and B ((4E,8E,12E,16E)-3,7,11,15-tetrahydroxy-4,6,8,10,12,14,16-heptamethyloctadeca-4,8,12,16-tetraen-oic acid), two new hydroxy polyunsaturated fatty acids, were acquired from the extract of Aspergillus versicolor M7 isolated from seawater. Their chemical structures were determined by interpretation of 1D/2D nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HRESIMS) data. Compounds 1 and 2 were evaluated for inhibiting the growth of three marine phytoplankton species, including Prorocentrum donghaiense, Heterosigma akashiwo, and Prorocentrum micans, and compound 1 exhibited weak inhibitory activity with the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values ranging from 62.8 to 86.9 μg/mL.

title: A new acylated quercetin triglycoside with anti-inflammatory activity from the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida
summary: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida led to the isolation of a previously undescribed acylated quercetin triglycoside (1), together with three known constituents (2–4). Their structures were established
content: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida led to the isolation of a previously undescribed acylated quercetin triglycoside (1), together with three known constituents (2–4). Their structures were established by HR-ESI-MS with 1D and 2D NMR analyses and, for the known compounds, by comparison with reported spectroscopic data. Compound 1 was elucidated as quercetin 3-O-[β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→3)]-[α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)]-[2-O-(E)-p-coumaroyl]-β-D-glucopyranoside. Compounds 1–3 inhibited lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 14.9 ± 1.7, 13.4 ± 2.6, and 37.7 ± 2.9 μM, respectively, while their CC50 values were >64 μM. 4 was cytotoxic (CC50 10.9 ± 0.7 μM) and was therefore not evaluated for nitric oxide inhibition. These findings expand the known chemical diversity of C. flavida var. flavida and identify 1 and 2 as moderate inhibitors of nitric oxide production.

title: Orsellinic acid derivatives with antibacterial activity from Alternaria sp. TY22 associated with Typha orientalis
summary: Filamentous fungi are renowned for producing structurally diverse secondary metabolites with significant biological activities. In the present study, seven compounds, including a pair of new isomeric 2,3-butylene orsellinate derivatives (1a
content: Filamentous fungi are renowned for producing structurally diverse secondary metabolites with significant biological activities. In the present study, seven compounds, including a pair of new isomeric 2,3-butylene orsellinate derivatives (1a/1b) and five known compounds (2–6), were isolated from the endophytic fungus Alternaria sp. TY22 derived from Typha orientalis. Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analysis. Antibacterial evaluation revealed that 2 and 3 showed strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis with MIC values ranging from 4 to 16 μg/mL, and the new isomers 1a/1b displayed moderate antibacterial activity with MIC values of 64 and 32 μg/mL against S. aureus and B. subtilis, respectively.

title: A new iridoid glycoside with anti-inflammatory activity from Lamiophlomis rotata
summary: A new iridoid glycoside (1), along with two known congeners (2−3), was isolated from Lamiophlomis rotata. The structure of new findings was elucidated by comprehensive analyses, including 1D/2D NMR, HRESIMS, hydrolysis derivatization and EC
content: A new iridoid glycoside (1), along with two known congeners (2−3), was isolated from Lamiophlomis rotata. The structure of new findings was elucidated by comprehensive analyses, including 1D/2D NMR, HRESIMS, hydrolysis derivatization and ECD spectroscopy. Compound 1 shows an obviously anti-inflammatory potential by inhibiting the secretion of NO, iNOS, COX-2 and ROS in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages at the concentration of 7.5 μM.

title: Graphene-Derived Nanomaterials for Wastewater Treatment: Bridging Laboratory Performance and Practical Feasibility
summary: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. Conventional wastewater treatment technologies often fail to re
content: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. Conventional wastewater treatment technologies often fail to remove trace contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, heavy metals, and emerging organic compounds. Graphene-based materials, including graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide, and graphene quantum dots, have emerged as promising candidates due to their high surface area, tunable surface chemistry, mechanical robustness, and unique electronic properties, enabling diverse removal mechanisms such as adsorption, catalysis, and membrane filtration. Laboratory studies have shown that these materials can achieve superior pollutant removal efficiencies; however, their large-scale implementation remains limited, highlighting the gap between laboratory performance and industrial feasibility.This review provides a structured assessment of graphene-based materials for wastewater treatment. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature review covering 2010–2024 was conducted, with emphasis on the latest 2025 studies addressing techno-economic and industrial feasibility. The review examines the types of graphene materials, their physicochemical properties, and functionalization strategies, followed by critical evaluation of their applications in removing various contaminants. Key research gaps, including aggregation, fouling, regeneration loss, toxicity, and lack of standardized protocols, are discussed. The techno-economic and industrial feasibility section analyzes production costs, scalability, energy requirements, and lifecycle considerations. Finally, future perspectives on AI-guided material design, smart membranes, and regulatory frameworks are outlined to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and practical development.

title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
source: International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS)
summary: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analys
content: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

title: Framework for Sustainable Water Management in Some Selected States in Northern Nigeria
summary: Both groundwater and surface water are the most reliable sources for domestic, agricultural, and industrial use in Nigeria. However, they face increasing pressure from above-ground human activities, such as uncontrolled urbanization, contin
content: Both groundwater and surface water are the most reliable sources for domestic, agricultural, and industrial use in Nigeria. However, they face increasing pressure from above-ground human activities, such as uncontrolled urbanization, continuous waste disposal, and poor land-use management. The impact on water users is unacceptable, and the purely technical solutions of this century have failed to address the growing contamination of this vital resource. This study examines existing issues in groundwater management and provides a platform for engaging various stakeholders whose involvement is necessary to address these problems. The steps taken to identify and involve stakeholders responsible for and affected by both surface and groundwater contamination are described and discussed. The paper assesses current water management approaches, the causes of contamination, stakeholders’ capacities and concerns, and offers sustainable solutions that will help transition from the current system to a more integrated and effective one. Sustainable strategies suitable for many developing countries are also recommended. The findings will contribute valuable insights to water managers, policymakers, and decision-makers working to implement sustainable groundwater management systems in Nigeria and other rapidly developing nations.

title: Kinetic Analysis of the Combustion Reaction of Sub-Bituminous Coal Blended with Empty Fruit Bunch (EFB) Waste
source: Scientific Experiences in Energy and Thermal Engineering
summary: This study evaluated the effect of blending ratios of sub-bituminous coal and Empty Fruit Bunch (EFB) biomass on the activation energy (Eₐ) of the combustion process using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) and the Coats–Redfern kinetic appro
content: This study evaluated the effect of blending ratios of sub-bituminous coal and Empty Fruit Bunch (EFB) biomass on the activation energy (Eₐ) of the combustion process using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) and the Coats–Redfern kinetic approach. The fuel samples consisted of 100% coal, 80% coal–20% EFB, and 60% coal–40% EFB blends. The results showed that the average activation energy during Stage I decreased from 91.16 kJ/mol for pure coal to 86.69 kJ/mol for the 20% EFB blend, before increasing to 91.64 kJ/mol for the 40% EFB blend. During Stage II, the activation energy decreased from 61.88 kJ/mol for pure coal to 48.70 kJ/mol for the 20% EFB blend, and then increased slightly to 49.50 kJ/mol for the 40% EFB blend. These findings indicate that the addition of 20% EFB produces a synergistic effect by enhancing the thermal reactivity of the fuel mixture, whereas increasing the EFB content to 40% results in a higher activation energy due to the greater complexity of lignin decomposition and the formation of an ash layer on the char surface. It can therefore be concluded that the 20% EFB blend represents the optimum co-firing ratio from a kinetic perspective.

title: Improved WOA-Based Multilevel Resource Coordinated Scheduling Strategy for Active Distribution Network
summary: To address the operational complexity caused by the high proportion of new energy integration into distribution networks, a multilevel resource-coordinated operation strategy based on an improved whale optimization algorithm (improved WOA)
content: To address the operational complexity caused by the high proportion of new energy integration into distribution networks, a multilevel resource-coordinated operation strategy based on an improved whale optimization algorithm (improved WOA) is proposed for active distribution networks (ADNs). A bilevel optimization model is established to ensure the economic and safe operation of ADNs. The upper level is used to minimize the total system operation cost, while the lower level is used to optimize the power balance. Subsequently, the improved WOA, integrated with an adaptive weight and chaotic disturbance mechanisms, is used to solve the bilevel model and obtain a multi-resource coordinated operation strategy. This framework can help to enhance convergence and avoid local optima. In the simulation section, the IEEE 33-bus system is used to test the performance of the multilevel resource coordinated operation strategy. The simulation results reveal that the proposed approach can reduce the total system operation cost to 9.72 × 104 CNY. Moreover, the fossil fuel consumption of the diesel generator and the charging cost of electric vehicles are reduced by 15% and 18%, respectively. In addition, the power supply–demand matching accuracy is increased to 99.8%. Compared with the multi-element heuristic algorithm, the improved WOA shows significant superiority and robustness. This research provides an economical and stable multi-resource coordinated scheduling solution for distribution networks with a high proportion of renewable energy.

title: A Robust Optimisation Strategy for Active Distribution Networks Using VMD-LSO-LSTM Prediction
summary: To address the critical challenges of power fluctuations and the imperative for efficient reactive power optimization in distribution networks with high photovoltaic (PV) penetration, this study proposes an innovative solution: a robust rea
content: To address the critical challenges of power fluctuations and the imperative for efficient reactive power optimization in distribution networks with high photovoltaic (PV) penetration, this study proposes an innovative solution: a robust reactive power optimization approach that integrates VMD-LSTM-based PV power forecasting with the advanced Lion Swarm Optimization (LSO) algorithm. The methodology commences by employing Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) to decompose the PV power sequence into distinct modal components in a seamless manner. Each modal component is subsequently modeled using a dedicated forecasting framework built on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, with the LSO algorithm optimizing the LSTM hyperparameters to attain outstanding prediction precision. Building upon these precise forecasts, we establish a robust reactive power optimization model tailored for distribution networks, thoughtfully accommodating the inherent uncertainties of PV generation. This dual-layer model has an upper layer that addresses challenging PV scenarios and a lower layer that orchestrates the coordinated scheduling of energy storage systems, capacitor banks (CB), and Static Var Compensators (SVC). The primary objective is to minimise network losses while optimising reactive power compensation strategies that enhance overall performance. Case studies reveal that our innovative VMD-LSO-LSTM model significantly outperforms single LSTM and VMD-LSTM models in predictive accuracy. Additionally, the robust reactive power optimization strategy effectively dampens power fluctuations, decreases network losses, and substantially boosts distribution network operations’ economic efficiency and stability—ensuring a more resilient and sustainable energy future.

title: Optimization Dispatch Strategy for Interconnected Shared Energy Storage Systems in Distribution Transformers Based on Regional Dynamic Partitioning
summary: To address the operational volatility and complexity caused by the high penetration of renewable energy in distribution networks, the traditional static and isolated operation mode of distribution transformers struggles to simultaneously en
content: To address the operational volatility and complexity caused by the high penetration of renewable energy in distribution networks, the traditional static and isolated operation mode of distribution transformers struggles to simultaneously ensure power supply quality and economic efficiency. This paper proposes a coordinated dispatch strategy for interconnected distribution transformers based on regional dynamic partitioning and shared energy storage systems. Firstly, an improved K-means partitioning model for distribution transformers is constructed. By integrating a comprehensive distance metric that combines load characteristics and geospatial information, the limitations of traditional single-dimensional partitioning are overcome. Furthermore, a bi-level optimization dispatch model is established, with the upper-level objective of minimizing voltage deviation and the lower-level objective of minimizing operational cost, achieving the coordinated optimization of power quality and economic operation. On this basis, a comprehensive evaluation index composed of voltage stability and economic efficiency is innovatively proposed, and a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism feedback-based on the electrical correlation degree of distribution transformers is designed. This mechanism drives the closed-loop dynamic optimization of the partitioning scheme, enabling it to adaptively respond to the spatiotemporal changes of loads and renewable energy. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy increases the renewable energy utilization rate of distribution transformers by 5% and the daily maximum energy storage utilization rate by 9%, while forming a reasonable partitioning scheme with geographical compactness and electrical tightness.

title: Data-Driven Voltage Control for Distribution Networks with High Penetration of PVs via Improved DDPG
summary: The highly increasing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) has brought significant challenges for distribution network voltage control, which struggles with fast and stochastic fluctuations. This paper proposes a data-driven volta
content: The highly increasing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) has brought significant challenges for distribution network voltage control, which struggles with fast and stochastic fluctuations. This paper proposes a data-driven voltage control method utilizing an improved deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to minimize power losses while maintaining voltage within a safe operating range. The data-driven voltage control framework is established first, with the controlling center formulated as the agent. Based on the distribution network system and the voltage control original model, the data-driven voltage control model is formulated via the Markov decision process (MDP). A voltage sensitivity-guided DDPG algorithm, which incorporates the voltage-reactive power injection sensitivity matrix into the actor policy gradient, is developed to embed physical grid knowledge and reduce the actor’s reliance on critic action-gradient estimates, thus the practicality and generalization of data-driven voltage control is improved. Numerical simulations on the modified IEEE 33-node test system show the method maintains all nodal voltages within limits and reduces total system losses under varying PV generation, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for future sustainable power systems.

title: Interlaboratory Comparison Tests of Coal for Fuel and Energy Complex Enterprises
summary: The study focuses on four key indicators selected from eleven parameters characterizing hard coal quality. It presents and substantiates statistical approaches for processing the results of interlaboratory comparison testing, with particula
content: The study focuses on four key indicators selected from eleven parameters characterizing hard coal quality. It presents and substantiates statistical approaches for processing the results of interlaboratory comparison testing, with particular attention to the assessment of sample homogeneity and stability. The stages of organizing and conducting interlaboratory comparisons are described, taking into account the specific features of fuel and energy sector enterprises. Selected statistical methods were applied to analyze coal quality indicators and to evaluate the reliability of the obtained measurement results. Based on the analysis, recommendations were developed to improve measurement procedures, enhance the interpretation of statistical outcomes, and increase the reliability and trueness of test results. The findings may be applied by fuel and energy enterprises in the validation and optimization of measurement procedures for hard coal quality indicators. The interlaboratory comparison involving 63 laboratories demonstrated that the measured values of gross calorific value (32225–32275 kJ/kg), volatile matter yield (11.558–11.73%), ash content (8.68–8.74%), and mass fraction of total sulfur (0.241–0.256%) are comparable and fall within permissible limits, with no outliers detected according to robust statistical analysis. These results confirm the homogeneity of the prepared coal samples and the reliability and consistency of the measurement procedures used by participating laboratories.

title: Results of a Geochemical Study of Core Samples from Petroleum Source Rock Deposits of Cretaceous and Jurassic Age in the Southwestern Part of the Yenisei–Khatanga Regional Trough
summary: This paper presents the results of a comprehensive geochemical investigation of core material, extracted bitumens, and gas condensates from the southwestern part of the Yenisei–Khatanga Regional Trough (Arctic region). The study aimed to ev
content: This paper presents the results of a comprehensive geochemical investigation of core material, extracted bitumens, and gas condensates from the southwestern part of the Yenisei–Khatanga Regional Trough (Arctic region). The study aimed to evaluate the petroleum source potential of the investigated stratigraphic units, determine the type and thermal maturity of organic matter, and clarify its genetic relationships with hydrocarbons. The research was carried out using total organic carbon (TOC) determination, programmed pyrolysis (Rock-Eval analogue) with analysis of the S1 and S2 parameters, solvent extraction of bitumens, and biomarker analysis by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). The obtained data revealed a wide range of TOC values and significant lithological and geochemical heterogeneity within the studied section. In several samples, elevated S1 values combined with low residual generative potential (S2) were identified, which is interpreted as evidence of advanced thermal transformation of organic matter and the presence of migrated hydrocarbons in certain intervals. Biomarker investigations enabled differentiation of genetic types of organic matter and revealed variations in depositional environments. The results refine current understanding of the petroleum source characteristics of the studied formations and may be applied in the interpretation of hydrocarbon genesis and in further petroleum geological investigations of the region.

This electrolyte flow rate results in a simultaneous improvement of Faradaic efficiency, productivity, and ammonia recovery in the gas phase. Overall, our results highlight the critical influence of cell-architecture-related parameters on Li-NRR and emphasize the need to disentangle device engineering from electrolyte tailoring and electrochemical performance optimisation to enable a rational understanding of the mechanism understanding towards the translation of Li-NRR to a scalable process.

title: Electrolysis without electrodes: thermodynamic and kinetic insights into decoupled alkaline water electrolysis
summary: Conventional water electrolysis is fundamentally limited by the kinetic constraints of coupled electrode reactions, particularly the oxygen evolution reaction, which necessitate substantial overpotentials despite decades of catalyst develop
content: Conventional water electrolysis is fundamentally limited by the kinetic constraints of coupled electrode reactions, particularly the oxygen evolution reaction, which necessitate substantial overpotentials despite decades of catalyst development. Recently, spatially and temporally decoupled electrolysis has emerged as a new paradigm in which electrochemical charge storage and catalytic fuel production are separated. This decoupling enables catalysis beyond the confines of the electrode surface and fundamentally alters how electrons are delivered to the catalyst. Here, we investigate redox-mediated hydrogen evolution in strongly alkaline media, examining the interplay between dissolved redox mediators and heterogeneous hydrogen evolution catalysts. Notably, we demonstrate that separating electron transfer from catalytic hydrogen evolution minimises some of the kinetic penalty associated with the electrode-electrolyte interface, enabling hydrogen evolution at potentials approaching the thermodynamic limit, even on nickel catalysts. Nevertheless, catalyst identity remains critical in determining reaction kinetics. Comparison of platinum and Raney® nickel reveals a prolonged activation period unique to nickel, demonstrating that catalyst surface chemistry continues to govern hydrogen evolution despite the absence of direct electrode-mediated electron transfer. These findings establish decoupled electrolysis as a fundamentally distinct model for investigating the interplay between charge transfer and catalysis, providing new insight into electrocatalytic energy conversion.

title: Optimizing CO2-EOR Strategies in Water-Sensitive Tight Conglomerate Reservoirs: Mechanisms and Field Application
summary: The sustainable development of conglomerate reservoirs in the Junggar Basin is critically constrained by low permeability, high illite content, and severe water sensitivity. Conventional water flooding has proven inefficient, characterized
content: The sustainable development of conglomerate reservoirs in the Junggar Basin is critically constrained by low permeability, high illite content, and severe water sensitivity. Conventional water flooding has proven inefficient, characterized by rapid pressure depletion and suboptimal recovery factors (avg. 5.5%). This study systematically investigates the efficacy of CO2 injection as an alternative Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) mechanism. Through integrated core-flooding experiments and numerical simulations, we evaluated the displacement efficiency of CO2, N2, and CH4. Results demonstrate that CO2 injection yields a superior ultimate recovery factor of 38.39%-substantially outperforming the historical water flooding baseline as well as N2 and CH4. This superiority is primarily due to CO2 effectively extracting light hydrocarbons (contributing 80% to incremental recovery) under high pressure and inducing significant oil swelling and viscosity reduction, significantly outperforming other media due to its ability to extract light hydrocarbons (contributing 80% to incremental recovery) and reduce oil viscosity. Furthermore, numerical optimization identifies horizontal well cyclic huff-and-puff as the optimal deployment strategy for this reservoir class. Field pilots of CO2 pre-pad energized fracturing validated these findings, achieving a 38% enhancement in initial productivity compared to conventional fractured wells. This stimulation effect sustained elevated production rates for approximately 150 days. These results provide a robust technical framework for revitalizing depleted, water-sensitive conglomerate reservoirs.

title: Study on the Erosion Characteristics of Flow-Passage Components in the Jet Mechanism of an Impulse Turbine
summary: Under China’s “Dual Carbon” strategy, which directs hydropower development toward the high-head regions of the southwest, impulse turbines have become the main turbine type for exploiting high-head hydropower resources. During the flood sea
content: Under China’s “Dual Carbon” strategy, which directs hydropower development toward the high-head regions of the southwest, impulse turbines have become the main turbine type for exploiting high-head hydropower resources. During the flood season, the high sediment loads carried by rivers in the southwest cause severe erosion of the jet mechanism, posing a significant threat to the safe and stable operation of the units. Taking a single jet mechanism of a six-nozzle impulse turbine at a hydropower station as the study object, a three-dimensional computational model covering the jet flow region was established. The renormalization group (RNG) k-ε turbulence model, the volume of fluid (VOF) multiphase model, and the Euler–Lagrange discrete phase model (DPM) were combined with the Oka erosion model to systematically investigate the effects of sediment particle diameter, volume fraction, and needle opening on the erosion characteristics of the nozzle and the jet needle. The results show that as the sediment particle diameter increases, the eroded area on the jet needle extends towards the shank, whereas erosion of the nozzle first increases, then drops sharply, and finally recovers gradually. The sediment volume fraction is positively correlated with the erosion rate, and this dependence is approximately exponential rather than linear; under the same operating conditions, the erosion of the jet needle is consistently greater than that of the nozzle. The needle opening is negatively correlated with the total erosion: erosion is most severe at small openings and decreases as the opening increases. When the needle opening increases from 0.23 to 0.63, the maximum erosion rate of the jet needle decreases by about 99.8%. This study identifies the high-erosion-risk regions and the main influencing factors in the jet mechanism of impulse turbines, providing a theoretical basis for the erosion-resistant design of the jet mechanism and for the formulation of operation and maintenance strategies for the units.

title: Coordinated Fault Ride-Through Strategy for Multi-Terminal VSC-HVDC System with Far-Offshore Wind Farms Integration
summary: With offshore wind power evolving toward clusterization in far-offshore areas, voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) technology remains the dominant transmission solution for connecting large-scale far-offsho
content: With offshore wind power evolving toward clusterization in far-offshore areas, voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) technology remains the dominant transmission solution for connecting large-scale far-offshore wind farms to the onshore grid. To mitigate the DC overvoltage risk caused by active power imbalance in VSC-HVDC system integrated with far-offshore wind farms during onshore fault, a coordinated fault ride-through strategy is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the topology and mathematical model of a multi-terminal VSC-HVDC with permanent magnet synchronous generator-based offshore wind turbines (PMSG-OWTs) are established, and its transient behavior under fault condition is analyzed. Secondly, according to the fault voltage magnitude, pre-fault active power of VSC stations, and the number of faulty converter stations, the unbalanced power between sending-end VSC stations and receiving-end VSC stations is quantified. This quantified value is then used in conjunction with the voltage reduction region model to generate appropriate voltage reduction commands for the sending-end VSC stations. By adopting a common-outer-loop voltage reduction control scheme, the sending-end stations collectively and rapidly reduce their output power, thereby eliminating the power imbalance without resorting to additional hardware such as VSC choppers. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively reduces surplus power and suppresses DC overvoltage under onshore fault scenarios, significantly improving the transient resilience of multi-terminal VSC-HVDC system integrated with far-offshore wind farms.

title: Performance Degradation Mechanisms and Mitigation Strategies for PEM Fuel Cell Systems in High-Altitude Environments
summary: As proton exchange membrane fuel cell systems are increasingly considered for transportation and stationary power applications in high-altitude regions, their performance degradation under low-pressure and oxygen-deficient environments has
content: As proton exchange membrane fuel cell systems are increasingly considered for transportation and stationary power applications in high-altitude regions, their performance degradation under low-pressure and oxygen-deficient environments has become a critical barrier to practical deployment. This review summarizes the key mechanisms responsible for PEMFC performance loss under high-altitude conditions, including reduced oxygen partial pressure, aggravated activation and concentration polarization, increased compressor load, and decreased system net power. Recent progress is reviewed from the perspectives of stack materials and components, air supply subsystems, system integration, control strategies, and energy management. Particular attention is given to catalyst-layer design, bipolar plate flow-field optimization, high-pressure-ratio air compressors, turbine-assisted energy recovery, oxygen excess ratio control, and net-power optimization. The analysis indicates that the major technical challenges for high-altitude PEMFC operation are no longer limited to stack materials, but are strongly associated with the coupled optimization of air supply, flow-field design, compressor operating boundaries, and altitude-adaptive control. Future research should therefore focus on integrated material–stack–system testing platforms, long-term field validation, and predictive models that couple degradation mechanisms with system-level control. This review provides a systematic reference for the design and optimization of PEMFC systems for high-altitude applications.
