title: Control-Barrier-Function Shielded Conservative Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Anti-Misoperation AGC of Thermal Power Units
summary: High shares of variable renewable generation increasingly require thermal units to provide deeper, faster, and more frequent automatic generation control (AGC) while operating close to low-load, steam-pressure, ramp-rate, and actuator limit
content: High shares of variable renewable generation increasingly require thermal units to provide deeper, faster, and more frequent automatic generation control (AGC) while operating close to low-load, steam-pressure, ramp-rate, and actuator limits. Under these conditions, an area-level regulation request that is valid for grid balancing can become unsafe at the plant interface because of nonlinear boiler–turbine dynamics, delayed measurements, sensor bias, and compound disturbances. This study therefore formulates AGC from the plant side: an area-level dispatcher allocates regulation among thermal generation, hydro generation, battery storage, and flexible load, while the proposed controller modifies only the command assigned to a 600 MW reheat thermal unit before it enters the plant distributed control system. A control-barrier-function (CBF) shielded conservative distributional reinforcement learning method is developed to prevent excessive ramping, steam-pressure excursions, valve over-actuation, low-load instability, and errors caused by delayed or biased measurements. Every transition used for training, validation, and testing is generated numerically by the declared behavior policy and benchmark generator; no measured AGC record or plant-historian data enter the reported results. Asynchronous signals are causally aligned on a 4 s decision grid, and a dedicated distributional safety-cost critic estimates the 0.95 conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of discounted constraint cost. The nonlinear simulator is additionally cross-checked against the published plant-derived Bell–Åström model at seven operating points. Normalized power-transient NRMSE is 0.021–0.079 with correlation r ≥ 0.995 , while pressure-transient NRMSE is 0.084–0.254 with r = 0.733 –0.970. Ten independent training seeds and 3500 held-out numerical episodes show that the controller reduces cumulative absolute ACE from 218 to 165 MW min and improves the frequency nadir from − 0.073 to − 0.041 Hz relative to PI AGC. No hard violation occurs in 525,000 feasible test decisions, giving a one-sided 95% binomial upper bound of 0.00057% on the per-decision violation probability. The safety statement remains conditional on the declared plant model, uncertainty set, robust control-invariant subset, and bounded prediction errors. End-to-end CPU execution requires 6.8 ms on average and 9.6 ms at the 95th percentile.

title: Land cover transformations in northern Algeria from 2001 to 2021: A MODIS-based spatiotemporal analysis
summary: Land use/land cover (LULC) changes in northern Algeria from 2001 to 2021 were investigated in this research. The assessment utilized the MODIS MCD12Q1 dataset combined with Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques. Substantial landsca
content: Land use/land cover (LULC) changes in northern Algeria from 2001 to 2021 were investigated in this research. The assessment utilized the MODIS MCD12Q1 dataset combined with Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques. Substantial landscape transformations were highlighted by the findings. Forests (+47.52%), shrublands (+17.65%), wetlands (+58.64%), and natural vegetation (+465.72%) experienced notable growth, whereas a drop of −14.13% was documented for barren lands by the end of study period. Moderate overall growth was displayed by agricultural lands, despite various fluctuations throughout the timeline. Concurrently, a continuous expansion (+3.90%) driven by escalating anthropogenic pressure was recorded in urban and built-up areas. Regional landscape evolution is clearly shaped by a combination of factors. Climatic variability, ecological succession, land management practices, and human activities collectively drive these observed dynamics. Partial alignment with previously documented vegetation recovery and urban expansion trends in Algeria was demonstrated by comparative literature reviews. However, the moderate spatial resolution (500 m) of the MODIS MCD12Q1 product likely caused several identified data discrepancies. Ultimately, the immense value of remote sensing and GIS approaches for regional environmental monitoring is proven by this project. Achieving better classification accuracy in heterogeneous Mediterranean environments, however, strictly necessitates the use of higher-resolution datasets.

title: MnO2/Co3O4 COMPOSITE ELECTRODES FOR POTENTIAL SUPERCAPACITOR APPLICATIONS
summary: As the global energy landscape shifts toward more sustainable and high-performance storage solutions, the development of next-generation supercapacitor electrodes has become increasingly critical. Addressing this demand, we developed a stra
content: As the global energy landscape shifts toward more sustainable and high-performance storage solutions, the development of next-generation supercapacitor electrodes has become increasingly critical. Addressing this demand, we developed a straightforward chemical co-precipitation method to synthesize manganese dioxide (MnO2) and cobalt oxide (Co3O4), incorporating a conductive carbon framework as a potential electrode material for supercapacitors. The resulting mixture was further combined with poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) and deposited onto a nickel foam/graphene monolayer substrate to fabricate test electrodes. This method bypasses the complexity of multi-step fabrication and post-processing, offering a streamlined, scalable approach to building multifunctional hybrid electrodes. The resulting composite exhibits rapid ion transport and enhanced charge storage, while Energy-Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the successful incorporation of Mn and Co elements. Furthermore, X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns indicated that the composite possesses an amorphous structure. Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) and Galvanic Charge/Discharge (GCD) measurements revealed excellent long-term cycling stability, indicating the viability of the fabricated composite for potential supercapacitor applications. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) was also performed to evaluate the internal resistance and charge-transfer properties, providing complementary insight into the electrode’s electrochemical behavior.

title: PREPARATION, SPECTRAL CHARACTERIZATION, MOLECULAR DOCKING, ANDANTIOXIDANT ACTIVITY OF NEW SYMMETRICAL DIMERS DERIVATIVES OFOXAZEPINE STARTING FROM PYRIDINE-5,7-DIONE ANHYDRIDE
summary: This study reports the synthesis of a series of oxazepine derivatives via a condensation reaction between amines and various benzaldehyde derivatives, using benzene as the solvent. The resulting intermediates were subsequently reacted with
content: This study reports the synthesis of a series of oxazepine derivatives via a condensation reaction between amines and various benzaldehyde derivatives, using benzene as the solvent. The resulting intermediates were subsequently reacted with pyridine-5,7-dione anhydride in dry benzene to afford oxazepine derivatives (H1–H6). The synthesized compounds were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance (¹H-NMR) spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry. Reaction progress was monitored using thin-layer chromatography (TLC). The antioxidant activity of compounds H1–H6 was evaluated and compared with that of vitamin C. In addition, molecular docking studies were performed for selected compounds (H1, H4, and H6) against tyrosinase (PDB ID: 3NM8) to identify optimal binding sites and evaluate interactions with neighboring residues. The docked complexes exhibited RMSD values of 1.16, 1.40, and 1.30 Å for H1, H4, and H6, respectively. Among the tested compounds, H4 showed the highest binding affinity, in good agreement with the experimental results. Overall, the synthesized oxazepine derivatives demonstrated moderate antioxidant activity, warranting further in vivo investigation.

title: ELECTROCHEMICAL SYNTHESIS OF NANOMAGNETITE MODIFIED WITH BIOCOMPATIBLE SURFACTANTS
summary: Magnetic nanoparticles are currently gaining significant attraction in various fields, including modern engineering and ecology, particularly in biomedical, therapeutic, and diagnostic technologies. An environmentally friendly electrochemic
content: Magnetic nanoparticles are currently gaining significant attraction in various fields, including modern engineering and ecology, particularly in biomedical, therapeutic, and diagnostic technologies. An environmentally friendly electrochemical synthesis method was used to produce magnetic nanoparticles. Iron sulfate was dissolved in a mixture of water-ethanol, while polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) was used to enhance the biocompatibility of the magnetite nanoparticles. Particle size in a sol obtained with 1 vol% PVP, at a current density of 20-60 A/dm2, and at varying water and ethanol ratios, was measured using the dynamic light scattering (DLS) method transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Zeta potential was measured to determine the stability of the magnetite sol. In the presence of PVP, the best results (12-18 nm) were obtained with water/ethanol ratios of 50/50 and 60/40 vol.%. Magnetite nanoparticles were characterized using a Zetasizer Malvern instrument, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and thermogravimetric analysis.

title: EVALUATION OF CALCIUM AMMONIUM NITRATE MODIFIED WITH POTASSIUM CHLORIDE: APPLICATION AND CONSUMER PROPERTIES
summary: Potassium-calcium-ammonium nitrate samples were obtained by varying the amounts of dolomite mineral (DM) and potassium chloride (KCl) from 0.5 to 25 g per 100 g of ammonium nitrate (AN) melt. The carbonate-chloride-nitrate melt was granulat
content: Potassium-calcium-ammonium nitrate samples were obtained by varying the amounts of dolomite mineral (DM) and potassium chloride (KCl) from 0.5 to 25 g per 100 g of ammonium nitrate (AN) melt. The carbonate-chloride-nitrate melt was granulated by the prilling method. At 170 °C, the nitrate melt activated the dolomite mineral, converting CaO and MgO into plant-available forms. The simultaneous addition of DM and KCl significantly improved the mechanical strength of the fertilizer granules while reducing caking, porosity, and diesel fuel absorbency by a factor of 2–3 compared with AN granules containing magnesite. The optimal composition (AN:DM:KCl=100:12:12) was characterized by EDS, SEM, and DTA analyses, which confirmed its favorable structural and physicochemical properties. These findings demonstrate the potential of NKCaMg as a mechanically stable and agronomically effective fertilizer formulation.

title: COMMERCIAL MESOPOROUS ZEOLITE-SUPPORTED TITANIUM OXIDE FOR THEPHOTOCATALYTIC DEGRADATION OF PHARMACEUTICAL POLLUTANTS
summary: The current research aims to evaluate the photocatalytic activity of (TiO2) with various loading ratios (5%-60%) supported on mesoporous aluminosilicate (zeolite type) called Siral, with aluminum content ranging from 20% to 70%, to enhance
content: The current research aims to evaluate the photocatalytic activity of (TiO2) with various loading ratios (5%-60%) supported on mesoporous aluminosilicate (zeolite type) called Siral, with aluminum content ranging from 20% to 70%, to enhance the performance of degradation of ibuprofen (IBP) as a pharmaceutical pollutant. The batch reactor is furnished with solarium light to simulate sunlight UV for efficient degradation. The supported substance (Siral) exhibits elevated surface area and a regular mesoporous structure; hence, it might be regarded as an efficient photocatalyst support. The characterizations and effectiveness of the prepared catalyst were achieved by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and UV-visible spectroscopy. The results exhibit the highest photo-degradation ratio (90%) for (60% TiO2/Siral40) after 4 hours. The highest surface area is 448.3685 m²/g for 15% TiO₂/Siral40. The photodegradation efficiency increases as the weight percentage of TiO2 particles rises from 5 to 60 %. TiO2/Siral NCs photocatalysts demonstrate remarkable photostability and reusability, especially in organic molecule degradation.

title: A THEORETICAL INVESTIGATION OF NITROBENZENE HYDROGENATION: GASPHASE, SOLVENT EFFECTS, AND Pd CATALYSIS
summary: This study presents a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation into the stepwise reduction of nitrobenzene to aniline via nitroso and hydroxylamine intermediates. Two mechanistic pathways were explored: a non-catalyzed ro
content: This study presents a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation into the stepwise reduction of nitrobenzene to aniline via nitroso and hydroxylamine intermediates. Two mechanistic pathways were explored: a non-catalyzed route in both gas and ethanol phases and a surface-catalyzed route facilitated by a palladium (Pd) catalyst. Geometry optimizations, thermodynamic parameters, frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analysis, and vibrational frequency (IR) simulations were carried out for all key species involved: nitrobenzene (Ph-NO₂), nitrosobenzene (Ph-NO), phenylhydroxylamine (Ph-NHOH), and aniline (Ph-NH₂). A comparison of gas-phase and solvent-phase geometries revealed solvent-induced elongation of N–O and N–H bonds, particularly in polar intermediates, consistent with ethanol’s stabilizing effect. FMO analysis showed a notable decrease in HOMO–LUMO energy gaps in the solvent phase, indicating enhanced reactivity. IR spectra further supported these findings, with observable shifts in characteristic stretching frequencies upon solvation. In the Pd-catalyzed pathway, adsorption of reactants and intermediates on the Pd surface significantly altered molecular geometries and lowered reaction energy barriers. Calculated adsorption energies and bond elongations suggest strong Pd–O and Pd–N interactions that facilitate bond activation. The overall energy profile indicates a smoother and more favorable reduction pathway on the Pd surface compared to the noncatalyzed routes. These results provide mechanistic insight into the catalytic role of Pd in hydrogenation reactions and highlight the importance of solvent effects in modulating electronic and structural properties. This comparative approach enhances our understanding of nitroarene reductions and offers valuable guidance for catalyst design and process optimization.

title: ONE-STEP ELECTROGENERATED MANGANESE OXIDE/CARBON COMPOSITE ASPOTENTIAL ELECTRODE MATERIAL FOR PSEUDO-SUPERCAPACITORS
summary: The increasing demand for energy worldwide has led to the development of supercapacitors, which are energy storage devices known for their high-power density, quick charging and discharging capabilities, large capacity, long lifespan, and e
content: The increasing demand for energy worldwide has led to the development of supercapacitors, which are energy storage devices known for their high-power density, quick charging and discharging capabilities, large capacity, long lifespan, and environmental benefits. Here, we discuss the method for synthesizing manganese oxide/carbon composite materials through a one-step electrolysis process for potential application as supercapacitive electrode materials. The deposition of manganese oxide on graphite, together with the exfoliation of carbon flakes from the graphite electrodes induced by gas evolution during water electrolysis, led to the electrogeneration of a manganese oxide–carbon composite powder. After investigation of physical properties, the powder of manganese oxides/carbon composite was coated onto planar indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. Evaluation of the electrochemical performance and charge storage capacity revealed that ITO electrodes modified with the electrogenerated composite exhibited superior electrochemical performance compared with those modified only with a physical mixture of manganese oxide and carbon nanotubes.

title: Advancements and Optimization Strategies for Hybrid Photovoltaic–Diesel–Battery Systems in Remote and Off-Grid Applications: A Narrative Review
summary: Hybrid photovoltaic (PV)–diesel–battery systems are an important option for remote and off-grid electrification, where diesel generation remains common despite high fuel costs, emissions, and logistical constraints. This structured narrativ
content: Hybrid photovoltaic (PV)–diesel–battery systems are an important option for remote and off-grid electrification, where diesel generation remains common despite high fuel costs, emissions, and logistical constraints. This structured narrative review synthesizes developments in system architecture, DC–DC converter topology, energy management, communication, and techno-economic optimization. The reviewed evidence indicates that integrating PV generation and battery storage can reduce diesel operation, improve autonomy, and lower lifecycle costs when components and dispatch strategies are matched to local conditions. In one representative study, total modeled pollutant emissions decreased from 15,922 kg/year for a diesel-only system to 606.9 kg/year for a PV–diesel–battery system, a reduction of approximately 96%. Remaining barriers include capital cost, battery degradation, application-layer interoperability, cybersecurity, and limited field validation of advanced artificial-intelligence-based control. The synthesis also shows that published cost of energy, net present cost, and renewable-fraction values should not be compared without accounting for location, load, fuel price, component cost, discount rate, and reliability assumptions.

title: Comparing electro- and thermo-catalytic ammonia decomposition, a crucial component in the green ammonia value chain as an H 2 vector
summary: -permeable membrane into the thermocatalytic route allows a substantial reduction in operating temperature while preserving catalytic performance. The Ru catalyst performs better than the others in both thermo- and electrocatalysis, but for
content: -permeable membrane into the thermocatalytic route allows a substantial reduction in operating temperature while preserving catalytic performance. The Ru catalyst performs better than the others in both thermo- and electrocatalysis, but for different mechanistic reasons. In particular, the behavior in electrocatalysis is determined by its superior ability to promote both anodic water electrolysis and ammonia electrolysis. However, Ru also has other limitations to consider when used as the preferred metal choice.

title: Horizontal-plane pendulum-based inertial wave energy harvester with sprag-clutch rectification for unmanned surface vehicles
summary: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) increasingly support long-duration ocean observation, yet their mission endurance remains constrained by limited onboard energy storage. Wave energy offers a continuous, weather-independent supply, although
content: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) increasingly support long-duration ocean observation, yet their mission endurance remains constrained by limited onboard energy storage. Wave energy offers a continuous, weather-independent supply, although most pendulum-based harvesters respond to only a single motion axis. This study presents a horizontal-plane pendulum-based inertial wave energy harvester integrated within the USV hull, with the pendulum configured parallel to the XY-plane to simultaneously exploit pitch and roll excitation. A sprag-clutch mechanical rotation rectifier (MRR), a three-stage planetary gearbox, a hypoid stage, and a Halbach-array permanent magnet generator are used to convert the irregular, bidirectional motion of the pendulum into stable, unidirectional electrical output. A Lagrangian-based dynamic model, partitioned into torque-transmitting and freewheeling states, was developed and validated against motion-platform experiments under sinusoidal, swept-frequency, and JONSWAP irregular-wave excitation. The system delivers 13.0 W under matched-load conditions (f = 0.51 Hz, Φ₀ = 15°), exhibits a monotonic increase in output across the principal ocean-wave band (0.10-0.70 Hz), reaches 91 W at Φ₀ = 30°, and yields a fourfold power gain over single-axis operation under in-phase pitch-roll excitation. Under JONSWAP excitation (Hₛ = 1.5 m, Tₚ = 7 s), the mean experimental output is 7.21 W, corresponding to a motion-to-electric conversion efficiency of approximately 43 % under matched-load conditions.

title: Benchmarking electronic-structure methods for nonadiabatic dynamics in a propeller-shaped molecular rotor: insights into conical intersections
summary: emerges as the dominant decay channel. MRSF-TD-CAM-B3LYP dynamics yield three outcomes: reformation of the initial geometry, formation of a diradical intermediate, and production of the bicyclic photoproduct, reflecting its bifurcating topo
content: emerges as the dominant decay channel. MRSF-TD-CAM-B3LYP dynamics yield three outcomes: reformation of the initial geometry, formation of a diradical intermediate, and production of the bicyclic photoproduct, reflecting its bifurcating topology and more reliable ground-state description relative to LR-TDDFT. A systematic analysis of exchange-correlation functional dependence within MRSF-TDDFT reveals strong consistency across functionals, with only minor deviations such as the borderline single-path behaviour of BHHLYP and DTCAM-AEE. These findings raise important questions about the reliability, limitations, and future development of black-box excited-state methods for modelling photochemical decay in molecular rotors.

title: Finite-Element Assessment of Concrete Mine-Shaft Lining: Lamé Validation and Groove Effects
summary: This paper presents a Lamé-verified finite-element workflow for assessing the stress–strain state and residual load-bearing capacity of concrete linings in vertical mine shafts with local technological grooves. A full three-dimensional 1 m
content: This paper presents a Lamé-verified finite-element workflow for assessing the stress–strain state and residual load-bearing capacity of concrete linings in vertical mine shafts with local technological grooves. A full three-dimensional 1 m high lining ring with an internal diameter of 6 m was modeled in Abaqus and verified against the analytical Lamé solution for a thick-walled cylinder under external pressure. Four scenarios were analyzed: an elastic intact reference model, an elastic model with an inner technological recess, a zonal concrete damage-plasticity model (CDPM2) without groove, and a zonal CDPM2 model with groove. The radial and hoop stress profiles closely matched the analytical solution. The groove caused pronounced stress redistribution, including a tensile hoop-stress concentration of approximately 24 MPa on the outer side of the lining opposite the groove and inner-contour ovalization with radial displacement from −9.0 to +7.4 mm. A parametric post-processing campaign evaluated groove depth, groove radius/opening, mesh density, concrete class, and zonal material assumptions using the normalized residual-capacity indicator R_FE. Groove depth governed the global residual-capacity trend, whereas groove radius/opening acted as a secondary geometric modifier. The Abaqus internal energy output (ALLIE) and dissipated/stabilization energy output (ALLSD) are interpreted as comparative energy indicators, not standalone failure criteria. The workflow connects finite-element assessment with field diagnostics while acknowledging limitations related to local peak-stress convergence, low-pressure proxy interpretation, and the adopted CDPM2 parameterization.

title: Analysis the Characteristics and Performance of Polyethersulfone-Carbon Nanotube Membranes Fabricated Using Electric Field Method for Water Filtration Applications
summary: This study aims to address the effect of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) addition on the characteristics and performance of polyethersulfone (PES) membranes fabricated using the Electric Field method. Four PES membranes were fabricated with addition
content: This study aims to address the effect of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) addition on the characteristics and performance of polyethersulfone (PES) membranes fabricated using the Electric Field method. Four PES membranes were fabricated with addition of CNT and denoted as SM0 (0% CNT), SM1 (0.5% CNT), SM2 (1% CNT), and SM3 (1.5% CNT). SEM observations showed average pore sizes of 0.62±0.12 μm to 0.82±0.18 μm, and AFM images showed the ability of CNTs to increase topographical complexity. The tensile test results indicated that addition of CNT increased the tensile strength of the membrane. The TGA and DTG test graphs showed that addition of CNT can increase the thermal resistance of the membrane. FTIR spectra were in agreement with characteristic PES functional groups. The XRD data showed that the amorphous nature remains dominant, indicating that this composite membrane successfully combines the mechanical strength and functional properties of CNTs without sacrificing the intrinsic pore structure of the PES polymer. Addition of CNT to the membrane increased its hydrophilicity, as evidenced by decrease in water contact angle on the membrane. Addition of CNT can also increase the membrane permeability, as indicated by an increase in the membrane permeability values in the range of 1 to 6 bar. In terms of durability, adding CNT to the membrane can increase its durability, meaning that membranes with added CNT can last longer than pure PES membranes.

title: Optimizing Cooling Mode Switchovers in Green Data Centers via a SC Metric and TRNSYS-PSO Simulation
summary: Driven by the demand for green and efficient data center cooling, this study develops a rack-level rear-door heat pipe (RDHP) cooling system and proposes a comprehensive metric SC by integrating Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Water Usage
content: Driven by the demand for green and efficient data center cooling, this study develops a rack-level rear-door heat pipe (RDHP) cooling system and proposes a comprehensive metric SC by integrating Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), and scoring components from the Chinese green data center standard GB/T 44989-2024. Optimizing the switchover between free, hybrid, and mechanical cooling modes is critical for improving the energy efficiency and reducing the carbon footprint of data centers. A delimiting temperature (Tdelimit) of 17°C was established to optimally balance enhanced free cooling utilization with operational safety, ensuring server inlet temperatures remained within the limits. The switchover temperatures were optimized for four climatically diverse Chinese cities using TRNSYS simulations coupled with the GenOpt tool and a Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. Results show that SC-oriented optimization effectively prolongs free cooling duration, reduces PUE, WUE, and CUE simultaneously, and outperforms empirical temperature settings. Also, the SC metric presents higher sensitivity than single indicators, while its optimization remains stable under varying grid carbon emission factors. This work provides a valuable methodology and a practical tool for advancing the green and low-carbon transformation of data centers, offering significant implications for policy-making and sustainable infrastructure planning.

title: Leveraging co-operative redox enhancement (CORE) for efficient electrochemical production
summary: The shift from traditional fossil-fuel-based chemical production to a renewable e-chemical industry requires innovation in the design of catalytic and electrocatalytic systems for both initial production of platform hydrocarbons and their s
content: The shift from traditional fossil-fuel-based chemical production to a renewable e-chemical industry requires innovation in the design of catalytic and electrocatalytic systems for both initial production of platform hydrocarbons and their subsequent upgrading to a core suite of feedstocks and chemical intermediates. To this end, we require selective and efficient catalytic systems that operate under relatively mild conditions. We have recently developed a new approach, termed Co-Operative Redox Enhancement (CORE), to the design of catalytic systems that leverage electrocatalytic driving forces to substantially enhance the activity of what, at first glance, would be considered a thermal catalytic process. Dissimilar, physically separated but electrochemically connected catalytic nanoparticles will establish a spontaneous, nanoscale, electrochemical gradient between them due to differences in the electrocatalytic selectivity of each particle towards the desired half reactions. This leads to polarization of the nanoparticles and associated enhancement in their selectivity and activity towards the half reactions, driving an overall increase in catalytic turnover. The extent of polarization is quantifiable and the impact on overall catalytic turnover is predictable through an electrochemical approach based on modified corrosion theory. This new approach to the design of catalytic systems has wide-ranging implications for the design of thermal and electrocatalytic systems for the e-chemical industry and beyond. In this work, we discuss the oxidative dehydrogenation of benzyl alcohol utilizing coupled Au/C and Pd/C catalysts as an exemplar of CORE. The role of CORE is demonstrated through a combination of thermocatalytic and electrocatalytic experiments, pointing towards CORE as an approach to design and implement both thermal and electrochemical catalytic systems for efficient e-chemical production.

title: Effects of wind-wave misalignment on motion responses of a floating wind turbine with a shared-anchor mooring system
summary: Wind-wave misalignment significantly affects the dynamic responses of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs). A fully coupled aero-hydro-mooring numerical model was established in OrcaFlex for a FOWT with a three-line shared-anchor mooring
content: Wind-wave misalignment significantly affects the dynamic responses of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs). A fully coupled aero-hydro-mooring numerical model was established in OrcaFlex for a FOWT with a three-line shared-anchor mooring system. The numerical analysis evaluated three representative sea states (LC1, LC2, and LC3) alongside multiple wind-wave heading combinations. The six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) motion responses of the floating platform were systematically investigated using motion trajectories, kernel density estimation (KDE), violin plots, and probabilistic statistical analyses. The results indicated that: (1) the motion responses of the floating platform were jointly governed by the sea state and wind-wave heading. The sea state primarily determined the response intensity and variability, whereas the wind-wave heading governed the motion pattern. Increasing wind-wave misalignment angle shifted platform motion from unidirectional response to multidirectionally coupled motions. This shift led to increasingly dispersed probability distributions. (2) Different motion degrees of freedom exhibited distinct environmental sensitivities. Roll and pitch were primarily controlled by the wind direction, whereas relative wind-wave heading dictated yaw sensitivity. Increasing sea-state severity significantly amplified motion responses without altering their directional response characteristics. (3) Variations in platform motions altered shared-anchor loading characteristics. Higher wind-wave misalignment shifted shared-anchor loads from unidirectional to multidirectional distributions. Consequently, mooring lines underwent continuous load redistribution. These findings clarified the coupled effects of wind-wave misalignment on floating platform motions and shared-anchor loading. This work provides theoretical guidance for designing and assessing shared mooring systems in FOWTs.

title: Technological Assurance of the Quality of Slide Bearing Shells Based on Two-Stage Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
summary: The article describes the methodology of a two-stage finishing process for slide bearing shells made of bronze. The goal of the first finishing stage was to form a base roughness profile with uniform values of the controlled parameters. Bas
content: The article describes the methodology of a two-stage finishing process for slide bearing shells made of bronze. The goal of the first finishing stage was to form a base roughness profile with uniform values of the controlled parameters. Based on the results of the first stage, regression equations were derived. These equations make it possible to evaluate the effectiveness of the influence of the process variable factors (tool rotational speed, feed rate, processing time, and workpiece diameter values) of magnetic abrasive finishing on the value of the controlled parameters. The results showed that the parameters of tool rotational speed and processing time have the greatest influence. In the second stage of the experimental research, a two-factor experiment (varying the time and abrasive grain sizes) was conducted. The aim of this stage was to test the possibility of applying oil-retaining grooves onto the formed profile. The results showed that the most noticeable grooves are formed at a processing time of 6 minutes and an abrasive grain size of 350 μm. The roughness parameters did not increase significantly compared to the values after the first processing stage. The need for further research to evaluate the operational characteristics of the machined workpieces during wear testing is established.

title: Biomechanical and Tensile Performance of Full-Body Swimsuits: Effects of Fabric-Seam Interactions in High-Stress Areas
summary: Designing a full-body swimsuit incorporates unique biomechanical considerations. This research aimed to investigate quantitatively and qualitatively the influence of fabric type and seam construction on the tensile performance of full-body
content: Designing a full-body swimsuit incorporates unique biomechanical considerations. This research aimed to investigate quantitatively and qualitatively the influence of fabric type and seam construction on the tensile performance of full-body swimsuits in high-stress areas. Two commercially available weft-knitted swimsuit fabrics were employed, nylon6-Lycra and polyester-Lycra blends. Two seam configurations, lapped and superimposed, were created utilizing stitch classes 406 and 504, respectively. The extension of the full-body swimsuit at the shoulder and thigh regions was quantified using a conductive yarn sensor consisting of 80% stainless steel fibers linked to an electrical circuit. Tests simulated arm and leg motions of the front crawl stroke to measure the sensor's electrical response during movement. In parallel, qualitative assessments were conducted by three female athletes through descriptive feedback on comfort and ratings on a 1-5 scale. Results showed that fabric type and seam construction significantly affected the sensor's output voltage. Higher voltage responses were observed for nylon6-Lycra fabric and superimposed seam, indicating greater resistance to motion, whereas lower responses were found for polyester-Lycra and lapped seam. The polyester-Lycra fabric provided enhanced comfort due to its lower resistance to elongation. Lapped seams reduced sensor response and improved swimmer comfort. The findings demonstrate that fabric type and seam construction influence swimsuit extension and comfort, ultimately affecting swimmer performance.

title: Improving Safety in Coal Mining Operations by Monitoring Radiation Environment
summary: Radiation safety remains an important concern in mining because coal and associated host rocks may contain naturally occurring radionuclides that contribute to radon accumulation in underground workings. This study investigates the radiatio
content: Radiation safety remains an important concern in mining because coal and associated host rocks may contain naturally occurring radionuclides that contribute to radon accumulation in underground workings. This study investigates the radiation environment of two operating coal mines in the Kuznetsk Coal Basin (Kuzbass) using field measurements and laboratory analyses. The results revealed a direct relationship between the radionuclide composition of coal and host rocks and radon activity concentration in the mine atmosphere. The investigated mines exhibited distinct radiogeochemical characteristics, which were reflected in differences in radon levels. The results further demonstrated that adequate ventilation can effectively limit radon accumulation, even where radionuclide activity in the surrounding rock mass is elevated. Based on the established relationship between radionuclide content and radon release, a monitoring and forecasting approach is proposed to identify areas requiring enhanced radiation control and to support the determination of appropriate ventilation requirements. Effective radiation protection should integrate systematic radon monitoring, assessment of radon progeny associated with deposited coal dust, and appropriate ventilation and dust-control measures. The proposed approach may also support regional radon-hazard mapping using spectrometric data from exploration cores and facilitate radiation-informed ventilation design, thereby improving the identification and management of potential occupational radon exposure in underground coal mines.

title: A New Group Decision-Making Framework for Multi-Objective Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem Under Interval-Valued Fuzzy Uncertainty
summary: The present study proposes a new comprehensive three-stage framework for solving the Multi-Objective Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (MO-RCPSP) under uncertainty. Addressing limitations in traditional scheduling models, the
content: The present study proposes a new comprehensive three-stage framework for solving the Multi-Objective Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (MO-RCPSP) under uncertainty. Addressing limitations in traditional scheduling models, the proposed framework integrates multi-skill and multi-mode resource allocation, time-cost-quality trade-offs, and buffer management. In the initial stage, a new Interval-Valued Fuzzy (IVF) Projection method is developed to incorporate expert opinion into multi-criteria decision-making. The second stage formulates an MO-RCPSP model using an extended goal programming approach, incorporating IVF parameters and buffer sizing based on the cut-and-paste method. The final stage introduces a buffer monitoring system to track project execution and enable real-time control. A numerical example, in the context of an IT integration project demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enhancing scheduling performance, improving cost efficiency, and increasing schedule flexibility. Sensitivity analysis confirms the model’s adaptability to changes in resource availability and budget constraints, highlighting its practical relevance for managing complex projects under uncertainty.

title: Dynamic gas-electric energy network construction and joint economic low-carbon dispatch optimization for hybrid ships
summary: To address the time-scale mismatch between gas network dynamics (minutes to hours) and power grid response (milliseconds) in hybrid ships, which renders steady-state gas network models overly conservative under propulsion load fluctuations
content: To address the time-scale mismatch between gas network dynamics (minutes to hours) and power grid response (milliseconds) in hybrid ships, which renders steady-state gas network models overly conservative under propulsion load fluctuations and limits gas-fired unit output, this paper proposes a dynamic gas network model via time-frequency transformation and a joint economic low-carbon dispatch framework. First, gas pipeline PDEs are reduced to frequency-domain algebraic equations, forming a dynamic circuit model with gas resistance, inductance, capacitance, and pressure sources. On a 4-node network, the method achieves a computational speedup of 4.6× over FDM (9.89 s) and 3.7× over FEM (7.9 s), with a runtime of 2.14 s (8 iterations) and mean absolute errors of 10⁻⁴, enabling fast dynamic power flow calculation. Second, the ε-constraint method solves the economic-carbon Pareto front, and a gas-electric closed-loop tightening mechanism yields a two-stage "rigid constraint-flexible regulation" strategy. Results show that applying dynamic constraints reduces gas-fired output by 6.7 % while increasing diesel output by 8.2-10.9 %, cutting total cost by 0.4 % at the expense of a 1.65 % emission increase - reflecting the inherent economic-environmental trade-off. Compared with the steady-state model, the dynamic model increases gas-fired generation share by 3.89 %, lowers cost by 0.13%, cuts emissions by 1.59 %, reduces gas-fired power fluctuation by 13.6-19.8 %, and decreases node pressure and flow fluctuations by approximately 72 % and 19-26 %, respectively, significantly enhancing operational stability and safety. The computation time of 55.7 s (5.65× that of the steady-state model) remains acceptable for day-ahead dispatch, and the method's robustness is confirmed by comprehensive sensitivity analyses. This work provides theoretical and technical support for economic low-carbon operation of hybrid ship gas-electric systems.

title: Dietary Isoflavonoids and Brain Tumors: Unlocking Neuroprotective Potential, Molecular Mechanisms, and Novel Therapeutic Avenues in Neuro-Oncology
summary: Brain tumours, particularly Glioblastoma (GBM), remain among the most aggressive malignancies because of profound molecular heterogeneity, Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)-restricted drug delivery, therapeutic resistance, and an immunosuppressive
content: Brain tumours, particularly Glioblastoma (GBM), remain among the most aggressive malignancies because of profound molecular heterogeneity, Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)-restricted drug delivery, therapeutic resistance, and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Naturally occurring dietary isoflavonoids, including genistein, daidzein, biochanin A, formononetin, glycitein, and the metabolite equol, have emerged as promising multitarget phytochemicals with potential applications in neuro-oncology. This review comprehensively summarises current evidence regarding the molecular mechanisms, pharmacokinetic characteristics, preclinical efficacy, translational advances, and emerging therapeutic applications of dietary isoflavonoids in brain tumour prevention and treatment, with particular emphasis on glioblastoma. A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science to identify English-language studies published between 2000 and 2025. Experimental investigations, clinical studies, systematic reviews, and relevant regulatory reports were critically evaluated. Evidence was synthesised to examine BBB transport, epigenetic regulation, oxidative stress modulation, apoptosis, angiogenesis, immune remodeling, anti-invasive mechanisms, nanotechnology-based drug delivery, and combination therapeutic strategies. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that dietary isoflavonoids regulate multiple oncogenic pathways by inhibiting DNA methyltransferases, suppressing PI3K/Akt, NF-κB, STAT3, and VEGF signalling, promoting mitochondrial apoptosis, reversing epithelial-mesenchymal transition, reducing matrix metalloproteinase activity, and enhancing antitumor immune responses through macrophage polarisation and PD-L1 modulation. Nanocarrier formulations substantially improve BBB penetration, bioavailability, and therapeutic efficacy while enhancing sensitivity to temozolomide and radiotherapy. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains constrained by metabolic variability, limited oral bioavailability, gut microbiota-dependent equol production, and sex-related pharmacokinetic differences. Dietary isoflavonoids represent promising multitarget adjunctive agents for precision neuro-oncology by simultaneously targeting tumour cells, the BBB, and the tumour microenvironment. Future well-designed clinical trials integrating biomarker-guided patient selection, nanomedicine platforms, microbiome-based interventions, and personalized pharmacokinetic optimisation are essential to establish their clinical value in brain tumour management.

title: Baseline of the energy management system for an agrivoltaic complex in the Yaqui Valley
source: Revista Facultad de Ingeniería Universidad de Antioquia
summary: This article presents the development of an energy baseline for an agrivoltaicsystem located in the Yaqui Valley, Sonora, Mexico, in accordance with ISO 50001:2018.The baseline was established by quantifying electricity and fuel consumption
content: This article presents the development of an energy baseline for an agrivoltaicsystem located in the Yaqui Valley, Sonora, Mexico, in accordance with ISO 50001:2018.The baseline was established by quantifying electricity and fuel consumption (gasolineand diesel) associated with agricultural activities, including irrigation, planting, andharvesting. Energy data were analyzed by two-month periods, and a linear regressionmodel was applied to the months with the highest activity, excluding low-consumptionperiods to avoid distortion. The consumption analysis was performed by dividing thetotal energy consumption during the corresponding period by the number of hectaresharvested. The results revealed that fuel use accounts for a significant share oftotal energy consumption, underscoring the need to evaluate all energy sources.The resulting baseline model enables disaggregation of fixed and variable loads andserves as a valuable tool for performance monitoring, energy audits, and continuousimprovement strategies. This baseline can be used as a reference for future energymanagement initiatives in similar agricultural settings.

title: A Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis on the Impacts of Different Materials, Thicknesses and Rotation Speeds on the Performance of a Parabolic Trough Solar Collector
summary: The aim of this study is to develop a dynamic numerical model for a parabolic trough solar collector with a rotating absorber tube and to systematically investigate the combined effects of rotation speed, tube material, and wall thickness o
content: The aim of this study is to develop a dynamic numerical model for a parabolic trough solar collector with a rotating absorber tube and to systematically investigate the combined effects of rotation speed, tube material, and wall thickness on its thermal performance. The main novelty is in the simultaneous investigation of three key design parameters—rotation speed (10 and 15 rad/s), absorber tube material (copper, brass, and nickel), and wall thickness (1.45, 1.65, and 1.85 mm)—which have not been studied collectively in previous literature. The simulations are analyzed by ANSYS. Because the non-uniform heat flux is not available in the ANSYS software, a user defined function (UDF) subroutine code for applying non-uniform heat flux is programmed. Results show that the rotation of the pipe has a major effect on the layers close to the wall, while the middle layers of the fluid are not influenced. Moreover, it is proven that as the fluid distance from the inlet increases, the rotational speed and consequently the maximum fluid velocity increase. This shows that the fluid gradually approaches its limiting velocity and that there is no significant change in the average velocity of the fluid inside the pipe as the pipe length increases. Besides, as the fluid progresses along the pipe, the rate of increase in its temperature gradually decreases and the fluid reaches a state close to a steady temperature. Finally, it is proven that among material alloys used, the copper tube has the best performance for heat penetration and creates the highest maximum temperature in the fluid.

title: An Engineering Case Study on Vortex-pressure Linkage in Clearance Flow and the Induced Abnormal Vibration of a High-head Pump-turbine
summary: Abnormal head-cover vibration is a persistent problem in high-head pump-turbines. A hydropower station in China installed crown bosses on the runner crown to mitigate such vibration. Field tests showed that the vibration intensified after t
content: Abnormal head-cover vibration is a persistent problem in high-head pump-turbines. A hydropower station in China installed crown bosses on the runner crown to mitigate such vibration. Field tests showed that the vibration intensified after the modification. This study combines SST-DES simulations with field tests to trace the full mechanism chain from the boss geometry through vortex dynamics and pressure spectrum reconstruction to the vibration response. The 26.6-degree boss turning angle reshapes the pressure spectrum in two opposing ways. In the downstream seal and outlet regions, pressure fluctuation amplitudes are reduced, with an average vorticity attenuation of 42.3% in the labyrinth seal. In the upstream inlet and development regions, the blade-passage frequency is enhanced, the 82.97 Hz discrete peak is eliminated, and low-frequency broadband energy below 50 Hz becomes dominant. Small-scale high-frequency vortex structures are replaced by large-scale low-frequency coherent structures. A pressure component near 195 Hz emerges post-modification and falls within the head cover natural frequency band of 194 to 196 Hz, with a 149% amplitude increase. The dominant vibration frequency shifts from 146 Hz to 183 Hz. These findings indicate that the current boss configuration is not a viable mitigation strategy for the unit studied. The vortex-pressure correlations identified in this work can inform future clearance passage designs that target specific frequency bands.

title: Assessment of Single-blade-sector Blade-resolved Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes Approach as Applied to Wind Turbines
summary: This study presents a systematic evaluation of blade-resolved Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulations for two benchmark wind turbines, the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Phase VI turbine and the Model Experiments in
content: This study presents a systematic evaluation of blade-resolved Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulations for two benchmark wind turbines, the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Phase VI turbine and the Model Experiments in Controlled Conditions (MEXICO) turbine, with a comprehensive comparison against experimental data and numerous previous computational fluid dynamics (CFD) studies. To improve computational efficiency, a single-blade sector configuration is adopted. The simulations capture the main aerodynamic trends observed in the experiments and show good agreement with the existing literature in terms of sectional loads and integrated aerodynamic quantities. Although some discrepancies remain in the stall and post-stall regions, the approach effectively balances computational efficiency and predictive accuracy. These results provide a clear assessment of the capabilities and limitations of the current modeling strategy, offering guidance for future CFD studies of wind turbines.

title: Forests and ecosystem services: Nature's invisible economy
summary: Forests are primarily valued for the resources and products that are evident and can be extracted, such as wood, fuelwood, and fruits, as well as for their aesthetic value. However, their most vital contributions are made without the price
content: Forests are primarily valued for the resources and products that are evident and can be extracted, such as wood, fuelwood, and fruits, as well as for their aesthetic value. However, their most vital contributions are made without the price tags, or market transactions. These benefits, termed ecosystem services, represent the invisible economy, the provider of clean water and food, the reduction of disaster risks, and the source of human well-being. The loss of forests does not immediately wipe out this economy; instead, it takes time for the effects to be felt in floods, droughts, declining crop yields, heat stress, and rising public costs. This article elaborates on the functioning of forests as natural capital, presents the data supporting their ecosystem services, and argues that forest conservation is economically necessary rather than environmentally luxurious.

title: Bio-Ethanol Production from Cocoyam (Xanthosoma Sagittifolium) Peels using Acid Hydrolysis
source: Journal of Advanced Materials Science and Engineering
summary: This research explored bioethanol production from cocoyam peels using two acid hydrolysis methods— hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sulfuric acid (H2SO4) with acid concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 1 M. Before hydrolysis and fermentation, the c
content: This research explored bioethanol production from cocoyam peels using two acid hydrolysis methods— hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sulfuric acid (H2SO4) with acid concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 1 M. Before hydrolysis and fermentation, the cocoyam peels were pretreated, and their proximate composition was analyzed. The study investigated how hydrolysis time, pH, temperature, and acid concentration influenced ethanol yield. To optimize sugar yield from acid hydrolysis, the Box-Behnken design within Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was applied. Results showed that sugar yield increased with temperature up to 150°C but declined beyond this point, with a significant decrease observed at 170°C. At 150°C, sugar yield was notably higher than at 130°C and 170°C. The effect of hydrolysis time varied with temperature: below 170°C, maximum sugar yield was reached before 150 minutes, whereas at 170°C, the peak occurred after 60 minutes. Importantly, simple sugar yields from HCl and H2SO4 hydrolysis were almost identical. The highest ethanol yield obtained from the acid hydrolysate was 4.55% (v/v). These findings indicate that cocoyam peels, containing approximately 50% carbohydrates, are a promising raw material for bioethanol production.

title: Post-fire assessment of soil physicochemical properties in Tamgout Forest, Northern Algeria
summary: Understanding how fires affect forest ecosystem components is crucial for predicting vegetation recovery and guiding forest management. Yet information on wildfire consequences for soil properties remains limited in Algeria. This study inve
content: Understanding how fires affect forest ecosystem components is crucial for predicting vegetation recovery and guiding forest management. Yet information on wildfire consequences for soil properties remains limited in Algeria. This study investigated the impact of wildfire on the physicochemical and structural properties of forest soil in the Tamgout area, northern Algeria. Soil samples were collected along a post-fire chronosequence (2, 10, and 18 years) and compared to an unburned soil (control). ANOVA analysis revealed significant fire-induced changes in key soil properties, including moisture content (M), texture, electrical conductivity (EC), total Nitrogen (TN), organic carbon (OC), organic matter (OM), and mineral content (K+, Ca2+, Na+, Fe, and Mn). In contrast, no significant differences were observed in pH, CaCO3, and Mg2+ contents. The Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed marked spectral shifts in mineral bands, particularly in the mid-infrared region, distinguishing burned from unburned soils. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis further demonstrated progressive crystallographic alterations, including peak broadening, reduced intensity, and microstructural degradation in fire-affected soils, indicating mineral disorder and reduced crystallinity. These findings highlight the long-term effects of fire on soil composition, structure, and other parameters that play a critical role in forest resilience, ecosystem recovery, and biodiversity conservation in Mediterranean woodland environments.

title: The Geography of Euroleague Basketball: Spatial Inequality, Travel Exposure and Home-Court Advantage in a Transnational League
summary: This study conceptualizes the EuroLeague as a transnational urban network and tests whether spatial position and nominal travel distance are associated with competitive outcomes. The design integrates three empirical layers: (i) a longitudi
content: This study conceptualizes the EuroLeague as a transnational urban network and tests whether spatial position and nominal travel distance are associated with competitive outcomes. The design integrates three empirical layers: (i) a longitudinal spatial panel covering the league-format era from 2016-17 to 2025-26; (ii) a completed 2025- 26 cross-section of 20 clubs in 17 nominal urban nodes and 11 countries; and (iii) a game-level model based on 1,943 available regular-season games from seven analytically retained seasons between 2016-17 and 2024-25. Great-circle distances were calculated between standardized club-city coordinates. Territorial concentration was assessed with the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI), spatial inequality with a normalized Structural Travel Burden Index, and home-win probability with logistic regression controlling for pre-game Elo difference, rest-day difference and season effects, with two-way cluster-robust inference by home and away team. The 2025-26 network had a mean pairwise distance of 1,765 km; Dubai Basketball increased the contemporaneous mean by 17.8% relative to the same network without Dubai and had a mean opponent distance of 4,163 km, compared with 1,288 km for Virtus Bologna. Country participation became less concentrated across the league-format era (HHI 0.148 in 2016-17 versus 0.110 in 2025- 26), although spatial extent fluctuated substantially and was not monotonically increasing. In the game-level sample, home teams won 62.2% of games. After adjustment, an additional 1,000 km of nominal inter-city distance was not significantly associated with home victory (OR=1.04, 95% CI 0.98-1.10, p=0.173), whereas a 100-point pre-game Elo advantage strongly increased the odds of home victory (OR=2.64, 95% CI 2.21-3.16). Championship success from 2000-01 to 2025-26 was markedly more concentrated geographically than current participation. The findings show that geography creates measurable inequalities in travel exposure, but spatial distance alone should not be interpreted as deterministic fatigue or competitive disadvantage. EuroLeague geography is best understood as a dynamic interaction among urban location, institutional design, scheduling, team quality and geopolitical contingencies.

title: Inhibitory activity of propolis and nano-propolis against isolates of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli
summary: Background: Propolis, a plant-derived material, is widely used to enhance antibiotic activity against common pathogenic bacteria which causes significant global economic losses. This research was designed to detect the role of propolis and
content: Background: Propolis, a plant-derived material, is widely used to enhance antibiotic activity against common pathogenic bacteria which causes significant global economic losses. This research was designed to detect the role of propolis and nano-propolis as natural antibiotic. Methods: Fifteen isolates of S. aureus and 15 of E. coli were cultured on plates of Nutrient Agar, incubated at 37 °C, then stored at -20 °C. Bacterial sensitivity of the 15 isolates to different important antibiotics were performed separately for each type of bacteria. Also, susceptibility test by Kirby Bauer disc diffusion method was utilized with three concentrations (125,250,375 μg/ml) of propolis and nano-propolis. Zones diameters of bacterial growth inhibition for the tested isolates were measured after 24 h of incubation. In the same time MIC and MBC for both materials was determined. Results: Results of bacterial sensitivity test show that 13 bacterial isolates of S. aureus were highly resistant to Benzylpenicillin (86.6%) and 12 isolates of S. aureus were resistant to Oxacillin (80%). While, 13 isolates of S. aureus were sensitive to Linezolid and Teicoplanin (86.66%). In addition, E. coli showed that 13 isolates were resistant to ampicillin (86.66) and 10 out of 15 isolates were sensitive to Piperacillin (66.66%). Furthermore, the inhibition zone of S. aureus was higher at 375 µg/ml as 18.36 mm and 11.87 mm with nano-propolis and propolis respectively. Moreover, E. coli cultures showed higher inhibition zone at 375 µg/ml as 11.78 mm with propolis and 12.56 mm with nano-propolis. Conclusion: This study indicates that propolis and nano-propolis inhibited bacterial growth and may potentiate antibiotic effect against gram positive and gram-negative bacteria. Suggesting a good strategy against pathogens. However, nano-propolis is a promising candidate as plant derived material to decrease MDR microbes.

title: Event Classification in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data: Multi-representation Feature Engineering with Leakage-controlled Benchmarking
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) benchmarks can be overly optimistic when overlapping windows or samples from the same recording cross training and test partitions.We evaluate multi-representation feature extraction and ensemble feature s
content: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) benchmarks can be overly optimistic when overlapping windows or samples from the same recording cross training and test partitions.We evaluate multi-representation feature extraction and ensemble feature selection on two public DAS datasets using leakage-controlled protocols.In the Cao dataset, 423 of 441 sessions span the released partitions; in Tomasov, every randomly partitioned test window overlaps a training window.Session-grouped and guarded blocked partitions eliminate these contamination sources.Our pipeline extracts 1,002 multi-representation features and benchmarks seven lightweight classifiers and six balancing strategies.Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) achieves 98.90 macro-F1 on Cao and 81.98 on Tomasov for segment-level generalization within represented recordings, exceeding convolutional neural network (CNN) baselines by 8.01 and 16.43 points on identical partitions, and exceeding five architectures published from 2024 onward, including graph and transformer models, under the same partitions.However, leakage control reduces the openclose F1 of our representation from 0.72 to 0.044, a loss a spectro-spatial graph model does not incur on the same partition, and Cao accuracy falls from 99.06% to 86.81% when acquisition dates are held out.Thus, group-aware, cross-campaign evaluation is essential for credible DAS benchmarking.

title: Knowledge Co-Production Practices To Promote Climate Resilience In Global Cities: A Systematic Literature Review. Geography
summary: Climate change presents complex challenges for cities worldwide, requiring innovative and collaborative approaches to enhance resilience and adaptability. In response to this phenomenon, knowledge co-production plays a vital role in integra
content: Climate change presents complex challenges for cities worldwide, requiring innovative and collaborative approaches to enhance resilience and adaptability. In response to this phenomenon, knowledge co-production plays a vital role in integrating diverse perspectives to address climate-related risks and promote adaptive urban environments. This research aims to investigate current consensus on how knowledge co-production is operationalised, particularly in climate resilience and urban settings. This study follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and MetaAnalyses (PRISMA) protocol to identify, screen, and analyse relevant publications systematically. A total of 36 publications were reviewed to examine the types of disturbances, the dimensions of stakeholder engagement, and current practices of knowledge co-production. The findings highlight the growing significance of knowledge co-production in addressing climate-related challenges through strong stakeholder engagement, local knowledge integration, and effective science– policy interfaces. Moreover, these processes require balanced and meaningful participation among all stakeholders, particularly local community involvement, to ensure that initiatives can be scaled up and become systemic rather than fragmented.

title: The Chernobyl Signature in Western Abkhazia: Assessing 137Cs Deposition Variability and Applicability for evaluation sediment redistribution rates
summary: This study presents the first documented evidence of radioactive contamination in Western Abkhazia linked to the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant accident. The data obtained show that the level of ¹³⁷Cs radioactive contamination in the study a
content: This study presents the first documented evidence of radioactive contamination in Western Abkhazia linked to the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant accident. The data obtained show that the level of ¹³⁷Cs radioactive contamination in the study area ranged from 50 to 160 kBq/m² in 1986. This corresponds to contemporary values of 25 to 79 kBq/m² when considering the radionuclide’s half-life. These measurements are highly consistent with data recorded in the adjacent Sochi region, where contamination levels varied between 40 and 185 kBq/m² in 1986. The local spatial variability of ¹³⁷Cs fallout was studied at four reference sites, located in different parts of the Mussera upland. All investigated sites demonstrated moderate variability, with value ranges of 17–25%. This heterogeneous distribution pattern is attributed to a combination of factors, including local topography, atmospheric deposition characteristics, and anthropogenic influence. Measurements of ambient dose equivalent rates ranged from 0.01 to 0.05 μSv/h. While no direct correlation was found between dose rates and the age or genesis of the underlying bedrock, a clear relationship was established between dose rates and terrain morphology. Elevated dose rates were consistently recorded in erosional landforms within topographically dissected areas. Analysis of peat cores from the Pitsunda Peninsula lagoon provided conclusive evidence of the Chernobyl disaster’s impact on Western Abkhazia, with a measured ¹³⁷Cs inventory of 20.7 kBq/m² (equivalent to 49.5 kBq/m² when corrected to 1986 values). Application of the non-equilibrium ²¹⁰Pb dating method yielded a peat accumulation rate of 0.1 cm/year. The Chernobyl accident resulted in a significant release of 137 Cs, leading to widespread radioactive fallout. This document assesses the 137 Cs inventory and its impact on ambient dose rates in the affected regions.

title: Snow Cover Pollution By Potentially Toxic Elements In Small And Medium-Sized Industrial Cities: Case Of Sverdlovsk Region, Russia
summary: This study aims to develop and validate a method for assessing urban air pollution by analysing undisturbed snow cover in residential areas of small and medium-sized industrial cities in Sverdlovsk Region, Russia: Kachkanar, Serov, Verkhnya
content: This study aims to develop and validate a method for assessing urban air pollution by analysing undisturbed snow cover in residential areas of small and medium-sized industrial cities in Sverdlovsk Region, Russia: Kachkanar, Serov, Verkhnyaya Pyshma, and Alapaevsk. Snow samples were collected in each city. The proposed approach is based on the analysis of the most contaminated solid fraction of snow (particles >2 µm and filtrate). This method has shown effectiveness in identifying pollutants and their sources. It is also more cost-efficient and offers better material accessibility than the approach that analyses both dissolved (<0.45 µm) and suspended (>0.45 µm) snow phases. The balanced set of qualitative and quantitative indicators includes the physical and chemical properties of snow, the accumulation intensity of PTEs, the calculation of indices ( I geo , EF, PI, PI sum , PI avg , and PI Nemerow ), dust load, and geochemical associations. Snow’s physical and chemical properties were influenced by natural conditions. Low mineralisation and suspended solids were mostly composed of calcium and magnesium bicarbonates and sulfates. Snow pH was slightly alkaline in Serov and mildly alkaline in other cities. Metallurgical and mining cities showed higher pollution according to the indices: elevated V and Fe in Kachkanar, Cr in Serov, Cu and As in Verkhnyaya Pyshma. Kachkanar was the most polluted city ( PI sum – 154, PI Nemerow – 12 ), while Serov and Verkhnyaya Pyshma were also significantly polluted with similar PI sum and PI avg values (66 and 4.2, respectively) and PI Nemerow values (5.1 and 7.2, respectively). Geochemical associations reflected local industrial profiles. Dust load ranged from 27 to 163 mg/m 2 /day, peaking in Kachkanar. The collected data indicate current atmospheric pollution in the studied cities. This method proved effective for assessing urban air pollution and is recommended for environmental monitoring in other industrial regions.

title: Fuzzy Logic in Predictive Models for Reducing Energy Consumption in Smart Grids
source: Global Journal of Engineering Innovations and Interdisciplinary Research
summary: In this study, we compare the effectiveness of fuzzy logic, neural networks, and decision trees foroptimizing energy consumption in smart grids. We evaluate these techniques based on their forecastingaccuracy, load balancing efficiency, com
content: In this study, we compare the effectiveness of fuzzy logic, neural networks, and decision trees foroptimizing energy consumption in smart grids. We evaluate these techniques based on their forecastingaccuracy, load balancing efficiency, computational time, and flexibility. Our results reveal that neuralnetworks exhibit the highest forecasting accuracy at 92.4% and superior load balancing efficiency of82.1%, though they require significant computational time (25 minutes). Fuzzy logic provides a balancedperformance with a forecasting accuracy of 85.2%, a load balancing efficiency of 78.5%, and a moderatecomputational time of 12 minutes. It also scores highly in flexibility, demonstrating strong adaptabilityto changing conditions. Decision trees, while the most computationally efficient with a processing timeof 8 minutes, show the lowest forecasting accuracy (80.1%) and load balancing efficiency (74.6%),indicating limitations in handling complex energy management tasks. This comparison highlights thestrengths and trade-offs of each technique, offering insights into their suitability for real-time energyoptimization in smart grids.

title: Hall methodology for Carbon-based/ZnO composite synthesis and it characterization
summary: Currently, new materials are being developed to remove contaminants from wastewater by combining materials to improve their individual properties. This chapter describes the production of the zinc oxide (ZnO) and carbon composite. The ZnO w
content: Currently, new materials are being developed to remove contaminants from wastewater by combining materials to improve their individual properties. This chapter describes the production of the zinc oxide (ZnO) and carbon composite. The ZnO was synthesized by electrolysis, adding Spend Coffee Grounds (SCG) to the electrolytic medium, and finally calcined at 400 °C for 30 min. ZnO, carbon, and the composite were synthesized and characterized. Scanning Electron Microscopy found that ZnO deposits in the pores of the carbon; Infrared Spectroscopy identified bonds associated with carbon and ZnO; X Ray Diffraction yielded a diffractogram with lower intensity compared to that of ZnO (JPDS-361451), due to the synthesis of amorphous carbon; μ-RAMAN Spectroscopy detected characteristic bonds of both materials; finally, the isoelectric point of the composite is 7.3, which will allows working with sorption in neutral systems.

title: Measuring performance and exhaust emissions in an internal combustion engine using renewable and non-renewable fuels
summary: The study of biofuels has become a priority research area in the field of mechanical and energy engineering. One of the most accessible and easily implemented biofuels is biogasoline, a blend of gasoline with a percentage of anhydrous ethan
content: The study of biofuels has become a priority research area in the field of mechanical and energy engineering. One of the most accessible and easily implemented biofuels is biogasoline, a blend of gasoline with a percentage of anhydrous ethanol, generally 10%. This type of blend has been introduced in various countries as a strategy to reduce dependence on petroleum and mitigate emissions of polluting gases. In this project, an experimental study was conducted focusing on analyzing the behavior of a 150 cc, four-stroke internal combustion engine operating with conventional 87-octane gasoline and with bio-gasoline. The results obtained show that the use of bio-gasoline allows for higher engine speeds, with a gain of up to 1000 rpm compared to conventional gasoline. However, the frequency spectra show differences in the high-frequency components, which could be related to changes in the combustion pattern or internal resonances of the system. This project contributes to the understanding of the technical impact of using biofuels in conventional engines and promotes the development of sustainable, accessible energy solutions that are compatible with the existing technological infrastructure.

title: Evaluation of a Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell [DSSC] device based on Agaricus bisporus extract
summary: This study evaluates the photoelectrochemical performance of natural extracts from Agaricus bisporus [Portobello variety] as photosensitizers in dye-sensitized solar cells [DSSCs]. Photoanodes were prepared with mesoporous TiO2, and activat
content: This study evaluates the photoelectrochemical performance of natural extracts from Agaricus bisporus [Portobello variety] as photosensitizers in dye-sensitized solar cells [DSSCs]. Photoanodes were prepared with mesoporous TiO2, and activated carbon counter electrodes were catalytic thermally activated. Photoelectric characterization under natural solar irradiance [930 W/m] demonstrated efficient charge injection promoted by DOPA-melanin chromophores. Prototypes achieved a maximum open-circuit voltage [Voc] of 34.2 mV, a fill factor [FF] of 0.454, and a overall power conversion efficiency [η] of 0.0374%. These results confirm the stability and technical feasibility of crude fungal biomass for sustainable optoelectronic devices, setting an experimental baseline for non-purified bio-sensitizers.

title: Ecological Consequences of Altered Water-Level Regulation on Wetland Plant Succession
summary: Wetlands represent highly variable ecosystems, where water level size, persistence, frequency, rate of changes and seasonality control plant colonization and community development. River regulation, reservoirs operation, water extraction, d
content: Wetlands represent highly variable ecosystems, where water level size, persistence, frequency, rate of changes and seasonality control plant colonization and community development. River regulation, reservoirs operation, water extraction, drainage and aquifer depletion may influence all these hydrological factors affecting plant viability, competition, species composition and succession processes. This review provides an analysis of scientific literature published from 2014 to 2022 that deals with the impact of modified water regimes on wetland and riparian vegetation. Three interrelated effects are examined: long-term flooding, long-term drawdown, and suppression of natural seasonal dynamics. Prolonged floods may cause oxygen and light limitation of flood-intolerant plants, whereas long-term drawdown may increase substrate exposure, reduce availability of aquatic habitats, and promote drought-resistant or terrestrial species. Regulation may also exclude major floods and substitute them with more small-scale frequent fluctuations, thus filtering plant communities by their tolerance abilities and life histories. This process is variable, as the response will depend on the type of wetland, geomorphology, the characteristics of the sediments, climate, the availability of propagules, and the amount of change in the hydrology. This literature review shows the consequences of hydrological change for biodiversity, habitat structure, nutrient cycling, productivity, and restoration. This paper emphasizes that the maintenance of a static water level is insufficient to achieve ecological goals. On the contrary, conservation should maintain an appropriate variability in the seasonality of the river-floodplain system, maintain connectivity, and study vegetation changes over many years.

title: NIST handbook 133: checking the net contents of packaged goods (2026 Ed.)
summary: This handbook has been prepared as a procedural guide for the compliance testing of net content statements on packaged goods. Compliance testing of packaged goods is the determination of the conformance results of packaging, distribution, a
content: This handbook has been prepared as a procedural guide for the compliance testing of net content statements on packaged goods. Compliance testing of packaged goods is the determination of the conformance results of packaging, distribution, and sale of commodities to specific legal requirements for net content declarations. This handbook has been developed primarily for the use of state, local, and some federal officials. However, it should be useful to commercial and industrial establishments areas of packaging, distribution, and sale of commodities. NIST has statutory responsibility for “cooperation with states in securing uniformity of weights and measures laws and methods of inspection and publishes this and other NIST Handbooks in partial fulfillment of this responsibility. This 2026 edition includes amendments made through the Committee on Laws and Regulations of the National Council on Weights and Measures (NCWM)with technical guidance from the Office of Weights and Measures (OWM) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and input from weights and measures officials and industry representatives. These amendments were adopted by the NCWM at its 110th Annual Meeting in July 2025. There may be years where there are no changes to this NIST Handbook 133; therefore, it would not be published on an annual basis in such instances. In conducting compliance testing, the conversion of measured quantity values between systems of measurement (e.g., from the metric system to the U.S. customary system) should be handled with careful regard to the implied correspondence between measurement accuracy and the number of digits displayed. For all conversions, the number of significant figures retained should be congruous with the accuracy of the corresponding measurement.
