For this edition of NISTHandbook 133, all quantity values obtained from devices or through test procedures have been rounded to two significant digits (e.g., 2.5 cm to 1.0 in), or to a precision level applicable to the test equipment (e.g., 200 kPa for 25 psi or 35 MPs for 5 000 psi).

title: ‘Falling Backward’, or How Crises Affect Integration: The EU and the Energy Crisis
summary: This paper investigates the applicability of the concept of ‘falling forward’ to crisis management in the European Union. An idea central to the literature is that the EU draws upon crisis situations to enhance its power and influence, as m
content: This paper investigates the applicability of the concept of ‘falling forward’ to crisis management in the European Union. An idea central to the literature is that the EU draws upon crisis situations to enhance its power and influence, as member states are willing to delegate further competencies to EU organs in order to collectively solve pressing problems. The assumption that crisis situations lead to an increase in the power of the supranational entity has been the subject of multiple studies, yet, the long-term impact of this process, which takes place with minimal public accountability, has been largely neglected. We seek to go beyond the short-term effects of crises on integration, to determine how shock events impact integration structures in the long run. A mixed methods inquiry, based on 102 survey responses and 15 interviews with EU experts, triangulated with Eurobarometer results, reveals that accelerated integration can foster dissatisfaction, bringing about a surge in elections of extremist and Eurosceptic parties. These political changes could pose a significant threat to EU integration and may cause the union to ‘fall backward’ rather than ‘forward’, as is systematically predicted in the existing academic literature. The case-study of the 2022 energy crisis in the EU confirms that the regional organisation does indeed gain in power and influence as it works to manage and mitigate the repercussions of a crisis but that this strengthening gives rise to new challenges for the union. This paper yields novel theoretical insights into the spill-over process (including the original concept of ‘falling backward’) and the functioning of regional organisations as complex polities.

title: Ultrasound Technologies in Support of Ballast Water Treatment on Board Ships
summary: This paper examines the challenges of ballast water treatment on board ships. While international maritime trade provides major economic benefits, it also facilitates the uncontrolled transfer of invasive aquatic species through ballast wat
content: This paper examines the challenges of ballast water treatment on board ships. While international maritime trade provides major economic benefits, it also facilitates the uncontrolled transfer of invasive aquatic species through ballast water, causing ecological imbalances that impact biodiversity, human health, and the economy. In response, the International Maritime Organization introduced the Ballast Water Management (BWM) Convention, requiring ships to install certified treatment systems. The study analyzes general treatment principles and a case study on the Mary Maersk, focusing on system performance in difficult conditions such as turbid waters. It also proposes integrating ultrasound technology to improve efficiency. By generating acoustic cavitation, ultrasound can disrupt microorganisms and prevent biofilm formation, maintaining effective disinfection with minimal additional energy consumption, while supporting environmental protection.

title: Aspects Regarding the Quality of Deep-Drawn Parts – Part Two
summary: In a previous study, it was argued that parts meeting quality requirements and obtained through a deep drawing process exhibit this 'quality' feature as a result of the interaction between two main factors: the technological system and the
content: In a previous study, it was argued that parts meeting quality requirements and obtained through a deep drawing process exhibit this 'quality' feature as a result of the interaction between two main factors: the technological system and the forming process itself. To demonstrate these interdependencies, three dies were designed and used to analyze how variations in the thickness of A3K steel strips affect the quality of the formed parts. The present paper continues this research by examining two additional types of rolled strips: one made of deep-drawing steel and the other of brass. Thickness frequency histograms were constructed, as variations in strip thickness are known to influence both the drawing and holding forces during the manufacturing of small cylindrical parts, thereby impacting the factors that define manufacturing quality.

title: Optical and Thermodynamic Properties of Benzene–Xylene and Benzene–Xylene–C60 Solutions
summary: A systematic experimental investigation of the thermodynamic and optical properties of benzene-xylene binary mixtures and benzene-xylene-C60 ternary systems has been carried out at 300.15 K. Refractive indices, densities, optical absorption
content: A systematic experimental investigation of the thermodynamic and optical properties of benzene-xylene binary mixtures and benzene-xylene-C60 ternary systems has been carried out at 300.15 K. Refractive indices, densities, optical absorptions, excess refractive indices, and excess molar volumes were determined for freshly prepared solutions and after 15 days of storage to elucidate intermolecular interactions and time-dependent structural relaxation effects. The combined thermodynamic and spectroscopic results demonstrate that competitive solvation in binary aromatic solvents plays a critical role in governing the structural stability and aggregation behavior of C60 in solution.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging and spatial localized spectroscopy using intermolecular multiple-quantum coherences: techniques and clinical utility for brain
summary: This review is focused on the investigation on brain microstructure using advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and spectroscopy (MRS). These echniques were introduced in the last decades using NMR based on intermolecular multiplequantu
content: This review is focused on the investigation on brain microstructure using advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and spectroscopy (MRS). These echniques were introduced in the last decades using NMR based on intermolecular multiplequantum coherences (iMQCs), excited and detected in the presence of the long-range dipolar inter-nuclear couplings induced by correlated gradients. The origin of multiple spin echoes and nonlinear coherence transfer echoes based on COSY revamped by asymmetric Z-gradient echo detection (CRAZED) in liquids are discussed using quantum-mechanics formalism. The accent of this review is on the intermolecular zero-quantum coherences (iZQCs) and intermolecular double-quantum coherences (iDQCs) excitation, evolution, and detection in the presence of correlated field gradients using the CRAZED pulse sequences. The applications of this pulse sequence to reduce the effect of inhomogeneous magnetic fields and to increase the image resolution is reviewed in the field of magnetic resonance imaging and localized spectroscopy with the accent on brain investigations. The physics related to the used of CRAZED methods is also addressed to produce fundamentally different contrast than does conventional imaging. The effects of spatial inhomogeneity and temporal instability of the NMR made at ultra-high magnetic field are nearly eliminated using iZQCs, thereby achieving a resolution enhancement. This will open new frontiers in the nonlinear spatial localized NMR spectroscopy and magnetic resonance imaging. The large nuclear magnetization induced by different hyperpolarization methods allows detection of intermolecular multiple-quantum coherences in liquids, for nuclei in low abundance and/or having low gyromagnetic ratio, and even in low density matter like gases.

title: Influence of Sintered Parameters and Composition of Zrx-Er1-x (x=0.25;0.50;0.75) Alloy on Microstructural Evolution
summary: The use of hydrogen as an energy source is important because it helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Hydrogen can be stored by three methods: gaseous, liquid and solid. Solid storage is achieved using metal hydrides. Studying methods for
content: The use of hydrogen as an energy source is important because it helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Hydrogen can be stored by three methods: gaseous, liquid and solid. Solid storage is achieved using metal hydrides. Studying methods for obtaining alloys that can form hydrides is very important to develop a material that has certain qualities. Sintered Zr-Er compacts are of interest for hydrogen storage because both materials can store and release hydrogen. In this paper, a study was carried out on obtaining sintered Zrx-Er1–x compacts, x = 0.25; 0.50; 0.75, by powder metallurgy, using zirconium and erbium raw materials. These materials were hydrided separately at 750°C, then the hydrides were processed to obtain fine powders. The obtained powders were dosed, mixed and characterized through SEM and XRD, then pressed into molds. The pressed samples were sintered at temperatures of 1150°C and 1250°C. After sintering, the compacts Zrx-Er1–x (x = 0.25; 0.50; 0.75), were analyzed by the following methods: geometric, SEM and XRD characterization. Following the characterizations, it was found that the sintering temperature influences the density, porosity and quantity of compounds formed between the zirconium and erbium elements, and their initial compositions influence the type of compound formed between the elements.

title: Exploring the Ar-plasma treatment capabilities for enhancing PLA filament 3D printability
summary: Investigations into atmospheric pressure plasma jet sources have been conducted using electrical, optical, and spectroscopic diagnostic methodologies. Polymers play an indispensable role across a diverse array of industrial sectors; neverth
content: Investigations into atmospheric pressure plasma jet sources have been conducted using electrical, optical, and spectroscopic diagnostic methodologies. Polymers play an indispensable role across a diverse array of industrial sectors; nevertheless, their surface modification is essential for numerous applications. This study investigates how an atmospheric pressure plasma generated in argon facilitates the modification of polylactic acid surfaces, leading to alterations in wettability characteristics and modifications in chemical composition with respect to surface oxidation. The study findings indicated that plasma exposure improved the surface wettability of the polymer by as much as 38%, along with an increase of 45% in adhesion work. The mechanical properties of the material exhibited a subtle transformation, indicating that the polymer samples were not thermally damaged by plasma treatment. Exposure of PLA to plasma led to significant modifications in the oxygen-containing functional groups of the polymer, corroborated by both XPS measurements, where Pindex increased by 20%, and FTIR analysis, which showed an increase in HI of more than 200%. Moreover, our results emphasize the applicability of plasma technologies for the non-chemical treatment of polymeric materials in 3D printing applications.

title: Mechanics of Advanced Materials and Structures: ICMAMS 2026
summary: This study investigates tool-temperature compensation (TTC) technique, a strategy aimed at optimizing the use of heated tooling during in-situ consolidation of thermoplastics in automated fibre placement (ICT-AFP).Rather than maintaining th
content: This study investigates tool-temperature compensation (TTC) technique, a strategy aimed at optimizing the use of heated tooling during in-situ consolidation of thermoplastics in automated fibre placement (ICT-AFP).Rather than maintaining the tool at a fixed temperature to promote crystallization and reduce residual stresses, in TTC the tool temperature is dynamically increased during deposition to improve through-thickness crystallinity uniformity.Although this strategy has been shown to reduce warpage and void content, its influence on mechanical performance has not yet been established, which constitutes the main objective of this paper.The performance of laminates manufactured via TTC is assessed through interlaminar behaviour, as determined by short-beam shear (SBS) tests, and through correlation with crystallinity, void content, and morphology.Indeed, employing TTC through varying the tool temperature between 150-200⁰C resulted in laminate layers of homogenous crystallinity with 18% crystallinity difference, compared with 41.4% for laminates manufactured using a fixed tool temperature of 150°C.This homogeneous crystallinity was also reflected in the mechanical response, as TTC specimens exhibited 20.72% higher shear modulus than their counterparts manufactured using a fixed tool temperature.

title: Coupled Flame Acceleration and NOx Suppression in Ammonia Combustion Assisted by Oxygenated Ignition Fuels
source: The Journal of Applied Engineering and Technologies
summary: Ammonia combustion suffers from low flame speed and high nitrogen oxide emissions, limiting its practical application as a carbon-free fuel. Herein, an oxygenated-fuel ignition chamber was designed to improve ammonia premixed combustion whi
content: Ammonia combustion suffers from low flame speed and high nitrogen oxide emissions, limiting its practical application as a carbon-free fuel. Herein, an oxygenated-fuel ignition chamber was designed to improve ammonia premixed combustion while controlling pollutant formation. Flame propagation was recorded by high-speed schlieren imaging, and NO, NO2, N2O, and NH3 slip were quantified by Fourier-transform infrared gas analysis. At an equivalence ratio of 0.9, the ignition-assisted system increased the laminar flame propagation velocity from 7.8 to 18.6 cm s⁻¹, while reducing ignition delay by 42.5%. The peak NO concentration decreased from 612 to 438 ppm when the chamber equivalence ratio was optimized, mainly due to enhanced early-stage radical generation and more complete NHx conversion. The results clarify the interaction between ignition enhancement and pollutant pathways in ammonia combustion.

title: Hydrological Functioning of a Bromeliad Green Roof: Interception Capacity and Evapotranspiration
source: Journal of Sustainable Development of Energy Water and Environment Systems
summary: This work presents an analysis of the contributions of plant interception and evapotranspiration to the water balance of a bromeliad green roof, based on experimental tests conducted in a prototype. The objective is to calculate the volume
content: This work presents an analysis of the contributions of plant interception and evapotranspiration to the water balance of a bromeliad green roof, based on experimental tests conducted in a prototype. The objective is to calculate the volume of water intercepted by bromeliads and the volume of water that undergoes evapotranspiration, and to compare these volumes with the volume precipitated over the green roof and the volume retained, to improve understanding of the mechanism of interaction among the parts. The main purpose is to improve the efficiency of compensatory techniques in urban drainage, thereby minimising urban flooding across all major cities. A literature review was conducted on the hydrological cycle and its stages, along with a description of the history and advantages of green roofs, to improve understanding of the system’s operation. This work contributes to improving the efficiency of green roofs for rainwater retention.

title: Energy Planning: A Fuzzy Multi-Objective Tool for Sustainable Energy Mixes in Colombia
source: Journal of Sustainable Development of Energy Water and Environment Systems
summary: This study introduces a computational tool developed to identify the most sustainable alternative for integrating a hybrid renewable energy system. The approach brings together a fuzzy optimisation model, focused on minimising both the Net
content: This study introduces a computational tool developed to identify the most sustainable alternative for integrating a hybrid renewable energy system. The approach brings together a fuzzy optimisation model, focused on minimising both the Net Present Value and carbon dioxide emissions, with the Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process, incorporating economic, technical, environmental, and social criteria. To enhance usability, the tool includes an Excel-based module that allows users to adjust quantitative parameters, while qualitative aspects can be modified through editable comparison matrices in the main graphical interface. This flexibility makes it adaptable to a wide range of geographical and contextual scenarios. The proposed framework was applied in a pilot-scale case study in the municipality of Tona, Colombia. The selected energy mix consists of 57.56% photovoltaic solar energy, 35.42% biomass-based generation, and 7.02% diesel generation, achieving a Net Present Value of USD 1,765.68 and total emissions of 1,216.08 kg of carbon dioxide. .

title: Eco-friendly geopolymer composites: leveraging parawood ash for sustainable construction materials
summary: Biomass is gaining in popularity as an energy source. However, the combustion process generates a significant amount of ash, posing an environmental challenge. Previous studies have explored the incorporation of biomass ash into cement conc
content: Biomass is gaining in popularity as an energy source. However, the combustion process generates a significant amount of ash, posing an environmental challenge. Previous studies have explored the incorporation of biomass ash into cement concrete to reduce its environmental impact; however, this has resulted in reduced strength performance. Biomass ash has been increasingly used as a component of geopolymer binder materials. This research examined how the treatment processes influence the physical and mechanical properties of geopolymer mortars that include parawood ash and fly ash. The parawood ash was mixed at 0%, 20%, 40%, and 60% by weight of the binder, and the specimens were subjected to heat curing at 80°C for 6, 12, and 24 h and cured at ambient temperature (30 ± 2°C) for 24 h. The compressive strength, bulk density, compressive strength loss after immersion in seawater, microstructure, chemical composition, and mineral composition of the test specimens were evaluated. The results demonstrated significant improvements in compressive strength. The geopolymer specimens with 20% parawood ash, cured at ambient temperature for 24 h, achieved the highest compressive strength of 32.31 MPa at 28 days. However, the specimens subjected to heat curing for 6-24 hours exhibited optimal compressive strengths within the first 24 h. Prolonged heat curing also effectively reduced the bulk density of the geopolymer. In addition to enhancing the compressive strength, the incorporation of parawood ash contributes to the reduction of waste materials.

title: Complex interfacial designs for mechanical performance in biodegradable bicomponent 3D printed parts
source: Journal of Engineering Sciences and Innovation
summary: Bicomponent and multimaterial fused filament fabrication (FFF) with biodegradable polymers offers a sustainable approach to producing structures with tailored mechanical properties. This study investigates the influence of interface geometr
content: Bicomponent and multimaterial fused filament fabrication (FFF) with biodegradable polymers offers a sustainable approach to producing structures with tailored mechanical properties. This study investigates the influence of interface geometry and printing parameters on the tensile performance of biodegradable FFF components. UltraFuse PLA Blue and PLA/PHA Shining Silver (Polylactic Acid/Polyhydroxyalkanoate) were used to print samples with four interface configurations: simple “T,” double “2T,” “dovetail,” and “double dovetail,” chosen to evaluate how interlocking complexity affects stress distribution, load transfer, and fracture behavior. Mechanical performance was assessed through uniaxial tensile testing, combined with fracture imaging and surface topography analysis. The results showed that both interface design and printing parameters, such as layer thickness and number of shells, significantly impact tensile strength. Thicker layers reduced filament-to-filament adhesion, particularly along the interface plane, while increasing the number of shells improved filament alignment along the loading direction but introduced potential transverse weaknesses. Among the configurations, the simple “T” interface exhibited the lowest cohesion and strength, whereas the “2T” and dovetail geometries promoted more uniform stress distribution and enhanced fracture resistance. These findings highlight the critical role of interface engineering in improving the mechanical reliability of biodegradable multimaterial FFF parts. Overall, the study demonstrates that simultaneous optimization of interface geometry and process parameters is an effective strategy for enhancing tensile performance, converting structurally vulnerable regions into mechanically robust zones, and providing practical guidance for the design of sustainable, high-performance biodegradable FFF structures.

title: Special mechanical properties of diboride ceramic composites with complex microstructures: comparative analysis of three study cases
source: Journal of Engineering Sciences and Innovation
summary: Ceramics are hard and brittle materials. They are usually difficult to machine by chipping due to a strength-ductility trade-off. Moreover, their strength decreases at high temperatures. In this work, we review the peculiar features of thre
content: Ceramics are hard and brittle materials. They are usually difficult to machine by chipping due to a strength-ductility trade-off. Moreover, their strength decreases at high temperatures. In this work, we review the peculiar features of three systems with unique mechanical properties. The MgB2 added with hBN (hexagonal BN) and G (graphene) is machinable by chipping and is assessed for bulk superconducting magnets. The second system is a TiB2-B4C structural ceramic composite (70/30 vol.) with a high bending strength of 1.1 GPa at 1800°C, showing an unusual shape of the bending strength–strain curve composed of elastic, ductile, and strengthening regions. The third system is the heterogeneous, multiphase high-entropy diboride (Ti0.25Ta0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25)B2. Remarkably, it demonstrates a deformation-resistant mechanism that persists with increasing temperature up to 1800°C. Ductile behavior (7.5% strain) is observed at 2000°C, while the bending strength (407 MPa) is 25% higher than at room temperature.

title: Selection and characterization of rhizobacteria from cocoa soils in Ecuador with potential for cadmium mitigation
summary: Bioprospecting for Cd-tolerant rhizobacteria that naturally inhabit cocoa (Theobroma cacao L.) soils contaminated with heavy metals contributes to the development of effective bioremediation strategies.The objective of this study was to sel
content: Bioprospecting for Cd-tolerant rhizobacteria that naturally inhabit cocoa (Theobroma cacao L.) soils contaminated with heavy metals contributes to the development of effective bioremediation strategies.The objective of this study was to select rhizobacteria from cocoa soils in Ecuador with the potential for Cd mitigation.Soil samples were collected from the provinces of Cañar, Esmeraldas, and Manabí.Morphological and biochemical characteristics, Cd tolerance, and molecular identification of the 16S rRNA gene were evaluated.Twelve rhizobacteria morphotypes were selected for their capacity to tolerate 50 mg Cd L -1 for 24 h while producing protease, catalase, and urease enzymes, biofilm production, and solubilizing phosphate and K. Autochthonous strains T-CADM-1, T-CADM-4, T-CADM-5, and T-CADM-6 were incubated at four Cd concentrations (0, 6, 12 and 24 mg L -1 ) for 7 d, maintaining significant cell persistence (p ≤ 0.05) of 2.06  10 9 , 2.02  10 9 , 2.08  10 9 and 1.96  10 9 CFU mL -1 , respectively.The strain T-CADM-5 was the most effective, precipitating bicarbonate (139%) and achieving an in vitro Cd removal rate of 82.4%.GenBank data identified the tolerant strains as Enterobacter sp.(86%), Serratia marcescens (98%), E. asburiae (92%) and E. hormaechei (98%).It was concluded that the strain T-CADM-5 retained its cell viability for 7 d under Cd stress, produced urease and phosphatase, and increased bicarbonate and sulfate anions.These factors positively correlated with Cd immobilization, indicating that these rhizobacteria actively modify their environment to reduce the bioavailability of the heavy metal.

title: Tidal inundation type and soil chemical properties determine rice productivity in tropical acid sulfate swamp ecosystems
summary: Ensuring sustainable rice (Oryza sativa L.) production in tidal swamp ecosystems is critical for strengthening food security in Indonesia.Soil chemical properties, tidal inundation type, and planting season strongly influence rice productiv
content: Ensuring sustainable rice (Oryza sativa L.) production in tidal swamp ecosystems is critical for strengthening food security in Indonesia.Soil chemical properties, tidal inundation type, and planting season strongly influence rice productivity in these systems.This study evaluated soil chemical characteristics and rice productivity across tidal swamp areas in Tanah Bumbu Regency, South Kalimantan, Indonesia, by inundation type and cropping season.Field surveys, soil analyses, and farmer interviews were conducted in five villages.Selimuran and Mudalang were classified as Type B tidal swamps.In contrast, Rantau Panjang, Api-api, and Segumbang were categorized as Type C. Type B soils were acidic, while Type C soils were very acidic.Although both types exhibited low organic C, total N, and exchangeable P, Type B soils had higher P and base cation availability and lower concentrations of exchangeable Al, Fe, sulfate, and pyrite.The pyritic layer was shallower in Type C soils, increasing oxidation risk.Rice productivity was significantly higher in Type B systems (5.43 t ha⁻¹) than in Type C systems (3.76 t ha⁻¹).Seasonal responses differed between tidal types.Yields in Type B fields declined by 0.95 t ha⁻¹ from the dry to the rainy season, whereas yields in Type C fields increased by 0.45 t ha⁻¹.These findings highlight the importance of site-and season-specific nutrient and water management to enhance productivity and sustainability in acid sulfate tidal swamp ecosystems.

title: Effect of Titanium Dioxide (TiO2) Nanoparticle Concentration on the Thermal Conductivity and Stability of Water-Ethylene Glycol Nanofluids
summary: Nanofluids have attracted considerable attention for their potential use as advanced heat transfer media in various cooling applications. This study investigates the effect of titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticle concentration on the therma
content: Nanofluids have attracted considerable attention for their potential use as advanced heat transfer media in various cooling applications. This study investigates the effect of titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticle concentration on the thermal conductivity and stability of nanofluids. Five concentrations of TiO2 nanofluids were prepared using water-ethylene glycol (60:40) as a base fluid and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as the surfactant. The TiO2 nanoparticles were characterized by ATR-FTIR, FESEM and EDX. Thermal conductivity measurements were carried out at room temperature (28 oC) and elevated temperature (e.g. 40 °C and 60 °C). The stability of the nanofluids was evaluated through visual inspection, UV-Vis spectroscopy and dynamic light scattering analysis. The TiO2 nanoparticles displayed spherical shape and tend to form clusters with an average particle diameter of approximately 30 nm. The 0.5 wt.% nanofluid achieved the greatest thermal conductivity value of 0.748 W/m·K resulting in 49.89% thermal conductivity enhancement at 60 °C. Freshly prepared nanofluids exhibited good dispersion stability and reduced when left undisturbed for extended period. Further improvements in long term stability are required for industrial applications.

title: Effects of Multi-objective Optimization of the First-stage Impeller on the Energy Loss Characteristics of a Multistage Molten Salt Pump
summary: To mitigate the prohibitive cost of simultaneously modifying all stages in multistage molten salt pumps used in concentrating solar power plants, address the substantial degradation of hydraulic performance under off-design operating condit
content: To mitigate the prohibitive cost of simultaneously modifying all stages in multistage molten salt pumps used in concentrating solar power plants, address the substantial degradation of hydraulic performance under off-design operating conditions, and resolve the difficulty of tracing cross-stage flow-loss coupling mechanisms, this paper presents a cost-effective retrofit strategy that limits geometric modifications to the first-stage impeller and harnesses the interstage flow-matching effect to improve system-wide performance. The methodology proceeds in four sequential phases. First, a comprehensive sample database is constructed using Latin hypercube sampling combined with high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics simulations. Second, the Adam optimization algorithm is used to train a backpropagation neural network, establishing a computationally efficient surrogate model to replace time-intensive numerical simulations. Third, the surrogate model is coupled with the NSGA-II multi-objective evolutionary algorithm to perform Pareto-front optimization, simultaneously maximizing hydraulic head and efficiency at the design operating point. Finally, based on entropy production theory, the evolution of energy loss before and after optimization is systematically characterized at four hierarchical levels: total entropy production, component-level entropy production, wall entropy production, and vortex structure evolution, through the joint analysis of local entropy production rate distributions and vortex identification using the Q-criterion. The optimization yields notable improvements: the hydraulic efficiency of the first-stage impeller increases from 78.42% to 81.83%; total entropy production under design conditions decreases by 8.63%; and entropy production within the first-stage guide vanes decreases by 45.23% at 1.2 times the design flow rate. Crucially, the second-stage impeller geometry remains unchanged, confirming that first-stage optimization propagates performance gains to all downstream stages through the interstage flow-matching mechanism. By limiting the scope of hydraulic modification from the full pump assembly to a single stage, the proposed framework establishes a practical pathway for low-cost hydraulic optimization of multistage molten salt pumps.

title: Effect of Gas Composition on Aerodynamic Performance and Internal Flow of Ethane Oxidation Dehydrogenation Centrifugal Compressor
summary: Effect of gas composition on aerodynamic performance and internal flow in ethane oxidation dehydrogenation (ODH) centrifugal compressors is investigated. Although inert gases are widely used to reduce explosion risk in ODH processes, the ef
content: Effect of gas composition on aerodynamic performance and internal flow in ethane oxidation dehydrogenation (ODH) centrifugal compressors is investigated. Although inert gases are widely used to reduce explosion risk in ODH processes, the effects of multi-component inert gases on compression thermodynamics and internal flow structures are not fully understood. The novelty of this work lies in a systematic quantification of how different inert-gas compositions change the evolution of internal flow, thereby influencing the loss mechanisms and isentropic efficiency in a high-pressure ODH environment. Three gas mixtures are evaluated: Mixture 1 (C2H6 55%, O2 15%, CO2 15%, 10%, H2 5%), Mixture 2 (C2H6 55%, O2 18%, CO2 10%, 7%, He 5%, N2 5%), and Mixture 3 (C2H6 53%, O2 18%, CO2 8%, N2 15%, 6%). Numerical simulations are conducted using a steady-state mean streamline model coupled with the SST turbulence model. The isentropic efficiency varies non-monotonically with mass flow rate, staying nearly constant from 6.5 to 7.1 kg/s and then decreasing markedly. Detailed flow analysis shows that low-density gases such as H2 and He promote leakage flow and flow separation, increasing energy dissipation; in contrast, N2 reduces separation-related losses. Compared with Mixture 1, the isentropic efficiency increases by 21.65% for Mixture 2 and further improves by 30.25% for Mixture 3 (a cumulative increase of 8.6% over Mixture 2). Overall, the results provide quantitative trends and mechanistic understanding of multi-component inert-gas effects on compressor performance, which can help researchers evaluate and design safer ODH compression systems and motivate further studies under other inert-gas combinations and operating conditions.

title: Capillary-driven Water Transport in Microfiber Textiles: Experimental Characterization and Application in a High-efficiency Multi-stage Passive Solar Desalination
summary: Given the escalating water and energy crises worldwide, the development of passive desalination systems has become inevitable. Among various approaches, particular attention has been directed toward capillary-driven systems, yet despite num
content: Given the escalating water and energy crises worldwide, the development of passive desalination systems has become inevitable. Among various approaches, particular attention has been directed toward capillary-driven systems, yet despite numerous studies in this field, selecting textiles with optimal capillary and evaporative properties remains a key research challenge. Unlike prior studies, this research for the first time systematically evaluates and compares the wicking performance of two distinct microfiber textile structures (woven (A) vs. brushed knit (B)) with capillary-related properties of the textiles for application in multi-stage passive solar desalination systems. Furthermore, this study introduces a new figure of merit, the Water Turnover Ratio (WTR), to assess textile suitability for wick‑based multi‑stage solar desalination, and establishes a clear structure–property–performance relationship for this application. A single-stage desalination system was constructed and the results showed that sample B exhibited a 19% higher Recovery Ratio and an 18.8% higher WTR compared to sample A. Consequently, the sample B is identified as a suitable candidate for passive desalination systems due to its superior performance. Subsequently, this textile was used to construct multi-stage desalination system. Results demonstrated a freshwater collection rate of 2.77 l/m²h and a gained output ratio (GOR) of 189% for the 5-stage system under a 1000 W/m² heat flux. Finally, an empirical correlation was proposed and validated to predict the freshwater production of the multi‑stage system over a wide range of operating conditions. The findings indicate that this system, with its low manufacturing cost, holds significant potential for use in remote areas.

title: Calcination-Induced Structural Evolution of Nickel Phosphate and Its Impact on Charge-Storage Kinetics
summary: Supercapattery performance is governed by the intrinsic properties of its electrode materials, particularly the relationship between microstructure and electrochemical behaviour. In a previous study, amorphous nickel phosphate (NP) has show
content: Supercapattery performance is governed by the intrinsic properties of its electrode materials, particularly the relationship between microstructure and electrochemical behaviour. In a previous study, amorphous nickel phosphate (NP) has shown superior electrochemical performance as a battery-type electrode despite the common expectation that crystalline materials perform better in electrochemical response. In this work, NP was synthesized via a sonochemical route and its crystallinity was modulated by varying calcination temperatures. At lower calcination temperatures (300–600 ºC), NPs remain predominantly amorphous but turn crystalline when higher temperatures are applied. The thermal treatment also influenced the degree of hydration, particle morphology and pore structure. Among all temperatures, NP calcined at lower temperatures delivered the higher specific capacity and showed predominantly diffusion-influenced Faradaic kinetics. In contrast, NP calcined at higher temperatures showed lower specific capacity, but a stronger surface-control contribution to charge storage. These findings demonstrate that a high degree of crystallinity does not necessarily guarantee high charge-storage capacity and reveal a clear trade-off between active-site utilization and reaction kinetics during the amorphous to crystalline evolution of NP.

title: Surface characterization and adsorption mechanism of carboxymethyl cellulose for cadmium(II) removal from aqueous solution
summary: A comprehensive analytical investigation was undertaken into the mechanistic process behind the adsorption of cadmium (II) onto the carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectrosc
content: A comprehensive analytical investigation was undertaken into the mechanistic process behind the adsorption of cadmium (II) onto the carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), equilibrium isotherm modeling, and adsorption kinetic analysis. The batch experiments were done under the previously optimized conditions (contact time = 50 min, pH = 6, T = 25 °C, C∘ = 20 mg/L, adsorbent dose = 1 g/L), at which the reference removal efficiency was 88%, and the equilibrium adsorption capacity was 17.6 mg/g. FTIR studies showed that the adsorption of Cd(II) led to a characteristic shift of the asymmetric (–COO⁻) stretching band from 1622.13 to 1608.63 cm-1, which is consistent with surface complexation between Cd(II) and the carboxymethyl functional groups of CMC. The presence of new sharp diffraction peaks in the XRD spectra of the Cd(II) loaded CMC was indicative of deposition of crystalline cadmium-containing phases over the adsorbent surface, and the SEM images showed a significant morphological change from an open fibrous network to a close-packed lamellar structure with near-cubic crystalline surface deposits. The Freundlich isotherm (R2 = 0.997, and RMSE = 0.612 mg/g) was the best model to define the equilibrium data, while the Langmuir model yielding a theoretical maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of qmax = 35.0 mg/g and separation factor RL = 0.091, indicating favorable adsorption within the Langmuir model framework. The pseudo-second-order model best fit the data gotten from kinetic analysis, with R2 = 0.998 and (qe)cal = 18.87 mg/g, which indicates that is consistent with a chemisorption-dominated mechanism and is consistent with the FTIR mechanistic evidence. A non-zero intraparticle diffusion intercept confirmed the multi-step rate control that included film and pore diffusion. Convergent evidence of all the characterization and modeling methods confirms that CMC is a well-defined, mechanistically effective, and biodegradable adsorbent, as reported in the literature, for the remediation of Cd(II) in contaminated water systems.

title: Imparting physiological resilience in wheat through potassium-regulated antioxidant adjustments under drought stress
summary: Under changing agroecological conditions, identification of high-yielding genotypes and imparting drought resilience in wheat through physiological adjustments are imperative for sustained wheat productivity and to ensure food security. In
content: Under changing agroecological conditions, identification of high-yielding genotypes and imparting drought resilience in wheat through physiological adjustments are imperative for sustained wheat productivity and to ensure food security. In this study, different doses of foliar-applied potassium (K), including 2% (8.98 g K per liter of water), 4% (17.96 g K per liter of water), and 6% (26.94 g K per liter of water) using K2SO4 (45% elemental K) were tested for growth parameters (length, fresh and dry weights of root and shoot), photosynthetic pigments, and antioxidant (ascorbate peroxidase APX, catalase CAT, peroxidase POD, and superoxide dismutase SOD) responses of promising wheat cultivars (Akbar and Ghazi) during the tillering stage under DS (40% of field capacity). The results revealed that foliar-applied K at 6% concentration was consistently superior, especially for the Akbar cultivar, by recording 75%, 57%, and 50% greater root length, root fresh and dry weights, respectively, than the control. The same combination (Akbar cultivar receiving 6% K) also markedly improved shoot length (42%), fresh weight (31%), and dry weight (66%) compared to the control. Regarding photosynthetic pigments, 6% K improved chlorophyll a (93%), chlorophyll b (51%), total chlorophyll (66%), and carotenoids compared to the control treatment (no K supplementation), indicating improved photosynthetic efficiency and enhanced plant vitality. Moreover, this treatment also enhanced the activity of APX (77%), CAT (107%), POD (101%), and SOD (43%) in the Akbar cultivar compared to the control. Based on the findings of this study, foliar application of K at 6% concentration may be recommended as a promising strategy to mitigate the deleterious effects of drought by enhancing the biosynthesis of photosynthetic pigments and antioxidants, particularly in drought-tolerant cultivars of wheat.

title: Sustainable soil stabilisation using recycled concrete fines for resource recovery from construction and demolition waste: A Ukrainian case study
summary: The accumulation of construction and demolition waste requires resource-efficient and scalable solutions based on the principles of the circular economy and the use of low-carbon materials. This study investigated the effectiveness of the i
content: The accumulation of construction and demolition waste requires resource-efficient and scalable solutions based on the principles of the circular economy and the use of low-carbon materials. This study investigated the effectiveness of the integrated application of recycled concrete fines (RCF) in the stabilisation of two soil types differing in their particle size distribution and mineralogical composition. RCF was utilised as a granulometric correction material, a microfiller, and a component of a low-carbon slag binder. The positive effect of co-grinding ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) with 20 wt.% RCF on the microstructure development and mechanical properties of the low-carbon slag binder for soil stabilisation was demonstrated. The compaction characteristics determined using the Modified Proctor test, mechanical properties, water resistance, freeze–thaw resistance, and phase formation of soils stabilised with a reference mixture containing 10 wt.% Portland cement (PC) and the developed low-carbon slag binder were investigated. A differentiated approach to the application of RCF depending on the soil particle size distribution was substantiated. RCF in the fine sand fraction proved to be the most effective for highly plastic soils, whereas ground RCF with a specific surface area of 3000 cm²/g was the most effective microfiller for soils with a higher sand content and a lower clay fraction. The developed low-carbon slag binder was shown to enable the effective partial replacement of PC in soil stabilisation. Furthermore, the mineralogical composition of the soil was found to govern the phase formation processes in stabilised soils. The obtained results confirm the potential of the integrated use of RCF and the developed low-carbon slag binder for resource-efficient soil stabilisation and the recycling of construction and demolition waste in geotechnical engineering.

title: Associations of redox conditions and organic matter with nickel and chromium partitioning in the Bahodopi River, a tropical lateritic mining river in Central Sulawesi
summary: Lateritic nickel mining can increase the transport of metal-bearing particles into river systems, where sediment–water partitioning governs metal mobility and ecological exposure. Although redox conditions and organic matter are recognized
content: Lateritic nickel mining can increase the transport of metal-bearing particles into river systems, where sediment–water partitioning governs metal mobility and ecological exposure. Although redox conditions and organic matter are recognized as factors associated with metal partitioning, their relative importance under tropical lateritic mining conditions remains poorly understood. This study examined associations between redox-related and organic matter-related variables and nickel (Ni) and chromium (Cr) partitioning between sediment and water at nine stations along the Bahodopi River, Indonesia, sampled during the dry season, using log-transformed distribution coefficients (logKd). Oxidation–reduction potential (ORP) showed the strongest association with Ni partitioning (ρ = 0.756, p = 0.018), while sediment organic matter showed the strongest association with Cr partitioning (ρ = 0.689, p = 0.040), sediment Fe/Mn ratio and dissolved organic carbon showed weak, non-significant associations with either metal. However, because ORP and logKd both increased with distance from the upstream station, partial correlation analysis showed that the ORP–logKd association weakened substantially and lost significance once this spatial trend was accounted for, indicating that spatial confounding contributed to the observed relationship. Multiple regression models explained a large share of variance in logKd for both metals, although only the Ni model was statistically significant, and diagnostics showed that model fit was disproportionately influenced by a small number of stations. These findings suggest that Ni and Cr partitioning may be associated with different environmental variables in this system, but given the small number of stations, single sampling campaign, and evidence of spatial confounding, these associations should be regarded as preliminary and warrant confirmation through spatially and temporally replicated sampling.

title: Yield responses of multi-crops to interaction of manure and microbial bio-fertiliser in a Surjan raised-bed intercropping system on rainfed drylands
summary: The intercropping cultivation system on rainfed land during the dry season often faces water availability constraints and declining soil fertility, which negatively affect crop productivity. The use of manure and liquid bio-fertilisers is o
content: The intercropping cultivation system on rainfed land during the dry season often faces water availability constraints and declining soil fertility, which negatively affect crop productivity. The use of manure and liquid bio-fertilisers is one approach to increase the soil’s organic matter content and microbiological activity, thereby improving nutrient availability for plants. This study aimed to analyse the effects of manure and liquid bio-fertiliser dosages, determine the optimum doses of these two inputs, and evaluate their interaction on the yield of five crop commodities in an intercropping system on rainfed land during the dry season. The results showed that crop response to the treatments was commodity-specific. The highest Cucumis sativus L. yield (23.1 t ha⁻¹) was obtained with a combination of 25 t ha⁻¹ manure and 3 L ha⁻¹ liquid bio-fertiliser. In comparison, butternut squash achieved a maximum yield of 15.0 t ha⁻¹ with a combination of 15 t ha⁻¹ manure and 3 L ha⁻¹ liquid bio-fertiliser. For Capsicum frutescens L., the highest yield (0.146 t ha⁻¹) was achieved with a combination of 25 t ha⁻¹ manure and 6 L ha⁻¹ liquid bio-fertiliser. In comparison, Vigna unguiculata L. produced its highest yield (0.70 t ha⁻¹) with the same combination. For Ipomoea aquatica F., the highest biomass yield (6.3 t ha⁻¹) was obtained with a combination of 25 t ha⁻¹ manure and 3 L ha⁻¹ liquid bio-fertiliser. Optimisation analysis indicated that Cucumis sativus L. and butternut squash yields followed a quadratic pattern, with optimum liquid bio-fertiliser dosages of approximately 2.88 L ha⁻¹ and 3.14 L ha⁻¹, respectively. In comparison, the optimum manure dosage for butternut squash was estimated to be approximately 15.19 t ha⁻¹. At the system scale, the intercrop was advantageous under every treatment (LER 1.75–2.95, mean 2.07; ATER 1.30–2.20), with cucumber acting as the dominant component. These results indicate that integrating manure and liquid bio-fertilizers increases the productivity of intercropping systems by improving soil organic matter content and microbial activity under rainfed conditions during the dry season.

title: Trade-Offs in Statistical and Machine-Learning-Based Imputation for Algal Time-Series: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation on Optical Density Data Without Ground Truth
summary: Missing values are pervasive in algal cultivation monitoring, where instrument failure and transmission loss remove whole runs of consecutive observations, and the repair method chosen silently shapes every downstream analysis. This study a
content: Missing values are pervasive in algal cultivation monitoring, where instrument failure and transmission loss remove whole runs of consecutive observations, and the repair method chosen silently shapes every downstream analysis. This study asks which repair method should be used, and on what evidence, when no complete reference series exists. Twelve methods are compared on optical density and ten covariates recorded across 30 open-pond production cycles at five geographically distinct sites: four interpolation schemes, a propagation scheme, two nearest-neighbour schemes, three chained-equation variants, a random-forest ensemble and a mechanistic growth-curve fit. The principal contribution is a validation framework organised in two clearly separate tiers. The first tier needs no ground truth and applies to the naturally missing values, comparing central tendency, dispersion, distributional shape, autocorrelation structure and coverage between observed and repaired series. The second tier withholds values that were in fact recorded and rebuilds them, so reconstruction error can be measured directly; it is replicated over ten random seeds, three masking proportions and four contiguous outage lengths, giving 25,200 paired evaluations in which every method sees an identical pattern of withhold cells. Key findings found that no method dominates. Ensemble and chained-equation learners rebuild individual values most accurately, with a normalised error of 0.1927 against 0.2645 for linear interpolation, but they compress dispersion and distort distributional shape, whereas shape-preserving interpolation and propagation protect those properties and rebuild less accurately. Gap structure matters: interpolation loses accuracy when gaps are contiguous rather than scattered, while multivariate learners gain. Regularising the chained equations removes a convergence failure that left one pond unrepaired. An aggregated decision analysis turns these trade-offs into a weight-dependent selection rule, giving practitioners an auditable basis for matching method to analytical objective instead of a single universal default.

title: Dynamics of carbon mineralization and in situ nutrient turnover in soil amended with anaerobic digestate
summary: Anaerobic digestate (AD) is an increasingly prominent component of circular agriculture, yet its rapid biogeochemical effects require nuanced evaluation across laboratory and field settings. This study integrated a fully controlled 28-day s
content: Anaerobic digestate (AD) is an increasingly prominent component of circular agriculture, yet its rapid biogeochemical effects require nuanced evaluation across laboratory and field settings. This study integrated a fully controlled 28-day soil incubation with an in situ longitudinal field tracking trial (15 m³·ha⁻¹ AD applied prior to winter wheat cultivation) to assess organic carbon mineralization kinetics and seasonal nutrient dynamics. In the incubation experiment, AD addition triggered an immediate acceleration of carbon mineralization, doubling the mineralization rate constant (k = 0.41 day-1 vs. 0.19 day-1 in the unamended control) and significantly reducing the biological carbon half-life from 3.7 to 1.7 days. In the field, the immediate post-application phase (Day 14, Term II) was marked by a transient flush of available N (+25%) and S (+67%), confirming rapid early-stage nutrient mobilization. Across the 295-day seasonal cycle (culminating after crop harvest in Term IV), the soil exhibited significant increases in organic matter, available P, and exchangeable K, alongside a pH shift from 7.0 to 7.5 and a reduction in bioavailable Fe and Mn. Because the field component employed a longitudinal baseline-tracking design, late-season nutrient and carbon increments represent the combined legacy of AD conditioning, ambient seasonal dynamics, and crop rhizosphere turnover. These findings demonstrate that AD serves as an active organic-mineral conditioner, optimizing early nutrient supply while supporting the progressive restructuring of the soil sorption complex over the cropping season.

title: Enzymatic green removal of anisidines from wastewater using partially purified Phaseolus vulgaris peroxidase
summary: Crude green bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) peroxidase (GBP) was extracted from fresh pods and partially purified. Following ammonium sulfate fractionation, dialysis, ion-exchange chromatography (DEAE-cellulose), and finally gel filtration, t
content: Crude green bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) peroxidase (GBP) was extracted from fresh pods and partially purified. Following ammonium sulfate fractionation, dialysis, ion-exchange chromatography (DEAE-cellulose), and finally gel filtration, the specific activity obtained was 40.8 U mg⁻¹ corresponding to a purification fold of 32.9 and yield of 49.35%. An enzyme activity assay was optimized and maximal activity was reached in the dark, at pH 7.5 and 25 °C; kinetic studies based on substrate variation showed a Km value of 0.064 mM, with a Vmax of 4.91 U mL⁻¹. Anisidine removal by GBP was studied in batch reactor experiments. At H₂O₂ of 0.2 mM, and at enzyme activity of 3.1 U mL⁻¹, > 95% removal was achieved within 3 h for both p-anisidine (at pH = 4.5) and o-anisidine (at pH = 5.5). Pseudo-first-order kinetics demonstrated speedy degradation within the initial 30 minutes, exhibiting rate constants of 3.93 × 10⁻² min⁻¹ for p-anisidine and 3.54 × 10⁻² min⁻¹ for o-anisidine, with corresponding half-lives of 17.6 and 19.6 minutes. Subsequent to 180 minutes, the rates diminished and the half-lives extended to 26.3 and 36.3 minutes. A 95 Eco-Scale score indicates a highly sustainable procedure utilizing plant-based peroxidase under moderate, a solvent-free for anisidine removal.

title: Temporal eligibility rules alter country composition and ecoregion representation in global river water-quality monitoring networks
summary: Temporal eligibility can reorganize a monitoring archive in directions that station loss alone does not predict. We characterized this instability in Caravan-Qual Lite version 1.1 over 2000–2020 using six constituents, country labels, 426 f
content: Temporal eligibility can reorganize a monitoring archive in directions that station loss alone does not predict. We characterized this instability in Caravan-Qual Lite version 1.1 over 2000–2020 using six constituents, country labels, 426 freshwater ecoregions, seven realms and Hill numbers q=0, 1 and 2. The primary rule retained 14,387 electrical-conductivity stations (Cohort A) and 4,373 stations jointly eligible for conductivity, phosphorus and dissolved oxygen (Cohort B). Across three-, five- and ten-year requirements, dissolved organic carbon lost 90.7% of stations while ecoregion q=2 increased from 3.909 to 6.594. Electrical conductivity and total phosphorus also gained q=2 ecoregion representation at selected thresholds, whereas dissolved oxygen declined across countries, ecoregions and realms. Nitrate and suspended solids realm q=2 rose slightly from three to five years before falling at ten. Thus comparable attrition did not imply a common geographic response. Equal-size references were treated as descriptive baselines rather than exchangeability tests. In Cohort B, ecoregion q=0 was 10.8% below its equal-size median while q=2 was 46.1% above it; a +0.5% within-country q=2 residual showed that the apparent evenness excess followed country composition, whereas the q=0 deficit persisted. Tightening seasonal coverage to all four quarters removed 40.1% of Cohort B stations and nine ecoregions and shifted country leverage. Temporal rules therefore changed country composition and FEOW representation in constituent- and order-specific ways that station retention alone could not summarize.

title: The effect of urea addition on biogas production from beneng taro starch wastewater
summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) applied to Beneng taro starch wastewater (BTSW) presents an attractive route for combining wastewater treatment with renewable energy recovery. Nevertheless, biogas generation from this type of substrate is often co
content: Anaerobic digestion (AD) applied to Beneng taro starch wastewater (BTSW) presents an attractive route for combining wastewater treatment with renewable energy recovery. Nevertheless, biogas generation from this type of substrate is often constrained because carbohydrate-dominated wastewater tends to contain insufficient nitrogen to support optimal microbial function. Accordingly, this study was designed to determine how nitrogen supplementation through urea influences the performance of AD when BTSW serves as the substrate. The experiment was performed in 500 mL batch digesters using a substrate and inoculum mixture at a volumetric ratio of 80:20. Urea concentrations of 0, 100, 150, 200, and 250 mg/L were evaluated, while FeCl 3 was maintained at 60 mg/L. Among these treatments, the 150 mg/L urea dose gave the largest cumulative biogas output (187.86 mL/g-TS substrate ), roughly triple that of the untreated control, and also produced the greatest methane yield (54.39 mL CH4/g-TS substrate ), the smallest buildup of VFAs, and the strongest reductions in TS (32.69%), TSS (33.33%), and TDS (32.10%). Kinetic evaluation with the modified Gompertz equation further confirmed this outcome, showing a very close fit to the experimental data (R 2 = 0.9979) and the largest P m value (187.90 mL/g-TS substrate ) among all treatments. Overall, these outcomes point to 150 mg/L as the most suitable urea dose for supplying nitrogen during BTSW digestion and for maximizing biogas output.

title: Fouling-regeneration mechanisms and life time prediction of rice husk-derived low-cost ceramic membranes for pretreatment-asssisted peat water treatment
summary: Peat water treatment is limited by high dissolved organic matter, acidity, colour, and membrane fouling. The fouling–regeneration behaviour and operational lifetime of a rice husk-derived low-cost ceramic membrane used after sequential pret
content: Peat water treatment is limited by high dissolved organic matter, acidity, colour, and membrane fouling. The fouling–regeneration behaviour and operational lifetime of a rice husk-derived low-cost ceramic membrane used after sequential pretreatment were investigated in this study. The tubular membrane was prepared from natural clay, rice husk activated carbon, and Fe₂O₃ at 82.5 : 15.0 : 2.5 wt.% and sintered at 900°C. The membrane was characterized by SEM-EDS, elemental mapping, XRD, TGA, image analysis and Archimedes method. Peat water was pretreated by sedimentation, slow-sand filtration, sponge filtration and activated-carbon adsorption before membrane filtration at 2 bar. Six filtration–backwashing cycles were performed, and fouling was interpreted by using the classical Hermia models. The membrane showed a heterogeneous porous structure with an average porosity of 47.927% and a high thermal stability. Turbidity, colour, Fe, Mn and nitrite were removed to the extent of 98.87%, 91.05%, 98.00%, 97.10% and 99.92% respectively and removal of detectable E. coli and total coliform was achieved by the integrated system. Fouling developed from internal pore constriction to cake layer formation and more serious pore blocking. The backwashing hydraulic flow reached 95.60-94.23% of flux recovery ratios. However, the irreversible fouling increased from 4.40 to 5.77% and the filtration time decreased from 77 to 13 h. Recovered flux followed Jn/J0 = e[-0.0498(n-1)] with R2 = 0.9958. Membrane lifetime was estimated to be 8.17 cycles or 211 h at 70% end-of-life threshold. The membrane thus provides high quality peat water polishing, but requires increased periodic cleaning to limit the accumulation of irreversible fouling.

title: Reactive dyes adsorption by chestnut shells coated with nanoparticles of zinc oxide: Characterization, isotherm and kinetic studies
summary: This investigation employed a new adsorbent composed of chestnut shell powder and covered with ZnO nanoparticles. Coated chestnut shell (CCS) was examined to assess adsorption of Reactive Blue-19 Dye and Red Reactive-2 from water-based mixt
content: This investigation employed a new adsorbent composed of chestnut shell powder and covered with ZnO nanoparticles. Coated chestnut shell (CCS) was examined to assess adsorption of Reactive Blue-19 Dye and Red Reactive-2 from water-based mixture. Considerable increases in the capability of adsorption of the chestnut shell were recognized following the coating of the powder particles with ZnO the nanoparticles. The adsorbent was surface area analysis, FTIR, SEM, and XRD to verify its structural and morphological properties. Batch adsorption Research was done to ascertain the optimum Situations, including solution the pH, adsorbent dosage, contact period, speed of shaking, and initial dye concentration, every conducted at room temperature, which is 25 °C. Both the Freundlich and Langmuir isotherm models were used to describe the equilibrium information on adsorption. As a result revealed that the process of adsorption followed Langmuir's isotherm model, using correlation values (R²) for 0.9886 for Reactive Red-2 and 0.9955 for Reactive Blue-19, demonstrating monolayer adsorption onto a uniform surface. The greatest CCS adsorption capacity was observed for Reactive Blue-19 (172.413 mg/g), followed by Reactive Red-2 (114.942 mg/g). Kinetic information was correlated using both pseudo-first-order and pseudo-second-order models. The findings demonstrated that the model of pseudo-second order gave greater results compared to the pseudo-first order model, considering correlation coefficients (R²) of 0.9951 for Reactive Red-2 and 0.9975for Reactive Blue-19, demonstrating that the process of chemisorption step that limits rate of adsorption mechanism. Thus, these results show that CCS is among the best and most efficient adsorbents for getting rid of wastewater tainted with reactive dye residues.

title: Effect of the cross-section on the energy absorption and bending behavior of bent tubes
source: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
summary: When a bent tube is subjected to transverse load, it has the capacity to resolve this load into both axial and bending components, allowing the structure to achieve a combined stress state. This confers higher structural efficiency compared
content: When a bent tube is subjected to transverse load, it has the capacity to resolve this load into both axial and bending components, allowing the structure to achieve a combined stress state. This confers higher structural efficiency compared with straight tubes. The crashworthiness performance of bent tubes depends on multiple factors such as material, configuration, and geometric parameters. However, studies on the cross-section of bent tubes have rarely been reported, despite their superior performance than their straight counterparts under bending loads. The current article first evaluates the mechanical response of a straight tube versus a bent tube. Subsequently, a second numerical analysis evaluates the effect of the cross-section on the bending resistance and energy absorption of bent tubes. For this purpose, five bent tubes with different cross-sections, including circular, triangular, square and rectangular shapes, were numerically evaluated using three-point bending tests. In all cases, the bent tubes had the same geometric characteristics and mass. During the simulations, the tubes were assigned an elastoplastic material model for aluminum alloy 6063-T5. The reliability of the numerical results was confirmed through the experimental validation of a circular straight tube subjected to a three-point bending test. According to the results, the effectiveness of the bent tube with respect to the straight tube was confirmed, with an E a improvement of 22.84%. Furthermore, the importance of the cross-section in the crashworthiness performance of bent tubes was demonstrated. The best crashworthiness performance was with the circular cross-section, which achieved a CFE value of 0.87 representing a 13.14% improvement with respect to the lowest CFE obtained for the rectangular bent profile (BR-01).

title: Preparation of silver nanoparticles using microwave plasma jet and study of their physicochemical properties and applications in photocatalysis
source: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
summary: Microwave plasma is considered a crucial engineering technology and an effective method for preparing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with controllable properties, thereby opening up numerous possibilities for their application in environmenta
content: Microwave plasma is considered a crucial engineering technology and an effective method for preparing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with controllable properties, thereby opening up numerous possibilities for their application in environmental remediation and water treatment technologies. The structural and optical characteristics of the prepared AgNPs, as well as their photocatalytic activity toward methylene blue dye degradation, were investigated. AgNPs were prepared using a microwave plasma system at operating voltages of 150, 160, and 170 V. Plasma diagnostics based on the Boltzmann plot revealed that increasing the applied voltage gradually increased the electron temperature (Te) from 4.02 to 6.13 eV. UV–Vis analysis confirmed the formation of silver nanoparticles through the appearance of the characteristic absorption band in the 290–300 nm range. X-ray diffraction (XRD) results revealed the formation of pure metallic silver (Ag) phases at 150 and 160 V, while mixed phases of silver and silver oxide (Ag/AgO) were observed at 170 V due to increased plasma activity and partial surface oxidation of the particles. Additionally, the average crystallite sizes of 18.7 nm at 150 V, 12 nm at 160 V, and 11.6 nm at 170 V indicate an improvement in crystallinity and a reduction in crystallite size. The results showed that 160 V achieved the best efficiency in dye degradation, recording the highest kinetic rate constant (k = 0.0602 min⁻¹) compared to 150 V and 170 V, indicating that this voltage provided a better balance between particle size, activity, and effective surface area, with the highest photodegradation efficiency of 97.5%. These results confirm that the microwave plasma system at atmospheric pressure is an effective and controllable engineering technique for producing highly efficient silver nanoparticles, making it promising for photocatalytic applications and the treatment of organic pollutants in water.

title: Exercise Heart Rate and DFAa1 Dynamics 24 and 48 h Following Unaccustomed High-Intensity Interval Running: An Exploratory Study of Recovery Responses
source: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
summary: This study investigates exercise heart rate (HR) and the utility of the short-term scaling exponent alpha1 of Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFAa1) within a monitoring battery to assess residual fatigue. In this exploratory repeated-measur
content: This study investigates exercise heart rate (HR) and the utility of the short-term scaling exponent alpha1 of Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFAa1) within a monitoring battery to assess residual fatigue. In this exploratory repeated-measures study, recreationally active females (n = 11) and males (n = 21) completed four laboratory visits. After one familiarization session and a second baseline visit (PRE), participants completed two unaccustomed high-intensity interval running (HIIT) sessions without a non-HIIT control group, followed by assessments at the third visit (POST24h) and additional follow-up testing at the fourth visit (POST48h). At PRE, POST24h, and POST48h, participants completed a monitoring battery comprising force production (isometric and dynamic strength), recovery-stress scales (ARSS), and a 10-min standardized submaximal cycling bout for assessment of exercise HR and DFAa1, followed by a ramp test to volitional exhaustion. ARSS scales indicated impaired overall recovery (p < 0.001, η2p = 0.53) and increased muscular stress (p < 0.001, η2p = 0.57), accompanied by reduced maximal isometric knee extensor strength (p = 0.001, η2p = 0.20) at POST24h and POST48h. Submaximal testing showed a main effect for HR (p < 0.001, η2p = 0.10), with lower values at POST48h versus PRE. DFAa1 demonstrated reduced values at POST24h (p = 0.003, η2p = 0.08). In the ramp test, HRPEAK was lower at POST48h (p = 0.004, η2p = 0.17). Analysis of HR and DFAa1 kinetics during ramp testing revealed lower HR values (p < 0.05) during the intensity spectrum at POST24h and POST48h, and higher DFAa1 values (p < 0.05) at the beginning of the ramp at POST48h. While neuromuscular performance and subjective recovery-stress responses remained impaired at 48h, the autonomic responses may be compatible with a shift toward recovery, this interpretation remains exploratory given the limited and localized DFAa1 differences. These findings support the need for multidimensional and individualized interpretation of exercise HR and DFAa1 responses when monitoring recovery.

title: Spatial measurement based threshold determination for polygon simplification using the Douglas-Peucker algorithm
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Forest and land fires occur almost annually in Indonesia, with hotspots serving as key indicators. Identifying high-risk areas requires visualizing hotspot distribution using polygons at the village level, covering 83,971 villages according
content: Forest and land fires occur almost annually in Indonesia, with hotspots serving as key indicators. Identifying high-risk areas requires visualizing hotspot distribution using polygons at the village level, covering 83,971 villages according to the Statistics Indonesia (BPS) in 2023. To enhance visualization efficiency, polygon simplification is necessary. Hotspot distribution at the village level is analyzed using an online analytical processing (OLAP) system. This study aims to determine an optimal threshold for polygon simplification. The success criteria include the number of coordinate (NuC) points, hotspot count, and GeoJSON file size. Village polygon and hotspot data were obtained from the Geospatial Information Agency (BIG) and MODIS FIRE, covering January 1, 2013 to December 31, 2023. The methodology consists of threshold determination using perimeter, area, and bounding box diagonal metrics; polygon simplification with the Douglas-Peucker (DP) algorithm; and spatial operations on hotspots and village polygons. Threshold values range from 0.05% to 0.25%. The results show that the optimal threshold is 0.15%, preserving most coordinates, maintaining hotspot count stability, and reducing the GeoJSON file size from 49.998 MB to

title: Grid search-based LDA optimization for agricultural topic discovery and intertopic distance map visualization
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Agricultural research has generated a substantial volume of scientific publications, yet this corpus remains underutilized for systematically identifying major research topics and thematic structures. This study aims to identify dominant to
content: Agricultural research has generated a substantial volume of scientific publications, yet this corpus remains underutilized for systematically identifying major research topics and thematic structures. This study aims to identify dominant topics in agricultural publications from 2012 to 2023 using latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) with systematic hyperparameter tuning and intertopic distance map visualization. An exploratory quantitative approach was applied to 75,031 publications retrieved from Scopus, ProQuest, and Web of Science (WoS). The analysis involved text preprocessing, phrase modeling, dictionary and corpus construction, and LDA topic modeling. An exhaustive grid search over a discretized parameter space identified a 17 topic model with alpha=0.1, beta=0.70, and a coherence score of 0.5075, followed by interactive visualization using pyLDAvis. The results revealed six major thematic groups: agricultural practices and food systems; data analysis applications; plant production and growth factors; environmental and land-use changes; effects and sample analysis; and plant genetics under environmental pressures. The findings demonstrate that LDA combined with systematic parameter tuning can reveal latent thematic structures and clarify relationships among agricultural research topics. The study provides a data-driven basis for exploratory mapping of research directions, while temporal trend evolution and direct policy implications require further longitudinal analysis.

title: Thermal image-based fault identification of induction motors using image features
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Three-phase induction motors are widely used in industrial systems, making reliable fault identification essential for safe and efficient operation. This study presents a non-contact thermal image-based approach for preliminary fault identi
content: Three-phase induction motors are widely used in industrial systems, making reliable fault identification essential for safe and efficient operation. This study presents a non-contact thermal image-based approach for preliminary fault identification of three-phase induction motors using interpretable image features and classification analysis. Thermal images of healthy and faulty motors were acquired under different load levels and processed using hue, saturation, and value (HSV) color-space transformation, hue-based analysis, and Otsu segmentation. Five image features, namely mean, mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), variance, and standard deviation (SD), were extracted to characterize thermal responses. The results show clear differences between healthy and faulty conditions, with faulty motors producing higher feature values and more prominent hotspots. For the four-bar rotor fault, maximum temperature increased from 26.6 °C at no load to 63.4 °C at full load. Classification performance also improved with increasing load, although overall performance remained limited. These findings demonstrate the potential of thermal imaging for non-contact induction motor condition monitoring and predictive maintenance.

title: Hybrid SNGNN–BKOA framework for intelligent congestion management in renewable-integrated power systems
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: The rapid integration of renewable energy sources (RES), such as wind and solar, introduces significant variability and uncertainty in modern power systems, which often leads to transmission congestion and operational inefficiencies. This p
content: The rapid integration of renewable energy sources (RES), such as wind and solar, introduces significant variability and uncertainty in modern power systems, which often leads to transmission congestion and operational inefficiencies. This paper proposes a hybrid congestion management framework that combines a similarity-navigated graph neural network (SNGNN) with the black-winged kite optimization algorithm (BKOA). The SNGNN model captures complex spatial relationships within the power network to accurately forecast load demand, while BKOA optimizes congestion mitigation by coordinating generator rescheduling and energy storage system (ESS) operations. The proposed framework was evaluated through MATLAB simulations under different renewable penetration levels. Results demonstrate that the SNGNN–BKOA approach achieves superior performance compared with benchmark algorithms such as grey wolf optimizer (GWO) and salp swarm algorithm (SSA). The proposed method reduces system power loss to 48.4 MW, achieves a forecasting RMSE of 0.164%, and lowers congestion mitigation costs to $5800.09/h at 10% renewable penetration and $6823.71/h at 40% penetration. These results indicate that the proposed hybrid learning–optimization framework improves grid stability, reduces operational cost, and enhances decision-making for congestion management in renewable-dominated smart grids.

title: Enhancing maggot farming with an internet of things-enabled watering and monitoring system
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Black soldier fly (BSF) maggot cultivation is a high-efficiency approach to organic waste bioconversion and sustainable protein production; however, productivity is critically sensitive to temperature and humidity, which are poorly regulate
content: Black soldier fly (BSF) maggot cultivation is a high-efficiency approach to organic waste bioconversion and sustainable protein production; however, productivity is critically sensitive to temperature and humidity, which are poorly regulated under conventional manual practices that are labor-intensive, error-prone, and unresponsive to environmental fluctuations. This study implements an internet of things (IoT)-enabled watering and monitoring system for BSF maggot farming, integrating an SHT20 sensor, ESP32 microcontroller, and three actuators (water pump, heating bulb, and blower fan). The system operates in two modes: manual mode via Telegram Bot API, and automatic mode governed by a Mamdani fuzzy logic inference engine with nine IF–THEN rules. Sensor accuracy was validated across 12 trials (22.5-43.8 °C; 45-89% RH). Mean temperature accuracy of 99.13% (error: 0.87%, SD:0.58%) and mean humidity accuracy of 99.27% (error: 0.73%, SD:0.56%) were achieved, both within the ±2% IoT sensing tolerance. Fuzzy logic evaluation confirmed consistent actuator activation with a mean response time of 1.4 s and no conflicting combinations across all trials.
