These findings highlight distinct molecular responses to dehydration and recovery in tef and may provide potential targets for breeding and biotechnological approaches aimed at improving drought resilience in tef and potentially other crops.

title: Risk committees and corporate disclosure: Evidence on risk and sustainability reporting with governance moderation
source: Risk Governance and Control Financial Markets & Institutions
summary: Environmental and social concerns related to sustainability can represent non-financial risks requiring effective risk management (Wong, 2014). In this context, risk committees may play a role in overseeing such risks and their related corp
content: Environmental and social concerns related to sustainability can represent non-financial risks requiring effective risk management (Wong, 2014). In this context, risk committees may play a role in overseeing such risks and their related corporate disclosures. This study investigates how risk committees impact both risk and sustainability disclosure, aiming to understand how corporate governance enhances transparency and investor confidence. It also examines whether board size, independence, and institutional ownership moderate these relationships, influencing the effectiveness of risk committees in corporate reporting. Using a quantitative approach, this study analyzed 807 samples from Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) companies that published sustainability reports between 2019 and 2023. The results show that risk committees positively influence risk disclosure but do not significantly affect sustainability disclosure. Moderation analysis indicates that board size and independence weaken the effect on risk disclosure. Conversely, institutional ownership strengthens the impact on sustainability disclosure, but not on risk disclosure. These findings suggest risk committees are more effective for traditional risk reporting than for sustainability transparency. This study provides new insights by testing the effectiveness of risk committees in enhancing both types of disclosures. It offers practical insights for regulators, investors, and corporate leaders, underscoring the importance of risk committees in improving disclosure quality to foster transparency and trust.

title: Developing Resilient Water Supplies for Great Plains Native American Reservations: Rosebud Sioux Tribe (South Dakota, USA) Challenges
summary: The Rosebud Sioux Tribe of southern South Dakota provides a case of study of the challenges Native American tribes in the Great Plains region face in developing sustainable water supplies that are resilient to both droughts and long-term cl
content: The Rosebud Sioux Tribe of southern South Dakota provides a case of study of the challenges Native American tribes in the Great Plains region face in developing sustainable water supplies that are resilient to both droughts and long-term climate change. The Rosebud Indian Reservation has a semiarid climate with water supplies that are particularly vulnerable to natural climate variation and a drying climate. The adaptive capacity of the tribe is constrained by the reservation having one of the highest poverty rates in the United States. Non-Indian irrigators are the largest groundwater users on the reservation, but their use is beyond the tribal government’s control. The Rosebud Sioux Tribe continues to implement measures to increase the resilience of its water supply. The Rosebud Sioux Rural Water System provides potable water to the majority of the reservation’s population using multiple water sources, both surface and groundwater, which increases the resilience of the residential potable water supply to climate change. Interventions, such as deepening or replacing shallow household wells and augmenting stock ponds with groundwater, can mitigate some immediate vulnerabilities. Establishing a large herd of bison (Wolakota Buffalo Range), a species well adapted to the Great Plains climate, will result in ecological restoration, increased economic development, and better food security. However, continuous, long-term drying and associated groundwater impacts may eventually force more transformative adaptations, particularly with respect to agriculture.

title: Analisis Karakteristik Limbah Asam pada Industri Asam Sulfat Berdasarkan Kandungan Cl-, H2SO4, dan Fe
summary: Limbah asam (waste acid) pada industri asam sulfat berdasarkan kandungan Cl⁻, konsentrasi H₂SO₄, dan logam Fe terlarut pada sampel. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis karakteristik waste acid pada industri asam sulfat berdasarkan k
content: Limbah asam (waste acid) pada industri asam sulfat berdasarkan kandungan Cl⁻, konsentrasi H₂SO₄, dan logam Fe terlarut pada sampel. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis karakteristik waste acid pada industri asam sulfat berdasarkan kandungan ion klorida (Cl⁻), konsentrasi H₂SO₄, logam Fe terlarut, dan pH serta mengetahui perbedaan karakteristik waste acid pada tiga titik proses gas purification, yaitu Scrubber 1, Packed Tower, dan Scrubber 2. Penelitian menggunakan desain eksperimen komparatif yang dilaksanakan di Laboratorium PT Merdeka Tsingshan Indonesia pada Maret–Mei 2026. Sampel waste acid diambil dari aliran dilute waste acid pada ketiga titik proses. Analisis Cl⁻, H₂SO₄, dan Fe dilakukan sebanyak 11 kali pengujian pada masing-masing titik, sedangkan pengukuran pH dilakukan sebanyak tiga kali. Analisis Cl⁻ menggunakan metode argentometri Volhard, H₂SO₄ menggunakan titrasi alkalimetri, Fe menggunakan ICP-OES berdasarkan EPA Method 6010D, sedangkan pH diukur menggunakan pH meter terkalibrasi. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif menggunakan nilai rata-rata dan simpangan baku serta dibandingkan antar titik proses menggunakan uji Kruskal–Wallis pada taraf signifikansi 5%. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Scrubber 1 memiliki konsentrasi tertinggi untuk Cl⁻ sebesar 199,13 mg/L, H₂SO₄ sebesar 76,45%, dan Fe sebesar 503,50 mg/L. Konsentrasi Cl⁻ dan H₂SO₄ menurun pada Packed Tower menjadi masing-masing 103,90 mg/L dan 34,52%, kemudian meningkat pada Scrubber 2 menjadi 134,18 mg/L dan 39,21%. Sebaliknya, Fe mengalami penurunan dari 503,50 mg/L pada Scrubber 1 menjadi 5,33 mg/L pada Packed Tower dan 0,68 mg/L pada Scrubber 2. Nilai pH berkisar 0,48–0,94. Hasil penelitian dapat digunakan sebagai dasar pemantauan distribusi kontaminan dan penentuan titik prioritas pengendalian waste acid sebelum memasuki proses pengolahan lanjutan di Waste Acid Treatment Plant (WATP).

title: Discovering the Drivers of Ecological Fashion Adoption Intention among Fast Fashion Consumers
source: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
summary: The environmental impact of fast fashion has garnered global attention due to its resource-intensive production, excessive waste, and pollution. In response, ecological fashion has emerged to promote sustainable consumption and mitigate env
content: The environmental impact of fast fashion has garnered global attention due to its resource-intensive production, excessive waste, and pollution. In response, ecological fashion has emerged to promote sustainable consumption and mitigate environmental harm. However, research on ecological fashion adoption intention in developing countries remains limited. Despite growing awareness, many consumers continue to prioritize fast fashion over eco-friendly alternatives. This study examines how the need for fashion and need for uniqueness influence ecological fashion adoption intention among Malaysian consumers. A quantitative survey was conducted with 396 participants using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS. Findings show that among the dimensions of the Need for Fashion, image consciousness and market knowledge significantly and positively influence ecological fashion adoption intention, while fashion awareness and fashion consciousness were not significant. For the Need for Uniqueness, creative choices and unpopular choices significantly affect adoption intention, whereas avoidance of similarity was not significant. These results highlight the importance of self-expression, creativity, and market awareness in driving sustainable fashion behavior in Malaysia. The study contributes theoretically by integrating fashion consciousness and uniqueness into ecological fashion adoption models in a developing country context. Practically, it offers insights for policymakers and marketers to design strategies that promote sustainable fashion adoption. By understanding consumer motivations, stakeholders can encourage environmentally responsible behavior, foster a greener lifestyle, and support Malaysia’s sustainable development objectives.

title: Analysis of Groundwater Vulnerability to Underground Petroleum Tank Leakages: Hydrogeological Risk Assessment, Residents' Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices on Associated Health Risks in Abeokuta Urban, Nigeria
summary: This study analyzed groundwater vulnerability to underground petroleum storage tank (UPST) leakages and assessed residents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding associated health risks in Abeokuta Urban, Nigeria. A mixed-meth
content: This study analyzed groundwater vulnerability to underground petroleum storage tank (UPST) leakages and assessed residents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding associated health risks in Abeokuta Urban, Nigeria. A mixed-methods design integrated hydrogeological vulnerability assessment with a household KAP survey. Nineteen petroleum filling stations and 187 associated groundwater sources were purposively sampled, while 374 household respondents completed a structured questionnaire. Hydrogeological vulnerability was classified using station age, elevation-derived hydraulic gradient, and spatial proximity analysis. Socio-demographic data revealed predominantly female respondents (58.3%), economically active adults (32.1% aged 26–35 years), high educational attainment (53.5% tertiary educated), and long-term residents (66.3% residing >12 years). Knowledge levels were low, with 74.6% exhibiting poor awareness of groundwater contamination pathways; only 43.3% recognized that filling stations affect groundwater quality, and just 25.1% understood associated health risks. Attitude scores were moderately positive (mean 3.19), though 93.0% remained neutral, and protective practices were poor (mean score 1.31 ± 1.12), with only 12.3% treating water and 9.6% reporting contamination. Chi-square analysis revealed a significant but weak relationship between knowledge and attitude while knowledge-practice association was not significant. Vulnerability mapping identified three high-risk (15.8%), nine medium-risk (47.4%), and seven low-risk (36.8%) stations, corresponding to 20 (10.7%), 80 (42.8%), and 87 (46.5%) groundwater sources at risk. Elevation-controlled flow demonstrated that stations positioned downgradient exhibited 76.9-100% at-risk sources. The study concludes that contamination risk arises from the interaction between physical vulnerability, inadequate community awareness and protective practices, requiring integrated regulatory enforcement and targeted community public health interventions to reduce exposure.

title: Leachate-Induced Groundwater Contamination Near the Pugu Kinyamwezi Dumpsite, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: Hadrochemical Facies and Pollution Risks
summary: This study assessed the impact of leachate induced groundwater contamination near the Pugu Kinyamwezi dumpsite and associated pollution risks - the region's largest dumpsite by landmass and waste volume. Groundwater samples were collected f
content: This study assessed the impact of leachate induced groundwater contamination near the Pugu Kinyamwezi dumpsite and associated pollution risks - the region's largest dumpsite by landmass and waste volume. Groundwater samples were collected from ten stations around the dumpsite, including one control station, with physicochemical parameters analyzed at Ardhi University’s Environmental Engineering Laboratory. Key parameters analyzed included pH, electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), major cations (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, K⁺), anions (NO₃⁻, Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, HCO₃⁻), and selected heavy metals (Fe, Mn, Zn, Pb, Cu). Aquachem modeling was used to assess water types and hydrochemical evolution. The results revealed that most groundwater samples met East African Standards (EAS 12:2018) and WHO drinking water standards. However, three stations (S5, S6, and S8) showed elevated levels of magnesium (up to 896.61 mg/L), nitrate (100.32 mg/L), and electrical conductivity (up to 2245 µS/cm), indicating contamination linked to landfill leachate. pH levels at several stations were below acceptable limits (<6.5), suggesting acidic conditions unfavorable for potable use. Elevated chloride of up to 421.37 mg/L and sulfate concentrations were also detected. Scatter plots confirmed a strong correlation between sodium and chloride, suggesting a common pollution source and Magnesium dominance over calcium in several stations were observed, indicating chemical alteration due to leachate intrusion. These findings highlight the urgent need for improved waste management, continuous groundwater quality monitoring and policy enforcement to mitigate further contamination. Strategic planning, landfill design improvements, and implementation of sustainable environmental practices are critical for safeguarding public health and the aquifer system.

title: Farmland biodiversity monitoring in Europe: Germany
source: Burleigh Dodds series in agricultural science
summary: Germany lacks a standardised and coordinated farmland biodiversity monitoring framework. However, several independent and heterogeneous programmes generate datasets for farmland-related biodiversity assessments. These programmes have limita
content: Germany lacks a standardised and coordinated farmland biodiversity monitoring framework. However, several independent and heterogeneous programmes generate datasets for farmland-related biodiversity assessments. These programmes have limitations, including limited taxonomic coverage, lack of long-term trends, and insufficient data on agricultural land use/management, affecting the early detection of declining ecosystem conditions. MonViA, launched in 2019, is a nationwide, representative, and science-based framework that addresses key gaps in farmland biodiversity monitoring, aiming to develop monitoring concepts and indicators for agri-environmental policy for Germany. MonViA complements existing monitoring programmes with its farmland focus, national-level indicators on habitat, species, and genetic diversity, and modular design. The chapter outlines key steps towards an integrated farmland biodiversity monitoring in Germany through improved survey designs, novel survey methods, and advancements in data management, access, and integration. Strengthening farmland biodiversity monitoring and integrating it into policy and practice is urgently needed for supporting effective conservation and land-management decisions.

title: Monitoring of PM2.5 and PM10 particulate matter concentrations in an urban area of Southern Amazonas, Brazil
summary: Humaitá, no Sul do Amazonas, enfrenta crescentes pressões ambientais associadas à expansão da fronteira agrícola, ao desmatamento e à intensificação das queimadas. Este estudo analisou a variabilidade sazonal do MP2.5 e MP10 entre 2023 e 20
content: Humaitá, no Sul do Amazonas, enfrenta crescentes pressões ambientais associadas à expansão da fronteira agrícola, ao desmatamento e à intensificação das queimadas. Este estudo analisou a variabilidade sazonal do MP2.5 e MP10 entre 2023 e 2024, utilizando dados da primeira estação automática de monitoramento da região Sul do Amazonas. A abordagem integrou monitoramento contínuo, modelagem de trajetórias atmosféricas e regressão logística para identificar limiares quantitativos de excedência dos padrões de qualidade do ar. Os resultados evidenciaram forte sazonalidade, com concentrações inferiores a 10 µg m-3 no período chuvoso, associadas à elevada precipitação (>300 mm). Em contraste, aumentos expressivos ocorreram entre junho e setembro, quando a precipitação média foi inferior a 5 mm mês-1 e os focos de queimadas se intensificaram em toda a região sul amazônica. No contexto estadual, Humaitá destacou-se em 2024 ao responder por cerca de 5,5% dos focos de queimadas registrados pelo INPE no Amazonas. Em 2024, o número de focos de queimadas foi 31% superior ao observado em 2023, associado ao aumento das concentrações de material particulado. Os maiores valores ocorreram em setembro de 2024, com concentrações de 172,3 µg m-3 para MP2.5 e 176,0 µg m-3 para MP10. Foram registrados 68 e 64 dias acima do limite diário de 15 µg m-3 para MP2.5 em 2023 e 2024, respectivamente, sendo 2024 marcado por episódios mais severos classificados como “Muito Ruim” e “Péssima”. A análise de limiar indicou probabilidade de 50% de excedência do limite diário com 85 focos dia-1 e 80% com 134 focos dia-1. As correlações entre MP2.5, MP10, focos de queimadas e variáveis meteorológicas evidenciaram a influência da queima de biomassa na degradação da qualidade do ar na região.

title: Development and preliminary validation of green logistics practices measurement scale: Evidence from Malaysian firms
summary: This research evaluates the psychometric properties of a modified instrument designed to examine green logistics implementation, organizational outcomes, and the regulatory influence of government. Drawing from validated 5-point Likert scal
content: This research evaluates the psychometric properties of a modified instrument designed to examine green logistics implementation, organizational outcomes, and the regulatory influence of government. Drawing from validated 5-point Likert scales in current literature, the study utilized a pilot sample of 50 participants, with data processed via SPSS v30.0. The refinement of the scale was achieved through internal consistency checks and exploratory factor analysis (EFA). Findings confirmed robust reliability, as Cronbach’s alpha coefficients for all constructs surpassed the 0.7 threshold. The final 40-item scale, organized into five theoretically aligned dimensions, demonstrated strong factor loadings and sampling adequacy (KMO > 0.7). By validating these core constructs, this work establishes a rigorous foundation for future empirical inquiries into the environmental performance of the trucking industry.

title: Green pharmaceutical investments and environmental sustainability: Evidence from the Indian healthcare ecosystem
summary: The purpose of this study is to prioritize key environmental sustainability dimensions and indicators within the pharmaceutical sector to support informed decision-making and policy formulation. The study adopts a quantitative methodology u
content: The purpose of this study is to prioritize key environmental sustainability dimensions and indicators within the pharmaceutical sector to support informed decision-making and policy formulation. The study adopts a quantitative methodology using RIDIT analysis to compare multiple sustainability indicators against a reference distribution and derive priority rankings. Survey data collected from 516 respondents were analyzed across environmental impact, environmental sustainability, impact investing, and adoption of green pharmaceutical practices. The findings reveal that environmental sustainability and environmental impact indicators receive the highest priority, indicating strong stakeholder emphasis on long-term ecological outcomes. Impact investing plays a moderate facilitative role, while green practice adoption ranks lowest, highlighting implementation gaps. The study offers practical implications for policymakers and industry managers by identifying areas requiring targeted interventions and resource allocation. The novelty of this research lies in the application of RIDIT analysis to systematically rank sustainability dimensions in the pharmaceutical context, providing a robust and interpretable prioritization framework.

title: A novel multi-attribute decision making method based on Partitioned Hamy Mean Aggregator and its applications in material selection problems
summary: In many multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) scenarios, decision makers face the challenge of evaluating both tangible and intangible attributes.These attributes often differ in nature and importance, making the decision process complex.F
content: In many multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) scenarios, decision makers face the challenge of evaluating both tangible and intangible attributes.These attributes often differ in nature and importance, making the decision process complex.Furthermore, the interrelationships among criteria must be carefully assessed, especially when the criteria are grouped or partitioned based on their inherent characteristics.To tackle these challenges, this paper introduces a novel multi-attribute ranking and selection approach under crisp environments called PHARSA (Partitioned Hamy Aggregator-based Ranking and Selection Approach).PHARSA is capable of addressing multi-attribute ranking and selection problems with non-ordered, ordered, ordinal, cardinal, or mixed attribute assessments.We introduce novel double-weighted partitioned Hamy mean (PHM) operators that apply weighting to both the attribute and the partitions.A real-world on-water pipe material selection is presented to demonstrate the practical applicability of the proposed method.Comparative analyses with existing methods prove that PHARSA is an effective tool for solving multi-attribute ranking and selection problems in management and engineering contexts.

title: A Data-driven XGBoost Model for Robust Prediction of Compressive Strength in Fly Ash-based Concrete
summary: This study presents a data-driven framework for predicting the compressive strength of fly ash concrete using the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm. A dataset of 1,030 experimental samples was used for model development, and an
content: This study presents a data-driven framework for predicting the compressive strength of fly ash concrete using the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm. A dataset of 1,030 experimental samples was used for model development, and an additional 198 independent samples from external studies were employed for validation. Seven key input parameters—cement, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, and curing age—were considered as predictors. To ensure robustness, a leakage-free preprocessing strategy and randomized search (RandomizedSearchCV) for hyperparameter tuning were applied for hyperparameter tuning. The optimized model achieved excellent predictive accuracy with R^2=0.9949 and RMSE = 1.20 MPa on the training set, and R^2=0.9390 with RMSE = 3.96 MPa on the testing set. When evaluated on the independent validation dataset, the model maintained acceptable accuracy (R^2=0.6745; 73.7% within ±20% tolerance). Feature importance analysis identified curing age and cement content as dominant factors influencing compressive strength. The results demonstrate that while machine learning models can achieve near-perfect accuracy internally, external validation is essential for assessing real-world generalization. The proposed XGBoost framework offers a reliable, interpretable, and efficient tool for data-driven mix design and sustainable concrete optimization.

title: Thermal and Economic Assessment of Cooling Technologies in a Combined Cycle Power Plant: A Case Study Bandar Abbas Hengam Power Plant
summary: The present study examined the Bandar Abbas Hengam combined cycle power plant (CCPP) equipped with a three-pressure heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) with reheat. Fogging and absorption chiller systems were used to improve power plant pe
content: The present study examined the Bandar Abbas Hengam combined cycle power plant (CCPP) equipped with a three-pressure heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) with reheat. Fogging and absorption chiller systems were used to improve power plant performance. The proposed power plant was simulated using the Thermoflow software and the GT PRO module. This research assessed the power plant’s thermal and economic performance in warm months (March–October), with and without cooling systems. The technical and economic simulation results were extracted using Thermoflow and COMFAR software. The energy analysis results indicated that the absorption chiller is the best alternative for boosting the power production capacity. However, the cycle without a cooling system was found to have the highest thermal efficiency. On the other hand, the economic analysis results demonstrated that the highest net present value (NPV) 638.27 Billion Rials ($1.06 Million) was obtained for the combined cycle with the absorption chiller cooling system, which also had an internal rate of return (IRR) of 43.65%. The next highest NPV 633.35 Billion Rials ($1.05 Million) was obtained for the combined cycle with the fogging cooling system, which had an IRR of 44.09%. Finally, the combined cycle without a cooling system had an NPV of 586.27 Billion Rials ($0.98 Million) and an IRR of 43.3%. Therefore, for short-term investment and quick returns, fogging is most economical due to its higher IRR. For long-term investment focused on maximizing net value, the absorption chiller is more viable.

title: Identifying the Factors Affecting the Feasibility of Lean Production toward Sustainability in the Iranian Automotive Industry Using Grey Theory
summary: This study aimed to identify and prioritize the factors affecting the feasibility of transitioning from lean production toward sustainability in the Iranian automotive industry using qualitative thematic analysis and Grey Relational Analysi
content: This study aimed to identify and prioritize the factors affecting the feasibility of transitioning from lean production toward sustainability in the Iranian automotive industry using qualitative thematic analysis and Grey Relational Analysis. This applied study employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, data were collected through a review of the literature and semi-structured interviews with 18 academic and professional experts selected purposively, with interviews continuing until theoretical saturation. The qualitative data were analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding to identify the principal dimensions and factors influencing sustainable lean production. In the quantitative phase, a researcher-developed questionnaire based on the extracted qualitative codes was administered to a population of 400 healthcare personnel in Ilam to assess the generalizability of the organizational components in a high-pressure service environment. Content and construct validity and Cronbach's alpha reliability were evaluated. Grey Relational Analysis was then used to transform uncertain judgments into grey numbers, normalize the data, calculate grey relational coefficients, and rank the identified factors. The analysis identified four overarching dimensions: technical and operational, economic and financial, environmental, and organizational and cultural. Grey Relational Analysis ranked reduction of production errors as the most influential factor (0.945), followed by process quality control (0.938), process optimization (0.931), reduction of production cycle time (0.924), and increased equipment efficiency (0.917). Waste reduction also received a high priority (0.910). Among supply-chain and technology factors, sustainable supply of raw materials ranked highest (0.840), while reduction of energy consumption was the leading environmental factor (0.735). Senior management support was the highest-ranked managerial factor (0.630). The transition toward sustainable lean production in the Iranian automotive industry should begin with operational stabilization and quality improvement, followed by supply-chain integration, digitalization, environmental efficiency, and sustained managerial and organizational support.

title: E-fuels for maritime decarbonisation: a well-to-wake life cycle perspective on pathway readiness and policy alignment
summary: International shipping faces a critical decarbonisation challenge, with lifecycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions continuing to rise despite efficiency improvements and projected to grow substantially without intervention. This paper evaluat
content: International shipping faces a critical decarbonisation challenge, with lifecycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions continuing to rise despite efficiency improvements and projected to grow substantially without intervention. This paper evaluates the viability of alternative maritime fuel pathways through a systematic well-to-wake (WtW) life cycle assessment (LCA), examining ammonia, methanol, hydrogen, and power-to-liquid fuels across a range of production routes. Results reveal substantial intra-pathway variability, with only fuels derived from low-carbon electricity and rigorously controlled carbon inputs consistently achieving intensities compatible with long-term decarbonisation targets. The analysis identifies a structural misalignment between empirical evidence and existing policy frameworks, which continue to rely in part on tank-to-wake (TtW) accounting. This misalignment risks incentivising fuel pathways that are formally compliant but environmentally ineffective, leading to inefficient capital allocation and potential technological lock-in. The paper argues for the adoption of quantitative WtW GHG intensity thresholds as the foundation of maritime fuel regulation, replacing reliance on categorical "colour" taxonomies. Beyond lifecycle emissions, the paper introduces a novel analysis of the geographical concentration of e-fuel production. Emerging supply chains are increasingly clustered in regions with low-cost renewable resources, creating a divergence between the locations of fuel production and regulatory demand, particularly in Europe and the UK. This raises critical concerns regarding lifecycle emissions from transport, the externalisation of industrial value, and the potential reconfiguration of global energy dependencies. The findings demonstrate that maritime decarbonisation is a systems-level challenge spanning emissions accounting, industrial strategy, and energy security. Effective policy must therefore integrate robust WtW methodologies with interventions that address supply chain geography and support the development of domestic e-fuel production capacity.

title: Reducing Hydrogen Diffusion Losses by Modification of Fluoroplastic Barrier Coatings for Increasing Efficiency and Safety of Hydrogen Transportation
summary: High pressure hydrogen transport can cause hydrogen embrittlement of steel pipelines, leading to loss of mechanical integrity and failures. Therefore, protective internal coatings are required to reduce hydrogen permeability. In this work,
content: High pressure hydrogen transport can cause hydrogen embrittlement of steel pipelines, leading to loss of mechanical integrity and failures. Therefore, protective internal coatings are required to reduce hydrogen permeability. In this work, the effect of composite fluoropolymer coatings modified with carbon nanotubes (CNTs), silicon carbide (SiC), and hexagonal boron nitride (h BN) on the hydrogen permeability of 1020 steel was studied using the Devanathan–Stachurski electrochemical method. The effective diffusion coefficient, steady state diffusion flux, and hydrogen concentration in the near surface layer were determined for uncoated steel, steel with a graphite layer, and various nanomodified PTFE coatings. Applying fluoropolymer coatings containing CNTs significantly reduced the effective diffusion coefficient and hydrogen flux compared to uncoated steel. Additional incorporation of SiC and h BN particles enabled further tailoring of the barrier properties. The PTFE based composition filled with CNTs and SiC provided the lowest effective diffusion coefficient and diffusion flux, which is attributed to the formation of a dense, low defect polymer structure with an elongated diffusion path. To evaluate the influence of the nanofiller composition on agglomeration and coating defectiveness, the ratio of reduction coefficients ηJ/ηD is proposed as an additional performance indicator. Diffusion loss calculations for a model pipeline section showed that the developed coatings substantially reduce hydrogen permeation through the steel wall, confirming their potential for internal pipeline protection in hydrogen transport and storage systems.

title: Energy Portfolios and Food Security in Developing Countries: A Water–Energy–Food Nexus Analysis Using Panel Smooth Transition Regression
summary: Agricultural production, processing and distribution in developing countries are energy-intensive, so the composition of the electricity generation portfolio is a plausible determinant of both food prices and physical supply security. The e
content: Agricultural production, processing and distribution in developing countries are energy-intensive, so the composition of the electricity generation portfolio is a plausible determinant of both food prices and physical supply security. The existing evidence, however, represents energy through aggregated indicators, analyses price and supply security separately, and assumes linearity, leaving open which generation technologies matter and under what conditions. This study therefore estimates six technologies—nuclear, geothermal, hydropower, solar, wind and biomass—jointly against both food outcomes within one nonlinear panel framework. The dataset combines IEA, IRENA, FAOSTAT and World Bank indicators for 82 developing economies over 2000–2023. Estimation uses Panel Smooth Transition Regression (PSTR) with energy intensity as the transition variable, supported by dynamic panel system-GMM and common correlated effects (CCE) estimators and by a compositional-data robustness specification based on the centred log-ratio transformation. Linearity is rejected and a single energy-intensity threshold is estimated at 0.436, with a transition speed of 7.84. Above that threshold, biomass generation is positively associated with food prices (0.067) and negatively with supply security (−0.055), whereas the continuously dispatchable sources—nuclear (−0.081) and geothermal (−0.094)—are negatively associated with price pressure and positively with supply security. Solar and wind attain significance only in the high regime, and the hydropower relationship reverses sign between low- and high-water-stress subsamples. Because the panel is observational and generation shares may be jointly determined with food outcomes, the coefficients are interpreted throughout as regime-dependent conditional relationships rather than causal effects. For policy, the findings imply that the generation portfolio should be planned jointly with water resources, grid integration and rural electrification rather than steered by a single aggregated renewable-energy target: biomass incentives warrant feedstock-origin conditionality, hydropower requires seasonal allocation rules where water stress is high, and variable renewables deliver food-security value mainly when paired with storage and irrigation-linked distribution.

title: An Overview of Renewable Hydrogen from Biomass Processes and Solar Energy Systems
summary: Renewable hydrogen has emerged as a promising energy carrier for achieving low-carbon and sustainable energy systems. Among the various production routes, biomass-based processes and solar energy–driven systems offer significant potential d
content: Renewable hydrogen has emerged as a promising energy carrier for achieving low-carbon and sustainable energy systems. Among the various production routes, biomass-based processes and solar energy–driven systems offer significant potential due to their renewable nature and wide resource availability. Biomass conversion pathways such as gasification, pyrolysis, and biological processes enable the utilization of agricultural residues, forestry waste, and organic by-products for hydrogen generation, while simultaneously addressing waste management concerns. These processes can be integrated with carbon capture techniques to further reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Solar energy systems, including photovoltaic-assisted electrolysis, solar thermochemical cycles, and photoelectrochemical water splitting, provide clean hydrogen production by directly harnessing solar radiation. The combination of biomass and solar routes enhances energy security by diversifying feedstocks and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. However, challenges related to conversion efficiency, system scalability, hydrogen storage, and economic viability remain critical for large-scale implementation. This overview examines the fundamental principles, recent technological developments, and key advantages of biomass-derived and solar-based hydrogen production pathways. Emphasis is placed on their role in supporting a sustainable hydrogen economy and contributing to global decarbonization goals.

title: Detection of Unmarked Non-Metallic Underground Pipelines Using Fine-Grained Strontium Ferrite-Based Powders
summary: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of
content: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of specific problems characteristic of plastic materials. One of such significant problems facing the gas industry is the problem of detecting underground non-metallic utilities and selectively identifying them from adjacent facilities. Pipelines not linked to the global coordinate system in a timely manner can lead to significant economic costs in case of abnormal situations during construction and installation works. The paper investigates an original method of searching for non-metallic utilities associated with the introduction of magnetic powder into the gas flow. It is shown that in the case of the site location in the urban area it is a low-information and ambiguous method. On the contrary, in the open area, in the absence of third-party ferromagnetic interference, this method is not only potentially applicable, but deserves close attention and further research, for which the appropriate design of the test site is proposed. Potential application of the method will increase the informative value of data on the underground location of non-metallic pipelines by 15% for gas distribution pipelines of various diameters, considering the achievement of a magnetic induction level above the pipeline in the range of 60-120 nT.

title: Improvement of Electrochemical Behavior of Nitinol by Hydroxyapatite–Tantalum Oxide Coating Fabricated via Electrophoretic Deposition for Biomedical Applications
source: نشریه علمی پژوهشی مواد پیشرفته در مهندسی
summary: Introduction and Objectives: The widespread application of NiTi alloys in biomedical implants is constrained by the release of nickel ions, which may provoke allergic responses and carcinogenic risks. Employing biocompatible hydroxyapatite
content: Introduction and Objectives: The widespread application of NiTi alloys in biomedical implants is constrained by the release of nickel ions, which may provoke allergic responses and carcinogenic risks. Employing biocompatible hydroxyapatite composite coatings offers a promising approach to suppress nickel ion leaching and improve the electrochemical performance of NiTi alloys. This study focuses on assessing how varying the concentration of a secondary phase within the composite affects the coating’s composition, microstructure, and the overall electrochemical behavior of the substrate. Materials and Methods: Hydroxyapatite–tantalum oxide composite coatings were produced on NiTi substrates via the electrophoretic deposition method. Tantalum oxide was introduced into the hydroxyapatite nanoparticle suspension at concentrations of 10, 15, and 20 wt.%. All coated samples were sintered at 800 °C for one hour under vacuum conditions. Results: Experimental findings, based on nickel ion release measurements, potentiodynamic polarization, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, clearly demonstrate that increasing the content of the secondary phase within the composite significantly enhances the corrosion resistance of the underlying NiTi substrate. The positive effect of the secondary phase on the adhesion strength of hydroxyapatite coating to NiTi was assessed using a tensile test. Conclusion: Engineering composite coatings with dense structural characteristics, designed to restrict the ingress of environmental corrosive species and to block nickel ion diffusion, presents a robust strategy for the safe and durable utilization of NiTi alloys in biomedical applications.

title: Improving the Wear Resistance of FeCrCoNiMnTix High-Entropy Alloys Coatings via In-Situ Formation of Ti-Rich Carbides During Spark Plasma Sintering Process
source: نشریه علمی پژوهشی مواد پیشرفته در مهندسی
summary: Introduction and Objectives: This study investigates the wear behavior of FeCrCoNiMnTix high-entropy alloy coatings deposited on AISI 431 martensitic stainless steel. Materials and Methods: The alloy powders were prepared via mechanical all
content: Introduction and Objectives: This study investigates the wear behavior of FeCrCoNiMnTix high-entropy alloy coatings deposited on AISI 431 martensitic stainless steel. Materials and Methods: The alloy powders were prepared via mechanical alloying in a planetary ball mill under an argon atmosphere. To evaluate their wear resistance, the synthesized powders were applied as coatings using the spark plasma sintering technique. Comprehensive analyses, including X-ray diffraction and field emission scanning electron microscopy, revealed that the addition of Ti induces a microstructural transition from a dominant FCC phase to a BCC-rich structure and facilitates the formation of Laves intermetallic phases. Microhardness measurements and pin-on-disk wear test were employed to assess the wear behavior. Results: The results strongly suggest that TiC formed in situ during the SPS process due to the interaction between Ti and carbon. This, combined with solid solution strengthening and the formation of intermetallic phases, resulted in an increase in hardness up to 1030 HV0.05 for the FeCrCoNiMnTi composition. Wear test results indicated that the best performance was achieved by the FeCrCoNiMnTi composition, with a wear rate of approximately 3.78 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N.m, which is nearly four times lower than that of the AISI 431 stainless steel. Conclusion: This improvement is attributed to the synergistic strengthening effects of the BCC matrix, laves intermetallic phases, and the in-situ formed carbides. The findings of this research suggest that FeCrCoNiMnTi high-entropy alloys are promising candidates for wear-resistant coatings and underscore the critical role of chemical composition design in engineering their structural and tribological properties.

title: Trade Openness and Environmental Sustainability in Armenia: An Empirical Analysis of CO2 Emissions (2001–2024)
summary: This paper examines the relationship between international trade openness, economic development, and environmen-tal sustainability in Armenia during 2001–2024. The main objective is to identify the relationship between trade openness, GDP p
content: This paper examines the relationship between international trade openness, economic development, and environmen-tal sustainability in Armenia during 2001–2024. The main objective is to identify the relationship between trade openness, GDP per capita, and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions. The study uses annual statistical data from the World Bank and applies descriptive statistical analysis, trend analysis, and multiple linear regression. The results demonstrate that Armenia experienced substantial growth in international trade and economic activity during the research period, accompanied by an overall increase in CO2 emissions per capita. However, the dynamics of these indicators were not uniform. The regression analysis revealed a positive but statistically insignificant relationship between trade openness and CO2 emissions. In contrast, GDP per capita demonstrated a positive and statistically significant association with carbon emissions. The regression model explained approximately 89.4% of the variation in the logarithm of CO2 emissions. The findings suggest that the environmental consequences of Armenia’s economic development cannot be explained by trade openness alone. The structure of foreign trade, energy consumption, and production characteristics may also play important roles. The research emphasizes the importance of combining international economic integration with improvements in energy efficiency, cleaner technologies, and sustainable production. The results provide a basis for further research on the relationship between international trade and environmental sustainability in small open economies.

title: Ecosystems long-cycle materialogy: Bioresources as the origin of future life
summary: Modern society faces an environmental crisis driven by non-degradable components, including synthetic plastics in daily products and industrial agriculture. Beyond simple plastic replacement, this editorial introduces “Ecosystems Long-cycle
content: Modern society faces an environmental crisis driven by non-degradable components, including synthetic plastics in daily products and industrial agriculture. Beyond simple plastic replacement, this editorial introduces “Ecosystems Long-cycle Materialogy”—a new paradigm that redefines human-made materials as integral elements of natural biogeochemical cycles. Within this framework, forests and oceans are envisioned as vast hubs for ultralong material circulation. For example, wood-mimetic microbeads for cosmetics are designed with the expectation that they will eventually enter natural biogeochemical cycles in a safe and controlled manner. Therefore, rather than becoming problematic waste, these deliberately designed bio-based materials participate in an extended carbon cycle. Once entering the ocean, they biodegrade and sequester carbon in the deep seabed, potentially on the order of 500 to 1,000 years. This philosophy shifts our objective from reducing environmental burden to complementing ecosystem cycles. By acknowledging that every material serves as the starting point for the next form of life, we can align manufacturing with the Earth’s long‑term resilience and survival.

title: Sustainability through IoT and Big Data Analytics in Tertiary Industry: A Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
source: Journal of Intelligent Systems and Internet of Things
summary: The tertiary industry is increasingly influenced by digital technologies that support service efficiency, data-driven decision-making and sustainability-oriented transformation. This study reviews the way the Internet of Things (IoT) and Bi
content: The tertiary industry is increasingly influenced by digital technologies that support service efficiency, data-driven decision-making and sustainability-oriented transformation. This study reviews the way the Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data Analytics (BDA) contribute to sustainability in service sectors, including healthcare, education, tourism, hospitality, logistics, transport, finance and smart-city services. A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis were conducted using Scopus and Web of Science for records dated from 2015 through 28 February 2025. From 1,969 initial records, 551 were used for bibliometric and metadata analysis and 136 studies were included in qualitative synthesis. The publication trend, productive sources, authors, countries, subject areas, keywords and science-mapping pattern were studied by using Bibliometrix, Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. The findings show rapid growth after 2019 and strong concentration in computer science, engineering, smart healthcare, smart cities and digital sustainability research. The main contribution is an integrated service-sector synthesis showing that IoT functions as the sensing and connectivity layer, while BDA, AI, cloud-edge architectures, blockchain and predictive analytics convert service data into monitoring, optimization, decision support and automation. Sustainability outcomes appear across environmental, economic and social dimensions, including energy savings, emissions reduction, waste recovery, cost efficiency, healthcare access, inclusion and service quality. Finally, the review concludes that IoT and BDA, among other factors, have sustainable value if supported by governance, data quality, cybersecurity, interoperability, skills and organizational readiness.

title: Application of Random Forest Algorithm for Viscosity Prediction in CO2-dissolved Crude Oil Systems
summary: With the increasing application of CO2-EOR technology, accurate prediction of CO2-dissolved crude oil viscosity has become essential for flow assurance and gathering transportation. In this study, the coupled effects of temperature (20–40 ℃
content: With the increasing application of CO2-EOR technology, accurate prediction of CO2-dissolved crude oil viscosity has become essential for flow assurance and gathering transportation. In this study, the coupled effects of temperature (20–40 ℃), pressure (0.5–3.5 MPa), and water cut (0–60%) on the viscosity behavior of CO2-saturated crude oil were systematically investigated through 64 laboratory experiments. Increasing temperature significantly reduced viscosity, whereas the pressure effect was comparatively weaker. As water cut increased, viscosity first increased and subsequently decreased sharply around the emulsion transition region.Among the evaluated empirical correlations, the Elsharkawy model showed comparatively better agreement with the experimental data and was therefore selected as the physical basis of the hybrid framework. To improve prediction accuracy under coupled operating conditions, a hybrid Elsharkawy–RF model was developed using Random Forest (RF)-based residual correction. For the independent testing dataset, the proposed model achieved an MAE of 1.3215 mPa·s, an RMSE of 1.8528 mPa·s, and an R² value of 0.9868. Feature importance analysis indicated that water cut was the dominant factor affecting viscosity variation, followed by temperature and pressure. The model provided accurate viscosity predictions within the tested temperature, pressure, and water-cut ranges. However, since the model was developed using a single crude-oil sample and a relatively limited dataset, further validation under broader reservoir and fluid conditions is still required.

title: Korporativno izvještavanje o održivosti u kontekstu regulatornih prilagodbi i prijelaznih izuzeća
summary: Rad analizira razvoj i prilagodbe regulatornog okvira korporativnog izvještavanja o održivosti u Europskoj uniji i Hrvatskoj, s posebnim naglaskom na odgode primjene obveza i prijelazna izuzeća uvedena nakon donošenja Direktive o korporativ
content: Rad analizira razvoj i prilagodbe regulatornog okvira korporativnog izvještavanja o održivosti u Europskoj uniji i Hrvatskoj, s posebnim naglaskom na odgode primjene obveza i prijelazna izuzeća uvedena nakon donošenja Direktive o korporativnom izvještavanju o održivosti (CSRD). Cilj rada jest ispitati u kojoj mjeri regulatorne izmjene pridonose usklađivanju ciljeva održive tranzicije s potrebom očuvanja konkurentnosti i smanjenja administrativnog opterećenja poduzetnika. U istraživanju se primjenjuju normativna i analitička metoda, uz pregled europskog i nacionalnog zakonodavstva te interpretaciju aktualnih zakonodavnih prijedloga. Rezultati ukazuju na postupno usklađivanje CSRD-a, Europskih standarda za izvještavanje o održivosti i Direktive o dužnoj pažnji za održivo poslovanje, uz jačanje proporcionalnosti i redefiniranje kruga obveznika. Empirijski pokazatelji, uključujući rezultate ESG ratinga za 2025. godinu i ESG akademije u razdoblju od 2022. do 2025. potvrđuju rastuću institucionalizaciju održivosti u poslovnoj praksi. Može se zaključiti kako se izvještavanje o održivosti transformira iz primarno regulatorne obveze u strateški instrument upravljanja rizicima i dugoročnom konkurentnošću.

title: A Moderating and mediating model of innovation performance
summary: Pioneer performances depend on entrepreneurial orientation for their success. This approach is crucial for converting green intellectual capital into actionable, practical innovations. Therefore, clever management techniques can accelerate
content: Pioneer performances depend on entrepreneurial orientation for their success. This approach is crucial for converting green intellectual capital into actionable, practical innovations. Therefore, clever management techniques can accelerate and improve overall growth. Before incorporating green intellectual capital into organisational structures, managers should carefully consider its potential. The current study is based on a quantitative method, in which data were gathered from middle managers working at the Defense Housing Authority, one of the renowned construction firms in Karachi. The data were analyzed using PLS-SEM (Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling). The results of the research showed that there is a significant positive relationship between green intellectual capital and entrepreneurial orientation, and between green intellectual capital and the financial and non-financial aspects of innovation performance. It also highlighted the significant role of knowledge management as a moderator between entrepreneurial orientation and innovative performance, whereas, in contrast, green self-efficacy had no moderating effect on the relationship between green intellectual capital and EO. These results have implications for management, as they can help identify specific areas of their industry that require improvement before committing significant financial resources to green intellectual capital. Furthermore, this understanding helps assess a company's readiness to apply these innovations successfully.

title: Energy Economics Review: Advancing Knowledge at the Nexus of Energy Economy and Sustainability
summary: The accelerating transformation of global energy systems presents complex challenges and opportunities for economies, institutions, and societies. This editorial introduces the Energy Economics Review (EER) as an interdisciplinary platform
content: The accelerating transformation of global energy systems presents complex challenges and opportunities for economies, institutions, and societies. This editorial introduces the Energy Economics Review (EER) as an interdisciplinary platform dedicated to advancing rigorous and policy-relevant research at the intersection of energy economics, environmental sustainability, and climate policy. It highlights the critical need for integrated analytical frameworks that capture the dynamic interplay between energy markets, technological innovation, financial systems, and governance structures. The editorial outlines the journal’s core thematic priorities, including energy transition strategies, renewable energy finance, market design and regulation, climate economics, and energy equity. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of sustainable finance, digitalisation, and institutional capacity in shaping low-carbon development pathways. The discussion further underscores the importance of methodological rigour, encouraging contributions employing advanced econometric techniques, system modelling, and comparative policy analysis. By fostering global inclusivity and interdisciplinary dialogue, EER aims to bridge the gap between academic research and policy implementation. The editorial concludes by positioning the journal as a critical forum for generating evidence-based insights that support economically viable, environmentally sustainable, and socially equitable energy systems in both developed and developing contexts.

title: Impact of Regulatory Impact Assessment on Policy Effectiveness in India: Evidence from ARDL Model
summary: This study investigates the impact of Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) on policy effectiveness in India by employing a time-series econometric framework. Drawing on annual data for India and incorporating key governance indicators and mac
content: This study investigates the impact of Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) on policy effectiveness in India by employing a time-series econometric framework. Drawing on annual data for India and incorporating key governance indicators and macroeconomic controls, the study applies the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds testing approach to examine both long-run and short-run relationships. The empirical results confirm the existence of a stable long-run equilibrium among RIA, governance quality, macroeconomic variables, and policy effectiveness. The findings reveal that RIA has a statistically significant and positive effect on policy effectiveness, indicating that systematic regulatory evaluation enhances the quality, coherence, and implementation of public policies. Governance indicators such as regulatory quality, government effectiveness, rule of law, and control of corruption also significantly contribute to improved policy outcomes. Additionally, GDP per capita and trade openness are found to strengthen policy effectiveness, highlighting the role of macroeconomic conditions in institutional performance. The Error Correction Model further confirms rapid adjustment toward long-run equilibrium, reinforcing the dynamic stability of the system. Overall, the study underscores the importance of integrating regulatory evaluation mechanisms with strong institutional frameworks to improve governance outcomes in India. The findings provide important implications for policymakers seeking to strengthen evidence-based policymaking and enhance regulatory efficiency.

title: Integrarea inteligenţei artificiale în oraşele viitorului / The role of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in the city of tomorrow
summary: Artificial intelligence offers various benefits to the field of architecture. These benefits include increased efficiency, improved design quality, improved durability and reduced cost. It can streamline various architectural processes such
content: Artificial intelligence offers various benefits to the field of architecture. These benefits include increased efficiency, improved design quality, improved durability and reduced cost. It can streamline various architectural processes such as design and construction, leading to faster project execution time and reduced labor costs. In addition, it can automate repetitive tasks such as drafting and documentation, freeing up time for architects to focus on more creative and complex tasks. Artificial intelligence can analyze and optimize design solutions, resulting in improved design quality. By considering multiple design constraints and criteria, it can suggest design options that meet the project's goals while taking into account environmental, social, and economic factors. In addition, it can help identify design flaws and improve safety and functionality. Artificial intelligence can contribute to sustainability in various ways, such as optimizing the energy performance of the building, reducing material waste and improving the quality of the indoor environment. By analyzing building data, it can optimize building systems and operations, reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions. Likewise, it can help architects make informed decisions about material selection and waste reduction strategies.

title: Are we thinking green? Determinants of green purchasing intention among the elderly towards green vehicles in sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Research background: Despite growing environmental concerns and active government promotion, electric vehicle (EV) uptake in sub-Saharan Africa remains notably low, representing a significant gap in the region’s transition towards sustainab
content: Research background: Despite growing environmental concerns and active government promotion, electric vehicle (EV) uptake in sub-Saharan Africa remains notably low, representing a significant gap in the region’s transition towards sustainable mobility. Furthermore, while the global shift towards green transportation continues to accelerate, the specific socio-demographic factors influencing EV adoption among older adults in the region remain substantially under-researched. Purpose of the article: This study aims to investigate the determinants of EV adoption intentions among older adults in sub-Saharan Africa, where EV uptake remains limited despite increasing environmental concerns and government support. Methods: Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the study analyses empirical data collected from a sample of 312 registered vehicle owners aged 55 years and older. By examining this specific cohort across three major metropolitan areas in Ghana, the study provides detailed demographic and behavioural insights into a population segment whose perspectives are important for understanding the region’s transition towards green mobility. The research hypotheses were tested using confirmatory factor analysis and covariance-based structural equation modelling. The data were analysed using IBM SPSS Amos. Findings & Value added: The findings identify four key factors that significantly and positively influence behavioural intentions to purchase environmentally friendly vehicles: attitudes and beliefs towards EVs, financial incentives, environmental concern, and uncertainty avoidance. Furthermore, uncertainty avoidance was found to positively moderate the relationships between these factors and behavioural intention, thereby strengthening the effects of attitudes, financial incentives, and environmental concern on purchase decisions. The study highlights the need for targeted and multifaceted strategies to encourage EV adoption among older consumers. Practical implications include fostering positive attitudes towards EVs, designing effective financial incentive programmes, promoting environmental awareness, and developing communication strategies that address risk-related concerns. By focusing on an under-researched demographic in a developing African context, the study provides valuable insights for policymakers and marketers seeking to advance sustainable transportation and reduce the environmental impacts of conventional vehicles in the region.

title: UNLEASHING HARMONIOUS GREEN PASSION IN HOSPITALITY ENTERPRISES: A MODERATED-MEDIATED ROLE OF PRO-ENVIRONMENTAL BEHAVIOR AND GREEN ORGANIZATIONAL CLIMATE
summary: Environmental sustainability in the hospitality sector increasingly depends on the alignment between employees’ intrinsic motivations, supportive organizational contexts, and environmentally responsible behaviors. Drawing on SelfDeterminati
content: Environmental sustainability in the hospitality sector increasingly depends on the alignment between employees’ intrinsic motivations, supportive organizational contexts, and environmentally responsible behaviors. Drawing on SelfDetermination Theory, this study examines how Harmonious Green Passion influences environmental performance in Egypt’s five-star hotels, focusing on the mediating role of pro-environmental behavior and the moderating effect of green organizational climate. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 402 hotel employees and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The findings demonstrate that Harmonious Green Passion positively influences both proenvironmental behavior and environmental performance, while pro-environmental behavior partially mediates the relationship between Harmonious Green Passion and environmental performance. Furthermore, green organizational climate significantly strengthens the positive relationship between Harmonious Green Passion and pro-environmental behavior, consequently reinforcing its indirect effect on environmental performance. These findings extend Self-Determination Theory by elucidating a motivation–behavior–performance mechanism through which employees’ environmentally oriented passion translates into organizational outcomes, while demonstrating that this process is contingent upon contextual organizational conditions. Practically, the findings suggest that hotel managers should cultivate supportive green organizational climates, encourage employees’ intrinsic environmental motivation, and facilitate pro-environmental behaviors through appropriate organizational practices. Such efforts can strengthen employees’ environmental engagement and contribute to improved environmental performance, offering hospitality organizations a pathway toward more sustainable operations and long-term environmental value creation.

title: DO TOURIST ARRIVALS AND ECONOMIC COMPLEXITY DRIVE LONG-TERM ECONOMIC GROWTH IN RCEP COUNTRIES? NEW EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE USING POOL MEAN GROUP
summary: This study aims to revisit the debate on the tourism-growth nexus, emphasising the importance of tourism and environmental sustainability in shaping long-term economic growth. The analysis particularly applies to Regional Comprehensive Econ
content: This study aims to revisit the debate on the tourism-growth nexus, emphasising the importance of tourism and environmental sustainability in shaping long-term economic growth. The analysis particularly applies to Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) policymakers who aim to optimise tourism’s economic potential while addressing environmental concerns. Mainly, this study empirically analyses the impact of tourism, carbon (CO2) emissions, economic complexity (ECI), and foreign direct investment (FDI) on economic performance, measured by GDP per capita using data from 14 RCEP countries (Australia, Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, and Vietnam) from 1995–2022. To address the objectives, we employ a panel-ARDL estimator, specifically the Pooled Mean Group (PMG). The main findings indicate the existence of long-run cointegration between all the selected variables. The PMG results confirm the positive impacts of tourism, ECI, FDI, and carbon emissions on economic growth in RCEP countries within the period under study. In the short term, only tourism and carbon emissions show significant effects, while ECI and FDI do not have an immediate impact. Causality tests reveal a bidirectional relationship between ECI and growth, as well as between carbon emissions and growth. However, there is no causal relationship between tourism and growth, thereby rejecting the Tourism-Led Growth hypothesis in the short-term context. Based on these findings, the study suggests that RCEP countries prioritise enhancing economic complexity through innovation policies and industrial diversification, strengthening quality investments, promoting environmentally sustainable tourism, and reinforcing economic structures to withstand post-pandemic external shocks.

title: CULINARY CATALYSTS: DECIPHERING THE ROLE OF SUSTAINABLE RESTAURANTS IN THE JOURNEY TOWARD GREEN DESTINATION STATUS: THE CASE OF URLA, İZMIR, TÜRKIYE
summary: Sustainable destinations are increasingly relies on integrating localized eco-friendly practices across key service sectors. Gastronomy plays a pivotal role in reinforcing destination sustainability and regional brand equity. This study exa
content: Sustainable destinations are increasingly relies on integrating localized eco-friendly practices across key service sectors. Gastronomy plays a pivotal role in reinforcing destination sustainability and regional brand equity. This study examines the strategic role of gastronomy in positioning Urla as a recognized green destination. Specifically, the contribution of Michelin Green Star awarded restaurants to the overall environmental, social, and economic sustainability performance of green destinations is analyzed theoretically and empirically through the case of Urla. The conceptual integration of sustainable tourism governance and gastronomy is established through an extensive literature review and a theoretical framework. A qualitative case study design is employed to conduct an in-depth evaluation of Urla, a region that serves as a prominent exemplar of sustainable culinary tourism. Consequently, sustainable restaurant practices, localized supply chain operations, and green destination criteria are systematically evaluated through qualitative content analysis. This methodological structure allows for a comprehensive assessment of how regional gastronomic actors align with broader environmental governance and sustainability frameworks. The findings reveal that sustainability practices within the gastronomy sector significantly enhance the environmental, social, and economic performance of the destination. Michelin Green Star awarded restaurants serve as benchmark models that accelerate eco-innovation, circular economy integration, and local heritage preservation. Consequently, strengthening the synergy between sustainable tourism policies and gastronomic practices is critical for fostering long-term destination resilience and sustainable regional development.

title: NTENTION TO BE A GREEN TOURIST IN MACHU PICCHU BASED ON SOCIAL IDENTITY THEORY AND VALUE-BELIEF-NORM MODEL
summary: This study investigates how environmental concern and environmental attitude influence visitors' intention to adopt green behaviors at Machu Picchu, focusing on the mediating roles of green identity, environmental commitment, and personal n
content: This study investigates how environmental concern and environmental attitude influence visitors' intention to adopt green behaviors at Machu Picchu, focusing on the mediating roles of green identity, environmental commitment, and personal norms. Grounded in Social Identity Theory (SIT) and the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) theoretical model, the research establishes an integrated framework to examine pro-environmental decision-making in an ecologically and culturally vulnerable destination. Empirical data were collected through a structured online survey administered to tourists, and the proposed structural relationships were tested using multivariate structural equation modeling techniques. The results demonstrate that environmental concern has a significant, positive effect on both environmental commitment (0.616) and personal norms (0.672). Subsequently, environmental commitment (0.472) and personal norms (0.325) emerge as significant direct drivers of tourists' intention to engage in green tourism practices during their visit. Environmental attitude also exerts a direct, significant positive effect on green tourist intention (0.133), confirming that cognitive evaluations operate alongside moral and identity-based motivators. By situating this empirical inquiry within an iconic, globally recognized sanctuary that balances intense visitor flows with strict ecological protection, the study provides valuable insights into how internalized norms and self-identification shape responsible travel choices in fragile environments. Rather than relying solely on generic informational campaigns, the empirical findings highlight that park managers, tourism operators, and local conservation authorities must actively cultivate visitors' ecological identity and appeal to their personal ethical standards. Implementing targeted digital communication strategies and pre-trip educational initiatives that activate these normative beliefs offers a practical strategy to curb negative human impacts while safeguarding vulnerable cultural and natural heritage destinations worldwide.

title: LET’S VISIT ANGKOR ARCHAEOLOGICAL PARK: INITIATING GREEN SERVICE VALUE AND CSR IN SIEM REAP PROVINCE, CAMBODIA
summary: In the modern tourism landscape, green service value and corporate social responsibility (CSR) have evolved from optional ethical choices to fundamental drivers of business sustainability and competitive advantage. The advancement of these
content: In the modern tourism landscape, green service value and corporate social responsibility (CSR) have evolved from optional ethical choices to fundamental drivers of business sustainability and competitive advantage. The advancement of these indicators within the tourist destinations can significantly influence not only public trust but also intention to visit the destinations. This research investigates tourists’ visit intention in Angkor Archaeological Park in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia, by examining its associations with green service value and trust, along with CSR as the moderator. 500 data were gathered from both local and international tourists at four different international airports of Cambodia. These data were analyzed by using a Path Analysis Method. Results revealed that green service value influenced trust and visit intention, while trust influenced visit intention. These statistics indicated that when tourists perceived more benefit from consuming green services around the Angkor Archaeological Park, they not only trusted but also wanted to visit the Angkor Archaeological Park. Furthermore, the advancement of their trust further promoted higher intention to visit the Angkor Archaeological Park. Meanwhile, CSR moderated the links between green service value and visit intention and between trust and visit intention. These moderating outcomes underscored that the more practices of CSR significantly advanced the impacts of green service value and trust on tourists’ intention to visit the Angkor Archaeological Park. This research underlined the significant r oles of green service value and CSR in promoting tourists’ visit intention in Angkor Archaeological Park, located in Siem Reap Province of Cambodia. These outcomes suggest that the Cambodian Ministry of Tourism must focus on advancing green service values and CSR campaigns among local entrepreneurs. Strengthening these indicators in Siem Reap Province will help maintain sustainable tourist visit rates for the Angkor Archaeological Park.

title: The Chemical Matrix of Architectural Conservation: Molecular Mechanisms, Materials Incompatibility, and Advanced Intervention Strategies
summary: The preservation of architectural heritage has evolved from an empirical, craft-based practice into a rigorous scientific discipline grounded in fundamental and applied chemistry. Historic structures represent complex, dynamic physicochemic
content: The preservation of architectural heritage has evolved from an empirical, craft-based practice into a rigorous scientific discipline grounded in fundamental and applied chemistry. Historic structures represent complex, dynamic physicochemical systems in continuous equilibrium or disequilibrium with their ambient environments. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the chemical mechanisms governing the degradation of traditional building materials, focusing on the sulfation of carbonate rocks, subflorescence-driven salt weathering in porous silicates, and the structural pathology induced by the historical misuse of Portland cement in lime-mortar systems. Furthermore, we evaluate modern targeted chemical interventions, including sol-gel organosilicon consolidants, fluorinated polymer networks, chelate-mediated cleaning regimes, and surface hydrophobization. Finally, we discuss contemporary diagnostic paradigms, incorporating X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energydispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX), alongside emerging frontiers in alcohol-dispersed nanolime formulations and bacterial biomineralization. Shifting the conservation paradigm from universal applications to site-specific, molecularly tailored interventions is essential for mitigating risks and ensuring the long-term preservation of global cultural heritage.

title: AI-Based Performance Analysis of Renewable Energy Systems for Sustainable Power Generation
source: Global Journal of Engineering Innovations and Interdisciplinary Research
summary: The growing demand for clean and reliable energy has accelerated the adoption of renewable energysystems such as solar photovoltaic and wind power technologies. However, the inherent variabilityof renewable resources poses significant chall
content: The growing demand for clean and reliable energy has accelerated the adoption of renewable energysystems such as solar photovoltaic and wind power technologies. However, the inherent variabilityof renewable resources poses significant challenges in performance prediction, system optimization,and reliable power generation. This study presents an artificial intelligence–based framework forperformance analysis of renewable energy systems aimed at supporting sustainable power generation.Operational and environmental data are utilized to develop machine learning models capable ofcapturing complex, nonlinear relationships between system inputs and energy output. The AI-basedapproach is evaluated against conventional analytical methods using performance indicators suchas power output, efficiency, prediction accuracy, and response time. The results demonstrate that AI-driven models significantly improve prediction accuracy, reduce analysis time, and enhance systemperformance assessment under varying operating conditions. The findings highlight the potential ofartificial intelligence to improve operational efficiency, support intelligent energy management, andstrengthen the integration of renewable energy systems into sustainable power networks.

title: Efficient design and use of sustainable packaging materials for the organic products of the TONAEM association of small producers from Villa del Carbón in the UAEM Valley of Mexico
summary: Small producers of healthy and sustainable food play a crucial role in the fight against hunger and poverty. This study aims to design and improve packaging using wooden baskets made from sustainable materials for transporting fruit and veg
content: Small producers of healthy and sustainable food play a crucial role in the fight against hunger and poverty. This study aims to design and improve packaging using wooden baskets made from sustainable materials for transporting fruit and vegetables from the TONAEM association, located in Villa del Carbón, State of Mexico. The goal is to optimize the protection of products against shocks, vibrations, and temperature changes, as well as to maintain their freshness and quality through a design that allows for ventilation and humidity control. Training of personnel in loading techniques and compliance with food safety regulations is also being considered. A cost analysis and process optimization are being carried out to ensure logistical efficiency and the delivery of products in optimal conditions. The results will contribute to strengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of small producers in the region.
