Although TP prediction can fill some data gaps, the models are prone to combinatorial explosion, and predicted TPs must be prioritized. This study implemented multistep environmental biotic and novel abiotic TP prediction of the ZeroPM GCI chemicals using BioTransformer 4.0, combined with toxicity and mobility models to prioritize which TPs are potentially persistent, mobile, and toxic. The resulting GCI-TPs database contains over 13 million predicted TPs, including 5481 compounds labeled as potential dead-end compounds (compounds that are not predicted to transform further), of which 478 were predicted to be either PMT or PvM compounds. From this, 38 substructures that can act as flags for potential PMT-TP formation were identified. The dead-end PMT-TPs are available on the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange and through the GCI-TPs website (https://gcitps.lcsb.uni.lu/).

title: Biodiversity credits hold promise, yet credit-generating protocols require safeguards to realize potential
summary: Given the existing gap in biodiversity funding, mobilizing private finance will be essential to achieving global biodiversity conservation goals, especially across lower- and middle-income countries with limited capacity and public finance.
content: Given the existing gap in biodiversity funding, mobilizing private finance will be essential to achieving global biodiversity conservation goals, especially across lower- and middle-income countries with limited capacity and public finance. The emerging voluntary biodiversity market (VBM) holds promise to leverage private finance for biodiversity, but credit-generating protocols must be robust to prevent greenwashing and maximize effectiveness. In this study, the first to move beyond theoretical critiques and general market assessments of the VBM, we extracted details of program structure and crediting issuance from protocols for 13 relatively well-established biodiversity-crediting organizations. With these data, we evaluated protocols’ alignment with both conservation and restoration biology principles and lessons learned from the voluntary carbon market (VCM). We find that action must be taken to improve quantification of biodiversity impacts, especially incorporating patch size and connectivity in crediting and assessing projects on ecologically relevant timelines. Further, safeguards for additionality, leakage, risk, and verification from the VCM must be more robustly integrated in the VBM, and deep engagement and investment in local communities must be improved to ensure durable biodiversity-positive outcomes.

title: Label-free detection of para -phenylenediamine associated changes on human hair samples using droplet stretching assay
summary: -phenylenediamine (PPD), highlights the need for accessible approaches to assess PPD in human hair. The feasibility of a label-free droplet stretching assay (DSA) is assessed to evaluate changes in hair-surface wettability/hydrophilicity as
content: -phenylenediamine (PPD), highlights the need for accessible approaches to assess PPD in human hair. The feasibility of a label-free droplet stretching assay (DSA) is assessed to evaluate changes in hair-surface wettability/hydrophilicity associated with PPD treatment. The assay exploits the stretching behaviour of a water droplet placed on a human hair strand positioned within an open-surface microfluidic channel, providing an indirect measure of changes in hair-surface hydrophilicity. The droplet-stretching distance increased progressively with nominal PPD treatment concentrations, from untreated hair to hair treated with 2-6% w/v PPD. Commercial hair dye samples also exhibited droplet-stretching responses within the range observed for laboratory-prepared PPD-treated hair. Complementary scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy analyses provided supporting evidence of morphological alterations and chemical features associated with PPD exposure. Numerical simulations further indicated that droplet elongation is predominantly governed by wetting forces associated with surface interactions. Overall, this proof-of-concept study demonstrates the potential of DSA as a label-free, user-friendly approach for indirectly assessing PPD-associated changes in hair-surface wettability. However, other constituents of the hair dye powder, particularly oxidizing and reducing agents and additives, may also influence hair-surface properties and droplet movement. Further investigations involving diverse hair samples and additional treatment conditions are required to establish the analytical performance and broader applicability of the assay.

title: One system, many deaths: structural violence, boundary capture, and the global political economy of harm
summary: Critical scholarship, including this journal's work on infrastructural harm, documents organized harm that global systems produce across human and nonhuman populations. This article explains why that harm can be named as violence rather tha
content: Critical scholarship, including this journal's work on infrastructural harm, documents organized harm that global systems produce across human and nonhuman populations. This article explains why that harm can be named as violence rather than cost, and why the boundary between human and nonhuman harm is maintained as though natural. Showing that none of Galtung's criteria requires a human subject, and that sentience and ecosystem science specify nonhuman flourishing without rights claims, it extends structural violence beyond its anthropocentric boundary. Industrial animal agriculture and ecological extractivism show human and nonhuman harm produced through shared mechanisms of accumulation, externalization and differential valuation, though the harms differ in history and form. The core contribution, boundary capture, is capture not of the rules governing recognized subjects but of the prior question of which beings count as subjects of harm at all, sustained by industry's manufactured doubt and invisibility and by accumulated economic infrastructure.

title: The 'Urf (custom) of Capitalism: Decolonizing Sustainable Finance through Islamic Political Economy
source: International Journal of innovative inventions in Social Science and Humanities
summary: Sustainable finance is usually presented as a neutral body of technique: taxonomies, ratings, green bond principles and disclosure rules. This article reads it instead as a custom. In Islamic jurisprudence, 'urf (custom) can acquire legal f
content: Sustainable finance is usually presented as a neutral body of technique: taxonomies, ratings, green bond principles and disclosure rules. This article reads it instead as a custom. In Islamic jurisprudence, 'urf (custom) can acquire legal force when a practice becomes general, settled and unopposed by a clear text, which is why the classical maxim holds that custom is made the arbiter. We argue that a comparable process has taken place in global finance. Practices that began as the habits of a few financial centres, such as interest-bearing green debt, investor-centred materiality and rating-based screening, have spread until they now define what counts as sustainable finance everywhere, including in Muslim-majority and postcolonial economies. Joining usul al-fiqh reasoning on custom with decolonial theory and Islamic moral economy, the article asks whether this capitalist custom meets the tests that fiqh sets for valid 'urf. We find that much of it does not, because it rests on riba, shifts risk onto weaker parties and was generalised by market power rather than by the free acceptance of those it governs. Recent data show the scale of the imbalance: green and sustainability sukuk made up only 1.6% of global ESG bond issuance in the first nine months of 2023. Bangladesh, where Bangladesh Bank sets green and sustainable finance targets for all banks including Islamic banks, is used as a running illustration. The article closes with proposals for regulators, Shariah boards and Islamic banks, and with a frank account of what a conceptual study cannot show.

title: Value co-creation of digital health services in healthcare ecosystems – enacting sustainability of business models
summary: Purpose Value co-creation of digital health services is a critical strategy to create new digital health services as a purpose to address complex healthcare challenges and achieving sustainable business models. The aim of this study is to e
content: Purpose Value co-creation of digital health services is a critical strategy to create new digital health services as a purpose to address complex healthcare challenges and achieving sustainable business models. The aim of this study is to explore how value co-creation of digital health services enables sustainable business models in healthcare ecosystems, addressing the challenges posed by technological advancements, regulatory changes, and global health issues. It was found in our study that sustainable business models integrate economic, environmental, and social aspects into value co-creation of digital health services, delivery and capture, ensuring innovations are effective, economically viable, and environmentally responsible. However, achieving sustainable business models is challenging for private companies co-creating digital health services working in healthcare ecosystems because it requires an extensive number of actions from policy makers and healthcare providers related to the regulations, public procurements, standards, and ethical rules. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a qualitative, interpretive case study approach to examine explore value co-creation of digital health services enables sustainable business models in healthcare ecosystems. The study was conducted using the European Union's Horizon 2020 research project, inDemand as a case context using 2 workshops with 15 participants and 20 individual interviews as a main data source. Thematic content analysis was used to analyze data. Findings Value co-creation of digital health services enables sustainable business models in healthcare ecosystems by fostering collaboration among stakeholders, integrating economic, environmental, and social aspects, and addressing regulatory and ethical issues. Commitment from policy and hospital management levels, continuous national funding, and legislative improvements are essential for achieving sustainable value co-creation and business model viability. Originality/value This study advances sustainability and service research by explicitly linking value co-creation to the enactment of sustainable business models at the healthcare ecosystem level. Moving beyond firm-centric perspectives, it develops and empirically validates an integrative framework – Value & Opportunity, Governance Design, Models & Principles, and Stakeholder Engagement – showing how these interdependent constructs enable or hinder sustainability. Drawing on rich, multi-actor evidence from a large EU Horizon 2020 project, the study reveals structural, regulatory, and cultural tensions that explain why co-created digital health innovations often fail to scale. The findings offer actionable insights for policymakers, healthcare organizations, and digital health firms aiming to achieve long-term, ecosystem-level sustainability.

title: The Study of a Hyperloop Network in Europe
summary: This study presents a European network vision and feasibility assessment for hyperloop, an ultra-high-speed, low-emission guided transport system that could sustainably connect distances of > 800 km, supporting Trans-European Transport Netw
content: This study presents a European network vision and feasibility assessment for hyperloop, an ultra-high-speed, low-emission guided transport system that could sustainably connect distances of > 800 km, supporting Trans-European Transport Network objectives. Three network concepts are synthesized, and an 11,200 km reference network is considered, connecting continental EU member states at 750 km/h. Demand is estimated using a multinomial logit mode-choice model, combined with a gravity model and Eurostat aviation data. Financial and socio-economic performance is appraised using €0.039/pkm access charges, €60 million/km construction costs, and discount rates of 4% and 3%, respectively. For the fully developed reference network, 1.2 billion annual passengers are predicted, where 85% travels >800 km, 56% of continental air demand is shifted, 33% of trips use rail as a feeder, and 7% is induced. In the reference case, assuming an aviation improvement rate of 3.6%, the appraisal indicates a Financial/Economic Net Present Value of €18/€197 billion and a Benefit-to-Cost Ratio of 1.08/1.87. Under a business-as-usual aviation improvement rate of 1.0%, the Economic Net Present Value rises to €581 billion and the Benefit-to-Cost Ratio to 3.56. Hyperloop may therefore be viable on high-impact European corridors complementary to rail and foster modal shift to more sustainable alternatives.

title: Modeling the isentropic efficiency of small compressors operating with transcritical CO₂: Experimental analysis and development of dimensionless correlations
summary: This study experimentally investigates the overall isentropic efficiency of a small hermetic reciprocating compressor (1.75 cm³/rev) operating in a transcritical CO₂ heat pump under warm climate conditions and develops predictive correlatio
content: This study experimentally investigates the overall isentropic efficiency of a small hermetic reciprocating compressor (1.75 cm³/rev) operating in a transcritical CO₂ heat pump under warm climate conditions and develops predictive correlations tailored to the investigated compressor. A total of 245 steady-state operating points, covering pressure ratios between 1.2 and 2.6, were obtained from a controlled experimental campaign. Conventional polynomial correlations based exclusively on the pressure ratio were initially developed and statistically evaluated, yielding coefficients of determination greater than 0.95. However, increased experimental data dispersion was observed at pressure ratios above approximately 2.0, which may be associated with the combined effects of elevated discharge temperatures, increased compression irreversibilities, and the strong thermophysical sensitivity of CO₂ in the transcritical region. To improve the predictive capability of the pressure-ratio-based models, a multivariable dimensionless correlation was developed for the investigated compressor, incorporating the pressure ratio, compressor volumetric efficiency, reduced temperatures, and gas cooler heat capacity ratio. The proposed model achieved an adjusted coefficient of determination of 0.989 and reduced the mean absolute relative deviation (MARD) of overall isentropic efficiency predictions to 4.29%, outperforming the conventional correlations based exclusively on pressure ratio within the investigated experimental domain. The experimental results further revealed an increasing trend in the overall isentropic efficiency throughout the investigated pressure ratio range, without identifying a maximum efficiency condition. This finding highlights the importance of considering the thermal operating limitations of the investigated compressor, particularly under warm climate conditions, where increasing discharge temperatures may restrict the accessible operating range before a maximum efficiency condition can be experimentally identified. Furthermore, integrating the proposed correlation into the heat pump thermodynamic model improved the prediction of the experimental coefficient of performance (COP), yielding a global MARD of 2.52% across the investigated operating conditions. An additional independent experimental assessment under representative warm climate conditions resulted in absolute relative deviations of 1.60% for overall isentropic efficiency and 1.16% for COP. Overall, the results demonstrate the importance of incorporating dimensionless parameters associated with the thermal and volumetric operating conditions when predicting the overall isentropic efficiency of the investigated small-capacity compressor. The proposed formulation provides an improved predictive representation within the experimentally investigated domain and can support the thermodynamic modeling of small-capacity transcritical CO₂ heat pumps operating under similar conditions, particula

title: From Policy to Proposals: A Training Manual on Integrating Gender and Health into Climate Finance
summary: This manual equips Commonwealth National Climate Finance Advisers and their counterparts in development and government with practical tools to integrate gender and health considerations into climate finance proposals, making it possible to
content: This manual equips Commonwealth National Climate Finance Advisers and their counterparts in development and government with practical tools to integrate gender and health considerations into climate finance proposals, making it possible to move from policy commitments to bankable investments.

title: Exploring Socio-economic Benefits of Digital Services in Freight Transport: A System Dynamics Approach
summary: Freight transport plays a key role in Sweden’s road system, but faces growing challenges related to safety, sustainability, and efficiency. Digital services are increasingly seen as promising tools to support planning, reduce emissions and
content: Freight transport plays a key role in Sweden’s road system, but faces growing challenges related to safety, sustainability, and efficiency. Digital services are increasingly seen as promising tools to support planning, reduce emissions and road wear, and complement physical infrastructure. Yet, their system-level benefits remain difficult to assess, due to context-specific factors and a lack of robust evaluation methods. This paper uses a systems thinking approach to explore two such services: Road Works Warning (RWW) and Intelligent Access Control (IAC). Four future scenarios were developed based on uncertainties in governance and digitalization by 2037, in line with the Swedish Transport Administration’s planning horizon. Drawing on stakeholder workshops and expert interviews, Causal Loop Diagrams (CLDs) were constructed to understand how feedback loops, actor roles, and institutional conditions shape the success or failure of these services. The results show that benefits are closely tied to governance coordination and stakeholder engagement, and that different actors play enabling roles depending on the scenario. This paper reflects on how CLDs, when combined with future scenarios, can support more adaptive and robust planning for digital freight services.

title: Message Framing Strategies in Sustainability Communication: An Analysis in Türkiye
summary: Sustainability communication has become a strategic priority for organizations demonstrating their environmental, social, and economic commitments, and social media makes audience reactions observable. This study asks whether the framing ch
content: Sustainability communication has become a strategic priority for organizations demonstrating their environmental, social, and economic commitments, and social media makes audience reactions observable. This study asks whether the framing characteristics of corporate sustainability messages affect consumer engagement in Türkiye. A total of 166 sustainability-related Instagram posts published in 2025 by companies in the BIST Sustainability 25 Index were content-analyzed across five framing variables; gain/loss framing, message direction, tonality, emotional appeal, and temporal focus, and engagement was measured through likes, comments, and shares. Three hypotheses were tested with independent samples t-tests on log-transformed engagement. Only temporal focus was significant: present-focused messages attracted higher engagement than future-focused ones, whereas tonality and emotional appeal did not. The immediacy of a message, rather than its tone, appears to drive engagement.

title: Smart and Green Logistics: Harnessing Digital Innovation for Maritime Decarbonization in Türkiye
summary: This study examines how digital technologies contribute to environmental sustainability and competitiveness in Türkiye’s maritime logistics industry. As Türkiye seeks to enhance its global logistics competitiveness while meeting internation
content: This study examines how digital technologies contribute to environmental sustainability and competitiveness in Türkiye’s maritime logistics industry. As Türkiye seeks to enhance its global logistics competitiveness while meeting international decarbonization targets, the research examines how innovations such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and smart port systems contribute to efficient, resilient, and low-carbon port operations. The study aims to establish an integrated framework that connects digital adoption with both environmental and operational performance, providing valuable insights for policy and practice. To achieve this, a mixed-methods design is utilized. Quantitative analysis is conducted using stakeholder surveys and secondary macro-level datasets. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) is applied to survey data to examine causal relationships among digital adoption, institutional readiness, and sustainability outcomes, while panel data regression is used to analyze national-level logistics and environmental indicators. These quantitative analyses are complemented by qualitative insights from expert interviews. The study presents a framework for integrating digital and green strategies into maritime logistics, offering policymakers and industry stakeholders valuable insights to align digital transformation with sustainability objectives. It contributes to discussions on smart transport systems and supports Türkiye’s shift towards climate-resilient logistics infrastructure.

title: Sustainable Cultivation and Nutritional Analysis of Pleurotus ostreatus Grown on Lignocellulosic Aquatic Waste Substrate.
summary: Sustainable management of agricultural waste remains a critical global issue, which requires innovative biotechnological solutions. These help to enhance resource efficiency and support a circular bioeconomy. This study assesses the efficac
content: Sustainable management of agricultural waste remains a critical global issue, which requires innovative biotechnological solutions. These help to enhance resource efficiency and support a circular bioeconomy. This study assesses the efficacy of water hyacinth as substrate for Pleurotus ostreatus cultivation, investigating the biological efficiency, growth parameters, and proximate analysis of P. ostreatus cultivated on water hyacinth and paddy straw, addressing the potential for these underutilized resources to enhance mushroom production. Also compared total yields over multiple harvests were also compared, and nutritional content was analyzed according to AOAC and IS standards. The results show that paddy straw substrate produces mushrooms with higher nutritional value and better yield. Indicating that water hyacinth, an invasive aquatic weed, is an effective protein- rich alternative to traditional agricultural residues for sustainable mushroom cultivation.

title: Benchmarking analysis of governance of Pakistan’s formative carbon market framework against China and India
summary: Currently, Pakistan faces twin challenges; extreme climate vulnerability and macroeconomic instability, both of which demand forward looking climate finance mechanisms. In this study, we evaluate Pakistan Policy Guidelines for Trading in Ca
content: Currently, Pakistan faces twin challenges; extreme climate vulnerability and macroeconomic instability, both of which demand forward looking climate finance mechanisms. In this study, we evaluate Pakistan Policy Guidelines for Trading in Carbon Markets: 2024 through a structured qualitative comparative analysis against two regional models: China’s compliance-based National Emissions Trading System (ETS) and India’s evolving Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS). We examine these frameworks across four core governance pillars: policy mandates, Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems, sectoral coverage, and economic resilience. The study identifies critical institutional capacity gaps in Pakistan, including the absence of mandatory industrial compliance obligations and a fully operational national carbon registry. Using the Porter Hypothesis and the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) as interpretive frameworks, the study suggests that the absence of mandatory carbon pricing may weaken incentives for industrial green innovation (SDG 9) and climate action (SDG 13). We recommend that Pakistan adopt a phased, hybrid transition model like India’s CCTS before shifting toward a mature compliance system like China’s National ETS.

title: Non-Compliance Probability Quantification to Assess Risks Hindering the Sustainability of Logistics Solutions
summary: In the rapidly evolving logistics sector, AI-driven solutions are increasingly used to optimize supply chains; however, significant gaps remain in assessing the sustainability performance of logistics operations. Standardized indicators and
content: In the rapidly evolving logistics sector, AI-driven solutions are increasingly used to optimize supply chains; however, significant gaps remain in assessing the sustainability performance of logistics operations. Standardized indicators and robust frameworks that reflect current technologies and industry practices are still needed. This study addresses these limitations by developing a novel framework that integrates performance indicators with Bayesian network modelling to quantify sustainability non-compliance risk. Through analysis of 428 logistics indicators from EU-funded projects and expert validation, a core set of indicators has been consolidated through a three-level filtering process to construct a probabilistic risk model. The Bayesian network captures causal relationships among organizational, technical, and operational factors influencing sustainability outcomes. Implemented to an AI-powered logistics marketplace, the framework demonstrates the ability to quantify non-compliance probability and identify critical risk factors. The framework provides logistics stakeholders with a comprehensive assessment tool that transforms diverse sustainability dimensions into a unified risk metric, enabling targeted mitigation strategies and informed decision-making for sustainable logistics operations.

title: Biomaterials and biofabrication in the Netherlands: state of the art in 2026
summary: Biomaterials and biofabrication are multidisciplinary and rapidly evolving fields that enable innovations that are crucial for addressing current healthcare challenges. The Netherlands has a broad, active, and collaborative research communi
content: Biomaterials and biofabrication are multidisciplinary and rapidly evolving fields that enable innovations that are crucial for addressing current healthcare challenges. The Netherlands has a broad, active, and collaborative research community that is developing advanced biomaterials and cutting.edge biofabrication methods, with applications in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, in vitro disease modeling, and biomedical devices. Dutch researchers have pioneered advanced biofabrication, supramolecular and inorganic chemistry for creating biomaterials, organoids and organ-on-chip in vitro platforms, and regenerative medicine. This paper presents recent work on biomaterials and biofabrication and their applications from 11 prominent research institutions across the Netherlands, and it describes joint initiatives that target broader goals within the field. Contributors from each institution provide insights into recent progress, key scientific contributions, and forward-looking perspectives. By presenting the state-of-the-art research landscape, this article serves as a reference for scientists actively engaged in or planning to initiate biofabrication or biomaterials-related research, offering guidance on technology selection, experimental design, academic collaboration, and translational development.

title: Valuing Nature in Rail Infrastructure: Applying the ECOV4R Framework in the UK and Spain
summary: Railways both depend on and impact nature, yet ecosystem services remain underrepresented in infrastructure planning and asset management. The Ecosystem Valuation for Railways (ECOV4R) framework addresses this gap by providing a scalable, s
content: Railways both depend on and impact nature, yet ecosystem services remain underrepresented in infrastructure planning and asset management. The Ecosystem Valuation for Railways (ECOV4R) framework addresses this gap by providing a scalable, structured methodology to assess and monetise ecosystem services influenced by rail infrastructure and operations. Designed for planners, asset managers, consultants, and decision-makers, ECOV4R complements environmental impact assessments and cost-benefit analyses by quantifying both positive contributions and negative impacts. It supports evidence-based decisions and the integration of ecosystem value into planning, project design, and sustainability reporting. The framework was piloted in two sites: the Cotswold Line in the UK, and a high-speed rail upgrade near León, Spain, demonstrating ECOV4R’s utility for both forward-looking design and post-construction evaluation.

title: The SPOTLOG Approach: A Review of Good Practices for Sustainable Last-Mile Logistics
summary: The logistics sector has been experiencing a growing demand for fast and flexible deliveries, largely due to the rise of e-commerce, which has led to an overload of road infrastructure (congestion), as well as environmental impacts caused b
content: The logistics sector has been experiencing a growing demand for fast and flexible deliveries, largely due to the rise of e-commerce, which has led to an overload of road infrastructure (congestion), as well as environmental impacts caused by the mode of transport used or the need for deliveries in low-density regions. Therefore, it is essential to create organised operations, route optimisation and the use of low-carbon vehicles to improve last-mile logistics and make it more sustainable. Political support for the transition to sustainable logistics is imperative for this to be possible. In this context, the SPOTLOG Project promotes the development of socially responsible logistics systems with zero carbon emissions, actively involving local communities and leveraging the digitalisation of freight and passenger transport. Focusing on low-density areas and medium-sized cities, SPOTLOG supports regional policy instruments aligned with the European goals of inclusive and sustainable mobility. Through a multidisciplinary consortium of 13 partners in eight European countries, along with discovery partners from Ukraine and Moldova, the project addresses last-mile delivery challenges and wider urban logistics impacts. By sharing good practices and integrating practical innovations with policy development, SPOTLOG provides a replicable framework for sustainable urban logistics across Europe.

title: Can We Afford to Drive? Developing a Framework for Vehicle Affordability Analysis in the European Union
summary: This paper presents a decision-tree framework for assessing vehicle affordability. The framework defines affordability across five stages: acquisition, loan eligibility and cost, fixed costs, variable costs, and budget impact, linking each
content: This paper presents a decision-tree framework for assessing vehicle affordability. The framework defines affordability across five stages: acquisition, loan eligibility and cost, fixed costs, variable costs, and budget impact, linking each to household disposable income. Unlike conventional approaches focused on purchase price or total cost of ownership, it reflects the full decision-making process faced by households. An illustrative case study for Italy shows that while households can often access and finance vehicles, ownership costs can create sustained financial pressure and may render ownership unaffordable, particularly for middle- and lower-income groups. Affordability pressures arise mainly from the total cost of ownership relative to income, rather than from constraints in purchasing vehicles. The framework provides a practical tool for identifying affordability stress. It is developed in the context of the European Union’s transition to carbon-neutral mobility, where it can be used to compare the affordability of different options and inform policies supporting a just transition.

title: Shifting Freight from Road to Water: Mapping the Innovation Ecosystem for Automated and Zero-Emission Inland and Coastal Shipping
summary: Achieving a modal shift from road to inland waterways and short-sea shipping is a key ambition of EU transport decarbonisation. Yet the operational deployment of automated navigation and zero-emission propulsion in freight-relevant inland a
content: Achieving a modal shift from road to inland waterways and short-sea shipping is a key ambition of EU transport decarbonisation. Yet the operational deployment of automated navigation and zero-emission propulsion in freight-relevant inland and coastal shipping remains fragmented across pilots and niche routes. This paper maps a European innovation ecosystem focused on (i) publicly funded research and innovation (R&I) activities and (ii) publicly reported demonstrators for freight-relevant vessels and transferable technologies. We screened 149 R&I projects, extracted 1,685 participant records, and consolidated them into 657 unique stakeholders. In parallel, we compiled a catalogue of 122 prototype and pilot vessels that demonstrate automation/autonomy and/or defined zero-emission operating potential (battery-electric and/or hydrogen fuel cell). The analysis separates shipbuilding-oriented roles (design, shipyards, system integrators) from operations-oriented roles (operators, logistics, ports, waterway authorities, shippers) and distinguishes component-level innovation from vessel-level integration (newbuild/retrofit pilots). Results point to dense collaboration networks, a stronger supply-side emphasis than demand-side participation, and clear dependencies on corridor infrastructure readiness. Geographic patterns are reported as observed clusters in the screened public sources and should not be interpreted as a complete ranking of national innovation capability.

title: Orchestrating Physical Internet-Led Urban Logistics Through Comprehensive Planning and Implementation Guidance from Meta Model Suite
summary: Rising CO 2 emissions from urban logistics, intensified by e-commerce growth, demand urgent sustainable solutions. Physical Internet (PI)-driven approaches, based on shared and collaborative concepts, show significant promise for creating e
content: Rising CO 2 emissions from urban logistics, intensified by e-commerce growth, demand urgent sustainable solutions. Physical Internet (PI)-driven approaches, based on shared and collaborative concepts, show significant promise for creating efficient, interconnected logistics networks. However, cities often lack the expertise to orchestrate such transformative actions and effectively integrate the necessary digital and physical infrastructure. The Meta Model Suite (MMS) of the EU-funded DISCO project addresses this gap, with a primary goal of providing comprehensive guidance to city authorities through a structured, digital framework. The MMS assists cities in assessing their current logistics systems (including PI-led innovation readiness and digital maturity), facilitates the creation of future logistics scenarios and supports the selection of tailored “DISCO-X” innovations. Furthermore, the MMS offers a blueprint for developing necessary data frameworks, including local urban logistics dataspaces, and provides access to a library of tools and identifies essential infrastructure and potentially supportive regulations for the successful implementation of these PI-led solutions. Demonstrations in Living Labs such as Ghent, Copenhagen, Thessaloniki and Helsinki aim to validate these PI-led solutions, showcasing their potential to reduce congestion and emissions while improving service delivery, thereby fostering more sustainable and digitally competitive urban environments.

title: From Circular Production to Consumer Value: Transparency and Layered Consumer Information as Market Mechanisms in Circular Agri-Food Systems
summary: Circular production systems can reduce resource dependency, retain nutrients and bio-mass in productive use, and valorize unavoidable side-streams, but their economic viability de-pends partly on whether consumers recognize and reward circu
content: Circular production systems can reduce resource dependency, retain nutrients and bio-mass in productive use, and valorize unavoidable side-streams, but their economic viability de-pends partly on whether consumers recognize and reward circular attributes that are often invisible at purchase. This conceptual article develops a Circular Value Translation Framework linking circular production to verified transparency and traceability, trust, perceived consumer value, willingness to pay (WTP), and value transmitted back to producers. Its two core contributions are a layered consumer information architecture combining a visible standardized verified core with optional channel-appropriate depth under realistic low-involvement food-choice conditions, and a value-capture feedback loop making producer adoption conditional on premium pass-through, bargaining power, and transition costs. Ten falsifiable propositions specify causal links, label substitution or complementarity, individual moderators, situational frictions, and value transmission. The synthesis integrates circular-food evidence with agricultural-economics research on technology adoption, credence labeling, market power, and vertical price transmission, and proposes prioritized empirical tests and practical implications for producers, cooperatives, certification bodies, retailers, and policymakers.

title: Synchromodal Network Transport Management System Adaptability for Inland Navigation. Lessons from Po River, Italy
summary: Inland navigation is one of the most environmentally friendly modes of freight transport, utilizing existing or human-made infrastructure and consuming only a fraction of the energy required by other modes, giving it significant potential t
content: Inland navigation is one of the most environmentally friendly modes of freight transport, utilizing existing or human-made infrastructure and consuming only a fraction of the energy required by other modes, giving it significant potential to contribute towards the pressing CO 2 emissions goals set by the EU through the Green Deal. However, a further shift of cargo to inland navigation requires a reliable and resilient Inland Waterway Transport (IWT) system of adequate capacity with aligned standards and regulations. Climate change impacts on rivers, operational issues arising from aging infrastructure and low digitalization, make it difficult for vessel operators to maintain competitiveness. This paper explores the potential contribution of Corridor Management Systems (CMS) adapted to river particularities and enabling the concept of synchromodality to build resilient and attractive IWT systems. Stakeholder consultations indicated unanimous agreement that such a system would improve continuity of operations within the logistics network, with over 75% also indicating that it would enhance navigability of inland waterways. The analysis focuses on core functionalities of such systems and implementation challenges, with particular focus to the Po River in Italy.

title: The Role of Plants in Industry: Eco-Friendly Approaches
summary: The utilization of industrial plants provides an interdisciplinary framework linking eco-design, sustainable production, and landscape architecture through their potential as renewable raw material resources and their multifunctional applic
content: The utilization of industrial plants provides an interdisciplinary framework linking eco-design, sustainable production, and landscape architecture through their potential as renewable raw material resources and their multifunctional applications. This study aimed to examine the potential applications of industrial plants across different industrial sectors and evaluate their aesthetic, ecological, and economic functions in landscape architecture. Within this scope, the fundamental principles of eco-design, industrial applications of plant-based raw materials, and design examples developed across different product categories were examined in detail. The review covered applications in household appliances, automotive, textiles, furniture, toys, packaging, architectural elements, and cosmetics, while the key characteristics, raw material potential, and landscape design applications of industrial plants were comparatively evaluated. The examined examples indicate that plant fibers, natural oils, starch derivatives, and biomass can be utilized in biobased material production, while ornamental plants with industrial value offer multifunctional applications through their visual and sensory characteristics, ecosystem services, and potential for raw material production. However, the renewable nature of plant-based raw materials alone is insufficient to ensure environmental sustainability. Cultivation conditions, water and energy consumption, processing methods, maintenance requirements, and end-of-life waste management must be evaluated from a life cycle perspective. In conclusion, it is considered that the selection of species suited to local ecological conditions, the reuse of plant-derived by-products, and the adoption of circular design principles could facilitate the more effective utilization of industrial plants in environmentally friendly production processes and the development of multifunctional urban landscapes.

title: Encouraging Sustainable Behavior in E-Commerce: Insights from Behavioral Research and Logistics Innovation
summary: The rapid growth of e-commerce is intensifying environmental im-pacts, particularly emissions and urban congestion from deliveries and returns. Addressing these challenges requires both innovative logistics solutions and a shift in consumer
content: The rapid growth of e-commerce is intensifying environmental im-pacts, particularly emissions and urban congestion from deliveries and returns. Addressing these challenges requires both innovative logistics solutions and a shift in consumer behaviour. This study explores how consumers understand the environmental footprint of e-commerce and what influences their delivery and return choices. Key barriers to sustainable behaviour include a lack of transparent information, limited low-emission options, and convenience-driven habits. In response, behavioural interventions such as eco-labels, de-fault settings, and targeted nudges have been designed to promote more sustainable decisions. These interventions are being integrated with zero-emission delivery strategies and circular return systems through a stakeholder co-creation process. Using design thinking, retailers, logistics providers, public authorities, and consumers col-laborate to ensure solutions are both impactful and user-friendly. The approach aims to reduce emissions, traffic, and waste associated with e-commerce while aligning with broader urban sustainability and mobility goals. This paper shares early behavioural insights and demonstrate how combining behavioural science with logistics inno-vation can support a more sustainable future for online shopping to-wards zero emission last mile delivery.

title: How an Intermodal Routing Platform Makes Rail Freight Accessible
summary: Freight volumes are rising across all transport modes, with logistics contributing approx. 25% of Europe’s CO 2 -equivalents. EU’s Green Deal targets a higher rail freight modal share to reduce transport-related emissions. While combined tr
content: Freight volumes are rising across all transport modes, with logistics contributing approx. 25% of Europe’s CO 2 -equivalents. EU’s Green Deal targets a higher rail freight modal share to reduce transport-related emissions. While combined traffic grows, rail freight faces challenges: complex routing, multiple stakeholders, and interface barriers, plus some customers lack sidings. However, rail’s environmental and efficiency advantages over road transport remain clear. Passenger transport has had user-friendly platforms for years (e.g. Google Maps, DB Navigator) providing seamless travel information regardless of necessary changes between means of transport. Rail freight lacks such an intermodal information resource facilitating the access. FP5-TRANS4M-R’s workstream Seamless Freight addresses this gap by delivering a routing platform for intermodal services. The platform’s functionalities are based on developed use cases considering stakeholder needs, enabling shippers and logistic service providers to compare door-to-door options from various operators, using intelligent algorithms considering time, cost, emissions, and loading gauges. Conversion to data standards allows for easy integration with additional operators. Complementing functions such as booking and tracking can be connected. In FP5-TRANS4M-R, value chain partners collaborate to address stakeholder needs, fostering practical solutions to current freight challenges. This paper introduces and envisions an information platform for intermodal services, improving access to sustainable transport solutions.

title: Just Transition: (Un)foreseen Consolidation in Shipping?
summary: Shipping is a hard-to-abate sector with strong fossil fuel path dependencies, yet the IMO now targets net-zero emissions by 2050. This paper investigates whether split incentives between shipowners and charterers, combined with growing regu
content: Shipping is a hard-to-abate sector with strong fossil fuel path dependencies, yet the IMO now targets net-zero emissions by 2050. This paper investigates whether split incentives between shipowners and charterers, combined with growing regulatory (IMO GHG Strategy, EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, RED III) and technological complexity (e.g., LNG, methanol, hydrogen, ammonia), implicitly drive market consolidation. Using a mixed-methods approach, stakeholder mapping, fleet data analysis, and semi-structured interviews, we find indications that larger owners adopt alternative fuels earlier, while smaller owners face disproportionate compliance burdens. Complexity, more than split incentives, emerges as a key consolidation driver, risking an unjust transition with unforeseen winners and losers. Policy should focus on reducing complexity, improving transparency, and promoting contractual innovations that align incentives with intended impact. Future research should quantify complexity (e.g., man-hours per vessel) and assess long-term distributional impacts to ensure a fair and effective maritime decarbonization pathway.

title: Kurumsal Sera Gazı Envanteri ve Karbon Bilgisinin Güvencesi
summary: Kurumsal sera gazı envanterleri, kuruluşların iklim performansını değerlendirmelerinde ve sürdürülebilirlik beyanlarını oluşturmalarında giderek daha önemli bir yer tutmaktadır. Ancak raporlanan emisyon ve uzaklaştırım miktarları, fiziksel
content: Kurumsal sera gazı envanterleri, kuruluşların iklim performansını değerlendirmelerinde ve sürdürülebilirlik beyanlarını oluşturmalarında giderek daha önemli bir yer tutmaktadır. Ancak raporlanan emisyon ve uzaklaştırım miktarları, fiziksel süreçlerin doğrudan bir yansıması değildir. Bu miktarlar, organizasyonel sınırların belirlenmesi, kurumsal tahsis, veri seçimi, hesaplama yöntemleri, sınıflandırma ve raporlama kararları sonucunda oluşturulan kurumsal bilgileri ifade eder. Bu kitap, söz konusu bilginin nasıl üretildiğini, hangi koşullarda güvenilir kabul edilebileceğini ve bağımsız değerlendirme sonuçlarının nasıl yorumlanması gerektiğini bütüncül bir yaklaşımla incelemektedir. On üç bölümden oluşan eser, kurumsal sera gazı muhasebesinin kavramsal ve normatif temellerini ISO 14064-1 ve GHG Protocol çerçevesinde ele almaktadır. Bunun yanı sıra sera gazı emisyonlarının nicelleştirilmesi, belirsizlik, Kapsam 2 ve Kapsam 3 muhasebesi, dönemler arası karşılaştırılabilirlik ve baz yılın yeniden hesaplanması konularını incelemektedir. Kaynak veri kalitesi, veri kökeni, işleme süreçleri, dijital sistemler, iç kontrol ve kurumsal yönetişim, doğrulama ve güvence mekanizmalarıyla birlikte ele alınmaktadır. Ayrıca bağımsız değerlendirmenin sağladığı güvenin kapsamı ve sınırları açıklanmaktadır. Kurumsal iklim beyanları, hesap verebilirlik ve yeşil aklama riski de bu çerçevede ele alınmaktadır. Kitabın temel katkısı, karbon bilgisinin güvenilirliğini yalnızca hesaplamaların doğruluğuna veya bir güvence görüşünün varlığına bağlamak yerine, fiziksel olgudan kurumsal beyana ve karar süreçlerinde kullanıma uzanan bilgi, kanıt ve sorumluluk zinciri üzerinden ele almasıdır. Bu yönüyle eser, araştırmacılar, sürdürülebilirlik uzmanları, raporlama sorumluları ve bağımsız değerlendirme alanındaki okuyucular için analitik bir başvuru çerçevesi sunmaktadır.

title: Influencer Marketing and Crisis Communication on Social Media: An Experimental Study of Moral Transparency and Spokesperson Type
source: Journal of Contingencies and Crisis Management
summary: Influencer marketing has become an increasingly important component of organizational communication strategies. As organizations align themselves with influencers, they may also become vulnerable to reputational risks associated with influe
content: Influencer marketing has become an increasingly important component of organizational communication strategies. As organizations align themselves with influencers, they may also become vulnerable to reputational risks associated with influencer misconduct: when influencers become involved in public controversies, negative perceptions may spill over onto associated brands, creating a need for organizations to respond effectively. Research on influencer‐related crises has examined how such spillover arises and how followers react, but has paid less attention to how the content and the source of the brand's own response shape stakeholder reactions. An online experiment ( N = 192) examined how moral transparency, spokesperson type, and emotional responses shape stakeholder evaluations and behavioral intentions following an influencer‐related sustainability crisis on Instagram. A response that admitted fault, explained the situation and announced corrective action led to higher message credibility and corporate trust and to lower negative word‐of‐mouth intentions than a vague non‐apology. Whether the response was posted from the CEO's personal account or from the brand account had no detectable effect on any outcome, and no interaction effects were found. Sympathy carried part of the effect of moral transparency on all three outcomes, whereas the evidence for apprehension was inconclusive. The findings suggest that the benefits of accountable, accommodative crisis responses identified in previous research also hold when the reputational threat originates with an associated influencer, and that sympathy is a likely pathway through which such responses work.

title: Agro-industrial residues as sustainable potting media for growth and flowering of chrysanthemum (Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat.)
summary: The effect of various agro-industrial residues as potting media on the growth and flowering of Chrysanthemum morifolium cv. ‘Basanti’ was evaluated in the present study during 2019, 2020 and 2021. Potting media combinations were prepared by
content: The effect of various agro-industrial residues as potting media on the growth and flowering of Chrysanthemum morifolium cv. ‘Basanti’ was evaluated in the present study during 2019, 2020 and 2021. Potting media combinations were prepared by separately mixing spent mushroom compost, burnt rice husk, bagasse, groundnut shells and soybean husk compost with cocopeat and perlite at a 1 : 1 : 1 (v/v/v) ratio. The experiments were laid out in a completely randomised design with 6 treatments and 4 replications. All the potting media combinations were analysed for initial chemical properties and nutrient content. Results revealed that spent mushroom compost : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) and soybean husk compost : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) were the most suited media for chrysanthemum plants. Average of 3 years data showed that chrysanthemum plants raised in soybean husk compost : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) exhibited significant increase in plant height (PH, 25.76 cm), plant spread (PS, 30.52 cm), secondary branches plant-1 (SB, 11.68), buds plant-1 (59.28) and flowers plant -1 (56.12) compared to plants grown in control. Flower yield was significantly higher in chrysanthemum plants grown in media spent mushroom compost : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) (134 g plant-1). Growth and flowering parameters were lowest in bagasse : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) and cocopeat : vermiculite : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) media. Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis (PCA) and correlation) also confirmed these results. Also, leaf nutrient content of chrysanthemum plants showed significant response to potting media combinations. Experimental results demonstrated that spent mushroom compost : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) and soybean husk compost : cocopeat : perlite (1 : 1 : 1) were most promising potting media combinations to produce potted chrysanthemum plants of cv. ‘Basanti’. Their use as potting media enables sustainable recycling of agro-industrial residues.

title: ESG disclosure, capital intensity, and corporate financial distress: the role of sustainability governance and executive incentives
summary: This study examines the joint effects of ESG disclosure and capital intensity on corporate financial distress and investigates whether sustainability governance verification (SGV) and ESG-linked executive compensation moderate these relatio
content: This study examines the joint effects of ESG disclosure and capital intensity on corporate financial distress and investigates whether sustainability governance verification (SGV) and ESG-linked executive compensation moderate these relationships. Using panel data from 568 firms across 40 countries over 2015–2024, obtained from the Bloomberg–DataStream database, the study employs firm fixed effects, year fixed effects, and firm-clustered standard errors as the primary estimation approach. Corporate financial distress is measured using the Altman Z-score, with higher values indicating stronger financial health and lower financial distress. Robustness is assessed using two-step system GMM, an alternative financial distress measure, disaggregated ESG dimensions, and subsample analyses based on industry and governance characteristics. The results show that capital intensity is negatively associated with the Altman Z-score, whereas ESG disclosure has no significant direct association with financial distress. However, the ESG × capital intensity interaction is positive and statistically significant, indicating that higher ESG disclosure attenuates the negative association between capital intensity and the Altman Z-score. Subsample analyses provide preliminary evidence that this moderating relationship is more evident among firms with sustainability governance verification and those incorporating climate-related or broader ESG objectives into executive compensation arrangements. The system GMM results confirm the positive and significant interaction, although the direct effect of capital intensity becomes statistically insignificant. Overall, the findings suggest that ESG disclosure provides a buffering mechanism that partially mitigates the adverse financial implications of capital intensity without eliminating its negative association with financial health.

title: Understanding post-adoption heterogeneity in electric vehicle use: A perception-based user segmentation
source: European journal of transport and infrastructure research
summary: This study investigates the perceptual dynamics of electric vehicle (EV) use in the post-adoption phase, focusing on how active users evaluate advantages and disadvantages. Moving beyond approaches that assume an inverse relationship betwee
content: This study investigates the perceptual dynamics of electric vehicle (EV) use in the post-adoption phase, focusing on how active users evaluate advantages and disadvantages. Moving beyond approaches that assume an inverse relationship between perceived benefits and risks, we argue that these perceptions can coexist and that the multidimensional nature of post-adoption experience should not be overlooked. The study addresses three research questions: (i) How are post-adoption perceptual dimensions shaped among active EV users? (ii) What benefit–risk perceptions emerge across user segments? (iii) What policy recommendations can be derived for Turkish and European urban contexts? Using data collected in early 2025, we examine Turkey’s Marmara Region, characterized by rapid EV adoption. Exploratory Factor Analysis and K-means Cluster Analysis identify eight perceptual dimensions and three segments: comfort-oriented satisfied users, performance-oriented users with high perceived technical risk, and cautious pragmatic users. Findings indicate that performance-oriented users exhibit strong sensitivity to technological risks due to high technical awareness despite high satisfaction. The majority perceive infrastructure constraints as a persistent barrier despite prolonged use. The results offer transferable insights for European urban contexts facing increasing EV user heterogeneity and support strategic interventions for decarbonization. To effectively foster a sustainable mobility transition, policy strategies must transition from generic, one-size-fits-all incentives to targeted, segment-specific interventions that simultaneously synchronize infrastructure reliability, address technological uncertainties, and account for the heterogeneity of the user base.

title: When Does Business Strategy Increase Climate‐Change Exposure? The Contingent Role of Managerial Ability
summary: Why does the same business strategy simultaneously mitigate and amplify firms' exposure to climate‐related risks? Prior research offers conflicting predictions regarding the environmental implications of innovation‐oriented Prospector strat
content: Why does the same business strategy simultaneously mitigate and amplify firms' exposure to climate‐related risks? Prior research offers conflicting predictions regarding the environmental implications of innovation‐oriented Prospector strategies, suggesting that they can both mitigate and amplify risk. We address this puzzle by developing a contingency framework that reconceptualises climate‐change exposure as arising from how firms organise and govern strategic flexibility. Drawing on organisational theory, the natural resource‐based view and a Neo‐Durkheimian perspective on risk governance, we argue that Prospector strategies embed a fundamental flexibility–control tension that simultaneously enhances adaptive capacity and increases coordination complexity. Climate‐change exposure therefore reflects how organisations manage and resolve this tension. We conceptualise managerial ability as a governance‐structuring capability that organises attention, prioritises competing risk signals and aligns dispersed activities under uncertainty. Using 13,547 firm‐year observations of US public firms from 2001 to 2024 and a machine learning‐based measure of climate‐change exposure derived from earnings call transcripts, we find that Prospector strategies are associated with higher exposure, but this relationship is attenuated in firms with higher managerial ability. Our findings advance a governance‐based perspective in which exposure emerges from the interplay between strategy, managerial capability and the organisational construction of uncertainty.

title: Introduction to AI in Manufacturing
summary: The manufacturing industry is undergoing a major transformation with the progressive integration of intelligent technologies that are redefining traditional production systems. Among these technologies, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emer
content: The manufacturing industry is undergoing a major transformation with the progressive integration of intelligent technologies that are redefining traditional production systems. Among these technologies, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most influential drivers of modernization, efficiency, and innovation. The present work focuses on the utilization of Artificial Intelligence concepts, methodologies, and various tools into the current state of manufacturing to enhance the effectiveness of manufacturing operations and accuracy in decision-making. It explores the evolution of AI from simple automation and rule-based systems to advanced machine learning algorithms capable of learning, predicting, and optimizing processes in real time. AI applications in manufacturing extend across multiple layers of industrial activity—ranging from product design and process planning to production scheduling, quality inspection, logistics, supply chain management, and maintenance. Machine learning and deep learning models enable manufacturers to evaluate massive datasets generated by industrial sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and production equipment. Through these analytical insights, manufacturers can accurately predict the possible machinery faults, reduce downtime, enhanced quality standards, and optimum consumption of energy to meet the sustainability goals. Intelligent vision systems and robotic automation further contribute to precision and flexibility in operations, allowing adaptive manufacturing that responds dynamically to changing market and production conditions. The chapter also emphasizes the growing role of AI in advancing smart manufacturing initiatives. These systems promote the integration of cyber-physical networks where digital twins, cloud computing, and edge analytics collaborate to create self-learning and self-correcting production environments. AI-driven predictive maintenance, virtual simulations, and autonomous decision-making mechanisms enhance both reliability and responsiveness within the production ecosystem. As industries shift from mass production to customized manufacturing, AI offers the ability to manage complexity, streamline workflows, and maintain consistent product quality at reduced costs. However, the transition toward AI-enabled manufacturing also presents notable challenges. Data reliability, interoperability between legacy systems, high implementation costs, and limited digital skills among the workforce remain major barriers. Ethical concerns such as data privacy, transparency in algorithmic decision-making, and potential risk of reduction in labor workforce need careful consideration in the use of AI in manufacturing. The chapter addresses these issues by outlining strategies for responsible AI adoption, workforce upskilling, and policy-level interventions to ensure equitable technological growth. In addition to exploring current capabilities, this chapter offers a forward-looking perspe

title: Transaction Costs, Extension Support and Equitable Benefit Sharing for Smallholder Farmers in Agricultural Carbon Markets
source: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports
summary: Background: Agricultural carbon markets are increasingly promoted as a means of financing climate-smart practices on smallholder farms while rewarding farmers for emission reductions and carbon removals. Two decades of project experience ne
content: Background: Agricultural carbon markets are increasingly promoted as a means of financing climate-smart practices on smallholder farms while rewarding farmers for emission reductions and carbon removals. Two decades of project experience nevertheless show modest farmer participation, small and delayed payments, and persistent doubts about the integrity of land-based credits. Aim and scope: This review critically examines how transaction costs, extension and advisory support, and benefit-sharing arrangements jointly shape whether smallholders in low- and middle-income countries can participate in, and gain from, carbon crediting and related payment schemes for soil carbon, agroforestry, conservation agriculture and rice methane mitigation. Approach: Peer-reviewed literature published from 2005 onwards was identified through multidisciplinary, economics and agricultural research sources, supplemented by citation tracking and institutional documents, and appraised qualitatively for relevance, design adequacy, transparency and transferability. Principal findings: The evidence consistently identifies fixed project costs and measurement, reporting and verification requirements as the binding constraint on smallholder inclusion; these costs fall with aggregation but simultaneously concentrate control and revenue among intermediaries. Training and advisory services appear to drive much of the observed practice change, yet their effects are seldom separated from carbon payments, and farmers' trust in delivery agents varies widely. Benefit sharing is frequently skewed towards larger, better-endowed and male-headed households, while revenue reaching farmers is often negligible relative to costs. Integrity reforms that require direct soil measurement or stricter additionality tests may further raise costs and exclude early adopters. Implications: Integrity, inclusion and cost efficiency cannot be maximised simultaneously; the defensible policy objective is to make the trade-offs explicit through transparent cost and revenue accounting, group-level measurement designs, publicly anchored extension and enforceable distributional rules. Conclusion: Carbon finance can complement, but not substitute for, agricultural development investment in smallholder systems, and stronger causal and distributional evidence is required before large-scale expansion.

title: A context sensitive framework for urban farming in bahrain: a review of heat mitigation, food system resilience, and digital management
summary: Bahrain’s limited urban land, water constraints, heat exposure, and reliance on food imports necessitate urban farming strategies that balance production, environmental performance, and long-term viability. This study develops a balanced pr
content: Bahrain’s limited urban land, water constraints, heat exposure, and reliance on food imports necessitate urban farming strategies that balance production, environmental performance, and long-term viability. This study develops a balanced production. Environmental performance and sustained operation. This research develops a context-sensitive framework for evaluating urban farming typologies in Bahrain, with attention to potential heat mitigation, food system resilience, and digital management. A structured literature review and comparative analyses of purposively selected international and regional cases examine cultivation systems, spatial arrangements, resource requirements, governance, and distribution, and interpret them against Bahrain’s planning context. The synthesis identifies site suitability, reliable water supply, energy demand, continuous financing, management capacity, and access to produce as recurring assessment considerations. Community plots, productive rooftops, and controlled environment systems serve different purposes and require different resources; the available evidence does not establish a universally preferable typology for Bahrain. Food production and cooling require separate assessment, while documented AI applications remain too limited to establish their added value over simpler management approaches. These findings inform a qualitative framework comprising five domains: spatial suitability, environmental performance, food production and distribution, socioeconomic and institutional capacity, and digital management. Varied case documentation, inconsistent outcome reporting, and the absence of comparable Bahraini farm profiles and field measurements limit transferability and prevent robust performance rankings or causal inference. The framework is therefore an evidence informed proposal for contextual evaluation and pilot selection, requiring local validation. Coordinated pilots with stakeholder participation and monitoring across hot and cooler seasons are recommended before wider implementation.

title: Internationalised unjust non-transitions: financialised design and powerless just transition coalitions in ‘Just Energy Transition Partnerships’ with South Africa and Indonesia
summary: ‘Just Energy Transition Partnerships’ (JETPs) are presented as international just transition flagships. But to what extent do they deliver on transition and justice, and why are they (not) working? We address this by analysing South Africa
content: ‘Just Energy Transition Partnerships’ (JETPs) are presented as international just transition flagships. But to what extent do they deliver on transition and justice, and why are they (not) working? We address this by analysing South Africa and Indonesia, the two most advanced JETP countries. We assess JETPs based on their promises of transitioning from fossil fuels to renewables, and of justice, understood as including domestic and international considerations. Building on empirical research, we present two arguments. First, we demonstrate that JETPs’ defining features have been the politically produced absences of transition and justice, which we call ‘internationalised unjust non-transitions’. Second, we argue that their fundamental roots lie in JETPs’ financialised designs, the material-cultural interests they promote in design and implementation, and the absence of powerful just transition coalitions. We conclude that international just transition efforts require a different type of partnership, and must address how to overcome powerful incumbents.

title: Board Human Capital Heterogeneity, Eco‐Initiatives and Carbon Performance: The Mediating Role of Firm Size
summary: We examine the relationship between board human capital heterogeneity (BHCH), eco‐initiatives (EI) and carbon performance (CP). Further, we examine the mediation of firm size (FS) between BHCH and CP. Drawing on multi‐theoretical framework,
content: We examine the relationship between board human capital heterogeneity (BHCH), eco‐initiatives (EI) and carbon performance (CP). Further, we examine the mediation of firm size (FS) between BHCH and CP. Drawing on multi‐theoretical framework, we argue that heterogeneous boards enhance monitoring quality and provide access to diverse knowledge and resources, which collectively support superior environmental decision‐making. Our sample consists of 9608 global firms from 71 countries during the period between 2015 and 2022. Our results report that BHCH and EI are positively and significantly related to CP. Moreover, we find that FS partially mediates the relationship between BHCH and CP. Our study documents that firms should have board with BHCH, and better EI strategies aim at capturing carbon issues. Besides, our findings evidence that FS is the crucial factor that assures resource base in the firm, which facilitates the board of directors to take timely and quick decisions regarding corporate contemporary issues like climate change issues. The findings contribute to the corporate governance and sustainability literature by moving beyond traditional demographic measures of board diversity and emphasising the strategic importance of human capital heterogeneity. The study also highlights the conditional nature of governance effectiveness, demonstrating that board attributes must be aligned with firm‐level capabilities and environmental strategies to achieve meaningful carbon performance improvements. Our study findings have greater implications in policy‐making levels and industry practitioners.

title: Thermal Demand and Conditional Economic Appraisal of Hybrid PV and Solar Thermal Water Heating in a Dodoma Hotel
summary: This study examined how demand uncertainty, consistent energy accounting, and storage selection affected the appraisal of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and solar thermal water heating for a 31-room commercial hotel in Dodoma, Tanzania. We audite
content: This study examined how demand uncertainty, consistent energy accounting, and storage selection affected the appraisal of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and solar thermal water heating for a 31-room commercial hotel in Dodoma, Tanzania. We audited an existing site-inventory workbook and dissertation, reproduced their calculations in Python, and compared alternative heating configurations using a continuous synthetic year with explicit tank losses, PV temperature effects, a storage high-limit, and power-limited auxiliary heating. The estimated volume of 2,110 L/day required 88.3 kWh/day when heated from 24 to 60°C; calendar integration of twelve supplied inlet-temperature scenarios gave 32.7 MWh/year. Interpreting the same volume as mixed water at 40°C reduced the reference requirement to 39.3 kWh/day. Correcting the irradiation–irradiance error yielded 25.7–32.4 kWh/day of potential PV energy delivered to the selected array. A battery-free configuration with 28.7 m² of collectors and approximately 1.06 m³ of thermal storage supplied 82.2% of annual useful heat from renewable sources, but retained temperature-service shortfalls under the assumed draw peaks. Against a modelled existing-solar baseline, its conditional net present value was TSh 25.5 million, compared with −TSh 32.5 million for the battery alternative. Missing tank, safety, and backup quotations made these financial results conditional. Combined financial scenarios reversed the conclusion on the battery-free investment. The findings support comparing demand boundaries and thermal storage before purchasing batteries; without measured hourly inputs, it is not possible to establish actual hotel performance or a final procurement design.

title: A Sustainable Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) Inventory Model with Backordered Demand for IC Engines After the Introduction of Electric Vehicles
source: Global Journal of Management and Business Research
summary: This The global automotive industry is undergoing a transformative shift as electric vehicles (EVs) rapidly expand market share and reshape long-standing mobility and energy consumption patterns. This transition, driven by technological adv
content: This The global automotive industry is undergoing a transformative shift as electric vehicles (EVs) rapidly expand market share and reshape long-standing mobility and energy consumption patterns. This transition, driven by technological advancements, environmental regulations, and changing consumer preferences, is diminishing demand for gasoline-powered vehicles and their associated spare parts. The International Energy Agency reports that EV growth displaced approximately 1.3 million barrels of oil demand per day in 2024, underscoring the material impact of electrification on conventional vehicle markets. As production volumes fall and demand becomes nonlinear and uncertain, inventory management for IC engine components must move beyond classical EOQ assumptions. This paper develops a sustainable EOQ framework for declining-demand environments that integrates quadratic and logistic demand functions, quadratic deterioration behaviour, nonlinear holding costs and planned backordering. The model is formulated in five sequential stages that capture inventory build-up logistic-like demand transition, intensified deterioration, shortage accumulation, and backorder clearance. By combining realistic deterioration modelling with backordering and sustainability-oriented cost elements, the proposed approach offers a pragmatic decision- support tool for automotive suppliers and policymakers seeking to maintain service continuity while managing costs and environmental impacts during the shift to electric mobility.

title: Potential Fermentation of Dahlia Tubers (Dahlia pinnata Cav.) with L. plantarum B1765 in the Production of Fructooligosaccharides
summary: Fructooligosaccharides (FOS) are functional food ingredients used as food additives in the food, pharmaceutical, and health industries. FOS can be produced by hydrolyzing inulin with the enzyme inulinase. One source of inulin is dahlia tube
content: Fructooligosaccharides (FOS) are functional food ingredients used as food additives in the food, pharmaceutical, and health industries. FOS can be produced by hydrolyzing inulin with the enzyme inulinase. One source of inulin is dahlia tubers. L. plantarum B1765 is known to possess inulinase activity. This study aimed to investigate the effect of fermentation time on dahlia tubers (Dahlia pinnata Cav.) using L. plantarum B1765 as a starter culture to produce FOS. An experimental research design was utilized with fermentation conducted for 0, 24, 48, and 72 hours at 37°C using a 3% (v/v) starter culture. Subsequently, LAB growth, pH, total titratable acidity (TTA), and FOS content were measured. Total LAB was determined using the Total Plate Count (TPC) method, pH was measured using a pH meter, and TTA was determined by acid-base titration. FOS content was analyzed using HPLC with a mobile phase consisting of 70% ammonium hydroxide solution and 30% acetonitrile. Fermentation duration influenced increases in LAB population, TTA, and FOS content, as well as decreases in pH. The results showed that optimal bacterial growth occurred after 24 hours of fermentation, with a total LAB count of 2.48 × 10⁸ ± 0.068 CFU/mL. FOS production continued to increase throughout the 72-hour fermentation period. The FOS produced after 72 hours of fermentation consisted of inulobiose (32.24 ± 0.16 mg/g), inulotriose (31.49 ± 0.56 mg/g), kestose (49.67 ± 0.24 mg/g), nystose (33.40 ± 0.60 mg/g), and fructosylnystose (23.90 ± 0.43 mg/g). These findings suggest that dahlia tubers fermented with L. plantarum B1765 have potential as a substrate for FOS production and may contribute to the development of the FOS industry. Ultimately, these practical implications highlight the potential of this bioprocess to advance functional food development and strengthen the commercial prebiotic industry.

title: MANAGING THE CIRCULAR ECONOMY TRANSITION IN BULGARIA: A GENDER-RESPONSIVE SKILLS PERSPECTIVE
summary: The transition to a circular economy (CE) requires not only technological innovation but a fundamental transformation of knowledge, skills, and institutional capacities. This article examines the role of higher education in fostering compet
content: The transition to a circular economy (CE) requires not only technological innovation but a fundamental transformation of knowledge, skills, and institutional capacities. This article examines the role of higher education in fostering competencies for sustainable and circular economic transitions, drawing on empirical evidence from Bulgaria's National Skills Needs and Gaps Analysis (2024) [1].
