Modele ilişkin bulgunun istihdam ve Ar-Ge serilerinin I(1) görünümü ve eşbütünleşme sonuçlarının model tercihine duyarlılığı sebebiyle istikrarlı bir uzun dönem ilişkisinin bağımsız kanıtı olarak yorumlanmasını sınırlandırmaktadır. Birinci fark, CCEMG ve dinamik uzun dönem modellerinde ise Ar-Ge katsayısı anlamlı bulunamamıştır. Bulgular, ikiz dönüşüm istihdam ilişkisinin özellikle Ar-Ge boyutunda model yapısına ve ülke heterojenliğine duyarlı olduğuna işaret etmektedir.

title: From access to affordability: The complex relationship between financial inclusion and housing prices
source: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
summary: The expansion of financial inclusion has enabled more low-income households to access housing loans, which may have significant effects on the housing market. This study examines the relationship between financial inclusion and housing pric
content: The expansion of financial inclusion has enabled more low-income households to access housing loans, which may have significant effects on the housing market. This study examines the relationship between financial inclusion and housing prices, focusing on how factors such as forest area, carbon emissions, urbanization, and government effectiveness moderate this relationship. Using panel data from 38 countries between 2008 and 2021, the analysis indicates that financial inclusion generally has a negative impact on housing prices. This suggests that increased access to financial services reduces housing price inflation by enabling low-income households to secure loans. However, the effect is not uniform across regions or market types. In advanced economies, financial inclusion tends to lower housing prices, whereas in emerging markets, the relationship is inconsistent. The findings also reveal that forest area, carbon emissions, urbanization, and government effectiveness play significant moderating roles. For example, in areas with larger forested land, the negative impact of financial inclusion on housing prices is weaker because land availability constraints limit housing supply, whereas in regions with higher carbon emissions from transport, the effect is stronger. The study concludes with policy recommendations to strengthen financial systems in emerging markets, promote affordable housing policies, encourage sustainable urbanization, and improve government effectiveness in order to mitigate the adverse impacts of financial inclusion on housing markets and ensure better housing affordability.

title: The Triple Duty Law for Mortality Accounted Infrastructure
summary: Modern civil engineering commits one measurable error at planetary scale: it builds single-duty objects. A bridge that only carries traffic, a dam wall that only resists water, a government building that only shelters files, each consumes l
content: Modern civil engineering commits one measurable error at planetary scale: it builds single-duty objects. A bridge that only carries traffic, a dam wall that only resists water, a government building that only shelters files, each consumes land, cement, steel, money and carbon to perform exactly one function, then decays in silence until it fails in public. This article proposes a replacement doctrine and then subjects it to the mathematics it demands of others. The doctrine has two halves. First, the Triple-Duty Law: every new publicly funded structure above a threshold value must simultaneously (1) bear load, (2) store value (gravitational or electrochemical energy, harvested water, or usable heat) and (3) confess, meaning it must continuously sense and publicly report its own structural condition. Second, Mortality Accounting: every such structure is sanctioned with a dated, public Structural Passport stating its design death date, and a ring-fenced Mortality Escrow, proposed at 4% of capital cost, spendable only on that named asset. The quantitative core is derived, not asserted. A Weibull reliability model (shape β = 2.5, scale η = 75 years, both labelled assumptions) shows that a nominal 75-year asset carries only 30.5 years of 90%-reliability life, and that monitored maintenance (η = 95) cuts the 50-year failure probability from 30.4% to 18.2%. A 60-year life-cycle net-present-value model of a representative Rs 10 crore asset finds the triple-duty design cheaper by Rs 0.89 crore (7.2%) at a 7% real discount rate, with a break-even construction premium of 20.9% and a break-even discount rate near 11.6%, and it fails, openly, if the second duty's value is not counted. Storage duties are sized from first principles: 10,000 cubic metres of water at 30 metres of head stores 818 kilowatt-hours gross (613 usable); 1,000 square metres of roof in Andhra Pradesh yields about 750 cubic metres of harvested rain a year; 500 square metres of photovoltaic surface yields 146 megawatt-hours a year. A Bayesian calculation prices the third duty: a sensor alarm raises the probability of actionable deterioration from a 2% prior to 26.9%, and sensor silence lowers it to 0.21%. The article closes with a 36-month district pilot whose sample sizes are derived from a stated power calculation, and five pre-registered predictions. If the predictions fail, the doctrine fails. That is the point.

title: Pathways to Practice: Evaluating Blue Carbon Capacity Development in Africa
summary: Blue carbon (BC) ecosystems are increasingly recognised for their roles in climate action, biodiversity conservation and community livelihoods. As interest in their protection and restoration grows, so does the need for capacity development
content: Blue carbon (BC) ecosystems are increasingly recognised for their roles in climate action, biodiversity conservation and community livelihoods. As interest in their protection and restoration grows, so does the need for capacity development that can support effective project design, implementation and sustained action. However, evidence of whether training translates into sustained practice and long‐term outcomes remains limited. This exploratory study examined 18 BC capacity development programmes in Africa, assessing programme design, alumni‐reported learning and application and conditions influencing progression from training to practice. Structured questionnaires were administered to training providers and alumni of programmes delivered between 2015 and 2025. Results indicate that training was primarily delivered by NGOs (50%) and universities (22%), with activity concentrated in East Africa. Programmes were predominantly face‐to‐face, field‐based and free of charge (69%), emphasising mangrove ecology (48%), restoration (24.4%) and community engagement (17.8%). Participating alumni reported high satisfaction, perceived knowledge gains, increased confidence and professional benefits. However, specialised competencies, including carbon accounting and finance, remote sensing and policy integration, received less attention (< 10%). Post‐training support and long‐term evaluation were also rare. Given the small, non‐probability sample and cross‐sectional, self‐reported data, these findings suggest that accessible, experiential training provides an important foundation for BC capacity development, but gaps in specialised learning and a ‘missing middle’ of institutional support, resources and opportunities may constrain progression towards broader outcomes. More progressive learning pathways, supported by specialised training, sustained mentoring, institutional partnerships and longer‐term evaluation, could strengthen BC capacity development and its contribution to conservation and climate goals.

title: Effect of planting dates and foliar application of mannitol on the growth and yield of flax (Linum usitatissimum L.)
summary: Determining the appropriate planting date is a crucial strategy for ensuring the efficient and stable cultivation of a specific crop. Planting timing is a fundamental factor influencing the success and productivity of agricultural productio
content: Determining the appropriate planting date is a crucial strategy for ensuring the efficient and stable cultivation of a specific crop. Planting timing is a fundamental factor influencing the success and productivity of agricultural production, as it is directly linked to prevailing environmental conditions-such as temperature, rainfall, relative humidity and photoperiod. Selecting the right planting date creates favourable conditions for seed germination and plant growth and development, thereby positively impacting both the quantity and quality of the yield. Furthermore, the study addressed the use of natural nutrients; accordingly, a field experiment was conducted during the 2023–24 winter season in Saqlawiyah (Anbar Governorate) to evaluate the response of the flax crop to varying planting dates (October 20, November 10, November 30 and December 20) and foliar application of the sugar alcohol mannitol at concentrations of 0, 3, 6 and 9 g L-1. The experiment was laid out in a randomised complete block design (RCBD) using a split-plot arrangement with 3 replicates. The results revealed significant variations based on planting dates, with the second date (November 10) showing significant superiority in plant height (145.20 cm), number of branches (3.83 branches plant-1), 1000-seed weight (7.47 g) and seed yield (1.64 t ha-1). Regarding mannitol, the highest concentration (9 g L-1) yielded the highest values for the growth and yield parameters under study.

title: Agroecological Influence on Proximate Composition of Parakan Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum L.)
summary: Parakan rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum L.) is an important local cultivar in Indonesia, valued for its sweet flavor, thick aril, and desirable postharvest quality. This study evaluated the proximate composition and nutritional characteristic
content: Parakan rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum L.) is an important local cultivar in Indonesia, valued for its sweet flavor, thick aril, and desirable postharvest quality. This study evaluated the proximate composition and nutritional characteristics of Parakan rambutan collected from three production sites in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia, and compared them with the local cultivar Tangkue as a reference cultivar. Proximate components, caloric values, vitamin C, total sugars, and total soluble solids (TSS) were determined using AOAC-standardized methods, while soil physicochemical properties were characterized to provide environmental context. Significant differences (p≤0.05) were observed among the evaluated samples for moisture, ash, protein, fat, carbohydrate, vitamin C, total sugars, and TSS. Parakan rambutan from the BPP Caringin site (R3) exhibited the highest protein (1.71%), carbohydrate (22.31%), and caloric value (98.38 kcal/100 g), whereas Tangkue (R4) showed the highest vitamin C content (46.75 mg/100 g) and TSS. The observed differences in proximate composition among Parakan samples collected from different production sites suggest that agroecological conditions may contribute to nutritional variation, while comparison with Tangkue provides additional context for variation between cultivars. Principal component analysis (PCA) and the Multi-trait Genotype–Ideotype Distance Index (MGIDI) integrated multiple nutritional traits and identified Parakan rambutan from the BPP Caringin site (R3) as the sample with the most desirable overall desirable overall nutritional profile. These findings provide a comprehensive nutritional characterization of locally important rambutan cultivars, suggest that agroecological conditions may contribute to variation in fruit nutritional composition, and demonstrate the usefulness of multivariate analysis for integrating multiple nutritional traits. The results also provide a foundation for future multi-location studies aimed at validating site-associated nutritional variation.

title: Optimise an After-Treatment System for an Ammonia Dual-Fuel Engine to Meet the Maritime Requirements
summary: Green ammonia can link renewable hydrogen production with ocean-going ship propulsion, but exhaust control for ammonia dual-fuel engines cannot be judged by carbon reduction alone. Ammonia combustion can still produce nitrogen oxides (NOx),
content: Green ammonia can link renewable hydrogen production with ocean-going ship propulsion, but exhaust control for ammonia dual-fuel engines cannot be judged by carbon reduction alone. Ammonia combustion can still produce nitrogen oxides (NOx), ammonia (NH 3 ) slip, and nitrous oxide (N 2 O). This study builds a steady-state exhaust gas recirculation selective catalytic reduction (EGR-SCR) after-treatment model for the 7S60ME-C10.5-LGIA ammonia dual-fuel main engine. Public engine data, reported EGR emission curves, and SCR catalyst data are used to calculate EGR split, gas density, NOx conversion, NH 3 slip use, external urea demand, and catalyst volume. At the representative steady-state points, EGR reduces engine-out NOx by 34.7–43.7% and increases engine-generated NH 3 slip by 27.8–51.4%. The highest NOx specific emission after SCR is 0.210 g/kWh, below the MARPOL Annex VI Tier III limit. The catalyst volume decreases from 7.29 m3 to 5.10 m3, and annual 40 wt% urea saving reaches 135.1 t/year.

title: Analysis of the Legal Regulation of the Contract for the Carriage of Goods by Sea in Albania in Light of the Recent Economic Developments and International Conventions
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
summary: In this article, we combine legal and economic perspectives to provide a comprehensive approach to maritime transport, focusing on the contract for the carriage of goods by sea as a central component of successful global trade. We examine t
content: In this article, we combine legal and economic perspectives to provide a comprehensive approach to maritime transport, focusing on the contract for the carriage of goods by sea as a central component of successful global trade. We examine the current regulations and provisions governing this contract in Albania and compare them with leading international standards, with particular emphasis on the Rotterdam Rules, which the Albanian government has not yet ratified, as well as relevant EU legislation, considering Albania’s official status as an EU candidate country. The novelty of this study lies in its interdisciplinary perspective, linking the analysis of the legal framework with research on the economic development of maritime transport and the role of technological innovation to conclude that legal reform remains a strategic driver of Albania’s long-term economic growth in the maritime industry. In this study, we apply a multilayered framework spanning global, regional, and local contexts, emphasizing Albania’s need to adapt its maritime legislation and address sectoral gaps to align with regional and international best practices, thereby positioning the country as a key hub within the region’s broader maritime transport network. title: Apples to Oranges: Perspectives from the Judges of the XPRIZE Carbon Removal
summary: The XPRIZE Carbon Removal, a competition launched in 2021 and concluded in 2025, awarded US$100 million in cash prizes to teams that demonstrated carbon dioxide removal (CDR) at a kilotonne scale. The competition was overseen by a panel of
content: The XPRIZE Carbon Removal, a competition launched in 2021 and concluded in 2025, awarded US$100 million in cash prizes to teams that demonstrated carbon dioxide removal (CDR) at a kilotonne scale. The competition was overseen by a panel of expert judges, who awarded monetary prizes to 38 teams from a field of over 1,400 competitors over 4 years. This article describes the evaluation process, offers reflections on the criteria used to judge competing teams and provides commentary on the strengths and weaknesses of the diverse CDR solutions showcased in the competition. The challenges were not uniform across different CDR pathways, and teams were faced with solving unique and often first-of-a-kind issues, especially during the 1-year demonstration period. Although only a few teams were selected to receive prizes, the ultimate goal of this XPRIZE was to stimulate a viable carbon removal industry. To that end, the prize competition format highlighted opportunities and challenges associated with scaling a nascent industry and offers instructive lessons for how this industry can grow.

title: Brief Analysis of Intelligent Manufacturing Reliability
summary: Against the backdrop of the deepening of the "Quality Power" strategy and the global industrial transformation, intelligent manufacturing has become the core path for the high-end, intelligent and green transformation of China's manufacturi
content: Against the backdrop of the deepening of the "Quality Power" strategy and the global industrial transformation, intelligent manufacturing has become the core path for the high-end, intelligent and green transformation of China's manufacturing industry. As the lifeline of the manufacturing industry, reliability is a key support for the effective implementation of intelligent manufacturing and the enhancement of industrial competitiveness. Combining typical practical cases, standard system construction and industry research in the fields of domestic intelligent manufacturing and reliability, this paper systematically sorts out the development status of China's intelligent manufacturing and reliability, deeply analyzes the problems in concepts, technologies, standards, talents and other aspects during the development process, and puts forward targeted solutions based on the practical experience and theoretical achievements in existing research, providing a theoretical reference for the integration of China's intelligent manufacturing and reliability and the promotion of the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry.

title: Beyond cost: a critical review of battery trade-offs for just energy transitions in developing and emerging economies
summary: Stationary battery selection in developing and emerging economies involves trade-offs between access to capital, reliable service, lifecycle burdens, and local governance. This review examines how these dimensions affect technology choice.
content: Stationary battery selection in developing and emerging economies involves trade-offs between access to capital, reliable service, lifecycle burdens, and local governance. This review examines how these dimensions affect technology choice. This structured critical review integrates selected technical, lifecycle, and energy-justice literature. Evidence is distinguished by application, geographical transferability, and commercial maturity. The literature is synthesized qualitatively; an illustrative multicriteria template specifies possible weighting scenarios without calculating technology scores or rankings. Lead–acid and lithium-ion batteries have established applications, but their relative whole-life costs depend on operating conditions, usable capacity, replacement, and financing. Evidence on lithium iron phosphate supports its consideration for stationary services without establishing universal superiority. Sodium-ion and iron-based flow batteries offer diversification opportunities with greater uncertainty in long-term field performance. Environmental comparisons depend on lifecycle boundaries and local end-of-life practices. Priorities should be defined for a specified service and jurisdiction with affected users, operators, and authorities. Upfront affordability, lifetime performance, environmental burden, and resilience/justice should be evaluated using explicit indicators, with safeguards for unacceptable health and safety risks. Equal and priority-weight scenarios are proposed only for future testing against local performance data; no optimal weights or rank reversals are demonstrated. Incomplete records of original source identification limit the reproducibility and coverage of this review.

title: Cyclic Generation of (Oxy)hydroxides on Bifacial Photoanodes Enables High‐Performing Solar Urea Oxidation With Stability Exceeding 120 Hours
summary: Replacing the conventional oxygen evolution reaction on photoanodes with urea oxidation reaction (UOR) attracts significant efforts to integrate solar‐driven hydrogen production with purification of urea‐rich wastewater. Real‐world implemen
content: Replacing the conventional oxygen evolution reaction on photoanodes with urea oxidation reaction (UOR) attracts significant efforts to integrate solar‐driven hydrogen production with purification of urea‐rich wastewater. Real‐world implementations of this technology require improvements in key performance indicators, including low onset potential, high current density, and long‐term device lifetime; yet no present technology satisfies all these criteria simultaneously. We implement a self‐evolving NiFe hydroxides‐alloy co‐catalyst layer on microstructured Si photoanodes with decoupled photon management from catalysis. The system reports the lowest onset potential of 0.782 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, a saturated current density of 40.7 mA , and stability over 120 hours, an improvement of sevenfold over the closest competitor in Si‐based systems. In situ Raman and reduction‐peak charge analysis demonstrate that the photoanode‐enhanced performance leverages dynamic transition cycles between oxyhydroxides and hydroxides of the NiFe alloy layer, suppressing the steady‐state accumulation of high‐valence NiFe oxyhydroxides. We then engineered bias‐free devices for UOR‐assisted solar hydrogen production, exhibiting a current density of 11.07 mA , representing the highest current density reported among low‐cost, non‐photovoltaic‐assisted PEC devices. This photoanode architecture opens to large‐scale implementations of solar fuel production coupled with industrially valuable reactions, including biomass oxidation and plastics valorization.

title: Glass-Nanofiber-Reinforced Strontium Aluminate/Epoxy Nanocomposite Coatings for Ceramics: Persistent Luminescence and Multifunctional Surface Protection
summary: A multifunctional photoluminescent nanocomposite coating for ceramic substrates was developed using epoxy resin (EPR) as the polymeric matrix, strontium aluminate nanoparticles (NSA; 9–18 nm) as the photoluminescent component, and glass nan
content: A multifunctional photoluminescent nanocomposite coating for ceramic substrates was developed using epoxy resin (EPR) as the polymeric matrix, strontium aluminate nanoparticles (NSA; 9–18 nm) as the photoluminescent component, and glass nanofibers (50–220 nm) as a reinforcing phase. The incorporation of glass nanofibers was designed to enhance the mechanical performance of the epoxy coating while maintaining its optical functionality. The morphological, structural, and surface characteristics of NSA, glass nanofibers, and NSA@EPR-coated ceramic films were systematically investigated using complementary analytical techniques. The resulting coatings exhibited high transparency under daylight, a green emission under UV irradiation, and a greenish-yellow afterglow in darkness. Upon excitation at 365 nm, the photoluminescent coatings displayed characteristic emission bands at 519 nm, corresponding to a strong green emission, and 438 nm, attributed to a weaker blue emission. Increasing the NSA loading progressively enhanced both the fluorescence intensity and long-persistent phosphorescence of the coatings. In addition to their photoluminescent behavior, the nanocomposite coatings demonstrated improved UV-shielding capability, scratch resistance, antibacterial activity, and hydrophobicity. The NSA-containing coatings also exhibited good durability and photostability, indicating their potential as robust multifunctional ceramic coatings for protective, decorative, and optical applications.

title: Meta Life Cycle Assessment, Techno-Economic Analysis, and Risk Assessment of Carbon Mineralization Pathways to Inform Policy Frameworks
summary: Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even th
content: Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even though carbon capture is already factored into all major global climate models, with mineralization (converting CO2 into stable carbonates) representing a major subset. If mineralization is to bolster the suite of climate mitigation strategies, it is vital that academic guidance be provided to inform the currently underinformed policy direction. To address this, this study presents a meta life cycle and techno-economic analysis of carbon mineralization pathways from both academia and industry, normalizing independent techno-economic, life cycle, and risk assessment (Monte Carlo) results within the context of US and EU policy. Results demonstrate that in situ mineralization achieves the greatest life cycle GHG emission reductions at the lowest cost and is the only pathway capable of gigaton-scale emission reductions commensurate with climate goals. Enhanced rock weathering also consistently delivers net-negative GHG removal at relatively low costs, but ex situ pathways achieve lower GHG emission reductions at higher costs, where several proposed pathways are net-CO2 positive as CO2 emitted throughout the process (transportation, electricity use, and natural gas combustion) offsets CO2 sequestered. Risks of leakage, hazards, global capacity, financial impact, and reversal are also quantitatively and qualitatively compared among the mineralization pathways, demonstrating that in situ mineralization has low financial risk when bolstered by state entities, faces uncertainties in non-governmental organization objection, and, ultimately, all pathways are victims of uncharted policy.

title: Waste-to-Energy in Malaysia: Technologies, Biomass Resources, Municipal Solid Waste Management, Techno-Economic Feasibility, Environmental Impacts and Future Prospects
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Waste-to-energy (WtE) technology has emerged as an important alternative for addressing the growing challenges of solid waste management while supporting the transition towards renewable and sustainable energy systems. In Malaysia, rapid ur
content: Waste-to-energy (WtE) technology has emerged as an important alternative for addressing the growing challenges of solid waste management while supporting the transition towards renewable and sustainable energy systems. In Malaysia, rapid urbanisation, population growth, industrial development and increasing consumption have contributed to rising municipal solid waste (MSW) generation, placing considerable pressure on existing landfill-based disposal systems. At the same time, Malaysia possesses substantial energy recovery potential from various waste streams, including food waste, agricultural residues, oil palm biomass, industrial waste and municipal solid waste. This paper presents a comprehensive review of waste-to-energy technologies, with particular emphasis on their suitability, performance, implementation challenges and future prospects in Malaysia. The review examines major WtE conversion pathways, including incineration, anaerobic digestion, landfill gas recovery, gasification, pyrolysis and hydrothermal carbonisation, together with emerging opportunities for biogas, biofuel and hydrogen production. Particular attention is given to the availability and characteristics of Malaysian waste feedstocks, especially organic municipal solid waste, food waste and oil palm residues. The paper further evaluates the technical, economic, environmental, institutional and social considerations influencing WtE implementation, including energy recovery efficiency, greenhouse gas emissions, investment requirements, waste segregation, feedstock sustainability, public acceptance and regulatory support. International experiences are incorporated to identify relevant technological approaches and implementation strategies that may be adapted to Malaysian conditions. The review highlights the importance of integrating waste-to-energy development with circular economy principles, effective source separation, resource recovery and sustainable waste management policies. It also identifies key research gaps concerning technology selection, commercialisation, operational performance and long-term environmental sustainability. An integrated framework is proposed to connect waste resource availability, conversion technologies, energy recovery, economic feasibility, environmental performance and policy development. The paper concludes that WtE technologies offer significant opportunities to strengthen Malaysia's waste management system and diversify its renewable energy portfolio, provided that technology selection, institutional coordination and economic viability are addressed through an integrated national approach.

title: SAHRA ALTI AFRİKA ÜLKELERİNDE İKTİSADİ BÜYÜME, İSTİHDAM, SAĞLIK HARCAMALARI VE HAVA KİRLİLİĞİNİN YAŞAM SÜRESİ ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİSİ
summary: Bu araştırmanın amacı, 43 Sahra Altı Afrika (SSA) ülkesinde iktisadi büyüme, istihdam, sağlık harcamaları ve hava kirliliğinin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisini panel veri yöntemiyle test etmektir. Araştırma 2000-2023 dönem
content: Bu araştırmanın amacı, 43 Sahra Altı Afrika (SSA) ülkesinde iktisadi büyüme, istihdam, sağlık harcamaları ve hava kirliliğinin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisini panel veri yöntemiyle test etmektir. Araştırma 2000-2023 dönemini kapsamaktadır. Araştırmada yapılan ön testler neticesinde analiz modelleri olarak panel otoregresif dağıtılmış gecikmeli (Panel ARDL) testiyle Dumitrescu & Hurlin panel nedensellik testi kullanılmıştır. Yapılan Panel ARDL analiz bulguları; iktisadi büyüme, istihdam ve sağlık harcamalarının doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkilerinin pozitif, hava kirliliğinin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisinin ise negatif olduğunu göstermektedir. Ayrıca kısa dönemli bulgulara göre iktisadi büyümenin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisi negatiftir. Panel nedensellik bulgularına bakıldığında, sağlık harcamaları ile hava kirliliğinden doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresine doğru tek yönlü nedensellik ilişkisine rastlanmıştır. İstihdam ile doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi arasında ise çift yönlü nedensellik ilişkisine rastlanmıştır.

title: Reduced fertilization sustains ecosystem multifunctionality and economic benefit in a temperate agroforestry system
summary: Agroforestry as a sustainable agricultural intensification strategy aims to optimize resource use and enhance the provision of ecosystem services when compared to treeless open croplands. Here, we evaluated the effects of fertilization rate
content: Agroforestry as a sustainable agricultural intensification strategy aims to optimize resource use and enhance the provision of ecosystem services when compared to treeless open croplands. Here, we evaluated the effects of fertilization rates and land use management on ecosystem functions, based on 37 ecological indicators, measured over five years (2019–2023). Reduced fertilization did not significantly affect overall ecosystem multifunctionality in either agroforestry or open cropland, although some indicators differed. This lack of reduced fertilization effect likely reflects a legacy effect of chronic over-fertilization in this agroecosystem. Compared to open cropland, agroforestry enhanced carbon sequestration but was associated with reduced water filtration likely due to spatially unadjusted fertilization rates in shade-affected, low-yielding crops near the trees. Economic performance indicators were collectively comparable among fertilization and land use management systems. Our results suggest that optimized fertilization in agroforestry can sustain food production, while promoting resilient, resource-efficient agriculture.

title: Carbon Credit Marketplace with Multi-Modal Verification for Smallholder Agroforestry - Satellite NDVI, Ground-Photo AI and Soil Carbon
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Smallholder agroforestry plots rarely market, because the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) step that backs each credit still rests on field visits that are too expensive to run on a one- or two-acre holding, in many respects; i
content: Smallholder agroforestry plots rarely market, because the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) step that backs each credit still rests on field visits that are too expensive to run on a one- or two-acre holding, in many respects; indeed, the platform is a FastAPI backend, a React web app and an Expo mobile app, with 139 automated tests covering it, to a significant degree. A rule-based fraud engine, role-separated farmer, auditor and buyer portals. The check is fusing satellite vegetation data (NDVI computed from real Sentinel-2 imagery inside the boundary the farmer draws), a ground-photo classifier (MobileNetV3-Small, 98.4% accuracy on 1,420 held-out real photos) and a soil organic carbon (SOC) reading into one weighted score, 0.40 NDVI + 0.35 photo + 0.25 SOC. A score of 75 or above is permitted, 55 to 75 is routed to a human auditor; indeed, we built a working prototype of a carbon-credit marketplace in which a plot can mint credits only after it clears an automated, explainable three-part check. And anything under 55 is rejected; if any single piece of indication is missing the plot stays pending, and no value is ever invented, and an Ethereum-style ledger (Ganache) are logging each credit from issuance, through the transfer to retirement. In an end-to-end run on live data, a real areca plot in Shivamogga, Karnataka created an NDVI of 0.794 from a Sentinel-2 scene dated 27 September 2026, was authorized at 84.9/100, minted a 20 tCO2 credit; and thus, as, well, that credit was then bought and retired.

title: Genuinely Quantum Algorithms for Bio-inspired Meta-heuristic Optimization
summary: Quantum computation offers a promising pathway toward advancing meta-heuristic optimization, particularly in Nature-inspired paradigms such as genetic algorithms and swarm intelligence. This study conducts a systematic literature review of
content: Quantum computation offers a promising pathway toward advancing meta-heuristic optimization, particularly in Nature-inspired paradigms such as genetic algorithms and swarm intelligence. This study conducts a systematic literature review of fifteen major meta-heuristics to assess current efforts toward their quantum realization. Emphasis is placed on identifying genuinely quantum proposals (those that can be implemented on quantum hardware) as opposed to quantum-inspired analogues that remain classically simulable. The review highlights the present landscape, emerging algorithmic strategies, and open challenges that define the path toward truly quantum meta-heuristic optimization.

title: East-West Coordination and Economic Dispatch of Libya's Power System: Economic Value and Transmission Capacity Sensitivity
summary: Independent day-ahead scheduling in interconnected regions can meet the needs of each region, the system-level economic efficiency is low due to the failure to fully utilize the limited exchanges between regions in the scheduling sequence.
content: Independent day-ahead scheduling in interconnected regions can meet the needs of each region, the system-level economic efficiency is low due to the failure to fully utilize the limited exchanges between regions in the scheduling sequence. This paper constructs a 24-hour mixed-integer linear programming model for the Libyan power system to coordinate and optimize unit combination, start-up and shutdown decisions, economic dispatch, and the total east-west exchange variable. Controlled experiments were conducted under three frameworks with the same regional demand, initial state, unit constraints, time constraints, and calibrated cost coefficients: independent scheduling with zero exchange, coordinated scheduling with an exchange limit of 349.6 MW, and a virtually unconstrained mixed baseline. The study is evaluated based on data from 19 authorized operating days starting in 2025, consisting of 25 thermal power plant modules. The MATLAB optimization toolbox provides the main solution, while independent SciPy/ HiGHS reconstructions validate the objective function, completeness, regional balance, ramp-up capability, and minimum time residual. Throughout the sample, coordinated operation reduced the total target capacity from 97.759 million comparative cost units (CUs) to 97.094 million, achieving 86.17% of the combined economic value, reducing the average committed operating units from 9.80 to 9.11, and decreasing the total number of start-ups and shutdowns from 205 to 196. The coordinated operation plan transmitted 105.85 GWh of absolute power and 87.32 GWh of net power from east to west, with model-predicted load shedding at zero. On peak-value days, the target capacity decreased by 1.448%; on peak days of 8166 MW, the decrease was 0.157%. Transmission capacity sensitivity analysis revealed diminishing returns: high-value cases reached saturation near 750 MW, while peak cases achieved almost all available benefits at 500 MW. These results provide a quantitative screening method for prioritizing detailed national grid studies and developing coordinated operation policies.

title: Forecast‐Driven Freight Resilience
summary: Global freight markets are increasingly shaped by rapid, compound shocks. Economic cycles, capacity lags, fuel and carbon cost uncertainty, port congestion, and geopolitical disruptions interact to produce spot-rate volatility that directly
content: Global freight markets are increasingly shaped by rapid, compound shocks. Economic cycles, capacity lags, fuel and carbon cost uncertainty, port congestion, and geopolitical disruptions interact to produce spot-rate volatility that directly affects budgets, service levels, and commercial commitments. This chapter argues that resilience is strengthened when firms treat spot-rates as a real-time market signal and build disciplined, explainable forecasting capabilities that convert turbulence into earlier decisions, rather than later firefighting. The chapter first explains why ocean freight spot-rates serve as a sensitive barometer of supply–demand imbalance and why their swings often precede broader indicators. It then maps the main volatility drivers and illustrates the nonlinear feedback loops that amplify rate moves when shocks collide. Building on this foundation, it translates forecasting into practice. It outlines data requirements, compares four modeling “lenses” from classical time series to machine learning and expert overlays, and shows how to manage uncertainty through validation and probabilistic bands. A practitioner playbook links forecast bands to concrete levers, including hedging and contract strategy, adaptive routing and capacity planning, and S&OP-driven inventory synchronization. A case study on potential Strait of Hormuz closure demonstrates how scenario-based spot-rate forecasts support negotiation, rerouting, and stakeholder communication. The chapter closes with a pragmatic 12-month action plan for implementing forecast-driven resilience at the lane level.

title: MXene and TEGA Compared: Stability, Manufacturing and Scale
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: MXenes, two-dimensional transition-metal carbides first reported in 2011, are again promoted as materials for future batteries, supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding and water treatment. Before any large-scale use, three practical ques
content: MXenes, two-dimensional transition-metal carbides first reported in 2011, are again promoted as materials for future batteries, supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding and water treatment. Before any large-scale use, three practical questions decide their fate: how long the material keeps its properties, how it is made, and how much of it can be produced. This preprint compares MXene with TEGA (thermally expanded graphite Arbok), a graphene-like carbon material produced in-house by ARBOK. In water dispersions Ti3C2Tx MXene oxidizes to titanium dioxide, and its conductivity falls to about 7% of the original value in 27 days unless it is stored at −80°C. MXene is made by etching MAX-phase ceramics in hydrofluoric acid, in some protocols for 90-118 hours. TEGA is pure carbon, does not oxidize, withstands up to 1500°C, is made from oxidized natural graphite at 50-100 USD per tonne and is sold at about 50 USD/kg. One TEGA line produces 50-300 kg/h, or 400-2,000 t/yr, against a world graphene output of 3,500-4,000 t in 2023. ARBOK data for TEGA-based supercapacitor electrodes and electromagnetic absorbers are given: 180-250 F/g, 500,000 cycles, more than 60 dB shielding. A scenario estimate puts the saving at 1-2 bln USD a year if one third of the electromagnetic shielding and supercapacitor markets moved to TEGA. Keywords: MXene, TEGA, thermally expanded graphite, oxidation stability, supercapacitor, electromagnetic shielding, scalable production

title: The Missing Link: A View of Food in the Age of Obesity
summary: The most visible form of non-communicable disease is, of course, obesity. Sadly, however, there is also a wide range of autoimmune diseases and, increasingly, of mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions that, all-too-often, are not r
content: The most visible form of non-communicable disease is, of course, obesity. Sadly, however, there is also a wide range of autoimmune diseases and, increasingly, of mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions that, all-too-often, are not recognised by the sufferers themselves. Another characteristic feature of modern disease is onset in ever-younger individuals. Babies may suffer from eczema, children from autism, and cases of type 2 diabetes in primary school. Alongside this, cancer in under-50-year-olds is best explained by an immunodeficiency problem. The view taken in this article is that such a wide range of diseases points to something missing in the intestinal microbiome of vulnerable people and that, rather than exclusively bacterial in origin, this “missing link” is an intergenerational microeukaryote sentinel cell component of the immune system, possibly one that evolved earlier than the vertebrates themselves. In turn, this implies a “dual inheritance” that, alongside the genetic inheritance of a baby, such sentinel cells are transferred from the intestinal microbiome of the mother to the child at birth. Unlike in normal usage, in this article, the word “dysbiotic”, or its derivatives, refers to people having a malfunctioning microbiome from birth, while the corresponding term “eubiotic” refers to the opposite, a person or population who exhibit none of the symptoms of non-communicable disease. Accordingly, a state of eubiosis is best regarded as a theoretical concept in Westernised populations, potentially being restricted to people living outside of modern-dominated environments. In this “missing link” concept it is a failure of a communication network within the growing child, an “immune-gut-brain triangle”, rather than the organs themselves, that define the problem. Food, including probiotics, is at the centre of this “triangle”, having direct effects on the microbiome, the brain, and the immune system. In addition, we should be able to investigate these relationships more closely with the aid of interkingdom messenger-detecting ingestible sensors.
