content: The move to sustainable transport supports the development of evaluation techniques for Electric Vehicles (EVs) and their energy storage systems.The uncertainty, discrepancies and subjective judgments of experts affect the rankings produced by conventional multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods.This paper therefore proposes a hybrid method that integrates the Fuzzy-Weighted Zero-Inconsistency Method (FWZIC) with Fuzzy MULTIMOORA.FWZIC derives criterion weights from direct importance ratings rather than pairwise comparisons, and Fuzzy MULTIMOORA combines three ranking perspectives, defuzzifying by the centroid operator.Large language models are used to generate several synthetic preference panels, which serve as a robustness experiment rather than as a substitute for human experts.The framework is demonstrated on four EV energy-storage technologies: Lithium-ion, Sodium-ion, Zinc-ion and a Potassium-ion capacitor, each characterised from published records on three criteria, Performance, Safety and Cost.Every criterion is built on a common parameter-wise normalisation domain shared by all four alternatives, so that a normalised value carries the same physical meaning for every chemistry.Quantitatively, FWZIC assigns weights of 0.318, 0.364 and 0.318 to Performance, Safety and Cost, and the integrated Fuzzy MULTIMOORA ranking is Li-ion > Na-ion > K-ion > Zn-ion (rank sums 3.5, 5.5, 9.5 and 11.5, lower being better).Ranks are assigned by the fractional-rank rule, so alternatives with equal scores receive equal ranks.Fuzzy TOPSIS and fuzzy VIKOR applied to the same matrix and weights reproduce this ordering exactly (Spearman ρ = 1.00 for both), and the ordering is unchanged across four synthetic preference panels, across expert-panel sizes of one to three, and across triangular-fuzzy spreads from 0.05 to 0.30.Propagating uncertainty from the raw source records by bootstrap (2000 replicates per configuration) gives a probability of 0.687 that Lithium-ion is ranked first, 0.198 for Zinc-ion, 0.075 for Sodium-ion and 0.040 for the Potassium-ion capacitor.The criterion set is a compact proxy set: Safety is represented by nominal voltage and Cost by durability indicators rather than monetary quantities, so the study is a methodological demonstration of the framework rather than a definitive technology recommendation.

title: Accuracy Preserving Selective Rare Attack Expert with Deep Cross Residual Learning for Imbalanced Network Intrusion Detection
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Severe class imbalance can make multiclass intrusion detectors appear reliable while rare attacks remain poorly recognized.This study proposes an Accuracy-Preserving Selective Rare Attack Expert (AP-SRAE) built on a Deep Cross Residual Netw
content: Severe class imbalance can make multiclass intrusion detectors appear reliable while rare attacks remain poorly recognized.This study proposes an Accuracy-Preserving Selective Rare Attack Expert (AP-SRAE) built on a Deep Cross Residual Network (DCRN) backbone.The term accuracy-preserving is operational and validationtolerance-bounded: candidate gates may reduce calibrated-backbone validation accuracy by at most 0.15 percentage point, but no test-set guarantee is implied.On the original 2,280,090-flow full-context random benchmark, AP-SRAE achieves 98.28% accuracy and raises macro F1 from 61.85% to 65.76%; exact paired predictions show 191 incorrectto-correct and 124 correct-to-incorrect transitions, for a net gain of 67 correct decisions.In an identifier-reduced rerun, macro F1 rises from 53.60% to 58.35% and balanced accuracy from 56.24% to 62.33%, with a 0.09-percentage-point accuracy decrease.On the official UNSW-NB15 split, five independent seeds yield balanced accuracy of 48.53% +/-0.55% for AP-SRAE versus 47.56% +/-0.52% for the backbone (paired t-test p=0.026), while accuracy decreases from 72.96% +/-0.59% to 72.60% +/-0.77%.Protocol-controlled IDS-MTran and TabTransformer reimplementations obtain higher official-split headline accuracy, but AP-SRAE is computationally lighter in the controlled run.An independent component-wise ablation further shows that the final gated and weighted expert improves over the calibrated backbone in macro F1 and balanced accuracy while leaving Normal-class F1 unchanged.

title: Causal-inspired Cross-asset Contrastive Multimodal Maintenance Network: A Proxy-benchmark Study for Renewable-energy Maintenance
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: This paper proposes a Causal-Inspired Cross-Asset Contrastive Multimodal Maintenance Network (C3M-Farm) for predictive-maintenance research in renewable-energy systems.The architecture combines modality-specific encoders, environment-aware
content: This paper proposes a Causal-Inspired Cross-Asset Contrastive Multimodal Maintenance Network (C3M-Farm) for predictive-maintenance research in renewable-energy systems.The architecture combines modality-specific encoders, environment-aware latent disentanglement, cross-modal contrastive learning, attention-based fusion, and graph reasoning.NASA C-MAPSS is used as a turbofan prognostics proxy rather than as direct renewable-energyfarm validation.The reported classification experiment achieved 96.0% accuracy, 95.7% precision, 95.2% recall, 95.4% F1-score, and 97.0%AUC.In the controlled same-pipeline RUL evaluation, C3M-Farm achieved RMSE values of 2.94 ± 0.12, 2.11 ± 0.08, 2.34 ± 0.09, and 2.94 ± 0.11 on FD001, FD002, FD003, and FD004, respectively.The paper reports lower RMSE values for C3M-Farm than for the evaluated baselines on the subsets for which corresponding results are available.These results are interpreted descriptively.The preliminary archived experiments (Tables 3456) are retained only for provenance and do not support superiority claims.The study therefore demonstrates proxy-benchmark performance while retaining explicit limitations concerning cross-study protocol equivalence, proxy-modality construction, physical farm-topology reasoning, and validation on genuinely heterogeneous renewable-energy assets.

title: Alternatif Enerji Kaynakları ve Enerjinin Geleceği
summary: This report presents the topics highlighted during the TÜBA-TÜBİTAK Summer School on Alternative Energy Sources and the Future of Energy, held at Mersin University from July 20 to 25, 2025. The report describes software programs commonly us
content: This report presents the topics highlighted during the TÜBA-TÜBİTAK Summer School on Alternative Energy Sources and the Future of Energy, held at Mersin University from July 20 to 25, 2025. The report describes software programs commonly used in energy system analysis and modeling, and examines thermodynamic analysis and energy efficiency. The report provides information on smart materials, nuclear energy, traditional and alternative fuels, and renewable energy. It also discusses energy storage systems and their applications. The “hydrogen age” was highlighted, and the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of energy were explained. Smart grid systems, smart transportation systems, and regional energy systems have been examined. Finally, the report discusses the role of artificial intelligence in energy, as well as the ethical and social dimensions of energy. With this comprehensive overview, the report aims to provide a perspective on future energy systems by highlighting the opportunities and challenges in the energy sector and related industries.

title: EV Charging Station Demand Analysis
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging networks are usually monitored through separate hardware logs and spreadsheets, so demand surges, queue delays and capacity needs are noticed only after they have occurred. This paper presents the EV Charging
content: Electric vehicle (EV) charging networks are usually monitored through separate hardware logs and spreadsheets, so demand surges, queue delays and capacity needs are noticed only after they have occurred. This paper presents the EV Charging Demand Analytics Platform, which brings the session records and station metadata of a charging network into one interactive web application. The data of 8,354 charging sessions across 20 urban and highway hubs are validated, merged and enriched with time, revenue, utilization and demand-level features. Six scikit-learn pipelines are trained: a Random Forest queue waiting-time regressor, a Gradient Boosting port-capacity advisor based on a 70% target-utilization rule, a Random Forest peak-hour classifier, a Gradient Boosting sessionenergy forecaster, a Random Forest high-demand hotspot classifier and a revenue regressor. A Streamlit and Plotly interface gives network key performance indicators, a station leaderboard, a day-of-week by hour-block density heatmap, a six-way non-restrictive filter and what-if prediction forms. The network totals are 8,354 sessions, Rs. 3,495,296 revenue, 226,603 kWh energy, 53.2% average load and 9.5 min average waiting time. The peak-hour and demand-tier classifiers reach 99.3% and 94.0% accuracy, while the waiting-time model does not beat the mean baseline (R2 = −0.008). The reasons for these results, including target leakage in several models, are discussed openly, and a plan for a stricter evaluation is given.

title: IoT-Based Smart Water Monitoring, Automated Billing and Excess Flow Control System: A Review
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Water conservation and its proper distribution are major problems in residential buildings and housing societies. Traditional methods of water management may involve manually reading meters, inspection, and late billing, which makes it hard
content: Water conservation and its proper distribution are major problems in residential buildings and housing societies. Traditional methods of water management may involve manually reading meters, inspection, and late billing, which makes it hard to detect excessive flow and leakage quickly. The IoT facilitates connectivity between sensors, microcontrollers, communication network, database, and user interface. This review highlights fifteen research papers regarding IoT-based water monitoring, smart metering, automatic billing, flow sensing, water quality monitoring, wireless communication, and intelligent water management. These research papers focus on residential water metering, apartment billing, retrofit monitoring, pressure and flow sensing, water distribution network, and resource management strategy. There are several possibilities of integrating flat wise consumption sensing, automatic billing, excessive flow sensing, alarming, and supply control using valves into one device. The framework for such integration is suggested in this paper. The effectiveness of such framework needs to be checked experimentally through flow sensing precision, billing precision, abnormal flow sensing precision, controlling reaction time, communication efficiency, and data integrity.

title: PEMODELAN DAN OPTIMASI SISTEM HIBRIDA PLTS–PLTB–GRID BERDASARKAN POTENSI ENERGI LOKAL MENGGUNAKAN HOMER PRO DI DESA GILI GEDE INDAH
summary: This study develops and optimizes a PV–wind–grid hybrid energy system based on local renewable energy potential in Gili Gede Indah Village, West Lombok, Indonesia, using HOMER Pro. The analysis considers solar and wind resources, electricit
content: This study develops and optimizes a PV–wind–grid hybrid energy system based on local renewable energy potential in Gili Gede Indah Village, West Lombok, Indonesia, using HOMER Pro. The analysis considers solar and wind resources, electricity demand, and techno-economic parameters to identify an appropriate system configuration for the study area. The simulation results show that the selected configuration consists of a 1,200 kW PV system, five 10 kW wind turbines, a grid connection with a capacity of 999.99 kW, and an 800 kW converter. The system produces 2,053,522 kWh/year from PV and 50,333 kWh/year from wind, while the grid supplies 649,741 kWh/year. The modeled annual electricity demand is 1,149,524 kWh, with zero unmet electrical load. The resulting NPC and COE are IDR 5,501,519,000 and IDR 165.86/kWh, respectively, while the Renewable Fraction is 74.7%. The results indicate that the modeled PV–wind–grid configuration can meet the simulated electricity demand and provide the evaluated technical and economic performance under the assumptions applied in HOMER Pro.

title: DEVELOPING A CLIMATE-RESILIENT INDUSTRIAL LEADERSHIP MODEL FOR RENEWABLE ENERGY ADOPTION
summary: The increasing effects of climate change and the need for sustainable industrial operations have highlighted the importance of effective leadership and renewable energy adoption. Industrial organizations face financial, technical, organizat
content: The increasing effects of climate change and the need for sustainable industrial operations have highlighted the importance of effective leadership and renewable energy adoption. Industrial organizations face financial, technical, organizational, and workforce-related challenges in implementing renewable energy technologies and climate-resilient practices. This study aimed to assess industrial leadership practices, employee engagement, and organizational readiness for renewable energy adoption; identify implementation challenges; and develop a climate-resilient industrial leadership model for sustainable industrial operations. The study employed a descriptive-developmental research design involving 50 respondents from selected industrial establishments in Pinamungajan, Toledo City, and Balamban, Cebu, Philippines. The respondents consisted of industrial managers, supervisors, technical personnel, and industrial employees. A researcher-developed questionnaire was used to gather data on leadership practices, employee engagement, organizational readiness, renewable energy adoption, and climate-resilient industrial practices. Frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and standard deviation were identified as the statistical tools for analyzing the collected data. The findings were intended to serve as the basis for developing the proposed leadership model. The illustrative assessment results indicated an overall mean of 3.97, interpreted as highly adopted. Leadership support for renewable energy adoption obtained a mean of 4.32, while integrating sustainability into organizational plans and policies received 4.24. Employee support for renewable energy initiatives obtained a mean of 4.16. In contrast, the availability of financial resources received a mean of 3.54, indicating an area requiring further improvement. These preliminary results highlighted the importance of leadership commitment, employee participation, technical capacity, resource allocation, and organizational preparedness in supporting renewable energy adoption. The study proposed a climate-resilient industrial leadership model integrating strategic leadership, employee engagement, organizational readiness, renewable energy principles, and climate-risk management. The model was intended to guide industrial organizations in strengthening decision-making, improving energy efficiency, addressing implementation challenges, and promoting sustainable industrial development. Further validation using actual survey results and expert evaluation was recommended to establish the model’s relevance, feasibility, and applicability.

title: HYBRID DATA-DRIVEN DISTRIBUTIONALLY ROBUST OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR OPTIMAL PV–BESS MICROGRID SIZING UNDER UNCERTAINTY
source: GNIOT JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT AND TECHNOLOGY
summary: Determining the appropriate capacity of photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) remains a critical challenge in microgrid planning, particularly in regions where historical data are limited and renewable generati
content: Determining the appropriate capacity of photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) remains a critical challenge in microgrid planning, particularly in regions where historical data are limited and renewable generation is highly uncertain. Conventional sizing approaches often depend on deterministic assumptions or predefined probability distributions, which may not accurately represent real operating conditions. This work presents a hybrid framework that combines data-driven learning with Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) to support reliable and cost-effective sizing of PV–BESS microgrids under uncertainty. The proposed approach utilizes available historical information together with uncertainty-aware optimization to identify system configurations capable of maintaining performance across a range of possible demand and generation scenarios. By incorporating robustness directly into the decision-making process, the framework reduces sensitivity to data limitations and unpredictable renewable energy behavior. Comparative evaluation using publicly available datasets indicates improvements in reliability, lower energy loss, and reduced lifecycle cost when compared with traditional deterministic and conventional robust optimization strategies. The findings suggest that integrating data-driven forecasting with DRO offers a practical pathway for designing resilient microgrids in rural, remote, and data-scarce environments where reliable energy access remains a significant concern.

title: Enhancing Grid Support and Renewable Utilization in EV Charging Networks through Advanced Energy Management
source: Research Digest on Engineering Management and Social Innovations
summary: This paper proposes power management strategies for a grid tied PV storage system in electric vehicle charging station (EVCS). The strategy is designed to be implemented in the power control system of the CS. The control proceeds depending
content: This paper proposes power management strategies for a grid tied PV storage system in electric vehicle charging station (EVCS). The strategy is designed to be implemented in the power control system of the CS. The control proceeds depending on the integration of renewable energy sources by adopting an optimization algorithm, in order to minimize stress on existing power and to reduce the cost of consumed energy based on the electrical grid in standalone mode. In this paper a strategy will be proposed for EV charging station to give priority to certain EV to charge faster and prevent the SOC from being the main drive in case of limited power source. The aim of this paper is to design and evaluate a charging algorithm that will prioritize EVs and fill some faster than others. This approach can be utilized by private businesses to categorize and lower the fees for charging, making EVs more attractive economically. To test the validation of this model, simulation results of several charging scenarios express the effectiveness of the proposed CS effectively. In this paper, a power predictive model was presented to forecast EVs power demand and to enhance the CS performance, in order to avoid an extra burden on the grid during peak hours. PV array with storage battery supported by the grid increased the reliability and flexibility of the system.

title: Development and Study of Mechanical Properties on Bamboo Fiber & Egg Shell Powder Reinforced Polypropylene Used for Prosthetic Applications: A Review
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Polypropylene (PP) is an attractive thermoplastic matrix for lightweight engineering components because of its low density, chemical resistance and compatibility with conventional melt-processing methods. Its mechanical response can be modi
content: Polypropylene (PP) is an attractive thermoplastic matrix for lightweight engineering components because of its low density, chemical resistance and compatibility with conventional melt-processing methods. Its mechanical response can be modified through fibre and particulate reinforcement. This review examines the potential of combining chopped bamboo fibre and eggshell powder in PP, with maleic-anhydride-grafted polypropylene (MAPP) as a compatibilizing agent, and considers the relevance of this material family to external lower-limb prosthetic components. The discussion covers natural-fibre/PP composites, bamboo-fibre reinforcement and surface modification, eggshell-derived calcium-carbonate fillers, hybrid reinforcement, processing effects and prosthetic performance requirements. Bamboo fibre may contribute reinforcement when fibre length, treatment, orientation and interfacial stress transfer are controlled, whereas eggshell powder can act as a mineral filler whose effects depend on particle size, loading and dispersion. The combination offers a potential route to valorize renewable and waste-derived feedstocks, but increased stiffness may be accompanied by reduced elongation or impact tolerance. MAPP is a potential compatibilization strategy, although its effectiveness depends on fibre treatment and processing conditions. The review identifies a need to evaluate hybrid PP composites containing bamboo fibre, MAPP and varying eggshell-powder contents using matched controls and consistent mechanical, microstructural and durability testing. Current evidence supports further material development but does not establish clinical suitability or the safety of a finished prosthetic device

title: Analyzing Cyber Threats and Vulnerabilities in Iran's Gas Industrial Control Systems and Presenting a Counter Measure System Model
summary: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) in the gas industry, as a part of the critical infrastructure of countries, are facing increasing cyber threats. These threats have created serious challenges due to the strategic importance of the gas indus
content: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) in the gas industry, as a part of the critical infrastructure of countries, are facing increasing cyber threats. These threats have created serious challenges due to the strategic importance of the gas industry in the national economy and security, as well as the very key role of industrial control systems in the gas industry. This research has been conducted with the aim of identifying and analyzing cyber vulnerabilities in the industrial control systems of the gas industry and presenting a systemic model to counter these threats. The research method is mixed (quantitative-qualitative), and the necessary data has been collected through field studies, in-depth interviews with experts, specialized questionnaires, and document analysis. The research results show that the main vulnerabilities include a lack of integration in the security architecture, the use of outdated systems, weakness in access management, and deficiencies in employee training. The proposed systemic model includes five protective layers (developed defense-in-depth) that, with an emphasis on a preventive and rapid response approach, can be implemented in the specific conditions of gas infrastructures.

title: Збірник матеріалів IX Міжнародної науково-практичної конференції текстильних та фешн-технологій KyivTex&Fashion (м. Київ, 16 жовтня 2025 р.): тези доповідей

title: Pengaruh Variasi Sudut Pitch Terhadap Performa Turbin Angin Darrieus H Berprofil Naca 0018 Menggunakan Metode CFD
source: UMS Library Center of Academic Activities (Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta)
summary: -Problem: The performance of a Darrieus-H wind turbine is influenced by the aerodynamic interaction between the airflow and the blades, one of which is affected by variations in the pitch angle. However, the effects of pitch angle variation
content: -Problem: The performance of a Darrieus-H wind turbine is influenced by the aerodynamic interaction between the airflow and the blades, one of which is affected by variations in the pitch angle. However, the effects of pitch angle variations on torque, mechanical power, Tip Speed Ratio (TSR), power coefficient (Cp), and airflow characteristics of a three-bladed Darrieus-H wind turbine with an NACA 0018 airfoil under the investigated operating conditions have not been comprehensively determined. Objective: This study aims to analyze the effect of pitch angle variations on the performance of a three-bladed Darrieus-H wind turbine with an NACA 0018 airfoil, analyze the relationship between TSR and Cp, and investigate the airflow characteristics around the turbine. Method: The study was conducted using the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method with ANSYS CFX 2026 R1 using a steady-state approach. The turbine model has a rotor diameter of 540 mm, a height of 660 mm, and a chord length of 125 mm, with pitch angle variations of 0°, 5°, 10°, 15°, 20°, and 25°, wind speeds of 7–10 m/s, and rotor speeds of 150–300 RPM. The analyzed parameters include torque, mechanical power, TSR, Cp, and airflow characteristics obtained from the CFD simulations. Results: Increasing the pitch angle and rotor speed increased torque and mechanical power within the simulated range, while Cp tended to increase with TSR. The highest Cp of 38.42790% was obtained at a TSR of 0.84823 and a pitch angle of 25°, with a torque of 2.670180 Nm and mechanical power of 83.88618 W at 300 RPM. CFD results showed an airflow velocity of approximately 6.08 m/s at the inlet and a maximum of 24.32 m/s around the leading edge and trailing edge, with wake and vortex formation behind the rotor. Thus, a pitch angle of 25° provided the highest performance within the simulated conditions, although the absolute optimum could not be determined because Cp continued to increase up to a TSR of 0.84823.

title: Managing energy transition in emerging economies: the role of green finance, policy innovation and governance
source: International Journal of Energy Sector Management
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how policy innovation and governance effectiveness condition the relationship between green finance and energy transition outcomes in emerging economies. It assesses the extent to which regulatory reforms,
content: Purpose This study aims to examine how policy innovation and governance effectiveness condition the relationship between green finance and energy transition outcomes in emerging economies. It assesses the extent to which regulatory reforms, financial incentives and institutional frameworks jointly enhance investment in sustainable energy systems. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data for 25 emerging economies over 2010–2023. A dynamic panel regression model estimated with two-step system-generalized method of moments (GMM) is used to analyse the relationships among green finance, policy innovation, governance effectiveness and renewable energy investment. Interaction models and a battery of robustness tests are used to evaluate the moderating roles of policy innovation and governance. Findings Policy innovation significantly strengthens the positive effect of green finance on renewable energy investment. The marginal effect of green finance nearly doubles when moving from low to high levels of policy innovation, and increases by approximately three-quarters when moving from weak to strong governance. Countries that continuously adapt their regulations, define clear green taxonomies and maintain regulatory stability convert green finance into renewable investment more effectively. The three-way interaction indicates that finance, policy and governance operate as complements rather than substitutes. Research limitations/implications There are a number of limitations to this research. The two-step system-GMM approach helps to overcome the issue of endogeneity; however, the results should be understood as strong conditional relationships, not as causal relationships. The analysis is based on secondary data at the country level from 25 emerging economies and can overestimate or underestimate disparities at subnational level, and may be less applicable to countries where data are not available. In addition, there is the issue of how well composite indices of green finance, policy innovation and governance deal with institutional complexity. Future studies should analyse individual policy instruments, introduce subnational/firm-level data and implement mixed-method/longitudinal designs to better understand how energy transition outcomes are realised. Practical implications This study offers recommendations for policymakers and financial institutions seeking to accelerate the energy transition, including sequenced reforms that pair green finance market development with policy clarity and institutional strengthening, differentiated by the institutional starting point of each economy. Social implications The findings underscore the potential of integrating financial mechanisms with policy innovation to support inclusive and sustainable energy development in emerging economies and to reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Originality/value This study contributes to the energy sector management literature by jointly modelling green finance, poli

title: Coordinated dual layer volt-var control for power distribution systems with electric vehicles and distributed generations
source: International Journal of Emerging Electric Power Systems
summary: Renewable distributed generators (DGs) such as solar PVs, and vehicle-to-grid technology (V2G) are gaining traction in the power distribution sector to ensure energy security. However, renewable DGs exhibit intermittency that can cause rapi
content: Renewable distributed generators (DGs) such as solar PVs, and vehicle-to-grid technology (V2G) are gaining traction in the power distribution sector to ensure energy security. However, renewable DGs exhibit intermittency that can cause rapid voltage fluctuations leading to frequent switching when performing voltage regulation using conventional feeder control devices such as on-load tap changers (OLTC) and capacitor banks (CB). The frequent switching can bring about increased equipment operation and maintenance costs. This issue of voltage regulation can be addressed through the 4-quadrant smart inverters functions of DGs and electric vehicles (EVs). Hence, this paper proposes a dual layer control method aimed at mitigating rapid voltage fluctuations to reduce switching operations for the feeder voltage regulating devices. Moreover, it also optimizes the reactive power operation of the inverters with the aim of reducing the aging rate of the inverters. The efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated through a modified IEEE 123-bus system by obtaining minimized voltage deviation, optimized reactive power consumption/generation of DGs to reduce inverter aging, and optimized charging/discharging of EVs for voltage regulation.

title: Biomass-enabled metal−organic framework-based macroarchitectural materials with advanced applications
summary: Purpose The rising global demand for energy, together with the environmental pressures linked to industrial growth, has made sustainable green development a global priority. This review focuses on biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures as a
content: Purpose The rising global demand for energy, together with the environmental pressures linked to industrial growth, has made sustainable green development a global priority. This review focuses on biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures as an important class of sustainable porous materials. Design/methodology/approach This review focuses on three main aspects: fabrication strategies, structure–property relationships (dimensions) and advanced applications. It covers key synthesis routes such as templating, interfacial assembly and reaction confinement, while showing how biomass components such as cellulose, lignin and chitosan influence material formation and performance. The review also explains how pore hierarchy, interface design, surface chemistry, transport pathways and mechanical stability determine the final properties of these systems. Findings By combining the tuneable structure and functionality of MOFs with the renewability, hierarchical architecture and easy processability of biomass, these materials address major drawbacks of conventional MOF powders, especially poor shape control, weak mechanical strength, limited mass transfer and difficult device integration. Their growing applications in adsorption, catalysis, environmental cleanup, energy storage and drug delivery are highlighted. Current challenges include large-scale production, interface control, durability and limited mechanistic understanding. Originality/value The article points to future directions for designing application-oriented biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures. These materials are expected to become a key platform for scalable and high-performance next-generation technologies.

title: Energy security risks and banking stability: the moderating roles of renewable energy and governance effectiveness
summary: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether energy security risk (ESR) is associated with country-level banking stability and whether this relationship varies with renewable energy development and governance effectiveness. Design/methodology
content: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether energy security risk (ESR) is associated with country-level banking stability and whether this relationship varies with renewable energy development and governance effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a panel of 64 countries from 2010 to 2021. Two-way fixed effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors provide the baseline estimates, while two-step system GMM is used as a supplementary dynamic check. Additional analyses consider the World Uncertainty Index, alternative banking indicators, net energy-trade position, nonlinearities and lagged moderators. Findings Higher ESR is associated with lower banking Z-scores, higher nonperforming loan ratios and lower net interest margins. The association remains after controlling for broader country-level uncertainty. It is stronger in net energy-importing economies and at higher ESR levels, but weaker where renewable energy penetration and governance effectiveness are greater. Lagged-moderator estimates provide strong support for the renewable energy interaction and more qualified evidence for governance effectiveness. Research limitations/implications The country-level design supports macroprudential inference but cannot identify heterogeneous responses across individual banks. The estimates are associational and do not establish causal effects. Practical implications Supervisors should incorporate energy-security indicators into macroprudential monitoring, scenario analysis and early-warning frameworks. Renewable energy development and institutional capacity may form part of broader strategies to strengthen banking-system resilience. Originality/value This paper links a multidimensional ESR index to aggregate banking stability and shows how this relationship varies across energy structures, institutional settings and exposure conditions.

title: Adaptive Surrogate Model for Real-Time Condition and Health Monitoring of Powertrain Components
summary: With the availability of powerful computing units and a wide range of on-board sensors, Digital Twins (DTs) have become a hot topic in the automotive sector. A DT enables seamless integration between physical and digital counterparts. Lever
content: With the availability of powerful computing units and a wide range of on-board sensors, Digital Twins (DTs) have become a hot topic in the automotive sector. A DT enables seamless integration between physical and digital counterparts. Leveraging Internet of Things (IoT) and digital technologies, it promises real-time condition monitoring (CM) and predictive maintenance. This paper presents a methodology for real-time CM of vehicle powertrain components, focusing on the development of a computationally efficient deep learning-based surrogate model for a traction inverter, derived from a multi-physical high-fidelity model. While accurate, high-fidelity models require heavy computation, making them unsuitable for real-time use. To address this limitation, the proposed model leverages extensive simulation data from the high-fidelity model to train neural networks. It employs multiple networks for steady-state and transient predictions, incorporating a gating mechanism for state-segregation. The networks use Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) hidden layers, together with a physics-informed training methodology to embed physical constraints during inference. Training results yield an R 2 score above 98 %, demonstrating the accuracy. Development of a computationally light model for power inverters is a significant step in the realization of ADTs for powertrain components. This research is conducted as part of the EU EFFEREST project (GA-101138266).

title: Global Policy Uncertainties, Carbon Risk Exposure, and Green Energy Transition Outputs: Evidence From Renewable Energy Technological Innovation Finance
summary: Using intensive large panel data from thirty‐one IEA‐member economies from 1974 to 2020, we provide cross‐country evidence on the long‐term roles of renewable energy technology innovation finance in renewable energy transition and climate r
content: Using intensive large panel data from thirty‐one IEA‐member economies from 1974 to 2020, we provide cross‐country evidence on the long‐term roles of renewable energy technology innovation finance in renewable energy transition and climate risk mitigation under policy uncertainty in the era of climate change. In line with the Environmental Kuznets curve (EKC) hypothesis, the study affirms the positive impacts of energy technology innovations on sustainable energy transition through the increase in renewable energy consumption and renewable electricity output as a percentage of total energy use across the sample countries. Based on the STIRPAT/IPAT framework, the role of Energy Technology RD&D Budgets is irrefutable toward SDGs through the world's uncertain times, when we test for both the global economic policy uncertainty (GEPU) and climate policy uncertainty (CPU) using the newly developed newspaper‐based indexes. Given that Energy Technology RD&D Budgets have been mainly dependent on the public sector, the study provides economically meaningful findings with critical policy implications for financing sustainable energy transitions, climate action, and other SDGs by the United Nations for the world economy, including IEA member economies.

title: Model choice and prompt framing in LLM sustainability judgments
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for sustainability assessment and decision support, yet their judgments may depend on the selected model and on how the task is defined. We compare 13 locally executed open-weight LLMs
content: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for sustainability assessment and decision support, yet their judgments may depend on the selected model and on how the task is defined. We compare 13 locally executed open-weight LLMs on 80 author-written sustainability scenarios using three prompt families that ask which actor should be responsible, bear the costs, or initiate action. Each model answered at two temperature settings with 100 repetitions, producing 624,000 deposited outputs, of which 610,708 contain a complete score vector. Scores were analyzed as relative actor support after removing each response’s overall level. Within this instrument, the cost prompt family produced the highest cross-model disagreement, exceeding both responsibility and catalyst by 7.37 points (question-cluster 95% intervals 5.56−9.15 and 5.38−9.36, describing variation across these 80 scenarios). It also produced the most lead-actor disagreement and the lowest full consensus. Moving from catalyst to cost reduced relative support for government and increased it for individuals and firms; moving from cost to responsibility largely reversed this pattern. These differences exceeded temperature-setting differences and persisted under model exclusion, alternative score transformations and tie rules, missing-response checks, and stems without explicit cost wording. Exploratory category patterns are conditional on uneven item coverage. Secondary rationale-language comparisons show the same within-model ordering but not the most cross-model variation under cost. Operational use should disclose model, prompt, and temperature choices; compare plausible alternatives; repeat generations; and refer high-disagreement judgments for human deliberation.

title: Expanding flavonoid production in Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 from lignin-derived aromatics
summary: Background Flavonoids are valuable plant secondary metabolites with broad applications in the food, nutraceutical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical industries. While microbial biosynthesis offers a renewable alternative for chemical synthesis a
content: Background Flavonoids are valuable plant secondary metabolites with broad applications in the food, nutraceutical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical industries. While microbial biosynthesis offers a renewable alternative for chemical synthesis and plant extraction, most production platforms rely on lengthy biosynthesis pathways from sugars, requiring extensive pathway engineering and often focusing on individual products. Lignin-derived aromatics (LDAs) offer attractive precursors for flavonoid biosynthesis, but their utilization requires a host capable of aromatic substrate tolerance and metabolism. Results We engineered Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 for the conversion of LDAs into multiple flavonoid products. We identified a novel heterologous enzyme combination CHS–CHI (CHS from Stenoloma chusanum and CHI from Medicago sativa ) that supported flavonoid biosynthesis, namely 3.4 mg/L homoeriodictyol from ferulate and 24.2 mg/L eriodictyol from caffeate in flask cultivations after 24 h. The engineered strain produced a different flavonoid from each tested substrate in flask cultivations, enabling product switching through feedstock selection without further genetic engineering. In fed-batch bioreactors fed with a mixture of ferulate, caffeate, and p -coumarate, the strain produced three flavonoids (homoeriodictyol, eriodictyol, and naringenin). Finally, flavonoid production was demonstrated directly from alkaline-pretreated liquors (APLs) derived from wheat straw and organosolv lignin. Ferulate and p -coumarate were detected in both liquors, yielding homoeriodictyol and naringenin, confirming the compatibility of the platform with complex lignin-derived feedstocks. Conclusions This work establishes A. baylyi ADP1 as a promising platform for the production of multiple flavonoids from LDAs, including directly from APLs. By leveraging native aromatic catabolism, the strain bypasses the need for extensive precursor biosynthesis and enables substrate-driven product diversification. These results provide a proof of concept for converting LDAs into structurally different flavonoids in a single microbial host.

title: Functional time series forecasting of air temperature using a functional autoregressive model with electricity demand as an exogenous variable
summary: Short-term air temperature (AT) forecasting is crucial for climate monitoring, integration of renewable energy, agricultural management, and environmental decision-making. The inherent complexity of the temporal structure of AT (nonlinear d
content: Short-term air temperature (AT) forecasting is crucial for climate monitoring, integration of renewable energy, agricultural management, and environmental decision-making. The inherent complexity of the temporal structure of AT (nonlinear dynamics, high diurnal periodicity, the interactions between various meteorological variables) makes the conventional statistical and machine learning models (which typically view AT observations as discrete time series and do not make effective use of the continuous functional structure of AT) less effective in predicting AT. This study proposes a functional autoregressive model with exogenous variable (FARX(1)) for predicting daily AT curves in a functional time series (FTS) context, overcoming these limitations. The proposed model is an extension of the classical functional autoregressive model of order one (FAR(1)), which maintains the time dependence and smooth functional structure of the daily temperature measurements; while additionally incorporating electricity demand as the exogenous variable, given its established association with diurnal temperature dynamics. The hourly AT data is approximated by smooth functional curves that enable efficient modeling of the diurnal temperature dynamics and observational noise in the data, and is obtained by an approximation of the data with Fourier basis functions. The ability of the proposed framework to forecast the performance is evaluated by comparing it with five widely used benchmark models: ARIMA, VAR, ANN, ARNN, and FAR(1) over extensive overall forecasting, hourly forecasting, weekly forecasting and monthly forecasting scenarios, employing the Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE), Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (sMAPE), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed FARX(1) model in minimizing the conventional FAR(1)’s forecasting error for all the evaluation scenarios, highlighting the significance of using the exogenous variable of electricity demand in the model for forecasting accuracy. The results also highlight the potential of representing AT as functional observations to obtain a flexible and statistically sound representation of complex temporal variations, which enhances the reliability and robustness of short-term AT forecasts. The concept is proposed as a solution for the meteorology community in operational forecasting to the weather community and as climate monitoring and decision support to weather dependent applications such as renewable energy management.

title: Влияние органо-минерального комплекса на технологические свойства модельных резиновых смесей на основе бутадиен-нитрильного каучука
summary: Инновации в области добавок для эластомерных композиций включают использование возобновляемых и экологически чистых ресурсов. Применение натуральных добавок в резиновых смесях способствует не только целенаправленному улучшению эксплуатацион
content: Инновации в области добавок для эластомерных композиций включают использование возобновляемых и экологически чистых ресурсов. Применение натуральных добавок в резиновых смесях способствует не только целенаправленному улучшению эксплуатационных характеристик конечного продукта, но и снижению экологического воздействия на протяжении всего жизненного цикла материала. В связи с растущими потребностями резиновой промышленности, актуальна разработка и внедрение новых технологических добавок для резиновых смесей, основанных на доступных продуктах растительного и минерального сырья. В статье исследована возможность применения органо-минерального комплекса на основе смеси жирных кислот и природного бентонита, в качестве частичной и полной замены отдельных компонентов вулканизующей системы в модельных резиновых смесях на основе бутадиен-нитрильного каучука марки БНКС-18АМН. Анализ полученных результатов показал, что использование органо-минерального комплекса взамен отдельных компонентов вулканизующей системы до 30% фактические не оказывает влияния на реологические свойства исследуемых резиновых смесей, в то время как увеличение содержания данного комплекса приводит к увеличению (до 21%) показателя вязкости по Муни. Также определено повышение стойкости резиновых смесей к преждевременной подвулканизации (до 97%) при замене компонентов вулканизующей системы на органо-минеральный комплекс во всех исследуемых дозировках, сокращению (до 48%) времени достижения оптимума вулканизации.

title: Chinese Knowledge Production and Flows: Learning from Others and Producing our Own Knowledge
summary: In China, knowledge generation and flows are strongly influenced by the country’s economic situation and foreign relations, that is, how China positions itself in the global context. The exchange and dissemination of knowledge about migrati
content: In China, knowledge generation and flows are strongly influenced by the country’s economic situation and foreign relations, that is, how China positions itself in the global context. The exchange and dissemination of knowledge about migration, as in other fields, is influenced by the country’s unique geopolitical features, now and in the past. In the following sections I show how significant historical periods in China have shaped its knowledge production and dissemination, and how recent advances in its economy and technological development affect this trajectory.

title: Who should govern public energy communities? The role of environmental awareness and privacy cost
summary: Energy communities are becoming an important instrument of the clean energy transition, but their performance depends on how they are governed. We develop a model in which a municipality invests in renewable-energy infrastructure and choose
content: Energy communities are becoming an important instrument of the clean energy transition, but their performance depends on how they are governed. We develop a model in which a municipality invests in renewable-energy infrastructure and chooses between public management and delegation to a private aggregator. Consumers differ in their willingness to pay, value self-produced energy, and incur privacy costs when consumption data are used beyond the operational baseline. Under the symmetric benchmark, private governance produces a smaller community because the aggregator applies a monopoly participation margin and does not internalize the benefit that additional members create for the rest of the community. Public governance therefore expands participation, while investment timing depends on how the operating surplus is allocated between the municipality, members, and the private operator. We then show that correcting the private participation distortion is only a partial alignment result: implementing the public-optimal community size does not by itself align member utility or investment timing. A regulated delegation contract can use a per-member inclusion payment to align participation, a membership-independent concession payment to align investment timing, and data-use restrictions to control privacy exposure. Finally, a numerical example relaxes operational symmetry by allowing the private operator to manage self-consumption more efficiently than the public operator. In this case, regulated delegation can combine public participation objectives with private operational efficiency when the relevant contractual margins are observable and enforceable.

title: A wind power generation and meteorological dataset for the entire Henan province in China across diverse landforms
summary: The high penetration of grid-connected wind power has created increasing demands for power forecasting, dispatch operations, and renewable energy integration studies in modern power systems. However, publicly available wind power datasets s
content: The high penetration of grid-connected wind power has created increasing demands for power forecasting, dispatch operations, and renewable energy integration studies in modern power systems. However, publicly available wind power datasets still vary considerably in spatial representativeness, temporal coverage, and the level of quality-control documentation. Here we present HENAN-WPF, a regional wind power dataset for Henan Province, China, covering 36 wind farms across all 18 cities. The dataset provides continuous power observations from January 2022 to December 2025 at a 15 min resolution and captures both plain and mountainous terrains. It further includes 1 h sampled products, detailed site metadata, and matched ERA5 meteorological variables. HENAN-WPF offers a robust benchmark for regional collaborative wind power forecasting, meteorological impact analysis under complex terrain, and spatiotemporal graph-based modelling.

title: Quaternary Solid Electrolytes of the Na11Sn2PS12 Type with an Sn/Group 5-Metal Combination
summary: Throughout the last decades, the research on sodium solid electrolytes (SSEs) has flourished and a wide variety of electrolytes have been generated and analyzed. One family is based on Na3PS4, the ionic conductivity of which is increased in
content: Throughout the last decades, the research on sodium solid electrolytes (SSEs) has flourished and a wide variety of electrolytes have been generated and analyzed. One family is based on Na3PS4, the ionic conductivity of which is increased in quaternary expansions of the formula, such as Na11Sn2PS12 (A) For the design and the performance of new SSEs, aliovalent and isovalent substitution play a particularly important role. However, in sulfide-based SSEs, incorporation of group five transition metals instead of phosphorus has not yet been done. Herein, we report on the formation of V-, Nb-, or Ta-based compounds, Na11.61Sn2.42V0.58S12 (1), Na11.25Sn2.48Nb0.52S12 (2), and Na10.93Sn2.41Ta0.59S12 (3), which are isostructural with recently published Na11.5Sn2.5P0.5S12. The hot-pressed compounds exhibit ionic conductivities of 0.35 mS·cm–1 (1), 0.20 mS·cm–1 (2), and 0.17 mS·cm–1 (3), respectively. Additional temperature-dependent 23Na NMR spectra and T1 relaxation times were acquired to investigate the local ionic motion, which reveals faster local hopping processes for A, 2 and 3.

title: ESFEX: an open-source framework for multi-model power-system optimization and energy-flexibility analysis
summary: ESFEX (Energy System Flexibility) is an open-source framework for the design, optimization and flexibility analysis of power systems and their transition toward high renewable penetration. Its distinguishing feature is a single reproducible
content: ESFEX (Energy System Flexibility) is an open-source framework for the design, optimization and flexibility analysis of power systems and their transition toward high renewable penetration. Its distinguishing feature is a single reproducible workflow from a region on a map to a solved planning study. An interactive GIS Studio builds the georeferenced network from OpenStreetMap and open power-plant databases, estimates spatial demand and hourly renewable availability, and passes them to an optimization core where stochastic and near-optimal capacity-expansion plans are re-evaluated in chronological dispatch with mixed-integer unit commitment, DC or AC optimal power flow and N-1 security, coupled with primary-energy supply, electric vehicles and rooftop solar. Established frameworks cover subsets of these capabilities, often through separate scripted toolchains, whereas ESFEX combines them under one data model, graphical interface and command line. The optimal power-flow core is verified against eight independent open-source implementations on ten IEEE and PEGASE systems of 9 to 13,659 busses, reproducing the consensus optimal cost within 10 –9 % in DC on systems up to 9241 busses and 10 –5 % in AC, and its measured runtime and memory delimit the study designs it supports.

title: The Clean Transition and Polycrisis Resilience: Energy Security, Decarbonization, Pollution Reduction and Industrial Transformation
summary: Energy systems sit at the centre of many of the pressures that make up the contemporary polycrisis. Fossil-fuel combustion drives climate change and most outdoor air pollution; dependence on imported fuels transmits price and supply shocks
content: Energy systems sit at the centre of many of the pressures that make up the contemporary polycrisis. Fossil-fuel combustion drives climate change and most outdoor air pollution; dependence on imported fuels transmits price and supply shocks into food, debt and household budgets; and the absence of affordable, reliable energy holds back industry, health services and education in much of the developing world. This paper asks whether a single large shift in how energy is produced, stored, moved and used can reduce several of these risks at the same time, and under what conditions it does so. It proposes that the clean transition be evaluated as a multi-dimensional resilience strategy rather than an isolated environmental objective. It sets out six research objectives, a six-part research architecture (renewable energy expansion; storage and system reliability; transportation electrification; industrial decarbonization; the household energy transition; energy infrastructure and security) and a five-dimension evaluation framework, and introduces a screening measure, multi-dimensional resilience impact, applied in an illustrative ranking of ten interventions. Benefits are not automatic: poorly planned transitions can create new vulnerabilities in critical minerals, supply-chain concentration, grid reliability, affordability and industrial employment. The paper closes with three strategic priorities (accelerate deployment, improve accessibility, integrate resilience into transition planning) and three stylized scenarios to 2050. Frameworks are proposals open to testing; projections are scenarios, not forecasts. Part of the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series.

title: Dynamic price-incentivized spatiotemporal coordination of grid-friendly data centers and distribution systems
summary: Data centers constitute not only rapidly growing high-density loads but also potential flexible resources for distribution networks, enabled by suitable price signals and coordination mechanisms. However, under practical demand response rul
content: Data centers constitute not only rapidly growing high-density loads but also potential flexible resources for distribution networks, enabled by suitable price signals and coordination mechanisms. However, under practical demand response rules with response thresholds and penalties for invalid responses, translating computational flexibility into valid and verifiable grid-side responses remains challenging. Here, we propose a bilevel framework that coordinates distribution network operations through dynamic electricity prices and schedules spatiotemporal workloads across multiple data centers. The framework explicitly incorporates the practical demand response mechanism implemented in Guangdong, China, and is solved by a lexicographic damped alternating algorithm with engineering stability. Simulations on a modified IEEE 32-bus system and a 60-bus practical system show that the proposed method decreases the cost of data centers, increases the accommodation of renewable energy, and improves valid response delivery. These results indicate that under threshold-based settlement, participation in the demand response is not necessarily beneficial unless flexibility can be delivered in a valid and verifiable form.

title: ANÁLISE NUMÉRICA DE UM SISTEMA OFF-GRID HÍBRIDO SOLAR-HIDROCINÉTICO UTILIZANDO O SOFTWARE HOMER, EM ACARÁ-PA
summary: O estudo avalia numericamente o desempenho técnico-econômico de um sistema híbrido fotovoltaico e hidrocinético isolado para o atendimento energético de um sítio na Comunidade Mangará, no município de Acará, Pará, Brasil. A pesquisa objetiv
content: O estudo avalia numericamente o desempenho técnico-econômico de um sistema híbrido fotovoltaico e hidrocinético isolado para o atendimento energético de um sítio na Comunidade Mangará, no município de Acará, Pará, Brasil. A pesquisa objetiva coletar e avaliar dados climáticos e de escoamento do Igarapé Arapiranga-Açu, estimar a curva de carga elétrica do perfil de consumo local, dimensionar e simular o sistema híbrido, realizar análise técnico-econômica comparativa visando substituir possíveis gerações a diesel e formular recomendações para projetos de sistemas híbridos sustentáveis em comunidades amazônicas remotas. A metodologia utiliza simulações computacionais no software HOMER Pro a partir de dados de irradiação solar, da estimativa sazonal da velocidade fluvial e da demanda residencial baseada nos equipamentos locais, acrescida de expansão de dez por cento para vinte e cinco anos. O resultado define uma arquitetura com 3,08 quilowatts-pico de geração fotovoltaica, uma turbina hidrocinética de 0,50 quilowatt, oito baterias de fosfato de ferro-lítio e um inversor de 2,00 quilowatts, configuração que respeita o limite de conexão elétrica das baterias, otimiza a área física e assegura autonomia de 20,2 horas. O sistema apresenta Custo Presente Líquido de 105.828,73 reais e Custo Nivelado de Energia de 2,88 reais por quilowatt-hora, valor inferior à tarifa de 8,12 reais por quilowatt-hora da opção a diesel, evitando a emissão acumulada de 111,57 toneladas de dióxido de carbono. Conclui-se que a matriz híbrida viabiliza o consumo local, recomendando-se equipamentos eficientes e o dimensionamento orientado ao período de estiagem.

title: Applicability of Machine Learning tool for the 2020-2099 forecasting of reservoir capacity
summary: Reservoir storage is crucial for managing water seasonal fluctuations and climate change impacts on U.S. water supplies. Due to their strategic location and the continuous loss of their storage, current reservoirs are considered a non-renew
content: Reservoir storage is crucial for managing water seasonal fluctuations and climate change impacts on U.S. water supplies. Due to their strategic location and the continuous loss of their storage, current reservoirs are considered a non-renewable resource for the country. Previous efforts developed a supervised machine learning (ML) tool that estimated reservoir capacity losses from reservoir design information and watershed characteristics. The objective of this study is to evaluate the capability of this ML tool to forecast reservoir capacity under future climate scenarios. The evaluation was run for three trial reservoirs of different initial capacities and basin characteristics. Results showed ML tool results aligned with extrapolating results, a common practice when projecting reservoirs storage, with the addition of confidence intervals that would incorporate the uncertainty of future climate conditions. Results also exhibited the possibility of implementing the ML tool for forecasting storage of reservoirs with limited surveys. Time step for capacity loss estimation was found to be a critical indirect parameter of the ML tool, with larger basins requiring larger time step for the computations. Projected reservoir capacity losses showed a higher temporal correlation with maximum precipitation values for small basins. Projected percentages of reservoirs’ capacity loss per year with respect to initial capacity were larger for the trial basin with largest maximum rainfall events, and steepest channel slope regardless of the average precipitation or the basin area.

summary: The article evaluates the efficiency of using solar thermal collectors, heat pumps and photovoltaic systems for building heating under the climatic conditions of Uzbekistan. For a typical residential building, the annual energy consumption
content: The article evaluates the efficiency of using solar thermal collectors, heat pumps and photovoltaic systems for building heating under the climatic conditions of Uzbekistan. For a typical residential building, the annual energy consumption and CO2 emissions of a gas boiler and of options based on renewable sources are compared. The results showed that a combination of a heat pump and a photovoltaic system can reduce emissions by up to 70 %, and that improving the building’s thermal insulation increases the effect even further.

title: Design and Feasibility Analysis of Small-Scale Wind Turbines
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The rapid growth of population, industrialization, and urban development has significantly increased global energy consumption, leading to excessive dependence on fossil fuels and associated environmental challenges such as greenhouse gas e
content: The rapid growth of population, industrialization, and urban development has significantly increased global energy consumption, leading to excessive dependence on fossil fuels and associated environmental challenges such as greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. In response to these concerns, renewable energy technologies, especially wind energy, have emerged as sustainable alternatives for clean and decentralized power generation. This study investigates the performance and feasibility of a vertical axis small-scale wind turbine (VSWT) installed at Jaichandpura village, Jaipur, Rajasthan under moderate wind conditions. The experimental turbine consisted of four FRP blades and was evaluated at wind speeds ranging from 3-8 m/s. Field observations indicated an average wind velocity of 5.75 m/s, while the maximum wind power density achieved was 31 3.6 W/m² at 8 m/s wind speed. The turbine generated a maximum energy output of 21 1 .68 Wh with an overall system efficiency of approximately 45%. The findings indicate that the proposed VSWT system is technically suitable for decentralized rural electrification and small-scale energy applications. Furthermore, the study highlights the potential integration of small-scale wind systems with hybrid renewable technologies to enhance energy reliability in remote regions. The proposed work contributes toward sustainable energy development and supports Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7: Affordable and Clean Energy, as well as SDG 1 3: Climate Action.

title: Greenhouse Farming: Cultivating the Future
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Greenhouse farming is widely promoted as a route to climate-resilient and resource-efficient food production, yet claims about its benefits are often repeated without clear baselines. This narrative review examines protected cultivation, wi
content: Greenhouse farming is widely promoted as a route to climate-resilient and resource-efficient food production, yet claims about its benefits are often repeated without clear baselines. This narrative review examines protected cultivation, with particular attention to India, covering structure types, automation and digital technologies, environmental and economic performance, policy support and socio-economic effects. Evidence was drawn from peer-reviewed studies, Indian farm-level economic analyses, official guidelines and recent survey data, and each quantitative claim is reported with its crop, location, comparison baseline and evidence type. About 14,400 ha of greenhouse structures were built in India between 2005 and 2020, over half of them low-technology, and expert estimates suggest that a large share is no longer operating. Water-use efficiency gains are well documented but shrink when the baseline is drip-irrigated field production or when evaporative cooling is needed. Recent Indian farm studies report higher yields and benefit–cost ratios above one for polyhouse vegetables, but with several-fold higher costs, and some crop–scale combinations are not viable. Greenhouse produce can have a higher carbon footprint per kilogram than open-field produce unless energy use is low or renewable. AI-based climate control has been demonstrated mainly in research-scale, high-technology compartments, and evidence on employment and women’s participation is thin. The paper concludes that greenhouse farming is a context-specific option rather than a universal improvement, and it identifies priorities for evidence, finance and policy.

title: Sustainable chemistry for the production of clean and renewable energy and its role in climate action
summary: The shift towards renewable and clean energy sources is key to addressing the issues related to climate change and minimizing the use of fossil fuels. Sustainable chemistry provides radical solutions to developing, optimizing, and integrati
tags: Environmental impact of the energy industry
content: The shift towards renewable and clean energy sources is key to addressing the issues related to climate change and minimizing the use of fossil fuels. Sustainable chemistry provides radical solutions to developing, optimizing, and integrating renewable energy technologies and reducing the environmental effects. This review indicates the current developments in the field of sustainable chemistry towards producing clean energy, with particular focus on solar conversion, artificial photosynthesis, bio-based fuels, hydrogen generation, and energy storage systems. The green chemistry concepts, such as the use of solvents that are environmentally friendly, recyclable catalysts, and circular design models, are addressed as major facilitators of scaling up renewable energy technologies. Specific attention is placed on photocatalytic and electrocatalytic water splitting to hydrogen, bio- materials valorization to biofuels, and green-based materials innovations to solar photovoltaics and improved storage systems. The scarcity of resources, scalability, and economic viability problems that limit their large-scale deployment are also critically reviewed. Simultaneously, prospects in nanotechnology, digital technologies, and policy frameworks are discussed in order to speed up the use of sustainable chemistry-based solutions. Through green considerations within renewable energy systems, sustainable chemistry offers a potent foundation for reducing the emission levels of greenhouse gases, enhancing resource efficiency, and developing global climate action objectives.

title: Representing Nature in Cosmetics Brand Advertisements on Instagram: An Eco-Imagistics Analysis
summary: With the growing adoption of nature-based imagery in cosmetics marketing, brands can link cosmetic products to the concepts of nature, sustainability, purity, wellbeing and environmental responsibility. But the symbolic imagery of nature in
content: With the growing adoption of nature-based imagery in cosmetics marketing, brands can link cosmetic products to the concepts of nature, sustainability, purity, wellbeing and environmental responsibility. But the symbolic imagery of nature in cosmetics advertising that is created through Instagram has not been adequately studied from the point of view of eco-imagism. This study explored the representation of nature in the Instagram ads of selected international cosmetic brands and the meanings created in these ads concerning beauty, naturalness, sustainability, authenticity, and environmental responsibility. The study used an interpretivist approach and the main analytical framework was Eco-imagistics. Ten advertisements were used, and ten international cosmetic companies' official Instagram accounts were used to purposively select an advertisement. Natural or environmental elements visible in the advertisement such as plants, flowers, fruits, water, landscape, botanical ingredients, natural colours, and ecological textures, were used to help determine the advertisements that were selected. The results identified that nature was always presented visually as purity, freshness, nourishment, health, authenticity and ecological value. The advertisements were analysed through the visual composition, botanical imagery, natural materials, lighting, textures and other visual elements related to nature. The study also revealed that nature was not only used as a decorative but also as a key visual element that brands used to create their brand image as environmentally friendly. The advertisements tended to idealize and commodity nature, making ecological harmony an aesthetically pleasing element of consumer culture.

title: Dataset and Source Code for "Wave-Energy Arrays for Reverse-Osmosis Desalination: A Forecast-Informed Energy–Water Nexus Assessment in the Saudi Red Sea"
summary: This study presents an integrated energy–water nexus framework for assessing the technical and economic feasibility of wave-powered reverse-osmosis desalination in the Saudi Red Sea. The proposed approach combines three-dimensional boundary
content: This study presents an integrated energy–water nexus framework for assessing the technical and economic feasibility of wave-powered reverse-osmosis desalination in the Saudi Red Sea. The proposed approach combines three-dimensional boundary element modelling (BEM), wave-energy converter hydrodynamics, power-take-off control strategies, multi-device interactions, forecast uncertainty propagation, and freshwater production modelling.A surface-piercing heaving wave-energy converter is investigated using Capytaine 2.3.1, with numerical verification performed across four mesh resolutions. The analysis compares fixed passive, sea-state-tuned passive, and constrained reactive control strategies under a representative synthetic wave climatology. Hydrodynamic interactions within three-device arrays are evaluated to quantify their influence on energy capture and overall system performance.The results demonstrate that sea-state-tuned passive control improves annual energy production by 9.9%, while array interactions introduce predominantly destructive interference. The best screened configuration delivers approximately 234.3 MWh of electricity and 73,210 m³ of freshwater annually. The corresponding levelized costs of water and electricity are estimated at USD 11.04/m³ and USD 2.94/kWh, respectively. A Monte Carlo analysis involving 5000 realizations further examines the influence of forecast uncertainty on predicted converter power.The associated research repository provides numerical results, documented modelling assumptions, computational scripts, and reproducibility resources supporting the energy–water nexus assessment. Reconstructed demonstration datasets are distinguished from manuscript-reported results, and the findings are intended for preliminary engineering screening rather than site-validated deployment predictions.This research contributes to the development of integrated modelling approaches for marine renewable energy, sustainable desalination, and energy–water system planning.

title: Rethinking Commons and Property in the Light of the Climate Crisis
summary: The climate crisis unfolds as a twin crisis of ecological degradation and global inequality. To address this crisis, international law has framed the atmosphere as a global commons, which is a shared resource domain that is disproportionate
content: The climate crisis unfolds as a twin crisis of ecological degradation and global inequality. To address this crisis, international law has framed the atmosphere as a global commons, which is a shared resource domain that is disproportionately overused and affects those first and hardest who have contributed the least to it. Taking the legal framing as its starting point, Verena Wolf analyzes how the overuse of the commons is regulated, focusing on the role of private property rights. In mainstream economic approaches, private property rights are the main tool to prevent the depletion of the commons and their shared resources. But does privatizing the commons resolve either ecological or social crises? Or should we rethink both commons theory and property theory? This study reframes the failure to mitigate the climate crisis as a failure of private property. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/legalcode

title: Post-Disaster Management of Mount Sinabung: A Systematic Literature Review from a Multi-Level Governance Perspective
source: Journal of Social and Political Sciences
summary: This literature review aims to investigate post-disaster management of the Sinabung volcano eruption. The analysis used Vos Viewer. The author limited the publication years of articles to 2014 to 2024. From the bibliometric review, the auth
content: This literature review aims to investigate post-disaster management of the Sinabung volcano eruption. The analysis used Vos Viewer. The author limited the publication years of articles to 2014 to 2024. From the bibliometric review, the author used the keyword "Multi-Level Governance" and found 565 documents published in reputable journals (Scopus). However, when the author used the keyword "Multi-Level Governance and Disaster," the author only found 49 documents. The author then continued using the keywords "Multi-Level Governance and Mount/Eruption" and "Multi-Level Governance and Disaster Management," which yielded "0" documents (no documents specifically using these keywords in the article titles). The review revealed the importance of multi-level governance in post-disaster management, such as encouraging refugee involvement in the complex relocation process, meeting social, economic, and cultural needs to support social ties among refugees in their new location, and building relationships and communication with local cultures. The author sees that research using the Multi-Level Governance concept needs to enrich the Multi-Level Governance concept itself and analyze the governance problems that arise in disaster management so that it is necessary to increase the use of the multi-level governance concept in analyzing disaster management, starting from the pre-disaster, emergency response and post-disaster stages.
