title: Landslide-Resilient Hillside Housing: An Integrated System of Biopolymer Soil Treatment, Bio-Engineering, Micropiles and Siphon Drainage
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Landslides triggered by rain repeatedly destroy homes and livelihoods on the steep, weathered slopes of the Western Ghats and other high-rainfall hill regions. The usual remedies, retaining walls and deep foundations, tend to be costly, car
content: Landslides triggered by rain repeatedly destroy homes and livelihoods on the steep, weathered slopes of the Western Ghats and other high-rainfall hill regions. The usual remedies, retaining walls and deep foundations, tend to be costly, carbonheavy and awkward to build on remote ground, and they are normally applied one at a time even though most slope failures have several causes working together. This paper presents the concept and test plan for an integrated, low-impact housing system that deals with the soil, the slope surface, the foundation and the groundwater together. The soil is strengthened with xanthan gum, a microbial biopolymer that bonds particles and lowers permeability. The surface is protected by vetiver contour hedgerows and bamboo clumps whose roots hold the upper soil. The house stands on micropiles socketed below the potential slip surface, and a French drain with siphon pipes removes the water that raises pore pressure, without pumping. We review the literature behind each component, explain how the weakness of one measure (for example the water sensitivity of the biopolymer) is covered by another, and set out the methodology: site selection, soil characterisation to Indian Standards, a xanthan gum dosage programme, bio-engineering, micropile and drainage design, limit-equilibrium and finite-element stability analysis of four scenarios, and a reduced-scale rainfall model. Expected outcomes are stated qualitatively because no test data exist yet. Materials, a prototype work plan, a maintenance routine and future research needs are also listed.

title: Internalising externalities through global technologies: an information systems–based extension of RBV and CBV
summary: Purpose This paper aims to advance strategic management theory by proposing iRBV – an Information Systems-based extension of the resource-based view (RBV) and capability-based view (CBV). This essay argues that globally available technologi
content: Purpose This paper aims to advance strategic management theory by proposing iRBV – an Information Systems-based extension of the resource-based view (RBV) and capability-based view (CBV). This essay argues that globally available technologies fundamentally change the role of firm resources and capabilities, enabling firms not merely to respond to market conditions but to reshape the rules by which markets operate. Drawing on RBV and CBV, the author proposes iRBV as a framework for understanding how firms can adopt and adapt global technologies – such as artificial intelligence and blockchain – to internalise externalities and create new markets. Design/methodology/approach This paper presents a viewpoint on how firms can proactively reshape their environment by incorporating externalities into their strategies. The author proposes iRBV – an information systems (IS)-based extension of the RBV, CBV and natural RBV – as a theoretical advancement that enables management scholars and practitioners to develop business models capable of addressing market externalities, including climate change, at the firm level. Findings Through two illustrative cases – ChatGPT and the Libra coin – this essay demonstrates how global technologies can enable firms to reshape markets and internalise externalities that lie beyond the scope of traditional RBV and CBV. Climate change mitigation is presented as one significant application of this mechanism. Research limitations/implications iRBV is presented as a theoretical provocation rather than a fully operationalised framework. Its primary limitation is the reliance on illustrative cases rather than systematic empirical evidence. Future research should develop the microfoundations of iRBV – specifically the routines, heuristics and higher-order capabilities that enable firms to adopt and adapt globally available technologies for externality internalisation. Additional boundary conditions require investigation, including the applicability of iRBV beyond digital technologies, the role of power asymmetries and path dependencies in capability activation and the conditions under which profit-maximisation logic aligns with – rather than diverges from – the internalisation of societal externalities. Practical implications iRBV equips managers with a theoretical lens for identifying externalities as strategic opportunities rather than regulatory obligations. Firms with strong IS capabilities – such as those already deploying artificial intelligence (AI) or blockchain – are well positioned to develop business models that internalise externalities while generating profit. iRBV encourages managers to incorporate a global view of their strategic environment into firm strategy, treating the internalisation of externalities not as a cost of doing business but as a potential source of market dominance. Social implications iRBV suggests that addressing societal externalities – including climate change – need not depend solely on top-dow

title: Educating for transformation: embedding strong and absolute sustainability in urban business education
source: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the integration of strong and absolute sustainability into urban business education, challenging mainstream economic assumptions that ignore biophysical realities. It explores pedagogical strategies to equ
content: Purpose This study aims to examine the integration of strong and absolute sustainability into urban business education, challenging mainstream economic assumptions that ignore biophysical realities. It explores pedagogical strategies to equip future professionals in the built environment to navigate the tensions between business objectives and planetary limits. Design/methodology/approach Using a practitioner-led action research approach, the instructor redesigned a master’s-level course at Malmö University. Outcomes were evaluated through a mixed-methods analysis, triangulating student questionnaires, instructor teaching journals and thematic analysis of student project outputs and learning reflections. Findings The curriculum successfully introduced frameworks like the flourishing business model canvas and absolute decarbonisation. However, students found the sobering reality of exceeded planetary boundaries emotionally draining. A primary challenge identified was a chicken-and-egg problem: the lack of existing practical examples for absolute sustainability in business made theoretical conceptualisation difficult. Students also struggled to reconcile long-term ecological timeframes with short-term market pressures and competitive realities. Originality/value This research fills a critical gap in business education where strong sustainability remains marginal, particularly within the built environment sector. It provides rare, empirically grounded guidance for educators seeking to move beyond efficiency-based weak sustainability toward transformative learning that prepares students to reshape business logic within the limits of the Anthropocene.

title: Historical and projected changes in tropical North and South Atlantic indices under different emission scenarios
summary: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability in the Tropical North Atlantic (TNA) and Tropical South Atlantic (TSA) plays a critical role in regulating regional climate systems, atmospheric circulation, and hydrological extremes. However, unce
content: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability in the Tropical North Atlantic (TNA) and Tropical South Atlantic (TSA) plays a critical role in regulating regional climate systems, atmospheric circulation, and hydrological extremes. However, uncertainties remain regarding the representation of tropical Atlantic SST variability and future warming patterns in CMIP6 climate models. This study investigated historical and projected SST anomaly characteristics over the TNA and TSA using NOAA ERSSTv5 observational data (1982--2014) and seven CMIP6 models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios (1967--2099). Statistical analyses including Taylor diagrams, Mann--Kendall trend tests, Sen’s slope estimation, anomaly frequency analysis, and persistence assessment were employed to evaluate model performance and future variability. Results showed that CMIP6 models reasonably reproduced observed SST variability, with correlation coefficients ranging approximately from 0.65--0.88 for TSA and 0.55--0.85 for TNA. NOAA observations indicated stronger positive anomaly dominance over TSA (218 warm events) and comparatively higher negative anomaly frequency over TNA (206 cold events). Under SSP5-8.5, projected warming intensified substantially, with Sen’s slope values increasing up to 0.0057 and projected SST differences reaching 0.0387$^\circ$C in the TNA region. Persistence analysis further revealed prolonged consecutive SST anomaly events exceeding 150 months in some models under high-emission forcing. The findings suggest that enhanced greenhouse gas emissions may amplify tropical Atlantic variability, strengthen ocean--atmosphere feedbacks, and increase climate-related risks across West Africa and adjacent regions. This study provides important scientific evidence for improving climate projection reliability and supporting regional climate adaptation and risk management strategies.

title: The past, the present and the future of the frog-killing fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) in Brazil: a review study and niche modeling of its distribution
summary: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis ( Bd ), the causative agent of chytridiomycosis, is one of the most significant emerging infectious pathogens affecting amphibians worldwide. Despite Brazil harboring the greatest amphibian diversity on planet
content: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis ( Bd ), the causative agent of chytridiomycosis, is one of the most significant emerging infectious pathogens affecting amphibians worldwide. Despite Brazil harboring the greatest amphibian diversity on planet, a comprehensive assessment of the occurrence patterns of Bd across the country remains lacking. Here, we combined literature records and original field surveys to assess the distribution, host diversity, and future climatic suitability of Bd in Brazil. A total of 5,539 Bd -positive individuals were compiled, encompassing 204 amphibian species distributed across multiple Brazilian ecoregions. Infection records were strongly concentrated in the southeastern Atlantic Forest, reflecting both favorable environmental conditions and historical sampling effort. Endemic species represented most of the positive records, and 25 threatened species were confirmed as infected. Species-level analyses revealed distinct regional host assemblages, highlighting the importance of stream-associated and humid forest microhabitats in pathogen persistence. Our models projected widespread current climatic suitability for Bd , including areas with limited surveillance, while future climate scenarios indicated a substantial contraction of climatically suitable areas, especially in inland regions. Under future climate scenarios, climatic suitability for the chytrid fungus is projected to persist predominantly along the coastal Atlantic Forest of southeastern and southern Brazil, with smaller isolated areas of long-term suitability occurring in other regions of the country, potentially representing additional areas of long-term climatic suitability for Bd . Our findings provide the most comprehensive overview of Bd occurrence in Brazil to date and highlight priority regions for surveys, key species for long-term monitoring and areas where climatic suitability may persist under future climate scenarios. These areas are highly important for Bd monitoring and for implementing conservation strategies for amphibians, given the synergistic threats posed by both Bd and ongoing climate change.

title: Fairness as a Driving Force for Congestion Pricing Acceptability
summary: Despite the growing implementation of road pricing schemes globally, public acceptance remains a significant barrier. This study investigates the role of perceived fairness in shaping user acceptance of a distance-based road user charging (
content: Despite the growing implementation of road pricing schemes globally, public acceptance remains a significant barrier. This study investigates the role of perceived fairness in shaping user acceptance of a distance-based road user charging (RUC) system, using Trondheim, Norway, as a case study. Ninety-four participants tested a GNSS-based RUC system over a two-month period, during which both objective driving data and subjective survey responses were collected. While only 24% of participants held negative views of the existing toll system, over half perceived it as unfair. After experiencing the RUC system, user attitudes became more divided; however, a majority still viewed distance-based pricing as fairer than the current toll model. The study found that fairness perceptions were not strongly influenced by socio-demographic factors, but were significantly associated with actual cost differences between the two systems. Although the RUC system did not lead to major changes in driving behavior, it increased awareness of travel habits and was seen as a potential tool for promoting sustainability. These findings highlight fairness as a critical factor in public acceptance of road pricing and suggest that experiential exposure to new systems can reshape user attitudes.

title: From Co-Design to Replication: Advancing Zero-Emission Sustainable Mobility Use Cases
summary: This paper presents the development and application of a structured Use Case Definition Framework (UCDF) designed to support the creation, validation, and replication of zero-emission mobility solutions in urban contexts. The framework has
content: This paper presents the development and application of a structured Use Case Definition Framework (UCDF) designed to support the creation, validation, and replication of zero-emission mobility solutions in urban contexts. The framework has proved to be key in facilitating scalability within the Horizon Europe project metaCCAZE, supporting ten Mission Cities in advancing their Climate City Contracts (CCC), Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (SUMP), and 2ZERO targets through the development of innovative use cases in areas such as automation, electrification, multimodality, and demand–supply optimisation. To ensure these solutions are deployment-ready, the project developed the UCDF, grounded in the European standard DIN SPEC 91387:2020–08 for Communities and Digital Transformation. Built on a WHY–WHAT–HOW logic, it guides cities in defining objectives, governance, infrastructure, and impact evaluation to facilitate scalability and replication. The UCDF not only enables the creation of new use cases but also functions as a replication tool, allowing cities to adapt and reproduce proven solutions.

title: Ecological Importance of Groundcover Plants in Xeriscape Landscape Design Under Mediterranean Climate Conditions
summary: Climate change has increased the need for ecologically resilient and water-efficient plant species in landscape design, particularly in the Mediterranean Basin, where rising temperatures, declining precipitation, and increasing pressure on
content: Climate change has increased the need for ecologically resilient and water-efficient plant species in landscape design, particularly in the Mediterranean Basin, where rising temperatures, declining precipitation, and increasing pressure on water resources pose significant challenges. This study evaluates the ecological importance of groundcover plants in climate-resilient xeriscape landscape design under Mediterranean climate conditions through a review of the current scientific literature. First, the vulnerability of the Mediterranean Basin to climate change and the fundamental principles of xeriscape landscape design are examined. Subsequently, the contributions of groundcover plants to water management, erosion control, biodiversity conservation, microclimate regulation, and green infrastructure enhancement are discussed within the framework of ecosystem services. In addition, the ecological and functional criteria for selecting groundcover plants suitable for Mediterranean conditions are evaluated, and native species occurring in the Mediterranean Basin and included in the flora of Türkiye are comparatively presented alongside exotic species that have successfully adapted to Mediterranean conditions. The study concludes that groundcover plants should be regarded not only as ornamental elements but also as strategic components of sustainable landscape design, contributing to climate change adaptation, water-use efficiency, biodiversity conservation, and the development of sustainable green infrastructure.

title: Landscape, Environment and Sustainability: Contemporary Approaches and Future Perspectives
summary: Landscape, Environment and Sustainability: Contemporary Approaches and Future Perspectives is a 16-chapter academic volume that brings together original research, literature reviews, and conceptual studies. It examines landscape planning an
content: Landscape, Environment and Sustainability: Contemporary Approaches and Future Perspectives is a 16-chapter academic volume that brings together original research, literature reviews, and conceptual studies. It examines landscape planning and design in relation to biodiversity conservation, access to public space, and climate adaptation. The book explores how dark infrastructure supports nocturnal habitats and biodiversity and how green corridors and ecological transportation systems contribute to ecological connectivity and ecosystem services. It examines nature-based solutions at Iğdır University and considers how traditional ecological design can inform contemporary approaches to thermal comfort. Chapters on public open space address inclusive playground design and access to public spaces through the 15-minute city approach. Case studies assess Ankara’s Başkent Millet Bahçesi against the design criteria of the National Gardens Guide, examine the landscape design of Konya’s Piri Reis Park, evaluate accessibility for people with disabilities at Muş Tulip Valley Park, and assess the use of Erzurum’s urban parks against women-friendly city criteria. A study of İzmir’s Kemeraltı Bazaar examines the relationship between spatial continuity and urban identity. A systematic literature review explores the sociodemographic and individual factors that shape users’ perceptions and preferences regarding urban green spaces and trees. The volume also examines environmentally responsible uses of plants in industry, the contribution of drought-tolerant trees to urban climate resilience, and the ecological role of groundcover plants in Mediterranean xeriscaping. A reading of the climate fiction novel The End We Start From considers how changing water regimes challenge human-centered understandings of landscape and raise questions of environmental ethics.

title: A Perspective on Iğdır University Campus Landscape Through the Lens of Nature-Based Solutions
summary: The global emergence of the escalating environmental, social, and economic impacts of climate change necessitates the development of sustainable planning and design approaches. In this context, university campuses, which can be considered s
content: The global emergence of the escalating environmental, social, and economic impacts of climate change necessitates the development of sustainable planning and design approaches. In this context, university campuses, which can be considered small-scale cities, bear significant responsibilities in addressing climate change, given their physical infrastructure, diverse user base, and institutional identity. Furthermore, because campuses occupy more contained and manageable spaces than urban settlements, they offer unique opportunities to develop, test, and monitor sustainable practices. In particular, the implementation of nature-based solutions at the campus scale aimed at climate change adaptation and mitigation allows these sites to serve as pilot projects and research grounds. Accordingly, this study presents a comparative analysis of the Iğdır University Şehit Bülent Yurtseven Campus, where landscaping projects were recently completed, examining its conditions both before and after these interventions. The study evaluates the extent to which nature-based solutions such as rain gardens, green roofs, permeable surfaces, biological stormwater management systems, and vegetative shading were incorporated into the landscape design, as well as which measures were omitted. The findings indicate that while certain features at the Şehit Bülent Yurtseven Campus can be classified as nature-based solutions, the existing ecological and climatic conditions were not adequately considered, despite the campus being newly developed. Given that the Iğdır University Şehit Bülent Yurtseven Campus is still in a phase of ongoing development, it is suggested that existing shortcomings be addressed and that a greater emphasis be placed on the integration of nature-based solutions.

title: Compatibilising Digital Data Exchange Across Transport Modes: Proof of Concept for TIC4.0 Compatibility with the IATA ONE Record Data Model
summary: Multimodal freight transport offers improved sustainability and efficiency in logistics. The EU promotes multimodal solutions to achieve climate neutrality by 2050, yet adoption remains slow due to coordination challenges and fragmented sys
content: Multimodal freight transport offers improved sustainability and efficiency in logistics. The EU promotes multimodal solutions to achieve climate neutrality by 2050, yet adoption remains slow due to coordination challenges and fragmented systems. Standardization and interoperability are essential for seamless operations, but diverse legacy systems across supply chain stakeholders hinder progress. This paper addresses these gaps by evaluating the semantic and syntactic compatibility between the Terminal Industry Committee’s (TIC4.0) and the International Air Transport Association’s (IATA) ONE Record data models. A case study approach is applied, analysing two EU contexts: Seaport–Airport Multimodal Transport in Greece, and Seaport–Subway Multimodal Transport in Spain. Findings show strong compatibility between the models, with TIC4.0 requiring additional fields for air transport. These results demonstrate that multimodal transport standardization is achievable, and targeted refinement at multimodal interfaces can deliver greater benefits than focusing solely on individual transport modes, supporting a more interconnected and sustainable European freight system.

title: A Modern and Sustainable Rail-Enabled Urban Logistics System and Its Economic Evaluation
summary: The European Union has set ambitious climate targets under the Paris Agreement and the European Green Deal. Urban freight transport remains a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution, and congestion, posing challenges to
content: The European Union has set ambitious climate targets under the Paris Agreement and the European Green Deal. Urban freight transport remains a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution, and congestion, posing challenges to sustainable urban development. Although policy and research interests are strong, few studies comprehensively integrate rail freight with low- or zero-emission last-mile delivery and assess the economic feasibility of such integration. This study proposes and evaluates an integrated model that combines inter-regional rail freight with micro-hubs near railway stations and environmentally friendly last-mile solutions, such as electric vehicles, cargo bikes, and crowdshipping. The methodology employs operational simulation and breakeven analysis to assess economic viability across different regulatory scenarios, particularly those involving European transport emissions allowances. Results show that carbon pricing substantially increases the cost of road-based regional deliveries using Heavy Goods Vehicles, while rail-integrated systems remain comparatively stable. A 40% modal shift from road to rail reduces monthly freight emissions by about 25%, mainly by replacing long-distance truck trips with low-carbon rail transport. The rail–bike configuration proves to be the most cost-effective and environmentally resilient under emission trading conditions. Overall, the study offers evidence-based guidance for policymakers, logistics providers, and urban planners, emphasizing the strategic importance of multimodal, rail-integrated freight systems for sustainable and resilient urban logistics.

title: Plant adaptation strategies to climate change in Malaysian agriculture
summary: Climate change poses significant effects and challenges to Malaysia’s agricultural sector through rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and increasing occurrences of extreme weather events. These climatic changes affect crop produ
content: Climate change poses significant effects and challenges to Malaysia’s agricultural sector through rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and increasing occurrences of extreme weather events. These climatic changes affect crop productivity, water availability, pest and disease dynamics, and the overall resilience of farming systems. An overview is provided of the current and projected impacts of climate change on major agricultural subsectors in Malaysia, namely rice, oil palm, rubber, and cocoa. Particular attention is given to the vulnerability of these crops to temperature stress, rainfall variability, droughts, and floods. Key adaptation strategies that can enhance agricultural resilience are examined, including the development of climate-resilient crop varieties, improved water management practices, climate-smart agriculture, and the use of climate information services and digital technologies. Sector-specific adaptation measures are discussed for rice, oil palm, rubber, and cocoa production systems. The importance of policy support, institutional strengthening, research, development, innovation, and multi-stakeholder collaboration in facilitating effective adaptation is also highlighted. Strengthening climate resilience through integrated and location-specific adaptation strategies will be essential and critical to sustaining agricultural productivity, ensuring food security, and supporting the long-term sustainability of Malaysia’s agricultural sector in a changing climate.

title: Sun-Shielding Earth From Space to Save Earth's Polar Icecaps
summary: Space-based solar radiation management has been proposed repeatedly since 1989 [12] — as L1 sunscreens [13], trillion-disk diffractive clouds, and dust veils — but always as a single global structure, dimming the entire planet to cool two p
content: Space-based solar radiation management has been proposed repeatedly since 1989 [12] — as L1 sunscreens [13], trillion-disk diffractive clouds, and dust veils — but always as a single global structure, dimming the entire planet to cool two places, at costs of trillions and with no way to throttle or recall the effect. We propose the opposite instrument: a fleet of lightweight, serviceable craft in near-polar orbit at ~550 km, shading only the ablation zones where ice-sheet loss is driven. Controllability is inherent to the design — each shield rotates between edge-on and perpendicular attitudes, turning shade on and off using only standard station-keeping type controls and no rocket propellant; the film is a consumable swapped by robotic servicers, while the structure endures for decades. Unlike any prior proposal, the Fleet touches only a global commons: no nation's agriculture, solar generation, or water supply is dimmed, and every component deorbits and burns up cleanly when the program ends. In phase 1, a small number of craft permit measuring the energy-balance delta against monitoring baselines. If the number of craft is sufficient, it's plausible a small fleet of 50 or less could obviate the need for phase 2, which calls for a sufficient constellation to stop the loss of polar ice. It costs on the order of tens to, with more craft, small hundreds of millions of dollars, a rounding error in federal budgets. Phase 3 aspires to regrow polar ice and thereby restore our weather patterns to something closer to our past. Whatever the full efforts cost, it is bounded by launch programs spacefaring nations already execute routinely, and the phases that follow scale only as verified melt-curve response justifies. Against the cost of losing every coastline civilization has built, the cost of acting to save the polar ice approaches zero. We argue it's irrational not to try. While surely other designs can work, we have chosen an example where the math works well. We contemplate each craft as a 1 by 25 km rectangle — multiple spans of coated Kapton-class film flanking a single pressurized telescoping boom — launched packed in a ~2.5 m drum. Starship's cargo bay holds seven such drums per launch alongside their film, establishing seven as the cost-effective fleet-building baseline per flight. Falcon-class and other international medium-lift vehicles loft service ships and their very low mass "Workers" that swap out components, provide propellant, and mount replacement film, making the initial demonstration achievable with roughly five coincident launches — one Starship and four medium-lift — and the growth fleet limited only by launch cadence, not by physics or technology. The arithmetic of the shadow is favorable. At 550 km altitude a 25 km craft crosses overhead at ~7.6 km/s, and the polar summer sun, circling at a low elevation, magnifies the shield's footprint on the ground several-fold: with the film perpendicular to the sun's rays, a 1 km-wide film

title: Urban climate dynamics in informal settlements: Spatiotemporal rainfall and temperature variability in Thembelihle, Johannesburg
summary: Climate change has emerged as a critical contemporary concern, marked by greater variability and severity in weather systems, from extreme heat to drought and intense precipitation. Africa is particularly vulnerable, with urban settlements
content: Climate change has emerged as a critical contemporary concern, marked by greater variability and severity in weather systems, from extreme heat to drought and intense precipitation. Africa is particularly vulnerable, with urban settlements facing disproportionate risks. This study investigates long-term temperature and rainfall dynamics in Thembelihle, an informal settlement in Johannesburg, alongside broader metropolitan trends, using robust statistical and geospatial methods. Temperature and rainfall data spanning five decades (1974–2024 for Thembelihle; 1981–2024 for Johannesburg) were examined using the non-parametric Mann-Kendall (MK) Test and Sen’s Slope estimation to detect monotonic trends. Rainfall indices included the number of wet days (NWDT), the highest number of consecutive wet days (HNCWD), the highest number of consecutive dry days (HNCDD), and the maximum daily rainfall (HRPD). Extreme temperature events in Thembelihle were examined using a Peak Over Threshold (POT) approach. Spatial interpolation of CHIRPS rainfall and ERA5 temperature anomalies was conducted in QGIS to visualize spatiotemporal variability across Johannesburg. Results reveal statistically significant warming in Thembelihle, with minimum temperatures increasing at 0.0505 °C/year and maximum temperatures at 0.0391 °C/year, remaining higher than Johannesburg’s anomaly trend, although the magnitude of this difference is reduced when trends are compared over a harmonised temporal baseline (1981–2024). Extreme heat events, though historically rare, have clustered in recent years, signalling emerging instability. Rainfall patterns in Thembelihle show high interannual variability with no significant long-term decline, though spring rainfall exhibits a borderline decreasing trend. Johannesburg’s rainfall metrics highlight intensifying extremes: longer dry spells (+1 day/year) and higher maximum daily rainfall (+0.30 mm/year). Drought analysis identifies overlapping severe years (1984, 1999, 2003), underscoring regional susceptibility, while Thembelihle’s higher variability points to localized vulnerability. Spatial analysis confirms rainfall gradients, with wetter conditions in the northeast and drier conditions in the south, alongside localized temperature hotspots. These findings demonstrate a dual climate challenge: accelerating heat stress and increasingly variable rainfall. Informal settlements such as Thembelihle are disproportionately exposed, requiring both water resource coordination and localized adaptation strategies.

title: Shrinking Non-CO2 Emission Inequality in China’s Municipal Wastewater Treatment
summary: Integrating emission equity into climate mitigation is essential for sustainable development but remains poorly understood in the wastewater-treatment sector. Here, we develop a long-term, high-resolution emission inventory covering 8703 mu
content: Integrating emission equity into climate mitigation is essential for sustainable development but remains poorly understood in the wastewater-treatment sector. Here, we develop a long-term, high-resolution emission inventory covering 8703 municipal wastewater treatment plants across China from 2001 to 2020 to assess methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) emission trends and their spatial inequality. National emissions increased substantially, although growth rates slowed after 2010 for CH4 and 2015 for N2O. Discrepancies with IPCC-derived estimates highlight the limitations of population-based approaches in capturing emission trends. Economic development dominated emission growth, with wastewater treatment intensity (wastewater treated per unit of GDP) contributing positively, even under scenarios that account for potential changes in emission factors associated with technological and management improvements. Significant emission inequality persisted, with economically developed cities (9% of the population) contributing 16% and 15% of CH4 and N2O emissions in 2020, whereas the least developed group (45% of the population) accounted for 28% and 32%, respectively. Nonetheless, this disparity narrowed over time with Gini coefficients falling from 0.54 to 0.26 for CH4 and from 0.51 to 0.22 for N2O. These findings support geographically differentiated mitigation strategies that prioritize high-emitting areas to promote effective and equitable climate mitigation.

title: Climate-driven habitat suitability and future distribution dynamics of the shisham defoliator (Plecoptera reflexa) in Uttarakhand, India using MaxEnt and CMIP6 projections
summary: Climate change is altering the distribution and ecological dynamics of forest insect pests, necessitating reliable tools for predicting future habitat suitability. This study assessed the current and future potential distribution of the shi
content: Climate change is altering the distribution and ecological dynamics of forest insect pests, necessitating reliable tools for predicting future habitat suitability. This study assessed the current and future potential distribution of the shisham defoliator, Plecoptera reflexa , in Uttarakhand, India, using the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model coupled with CMIP6 climate projections from the MIROC6 General Circulation Model. A total of 197 occurrence records collected during field surveys (2023–2025) were compiled, of which 117 spatially filtered records were used for model development. Nineteen bioclimatic variables were initially evaluated, and highly correlated predictors were excluded prior to modelling. The MaxEnt model showed excellent predictive performance (AUC = 0.996). Jackknife analysis identified precipitation of the warmest quarter (bio18), precipitation seasonality (bio15), minimum temperature of the coldest month (bio6), and isothermality (bio3) as the principal environmental drivers governing habitat suitability. Response curves indicated that P. reflexa is associated with moderate thermal stability and intermediate precipitation regimes. Under the current climate, highly suitable habitats were concentrated primarily in the southwestern and central parts of Uttarakhand. Future projections under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5 scenarios indicated progressive fragmentation of highly suitable habitats, accompanied by expansion of low-suitability areas and a consistent decline in moderately suitable habitats, particularly under higher emission pathways. These findings provide a climate-based framework for anticipating future distribution shifts and support targeted monitoring, early-warning surveillance, and climate-resilient management strategies for the sustainable protection of shisham forests.

title: Mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride fibers: a comparative study
summary: We present a comparative study of mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride optical fibers driven by a low-noise, Kerr-lens mode-locked Cr:​ZnS laser oscillator delivering ultrashort 35-fs pulses centered at 2300 nm. By investigati
content: We present a comparative study of mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride optical fibers driven by a low-noise, Kerr-lens mode-locked Cr:​ZnS laser oscillator delivering ultrashort 35-fs pulses centered at 2300 nm. By investigating three commercial fluoride fibers with varying core geometries, numerical apertures, and chromatic dispersion profiles, we characterize how the magnitude of anomalous dispersion affects the dynamics of spectral broadening and the homogeneity of the supercontinuum. In fibers exhibiting high and steep anomalous dispersion, temporal pulse stretching triggers higher-order soliton fission, resulting in deeply modulated and fragmented spectra. However, combining a flat, near-zero anomalous dispersion profile with tighter spatial mode confinement supports efficient soliton dynamics and prevents early pulse walk-off. This results in the generation of a smooth, octave-spanning supercontinuum. Our experimental results, supported by numerical simulations based on the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation, demonstrate an ultrabroadband mid-infrared spectrum spanning 1600 nm to 5350 nm, with an average output power of 140 mW. These results highlight low-dispersion fluoride fibers pumped by femtosecond solid-state oscillators as a compact, robust platform for high-brightness, broadband mid-infrared light sources well-suited for molecular spectroscopy and trace-gas sensing.

title: Ensemble Land Surface Temperature (LST) predictions with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and probabilistic models: a case study of Greater Accra region, Ghana
summary: Predicting land surface temperature in an area is crucial as it equips stakeholders and governmental organizations with enhanced insights into the temperature dynamics, facilitating informed decision- making and planning. The primary aim of
content: Predicting land surface temperature in an area is crucial as it equips stakeholders and governmental organizations with enhanced insights into the temperature dynamics, facilitating informed decision- making and planning. The primary aim of this study is to predict the daily land surface temperature of the Greater Accra region. This research first employed the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to decompose temperature data into signals representing lower and higher frequencies. Six distinct Backpropagation Artificial Neural Network machine-learning techniques were employed: Bayesian Regularization, Levenberg-Marquardt, Scaled Conjugate Gradient, Resilient algorithm, Fletcher-Reeves Conjugate Gradient, and Polak-Ribiere Conjugate Gradient. Additionally, two unsupervised machine learning methodologies, specifically the Radial Basis Function and Generalized Regression, with three conventional techniques, Autocorrelation Integrated Moving Average, Multiple Linear Regression, and Total Least Squares, were employed. The decomposed data were utilized in the training of these algorithms. The collection comprises 58 years of temporal temperature data, spanning from 1960 to 2018, obtained from the Ghana Meteorological Agency. The research examines four discrete statistical metrics to evaluate the efficacy of these algorithms. The findings indicated that the performance measures of all algorithms are promising. Upon analysis of all the methods, it was observed that the ARIMA had subpar performance for the MSE and RMSE measures. The GRANN algorithm was identified as the most effective. All approaches described in this study may be applied globally to precisely predict daily temperature.

title: GWAS of winter hardiness and flowering time in autumn- versus spring-sown oats across five european sites: breeding implications
summary: KEY MESSAGE: Autumn sowing of spring oat in Central Europe improves yield and agronomic performance with genomic analyses highlighting VRN1- and VRN3-linked loci as breeding targets for winter resilience. Milder winters in Central Europe en
content: KEY MESSAGE: Autumn sowing of spring oat in Central Europe improves yield and agronomic performance with genomic analyses highlighting VRN1- and VRN3-linked loci as breeding targets for winter resilience. Milder winters in Central Europe enable autumn sowing of spring oats, but risks and benefits still largely remain unclear. To address this knowledge gap, a panel of 250 spring oat lines was seeded in autumn and spring across five European sites over two seasons using unreplicated augmented designs with ten replicated controls. Winterkill varied by site, occurring in four experiments (including complete loss in one site-year), primarily due to insufficient snow cover and frost durations of more than four days between - 5 and - 8 °C. Canopy damage (CAN, scored with Canopeo app) had a heritability estimate of 0.55. Across all experiments, autumn sowing increased grain yield by 5-79% compared to spring sowing, driven by advanced development, lower mildew infection and extended tillering, though associated with higher lodging. GWAS (GAPIT3; 14,614 SNPs) identified 17 robust MTAs for winter hardiness, clustering on chromosomes 2D (novel), 4A and 4D (overlapping with VRN1), 6D, and 7D (near VRN3). Genomic prediction accuracy for CAN was 0.66. Based on our observations, we suggest that breeding should prioritize region-specific trials, winter oat crosses, and genomic selection to mitigate mycotoxin/lodging risks while exploiting yield gains in autumn sown oat.

title: La ventaja climática de Colombia está medida en hectáreas, calendarios y dólares, pero no se cobra: de 42,9 millones de hectáreas de frontera agrícola, solo cerca de 5,5 millones están en uso
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: La ventaja climática colombiana —disponibilidad y variabilidad climática como activo productivo— está documentada con evidencia nacional en tres registros medibles, y en los tres aparece subcobrada. En tierra: la frontera agrícola oficial a
content: La ventaja climática colombiana —disponibilidad y variabilidad climática como activo productivo— está documentada con evidencia nacional en tres registros medibles, y en los tres aparece subcobrada. En tierra: la frontera agrícola oficial actualizada por la UPRA (2024) suma 42.944.940 hectáreas bajo la Resolución 261 de 2018, de las cuales 22.803.490 son condicionadas y 20.141.450 no condicionadas, y las zonificaciones de aptitud de la misma entidad (UPRA, 2025) identifican 23,3 millones de hectáreas aptas para yuca (54,1 % de la frontera), 14,4 millones para plátano (33,6 %) y 7,2 millones para fríjol (16,9 %), con más de 30 millones de hectáreas analizadas para apicultura. En calendario: el régimen bimodal de lluvias de la zona central cafetera sostiene dos cosechas de café al año con recolección durante los doce meses en cinco de las seis localidades estudiadas por Cenicafé (Alvarado-Alvarado & Moreno-Ruiz, 1999), con menos del 5 % de la producción en los meses bajos y concentraciones del segundo semestre que varían entre el 65 % y el 95 % según la localidad. En mercado: las exportaciones colombianas de frutas alcanzaron USD 2.178 millones en 2025, con crecimiento del 20,4 % y una tasa anual compuesta del 11,7 % en cinco años, sobre una producción nacional de frutas frescas superior a 13,6 millones de toneladas (ProColombia, s. f.). Sin embargo, según la misma entidad promotora, de los 42,9 millones de hectáreas de frontera agrícola solo cerca de 5,5 millones están en uso, alrededor del 13 %, y ninguna fuente leída cuantifica el premio de precio de vender en contraestación: la ventaja existe en los mapas y en los calendarios, pero su conversión en ingreso por hectárea sigue sin medirse.

title: Accounting for income inequality supports stronger climate policy
summary: Optimal climate policy depends on how burdens of climate damage and emissions abatement are distributed across incomes, yet integrated assessment models typically do not consider these distributional factors. We examine how the distribution
content: Optimal climate policy depends on how burdens of climate damage and emissions abatement are distributed across incomes, yet integrated assessment models typically do not consider these distributional factors. We examine how the distribution of vulnerability to climate damage across incomes and the sharing of abatement costs affect the equity-adjusted social cost of carbon and climate outcomes. We introduce a Lorenz curve representing income distribution into a welfare-maximizing integrated assessment model that optimizes abatement and savings jointly. With a flat tax and uniform damage vulnerability, the social cost of carbon in 2030 is $43/tCO2 and year 2100 temperatures exceed 3 ◦C. When climate damage falls disproportionately on people with low incomes and abatement is financed by a highly progressive tax, the social cost of carbon increases to $207/tCO2 and warming stays below 2 ◦C. Sound climate policy depends on appropriate consideration of who suffers climate damage and who pays for emissions abatement.

title: Urban greening, planning instruments and heat risk reduction in Lagos, Nigeria
summary: Urban heat is an intensifying challenge in rapidly growing cities across sub-Saharan Africa, yet the role of planning instruments in managing heat risk remains poorly understood. This study examines the relationship between urban greening,
content: Urban heat is an intensifying challenge in rapidly growing cities across sub-Saharan Africa, yet the role of planning instruments in managing heat risk remains poorly understood. This study examines the relationship between urban greening, planning instruments, and heat risk reduction in the Lagos Metropolitan Area using a mixed-methods approach, combining geospatial analysis of Landsat imagery (2002, 2013, 2024) with semi-structured interviews with nine planning professionals. Land surface temperature (LST), vegetation cover (NDVI), and population density were integrated via the Analytical Hierarchy Process into a composite Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (UHVI). Mean LST rose progressively across the study period, from 25.79 °C in 2002 to 28.11 °C in 2024, with warming accelerating notably after 2013, while dense vegetation cover declined steadily (NDVI High/Very High classes fell from approximately 44% to 18%) and population density continued to rise throughout. Regression analysis indicated a consistent inverse NDVI- LST association across all three years (R² ranging from 0.68 to 0.75), though the cooling effect of vegetation weakened over time, with the regression slope flattening from around − 0.054 in 2002 to − 0.038 by 2024. The composite UHVI showed a corresponding shift toward higher vulnerability, with the High and Very High risk classes together expanding from roughly a fifth to nearly half of the study area over the same period. Qualitative analysis identified five interrelated governance themes constraining green infrastructure integration into planning practice, namely the policy-to-practice gap, institutional and political constraints, non-compliance, economic and urbanisation pressures, and the decline and mismanagement of existing infrastructure, consistent with an enforcement gap operating alongside existing policy provisions. The study advances a distributed residential greening model that mobilises household- and community-level vegetation as a feasible complement to large-scale green infrastructure, with direct implications for planning reform in Lagos State and other similar contexts.

title: Climate Diplomacy: How Kazakhstan and the Gulf States Shape Sustainable Energy Policies
summary: Purpose: To analyze the role of sustainable energy policies in the climate policies with the view of comparing Kazakhstan and GCC member states using SDG performance trend. Design/Methodology/Approach: This study is quantitative longitudina
content: Purpose: To analyze the role of sustainable energy policies in the climate policies with the view of comparing Kazakhstan and GCC member states using SDG performance trend. Design/Methodology/Approach: This study is quantitative longitudinal in design, with the use of Sustainable Development Report (SDR) indicators of SDG 7 and SDG 13 and SDG Index. Evaluation of progress and interrelationships is done through trend analysis, descriptive statistics and correlation analysis. Findings: The performance of SDG is increasing in all countries with the UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia leading. Investment in renewables and infrastructure helps GCC states to be better than Kazakhstan in SDG 7, whereas previous mitigation policies allow Kazakhstan to lead SDG 13. The Gulf has the lowest climate action. Original/Value of the Paper: Gives empirical data on the topic of sustainable energy changes and inter-regional collaboration in the era of the changing geopolitics. Research Limitations/Implications: Findings are based on SDR indicators and are not wholly reflective of institutional and political forces influencing implementation of policies. Keywords: Kazakhstan; GCC; SDG 7; SDG 13; Sustainable Energy; Climate Diplomacy Citation: Ahmad, A. S. O., Kurmangali, A., Twaissi, S. and Abusham, E. E. A. A. (2026): Climate Diplomacy: How Kazakhstan and the Gulf States Shape Sustainable Energy Policies. In Ahmed, A. (Ed.): World Sustainable Development Outlook 2026, Vol. 22, pp. 329-344. WASD: London, United Kingdom.

title: Yeast Products: Application Effects and Species-Specific Host Physiological Responses in Animal Production
summary: Yeasts are unicellular eukaryotic fungi whose cell walls are rich in β-glucan and mannan, and whose intracellular contents are abundant in proteins, nucleotides, and enzymes. Yeast products, including inactivated or autolyzed whole-cell yea
content: Yeasts are unicellular eukaryotic fungi whose cell walls are rich in β-glucan and mannan, and whose intracellular contents are abundant in proteins, nucleotides, and enzymes. Yeast products, including inactivated or autolyzed whole-cell yeasts and yeast cell-wall extracts, elicit a spectrum of physiological effects, such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, gut microbiota-regulating, and growth-promoting activities, and have therefore been widely adopted as feed ingredients in animal production. In recent years, accumulating evidence has revealed their broader potential applications; however, the molecular signalling pathways underlying many of these effects remain poorly defined, and evidence in target animals is still largely phenotypic. This narrative review synthesizes studies published since 2021, focusing on the functional roles of yeast products and the mechanisms proposed so far across diverse animal-production systems. It critically assesses current mechanistic evidence, clarifies its limitations, identifies key knowledge gaps, and provides a theoretical foundation for the rational application of yeast products while informing future research and product development.

title: Conservation status, governance challenges and the path to integrated landscape management of Peat Swamp Forests in Peninsular Malaysia
summary: Peat Swamp Forests (PSF) were once among Malaysia’s most extensive wetland ecosystems, and remain critically important for biodiversity conservation, carbon storage, hydrological processes, and sustainable resource use. Historically, they o
content: Peat Swamp Forests (PSF) were once among Malaysia’s most extensive wetland ecosystems, and remain critically important for biodiversity conservation, carbon storage, hydrological processes, and sustainable resource use. Historically, they occupied about 2.56 million ha, equivalent to nearly 8% of Malaysia’s land area and roughly 720,000 ha or 5.45% of the land area in Peninsular Malaysia. The PSF areas in Peninsular Malaysia declined by 66% from an estimated 670,000 ha in 1981 to 226,000 ha in 2010. Between 2010 to 2026, the PSF area declined further 5% to an estimated 192,788 ha in 2026. PSFs are habitat to a large number of rare, threatened, and endangered (RTE) species, with many specially adapted to its unique acidic wetland environment. Their specialised plant communities support a wide range of animal species, including 140 species of fish, with more than 60 blackwater species restricted to this habitat in Peninsular Malaysia. In the past half-century, PSFs have been logged, cleared, drained, burnt, and developed for other commercial uses, especially oil palm plantations. PSF areas have been totally lost or reduced to less than 1% in Kelantan, Perak and Negeri Sembilan, while only 3.5% remain in Johor; extensive PSFs only persist in Selangor and Pahang with an estimated total area of 170,000 ha. While PSF areas have declined in all states between 2010 to 2026, the significant increase in Selangor reflects the success of proactive conservation measures leading to reduced fires and enhanced forest recovery. Successful conservation measures developed for PSFs in Selangor are now being introduced in Pahang and Johor. The montane peatland forest of Pahang have also been recently documented. This chapter highlights governance and resourcing issues, as well as key challenges, opportunities, and policy recommendations to further enhance the conservation of PSFs in Peninsular Malaysia.

title: Effects of zinc-enriched and acid-modified biochar on soil physicochemical properties and wheat growth in calcareous soils
summary: In calcareous soils, where zinc (Zn) fixation restricts crop productivity, modified biochars have been proposed as promising carriers for micronutrient management. This study aimed to characterize the Zn adsorption–desorption behavior of ol
content: In calcareous soils, where zinc (Zn) fixation restricts crop productivity, modified biochars have been proposed as promising carriers for micronutrient management. This study aimed to characterize the Zn adsorption–desorption behavior of olive pruning waste-derived biochar (BC) produced at 400 °C and modified with 1 mol L -1 HNO 3 (NA), H 3 PO 4 (PA), and H 2 SO 4 (SA), and to evaluate the agronomic performance of Zn-enriched biochars under wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) cultivation. Adsorption experiments (0–400 mg L -1 Zn) showed that Zn retention depended strongly on modification type. The original BC followed an H-type isotherm and removed 91% of the added Zn at an initial concentration of 100 mg L -1 , whereas the acid-modified materials showed S-type behaviour and removed only 1-10%, reflecting the strongly acidic post-contact solution conditions (pH 1.26–2.03) maintained by residual acid. Desorption in 0.01 M CaCl 2 released 1.6-17.8% of the Zn retained by the original BC but a considerably larger proportion of that retained by the acid-modified materials. In the greenhouse pot experiment, biochar was applied at 1% (w/w) and prepared at nominal target Zn loadings of 30, 300, and 1000 mg kg -1 Zn in a completely randomized design using the Bayraktar 2000 bread wheat cultivar. Wheat dry weight increased from 1.37 g pot -1 in the control to 4.93 g pot -1 under PA+BC+Zn 300 . Plant elemental composition was significantly affected by all treatments, with the highest N concentrations in NA+BC+Zn 300 and NA+BC+Zn 1000 (up to 37.1 g kg -1 ), the highest P in PA+BC+Zn 1000 (7.53 g kg -1 ), and the highest Zn in NA+BC+Zn 1000 (73.0 mg kg -1 ). In soil, the highest available P 2 O 5 was observed in the PA+BC+Zn 1000 treatment (640.5 kg ha -1 ), biochar treatments generally increased organic matter, and Zn enrichment increased soil Zn concentrations by 1.38 mg kg -1 compared with the control. Correlation analysis showed that wheat dry weight was strongly associated with plant N (r ≈ 0.90) and soil organic matter (r ≈ 0.82), whereas multivariate analyses (PCA and hierarchical clustering) demonstrated that acid-modified biochar+Zn treatments clustered along a favorable nutrient–biomass axis. Overall, acid modification altered Zn retention–release behavior and influenced short-term wheat vegetative growth and nutrient status under calcareous soil conditions. The responses varied according to acid modification type and Zn enrichment level, with PA+BC+Zn 300 producing the highest wheat dry biomass and NA-modified treatments generally showing high plant N and Zn concentrations.

title: Accumulation by legalization: the accelerated transformation of California’s drug war agrarianism
summary: Legalization has profoundly altered the agrarian system of California’s (once) most valuable cash crop: cannabis. For decades, illicit cannabis reaped a ‘prohibition premium’ that kept prices and profits high. Small-scale growers formed an
content: Legalization has profoundly altered the agrarian system of California’s (once) most valuable cash crop: cannabis. For decades, illicit cannabis reaped a ‘prohibition premium’ that kept prices and profits high. Small-scale growers formed an illegalized peasantry concentrated in remote areas of the state, shielded from detection by customary local norms. Legalization eliminated that premium, eviscerated local norms and glutted the market. Overproduction appears set to accomplish what prohibition never did: eradicate the vast majority of cannabis cultivators. In this paper, told through four indicative farmer narratives, we conceptualize a plural model of ‘drug war agrarianism’ to adequately assess the rapid transformations, or ‘accelerated agrarian change,’ brought about by legalization. While legality augurs market rationalization – what we term ‘accumulation by legalization’ – illegal farming and markets do not disappear, but rather, rearticulate after legalization. They persist as livelihood strategies among marginalized populations and become critical supports for an unstable, legally uneven market. Policy responses that merely add regulatory costs and enforcement intensity without reimagining how markets work and for whom will fall short of achieving justice in the wake of the drug war.

title: Mobility-driven changes in urban air quality during the COVID-19 lockdown: Evidence from the Baridhara monitoring station, Dhaka, Bangladesh
summary: The COVID-19 lockdown created a natural experiment for examining how large changes in human activity coincided with urban air-quality change. This study evaluated daily Air Quality Index (AQI) and PM2.5 measured at the U.S. Embassy Baridhar
content: The COVID-19 lockdown created a natural experiment for examining how large changes in human activity coincided with urban air-quality change. This study evaluated daily Air Quality Index (AQI) and PM2.5 measured at the U.S. Embassy Baridhara monitoring station in northern Dhaka, Bangladesh, using a 2016–2022 air-quality record, Bangladesh-level Google Community Mobility Reports, and NASA POWER meteorological variables. Because the mobility series were available only at national scale, they were treated as contextual proxies for broad activity change rather than as direct measurements of mobility within Dhaka. Four complementary approaches were applied: a SARIMAX interrupted time-series model, partial wavelet coherence, artificial-neural-network weather normalization selected from eight machine-learning models by five-fold time-series cross-validation, and eight mobility-prediction models interpreted with SHAP. The interrupted time series identified a large immediate decline at lockdown onset (AQI −90.3 units; PM2.5 −110.0 µg m − 3; p < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.80 and 0.87). After meteorological adjustment, mobility–pollution coherence remained moderate, with the strongest bands at 8–16 days for AQI and 2–4 days for PM2.5. A direct correlation analysis, performed to complement the normalization, showed that the meteorology–pollution relationships of the lockdown months were indistinguishable in sign and magnitude from those of the pre-pandemic and post-lockdown March–June windows. Random Forest best predicted weather-normalized AQI (R2 = 0.60), while XGBoost best predicted weather-normalized PM2.5 (R2 = 0.66); confidence intervals overlapped among leading ensembles. SHAP indicated that residential, grocery and pharmacy, workplace, and transit mobility were the most influential predictors in the fitted models. The findings show a temporary, weather-independent association between broad mobility change and air quality at one monitoring site, but they do not establish a city-wide or causal effect. The results support transport-demand and emissions-management strategies that can deliver local air-quality benefits while complementing climate-mitigation goals.

title: Modeling Aerobic-Anaerobic Microbial Electrolysis Cells for Multi-step Methane Conversion
summary: The bioconversion of methane by anaerobic methanotrophs has a higher carbon and energy efficiency compared to aerobic processes, suggesting significant potential for producing value-added chemicals and reducing green-house-gas emissions. Ho
content: The bioconversion of methane by anaerobic methanotrophs has a higher carbon and energy efficiency compared to aerobic processes, suggesting significant potential for producing value-added chemicals and reducing green-house-gas emissions. However, their practical use still faces many challenges regarding their culturing, genetic manipulation, and integration into multi-species consortia. Here we mathematically model a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) to study the division of labor inside an anode-attached vertically stratified biofilm, where genetically modified Methanosarcina acetivorans and Escherichia coli perform the anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) to acetate followed by the aerobic conversion to 2,3-butanediol, respectively. We find that such a design is theoretically feasible, and we identify minimum biological improvements and operational conditions so that the aerobic layer effectively acts as oxygen-consuming living membrane protecting the anaerobic layer. Considering current biotechnological parameters points to a significant yet feasible need for further microbial engineering to increase the AOM rate. A comparison to a more traditional two-stage reactor at equivalent biomass reveals advantages and drawbacks of both designs, e.g., tradeoffs between peak product yield, reactor volume, and operational complexity. These results inform AOM driven microbial upgrading via aerobic-anaerobic stratified biofilms as well as value-added production via cooperative consortia in general.

title: Outcomes of a multi-objective diet optimization model as a basis for food-based dietary guidelines
summary: Background: While nutrient adequacy has been at the core of food-based dietary guidelines (FBDG) for Germany since their beginning, aspects of health-promoting and more sustainable diets have not yet been integrated into their quantitative
content: Background: While nutrient adequacy has been at the core of food-based dietary guidelines (FBDG) for Germany since their beginning, aspects of health-promoting and more sustainable diets have not yet been integrated into their quantitative derivation. Objective: To consider multiple aspects relevant to FBDGs simultaneously via a multi-objective diet optimization model and to conceptualize an approach to transfer the outcomes into a basis for FBDGs, i.e. food guide and messages, on the example of adults in Germany. Methods: The optimization model included FoodEx2 food codes as decision variables (n = 593, level 4), constraints on nutrient intake recommendations, acceptability, and agronomic dependencies, and a multi-objective function that simultaneously minimized diet-related disease burden (disability-adjusted life years, DALYs), environmental impact (greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) and land use), and deviation from the observed diet. Ten model variants were evaluated using five different weighting schemes for the components of the objective function and two scenarios. For the transfer, optimization results were first further aggregated, then transferred into circular charts for the food guide and into servings for the FBDG messages. Results: Meeting all constraints, the optimized diets reduced DALYs by 39-77 %, GHGE by 40-48 % and land use by 44-57 %. Compared with the observed diet, optimized diets were characterized by a higher share of plant-based foods in the total quantity of foods (66-70 % vs. 55 %), energy contribution (77-79 % vs. 58 %), and protein contribution (63-68 % vs. 40 %). The optimized food group quantities (coefficient of variation ranging from 0 to 1.0), the circular charts, and the servings showed high similarity across the ten model variants. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate that diet optimization outcomes can serve as a basis for health-promoting and environmentally more sustainable FBDGs. The model's flexibility allows future improvements in data quality and availability to be incorporated.

title: Sensitivity of early vegetative stage rice to reduced rates of trifludimoxazin + saflufenacil
summary: Trifludimoxazin + saflufenacil is a premixed herbicide that inhibits protoporphyrinogen oxidase with both preemergence and postemergence activity for preplant burndown purposes ahead of planting corn, grain sorghum, soybean, and wheat. Beca
content: Trifludimoxazin + saflufenacil is a premixed herbicide that inhibits protoporphyrinogen oxidase with both preemergence and postemergence activity for preplant burndown purposes ahead of planting corn, grain sorghum, soybean, and wheat. Because early season rice growth often occurs simultaneously with preplant burndown in later-planted soybean and grain sorghum, the odds of negative effects from off-target herbicide movement to the crop increase. Field studies in 2024 and 2025 carried out at four different sites aimed to evaluate the effect of reduced rates of trifludimoxazin + saflufenacil (12.5% to 0.4% of the lowest proposed labeled application rate of 38.3 g ai ha −1 ) applied to 1-leaf or 3-leaf rice. Visibly estimated injury 1 wk after treatment (WAT) for the 1- and 3-leaf growth stages averaged 23% to 5%, while at 2 WAT injury ranged from 5% to 2% after the herbicide was applied early and 15% to 2% when it was applied at the 3-leaf stage. Trifludimoxazin + saflufenacil at applied rates had no negative season-long impact, as early-season visibly estimated injury observed did not manifest in a reduction in rice height at 2 WAT or rough rice yield in comparison to no herbicide application. Off-target movement of trifludimoxazin + saflufenacil directly adjacent to rice in early vegetative stages of growth should be avoided or drift reduction measures taken because visibly estimated injury will occur. When off-target movement does occur and plants are exposed to reduced rates/spray droplet concentrations evaluated here, the affected rice should be expected to fully recover with no negative effect on growth and yield, assuming adequate growing conditions and agronomic/pest management are provided.
