title: Stochastic Collaborative Supply Chain Optimization With Fair Hierarchical Gain-Sharing
source: Journal of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering
summary: Horizontal supply chain collaboration (HSCC) offers substantial cost savings and carbon footprint reductions, yet commercial adoption remains hindered by non-scalable gain-sharing mechanisms and operational disruption risks. This study pres
content: Horizontal supply chain collaboration (HSCC) offers substantial cost savings and carbon footprint reductions, yet commercial adoption remains hindered by non-scalable gain-sharing mechanisms and operational disruption risks. This study presents a scalable two-stage hierarchical framework for post-Pareto selection, integrating a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear program (MILP, Level 1) with an Equal Profit Method linear program (EPML, Level 2) to optimize multi-objective routing and equitable profit allocation across multi-partner logistics networks. Evaluated on a medium-scale benchmark network (15 partners, 8 demand nodes, and 50 stochastic scenarios), the framework achieves an alliance-wide cost reduction of 18.42% and a carbon reduction of 14.10% relative to non-cooperative baselines. At Level 2, the EPML engine executes in 0.32 s for 15 partners and 1.87 s for 30 partners, overcoming the exponential computational bottlenecks of traditional cooperative game theory methods while theoretically guaranteeing expected individual rationality $\left(E\left[\pi_i\right] \geq \pi_i^0\right)$, where $E\left[\pi_i\right]$ denotes partner $i$'s expected collaborative profit and $\pi_i^0$ denotes that partner's standalone baseline profit—provided that the selected physical solution satisfies the net-synergy feasibility condition $(\sum_{i \in I} E\left[\pi_i\right] \geq \sum_{i \in I} \pi_i^0)$, where $I$ is the set of alliance partners. The framework also achieves empirically verified core stability, with $e_{\max} \leq 0$, where $e_{\max}$ denotes the maximum excess across the tested subcoalition. Sensitivity analysis demonstrates robust customer fulfillment (99.59% service level) under high shortfall penalties $\left(p_j^{\text {pen}} \geq 2.5 \times p_j^{\text {sell}}\right)$ and a marginal abatement cost (MAC) of \$2,318.68 per metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO$_2$e) at executive compromise configurations. To facilitate industry adoption, we translate these algorithmic outputs into a practical 4-step managerial decision protocol balancing ex-ante contractual rules, ex-post financial settlements, and alliance-level greenhouse gas (GHG) reporting boundaries. The framework effectively resolves the trade-off between allocation fairness and computational scalability in stochastic environments, providing supply chain decision-makers with a practical, mathematically rigorous, and computationally efficient post-Pareto decision-support tool to establish stable, equitable, and resilient horizontal logistics coalitions.

title: Land use and environmental drivers of nutrients and primary production in 49 inland and coastal saline lakes of semi-arid Türkiye
summary: Saline lakes are increasingly threatened by climate and anthropogenic pressures, yet comparative assessments of nutrients and primary production in inland and coastal saline lakes remain scarce. We assessed 49 saline lakes across semi-arid
content: Saline lakes are increasingly threatened by climate and anthropogenic pressures, yet comparative assessments of nutrients and primary production in inland and coastal saline lakes remain scarce. We assessed 49 saline lakes across semi-arid Türkiye (21 inland, 28 coastal) to identify the main environmental and anthropogenic drivers of physicochemical variables, including nutrients, primary production, and macrophyte percent volume infested (PVI%). Inland lakes exhibited significantly higher nutrient concentrations, particularly total phosphorus (TP) and total nitrogen (TN), with mean values several-fold higher than those in coastal lakes (Wilcoxon test, P <0.001). Inland lakes also tended to have sparse submerged vegetation, likely reflecting more intensive agriculture-dominated catchments, higher evaporative potential and salinization, and lack of hydrological outflow. In contrast, coastal lakes maintained lower nutrient concentrations and higher macrophyte PVI%, associated with more heterogeneous land cover and periodic marine connectivity, the latter likely modulating salinity effects and diluting nutrients. Random forest analyses identified land use as the dominant driver of water nutrient concentrations, followed by meteorological variables, and salinity, while water clarity was mainly explained by in-lake nutrient concentrations (TP, TN, and silicate), temperature, and salinity. Across our inland-lake samples, submerged macrophytes were observed only up to a salinity of 3.5 g/L and absent at salinities ≥22.4 g/L (no inland lakes had salinities in between). In coastal lakes, macrophytes persisted up to 43.5 g/L ( Ruppia cirrhosa (Petagna) Grande), reflecting this species’ strong osmoregulatory capacity compared to inland taxa. Our findings underline the divergent ecological trajectories of inland and coastal saline lakes and highlight the need for differentiated management. Conservation strategies should focus on reducing catchment nutrient inputs and water use in inland lakes, as well as on maintaining natural hydrological connectivity and catchment integrity in coastal lakes.

title: Behavioural factors influencing drip irrigation adoption among marginal mango farmers: an extended behavioural Reasoning framework
summary: Drip irrigation improves water-use efficiency and supports sustainable mango production, yet adoption among marginal farmers remains limited. This study examined behavioural factors influencing adoption among marginal mango farmers in the i
content: Drip irrigation improves water-use efficiency and supports sustainable mango production, yet adoption among marginal farmers remains limited. This study examined behavioural factors influencing adoption among marginal mango farmers in the integrated Vellore region of Tamil Nadu, India, using Behavioural Reasoning Theory (BRT). Data from 331 farmers were collected through structured questionnaires and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Perceived usefulness, social influence, government subsidy, perceived price, and perceived risk were examined as determinants of attitude, which influenced adoption intention. Perceived usefulness (β = 0.125, p = 0.015), social influence (β = 0.165, p = 0.001), and government subsidy (β = 0.140, p = 0.006) positively influenced attitude, whereas perceived price (β = −0.115, p = 0.035) and perceived risk (β = −0.267, p < 0.001) negatively influenced it. Perceived risk had the strongest effect. Attitude positively influenced adoption intention (β = 0.294, p < 0.001). The model explained 14.9% of variance in attitude (R² = 0.149) and 8.6% in adoption intention (R² = 0.086). Indirect effects through attitude were significant for usefulness, social influence, subsidy, and risk, but not price. Only 9.67% (32/331) used drip irrigation. Addressing technological risks alongside financial, institutional, and social factors is essential to encourage adoption.

title: Decision-making model on the evaluation of high-powered computing based on the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation and analytic hierarchy process method
source: Advances in Operation Research and Production Management
summary: High-performance computing (HPC) exerts complex, multi-constrained environmental impacts. This work integrates the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) to construct a decision-making model on the evaluat
content: High-performance computing (HPC) exerts complex, multi-constrained environmental impacts. This work integrates the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) to construct a decision-making model on the evaluation of high-powered computing. Nonlinear regression estimates the 2027 annual power consumption of the target HPC at 1.4×10 4 kWh. Six evaluation indices, namely water resource, electronic waste, land use, air quality, chemical usage and resource consumption indices, are established, followed by data collection, normalization and imputation. AHP ranking yields XD HPC > PKU HPC > THU HPC > SJTU HPC > CSU HPC > TC HPC. The more objective FCE further identifies PKU, THU and SJTU HPCs as environmentally favorable, whereas CSU and TC HPCs show adverse overall environmental effects. A logistic growth model is adopted to project HPC expansion, energy demand and energy mix scenarios toward 2030; energy demand gradually rises and saturates under HPC-scale and environmental constraints. Carbon emission abatement is quantified for higher renewable energy penetration, and sensitivity analysis examines how adjusted water resource indices alter overall scores. Upon implementing a proposed mitigation measure, ordinary and partial differential equations are incorporated to update the judgment matrix, re-derive indicator weights and re-run the AHP-FCE evaluation. Validated on five HPC cases, the integrated AHP-FCE framework supports HPC impact assessment. A recommendation is submitted to the advisory board to add detailed HPC environmental targets to the 2030 roadmap.

title: The Green Mandate: Turning Volatility into an Industrial Engine
summary: This chapter architectures the green mandate, reframing the climate crisis from an environmental ‘brake’ on development to the primary industrial engine of the Second Republic. It diagnoses the ‘institutional mismatch’ between India’s twent
content: This chapter architectures the green mandate, reframing the climate crisis from an environmental ‘brake’ on development to the primary industrial engine of the Second Republic. It diagnoses the ‘institutional mismatch’ between India’s twenty-first-century technological triumphs—including achieving 52.2 per cent non-fossil installed capacity by February 2026—and its legacy ‘analogue’ administrative software. This mismatch is quantified as a 4.2-trillion-dollar ‘Friction Tax’ that suppresses total factor productivity and national resilience. To resolve this, the chapter proposes a three-pillar blueprint: mitigation through market fusion, adaptation through hydrological realism, and a just transition through social solidarity. Central to this transition is the neural grid, governed by the Electricity Amendment Bill 2026, and the Indian Carbon Market, which acts as a sovereign shield against ‘carbon colonialism’. By leveraging the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development’s ‘AAA magic’ to unlock a 10.1-trillion-dollar green investment pipeline and creating 48 million green jobs, the chapter demonstrates how India secures its strategic energy sovereignty. Ultimately, the green mandate ensures that India’s ascent to a 30-trillion-dollar frontier by 2047 is not only high-velocity but also structurally unbreakable, establishing India as the definitive green superpower.

title: The Role of Automation and Digital Technologies in Improving Australian Freight Efficiency
summary: Australia moves large volumes of bulk commodities, containers and consumer goods over long distances with a road-dominated freight system, so small gains in cost, time and energy per tonne carried translate into large national benefits. The
content: Australia moves large volumes of bulk commodities, containers and consumer goods over long distances with a road-dominated freight system, so small gains in cost, time and energy per tonne carried translate into large national benefits. The question addressed here is whether, and under what conditions, automated and digitally enabled operations make Australian freight more efficient. Thirty refereed journal articles, each with a final publication year in the 2020–2025 window, form the evidence base; they were chosen by systematic integrative review and organised around a review of road freight and alternative modes in Australia and a study of artificial intelligence use cases in freight logistics. Seven of the articles examine Australian freight directly, and the others provide technical and international evidence on road, rail, terminal and last-mile operations. Each study was coded by technology family and by the efficiency dimension it addresses. The evidence indicates that automated and platooned trucks lower operating cost and energy use in modelled scenarios, that driverless heavy-haul rail and digitally monitored wagons support higher asset productivity, and that telematics, platforms and analytics improve coordination and visibility. Container terminal automation shows mixed productivity results, and digitalisation can reduce efficiency before it improves it. Gains depend on interoperability, investment cost, workforce acceptance and skills, and regulation, while Australian logistics providers report integration difficulties and partner costs as major barriers. A conceptual model is proposed that links technology layers to efficiency mechanisms and outcomes under these moderating conditions, together with propositions and implications for freight policy and practice in Australia.

title: PERUBAHAN IKLIM DAN KEMISKINAN: SUATU KAJIAN LITERATUR SISTEMATIK
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Perubahan iklim dan kemiskinan merupakan cabaran global yang saling berkait serta memberi kesan langsung terhadap kesejahteraan sosial dan pembangunan ekonomi masyarakat, khususnya dalam kalangan komuniti rentan. Walaupun pelbagai inisiatif
content: Perubahan iklim dan kemiskinan merupakan cabaran global yang saling berkait serta memberi kesan langsung terhadap kesejahteraan sosial dan pembangunan ekonomi masyarakat, khususnya dalam kalangan komuniti rentan. Walaupun pelbagai inisiatif dan dasar berkaitan perubahan iklim telah diperkenalkan, masih terdapat jurang dalam memahami bagaimana perubahan iklim mempengaruhi kemiskinan multidimensi serta bentuk adaptasi komuniti rentan dalam mengurangkan impak tersebut. Kajian ini bertujuan mengenal pasti bagaimana perubahan iklim mempengaruhi kemiskinan serta menganalisis strategi adaptasi komuniti rentan dalam menghadapi impak perubahan iklim. Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) berasaskan garis panduan PRISMA bagi memastikan proses pencarian, pemilihan dan analisis literatur dijalankan secara sistematik serta telus. Proses pencarian artikel dilakukan melalui dua pangkalan data utama iaitu Scopus dan Web of Science dengan memfokuskan artikel jurnal berbahasa Inggeris yang diterbitkan antara tahun 2021 hingga 2025. Sebanyak 54 penerbitan telah dikenal pasti dan memenuhi kriteria inklusi dan penilaian kualiti dipilih untuk dianalisis menggunakan pendekatan analisis tematik. Dapatan kajian menunjukkan bahawa perubahan iklim memberi kesan signifikan terhadap peningkatan kemiskinan multidimensi melalui gangguan terhadap sektor pertanian, keselamatan makanan, pendapatan isi rumah dan ketidaksamaan sosial. Kajian turut mendapati bahawa strategi adaptasi seperti kepelbagaian sumber pendapatan, penggunaan teknologi hijau, perlindungan sosial dan pengukuhan kapasiti komuniti dapat membantu mengurangkan risiko kemiskinan. Kesimpulannya, perubahan iklim dan kemiskinan merupakan isu yang memerlukan pendekatan dasar yang inklusif, mampan dan berdaya tahan. Kajian ini signifikan dalam menyediakan pemahaman yang lebih menyeluruh mengenai hubungan antara perubahan iklim dan kemiskinan serta membantu menyokong pembangunan dasar dan strategi adaptasi yang lebih efektif bagi komuniti rentan.

title: Motivational drivers of sustainable food choices among university students: the role of ecological footprint awareness and social media use integration
summary: Introduction Young adults are considered an important population in shaping future food systems, making it important to understand the motivations underlying sustainable food choices. This study aimed to investigate the motivational drivers
content: Introduction Young adults are considered an important population in shaping future food systems, making it important to understand the motivations underlying sustainable food choices. This study aimed to investigate the motivational drivers of sustainable food choices among university students and examine the roles of ecological footprint awareness and social media use integration. Methods This cross-sectional study included 280 university students aged 18-24 years in Istanbul, Türkiye. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using validated instruments, including the Sustainable Food Choice Questionnaire, the Awareness Scale for Reducing Ecological Footprint, and the Social Media Use Integration Scale. Descriptive statistics, group comparison tests, Pearson's correlation analyses, and path analysis using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) were performed. The effects of ecological footprint awareness and social media use integration on sustainable food choice motivation were examined while adjusting for body mass index. Results The “general sustainability” dimension demonstrated significantly higher mean scores than the “local, seasonal, and environmental welfare” dimension ( p < 0.001), indicating greater relative prominence within sustainable food choice motivation. The model explained 37% of the variance in sustainable food choice motivation ( R 2 = 0.37). Ecological footprint awareness was significantly associated with sustainable food choice motivation (β = 0.51, p < 0.001), whereas social media use integration showed no significant association (β = 0.02, p = 0.72). Discussion These findings suggest that environmental awareness and value-based motivations may be relevant factors associated with sustainable food choice motivation among young adults.

title: Evaluation of RGB sensor system for nondestructive detection of salinity stress in arugula
summary: Purpose Salinity stress silently erodes crop yields long before symptoms appear, making early, non-invasive detection essential for precision agriculture. Methods We evaluated a low-cost RGB sensor platform, with possible integartion of wir
content: Purpose Salinity stress silently erodes crop yields long before symptoms appear, making early, non-invasive detection essential for precision agriculture. Methods We evaluated a low-cost RGB sensor platform, with possible integartion of wireless networking, for real-time phenotyping of hydroponically grown arugula ( Eruca sativa (Mill.) Thell.) under 0, 40, and 80 mM NaCl. Results The sensor captured reflectance across seven spectral channels, generating leaf color metrics in situ. Principal component analysis, canonical correlation and clustering analysis confirmed tight coupling between RGB channels and ion ratios. Physiological, CIELAB, and optical datasets were fused using DIABLO, (Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker discovery using Latent components), achieving exceptional performance (mean error rate = 0.083 for component 1; zero for component 2) with only three features per block. High-stability variables (Na⁺, Na⁺/K⁺, Na⁺/Mg2⁺, b*, Chroma, White, Green, Red) tracked a clear dose-dependent stress gradient, linking ionic imbalance to possible pigment degradation and reflectance shifts. Particularly, sensor-derived indices detected spectral shifts preceding visible chlorosis, enabling early diagnosis. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that compact RGB-based sensing, empowered by integrative analytics, can deliver rapid, non-destructive, and biologically grounded stress diagnostics. The approach is readily deployable in controlled or open-field systems, providing a scalable pathway for precision stress monitoring before yield losses occur. Graphical abstract Optional description: Optical sensor module, connected to Arduino mega 2560 along with a Wi-Fi module, is capturing reflectance of arugula leaves under salinity treatments. The sensor setup is shown measuring leaves grown at 0, 40, and 80 mM NaCl in a deep water culture system. Physiological, CIELAB, and sensor-derived data were integrated and analyzed using multivariate approaches and the DIABLO framework to validate the sensor’s potential for early, non-destructive detection of salinity stress.,

title: GoNorth 2025 Cruise Report
summary: The fourth and final GoNorth expedition, conducted on the Norwegian Research Vessel Kronprins Haakon, took place over three weeks in the Arctic Ocean and concluded in Tromsø on December 17, 2025. The overarching objective was to advance und
content: The fourth and final GoNorth expedition, conducted on the Norwegian Research Vessel Kronprins Haakon, took place over three weeks in the Arctic Ocean and concluded in Tromsø on December 17, 2025. The overarching objective was to advance understanding of the formation, evolution, and dynamics of the Arctic Ocean through an integrated, multidisciplinary research approach. This strategy brought together expertise from atmospheric sciences, oceanography, geophysics, geology, and biology, enabling investigations that span from the atmosphere to the deep subsurface. By combining diverse methods and perspectives, the expedition aimed to enhance the knowledge of Arctic systems and their interactions under changing environmental conditions. The scientific program encompassed a wide range of activities: continuous atmospheric water vapor isotope measurements, sea-ice imaging and thickness mapping, water column profiling, bathymetric and geophysical surveys, in-situ seafloor imaging, and sampling of biological and geological material. Sediment coring provided archives for palaeoceanographic reconstructions, contaminant studies, and biodiversity assessments using environmental DNA. Microbial and geochemical analyses of pore fluids will target subsurface processes and biogeochemical cycles. Integrated and opportunistic sampling complemented planned operations, including thecollection of macrofauna from recovered rocks and sediments, ensuring maximum scientific return from each station. One of the primary goals of the expedition was to reach Ultima Thule, the hydrothermal vent discovered during the GoNorth 2023 expedition, for further sampling and exploration. However, unforeseen technical challenges, specifically an engine malfunction that reduced propulsion capacity, made it unviable to attempt to break through the heavy ice conditions required to reach this target. This limitation underscores the inherent unpredictability of research in remote polar environments and highlights the necessity of adaptability in expedition planning and execution. Despite these constraints, the team successfully redirected efforts to alternative sites, achieving most of its scientific objectives. Key accomplishments include acquisition of seismic profiles across the East Greenland Ridge and adjacent structures, complemented by gravity, magnetic, and bathymetric data to refine models of Arctic seafloor morphology and tectonic history. ROV-based operations enabled direct observation and sampling of seafloor features at the East Greenland Ridge (Boreas Basin), Mosby and Polarstern seamounts (Sophia Basin), providing critical geological and biological specimens for post-cruise analyses. Biological surveys documented species diversity in deep-sea ecosystems, including hydrothermal habitats, while ethnographic research examined the human dimensions of scientific work at sea, contributing to broader studies on emerging ocean industries. The expedition delivered a comprehensive dataset

title: Solar radiation glazing factors of two polymer-dispersed liquid crystal smart window films of different thicknesses
summary: Fenestration is a primary pathway for solar heat gain in buildings. Polymer-dispersed liquid crystal (PDLC) films can be switched between a translucent scattering state and a transparent clear state under an applied electric field. They rep
content: Fenestration is a primary pathway for solar heat gain in buildings. Polymer-dispersed liquid crystal (PDLC) films can be switched between a translucent scattering state and a transparent clear state under an applied electric field. They represent a promising strategy for dynamic solar control in buildings, i.e., as smart windows. Apart from material usage and manufacturing cost considerations, PDLC film thickness can also affect the solar radiation performance of PDLC smart windows. Integrating sphere measurements and solar radiation glazing factor calculations on selected commercial PDLC films, 0.487 mm and 0.549 mm thick, revealed that the thicker film was associated with an 8.2 percentage-point lower solar transmittance ( T sol , 59.6% against 67.8%) in the translucent state, compared to a 3.0 percentage-point difference (77.1% against 80.1%) in the transparent state. Of the translucent-state difference, 3.2 percentage points were additional reflectance and 5.0 percentage points were additional absorptance. The concentration of the difference in the translucent state indicates that it involves the scattering active layer. Ultraviolet (UV) transmittance remained below 1.7%, and the colour rendering factor (CRF) was at least 0.948 in all configurations, regardless of PDLC film thickness or switching state.

title: Understanding complex interactions between climate mitigation and adaptation measures: a methodological framework
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Meeting the linked goals of climate mitigation and adaptation requires a step change in the understanding of how our responses, often taken in isolation, interact dynamically, in real-world contexts. The actions taken by governments, sector
content: Meeting the linked goals of climate mitigation and adaptation requires a step change in the understanding of how our responses, often taken in isolation, interact dynamically, in real-world contexts. The actions taken by governments, sectors, individual and other actions often lead to unintended consequences (response risks) which propagate across systems. The consideration of such interactions is underdeveloped and often missing in practice, resulting in potentially substantial unrealised benefits or underestimated rebound effects. Both aspects can be accounted for by taking an integrated systems view of governmental, institutional and individual actions. This paper proposes a novel framework for structuring and presenting the current understanding of complex interactions between climate mitigation and adaptation on a cross-sectoral basis. Using a structured approach to literature review and expert elicitation, it synthesises and structures the required information to produce ‘Causal Loop Diagrams’ representing the qualitative relationships between mitigation and adaptation actions and the resulting response risks and opportunities. These visualisations offer the basis for further interrogation by stakeholders and experts to identify strategies and intervention points to reduce response risks and increase opportunities with a greater understanding of the potential dynamic interactions within the wider system.

title: Application of SWOT analysis and stakeholder engagement to identify strategic priorities for water resources management in Nunavut
summary: This study investigates the biophysical, sociocultural, regulatory and institutional dynamics that influence water management in Nunavut, Canada. Twenty-two interviews were conducted, followed by a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and t
content: This study investigates the biophysical, sociocultural, regulatory and institutional dynamics that influence water management in Nunavut, Canada. Twenty-two interviews were conducted, followed by a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT) analysis to identify strategic priorities for policymakers to improve Nunavut’s water management system. Five priorities were identified: (i) foster the participation of Inuit rights holders and invest in human capital development programs; (ii) promote cross-institutional resource sharing, centralization of water resources management (WRM)-adjacent services (e.g., IT, HR) and horizontal integration to mitigate capacity shortages, while maintaining the consideration of regional WRM specificities and community needs; (iii) improve the agility of decision-makers; (iv) employ participatory system dynamics modeling to elucidate the interconnected nature of Northern water management challenges and identify leverage points to disrupt adverse feedback mechanisms, address systemic drivers and promote effective localized solutions; and ( v ) focus on the design and implementation of long-term water management strategies and policies to achieve stable WRM outcomes. This research complements advocacy for leaders to recognize that acting on Indigenous priorities is foundational to achieving effective WRM outcomes globally. Further research should focus on the interaction between water and non-water resource systems in the territory and the application of Nunavut-specific decision-support tools.

title: Biomass-Based Carbon Materials for Electrochemical Reduction of Carbon Dioxide
summary: The electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> ( CO 2 ) is one of the prime concerns today to overcome global warming and convert it into fuels/chemicals for a sustainable environment
content: The electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> ( CO 2 ) is one of the prime concerns today to overcome global warming and convert it into fuels/chemicals for a sustainable environment and circular economy. Carbon-based nanostructured materials have enabled sophisticated electrochemical https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 reduction due to their distinct physical and chemical characteristics. Concerning the sustainability of cost and environment for synthetic materials, the scientific community has paid attention to reducing https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 concentration from biomass-derived nanomaterials. Biomass-derived carbon materials (BCMs) are greener and safer than other carbon compounds. BCMs, such as graphene (Gr), graphene oxide (GO), and biochar, have shown tremendous potential for https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 reduction. This chapter summarizes the fundamentals of electrochemical https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 reduction mechanisms for developing eco-friendly and cost-effective fuels/chemicals. Furthermore, we emphasize the issues raised in this field of sustainable systems and future perspectives on the electrochemical reduction of https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 using BCMs.

title: Dual loop neural Lie derivative estimation enhanced PSO tuned super-twisting control for maximum power point tracking in PMSG wind systems
summary: A robust nonlinear control methodology is developed for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of wind energy conversion systems (WECS) utilizing permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs). The control framework merges a generalized super
content: A robust nonlinear control methodology is developed for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of wind energy conversion systems (WECS) utilizing permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs). The control framework merges a generalized super-twisting sliding mode controller (Gen-STSMC) with a dual-loop recursive emotional neural network (DLRENN) estimator, enhanced through PSO-based gain optimization. Through its recursive structure, the DLRENN enables online estimation of nonlinear Lie derivative functions, avoiding the necessity of analytical modeling for aerodynamic and electrical uncertainties. PSO is also applied to the optimal tuning of the controller parameters, achieving a desirable trade-off among tracking accuracy, robustness, control effort, and chattering attenuation to further improve controller performance. The stability of the closed-loop system is ensured by the input-output linearization and the zero-dynamics analysis. Simulation results on a 3 kW benchmark show that the proposed method and the three benchmark controllers–feedback-linearization control (FLC), the real-twisting algorithm (RTA), and conventional sliding mode control (CSMC)—all reach an MPPT efficiency of about 99.97% under a highly turbulent wind profile, while the proposed method yields the lowest power-coefficient ripple and chattering. The combination of neural approximation and optimization-based gain tuning provides a practical and efficient solution for practical WECS applications.

title: Global Surface Coal Mine Segmentation with Multi-Spectral Sentinel-2 Imagery: Overcoming Spectral Dilution using Geospatial Foundation Models
summary: Surface coal mines are a diffuse, undermonitored source of methane, whose reduction could deliver measurable near-term climate benefit. A lack of precise spatial boundaries and reliance on global emission inventories (based on point coordin
content: Surface coal mines are a diffuse, undermonitored source of methane, whose reduction could deliver measurable near-term climate benefit. A lack of precise spatial boundaries and reliance on global emission inventories (based on point coordinates with kilometer-scale spa- tial uncertainty), limit their continuous spaceborne attribution and monitoring. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Global Surface Coal Mine (GSCM) Polygons dataset, obtained by spatially match- ing the Global Coal Mine Tracker to the Global Mining Footprint and linking candidate polygons to cloud-free Sentinel-2 imagery. We benchmark semantic-segmentation models from convolutional, vision-transformer, and geospatial-foundation-model families. On spatially isolated test tiles containing mine pixels, a pre-trained Prithvi-EO-2.0 model with six visible and infrared bands obtains the best mine recall (0.6975) and mIoU (0.6971). In contrast, adding channels to an ImageNet-pretrained SegFormer causes mine IoU to fall to 0.0094 at 15 bands. We term this spectral dilution. While the positive-only evaluation does not establish global mine discovery or operational readiness, the results support a practical baseline for delineating known surface mines.

title: Prediction and Dissection of Nitrogenase Activity Based on Protein Sequences using Dual Descriptor
summary: Nitrogenase reduces N2 to ammonia at ambient temperature and pressure, but its activity differs markedly among natural sequences, and conventional wet-laboratory screening suffers from low throughput and long turnaround times. Existing comp
content: Nitrogenase reduces N2 to ammonia at ambient temperature and pressure, but its activity differs markedly among natural sequences, and conventional wet-laboratory screening suffers from low throughput and long turnaround times. Existing computational methods have partially alleviated this bottleneck, yet most of them rely on protein embeddings obtained from protein language models together with features such as gene expression, and their interpretability analyses mostly stop at the level of feature contribution. Here we present CarmnaDD, a purely sequence-driven framework built on the dual descriptor (DD): two learnable components, the composition weight map (CWM) and the position weight function (PWF), jointly generate a position-resolved description N(k), so that activity can be predicted without any prior knowledge beyond the sequence. On the same dataset used by Carmna, CarmnaDD attains R2 = 0.60 for regression and AUC = 0.94 and F1 = 0.86 for classification, better than our previous Carmna, which integrates multiple features. Interpretability analysis shows that the amplitude of the periodic terms of the PWF decreases as the rank increases, indicating that the positional encoding strategy adapts to the rank; the high-weight 3-mer fragments in the CWM are significantly enriched in polar uncharged residues, which corroborates the SHAP-based conclusion of Carmna; sliding-window scanning identifies fragments significantly associated with activity (FDR < 0.05), and the strongest window displays a D-X-E pattern with conserved flanks and a polymorphic center, sequences carrying R at the central position showing the highest activity; conservation is significantly negatively correlated (ρ = −0.30) with description intensity. Mapping the key windows onto the protein structure shows that four highly correlated windows converge on the nucleotide-binding interface and the conformational-transmission/protein-docking interface of NifH. These results provide a purely sequence-based framework for nitrogenase activity prediction that balances performance and interpretability.

title: Solitary bees: understanding its contribution and prospecting key areas for its use in crop pollination in Brazil
summary: Animal pollination is a key factor for agricultural production, with bees considered the most important pollinating agents. Despite the high diversity within this group, Apis mellifera is the species most widely used for crop pollination; h
content: Animal pollination is a key factor for agricultural production, with bees considered the most important pollinating agents. Despite the high diversity within this group, Apis mellifera is the species most widely used for crop pollination; however, numerous factors have driven the search for alternative pollinators. This review investigates the role played by solitary bees in agricultural pollination in Brazil and aims to identify and synthesize information from the available scientific literature on interactions between solitary bees and agricultural crops in Brazil, one of the world’s leading agricultural countries, while prospecting regions favorable for their potential use. A total of 163 floral visitor species associated with 26 agricultural crops were identified, with emphasis on the genera Centris and Xylocopa . Only 11 bee species were evaluated for pollination efficiency. The main benefits reported included higher pollen deposition on stigmas, increased total fruit production, larger fruits, improved fruit shape, and higher seed number. Coastal areas and central regions of Brazil were identified as promising for the use of native solitary bees in agricultural pollination. The study demonstrates that, despite the large number of species associated with agricultural crops and their potential for directed pollination, there is a substantial knowledge gap regarding the pollination efficiency of the vast majority of these species.

title: Valorisation of organic materials for sustainable growing media: effects on early cucumber and tomato growth
summary: Introduction This study evaluated soil- and peat-based growing media in which solid digestate was used as the principal partial replacement component, whereas spent coffee grounds (SCG) and sapropel (Sp) were incorporated at low proportions
content: Introduction This study evaluated soil- and peat-based growing media in which solid digestate was used as the principal partial replacement component, whereas spent coffee grounds (SCG) and sapropel (Sp) were incorporated at low proportions as supplementary organic components intended to contribute organic matter and additional nutrient inputs. Methods Soil, peat, two solid digestate fractions (TEV and KP), SCG, and Sp were physicochemically characterized. A total of 50 substrate formulations (25 for cucumber and 25 for tomato) were screened, containing 20%– 80% solid digestate fraction, 0%–5% SCG, and 5%–10% Sp, with the remaining proportion consisting of soil or peat. Selected formulations were subsequently evaluated in 30-day pot experiments at 23 °C–25 °C. Plant length, root length, leaf number, fresh biomass, and air-dried biomass were determined, and the data were analysed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test ( p ≤ 0.05). Results During the preliminary cucumber screening, KP-containing formulations showed poor seedling survival and were excluded from the subsequent cucumber cultivation experiment. In soil-based cucumber substrates, the highest plant length (29.50 ± 2.12 cm) and fresh biomass (2.05 ± 0.11 g) were obtained with 50% soil, 40% TEV digestate, and 10% Sp. In peat-based cucumber substrates, plant length and leaf number were significantly higher in selected TEV-containing formulations than in the peat control, while treatment 4PC also showed significantly greater fresh biomass. Tomato responses were more variable: soil-based treatments differed significantly in plant length, root length, and leaf number, whereas biomass did not differ significantly; in peat-based treatments, only root length differed significantly. Discussions The results indicate that selected complete substrate formulations can support early cucumber and tomato growth and may allow partial replacement of conventional growing-medium components. However, their performance depended on substrate composition and crop species, and further evaluation of final mixture properties and longer-term plant performance is required.

title: Embedding collaborative research into residential land development: a translational approach to ecology with cities
summary: The expansion of urban and residential landscapes causes habitat and biodiversity loss, and many other environmental impacts associated with how these landscapes are designed, constructed, and managed. Here we describe a collaboration among
content: The expansion of urban and residential landscapes causes habitat and biodiversity loss, and many other environmental impacts associated with how these landscapes are designed, constructed, and managed. Here we describe a collaboration among researchers, outreach professionals, private companies, design professionals, NGOs, and municipal leaders that employed a translational ecology approach aimed at mitigating these impacts in a 36,000-home development in central Florida, United States. The company leading this development project approached researchers to seek strategies to conserve water due to Florida’s increasing water scarcity. The developer and researchers then brought in other collaborators with the goal of implementing drought tolerant, native plant-dominated landscaping as a water saving strategy. Two research projects were then incorporated into the development aimed at identifying strategies to establish native plants in the low-quality subsurface soils used in land development projects and at confirming both the irrigation savings and ecological benefits of this unconventional landscaping strategy. This paper communicates how collaborators worked together to implement these two research projects and translate their findings into better land development and landscaping practices, including reducing irrigation by only irrigating when needed as opposed to regularly; nearly eliminating the use of pesticides and mineral fertilizers; installing native plant-dominated, turf-free landscapes around new homes; and amending soils with compost to improve soil and plant health. This case study demonstrates how employing a translational ecology approach can lead to better environmental decisions, practices, and outcomes for ecology with cities collaborations.

title: Food Waste-to-Biochar from Low-Temperature Microwave-Assisted and Conventional Pyrolyses for Supermarket Food Waste Sustainability
summary: This study investigated the physicochemical characteristics of supermarket food waste (SFW) biochar produced through low-temperature conventional pyrolysis (CP) and microwave-assisted pyrolysis (MP) to evaluate its potential for sustainabil
content: This study investigated the physicochemical characteristics of supermarket food waste (SFW) biochar produced through low-temperature conventional pyrolysis (CP) and microwave-assisted pyrolysis (MP) to evaluate its potential for sustainability applications. Conventional pyrolysis at 300 °C (CP-SFW-300) produced biochar with high fixed carbon (FC) (48.1 wt % db), ash (11.8 wt % db), and carbon (C) (57.1 wt % db) contents, high higher heating value (HHV) (22.9 MJ/kg db), high N:C (0.1) but low H:C (0.9) ratios, and reduced abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups. In contrast, microwave-assisted pyrolysis at 240 °C (MP-SFW-240) produced biochar with high volatile matter (VM) (66.5 wt % db), abundant oxygen-containing functional groups, and more developed porosity and surface area (11.0 m2/g). These characteristics indicate that both CP-SFW-300 and MP-SFW-240 have potential as quality solid fuels and as substitutes for low-rank coals as their HHVs are comparable while offering the potential for lower greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, MP-SFW-240 may offer advantages for soil amendment by improving water retention and organic matter supply, although its lower ash content may reduce its contribution of mineral nutrients compared with CP-SFW-300. These findings demonstrate that low-temperature pyrolysis can tailor the characteristics of SFW biochar for specific sustainability applications while providing a sustainable pathway for SFW recovery.

title: Enhancing crop resilience under excess water stress: Physiological adaptations, management strategies and molecular advances
summary: Recent climatic variability has increased the frequency of waterlogging and flooding events, posing serious threats to crop productivity and food security worldwide. Excess water stress results from prolonged soil saturation, which restrict
content: Recent climatic variability has increased the frequency of waterlogging and flooding events, posing serious threats to crop productivity and food security worldwide. Excess water stress results from prolonged soil saturation, which restricts oxygen availability in the root zone or causes partial to complete plant submergence. This review systematically synthesises current knowledge of the morphological, physiological and biochemical mechanisms associated with crop adaptation to excess water stress, with emphasis on major agricultural crops. Key adaptive responses include adventitious root formation, aerenchyma development, lenticel hypertrophy and shoot elongation, which facilitate internal oxygen transport and plant survival under hypoxic conditions. From a functional perspective, crops generally adopt low-oxygen escape syndrome (LOES) or low-oxygen quiescence syndrome (LOQS) strategies to tolerate oxygen deficiency. Excess water stress also induces oxidative damage through the accumulation of reactive oxygen species, which tolerant plants mitigate through enhanced antioxidant defence systems. In addition to intrinsic adaptive mechanisms, field-level management approaches such as improved drainage, raised-bed cultivation, optimised nutrient management, rescue nutrition, plant growth regulator application, microbial inoculation and climate-smart agronomic practices have shown considerable potential for improving stress resilience and yield stability. Recent advances in molecular breeding, quantitative trait locus (QTL) identification and precision agriculture further support the development of waterlogging-tolerant cultivars and sustainable management strategies. However, large-scale implementation remains constrained by environmental variability, economic limitations and inconsistent field performance. Future research should therefore focus on integrating physiological insights, molecular breeding, precision water management and region-specific agronomic interventions to strengthen crop resilience under increasing flooding and excess water stress scenarios.

title: Combining Life Cycle Assessment and Planetary Boundaries for Sustainable Energy System Designs
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The global energy system is responsible for over 73% of global greenhouse gas emissions and is, thereby, the main driver of climate change. Hence, to mitigate climate change, energy systems must shift towards net-zero greenhouse gas emissio
tags: Environmental impact of the energy industry
content: The global energy system is responsible for over 73% of global greenhouse gas emissions and is, thereby, the main driver of climate change. Hence, to mitigate climate change, energy systems must shift towards net-zero greenhouse gas emissions. However, the shift towards net-zero may be accompanied by a shift in the environmental burden of energy systems from climate change towards other environmental impacts, possibly compromising the absolute environmental sustainability of energy systems. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) enables the identification and quantification of burden-shifting, but does not facilitate the assessment of absolute environmental sustainability. By integrating the planetary boundary framework into LCA, absolute environmental sustainability assessment of energy systems becomes feasible. Current absolute environmental sustainability assessments of energy systems solely focus on single-sector energy systems without analysing cross-sectorial interactions and fail to identify obstacles and enablers of absolute sustainable energy system designs. We employ an energy system modelling and optimisation framework with integrated LCA (SecMOD) for the case of Germany that encompasses multiple, coupled energy sectors, to assess energy system designs in terms of absolute sustainability, identify critical technologies preventing absolute sustainability of energy systems, and utilize multi-criteria optimization methods to span a design space for absolute sustainable energy systems. We find that an absolute sustainable energy system for Germany cannot be achieved by an autarkic and sector-coupled energy system if energy demand is not reduced. We disclose the main technologies in the German energy system’s supply chain compromising absolute sustainability. To enable an absolute sustainable energy systems, we span a design space including energy imports and energy demand reduction, e.g. by increase of energy efficiency. For the obtained energy system designs, we also provide cost estimates. We emphasise the need for considering environmental impacts beyond climate change in the design of future energy systems, as environmental burden-shifting prevents the absolute environmental sustainability of energy systems. Additionally, we conclude that absolute sustainable energy system design can be achieved through energy demand reduction and energy imports.
