title: Toward smart management of stored grains: integrating AI, IoT, and climate-resilient pest management for global food security
summary: Maintaining the quality and quantity of cereal grains is fundamental to global food security. However, persistent post-harvest losses caused by insects and vertebrate pests, storage molds, and environmental variability continue to threaten
content: Maintaining the quality and quantity of cereal grains is fundamental to global food security. However, persistent post-harvest losses caused by insects and vertebrate pests, storage molds, and environmental variability continue to threaten grain availability and safety. Conventional storage systems, which require routine inspection and chemical intervention, are challenged by climate change, emerging pests, and growing demand for safe and sustainable food. This review critically evaluates recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT)-based sensors, machine learning (ML), multimodal sensing, decision-support systems, climate-controlled storage, and reduced-risk pest management strategies, with an emphasis on their integration into predictive management systems. The effectiveness of sustainable management strategies, including hermetic storage, biopesticides, diatomaceous earths (DEs), and semiochemical-based approaches, is evaluated with an emphasis on efficacy, scalability, and practical feasibility, focusing on risk-based rather than blanket interventions. Based on these advances, the review proposes a six-stage conceptual framework encompassing the sensing of storage conditions, data analysis, risk prediction, decision-making, targeted intervention, and outcome verification. The central theoretical contribution is the development of a conceptual framework that integrates digital monitoring, climate risk assessment, and sustainable pest management. The framework provides practical guidance for storage managers to identify new risks, choose suitable actions, and assess management outcomes. Major constraints include limited datasets, sensor accuracy, model transferability, interoperability, and cost-effectiveness in smallholder systems. Future priorities include advancing edge and explainable AI, digital twins, and other technologies such as multimodal sensing and low-cost smart storage solutions for resource-constrained regions. Integrating digital technologies, climate adaptation, and sustainable pest management could enable adaptive, predictive stored grain management, reducing post-harvest losses, improving grain quality and safety, and strengthening global food security.

title: Translational Chemical Ecology: Bridging Mechanisms and Applications
summary: Understanding plant volatile chemistry is, in a very real sense, understanding how plants participate chemically in the living world around them . Translational chemical ecology explores how plants use volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as d
content: Understanding plant volatile chemistry is, in a very real sense, understanding how plants participate chemically in the living world around them . Translational chemical ecology explores how plants use volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as dynamic chemical signals that mediate interactions with insects, microbes, and neighbouring plants. It connects fundamental mechanisms of VOC biosynthesis, regulation, and ecological function with their translational potential in agriculture, biotechnology, and environmental resilience. This book integrates recent advances in molecular biology, omics technologies, and ecological modelling to demonstrate how plant volatiles can be harnessed for sustainable crop protection and smart farming systems. Designed for researchers, graduate students, and professionals in plant science, chemical ecology, and integrated pest management, this volume offers an interdisciplinary perspective linking basic mechanisms to real-world applications. Its clear organization and applied focus make it a valuable reference for understanding and utilizing the chemical language of plants in both natural and managed ecosystems.

title: UKCM2-LL: a new low-resolution GC5 configuration with constrained climate sensitivity - evaluation of CMIP7 DECK simulations
summary: This study presents UKCM2-LL, a new configuration with constrained climate sensitivity aligned to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) likely range. UKCM2-LL is based on the Met Office Hadley Ce
content: This study presents UKCM2-LL, a new configuration with constrained climate sensitivity aligned to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) likely range. UKCM2-LL is based on the Met Office Hadley Centre Global Environmental Model Global Coupled configuration version 5.0 (HadGEM3 GC5.0). We document the development and evaluation of UKCM2-LL through CMIP7 DECK simulations, including the spin-up and equilibration of the pre-industrial control, the calculation of the Effective Climate Sensitivity (EffCS), Transient Climate Response (TCR), effective radiative forcing (ERF) and climate feedbacks from abrupt and ramped CO2 experiments. The new UKCM2-LL configuration achieves an EffCS of 3.6 K, within the IPCC AR6 likely range of 2.5–4.0 K, primarily through more negative shortwave cloud feedbacks compared to the parent GC5.0 model (EffCS of 6.6 K). Evaluation against observations and CMIP6 models demonstrates improved simulation of the historical temperature record since the 1970s, with better agreement in interhemispheric temperature anomalies. The 1985–2014 global-mean trend reduces from 0.43 K per decade to 0.33 K per decade, closer to the observed trend of 0.18 K per decade. While present-day climatological metrics show approximately 30 % higher root mean square errors (RMSE) across a wide range of metrics relative to GC5.0, climatological performance remains reasonable relative to CMIP6 models. The introduction of CMIP7 forcings degrades the simulation of the historical temperature record, especially the interhemispheric anomalies. This work demonstrates the efficacy of Perturbed Parameter Ensemble (PPE) methodologies to develop climate models with constrained emergent properties while maintaining acceptable present-day performance, providing a valuable tool for climate projection studies requiring models within the IPCC-assessed climate sensitivity range.

title: Hidden Costs of Climate Goals: code, characterization factors and aggregated results (SCENE pipeline v19nov2026)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Code (Jupyter notebooks and configuration), regionalised PM2.5 characterization factors (56 world regions, SSP2), aggregated results (DALYs and external costs by scenario, sector, emission region and pollutant) and run manifests for the art
content: Code (Jupyter notebooks and configuration), regionalised PM2.5 characterization factors (56 world regions, SSP2), aggregated results (DALYs and external costs by scenario, sector, emission region and pollutant) and run manifests for the article “Hidden Costs of Climate Goals: A Life Cycle Perspective on the Net-Zero Path of the Swiss Energy Sector” (Uribe Poblete, Catoja, Heck; submitted to Energy Reports; preprint https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5861062). Life-cycle inventories derived from ecoinvent/premise and STEM scenario inputs are not included because of licensing restrictions; the manifests document the SHA-256 hash of every input used. Supported by the ETH Board through the SCENE Joint Initiative.

title: An impact-embedded framework for product-level circularity assessment: Evidence from railway materials and components
summary: : The circular economy (CE) is increasingly promoted to improve resource efficiency and reduce environmental impacts, particularly in material-intensive sectors such as transport infrastructure. However, most existing circularity indicators
content: : The circular economy (CE) is increasingly promoted to improve resource efficiency and reduce environmental impacts, particularly in material-intensive sectors such as transport infrastructure. However, most existing circularity indicators remain material-centric, focusing on material flows and recycling rates while treating environmental impacts separately. Consequently, these indicators may not adequately capture whether increased material circularity is accompanied by improved environmental performance. To address this limitation, this study introduces the Impact-embedded Product Circularity indicator (iCp), a product-level metric that integrates material circularity with environmental performance. The proposed framework extends the Ellen MacArthur Foundation’s Material Circularity Indicator (MCI) with an impact-based adjustment factor derived from life cycle impact assessment results. The framework is applied to conventional and recycled railway ballast and sleeper configurations under multiple environmental assessment scenarios. The results demonstrate that increased material circularity does not necessarily correspond to consistent reductions in environmental impacts, as recycling strategies may involve trade-offs across impact categories. The proposed iCp indicator accounts for these environmental differences at the aggregated level by adjusting material circularity scores according to relative life cycle environmental performance. Overall, the iCp framework provides an environmentally informed extension of conventional product-level circularity assessment, supporting more informed comparisons of circular economy strategies and decision-making.

title: A Judicial Quest for Solid Legal Ground. The Role of Perceived Societal Impact in Judicial Decision-Making in PIL Cases
summary: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) cases inherently extend beyond the interests of the litigating parties and affect society at large. Hence, such rulings may provoke political and societal backlash. In the Netherlands, recent high-impact jud
content: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) cases inherently extend beyond the interests of the litigating parties and affect society at large. Hence, such rulings may provoke political and societal backlash. In the Netherlands, recent high-impact judicial decisions have sparked public debate, incomprehension and criticism. Courts are accused of encroaching upon the political domain, the government appears increasingly reluctant to comply with judicial orders, and legislative initiatives have been proposed to restrict the access of public interest organisations to the courts. In short, the legitimacy of judicial interventions in PIL cases is challenged. This contribution examines how courts address the potential societal impact of PIL cases in their decision-making, and in doing so, construct legitimacy at the intersection of law, society and politics against a background of increasing backlash against the exercise of judicial authority. Drawing on a mixed-methods approach it demonstrates that while a ruling’s anticipated impact is no independent consideration in determining the outcome of case, it serves as a factor shaping how courts understand and articulate their institutional role.

title: Assessing the susceptibility to mould growth of mycelium-based composite insulation
summary: Mycelium-based composites (MBCs) are promising sustainable insulation materials. However, susceptibility to mould growth remains poorly characterised and represents a barrier to safe adoption. This study addresses this by applying a method
content: Mycelium-based composites (MBCs) are promising sustainable insulation materials. However, susceptibility to mould growth remains poorly characterised and represents a barrier to safe adoption. This study addresses this by applying a method adapted from EN 17886:2023 for assessing mould susceptibility in lab-produced and commercially supplied MBCs. Thermal conductivity, water absorption, and wettability were measured to contextualise biological performance. Mould susceptibility was assessed using a protocol adaption from the EN 17886:2023 method, scored on an ordinal 0-3 scale. Specimens (n = 6 per condition) were incubated for 28 days under five combinations of relative humidity (RH) and temperature, followed by a wetting phase and 14 days of further incubation. No visible mould developed at 80% RH and 25 °C, but growth increased at higher humidity and temperature, with statistically significant differences between materials under selected conditions. All materials supported extensive mould development at 90% RH and 30 °C. All specimens included in a wetting phase and a further 14 days of incubation showed extensive mould growth. These results demonstrate the importance of material-specific testing for the specification of mycelium-based insulation and highlight extensive mould development following wetting and extended incubation. These findings support development of sustainable construction materials that do not compromise occupant safety.

title: Exploring Sustainability Practices and Perspectives in US Intensive Care Units Through a Cross-Sectional Survey
summary: Intensive care units (ICUs) are resource-intensive clinical environments, but information on staff-reported sustainability practices and implementation challenges in US ICUs remains limited. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined
content: Intensive care units (ICUs) are resource-intensive clinical environments, but information on staff-reported sustainability practices and implementation challenges in US ICUs remains limited. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined current practices, training, perceived barriers and facilitators, and motivators among a voluntary convenience sample of ICU stakeholders recruited across the United States. Closed-ended responses were summarized as counts and percentages, and open-ended responses were thematically coded. The descriptive sample included 145 US respondents. Most reported that sustainability was not part of their role (111/145, 77%) and that they had received no sustainability training (115/145, 79%). Respondents frequently described disposing of single-use products (89/145, 61%) and opened, unused items (60/145, 41%) in the trash. Perceived barriers included infection prevention and control concerns and costs. Among 129 respondents assessed for motivation, contributing to climate change mitigation (55/129, 43%) and alignment with personal values (42/129, 33%) were the most frequently reported motivators. Findings identify potential opportunities for education, staff engagement, and organizational support within the surveyed settings. Small professional subgroups, self-selection, and uncertain nonresponse bias limit comparisons and generalizability; the findings do not estimate national prevalence or establish intervention effectiveness.

title: On Integrating Computation into the Built Environment
summary: Cities are responsible for up to 70% of the planet’s carbon emissions. Why has the integration of computation into our cities and buildings not helped manage their resource use in any noticeable way? This book offers an urgent and practical
content: Cities are responsible for up to 70% of the planet’s carbon emissions. Why has the integration of computation into our cities and buildings not helped manage their resource use in any noticeable way? This book offers an urgent and practical rethinking of how we integrate computation into our built environment. Author Alex Webb suggests that the reason why integrations of computation into the built environment—smart cities, IoT and civic hacking—have been less than productive is a product of how we think about designing them. This book proposes drawing from machinic life, a unique blend of robotics, psychology and computer science that has focused on the development of adaptive, responsive machines. These machines avoid prediction and rely upon simple responses to produce complex behaviors in unpredictable worlds. While smart city projects continue to develop and attract attention, familiar products like The Nest and the Roomba quietly suggest a path forward that leverages the best of computation in the fight against climate change. On Integrating Computation into the Built Environment shows how the strategies for dealing with uncertainty in robotics are applicable to responsive environments and adaptive infrastructure. This book will be of great interest to upper‑level students, academics and those bridging research and practice in the fields of architecture, design computation, urban design, planning and robotics.

title: Eco-innovation in Mediterranean sheep farming informed by life cycle assessment evidence: stakeholder insights from a Sardinian case study
summary: Achieving sustainable transitions in extensive livestock systems requires environmental evidence that is not only scientifically robust but also relevant to farmers and other stakeholders operating in specific rural contexts. While Life Cyc
content: Achieving sustainable transitions in extensive livestock systems requires environmental evidence that is not only scientifically robust but also relevant to farmers and other stakeholders operating in specific rural contexts. While Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) provides valuable insights into environmental performance, its contribution to decision-making remains limited when it is not aligned with stakeholder priorities, local knowledge, and contextual constraints. This study explores how stakeholders perceive and prioritise three eco-innovations, precision livestock farming, pasture improvement practices, and environmental labelling, and examines the drivers, trade-offs, and barriers influencing their adoption in Mediterranean sheep farming systems. The analysis builds on environmental evidence from previous LCA studies and combines participatory data from two multi-actor focus groups in Sardinia (Italy) with strategic evaluation and multivariate analysis to explore interactions among technical, economic, institutional, and socio-cultural factors. Pasture improvement practices emerged as the most promising option, showing strong alignment between environmental benefits and farm-level feasibility. Precision livestock farming demonstrated potential to improve system efficiency but was constrained by high investment costs, limited adaptability, and infrastructural shortcomings. Environmental labelling was perceived as the least attractive option because of market uncertainty, concerns about credibility, and weak knowledge exchange. Across all practices, adoption emerged as a context-dependent process shaped by interacting system components, with external constraints outweighing internal limitations. The study shows how stakeholders interpret environmental evidence and how this could support the adoption of context-specific eco-innovations. It reveals persistent mismatches with farm-level decision-making and highlights the need for context-specific innovation pathways, stronger knowledge exchange, and coordinated policy support to enable more effective sustainability transitions in extensive livestock farming.

title: From agricultural residues to tradeable bio-assets in Africa: a policy and practice framework for circular agro-industrial value chains
summary: Agricultural residues in Sub-Saharan Africa are often described as an underused resource, but their conversion into marketable products is constrained by feedstock variability, competing uses, logistics, product standards, environmental ris
content: Agricultural residues in Sub-Saharan Africa are often described as an underused resource, but their conversion into marketable products is constrained by feedstock variability, competing uses, logistics, product standards, environmental risks, and uncertain demand. Utilizing a critical narrative policy synthesis, this paper develops a policy and practice framework for assessing when selected agricultural residues can become credible circular bio-assets for local use and, where conditions permit, regional trade. The framework connects four decision layers: (1) technically and economically recoverable feedstock, ownership, and explicit smallholder and land-use safeguards; (2) technology and product selection; (3) environmental, technical, and economic evidence; and (4) quality assurance, finance, MSME AfCFTA compliance costs, and trade infrastructure. It examines cassava processing effluents, cocoa pod husks, palm oil mill effluents and other palm residues, sugarcane bagasse, and livestock manure across biochemical, thermochemical, bioconversion, and physicochemical pathways. Material Flow Analysis, Life Cycle Assessment, and Techno-Economic Analysis are treated as complementary evidence rather than as stand-alone proof of viability. The paper also examines the conditions under which AfCFTA trade facilitation, quality-assurance infrastructure, payment systems, and development finance can support commercialization. A critical comparison with existing African circular-bioeconomy reviews shows that prior work has largely focused on the potential and challenges of circular bioeconomy, the status of circular practices in selected food systems, or specific technology portfolios. This paper extends that literature by linking resource security, technology choice, evidence thresholds, product quality, market validation, and cross-border transaction requirements within one staged decision architecture governed by conditional decision gates. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not assume that residues are costless, that regional trade is preferable to local use, or that technological maturity implies bankability. The proposed roadmap is therefore designed to guide policy screening, demonstration funding, and investment due diligence while identifying priorities for empirical validation.

title: Promises and challenges of artificial intelligence to combat climate change
summary: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the development of strategies to mitigate and to adapt to climate change is growing worldwide. Diversity of thematic scope and geographical delimitation means that this area of digitalisation is in
content: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the development of strategies to mitigate and to adapt to climate change is growing worldwide. Diversity of thematic scope and geographical delimitation means that this area of digitalisation is in constant progress. Developments are happening at global, national, and local levels and are considered for a wide range of applications. At the same time, using AI to tackle climate change also implies negative consequences. This contribution questions how AI is reshaping climate change mitigation and adaptation actions, by presenting an array of examples of AI-driven solutions being adopted in different places across the world. It also aims to identify the challenges and risks that the use of AI represents for climate change so far. The speed at which these developments are happening is tantalising, and this is acknowledged by the international community, with the private sector and non-profit organisations taking the lead in current AI developments. The pace at which this is happening suggests the urgent need to develop the appropriate policies to regulate the use of AI, considering that it can also foster the problem it is expected to address.

title: Predicting Unprecedented Hot Temperature Extreme Occurrences Up to a Year in Advance
summary: Unprecedented hot temperature extremes (UTEx) severely stress human and natural systems by exceeding historical climate ranges and regionally even breaching potential adaptability limits, making reliable predictions crucial. Using initialis
content: Unprecedented hot temperature extremes (UTEx) severely stress human and natural systems by exceeding historical climate ranges and regionally even breaching potential adaptability limits, making reliable predictions crucial. Using initialised decadal hindcasts and historical forcing simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6, we explore to what extent UTEx can be predicted on interannual time scales. We find that the occurrence of UTEx in the following year can be skilfully predicted in some predominantly tropical regions using initialised climate predictions, while historical climate simulations show little skill. This suggests that to predict the annual occurrences of UTEx, correctly capturing the phase of climate variability is key. UTEx in these regions occur predominantly during El Niño years, grounding the prediction of such extremes in tropical Pacific predictability. Our findings establish the feasibility of predicting annual occurrences of unprecedented climate extremes, providing a foundation for future early warning systems.

title: A multi-domain field dataset to evaluate agricultural impacts at the edge of a Kenyan savanna
summary: Sub-Saharan Africa has experienced both rapid population growth and loss of arable land due to soil degradation, leading to the expansion of agriculture into savanna ecosystems. Sustainable agricultural intensification has been promoted to
content: Sub-Saharan Africa has experienced both rapid population growth and loss of arable land due to soil degradation, leading to the expansion of agriculture into savanna ecosystems. Sustainable agricultural intensification has been promoted to reduce expansion into native ecosystems while minimizing impacts of increased agricultural inputs on existing farmland. However, there are few high-resolution spatiotemporal datasets available to evaluate existing agroecosystem conditions and proposed management scenarios at the upstream edge of natural savanna ecosystems. The dataset presented here contains daily and sub-daily streamflow and precipitation data, soil physicochemical properties, and farm management data collected from the Nanyuki River watershed in the Mount Kenya region of the Upper Ewaso Ng’iro basin (Laikipia, Meru, and Nyeri counties) from 2021–2024. Derived products include stream channels, subwatersheds and their attributes, and 10 m land cover and curve number layers that distinguish large farms from smallholder fields. The datasets provide comprehensive information for calibrating and evaluating hydrologic, ecosystem, and agricultural models at daily and sub-daily time steps.

title: When early success risks failure: applying Integrative Anticipatory Policy Design to accelerate the EV transition in Vietnam
summary: Non-Technical Summary Vietnam's electric vehicle (EV) sales surged from 140 in 2019 to 190,000 in 2025. This remarkable success masks potential risks of deceleration, because the protectionist policies that enabled rapid growth may trigger
content: Non-Technical Summary Vietnam's electric vehicle (EV) sales surged from 140 in 2019 to 190,000 in 2025. This remarkable success masks potential risks of deceleration, because the protectionist policies that enabled rapid growth may trigger future stagnation. To address this problem, we apply the Integrative Anticipatory Policy Design (IAPD) framework to identify, before it is too late to adjust, how positive trajectories might turn negative. We specifically show how VinFast's monopoly in charging infrastructure, which accounts for initial acceleration, is also expected to eventually hinder market competition and decelerate innovation in subsequent steps. We then discuss ‘critical juncture’ policy interventions to continue upward trajectories. Technical Summary Vietnam's EV deployment surged from 140 to 190,000 units over the 6 years from 2019 to 2025, representing exceptional growth in the region. However, the very policies driving this initial acceleration may produce decelerating effects that threaten long-term transformation. This paper applies the IAPD framework, which builds on and expands work on backward- and forward-looking analysis of policy path dependency to identify and mitigate these risks. By applying four diagnostic questions across a multi-step transition staircase, we analyze Vietnam's reliance on a national champion model and proprietary charging infrastructure. Our findings reveal that while initial successes were driven by concentrated private capital and unique internal demand loops, they have created structural lock-ins that threaten sustainability. We identify a critical 2–3-year window for interventions to prevent technological divergence and market stagnation before these dynamics become irreversible. Unlike research that reacts only after empirical failure manifests, the IAPD framework generates anticipatory policy mixes designed to avoid deceleration before it occurs. We propose phased interventions, specifically technical standardization and mandated infrastructure sharing, to convert undermining dynamics into sustained transformation. This analysis demonstrates how anticipatory design can redirect path dependencies, ensuring that early-stage momentum translates into durable, long-term sustainability transitions. Social Media Summary Behind Vietnam's EV boom: early success may trigger future failure. New anticipatory policy design framework spots when progress reverses.

title: The potential of policy measures to mitigate consumption-based greenhouse gas emissions in the Nordic countries
summary: The Nordic countries have positioned themselves as climate frontrunners, in part by addressing consumption-based greenhouse gas emissions, which include emissions embedded in imports. Meanwhile, the IPCC et al. (2023) has underscored that d
content: The Nordic countries have positioned themselves as climate frontrunners, in part by addressing consumption-based greenhouse gas emissions, which include emissions embedded in imports. Meanwhile, the IPCC et al. (2023) has underscored that demand-oriented strategies are imperative for achieving greenhouse gas reductions in line with the Paris Agreement. However, evaluations of policies aimed at mitigating consumption-based emissions remain scarce. Addressing this gap, this article explores existing Nordic strategies and examines policy measures to reduce these emissions. Through a scoping review of academic and grey literature, approximately 100 unique policy measures were identified, of which 21 were selected for in-depth analysis using the Policy Delphi method. In two rounds of ranking and dialogue, 23 Nordic experts assessed the measures' potential to curb greenhouse gas emissions and their feasibility. The Policy Delphi showed promise as a flexible and accessible method for multi-dimensional policy evaluation, albeit with limited precision. The results show that many consumption-oriented measures already exist, and that strategies could build on intensifying and expanding them to achieve more significant emissions reductions. Among the measures assessed, experts rated regulatory standards as having particularly high potential to reduce consumption-based emissions. Yet, stronger measures may entail trade-offs in feasibility, notably lower public and political acceptance. Drawing on the Nordic frontrunner cases, the article recommends quantified consumption-based targets supported by improved statistics, as well as compensatory measures to enhance feasibility. Policy packages combining push, pull, and information measures could further increase both effectiveness and acceptability.

title: Electricity Intensity and Co₂e Emission Performance in Paper Production: Benchmarking and Decomposition Analysis of an Industrial Plant in Türkiye
summary: The pulp and paper industry is characterized by substantial energy and resource requirements, making improvements in process efficiency important for reducing environmental impacts. This study evaluates the electricity- and process-related
content: The pulp and paper industry is characterized by substantial energy and resource requirements, making improvements in process efficiency important for reducing environmental impacts. This study evaluates the electricity- and process-related performance of an anonymized paper-production facility in Türkiye through an integrated benchmarking and decomposition framework. Plant-level data were used to quantify electricity intensity, electricity-related CO₂e emission intensity, recycled-pulp utilization, steam utilization, and wastewater generation. The facility was evaluated against a product-matched European reference for recycled-fibre (RCF) mills without deinking producing packaging paper, an industrial reference from Türkiye, and broader sector-level estimates for Türkiye, Europe, and the United States. The analyzed plant exhibited an electricity intensity of 320 kWh/ton, approximately 8.6% below the lower boundary and 28.9% below the upper boundary of the product-matched European reference range of 350–450 kWh/ton. Its electricity-related CO₂e emission intensity was approximately 141 kg CO₂e/ton. When the product-matched European electricity-intensity range was combined with the European grid emission factor of 0.251 kg CO₂e/kWh, the corresponding illustrative emission-intensity range was approximately 88–113 kg CO₂e/ton. Decomposition analysis showed that the lower electricity intensity of the analyzed plant reduced emissions by approximately 13–57 kg CO₂e/ton relative to the product-matched European reference, whereas the higher Turkish grid emission factor increased them by approximately 67–86 kg CO₂e/ton, resulting in a net increase of approximately 29–54 kg CO₂e/ton. Relative to the estimated Türkiye sector-level reference, the approximately 242 kg CO₂e/ton reduction was entirely attributable to lower electricity intensity because both systems shared the same grid emission factor. Process assessment further indicated an 85% recycled-pulp ratio and a 64.3% steam-utilization ratio. Overall, the results demonstrate that comparatively low plant-level electricity consumption does not necessarily result in lower electricity-related CO₂e emissions when the electricity supply has a higher carbon intensity. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for distinguishing plant-level electricity-efficiency effects from electricity-grid carbon-intensity effects in paper-production benchmarking.

title: From The Root Climate Change Mitigation Model: A Sustainability Guide
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Numerous climate change mitigation models exist, climate change remains a persistent global challenge. This study proposes the From the Root Climate Change Mitigation Model to address existing gaps by promoting continuous climate education
content: Numerous climate change mitigation models exist, climate change remains a persistent global challenge. This study proposes the From the Root Climate Change Mitigation Model to address existing gaps by promoting continuous climate education from early childhood through all stages of formal and informal learning. Using a literature-based confirmatory approach and system analysis, the study reviewed existing models to identify their strengths, limitations, and the need for a more comprehensive framework. The proposed model comprises seven interconnected components: foundational climate education, progressive learning, climate-focused research centres, a Global Climate Change Mitigation Day, climate-based archival systems, and inclusive stakeholder participation. The review revealed that existing models provide important mitigation strategies but pay limited attention to sustained, intergenerational climate knowledge acquisition and preservation. The study concludes that the proposed model offers a sustainable framework for climate action and recommends its adoption to strengthen climate policy, education, research, implementation, and long-term environmental sustainability. Keywords: Climate change, climate change mitigation, climate education, climate knowledge transmission, environmental sustainability, model

title: Forecasting end-of-life electric vehicle batteries in Palestine: Circularity readiness assessment, scenario analysis, and policy roadmap for sustainable battery management
summary: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) is expected to increase future end-of-life (EOL) lithium-ion battery flows, creating environmental, infrastructure, and circular-economy challenges. These issue
content: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) is expected to increase future end-of-life (EOL) lithium-ion battery flows, creating environmental, infrastructure, and circular-economy challenges. These issues are particularly relevant in Palestine, where dedicated battery management systems and recycling infrastructure remain limited. This study develops an integrated framework combining electric-mobility growth projections, battery-demand estimation, EOL battery forecasting, circularity assessment, material-recovery evaluation, scenario-based battery-management analysis, and a Battery Circularity Readiness Index (BCRI). The framework is designed to evaluate future battery flows, resource-recovery opportunities, circularity potential, and national preparedness for sustainable battery management. The results indicate a substantial increase in battery demand and EOL battery generation associated with the projected expansion of electric mobility. By 2035, recalculated annual retiring nominal battery capacity reaches 88.38 MWh under the conditional hybrid-capacity assumptions, equivalent to 21.57% of annual nominal battery-capacity demand. Scenario analysis demonstrates that improved collection systems, second-life deployment, and recycling partnerships can significantly reduce disposal requirements while enhancing resource recovery. The BCRI assessment yields a readiness score of 29.5/100, indicating a low level of preparedness under current conditions and revealing critical gaps in collection infrastructure, regulatory frameworks, and recycling capability. However, the assessment also identifies significant opportunities for second-life battery applications and future circular-economy development. Overall, the study provides a forecasting, readiness-assessment, and policy-planning framework for sustainable battery management in Palestine. The findings support the development of collection systems, regulatory mechanisms, and circular-economy strategies required to facilitate a resilient and sustainable electric-mobility transition.

title: Unboxing the Quadruple Bottom Line of Corporate Sustainability: Index Development and Validation
summary: To date, research has focused on the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) of corporate sustainability, yet it has paid limited attention to the religious rituals that contribute to sustainability. Accordingly, this research seeks to develop and validat
content: To date, research has focused on the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) of corporate sustainability, yet it has paid limited attention to the religious rituals that contribute to sustainability. Accordingly, this research seeks to develop and validate a multidimensional index for measuring corporate sustainability performance. This research introduced the religious aspect and its indicators. Consequently, it integrated it with the TBL of corporate sustainability, which advanced the idea of ‘Quadruple Bottom Line’ (QBL or 4BL). This research followed the index development procedures suggested by prior research. The study tested the validity and reliability of the measurement index using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). The results confirmed four dimensions: economic sustainability, social sustainability, environmental sustainability, and religious sustainability, comprising 31 indicators. Furthermore, the study assessed nomological validity by statistically testing the four dimensions of corporate sustainability. The newly established index may be highly relevant to scholars and practitioners exploring the factors and outcomes of corporate sustainability. This is the first index to make corporate sustainability performance measurable and accessible to concerned stakeholders. This research offers practical implications for policymakers, corporate boards, top management, customers, and relevant authorities in assessing a corporation’s contributions to achieving the SDGs. This research will serve as a springboard for developing a multidimensional tool to measure corporate sustainability performance.

title: DISCO2VERY: Life Cycle Assessment of Innovative Pathways for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Chemicals
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Climate change, driven by greenhouse gas emissions like CO2, is one of the most pressing challenges of our time. The chemical industry, responsible for approximately 5% of global CO2 emission, significantly contributes to climate change, pr
content: Climate change, driven by greenhouse gas emissions like CO2, is one of the most pressing challenges of our time. The chemical industry, responsible for approximately 5% of global CO2 emission, significantly contributes to climate change, primarily due to its dependence on fossil-based carbon feedstocks. A promising solution to mitigate the chemical industry’s direct CO2 emissions involves replacing the fossil-based carbon feedstocks with CO2 captured from the atmosphere. The captured CO2 is electrochemically reduced (eCO2R) to produce CO2-based chemicals, potentially reducing the chemical industry's climate impact. However, eCO2R pathways demand substantial amounts of energy, which may negate the climate benefits of CO2-based chemicals and shift the environmental burden of CO2-based chemicals to other environmental impact categories, depending on the exploited energy source. Additionally, eCO2R pathways require certain materials for electrochemical components that may introduce new environmental impacts, such as the emission of PFAS due to the use of fluorine-containing binders. The DISCO2VERY project aims to develop innovative components for eCO2R pathways to reduce the environmental impact of CO2-based chemicals, focusing on advanced gas diffusion electrodes, novel catalysts and, fluorine-free binders. To guide the development of these components, the Institute of Technical Thermodynamics (LTT) supports the project with a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). LCA is a standardized method that assesses multiple environmental impacts over the entire life cycle of a production system, such as eCO2R pathways.

title: A review of reservoir evolution and coupled processes in CO₂ plume geothermal systems
summary: CO₂ plume geothermal (CPG) systems combine geothermal heat recovery with geological CO₂ storage, but their long-term performance depends on how the reservoir and wellbore evolve during continuous circulation. This review examines the intera
content: CO₂ plume geothermal (CPG) systems combine geothermal heat recovery with geological CO₂ storage, but their long-term performance depends on how the reservoir and wellbore evolve during continuous circulation. This review examines the interacting thermal, hydraulic, geochemical, geomechanical, and wellbore processes controlling this evolution. Published studies demonstrate substantial performance potential but also important operational limitations: CO₂-based systems have reported up to 2.9 times greater heat extraction than water-filled conventional geothermal systems, while reservoir pressure losses may be approximately 3–12 times lower than for brine at equivalent mass flow rates. Conversely, fluid–rock interactions and salt precipitation have been shown to reduce heat-mining rates by up to approximately 40%, highlighting the importance of evolving near-well conditions. Field experience at the Cranfield site further shows that multiphase reservoir–wellbore behaviour can constrain circulation predicted by numerical models. To connect these processes across different timescales, this review proposes a Dynamic Reservoir Evolution Framework (DREF) that organizes evolving reservoir–wellbore states, coupled THMC-W feedbacks, monitoring observations, performance and risk indicators, and operational controls. DREF is presented as a conceptual architecture rather than a validated numerical model. The review highlights the need for CPG-specific field evidence, coupled long-term modelling, monitoring-informed model updating, and uncertainty-aware adaptive operation to improve the reliability and sustainability of future CPG systems.

title: The Strategic Governance Paradox: Institutional Continuity and Environmental Quality Trends Amidst Political Regime Transitions in Ethiopia (1996-2025)
source: Cureus Journal of Business and Economics.
summary: This study examines the strategic alignment between institutional governance and environmental outcomes in Ethiopia from 1996 to 2025. Using an explanatory mixed-methods design, it investigates how national strategic frameworks - from the p
content: This study examines the strategic alignment between institutional governance and environmental outcomes in Ethiopia from 1996 to 2025. Using an explanatory mixed-methods design, it investigates how national strategic frameworks - from the post-Derg developmental state to the Prosperity Party’s market-oriented reforms - have co-moved with environmental quality and sustainable growth. The analysis is organized around three observables: a composite Environmental Governance Index (EGI), constructed as the unweighted mean of the six Worldwide Governance Indicators; carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions per capita from the World Bank World Development Indicators series EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5, multiplied by 1,000 and analysed in kilograms per person per year; and real gross domestic product (GDP) per capita in constant 2015 US dollars (series NY.GDP.PCAP.KD). The estimation sample is the 30 calendar years 1996-2025. Four incomplete slots - the six governance estimates in 1997, 1999 and 2001, and CO₂ emissions per capita in 2025 - are filled by multiple imputation by chained equations. Real GDP per capita is observed in every year, including 2025. The baseline ordinary least squares model is estimated in levels on each imputed data set, with Newey-West standard errors pooled by Rubin’s rules. Descriptive and regression results show a very strong positive association between real GDP per capita and CO₂ emissions per capita (Pearson r = 0.959). Each additional constant-2015 US dollar of real GDP per capita is associated with 0.152 kg of CO₂ per person (95% confidence interval: 0.123-0.182; p < 0.001). The EGI coefficient is 27.61 (p = 0.222). It is not statistically significant and is not interpreted as evidence that governance causes higher emissions. The EGI series remains persistently negative and does not exhibit a stable improving trend across political regimes. Qualitative triangulation of national environmental laws and strategies (including the Climate-Resilient Green Economy strategy and the Green Legacy Initiative) suggests an implementation gap: high-level policy branding has evolved, while operational enforcement capacity has remained constrained. These patterns are consistent with strategic inertia and institutional path dependency, but they are associational rather than causal. Non-stationarity of the EGI is treated as a statistical property of the series, not as proof of strategic instability. The paper contributes to institutional and sustainable-business strategy debates by showing how organizational continuity can coexist with ambitious green-growth rhetoric. Policy implications emphasize regime-agnostic regulatory mandates and the integration of ecological targets as core performance indicators in national development plans.

title: Evaluating Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope Imagery for Detecting Ice Phenology in Alaskan Lakes and Ponds
summary: Lake ice serves as both an indicator and driver of climate change, yet past studies have often overlooked ice phenology in small lakes and ponds due to the spatiotemporal limitations of existing satellite missions. Here we produce annual ic
content: Lake ice serves as both an indicator and driver of climate change, yet past studies have often overlooked ice phenology in small lakes and ponds due to the spatiotemporal limitations of existing satellite missions. Here we produce annual ice cover time series for 15,885 Alaskan lakes using high-resolution Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope imagery for the years 2019–2025. We assess the relative performance of both missions, then use our time series data to analyze the controls on lake ice timing across Alaska. We find that Sentinel-2 outperforms PlanetScope for ice phenology monitoring, especially at high latitudes, due to its superior revisit timing and improved classification performance. Planet’s underperformance stemmed from its lower spectral resolution and overarching issues with its cloud mask. Our analysis of ice-on and ice-off timing demonstrates that large lakes maintain ice cover for, on average, 7 days longer than small ponds. This difference is primarily driven by delayed ice-off timing in large lakes, as ice-on took place synchronously across lake sizes. Climatologically, we confirm that the seasonal 0 °C isotherm date is highly correlated with both ice-off and ice-on timing. We also find that lake ice cover responds more slowly to earlier warming in spring (and, conversely, faster to later cooling in fall), a moderate negative feedback which could dampen the number of lost ice cover days due to climate change. Overall, our findings reveal the value of high-resolution remote sensing data for studying lake ice dynamics in small lakes and emphasize Sentinel-2’s particular utility for high-latitude observation.

title: A Study on Individuals’ Perception of Climate-Friendly Health Services
summary: Purpose:The main purpose of the study is to explore individuals’ perspectives on climate-friendly healthcare services.Methods: This is a cross-sectional, descriptive study. A convenience sampling method was used in the study, and the sample
content: Purpose:The main purpose of the study is to explore individuals’ perspectives on climate-friendly healthcare services.Methods: This is a cross-sectional, descriptive study. A convenience sampling method was used in the study, and the sample consisted of 405 people. Data were collected through face-to-face and online surveys. The survey consisted of two parts. The first part included a personal and demographic information form prepared by the researchers to get to know the participants and determine their general information. The second part of the survey used the “Patient perspectives on climate-smart healthcare services” scale developed by Cohen et al. (2025). Descriptive statistical methods and difference analyses were used to evaluate the findings of the study using SPSS 25.0. Data were analyzed at a 95% confidence level.Results: The study found that a large portion of individuals are knowledgeable about climate change and believe that climate change is caused by them. The study also found that individuals are concerned about the consequences of climate change, that the healthcare sector’s impact on climate is seen as a relatively significant problem, and that individuals do not favor climate-friendly healthcare strategies, such as offering only vegetarian meals in hospitals. However, individuals are hesitant about increasing costs for climate-friendly insurance.Conclusion: The study concluded that individuals are concerned about climate change but are willing to contribute to climate change mitigation strategies in healthcare by opting for climate-friendly treatment alternatives, at least in part.

title: Precipitation extremes in the Argentine Pampas: Current declining trends and projected intensification under climate change
summary: Climate change is intensifying precipitation extremes globally, posing challenges to agriculture and water management in vulnerable regions such as the Argentine Pampas, one of the world’s major agricultural zones. This study analyses long-
content: Climate change is intensifying precipitation extremes globally, posing challenges to agriculture and water management in vulnerable regions such as the Argentine Pampas, one of the world’s major agricultural zones. This study analyses long-term evolution of precipitation patterns and extremes in the Argentine Pampas to inform agricultural planning, water management and adaptation strategies. We examine spatiotemporal variability across three time periods: present (2010–2024), near future (2025–2039) and far future (2085–2099). Ten precipitation indices defined by the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI) were assessed using data from 48 meteorolog­ical stations and projections from two global climate models (CCSM4 and CNRM-CM5) under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5 scenarios. Currently, several indices show significant decreasing trends, especially annual precipitation on wet days (Prcptot), where 71% of stations showed statistically significant trends (Mann–Kendall test, p < 0.05), maximum 1-day precipitation (RX1day) at 53% of decreasing stations, and consecutive wet days (CWD) at 73%. However, under the RCP 8.5 far-future scenario, rainfall extremes intensify substantially. Prcptot increases in 65% of stations (+160 mm/15 years), extremely wet days (R99p) increase in 88% of stations (+96 mm/15 years), and heavy precipitation days show marked increases in northern and eastern areas. The northeast emerges as the most vulnerable subregion, while south­ern and western areas show more moderate increases. These findings inform targeted adaptation strategies for man­aging future precipitation variability.

title: From waste management to carbon removal: Assessing municipal solid waste-based BECCS options in the UAE
summary: Municipal solid waste (MSW) treatment systems are increasingly deployed to address waste management challenges, yet their potential contribution to engineered carbon dioxide removal remains underexplored. This study evaluates the techno-eco
tags: Bio-energy with carbon capture and storage
content: Municipal solid waste (MSW) treatment systems are increasingly deployed to address waste management challenges, yet their potential contribution to engineered carbon dioxide removal remains underexplored. This study evaluates the techno-economic performance of two MSW-based pathways capable of delivering negative emissions: thermal incineration with post-combustion carbon capture and storage (INC-CCS) and landfill gas recovery with biomethane upgrading and CO 2 storage (BMU-CCS). Four configurations (INC, INC-CCS, BMU, BMU-CCS) are compared under consistent assumptions for waste throughput, plant performance, and financial parameters calibrated to UAE conditions. Results show that both CCS-enabled pathways achieve net negative emissions, but with markedly different characteristics. INC-CCS provides the largest removal potential (−156 ktCO 2 /y) but at a higher cost (131 US$ 2023 /tCO 2 removed) due to capital requirements and efficiency penalties, increasing electricity costs from 70 to 194 US$ 2023 /MWh. In contrast, BMU-CCS delivers smaller removal volumes (−14.1 ktCO 2 /y) but at a lower cost (51.3 US$ 2023 /tCO 2 removed), reflecting the high purity of the CO 2 stream generated during upgrading and the limited additional infrastructure required. These cost values represent plant-gate capture or separation and CO 2 compression costs and exclude downstream CO 2 transport and geological storage; they should therefore not be interpreted as full-chain CCS or permanent carbon-removal costs. Nevertheless, the findings highlight a fundamental trade-off between the scale of removal and its cost in waste-based bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) systems. The results suggest that MSW treatment infrastructure can contribute meaningfully to net-zero strategies, particularly in regions with limited biomass resources but growing waste streams. While calibrated to the UAE, the framework and insights are applicable to rapidly urbanizing regions worldwide.

title: MUDANÇAS CLIMÁTICAS, MEIO AMBIENTE E AGRICULTURA SUSTENTÁVEL: IMPACTOS SOCIOAMBIENTAIS, CONSERVAÇÃO DOS RECURSOS NATURAIS E PERSPECTIVAS PARA O ALCANCE DOS ODS
summary: As mudanças climáticas representam um desafio crescente à sustentabilidade dos sistemas agrícolas, considerando suas repercussões sobre a conservação dos recursos naturais, a estabilidade dos ecossistemas e as condições socioeconômicas dos
content: As mudanças climáticas representam um desafio crescente à sustentabilidade dos sistemas agrícolas, considerando suas repercussões sobre a conservação dos recursos naturais, a estabilidade dos ecossistemas e as condições socioeconômicas dos territórios rurais. Nesse contexto, a presente pesquisa teve como objetivo analisar as inter-relações entre mudanças climáticas, impactos socioambientais e agricultura sustentável, considerando as estratégias de conservação dos recursos naturais e suas contribuições para o alcance dos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). No que diz respeito aos procedimentos metodológicos, adotou-se uma abordagem qualitativa, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, fundamentada em revisão bibliográfica da literatura científica, mediante análise de publicações em língua portuguesa, compreendidas entre 2020 e 2025, relacionadas às transformações climáticas, à sustentabilidade agropecuária e à gestão ambiental. A interpretação das contribuições teóricas foi organizada em três eixos temáticos, contemplando os impactos socioambientais das mudanças climáticas sobre os sistemas agrícolas, as estratégias de conservação dos recursos naturais e as perspectivas de integração da agricultura sustentável às metas da Agenda 2030. Os resultados evidenciaram que as alterações nos regimes pluviométricos, a elevação das temperaturas e a intensificação de eventos climáticos extremos constituem fatores associados à instabilidade produtiva, à degradação ambiental e à ampliação das vulnerabilidades socioeconômicas, especialmente em territórios caracterizados por limitações estruturais e tecnológicas. Identificou-se, ainda, que práticas conservacionistas de manejo do solo, gestão eficiente dos recursos hídricos, diversificação produtiva, transição agroecológica e incorporação de tecnologias sustentáveis apresentam potencial para fortalecer os agroecossistemas e reduzir pressões sobre os recursos naturais. Nesse cenário, a efetividade dessas estratégias depende da articulação entre políticas públicas, instrumentos de financiamento, assistência técnica e mecanismos participativos de governança socioambiental.

title: Design of a PI-Controlled PWM Three-Phase Rectifier for DC Voltage Regulation in Low-Speed PMSG Wind Energy Systems
source: Journal of Collective Sciences and Sustainability
summary: Wind energy in Malang, Indonesia, generally has low wind speeds, causing voltage fluctuations in the outputs of permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs). This study aims to design and evaluate a three-phase rectifier based on pulse w
content: Wind energy in Malang, Indonesia, generally has low wind speeds, causing voltage fluctuations in the outputs of permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs). This study aims to design and evaluate a three-phase rectifier based on pulse width modulation (PWM) with a proportional-integral (PI) controller to improve DC voltage stability in low-speed wind energy conversion systems. Evaluation was carried out through MATLAB/Simulink and Proteus simulations with variations in the input voltage, duty cycle, and resistive (R) and resistive–inductive (R–L) load conditions. The simulation results revealed that under open-loop conditions, the maximum DC voltage was close to the theoretical value of 64.8 V. At the same time, the duty cycle variation affected the minimum voltage and produced a voltage ripple of approximately 9–10%. The PI controller reduces the voltage ripple to approximately 1–3% and improves the stability of the DC output voltage at input voltages of 36 V and 48 V. The results show that the PI controller can improve the regulatory performance of the PWM rectifier voltage under varying input voltage and load conditions. This study contributes to the development of a PMSG-based wind energy conversion system for areas with low wind potential. Although this study is based on simulation results, it provides a basis for further experimental validation to evaluate the performance of the proposed system under real operating conditions.

title: Beyond Green Rhetoric: How Human Resource Management Bridges Strategy and Sustainability in Hotels
summary: Drawing on the natural resource‐based view (NRBV) and social cognitive theory (SCT), this study examines the relationships among strategic green intentions, green human resource management (Green HRM) practices, sustainable business perform
content: Drawing on the natural resource‐based view (NRBV) and social cognitive theory (SCT), this study examines the relationships among strategic green intentions, green human resource management (Green HRM) practices, sustainable business performance and employee outcomes in Ghana's hospitality industry. Two independent quantitative studies were conducted in star‐rated hotels. Study 1 surveyed 282 managers and supervisors to examine Green HRM practices as mediating mechanisms linking strategic green intentions to economic, social and environmental performance. Study 2 surveyed 302 frontline employees to investigate employee green commitment as a mediator of the relationships between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour and turnover intention. Data were analysed using a disjoint two‐stage PLS‐SEM approach. Study 1 revealed that strategic green intentions were directly associated with social performance but not with economic or environmental performance. Green HRM practices exhibited significant positive indirect effects across all three performance dimensions, with indirect‐only mediation for economic and environmental performance and complementary mediation for social performance. Study 2 demonstrated that employee green commitment significantly mediated the positive relationship between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour. However, neither Green HRM practices nor employee green commitment was significantly associated with turnover intention, and the corresponding indirect effect was nonsignificant. The findings refine NRBV and SCT‐informed explanations by demonstrating differentiated relationships between environmental strategic intentions and sustainability performance, while highlighting the outcome‐specific relevance of employee green commitment. Practically, the research underscores the importance of embedding environmental priorities in credible Green HRM practices while recognising that broader employment outcomes may require complementary employee‐support strategies.

title: Biochar‐Based Controlled‐Release Nitrogen Fertilizers on Maize Production in South Dakota: A Field Study
source: Journal of Sustainable Agriculture and Environment
summary: The efficient management of Nitrogen (N) in corn production remains a major challenge due to low N use efficiency (NUE) and substantial environmental losses from conventional fertilizers. Biochar‐based controlled‐release urea fertilizers (B
content: The efficient management of Nitrogen (N) in corn production remains a major challenge due to low N use efficiency (NUE) and substantial environmental losses from conventional fertilizers. Biochar‐based controlled‐release urea fertilizers (BCRUFs) have been proposed as an alternative that combines the nutrient retention benefits of biochar with the gradual nutrient release of controlled‐release formulations. This 2‐year field study (2022–2023) evaluated the agronomic performance of two BCRUF formulations—non‐coated (BCRUF‐NC, 31.5% N) and polylactic acid‐coated (BCRUF‐C, 30.3% N)—against conventional urea (46.7% N) and Environmentally Smart N (ESN, 44% N) under tilled and no‐till conditions. Fertilizers were applied at 75% of the recommended N rate (134.5 kg/ha) in a randomized complete block design. Mixed‐model analysis revealed significant treatment × tillage interactions for both grain yield and biomass yield, where only tilled sites showed treatment differences compared to the Control. Grain yields under fertilized treatments ranged from 11.23 to 12.00 t ha −1 in tilled sites, significantly different from Control (8.15 t ha −1 ). Soil levels were dynamic, showing significant four‐way interactions between treatment × tillage × depth × growth stage ( p = 0.015). In contrast, and Total soil N % (TN %) were primarily influenced by depth and growth stage ( p < 0.05) rather than specific fertilizer treatments. While NUE for BCRUF‐NC (35.92%‐no till and 46.0%‐tilled) and BCRUF‐C (38.04%‐no till and 47.88%‐tilled) were not significantly different from the urea and Control treatments. This study demonstrates that BCRUFs can achieve yields and NUE similar to conventional fertilizers while enhancing soil N retention under certain conditions. However, their agronomic advantages were inconsistent, indicating the need for multi‐site, long‐term trials to optimize formulation, application strategy, and integration with adaptive management practices.

title: Environmental Computronics: A Theoretical Study on the Fusion of Deep Learning, the Internet of Things and Environmental Management
source: Internet of Things and Cloud Computing
summary: Environmental management has historically depended on sparse field sampling, periodic reporting, and slow regulatory feedback, leaving decision-makers to act on incomplete, delayed, and coarse information in space and time. Two technologica
content: Environmental management has historically depended on sparse field sampling, periodic reporting, and slow regulatory feedback, leaving decision-makers to act on incomplete, delayed, and coarse information in space and time. Two technological movements are now changing that condition. The Internet of Things (IoT) has made dense, continuous and low-cost observation of air, water, soil, climate and waste systems practicable, while deep learning has made it possible to extract structure, forecasts and anomalies from the large, heterogeneous and noisy data streams that such observation produces. This paper proposes and develops the concept of Environmental Computronics, defined as the integrated science and engineering of sensing, communicating, learning from and acting upon environmental systems through networked electronic devices and computational intelligence. Using a theoretical research design built on an integrative review of verifiable peer-reviewed literature and conceptual synthesis, the study traces the intellectual roots of the field in cybernetics, general systems theory, social-ecological systems and resilience thinking, adaptive management, estimation theory and theory-guided data science. It then advances a seven-layer Environmental Computronics Framework (ECF) spanning physical sensing, connectivity, edge intelligence, data fusion and learning, knowledge guidance, decision and actuation, and governance. The framework is expressed formally as a closed-loop, knowledge-guided state-estimation and control problem, and eight testable propositions are derived from it. Applications to air quality, water resources, weather and climate, land and biodiversity, solid waste and the oil and gas sector are examined, followed by a critical appraisal of limitations including data quality, the energy and carbon cost of computation, electronic waste, interpretability, cybersecurity, equity and institutional readiness. The paper concludes that the value of fusing deep learning and IoT for the environment lies not in the technologies themselves but in closing the loop between observation, understanding and accountable action, and it sets out a research agenda for building that loop responsibly, with particular attention to developing-country contexts such as the Niger Delta.

title: Redefining the Role of the Private Sector in the Provision of Urban RTH: An Analysis of the Implementation of Green Building in NIPAH PARK Makassar
summary: Rapid urbanization in Makassar, Indonesia, has contributed to a substantial deficit in urban green open space (Ruang Terbuka Hijau, RTH), which accounted for only 12.42% of the city's area in 2024, considerably below the 30% requirement sti
content: Rapid urbanization in Makassar, Indonesia, has contributed to a substantial deficit in urban green open space (Ruang Terbuka Hijau, RTH), which accounted for only 12.42% of the city's area in 2024, considerably below the 30% requirement stipulated in Law No. 26 of 2007, while built-up areas occupied approximately 75–80% of the urban landscape. This study examined how privately developed commercial infrastructure could function as socioecological infrastructure to help address the urban green space deficit. Employing a descriptive case study with a mixed-methods approach, the research integrated quantitative spatial analysis and qualitative architectural assessment of NIPAH PARK, an open-air commercial development in Makassar. Data were obtained from site plans, regulatory documents, field observations, and operational records. The findings revealed that NIPAH PARK provided 4,241.07 m² of landscaped green space (softscape), with a reported tree canopy coverage ratio of 98.21%, predominantly comprising broad-canopied species such as Terminalia mantaly and Samanea saman. Water conservation measures achieved reported savings of 90.24% in the mall and 89.57% in the office building. The development also functioned as an inclusive privately owned public space (POPS), providing publicly accessible jogging tracks, communal parks, pedestrian crossings, and wheelchair-accessible ramps, supported by systematic waste segregation and tenant fit-out regulations. The study concluded that integrating green building principles into commercial developments could contribute to ecological performance, economic value, and spatial equity. It further recommended that local governments expand conventional two-dimensional land-use planning to incorporate three-dimensional ecological considerations and introduce incentives to encourage compliance with green building standards.

title: Does educational attainment change the association between meat intake and obesity? A case-study from urban Brazil.
summary: Brazil is one of the higher meat producer and consumer worldwide. Recently, the sustainability of the meat market is questioned on regard to its high contribution to climate change and public health concerns such as obesity. Hence, further
content: Brazil is one of the higher meat producer and consumer worldwide. Recently, the sustainability of the meat market is questioned on regard to its high contribution to climate change and public health concerns such as obesity. Hence, further public policies are likely to regulate the meat market and simultaneously reduce meat production and consumption. However, in the context of middle-income countries marked by strong inequalities such as Brazil, the nutritional effect of such market regulation is uncertain. Indeed, one can hypothesize that meat intake plays a protective role against poor nutritious food intake and weight gain among underprivileged settings. To test this hypothesis, this study analyzes household cross-sectional yearly surveys collected from 2018 to 2023 in the 27 Brazilian State capitals. As expected, multivariate estimates show education-specific associations between meat intake and obesity. Among the most educated individuals, declaring not consuming any meat the previous day before the survey is associated with lower body mass index (BMI) and obesity risk, as observed in previous epidemiological studies. By contrast, declaring consuming meat the previous day before the survey appears to be protective against weight gain among poorly educated individuals. We also observe education-specific meat substitution behaviors that help explain these findings. In facts, meat is more likely to be replaced by sweets and ready-to-eat meals among poorly educated individuals compared to more educated ones. We conclude that, everything being equals, meat market regulation policy might worsen public health concerns for under-privileged individuals. Important investments in the education sector and anti-poverty programs are thus needed to limit the raise of nutritional inequalities.

title: Responsive planning of food loss and waste prevention actions over time: a methodological framework using system dynamics
summary: This study presents a system dynamics (SD) model to support exploratory decision-making for dynamic planning of food loss and waste (FLW) prevention actions, focusing on consumer-behavior change to meet Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12
content: This study presents a system dynamics (SD) model to support exploratory decision-making for dynamic planning of food loss and waste (FLW) prevention actions, focusing on consumer-behavior change to meet Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12.3. The model captures temporal dynamics by simulating how behavior-based interventions lose effectiveness over time, allowing planners to determine when and how often to implement such actions to sustain FLW reductions. The SD model integrates life cycle assessment (LCA) principles to quantify the environmental benefits of avoided FLW across all stages of the food-supply chain (FSC). We present a case study on prepared salads in Spain to illustrate the model’s capacity to estimate environmental impacts and assess intervention effectiveness. Scenario analysis of 50 simulations shows that the permanence of behavioral change, not intervention intensity or duration, is the key determinant of long-term system stability and environmental benefit. Results emphasize the strategic importance of timing FLW interventions based on consumption trends and lasting behavioral shifts. The model offers a conceptual planning tool for exploring FLW policies that are both time-responsive and environmentally effective, providing a novel approach to evaluate and schedule consumer-targeted waste-prevention actions within national and regional food systems.

title: ASSESSING ENERGY DEMAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL EMISSIONS ASSOCIATED WITH MODERN AGRICULTURAL MECHANIZATION
source: International Research Journal in Applied Sciences and Engineering
summary: Agricultural mechanization has become an essential component of modern agricultural production, contributing to improved productivity, operational efficiency, and reduced labour requirements. However, the increasing adoption of agricultural
content: Agricultural mechanization has become an essential component of modern agricultural production, contributing to improved productivity, operational efficiency, and reduced labour requirements. However, the increasing adoption of agricultural machinery has intensified energy consumption and raised environmental concerns, particularly greenhouse gas emissions and the depletion of non-renewable energy resources. This study examines energy demand and emission trends associated with agricultural mechanization, highlighting the relationship between technological advancement, energy utilization, and environmental sustainability. It explores direct and indirect energy consumption in agricultural operations, including fuel and electricity use, machinery production, fertilizer application, and other production inputs. The study further emphasizes the importance of energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy adoption, and improved mechanization practices in reducing agricultural emissions. It argues that sustainable agricultural development requires policies and technological innovations that balance productivity improvements with environmental protection and efficient resource utilization. Promoting energy efficiency and low-emission machinery is therefore essential for strengthening agricultural sustainability, improving rural economic development, and mitigating the environmental impacts of agricultural modernization.

title: The Challenges and Opportunities of Artificial Intelligence for Supporting Health Behavior Change in Older Adults: A Research Centers Collaborative Network Workshop Report
summary: Nearly a century of focused behavioral sciences research has attempted to tackle widespread behavioral challenges, including insufficient levels of physical activity, poor quality eating patterns, poor adherence to medical regimens, and mor
content: Nearly a century of focused behavioral sciences research has attempted to tackle widespread behavioral challenges, including insufficient levels of physical activity, poor quality eating patterns, poor adherence to medical regimens, and more. Behavioral scientists are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI)-based technologies to advance the study of behavioral sciences, extend the precision and reach of their programs, and improve their ability to intervene at key moments. There are also new challenges associated with AI technologies, including a discrepancy between the speed of technological development and that of scientific process, ethical and environmental concerns, and the need to ensure that AI-enabled tools are appropriate, accessible, and attractive to diverse older adult users. At this early stage, it is critical that experts from diverse and relevant fields provide their perspectives on opportunities and challenges in the implementation of AI for guiding behavior change in older adults. To this end, the National Institute on Aging Research Centers Collaborative Network hosted a workshop, where a various body of scientific and clinical experts discussed opportunities and challenges regarding the use of AI in behavior change interventions for older adults. We summarize this discussion, highlighting both opportunities and challenges, and present several key areas for future research.

title: ВИЛУЧЕННЯ МЕТАНУ З ВУГІЛЬНИХ ПЛАСТІВ З ОДНОЧАСНИМ ЗАХОРОНЕННЯМ ДІОКСИДУ ВУГЛЕЦЮ
summary: Сучасний етап реалізації екологічної стратегії України в рамках європейського курсу Green Deal вимагає швидкого пошуку та впровадження ефективних промислових технологій уловлювання, використання та захоронення вуглецю CCUS ( Carbon Capture,
content: Сучасний етап реалізації екологічної стратегії України в рамках європейського курсу Green Deal вимагає швидкого пошуку та впровадження ефективних промислових технологій уловлювання, використання та захоронення вуглецю CCUS ( Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage ). Для індустріального сектору України одним із найбільш перспективних рішень є впровадження технології CO₂-ECBM (Enhanced Coal Bed Methane Recovery) — інтенсифікації вилучення метану з вугільних пластів шляхом нагнітання діоксиду вуглецю. Суть технології та ефект подвійного призначення. Технологія базується на нагнітанні діоксиду вуглецю (зокрема у суперкритичному стані sc-CO2 при тисках понад 7,38 МПа та температур вище 31,1 °C) у глибокі, некондиційні для традиційного шахтного видобутку вугільні пласти з метою витіснення адсорбованого метану CH4. Геоекологічна привабливість процесу полягає у синергії двох ефектів: промисловому отриманні екологічно чистого енергоносія (метану) та довгостроковому безпечному захороненні газу CO 2 у вугільній матриці. Це робить технологію ключовим елементом концепції Green Deal та систем декарбонізації енергетичного сектору.
