title: Consequences of Sudden Port Call Changes on Maritime Stakeholders
summary: Sudden changes in port calls are quite frequent and can have significant financial and environmental impacts, yet its normalization in the industry has led to limited research on their effects across supply chains. Addressing this gap, this
content: Sudden changes in port calls are quite frequent and can have significant financial and environmental impacts, yet its normalization in the industry has led to limited research on their effects across supply chains. Addressing this gap, this study explores how sudden port call changes affect different stakeholders involved in the port call process. A multi-stakeholder perspective is adopted through interviews with 32 professionals representing port authorities, terminal operators, shipping lines, cargo owners, logistics and freight forwarding companies, port service providers, maritime software providers, and regulatory agencies across Europe. Using thematic analysis, the study identifies ten impact themes. Queueing of vessels emerged as the most significant consequence, followed by increased costs due to port call changes. Stakeholders also highlight the cascading effects of such changes throughout the value chain. The findings confirm the necessity of streamlining the port call process by integrating Just-In-Time arrivals. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the importance of incorporating the perspectives and concerns of diverse stakeholders when designing improved port call systems and related regulations. This inclusive approach is essential for effective incentivization and the successful adoption of a more streamlined port call process.

title: Materials science scales South Korean energy innovation through universities and concentrates impact in industry
summary: Materials science underpins innovation in resource-poor economies such as South Korea. Here we show that South Korea ranked seventh globally in materials science publication output and sixth in citation impact between 2015 and 2024, while m
content: Materials science underpins innovation in resource-poor economies such as South Korea. Here we show that South Korea ranked seventh globally in materials science publication output and sixth in citation impact between 2015 and 2024, while maintaining the highest researcher density among leading countries. Universities generated most publications and citations, whereas research institutes and corporations achieved higher output and impact per researcher. Analysis of the top 1% most cited papers further revealed a concentration of high impact research in technologies linked to energy and information systems, with batteries, flexible and stretchable devices, and solar and optoelectronic technologies accounting for more than 60% of this segment. Using an integrated bibliometric framework that combines productivity, citation impact, researcher density, collaboration patterns and institutional sector performance, we map the structure of South Korea’s materials science ecosystem and identify the institutional and technological foundations of its research strengths. This framework could support comparative assessments of national research systems and their contributions to strategic technology development.

title: Rock Typing in the Digital Age: A Systematic Review of Petrophysical Foundations, Advanced Conventional Formulations, and the Ascent of Physics-Informed Artificial Intelligence
summary: Petrophysical rock typing (PRT) is the cornerstone of reservoir characterization, bridging microscopic pore-throat morphology and macroscopic dynamic flow behavior to control hydrocarbon-in-place estimates, saturation–height functions, and
content: Petrophysical rock typing (PRT) is the cornerstone of reservoir characterization, bridging microscopic pore-throat morphology and macroscopic dynamic flow behavior to control hydrocarbon-in-place estimates, saturation–height functions, and numerical simulation grid-block properties. For over five decades, reservoir workflows have relied on conventional frameworks rooted in capillary pressure curves (Leverett, 1941; Thomeer, 1960), pore-throat size calibrations (Winland R₃₅; Pittman, 1992), and the modified Kozeny-Carman formulation, most notably the Reservoir Quality Index (RQI) and Flow Zone Indicator (FZI) proposed by Amaefule et al. (1993). However, these classical formulations frequently struggle in complex carbonate systems, tight gas sandstones, and multi-modal reservoirs due to fundamental physical limitations, including the conflation of static capillary storage with dynamic flow capacity, non-Darcy flow regimes, and unresolved multi-scale heterogeneity. This review systematically traces the methodological evolution of rock typing from its historical foundations to the contemporary ascent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). We first evaluate advanced conventional advancements that address classical shortcomings, including the rigorous decoupling of Petrophysical Static Rock Types (PSRT) from Petrophysical Dynamic Rock Types (PDRT), the calibration of effective flow porosity (PHIZ) via Purcell-PSKT porosimetry, and fractal bound-water models for low-permeability rocks. We then conduct an in-depth critical analysis of data-driven AI, examining how unsupervised clustering (Self-Organizing Maps, K-Means, Fuzzy C-Means, DBSCAN) automates electrofacies discovery from multi-well wireline logs, and how supervised tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) and deep architectures predict rock classes and continuous permeability. Crucially, we highlight the paradigm shift toward Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML), where non-Darcy flow physics and mass conservation are embedded directly into loss functions, and Explainable AI (SHAP, LIME) is leveraged to eliminate black-box opacity. We further analyze the revolution in Digital Rock Physics (DRP) and Image-based Microscale Rock Typing (IMRT), which combines micro-CT, FIB-SEM, and deep learning segmentation (PRRT and TSRT) with Lattice Boltzmann flow simulation to provide verifiable ground truth. Finally, we replace speculative risks with an industry-grounded audit of genuine operational pitfalls in AI petrophysics — including spatial autocorrelation data leakage, out-of-distribution extrapolation failure, core-to-log depth-matching errors, and regulatory compliance — and synthesize these insights into a unified, multi-scale, physics-informed digital rock typing roadmap for resilient reservoir modeling.

title: Thin Films of Some Macrocyclic Organic Materials Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensors: A Comprehensive Review on Selective Gas and VOC Detection
summary: This review provides a detailed evaluation of surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors fabricated from thin films based on macrocyclic organic materials, including calixarenes/calixresorcinarenes, pillararenes, porphyrins, and crown ethers,
content: This review provides a detailed evaluation of surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors fabricated from thin films based on macrocyclic organic materials, including calixarenes/calixresorcinarenes, pillararenes, porphyrins, and crown ethers, as reported in the literature. While evaluating the studies, particular emphasis was placed on the structural properties of the sensor surface, host-guest interactions, and the potential for selective detection of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and gas. The SPR technique has been determined to be highly useful for real-time, high-sensitivity measurements with thin films of macrocyclic materials and is highly suitable for accurately obtaining the performance parameters of the fabricated sensor. Langmuir–Blodgett (LB), Langmuir–Schaefer (LS), and spin-coating (SC) methods allow for the controlled growth of functional thin films on solid surfaces, with some significant impact on the sensitivity, reproducibility, and stability of the sensors. Based on the studies examined in this review, insightful information has been provided for the development of gas and VOC sensors with selective, rapid, and significantly lower detection limits using some macrocyclic-based sensing surfaces with a wide range of properties.

title: Oxidative torrefaction of sugarcane bagasse: Effect of temperature and carrier gas oxygen concentration on fuel properties
summary: Sugarcane bagasse (SB), a byproduct of the sugar industry, is an abundant and renewable biomass widely used in Brazil for energy production. However, its high moisture content, low energy density, and poor grindability limit its efficiency
content: Sugarcane bagasse (SB), a byproduct of the sugar industry, is an abundant and renewable biomass widely used in Brazil for energy production. However, its high moisture content, low energy density, and poor grindability limit its efficiency as a fuel. This study investigates oxidative torrefaction as a thermochemical pre-treatment to improve SB’s fuel properties, comparing the effects of different oxygen concentrations in the carrier gas (0%, 10%, and 20%) at torrefaction temperatures ranging from 200 °C to 300 °C for 30 minutes. The results show that oxidative torrefaction enhances the fixed carbon content and high heating value of SB, while reducing volatile matter and mass yield. Notably, the presence of oxygen in the carrier gas promoted internal heat generation, a phenomenon known as overheating, which enabled improved biomass quality at lower temperatures. This study aims to address a gap in literature by exploring the oxidative torrefaction behavior of sugarcane bagasse and reporting the occurrence of the overheating phenomenon, both of which have received limited attention in previous studies. Despite lower energy and mass yields, the enhancement factor increased significantly under oxidative conditions, indicating improved fuel quality. These findings suggest that oxidative torrefaction offers a promising route for upgrading sugarcane bagasse for bioenergy applications.

title: Decoding the inflammatory tumor microenvironment: cellular interactions and functional reprogramming
summary: Cancer-associated inflammation is a central driver of tumor progression, immune escape, and therapeutic resistance. However, the inflammatory tumor microenvironment (TME) should not be viewed merely as a collection of soluble cytokines or c
content: Cancer-associated inflammation is a central driver of tumor progression, immune escape, and therapeutic resistance. However, the inflammatory tumor microenvironment (TME) should not be viewed merely as a collection of soluble cytokines or chemokines. Emerging single-cell, spatial, and functional studies indicate that inflammation operates through dynamic multicellular communication networks involving tumor cells, macrophages, fibroblasts, neutrophils, dendritic cells, NK cells, and T cells. These interactions generate either immunosuppressive circuits or immune-activating niches depending on cellular state, spatial organization, metabolic pressure, and treatment context. In this review, we decode the inflammatory TME as a functional ecosystem organized by tumor-cell-intrinsic inflammatory programs, myeloid and stromal suppressive circuits, regulatory and B-cell states, vascular control of immune trafficking, cDC1–CD8 + T-cell immune niches, and CD8 + T-cell functional reprogramming. We further discuss how cross-cutting regulatory compartments (Tregs, B cells, MDSCs, and endothelial cells) and shared inflammatory, metabolic, and stromal factors-including PGE2, IL-6, lipid metabolic stress, obesity-associated inflammation, acidosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ECM/collagen remodeling—connect these modules and shape immune suppression, productive antitumor immunity, and therapeutic response. Finally, we highlight therapeutic strategies aimed at selectively reprogramming harmful inflammatory circuits while preserving productive antitumor immune niches. This framework may support the development of inflammatory TME signatures for predicting immunotherapy response and guiding rational combination therapies.

title: Beyond dysbiosis: the SCIM axis as a functional framework for integrating bacterial soluble and extracellular vesicle signals in colorectal cancer
summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is associated with alterations in the gut microbiota. Changes in microbial composition alone do not adequately explain how these communities influence mucosal homeostasis, immune regulation, and tumor-associated infl
content: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is associated with alterations in the gut microbiota. Changes in microbial composition alone do not adequately explain how these communities influence mucosal homeostasis, immune regulation, and tumor-associated inflammation. The persistence of beneficial commensals within dysbiotic ecosystems challenges the assumption that microbial presence reflects functional activity. Although microbial metabolites and bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are increasingly recognized as mediators of host–microbiota communication, their relative contributions and interactions remain insufficiently resolved in CRC. Here, we propose the SCIM axis—Short-chain fatty acid production, Control of mucin dynamics, Immunomodulation, and Mucosal integrity—as a framework for investigating the functional state of the intestinal mucosa. We hypothesize that mucosal homeostasis depends not only on microbial activities but also on their integration with host responses. Accordingly, disruption of metabolic and extracellular signaling networks may contribute to functional insufficiency even when commensal populations remain detectable. Within this framework, soluble bacterial products and BEVs represent communication routes whose effects may vary according to microbial origin, molecular cargo, epithelial barrier status, and inflammatory context. In particular, BEVs provide a route for delivering microbial proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and cell-envelope components to epithelial and immune cells, thereby engaging innate immune sensing pathways and shaping mucosal inflammatory responses. To translate this hypothesis into a testable model, we outline readouts for each SCIM component: short-chain fatty acid profiling and microbial functional gene analysis; MUC2 expression, mucus organization, and mucinolytic activity; cytokine profiles and TLR/NOD–NF-κB-associated signaling; and epithelial barrier assessment through transepithelial electrical resistance, permeability assays, and tight junction markers. We further propose fractionation and reconstitution strategies to distinguish vesicle-associated activities from soluble factors and determine whether their effects are independent, additive, synergistic, or antagonistic. Commensals, including Akkermansia , Roseburia , and Faecalibacterium , together with CRC-associated pathobionts such as Fusobacterium nucleatum , provide biological contexts in which to investigate these relationships. By connecting microbial activity, extracellular communication, and host responses, the SCIM axis offers an approach to studying mucosal functional sufficiency and its disruption in CRC. Rather than introducing another taxonomic signature, this framework provides a basis for evaluating mechanisms of microbiota-associated mucosal dysfunction and, following validation, may inform biomarker and microbiome-directed therapeutic development.

title: Post‐Synthetic Ligand Modification of a MOF‐74 Analogue via Criss‐Cross Cycloaddition of Azine Linkages With Isocyanates for Toluene Removal
summary: Modifying the pore environment of MOF‐74‐type frameworks remains challenging because existing functionalization strategies often suffer from limited versatility, poor reproducibility, or compromised structural stability. Herein, we report a
content: Modifying the pore environment of MOF‐74‐type frameworks remains challenging because existing functionalization strategies often suffer from limited versatility, poor reproducibility, or compromised structural stability. Herein, we report a post‐synthetic ligand modification strategy for Mg 2 (hob) (hob 4− = 5,5′‐(hydrazine‐1,2‐diylidenebis(methanylylidene))bis(2‐oxidobenzoate)), a MOF‐74 analogue containing reactive azine linkages, through criss‐cross cycloaddition with alkyl isocyanates of varying chain lengths. The resulting Mg 2 (hob)‐Cx series (x = 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 18) was comprehensively characterized, confirming the formation of bicyclic fused‐ring structures throughout the framework. Incorporation of alkyl chains systematically increased pore hydrophobicity, as evidenced by contact‐angle measurements and water‐vapor sorption analyses. Compared with pristine Mg 2 (hob), the modified frameworks exhibited significantly enhanced stability under humid conditions, with Mg 2 (hob)‐C8 to Mg 2 (hob)‐C18 retaining their crystallinity after exposure to 90% relative humidity. Furthermore, the hydrophobic pore environment improved toluene adsorption under humid conditions, with Mg 2 (hob)‐C8 displaying the best balance between adsorption capacity and moisture tolerance. This work demonstrates that isocyanate‐based criss‐cross cycloaddition provides an effective route for framework‐wide post‐synthetic ligand modification, enabling the design of hydrophobic MOFs with enhanced environmental stability and adsorption performance.

title: Discovery of a phenylalanine hydroxylase stabilizer that lowers blood phenylalanine in PahR408W/R408W phenylketonuria mice
summary: Background: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inherited metabolic disease that is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the liver enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), which metabolizes blood phenylalanine (Phe) to tyrosine (Tyr). The result
content: Background: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inherited metabolic disease that is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the liver enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), which metabolizes blood phenylalanine (Phe) to tyrosine (Tyr). The result is the systemic accumulation of Phe in the body that can lead to neurotoxic effects if left untreated. Numerous mutations in PAH lead to the destabilization and misfolding of the enzyme that result in PKU. Methods: A cellular phenotypic assay was developed to identify compounds that could stabilize PAH and increase the conversion rate of Phe to Tyr. Screening hits were then used to design an exemplar compound which was scaled up and crystallized with purified enzyme to determine the PAH binding site, and also orally dosed to mice engineered with the most common mutation that causes PKU in humans, R408W. Results: Here, we report the discovery of a small-molecule chaperone that promotes stabilization of PAH R408W both in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, this molecule restores the endogenous metabolic pathway, thus normalizing the elevated blood Phe concentrations of the PAH R408W homozygous mice. Conclusions: These studies demonstrate in a preclinical mouse model that use of a drug-like small-molecule pharmacological chaperone can be a viable approach for the treatment of severe PKU.

title: Functional changes of testicular Sertoli cells induced by prenatal caffeine exposure and their mechanisms
summary: Our previous studies have shown that prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) can impair the function of testicular Leydig cells in offspring, but its effect on Sertoli cells remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to investigate the changes of in
content: Our previous studies have shown that prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) can impair the function of testicular Leydig cells in offspring, but its effect on Sertoli cells remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to investigate the changes of inhibited WT1 expression in testicular Sertoli cells induced by PCE in offspring rats and its underlying mechanisms. Pregnant Wistar rats were orally administered with caffeine at doses of 30, 60, and 120 mg/kg·d from gestational day (GD) 9 to 20. The results showed that PCE led to abnormal testicular morphology and decreased expression of Sertoli cell development marker genes (Wt1 and Sox9) in offspring. After birth, the Sertoli cells’ secretory function was impaired (reduced levels of ABP and INH-β), and the expression of blood-testis barrier constituents (Cx43) was decreased. PCE increased sperm deformity and reduced sperm motility at PW12, whereas chronic stress additionally reduced sperm count and further aggravated sperm abnormalities. Under the conditions tested, corticosterone reduced the expression of several Sertoli cell markers in TM4 cells. Caffeine treatment did not significantly change the mRNA levels of these markers. The molecular and cell intervention experiments support a potential role for GR/P300/miR-199a-5p/WT1 signaling in the Sertoli cell changes associated with prenatal caffeine exposure.

title: Suspended TiO 2 /AlGaN/GaN Synaptic‐Like Photodetectors With Integrated Microheaters for Spatially Resolved UV Discharge Monitoring
summary: Partial discharge in power grids emits weak ultraviolet (UV) signals, yet continuous spatial imaging with sensitivity remains challenging for conventional sensors. Although standard photodetectors suffer from low signal‐to‐noise ratio (SNR)
content: Partial discharge in power grids emits weak ultraviolet (UV) signals, yet continuous spatial imaging with sensitivity remains challenging for conventional sensors. Although standard photodetectors suffer from low signal‐to‐noise ratio (SNR) and high‐power consumption, synaptic‐like designs utilizing persistent photoconductance (PPC) address these issues through in‐sensor integration but face difficulty in resetting the conductance state. We demonstrate a suspended TiO 2 /AlGaN/GaN synaptic‐like UV photodetector with an on‐chip Pt microheater. Oxygen vacancies in TiO 2 and donor‑impurity X (DX) centers in AlGaN serve as optically writable and thermally erasable traps that modulate the AlGaN/GaN two‑dimensional electron gas (2DEG), enabling time‑integrated sensing and thermal reset. The suspended membrane confines Joule heating to the active region, allowing reset within 2 s. Under 365 nm at 0.42 µW/cm 2 , the device exhibits a photoconductive gain of 2.8 × 10 7 and a responsivity of 2.12 × 10 6 A/W, with stable operation over 120 cycles. A 3 × 3 array enables spatially resolved detection with improved contrast, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) distinguishes corona‑ and arc‑like patterns from simulated images. These results support the use of this detector array for partial discharge inspection in power systems.

title: Deciphering key root traits involved in phosphorus deficiency tolerance of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)
summary: Background and Aims: Crops adapt to phosphorus (P) deficiency primarily by modifying their root system. A high-throughput phenotyping platform was used to identify root traits linked to P-deficiency tolerance in 30 bread-wheat ( Triticum ae
content: Background and Aims: Crops adapt to phosphorus (P) deficiency primarily by modifying their root system. A high-throughput phenotyping platform was used to identify root traits linked to P-deficiency tolerance in 30 bread-wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes. Methods P acquisition efficiency (PAE), P use efficiency (PUE) and phosphorus-related acquisition efficiency (PRAE) were estimated with three indicators. Plants were grown under controlled, low-P conditions on a non-destructive phenotyping platform. After 30 days, shoot biomass was recorded and a deep-root phenotyping pipeline quantified a range of root morphological traits and their dynamics. Relations between root traits and the three P-efficiency indicators were explored, including a Random-Forest analysis. Results The screening distinguished genotypes with contrasting capacities to acquire and/or use P under limitation. Random-Forest analysis showed that PAE and PUE were mainly associated with total root length, exploration area and root density, whereas PRAE exhibited only weak links with the measured morphometric traits. Conclusion Combining static root morphometrics with dynamic, non-destructive monitoring allowed the identification of traits characterising the most P-efficient genotypes and clarified whether they relate to acquisition or utilization under low-P conditions.

title: Hyperconjugation‐Mediated Design of Dissolution‐Resistant Organic Cathode for Durable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
summary: Small‐molecule organic carbonyl compounds (SMOCCs) have emerged as promising cathode candidates for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) by virtue of their high theoretical capacity and tunable redox potential. However, their practical implem
content: Small‐molecule organic carbonyl compounds (SMOCCs) have emerged as promising cathode candidates for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) by virtue of their high theoretical capacity and tunable redox potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by intrinsically poor electronic conductivity and pronounced dissolution in aqueous electrolytes, leading to unsatisfactory rate capability and cyclic stability. Herein, we report a hyper‐conjugative structural design strategy to construct a TAPT@rGO composite, in which 2,3,5,6‐tetraamino‐1,4‐benzoquinone (TABQ) and 1,10‐phenanthroline‐5，6‐dione (PTD) are covalently integrated with graphene oxide (GO) to yield a nitrogen‐heteroatom‐extended conjugated framework. This architecture not only ensures homogeneous dispersion of nanosized TAPT crystallites on the rGO substrate, but also establishes an N‐heterocycle‐mediated extended conjugation linkage between the organic species and the carbon scaffold, which synergistically enhances electronic transport kinetics and suppresses active material dissolution. As a cathode for AZIBs, the TAPT@rGO composite delivers a high initial capacity of 271 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 with an average operating voltage of 0.8 V, together with exceptional cycling stability (93.5% capacity retention over 100 cycles at 0.1 A g −1 and 82.5% retention over 10000 cycles at 5 A g −1 ). This work demonstrates that hyperconjugation engineering provides a rational molecular design for developing high‐performance organic cathodes toward durable multivalent ion storage.

title: Synergistically Driven Catalytic Activity in Amorphous–Crystalline CoCe–NiMo‐Oxide Heterostructures for Efficient Ampere‐Level Water Splitting
summary: To counter the environmental issues, recently hydrogen has emerged as a substitute candidate for fossil fuels which can produce via electrolysis of the water requiring efficient electrocatalyst. In this work, we synthesized amorphous–crysta
content: To counter the environmental issues, recently hydrogen has emerged as a substitute candidate for fossil fuels which can produce via electrolysis of the water requiring efficient electrocatalyst. In this work, we synthesized amorphous–crystalline heterostructured CoCe–NiMo composite electrocatalysts via a single‐step hydrothermal technique, and their interface‐engineered electrochemical properties are investigated. CoCe–NiMo composite electrocatalyst shows enhanced HER activity with the lowest overpotential of 129 mV at current density of 10 mA cm −2 and Tafel slope of 117 mV dec −1 . Remarkably, it achieved an industrial‐grade current density of 1000 mA cm −2 only at 486 mV, excellent operational stability, and maximum current density of 2500 mA cm −2 . The overall water splitting (OWS) activity of the electrolyzer fabricated using CoCe–NiMo at cathode (HER) and CoCe at anode (OER) obtained current density of 10 mA cm −1 only at a cell voltage of 1.66 V, whereas an industrial‐grade current density of 800 mA cm −2 is also achieved at lowest voltage of 2.28 V. Moreover, the OWS performance at elevated temperature of 55°C with 6 M KOH electrolyte was further reduced to 1.53 V and 2.33 V to achieve current density of 10 and 2000 mA cm −2 demonstrating its commercial applicability. The excellent electrochemical properties and durability at harsh condition in alkaline medium suggesting the potential of the CoCe–NiMo‐based catalyst for commercial electrolyzers.

title: Residual LiF‐Derived Interfacial Engineering Enables Stable SiO x /Spent Graphite Anodes With Fast Li + Transport and Superior Interfacial Stability
summary: Although SiO x /graphite composite anodes can mitigate SiO x volume expansion and poor electronic conductivity, loose physical contact between both phases leads to suboptimal performance. Meanwhile, large‐scale disposal of spent graphite (S
content: Although SiO x /graphite composite anodes can mitigate SiO x volume expansion and poor electronic conductivity, loose physical contact between both phases leads to suboptimal performance. Meanwhile, large‐scale disposal of spent graphite (SG) remains a challenge. SG contains residual LiF and LiF‐derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) components. Herein, we propose integrating SG with SiO x via mechanical ball milling. Mechanical forces roughen SiO x surfaces and embed LiF, distributing lithiation and delithiation stresses, minimizing volume mismatch with graphite layers, and promoting intimate contact. An optimal SiO x ‐to‐SG mass ratio of 8:2 ensures capacity and electrochemical performance. LiF modulates interfacial side reactions, absorbs mechanical stress, harmonizes interfacial electronic structures, and enhances Li + diffusion kinetics and structural stability. The SiO x /SG half‐cell with 2 wt.% LiF delivers 766.8 mAh g −1 at 2 C and retains 921.4 mAh g −1 after 200 cycles at 400 mA g −1 (80.1% capacity retention). The full cell paired with NCM811 also exhibits improved cycling stability. Further FEC‐free tests support a beneficial role of pre‐introduced LiF in interfacial impedance evolution, Li + diffusion kinetics, and cycling performance. Applicable to diverse SG types, this study highlights a sustainable interfacial engineering strategy for high‐value SG recycling and durable high‐capacity SiO x anodes, offering economic and environmental benefits.

title: Interfacial Transition-Metal Reduction, Surface Oxygen Depletion and LiNbO 3 Protection in NCM622/Li 6 PS 5 Cl Cathodes Resolved by In Situ Nanoscale XPEEM
summary: Degradation at the cathode-solid electrolyte interface limits high-energy-density sulfide-based allsolid-state batteries. For Ni-rich LiNi 0.6 Mn 0.2 Co 0.2 O 2 (NCM622), cathode surface reduction and electrolyte oxidation are coupled throu
content: Degradation at the cathode-solid electrolyte interface limits high-energy-density sulfide-based allsolid-state batteries. For Ni-rich LiNi 0.6 Mn 0.2 Co 0.2 O 2 (NCM622), cathode surface reduction and electrolyte oxidation are coupled through interfacial (electro-)chemical reactions. Although LiNbO 3 coatings are known to mitigate interfacial resistance growth, their effect on this coupling during operation remains unclear. Here, we combine operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and in situ X-ray photoemission electron microscopy (XPEEM) to follow the chemical evolution of the NCM622 surface and interfaces with Li 6 PS 5 Cl (LPSCl) with depth sensitivity and nanoscale spatial resolution. Already at open-circuit potential, reduced transition-metals, oxygendeficient domains and sulfate species co-localize where NCM622 particles contact LPSCl. Upon high-voltage charging, electrochemically inactive Ni 2+ , Co 2+ , and Mn 2+/3+ species become enriched at these contact regions, while oxygen depletion propagates inward across the particle surface. The LiNbO 3 coating suppresses transition-metal reduction, improves surface electrochemical activity by increasing surface Ni and Co oxidation and confines oxygen depletion to the contact regions. Residual degradation nevertheless persists, consistent with inhomogeneous LiNbO 3 coating coverage and its partial decomposition at high voltage. These findings provide nanoscale insight evidence that cathode and electrolyte degradation are interdependent and coupled through oxygen activity at the cathode surface and that effective coatings must suppress the cathode surface degradation.

title: Physics-Informed Cascade Neural Network for Reliable Prediction of CO2/H2O Co-Electrolysis in SOEC
summary: Co-electrolysis of CO 2 /H 2 O in solid oxide electrochemical cell (SOEC) is an emerging technology for renewable hydrogen and synthetic fuels. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Cascade Neural Network (PCNN) for reliable multi-objectiv
content: Co-electrolysis of CO 2 /H 2 O in solid oxide electrochemical cell (SOEC) is an emerging technology for renewable hydrogen and synthetic fuels. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Cascade Neural Network (PCNN) for reliable multi-objective performance prediction. PCNN integrates a cascade propagation mechanism to capture causal relationships among variables, an adaptive weighting strategy using homoscedastic uncertainty for multi-objective optimization, and a physics-informed grey-box architecture to identify hidden non-ideal parameters. Trained on published SOEC data and validated with independent experiments, PCNN consistently outperforms conventional artificial neural network (ANN), convolutional neural network (CNN), cascade-forward neural network (CFNN), and physics-informed neural network (PINN) models, achieving over 99% prediction accuracy. It also estimates Faradaic efficiency and non-ideal heat loss, improving interpretability and reducing the mean relative residual of mass conservation from 9.02% to 3.21%. This framework offers a general methodology for intelligent modeling and control of SOEC co-electrolysis and other electrochemical energy conversion systems.

title: Autonomous Water Infrastructure Management for High-Demand Facilities: A Hierarchical AI Framework Integrating Physics-Informed Digital Twins and Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning
source: American Journal of Innovation in Science and Engineering
summary: Municipal water distribution systems operating under conventional SCADA-based supervisory control lose between 28% and 35% of treated production volume before delivery to registered consumer meters, a failure rate attributable to static hyd
content: Municipal water distribution systems operating under conventional SCADA-based supervisory control lose between 28% and 35% of treated production volume before delivery to registered consumer meters, a failure rate attributable to static hydraulic model parameterization and decoupled subsystem architectures rather than to any fundamental physical constraint. This paper presents a unified framework coupling a continuously self-calibrating physics-informed digital twin, a hierarchical reinforcement learning controller decomposed via Lagrangian relaxation across three operational tiers, and a temporal fusion transformer whose probabilistic quantile outputs propagate directly into the controller’s risk-sensitive reward function. Evaluated on a 1,847-node, 312 km distribution network serving four hyperscale data center facilities over a 12-month period, the framework achieves a 33.3% reduction in non-revenue water loss, a 29.3% reduction in specific energy consumption, and a 90.7% reduction in pipe burst detection latency relative to the SCADA baseline operating on identical sensor and tariff infrastructure.

title: Beyond measurement: analytical chemistry as a driver of sustainable innovation in the biomethane industry and hydrogen sulfide removal
summary: Analytical chemistry has traditionally supported industrial processes through composition analysis, quality control, process monitoring, and regulatory compliance. However, its role can extend beyond measurement. The increasing complexity o
content: Analytical chemistry has traditionally supported industrial processes through composition analysis, quality control, process monitoring, and regulatory compliance. However, its role can extend beyond measurement. The increasing complexity of industrial processes and the need to reduce their environmental impact create opportunities for analytical data to contribute directly to the design, selection, and optimization of new technological solutions. Biomethane production provides a relevant example. Raw biogas is a chemically variable mixture containing methane and carbon dioxide together with hydrogen sulfide, volatile organic compounds, siloxanes, ammonia, and other contaminants. Their concentrations depend strongly on feedstock and operating conditions, making reliable analytical characterization essential for process control and gas upgrading. At the same time, analytical information can support the development of new purification technologies. In particular, deep eutectic solvents illustrate this transition well. Their composition can be varied over a broad chemical space, while experimental analysis combined with molecular modeling can be used to identify systems with favorable H 2 S capacity, selectivity, absorption kinetics, and regeneration behavior. This perspective discusses biomethane purification as a case study for a broader role of analytical chemistry in industry. We argue that analytical chemistry can form a link between molecular-level understanding, material selection, process optimization, and industrial decision-making. In this framework, measurement is not the endpoint of analytical work but a part of an iterative process leading from characterization to technological development.

title: An optimized sustainable task scheduling using TOPSIS integrated quantum firefly algorithm in cloud environments
summary: Sustainability has emerged as a fundamental requirement in modern healthcare systems, particularly within cloud computing environments where the efficient scheduling of computational tasks directly impacts environmental and economic outcome
content: Sustainability has emerged as a fundamental requirement in modern healthcare systems, particularly within cloud computing environments where the efficient scheduling of computational tasks directly impacts environmental and economic outcomes. Task scheduling problem in cloud based healthcare inherently NP-Hard due to the increasing volume of tasks, the heterogeneity of VMs, and the necessity to optimize multiple conflicting objectives, including cost, energy consumption, carbon emissions, and makespan. Some popular Multi-objective optimization techniques offer a robust framework for navigating these trade-offs, promoting resource efficiency and environmental responsibility. This study proposed T-QFA, a hybrid multi-objective task scheduling algorithm using Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) and Quantum Firefly Algorithm (QFA) optimizing the sustainability along with the client’s quality of services line costspan, makespan, etc. The effectiveness and performance of the T-QFA in a heterogeneous scheduling environment has been investigated against several state of the art algorithms namely, the QFA, TOPSIS, Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II, and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III. The outcome of the results demonstrate that T-QFA consistently outperforms other methods, achieving the lowest cost (64.690316 cost units), energy consumption (0.293531 kwh), carbon emissions (0.143963 kg $CO_{2}$), and makespan (7.118351 time units) comparative to the competitive algorithms. These findings underscore the potential of T-QFA in significantly advancing the sustainability and operational efficiency of healthcare cloud infrastructures.

title: An automated, flexible system for dish preparation and labelling in assisted reproductive technology
summary: The demand for fertility services is increasing, yet in vitro fertilization (IVF) laboratories remain dependent on manual procedures that are difficult to scale and standardize, such as culture dish preparation, a critical and time-sensitiv
content: The demand for fertility services is increasing, yet in vitro fertilization (IVF) laboratories remain dependent on manual procedures that are difficult to scale and standardize, such as culture dish preparation, a critical and time-sensitive process. We developed a programmable automated dish preparation system (ADPS​) that integrates laser-based dish marking for identification, automated pipetting and dish handling, and environmental control. We assessed weight consistency and preparation time in 328 dishes across six use-case configurations including wells, microdroplets, large volumes, and an oil overlay. We also evaluated pH, osmolality, and biocompatibility through mouse embryo assays (MEA). The ADPS produced dishes with a weight coefficient of variation ranging from 0.6% to 2.2%, and bicarbonate buffered media remained within acceptable pH ranges at 24 h of incubation. Rapid and simultaneous automated oil overlay application reduced evaporation, preserving osmo​lality. Mean preparation times ranged from 17.1 ± 4.8 to 126.0 ± 3.6 s per dish, depending on complexity and volumes. Three biocompatibility experiments (laser-marked dishes, media exposed to the ADPS environment, and fully automated preparation) showed expanded blastocyst formation rates above the acceptance threshold of 80%. Optical coherence tomography imaging found no dish surface changes after laser marking, and air quality parameters (volatile organic compounds, formaldehyde) within the unit remained within recommended thresholds, though particle counts exceeded targets in the workshop testing environment. The system offers flexible configurations, standardization, biocompatibility, and potential for standalone operation or integration with downstream IVF automation systems.

title: FireNet-D5: A genetic algorithm-optimized architecture with BiFPN and SE attention for multi-class indoor fire and smoke detection
summary: Fire safety can be significantly improved using deep learning (DL) models, which reduce false alarms and enable reliable real-time detection. However, existing DL-based object detectors often struggle with achieving consistent accuracy and
content: Fire safety can be significantly improved using deep learning (DL) models, which reduce false alarms and enable reliable real-time detection. However, existing DL-based object detectors often struggle with achieving consistent accuracy and efficient multi-class detection of indoor fire and smoke due to complex environmental dynamics. This study introduces the FireNet-D5 model for effective indoor fire and smoke detection to address these challenges. FireNet-D5 incorporates a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention module in the backbone to strengthen feature representation and a Bi-directional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) in the neck for multi-scale feature fusion. The model is further optimized using a genetic algorithm to determine optimal hyperparameters, while Grad-CAM is applied to ensure transparency of model predictions in safety-critical settings. To evaluate performance, a new indoor fire and smoke dataset (ISFire-4) is created, containing four classes: Blue Fire, Black Smoke, Yellow-Orange Fire, and White-Gray Smoke. FireNet-D5 and six benchmark object detection models are re-implemented and trained on ISFire-4. Statistical analysis using Cohen's d validates practical significance, showing FireNet-D5 improves mAP@0.5 by 3.0%, reduces parameters by 3.3%, and provides a 32% comparative difference in effect size relative to its baseline configuration. Five-seed evaluation confirms stable performance, and cross-dataset testing shows improved generalization with respect to the existing methods. These results highlight that the proposed model enables intelligent fire safety management while improving detection reliability, emergency response, and decision-making.

title: Date palm waste-derived ozonized and nutrient doped biochar and carbon dots for heavy metals removal from multi-metal contaminated water
summary: Heavy metal (HM) contamination of surface water and groundwater from mining, industrial effluents and agrochemical sources is a persistent global problem. Converting agricultural waste into biochar offers a low-cost, circular route to overc
content: Heavy metal (HM) contamination of surface water and groundwater from mining, industrial effluents and agrochemical sources is a persistent global problem. Converting agricultural waste into biochar offers a low-cost, circular route to overcome this problem; however, pyrolysis destroys much of the oxygen-bearing surface functionality on which HM binding depends. Post-pyrolysis oxidation or nutrient enrichment could restore this functionality. Therefore, date palm waste biochar (BC) pyrolyzed at 500°C was engineered through ozonization, nutrient doping with N, P and K and hydrothermal conversion into carbon dots (CD), alone and combined, yielding eight pyrolysis-derived materials characterized and tested for Pb 2+ , Cd 2+ , Mn 2+ and Zn 2+ removal from contaminated aqueous solution. Pyrolysis process increased the BET surface area from 4.30 to 52.32 m 2 g − 1 (12-fold), yet ozonization and nutrient doping decreased it to by 35% to 72%, while restoring C–O–C, C–O and Si–O functionality and forming crystalline mineral phases. At pH 5 and 1 g L − 1 , nutrient-doped ozonized carbon dots (NOCD) increased Pb 2+ removal from 43% to 97% and Langmuir capacity by 50% to 158% for all four competing metals, although Pb 2+ was retained preferentially (Pb 2+ > Zn 2+ > Cd 2+ > Mn 2+ ). The uptake of HM increased with reducing surface area, indicating restored surface chemistry, not porosity, governed performance with pseudo-second-order kinetics and Dubinin–Radushkevich isotherm indicating monolayer chemisorption via complexation, cation exchange and surface precipitation. These results show that post-pyrolysis oxidative and nutrient functionalization can engineer pyrolysis into a scalable, low-cost sorbent for remediating multi-metal contaminated water.

title: Ba-Modified Bi4Ti3O12 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Electrochemical Energy Storage and Photocatalytic Methylene Blue (MB) Degradation
summary: To study the effect of Ba-substitution on the morphological, optical, structural and electrochemical and photo catalytic properties of Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 nanoparticles (NPs), the Ba-modified Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 NPs were successfully synthesized. XPS
content: To study the effect of Ba-substitution on the morphological, optical, structural and electrochemical and photo catalytic properties of Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 nanoparticles (NPs), the Ba-modified Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 NPs were successfully synthesized. XPS, XRD and EDX confirmed the formation of bismuth titanate crystal structure and phase purity. Non-linear GCD profiles indicated that a pseudo capacitive charge-storage mechanism and electrochemical analysis demonstrated a significant dependence on a specific Ba concentration. The optimized BBTO-2 composition exhibited a maximum specific capacitance(Cs) of 691 Fg − 1 at 1 Ag − 1 due to improved interfacial ion-transport kinetics and reduced charge-transfer resistance, as demonstrated by electrochemical EIS and Bode analysis. Moreover, the optimized sample showed better catalytic activity toward the photo catalytic degradation of methylene blue (MB) under solar light irradiation with 87% degradation efficiency within 80 min. Results demonstrate that the controlled Ba modification can be utilized to synthesize the multifunctional Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 NPs, applications in energy storage and environmental application.

title: Leaf‐Inspired Porous Cement‐Based Solar Evaporator With Integrated Water Transport and Thermal Insulation for Stable Wastewater Purification
summary: Solar interfacial evaporation offers a highly promising sustainable strategy for wastewater purification, while existing evaporators still face challenges such as wet‐state structural instability and the difficulty of simultaneously achievi
content: Solar interfacial evaporation offers a highly promising sustainable strategy for wastewater purification, while existing evaporators still face challenges such as wet‐state structural instability and the difficulty of simultaneously achieving efficient water transport and thermal insulation. To address these limitations, a plant‐leaf‐inspired biomimetic porous cement‐based evaporator consisting of a carbon black photothermal conversion layer and a porous cement‐based matrix is designed in this work. The upper layer is responsible for converting light energy into thermal energy, while the lower matrix integrates capillary water transport, thermal insulation, and structural support. The rough porous structure and carbon black synergistically enhance light capture, achieving a solar absorptance of approximately 98%. Meanwhile, the interconnected porous structure continuously delivers water to the evaporation interface, whereas closed pores suppress heat dissipation. The evaporator achieves an evaporation rate of 1.83 kg m −2 h −1 under an irradiation intensity of 1 kW m −2 . Simulated industrial wastewater tests further demonstrate its effective retention of heavy metal ions and dye molecules, highlighting its potential for low‐cost and scalable wastewater treatment.

title: Preparation of Sn/Na-Co3O4 Nanospheres for Improved Triethylamine Sensing Performance Research
summary: Here, a series of Sn/Na co-doped Co 3 O 4 nanospheres are synthesized by a one-step solvothermal method. The gas sensing performance of Co 3 O 4 -based nanospheres toward triethylamine is investigated in detail. The optimal operating temper
content: Here, a series of Sn/Na co-doped Co 3 O 4 nanospheres are synthesized by a one-step solvothermal method. The gas sensing performance of Co 3 O 4 -based nanospheres toward triethylamine is investigated in detail. The optimal operating temperature of 1%Sn5%Na-Co 3 O 4 nanospheres to 100 ppm triethylamine is lower 20 ℃ than that of pure Co 3 O 4 . Compared with pure Co 3 O 4 , the response of 1%Sn5%Na-Co 3 O 4 nanospheres is increased by approximately 7.2 times. Furthermore, the 1%Sn5%Na-Co 3 O 4 sensor exhibits better anti-humidity and lower detection limit. At last, the possible gas mechanism is discussed according to the modulation of the Co 3 O 4 microstructure and surface chemistry by co-doping Sn/Na. Therefore, the Sn/Na-Co 3 O 4 nanospheres offer new insights for the design of triethylamine sensors and provide potential application in food safety monitoring and the early detection of fish spoilage.

title: Segregated Actuator Based on Micro‐Foamed Films Featuring Beneficial Load‐Bearing Capacity and Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Performance
summary: Soft actuators serve as essential functional units for intelligent flexible equipment and extreme‐environment actuating devices. Traditional dense‐film actuators suffer from heavy weight and poor radiation stability, which greatly restrict
content: Soft actuators serve as essential functional units for intelligent flexible equipment and extreme‐environment actuating devices. Traditional dense‐film actuators suffer from heavy weight and poor radiation stability, which greatly restrict their practical applications. Herein, a segregated microcellular film actuator is successfully fabricated for the first time. Relying on the differential heat transfer characteristics on both sides of the electrothermal layer, this actuator achieves improved mechanical performance together with satisfactory electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding capability. The segregated microcellular structure can effectively regulate the asymmetric behavior of the actuator, enhance its mechanical strength after deformation, and remarkably improve load stability. The optimized actuator delivers a maximum driving force of 1.02 N and maintains intact conductive pathways under bending and folding deformations, thereby demonstrating application potential under complex loads. Furthermore, the highly conductive inner layer can efficiently attenuate electromagnetic waves and isolate alternating electric fields; meanwhile, the microcellular structure synergistically endows the actuator with infrared stealth performance. The as‐prepared segregated microcellular actuator possesses favorable mechanical reliability and EMI shielding capacity, exhibiting promising application value.

title: Evaluating Decision Criteria for Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting Retrofits in Institutional Buildings: A Critical Integrative Review
summary: Rooftop rainwater harvesting retrofits in institutional buildings require evidence on water performance, affordability, constraints, and operations, yet inconsistent boundaries limit transferability. This critical integrative review examine
content: Rooftop rainwater harvesting retrofits in institutional buildings require evidence on water performance, affordability, constraints, and operations, yet inconsistent boundaries limit transferability. This critical integrative review examines the decision criteria and evidentiary requirements supporting institutional retrofit decisions. A purposive sample of 83 full-text publications, screened from 309 Web of Science records, was systematically evaluated against 24 predefined criteria spanning financial, environmental, technological, structural, innovation, and social dimensions. Following a targeted verification audit across 1,992 publication–criterion pairs, the resulting evidence matrix documented 205 direct and 402 indirect construct correspondences. Financial and maintenance-related criteria received substantially broader coverage than thermal, structural, and innovation criteria. Direct correspondence spanned diverse forms of support from conceptual inclusion and design assumptions to modelled and measured outcomes. Financial recovery depended heavily on expenditure boundaries and tariff assumptions, while long-term runoff retention and event-scale discharge control represented non-interchangeable hydrological outcomes. A proposed decision architecture separates building context and mandatory eligibility screening from stakeholder preferences and alternative-specific performance, establishing baseline information requirements prior to retrofit comparison. By distinguishing evidentiary depth and exposing overlapping measures, the review establishes a transparent foundation for criterion selection. Although purposive sampling, single-researcher appraisal, and heterogeneous evidence limit generalizability, the prospective framework offers a rigorous basis for future building-specific validation.

title: Design and psychometric properties of the Persian knowledge, attitude, and practice about microplastics in human health (MIKAP) questionnaire among Iranian women
summary: INTRODUCTION: Given the growing concern over the impact of microplastics (MPs) on both environmental and human health, there is a critical need for tools to effectively assess public behavior regarding MPs. This study aimed to design and ps
content: INTRODUCTION: Given the growing concern over the impact of microplastics (MPs) on both environmental and human health, there is a critical need for tools to effectively assess public behavior regarding MPs. This study aimed to design and psychometrically validate a tool to assess the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) of women regarding MPs. Women were specifically selected as the target population due to their primary roles in household management, food preparation, and higher usage of personal care products, which are key pathways for microplastic exposure. METHOD: The instrument was developed using a deductive approach, and the psychometric properties of the MIKAP questionnaire were evaluated in terms of validity and reliability. An initial pool of 61 items was generated, which was subsequently reduced through rigorous validity assessment phases to a final 43-item version. Data were collected from two groups of 244 and 310 women aged 18 and above, who were selected for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), respectively. RESULTS: The MIKAP questionnaire consisted of 43 items across three domains defined a priori by the Knowledge-Attitude-Practice (KAP) theoretical framework; the nine factors identified by exploratory factor analysis were nested within these domains based on item loadings. Most items demonstrated acceptable quantitative face validity (impact score >1.5); two conceptually important items with lower impact scores were retained based on their theoretical relevance. Item-level CVR values ranged from 0.60 to 1.00. One item fell marginally below the predefined threshold of 0.62 and was retained after revision because of its conceptual relevance. I-CVI ranged from 0.8 to 1; S-CVI = 0.92; and Kappa ranged from 0.79 to 1, with an average of 0.92. The application of exploratory factor analysis to the data was significant (χ² = 4363.096; df = 903; p < 0.001). Confirmatory factor analysis of the three-domain MIKAP model resulted in the following fit indices: χ²/df: 1.536; p < 0.001; GFI: 0.84; CFI: 0.87 (modest values, below more stringent conventional cut-offs, and interpreted cautiously given the model's complexity and large degrees of freedom); RMSEA: 0.042; AGFI: 0.82; PGFI: 0.74; PNFI: 0.64; PCFI: 0.80, indicating acceptable, although not uniformly strong, overall model fit. Internal consistency estimates were acceptable to high at the domain level with a total Cronbach's alpha of 0.920 and ICC = 0.846 (95% CI: 0.742-0.910). CONCLUSION: The findings provide evidence supporting the validity and reliability of the MIKAP questionnaire for assessing the three constructs of knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding microplastics and health. This instrument can serve as a practical tool for health policymakers and environmental educators to design targeted interventions for reducing microplastic exposure.Clinical trial number: IRCT20240529061941N1 Registration Date 2024-07-12, 1403/04/22.

title: PAFTI-Net predicts termite infestation risk levels from multivariate gas monitoring data
summary: In response to the problems that traditional termite monitoring is difficult to quantify the degree of invasion and that there are noise interference in multi-temporal data as well as difficulties in jointly modeling local–global patterns,
content: In response to the problems that traditional termite monitoring is difficult to quantify the degree of invasion and that there are noise interference in multi-temporal data as well as difficulties in jointly modeling local–global patterns, this paper proposes and implements Parallel Adaptive Fusion and Temporal Interaction Network (PAFTI-Net) based on the self-built gas monitoring platform. The model’s front end adopts adaptive feature fusion to dynamically weight CO2, CH4, temperature and humidity, and temporal features; the middle layer constructs three parallel paths: multi-scale convolution, cross-temporal global dependency modeling, and factor-level nonlinear interaction; the back end outputs low, medium, and high risk levels through dynamic fusion. On a structured dataset containing 89 independent experimental batches and 26,820 window samples, the test accuracy of PAFTI-Net reaches 91.50%, and the F1-score is 91.03%. Compared with the optimal baseline model ESD-TripleStream, it has achieved absolute improvements of 2.95% and 2.40% respectively, and a 3.69% increase in recall rate. The results indicate that PAFTI-Net has significant advantages in discriminating termite invasion risk levels under controlled conditions, providing a feasible technical path for intelligent prevention and control based on gas monitoring.

title: Assessment of Various Biochemical Indicators and Gene Markers Regulating Plant Physiology and Biochemistry Under Fluoride Toxicity
summary: Fluoride (F - ) is recognized as a persistent and potent phytotoxicant, widely distributed in the Earth's crust (0.06–0.09%) and gradually mobilized through anthropogenic activities such as phosphate fertilizer (SSP & DAP) application and a
content: Fluoride (F - ) is recognized as a persistent and potent phytotoxicant, widely distributed in the Earth's crust (0.06–0.09%) and gradually mobilized through anthropogenic activities such as phosphate fertilizer (SSP & DAP) application and aluminum smelting. Unlike other halides, F − ’s high electronegativity permits it to accumulate within plant tissues, primarily through stomatal uptake or root absorption, leading to profound physiological perturbations. This review synthesizes a comprehensive understanding regarding the mechanisms of F − uptake through various F − transporters and the toxicity disrupting the fundamental biochemistry of plant systems. At the cellular level, F − stress induces a cascade of metabolic dysfunctions. It significantly impairs the synthesis and stability of essential molecules, including structural proteins and fatty acids, leading to membrane lipid peroxidation and altered fluidity. Photosynthetic efficiency is often compromised due to the degradation of chlorophyll pigments and the inhibition of Rubisco activity. Furthermore, F-stress alters the profile of amino acids and secondary metabolites, often triggering an overproduction of proline and polyphenols as a defensive response. The various reported F − transporters in plants viz. FEX, ABC transporters, ALMT, CLC, NRT/NPF, and their mechanism is reviewed and a generalized view have been proposed mostly from Camelia sinensis and Arabidopsis thaliana . The review also highlights the proposed mechanism of transport of F − across the various reported transporters and the knowledge gap for future research.

title: Does choosing processed-potato marketing channels affect household income? Evidence from Musanze District, Rwanda
summary: Enhancing smallholder farmers’ access to reliable markets is a key strategy to improving incomes in the developing countries such as Rwanda. However, smallholder farmers face substantial barriers in their attempt to access direct marketing
content: Enhancing smallholder farmers’ access to reliable markets is a key strategy to improving incomes in the developing countries such as Rwanda. However, smallholder farmers face substantial barriers in their attempt to access direct marketing channels. Despite the establishment of potato processing factories to complement the existing facilities through Community processing centers in the high production zone to facilitate market access, participation in this growing marketing channel has reportedly remained low, resulting in continued losses. While previous studies have assessed the factors that influence market participation, limited attention has been given to the income impact of participating in processed-potato marketing channel. This study assessed the impact of participation in processed-potato marketing channels on household income in Musanze District, Rwanda, using survey data from 408 households selected through a multistage sampling procedure employing an Endogenous Switching Regression (ESR) model. Results revealed that overall, participation in the processed-potato marketing channel had a positive impact on household income. Access to credit, wealth status, and total production cost influenced household income across both participants and non-participants. However, household size was only significant for non-participants, while experience and cropping system influenced income exclusively among participants.

title: Safeguarding nutritional integrity in mango: multi-omics revelations on chilling injury-induced quality deterioration and innovative preservation strategies
summary: Mango ( Mangifera indica L.) is highly susceptible to chilling injury (CI) during cold-chain logistics, which triggers extensive degradation of nutritionally valuable phytochemicals beyond visible peel and flesh disorders. This review integ
content: Mango ( Mangifera indica L.) is highly susceptible to chilling injury (CI) during cold-chain logistics, which triggers extensive degradation of nutritionally valuable phytochemicals beyond visible peel and flesh disorders. This review integrates transcriptomic, metabolomic, proteomic, and lipidomic datasets to construct a cross-dimensional regulatory network linking cold stress to nutrient decomposition. Conserved cold signatures include elevated phosphatidic acid, reduced unsaturated-to-saturated fatty acid ratios, depleted flavonol reserves, and disrupted sugar–acid balance, while proteomic profiling identifies insufficient HSP70 expression mediated by impaired m 6 A transcript stabilization as a conserved vulnerability. The phenylpropanoid cascade emerges as the core manipulable target, with cold stress exerting a dual nutritional effect by inducing flavonoid accumulation yet depleting carotenoids, ascorbic acid, soluble sugars, and aroma volatiles. Physical, chemical, biological, and composite preservation strategies converge on antioxidant amplification, membrane stabilization, and energy reprogramming, yet efficacy remains constrained by limited duration and insufficient molecular targeting. Future work should prioritize time-resolved multi-omics integration, in vivo functional validation of hub regulators, and biomarker-guided composite protocols for scalable nutrition-preserving cold-chain management.

title: Serverless Computing: A Survey of Programming Model, Orchestration, and Opportunities
summary: Serverless computing is growing in popularity as a deployment paradigm for micro-services. It brings benefits including simplified management, fine-grained resource accounting and billing, and lightweight virtualisation. In particular, it e
content: Serverless computing is growing in popularity as a deployment paradigm for micro-services. It brings benefits including simplified management, fine-grained resource accounting and billing, and lightweight virtualisation. In particular, it enables users to focus on function development while service providers focus on efficient resource management and high-performance scheduling. In this article we systematically review serverless computing to facilitate future research and exploration of opportunities enabled by this paradigm. Our primary contribution to the state of the art is to survey and analyse the literature from the perspective of programming models and orchestration. We distinguish six categories of programming models and summarize the various programming languages supported by different platforms. We then analyse orchestration models from cluster, function and kernel perspectives based on their different objectives. We also overview the commercial and open-source platforms that dominate the market at present. Finally, we discuss the research gaps and opportunities in serverless computing that need further attention.

title: Transducing a CO2 Concentration Gradient into Electrical Energy through Copper–Ethylenediamine Coordination
summary: A gas-phase concentration gradient contains Gibbs free energy, while converting this energy into electricity requires a chemical transduction mechanism. Here, we convert a CO2 concentration gradient into a Cu redox-potential difference thro
content: A gas-phase concentration gradient contains Gibbs free energy, while converting this energy into electricity requires a chemical transduction mechanism. Here, we convert a CO2 concentration gradient into a Cu redox-potential difference through copper–ethylenediamine coordination. Ethylenediamine (eda) acts as a bifunctional molecular transducer: its coordination stabilizes the Cu2+ state, whereas CO2-induced protonation of eda diminishes coordination ability and stabilizes the metallic Cu. A cell consisting of copper electrodes and copper–ethylenediamine electrolyte generates an open-circuit voltage of 120 mV under a CO2/N2 gradient. A peak power density of 26.3 mW m−2 was achieved with a dialysis membrane, and Faradaic current was sustained for approximately 48 h. pH-dependent redox potentials and CO2 concentration-dependent pH shifts account for the generated open-circuit voltage. These results demonstrate a molecular strategy for coupling the chemical-potential difference associated with a CO2 concentration gradient to electrical output through linked acid–base, coordination, and redox equilibria without direct CO2 reduction.

title: Candidate gene mining of a fragmented Tipularia discolor Pursh (Nutt.) genome assembly reveals genes putatively associated with specialized metabolite production.
summary: Orchids are a large and diverse group of plants with unique adaptations that have enabled the utilization of many different environmental habitats across almost all continents. These adaptations are mediated by an as-yet-underexplored genet
content: Orchids are a large and diverse group of plants with unique adaptations that have enabled the utilization of many different environmental habitats across almost all continents. These adaptations are mediated by an as-yet-underexplored genetic resource. Nearly all sequenced orchid genomes are of Asian origin and represent less than 0.1% of all orchid species, limiting the ability to explore and mine the gene space of this complex plant family. Greater representation of orchids in genome databases could provide important insights into the genes responsible for adaptive phenotypes, which could be useful for targeted crop improvement and in orchid conservation efforts. To begin to expand the palette of orchid genomes, an effort was undertaken to sequence the genome of a North American terrestrial orchid, Tipularia discolor. K-mer analysis estimated a haploid genome size of approximately 1.7 Gb, with a high proportion of repetitive sequences. Although a complete genome was not obtained, the implementation of a conservative gene mining approach and the generation of a candidate gene mining pipeline led to the identification of 68 consensus contig objects containing whole or partial genes related to sucrose, trehalose, terpenoid, and phenylpropanoid metabolism. Of note, two bibenzyl synthase homologs were identified with high confidence and clustered with characterized orchid bibenzyl synthases in a CHS/BBS phylogeny, indicating that T. discolor, like its Asian and South American relatives, has the capacity to produce this distinct class of phenylpropanoids. Thus, despite substantial fragmentation, the T. discolor assembly contains sufficient gene space representation for targeted candidate gene discovery. This works lays the foundation for functional characterization of selected candidates and development of a more complete genome assembly for comparative genomic studies.

title: Coupled Self‐Alkalization and Chelation Chemistry Enables Highly Reversible Zn Anodes and Rechargeable Alkaline Zn–I 2 Batteries
summary: The practical development of alkaline rechargeable zinc‐based batteries (ARZBs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off among redox potential, high Zn 2+ concentration, and Zn anode stability. Herein, we report a synergistic “se
content: The practical development of alkaline rechargeable zinc‐based batteries (ARZBs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off among redox potential, high Zn 2+ concentration, and Zn anode stability. Herein, we report a synergistic “self‐alkalization + chelation chemistry” electrolyte using ethylenediamine (EN) as a multifunctional co‐solvent. Acting simultaneously as an organic base and a Zn 2+ chelating ligand, EN enables in situ OH − generation while forming soluble five‐membered Zn chelates, thereby reconstructing Zn dissolution chemistry in alkaline media. The resulting electrolyte achieves a Zn 2+ concentration of 1 M at pH 12.45, transforming Zn transport from diffusion‐limited to migration‐assisted behavior. Meanwhile, preferential adsorption and in situ decomposition of EN generate an organic–inorganic hybrid interphase that effectively suppresses corrosion and parasitic reactions. As a result, Zn||Zn coin cells exhibit stable Zn plating/stripping for 380 h. Furthermore, EN stabilizes reactive I + intermediates through coordination chemistry, enabling rechargeable alkaline Zn||I 2 batteries with a high energy density of 812.9 Wh kg −1 . More importantly, the exceptionally high Zn 2+ flux and interfacial reversibility enable the first demonstration of anode‐free alkaline Zn||I 2 batteries, which operate stably for 860 cycles. This work establishes a general electrolyte engineering strategy for decoupling the long‐standing electrolyte trilemma in ARZBs and advancing high‐energy aqueous batteries.

title: SlitOBP9 contributes to cis ‐3‐hexenol recognition and larval orientation in Spodoptera litura
summary: Cis-3-hexenol is a typical green leaf volatile (GLV) that plays an important regulatory role in plant-insect interactions. Spodoptera litura is a globally significant agricultural pest whose larvae cause severe damage to a wide range of cro
content: Cis-3-hexenol is a typical green leaf volatile (GLV) that plays an important regulatory role in plant-insect interactions. Spodoptera litura is a globally significant agricultural pest whose larvae cause severe damage to a wide range of crops, yet the olfactory molecular mechanism underlying larval recognition of this volatile has remained unclear. Two-choice behavioral assays showed that a low dose (0.1 µg) of cis-3-hexenol exerted a significant attractive effect on S. litura larvae. Tissue-specific expression analysis identified an odorant-binding protein, SlitOBP9, that is highly expressed in the larval antennae. Fluorescence competitive binding assays confirmed that SlitOBP9 binds cis-3-hexenol, with the highest binding affinity at neutral pH (7.4); binding capacity was lost under acidic (pH 5.0) or alkaline (pH 9.0) conditions. RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated silencing of SlitOBP9 significantly reduced larval chemotactic behavior toward cis-3-hexenol. Relative to siNC controls, siOBP9-injected larvae showed a marked decrease in food intake on maize and cabbage, together with highly significant reductions in body-weight gain, and frass production. These results indicate that SlitOBP9 contributes to the perception of cis-3-hexenol and provide a systematic account of the olfactory mechanism by which S. litura larvae recognize this ecologically important volatile. These findings may provide a basic mechanistic lead for future studies, but further work is needed before any practical pest-control application can be considered.

title: Ligand‐Engineered Metal‐Organic‐Covalent‐Organic Frameworks Enable Red‐Light‐Driven H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Tunable Biomass Upgrading
summary: Harvesting low‐energy photons, particularly in the deep‐red and near‐infrared regions, for artificial photosynthesis remains a significant challenge due to the inherent difficulty in driving multi‐electron redox processes with limited photo
content: Harvesting low‐energy photons, particularly in the deep‐red and near‐infrared regions, for artificial photosynthesis remains a significant challenge due to the inherent difficulty in driving multi‐electron redox processes with limited photon energy. Herein, we reported a tunable ligand engineering strategy to construct a series of isostructural metal‐organic‐covalent‐organic frameworks (MOCOFs), namely MOCOF‐phen x ( x = 0, 1, 2 and 3). By gradient increasing the number of phenanthroline ligands around the Ru(II) center, we precisely modulated the electronic structures and excited‐state properties of the resulting MOCOFs. Remarkably, the ligand‐engineered MOCOFs showed excellent red‐light‐driven H 2 O 2 generation coupled with switchable biomass upgrading, in which the reaction selectivity of furfuryl alcohol oxidation was profoundly governed. MOCOF‐phen 0 preferentially affords 6‐hydroxy‐2H‐pyran‐3(6H)‐one (PN) with 91.4% selectivity, whereas MOCOF‐phen 3 steers the reaction towards 5‐hydroxy‐2,5‐dihydrofuran‐2‐one (FN). This work establishes a molecular‐level design blueprint for low‐energy‐light‐driven photocatalysis, demonstrating ligand engineering in crystalline framework materials for optimizing activity and selectivity towards sustainable photosynthesis.

title: One‐Step Conversion of Thermoplastic Elastomers into Ionic Ordered Mesoporous Polymers via Interface‐Directed Chain Scission: A Plastic Upcycling Strategy for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
summary: As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TP
content: As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) can be a notable exception. These materials can intrinsically self-assemble into ordered nanostructures, yet most upcycling methods discard this morphological asset, leaving TPEs a compelling but underexploited feedstock for high-value applications. Here, we report a one-step approach that upcycles TPEs into ionic ordered mesoporous polymers (OMPs) in their solid state, through interface-directed chain scission. Adding a small amount of radical initiator (dicumyl peroxide) during the sulfonation of polystyrene-block-poly(ethylene-ran-butylene)-block-polystyrene (SEBS) leverages a diffusion-controlled reaction front to selectively cleave the minority polystyrene domains, while crosslinking and sulfonating the majority phase. This one-step process at 145°C installs ionic character and establishing uniform mesoporosity without the high-temperature calcination (typically > 350°C) that conventionally erodes functional groups. Furthermore, the resulting OMPs act as high-performance sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting, demonstrating rapid kinetics, solar-driven regeneration, and excellent cycling stability, while a simple lithium chloride (LiCl) encapsulation step enhances their water uptake capacity to 2.46 g/g.

title: Ni‐Embedded Carbon Fibers Enable Synergistic Confinement and Catalytic Conversion of Iodine Species for Zn–I 2 Batteries
summary: Due to their affordability, safety and high capacity, aqueous Zn–I 2 batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage. Nevertheless, the dissolution of I 3 − intermediates leads to the iodine shuttle effect, which results in ir
content: Due to their affordability, safety and high capacity, aqueous Zn–I 2 batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage. Nevertheless, the dissolution of I 3 − intermediates leads to the iodine shuttle effect, which results in irreversible capacity loss and poor cyclability, thus hindering practical deployment. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy combining hierarchical pore confinement with catalytic iodine conversion to suppress the shuttle effect. A self‐standing cathode is synthesized, consisting of Ni nanoparticle‐embedded carbon nanoboxes enclosed within carbon macroporous fibers (Ni@CNBs‐CMFs). The abundant hierarchical porous structure provides physical confinement for iodine species, while Ni nanoparticles serve as active centers to accelerate iodine conversion via d–p orbital interactions. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement in iodine accommodation and reaction kinetics, the self‐standing Ni@CNBs‐CMFs iodine cathode delivers a cycle life of 16 000 cycles with a capacity of 144.5 mAh g −1 and maintains a Coulombic efficiency of 90.0% after a 168‐h resting period. Moreover, the cathode also achieves a capacity of 382.8 mAh g −1 at a current of 2 A g −1 via the I − /I 0 /I + redox pathway.

title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
