title: Landscape Heterogeneity Changes and Their Implications for Agriculture in Europe
summary: This dissertation examines the extent and implications of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity in Europe. Landscape heterogeneity is conceptualized as the combination of two complementary dimensions: landscape composition, referrin
content: This dissertation examines the extent and implications of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity in Europe. Landscape heterogeneity is conceptualized as the combination of two complementary dimensions: landscape composition, referring to the relative abundance of different land use and land cover types, and landscape configuration, i.e. their spatial arrangement. Both dimensions can critically influence biophysical processes such as energy and water cycles, which underpin ecosystem functions and affect agricultural production. The dissertation is organized around three themes: (1) the extent and climate relevance of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity, (2) the underlying biophysical processes associated with these changes, and (3) their implications for agricultural systems. The first theme quantifies recent, widespread trajectories of change in landscape composition and configuration across Europe and assesses their potential influence on bioclimatic variables. The second theme focuses specifically on changes in landscape configuration and examines the biophysical processes through which forest fragmentation affects local temperatures. The third theme applies an agricultural economics perspective to a case study in Germany, investigating the causal effects of historical variations in landscape heterogeneity on grassland ecosystems during a severe compound drought and heatwave event. Overall, this dissertation contributes with novel evidence on the importance of accounting for both landscape composition and configuration in climate adaptation and mitigation strategies. It identifies deforestation trajectories as the primary compositional factor and forest fragmentation as the primary configurational factor affecting the ecosystem's climate-regulation functioning. Conversely, higher landscape heterogeneity in agricultural landscapes emerges as a potentially effective mitigation strategy against extreme hydrometeorological events.

title: Quantitative strengthening and corrosion correlation for partial and full substitution of nickel by nitrogen on AISI 316 stainless steel via VIM
summary: Nickel stabilization of the austenitic phase in stainless steels faces economic and supply-chain pressures, motivating partial or near-complete nickel substitution through nitrogen alloying as an alternative alloy-design strategy. This stud
content: Nickel stabilization of the austenitic phase in stainless steels faces economic and supply-chain pressures, motivating partial or near-complete nickel substitution through nitrogen alloying as an alternative alloy-design strategy. This study systematically evaluates partial (0.24 N, 6.56 wt% Ni retained) and near-complete (0.52 N, 0.01 wt% Ni) nitrogen substitution in AISI 316 stainless steel, produced via vacuum induction furnace (VIM) under controlled-nitrogen-pressure melting at 18 and 32 bar, respectively. Nitrogen addition refined austenite grain size by 53.4% (from 29 to 13.5 μm) and increased dislocation density from 0.13 × 10 14 to 1.97 × 10 14 m −2 , with the 0.52N alloy developing a duplex (γ + α) microstructure. A phase-resolved strengthening model decomposed yield strength contributions into grain refinement, solid-solution, and dislocation mechanisms, achieving good agreement with experimental results. Nitrogen shifted corrosion potential positively, reduced corrosion current density from 9.1 to 2.4 µA cm −2 , and EIS analysis showed the passive film’s charge-transfer resistance rising from 121.5 to 193.5 kΩ cm 2 with a corresponding fall in effective capacitance, while the electrical-equivalent film thickness recalculated from these parameters increases only modestly, from 0.10 to 0.12 nm. Dilatometry revealed a thermal instability window (780–840 °C) unique to the 0.52N alloy, consistent with thermally activated phase evolution within its γ + α duplex microstructure. The 0.24N alloy provides the most balanced combination of strength, ductility, corrosion resistance, and thermal stability among the investigated conditions, while the 0.52N alloy provides the highest strength but also exhibits greater phase complexity and a thermal-instability window; therefore, both alloys require application-specific validation of processing, weldability/forming behaviour, and long-term service performance before industrial deployment.

title: Impact of butterfly pea tea, green tea, and milk mixtures on the physicochemical, microbiological, antioxidant, and sensory characteristics of kombucha‑like beverages
summary: The current study evaluated the development of kombucha-like beverages using butterfly pea tea (BPT) as an unconventional herbal ingredient. Model samples were prepared with varying concentrations of BPT infusion, both independently and in
content: The current study evaluated the development of kombucha-like beverages using butterfly pea tea (BPT) as an unconventional herbal ingredient. Model samples were prepared with varying concentrations of BPT infusion, both independently and in combination with green tea, and selected formulations which were enriched with milk. Fermentation was monitored during 168 h, and analyses were conducted to assess physicochemical, rheological, antioxidant, and sensory properties. Moreover, microbiological assessments and measurements of biomass growth and carbon dioxide production were also performed. The results indicated that the kombucha-like model samples could be classified as low-alcoholic beverages. Furthermore, a gradual decrease in pH was recorded during fermentation, with the most pronounced changes occurring in milk-enriched samples. Microbiological analyses confirmed the absence of pathogenic microorganisms throughout the fermentation process. Sample composition affected antioxidant activity, phenolic content, colour, and sensory profile. Samples containing green tea showed higher antioxidant activity, whereas BPT enhanced visual and functional properties. Although milk improved viscosity and microbial growth, it reduced sensory acceptability. Overall, the study could expand current knowledge on non-traditional kombucha substrates by demonstrating the feasibility of using BPT flower infusion, alone or in combination with green tea and milk, thereby supporting the development of novel fermented beverages with enhanced technological and sensory attributes.

title: A hierarchical resilient tri-level energy management for islanded multi-energy system with risk-aware learning-in-the-loop RL algorithm
summary: Coordinated energy management is crucial for the effective operation of integrated multi-energy systems (IMESs), which integrate water, heat, and electricity networks. The primary objectives of this coordination include reducing operational
content: Coordinated energy management is crucial for the effective operation of integrated multi-energy systems (IMESs), which integrate water, heat, and electricity networks. The primary objectives of this coordination include reducing operational costs, minimizing hazards, and ensuring a reliable supply of energy. Traditional methodologies tend to address these objectives within a singular optimization framework, which often constrains their capacity to accommodate the distinct operational requirements associated with economic scheduling, vulnerability assessment, and service restoration. This study investigates the potential for enhancing system performance by dispersing these objectives into three interconnected decision-making tiers and coordinating their outputs throughout the operational phase. At the highest level, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is utilized to facilitate operational decisions that improve energy supply and service restoration during disruptions. The intermediate level employs a sensitivity-based risk assessment to pinpoint vulnerable system components and evaluate their effects on operational performance. At the foundational level, resources pertaining to power, heat, water, storage, and energy conversion are scheduled through Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), which integrates resilience and risk outcomes as operational constraints and decision-making priorities. Furthermore, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent manages real-time operations by coordinating the outputs from these three levels, dynamically adjusting operational choices based on prevailing system conditions. This hierarchical flow of information enables resilience requirements and vulnerability assessments to inform economic scheduling without conflating all objectives into a single optimization problem. Simulations conducted on an IMES reveal that the proposed framework enhances energy supply during disruptions by 35.14% and reduces daily operating costs by 13.79% when compared to traditional benchmark approaches. These findings suggest that the proposed structure improves supply continuity and economic efficiency while effectively addressing operational vulnerabilities and network limitations.

title: Optimization of Hydrothermal Acid Activation of Coir Fibers: Enhancing Cellulose Yield and Cationic Dye Removal
summary: The development of sustainable biosorbents from lignocellulosic biomass is often limited by low yield and the energy-intensive fractionation required to enhance specific components and tailor their physicochemical properties for industrial
content: The development of sustainable biosorbents from lignocellulosic biomass is often limited by low yield and the energy-intensive fractionation required to enhance specific components and tailor their physicochemical properties for industrial scalability. To address this, an I-optimal response surface methodology (RSM) optimization approach was used to optimize the parameters of the acid-assisted hydrothermal activation process for coir fibers, simultaneously maximizing cellulose yield and methylene blue (MB) removal efficiency. The synergistic effects of acid concentration (0.5–1.0 mol/L), temperature (90–160 °C), activation time (30–150 min), and acid type (HCl, H3PO4) were evaluated. 1.0 mol/L HCl stood out, and the linear model was the best fit for both cases; the acid type influenced MB removal efficiency, while temperature and time negatively impacted the cellulose yield. Optimal conditions (1.0 M HCl, 120 °C, 90 min) achieved a balanced performance with 80.6% cellulose yield and MB removal efficiency (90.7%, 9.07 mg/g). The distinct mesoporous profile framework and the shift of surface charge from 5.8 to 2.1 pHpzc were confirmed by BET surface analysis and the point of zero charge plot. Adsorption of MB onto the surface of the modified coir fiber adsorbents was endothermic chemisorption (ΔH0 = +117.84 kJ/mol) and underwent a spontaneous shift at elevated temperature (45 °C), well fitted by Temkin, Langmuir, pseudo-second-order kinetic (PSO), and intraparticle diffusion (IPD) models for describing the adsorption mechanism. The maximum efficiency (97.82%, 9.78 mg/g) was recorded at the optimum conditions (initial MB concentration = 50 mg/L, dose = 0.5 g/L, pH 11, contact time = 150, temperature 45 °C). Hence, the hydrochar produced in this work has shown promise for scalability.

title: Next-generation plant-wearable sensors: materials, sensing mechanisms, and plant health monitoring
summary: Over the past decade, plant-wearable sensors have attracted significant attention due to the demand for sustainable agriculture. Conventional plant monitoring systems often suffer from delayed diagnosis, destructive testing, and poor early-
content: Over the past decade, plant-wearable sensors have attracted significant attention due to the demand for sustainable agriculture. Conventional plant monitoring systems often suffer from delayed diagnosis, destructive testing, and poor early-stress detection. In contrast, plant-wearable sensors can continuously monitor plant physiological and biochemical activities in real time. Rapid advances in flexible electronics, biodegradable materials, bioelectronics, and self-powered sensing technologies have accelerated the development of wearable sensing systems that can be attached to plant surfaces. This review discusses recent progress in plant-wearable sensors, with particular emphasis on substrate materials, target physiological parameters, and sensing mechanisms. It first compares the substrates used in plant-attached devices with biodegradable alternatives. It then defines the key physiological targets, namely plant moisture, growth, volatile organic compounds, metabolites and agrochemical residues, and electrophysiological and stress signals. Finally, it reviews the electrochemical, resistive and capacitive, triboelectric self-powered, and optical sensing mechanisms used to measure them, together with their validation conditions. The review closes with current challenges in long-term stability, biocompatibility, large-scale deployment, and data-driven intelligent agriculture, along with future opportunities for sustainable, self-powered, multifunctional bioelectronics for smart farming applications.

title: Digital twin reconstruction of red blood cell aging using Raman chemometrics and systems modeling
summary: Red blood cell (RBC) storage aging involves progressive metabolic and oxidative alterations that compromise membrane integrity and transfusion quality. However, conventional endpoint measurements provide limited information on individual ag
content: Red blood cell (RBC) storage aging involves progressive metabolic and oxidative alterations that compromise membrane integrity and transfusion quality. However, conventional endpoint measurements provide limited information on individual aging dynamics and their predictability. This study presents an experimentally constrained digital twin framework integrating Raman spectral analysis, chemometric modeling, and mechanistic simulation to reconstruct RBC aging trajectories and predict donor-specific hemolysis. Longitudinal Raman spectra and biochemical measurements from packed RBC units stored for eight weeks were analyzed using principal component analysis, least squares decomposition, multivariate curve resolution–alternating least squares, and partial least squares regression. A MATLAB/SimBiology model coupled glucose metabolism, redox regulation, oxidative membrane deterioration, and hemoglobin release. The integrated approach resolved continuous biochemical trajectories characterized by glucose depletion, lactate accumulation, and progressive hemolysis. Despite broadly comparable metabolic kinetics, female-derived RBCs showed slower hemolysis than male-derived RBCs (0.05 ± 0.03 versus 0.40 ± 0.14 week-1). Early Raman spectral features predicted donor-specific hemolysis kinetics (R2 = 0.69), supporting their potential as predictive biomarkers of storage stability. The digital twin reproduced observed metabolic and hemolysis trajectories and implicated hydrogen peroxide regulation, glutathione availability, and GSH/GSSG turnover as candidate contributors to sex-dependent differences. By linking high-dimensional spectroscopic signals with interpretable mechanistic modeling, this framework provides a strategy for tracking RBC storage deterioration and estimating individual aging behavior from early measurements. It may support future development of personalized blood-quality assessment tools.

title: Programming Polymer Lifecycle through Catalyst-Free Photodepolymerization and Value-Added Upcycling
summary: The durability and functional versatility of polymeric materials underpin their widespread use, yet also contribute to persistent plastic waste and the formation of micro/nanoplastics throughout the polymer lifecycle. Developing polymer sys
content: The durability and functional versatility of polymeric materials underpin their widespread use, yet also contribute to persistent plastic waste and the formation of micro/nanoplastics throughout the polymer lifecycle. Developing polymer systems that reconcile functional performance with controlled depolymerization and value-added upcycling remains a major challenge. Here, we demonstrated a functional polymer platform with intrinsic photooxidative cleavage by repurposing conjugated carbon-carbon double bonds as programmed cleavage sites within polymer backbones. The resulting polyamides and polyurethane undergo catalystfree depolymerization under ambient conditions, incorporating oxygen from air to yield structurally defined carbonyl-containing products. Contrary to the conventional paradigm, aggregation accelerates depolymerization by reshaping excited-state dynamics and promoting ROS generation, revealing an unexpected role of aggregation in driving photochemical depolymerization. Concurrently, the evolution of fluorescence provides an intrinsic optical readout of the depolymerization process. Notably, this strategy enables the photochemical transformation of micro/nanoplastic-like particles in water under natural sunlight, extending the cleavage pathway beyond bulk materials. Importantly, the resulting photoproducts resist further oxidation while retaining distinct photophysical and photoactivated properties, realizing value-added utilization. By coupling polymer functionality, programmed photodepolymerization, and product valorization, this work establishes a versatile design principle for controlling polymer lifecycles and advancing sustainable functional materials.

title: Hydroxylated metatitanic acid engineering of K2CO3/Al2O3 sorbents enables highly regenerable and cyclically stable CO2 capture
summary: Carbonate-based solid sorbents are promising for low-temperature CO 2 capture, but their practical application is often hindered by incomplete regeneration and capacity loss arising from strong interactions between K 2 CO 3 and alumina. Alt
content: Carbonate-based solid sorbents are promising for low-temperature CO 2 capture, but their practical application is often hindered by incomplete regeneration and capacity loss arising from strong interactions between K 2 CO 3 and alumina. Although titanium-containing modifiers have been investigated in related sorbents, the role of hydroxyl-rich metatitanic acid (TiO(OH) 2 ) in K 2 CO 3 /Al 2 O 3 systems remains insufficiently established. Herein, K 2 CO 3 was supported on high-surface-area active alumina derived from NH 4 HCO 3 -modified flash-calcined gibbsite and subsequently modified with hydroxyl-rich metatitanic acid (TiO(OH) 2 ) to engineer the carbonate–oxide interface. The modified alumina provided a high accessible surface area of 350 m 2 g − 1 , facilitating K 2 CO 3 dispersion and interfacial modification. The optimized sorbent containing 20 wt% K 2 CO 3 and 30 wt% metatitanic acid achieved a CO 2 adsorption capacity of 2.96 mmol g − 1 at 20°C and 7 bar, consistent with response surface model predictions. Metatitanic acid substantially reconstructed the porous structure, increasing the accessible surface area of K 2 CO 3 /Al 2 O 3 from 114.7 to 243.7 m 2 g − 1 while maintaining a highly dispersed carbonate phase. Equilibrium data were best described by the Freundlich model, indicating heterogeneous adsorption sites, while thermodynamic analysis revealed spontaneous and exothermic adsorption. Most importantly, metatitanic acid markedly enhanced regenerability, with an optimized regeneration condition of 140°C for 40 min yielding ~ 99% regeneration efficiency. The optimized sorbent retained 96.5% of its initial capacity after ten adsorption–regeneration cycles. These results demonstrate that hydroxyl-rich metatitanic acid is an effective interfacial engineering strategy for developing regenerable and durable K 2 CO 3 /Al 2 O 3 sorbents for low-temperature CO 2 capture.

title: Microfibrillated Cellulose as a Reinforcement Agent in Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate (ASA) for MEX 3D Printing: A Thermomechanical and Rheological Filler Content Assessment
summary: In this study, acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA), a thermoplastic with great resistance to weather conditions, was combined with the nature-sourced microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) to produce composites with improved properties in additi
content: In this study, acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA), a thermoplastic with great resistance to weather conditions, was combined with the nature-sourced microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) to produce composites with improved properties in additive manufacturing (AM). Filament extrusion was used to fabricate the filaments. The test specimens were 3D printed for thermal, rheological, dynamic mechanical, and mechanical characterization. The thermal behavior was assessed by thermogravimetric analysis and differential scanning calorimetry, while the rheological performance was evaluated through viscosity and material flow rate measurements. The effect of MFC on quality metrics (dimensional accuracy and porosity) was also assessed using microcomputed tomography. Among the five composites investigated (0.5–2.5 wt % MFC, step 0.5 wt %), the 1.5 wt % sample showed the best overall performance, except in Vickers microhardness. Compared with pure ASA, this composite improved tensile strength and toughness, flexural toughness, and Charpy impact strength by approximately 13%, tensile modulus by 15%, flexural modulus by 12%, and flexural strength by approximately 28%. The highest Vickers microhardness was achieved by the 1.0 wt % composite, showing a 30.8% increase over pure ASA. Overall, the introduction of the biobased MFC, even at low loadings, enhanced the mechanical strength of ASA and improved the quality metrics. Such findings highlight the potential of ASA/MFC as a sustainable composite for outdoor 3D printing applications.

title: AI-enabled gas sensors for breath-based diagnostics: smart mask platforms toward personalized healthcare
summary: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with breath-based gas detection is paving the way for promising advances in noninvasive diagnostics at the point of care. Specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled human breath act
content: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with breath-based gas detection is paving the way for promising advances in noninvasive diagnostics at the point of care. Specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled human breath act as biomarkers of several diseases. However, accurate breath analysis remains challenging because VOC concentrations vary from parts per billion (ppb) to parts per million (ppm). Conventional gas sensors suffer from humidity interference, baseline drift, signal noise, poor selectivity and sensor variability. AI enables robust pattern recognition, feature extraction and classification with improved accuracy. This review discusses how machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and the Internet of Things (IoT) transform conventional gas sensors into intelligent breath-monitoring devices. We review face-mask integration strategies, including fibre embedded, directly fabricated, and externally attached modular designs for real-time monitoring. We further discuss sensing materials, device architecture, data acquisition systems, cloud and edge computing platforms and ML and DL algorithms for disease prediction and wearable deployment. We also examine commercialization challenges, including the lack of universally accepted VOC biomarkers, the limited clinically validated datasets, privacy, model interpretability, and regulatory requirements. Finally, we highlight future directions toward clinically reliable, AI-enabled wearable breath diagnostic systems for personalized healthcare.

title: TWO ROADS TO A BIOECONOMY: CLUSTERING THE WORLD’S LEADING BIOFUEL PRODUCERS
source: EPRA International Journal of Research & Development (IJRD)
summary: The global shift towards decarbonization has made biofuels an important transitional energy resource. However, existing assessments often focus on production volume while overlooking differences in national sustainable development strategie
content: The global shift towards decarbonization has made biofuels an important transitional energy resource. However, existing assessments often focus on production volume while overlooking differences in national sustainable development strategies. To address this gap, this study examines whether the global biofuel market follows distinct sustainable development pathways. Analysing 22 countries that account for over 90% of global biofuel supply, the study uses time-series forecasting to impute missing data and K-means clustering to group countries based on economic innovation, environmental performance, social dependence, and production scale. The findings identify two main models: an “Agriculture-Driven” model characterized by high labour intensity and an “Innovation-Led” model marked by higher R&D expenditure. Although the two models differ in their socio-economic characteristics, they show no significant differences in production output or transport decarbonization potential. This suggests that high-tech industrialization is not the only requirement for a high-performing bioeconomy. The study therefore emphasizes the need for policies that account for these different development pathways rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach.

title: Temozolomide exposure and delivery barriers in glioma: cross-compartment pharmacokinetics and implications for resistance
summary: Temozolomide (TMZ) remains central to glioblastoma therapy, yet treatment failure reflects both pharmacodynamic resistance and incomplete exposure across relevant intracranial compartments. In this evidence-audited narrative review, we trac
content: Temozolomide (TMZ) remains central to glioblastoma therapy, yet treatment failure reflects both pharmacodynamic resistance and incomplete exposure across relevant intracranial compartments. In this evidence-audited narrative review, we trace TMZ from the systemic circulation across the blood–brain and blood–brain tumor barriers to regional distribution, cellular uptake or export, intracellular retention, chemical activation, and DNA damage. Combined adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-binding cassette subfamily B member 1 (ABCB1)/ATP-binding cassette subfamily G member 2 (ABCG2) deficiency increases brain penetration in mice without changing systemic exposure, supporting a contribution from endothelial transport; however, evidence that individual tumor-cell transporters directly export TMZ is heterogeneous and includes negative findings. Transporter-mediated influx and vesicular partitioning further indicate that inadequate uptake or intracellular removal can be mistaken for classical efflux. Human cerebrospinal fluid and brain-interstitial studies demonstrate partial, compartment-dependent penetration, whereas focused-ultrasound studies support the feasibility of barrier opening. Survival outcomes from single-arm studies cannot be attributed to ultrasound without a randomized comparison. A focused full-text audit of 15 TMZ-containing delivery-platform studies identified extensive formulation and efficacy reporting but only three studies with direct analyte-specific measurements targeting parent TMZ in biological samples. These measurements were limited to plasma or whole blood and single-time-point total-tissue extracts of whole brain or brain tumor; none established regional unbound parent-TMZ pharmacokinetics. We propose a claim–evidence framework that separates direct transport and pharmacokinetic evidence from functional sensitization, association, delivery-concept, and negative evidence. Linking parent-drug exposure, regional distribution, pharmacodynamic competence, safety, and clinical feasibility can help determine when inadequate exposure is a modifiable component of glioma resistance.

title: Cross-Facility Materials Discovery Platform: Integrating Heterogeneous Data and Automated Experimental Pipelines into High-Throughput Workflows
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven materials discovery depends on the availability of large, highly annotated experimental datasets. However, data generated in typical materials science projects are fragmented across heterogeneous instrume
content: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven materials discovery depends on the availability of large, highly annotated experimental datasets. However, data generated in typical materials science projects are fragmented across heterogeneous instruments, laboratories, and user facilities, each with its own formats, schedules, and degree of curation. In addition, manual sample preparation, time-consuming characterization, and changing sample form factors and holders between process steps often limit throughput and therefore dataset size. Here, we present a modular cross-facility workflow that addresses both the physical and the data bottlenecks. We combine robotic thin-film deposition, a custom robotic UV-vis setup, and high-throughput synchrotron end stations with custom, QR-code-tagged sample holders, preserving each film’s identity as it moves between experimental setups. Using Crucible, a schema-free data management platform developed at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, we link every sample, container, and dataset into a provenance network that traces each thin film through synthesis, deposition, characterization, and analysis. A Python client and custom web interfaces connect the Molecular Foundry with two beamlines at the Advanced Light Source and enable streamlined, high-throughput data collection pipelines. To demonstrate this workflow, we fabricated 6,105 thin films spanning 618 hybrid metal halide compounds over six months, of which approximately 3,400 were characterized by robotic grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering and 2,000 by residual gas analysis under extreme-ultraviolet exposure, generating a highly curated AI-ready materials discovery dataset that accurately reproduces a subset of matched manually prepared samples. We further demonstrate automated downstream analysis, including human-in-the-loop machine-learning classification and mechanistic evaluation of structure-property relationships. Together, the dataset and infrastructure provide a blueprint for scaling materials experimentation to facility-level AI platforms.

title: CRISPR/Cas-Enabled Point-of-Care Screening of Human Papillomavirus in Cervical Cancer
summary: Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistent infection, particularly involving high-risk subtypes, remains the primary driver of cervical cancer, underlining the exigent need for rapid, accessible point-of-care (POC) diagnostics. CRISPR/Cas-based
content: Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistent infection, particularly involving high-risk subtypes, remains the primary driver of cervical cancer, underlining the exigent need for rapid, accessible point-of-care (POC) diagnostics. CRISPR/Cas-based biosensors have developed as transformative tools for POC testing (POCT) because of their exceptional specificity and programmable cleavage activity. This review systematically evaluates HPV biomarkers, including DNA, RNA, and proteins, with a focus on CRISPR/Cas-enabled technologies for POC detection of HPV. We discuss the performance of diverse CRISPR/Cas systems for multiplex biomarker detection in POC settings for HPV infection screening. Recognizing the critical role of signal readout in POCT, we explore several signal-enhancement strategies, including nucleic acid amplification, preamplification-free assays, and integrated platforms tailored to POCT practicality, all aimed at balancing accuracy and practicality. Finally, we address key barriers to clinical translation and propose a roadmap that highlights the emerging role of AI-assisted platforms in advancing multiplexed detection, thereby supporting future decentralized HPV screening and contributing to the global elimination of cervical cancer.

title: Loan Management of Micro Financing Companies
source: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
summary: This research examined the loan management practices of microfinance companies (MFCs) in the Fifth District of Pangasinan, focusing on the strategies used for loan assessment, approval, risk management, policy and repayment processes, as we
content: This research examined the loan management practices of microfinance companies (MFCs) in the Fifth District of Pangasinan, focusing on the strategies used for loan assessment, approval, risk management, policy and repayment processes, as well as identifying the challenges these institutions face in managing loans. The study aims to understand the effectiveness of these practices and how they impact the financial stability and sustainability of microfinance operations in the region. The research employed a descriptive methodology, utilizing quantitative data from surveys. The respondents included managers, loan officers, and clients from 36 microfinance institutions operating in the Fifth District of Pangasinan, providing a broad perspective on the practices and challenges faced by MFCs. The results of the study indicate that microfinance companies predominantly rely on business aspects and repayment capacity when assessing loan applications. Risk management is primarily focused on categorizing clients by risk levels, although the study identified gaps in the reporting of these risks, leading to potential vulnerabilities. In terms of loan repayment, regular reminders are used effectively, but difficulties in tracking overdue accounts and poor documentation practices hinder timely collections. Moreover, MFCs face challenges in ensuring strict compliance with loan policies and struggle with adequately training staff and communicating policy changes. The study also found that technological support for loan management is limited, with few institutions collecting client feedback to improve services. In conclusion, the study underscores the importance of improving risk management, loan monitoring, and staff training within microfinance institutions. It is recommended that MFCs implement more effective risk management systems, strengthen their loan collection efforts, and invest in technology to enhance operational efficiency and client engagement.

title: Continuous Solar-Powered Syngas Production: Advancements and Insights From the EU SOMMER Project
summary: The EU-funded SOMMER project aims to develop and demonstrate a novel carbon-neutral pathway for syngas production by integrating solar energy into a catalytic membrane reactor for the splitting of H₂O and CO₂. CO₂ can be sourced from high-c
content: The EU-funded SOMMER project aims to develop and demonstrate a novel carbon-neutral pathway for syngas production by integrating solar energy into a catalytic membrane reactor for the splitting of H₂O and CO₂. CO₂ can be sourced from high-carbon-emitting industries or via direct air capture, enabling syngas production without fossil-based energy and replacing natural gas as feedstock. Syngas, a mixture of H₂ and CO, is a key intermediate in the chemical industry, and SOMMER addresses the full value chain, from CO₂ provision at a cement plant to syngas formation and further conversion into valuable products such as dimethyl ether (DME) or methanol. The core of SOMMER technology is the optimized energy integration of a single-step CO₂ and H₂O thermochemical conversion process, supported by highly selective catalysts and a ceramic oxygen transport membrane. A concentrated solar-thermal plant provides the required thermal energy. Key outcomes include experimental demonstration of the solar-powered membrane reactor and the development of high-performance, cost-effective membranes. Membrane manufacturing will be advanced via conventional extrusion methods and additive manufacturing to optimize effective membrane surface area within the reactor. The concept allows flexible operation under two scenarios: (1) a purely solar-driven approach at 1500 °C and (2) a biogas-supported approach at 900 °C. SOMMER will also assess the technological, ecological, and economic potential of flexible, efficient solar syngas production. Overall, the project aims to advance solar-powered membrane technology toward scalable, low-carbon chemical production, contributing to sustainable industrial processes and a circular carbon economy.

title: Computing Hosoya index using an efficient matrix-based approach in MATLAB for general graphs
summary: Topological indices serve as essential analytical tools in fields ranging from pharmaceutical research to network analysis. Among these, the Hosoya index is one of the most significant indices, introduced by Haruo Hosoya in 1971. It is defi
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Topological indices serve as essential analytical tools in fields ranging from pharmaceutical research to network analysis. Among these, the Hosoya index is one of the most significant indices, introduced by Haruo Hosoya in 1971. It is defined as the sum of non-adjacent edge sets (matchings) for a given graph. In this article, we introduce a new matrix-based approach for calculating the Hosoya index using an effective algorithm. This technique includes a MATLAB-based implementation that systematically identifies independent edge sets. To demonstrate the application of the approach to chemical graph structures, illustrative examples involving alkane molecular graphs, RNA secondary structures, and selected chemical compounds are provided, highlighting its effectiveness and computational efficiency.
