title: Perfluoropolyether Functionalized Polyhedral Oligomeric Silsesquioxane: Synthesis, Rheology, and Crystallization Suppression in Fluorinated Blended Composite Formulations
summary: Perfluoropolyethers (PFPEs) are highly valued liquid lubricants for extreme environments due to their wide liquid-phase ranges and low glass transition temperatures (Tg); however, they remain highly susceptible to catastrophic Lewis acid-ca
content: Perfluoropolyethers (PFPEs) are highly valued liquid lubricants for extreme environments due to their wide liquid-phase ranges and low glass transition temperatures (Tg); however, they remain highly susceptible to catastrophic Lewis acid-catalyzed chain scission at their acetal linkages. To address this vulnerability and improve the stability of fluorinated composite formulations, we report the synthesis, characterization, and rheological performance of a novel perfluoropolyether-functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (Q8M8PFPE). Q8M8PFPE was synthesized in high yield (>90%) via the platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation of a hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO) derived oligomeric allyl ether with octakis(dimethylsiloxy)silsesquioxane. The resulting core-shell macromer exhibits a low Tg of -73 °C, closely mimicking commercial PFPE, specifically Fomblin Y, while providing an inorganic silsesquioxane silica core capable of forming a protective, passivating silica char under thermal stress. Furthermore, we demonstrate that Q8M8PFPE acts as an effective compatibilizer when blended with highly symmetric fluorinated POSS cages, specifically (1H,1H,2H,2H-heptadecafluorodecyl)8Si8O12 (T8FD). Q8M8PFPE/T8FD blends undergo programmable phase separation and crystallization over variable weight fractions, and the flexible PFPE tails establish a cohesive solvation shell that suppresses crystallization to ensure a homogeneous, shear-resistant molecular dispersion. This work establishes Q8M8PFPE as a highly compatible drop-in modifier or standalone lubricant grease capable of overcoming the performance thresholds of traditional fluorinated fluids.

title: Ferroptosis in Parkinson’s disease: mechanistic links, natural products, and translational challenges
summary: Parkinson’s disease features dopaminergic neuron loss, α-synuclein pathology, and motor and non-motor manifestations. Ferroptosis is associated to regional iron dyshomeostasis, impaired glutathione defenses, mitochondrial dysfunction, dopam
content: Parkinson’s disease features dopaminergic neuron loss, α-synuclein pathology, and motor and non-motor manifestations. Ferroptosis is associated to regional iron dyshomeostasis, impaired glutathione defenses, mitochondrial dysfunction, dopamine oxidation, and membrane injury. In preclinical models, natural compounds and traditional Chinese medicine formulas modulate iron handling, NRF2-system x c - -GSH–GPX4 signaling, ferritinophagy, lipid remodeling, and mitochondrial quality control. This review examines these mechanisms and translational requirements for ferroptosis-directed PD interventions.

title: Beyond pathogen-intrinsic resistance: the host context in AMR evolution
summary: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is traditionally viewed as a pathogen-intrinsic, genetically encoded trait. However, growing evidence indicates that antimicrobial susceptibility is dynamically shaped by the host context during an infection.
content: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is traditionally viewed as a pathogen-intrinsic, genetically encoded trait. However, growing evidence indicates that antimicrobial susceptibility is dynamically shaped by the host context during an infection. Gradients in oxygen, nutrients, pH, immune effectors, spatial structure, and polymicrobial interactions generate a highly dynamic microenvironment that can profoundly influence microbial physiology and drug response. Within each of these gradient niches, pathogens can frequently occupy metabolic states that alter their kill kinetics, promote tolerance, and enable persistence even without intrinsic genetic elements. Experimental models of infection further demonstrate that antimicrobial efficacy depends not only on drug potency and microbial genotype, but also on host-imposed constraints. In this review, we highlight a systems-level framework in which AMR emerges from dynamic interactions between the pathogen, host microenvironment, and antimicrobial exposure. Such a framework takes into account tolerance, persistence, and resistance along a physiological continuum shaped by a dynamic host-pathogen-drug interaction. Therefore, recognizing AMR as an emergent property of a dynamic interplay between host-pathogen and drug exposure challenges reliance on standardized in vitro susceptibility testing and underscores the need for physiologically relevant infection models. By incorporating host context into experimental design and therapeutic strategy, this framework offers a more mechanistic understanding of antimicrobial susceptibility and resistance evolution, and suggests new avenues to be explored for therapeutic development and future research.

title: Polarized light microscopy to quantify changes in the tympanic membrane microstructure in chronic otitis media
summary: Introduction Chronic otitis media (COM) induces progressive structural remodeling of the tympanic membrane (TM), beginning with epithelial hyperplasia and advancing to disruption of the organized collagen architecture that underlies its mec
content: Introduction Chronic otitis media (COM) induces progressive structural remodeling of the tympanic membrane (TM), beginning with epithelial hyperplasia and advancing to disruption of the organized collagen architecture that underlies its mechanical behavior. Loss of collagen integrity within the TM has been associated with an increased risk of retraction and perforation, yet no clinically available method directly assesses layer-specific TM structure in vivo . Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) has recently been proposed as a promising approach for evaluating TM microstructure, but it has not yet been applied to pathologic TMs. Quantitative polarized light microscopy (qPLM) of diseased TM sections provides disease-relevant biological support for future evaluation of PS-OCT in pathologic TMs. We aimed to measure changes in optical retardance of collagen layers in both normal and pathologic TMs. Methods Mice were intranasally inoculated with an upper respiratory pathogen to induce otitis media. Auditory brainstem responses were recorded before (baseline) and at 7 and 28 days post-inoculation (DPI) to confirm middle ear involvement. TMs from control and OM mice were harvested at 28 DPI, embedded in Araldite resin, and sectioned at 7 μm thickness. Optical retardance of TM collagen layers was quantified using polarized light microscopy. Polarized light microscopy for assessing the integrity of collagen structures was validated using harvested human TMs. Results TM sections from mice with chronic otitis media exhibited notable alterations in optical retardance at 28 days post-inoculation (DPI). Regions of structural alteration demonstrated a significantly reduced mean retardance (4.62 ± 1.34 nm) compared with adjacent, unaltered regions within the same TM (9.78 ± 0.95 nm). Control TMs exhibited comparable retardance values (9.16 ± 0.87 nm). Retardance in altered TM regions was significantly lower than both unaltered regions of the same TM and control TMs ( p < 0.05 for both comparisons). This is consistent with collagen disorganization and tissue degradation associated with otitis media. Induced heat damage in a human TM shows similar changes in retardance to those seen in mouse models of OM. Conclusions qPLM provides a robust method for evaluating TM structure following otitis media. Optical retardance was significantly reduced in regions classified as disrupted within COM TMs, consistent with progressive collagen degradation during disease. Once optimized, PS-OCT-equipped otoscopes may offer a valuable, clinically translatable approach for assessing TM layer integrity in vivo .

title: Advancements in Solar Drying Technology: Enhancing Food Preservation and Solar Power Systems for Sustainable Solutions
summary: Global food insecurity and escalating postharvest losses, which affect nearly one‐third of total food production, necessitate sustainable preservation technologies aligned with the Food and Agriculture Organization targets and the United Na
content: Global food insecurity and escalating postharvest losses, which affect nearly one‐third of total food production, necessitate sustainable preservation technologies aligned with the Food and Agriculture Organization targets and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Solar drying has emerged as an energy‐efficient and environmentally benign alternative to conventional fossil‐fuel‐based dehydration methods. This review critically examines advancements in direct, indirect, and hybrid solar drying systems, evaluating their design configurations, thermal performance, operational parameters, and product quality outcomes. Comparative assessments indicate that hybrid systems integrating auxiliary heating (biomass, electric, or heat pumps) enhance drying reliability under fluctuating climatic conditions while improving overall thermo‐economic efficiency. The study further explores advanced performance‐enhancement strategies, including jet‐impingement air heaters, thermal energy storage (sensible, latent, and thermochemical systems), desiccant‐assisted dehumidification, nanofluid‐based heat‐transfer augmentation, and solar thermal selective coatings. Integration of phase change materials and composite desiccants significantly improves moisture removal rates, energy efficiency, and off‐sunshine operability. Emerging nanofluid and surface‐modification technologies demonstrate notable improvements in collector efficiency and heat‐transfer coefficients. The review identifies current technical limitations, economic considerations, and scalability challenges while outlining future research directions for high‐efficiency, sustainable solar drying systems applicable to agricultural and industrial sectors.

title: Manipulating Monomicelle Monolayer Assembly via Salt Effect Toward Tailorable Mesoporous Polydopamine Superstructures for Aqueous Batteries
summary: The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous
content: The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous superstructures poses a significant challenge. Here, we report a salt effect-modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for the precise construction of monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures. The concerted salt effect arising from Debye screening and salting-out stabilizes the composite monomicelles, reduces their hydrophilicity, and promotes their migration and lateral monolayer assembly at the emulsion interface. Increasing the salt content accelerates assembly kinetics, enhances interfacial affinity, and increases micellar rigidity, enabling tunable interfacial coverage and thereby producing a series of monolayer mesoporous superstructures, including monolayer honeycomb-like mesoporous nanosheets, monolayer honeycomb-like mesoporous vesicles, monolayer compound eye-like mesoporous vesicles, and monolayer compound eye-like mesoporous nanosheets. As a proof of concept, monolayer honeycomb-like nanosheets with open mesochannels and abundant functional groups were demonstrated as a nano-ion divider. By homogenizing the ion flux and enhancing ion affinity and transport, this architecture enables dendrite-free Sn aqueous batteries with an exceptional lifespan of 2794 h. This work opens new avenues for constructing monolayer superstructures with unparalleled architectural modularization.

title: The M4 Earthquakes Induced by the Quest Carbon Capture and Storage Project
summary: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) projects have not yet induced significant earthquakes, and many experts assume that seismicity poses a small risk. Recent earthquakes in Canada challenge this assumption. Since August 2015, the Quest CCS pro
content: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) projects have not yet induced significant earthquakes, and many experts assume that seismicity poses a small risk. Recent earthquakes in Canada challenge this assumption. Since August 2015, the Quest CCS project has been injecting ∼1 Mt/year of CO 2 into basal sediments that overlie crystalline basement. Contemporaneously, induced earthquakes have reactivated reverse‐slip on basement faults. We find a strong temporal relationship (>99% confidence) between earthquakes and injection. These events have now reached M4, were widely felt in Edmonton, Canada, and are the largest known CCS induced earthquakes worldwide. Reservoir modeling suggests small overpressures (∼2 to 40 kPa) at the time of the distant (∼35 km) earthquake, and require additional data for validation. Pressure management efforts could take several years before reductions are realized at these distances. Our results highlight that CCS projects require careful monitoring and risk assessment strategies, above‐and‐beyond the currently applied levels.

title: Institutional Thresholds and the Environmental Effectiveness of Green Finance: Evidence From Biodiversity Conservation in Africa
summary: Green finance is increasingly expected to reconcile climate action with biodiversity conservation, yet its effectiveness remains heterogeneous across Africa. This study examines how institutional conditions shape both the allocation of Gree
content: Green finance is increasingly expected to reconcile climate action with biodiversity conservation, yet its effectiveness remains heterogeneous across Africa. This study examines how institutional conditions shape both the allocation of Green Official Development Assistance (GODA) and its association with biodiversity‐related conservation coverage across 48 African countries over 2000–2017. Building on the Conduit‐Filter‐Interaction‐Bypass Institutional (CFIB‐I) framework, the study conceptualizes green finance as an institutionally conditioned process in which formal and informal institutions influence both resource allocation and the conversion of environmental resources into conservation‐related outcomes. Empirically, we estimate two fixed‐effects panel specifications addressing these distinct dimensions, using Driscoll–Kraay standard errors to account for cross‐sectional dependence and serial correlation. The results show that political stability is positively associated with GODA allocation, while the conditioning role of formal and informal institutions varies across income groups and regions. GODA is not significantly associated with biodiversity‐related conservation coverage in the full‐sample baseline, indicating that resource mobilization does not automatically translate into conservation outcomes. Its association with conservation coverage becomes institutionally conditional in specific regional and income‐group settings, while renewable energy exhibits similarly heterogeneous relationships across institutional contexts. Substantial regional, income‐group and temporal heterogeneity further shows that no single institutional configuration characterizes the green finance biodiversity relationship across Africa. These findings suggest that increasing environmental finance alone is insufficient to improve conservation‐related coverage and should be accompanied by stronger implementation capacity, public integrity, accountability and context‐specific institutional arrangements.

title: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
summary: Polymer-solvent-nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid-liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer-induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation
content: Polymer-solvent-nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid-liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer-induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres, yet the process is often limited by coarsening of pores or collapse within the fibre core, leading to structural inhomogeneity. Here, we advance this strategy through Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer induced assembly (CAST), in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ during solvent exchange and preferentially retained within the polymer rich phase. These precipitates act as a distributed molecular retarding agent that delays domain growth, thereby preserving bicontinuity throughout the fibre cross-section to up to 250 µm. Using a poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate-ethanol-water system with a phenolic oligomer coprecipitate, we demonstrate that CAST stabilizes the hollow bicontinuous domain structure, extending the attainable specific surface area by ca. 100%. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

title: Digital Intensity and Labour Productivity in the European Union: Between-Country, Within-Country and Within-Sector
summary: The European Union's Digital Decade programme aims for more than 90% of small and medium-sized enterprises to reach at least basic digital intensity by 2030, assuming that digitalisation raises productivity. Yet studies comparing EU countri
content: The European Union's Digital Decade programme aims for more than 90% of small and medium-sized enterprises to reach at least basic digital intensity by 2030, assuming that digitalisation raises productivity. Yet studies comparing EU countries disagree on whether more digitally intensive economies are more productive once their development level is considered. This study investigates how two indicators of enterprise digitalization, the percentage of enterprises achieving at least basic digital intensity and the percentage engaging in online sales, are associated with labour productivity.. The association is examined between countries, within countries over time, and between sectors within the same country and year, using Eurostat data for the EU-27 over 2015–2024. The results show that countries with more digitally intensive enterprises are more productive, but this association disappears once economic development is controlled. Within the same country, more digitally intensive sectors are significantly more productive. However, increases in digital intensity over time are not followed by measurable productivity gains. Digital intensity is therefore a marker of productive economies and sectors rather than a demonstrated short-run driver of productivity growth, and adoption targets should be accompanied by support for skills, management and complementary investment.

title: Simultaneous quantification of DMSP-related sulfur metabolites reveals hidden metabolic diversity in marine bacteria
summary: Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a key organosulfur compound in marine ecosystems, and its microbial metabolism involves multiple biosynthetic and degradative pathways that are difficult to fully resolve using conventional stepwise appr
content: Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a key organosulfur compound in marine ecosystems, and its microbial metabolism involves multiple biosynthetic and degradative pathways that are difficult to fully resolve using conventional stepwise approaches. In this study, we developed a targeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of six key DMSP-related sulfur metabolites in a single analysis, including L-methionine (L-Met), S-methyl-L-methionine (SMM), 4-methylthio-2-hydroxybutyrate (MTHB), 3-methylthiopropylamine (MTPA), 3-methylmercaptopropionate (MMPA), and DMSP. The method was validated over the concentration range of 0.1–1,500 ng/mL and showed good specificity, linearity, precision, accuracy, extraction recovery, matrix effects, and stability. Its applicability was assessed in the model DMSP-degrading strain Ruegeria pomeroyi DSS-3 and the DMSP-producing strain Roseibium aggregatum LZB033, where time-course experiments captured metabolite dynamics consistent with their established pathways. Application to 42 marine bacterial isolates identified metabolite profiles consistent with PCR detection of known DMSP metabolic genes, as well as unexpected patterns in strains for which the corresponding genes were not amplified. These included MMPA accumulation after DMSP supplementation without detectable dmdA amplification, the co-occurrence of MTPA, MMPA, and DMSP without amplification of the screened DMSP biosynthesis genes, and high MMPA levels after L-Met supplementation without detectable DMSP. These findings highlight potential metabolic routes that warrant further investigation. Collectively, this metabolite-guided LC-MS/MS method offers a rapid and integrated tool for characterizing bacterial DMSP-related metabolic phenotypes, and identifying candidate pathways for further genetic and biochemical characterization. IMPORTANCE Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is one of the most abundant organic sulfur compounds in the ocean, and an important component of marine sulfur cycling. Marine bacteria transform DMSP through diverse metabolic pathways, but these pathways remain difficult to fully resolve because metabolites are often analyzed individually. We developed a rapid analytical approach that simultaneously measures six DMSP-related sulfur metabolites, providing a more complete view of bacterial sulfur metabolism. Applying this approach to diverse marine bacteria revealed metabolic patterns that could not be explained by currently known pathways. In several strains, sulfur compounds accumulated despite the absence of expected metabolic genes, pointing to previously unrecognized routes of DMSP metabolism. Our findings demonstrate that marine bacteria possess greater sulfur metabolic diversity than currently appreciated and provide a new approach for uncovering hidden pathways in marine sulfur cycling.

title: A review of major volatile organic compounds in plant defence priming, with a focus on geraniol’s understudied potential
summary: The intricate world of plant-plant and plant–insect communication is heavily mediated by volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which serve as crucial external signaling molecules. Among their many functions, VOCs induce plant defence priming,
content: The intricate world of plant-plant and plant–insect communication is heavily mediated by volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which serve as crucial external signaling molecules. Among their many functions, VOCs induce plant defence priming, a state characterized by enhanced and accelerated immune responses to future stressors. Despite a substantial amount of literature on prominent priming agents such as green leaf volatiles (GLVs) and specific terpenes, a significant knowledge gap persists concerning the full potential of other VOCs, particularly geraniol. This review synthesizes current research on major classes of VOCs, including mono- and sesquiterpenes, and few other compounds, and provides a detailed overview of their molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways. A specific focus is placed on geraniol, whose role in plant communication and pathogen resistance remains significantly understudied compared to its well-documented antibacterial and insect-repellent properties. This article evaluates geraniol’s potential as a sustainable and bio-friendly agent for agricultural applications. The findings suggest that a deeper investigation into geraniol's priming efficacy and its synergistic interactions with other volatile compounds can unlock novel strategies for improving crop resilience and reducing reliance on synthetic pesticides. Consequently, this work highlights geraniol as a promising, yet overlooked, candidate for future research in the field of plant defence priming.

title: Nanobiosensors for cardiac biomarker monitoring using electrochemical and optical detection
summary: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) accounting for a large portion of both the clinical and economic burden. Sensitive and specific cardiac biomarkers that
content: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) accounting for a large portion of both the clinical and economic burden. Sensitive and specific cardiac biomarkers that enable rapid diagnosis of ACS and associated intervention can therefore profoundly impact accordingly. A diverse array of in vitro diagnostics exists for the detection of myriad cardiac biomarkers, notably troponin, CK-MB, and myoglobin, each capable of fulfilling diagnostic and/or prognostic roles. Recent advances in electrochemical and optical nanobiosensors have enabled highly sensitive, rapid, and point-of-care detection of cardiac biomarkers. The integration of nanomaterials, including gold nanoparticles, graphene derivatives, carbon nanotubes, and quantum dots, has significantly improved analytical performance by enhancing sensitivity, specificity, and signal amplification. This review systematically summarizes recent developments in nanobiosensor platforms for troponin, CK-MB, and myoglobin detection, highlighting sensing mechanisms, analytical performance, clinical applicability, current challenges, and future translational opportunities.

title: Impact of CO₂ Storage on Thermochemical Energy Storage System for Solar Power Tower
summary: The integration of thermochemical energy storage (TCES) based on calcium looping with supercritical CO₂ Brayton cycles offers a promising pathway to enhance the efficiency, dispatchability, and economic performance of solar power tower plan
content: The integration of thermochemical energy storage (TCES) based on calcium looping with supercritical CO₂ Brayton cycles offers a promising pathway to enhance the efficiency, dispatchability, and economic performance of solar power tower plants. This study evaluates five CO₂ storage line configurations in total: a baseline layout and four advanced alternatives including an external bypass, a turbine+preheater integration, and heat recovery via molten salt or thermal oil subsystems (which utilize internal bypass). A dynamic model developed in OpenModelica and Python was used to simulate dynamic operation under meteorological conditions from Carrera Pinto, Chile. Results show that bypasses prevent overcharging and improve flexibility, while expanders reduce parasitic compression losses. Heat recovery systems significantly reduce heater consumption and enhance net power output, with the thermal oil system achieving the highest capacity factor (65.1%) and largest reduction in energy losses (75.5%) relative to the baseline. Economic analysis indicates that the CO₂ line moderately impacts total plant cost (<12 MUSD), yet thermal oil and molten salt options achieve lower LCOE and LCOS, with the thermal oil configuration delivering a 50% improvement over the baseline. These results highlight the potential of optimized CO₂ line designs to improve the techno-economic viability of CSP plants and provide guidance for selecting high-performance, cost-effective storage configurations.

title: Engineering Narrow-Bandgap g-C3N4/AgIn5S8 Heterojunction for Boosted Visible-Light Tetracycline Degradation
summary: Tetracycline contamination in aquatic environments motivates the development of efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts with improved light utilization and interfacial charge-transfer capability. Herein, a narrow-bandgap g-C3N4/Ag
content: Tetracycline contamination in aquatic environments motivates the development of efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts with improved light utilization and interfacial charge-transfer capability. Herein, a narrow-bandgap g-C3N4/AgIn5S8 (NCN-AIS) heterojunction was rationally engineered. Characterization results revealed robust interfacial contact between AgIn5S8 nanoparticles and NCN, with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) results suggesting possible In–N-associated interfacial interactions, supporting the successful establishment of the heterojunction interface. Notably, the optimal sample (NCN-AIS-20%) achieved a remarkable tetracycline degradation efficiency of 90.97%, with a reaction rate constant that was 1.4 and 1.8 times higher than those of pristine NCN and AIS, respectively. Besides the enhanced short-wavelength visible-light response and excellent reusability, ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (UHPLC–MS) analysis clearly mapped out the complete stepwise oxidative degradation pathway of tetracycline into CO2 and H2O. Mechanistic insights revealed that the narrow bandgap of the NCN-AIS heterojunction broadened visible light absorption and drastically accelerated photogenerated charge separation and transfer. Radical trapping experiments demonstrated a synergistic effect among h+, •O2–, and •OH, where h+ and •O2– dominated the degradation process. Furthermore, DFT calculations of the difference charge density provided profound theoretical support for the charge transfer mechanism at the atomic level. Consequently, this work not only supplies an efficient photocatalyst for mitigating aqueous antibiotic pollution but also sheds light on the rational design and mechanistic understanding of analogous heterojunction systems.

title: Combating systemic risk contagion in supply chain: The dual governance role of digital transformation
summary: Supply chains are fundamental to business operations and national economic development. The digital economy offers new ways to mitigate systemic risk and stabilize supply chains. This study emphasizes the pivotal role of customer digital tr
content: Supply chains are fundamental to business operations and national economic development. The digital economy offers new ways to mitigate systemic risk and stabilize supply chains. This study emphasizes the pivotal role of customer digital transformation in governing systemic risks within supply chains. By analyzing data from the top five suppliers of China's A-share listed companies (2010-2023), it measures the systemic risk spillover between upstream and downstream enterprises, explores whether customer digital transformation mitigates risk contagion, and delves into the underlying mechanisms from both internal and external supply chain governance perspectives. The findings reveal that customer digitalization reduces bidirectional risk spillovers, while supplier concentration exerts a nonlinear impact on this risk mitigation effect. Furthermore, digital transformation contributes to diminishing the market risk effects on demand, curbing the spread of credit risk, and reducing deviations between supply and demand. Finally, the heterogeneity analysis demonstrates that the risk-mitigating effect of customer digitalization is particularly pronounced in state-owned enterprises, geographically proximate supply chains, and customers with robust operational efficiency and internal controls quality. These findings provide fresh insights into the relationship between digital transformation and systemic risk contagion in supply chains, suggesting strategies to enhance supply chain risk management in the era of the digital economy.

title: Novel α-Microspheres Potentiate Radioembolization for Liver Cancer via Synergistic Vascular Disruption and Self-Powered Cerenkov Photodynamic Therapy
summary: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) with β-emitting microspheres such as 90 Y serves as standard palliative care for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet embolism-triggered intratumoral hypoxia confers radioresistance and limits
content: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) with β-emitting microspheres such as 90 Y serves as standard palliative care for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet embolism-triggered intratumoral hypoxia confers radioresistance and limits therapeutic efficacy. Unlike β-rays, α-particles possess ultra-high linear energy transfer (LET) and oxygen-independent cytotoxicity, allowing efficient elimination of hypoxic tumor cells. Herein, we fabricated α-emitting 223 Ra-labeled chitosan/calcium phosphate microspheres (denoted 223 Ra-Chi/CaP MS). Capitalizing on the potent hypoxia-insensitive cytotoxicity of α-particles, these microspheres eradicate perivascular tumor cells and disrupt tumor vascular endothelium. To further eliminate tumor cells located distally from the vasculature, the microspheres were loaded with the photosensitizer methylene blue (MB) to harness Cerenkov photons emitted from the 223 Ra decay chain and achieve Cerenkov radiation-induced photodynamic therapy (CR-PDT), thereby expanding the therapeutic reach. The resulting 223 Ra-Chi/CaP-MB MS exhibited excellent physicochemical stability, sustained MB release, and prolonged tumor retention following hepatic artery delivery. In vitro studies demonstrated that the synergistic action of 223 Ra and CR-PDT triggered extensive DNA double-strand breaks and robust ROS generation, leading to enhanced apoptosis even under hypoxic conditions. In a rat orthotopic liver tumor model, TARE using 223 Ra-Chi/CaP-MB MS exerted more potent tumor growth inhibition than embolization controls or plain 223 Ra-Chi/CaP MS, predominantly through disrupting tumor blood vessels, blocking compensatory angiogenesis, and triggering extensive tumor cell apoptosis. With confirmed biosafety, this 223 Ra-based microsphere platform represents a transformative strategy to revitalize TARE for β-refractory liver cancer.

title: Di/tripeptides in cancer: from mechanisms to therapeutics
summary: Research on tumor metabolic reprogramming has long centered on glucose, lipids and free amino acids. By contrast, di/tripeptides, which lie at the interface between protein breakdown products and functional metabolic signals, have only rece
content: Research on tumor metabolic reprogramming has long centered on glucose, lipids and free amino acids. By contrast, di/tripeptides, which lie at the interface between protein breakdown products and functional metabolic signals, have only recently begun to be recognized as a distinct molecular tier in cancer biology. Compared with longer peptides, di/tripeptides display greater metabolic mobility and a clearer dependence on dedicated transport systems. Here we systematically review the sources, transport, metabolic use, biological functions and clinical translational potential of di/tripeptides in cancer. Current evidence indicates that di/tripeptides arise from endogenous protein degradation, dietary digestion and microbial metabolism. Under nutrient limitation, tumor cells can recover amino acids through carnosine dipeptidase 2 (CNDP2)-mediated extracellular cleavage of dipeptides or uptake of intact di/tripeptides followed by intracellular hydrolysis. Beyond their role as nutrient substrates, selected di/tripeptides directly influence tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis and drug resistance, and shape the tumor microenvironment by modulating acid base balance, redox homeostasis, angiogenesis and immune cell function. At the clinical translational level, di/tripeptides have emerged as candidate metabolomic and peptidomic biomarkers, transporter targeted imaging probes, functionally modified therapeutic agents and engineered delivery modules. Di/tripeptides should be viewed as molecular nodes that connect tumor nutrient adaptation, signaling control, microenvironmental remodeling and clinical translation, with significance extending beyond their role as transient intermediates in protein metabolism.

title: Circular Economy, Waste Minimization and Resource Efficiency in Nigeria
summary: Nigeria’s growing waste generation and inefficient resource utilization pose significant challenges to environmental sustainability and economic resilience. This study examines the role of circular economy practices in promoting waste minim
content: Nigeria’s growing waste generation and inefficient resource utilization pose significant challenges to environmental sustainability and economic resilience. This study examines the role of circular economy practices in promoting waste minimization and resource efficiency in Nigeria using a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 398 respondents drawn from manufacturing firms, waste management agencies, and environmental regulatory institutions, while qualitative insights were obtained from semi-structured interviews with 15 key informants across the same sectors. Descriptive statistics and regression analysis were employed to test two hypotheses, complemented by thematic analysis of interview data. The findings reveal that circular economy practices have a significant positive effect on waste minimization (β = 0.621, p < 0.05) and resource efficiency (β = 0.584, p < 0.05). Qualitative evidence further shows that recycling, material reuse, and recovery initiatives reduce landfill disposal, improve material productivity, and lower operational costs, although their effectiveness is constrained by weak policy enforcement, limited financing, and inadequate technical capacity. Anchored on ecological modernization theory and the resource-based view, the study concludes that a transition from linear to circular production systems is essential for achieving sustainable development in Nigeria. The study recommends strengthening regulatory frameworks, investing in circular infrastructure, and integrating informal sector actors to scale circular economy implementation.

title: Navigating Legal Constraints in Asnaf Housing Development on Waqf Land in Malaysia
summary: Zakat and waqf are Islamic social finance instruments with considerable potential to address the housing needs of the asnaf in Malaysia through a combination of immediate financial support and long-term asset-based provision. However, susta
content: Zakat and waqf are Islamic social finance instruments with considerable potential to address the housing needs of the asnaf in Malaysia through a combination of immediate financial support and long-term asset-based provision. However, sustainable asnaf housing remains difficult to realise despite the increasing number of housing initiatives undertaken by zakat and waqf institutions under the State Islamic Religious Councils. This difficulty is not attributable solely to financial and administrative constraints, but also reflects structural legal and institutional issues, including regulatory fragmentation, the legal status of waqf land, institutional disharmony among State Islamic Religious Councils, and the absence of clear legal engineering mechanisms for integrating zakat and waqf in housing development. Existing studies have largely examined zakat and waqf separately, leaving a significant gap in the absence of an operational legal and institutional framework for their integration into asnaf housing development in Malaysia. Accordingly, this study aims to examine the theoretical foundations of zakat waqf integration and to analyse the principal challenges affecting asnaf housing and waqf land development. The study employed a qualitative narrative literature review supported by thematic content analysis of primary and secondary sources, including academic journals, research reports, books, and relevant legal materials. The findings show that asnaf housing problems are shaped by interrelated economic, governance, and legal factors, including limited access to adequate housing, financing constraints, weak waqf asset management, fragmented institutional practices, and unresolved legal issues that hinder the operational integration of zakat and waqf. This study contributes by demonstrating that the challenge of asnaf housing development is not merely a matter of welfare delivery or resource limitation. However, it reflects a structural gap in the legal and institutional construction of zakat and waqf governance within Malaysia’s multi-layered legal system.

title: Asesmen Pasca-MEF dalam Holding Defend ID Terhadap Resiliensi Manajemen Industri Pertahanan Indonesia
summary: Penelitian ini menyajikan analisis mengenai evolusi manajemen industri pertahanan Indonesia pada periode transisi krusial pasca-berakhirnya Rencana Strategis Minimum Essential Force (MEF) dan pembentukan Holding BUMN Industri Pertahanan (De
content: Penelitian ini menyajikan analisis mengenai evolusi manajemen industri pertahanan Indonesia pada periode transisi krusial pasca-berakhirnya Rencana Strategis Minimum Essential Force (MEF) dan pembentukan Holding BUMN Industri Pertahanan (Defend ID). Dengan latar belakang volatilitas rantai pasok global dan pergeseran doktrin pertahanan dari efisiensi biaya menuju keamanan pasokan, penelitian ini mengevaluasi efektivitas strategi Lead Integrator, kesehatan finansial entitas strategis (PT PAL, PT Pindad, PT Dirgantara Indonesia), serta implementasi konsep teknologi guna-ganda (dual-use technology). Metodologi penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif yang diperkuat dengan analisis rasio finansial dan kerangka evaluasi CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product). Temuan utama menunjukkan bahwa konsolidasi di bawah Defend ID telah meningkatkan posisi tawar strategis dan memperbaiki struktur permodalan melalui restrukturisasi utang historis, seperti yang terjadi pada PT Dirgantara Indonesia. Namun, tantangan fundamental tetap persisten, terutama terkait ketidaksiapan sistem pemeliharaan akibat manajemen logistik yang tidak terintegrasi selama era MEF, serta ketergantungan rantai pasok hulu pada komponen asing dalam program unggulan seperti kendaraan taktis Maung. Penelitian ini juga menyoroti keberhasilan model Integrasi Sipil-Militer (Civil-Military Integration/CMI) melalui sertifikasi militer fasilitas MRO komersial (seperti: GMF AeroAsia) sebagai best practice yang harus direplikasi. Kesimpulan laporan merekomendasikan reorientasi kebijakan pengadaan dari pembelian lepas menuju kontrak berbasis kinerja siklus hidup (Life Cycle Support) dan pendalaman struktur industri komponen tier-2 dan tier-3 untuk menjamin kemandirian strategis yang berkelanjutan.

title: Penentuan beban fisik menggunakan metode analisis Cardiovaskular Load (CVL)
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui lamanya waktu istirahat berdasarkan beban kerja fisik pada analis laboratorium dengan membandingkan denyut nadi dan jumlah asupan kalori dari analis tersebut. Dari hasil perhitungan beban kerja (% C
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui lamanya waktu istirahat berdasarkan beban kerja fisik pada analis laboratorium dengan membandingkan denyut nadi dan jumlah asupan kalori dari analis tersebut. Dari hasil perhitungan beban kerja (% CVL) dapat dilihat bahwa nilai % CVL pada setiap analis adalah sebagai berikut: analis 1 (24.81%), analis 2 (22,84%), analis 3 (23,80%), analis 4 (20,28%), analis 5 (20,99%) dan analis 6 (20,36%). Dimana semua analis dikategorikan kerja ringan sehingga tidak diperlukan perbaikan. Adapun jumlah kandungan kalori rata – rata pada asupan makanan pekerja adalah pada analis 1 (2.100 KKal), analis 2 (2.067 KKal), analis 3 (2.046 KKal), analis 4 (2.049 KKal), analis 5 (2.004 KKal) dan analis 6 (1.990 KKal). Adapun waktu istirahat tambahan yang diperlukan pada masing – masing analis adalah sebagai berikut: analis 1 (1,24 menit), analis 2 (48,81 menit), analis 3 (3,56 menit), analis 4 (3,04 menit), analis 5 (1,79 menit), dan analis 6 (36,37 menit).

title: Impact of Agile Methods on Tacit Knowledge Sharing from Self-Determination Perspective: A Mixed Method Study of Chinese IT Teams
source: SBS Journal of Applied Business Research
summary: The purpose of the study is to examine whether agile methods foster tacit knowledge sharing in IT project teams and to identify the motivational mechanisms, especially basic psychological needs and shared goals, underpinning this relationsh
content: The purpose of the study is to examine whether agile methods foster tacit knowledge sharing in IT project teams and to identify the motivational mechanisms, especially basic psychological needs and shared goals, underpinning this relationship in Chinese contexts. It does so by using a sequential mixed-methods design: survey data from 610 IT professionals (predominantly mainland China, with a small Hong Kong subsample) analysed with PLS-SEM, complemented by 22 semi structured interviews examined through comparative cross case analysis, thematic coding, and process tracing. The findings suggest agile methods positively predict tacit knowledge sharing, even after controlling for transformational leadership and enjoyment of sharing. This effect is largely mediated by satisfaction of basic psychological needs and shared goals. Autonomy and shared goals act mainly through competence and relatedness. Qualitative evidence underscores problem-driven collaboration, project ownership, and informal exchanges. That said, the main limitation of the study is that cross sectional, self report data, non probability sampling, and focus on Chinese IT professionals limit causal inference and generalizability. Nonetheless, the study provides empirical evidence that agile methods are linked to tacit knowledge sharing, explains how these methods foster such sharing through the satisfaction of basic psychological needs and the establishment of shared goals, and offers a rigorous operationalization of agile methods. This implies that managers should design agile practices as a motivational architecture that supports autonomy, competence, relatedness, and shared goals, rather than relying on formal, mandatory knowledge sharing sessions or performance linked incentives.

title: Localizing Multivariate CAViaR
summary: Risk transmission among financial markets and their participants is time-evolving, especially for extreme risk scenarios.Possibly sudden time variation of such risk structures asks for quantitative techniques that can cope with such situati
content: Risk transmission among financial markets and their participants is time-evolving, especially for extreme risk scenarios.Possibly sudden time variation of such risk structures asks for quantitative techniques that can cope with such situations.Here we present a novel localized multivariate CAViaRtype model to respond to the challenge of time-varying risk contagion.For this purpose, we construct a test for parameter homogeneity with totally datadriven critical values.We prove that these critical values lead to the required confidence level.Based on this test, we propose an estimation procedure that adapts to a possible time-variation of the parameter.A comprehensive simulation study supports the effectiveness of our approach in detecting structural changes in multivariate CAViaR.Finally, when applying for the US and German financial markets, we can trace out the dynamic tail risk spillovers and find that the US market appears to play a dominant role in risk transmissions, especially in volatile market periods.

title: Generative AI adoption culture in organizations: A bibliometric review and research agenda (2022–2026)
summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has reshaped organizational work since the release of ChatGPT in late 2022, yet research on the cultural dimensions of its adoption remains fragmented. This study synthesizes the emerging field thr
content: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has reshaped organizational work since the release of ChatGPT in late 2022, yet research on the cultural dimensions of its adoption remains fragmented. This study synthesizes the emerging field through a bibliometric review combining performance analysis, science mapping, and the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework. A Scopus search executed on 5 May 2026 yielded 257 records, refined to 128 by automatic filters, and reduced to 69 articles after PRISMA 2020 screening. Analysis employed bibliometrix (R 4.3.0) and four VOSviewer 1.6.20 networks. The field exhibits an annual growth rate of 114.07%, with publications rising from one in 2022 to 36 in 2025 and 21 in early 2026 across 65 sources and 23 countries (China leads with 12 articles), anchored by Ng et al. (2025), Jo and Bang (2023), and Lee and Park (2024). The keyword map yields four thematic clusters; the co-citation map reveals three intellectual sub-structures (Technology Acceptance, Methodological and Applied GenAI, and GenAI in Management). Both layers converge on a technology-acceptance dominant, methodologically homogeneous, and culturally thin configuration: classical culture references (Schein, Cameron, and Quinn) and dedicated AI-ethics works do not reach the co-citation core. To redress this asymmetry, we propose an integrative framework: Leadership Vision → AI Literacy and Trust → Psychological Safety → Ethical Climate → GenAI Adoption Culture → Productivity, Innovation, and Well-being. The agenda outlines five priorities, including cross-cultural instruments, longitudinal multi-wave designs, and emerging-market studies foregrounding Indonesia and ASEAN.

title: The nexus of inclusive finance, institutional governance, and FinTech adoption in the banking industry: A systematic review of project implementation dynamics
summary: This systematic review synthesizes 40 peer-reviewed studies to examine the role of inclusive finance and institutional governance in FinTech adoption in Pakistan's banking sector. While user-centric behavioural models are the dominant narra
content: This systematic review synthesizes 40 peer-reviewed studies to examine the role of inclusive finance and institutional governance in FinTech adoption in Pakistan's banking sector. While user-centric behavioural models are the dominant narrative in global discourse, this review highlights the underappreciated role of institutional trust, regulatory design, and structural inclusion in the scalability of FinTech ecosystems. The paper identifies four thematic clusters using PRISMA and TCCM frameworks, namely, user-level drivers, governance enablers, financial inclusion mechanisms, and integrated adoption frameworks. Findings suggest that inclusion should be reimagined not just as an objective but also as a prerequisite to digital finance, and quality of governance directly moderates trust and adoption behaviour. The study presents an original conceptual framework that links ecosystem-level conditions and adoption dynamics, highlighting the need for multi-level theoretical approaches that incorporate behavioural, institutional, and infrastructural dimensions. Implications are drawn for policymakers, FinTech innovators, and financial regulators who are looking for inclusive, trusted, and sustainable digital finance solutions in emerging markets.

title: Validation of a Diagnostic Model for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs)
source: Tiknuluzhī dar kār/āfarīnī va mudīriyyat-i istrātizhīk.
summary: This study aimed to validate a diagnostic model for small and medium-sized enterprises and evaluate its reliability, validity, explanatory power, predictive relevance, and overall model fit. This applied study employed a quantitative, cross
content: This study aimed to validate a diagnostic model for small and medium-sized enterprises and evaluate its reliability, validity, explanatory power, predictive relevance, and overall model fit. This applied study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design. The statistical population consisted of managers of active SMEs in East Azerbaijan, West Azerbaijan, Ardabil, and Zanjan provinces. A total of 350 managers were recruited through non-probability convenience sampling. The eligibility criteria included holding a managerial position, having at least three years of managerial or executive experience, and possessing sufficient knowledge of organizational processes and challenges. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire based on the constructs and indicators of the proposed diagnostic model. Content validity was assessed through expert judgment and the content validity ratio and content validity index. Internal consistency was examined using Cronbach’s alpha, rho_A, and composite reliability. Data were analyzed using SPSS and SmartPLS through partial least squares structural equation modeling. All indicator loadings were within the acceptable range, and Cronbach’s alpha, rho_A, and composite reliability values exceeded 0.70 for all constructs. Average variance extracted values ranged from 0.586 to 0.743, confirming convergent validity, while discriminant validity was supported by the Fornell–Larcker criterion. Bootstrapping results showed that all model indicators had t values greater than 1.96 and significance levels below 0.05. The coefficients of determination were 0.308 for strategies, 0.568 for the central diagnostic construct, and 0.612 for organizational consequences. All Q² values exceeded 0.35, indicating strong predictive relevance. The SRMR values were 0.051 for the saturated model and 0.0706 for the estimated model, while the corresponding NFI values were 0.941 and 0.906. The proposed model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, validity, explanatory power, predictive relevance, and overall fit. It can therefore be used as a valid framework for systematically identifying organizational deficiencies, examining relationships among organizational factors, and designing corrective strategies in SMEs.

title: Innovazione tecnologica, modello sviluppista e aiuti di Stato
source: European Journal of Privacy Law & Technologies
summary: Il saggio prende in esame la nuova stagione della programmazione europea ponendo in risalto l'aderenza delle politiche per incentivare lo sviluppo dell'innovazione tecnologica alla prospettiva teorica dello Stato sviluppista. Vengono messi
content: Il saggio prende in esame la nuova stagione della programmazione europea ponendo in risalto l'aderenza delle politiche per incentivare lo sviluppo dell'innovazione tecnologica alla prospettiva teorica dello Stato sviluppista. Vengono messi in luce alcuni elementi che, alla luce dell’esperienza, possono essere accomunati alle dinamiche del Developmental State come, ad esempio, l’impulso al sostegno delle imprese e delle attività produttive in settori connessi allo sviluppo tecnologico.

title: Discovering the Components of Organizational Loyalty Through a Phenomenological Approach: A Case Study of Teachers in Mashhad
source: Management Education and Development in Digital Age
summary: This study aimed to identify and explain the dimensions and components of organizational loyalty among teachers in Mashhad and to examine the factorial validity of the resulting model. This study employed a qualitative design based on Colai
content: This study aimed to identify and explain the dimensions and components of organizational loyalty among teachers in Mashhad and to examine the factorial validity of the resulting model. This study employed a qualitative design based on Colaizzi’s phenomenological approach. The participants were 17 selected and experienced teachers working in the Mashhad education system, recruited through purposive sampling until theoretical saturation and repetition of responses were achieved. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews using open-ended questions and analyzed according to Colaizzi’s seven-step procedure. The analytic process involved transcription of the interviews, extraction of significant statements, formulation of meanings, clustering of concepts, identification of themes, development of a comprehensive description of the phenomenon, and returning to selected participants for validation of the findings. MAXQDA was used to code and organize the qualitative data and classify the semantic categories. The extracted structure was additionally examined using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, as reported in the study, with SPSS version 26. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the proposed four-dimensional structure of organizational loyalty. The second-order factor loadings for structural, attitudinal, motivational, and behavioral loyalty were 0.955, 0.853, 0.846, and 0.790, respectively, and all relationships were statistically significant (p<0.001). All observed indicators had statistically significant factor loadings exceeding 0.40, supporting the adequacy and homogeneity of the measurement model. Indicator loadings ranged from 0.909 to 0.940 for attitudinal loyalty, 0.819 to 0.882 for structural loyalty, 0.583 to 0.925 for behavioral loyalty, and 0.851 to 0.907 for motivational loyalty. Overall, the factorial evidence supported four dimensions and 14 associated components of organizational loyalty. Organizational loyalty among teachers appears to be a multidimensional construct shaped not only by individual attitudes and behaviors but also by structural and motivational conditions in the workplace. Accordingly, strengthening job security, meritocracy, organizational and welfare support, effective communication, professional development, emotional attachment, perceived fairness, and the social status of teachers may provide an evidence-based foundation for human resource policies designed to enhance organizational loyalty within the education system.

title: Digitalisasi Desa Wisata Berbasis Community-Based Sustainable Tourism (CBST) dan Hubungannya dengan Daya Saing serta Keberlanjutan Desa Wisata Karawang
summary: Digital technology has become a strategic instrument for tourism village management. This study examines the association of Community-Based Sustainable Tourism (CBST)-based tourism village digitalization with perceived community empowerment
content: Digital technology has become a strategic instrument for tourism village management. This study examines the association of Community-Based Sustainable Tourism (CBST)-based tourism village digitalization with perceived community empowerment, destination competitiveness, and tourism village sustainability in Karawang Regency. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. The quantitative phase involved 200 local community members and tourism village actors, while the qualitative phase engaged a subset of the same respondents through focus group discussions. Regression results indicate positive and statistically significant associations between digitalization and the three outcomes. Because the data are cross-sectional and perception-based, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than evidence that digitalization causally boosts residents’ economic or social conditions. Integration of both phases produced a proposed CBST-based digitalization model.

title: Peran Social Media Marketing dalam Membentuk Purchase Intention melalui Brand Awareness dan Brand Trust
summary: This study aims to examine the effects of Social Media Marketing on Brand Awareness, Brand Trust, and Purchase Intention, as well as the effects of Brand Awareness and Brand Trust on Purchase Intention among Generation Z TikTok users intere
content: This study aims to examine the effects of Social Media Marketing on Brand Awareness, Brand Trust, and Purchase Intention, as well as the effects of Brand Awareness and Brand Trust on Purchase Intention among Generation Z TikTok users interested in purchasing Skintific facial moisturizer in Semarang City. This study is motivated by the need to understand the factors influencing consumers' purchase intention amid the increasingly competitive skincare industry and the rapid growth of social media marketing. A quantitative approach was employed, with data collected through questionnaires from 150 respondents. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The findings reveal that Social Media Marketing has a positive and significant effect on Brand Awareness, Brand Trust, and Purchase Intention. In addition, Brand Trust has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention, whereas Brand Awareness does not have a significant effect on Purchase Intention. The study concludes that Social Media Marketing and Brand Trust are key determinants of consumers' Purchase Intention toward Skintific facial moisturizer. These findings provide practical implications for companies by emphasizing the importance of optimizing social media marketing strategies through informative, interactive, and credible content to strengthen consumer trust, which in turn can enhance consumers' intention to purchase the product.

title: Rethinking Public Policy and Governance in a Globalized Era: Advancing the Interdisciplinary Research
summary: This editorial introduces the Journal of Policy Affairs (JPA) as a comprehensive, open-access platform dedicated to advancing rigorous scholarship in public policy, governance, and institutional studies. It situates the journal within the c
content: This editorial introduces the Journal of Policy Affairs (JPA) as a comprehensive, open-access platform dedicated to advancing rigorous scholarship in public policy, governance, and institutional studies. It situates the journal within the contemporary global context characterized by economic volatility, digital transformation, environmental challenges, social inequality, and increasing interdependence among nations. The editorial outlines the journal’s core aim to bridge theory and practice by publishing high-quality, interdisciplinary research that contributes to both academic discourse and policy implementation. Emphasizing methodological pluralism and global inclusivity, JPA welcomes diverse analytical approaches that address the design, execution, evaluation, and reform of public policies across varied institutional settings. The editorial further elaborates on the journal’s thematic priorities, including public administration, political economy, public finance, environmental governance, social policy, digital governance, crisis management, and international policy coordination. By highlighting the interconnected nature of modern governance challenges, it underscores the need for comparative and cross-disciplinary research capable of informing evidence-based policymaking. Ultimately, this editorial articulates JPA’s vision of fostering intellectually robust and practically relevant scholarship that strengthens institutional resilience, promotes inclusive development, and contributes to more effective and accountable governance systems worldwide.

title: The Impact of Brand Equity Dimensions on Consumer Buying Behavior: The Moderating Roles of Trust, Loyalty, and Price Sensitivity
summary: Consumer buying behavior knowledge helps in understanding how and why people make purchase decisions. It also helps firms to make better marketing strategies in the context of product development and customer satisfaction. Given its importa
content: Consumer buying behavior knowledge helps in understanding how and why people make purchase decisions. It also helps firms to make better marketing strategies in the context of product development and customer satisfaction. Given its importance, we developed a model that uses three predictors (brand image, perceived quality, and emotional attachment) and three moderators (consumer trust, brand loyalty, and price sensitivity). The dependent variable in this study was consumer buying behavior. The study distributed 350 questionnaires and received 300 completed questionnaires. All constructs and items used in this study were adapted from prior studies. The study used smart PLS for statistical analysis. We develop six hypotheses. Five were accepted, and one was rejected. The result supported Hypothesis 1: Brand image positively affects consumer buying behavior. We also found support for Hypothesis 2: Perceived quality affecting consumer buying behavior. Similarly, we found support for Hypothesis 3: Emotional attachment promotes consumer buying behavior. We also found support for Hypothesis 4: Consumer trust moderates the relationship between brand image and consumer buying behavior. We also accepted Hypothesis 5: Brand loyalty moderates emotional attachment and consumer buying behavior. We rejected Hypothesis 6: Price sensitivity moderates emotion attachment and consumer buying behavior. All the results of our study align with the past literature.

title: The “Rassemblement national” vote of farmers and rural voters: what sociological analysis? What difficulties does it reflect?
source: Notes Académiques de l Académie d agriculture de France / Academic Notes of the French Academy of Agriculture
summary: The continuous rise in support for the “Rassemblement national” in rural areas was particularly highlighted by the media during the June 2024 legislative elections. The French Academy of Agriculture, in its mission of scientific objectivity
content: The continuous rise in support for the “Rassemblement national” in rural areas was particularly highlighted by the media during the June 2024 legislative elections. The French Academy of Agriculture, in its mission of scientific objectivity and social responsibility, examined this rural vote, both in itself and in comparison, with the agricultural vote, focusing on sociological analyses that could identify differences between these votes and their explanatory factors. To this end, the Academy organised an internal debate within itself, encouraging open discussion, featuring three presentations by sociologists and a discussion with its members. This opinion paper, which reflects only the views of its authors, summarises the main contributions, aiming to better understand this crisis of democracy and enrich the societal debate.

title: Agentic Commerce and SME Competitiveness: An Integrative Review and Theory-Informed Research Framework
summary: Research background: Artificial intelligence is shifting online shopping from recommendation-based assistance towards delegated search, comparison, configuration, and, in emerging cases, transaction execution. For SMEs, this transition may
content: Research background: Artificial intelligence is shifting online shopping from recommendation-based assistance towards delegated search, comparison, configuration, and, in emerging cases, transaction execution. For SMEs, this transition may expand market access while simultaneously creating new forms of algorithmic gatekeeping and platform dependence. Purpose of the article: This integrative review develops a theory-informed explanation of how agentic commerce may affect SME competitiveness. Competitiveness is conceptualised as the joint ability to capture agent-mediated demand while preserving strategic option value, customer access, and bargaining autonomy over time. Methods: Seventeen documented OpenAlex title-and-abstract queries were used to identify English-language journal articles published between 2015 and July 2026. Following deduplication and eligibility screening, 117 Scopus- and/or Web of Science-indexed articles were reviewed in full, comprising 82 consumer-agent studies and 35 SME-platform studies. A concept-centric synthesis was conducted using dynamic capabilities and resource dependence as the principal theoretical lenses. The review does not claim exhaustive coverage or pooled causal effects, as the discovery process relied on a single source and only one record was identified through direct merchant-bridge queries. Claims were therefore calibrated according to evidential directness, convergence across research designs, and proximity to the outcome of interest. Findings & Value added: The synthesis identifies five core themes: assistance-to-delegation, machine legibility, trust transfer, empowerment–dependence, and offering/governance contingency. The proposed framework distinguishes foundational capabilities—product-data legibility, interface and transaction readiness, and verifiable trust evidence—from higher-order sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring capabilities. These mechanisms operate through eligibility and visibility, trust transfer, delegation depth, and dependency exposure. The evidence is moderate for consumer trust mechanisms and established forms of platform dependence, but remains limited for execution-capable agents, direct SME outcomes, and comparative boundary effects. Six propositions are developed to provide a testable rather than validated causal framework. The findings are relevant to SME managers, platform and AI-agent designers, policymakers, and researchers seeking to understand how firms can capture agent-mediated demand without surrendering strategic option value.

title: CORPORATE STRATEGY TO HUMAN CAPITAL: THE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE TRANSITION IN HOSPITALITY WITH A BIBLIOMETRIC APPROACH
summary: Within The Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework has become a defining paradigm in the transformation of the hospitality industry, shifting the focus from profit-oriented models to integrated sustainability and accountabilit
content: Within The Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework has become a defining paradigm in the transformation of the hospitality industry, shifting the focus from profit-oriented models to integrated sustainability and accountability systems. In this context, understanding how ESG research evolves and what dimensions dominate the discourse becomes increasingly important. The aim of this study is to analyse the development of ESG-related research in hospitality between 2009 and 2025, with particular attention to the transition from financial governance to human capital-oriented approaches. Despite the expansion of the field, the literature remains fragmented, characterised by conceptual ambiguity with Corporate Social Responsibility, inconsistent measurement practices, and limited integration of ESG dimensions within servicebased industries. The research is based on a bibliometric analysis of 987 publications indexed in the Web of Science database. The methodological approach combines performance analysis with science mapping techniques in order to identify publication trends, intellectual structures, and conceptual developments within the field. The results indicate a significant increase in research activity after 2019, accompanied by a shift in thematic focus. Earlier studies primarily emphasised financial performance, environmental efficiency, and external stakeholder perceptions. In contrast, recent research highlights the growing importance of employees as key drivers of ESG value creation. This reflects a redefinition of the Social dimension, which increasingly functions as an internal governance mechanism centred on employee engagement, well-being, and organisational behaviour. At the same time, the Environmental and Governance dimensions remain strongly interconnected through performance metrics and regulatory requirements, resulting in an imbalanced ESG structure. The internal social dimension is less standardised and insufficiently integrated into strategic decision-making processes. The study concludes that this imbalance limits the effectiveness of ESG implementation in the hospitality sector. The findings suggest that future development depends on the systematic integration of human capital considerations into governance frameworks, particularly in response to emerging European sustainability regulations. The contribution of the paper lies in identifying the internal social dimension as a key frontier of ESG research and in providing a structured overview of the field’s evolution, offering both theoretical clarification and practical relevance for sustainability-oriented management in hospitality.

title: SMALL TOWN INFORMAL ENTREPRENEURS OF THE GLOBAL SOUTH: INSIGHTS FROM INFORMAL BUSINESS TOURISM IN ZIMBABWE
summary: Existing research on the informal entrepreneurship in tourism is dominated by participation in leisure tourism. A knowledge gap surrounds informal entrepreneurship in business tourism and the phenomenon of informal business tourism. The aim
content: Existing research on the informal entrepreneurship in tourism is dominated by participation in leisure tourism. A knowledge gap surrounds informal entrepreneurship in business tourism and the phenomenon of informal business tourism. The aim is to contribute to scholarship on the mobilities of informal business tourists in the study setting of Zimbabwe. The specific focus is on informal business tourists who are residents of the nation’s small towns. A key finding is that most domestic informal business tourists visiting Harare originate from small towns or surrounding rural settlements. Significant contributions are made by these informal business tourists towards food provisioning and food security of Harare citizens. The shopping undertaken by these tourists in the markets of Harare provides a range of goods which otherwise would not be readily available for sale to residents of Zimbabwe’s ‘leftbehind’ small town economic spaces. Nevertheless, small town informal entrepreneurs function in a precarious business environment dominated by anti-informal economy regulations from Harare authorities and the constant threat of police harassment, loss of stock and reduced business income.

title: Growing chinese influence in the indian ocean region: impact on trade and security of Sri Lanka
summary: This study examines the growing geopolitical influence of China in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and its implications for Sri Lanka as a strategically located Island Nation in the IOR. Sri Lanka’s Gl position at the crossroads of major inte
content: This study examines the growing geopolitical influence of China in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and its implications for Sri Lanka as a strategically located Island Nation in the IOR. Sri Lanka’s Gl position at the crossroads of major international shipping routes has heightened its strategic importance, which makes this small, tiny state a focal point in contemporary geopolitical competition. The study is both timely and significant, given China’s expanding role in maritime security, global trade and regional power dynamics, most importantly through initiatives such as the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and the evolving “String of Pearls” strategy. The significance of the study is further underscored by Sri Lanka’s recent economic crisis, which further intensified in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic. Sri Lanka's high levels of external debt, consisting of a considerable share linked to Chinese financing in the country, have raised critical concerns regarding debt sustainability, national sovereignty as an independent state and economic dependency. Amid this backdrop, this study aims to assess whether Sri Lanka’s reliance on Chinese FDI, High Interest loans and infrastructure partnerships has contributed to creating a vulnerable geopolitical and economic status in the country. The Key objectives of the research are threefold: to analyze the nature and extent of China’s geopolitical and economic engagement in Sri Lanka, examine the impact of those engagements on the country’s trade, security and strategic autonomy and to examine how Sri Lanka’s role within China’s broader Indian Ocean strategy influences regional power dynamics, particularly in relation to India and the USA. The study employed a qualitative research methodology and used secondary data sources to obtain and analyse information. At the same time, the study adopted a historical and analytical approach to trace the evolution of Sino-Sri Lankan relations from early cultural and trade ties to a multifaceted partnership encompassing economic, military and diplomatic dimensions. The findings indicate that Chinese investments in Sri Lanka, particularly in major infrastructure projects such as Hambantota Port Development, Colombo Port City, and the joint project on expansion of Colombo International Container Terminal, have boosted the infrastructure and economic potential of the country. However, it also noted that all these gains come with adjoining risks such as rising debt, long term financial burdens and sovereignty challenges. Finally, the study highlights the need for Sri Lanka to adopt a balanced strategic approach that would strengthen institutions, diverse partnerships and safeguard its autonomy in the Indian Ocean.
