title: Zakat Education in the Context of Unlicensed Gold Mining: An Islamic Law and Islamic Education Perspective in North Molosipat under Law Number 3 of 2020
summary: This study aims to examine zakat education in the context of unlicensed gold mining in North Molosipat Village, Popayato Barat District, Pohuwato Regency, by integrating Islamic law and Islamic education perspectives. The study employed fie
content: This study aims to examine zakat education in the context of unlicensed gold mining in North Molosipat Village, Popayato Barat District, Pohuwato Regency, by integrating Islamic law and Islamic education perspectives. The study employed field research with an empirical approach and a descriptive qualitative design. Data were collected through non-participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation involving miners, community members, religious leaders, and village authorities, and were analyzed through data reduction, presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that zakat implementation is constrained by limited understanding of zakat al-mal, inadequate religious guidance, uncertainty concerning zakat calculation, and the absence of an organized village-level zakat management mechanism. Islamic law analysis indicates that gold is categorized as ma'din and may constitute zakatable wealth when its legal and ownership requirements are fulfilled. However, unlicensed mining creates substantive problems concerning milk al-tam, lawful acquisition, halalan tayyiban, obedience to legitimate regulation, and environmental consequences. The novelty of this study lies in conceptualizing zakat education as an Islamic educational intervention that connects fiqh literacy, ethical economic behavior, environmental responsibility, and community empowerment in mining communities.

title: Pengaruh CAR, BOPO, dan Inflasi terhadap ROA pada PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. Periode 2021–2025
summary: The profitability of PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk., as proxied by Return on Assets, fluctuated during the post-merger period of 2021–2025, making it necessary to analyze the internal and external factors affecting it. This study aims to an
content: The profitability of PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk., as proxied by Return on Assets, fluctuated during the post-merger period of 2021–2025, making it necessary to analyze the internal and external factors affecting it. This study aims to analyze the effect of the Capital Adequacy Ratio, Operating Expenses to Operating Income, and Inflation on Return on Assets at PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. for the 2021–2025 period. The study employs a quantitative method with an associative approach. The secondary data consist of the quarterly financial statements of PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. and inflation data published by Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik), comprising 20 observations from the first quarter of 2021 to the fourth quarter of 2025, selected using a purposive sampling technique. This study is limited to a single company, namely PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, the coefficient of determination, the t-test, and the F-test with the aid of IBM SPSS 25. The results show that the Capital Adequacy Ratio has a positive and significant effect on Return on Assets, whereas Operating Expenses to Operating Income has a negative and significant effect on Return on Assets. Inflation has a positive but insignificant effect on Return on Assets. Simultaneously, the three variables have a significant effect on Return on Assets. The study concludes that the profitability of PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. during the study period was influenced by capital adequacy and operational efficiency, while inflation did not show a significant effect.

title: Pengaruh Personalisasi Rekomendasi Produk Terhadap Perilaku Pembelian Konsumen Dengan Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Pengguna Shopee
summary: Product recommendation personalization helps e-commerce platform users find products that match their needs and preferences. This study examines the effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Trust, the effect of Trust on Purchase
content: Product recommendation personalization helps e-commerce platform users find products that match their needs and preferences. This study examines the effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Trust, the effect of Trust on Purchase Behavior, and the mediating role of Trust among Shopee users based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling, resulting in 111 eligible respondents, comprising 72.07% male and 27.93% female respondents aged 14–69 years. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The results indicate that Product Recommendation Personalization has a positive and significant effect on Trust (β = 0.696; p < 0.001). Trust also has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Behavior (β = 0.719; p < 0.001). The indirect effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Purchase Behavior through Trust is also significant (β = 0.501; p < 0.001), confirming the mediating role of Trust. These findings support the S-O-R mechanism and highlight the importance of recommendation relevance and user trust in supporting online purchasing behavior.

title: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
summary: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 exhibited persistent X-ray activity for more than 26 years after its discovery, prior to entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-waveleng
content: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 exhibited persistent X-ray activity for more than 26 years after its discovery, prior to entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-wavelength observations suggest that this low X-ray state results from the emergence of a complex layer of absorbing material, whose exact nature remains unknown. Since the X-ray emission is obscured, radio jet observations provide an unobstructed view of the physical changes associated with this phase. Recently published Very Large Array (VLA) and East Asian VLBI Network (EAVN) observations have revealed substantial changes in the jet position angle (PA). Here, we present higher-resolution VLBI observations to investigate the connection between the obscuration event and the jet behaviour close to the launch region. We observed GRS 1915+105 with the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) and European VLBI Network (EVN) during the early X-ray obscuration phase across four epochs spanning 2019--2021, sampling a diverse range of jet and accretion behaviours. In this paper, we focus on the milliarcsecond jet morphology and PA changes across the four epochs and contextualize these in relation to the reported X-ray behaviour. Many of the PAs measured post-2018 are significantly offset from GRS 1915+105's pre-obscuration jet axis, which has a weighted mean of 142^ ̧irc ± 7^ ̧irc on milliarcsecond scales. We find a maximum offset of 57^ ̧irc ± 8^ ̧irc from this axis, the largest such offset reported for GRS 1915+105 to date. Our four epochs reveal a broad variety of jet behaviours, ranging from a stable, compact source with a large PA offset, to a bright, flaring source with a similarly large offset, to an extended jet with a PA that is closer to the pre-obscuration axis, and finally to a non-detection. The lack of measurable PA changes within individual eight-hour epochs rules out rapid Lense-Thirring precession of the inner disc as the direct driver of the jet reorientation. Instead, given the timescales involved, coupled with the system's geometry and the apparent connection to the X-ray obscuration event, favour a radiation-driven warped accretion disc, in a configuration that could naturally explain the persistent obscuration.

title: Theory building review: beyond the rational egoist: a diagnostic framework for defensive and involuntary free riding in enterprising communities
source: Journal of Enterprising Communities People and Places in the Global Economy
summary: Purpose The free rider problem undermines the production of common goods within dynamic networks and organizational ecosystems. Through a theory-building review, this paper aims to challenge the traditional view of the free rider as a calcu
content: Purpose The free rider problem undermines the production of common goods within dynamic networks and organizational ecosystems. Through a theory-building review, this paper aims to challenge the traditional view of the free rider as a calculative egoist, arguing that this monolithic perspective causes a diagnostic failure in fostering social innovation and community resilience. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper synthesizes findings from 115 foundational and recent studies. Adopting an antecedents–decisions–outcomes framework, it integrates behavioral psychology, neo-institutionalism and structural capacity perspectives to re-evaluate non-compliance at the micro and meso levels of community organization. Findings Non-compliance in modern collaborative networks does not stem exclusively from strategic cunning. Two additional phenotypes emerge: the involuntary free rider, who lacks the capacity to contribute due to structural constraints, and the defensive free rider, who refrains from contributing due to institutional distrust. Originality/value The main contribution is the motivational diagnostic framework, which shifts the focus from blind enforcement to diagnostic governance within enterprising communities. By differentiating interventions based on capacity and trust, it provides community leaders and social entrepreneurs with a testable model to manage collective action and support sustainable development.

title: Investing in a Green Future: Finance, Industrial Policy and the Green Transition
summary: We present a framework to assess green climate finance and the pathways to building a climate aligned financial system. The green mission demands aligning finance to climate goals at the necessary scale, pace and direction requires the cali
content: We present a framework to assess green climate finance and the pathways to building a climate aligned financial system. The green mission demands aligning finance to climate goals at the necessary scale, pace and direction requires the calibration of financial flows across three axes: ‘public-private’; ‘real-financial’ and ‘national-international’. Along the first axis the nature-depleting, climate imperiling logic of short-term private profitability needs to be contained if we are to successfully pursue the public priorities of climate action. Along the second axis, policy efforts must be geared to ensuring that financial flows are financing investments in climate mitigation and adaptation and not simply providing more fodder for the global portfolio glut and financial accumulation. Finally, along the third axis stewarding global funding and providing support on appropriate terms to the most vulnerable countries while buttressing national ownership of the green mission. This involves a strategic reorientation of central bank interventions, national development banks and multilateral and regional banks, purposive collaborations between these institutions, and interventions to decisively reshape and restructure the contemporary global financial system tin line with the long-term imperatives of climate action.

title: Promoting or inhibiting: the impact of environmental regulation on enterprises' digital transformation
summary: Purpose The impact of stringent environmental regulations on corporate investment and financing decisions is increasingly prominent. The implementation of China's new Environmental Protection Law (the new EPL) in 2015 represents a significa
content: Purpose The impact of stringent environmental regulations on corporate investment and financing decisions is increasingly prominent. The implementation of China's new Environmental Protection Law (the new EPL) in 2015 represents a significant increase in environmental regulatory intensity in developing countries. Heavy-polluting enterprises must strike a balance between the dual transformation tasks of green transformation and digital transformation. Design/methodology/approach Based on the new EPL, we construct a quasi-natural experiment to explore the impact of environmental regulation on enterprises' digital transformation. Findings Our findings reveal that the new EPL significantly inhibits corporate digital transformation. Mechanism analysis indicates that, on the one hand, the new EPL crowds out firms' operational resources and weakens their financial support conditions for digitalization; on the other hand, it exacerbates business risks and dampens firms' willingness to undertake digital activities. These two channels jointly impede corporate digital transformation. Furthermore, additional analyses show that the inhibitory effect of the new EPL on digital transformation is more pronounced among smaller firms, in more competitive industries or in regions with lower levels of marketization. Practical implications The research results of this paper provide empirical evidence and decision-making reference for coordinating green development and digital economy development goals. Originality/value First, We examine the impact of environmental regulation on the digital transformation of enterprises, enriching the relevant research on the microeconomic effects of environmental regulation from the perspective of digital transformation. Second, from the perspective of environmental regulation, we enrich the literature research on the driving factors of enterprise digital transformation and provide a new perspective for the government to promote the development of the digital economy.

title: Gender in entrepreneurship education: a bibliometric analysis and research agenda
summary: Purpose This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of research on gender in entrepreneurship education (EE) and examines how existing studies report and explain gender differences in EE effectiveness, identifying impl
content: Purpose This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of research on gender in entrepreneurship education (EE) and examines how existing studies report and explain gender differences in EE effectiveness, identifying implications for programme design and future research. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis of 590 Scopus-indexed documents (2005–2026) was conducted using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny to examine keyword co-occurrence, citation networks and thematic evolution. Additionally, 20 highly cited studies reporting gender differences in EE effects were coded according to the direction of these differences and the explanations provided. A broader dataset of 6,030 EE publications served as a comparative baseline. Findings The literature predominantly focuses on entrepreneurial intention and self-efficacy, while structural and contextual perspectives remain less developed. Among the 20 studies, EE effects were larger for women in seven, larger for men in six, no significant gender differences were found in two and mixed results were reported in five. Nine studies provided no explanation, while five offered individual-level explanations, five contextual explanations and only one integrated both perspectives. Digital and AI-related research also remains limited, representing approximately half the relative share of the broader EE literature. Originality/value This study reveals a disconnect between established individual and structural perspectives and their limited integration in explaining gender differences in EE effectiveness. It highlights the need for gender-disaggregated evaluations and theoretically grounded explanations of how and for whom EE works.

title: Estimations for strong and weak hot Jupiter magnetism. A Python package with interpolators and scaling laws
summary: Hot Jupiters (HJs) are commonly thought to host the strongest dynamo-generated magnetic fields among exoplanets, exceeding Jupiter's by up to an order of magnitude, which can potentially induce observable star--planet interaction (SPI) and
content: Hot Jupiters (HJs) are commonly thought to host the strongest dynamo-generated magnetic fields among exoplanets, exceeding Jupiter's by up to an order of magnitude, which can potentially induce observable star--planet interaction (SPI) and planetary radio emission. However, while several indirect, model-dependent estimates of HJ magnetic fields have been reported from SPIs and recent transmission spectroscopy diagnostics, no unambiguous direct (radio) detection has yet been achieved. We aim to provide a range of magnetic field estimates for HJs, considering at the same time the mechanisms responsible for inflation and the convective flux that enters into the magnetic field scaling law. Given that their dynamos operate in the fast-rotating regime (Rossby number łesssim 0.1), we combined one-dimensional evolutionary interior models with magnetic field scaling laws under two limiting heating scenarios within the convective zone: deep and shallow energy depositions. Using interpolators built from the simulated data output, we provide magnetic field predictions for the HJ population. The deep-heating scenario maximizes convective heat flux in the dynamo and predicts strong magnetic fields of up to ∼100 G, whereas shallow heating, which is arguably more realistic for most proposed physical mechanisms, weakens convection and yields much weaker fields of $ ̧al O (1)$ G. The strong field scenario is compatible with indirect SPI detections, and the weak field scenario is in agreement with recent atmospheric constraints. We derived easy-to-use scaling law relations based on observables, i.e., planetary mass, radius, and/or incident stellar flux, that roughly reproduce the magnetic field estimates of our interior models: B_ ̊m strong = 19 , ̊m P ^ 0.6 R_ ̊m P ^ 1.7 G and B_ ̊m weak = 0.8 , M_ ̊m P ^ 1.5 R_ ̊m P ^ -1.2 G. With this range of magnetic field estimates for the current observed HJ population, our predictions provide a framework for interpreting future atmospheric wind measurements, SPI signatures, and radio observations, which may ultimately discriminate between competing interior-heating scenarios.

title: From Sight to Speed: A Dual Approach to Creating Safe Urban Pedestrian Crossings in the Era of AV
summary: Ensuring safe pedestrian crossings requires well-dimensioned visibility zones that accommodate both human-driven vehicles and autonomous vehicles. This paper proposes a novel design approach using stopping sight distance calculations, refle
content: Ensuring safe pedestrian crossings requires well-dimensioned visibility zones that accommodate both human-driven vehicles and autonomous vehicles. This paper proposes a novel design approach using stopping sight distance calculations, reflecting the significant divergence in reaction times of human drivers (2.0 s) and autonomous vehicles (0.5 s). Stopping sight distance-based visibility thresholds were established under typical urban speed limits (30, 40, 50 km/h), and a 1.0 m pedestrian visibility setback was introduced in line with European design standards. From these inputs, kerbside clearance requirements were derived using geometric relationships. In cases where full clearance cannot be ensured, the methodology estimates safe approach speeds as an alternative means to guarantee yielding. Results show that autonomous vehicles require consistently shorter stopping sight distance and clearance, reducing the number of spaces to be kept free and allowing higher feasible speeds under constrained visibility. These findings highlight practical implications for urban design and traffic regulation in mixed-traffic environments, while indicating potential long-term benefits of autonomous technology.

title: A pre-generative AI baseline of digital technology integration in accounting curricula: Evidence from Australian universities
summary: Accounting researchers have identified a diverse collection of established and emerging digital technologies (DTs) requiring integration into accounting curricula. This study investigates the extent to which the integration of these DTs was
content: Accounting researchers have identified a diverse collection of established and emerging digital technologies (DTs) requiring integration into accounting curricula. This study investigates the extent to which the integration of these DTs was evidenced within the publicly available accounting syllabi of top-ranked Australian universities prior to the public release of ChatGPT and the subsequent rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (AI), as well as the approaches used to integrate them. Data were collected between November 2021 and January 2022 from 36 QS-ranked universities, with 35 yielding the final sample of 33 undergraduate degrees, 35 postgraduate degrees, and 532 mandatory subjects. Using thematic and quantitative content analysis, the study identifies evidenced integration levels for a range of established and emerging DTs across undergraduate and postgraduate programs, and across different types of mandatory accounting degree subjects. The study reveals seven distinct approaches used to integrate DTs into accounting curricula at both the degree and subject levels. These findings provide insights into how integration levels and integration approaches may influence accounting education's ability to support the digital transformation of the profession. This study contributes to the literature by advancing understanding of the nature of digital technology integration into accounting curricula, its potential drivers and barriers, and strategies for its optimisation. The study establishes a pre-generative AI baseline of digital technology integration, providing a benchmark for subsequent research examining the impact of AI on accounting education.

title: Positive selection tends to act on exposed extracellular regions and delineate interaction modules targeted by pathogens
summary: Background Positive selection shapes protein function by favoring amino acid substitutions that increase fitness. Although numerous studies have identified positively selected genes (PSGs), the structural principles underlying residue-level
content: Background Positive selection shapes protein function by favoring amino acid substitutions that increase fitness. Although numerous studies have identified positively selected genes (PSGs), the structural principles underlying residue-level positive selection remain incompletely understood and previous studies have produced conflicting conclusions, particularly regarding the preferential location of positively selected residues (PSRs) within intrinsically disordered regions. In order to resolve these issues and to better understand the driving forces underlying positive selection in human proteins, we performed a comprehensive analysis on a manually curated, high-quality collection of PSGs and PSRs as well as on a large-scale PSR dataset restricted to proteins with experimental structures. Results Human PSRs were significantly enriched in secreted and cell membrane proteins and preferentially localized to extracellular regions, solvent-exposed protein surfaces, coil structures, and protein-protein interaction interfaces, whereas neither domains nor intrinsically disordered regions showed an enrichment. Spatial clustering analysis reinforced that PSRs accumulate within localized surface patches. Integration of host-pathogen interaction data highlighted that adaptive changes preferentially affect extracellular molecular recognition surfaces, recurrently appearing in certain pathogen-interacting membrane protein families and particular domain types. Additionally, PSRs showed an enrichment in the residues of human-pathogen interaction interfaces that are in direct contact with pathogenic proteins, implying that neutralizing pathogen attacks is one of the driving forces behind the adaptive evolution of human proteins. By analysing human variation data we found that PSRs are enriched in benign but depleted in pathogenic substitutions, extending previous observations that positively selected genes contain elevated levels of missense variation. Notably, PSGs of the large-scale dataset were also enriched among clinical-stage drug targets, suggesting a potential link between positive selection and pharmacological relevance. Conclusion Together, our results provide a refined structural model of adaptive evolution in human proteins and identify extracellular exposed molecular recognition surfaces and human-pathogen interaction interfaces as recurrent hotspots of positive selection. Our results point to the direction that precise identification of human PSRs could delineate important host-pathogen interfaces that exert evolutionary selection pressure on humans and appoint novel targets with therapeutic potential.

title: Patient adherence to hereditary cancer risk management: a 10-year experience in Singapore
summary: As the Cancer Genetics Service (CGS) in Singapore marks its tenth year, we evaluated adherence to recommended risk management among patients with hereditary cancer syndromes (HCS) to inform service improvements and cost-effectiveness analys
content: As the Cancer Genetics Service (CGS) in Singapore marks its tenth year, we evaluated adherence to recommended risk management among patients with hereditary cancer syndromes (HCS) to inform service improvements and cost-effectiveness analyses. We conducted a retrospective review of surveillance behaviours, uptake of risk-reducing surgery, and cancers detected during follow-up. Statistical tests were conducted to assess association between patient characteristics and adherence behaviours. There were 729 patients with HCS, largely comprised of females (79.7%), Chinese (73.5%), with a syndrome-related manifestation prior to testing (74.1%) and a family history of cancer (90.9%). Overall, 66.4% of our patients were fully adherent (FA) to recommended risk management; 10.4% were highly adherent (HA), 14.4% were lowly adherent (LA) and 8.8% were non-adherent (NA). Overall adherence was high across most HCS cohorts. Higher adherence was observed among individuals with high risk HCS, including Hereditary Breast Ovarian Cancer Syndrome, Lynch Syndrome and Familial Adenomatous Polyposis. High adherence of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 patients suggests that access to coordinated, multidisciplinary services may facilitate adherence. As healthcare systems move toward precision public health, strengthening risk communication and investing in multidisciplinary care models should be prioritised to support adherence to recommended risk-management strategies, particularly in high-risk populations.

title: A simulated dataset of university financial reimbursement records with multi-dimensional risk annotations
summary: This Data Descriptor presents a structured synthetic dataset of 5,200 university financial reimbursement records, designed to support reproducible research on financial risk detection, anomaly classification, and intelligent auditing in hig
content: This Data Descriptor presents a structured synthetic dataset of 5,200 university financial reimbursement records, designed to support reproducible research on financial risk detection, anomaly classification, and intelligent auditing in higher education institutions. The dataset encompasses six reimbursement categories: daily expenses, travel expenses, asset procurement, advance payments, labour fees, and miscellaneous expenses. Each is annotated with a multi-dimensional risk label system spanning four dimensions: fictitious-source fraud, amount manipulation, out-of-scope expenditure, and procedural non-compliance. Each record carries a quantitative risk score (0–7), a categorical risk level (low/medium/high), a detailed anomaly behaviour description, and an approval status. Risk labels are deliberately unbalanced across categories to reflect realistic institutional audit distributions. The data were generated using a fully transparent Python script with deterministic random seeding and are made freely available under the CC0 1.0 licence, with the generation script released under the MIT licence. This resource is intended to serve as a benchmark dataset for machine-learning-based financial audit models, risk-scoring algorithms, and regulatory-compliance studies in the domain of university financial management.

title: The impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on employee green well-being: The mediating role of employee engagement in Vietnamese enterprises
source: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
summary: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into workplaces is transforming not only how employees perform their tasks but also how they experience work. However, the implications of this transformation for sustainab
content: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into workplaces is transforming not only how employees perform their tasks but also how they experience work. However, the implications of this transformation for sustainable development remain insufficiently understood, particularly regarding whether AI-enabled workplaces can support employees’ long-term well-being and resilience. Addressing this gap, this study examines how positive attitudes toward Generative AI (POS_ATT) and responsible AI signals (RAIS) contribute to multidimensional Green Well-being through employee engagement (ENG). Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model, Signaling Theory, and the Job Demands–Resources theory, Green Well-being is conceptualized as a sustainable state encompassing emotional (GEW), cognitive (GCW), and social well-being (GSW). A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 342 knowledge workers employed by Vietnamese organizations using Generative AI. Participants were recruited using convenience and snowball sampling. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The results show that both POS_ATT (β = 0.312, p < 0.001) and RAIS (β = 0.287, p < 0.001) are positively associated with employee engagement. ENG, in turn, is positively associated with all three dimensions of Green Well-being, with the strongest relationship observed for emotional well-being (β = 0.441), followed by cognitive (β = 0.418) and social well-being (β = 0.397), all at p < 0.001. Moreover, ENG fully mediates the relationships between POS_ATT and RAIS and the three Green Well-being dimensions. These findings broaden understanding of sustainable development in AI-enabled workplaces by showing that the potential human benefits of Generative AI are not associated solely with technology adoption. Rather, favorable employee perceptions and responsible implementation need to be translated into meaningful work engagement before they are associated with sustainable well-being outcomes. The study therefore identifies responsible AI, employee engagement, and multidimensional well-being as interconnected elements of a human-centered approach to sustainable digital transformation. Practically, organizations should complement investments in AI capabilities with transparent, explainable, and fair AI governance and engagement-oriented work design to preserve and develop human resources during digital transformation. Because the cross-sectional design captures relationships at a single point in time, the findings establish associations rather than causal effects. Longitudinal and cross-national research is therefore needed to examine whether these relationships persist over time and contribute to long-term employee and organizational resilience. Keywords: Generative artificial intelligence; responsible AI; employee engagement; Green Well-being; sustainable development; sustainable digital tr

title: High-resolution DNA methylation dataset of a wheat-barley 7H chromosome addition line and its parental cultivars
summary: Interspecific hybridisation is an important strategy for expanding genetic diversity in crop breeding; however, the DNA methylation profiles of alien chromosomes maintained within wheat genomic backgrounds remain insufficiently characterise
content: Interspecific hybridisation is an important strategy for expanding genetic diversity in crop breeding; however, the DNA methylation profiles of alien chromosomes maintained within wheat genomic backgrounds remain insufficiently characterised. Here, we present a reduced representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS) dataset comprising single-base-resolution DNA methylation profiles in CpG, CHG, and CHH sequence contexts from a stable wheat-barley 7H chromosome addition line (7Hadd) and its parental cultivars, winter wheat Mv9 and winter barley Igri. Genomic DNA was extracted from leaf tissues of vernalized seedlings, with three independent biological replicates per genotype, and sequenced using paired-end Illumina technology. Sequencing reads were processed and aligned against a composite wheat–barley reference genome to enable the characterisation of methylation profiles across the wheat chromosomes and the introduced barley 7H chromosome. The dataset includes raw sequencing reads and processed methylation measurements, providing a resource for evaluating locus-specific methylation patterns, comparing shared genomic regions between the addition line and its parental cultivars, and integrating epigenomic information with future genomic and transcriptomic studies of wheat–barley introgression lines.

title: Causal and Stochastic Economic Assessment of Irrigation Technologies, Farm Profitability, and Energy Risk in Tanzanian Paddy and Horticultural Systems
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Background: Sustaining smallholder food security across Sub-Saharan Africa requires evaluating irrigation across food availability (yields), economic access (net income after hidden labor costs), stability (climate and fuel shocks), and gro
content: Background: Sustaining smallholder food security across Sub-Saharan Africa requires evaluating irrigation across food availability (yields), economic access (net income after hidden labor costs), stability (climate and fuel shocks), and groundwater sustainability while separating observed adoption evidence from ex-ante solar pumping projections. Methods: We harmonized 21,909 smallholder plots (paddy rice, tomato, and onion) across four nationally representative Tanzanian surveys (2019–2025; 254 strata, 6,023 primary sampling units, 9 agroecological zones). Conditional on confounders and survey weights, we combined ridge-regularized Entropy-Balanced Inverse Probability Weighted Regression Adjustment with a calibrated Multivariate Empirical copula simulation validated out-of-sample on 2024/25, partial-cash versus full economic net farm income (NFI) budgets, and risk-efficiency ranking. Empirical evaluation covered four observed regimes (rainfed, gravity/canal, manual lifting, motorized fossil pumps), whereas commercial, stochastic-reliability, and concessional solar photovoltaic water pumping scenarios (supplemental dry-spell paddy irrigation) were modeled ex-ante (<1% surveyed ownership). Results: Post-weighting covariate imbalance fell from 0.1298 to 0.0158. Gravity maximized pooled horticultural yield gains (+4.65 t/ha, p < 0.001) and certainty equivalents across all risk preferences, and delivered the most precise, input-robust paddy gain (+0.79 ± 0.08 t/ha [+0.44 t/ha net milled rice after post-harvest losses], p < 0.001), whereas motorized pumping achieved the highest point paddy gain (+0.92 ± 0.19 t/ha) and led disaggregated tomato and onion NFI. Manual paddy lifting drained 76.4% of revenue (incremental energy return −1.27), while motorized pumping earned the highest paddy economic NFI (Tanzanian Shillings 2.72 million/ha; ~USD 1,025/ha) yet exposed 44.6%–48.1% of plots to >20% energy burden under +50% to +75% fuel shocks. Global sensitivity showed dry-season solar yield reliability (40.7%–65.2% normalized rank-explained share; Sobol total-order 0.18–0.29) and pump lifespan (20.4%–26.5%) outweighed fuel shocks (5.5%–8.4%). Conclusions: Advancing Tanzanian food security requires prioritizing gravity canal rehabilitation where feasible, replacing manual paddy lifting with shared pumping hubs, and pairing regional tariff relief and concessional green finance with battery-free hydraulic buffer sizing, flexible repayment, and aquifer depletion monitoring.

title: WALLS OF PAPER: ANATOMY OF THE SPANISH HOUSING CRISIS AND PATHWAYS OUT OF THE TUNNEL A Comprehensive Legal, Economic, and Structural Analysis
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This monograph presents a rigorous legal, economic, and structural analysis of Spain's housing crisis, which by late 2026 has evolved into a profound political emergency triggering nationwide strikes and calls for early elections. The Bank
content: This monograph presents a rigorous legal, economic, and structural analysis of Spain's housing crisis, which by late 2026 has evolved into a profound political emergency triggering nationwide strikes and calls for early elections. The Bank of Spain estimates a cumulative deficit of 750,000 housing units, projected to reach one million by 2028, driven by the post-2008 construction collapse, financialization through SOCIMIs and vulture funds, the distortion of seasonal and tourist rentals, and bureaucratic fragmentation across autonomous communities. The book navigates the constitutional tension between Article 33 (property rights) and Article 47 (right to housing), grounding proposals in the Spanish Constitutional Tribunal's jurisprudence (STC 16/2024), while ensuring compliance with EU State Aid rules through the SGEI framework. It proposes a tiered solution architecture: closing seasonal rental loopholes, establishing public rental guarantee funds, expanding social housing to include the middle class following Vienna's model, deploying municipal land banks with long-term surface rights, and counteracting the AVE tunnel effect through mandatory localization agreements. A realistic financing engineering roadmap is provided, combining NextGenerationEU allocations, bulk sales transaction taxes, municipal green bonds, and a reformed two-tier SOCIMI regime. Comparative analysis of German, Singaporean, Viennese, and South Korean models offers actionable lessons while acknowledging institutional limits. The conclusion argues that housing must be reclaimed as critical infrastructure, not a speculative asset, requiring a grand bargain between state, private sector, and society. Digital Object Identifier: 10.5281/zenodo.24423020

title: Introduction to Continuum Mechanics of Solid Bodies
summary: Introduction to Continuum Mechanics of Solid Bodies is a comprehensive textbook which guides students through the essential principles and applications of this critical field. With a focus on clarity and accessibility, this book offers a ba
content: Introduction to Continuum Mechanics of Solid Bodies is a comprehensive textbook which guides students through the essential principles and applications of this critical field. With a focus on clarity and accessibility, this book offers a balanced introduction to tensor algebra, analysis, and the notational systems used in continuum mechanics. This textbook is structured into eight meticulously crafted chapters, covering topics such as nonlinear deformations, kinematic quantities, stress tensors, and the fundamental laws governing solid bodies. Readers will gain a deep understanding of energy principles, virtual work, and constitutive theories, including nonlinear elasticity and heat effects in linear theory. Each chapter is enriched with practical examples and problem sets, with solutions provided at the end of the book, ensuring that students can apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios. The inclusion of appendices further supports learning by providing detailed mathematical transformations and problem solutions. Designed for advanced undergraduate and graduate students in mechanical engineering, applied mechanics, and related fields, this book is an indispensable resource for those studying continuum mechanics, equipping students with the knowledge and tools to excel in their studies and professional endeavours. Figure slides are available at www.routledge.com/9781041426141 for qualified textbook adoption.

title: Neyman-Pearson and equal opportunity: when economic efficiency meets societal fairness in classification
source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Organizations have increasingly used statistical algorithms to make decisions. While fairness and other social considerations are important in these automated decisions, economic efficiency remains crucial to the survival and success of org
content: Organizations have increasingly used statistical algorithms to make decisions. While fairness and other social considerations are important in these automated decisions, economic efficiency remains crucial to the survival and success of organizations. Therefore, a balanced focus on both algorithmic fairness and economic efficiency is essential for promoting fairness in real-world data science solutions. Among the first efforts towards this dual focus, we incorporate the equal opportunity (EO) constraint into the Neyman-Pearson (NP) classification paradigm. Under this new NP-EO framework, we derive the oracle classifier, propose data-driven classifiers with high-probability guarantees for the population-level fairness and efficiency metrics, and demonstrate the statistical and social effectiveness of our algorithms on simulated and real datasets.

title: COVID-19 and the rise of digital talent platforms amongst skilled professionals in Lebanon
summary: The global growth of digital talent platforms is well-documented, yet adoption in fragile emerging markets remains underexplored. This study examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the attractiveness and adoption of these platforms
content: The global growth of digital talent platforms is well-documented, yet adoption in fragile emerging markets remains underexplored. This study examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the attractiveness and adoption of these platforms among skilled professionals in Lebanon between 2018 and 2024. The research is grounded in a quantitative methodology, combining Google Trends of online interest with survey data to identify temporal trends. The study, conducted in the Middle East, offers a social and cultural layer. It encompasses HR professionals, recruiters and hiring managers. It establishes the foundation for understanding the relationship between the COVID-19 pandemic and the adoption of digital talent platforms among skilled professionals in Lebanon within the context of a multifaceted local crisis. Findings revealed a 76% increase in platform-related search interest and higher adoption rates during the COVID-19 pandemic, a crisis that normalized remote work and enabled Lebanese professionals to participate in global labor markets without physical relocation. Conversely, domestic shocks, such as political unrest and the Beirut port explosion, were associated with heightened emigration interest rather than platform engagement. This distinction challenges the assumption that all shocks uniformly drive platform adoption. It underscores that while digital talent platforms offer a mechanism for resilience during systemic disruptions, their success is contingent upon the infrastructure, stability and trust that local crises erode. By differentiating between crises through the Event System theory and the Resource-based View theory, this research contributes to the literature on digital talent markets and offers insights for talent-exporting countries with prolonged instability.

title: Measuring general associations in time series: an adaptation and empirical evaluation of the CODEC coefficient in determining autoregressive dynamics
source: Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation
summary: Identifying the maximum informative lag to include in an autoregressive model remains an open research problem due to the computational burden of treating it as a hyperparameter, especially in complex models. This study explores model-agnos
content: Identifying the maximum informative lag to include in an autoregressive model remains an open research problem due to the computational burden of treating it as a hyperparameter, especially in complex models. This study explores model-agnostic association measures, including Pearson, Spearman, Kendall, and an adaptation of the recently proposed conditional dependence coefficient (CODEC), together with Akaike’s and Bayesian information criteria, for guiding lag selection in time series. We adapt and implement the CODEC-based Feature Ordering by Conditional Independence (CODEC-FOCI) algorithm and evaluate its performance through extensive simulations across linear, nonlinear, stationary, nonstationary, seasonal, and heteroskedastic processes. Results show that CODEC is particularly competitive in nonlinear and nonstationary settings, especially with larger sample sizes, whereas Pearson and Spearman perform well for predominantly linear dependence structures, and Kendall shows the best overall performance among the association measures. Moreover, the proposed methodology consistently identifies informative lag structures directly from the original series, with differencing and seasonal decomposition generally providing no improvement and often degrading performance. Applications to benchmark datasets confirm that the detected lag structures are consistent with those reported in the literature. These findings highlight CODEC’s potential as a practical, model-free tool for exploratory autoregressive lag identification in time series analysis.

title: GA-NIFS: A post-starburst main sequence disk galaxy undergoing ordered rotation at z = 4.26
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Rotating galaxies with relaxed gaseous disks have been discovered across cosmic time, from the local Universe to high redshift. But few such sources have been confirmed at z > 4, making them a precious sample to examine the conditions requi
content: Rotating galaxies with relaxed gaseous disks have been discovered across cosmic time, from the local Universe to high redshift. But few such sources have been confirmed at z > 4, making them a precious sample to examine the conditions required for such ordered kinematics in an early, more chaotic Universe. One of the best examples of this sample is the galaxy $\rm DLA0817g1$ (z = 4.2603), which shows remarkably clear rotation in ALMA [C ii] data. We present JWST/NIRSpec IFU data (R ∼ 2700) of $\rm DLA0817g1$, which we combine with archival ALMA [C ii] observations to place constraints on its ISM conditions and morpho-kinematics. From a combination of line ratios, we find a high gas-phase metallicity (Zgas ∼ 0.8 Z⊙), high fraction of obscured star formation, low ionisation (compared to other high-redshift galaxies observed with JWST), and no significant evidence for AGN. Dynamical modelling with $\rm ^{3D}$Barolo reveals nearly identical rotation in $\rm H\alpha$ and [C ii]. Using our metallicity estimate and previous CO and [C ii] detections, we derive a new estimate of the molecular gas mass, relieving a previous strain in the mass budget. Altogether, we suggest that this is a post-burst, main-sequence galaxy, where high levels of past star formation resulted in significant chemical enrichment (i.e., Zgas and Mdust), but the current activity is lower (i.e., lower ionisation parameter and lack of starburst activity). These new observations have opened a window into the interplay of gas, metallicity, star formation, and kinematics in a prototypical early disk galaxy.

title: Word embeddings from text corpora: A simulation study on the representation of underlying structures
summary: The grounding problem concerns how symbolic representations acquire meaning through connections to what they refer to. For word embeddings learned from text, a related empirical question is how much of the structure that generated the text
content: The grounding problem concerns how symbolic representations acquire meaning through connections to what they refer to. For word embeddings learned from text, a related empirical question is how much of the structure that generated the text they retain. This is difficult to test in natural corpora because that structure is generally unknown. We employed a microsimulation methodology to generate a controlled text corpus from a known spatial structure. A virtual language supermarket with 40 shelves organised into four departments (fruit, vegetables, beverages, extras) served as the generative environment. Product sequences from 80,000 simulated shoppers formed a corpus of 804,422 product selections, with each sequence unique. The GloVe algorithm was applied to this corpus to learn 50-dimensional word embeddings, which we compared with the network of shelves. Cosine distance between products correlated with their shortest-path distance in the network (Spearman ρ = 0.79 over all 7,140 product pairs, Mantel p = 0.001), and on average 61% of a product's network neighbours were among its nearest neighbours in the embedding, against 7% expected by chance. Over ten independent simulations these values were 0.80 ± 0.01 and 0.62 ± 0.02, and shuffling words across the corpus removed the association. Raw co-occurrence counts, PPMI, SVD and word2vec also captured global distance structure but retrieved fewer neighbours (29-50%). Recovery was best with a context window of one word (ρ = 0.93) and was weaker for rare products. K-medoid clustering of all 120 products separated the fruit and extras departments completely, while vegetables and beverages, which are interleaved in the network, were mixed (adjusted Rand index 0.82). UMAP projections followed the network closely (ρ = 0.92) but distorted some parts of it. These findings show that distributional word embeddings can recover much of the structure that a generating process puts into co-occurrence statistics. They do not show that the embeddings are grounded in, or understand, what the words refer to. This controlled simulation provides a reproducible way to measure structural recovery by word embeddings.

title: Reducibility of native weighted graphs on Rydberg arrays
summary: We investigate the classical reducibility of random unit-disk graph (UDG) instances of the maximum independent set and maximum weighted independent set problems, which can be natively realized in Rydberg atom quantum processors. Using state
content: We investigate the classical reducibility of random unit-disk graph (UDG) instances of the maximum independent set and maximum weighted independent set problems, which can be natively realized in Rydberg atom quantum processors. Using state-of-the-art kernelization techniques, we systematically probe how far classical preprocessing can simplify such native optimization problems of varying size and connectivity. While many small or sparse instances can be fully reduced, dense graphs often retain finite irreducible kernels even after extensive reductions. Introducing vertex weights tends to increase reducibility, whereas extending the interaction range in the underlying UDG connectivity suppresses the reduction efficiency. By exploring where classical reductions cease to be effective, we aim to delineate the regime of problem instances that remain computationally demanding—those most relevant for testing and benchmarking near-term quantum optimization hardware. We find that for the remaining finite kernels, quantum execution would require non-native embeddings with substantial resource overheads, suggesting that directly running native instances may be more practical than embedding a reduced kernel.

title: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics of collapse models in the strongly non-Gaussian regime
summary: Standard objective collapse models offer a unified approach to the quantum measurement problem but predict an unphysical, indefinite increase in the energy of the system. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model and Continuous Spontaneous
content: Standard objective collapse models offer a unified approach to the quantum measurement problem but predict an unphysical, indefinite increase in the energy of the system. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model and Continuous Spontaneous Localization (dCSL) model resolve this heating issue by introducing a linear friction mechanism. However, this modification induces complex, non-Gaussian phase-space dynamics. We investigate the thermodynamic consistency of the linear-friction mechanism across weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes in the one-dimensional dCSL model, establishing non-negative relaxation entropy production analytically for free-particle momentum dynamics and numerically for the harmonic-oscillator evolutions studied. Using the Wigner phase-space formalism, we go significantly beyond the quadratic approximation and, to bypass the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation, introduce a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach. Our analysis reveals that the system subjected to the dCSL mechanism does not reach a Gibbs state, but rather settles into a non-Gaussian, possibly non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) where the asymptotic non-Gaussianity grows as a power law, with exponent close to 2.3, of the dissipation parameter β. By evaluating the Wigner entropy production, we confirm the thermodynamic validity of the model— i.e. positive entropy production rate.

title: Double Quantum Spin Hall Phase in Bilayer ZrTe5
summary: Quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulators host helical edge states that enable dissipationless transport, but realizing multiple conducting channels in experimentally accessible materials with large band gaps remains challenging. Here, we show tha
content: Quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulators host helical edge states that enable dissipationless transport, but realizing multiple conducting channels in experimentally accessible materials with large band gaps remains challenging. Here, we show that AB-stacked untwisted bilayer ZrTe5 naturally realizes a double QSH phase in its energetically most stable structure, revealing an unexpected multichannel transport regime. The phase hosts two pairs of helical edge states and a doubled quantized spin Hall conductivity, with spin Chern number Cs = 2 despite the conventional Z2=0 classification. Lattice deformation tunes the system through a metallic state to a conventional QSH phase with Z2=1, enabling control of the number of helical channels. Remarkably, the quantized spin Hall response persists over an energy window substantially larger than the bulk band gap, exceeding 100 meV. Our results establish bilayer ZrTe5 as an experimentally accessible multichannel QSH system in which interlayer coupling and lattice deformation control topological edge transport.

title: Sensitivity of silicon-to-water dose conversion and Bragg-peak metrics to stopping-power datasets in proton dosimetry
summary: OBJECTIVE: Accurate proton dosimetry requires internally consistent stopping-power data for detector-to-water dose conversion and Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations. This study quantifies how water-to-silicon stopping-power ratios,
content: OBJECTIVE: Accurate proton dosimetry requires internally consistent stopping-power data for detector-to-water dose conversion and Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations. This study quantifies how water-to-silicon stopping-power ratios, converted dose-to-water distributions, and Bragg-peak metrics vary with the stopping-power dataset for a 67.5 MeV pristine proton beam in water. APPROACH: PHITS simulations were performed using dataset-specific stopping powers from SRIM-2013, PSTAR/NIST, ATIMA, and TDDFT-Penn for proton energies up to 10 MeV, combined with a common SBETHE-based high-energy extension above 10 MeV. Normalized percentage depth-ionization data from the PTW silicon diode in the published benchmark of Faddegon et al. (2015) were converted into relative percentage depth- dose distributions in water using depth-dependent water-to-silicon stopping-power ratios. Direct dose-to-water simulations were performed to evaluate Bragg-peak and distal-range metrics. MAIN RESULTS: The water-to-silicon stopping-power ratio exhibited a pronounced depth dependence, with relative entrance-to-distal variations ranging from 17.40% to 22.10% across the datasets. All converted relative PDD curves reached their maximum at 36.86 mm, with no dataset-dependent shift. This position agrees with the experimental Bragg-peak depth of (36.81 ± 0.15) mm, defined as the midpoint between adjacent PDI maxima at 36.76 and 36.86 mm. The converted curves were approximately 3% below the reference curve throughout the entrance and plateau regions, while dataset-dependent deviations of up to 2.1% were observed near the Bragg peak. Direct PHITS calculations predicted Bragg-peak depths ranging from 36.575 to 36.675 mm; only the TDDFT-Penn result lay within the quoted experimental uncertainty. SIGNIFICANCE: For this benchmark, the stopping-power treatment affects the normalization of the converted dose throughout the entrance, plateau, and distal regions more strongly than it affects the Bragg-peak position. Harmonizing stopping-power data between detector-to-water conversion and Monte Carlo transport, or explicitly including dataset dependence in the uncertainty budget, is important for proton-beam calibration, commissioning, quality assurance, and Monte Carlo validation.

title: Magnetic ground states of CrPS 4 and NiPS 3 monolayers from long-range exchange interactions
summary: We investigate the magnetic properties of monolayer CrPS4 and NiPS3 by combining first-principles calculations, second-principles spin models, and Monte Carlo simulations. Unlike conventional approaches that truncate exchange interactions a
content: We investigate the magnetic properties of monolayer CrPS4 and NiPS3 by combining first-principles calculations, second-principles spin models, and Monte Carlo simulations. Unlike conventional approaches that truncate exchange interactions after only a few shells and determine them by fitting total energies, we extract the magnetic exchange tensors directly from density functional theory using the LKAG formalism and include interactions until numerical convergence is achieved. We show that long-range exchange interactions qualitatively modify the magnetic behavior of both materials. In CrPS4, they destabilize the previously predicted ferromagnetic ground state and stabilize a spin-spiral phase, reducing the critical temperature to about 21 K, in agreement with available experiments. The resulting magnetic phase diagram contains multiple collinear and non-collinear phases that can be tuned by temperature and external magnetic fields. In NiPS3, the experimentally observed zigzag antiferromagnetic order only emerges when exchange interactions up to the fifth shell are included. These results demonstrate that quantitatively predictive spin models for thiophosphate monolayers require long-range exchange interactions and provide a predictive framework for accurately describing two-dimensional van der Waals magnets.

title: Risk, Return, and Anomalies in Islamic Equity Markets: A Post-2020 Review
source: Journal of Integrated Socio-Economic Systems and Islamic Finance
summary: Background: The rapid growth of the Islamic capital market has spurred significant academic interest in developing and validating asset pricing models that adhere to Shariah principles. Traditional models like the Capital Asset Pricing Mode
content: Background: The rapid growth of the Islamic capital market has spurred significant academic interest in developing and validating asset pricing models that adhere to Shariah principles. Traditional models like the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) are often inadequate due to their reliance on interest-based risk-free rates and assumptions that may not hold in Shariah-compliant contexts. Objective: This study conducts a systematic literature review of academic research published between 2021 and 2025 complemented by seminal pre-2021 benchmark studies, to synthesize the current state of knowledge on asset pricing models for Shariah-compliant stocks. It aims to identify the dominant models, key pricing factors, and persistent anomalies, while highlighting methodological trends and research gaps. Methods: Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, reproducible searches of Scopus and Web of Science identified 209 records, from which 46 studies met the inclusion criteria. The review focuses on studies examining the efficacy of various pricing models, including the Shariah-Compliant Asset Pricing Model (SCAPM), multi-factor models (e.g., Fama-French), and the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT), as well as the influence of behavioral factors, ESG criteria, and downside risk. Results: The review reveals a clear shift from traditional CAPM towards multi-factor models, with the Fama-French five-factor model emerging as the most widely adopted and generally best-performing benchmark, although its advantage is not unconditional. There is evidence of at least partial market segmentation, suggesting that Islamic-specific factors better explain the cross-section of returns than market-wide factors. Key themes emerging from recent literature include the outperformance of Islamic indices during crisis periods, the significance of value and momentum premiums, and the growing influence of ESG and behavioral factors in pricing Islamic equities. Conclusion: The asset pricing landscape for Shariah-compliant stocks is evolving towards more sophisticated, multi-factor frameworks that incorporate both financial and ethical considerations. Future research should focus on developing more robust Islamic-specific pricing factors, exploring the impact of new screening methodologies, and examining the integration of Islamic markets with the global financial system. The review contributes a critical comparison of competing models and sets out implications for Islamic financial institutions, portfolio managers, regulators and Shariah supervisory boards.

title: Cross-Modal Attention Fusion for Clinical Risk Prediction: Integrating EHR Data with Dual-Attribution Explain ability
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EVALUATION AND PHYSICAL REPORT
summary: Clinical prediction models have historically relied on structured electronic health record data, leaving the rich prognostic signal embedded in free-text clinical documentation systematically underutilized. The proposed Clinical Multimodal
content: Clinical prediction models have historically relied on structured electronic health record data, leaving the rich prognostic signal embedded in free-text clinical documentation systematically underutilized. The proposed Clinical Multimodal Adaptive Clinical Prediction (CMACP) architecture — a dual-pathway prediction system integrating structured EHR features through gradient-boosted tree processing with unstructured clinical note embeddings through Clinical BERT encoding, unified by a cross-modal attention mechanism that weighs each modality's contribution by predictive confidence. The architecture is designed for geriatric acute care settings where clinical notes capture disease severity, symptom trajectory, and functional context unavailable from structured data alone. A federated fine-tuning protocol enables privacypreserving multi-institutional model development across health systems with different EHR platforms and patient populations. An attribution framework combining SHAP-based structured feature importance with Integrated Gradients note concept attribution provides role-differentiated clinical explanations, with a concordance quality badge signalling modality alignment. A governance framework specifies deployment standards, post-market performance monitoring, and equity evaluation protocols calibrated to multi-site clinical NLP systems. The CMACP framework addresses the technical and governance requirements for safe deployment of multimodal clinical AI in settings where older adult patients are most vulnerable to prediction errors. External validation across multiple health system types, equity stratification by race and documentation quality environment, and prospective evaluation of attribution quality are identified as priority research requirements.

title: Conversion of optical to mechanical states at the few-photon level
summary: Coherent interfaces between optical photons and mechanical excitations provide a promising route towards phonon-state engineering and hybrid quantum information processing. Cavity optomechanical systems enable such interfaces via optomechan
content: Coherent interfaces between optical photons and mechanical excitations provide a promising route towards phonon-state engineering and hybrid quantum information processing. Cavity optomechanical systems enable such interfaces via optomechanically induced transparency (OMIT), allowing coherent mapping between traveling optical fields and localized mechanical modes. However, previous implementations of OMIT conversion protocols were limited to classical input signals with large coherent state photon numbers due to room temperature operation and corresponding thermal mechanical noise. Here, we demonstrate efficient low-noise photon–phonon state transfer at the few-photon level in an optomechanical crystal operated at Millikelvin temperatures. Using weak coherent optical input pulses, we achieve a record-level photon–phonon conversion efficiency of η = 0.75 ± 0.12 , a mechanical storage lifetime of $T_\mathrm{1}=\SI{7.3}{\micro\second}$ , and a tunable conversion bandwidth up to $\SI{4.5}{\mega\hertz}$ . Hanbury Brown–Twiss measurements of the retrieved signal demonstrate the coherent nature of the converted phononic state, evidencing low added thermal noise in the conversion process ( n t h = 9.0 ± 1.4 ). These results establish optomechanical crystals as efficient optical interfaces to GHz mechanical modes and provide a pathway toward deterministic single-quantum-level mechanical state preparation.

title: Association of Mediterranean–DASH intervention for neurodegenerative delay (MIND) diet with cognition and total and cardiovascular mortality: results from the HAPIEE cohort
summary: BACKGROUND: The Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) dietary pattern, developed to slow cognitive decline, has been linked to cardiometabolic benefits and lower mortality. Its associations with cognition and mo
content: BACKGROUND: The Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) dietary pattern, developed to slow cognitive decline, has been linked to cardiometabolic benefits and lower mortality. Its associations with cognition and mortality have not been studied in Eastern European populations. This study aimed to assess the relationship between MIND diet, cognition and mortality in Eastern European adults. METHODS: Data from 15,427 adults aged 45-69 years at baseline in the Czech and Polish cohorts of the Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors in Eastern Europe prospective cohort were analyzed. Baseline MIND diet scores (range 0-15), derived from validated food frequency questionnaires, were classified into three groups: low (<6), moderate (6-7), and high (>7). Trained nurses assessed cognitive domains at baseline. Deaths were ascertained via national registries. Multivariable regressions estimated the MIND diet-mortality and MIND diet-cognition associations, adjusting for sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics. RESULTS: Over about 20 years of follow-up, 3,792 deaths occurred. After controlling for age and sex, MIND diet adherence was associated with lower total and CVD mortality and better cognitive outcomes. However, after full adjustment, the associations were no longer significant (high vs low adherence for all-cause mortality: HR = 1.01, 95%CI:0.93-1.10; for CVD mortality: HR = 1.01, 95%CI:0.88-1.16), and only the positive association with verbal fluency remained significant (high vs low: coefficient 0.058, SE 0.024, p = 0.015). CONCLUSION: This study of MIND diet in Central and Eastern European cohort did not find clear evidence on mortality, but the results on cognition, particularly verbal fluency, were generally consistent with the literature.

title: A Cultural Political Economy of Management Consultants in the Gulf
source: SOAS Research Online (SOAS University of London)
summary: Represented by international firms, management consultants have become pivotal agents in the political economy of the Gulf. Embedded within the highest rungs of decision-making, consultants support leaders in envisioning development pathway
content: Represented by international firms, management consultants have become pivotal agents in the political economy of the Gulf. Embedded within the highest rungs of decision-making, consultants support leaders in envisioning development pathways, enacting policy paradigms, and articulating problematisations and solutions to the current conjuncture through extensive publishing and advisory work. Drawing on 20 qualitative interviews with management consultants, government advisors, managers, and public-sector workers, alongside a systematic analysis of consulting, public-sector, and INGO documents, this thesis employs Cultural Political Economy (CPE) to analyse the role of consultants in maintaining the hegemony of state-led development in the Gulf. The thesis combines CPE with tools from Critical Discourse Analysis and Systemic Functional Linguistics to examine the discursive production of consultants and Gulf elites. It argues that management consultants function as organic intellectuals who attach themselves to dominant social groups and participate in the organisation and stabilisation of hegemonic projects. The analysis identifies a set of strategic alliances between consultants and elites, conceptualised as the “consulting union”: a contingent class alliance mobilised to intervene in the functioning of the political economy. This union is expressed through co-authored publications, the joint development of knowledging technologies, and coordinated strategic actions that advance shared material and ideal interests. Through a series of discursive and extra-discursive case studies, the thesis demonstrates how state-led development pathways are elaborated, operationalised, and experimentally enacted, contributing to their stabilisation as common sense. In doing so, this thesis studies the role of management consultants in the political economy of the Gulf to provide an original and timely contribution to the fields of sociology, international political economy, and Gulf studies.

title: 绿色金融助推实体经济高质量发展路径探析
summary: 绿色金融通过缓解融资错配、内化环境外部性、优化长期资本配置，赋能产业绿色转型。基于2013—2023年30个省份面板数据，运用双向固定效应模型实证检验赋能效应。结果显示，绿色金融显著助推实体经济高质量发展，绿色信贷、绿色债券、碳金融均发挥正向作用，存在融资约束缓解、技术创新两大传导机制，赋能效应呈区域异质性，西部边际效应最显著。
