title: Adaptive Preference Elicitation in Preference Robust CPT-Based Shortfall
summary: This paper investigates the cumulative prospect theory (CPT)-based shortfall risk measure where the value (utility) function and the distortion (probability weighting) functions are ambiguous. We propose a worst-case CPT-based shortfall ris
content: This paper investigates the cumulative prospect theory (CPT)-based shortfall risk measure where the value (utility) function and the distortion (probability weighting) functions are ambiguous. We propose a worst-case CPT-based shortfall risk measure where the capital requirement is based on the worst-case value function and distortion functions from an ambiguity set constructed with user-specific information (e.g., preference between risky and certain lotteries) and well-known general information such as the S-shape of the value functions. When the underlying random loss is discretely distributed and parameters in pairs of lotteries remain undetermined, we demonstrate that the worst-case value function and the distortion functions have a piecewise linear structure. Based on this observation, we develop an adaptive preference elicitation approach extended from the well-known polyhedral method to simultaneously elicit the distortion functions and the positive and negative parts of the value function by solving a sequence of mixed-integer linear programs. Based on the elicited distortion, we design new queries to construct a feasible set of the holistic value functions. The proposed framework iteratively shrinks the ambiguity set through designed queries, yielding a computationally implementable robust CPT-based shortfall risk measure. To examine the in-sample and out-of-sample performance of the elicited CPT-based preference functions and the resulting preference robust shortfall risk measure, we conduct numerical experiments under an S-shaped value function and inverse S-shaped distortion functions and report the corresponding results.

title: Economic efficiency and development standards of cultural - agritourism corridors in Shida Kartli
summary: This paper examines the prospects for the development of rural and agritourism in the Shida Kartli region of Georgia. The research is based on a synthesis of the "cultural-agritourism corridors" concept and the operational standards outline
content: This paper examines the prospects for the development of rural and agritourism in the Shida Kartli region of Georgia. The research is based on a synthesis of the "cultural-agritourism corridors" concept and the operational standards outlined in the "National Guidelines for Rural Tourism 2025." The objective of the study is to evaluate how proximity to major cultural heritage magnets influences the economic sustainability and profitability of small family-owned agritourism ventures, and to define the operational mechanisms required for their long-term viability. Michael Porter's cluster analysis and ALCP2 practical indicators serve as the theoretical and empirical framework. Based on field data, participation in integrated corridors increases business revenue by an average of 40% while reducing Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) by 35%. The paper further addresses sector-wide hurdles, including high seasonality, authenticity preservation, and digital visibility.

title: Evidence-graded supply chain readiness for process innovation: an operational assessment and claim-governance framework
source: International Journal of Industrial Engineering and Operations Management
summary: Purpose This study develops an operational, evidence-graded supply-chain readiness framework (E-SCRL) that separates capability maturity, lifecycle state and evidential sufficiency in process-innovation decisions. Design/methodology/approac
content: Purpose This study develops an operational, evidence-graded supply-chain readiness framework (E-SCRL) that separates capability maturity, lifecycle state and evidential sufficiency in process-innovation decisions. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a structured integrative evidence-mapping and methodological framework-development approach. An analysis of 44 studies informs the identification of seven supply-chain readiness domains and the development of the E-SCRL assessment framework. The proposed instrument integrates cumulative maturity requirements (M0–M4), independent lifecycle classifications (observed, reconstructed and projected), ordinal evidence grades (E0–E3), and a threshold-based evidence-coverage profile. Non-compensatory assessment criteria and state-specific decision rules are examined through logical consistency tests and applied to two process-innovation contexts, addressing projected modelling readiness and reconstructed operational practices. Findings Maturity research covers operational integration, digitalisation, performance, sustainability and resilience, but the reviewed reporting fields do not consistently identify whether a score is observed, reconstructed or projected. E-SCRL prevents lifecycle state from being confused with insufficient evidence and prevents strong evidence for a model from being interpreted as evidence of implementation. Research limitations/implications The evidence map is not a multi-database full-text systematic review, and the governance thresholds require field calibration and inter-rater testing. Practical implications The instrument supplies reproducible requirements, evidence thresholds, permissible wording and next actions for operational improvement and capital-design gates. Originality/value E-SCRL converts a maturity score into a governed claim: a domain profile, lifecycle state, evidence-coverage vector and sufficiency flag. It therefore supports ex post and ex ante assessment without treating them as evidentially equivalent.

title: Ferry transport services as an international tourism booster for the islands: assessing the challenges of achieving optimal service efficiency and safety
summary: Purpose Ferry transport is vital for island economies, yet persistent operational challenges threaten service reliability and sustainability. This study aims to systematically prioritise key challenges in Langkawi's ferry services to guide
content: Purpose Ferry transport is vital for island economies, yet persistent operational challenges threaten service reliability and sustainability. This study aims to systematically prioritise key challenges in Langkawi's ferry services to guide targeted improvements. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory sequential mixed-method approach was used. Content analysis first identified the key operational challenges, which were then ranked using the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) based on stakeholder perceptions. Findings High operating costs, ferry system failures and management inefficiencies emerged as the highest-ranked challenges. Workforce shortages, scheduling inefficiencies and lack of security and safety awareness were moderately ranked, while infrastructure limitations and navigation constraints were ranked as lower-priority challenges but relevant long-term concerns. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on Langkawi's ferry system; thus, the findings may reflect contextual characteristics specific to island-based operations. However, the methodological framework provides a basis for comparative studies in similar maritime settings. Practical implications The prioritised mitigation framework supports operators and policymakers in implementing cost optimisation, predictive maintenance of assets and infrastructure, workforce training and digitalisation strategies to enhance operational efficiency. Social implications Improved ferry reliability strengthens tourism sustainability, regional economic development and community mobility in island environments. Originality/value This study integrates qualitative exploration with AHP-based prioritisation to coordinate a structured, decision-oriented mitigation strategy for sustainable ferry transport systems.

title: Successful Implementation of Sustainable Last Mile Logistics Innovations by Using the Planning Analysis Framework
summary: While numerous projects have tested sustainable last mile logistics innovations, their permanent implementation is hampered by several barriers such as a lack of operators, funding and space. Explanations are often kept very general and are
content: While numerous projects have tested sustainable last mile logistics innovations, their permanent implementation is hampered by several barriers such as a lack of operators, funding and space. Explanations are often kept very general and are only analysed in limited depth without following a specific systematic holistic methodology. This paper applies the Planning Analysis Framework (PAF) as a systematic approach to identify barriers and success factors of implementation processes and to derive recommendations for action. The PAF comprises five steps that can be used to describe, analyse and design planning processes and is based on a political science and systems theory perspective. To demonstrate the applicability of the PAF, a detailed Planning Analysis is carried out for a real-life use case in Istanbul involving a forecasting tool and electric cargo bikes as part of the EU-project DECARBOMILE. The necessary data is obtained through qualitative and quantitative measures. Results show that a more in-depth approach is important to identify deeper-rooted reasons such as the influence of the stakeholder landscape or communication that can have a greater impact due to interdependencies in a very complex socio-technical system.

title: A holistic study of the basic socialist economic system: a re-examination based on the methodology of totality
summary: Purpose This paper aims to examine China's basic socialist economic system through the lens of the Marxist methodology of totality, addressing the limitation of conventional approaches that analyse components in isolation. It seeks to provi
content: Purpose This paper aims to examine China's basic socialist economic system through the lens of the Marxist methodology of totality, addressing the limitation of conventional approaches that analyse components in isolation. It seeks to provide a holistic understanding of the system's historical evolution, structural composition and integrated advantages. Design/methodology/approach Adopting the Marxist methodology of totality encompassing historical, structural and critical dimensions, this paper conducts a qualitative theoretical analysis grounded in Marxist political economy, drawing on CPC Central Committee decisions and historical documents to re-examine the evolution, organic structure and overall advantages of the basic socialist economic system. Findings: The paper finds that the basic socialist economic system embodies a dialectical unity of historical continuity, structural interdependence and critical construction, forming an organic whole rather than a mechanical aggregation of isolated elements. It demonstrates that the integration of the ownership structure, the distribution system and the socialist market economy yields synergistic advantages surpassing the sum of individual components, and that the system's evolution reflects a unified process of destruction and construction grounded in the contradictory movement between productive forces and relations of production. Originality/value: This paper offers a novel theoretical framework applying the Marxist methodology of totality to re-examine the basic socialist economic system, moving beyond partial or static analyses of individual components. It provides an academic foundation for enhancing institutional integration, advancing high-quality development and promoting Chinese modernisation, while deepening theoretical understanding of the advantages of the socialist economic system and offering a holistic perspective on institutional maturity and consolidation.

title: Generic Frugality in CCS System
summary: In France, regional lines play a key role in connecting urban areas, providing access to rural areas and to tourist and heritage sites. Yet, non-regenerated regional lines are falling into disrepair and costs are rising, while attractivenes
content: In France, regional lines play a key role in connecting urban areas, providing access to rural areas and to tourist and heritage sites. Yet, non-regenerated regional lines are falling into disrepair and costs are rising, while attractiveness is declining. Modernizing regional lines is a challenge, given their diversity and the state of their infrastructure. The first response to the frugal regeneration of an aging system is to control the total cost of the ownership of those low-density traffic lines. A wide range of constraints needs to be considered to propose an appropriate response to the targeted operational performance. Achieving frugality for a Control Command and Signalling system in Europe means looking for generic frugality criteria above costly ERTMS deployment plans: trackside and on-board integration and migration criteria, compatibility and interpenetration criteria with the EU Comprehensive network, and operational performance criteria. In order to do so, we are exploring several approaches: Stability approach based on a light version of ERTMS without any modification of ETCS-equipped fleet. Innovative interoperable approach based on future game changers on top of ETCS. Cost reduction for regional lines is the cornerstone of a CCS frugality strategy to foster a possible generalization of ETCS deployment

title: Do Foreign Remittances Move Poor Indian Households into the Middle Class? Before-and-After Class Status, Years Abroad, and the Gulf, European, Canadian and United States Corridors
summary: India is the world’s largest recipient of remittances: private transfers reached a record US$135.5 billion in 2024-25. Yet the composition of these flows has changed. Advanced economies now send more than half, while the share of the Gulf C
content: India is the world’s largest recipient of remittances: private transfers reached a record US$135.5 billion in 2024-25. Yet the composition of these flows has changed. Advanced economies now send more than half, while the share of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries fell from 46.7 percent in 2016-17 to 37.9 percent in 2023-24 (RBI, 2025), even though the Gulf still absorbs almost all of India’s low-skilled, emigration-check-required (ECR) workers. This paper asks whether remittances move poor Indian households into the middle class, and whether that movement lasts once remittances stop. Using the income classes of the PRICE ICE 360° survey (destitute, aspirer, and a middle class subdivided into ‘seekers’ and ‘strivers’), uprated to 2024-25 prices, we distinguish each origin household’s class before migration, its observed class while remittances flow and its durable class on remittance-independent income. We build a calibrated cohort microsimulation of 20,000 destitute and aspirer households per corridor, with parameters drawn from Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Kerala Migration Survey (KMS) data and published studies, and compare four regimes: the Gulf (fixed-term contract labour from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and the South), Southern Europe (Punjabi agricultural and service migration to Italy and Portugal, often through irregular routes), Canada (the study-permit-to-permanent-residence route from Punjab and Haryana) and the United States (for poor households, the irregular ‘dunki’ route from Punjab, Haryana and Gujarat). The results differ sharply from the common view. A single low-skilled Gulf migrant lifts a poor household out of destitution and into the upper-aspirer band within two years, but almost never into the middle class: fewer than 9 percent cross the lower-middle (seeker) threshold even while remittances flow, and only about 2 percent do so on a durable basis. The European corridor carries half of households into the seeker band on an observed basis by year six, but durable middle-class status remains below 10 percent after 15 years. The Canadian route is the most expensive and, for genuinely poor households, the most dangerous: its debt pushes many households into durable destitution for the first five to eight years. The United States corridor, India’s largest source of remittances but for poor households mainly an irregular route costing Rs 35-57 lakh, works like a lottery: households whose migrant stays send the highest remittances of any corridor, but with deportation risk high, about one household in five ends in durable destitution. Remittances in India buy an exit from destitution and a secure aspirer position, not entry into the middle class. We set out corridor-specific policies and an econometric design for testing these predictions on PLFS, HCES and KMS microdata. JEL classification: F22, F24, I32, D31, O15

title: OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE AND TAX AGGRESSIVENESS : THE MODERATING ROLE OF INDEPENDENT COMMISSIONERS
summary: This study examines whether institutional and managerial ownership affect on tax aggressiveness and whteher the proportion of independent commisioners moderates these efect, using non-financial firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (
content: This study examines whether institutional and managerial ownership affect on tax aggressiveness and whteher the proportion of independent commisioners moderates these efect, using non-financial firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) over 2021-2025 period. Applying purposive sampling to every non-financial IDX sector, 231 companies qualified, producing 1,155 firm-year data points arranged as a strongly balanced panel. The panel was processed in Stata, and the Random Effect Model (REM) emerged as the estimator of choice. Neither institutional nor managerial ownership exerts a statistically meaningful influence on tax aggressiveness, and independent commissioners fail to condition either association. The low R-squared value obtained indicates that ownerhip structure is not primary determinant of tax aggresiveness within this sample, suggesting that governance mechanisms based on ownership structire are insufficient to explain corporate tax behavior and should be complemented by other firm specific drivers, for example as profitability, capital intensity and auditor quality.

title: Political Instruments for Freight Modal Shift: A Transport Policy Evaluation in the Austrian Context
summary: Despite longstanding political efforts within the European Union to shift freight transport modes, road transport remains dominant. This imbalance hinders the achievement of climate neutrality goals under the European Green Deal and exacerb
content: Despite longstanding political efforts within the European Union to shift freight transport modes, road transport remains dominant. This imbalance hinders the achievement of climate neutrality goals under the European Green Deal and exacerbates the problem of severe traffic congestion on European highways. Although various political instruments have been introduced, evidence of their effectiveness in changing freight mode choices remains scarce. This paper examines the Austrian case using a two-step approach: (1) a literature review of modal shift policies was conducted to identify ten relevant policy measures, followed by (2) a quantitative survey of 61 Austrian freight stakeholders. The results reveal three novel findings: First, stakeholders rate the overall effectiveness of existing measures as low (mean = 2.7/5), indicating minimal influence on actual mode choice. Second, stakeholders distinguish between policy types: regulatory instruments such as mandatory rail transport for waste, scored 3.7, while financial incentives like terminal funding and subsidies reached up to 4.0, suggesting stronger leverage. Third, a paradox emerges in road pricing: firms with >50% road share report no intention to shift modes, despite Austria facing some of the highest toll levels in Europe. The paper concludes that a successful modal shift requires targeted measures that reduce administrative burden and address infrastructure bottlenecks in line with supply chain logic.

title: Designing Resilient and Sustainable Multimodal Logistics Platforms: Functional Requirements and Industry Ecosystem Integration
summary: Disruptions in global supply chains and increasing sustainability demands challenge Europe’s multimodal logistics systems. This paper conceptualises the modular requirements of a digital platform solution designed to improve resilience and
content: Disruptions in global supply chains and increasing sustainability demands challenge Europe’s multimodal logistics systems. This paper conceptualises the modular requirements of a digital platform solution designed to improve resilience and sustainability by identifying multimodal route alternatives and enabling efficient route planning and orchestration utilising real-time data exchange. Derived from expert interviews and an online survey focusing on challenges caused by disruptions in the transport system, functional, non-functional, and technical requirements for resilient platform design have been identified. Employing a Design Science Research (DSR) approach, the paper conceptualises platform modules that support resilience and sustainability goals, emphasising the reduction of environmental impacts and promoting multimodal transport alternatives. The focus lies on the collaborative approach to adaptive route orchestration and optimisation through predictive analytics and cross-system data availability for all relevant stakeholders of the multimodal transport ecosystem. The modular approach enables the proposed structure to be extended in future research and practical implementation. The Horizon Europe research project ReMuNet leverages intelligent algorithms and digital platforms to enhance multimodal networks, optimise route planning, and improve disruption response, contributing to the vision of the Physical Internet.

title: Long‐term Orientation and Proactive Environmental Strategies in Emerging Markets: Evidence From India
summary: This study examines how emerging market firms characterized by a long‐term orientation (LTO) develop the organizational routines that support proactive environmental strategies (PES). These strategies are essential for sustaining operations
content: This study examines how emerging market firms characterized by a long‐term orientation (LTO) develop the organizational routines that support proactive environmental strategies (PES). These strategies are essential for sustaining operations within evolving institutions and for adopting environmentally friendly practices in institutionally weak settings. Thus, building on the perspective of organizational routines, this study establishes a positive association between firms' LTO and their likelihood of adopting PES in emerging markets. Furthermore, drawing on informal institutions and transaction‐cost reasoning, the findings suggest that informal competition and crime in emerging markets discourage firms from investing in PES, thereby weakening the baseline relationship. Based on a sample of 6547 Indian firms, we find support for all hypotheses. This research advances the literature on PES by providing insights into how firms' LTO, industry‐level informal competition, and societal‐level crime collectively influence their sustainability strategies in emerging markets.

title: Ultra-High-Frequency ECG-Derived Local Depolarization Duration as a Potential Digital Biomarker of Myocardial Scar in Dilated Cardiomyopathy
summary: Myocardial scarring, detected by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, is associated with sudden cardiac death in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). Ultra-high-frequency electrocardiography (UHF-ECG) char
content: Myocardial scarring, detected by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, is associated with sudden cardiac death in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). Ultra-high-frequency electrocardiography (UHF-ECG) characterizes local ventricular activation and may reveal electrical disturbances associated with myocardial scarring. We investigated the relationship between UHF-ECG-derived local depolarization duration and LGE presence and extent in a prospective multicentre cohort of 87 patients with DCM. Mean local depolarization duration across leads V1–V6 was compared with CMR findings, with analyses stratified by QRS duration and morphology. In patients with narrow QRS complexes (n = 34) or intraventricular conduction delay (n = 23), longer mean local depolarization duration correlated with greater LGE extent (ρ = 0.559 and 0.473, respectively). In these subgroups, local depolarization duration also discriminated between patients with and without LGE. No significant association with LGE presence was observed in the overall cohort or in patients with left bundle branch block. These findings suggest that the relationship between local depolarization duration and myocardial scarring may depend on QRS characteristics. UHF-ECG-derived local depolarization duration may serve as a digital biomarker of myocardial scarring in selected patients with DCM, although these exploratory findings require independent validation.

title: Belt and road initiative’s investment effects on Central Asian trade. Does the pattern of regionalisation matter?
summary: Central Asian countries’ economic integration into world trade has recently been reoriented by regional integration schemes or investment plans supported by China and Russia. Predominantly, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is expected to
content: Central Asian countries’ economic integration into world trade has recently been reoriented by regional integration schemes or investment plans supported by China and Russia. Predominantly, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is expected to ease infrastructure development in the region. However, the reduced effectiveness of past trade regionalisation attempts has recently hindered intraregional trade growth. This study aims to examine the impact of the BRI, World Trade Organization (WTO), the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) on trade flows among Central Asian countries. In order to achieve this objective, data between 2010 and 2023 were gathered to perform a gravity equation under random and fixed effects models. According to our analysis, the SCO, EAEU and BRI have recently favoured trade flows, but the WTO has not exerted a positive influence. Consequently, authoritarian regionalism schemes such as the BRI, SCO or EAEU have succeeded in establishing trade links among members.

title: Crisis Federalism or Federalism in Crisis? The Political Economy of Intergovernmental Fiscal Relations in an Age of Uncertainty
summary: The politics of intergovernmental fiscal relations in federations are showing the strain of a series of crises with enduring implications. Since the Global Financial Crisis, the political economy of many federations’ long-established fiscal
content: The politics of intergovernmental fiscal relations in federations are showing the strain of a series of crises with enduring implications. Since the Global Financial Crisis, the political economy of many federations’ long-established fiscal settlements has been steadily reshaped by demographic change, global warming, deteriorating public finances, the rise of right-wing economic populism, and, most recently, the COVID-19 pandemic. Some of these developments reflect the natural evolution of institutions and political compacts that have always adapted to changes in their social and economic contexts, but others increasingly seem like more decisive ruptures. This chapter offers a broad, comparative perspective on how the structures and normative foundations of fiscal federalism are faring in a period of profound uncertainty. Whether this period will underscore the enduring relevance of fiscal federalism as an adaptable institutional expression of national solidarity or herald the return of a more autonomous ‘fend-for-yourself’ federalism remains to be seen.

title: Alignment and expansion in national adaptation of the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines: a cross-national analysis
summary: Background: The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (EML) provides a common global reference for national medicines selection. National adaptation frequently involves both the adoption of WHO-recommended medicines and the addition of medi
content: Background: The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (EML) provides a common global reference for national medicines selection. National adaptation frequently involves both the adoption of WHO-recommended medicines and the addition of medicines beyond WHO EML, which have not been distinguished in comparative analyses. This study quantifies how countries adapt the WHO EML by distinguishing alignment from expansion, exploring country-level characteristics potentially associated with these dimensions. Methods: We compared national essential medicines lists (NEMLs) from 137 countries with the WHO EML. We constructed two independent measures: the Alignment Ratio, representing the proportion of WHO-recommended medicines included in each NEML, and the Expansion Ratio, representing the proportion of NEML medicines not included in the WHO EML. Countries were also classified into four adaptation modes based on combinations of alignment and expansion. Associations with country-level characteristics were examined using multivariable beta regression. Results: Countries displayed substantial heterogeneity in adaptation patterns, with representation across all four adaptation modes defined by alignment with and expansion beyond the WHO EML. Fifty countries were categorized as restrictive/constrained adoption (low alignment, low expansion), thirty-five countries as normative dependence (high alignment, low expansion), sixteen countries as autonomous divergence (low alignment, high expansion) and thirty-six countries as capacity-driven expansion (high alignment, high expansion). Higher under-five mortality was associated with lower alignment (β = −0.294; 95% CI: −0.497 to −0.091) and lower expansion (β = −0.481; 95% CI: −0.697 to −0.264). Higher globalization index scores and more recent NEMLs were associated with higher alignment, but not expansion. Conclusion: While some countries closely followed the WHO EML with limited additions, a substantial proportion combined high alignment with extensive expansion beyond the WHO benchmark, suggesting that national adaptation often involves supplementation rather than substitution of WHO recommendations.

title: Education-Skill Mismatches in Thailand: A Conceptual Framework Addressing Challenges and Pathways to an Innovation-Driven Economy
summary: Thailand’s ambition to become an innovation-driven economy continues to be challenged by a mismatch between its education system output and the demands of its labor market. This study takes a close look at national policies, academic studie
content: Thailand’s ambition to become an innovation-driven economy continues to be challenged by a mismatch between its education system output and the demands of its labor market. This study takes a close look at national policies, academic studies, and major reports from the past years to understand reasons that Thai graduates struggle to find jobs that match with their education, especially in emerging fields like STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) and digital technology. The analysis reveals interconnected contributing factors, including outdated curricula, slow policy coordination, rapid demographic changes, and weak linkages between education and industry demands. Following this, many graduates find themselves underprepared to work in the real world, especially in non-technical fields. To address these issues, the country requires consistent collaboration, investment in lifelong learning, and practical inclusive solutions that are suitable across the country. This paper offers a conceptual framework to guide these reforms and emphasizes that closing the gap between education and employment is crucial if Thailand is to achieve its economic development goals.

title: State Capital Participation and AI Transformation in Private Firms: Evidence from Persistent Minority State Ownership in China
summary: This study examines minority state ownership and AI transformation in privately controlled Chinese A-share firms during 2010–2025 using CSMAR data. Persistent State Entry begins in the second of two consecutive years with aggregate state ow
content: This study examines minority state ownership and AI transformation in privately controlled Chinese A-share firms during 2010–2025 using CSMAR data. Persistent State Entry begins in the second of two consecutive years with aggregate state ownership of at least 5%. AI transformation is measured by the number of distinct AI terms in MD&A (AI Breadth) and log one plus granted group-level AI invention patents (AI Patents). Firm, industry-by-year, and province-by-year fixed-effects estimates show positive associations with both outcomes, with stronger statistical support for patents. Results are consistent with R&D, technical staffing, knowledge assets, and financing channels, and associations are more favorable among firms with stronger pre-confirmation technological foundations and in competitive industries. Because treatment marks persistence confirmation rather than initial entry, the estimates are associational and do not identify a first-exposure shock.

title: Communication barriers to emergency medical services among stateless and displaced populations in Thailand: provider perspectives and the development of a community intermediary model
summary: Background: Stateless and displaced populations in Thailand are legally entitled to emergency medical care, yet a profound equity gap persists between legal entitlement and actual access. These marginalized groups rarely utilize the nationa
content: Background: Stateless and displaced populations in Thailand are legally entitled to emergency medical care, yet a profound equity gap persists between legal entitlement and actual access. These marginalized groups rarely utilize the national emergency number (1669). Empirical evidence on restructuring emergency medical services (EMS) to reach them remains scarce. This study aimed to examine systemic communication barriers to EMS access from the perspective of providers, compare them with community experiences, and develop a theory-grounded community intermediary model to close this access gap. Materials and Methods: We conducted a three-phase, mixed-methods intervention development study informed by the Medical Research Council (MRC) framework and INDEX guidance across two geographically contrasting settings: Chiang Mai (highlands) and Ranong (islands). Phase 1 engaged 76 EMS, healthcare, local government, and civil society personnel through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews, comparing their insights against a parallel community survey (n = 269). Phase 2 translated these empirical findings into intervention design principles using health communication and access theories. Phase 3 refined the resulting model through expert interviews and a consultation meeting with 15 key stakeholders. Results: Stateless individuals rarely contact 1669 directly, relying instead on an indirect help-seeking chain (employers, volunteers, and community leaders), which causes critical delays and information loss. Providers reported that clients favored local administrative agencies over the 1669 hotline (92.9% vs 54.8% in Chiang Mai). Providers' lowest self-rated competence was conducting clinical assessments in clients' native languages (means: 2.71 and 2.88 out of 5). Five core themes emerged: an indirect help-seeking chain; language and geographic isolation barriers; layered institutional fears (legal status, costs, and authority); divergent definitions of medical emergencies; and individual goodwill lacking systemic support. Notably, providers over-estimated infrastructural barriers but under-estimated obstacles stemming from their own linguistic limitations and medical jargon (p < 0.05). The co-designed Community Intermediary Model establishes formally registered, community-nominated intermediaries backed by a targeted fear-reduction campaign, a multilingual interpreter registry, visual communication toolkits, offline-first digital channels, and formal cross-agency safe-zone policies. Conclusions: Communication barriers span every dimension of healthcare access—from perceiving need to engaging with providers. Designing EMS frameworks around trusted community intermediaries, rather than enforcing direct-to-system contact, offers a structurally competent and feasible pathway to translate universal legal entitlements into equitable emergency care access.

title: GCP: A Safety-Aware, Payment-Agnostic Commerce Protocol for Automotive and Mobility Agents
summary: Personal agents are moving from conversation to commerce. Emerging protocols such as Poppy, UCP, and ACP define how an agent proves whom it represents, discovers merchants, fills a cart, and completes an online checkout. None of them is des
content: Personal agents are moving from conversation to commerce. Emerging protocols such as Poppy, UCP, and ACP define how an agent proves whom it represents, discovers merchants, fills a cart, and completes an online checkout. None of them is designed for the commerce that automotive and mobility users actually need: buying a brake pad that fits a specific VIN, booking maintenance at an authorized dealer, binding insurance, or placing a vehicle reservation under safety and consumer-protection rules. This paper proposes GCP 1.0 , an open, capability-based commerce protocol for automotive and mobility agents. GCP adds four things that general commerce protocols lack: (i) vehicle context and safety gates as first-class protocol objects; (ii) a delegation and authorization ladder that lets a human grant bounded purchase authority and revoke it at any time; (iii) a payment-agnostic intent layer that abstracts card, wallet, Alipay, WeChat Pay, OEM finance, and agent-native payment tokens; and (iv) a typed exception and recovery model for the failure modes of real commerce. GCP is compatible by translation: it consumes Poppy identity and session credentials, maps its catalog/cart/checkout objects to UCP and ACP, and carries GCP-specific safety and authorization fields as extension namespaces. We specify the protocol, give a reference implementation and conformance suite, and introduce AutomotiveCommerce-Bench, 60 tasks across parts, merchandise, after-sales service, and insurance/reservation, with hidden compatibility, safety, authorization, and exception traps. In a real-LLM study with three models, GCP raises task success from 64.5% (manual web) and 69.4% (generic agent commerce) to 92.2%, cuts misbuy from 35.5%/30.6% to 7.8%, and raises exception recovery from about 58% to 89.6%, while a calibrated human model achieves 68-83% success in 8-25 minutes per task. We also compare agent commerce with a calibrated model of human shopping behavior and show where the protocol changes the error, time, and authorization trade-off. Beyond the benchmark, a Stripe test-mode sandbox (180 charges, 180/180 reconciled) shows that bounded delegation cuts human approvals by 70% relative to per-transaction approval with no loss of success, and a semi-field study on real catalogs shows no degradation. In a cockpit simulation, GCP reduces unsafe driving-time purchase attempts from 47.9% to 0% (deferral rises to 81.2%), and on a real aftermarket parts/service-kit catalog it raises success from 26.7% to 100%. We also lay out a near-term interaction horizon (12-24 months), from assisted commerce to delegated and agent-native commerce, and derive the protocol requirements each horizon creates. The protocol, benchmark, and all raw results are released.

title: Agricultural Formalisation and the Foundations of Green Innovation: Evidence from the 2020–2024 Business Register
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
summary: We describe how the number of registered farmers and other active legal units in Albania changed between 2020 and 2024, and what this wider administrative coverage could mean for later research on green innovation in agriculture. The analys
content: We describe how the number of registered farmers and other active legal units in Albania changed between 2020 and 2024, and what this wider administrative coverage could mean for later research on green innovation in agriculture. The analysis uses two INSTAT business-register tables: annual stocks for 2020–2024 and the 2024 breakdown by economic activity and legal form. Registered farmers rose from 49,053 to 105,709 (+115.5%; compound annual growth rate 21.2%), while other active enterprises rose from 117,333 to 132,172 (+12.6%; 3.0% a year). The farmers' share of all active legal units went from 29.5% to 44.4%, and farmers account for 79.2% of the net increase in the register. The biggest jump came in 2021–2022, at the time of fiscal measures linked to registration, but aggregate counts cannot tell us whether these measures caused it. In 2024, 98.7% of the active legal units in agriculture, forestry and fishing were registered farmers. The counts do not measure green technology use, productivity or environmental results. For this reason we only propose four hypotheses for future farm-level work, on finance, relative prices, price volatility and registration, and do not test them. The paper gives a reproducible baseline for monitoring farmer registration and for designing future evaluations. Received: 27 March 2026 │ Accepted: 11 October 2026 │ Published: 20 November 2026

title: Closing the Knowledge Gap: How Moral Obligations, Perceived Benefits, and Dispositional Greed Shape Influencer Advertising Code Compliance
summary: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has outpaced regulatory enforcement and has increased the risk of noncompliance through misleading promotions and inadequate sponsorship disclosures. This study investigates whether and how enhancing
content: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has outpaced regulatory enforcement and has increased the risk of noncompliance through misleading promotions and inadequate sponsorship disclosures. This study investigates whether and how enhancing influencers’ advertising code knowledge affects their intentions to comply with advertising regulations. Specifically, it examines whether increased knowledge enhances compliance intentions, whether this relationship is mediated by moral obligations and perceived benefits, and whether dispositional greed moderates these mediating pathways. Across four studies, involving 1,082 U.K.-based social media influencers, we employed diverse research designs. Study 1 uses a single-session pre–post design (N = 154); Study 2 adopts a two-wave pre–post design (N = 213); Study 3 applies a third-person, between-subjects design (N = 228); and Study 4 employs a randomized experimental design (N = 487). The findings reveal that greater advertising code knowledge significantly increases influencers’ intentions to comply. This effect is mediated by stronger moral obligations and heightened recognition of the compliance benefits. Furthermore, dispositional greed moderates the influence of knowledge on both moral obligations and perceived benefits. These findings highlight the importance of targeted education and training that build influencers’ advertising code knowledge as a lever for strengthening ethical conduct and regulatory compliance.

title: ArcTrace: Black-Box Ownership Verification of LLM-Based Forecasting Models via Learned Numeric Preferences
summary: Large language models (LLMs) adapted into numeric forecasters increasingly inform decisions in energy, transport, finance and public health. Enforcing trade-secret protection, model licenses and the traceability expected by recent AI regula
content: Large language models (LLMs) adapted into numeric forecasters increasingly inform decisions in energy, transport, finance and public health. Enforcing trade-secret protection, model licenses and the traceability expected by recent AI regulations requires tracing such a model to its source after it has been copied, fine-tuned or imitated, yet a suspicious forecasting service reveals nothing but numbers. In this paper, we revisit black-box model watermarking for LLM-based forecasters. We argue that a watermark survives clean adaptation only when the model learns it as a strong, recurring part of ordinary forecasting. Direct ports of existing designs fail this condition, because clean adaptation erases behavior outside ordinary forecasting and keyed, context-dependent preferences are learned only weakly from decimal text. We further reveal a bias--evidence inversion, which identifies the keyed rule rather than the returned output as the unit of ownership evidence. Motivated by these findings, we propose ArcTrace, which embeds a watermark by modifying the forecaster's conditional digit distribution and counts its evidence per keyed rule, and we analyze the calibration and detection power of its test. Across 32 owner keys and 17 models from six series, ArcTrace detects the watermark for all 32 owner keys, verifies ownership from 375 forecasts on synthetic histories, and persists through quantization, light fine-tuning, key overwriting and distillation, at a cost of about 1\% in mean absolute scaled error on the development data and a median of 6.5\% across 17 models. These results suggest the provenance of a deployed forecaster can be established from numbers it returns.

title: Using causal inference to evaluate the direct and balloon effects of housing policy
source: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
summary: Policy impact assessment is a key priority for researchers and policymakers. Housing policies have significant economic and political implications, and their evaluation necessitates rigorous causal inference. This study investigates the eff
content: Policy impact assessment is a key priority for researchers and policymakers. Housing policies have significant economic and political implications, and their evaluation necessitates rigorous causal inference. This study investigates the effects of the housing policy introduced by the South Korean government on June 17, 2020. Using apartment transaction data from Seoul (January 2015 to December 2024), we analyze both the direct and indirect impacts of the policy through the synthetic control method and an event study design. Our findings show that the June 2020 policy achieved its primary objective of reducing apartment prices in the regulated zone, with the effect lasting approximately two years. However, adjacent non-regulated areas experienced a balloon effect of rising house prices, that manifested in two forms: a persistent effect characterized by sustained price increases, and a temporary effect, where prices initially rose but returned to pre-policy levels within two years. By evaluating both the intended and unintended consequences of the policy, this study provides a comprehensive assessment of its effectiveness, and offers insights for researchers and policymakers.

title: Evaluating the Governance of a School-Developed Learning Management System at SMP Negeri 2 Sei Bingai: A Qualitative CIPP-Based Case Study
source: Tanwiruna Jurnal Pendidikan dan Sosial Keagamaan
summary: This study evaluated the governance of a school-developed learning management system (LMS) at SMP Negeri 2 Sei Bingai, Indonesia, focusing on institutional needs, resource readiness, implementation and reported administrative benefits. It a
content: This study evaluated the governance of a school-developed learning management system (LMS) at SMP Negeri 2 Sei Bingai, Indonesia, focusing on institutional needs, resource readiness, implementation and reported administrative benefits. It adopted a qualitative, evaluative, holistic single-case design, with CIPP as the primary framework and selected DeLone–McLean dimensions as a supporting perspective. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observations and institutional documents, then analysed using the Framework Method with deductive and inductive coding. The LMS was developed because existing platforms were perceived to have insufficient user capacity and limited feature flexibility. It included functions for managing timetables, learning materials, teaching records, attendance, assignments and assessments. Unstable internet connectivity, limited funding and the need for technical expertise constrained its operation. Although the LMS was used for learning administration, the available evidence did not establish how consistently teachers used it. The administrator reported benefits for documentation, monitoring and information access, but these were not independently verified. The evaluation distinguishes the availability of LMS functions from consistent implementation and substantiated administrative benefits, pointing to the need for reliable connectivity, technical support and systematic monitoring.

title: Supplying metals needed for the energy transition: The value of creative reassembly as a conceptual lens
summary: Demand for metals continues to increase rapidly due to global income and population growth and is expected to accelerate due to the metal requirements of the clean energy transition. However, the metal supply system, which operates at both
content: Demand for metals continues to increase rapidly due to global income and population growth and is expected to accelerate due to the metal requirements of the clean energy transition. However, the metal supply system, which operates at both a local and global scale, has an organizational structure that impedes its ability to satisfy this demand. Observed increases in the amount of metal supplied by the system have resulted from a variety of changes (or reassemblies) to the relationships between existing organizations and groups in the system. There are several types of possible reassemblies, but only a few are common. Policies are needed to encourage or incentivize more of such reassembly activity. If reassembly were more common, metal supply systems would be more visible and accessible, leading to greater societal awareness of their importance. Non-traditional participation in the system would become a viable but unexplored alternative.

title: Design and proof of concept of a CRISPR/Cas13a-catalytic hairpin assembly framework for circulating microRNA detection in sepsis
summary: Sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, largely because early diagnosis is slow. Current biomarkers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin lack specificity and need up to 24 h to peak, delaying diagnosis in a condition
content: Sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, largely because early diagnosis is slow. Current biomarkers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin lack specificity and need up to 24 h to peak, delaying diagnosis in a condition where each hour increases mortality risk. Circulating microRNAs are promising early biomarkers, reflecting rapid molecular changes in the host response to infection. We propose a diagnostic framework combining CRISPR/Cas13a molecular recognition with a Catalytic Hairpin Assembly amplification circuit. Cas13a is programmed to recognize a short microRNA; on activation it cleaves a synthetic substrate collaterally, releasing an initiator that triggers an enzyme-free amplification cascade. In a proof-of-concept experiment a complete redesigned hairpin set (H0, H1 and H2) raised the share of the hairpin pool migrating as the H1-H2 duplex from approximately 34% to approximately 90% relative to a published set used in the same architecture, measured as band intensity in parallel lanes of a single gel. This is reported as a preliminary observation: the comparison rests on technical replicates of one reaction and lacks the no-target control that would establish target-dependent operation of the complete cascade. The system is designed for integration into a portable microneedle-microfluidic biosensor that would permit minimally invasive, serial sampling with an end-to-end assay time of approximately 4 h per measurement; that device has not been built and is described here as a specification. The two microRNAs were chosen by exhaustive screening of a public whole-blood cohort. They separate septic patients from healthy volunteers well (ROC-AUC 0.95) but separate them from patients with non-infectious inflammation poorly (ROC-AUC 0.64), and no panel of up to 263 curated microRNAs improved on that second figure, which is the comparison that matters clinically. That evidence comes from whole blood, a cell-associated compartment, whereas the proposed device would sample interstitial fluid, which is cell-free; performance in the intended sample therefore remains an open question. This article presents a hypothesis and a design, together with the computational and bench evidence that bears on them. No sensitivity, specificity or clinical performance is claimed, and the experiments that would test the proposal are set out explicitly.

title: GreenRise 2026 Impact Report
summary: Programme Title: GreenRise AgriVentures Academy 2026 Theme: From Knowledge to Enterprise: Building Climate-Smart Agripreneurs Dates: October 22–24, 2026 Location & Venue: Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria (RURCON Headquarters, Jos) Lead Organiser
content: Programme Title: GreenRise AgriVentures Academy 2026 Theme: From Knowledge to Enterprise: Building Climate-Smart Agripreneurs Dates: October 22–24, 2026 Location & Venue: Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria (RURCON Headquarters, Jos) Lead Organiser: TransGreen Foundation Programme Partners: Quantum Microfinance Bank, YMCA Northern Zone Nigeria, RURCON, and participating technical partners (including Farm Ferry Agro, EcoFarms & Agro Services Ltd., Green Eden Farms, and Farmnatics). Also notes a Development Finance Sensitisation session facilitated by the Central Bank of Nigeria.
