Programme Structure & CurriculumThe report is organized into ten sections (plus an "About TransGreen Foundation" closing page)and documents a progressive three-day learning model built around five core dimensions: climate awareness, technical capacity, enterprise development, financial capability, and practical application.

title: Superstars have the power? Technological M&As and firm markups
summary: We study whether acquisitions of patent-holding firms (technological M&As) raise acquirer markups, exploiting the staggered timing of first technological acquisitions in a panel of 7,796 listed firms in 79 countries over 2009–2020. Technolo
content: We study whether acquisitions of patent-holding firms (technological M&As) raise acquirer markups, exploiting the staggered timing of first technological acquisitions in a panel of 7,796 listed firms in 79 countries over 2009–2020. Technological M&As raise acquirer markups by 1.7 percent, roughly two years of growth in the aggregate US markup, with larger effects among top R&D investors. Post-acquisition patenting shows no detectable increase, and productivity declines. Markup gains increase with the size of the acquired patent stock and with technological proximity to the target, consistent with acquired patents shielding acquirers from rivals rather than with innovation or efficiency gains.

title: Bridging Evidence Gaps in Diabetes Devices in India: The Role of HTA in Policy and Value Assessment
summary: The prevalence of diabetes in India is rising rapidly, which results in substantial economic burden and productivity loss. Diabetes devices including continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), insulin pumps, and smart insulin pens, are critical fo
content: The prevalence of diabetes in India is rising rapidly, which results in substantial economic burden and productivity loss. Diabetes devices including continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), insulin pumps, and smart insulin pens, are critical for effective diabetes management. However, they remain underutilized due to high out-of-pocket expenditures, limited insurance coverage, and regional disparities in healthcare access. This paper highlights the need for economic evaluation of diabetes management devices in the Indian healthcare setting to improve accessibility and health outcomes. This paper also provides actionable insights for strengthening health technology assessment guidance for diabetes devices such as the need to establish real-world evidence (RWE) registries, incentivize local manufacturing, and integrate cost-effectiveness assessment into national/state health policy programs to improve access. We also provide guidance for future research to strengthen public-private partnership and incorporation of equity considerations in policy development. Strengthening economic evaluation is essential to achieve sustainable diabetes care in India.

title: Why Do Financial Institutions Underuse Satellite Data for Environmental Risk Assessment? Expert Evidence from Europe, the United States and Türkiye
source: Journal of risk and financial management
summary: Financial institutions need asset-level environmental information to price physical and transition risk, verify sustainable finance claims and meet new disclosure rules, yet satellite Earth observation (EO), an independent source of such in
content: Financial institutions need asset-level environmental information to price physical and transition risk, verify sustainable finance claims and meet new disclosure rules, yet satellite Earth observation (EO), an independent source of such information, remains marginal in practice. We ask whether this reflects a failure to recognise the information as decision-useful, frictions in acquiring and integrating it, or genuine limits on what satellites can measure. We develop a demand–use–capability gap framework and apply it to 32 financial management needs in investment management, green finance, risk analysis and insurance, mapped to 38 EO product suites. Finance specialists scored demand and use, and EO specialists scored capability in Europe and the United States; the framework was then applied in Türkiye through an exploratory expert survey of 39 respondents (780 evaluations), of whom 37 were EO data experts and providers and two represented financial institutions. Recognition and adoption gaps dominate in both settings. Hazard screening, natural-capital baselines and building exposure data are mature but underused, while emissions attribution is the only area where capability falls short of demand (2.9 against 4.0). In Türkiye, 76.7% of evaluations report medium or high demand but 39.4% report low or no use. The dominant constraint in the expert assessments is organisational. In Europe and the United States, the quality of institutions’ own asset-location data appears to condition whether satellite evidence reaches risk and reporting decisions; the Türkiye responses, which reflect EO-sector perceptions, point to a similar organisational pattern, with awareness and cost the most frequently cited barriers.

title: Designing university-employer engagement for graduate employability: Learning environments and curriculum co-design in Ireland and Wales
source: Journal of Teaching and Learning for Graduate Employability
summary: This study examined stakeholder perspectives on how learning environments and curriculum co-design can support effective university-employer engagement for employability-focused learning. Drawing on qualitative interviews and focus groups w
content: This study examined stakeholder perspectives on how learning environments and curriculum co-design can support effective university-employer engagement for employability-focused learning. Drawing on qualitative interviews and focus groups with 29 participants comprising ten employers and ten academics across Ireland and Wales and nine students in Ireland, the study used inductive thematic analysis informed by Clarke and Braun (2017) and Naeem et al. (2023), incorporating open and axial coding to identify spatial, relational and curricular conditions that enabled or constrained campus-based engagement. Nine themes highlighted the importance of human connection, inclusive and fit-for-purpose learning environments, purposeful curriculum activity, preparedness, technology, communication and ongoing relationship development, alongside barriers associated with inflexible and inaccessible spaces and inconsistent approaches to inclusion. The study contributes to existing scholarship by bringing together learning environments and curriculum co-design as interdependent dimensions of university-employer engagement, areas more commonly considered separately. Building on the empirical findings, it proposes a framework integrating preparation and relationship formation, inclusive learning environment design and purposeful curriculum activity, and post-event relationship development as connected stages of employability-focused university-employer collaboration. The framework provides an empirically informed approach to planning such engagement while offering a basis for further research into its application and effects on student learning and graduate employability.

title: EXTRAFISCALIDADE AMBIENTAL E INDICAÇÕES GEOGRÁFICAS: UM MODELO DE INCENTIVOS CONDICIONADOS PARA BIOECONOMIA DA SOCIOBIODIVERSIDADE DO CERRADO
summary: O Cerrado brasileiro, segundo maior bioma do país e hotspot de biodiversidade global, abriga rica sociobiodiversidade expressa em produtos como baru, pequi, buriti, cagaita, mangaba e mel nativo. Apesar do potencial econômico e ambiental de
content: O Cerrado brasileiro, segundo maior bioma do país e hotspot de biodiversidade global, abriga rica sociobiodiversidade expressa em produtos como baru, pequi, buriti, cagaita, mangaba e mel nativo. Apesar do potencial econômico e ambiental dessas cadeias extrativistas, persistem desafios na articulação entre políticas ambientais, tributárias e de propriedade intelectual. Este artigo investiga em que medida a extrafiscalidade tributária, articulada às Indicações Geográficas (IGs), pode contribuir para a valorização econômica dos produtos da sociobiodiversidade e para o desenvolvimento sustentável do Cerrado. A hipótese central sustenta que as IGs podem funcionar como infraestrutura institucional para políticas tributárias extrafiscais voltadas à bioeconomia, desde que os incentivos sejam condicionados à comprovação de resultados relacionados à conservação da biodiversidade, rastreabilidade, governança territorial e inclusão socioprodutiva. Propõe-se um modelo de incentivo tributário condicionado, estruturado em critérios de elegibilidade, indicadores socioambientais e territoriais, instrumentos tributários nos três níveis federativos e mecanismos de monitoramento e avaliação. O modelo é aplicado a quatro produtos estratégicos do Cerrado: baru, pequi, buriti e mel de abelhas nativas. A análise indica a plausibilidade jurídica-institucional da utilização das IGs como infraestrutura de governança e rastreabilidade para políticas extrafiscais ambientalmente condicionadas e por promover a captura territorial de valor, desde que respeitados os princípios da isonomia, neutralidade tributária e responsabilidade fiscal.

title: Cross-cultural assessment of wine aging potential and sensory profiles by wine professionals
summary: How wine professionals judge aging potential, whether it tracks liking, and whether panels across countries read it alike remain open questions. In Bordeaux, London, São Paulo, Chengdu, and Davis, 140 wine professionals blind-tasted 13 Arge
content: How wine professionals judge aging potential, whether it tracks liking, and whether panels across countries read it alike remain open questions. In Bordeaux, London, São Paulo, Chengdu, and Davis, 140 wine professionals blind-tasted 13 Argentinian wines from one producer (nine red, four white; 3–35 years), rated liking, projected an aging window, and described each wine. Panels shared a descriptor core (54 of 83 red-wine descriptors used at every site), but their descriptor use was less similar than expected by chance, most clearly in Bordeaux’s emphasis on structure and evolution. Projected windows contracted with bottle age in the red wines (odds ratio 0.30 per 10.9 years). Judgments nonetheless stayed spread across categories at every age: even for the 35-year-old wine, over a third of panelists placed it at its optimum or later. Liking was modestly related to the projected window (rho 0.37). Because wine professionals disagreed this widely, the distribution of judgments is more informative than any single category per wine.

title: The Effect of Organizational Culture and Transformational Leadership Style on Construction Service Company Performance Mediated by Employee Job Satisfaction
source: OPSearch American Journal of Open Research
summary: Intensifying competition among construction companies in Bali has highlighted the importance of understanding the relationships between organizational culture, transformational leadership, and company performance. This study examined the di
content: Intensifying competition among construction companies in Bali has highlighted the importance of understanding the relationships between organizational culture, transformational leadership, and company performance. This study examined the direct effects of organizational culture and transformational leadership on company performance and investigated the mediating role of employee job satisfaction in these relationships. A quantitative research approach was employed, using purposive sampling to select 100 permanent and contract employees from medium- and large-sized construction companies registered with the Indonesian Contractors Association (Gabungan Pelaksana Konstruksi Nasional Indonesia, GAPENSI) in Bali. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using second-order partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. Company performance was assessed using the Balanced Scorecard (BSC) framework. The results indicated that organizational culture and transformational leadership had positive but statistically nonsignificant direct effects on company performance. However, both variables had positive associations with employee job satisfaction, which was positively associated with company performance. Furthermore, employee job satisfaction significantly mediated the relationships between organizational culture and company performance (? = 0.238, p = 0.013) and between transformational leadership and company performance (? = 0.297, p = 0.002). These findings suggest that organizational culture and transformational leadership were indirectly associated with company performance through employee job satisfaction, highlighting its importance as a mediating mechanism. The study concluded that improving employee job satisfaction could support organizational performance enhancement. Accordingly, construction company managers should prioritize employee recognition, equitable compensation practices, and supportive supervisor–employee relationships to foster job satisfaction and improve overall company performance.

title: A Geospatial Intelligence System for Land Price Modelling and Property Management: An Offline/Online Android Application for Nyamata Sector, Rwanda
source: East African Journal of Information Technology
summary: Property valuation and management in Rwanda face challenges such as fragmented data, manual valuation methods, inconsistent pricing, and limited use of geospatial technologies, leading to inaccurate valuations and inefficient land administr
content: Property valuation and management in Rwanda face challenges such as fragmented data, manual valuation methods, inconsistent pricing, and limited use of geospatial technologies, leading to inaccurate valuations and inefficient land administration. To address these challenges, this study developed a Geospatial Intelligence System integrating GIS, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and an Android offline/online application for property management and land price modelling in Nyamata Sector, Bugesera District. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study integrated spatial and non-spatial data from cadastral records, satellite imagery, valuation databases, socio-economic datasets, and GPS/GNSS field surveys. Data were collected through satellite imagery, field observations, questionnaires, interviews, and institutional records. A purposive sample of 105 stakeholders, including land officers, valuers, GIS specialists, planners, regulators, telecom professionals, and property owners, participated in the study. Advanced analytical tools such as ArcGIS, QGIS, Python, Multiple Linear Regression, Geographically Weighted Regression, Random Forest, Neural Networks, and XGBoost were used for analysis. The results showed successful integration of over 85% of datasets, with more than 90% of land parcels linked to thematic information. The AI-based valuation model demonstrated excellent predictive performance (R²=0.985; RMSE=222,921 RWF) and achieved over 90% agreement between predicted and actual market values, with an overall spatial accuracy of 93.8%. Accessibility, digital infrastructure, environmental quality, and neighbourhood conditions were identified as the main factors influencing land values. The Android application effectively supported automated valuation, parcel identification, GIS mapping, and decision-making. The study concludes that geospatial intelligence significantly improves valuation accuracy, transparency, and efficiency in property management. It recommends nationwide adoption of GIS- and AI-based valuation systems, enhanced geospatial data sharing, and integration of real-time market data, drone imagery, and advanced AI models to strengthen sustainable land governance in Rwanda.

title: The carbon stable isotope canopy effect extends beyond the edges of temperate forest
summary: The canopy effect—the relative depletion of 13 C isotope in plants under closed canopies—is a phenomenon used for interpreting stable isotope data in ecological and palaeoecological studies of herbivore foraging behavior. However, the horiz
content: The canopy effect—the relative depletion of 13 C isotope in plants under closed canopies—is a phenomenon used for interpreting stable isotope data in ecological and palaeoecological studies of herbivore foraging behavior. However, the horizontal extent of this effect near forest boundaries or within forest clearings is still poorly understood, in particular in high-latitude ecosystems. We investigated the distribution of the canopy effect across a gradient from dense forest to open areas in and around the Białowieża Primeval Forest (Eastern Europe) through analysis of δ 13 C values in 10 plant species commonly foraged by large herbivores. Our results demonstrate a significant canopy effect of around 3.7‰ VPDB in the Białowieża Forest. We found that the canopy effect is not confined to the dense forest, but it extends beyond forest edges, significantly affecting plants within approximately 200 m of dense forest.The mechanism beyond is likely the lateral dispersal of 13 C-depleted CO₂ from the forest. To quantify this phenomenon, we propose the parameter “Canopy Impact Distance”, representing the zone around dense canopies where the canopy effect remains measurable. These findings have implications for interpreting isotopic data from herbivores. Low δ 13 C values in herbivore tissues may reflect foraging in dense forests, as well as in forest-adjacent contexts, such as ecotones or near forest edges. This observation challenges simplified forest-versus-grassland models in palaeoecology.

title: Heterogeneous Farmer Education, Technology Gaps, and Technical Efficiency in Ghana
summary: Education is widely viewed as a driver of agricultural productivity, yet its association with technology gaps and farming efficiency remains ambiguous. Ghana provides a revealing case, where major educational reforms have coincided with per
content: Education is widely viewed as a driver of agricultural productivity, yet its association with technology gaps and farming efficiency remains ambiguous. Ghana provides a revealing case, where major educational reforms have coincided with persistent yield gaps. Using nationally representative data from 19,862 households in the sixth and seventh rounds of the Ghana Living Standards Survey, we apply a stochastic metafrontier framework combined with Euclidean distance matching to assess how farmer education is associated with estimated technology gaps (TGRs) and technical efficiency. Our results show that farmer education is associated with higher managerial capacity and larger estimated TGRs. Educated farmers record higher technical efficiency (0.799 vs. 0.606 for uneducated peers), but they also face a 10% points estimated technology gap. When disaggregated, receiving some formal education and training, being literate and numerate and current school enrolment are all associated with significant efficiency gains. Other education measures are either not statistically significant or are negatively associated with efficiency, underscoring the heterogeneous relationship between education and farm performance. These findings point to the possible value of combining education with measures that ease potential technological constraints. Sector‐specific training and targeted incentives may be relevant to technological endowment and sustained productivity growth.

title: BADF-Net: a boundary-aware dynamic fusion network for robust multi-anatomical structure segmentation in abdominal ultrasound
summary: Introduction Automated segmentation of multiple anatomical structures in abdominal ultrasound could enhance clinical decision–making by providing consistent quantitative measurements for disease monitoring. However, ultrasound–specific arti
content: Introduction Automated segmentation of multiple anatomical structures in abdominal ultrasound could enhance clinical decision–making by providing consistent quantitative measurements for disease monitoring. However, ultrasound–specific artifacts including speckle noise, low contrast and weak boundaries challenge existing deep learning models. Materials and methods We propose BADF-Net, an architecture that integrates a Boundary-Aware Dynamic Attention (BADA) module with Boundary Confidence Estimation (BCE) at every stage of a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) recalibrated ResNet-34 encoder, a Cross-Scale Boundary Fusion (CSBF) module that adaptively combines multi-scale boundary cues into a shared guidance feature and a boundary-guided decoder with attention-gated skip fusion, to improve boundary localization and tissue discrimination. Results On a multi-anatomical kidney and spleen ultrasound dataset, BADF-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.8174, Pixel Accuracy of 0.9703 and Mean Pixel Accuracy of 0.8521, outperforming 11 baselines with the lowest HD95 (11.49), and showing the largest gains in low-contrast structures such as kidney cortex and medulla. Agreement with expert radiologist annotations was strongest for well-defined structures such as the spleen (0.9786). By reducing operator dependency and inter-observer variability, BADF-Net can serve as a reliable second-reader tool in high-volume clinical workflows, processing images in 0.016 seconds for real-time integration. Discussion Our approach demonstrates how dynamic boundary attention, confidence-weighted feature refinement and channel recalibration jointly address key ultrasound segmentation challenges with direct clinical applicability. The complete experiment code is publicly available at our GitHub repository: https://github.com/rashed200613/BADF-Net .

title: ANÁLISE DE VIABILIDADE ECONÔMICA E OPERACIONAL DE UMA PLATAFORMA CULTURAL COM ÊNFASE NA PROTEÇÃO DOS DIREITOS DO AUTOR
summary: A valorização da arte e da criatividade depende da proteção efetiva das obras e dos direitos autorais. Diante dos desafios enfrentados por artistas para proteger e comercializar suas criações, o modelo de negócio “Criativo Seguro” foi desen
content: A valorização da arte e da criatividade depende da proteção efetiva das obras e dos direitos autorais. Diante dos desafios enfrentados por artistas para proteger e comercializar suas criações, o modelo de negócio “Criativo Seguro” foi desenvolvido como uma solução integrada. Voltado para artistas locais, ele propõe um ecossistema seguro e transparente para valorização, proteção e comercialização de obras, desenvolvido com base nas pesquisas e análises de demanda por parte de possíveis usuários do empreendimento. Este relatório técnico tem como objetivo fornecer uma análise detalhada do processo de desenvolvimento do modelo, incluindo a utilização de ferramentas de análise, a metodologia aplicada, as referências bibliográficas consultadas, as análises e pesquisas realizadas, e a conclusão sobre a viabilidade do projeto. A abordagem metodológica deste relatório foi dividida por etapas: mapeamento sistemático da temática, busca de anterioridade com base bibliográfica sólida, desenvolvimento das etapas do modelo de negócios com base na ferramenta gerencial Business Model Canvas e aplicação de método para validação da viabilidade. Esta proposta visa atender a uma demanda crescente entre artistas independentes por uma solução eficaz e transparente para a proteção de suas obras e a geração de receita.

title: SUSTAINABLE PROJECT PORTFOLIO SELECTION USING AN INTEGRATED QFD–FANP–DEA APPROACH: A PUBLIC UTILITY CASE
source: International Journal of the Analytic Hierarchy Process
summary: In today’s dynamic and uncertain environments, selecting an optimal portfolio from among available projects has become one of the fundamental challenges of project management. Organizations face financial, time, and human resource constrain
content: In today’s dynamic and uncertain environments, selecting an optimal portfolio from among available projects has become one of the fundamental challenges of project management. Organizations face financial, time, and human resource constraints and are therefore required to select, from multiple projects, a combination that provides the highest return and alignment with the organization’s strategic objectives, while also adhering to the principles of sustainable development. In many cases, the complexity of this process arises from interdependencies among projects, the diversity of evaluation criteria, and the presence of uncertainty in human judgments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid model based on Quality Function Deployment (QFD), Fuzzy Analytic Network Process (FANP), Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) and integrates project interactions to support final portfolio formation. The proposed model translates the qualitative and strategic needs of the organization into quantitative indicators and enables fuzzy weighting of decision-making criteria as well as the assessment of the relative efficiency of projects. The results obtained from applying the proposed model to a set of real-world projects indicate that the model demonstrates strong capability to distinguish between efficient and inefficient projects and is able to reflect the effects of sustainability criteria and their interrelationships. Furthermore, the findings show that the integration of QFD–FANP–DEA can provide a coherent and robust representation of project performance and can be effectively used to support decision-making in the selection of sustainable projects in the water and wastewater sector.

title: Integrated reporting and financial reporting quality: Evidence from JSE Top 40.
source: International Journal of Advanced Business Studies
summary: In line with stakeholder and legitimacy theories, the integrated reporting framework enables firms to communicate both financial and non-financial information coherently to stakeholders to improve transparency and information quality about
content: In line with stakeholder and legitimacy theories, the integrated reporting framework enables firms to communicate both financial and non-financial information coherently to stakeholders to improve transparency and information quality about a firm’s value creation process. However, in countries such as South Africa, where integrated reporting (IR) has become a standard reporting practice, some companies treat it as a compliance-driven institutional exercise, or as a means of maintaining legitimacy, rather than as an opportunity for embedding the principles of integrated thinking into business operations. This raises concerns about the effectiveness of IR in fulfilling its objective of providing useful and transparent information to stakeholders. This paper investigates the effect of IR on the financial reporting quality (FRQ) of JSE-listed firms after the adoption of King Report IV, which represents a substantial regulatory shift in South Africa. Accruals-based earnings management and real earnings management were employed as proxies for financial reporting quality. Using a sample of 200 observations drawn from the top 40 JSE-listed companies, the study found that IR may assist in reducing accruals-based earnings management. However, it may not assist in limiting operations-driven earnings management. These findings suggest that additional governance mechanisms are needed to enhance financial reporting quality, and have practical implications for regulators, standard setters and investors.

title: Applicable Law in Cross-Border Insurance Contracts and Environmental Liability Insurance in the EU
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
summary: Insurance contracts constitute a special category of contracts in private law due to their function in the transfer and management of risk, as well as due to the combination of elements of private law with public regulation of the insurance
content: Insurance contracts constitute a special category of contracts in private law due to their function in the transfer and management of risk, as well as due to the combination of elements of private law with public regulation of the insurance market. Within the framework of the internal market of the European Union, the development of cross-border insurance has increasingly stimulated the need to clearly determine the law applicable to insurance contracts. Although these contracts are based on the principle of the autonomy of the parties' will, the particularities of the insurance sector and the need to protect the insured have led to the creation of a special regime for determining the law applicable in this area. Using a doctrinal legal method based on the analysis of EU legislation, CJEU case law and legal scholarship, this paper analyses the legal nature of the insurance contract and the determination of the law applicable to cross-border insurance contracts under Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 593/2008 (Rome I). It then examines environmental liability insurance, which relates to complex and often long-term risks arising from environmental damage and the application of the "polluter pays" principle under Directive 2004/35/EC. The paper finds that Article 7 of Rome I allocates, rather than harmonises, the applicable law, leaving national divergences intact, and that this fragmentation is most acute in environmental liability insurance, where the cover may be governed by a different law from the liability it secures. In this context, the paper contributes to the existing literature by showing that environmental liability insurance is a field where insurance law, environmental law and the rules on the law applicable to cross-border insurance contracts are particularly intertwined. title: O'zbekistonning yashil iqtisodiyotga o'tishida moliyaviy samaradorlikni oshirish yo'llari
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Annotatsiya. Mazkur maqolada O'zbekiston Respublikasining yashil iqtisodiyotga o'tish jarayonida moliyaviy samaradorlikni oshirishning nazariy asoslari, amaliy mexanizmlari va istiqbolli yo'llari tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotda 2019–2030-yillar
content: Annotatsiya. Mazkur maqolada O'zbekiston Respublikasining yashil iqtisodiyotga o'tish jarayonida moliyaviy samaradorlikni oshirishning nazariy asoslari, amaliy mexanizmlari va istiqbolli yo'llari tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotda 2019–2030-yillarga mo'ljallangan "Yashil" iqtisodiyotga o'tish strategiyasi, keyingi yillarda qabul qilingan normativ-huquqiy hujjatlar, xalqaro moliyaviy institutlar ishtiroki hamda yashil moliyalashtirish instrumentlarining roli o'rganilgan. Natijalar shuni ko'rsatadiki, yashil iqtisodiyotga o'tishda moliyaviy samaradorlikni oshirish uchun yashil obligatsiyalar, davlat-xususiy sheriklik, yashil taksonomiya, xalqaro investitsiyalarni jalb etish va davlat mablag'larini qayta yo'naltirish mexanizmlarini rivojlantirish muhim ahamiyat kasb etadi. Аннотация. В статье анализируются теоретические основы, практические механизмы и перспективные пути повышения финансовой эффективности в процессе перехода Республики Узбекистан к зеленой экономике. Исследование опирается на Стратегию перехода к «зеленой» экономике на 2019–2030 годы, последующие нормативно-правовые акты, участие международных финансовых институтов и роль инструментов зеленого финансирования. Результаты показывают, что для повышения финансовой эффективности необходимы развитие зеленых облигаций, государственно-частного партнерства, зеленой таксономии, привлечение международных инвестиций и переориентация государственных средств. Abstract. This article analyzes the theoretical foundations, practical mechanisms and promising ways to increase financial efficiency in the process of Uzbekistan's transition to a green economy. The study examines the Strategy for the Transition to a Green Economy for 2019–2030, subsequent regulatory acts, the participation of international financial institutions and the role of green financing instruments. The results indicate that increasing financial efficiency requires the development of green bonds, public-private partnerships, green taxonomy, attraction of international investments and reorientation of public funds.

title: Is agricultural globalisation slowing? Evidence from four decades of global trade networks
summary: Economists and institutions have warned that the world may be entering a phase of deglobalization, characterised by weakening trade interdependence, slower economic growth, trade wars, protectionism and nationalism. Global agricultural trad
content: Economists and institutions have warned that the world may be entering a phase of deglobalization, characterised by weakening trade interdependence, slower economic growth, trade wars, protectionism and nationalism. Global agricultural trade flows may be affected through long-term structural changes in food, feed and biofuel supply chains, potentially prompting strategic realignment of trading networks in response to concerns about food sovereignty and security. Short-term shifts in trading networks may alter the long-term strength, composition and structure of agricultural globalization. Here, we assess whether agricultural trade globalization remains resilient and analyse changes in globalization patterns from 1986 to 2023 using international trade and ancillary data. At a global level, we find a continuing, but slowing long-term trend toward agricultural globalization. Early signs of deglobalization are emerging behind global totals, including increasing on- and near-shoring of crop production, rising trade within free trade zones, and growing concentration between a few trading partners for specific crops. We show that recessions, currency changes and high production costs coincide with short-term shifts (<5yrs) in trade flows, and may have contributed to long-term structural changes (>10yrs). Given current economic uncertainties, a prolonged recession—compounded by persistent supply-demand imbalances and price volatility—could tip the global food system into a period of deglobalization, reshaping food systems and undermining long-term food security.

title: SDG ADHERENCE IN BRAZILIAN MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES: A THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK LINKING PERCEIVED RESPONSIBILITY, COMPETITIVENESS AND MARKET PERFORMANCE
summary: A pesquisa sobre o engajamento empresarial com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) apoia-se, em grande parte, em evidências de empresas grandes o bastante para publicar relatórios de sustentabilidade, condição amostral que dei
content: A pesquisa sobre o engajamento empresarial com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) apoia-se, em grande parte, em evidências de empresas grandes o bastante para publicar relatórios de sustentabilidade, condição amostral que deixa de fora as micro e pequenas empresas (MPEs), ainda que elas representem a maior parte das empresas ativas no Brasil. Este artigo conceitual pergunta por quais mecanismos a aderência aos ODS pode se relacionar com responsabilidade percebida, competitividade e desempenho de mercado em MPEs brasileiras e sob quais condições essa relação deve se sustentar. Adotando um desenho de síntese teórica (Jaakkola, 2020), o texto articula a teoria dos stakeholders (Freeman, 1984; Parmar et al., 2010), a visão baseada em recursos e sua extensão aos recursos naturais (Barney, 1991; Hart, 1995) e a teoria institucional (DiMaggio; Powell, 1983; Scott, 2014) a estudos empíricos sobre relato de ODS, práticas de sustentabilidade em pequenas empresas e relação entre responsabilidade social corporativa e desempenho. Daí resultam cinco proposições, segundo as quais a prática orientada aos ODS funciona como recurso cujo valor depende da integração às rotinas centrais, do canal institucional de adoção, da percepção pelos stakeholders diretos, da inserção local da empresa e da visibilidade ambiental do setor. Em seguida, o artigo especifica um protocolo misto sequencial explanatório para testar o modelo, com amostragem intencional estratificada de proprietários-gestores, sequência de desenvolvimento de escala, modelagem de equações estruturais por mínimos quadrados parciais no SmartPLS 4 e análise de conteúdo dirigida no MAXQDA. A contribuição está em deslocar o desfecho de interesse do compromisso divulgado para a responsabilidade percebida pelos stakeholders da empresa, o que torna a questão respondível para empresas que não publicam relatórios. As proposições ainda não foram testadas, e a heterogeneidade das MPEs restringe o alcance de qualquer estudo isolado.

title: Urban green space and its co-evolution with socio-economic development in 10,511 global cities
summary: Urban development is increasingly expected to be both green and equitable. Yet urban green space (UGS), a central component of urban greenness, is rarely assessed as a multidimensional spatial structure or examined through its co-evolution
content: Urban development is increasingly expected to be both green and equitable. Yet urban green space (UGS), a central component of urban greenness, is rarely assessed as a multidimensional spatial structure or examined through its co-evolution with socio-economic development. Using 10,511 cities from the GHS-UCDB, we construct a multidimensional UGS index from 30-m land-cover data, use nighttime light intensity as socio-economic proxy, and analyse cities’ co-evolutionary positions, green-prioritized rankings, transition pathways and structural correlates. We find persistent inequalities between North America/Europe and Africa/parts of Asia. Q1 cities with above-average relative greenness and socio-economic development generally dominated the green-prioritised ranking, but this status did not guarantee balanced co-evolution with nearly one-third of Q1 cities fell outside the top quartile. Factors associated with co-evolutionary position do not necessarily move cities toward more balanced green–socioeconomic development with clear regionality. These findings call for region-specific strategies to align greenness with socio-economic development.

title: Digital Platforms and Retail Participation in Climate Finance: Evidence from the Indian FinTech Ecosystem
summary: In India, the Net Zero will be implemented by mobilising the private capital particularly the emerging retail industry. Although institutional climate finance is a well-studied issue, the contribution of digital FinTech to the democratizati
content: In India, the Net Zero will be implemented by mobilising the private capital particularly the emerging retail industry. Although institutional climate finance is a well-studied issue, the contribution of digital FinTech to the democratization of sustainable investments is not a theme that has been studied in detail within the developing economies, including India. The other variables, which will be discussed in the paper, are the ones that determine the role of retail investors in climate finance via digital investment platforms, and the mediation of investment behaviour by the platform adoption and the age of the investor. The research design that was employed to investigate 450 retail investors in the metropolitan regions of India that are important was the quantitative research design and structured questionnaire. The theoretical model incorporates the incorporation of Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) of the variables Digital Financial Literacy, Perceived Transparency and Trust and the statistical data were modeled in Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) on the SmartPLS. The findings indicate that Digital Financial Literacy and Perceived Transparency are the most relevant predictors of trust in the platform and subsequent adoption. The perceived Ease of Use can be an early adopting factor, whereas Trust is the actual financial adopting factor of climate-consistent assets, including green bonds and ESG funds. Moreover, the age is also a mediator between the platform adoption and climate investment participation since the Generation Z is more pro-environmental and less capitalized than other generations. The research design is the quantitative and explanatory research design. The structured questionnaire was used to gather the data on the 5-point Likert scale (1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree). Convenience sampling technique was used to sample the 450 big cities in India with retail investors. The available literature assisted in revising the constructs in order to be valid. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was applied to analyze the data with the help of SmartPLS. Cronbachs alpha, composite reliability, and average variance extracted (AVE) were used to measure reliability and validity.The paper concludes that FinTech platforms can bridge the climate financing gap, and advises providers to concentrate on how they can best report their effect and open participants to educational nudges are the most effective methods of boosting participation. These conclusions can provide viable recommendations to policymakers and developers of FinTech in an attempt to ensure that the retail wealth is geared towards the sustainability objectives of the entire India.

title: State of nature conservation of mangroves in Malaysia
summary: Malaysia’s mangroves are ecologically rich and socioeconomically vital coastal ecosystems, not only supporting biodiversity, but also fisheries, shoreline protection, and climate regulation. This chapter reassesses their status since 1991,
content: Malaysia’s mangroves are ecologically rich and socioeconomically vital coastal ecosystems, not only supporting biodiversity, but also fisheries, shoreline protection, and climate regulation. This chapter reassesses their status since 1991, highlighting improved knowledge, expanded protection, and increased recognition of ecosystem services, including the now “popular” blue carbon. Despite restoration progress, mangroves continue to decline due to multiple anthropogenic threats, including urbanisation, agriculture and aquaculture expansion, pollution, and climate change, with recent losses outpacing gains from restoration. Current challenges include inconsistent mapping, and ineffective restoration practices and governance. Moving forward, integrated management, ecosystem-based restoration, community stewardship, and coherent national policies are essential to ensure resilient, biodiversity-rich and most importantly, functional mangrove ecosystems for Malaysia’s sustainable future.

title: Perceived campus restorative environment and study engagement among Chinese college students: the mediating role of attention restoration and the moderating role of environmental sensitivity
summary: Introduction University students spend most of their waking hours on campus, yet the role of the campus environment in sustaining the attentional resources behind study engagement remains understudied. Drawing on attention restoration theor
content: Introduction University students spend most of their waking hours on campus, yet the role of the campus environment in sustaining the attentional resources behind study engagement remains understudied. Drawing on attention restoration theory and the environmental sensitivity framework, this study tested whether attention restoration mediates the association between perceived campus restorative environment and study engagement, and whether environmental sensitivity moderates the first stage of this indirect path. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 560 college students from four universities in Henan Province, China, measuring perceived campus restorativeness, attention restoration, study engagement, and environmental sensitivity. A first-stage moderated mediation model corresponding to PROCESS Model 7 was estimated with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. Results Perceived campus restorative environment was positively associated with study engagement (total effect b = 0.436). Attention restoration partially accounted for this association (indirect effect at the mean of the moderator = 0.165, 95% CI [0.122, 0.216]). Environmental sensitivity moderated the path from perceived restorativeness to attention restoration (interaction b = 0.277, p < 0.001): the indirect effect was 0.108, 0.165, and 0.222 at low (−1 SD), mean, and high (+1 SD) sensitivity, and the index of moderated mediation was 0.096 (95% CI [0.053, 0.148]). The Johnson-Neyman region of significance for the conditional indirect effect covered 97.9% of the sample. Discussion Perceived campus restorativeness is associated with study engagement partly through attention restoration, and students high in environmental sensitivity draw the largest attentional benefit from restorative campus settings. Because the design is cross-sectional, these findings identify associations rather than causal effects. They connect attention restoration theory to engagement research and suggest campus environmental quality as a candidate antecedent of study engagement.

title: Искусственный интеллект и машинное обучение в исследованиях экономического роста и развития: библиометрическое картирование
source: The Journal of Economic Research & Business Administration
summary: The rapid development of research in the field of artificial intelligence underscores the need for a systematic organization of knowledge regarding its relationship with economic growth and development. This study aims to describe the publi
content: The rapid development of research in the field of artificial intelligence underscores the need for a systematic organization of knowledge regarding its relationship with economic growth and development. This study aims to describe the publication dynamics, geographical distribution, thematic structure, and temporal characteristics of academic work in this field. The scope of the research encompasses international publications focused on artificial intelligence, economic growth, development, and productivity. The empirical basis consists of 3,192 English-language articles and reviews indexed in the Scopus database between 1987 and 2025. Using VOSviewer software, a bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping were conducted based on the co-occurrence of author-provided keywords. By segmenting the keywords - using a threshold of 10 occurrences - a network of 133 keywords was created, and organized into 8 thematic clusters. The research findings indicate that publication activity was concentrated primarily toward the end of the period under study, with 71.6% of the articles in the sample published in period between 2023 and 2025. The most prominent research originated from China, the United States, India, and the United Kingdom. The topics addressed in the research include areas such as productivity and innovation, digitalization and "green" transformation, forecasting, decision support, and applied analytics. Publications on subjects such as generative artificial intelligence, explainable machine learning, inclusive finance, and the energy transition have emerged relatively recently. This study contributes to the field by analyzing the research landscape and distinguishing between artificial intelligence as a driver of economic change and as a tool for analyzing processes of change. The study concludes that while the rise in publication activity reflects growing academic interest, this does not, in itself, demonstrate a positive impact of artificial intelligence on overall economic growth.These findings help refine future research directions and highlight the limitations of using bibliometric indicators to guide economic policy. Key words: artificial intelligence, economic growth, economic development, productivity, bibliometric analysis, thematic mapping, machine learning.

title: Phosphatidic acid phosphatase PAP2-2 controls lipid metabolism and membrane homeostasis in Leishmania mexicana
summary: Phosphatidic acid phosphatases (PAPs) regulate lipid metabolism by controlling the interconversion of phosphatidic acid (PA) and diacylglycerol (DAG), thereby influencing membrane composition and multiple downstream cellular processes. We i
content: Phosphatidic acid phosphatases (PAPs) regulate lipid metabolism by controlling the interconversion of phosphatidic acid (PA) and diacylglycerol (DAG), thereby influencing membrane composition and multiple downstream cellular processes. We investigated the role of PAP2-2 in Leishmania mexicana using CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene ablation and genetic complementation. Immunofluorescence analyses revealed partial co-localization of PAP2-2 with the endoplasmic reticulum. Ablation of the PAP2-2-encoding gene LmxM.19.1350 significantly reduced total phosphatidic acid phosphatase activity, resulting in marked accumulation of endogenous PA and alterations in lipid composition, including changes in phosphatidylcholine, cardiolipin, sterols, and selected DAG species. PAP2-2-deficient parasites displayed altered cell morphology, reduced growth, and delayed differentiation into metacyclic promastigotes and amastigotes. Furthermore, loss of PAP2-2 impaired mitochondrial physiology, as evidenced by reduced basal respiration, diminished oxidative phosphorylation capacity, altered electron transport chain activities, and decreased responsiveness to respiratory substrates and inhibitors. Our findings identify PAP2-2 as an important regulator of PA/DAG homeostasis in L. mexicana and demonstrate that disruption of this enzyme triggers extensive lipid remodeling with downstream effects on mitochondrial function, parasite development, and cellular morphology. These results highlight the central role of membrane lipid homeostasis in the physiology of Leishmania and establish PAP2-2 as a previously underappreciated determinant of parasite fitness that may represent a promising target for future mechanistic and therapeutic investigations.
