title: Misinformation and organizational capacity in extension and advisory services: building resilience in the age of artificial intelligence
summary: Extension and Advisory Services (EAS) play a critical role in connecting research, policy, and practice to support millions of farmers worldwide. However, the increasing complexity of information systems and the emergence of powerful digita
content: Extension and Advisory Services (EAS) play a critical role in connecting research, policy, and practice to support millions of farmers worldwide. However, the increasing complexity of information systems and the emergence of powerful digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) have introduced both opportunities and challenges for these organizations. EAS institutions, already constrained by limited budgets and workforce shortages, are under pressure to integrate digital tools while maintaining trust, accuracy, and inclusivity in information dissemination. Historically, EAS organizations have adapted to successive waves of technological change, from the introduction of mobile phones and ICT-based platforms to the widespread use of social media for agricultural communication. Each transformation has required not only technical adaptation but also organizational learning, communication restructuring, and capacity development—both within EAS and among their primary clients, the farmers. The integration of AI technologies presents a new and more complex frontier. While AI can enhance decision support, automate communication, and strengthen data management, it also amplifies risks related to misinformation, data bias, ethical use, and erosion of human-centric extension principles. This perspective paper proposes to examine how misinformation management intersects with the organizational capacity and resilience of EAS systems in the context of rapid technological change. It will explore how EAS organizations can build institutional readiness to detect, counter, and manage misinformation while maintaining trust and credibility in high-stakes decision-making environments. The discussion will draw from communication and resilience theories to highlight pathways for strengthening adaptive capacity—integrating human, technological, and organizational dimensions—to ensure accurate information flows within increasingly digital agri-food systems.

title: Edukasi dan Praktik Pertolongan Pertama Cedera Olahraga Ringan pada Siswa SMA Islam Shafta Surabaya
summary: Cedera olahraga ringan di sekolah memerlukan pertolongan awal yang aman dan sesuai kemampuan penolong. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan membekali siswa dengan pengetahuan dan pengalaman praktik pertolongan pertama serta mengidentifikasi ke
content: Cedera olahraga ringan di sekolah memerlukan pertolongan awal yang aman dan sesuai kemampuan penolong. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan membekali siswa dengan pengetahuan dan pengalaman praktik pertolongan pertama serta mengidentifikasi kebutuhan penguatan materi. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 16 Oktober 2026 bersama 40 siswa kelas X SMA Islam Shafta Surabaya melalui edukasi, demonstrasi, praktik kelompok dengan pendampingan dosen, dan materi buku saku. Setiap sesi berlangsung 30 menit. Evaluasi menggunakan pre-test dan post-test berbeda, masing-masing 10 soal dengan bobot 1 poin per jawaban benar, kemudian dikonversi ke skala 0–100. Dari 33 formulir pada setiap pengukuran, diperoleh 26 pasangan individual setelah audit identitas dan penskoran. Rerata pre-test sebesar 87,69±13,66 dan post-test 90,38±12,16, dengan selisih rerata 2,69 poin. Uji Wilcoxon eksploratif tidak menunjukkan perbedaan bermakna (p=0,562). Hanya 46,2% siswa menjawab benar tindakan yang harus dihindari pada keseleo. Kegiatan menyediakan kesempatan praktik dan memetakan kebutuhan pembelajaran, tetapi perbedaan paket tes membatasi interpretasi perubahan skor. Latihan ulang terarah, instrumen yang setara, dan penilaian keterampilan langsung diperlukan. Edukasi kesehatan, pembelajaran praktis, dan kemitraan perguruan tinggi dengan sekolah selaras dengan SDGs 3, 4, dan 17

title: Electrosprayed OSA-starch microparticles for blackberry extract stabilization: structural characterization, antioxidant potential, and cytocompatibility
summary: The objective of this study was to evaluate the preservation and functionality of blackberry ( Rubus sp.) extract through the production of octenyl succinic anhydride-modified starch (OSA-starch)-based microparticles containing 10, 15, and
content: The objective of this study was to evaluate the preservation and functionality of blackberry ( Rubus sp.) extract through the production of octenyl succinic anhydride-modified starch (OSA-starch)-based microparticles containing 10, 15, and 20% extract. The free extract was phytochemically characterized, and the microparticles were evaluated regarding morphology, encapsulation efficiency, functional groups (FTIR), antioxidant activity, and cytotoxicity in healthy cells. Particles with a biconcave morphology were obtained, with mean diameters ranging from 1.01 to 1.11 μm, and no significant morphological differences were observed with increasing extract concentration. Encapsulation efficiency ranged from approximately 67 to 74%, indicating effective retention of the extract within the polymeric matrix. FTIR analysis confirmed molecular interactions, particularly hydrogen bonding, between the extract and OSA-starch. The encapsulation system demonstrated effective protection of bioactive compounds, providing a sustained time-dependent antioxidant response for 72 h. Additionally, no cytotoxic effects in L929 fibroblast cells were observed, confirming the cytocompatibility of the developed system. Overall, these results demonstrate that OSA-starch microparticles produced by electrospraying represent a promising strategy for preserving phenolic-rich extracts, with potential applications in food and biomedical systems.

title: Green Innovation Capabilities and Sustainable SME Performance: An Integrative Literature Review
source: Journal of Economic and Business Advancement
summary: This integrative literature review asks how external pressures and organizational capabilities combine to support green innovation and multidimensional sustainable performance in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). A transparent audi
content: This integrative literature review asks how external pressures and organizational capabilities combine to support green innovation and multidimensional sustainable performance in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). A transparent audit of the manuscript bibliography identified 62 cited entries; removing two duplicates and separating three institutional reports yielded 57 distinct scholarly sources for citation-based thematic synthesis, with recent evidence emphasized and seminal theory retained. The analysis compares external drivers, capability formation, product and process innovation, environmental and economic outcomes, digital complementarity, and contextual constraints. Across the reviewed evidence, stakeholder pressure and regulation are more likely to stimulate innovation when knowledge management, absorptive capacity, leadership, and green dynamic capabilities support implementation. Environmental gains are more consistent than short-term financial returns; firm size, financing, readiness, industry, and commercialization shape the variation. Digitalization and artificial intelligence are treated as conditional enabling capabilities, not automatic performance drivers. Drawing primarily on dynamic capability theory, the review proposes a six-stage green capability cycle that connects sensing, mobilization, innovation, measurement, learning, and resource reconfiguration. The cycle is a literature-informed conceptual proposition requiring longitudinal validation, not an empirically tested causal model.

title: IMPACT OF GREEN FINTECH ON INVESTMENT BEHAVIOUR OF WORKING WOMEN
summary: The three main criteria for this issue are Trust (TRST), Ease of Use (EOU), and Environmental Concern (ENV). The article explores the effect of Green FinTech on the investment attitude of working women in Bengaluru. A structured questionnai
content: The three main criteria for this issue are Trust (TRST), Ease of Use (EOU), and Environmental Concern (ENV). The article explores the effect of Green FinTech on the investment attitude of working women in Bengaluru. A structured questionnaire was used to collect data from 430 responses, using multiple regression analysis of the results of the five-point Likert scale adopted. The results show that all three factors are significant and positive drivers of this investment decision, with environmental concerns being the strongest. The model accounted for an explanatory power of R²= 0.947 – the variance in investment behaviour could be explained by the model’s variables at 94.7 per cent. These findings illustrate the growing relevance of sustainable digital finance and the impression that, upon adding (sustainable) measures of environmental responsibility, user-friendliness and safe systems, FinTech platforms have a higher potential to reach and retain female investors. Drawing on the research, this paper introduces a series of financial policies (the financial solutions) meant to boost inclusive and sustainable investing and address the lack of awareness of Green FinTech.

title: Infrastructure Delivery Delays and Regional Economic Performance: Evidence from U.S. Transportation Investment Projects
source: International Journal of Science and Engineering Applications
summary: Infrastructure investment supports economic productivity, regional connectivity, and long-term development by improving the movement of people, goods, and services.However, delays in transportation project delivery can increase construction
content: Infrastructure investment supports economic productivity, regional connectivity, and long-term development by improving the movement of people, goods, and services.However, delays in transportation project delivery can increase construction costs, postpone anticipated benefits, and constrain economic activity across affected communities.This study examines the relationship between infrastructure delivery delays and regional economic performance in the United States, focusing on highway, bridge, rail, and public transit investment projects.It proposes an analytical framework linking project completion schedules, cost overruns, funding constraints, procurement challenges, and regulatory processes with employment growth, business activity, productivity, and regional investment.Using secondary data from federal transportation agencies, state infrastructure records, and regional economic databases, the study proposes panel regression, spatial analysis, and comparative project evaluation to investigate variations across states and metropolitan areas.Particular attention is given to whether delay effects differ according to project scale, regional economic conditions, and transportation network importance.The research aims to identify mechanisms through which delayed infrastructure delivery influences regional development and to inform evidence-based policies that improve project governance, investment efficiency, and the timely realization of economic benefits.

title: Construction and empirical test of an evaluation system for the high-quality development of national fitness facilities in Hunan Province
summary: Background Public fitness facilities shape opportunities for physical activity, yet evaluations of national fitness facilities in China have emphasized quantity over quality and often use poorly defined dimensions. This study developed and
content: Background Public fitness facilities shape opportunities for physical activity, yet evaluations of national fitness facilities in China have emphasized quantity over quality and often use poorly defined dimensions. This study developed and empirically tested a multidimensional evaluation system for the high-quality development of national fitness facilities in Hunan Province. Methods Candidate indicators derived from policy documents, facility standards, and the literature were screened in a two-round Delphi consultation with 15 experts using retention criteria (mean importance > 3.5 and coefficient of variation < 0.25), resulting in an indicator system based on the five development concepts of innovation, coordination, green development, openness, and sharing. Indicator weights were derived with the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) from geometric-mean group judgment matrices. Current performance was assessed by two-level fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) using 475 valid questionnaires from managers and residents in 10 cities and prefectures. Sensitivity analyses of weights (228 scenarios) and grade thresholds, along with bootstrap resampling (2,000 resamples), tested robustness. Results The final system comprised 5 first-level and 33 second-level indicators, and all AHP judgment matrices had CR < 0.10 (criterion level: CR = 0.0422). Exploratory factor analysis yielded a five-factor structure consistent with the proposed dimensions. The comprehensive evaluation vector was (0.2280, 0.3752, 0.2683, 0.1027, 0.0258), yielding an overall score of 3.6768 (95% bootstrap CI: 3.624–3.726) and a good grade. Dimension scores were 3.8085 for coordination, 3.7821 for innovation, 3.6538 for openness, 3.5278 for green development, and 3.5025 for sharing. For green development and sharing, the confidence intervals spanned the boundary between the good and moderate grades. The overall grade was unchanged in all weight scenarios but changed when the grade boundaries were increased by 0.25. Conclusion Per capita venue area, water consumption, and the opening of public and school venues were above average in importance but below average in performance and should be prioritized for verification and improvement. The framework separates expert-defined importance from stakeholder-perceived performance and documents each computational step, so that it can be checked and re-applied. Because scores reflect stakeholder perceptions in a non-probability sample, they should be validated against administrative and facility-level data before being used to allocate resources.

title: Is the Regulatory State Undergoing Organ Rejection Syndrome in Nigeria?
source: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
summary: Despite decades of reform and the adoption of regulatory frameworks modeled on international best practices, Nigeria’s regulatory state continues to grapple with persistent inefficacies, operational misalignments and public skepticism. This
content: Despite decades of reform and the adoption of regulatory frameworks modeled on international best practices, Nigeria’s regulatory state continues to grapple with persistent inefficacies, operational misalignments and public skepticism. This article explores the phenomenon of “organ rejection syndrome” in the Nigerian regulatory context, in which externally introduced institutions and policies are resisted, distorted or rendered ineffective by local political, economic and social dynamics. Drawing on case studies of two ubiquitous sectors, electric power and petroleum, set against the contrasting case of telecommunications, the paper analyzes the assimilation of the regulatory state in Nigeria, the misalignment between imported regulatory models and their baselines on the one hand and indigenous realities on the other, and the resultant challenges in implementation. The paper evaluates context-sensitive alternatives that are responsive to the political economy realities of Nigeria and makes a case for moving away from mimetic isomorphism in order to avoid this “organ rejection”, proffering an indigenous mitigating framework that seeks to minimise and ultimately eliminate discretion, and to promote transparency and a solution-based approach to the provision of public goods and services that tackles the hydra-headed menace of corruption in the infrastructure marketplace. Ultimately, the study concludes that achieving true institutional “fit” and effective governance in Nigeria demands an adaptive, low-discretion regulatory architecture grounded in local ownership, flexibility and incremental change.

title: Linking satellitome dynamics to chromosomal evolution in Streptoprocne swifts (Apodiformes: Apodidae)
summary: Bird karyotype evolution is typically conservative, although some lineages exhibit extensive chromosomal reorganization. Satellite DNA (satDNA) is a dynamic genomic component, but its role in avian karyotype evolution remains poorly explore
content: Bird karyotype evolution is typically conservative, although some lineages exhibit extensive chromosomal reorganization. Satellite DNA (satDNA) is a dynamic genomic component, but its role in avian karyotype evolution remains poorly explored. This study investigates the relationship between satellite DNA and karyotype diversification in Streptoprocne biscutata and Streptoprocne zonaris (Apodidae) using cytogenomic and Satellitome analyses. S. biscutata has 2n = 72, whereas S. zonaris has 2n = 68. The reduced chromosome number could possibly indicate predominant fusions involving macro- and microchromosomes. The Satellitome revealed six homologous satDNA families with high sequence similarity. Variation in genomic abundance and repeat landscapes indicates independent evolution after lineage divergence. Chromosomal localization revealed that satDNA expansion or contraction correlates with the number of chromosomal sites. Telomeric expansion occurred in autosomes and the W chromosome of S. zonaris, but only in the W chromosome of S. biscutata. An exclusive satDNA family of S. zonaris containing a derived telomeric motif may have originated from fusion events involving microchromosomes. These results support a model in which karyotype evolution is shaped by structural rearrangements and satellite DNA dynamics, emphasizing the role of the Satellitome in genome differentiation and speciation in Streptoprocne swifts.

title: Trust and Financial Literacy as Drivers of InsurTech Adoption for Financial Inclusion in India
summary: Insurance technology (InsurTech) is changing how consumers in emerging markets find, compare and buy insurance, yet insurance penetration in India remains low, and little is known about what drives adoption outside metropolitan centres, lim
content: Insurance technology (InsurTech) is changing how consumers in emerging markets find, compare and buy insurance, yet insurance penetration in India remains low, and little is known about what drives adoption outside metropolitan centres, limiting progress toward financial inclusion and sustainable development. This study examines how performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, perceived trust and facilitating conditions shape the intention to adopt InsurTech and its actual adoption and whether financial literacy moderates the effect of performance expectancy. It employs cross-sectional survey data from 412 insurance consumers in urban, semi-urban and rural Uttar Pradesh, analysed through reliability and validity assessment followed by structural path modelling based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology. The results show that performance expectancy has the largest effect on behavioural intention (β = 0.325, p < 0.001), followed by perceived trust (β = 0.198, p < 0.001), effort expectancy (β = 0.179, p < 0.001) and social influence (β = 0.133, p = 0.003). Financial literacy strengthens the effect of performance expectancy on intention (β = 0.135, p = 0.002). Behavioural intention (β = 0.323, p < 0.001) and facilitating conditions (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) predict actual adoption. The model explains 24.7% of the variance in intention and 16.9% in adoption. The findings suggest that expected usefulness and trust are the main drivers of the intention to use digital insurance innovation, that financial literacy shapes how far usefulness beliefs translate into intention, and that inclusive adoption depends on enabling infrastructure as well as intention. JEL Classification Codes: G22, G53, O33, D12, D91.

title: Rebuilding Wellbeing After Acquired Brain Injury: A Systems-Informed Positive Psychotherapy Approach to Neurorehabilitation
summary: This pioneering book presents a practical, evidence-based approach to supporting wellbeing in people living with brain injury. Developed through more than a decade of collaboration between researchers, clinicians, and people with lived expe
content: This pioneering book presents a practical, evidence-based approach to supporting wellbeing in people living with brain injury. Developed through more than a decade of collaboration between researchers, clinicians, and people with lived experience, the book introduces a nine-week structured, systems-informed positive psychotherapy programme designed for neurorehabilitation. Rooted in an eco-biopsychosocial framework, the group-based programme goes beyond the traditional neurorehabilitation approaches focused on alleviating symptoms and instead is crafted to enhance wellbeing through deep connections with self, others, and nature. It extends the focus beyond individuals to encompass the systems within which people are embedded. The programme introduces a sequence of themes including living with difficult emotions, identifying and using character strengths, building positive emotions, connecting to body and mind, connecting to others, connecting to nature, meaning and purpose, translating values into action, and behaviour change while managing ups and downs. The intervention is described step-by-step through a detailed clinician manual. Additional resources – including guided meditation recordings, session slides, and a participant workbook – support practitioners in delivering the programme in rehabilitation and community settings. Through insightful narratives and actionable guidance, the book equips health professionals with tools to support people living with ABI in improving their wellbeing and reconnecting with their communities and the natural environment. The book defines true wellbeing as not merely the reduction of suffering, but about building strengths, enhancing social bonds, and encouraging sustainable engagement with the environment. Offering a fresh perspective on recovery and resilience, it is a compelling resource for clinicians, psychologists, other health professionals, and trainees focused on neurorehabilitation.

title: Mapping intersectionality in forced migration research: a systematic scoping review
summary: Introduction Intersectionality is increasingly used to examine inequalities in forced migration and humanitarian settings, but its conceptualisation and methodological application remain fragmented. This review maps its use across disciplin
content: Introduction Intersectionality is increasingly used to examine inequalities in forced migration and humanitarian settings, but its conceptualisation and methodological application remain fragmented. This review maps its use across disciplines, populations, geographic contexts and humanitarian sectors. Methods We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic scoping review of 291 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2010 and the final database search on 14 July 2025. Records from Scopus, Web of Science and Ovid MEDLINE were screened, and included articles were coded for study characteristics, intersectionality framing, methods and substantive focus. Results Most studies used intersectionality primarily as a conceptual or theoretical framing (76%, n = 221); fewer applied it as an analytical or methodological tool (11%, n = 31). Research concentrated on health and well-being (41%, n = 120) and protection and rights (23%, n = 67). Quantitative and comparative approaches were uncommon, and coverage across settings, institutions and marginalised groups was uneven. Discussion The review identifies a need for more explicit methodological operationalisation, multi-level and comparative analysis, and stronger engagement with humanitarian governance, programme design and research led or co-produced in displacement-affected settings.

title: Developing an Islamic Holistic Entrepreneurship Education Framework (IHEEF): A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Entrepreneurship education plays an essential role in preparing graduates to navigate global economic challenges, digital transformation, and sustainable development. However, conventional frameworks primarily focus on economic competencies
content: Entrepreneurship education plays an essential role in preparing graduates to navigate global economic challenges, digital transformation, and sustainable development. However, conventional frameworks primarily focus on economic competencies, leaving ethical and spiritual dimensions underaddressed. Addressing this gap, this study aims to systematically synthesize current developments in Islamic entrepreneurship education to identify core research themes, pedagogical models, and key competencies. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted across three primary databases. Applying rigorous inclusion and exclusion criteria specifically targeting peer-reviewed studies explicitly addressing Islamic core values in higher education curricula yielded a focused corpus of 10 primary studies (2015–2023). Thematic synthesis revealed five dominant themes: (1) entrepreneurial competencies, (2) Islamic ethical values, (3) pedagogical innovation, (4) digital entrepreneurship, and (5) sustainability grounded in Maqaṣid al-Shariah. Synthesizing these findings, this study proposes the Islamic Holistic Entrepreneurship Education Framework (IHEEF), anchoring Tawhid and Maqaṣid al-Shariah as its foundational philosophy alongside digital capability and social impact. IHEEF provides a conceptual model for curriculum redesign and establishes a foundation for future empirical validation.

title: Mirrored Suspicion: Conspiracy, Securitization, and the Opposition to Jewish–Muslim Engagement in the United States since 9/11
summary: Since September 11, 2001, efforts to build durable relationships between American Jewish and American Muslim communities have met organized opposition from within both communities. This article argues that the opposition follows a logic of
content: Since September 11, 2001, efforts to build durable relationships between American Jewish and American Muslim communities have met organized opposition from within both communities. This article argues that the opposition follows a logic of mirrored suspicion: opponents of engagement in each community read the other’s outreach as a surface concealing hostile intent. The form that suspicion takes, however, tracks each community’s position relative to the American security state. Among American Muslims, opposition tends toward a conspiratorial register in which interfaith programs, particularly those connected to Zionist institutions, are read as covert normalization, surveillance, or co-optation. Among American Jews, opposition tends toward a securitizing register in which Muslim partners are read as fronts for Islamist networks or for a “red-green” convergence of Islamism and the radical left. Drawing on peer-reviewed research in social psychology, the sociology of religion, security studies, and digital religion, and on five episodes from 2001 to 2024, the article shows that the two registers share a narrative grammar of concealment and exposure, that both are concentrated in organizational and online arenas rather than in lay opinion, and that digital platforms reward them. It proposes symmetrical criteria for distinguishing principled dissent from suspicion and outlines a research design for testing the argument. Mirrored suspicion, the article concludes, is a structural obstacle to pluralism that neither community can dismantle alone.

title: Large-scale Nanopore sequencing resolves species diversity and distribution of European Ulva
summary: The green algal genus Ulva is widespread and ecologically important in European coastal ecosystems. However, species diversity and distributions remain poorly resolved due to phenotypic plasticity and historical taxonomic uncertainty. By ad
content: The green algal genus Ulva is widespread and ecologically important in European coastal ecosystems. However, species diversity and distributions remain poorly resolved due to phenotypic plasticity and historical taxonomic uncertainty. By adopting a large-scale sampling and barcoding effort, we provide a unique continent-scale assessment of Ulva species diversity and distribution. We developed a novel high-throughput Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing strategy, pooling 768 samples (eight 96-well plates) per run and sequencing tufA and ITS simultaneously. Nanopore barcoding was accurate and efficient, with 96.3% of samples yielding at least one informative marker. Consensus sequences showed 99.4-100% similarity to Sanger sequences. By analysing 3,657 samples from 30 countries, we identified 46 species with contrasting distribution patterns and substantially expanded their known geographic ranges. This includes numerous country-level first records and the first records of Ulva howensis outside Australia and U. meridionalis within the study area. Five non-indigenous Ulva species were also detected, including widespread occurrences of U. australis. However, 10 species could not be assigned to named taxa because suitable reference sequences were unavailable or unreliable, highlighting persistent taxonomic gaps in public databases. Our findings demonstrate the power of coordinated, high-throughput molecular surveys to resolve cryptic marine biogeography at continent scales. The resulting high-resolution spatial baseline facilitates the early detection of non-indigenous species and range expansions. It also enables coastal managers to monitor invasion pathways, evaluate ecosystem risks associated with opportunistic bloom-forming taxa, and detect climate-driven distribution shifts across European waters.

title: EU Conditionality and Regional Relations Restructuring: Evidence from Albania’s Reform Trajectory (2014–2025)
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
summary: This article addresses two gaps in the EU conditionality literature: the absence of systematic accounts of how domestic conditionality-driven reforms reshape candidate states’ bilateral and regional relations, and the absence of theoretical
content: This article addresses two gaps in the EU conditionality literature: the absence of systematic accounts of how domestic conditionality-driven reforms reshape candidate states’ bilateral and regional relations, and the absence of theoretical tools for capturing the interaction among multiple overlapping conditionality frameworks. Using Albania’s 2014–2025 trajectory as a revelatory case, the study combines systematic thematic analysis of a documentary corpus (twelve European Commission Country Reports, Council Conclusions, Berlin Process communiqués, the Growth Plan Reform Agenda, and bilateral instruments) with structured causal-process observations in the Brady and Collier (2010) tradition. Four hypotheses are tested. The findings are that judicial vetting and the Special Structure against Corruption and Organized Crime (SPAK) operated as credibility-building mechanisms with measurable regional spillover (H1); that conditionality produced asymmetric bilateral effects, reinforcing some cooperative dynamics while generating friction in others (H2); that the simultaneous operation of accession conditionality, Berlin Process commitments and the Growth Plan produced strategic compliance prioritization rather than uniform reform (H3); and that geopolitical alignment after 2022 functioned as a supplementary credibility resource (H4). The article contributes an embedded multiple conditionality framework that extends the External Incentives Model by integrating insights from the policy-layering literature, and offers the first systematic peer-reviewed study of Albania’s post-2022 accession trajectory. title: Governance of Unsafe Behavior in Electric Power Maintenance: A Three-Population Evolutionary Game with Endogenous Risk and a Conserved Quantity
summary: Maintenance crews work inside short windows on de-energized equipment, and the casualties that follow are few, severe and almost always preceded by a departure from a written procedure. Three agents decide whether that departure happens: th
content: Maintenance crews work inside short windows on de-energized equipment, and the casualties that follow are few, severe and almost always preceded by a departure from a written procedure. Three agents decide whether that departure happens: the crew, the supervisor and the utility that pays for supervision. We model the layers as a three-population evolutionary game in which accident probability is endogenous and super-linear, penalties are proportional to fault, and the supervisor has a reason to look away. A vertex criterion classifies the eight pure-strategy states, and a Latin hypercube design with partial rank correlation ranks the parameters. Three closed-form thresholds split the risk sensitivity into four regimes, with no stable pure strategy between the last two; there the flow preserves volume in logit coordinates, the compliance face admits an explicit first integral, and the equilibrium is a nonlinear center of computable period. Costlier regulation destroys the center and makes two delegated-governance states bistable. The levers are the effort a shortcut saves, regulation cost, accountability and schedule pressure, not the penalties.

title: The Role of Good Corporate Governance and Islamic Business Ethics in Strengthening Sustainable Management of Halal Culinary MSMEs in Bukittinggi
summary: This study examines how Good Corporate Governance (GCG) and Islamic business ethics can be translated into practical governance mechanisms for halal culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Bukittinggi. Rather than treating
content: This study examines how Good Corporate Governance (GCG) and Islamic business ethics can be translated into practical governance mechanisms for halal culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Bukittinggi. Rather than treating GCG as a large-corporation structure, the study reframes it as a set of proportional routines that can be embedded in daily MSME management. A qualitative descriptive library research (studi pustaka) design was applied, supported by document analysis and a focused literature review covering local MSME conditions, halal governance, GCG, Islamic business ethics, and sustainable management. Four conceptual findings emerge from the synthesis of secondary sources; these findings have not been empirically tested among halal culinary MSMEs in Bukittinggi. First, GCG becomes more relevant to MSMEs when its principles are translated into simple routines for transparency, accountability, responsibility, fairness, and independent decision-making. Second, Islamic business ethics functions as an internal moral control that gives substantive meaning to those routines through sidq, amanah, 'adl, and mas'uliyyah. Third, halal certification should be positioned as a governance capability rather than merely a product label because certification creates value only when supported by continuous control of ingredients, suppliers, processes, records, and consumer communication. Fourth, the integration of governance and ethics forms a pathway from halal integrity to stakeholder trust and sustainable business continuity. The paper contributes a context-sensitive governance framework for halal culinary MSMEs and proposes four analytical propositions for future empirical testing. The findings offer implications for MSME owners, halal facilitators, universities, business associations, and local government in strengthening post-certification governance.

title: Determinants of Onion Market Supply and Marketing Outlet Choice among Smallholder Farmers in Gode District in the Somali Regional State of Ethiopia
summary: Onion (Allium cepa L.) is an important horticultural crop in Ethiopia, contributing to smallholder income, food availability, and employment along the agricultural value chain. However, constraints in production, market information, credit
content: Onion (Allium cepa L.) is an important horticultural crop in Ethiopia, contributing to smallholder income, food availability, and employment along the agricultural value chain. However, constraints in production, market information, credit access, extension services, transportation, and market linkages limit the ability of smallholder farmers to supply markets and select suitable marketing outlets. This study examined the determinants of onion market supply and marketing outlet choice among 245 smallholder farmers in Gode District, Somali Regional State, Ethiopia, using multistage sampling. Primary household survey data and secondary data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, multiple linear regression, and a multivariate probit model. The results showed that household head age negatively affected market supply, whereas access to market information, farming experience, quantity produced, credit utilization, oxen ownership, and extension contact had significant positive effects. The multivariate probit estimates indicated that age, education, access to market information, farming experience, production quantity, distance to market, credit utilization, and trust in buyers significantly influenced the choice of marketing outlets. Wholesalers and retailers were the major outlets used by producers. The findings suggest that strengthening market information systems, agricultural credit, extension services, rural transport infrastructure, farmer-trader linkages, and productivity-enhancing technologies can improve market participation and smallholder livelihood opportunities. These measures are relevant to sustainable rural development and contribute particularly to SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) by supporting agricultural commercialization, productive economic activity, improved market access, and more inclusive rural value chains. Clinical Trial Registration Not applicable. This study is not a clinical trial.

title: Localizing Twelver Shi‘i Clerical Authority in East and West Africa: Contrasting Prophetic and Academic Genealogies
source: Comparative Studies in Society and History
summary: How do Muslim leaders claim Islamic authority in different geographical contexts? This article presents comparative ethnographic case studies of Twelver Shi‘a in East and West Africa who take divergent approaches to following a dominant mar
content: How do Muslim leaders claim Islamic authority in different geographical contexts? This article presents comparative ethnographic case studies of Twelver Shi‘a in East and West Africa who take divergent approaches to following a dominant marja‘ , a supreme religious-juridical authority. Efforts in Senegal to pave an indigenous Shi‘i path independent of traditional, geographically situated religious power structures are contrasted with Tanzanian links to Ayatollah Shirazi, who is outside the Shi‘i mainstream. In Muslim-majority Senegal, Institut Mozdahir International competes for followers with Sufi orders. In religiously mixed Tanzania, Ahl al-Bayt Centre works within the background of Muslim marginalization and situates its turn toward the Middle East within a colonial history of ethnic and racial tensions. In exploring the diverse nature of African religious authority, this article contrasts a homegrown Senegalese Shi‘ism that foregrounds familial claims to Prophetic genealogy with a Tanzanian academic genealogy built on intellectual networks to Islamic seminaries in Iran. In so doing, it contextualizes the spread of alternative religious interpretations of Shi‘i Islam within East and West African histories, shifts the Sunni-centric focus of scholarship on Islam in Africa toward an exploration of African Shi‘ism, and rethinks Sufi-Salafi debates about the localization of Islamic authority in Shi‘i developments. Biography, genealogy, and scholarly lineage are decisive factors that contribute to the influence of local Islamic leaders and their transnational connections, including to Kuwaiti benefactors.

title: When Markets Fall Together: Can Bitcoin, Tokenized Gold, and Innovation Stocks Still Diversify Risk?
summary: Investors hold a mix of assets so that a loss on one is offset by the others, but this protection often fails in a crisis, when most assets fall at the same time. This paper asks whether a group of newer assets that trade with few restricti
content: Investors hold a mix of assets so that a loss on one is offset by the others, but this protection often fails in a crisis, when most assets fall at the same time. This paper asks whether a group of newer assets that trade with few restrictions, namely Bitcoin, tokenized gold (PAX Gold, PAXG), and the stocks of financial technology (FinTech) and artificial intelligence (AI) firms, can still help investors spread risk when markets are under extreme stress. Using daily data from 2020 to 2025, we apply the Quantile‐on‐Quantile (QQ) connectedness framework to measure state‐dependent return spillovers. The results indicate a pronounced regime pattern: connectedness is relatively low around the median but increases sharply in both lower‐ and upper‐tail states (often exceeding 70%–80%). Directional spillovers are also regime dependent, with AI‐related assets and Bitcoin frequently emerging as net transmitters in tail conditions. Importantly, PAXG does not consistently behave as a safe haven under extreme downside states, where it becomes more tightly connected to the broader system. Overall, the findings suggest that diversification benefits across the examined asset system weaken precisely when tail risk materializes, underscoring the need for tail‐sensitive risk assessment beyond mean‐based analysis.

title: Insights into sulfate speciation on the surface of SnO2 catalysts active for levulinic acid esterification
summary: The production of fuels and chemicals from renewable sources has attracted increasing attention worldwide, driving the development of biomass conversion technologies. Acid hydrolysis of biomass can produce significant amounts of levulinic a
content: The production of fuels and chemicals from renewable sources has attracted increasing attention worldwide, driving the development of biomass conversion technologies. Acid hydrolysis of biomass can produce significant amounts of levulinic acid, which can be used to synthesize several valuable chemicals, such as ethyl levulinate, through esterification. This ester has potential as a renewable additive to diesel fuel. Sulfated tin oxide has demonstrated high activity for this process; however, the influence of sulfation conditions on catalyst properties and performance remains insufficiently investigated. In this work, several sulfated tin oxides were evaluated for the esterification of levulinic acid with ethanol under mild reaction conditions. The influence of the sulfation method on the physicochemical properties of the solids was investigated using FTIR, XRD, N₂ adsorption, NH₃-TPD, SEM, Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results indicated that sulfated tin oxide prepared using a 3 mol L⁻¹ sulfuric acid solution exhibited higher acidity than materials prepared at other concentrations and presented monodentate sulfate species on its surface, in addition to the bidentate species identified in all materials. Among the impregnated materials, tin oxide containing 5% of sulfur and prepared by sulfuric acid treatment exhibited the highest catalytic activity, with results also consistent with the presence of monodentate sulfate species. Reusability tests of the three most active catalysts revealed a decline in catalytic performance, which may be associated with sulfate leaching. Overall, this study elucidates how sulfation procedures influence surface sulfate speciation and its relationship with catalytic activity, providing fundamental insights into the structure-acidity-activity relationships of sulfated SnO₂ catalysts and a basis for the rational design of more active and stable solid acid catalysts for ethyl levulinate production from levulinic acid under mild reaction conditions.

title: Machine learning computational study on solubility estimation of hydrogen in diesel
summary: This study develops and evaluates three regression approaches for predicting hydrogen (H 2 ) solubility in catalytic diesel from temperature and pressure: Decision Tree (DT), Gamma Regression (GR), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). The contr
content: This study develops and evaluates three regression approaches for predicting hydrogen (H 2 ) solubility in catalytic diesel from temperature and pressure: Decision Tree (DT), Gamma Regression (GR), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). The contribution is a leakage-controlled assessment of these models on a small, structured experimental dataset, together with Harmony Search (HS) hyperparameter optimization and comparison against conventional regression and machine-learning benchmarks. The 30 observations cover 353.2–453.2 K and 1.15–5.86 MPa. Generalization was evaluated by nested leave-one-temperature-level-out cross-validation: each temperature level served once as an outer test group, while HS operated exclusively within the remaining training groups. From pooled out-of-fold predictions, DT, GR, and MLP achieved R 2 values of 0.732, 0.959, and 0.971; RMSE values of 0.752, 0.294, and 0.245; MAE values of 0.593, 0.254, and 0.201; and MAPE values of 21.65%, 9.99%, and 6.52%, respectively. The MLP therefore provided the best overall predictive performance, although the ablation analysis showed that HS materially improved GR but did not uniformly improve DT or MLP under unseen-temperature testing. Pressure was the dominant sensitivity for all three models. The validated applicability domain is restricted to catalytic diesel within the experimental temperature-pressure range, where the models may support preliminary hydroprocessing calculations but do not replace equilibrium measurements outside that domain.

title: Effets de contexte et simulation multi-agents calibrée
summary: Pour améliorer leurs ventes, les entreprises commerciales mettent en place différentes stratégies pour influencer le comportement des clients. Parmi ces différentes stratégies, les effets de contexte sont un levier important pour ces entrep
content: Pour améliorer leurs ventes, les entreprises commerciales mettent en place différentes stratégies pour influencer le comportement des clients. Parmi ces différentes stratégies, les effets de contexte sont un levier important pour ces entreprises. Dans cet article, nous proposons un modèle capable d’analyser trois effets de contexte bien connus du domaine : l’effet de leurre, l’effet de compromis et l’effet de similarité. À travers différents exemples, nous montrons comment fixer les prix pour influencer le comportement des clients. Ensuite nous proposons de calibrer précisément les paramètres du modèle à l’aide de données empiriques issues de différentes sources : deux ans de tickets de caisse d’une grande enseigne de distribution (correspondant à 5 millions de produits vendus) et les données sur les revenus de la population française fournies par l’INSEE. Après validation du modèle, qui reproduit fidèlement les distributions observées dans les données réelles, nous montrons qu’il est capable de fournir des recommandations pertinentes sur les stratégies de tarification. Ce système offre ainsi la possibilité d’optimiser les prix des produits existants et de prédire les prix à appliquer lors de l’introduction de nouvelles offres, en se basant uniquement sur l’historique des ventes et une description synthétique des clients.

title: In silico feasibility and robustness evaluation of a single-spot proton Bragg peak FLASH platform for small-animal irradiation using a generalized 3D-printed bolus
summary: Objective FLASH radiotherapy has shown potential to reduce normal tissue toxicity while maintaining tumour control, motivating the development of clinical delivery strategies. However, most preclinical proton FLASH studies rely on transmiss
content: Objective FLASH radiotherapy has shown potential to reduce normal tissue toxicity while maintaining tumour control, motivating the development of clinical delivery strategies. However, most preclinical proton FLASH studies rely on transmission beams or spread out Bragg peaks, which do not reflect conformal clinical dose distributions. This work aims to develop and evaluate an irradiation setup for ultra-high dose-rate Bragg peak proton delivery to orthotopic mammary tumours in mice, employable in image-guided research rooms powered by clinical cyclotrons. Approach We built a simulation framework (Python+TOPAS) to assess a single spot, ablative configuration comprising a copper degrader, collimator, and generalised (3D-printed) bolus. Performance was investigated on a Phantom Mice Cohort (N=6) using personalised boluses and a Real Mice Cohort (N=10; µCT/PET) using a cohort-derived generalised bolus. Planning goals were D99%,GTV=19.0Gy and HIGTV≤1.30. Physical dose-rate feasibility was evaluated against a nominal 40Gy/s DRmin,skin threshold under an assumed 500nA beam current cap; this metric does not establish a biological FLASH effect. Robustness evaluation included 0.35 and 0.5mm setup errors and ±3% range uncertainties. Main results Simulated plans met target and heterogeneity goals across cohorts, with the 40Gy/s DRmin,skin criterion met under the assumed beam current conditions (Dmean,skin≈18.5-19.3Gy). The modelled dose-rate criterion was met below the 500nA beam current limit in both cohorts. Under the evaluated 0.35mm setup and ±3% range uncertainties, reduction in D99%,GTV remained within 3% for 9/10 real mouse cases. The generalised bolus achieved the simulated dosimetric performance across ten anatomically distinct mice; applicability to independent cohorts remains unestablished. Significance This in silico evaluation supports the simulated dosimetric and physical dose-rate feasibility of conformal Bragg peak proton delivery in small animals using a generalised bolus. The presented framework enables further development in image-guided proton research facilities, forming a strong basis for experimental validation and commissioning toward in situ small animal studies. .

title: Factors Driving Electric Three Wheeler Adoption in India using an Integrated Behavioral Framework
summary: Background and Objective: The urban mobility revolution in India has entered a new phase with the rapid electrification of three-wheelers (3W). India currently represents the world’s largest electric three-wheeler (E3W) market, recording ov
content: Background and Objective: The urban mobility revolution in India has entered a new phase with the rapid electrification of three-wheelers (3W). India currently represents the world’s largest electric three-wheeler (E3W) market, recording over 6 lakh registrations in 2024. This study investigates the multidimensional determinants influencing the adoption of electric three-wheelers in India’s last-mile mobility market, encompassing both passenger (auto-rickshaws) and cargo applications Materials and Methods: The study utilized a mixed-source approach based on secondary literature, market reports, and primary survey data collected from 450 commercial operators, fleet managers, and policymakers across six Indian cities. A combined theoretical framework integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) was employed. Multiple regression analysis was conducted to examine the determinants of E3W adoption. Results: The findings identified nine key drivers of adoption: government policies and financial incentives, economic benefits through lower total cost of ownership, charging infrastructure availability, battery swapping practicality, social influence and peer adoption, financing access, environmental concern, perceived range adequacy, and urban growth with rising last-mile demand. The regression model showed significant explanatory power (R² = 0.581, F(9, 440) = 67.78, p < .001), with charging infrastructure (β* = 0.329) and economic benefit (β* = 0.289) emerging as the strongest predictors. All nine direct-effect hypotheses (H1–H9) were supported. Conclusion: The study highlights the critical role of infrastructure development, financial viability, and supportive policy frameworks in accelerating electric three-wheeler adoption in India. The findings provide practical insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders to strengthen sustainable last-mile mobility systems while identifying directions for future research.

title: PERENCANAAN SISTEM JARINGAN DISRIBUSI AIR BERSIHDISTRIK WAPOGA KABUPATEN WAROPEN
source: Prosiding: Seminar Nasional Teknik Sipil Universitas Yapis Papua
summary: Ketersediaan air bersih yang memadai merupakan kebutuhan mendasar bagi kesehatan dan kesejahteraan masyarakat. Wilayah Distrik Wapoga, Kabupaten Waropen, saat ini masih menghadapi kendala pemenuhan air bersih layak minum, di mana sebagian b
content: Ketersediaan air bersih yang memadai merupakan kebutuhan mendasar bagi kesehatan dan kesejahteraan masyarakat. Wilayah Distrik Wapoga, Kabupaten Waropen, saat ini masih menghadapi kendala pemenuhan air bersih layak minum, di mana sebagian besar warga masih mengandalkan sumber air baku dengan kualitas yang kurang memenuhi syarat. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memproyeksikan kebutuhan air bersih hingga tahun 2045 pada empat kampung rencana (Wapoga Kampung, Waweri, Kamarisano, dan Dokis), merencanakan dimensi unit pengolahan Saringan Pasir Lambat (SPL) serta bangunan pelengkapnya, dan menguji kinerja hidrolika jaringan distribusi menggunakan pemodelan EPANET 2.2.Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif kuantitatif. Proyeksi pertumbuhan penduduk dihitung mengelompokkan analisis proyeksi aritmatika, geometrik, atau eksponensial untuk periode 20 tahun mendatang. Data debit ketersediaan air baku dari sumber terukur sebesar 69,3 L/detik, yang membuktikan kecukupan pasokan terhadap kebutuhan masyarakat. Hasil analisis menunjukkan total penduduk target pada tahun 2045 diperkirakan mencapai 2.394 jiwa. Total kebutuhan air rata-rata harian diproyeksikan sebesar 2,87 L/detik, dengan kebutuhan harian maksimum (Qmaks) sebesar 3,30 L/detik dan debit jam puncak (Qpuncak) sebesar 4,74 L/detik. Berdasarkan debit perencanaan tersebut, dirancang dimensi bangunan intake, unit pengendapan awal, bak Saringan Pasir Lambat (SPL), serta resevoir penyimpanan. Sistem pengaliran dikombinasikan antara pemompaan transmisi dan distribusi secara gravitasi. Hasil simulasi hidrolika pada jaringan pipa distribusi menggunakan EPANET 2.2 menunjukkan bahwa nilai tekanan (head) dan kecepatan aliran (velocity) pada tiap titik buhul (node) dan pipa telah memenuhi kriteria teknis standar kementerian PU.Kata Kunci: Air Bersih, Distrik Wapoga, Proyeksi Penduduk,Kebutuhan air,intek, reservoir,Saringan Pasir Lambat,pompa sentrifugal, Sistem jaringan Epanet 2.2

title: STRATEGI IMPLEMENTASI GREEN BUILDING PADA PEMBANGUNAN INFRASTRUKTUR PUBLIK DI KAWASAN 3T(TERDEPAN, TERLUAR, DAN TERTINGGAL)
source: Prosiding: Seminar Nasional Teknik Sipil Universitas Yapis Papua
summary: Penerapan prinsip green building pada pembangunan infrastruktur publik di kawasan 3T (Terdepan, Terluar, dan Tertinggal) menjadi tantangan sekaligus peluang dalam mewujudkan pembangunan yang efisien, adaptif, dan berkelanjutan. Penelitian i
content: Penerapan prinsip green building pada pembangunan infrastruktur publik di kawasan 3T (Terdepan, Terluar, dan Tertinggal) menjadi tantangan sekaligus peluang dalam mewujudkan pembangunan yang efisien, adaptif, dan berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merumuskan strategi implementasi green building yang kontekstual dan aplikatif di wilayah Papua sebagai representasi kawasan 3T. Metode yang digunakan adalah studi kasus kualitatif dengan pendekatan observasi lapangan, wawancara mendalam, dan studi dokumen pada tiga lokasi: Sekolah Dasar di Kabupaten Jayapura, Puskesmas di Kabupaten Asmat, dan Gedung Pelayanan Publik di Manokwari. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ketiga lokasi belum mengadopsi prinsip desain hijau, namun memiliki potensi tinggi untuk penerapan desain pasif, sistem pemanenan air hujan, pemanfaatan energi terbarukan, serta material lokal ramah lingkungan. Faktor-faktor penghambat utama meliputi minimnya kapasitas teknis, keterbatasan pasokan energi dan air, serta belum adanya regulasi lokal yang mendukung. Strategi implementasi yang diusulkan mencakup peningkatan kapasitas SDM lokal, integrasi green design dalam dana desa dan DAK fisik, serta pemanfaatan model modular adaptif. Penelitian ini merekomendasikan bahwa keberhasilan green building di kawasan 3T sangat bergantung pada pendekatan yang berbasis lokal, partisipatif, dan lintas sektor.Kata kunci: green building, kawasan 3T, strategi implementasi, infrastruktur publik, Papua, pembangunan berkelanjutan
