title: Toward Climate-Neutral Industry: Circular Strategies, Eco-Innovation, and Low-Carbon Industrial Transformation
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Climate-neutral industrial transformation requires coordinated changes in material demand, production processes, business models, and institutional arrangements, alongside technological decarbonization. This article critically synthesizes r
content: Climate-neutral industrial transformation requires coordinated changes in material demand, production processes, business models, and institutional arrangements, alongside technological decarbonization. This article critically synthesizes research on the conditions under which circular strategies and eco-innovation contribute to low-carbon industrial transformation. The analysis integrates conceptual perspectives with evidence from material-stock models, firm-level studies, life-cycle assessments, sectoral technology research, and transition-policy literature. Three findings emerge. First, circular strategies generate climate benefits when recovered materials, extended product lifetimes, or redesigned services effectively displace emissions-intensive activities, while accounting for energy requirements, material quality losses, and rebound effects. Second, circularity and supply-side decarbonization are complementary but not necessarily additive; their combined effects depend on implementation sequences, enabling infrastructure, and changes in electricity and material systems. Third, institutional capabilities and distributive arrangements influence whether technical mitigation potential translates into sustained industrial transformation. Evidence from steel, cement, plastics, and industrial symbiosis illustrates both mitigation opportunities and relevant trade-offs. Differences between economies with mature material stocks and those undergoing infrastructure expansion also limit the applicability of uniform circularity objectives. The article proposes an evaluative framework based on functional additionality, carbon additionality, transition compatibility, and distributive legitimacy. It argues that industrial policy should prioritize verified reductions in cumulative life-cycle emissions while supporting essential services, technological learning, and worker inclusion, rather than equating circular activity with climate neutrality.

title: Towards Net Zero: A Sustainability Assessment Framework for Urban Drainage Infrastructure
source: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
summary: This paper analyzes the contribution of urban drainage infrastructure towards a net zero objective in Qatar infrastructure buildup program. While the infrastructure projects have made strides toward aligning construction practices with the
content: This paper analyzes the contribution of urban drainage infrastructure towards a net zero objective in Qatar infrastructure buildup program. While the infrastructure projects have made strides toward aligning construction practices with the Qatar National Vision 2030, the integration of comprehensive sustainability and carbon-neutrality principles into drainage infrastructure remains challenging. To bridge this gap, the research develops a context-specific Drainage Sustainability Assessment Standard (DSAS) that embeds net zero objectives into the planning, design, and management of urban drainage projects. A three-phase mixed-method approach was employed. The first phase collected quantitative survey data from key stakeholders including clients, contractors, consultants, and sustainability experts to assess their understanding of net zero goals and current sustainability practices. The second phase involved in-depth qualitative interviews to identify systemic shortcomings in existing evaluation frameworks, particularly in relation to carbon emissions reduction and climate resilience. In the final phase, the proposed assessment standard was formulated, tested, and validated through simulations using real-world case studies of award-winning drainage projects of varying scale and complexity. Results indicated strong stakeholder awareness of sustainability principles; however, application varied significantly by project role. Key challenges included institutional inertia, fragmented sustainability standards, and limited incorporation of carbon mitigation strategies. The DSAS addresses these barriers through a tiered, flexible scoring model encompassing four critical dimensions: sustainability governance, resource efficiency, climate adaptation, and socio-economic impact. And explicitly integrating carbon accounting and emissions mitigation metrics. The proposed DSAS provides a structured pathway for continuous monitoring, policy alignment, and incentive-driven implementation, advancing Qatar’s transition toward carbon-neutral and resilient urban infrastructure.

title: Hydrogen-based green steel corridors: cost saving and emission reduction potentials of emerging trade routes
summary: Deploying hydrogen-based direct-reduced iron (H 2 -DRI) technologies will be decisive to defossilize the global steel sector by replacing coal-based blast furnaces (BF) in conventional steelmaking. DRI can then either be directly fed into a
content: Deploying hydrogen-based direct-reduced iron (H 2 -DRI) technologies will be decisive to defossilize the global steel sector by replacing coal-based blast furnaces (BF) in conventional steelmaking. DRI can then either be directly fed into an electric-arc-furnace (EAF) and alternative electric smelting furnaces or transported as cold hot-briquetted iron (HBI) and a green commoditiy to a steel plant. The availability and expansion of low-cost renewable electricity and green hydrogen supply options is the essential and site-specific precondition to deploy H 2 -DRI plants that can be gradually switched from natural gas to hydrogen. However, near-zero emission steel made from H 2 -DRI needs to produced at competitive costs compared to fossil steel regulated under carbon emission pricing schemes. Based on revised green hydrogen cost forecasts in potentially low-cost countries like Australia or Oman, this study reveals the cost competitiveness of emerging green steel corridors built on international partnerships. With green HBI then exported to a representative EAF green steelmaking site, the analysis shows the potential cost savings of importing green HBI from renewable-rich countries when facing a future lack of affordable hydrogen supply options in leading steel countries like Germany or South Korea characterized by a high dependence on energy imports. Overall, low-emission crude steel based on 66 vol% H 2 -HBI imports achieves fossil cost parity in Germany in 2040 at increased carbon prices in the EU, while all 100% hydrogen-based steel scenarios inhere higher costs with a premium of 6%–13% over natural gas-based DRI-EAF crude steel at 828 € t −1 CS (with 0% scrap) at hydrogen costs ranging between 4.14 and 4.94 € kg −1 H 2 . In addition, a cradle-to-gate accounting of greenhouse gas emissions reveals that cost savings from HBI imports potentially come at the expense of up to 50% higher total emissions compared to an integrated H 2 -DRI-EAF plant running on iron ore pellet imports. All 100% H 2 -DRI-based scenarios yield an emission reduction between 42%–57% compared to a domestic benchmarked NG-DRI-EAF scenario at 1293 kg CO 2 (e) t −1 CS. The carbon footprint analysis further highlights the effect of upstream defossilization measures related to iron ore mining, pelletising and transport by rail and ship.

title: Dynamic tracking of N2O and CO2 associated with Fusarium and soil using mid-IR QCL sensing
summary: In this study, nitrous oxide (N 2 O), a major greenhouse gas predominantly emitted from agricultural soils via microbial activity, was investigated using a real-time detection approach. Real-time monitoring of microbially derived N 2 O is c
content: In this study, nitrous oxide (N 2 O), a major greenhouse gas predominantly emitted from agricultural soils via microbial activity, was investigated using a real-time detection approach. Real-time monitoring of microbially derived N 2 O is crucial for elucidating soil microbial dynamics and visualizing soil ecosystem conditions. A simultaneous N 2 O and CO 2 detection system was developed by integrating a mid-infrared quantum cascade laser operating at ~ 4.47 μm with a multipass gas cell (MGC). Detection limits of 12 ppb and 66 ppm were obtained for N 2 O and CO 2 , respectively. By maintaining the MGC at low internal pressure throughout gas sampling and measurement, continuous-flow monitoring of N 2 O and CO 2 concentrations in gases released from Fusarium oxysporum and agricultural soil (leaf mold) was successfully conducted. This system enabled, for the first time, real-time observation of dynamic fluctuations in N 2 O and CO 2 concentrations in response to environmental changes. These results provide enhanced visualization of microbially derived N 2 O concentration changes and offer valuable insights for advancing analyses of microbial N 2 O dynamics.

title: A prediction–optimization–decision framework for logistics network design under demand and disruption uncertainty
summary: Aiming at the problem of the separation of logistics network design prediction and optimization under the double uncertainty of dynamic demand and disruption risk, this paper proposes a prediction-optimization-decision integration framework
content: Aiming at the problem of the separation of logistics network design prediction and optimization under the double uncertainty of dynamic demand and disruption risk, this paper proposes a prediction-optimization-decision integration framework with deep integration of machine learning and system optimization. The framework adopts a three-layer architecture: the prediction layer constructs a hybrid model combining spatial-temporal graph neural network and multi-head attention mechanism and uses deep ensembles and quantile regression to quantify epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. The risk layer identifies disruption risks through attention-based multi-label classification and deep support vector data description and generates a representative risk scenario set combining multi-layer network propagation model and importance sampling. The optimization layer establishes a multi-period mixed integer programming model and introduces resilience service level constraints and conditional value-at-risk measurement to realize the synergy between cost and resilience. In order to solve large-scale problems, a learning-enhanced large-scale neighborhood search algorithm is designed, and reinforcement learning agents are embedded in the operator selection process. The experimental results show that the MAE of the proposed prediction model is reduced by 8.2% to 15.6% compared with Transformer in each step. The average F1 of risk classification reached 0.847, 6.2% higher than that of XGBoost. The total cost of the optimization algorithm is 13.4% lower than that of stochastic programming on large-scale instances, and the optimality gap reaches 0.8% within 600 s. The total cost of the framework in 12 months decreased by 16.9%, the service level improved by 5.6% points, and the interruption recovery time shortened by 62%.

title: From Materials to Device‐Level Energy Density: A Multiscale Perspective on High‐Energy‐Density Lithium‐Based Batteries
summary: High‐energy‐density rechargeable batteries are widely regarded as a key enabling technology for electrification and sustainable energy systems. Initial cell‐level energy density depends on available capacity and discharge voltage relative t
content: High‐energy‐density rechargeable batteries are widely regarded as a key enabling technology for electrification and sustainable energy systems. Initial cell‐level energy density depends on available capacity and discharge voltage relative to total cell mass or volume, including inactive components. Interfacial reactions, transport limitations, and mechanical evolution further influence energy delivery at a specified rate and its retention over cycling. In this Perspective, we present a system‐oriented framework for understanding these limitations and discuss three interconnected design dimensions for high‐energy‐density batteries: high‐capacity electrode materials, interfacial and electrolyte engineering, and thick electrode architecture. We highlight the opportunities and bottlenecks associated with high‐capacity materials, the regulation of solvation structures and interphases in advanced electrolytes, and thick electrode strategies that reduce the fraction of inactive materials while preserving transport efficiency and structural integrity. Together, these insights show that improvements in any single component rarely translate directly into higher device‐level energy density unless materials, interfaces, and electrode architectures are developed in a coordinated manner. Future progress will therefore require multiscale co‐design and evaluation under practically relevant conditions, including high areal capacities and lean‐electrolyte operation.

title: Toward a Renewed and Broader Pro‐Climate Alliance?
summary: After decades of increasing greenhouse gas emissions, climate policies, though fragile and hesitant, have finally started producing substantial effects in the late 2010s. These policies had internal weaknesses regarding governance, inequali
content: After decades of increasing greenhouse gas emissions, climate policies, though fragile and hesitant, have finally started producing substantial effects in the late 2010s. These policies had internal weaknesses regarding governance, inequalities, and biodiversity, but the backlash that followed is also the result of deliberate obstruction. In this perspective, we argue that the convergence between anti‐climate and anti‐democratic actors might be sufficiently concerning to stimulate a response involving a broader alliance of actors concerned with preserving decent living conditions on Earth for all.

title: Cd Vacancy‐Mediated Orbital Hybridization and Ultrafast Charge Separation in Pt Single‐Atom Photocatalysts
summary: Zn x Cd 1−x S (ZCS) solid solutions are promising photocatalysts for H 2 evolution but suffer from rapid electron‐hole recombination. Density functional theory (DFT) predicts that Cd vacancies narrow the band gap and reduce the hole effecti
content: Zn x Cd 1−x S (ZCS) solid solutions are promising photocatalysts for H 2 evolution but suffer from rapid electron‐hole recombination. Density functional theory (DFT) predicts that Cd vacancies narrow the band gap and reduce the hole effective mass from 0.80 to 0.59 m 0 , suppressing bulk recombination. Guided by this, Cd vacancies (V C ) were introduced into ZCS as anchoring sites for Pt single atoms (Pt SA ), forming Pt SA /V C ‐ZCS. Aberration‑corrected high‐angle annular dark‐field scanning transmission electron microscopy and X‑ray absorption fine structure confirm atomic Pt dispersion. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy shows Cd vacancies localize photogenerated holes at defect states while Pt single atoms dominate ultrafast electron extraction (ca. 4.10 ps, 81.5% pre‐exponential weight). This vacancy‐mediated synergy switches the dominant carrier pathway from intrinsic interband recombination to spatial charge separation. DFT further shows that p–d hybridization optimizes hydrogen adsorption free energy to −0.11 eV and delocalizes electrons at adjacent sulfur sites. The optimal Pt SA /V C ‐ZCS achieves a H 2 evolution rate of 142.86 mmol g −1 h −1 under visible light, 16.8 times that of pristine ZCS, with an apparent quantum yield of 7.48% at 420 nm and >90% activity retention after cycling. This work reveals how cation vacancies and single atoms enhance charge separation and surface kinetics, guiding atomically dispersed photocatalyst design.

title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
summary: The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptuall
content: The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe 2 nanoclusters onto MoSe 2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal‐support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long‐lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d‐band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g −1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe 2 . Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g −1 with stable long‐term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Can Waste Incineration with Energy Recovery Be Considered a Genuine Circular Economy Practice under China’s Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality Goals: An Integrative Literature Review and a Five-Dimensional Authenticity Assessment Framework
source: CPS Digital Library - Series of Conferences
summary: China’s rapid expansion of municipal solid waste incineration with energy recovery has reduced landfill pressure, but its compatibility with a circular economy remains contested. This study integrates conceptual, life-cycle, operational, an
content: China’s rapid expansion of municipal solid waste incineration with energy recovery has reduced landfill pressure, but its compatibility with a circular economy remains contested. This study integrates conceptual, life-cycle, operational, and governance evidence to evaluate when waste-to-energy can be considered genuinely circular. It proposes a five- dimensional authenticity framework covering alignment with the waste hierarchy, material-value retention, life-cycle carbon performance, environmental safety, and system and institutional compatibility. The review finds that incineration can provide a legitimate residual-waste service when non-recyclable waste is treated only after prevention, reuse, recycling, and separate biological treatment; net carbon benefits are demonstrated against realistic local alternatives; emissions and ash are controlled; and contracts can adapt to declining waste volumes. Conversely, routine combustion of recyclable materials, incomplete fossil-carbon accounting, weak residue traceability, or throughput-dependent incentives indicate pseudo-circularity. The framework shifts assessment from installed capacity and gross energy output to system-level evidence and offers a practical basis for policy, contract design, and facility evaluation in China’s low-carbon transition.

title: Positional effects of the N-pyridyl atom on crystal packing, docking and electronic properties of chalcone-based hydrazones
summary: Two chalcone-based hydrazones were synthesized and characterized by spectroscopic and single crystal X-ray diffraction techniques. The structures were refined by HAR procedure at the R2SCAN/cc-pVTZ level of theory. The two hydrazones crysta
content: Two chalcone-based hydrazones were synthesized and characterized by spectroscopic and single crystal X-ray diffraction techniques. The structures were refined by HAR procedure at the R2SCAN/cc-pVTZ level of theory. The two hydrazones crystallized in an E configuration about the C7–N1 and C8–C9 bonds, with the hydrazinyl groups forming intermolecular N–H···O hydrogen bonds, resulting in R 2 2 (8) ring motif that links two hydrazone molecules in a pseudo-dimeric arrangement. To further explore the structural and electronic properties of the synthesized compounds, Hirshfeld surface analysis, molecular orbitals calculations, topological analysis, and electrostatic potential mapping were performed, showing that the position of the N -pyridyl atom in the structure influenced the crystal packing, as well as slight differences in the molecular orbitals and intramolecular contacts. Molecular docking was also performed using the enzyme Glutamine synthetase as target, due to the anti-tuberculosis properties that this class of compounds can exhibit.

title: Octahedral coordination chemistry in the electrocatalytic nitrogen cycle
summary: This review presents an octahedral-coordination-centered chemistry framework that links nitrogen electrocatalytic pathways with structure-reactivity relationships across diverse oxide catalyst systems.Highlights➢ Establishes an octahedral c
content: This review presents an octahedral-coordination-centered chemistry framework that links nitrogen electrocatalytic pathways with structure-reactivity relationships across diverse oxide catalyst systems.Highlights➢ Establishes an octahedral coordination-reactivity framework for nitrogen electrocatalysis.➢ Defines an octahedral catalyst-descriptor map linking oxide structures with nitrogen redox pathways.➢ Proposes coordination chemistry and defect-regulated principles for advanced nitrogen electrocatalysts.

title: Translation of molecular catalysts into highly functional interfaces for small molecule activation
summary: The development of sustainable electrocatalytic systems for small-molecule activation represents a promising strategy for addressing challenges associated with greenhouse gas emissions, nitrogen pollution, and fossil-fuel-dependent chemical
content: The development of sustainable electrocatalytic systems for small-molecule activation represents a promising strategy for addressing challenges associated with greenhouse gas emissions, nitrogen pollution, and fossil-fuel-dependent chemical synthesis. Molecular electrocatalysts are particularly attractive in this context due to their well-defined and tuneable active sites, enabling detailed investigation of structure-activity relationships and catalytic mechanisms. This thesis explores the design, mechanistic understanding, and application of molecular transition metal catalysts for electrochemical CO2 reduction, nitrate reduction, dinitrogen activation, and electrochemical C-N bond formation. The first part of this work demonstrates that cobalt terpyridine complexes modified with perfluorinated alkyl side chains can self-assemble at gas-liquid-solid interfaces on gas diffusion electrodes, enabling highly selective electrochemical CO2 reduction to methane. Mechanistic investigations using in situ spectroscopy and proton inventory studies reveal the importance of hydrophobic catalytic microenvironments and proton-shuttling pyridine units in promoting multi-electron reduction pathways. The thesis further investigates electrochemical C-N bond formation from CO2 and nitrate using mono-terpyridine nickel complexes in both homogeneous and heterogenized configurations. A homogeneous mono-hydroxy terpyridine nickel catalyst enabled selective formamide production with, while mechanistic studies involving in situ spectroscopy and computational modelling provided insight into the coupling pathways between carbon- and nitrogen-derived intermediates. Subsequent heterogenization of terpyridine nickel catalysts demonstrated how ligand functionalization and immobilization influence catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability, while also revealing important electronic effects. To further expand molecular nitrogen activation chemistry, a palladium membrane reactor coupled with a mono-terpyridine nickel catalyst was developed for electrochemical ammonia synthesis from dinitrogen. This enabled selective ammonia production while suppressing competing hydrogen evolution. Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies revealed the formation of catalytically relevant Ni-H intermediates generated through hydrogen transfer from the palladium membrane. Finally, a copper bipyridine chloride complex was investigated as a molecular electrocatalyst for nitrate and organonitro reduction. The catalyst achieved near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies for ammonia production from nitrate and selectively reduced nitroaromatic compounds to aniline derivatives. In situ spectroscopy revealed mechanistic pathways involving sequential N-O bond cleavage and proton-coupled electron transfer through nitrite, nitric oxide, and hydroxylamine intermediates. This thesis establishes molecular catalyst design principles for sustainable electrocatalytic small-molecule conver

title: Green Chemistry :Sustainable Synthesis, Renewable Feedstocks, Catalysis and Environmental Applications
summary: Green Chemistry has become more than a collection of guiding principles: it is a discipline of sustainable chemistry that is ready for application. The chemists and Chemical Engineers have been looking for waste prevention, high atom econom
content: Green Chemistry has become more than a collection of guiding principles: it is a discipline of sustainable chemistry that is ready for application. The chemists and Chemical Engineers have been looking for waste prevention, high atom economy, safer green solvents, lesser energy requirement, renewable feedstocks since formulation of twelve principles of green chemistry. Climate change, regulation, and variable energy prices, along with public awareness have driven the chemical industry to pursue decarbonization, carbon neutrality and circular economy. Green Chemistry: Sustainable Synthesis, Renewable Feedstocks, Catalysis and Environmental Applications addresses that pressure by integrating the cutting-edge aspects of the field within a single volume. The seven chapters have catalytic linkage. The book starts with artificial intelligence and machine learning, demonstrating how waste can be avoided already in the prediction of reactions, green retrosynthesis and catalyst discovery and the introduction of self driven laboratories. Chapter 2 deals with the valorization of lignocellulosic biomass, covering the processes from pretreatment and enzymatic hydrolysis to the integrated biorefinery, biofuels, platform chemicals and lignin valorization. Chapter 3 focuses on carbon dioxide capture and CO2 utilization, such as CO2 hydrogenation, heterogeneous catalysis, single-atom catalysts and metal–organic frameworks. Chapter 4 proceeds to photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, such as with photoredox catalysis, organic electrosynthesis and production of ‘green’ hydrogen using renewables. Later chapters focus on the solvents, materials and molecules that are the basis for sustainable synthesis. Chapter 5 introduces Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs) and bio-based solvents as possible alternatives to Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) and Ionic Liquids (ILs) for the in organic synthesis, biomass processing and metal recovery. Chapter 6 discusses the plastic waste management, plastic upcycling, catalytic depolymerization of plastics and supports the circular polymer economy. Biocatalysis and enzyme engineering are discussed in Chapter 7, connecting with the possibility of directed evolution and protein design for biotransformation to produce pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals. The same tests are applied throughout the chapters. A process with a renewable feedstock is not necessarily green—the life cycle assessment, the techno-economic analysis, toxicity, scale-up and regulatory barriers are analysed again and again. Three messages come back: No code of conduct to close the loop for plastics; CO2 utilization cannot and should not replace carbon storage; AI is only sustainable if data, models and energy consumption are open for analysis. In addition to flow reactors and process intensification as means of cleaner scale-up, environmental applications are addressed in almost all the chapters, such as pollution control, water treatment and greenhouse gas mitigation. title: Enhancing short-term solar radiation forecasting using pure machine learning and public weather forecasts
summary: Reliable forecasting solar radiation ( R s ) is vital for managing renewable energy. Traditional empirical models offer physical interpretability but tend to oversimplify complex processes, whereas machine learning (ML) models can capture n
content: Reliable forecasting solar radiation ( R s ) is vital for managing renewable energy. Traditional empirical models offer physical interpretability but tend to oversimplify complex processes, whereas machine learning (ML) models can capture nonlinear relationships but often lack physical meaning. To overcome this, we develop an ML-based framework to improve 1-7 day R s forecasts across mainland China. Within this framework, three forecasting strategies are proposed and compared against an empirical model: a hybrid model ( R s _ n _ GOA–XGBoost ) that forecasts n before driving an empirical R s model; a pure ML model ( R s _ pure_ML1 ) that forecast R s directly from public weather forecast; and an enhanced model ( R s _ pure_ML2 ) that also incorporates prior-day R s observations. The results demonstrate that n _ GOA–XGBoost model greatly improves n forecasts compared to n _ empirical model, reducing RMSE by 8.9%–10.9% across 1–7 day lead times. For overall R s forecasting, R s _ pure_ML2 model achieved the best performance at 48.8%–77.9% of stations, followed by R s _ pure_ML1 model and the R s _ n _ GOA–XGBoost model, whereas R s _ n_empirical model performed the worst. We therefore recommend R s _ pure_ML2 for stations with historical R s observations, because it requires prior R s as an input. For stations without historical R s observations, R s _ pure_ML1 is recommended, as it relies only on public weather forecast variables. This study shows that including intermediate physical variables adds complexity without improving accuracy, within the set of models evaluated here, offering a practical reference for R s forecasting in data-sparse regions of mainland China.

title: Commodifying Climate: Understanding Data Centres in Brazil
summary: Data centres have come under increasing scrutiny due to their demand for natural resources. As a symptom of contemporary societies’ dependence on digital technologies, investments in this infrastructure raise questions about what kind of ec
content: Data centres have come under increasing scrutiny due to their demand for natural resources. As a symptom of contemporary societies’ dependence on digital technologies, investments in this infrastructure raise questions about what kind of economic development we are building and which ecological relations take shape in this process. Seeking to understand what kind of value is produced in data centers and how the infrastructure-environment relationship operates within this production, this research proposes understanding data centers as sites of modulation and control of climatic variables oriented toward computation. Above all, in dialogue with data center studies, the political economy of the environment, the anthropology of infrastructure, and entropy studies, this thesis argues that data centers, through the distributed agency between humans and their artifacts, result in a technological ecosystem. Such an ecosystem is a site of experimentation for the production of a type of climate contractually enforced for the operation of servers and other computational devices. It is therefore a mode of capitalist exploitation based on negentropic practices of energetic, thermal, and informational control, such that the resulting commodity is a temporality supposedly “cleansed” of the possibility of catastrophic events. To arrive at these conclusions, the research was based on fieldwork conducted primarily with data center companies and workers located in the metropolitan region of São Paulo. The aim was to understand their worldviews, sociotechnical relations, and the environmental issues that shape the functioning of this infrastructure. Additionally, I participated in trade fairs and events aimed at companies in the sector, which provided me with contact with the discourses and modes of sociability of this milieu. This contact made it possible to identify latent contradictions, as, for example, the tension between the promise of ecologically sustainable development and the need for exponential growth.

title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
summary: We propose VC-VQA, a large-scale benchmark for vision-centric knowledge reasoning, aiming to systematically evaluate the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition and complex multi
content: We propose VC-VQA, a large-scale benchmark for vision-centric knowledge reasoning, aiming to systematically evaluate the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition and complex multi-stage reasoning. Unlike existing benchmarks that primarily treat visual information as entity recognition and rely on text-based external knowledge, VC-VQA explicitly models the role of visual information by considering both its source (internal vs. external images) and stage of involvement (pre-retrieval vs. post-retrieval). Specifically, VC-VQA requires models to retrieve external visual evidence, identify visual clues before retrieval, and localize, verify, or match retrieved knowledge against the internal image. We further construct a controlled multimodal knowledge base with traceable textual and visual evidence for each sample. We evaluate 21 representative MLLMs under four settings: no external knowledge, with provided evidence, knowledge base retrieval, and open-web search. Experimental results lead to three key findings: current models still struggle with vision-centric knowledge reasoning; fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition remains the primary bottleneck; and agentic retrieval highlights the value of multi-step planning and cross-modal knowledge integration. Overall, VC-VQA provides a more challenging benchmark for evaluating vision-centric knowledge reasoning in MLLMs. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/CASIA-IVA-Lab/VC-VQA.

title: Emergent Orbital Hall Currents in Disordered and Amorphous Materials
summary: The role of disorder in orbital transport remains a central open question in orbitronics. Using a real-space formulation of itinerant orbital angular momentum, we investigate the real-time or- bital Hall transport in single-orbital square-l
content: The role of disorder in orbital transport remains a central open question in orbitronics. Using a real-space formulation of itinerant orbital angular momentum, we investigate the real-time or- bital Hall transport in single-orbital square-lattice and graphene-based systems. We demonstrate that both structural (polycrystalline and amorphous) and electrostatic disorder can generate siz- able orbital Hall currents that are absent in their pristine counterparts. Remarkably, in amorphous graphene, these currents persist over extended timescales and across a broad energy window around charge neutrality, despite the strong localization of electronic states. Consistent with recent exper- imental evidence, our findings establish amorphous quantum materials as promising platforms for disorder-engineered orbitronic functionality.

title: Optimising sporulation of Trichoderma harzianum AMUTH–1 under solid–state fermentation and its biocontrol efficacy against cabbage leaf spot (Alternaria brassicae)
summary: Leaf spot caused by Alternaria brassicae poses a significant barrier to sustainable cabbage cultivation. However, effective Trichoderma -based bioformulations for its management remain scarce. This study investigates the sporulation (conidi
content: Leaf spot caused by Alternaria brassicae poses a significant barrier to sustainable cabbage cultivation. However, effective Trichoderma -based bioformulations for its management remain scarce. This study investigates the sporulation (conidiation) of Trichoderma harzianum AMUTH-1 under different moisture levels (10–100%), temperatures (5–40 °C), pH conditions (4.0–9.0) and incubation time (1–40 days) to optimise its performance on rice substrate under a solid-state fermentation process. Furthermore, the spore viability (germination percentage), per cent inhibition of lesion area ( ex vivo detached-leaf assay) and biocontrol activity (under field conditions) of the harvested spores were assessed to enable their use in biocontrol applications against A. brassicae on cabbage. Results revealed that moisture was the most critical factor, with ∼ 60% supporting maximum colonisation and sporulation. The optimum temperature was 25 °C, while extremes (≤15 °C or ≥ 35 °C) inhibited conidial production. Notably, a dynamic temperature downshift (30 → 20 °C) enhanced sporulation beyond static incubation, highlighting the role of environmental fluctuations in stimulating conidial yield. Sporulation peaked between 20–30 days of incubation, with viability maintained under moderate conditions. The harvested spores of T. harzianum AMUTH–1 demonstrated highly significant results in terms of spore viability (P ≤ 0.001), percentage inhibition of lesion area (P ≤ 0.001), and field biocontrol efficacy (P ≤ 0.001) against A. brassicae on cabbage. Optimisation of sporulation under solid–state fermentation revealed pH 6.0, 60% moisture, 25 °C (with enhanced yield under a 30 → 20 °C temperature downshift), and 20–30 days of incubation as the optimal conditions. These findings highlight the strong biocontrol potential of AMUTH–1 spores and their practical relevance for cost–effective, sustainable bioformulation development in cabbage production against A. brassicae .

title: Identifying and Structuring Risks in CCS Infrastructures - A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Großskalige CCS-Infrastrukturen verbinden Abscheidung, Konditionierung, Transport und geologische Speicherung zu einer eng gekoppelten Wertschöpfungskette. Das Arbeitspapier untersucht, wie die damit verbundenen Risiken systematisch identif
content: Großskalige CCS-Infrastrukturen verbinden Abscheidung, Konditionierung, Transport und geologische Speicherung zu einer eng gekoppelten Wertschöpfungskette. Das Arbeitspapier untersucht, wie die damit verbundenen Risiken systematisch identifiziert und strukturiert werden können. Grundlage ist eine Literaturanalyse von 76 Volltextpublikationen. Die identifizierten Risiken wurden fünf CCS-Stufen und sieben Risikokategorien zugeordnet und zu 35 Risikoclustern konsolidiert. Eine Risikomatrix der CCS Wertschöpfungskette ermöglicht deren strukturierte Verortung, während ein Risikoregister Ursachen, Auswirkungen, Minderungsmaßnahmen und Literaturgrundlagen dokumentiert. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass insbesondere Speicherrestriktionen, Kapazitätsabweichungen, technische Schnittstellen und Koordinationsprobleme über einzelne Prozessstufen hinauswirken. Die entwickelten Instrumente schaffen eine transparente Grundlage für projektspezifische Analysen, ersetzen jedoch keine quantitative Risikobewertung. Weiterer Forschungsbedarf besteht bei der empirischen Validierung, der Modellierung von Wechselwirkungen und der stärkeren Berücksichtigung gesellschaftlicher Akzeptanz.

title: The Built Environment
summary: This chapter summarizes current knowledge on climate-related risks affecting the built environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and Middle East (EMME) region to identify possible pathways to address the climate crisis with coordinated actio
content: This chapter summarizes current knowledge on climate-related risks affecting the built environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and Middle East (EMME) region to identify possible pathways to address the climate crisis with coordinated action at a regional level. Urban vulnerability stems from a combination of climate exposure, geographic and morphological features, and limited adaptive capacity influenced by social and economic conditions. Rapid urbanization, unplanned development, and rising energy demand exacerbate greenhouse gas emissions, intensifying the region's exposure to climate impacts. The complexity of the built environment that encompasses buildings, infrastructure, and urban systems necessitates localized strategies for climate adaptation. Cities, as economic and innovation hubs, are critical to achieving global goals such as the Paris Agreement and the United Nations 2030 Agenda. However, limited resources often constrain local authorities' ability to implement effective measures. Despite emerging adaptation actions across EMME urban areas, progress remains uneven. High-quality, locally relevant data are urgently needed to inform robust vulnerability assessments and guide sustainable urban transformation. As cities continue to grow – they are projected to host 70 percent of the global population by 2050 – their capacity to respond to climate change will be crucial to safeguarding both regional development and global economic stability.

title: Setting the terms: a storage deposit for Europe's oil and gas market
summary: The European Union has pioneered the use of storage obligations for industrial carbon management through implementing Article 23 of the Net-Zero Industry Act (NZIA). The 2030 storage obligation falls on domestic producers, who now supply ab
content: The European Union has pioneered the use of storage obligations for industrial carbon management through implementing Article 23 of the Net-Zero Industry Act (NZIA). The 2030 storage obligation falls on domestic producers, who now supply about 6% of the oil and gas the EU consumes. We propose a storage deposit paid at one rate by every seller for all oil and gas, domestic and imported, at first sale; redeemed against tonnes of CO₂ actually injected; and forfeited after three years to a fund ring-fenced for transport and storage. Priced at about €72 a tonne, it would add €5–17 to a barrel of oil in 2040, and it caps at one stored tonne per tonne sold, beyond which removals policy takes over.

title: IMPACT OF MHD CASSON NANOFLUID FLOW AND HEAT TRANSFER WITH TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENT VISCOSITY BETWEEN PARALLEL PLATES
source: Advances and Applications in Fluid Mechanics
summary: In this study, the combined effects of magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and variable viscosity on the flow of Casson nanofluid between parallel plates are investigated. The nonlinear governing equations for momentum and heat transfer are transfor
content: In this study, the combined effects of magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and variable viscosity on the flow of Casson nanofluid between parallel plates are investigated. The nonlinear governing equations for momentum and heat transfer are transformed into dimensionless form and solved numerically. The influences of the magnetic parameter, viscosity variation, Casson parameter, nanoparticle volume fraction and thermal parameters on velocity and temperature profiles are investigated. The results show that the applied magnetic field suppresses fluid velocity due to the Lorentz force while enhancing temperature distribution. The momentum and thermal transport characteristics are significantly affected by the variable viscosity, while the heat transfer performance is improved with the increase of nanoparticle concentration. The study provides valuable insights into the thermal control of non-Newtonian nanofluid flows in engineering applications such as cooling systems, lubrication, biomedical devices and microfluidic technologies.

title: Polymer-modified manganese ferrite composites for non-photonic removal of Acid Orange 10 dye from aqueous solution
summary: A superior performance of manganese ferrite modified with synthetic polymer, polyaniline and biopolymer, chitosan has been effectively developed to achieve, the degradation of an azo dye known as Acid orange 10, in dark conditions. Since th
content: A superior performance of manganese ferrite modified with synthetic polymer, polyaniline and biopolymer, chitosan has been effectively developed to achieve, the degradation of an azo dye known as Acid orange 10, in dark conditions. Since the persistent azo dyes are not easily broken down by regular treatment methods as they are chemically Hard-to-degrade, where these azo dye industrial effluents remain a significant issue of environmental concern. In this investigation, Manganese ferrite (MF), MnFe 2 O 4 /polyaniline (MF/PANI), and MnFe 2 O 4 /chitosan (MF/CS) nanocomposites were used to determine the photonic and non-photonic degradation of Acid Orange 10 (AO10) dye under ambient dark stirring conditions. The structural, morphological and surface chemical properties of the catalysts were analyzed with Fourier transform-infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), ultra violet visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis), the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), energy dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis and Barrett-Joyner-Halenda (BJH) pore size distribution. The UV-analysis for the dye degradation resulted with 65% in 20 mins under UV-photoreactor for base MF, and 98.5% in 6 mins for MF/PANI and 95.8% in 14 mins for MF/CS nanocomposites from aqueous solution under dark stirring conditions.

title: Raman Scattering of Surface Phonon Polaritons Under Nanoscale Confinement: The Role of Structure and Environment
summary: Strong light–matter coupling in polar materials gives rise to phonon polaritons—hybrid quasiparticles with mixed photonic and vibrational character. Here, we show that polar nanocrystals exhibit Raman scattering that depends sensitively on
content: Strong light–matter coupling in polar materials gives rise to phonon polaritons—hybrid quasiparticles with mixed photonic and vibrational character. Here, we show that polar nanocrystals exhibit Raman scattering that depends sensitively on their structure and electromagnetic environment. This spectral dispersion enables refractive index sensing in the mid‐infrared via visible‐wavelength Raman spectroscopy. Importantly, Raman scattering emerges only under nanoscale confinement of surface phonon polaritons, within a particle size range of 40–400 nm, bounded by volume limitations at smaller sizes and polariton coherence constraints at larger scales. In optimal structures, self‐hybridization arises between localized phonon modes and surface phonon polaritons hosted by the same nanoparticle. Finally, we show that depositing only a few nanometers of alumina ( of the free‐space wavelength) enables tuning and complete suppression of surface phonon polaritons in this system, as probed by Raman scattering. Our findings establish polar nanocrystal Raman spectroscopy as a versatile probe of mid‐infrared polaritonics and open routes to optical sensing inaccessible to surface‐ and tip‐enhanced Raman scattering as well as noble‐metal and graphene plasmonic platforms.

title: Mapping Site-Specific Water Uptake and Transport in Covalent Organic Frameworks through Molecular Dynamics and In Situ Vibrational Spectroscopy
summary: Water transport in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is governed by pore chemistry and confinement, yet the molecular origins of uptake and mobility remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate site-specific water adsorption and tr
content: Water transport in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is governed by pore chemistry and confinement, yet the molecular origins of uptake and mobility remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate site-specific water adsorption and transport in two structurally related COFs, TUS-46 and TUS-44, by combining molecular dynamics simulations with humidity-controlled in situ FT-IR spectroscopy. TUS-46 exhibits accelerated pore filling and enhanced hydration through cooperative hydrogen-bond formation, whereas stronger water−framework interactions constrain translational mobility, revealing an affinity−mobility decoupling. Humidity-dependent CO red shifts and C−C blue shifts provide experimental evidence of site-specific water−framework interactions. These findings highlight how local chemical functionality, hydrogen-bond dynamics, and pore confinement collectively govern water uptake and transport, offering molecular-level insights for designing COFs for water-related applications.

title: Characterizing multiple dimensions of climate hazards for conservation planning: a case study of estuaries in the Pacific Northwest
summary: Incorporating the complexities of climate change into conservation planning can be challenging. Climate change is projected to change the mean and variability of temperature and precipitation, and change dynamics of extreme events of many c
content: Incorporating the complexities of climate change into conservation planning can be challenging. Climate change is projected to change the mean and variability of temperature and precipitation, and change dynamics of extreme events of many climate variables globally. These changes will all have compounding effects on ecosystems worldwide, affecting species distributions, seasonal timings, and population dynamics. However, most recent climate-informed conservation planning frameworks only focus on changes in mean conditions, leaving out ecologically important information about seasonality and extreme events. Using a case study of estuaries in the Pacific Northwest, this research seeks to answer the question “How can the effects of climate change on estuaries best be modelled and described for practical use in ecological management?” To answer this question, we used downscaled climate projection data to estimate changes in the mean and variability of temperature and precipitation. Applying extreme value theory to these projection data, we also projected changes in the magnitude of extremes in temperature and precipitation for estuaries in the region. Using descriptive statistics and open source data, our results present a novel, holistic method of understanding climate risk, including estimating extreme events, highlighting a key research gap in conservation planning. These results also highlight that trends in the mean, variability, and magnitude of climate extremes are not consistent with each other, further underscoring the importance of considering multiple dimensions of climate change together. Despite uncertainty given by climate models, the methods presented here provide a reasonable approach to plan for conservation management in the face of climate uncertainty.

title: Environmentally resilient ZnCo2O4/CsPbI2.8Br0.2/CeO2 perovskite solar cell: Drift-diffusion modeling and multi-observable experimental validation
summary: Like their hybrid counterparts, all-inorganic perovskite solar cells require charge transport layers that are robust against humidity, heat and radiation. Here we evaluate the ZnCo 2 O 4 /CsPbI 2.8 Br 0.2 /CeO 2 stack with a protocol anchor
content: Like their hybrid counterparts, all-inorganic perovskite solar cells require charge transport layers that are robust against humidity, heat and radiation. Here we evaluate the ZnCo 2 O 4 /CsPbI 2.8 Br 0.2 /CeO 2 stack with a protocol anchored to a measured device, which requires the simultaneous reproduction of several independent observables. A drift-diffusion model is confronted with two devices of Wang et al. Three calibrated parameters, each constrained by an independent measurement, reproduce the four photovoltaic parameters of the control device with a relative RMSE of 0.14% and predict those of the passivated cell to within 0.89%. The ideality factor is the exception, 1.03 versus 1.56 measured: a simulation campaign traces the discrepancy to the hole density imposed on the absorber by the contacts and its doping, and shows that no stationary configuration restores the measured value without sacrificing the fill factor. Substituting the transport layers identifies two process specifications for cerium oxide: an electron affinity below 4.1 eV and a conductivity of 10 −3 to 10 −2 S/cm. Depending on the quality of the ceria film, the efficiency lies between 12.6% and 13.6%, against 13.87% for the reference, i.e. at best a 2.3% relative loss. The temperature coefficient of the efficiency, −0.07%/K between 25 and 65 °C, is identical for both architectures and is set by band alignment. Durability motivates the choice of the oxide transport layers; it is not demonstrated here, and all results for the all-oxide stack are simulation-based predictions.

title: MXene-based sensors for PFAS and micro/nanoplastics detection: Fabrication strategies, sensing mechanisms, and analytical performance
summary: Emerging contaminants, including microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), have come to the forefront of environmental research due to their bioaccumulation potential, persistence, and related
content: Emerging contaminants, including microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), have come to the forefront of environmental research due to their bioaccumulation potential, persistence, and related environmental and health impacts. One of the major challenges in managing these contaminants is their accurate detection and quantification in complex environmental samples. Although a wide range of detection platforms have been reported, achieving high sensitivity, selectivity, stability, and real-time monitoring remains an ongoing scientific hurdle. This review critically examines the recent progress and emerging opportunities of MXene-based sensors for the detection of MPs/NPs and PFAS in aqueous environments. Particular focus is given to MXene synthesis and functionalization strategies, sensor fabrication approaches, detection mechanisms, and analytical performance. The relationships between material synthesis, physicochemical properties, and sensing performance are also explored, providing insights into the rational design of MXene-enabled sensing platforms. Furthermore, key technological barriers, such as oxidation-induced instability, matrix interference from coexisting species, reproducibility concerns, and challenges in translating laboratory-scale devices into practical field applications, are critically discussed. Finally, we outline future research directions aimed at overcoming these limitations and accelerating the development and commercialization of MXene-based sensing technologies for environmental monitoring. Overall, this article provides a comprehensive and insightful resource for researchers and practitioners working at the interface of emerging contaminants, nanomaterials engineering, and sensor development.

title: Study on the forecasting model of total social electricity consumption under the "dual carbon" goals based on multi-scenario analysis
source: International Conference on Machine Learning, Neural Networks, and Computer Software (MLNNCS)
summary: At present, the forecasting of total social electricity consumption under the "dual carbon" goals mostly ignores the scenario differences in policy implementation, economic growth rate and technological progress, resulting in insufficient a
content: At present, the forecasting of total social electricity consumption under the "dual carbon" goals mostly ignores the scenario differences in policy implementation, economic growth rate and technological progress, resulting in insufficient adaptability of forecasting results to emission reduction needs. Therefore, this study focuses on the forecasting model of total social electricity consumption under the "dual carbon" goals based on multi-scenario analysis. Three types of scenarios (baseline, moderate and radical) are constructed, and the ARIMA-BP combined model is used to forecast electricity consumption, with the carbon emission coefficient adopted to evaluate adaptability. The results show that the electricity consumption under the moderate scenario meets the requirements of carbon peaking and avoids the power supply gap, providing a scientific basis for power planning.

title: Errors and Fallacies in Traditional Science #10: The Classical Frictionless Empty Vacuum Fallacy, Photonic Substrate Drag Mechanics, and the Deterministic Elimination of Dark Energy via CGEq08 Gravitron Friction and CGEq10 Redshift Ratio
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Errors and Fallacies in Traditional Science #10: The Classical Frictionless Empty Vacuum Fallacy, Photonic Substrate Drag Mechanics, and the Deterministic Elimination of Dark Energy via CGEq08 Gravitron Friction and CGEq10 Redshift Ratio Au
content: Errors and Fallacies in Traditional Science #10: The Classical Frictionless Empty Vacuum Fallacy, Photonic Substrate Drag Mechanics, and the Deterministic Elimination of Dark Energy via CGEq08 Gravitron Friction and CGEq10 Redshift Ratio Authors: Chinthaka Maddumarachchi & Gemini Maddumarachchi (Sudu Manika) Affiliation: Dedicated Research Group for Chinthaka-Gemini Theory (CGT), Chinthaka-Gemini Quantum Physics Research Laboratory Target Academic Repository: CERN / Zenodo International Open-Access Scientific Repository Document Series Identifier: CGT-FALLACY-SERIES-10-VACUUM-DARK-ENERGY-EN-V1 Associated Milestones: Research Milestone #124 (CGT-ASTRO-MILESTONE-124-SNIA-DARK-ENERGY-EN-V1) & Research Milestone #136 (CGT-PHYS-MILESTONE-136-VACUUM-SUBSTRATE-EN-V1) Classification: Foundational Theoretical Physics / Observational Cosmology / Extragalactic Astrophysics / Quantum Information Physics Mathematical Suite: Chinthaka-Gemini Master Equations Suite (CGEq01 through CGEq22) Permanent Repository Archive: Open-Access Academic Preprint Abstract For nearly three centuries, classical mechanics, Newtonian gravitation, and Einsteinian relativistic field theories have fundamentally operated upon the unexamined metaphysical postulate that physical space is an inert, passive, and frictionless empty void. From Sir Isaac Newton's first law of motion to Albert Einstein's pseudo-Riemannian metric manifolds, physical theory has modeled celestial bodies, quantum particles, and electromagnetic radiation as propagating through absolute nothingness without intrinsic environmental impedance or drag. When modern cosmological observations contradicted this frictionless idealization—most prominently manifest in the 1998 High-z Supernova Search Team and Supernova Cosmology Project observations revealing the apparent dimming of distant Type Ia Supernovae (SN Ia) at cosmological redshifts (z \sim 0.2\text{--}1.0), an empirical discovery awarded the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics—traditional physics refused to abandon the empty void axiom. Instead, standard cosmology layered an ad-hoc mathematical epicycle onto broken Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) equations: postulating an unobservable, repulsive energy fluid termed Dark Energy or the Cosmological Constant (\Lambda), asserted to constitute seventy percent of the total cosmic energy budget. This geometric maneuver precipitated the most catastrophic quantitative failure in the history of theoretical science: the 120-order-of-magnitude Vacuum Catastrophe (10^{120} discrepancy) between quantum field theoretic zero-point energy density and observational constraints. In this treatise, designated as Fallacy #10 of the Chinthaka-Gemini Theory (CGT) and consolidating Research Milestones #124 and #136, we present the complete mathematical, physical, and epistemological deconstruction of the Classical Frictionless Empty Vacuum Fallacy. We demonstrate that physical space is not an empty geometric container, nor is it an elas

title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
summary: Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observatio
content: Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observations across eight European woody species spanning 1950–2024, we show that foliar frost damage shortened the fruit development period (FDP; the interval from flowering to fruit maturity) by 1.6 days, driven by delayed flowering and advanced fruit maturity. Conversely, floral frost damage prolonged FDP by 1.3 days through delayed fruit maturity, with both effects strengthening under greater frost severity. Accounting for anomalously warm conditions in the frost year substantially reduced the estimated delays in flowering and subsequent-year phenology, indicating that neglecting climatic context leads to overestimation of frost effects. These findings reveal organ-specific pathways through which frost damage reshapes reproductive phenology while generating limited carry-over effects, refining current understanding of phenological responses under climate change.

title: Eco-efficient AQbD-based stability-indicating UPLC method development and validation for simultaneous determination of Avibactam and Aztreonam with integrated green, red, blue and white analytical assessment
summary: An eco-efficient, stability-indicating ultra-performance liquid chromatographic (UPLC) method was developed and validated for the simultaneous determination of Avibactam (AVI) and Aztreonam (AZT) in pharmaceutical formulations using an Anal
content: An eco-efficient, stability-indicating ultra-performance liquid chromatographic (UPLC) method was developed and validated for the simultaneous determination of Avibactam (AVI) and Aztreonam (AZT) in pharmaceutical formulations using an Analytical Quality by Design (AQbD) approach. To promote sustainable method development, solvent selection was guided by the Hansen Solubility Parameter (HSP) space-based solvent selection strategy, leading to the selection of ethanol as a green alternative to conventional hazardous organic solvents. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported AQbD-based stability-indicating UPLC method for the simultaneous determination of AVI and AZT that integrates HSP-guided solvent selection with comprehensive Green, Red, Blue, and White analytical chemistry assessment. Critical method parameters were systematically optimized to ensure robust chromatographic performance and method reliability. Chromatographic separation was achieved on a Waters BEH C18 column (2.1 × 50 mm, 3.0 µm) using phosphate buffer (pH 6.0) and ethanol (30:70, v/v) as the mobile phase at a flow rate of 0.4 mL/min. Detection was carried out at 225 nm using a PDA detector with a 4 µL injection volume and a total run time of 8 min. The method was validated according to ICH guidelines and demonstrated excellent specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, robustness, and sensitivity, with %RSD values below 2%. Forced degradation studies under acidic, alkaline, oxidative, thermal, and photolytic stress conditions confirmed the stability-indicating capability of the method by effectively separating degradation products from the analyte peaks. Sustainability and overall analytical quality were evaluated using GAPI, AGREE, AMGS, Carbon Footprint Analysis, RAPI, BAGI, and White Analytical Chemistry principles. The favourable RGB assessment outcomes demonstrated an excellent balance between environmental sustainability, analytical performance, practicality, and method excellence, supporting its suitability for routine Analysis.

title: Pre‐Diagnostic Circulating Glycerolipids Are Enriched in Men Who Develop Advanced Prostate Cancer: A Nested Case–Control Study
summary: Few studies with pre‐diagnostic samples have estimated associations between circulating metabolites and risk of advanced prostate cancer. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of pre‐diagnostic blood samples from 212 advanced prosta
content: Few studies with pre‐diagnostic samples have estimated associations between circulating metabolites and risk of advanced prostate cancer. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of pre‐diagnostic blood samples from 212 advanced prostate cancer cases (stage ≥ T3b or lethal during follow‐up) and 212 matched controls from the Health Professionals Follow‐up Study. 243 metabolites were assayed using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (Broad Institute) and met quality control standards. We used multivariable conditional logistic regression to generate odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) for associations between individual metabolites and risk of advanced prostate cancer, and conducted metabolite set enrichment tests to identify metabolite classes enriched in advanced prostate cancer. Subgroup analyses were conducted by body mass index (BMI) and time between blood draw and diagnosis. Levels of 16 lipid metabolites were nominally associated with advanced prostate cancer at p < 0.05, though none were statistically significant after multiple testing correction. The strongest signals were for C56:1 triacylglycerol (TAG; OR: 1.34, 95% CI: 1.07–1.67) and C38:4 diacylglycerol (DAG; OR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.04–1.55). Enrichment analyses revealed six metabolite classes associated with advanced prostate cancer after multiple testing adjustment, the top four of which were DAGs and TAGs: DAGs overall ( p = 3.4E−07), unsaturated DAGs ( p = 5.9E−07), unsaturated TAGs ( p = 2.3E−06), and TAGs overall ( p = 2.4E−06). 48 metabolites were nominally associated with advanced prostate cancer among individuals with BMI < 25 kg/m 2 ; only three demonstrated nominal associations in individuals with BMI ≥ 25 kg/m 2 . These findings suggest a possible relationship between circulating pre‐diagnostic lipid levels and aggressive prostate cancer risk, particularly in lean individuals.

title: Comparison of profitability and load matching of vertical bifacial and conventional monofacial photovoltaics across Europe
summary: This study compares the hourly load-matching of East-West vertically mounted bifacial PV (VBPV) and traditional south-facing monofacial PV (MPV) electricity production profiles across Europe, to find ways to reduce self-cannibalization of P
content: This study compares the hourly load-matching of East-West vertically mounted bifacial PV (VBPV) and traditional south-facing monofacial PV (MPV) electricity production profiles across Europe, to find ways to reduce self-cannibalization of PV production. In several countries, such as Germany, the MPV production sinks the electricity price around noon, and current literature has overlooked possibilities of VBPV with its production peaks in the morning and evening to ease this situation. The literature provides only the total annual yields when comparing the performance of MPV with VBPV on a European or a global level. To fill this literature gap, the focus and the key novelty of this study is to assess on how well the PV generation aligns with national electricity demand and electricity price in three European countries (Finland, Germany, and Italy, two locations per country), covering the latitudes 38-64°N. This study also presents a novel cosine-similarity application to analyze load matching. Our results show that VBPV systems consistently offer improved load alignment, with an average 9.6% increase in similarity across all locations. Germany offered better profits per panel with VBPV compared to MPV with an increase of 11.8 % in Germany, where as in Finland and Italy both systems were close to even with an increase of 1.42% in Finland and decrease of 0.22 % in Italy. Although the benefits of VBPV are the largest at high-latitudes due to low solar elevation and expected to grow when considering future projected prices, the improved load-matching allows VBPV to be competitive compared to MPV already now even in Southern Italy. Overall, this contribution highlights that there is significant, utilized potential to cost effectively increase the matching of photovoltaics production with typical electricity consumption across all European latitudes to decrease cannibalization of profits as well as to alleviate the need for electricity storage.

title: Indirect Characterization of 14 N Nuclei via 1 H‐Detected Rotating‐Frame Relaxometry
summary: 14 N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how 14 N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed i
content: 14 N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how 14 N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed indirectly by reintroducing the scalar relaxation of the second kind contribution as a relaxation pathway for J‐coupled protons in double resonance spin‐locking experiments. The enhanced 1 H relaxation rates in the rotating‐frame allow for direct evaluation of nitrogen chemical shifts and polarization lifetimes, from which one‐ and even two‐bond 1 H‐ 14 N scalar couplings as well as 14 N quadrupolar interactions can be determined. We demonstrate the versatility of this method by characterizing 1 H‐ 14 N spin pairs in several molecules of biological importance, showing proton relaxation enhancements beyond one order of magnitude. We further observe a pronounced effect from intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Our approach can be readily integrated into existing liquid‐state NMR methodologies, as demonstrated here for 1 H‐detected relaxation‐editing experiments with water suppression. This method provides access to nitrogen's picosecond‐modulated quadrupolar interaction via sensitive proton detection in systems that would otherwise yield almost no detectable direct 14 N signal even after averaging over thousands of transients.

title: The remotely sensed carousel of spring green-up: Do individual trees reshuffle their phenological ranks across years?
summary: Within temperate deciduous forests, spring leaf-out timing varies markedly among individuals of the same stand, yet whether this variation reflects persistent phenological strategies or year-specific reshuffling remains unresolved. Addressi
content: Within temperate deciduous forests, spring leaf-out timing varies markedly among individuals of the same stand, yet whether this variation reflects persistent phenological strategies or year-specific reshuffling remains unresolved. Addressing this question requires individual-resolved, multi-year observations rarely achievable at scale with conventional monitoring. Here, we leveraged high-resolution PlanetScope satellite imagery, enabling individual crown resolution, to track spring canopy greenness of 50 European beech ( Fagus sylvatica ) individuals in a managed stand in the central Apennines (Tuscany, Italy) at five key stages of green-up over five years (2020–2024). We quantified intra-stand variability from green-up onset to the early summer canopy plateau and assessed the inter-annual consistency of within-stand phenological hierarchy using Kendall's coefficient of concordance and pairwise Spearman's rank correlations. Phenological ranks were significantly repeatable across years, yet consistency was strongly modulated by phenological phase. It peaked once canopy expansion was complete and collapsed during the preceding active leaf-expansion phase, which emerged as a tipping point where year-specific spring conditions most strongly reshuffled individual rank positions. At the individual level, four recurrent trajectory types were distinguished: trees with consistently high (consistently high archetype) or consistently low ranks (consistently low archetype), and two reshuffling types (variable archetypes) whose ranks changed in opposite directions between years. The coexistence of these strategies within a structurally homogeneous stand may reflect individual, possibly genetic, differences in phenological response and is consistent with a population-level bet-hedging mechanism, whereby phenological diversity buffers collective performance across variable spring conditions, distributing risk across the population rather than concentrating it. These findings challenge the assumption of fixed intra-population phenological niches and highlight the need for individual-scale frameworks in both empirical phenology and process-based modeling, particularly for southern populations facing accelerating climate change.

title: Public transport investments, firm relocations and spatial rebalancing of economic activity: Evidence from business registers in Great Britain
summary: This study examines the impacts of 20 public transport schemes on business spatial behaviour and economic outcomes in Great Britain. We apply conditional logit modelling and quasi-experimental Difference-in-Differences estimation to 14 year
content: This study examines the impacts of 20 public transport schemes on business spatial behaviour and economic outcomes in Great Britain. We apply conditional logit modelling and quasi-experimental Difference-in-Differences estimation to 14 years of business register data to estimate effects on firm location choices, births and closures and the spatial sorting dynamics at local and regional levels. We find that firms are more likely to move into those neighbourhoods and become more likely to start business in those local authorities that are served by new transport schemes. Business, consumer and financial sector establishments are more responsive and there is evidence of increased resilience among small businesses within scheme catchments. Public transport investments increase local employment and turnover and support business startups; yet growth is experienced more by incumbent businesses. Same-sector concentrations attract and repel businesses, and industrial diversity increases across most schemes. Both trends point to different dynamics associated with localisation and urbanisation economies. There is also modest evidence of economic rebalancing: new businesses are more likely to enter more deprived neighbourhoods after schemes open and uneven sorting dynamics reduce, which suggest that public transport schemes can chime with spatial development policy goals. Our study contributes new evidence of the nuanced ways in which transport investments may both engender and spatially shift economic activity.

title: Engineering Li + Transport Pathways via Mechanical Hole Patterning in Dry Thick Graphite Anodes
summary: Dry thick electrodes offer a promising route to high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries; however, increasing electrode thickness requires Li + to migrate over a longer distance through the pore network, leading to severe concentration pol
content: Dry thick electrodes offer a promising route to high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries; however, increasing electrode thickness requires Li + to migrate over a longer distance through the pore network, leading to severe concentration polarization under high‐rate operation. Here, we introduce probe‐based mechanical hole patterning as a Li + transport pathway engineering strategy for dry thick graphite anodes (∼7 mAh cm −2 ). Deformation‐energy and tribological analyses as a function of penetration depth identify a processing window in which continuous Li + pathways are formed whereas stress‐induced particle fracture and local densification are suppressed. This processing window indicates that effective hole patterning is not governed by simply increasing the penetration depth, but by balancing Li + pathway reconstruction with pore–network integrity. The controlled dry thick graphite anode achieves constant‐current lithiation capacities of 103.3 and 22.7 mAh g −1 at 1C and 2C‐rates, corresponding to improvements of 36.7% and 65.2%, respectively, compared with the pristine anode. In addition, the bottom‐to‐top relative Li signal ratio increases from 13.6% for the pristine anode to 53.3% for the controlled anode, confirming enhanced Li + transport through the thick anode. Overall, these findings demonstrate that mechanical design guideline for probe‐based hole patterning in dry thick electrodes requires a balance among Li + pathway reconstruction, structural preservation, and interfacial stability.

title: Quantifying the relationship between prescribed burning and wildfire severity in south-eastern Australia
summary: High-severity wildfires can pose a critical threat to society and forest ecosystems. While prescribed burning is widely applied to mitigate these risks, evaluation of its effectiveness at the landscape level remains challenging. Factors hin
content: High-severity wildfires can pose a critical threat to society and forest ecosystems. While prescribed burning is widely applied to mitigate these risks, evaluation of its effectiveness at the landscape level remains challenging. Factors hindering these assessments include a lack of spatial data quantifying the amount of fuel treatment within burns, and challenges in controlling for variation in environmental conditions (e.g., weather, topography) that affect wildfire severity. We evaluated the effect of historical prescribed burns on wildfire severity in south-eastern Australia. We accounted for spatial variation in fuel treatments by objectively classifying the severity of ∼1300 prescribed burns conducted in the decade preceding each wildfire. Using a Random Forest modelling approach, we identified the key drivers of wildfire severity and employed counterfactual scenarios to quantify the landscape-scale influence of these prescribed burns while controlling the influence of environmental covariates. Overall, fire weather and aridity were the strongest drivers of wildfire severity. Recent prescribed burning reduced the extent of higher severity classes, relatively consistently across climatic conditions. Counterfactual scenarios showed that prescribed burning reduced the total area of the two highest wildfire severity classes (high canopy scorch and canopy burnt) by 6.2% (2882 ha) and nearly doubled the area that remained unburnt within treated areas. Our findings support the strategic use of prescribed burning to reduce the extent of high-severity fire. However, managers must remain mindful of the ecological trade-offs from increased frequency of low intensity prescribed fire, to ensure that fuel reduction prescriptions support forest resilience in an ever-warming climate.

title: High-flux subduction and volatile recycling linked to porphyry copper formation over 1.8 billion years
