summary: Porphyry copper deposits supply more than 60% of the world's copper, yet their occurrence through geological time is highly uneven despite the long-lived presence of subduction. Existing models emphasize magmatic fluid evolution and host ro
content: Porphyry copper deposits supply more than 60% of the world's copper, yet their occurrence through geological time is highly uneven despite the long-lived presence of subduction. Existing models emphasize magmatic fluid evolution and host rock properties, but these parameters do not explain global spatio-temporal variations in porphyry copper occurrence. Such deposits are scarce during assembly of the Proterozoic Nuna and Rodinia supercontinents. In contrast, intervals of continental dispersal and the assembly of Pangea are rich in porphyry copper deposits. Here, we investigate tectonic and geochemical factors associated with long-term variations in porphyry copper formation using machine learning. By integrating a global porphyry copper deposit database with reconstructions of plate boundaries and now-subducted oceanic plates since 1.8 Ga, we identify a nonlinear transition in porphyry copper likelihood when the mean age of subducting oceanic crust exceeds ∼130 Myr. This threshold marks a shift from high-flux tectonic regimes with rapid convergence and efficient recycling of oceanic lithosphere to lower-flux regimes typical of Proterozoic supercontinent assemblies. Pangea was an exception, retaining relatively high-flux subduction conditions despite continental aggregation, reflecting long-lived Tethys and western North American arc systems. Sediment delivery into trenches, convergence rates and subducting crustal age emerge as the strongest tectonic predictors of porphyry copper occurrence, indicating that porphyry copper systems form where efficient tectonic transport of volatile-rich and chemically modified slab material into subduction zones sustains fertile magmatic systems and links metallogenic cycles to tectonic cycles, conditional on the adopted plate reconstruction and the preserved deposit record.

title: Weldability of Fe–9 Wt Pct Ni Binary Alloys of Meteoritic Composition with Phosphorous and Sulfur Impurities
summary: Fe–Ni asteroids and meteorites contain metallic elements in their native state that are potentially useful structural materials for in situ resource utilization materials to meet future space colonization needs. Although Fe–Ni alloys have h
content: Fe–Ni asteroids and meteorites contain metallic elements in their native state that are potentially useful structural materials for in situ resource utilization materials to meet future space colonization needs. Although Fe–Ni alloys have high strength and ductility and ability to resist the harsh conditions of space, extraterrestrial Fe–Ni asteroids and meteorites have poor mechanical properties and are not suited for fabrication due to their high concentrations of P, S, and C impurities. Metallurgical refinement of asteroidal Fe–Ni metal will be required to make useful alloys from them, and this study investigates the level of refinement required to meet weldability needs through the analysis of Fe–9 pct Ni binary alloys synthesized with controlled levels of P and S impurities. Small cast buttons, and electron beam welds made on them, show target levels for P and S refinement of Fe–Ni meteorites to be similar to those required for steel and austenitic stainless-steel alloys.

title: Effect of Photoelectrochemical Conditions on Cu2WO4 Stability during CO2 Conversion
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Photoelectrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (PEC–CO2RR) using p-type semiconductors offers a sustainable pathway to transform this greenhouse gas into value-added chemicals. Cu2WO4, applied as a photocathode for PEC–CO2RR, exhibits suitable
content: Photoelectrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (PEC–CO2RR) using p-type semiconductors offers a sustainable pathway to transform this greenhouse gas into value-added chemicals. Cu2WO4, applied as a photocathode for PEC–CO2RR, exhibits suitable optoelectronic properties but low long-term stability. In this work, we investigate the degradation process of arc-synthesized Cu2WO4 during PEC–CO2RR by systematically varying the applied bias and combining ICP-OES, XRD, XPS, SEM, and EDS analyses with in situ Raman spectroscopy to monitor structural changes in real time. The results reveal that the electrolyte pH, irradiation, and applied potential promote structural changes in Cu2WO4 and lixiviation of Cu and W, with a relatively lower Cu:W concentration in the electrolyte. In the dark, 0.3 V vs RHE produced Cu0 as a product from Cu2WO4 degradation, which is attributed to an electrochemical process that also released WO42– in the electrolyte. Irradiation below 0.4 V vs RHE leads to Cu0 and Cu2O formation, and the proposed degradation reaction involved hydroxide anions in the electrode vicinity. The W leaching was suppressed in the borate buffer, attributed to a lower availability of hydroxide anions near the electrode surface. This study provides an understanding of the effects of applied potential, illumination, and electrolyte pH on Cu2WO4 instability, which is essential for improving its applicability in PEC devices.

title: Foaming and crystallization behaviors of natural ramie fiber reinforced poly(lactic acid) composites
source: Journal of Reinforced Plastics and Composites
summary: The microcellular foams based on biocompatible and biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) produced by supercritical fluids can improve the toughness, achieve lightweighting, and reduce production cost. This study proposes an eco-friendly appro
content: The microcellular foams based on biocompatible and biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) produced by supercritical fluids can improve the toughness, achieve lightweighting, and reduce production cost. This study proposes an eco-friendly approach by incorporating ramie fiber (RF) with PLA to enhance the foaming ability without compromising the biodegradable nature. In this work, the influence of foaming pressure and temperature in one-step autoclave press relief process on the foaming and crystallization behaviors of composite foams are systematically researched, and the influencing laws and mechanisms are clarified. Experimental results indicate that, the maximum expansion ratio can be reached 10.43, when using processing temperature of 112°C, pressure of 15 MPa, and foaming time of 40 min, respectively. The thermal performance of RF-reinforced PLA composite foam is significantly influenced by the foaming temperature and CO 2 plasticizing effect. PLA/RF foam manufactured at low foaming temperature (100–115°C) and low saturation pressure (10–17.5 MPa) shows double peaks of melting, and in contrast high foaming temperature (120°C) and high saturation pressure (20 MPa) assigns a single peak of melting. This study provides an effective autoclave foaming method using physical agent CO 2 for preparing a green natural fiber composite foam, with potential application value in packaging, automotive/aircraft interior decoration, building decoration, and other fields.

title: Combining Fiber Optic Sensing with Interrupts and Pulses for Improved State of Health Analysis of Lithium-Ion Batteries
summary: This study combines Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) optical sensing with Galvanostatic Intermittent Titration Technique protocols to examine relaxation dynamics in commercial LiCoO2-based cells, using either graphite or 10% SiOx/graphite composit
content: This study combines Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) optical sensing with Galvanostatic Intermittent Titration Technique protocols to examine relaxation dynamics in commercial LiCoO2-based cells, using either graphite or 10% SiOx/graphite composite anodes over 400 charge−discharge cycles. Tandem polymer-based and silica-based FBG sensors attached to the external casing of the cells allow for separate monitoring of strain and temperature over long periods of cycling with sustained accuracy. This non-invasive approach enables the collection of thermal and mechanical relaxation dynamics over the full range of state of charge and relevant scope of state of health during rest periods, inherent to any cell operation scenario. We show that the unique thermomechanical relaxation dynamics associated with cycling interrupts and pulses can be used to enhance our understanding of battery operation, material dynamics, and degradation mechanisms, potentially leading to improved battery design, management strategies, and safety protocols in various applications ranging from consumer electronics to electric vehicles.

title: Isoniazid-Loaded Nano-Embedded Microparticles: Development, Optimization, and Physicochemical Characterization
summary: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis , with high global incidence and significant mortality. Isoniazid (ISN) is a first-line antituberculosis drug whose low permeability and rapid elimination may limit
content: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis , with high global incidence and significant mortality. Isoniazid (ISN) is a first-line antituberculosis drug whose low permeability and rapid elimination may limit its efficacy. Building upon our previous work on ISN-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)-chitosan polymeric nanoparticles (ISN-PLGA-CHI-PNs), the present study aimed to develop and optimize nano-embedded microparticles (NeMs) using spray drying and a Box-Behnken experimental design. The ISN-PLGA-CHI-PNs were incorporated into a lactose matrix, and the resulting ISN-NeMs were evaluated for redispersibility, colloidal stability, and physicochemical properties. The original PNs exhibited a particle size of 230 ± 0.70 nm, a positive zeta potential of 27.4 ± 0.26 mV, and physical stability over 150 days at 4 °C. Nanoparticle mucin interaction and cellular internalization by J774 macrophages were also observed. Following spray drying, the ISN-NeMs exhibited spherical morphology, geometric particle sizes ranging from 1 to 4 μm, and a moisture content of 4.86%. The experimentally selected formulation achieved a redispersion index of 0.95, with recovery of the nanoscale characteristics of the embedded PNs and preservation of colloidal stability after redispersion. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of converting ISN-loaded nanoparticle suspensions into dry, redispersible microparticulate formulations while maintaining their main physicochemical characteristics.

title: Anisotropic Conductivity of Thermally Activated and Field-Assisted Charge Transport in Cu–CQD–Cu Junctions
summary: Carbon Quantum Dots are promising nanomaterials for electronic transport and energy-harvesting applications because of their tunable conductivity, hopping transport and field-responsive charge dynamics. Anisotropic charge transport in Coppe
content: Carbon Quantum Dots are promising nanomaterials for electronic transport and energy-harvesting applications because of their tunable conductivity, hopping transport and field-responsive charge dynamics. Anisotropic charge transport in Copper-Carbon Quantum Dots-Copper junctions under the coupling of thermal and electric field effects is important for the design of advanced electronic devices. In this theory work we aim to develop a modified tensor-based conductivity model to study radial, azimuthal, and axial current transport in the junction under potential bias, temperature variation, and electric-field modulation. The resistivity tensor was expressed in terms of thermally activated hopping and field assisted barrier lowering mechanisms. The current densities were obtained in cylindrical coordinates. Results show strong anisotropic transport behavior, with the radial and azimuthal current densities showing a pronounced angular dependence governed by the conductivity tensor components. Higher temperature strongly enhances carrier activation, leading to larger transverse currents and less transport anisotropy. The transport is dominated by the axial current density and increases in a nonlinear way with temperature and electric field due to the field assisted activation similar to past studies. But, the novelty of this work is the development of a unified anisotropic tensor framework to simultaneously capture the angular, thermal and electric-field dependent charge transport in the junctions.

title: Recycled steel fibers reinforced concrete: review on fiber heterogeneity challenges and mechanical performance analysis
summary: Recent advancements in high-performance concrete have led to a growing demand for steel fiber reinforcement due to its potential to enhance the tensile strength and durability of concrete. However, the high cost and environmental impact of
content: Recent advancements in high-performance concrete have led to a growing demand for steel fiber reinforcement due to its potential to enhance the tensile strength and durability of concrete. However, the high cost and environmental impact of industrial steel fibers have raised concerns, prompting the exploration of sustainable alternatives. Recycled steel fibers (RSFs) have thus emerged as a promising solution. While studies have demonstrated promising benefits of RSF on concrete performance and environmental savings, the variability in its properties, geometry, and sources has limited its broader adoption. In response, this review explores available studies on RSF-reinforced concrete performance, highlighting variations in RSF properties and their influence on concrete. Correlations between manufacturing procedures and fiber heterogeneity were outlined in relation to available prediction approaches. Key parameters such as shape distribution and volumetric content were examined to evaluate performance variation. Additionally, recommendations addressing fiber heterogeneity were added based on the latest studies.

title: Transformation products of hydroxychloroquine produced by different oxidants in the presence of UVC radiation: Mechanism discussion and toxicity analysis
summary: The environmental fates of hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) and its transformation products (TPs) remain a cause for concern, mainly due to the increased use of the drug during the COVID-19 pandemic and the inability of wastewater treatment plants
content: The environmental fates of hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) and its transformation products (TPs) remain a cause for concern, mainly due to the increased use of the drug during the COVID-19 pandemic and the inability of wastewater treatment plants to eliminate recalcitrant organic compounds. This study investigated, for the first time, the use of UVC, UVC/H 2 O 2 , and UVC/S 2 O 8 2− processes to degrade HCQ in ultrapure water. Eleven initial TPs of HCQ degradation were identified by LC-QTOF MS analysis, nine of them not previously described in the literature. These TPs were formed by homolytic UVC cleavage and by the attack of HO • and/or SO 4 •– on the α carbon of aminoethanol. Although in silico (Q)SAR models predicted high mobility for TP 128 HCQ and TP 174 HCQ, and carcinogenicity for TP 261 HCQ and TP 279 HCQ, these TPs of concern were efficiently removed during the UVC/oxidant treatment. This demonstrated the ability of the process to eliminate both the target compound and its most hazardous TPs, although conclusions concerning actual toxicity mitigation remain tentative, in the absence of direct experimental toxicity assays.

title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
summary: In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuri
content: In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC + with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
summary: Anastomotic leaks are severe complications following gastrointestinal surgery. The shape conformability of powder-based hydrogels makes them potentially suitable for leak-sealing, but they typically cause undesirable tissue adhesion, prohib
content: Anastomotic leaks are severe complications following gastrointestinal surgery. The shape conformability of powder-based hydrogels makes them potentially suitable for leak-sealing, but they typically cause undesirable tissue adhesion, prohibiting clinical applications. Here we present a powder-based Janus hydrogel that forms in situ to simultaneously prevent anastomotic leaks and tissue adhesions. By rational regulation of dissolution and gelation kinetics, a powder mixture of chitosan lactate and oxidized chondroitin sulfate rapidly forms an adhesive porous scaffold in situ via amine-aldehyde condensation. A zwitterionic anti-adhesive layer is synthesized on the peritoneal side of the porous layer, creating a stable Janus structure via mechanical interlocking. The chemical and structural asymmetry between the serosal and peritoneal surfaces reconciles the conflicting demands of robust tissue integration, leakage prevention, and anti-adhesive safety. Further, the Janus hydrogel improves short- and long-term survival by reducing immune responses and perianastomotic adhesions, highlighting its potential for clinical translation in gastrointestinal surgery.

title: Design of Co–Cr substituted BaM/PANI composites for enhanced microwave absorption
source: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology
summary: This study details the design and optimization of Co 2+ /Cr 3+ substituted (BaFe 12 O 19 /polyaniline BaM/PANI) composites, BaCo x Cr x Fe 12-2x O 19 /PANI (ZP1 for x = 0.0, ZP2 for x = 0.6, and ZP3 for x = 0.8), for superior microwave abso
content: This study details the design and optimization of Co 2+ /Cr 3+ substituted (BaFe 12 O 19 /polyaniline BaM/PANI) composites, BaCo x Cr x Fe 12-2x O 19 /PANI (ZP1 for x = 0.0, ZP2 for x = 0.6, and ZP3 for x = 0.8), for superior microwave absorption performance. The M-type hexagonal structure was confirmed by XRD, showing slight unit cell contraction with doping. Magnetic analysis revealed that increasing Co–Cr substitution efficiently tunes the magnetic properties, leading to a significant decrease in saturation magnetization (M s ) from 45.92 emu/g (x = 0.0) to 22.55 emu/g (x = 0.8) and a notable reduction in coercivity (H c ). The tailored substitution level successfully balanced the dielectric and magnetic loss mechanisms, achieving optimal impedance matching for microwave absorption. Notably, the BaCo 0.8 Cr 0.8 Fe 10.4 O 19 /PANI composite (ZP3) exhibited the highest performance, achieving a minimum reflection loss (RL) of -41.01 dB at 11.31 GHz with a thin absorber thickness. These results demonstrate that Co–Cr substitution provides an effective strategy for creating high-performance, lightweight electromagnetic wave absorbers.

title: Quantitative and Mathematical Approaches to the Kinetics of Copper Enzyme Mimics: Bioinorganic Chemistry
source: Innovation of Chemistry & Materials for Sustainability
summary: Copper-containing enzymes and their synthetic mimics play important roles in oxidation and reduction reactions. Understanding the kinetics of these systems is essential for identifying reaction mechanisms, characterizing reactive intermedia
content: Copper-containing enzymes and their synthetic mimics play important roles in oxidation and reduction reactions. Understanding the kinetics of these systems is essential for identifying reaction mechanisms, characterizing reactive intermediates, and improving catalyst performance. In this study, we develop a quantitative kinetic and mathematical framework for analyzing copper enzyme mimics, including mononuclear and polynuclear copper complexes, copper-based nanozymes, and molecular catalysts. The framework combines mass-action or dinary differential equation models, quasi-steady-state and rapid-equilibrium approximations, Michaelis-Menten-type formulations, numerical integration, global fitting, sensitivity analysis, and parameter identifiability analysis. Experimental kinetic approaches, including stopped flow spectrophotometry and electrochemical measurements, are considered together with computational modeling to relate observable kinetic responses to microscopic rate constants. The proposed framework is applied to three representative classes of copper biomimetic systems: tyrosinase-like dicopper complexes, laccase-like multicopper oxidase mimics, and mononuclear copper monooxygenase mimics. The analysis demonstrates that these systems exhibit distinct kinetic signatures associated with copper-oxygen intermediate formation, proton-coupled electron transfer, electron-transfer processes, and substrate-triggered oxygen activation. Dimensionless parameters are introduced to characterize the relative contributions of protonation, substrate conversion, and oxygen binding to the overall catalytic behavior. The case studies further illustrate how global kinetic fitting and sensitivity and identifiability analyses can assist in distinguishing mechanistic regimes and estimating relevant kinetic parameters.

title: Wood-fibre-reinforced PLA/PBAT/Bio-PBS biocomposites: Formulation screening, processing, and property trade-offs
summary: To help reduce persistent plastic waste and its associated environmental impacts, biodegradable polymer alternatives are needed to replace conventional non-biodegradable petroleum-based plastics in suitable applications with appropriate end
content: To help reduce persistent plastic waste and its associated environmental impacts, biodegradable polymer alternatives are needed to replace conventional non-biodegradable petroleum-based plastics in suitable applications with appropriate end-of-life conditions. This study evaluated PLA/PBAT/Bio-PBS biocomposites reinforced with 30 wt% wood fibres to examine trade-offs among stiffness, toughness, thermal behaviour, and processability. Eleven formulations containing different polymer ratios and selected combinations of an impact modifier, coupling agents, and a lubricant were prepared by twin-screw extrusion and injection moulding. Tensile, flexural, and impact tests were performed, while melt flow index, thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, and dynamic mechanical analysis were used to assess processing-related and thermal behaviour. Pure PLA showed a tensile strength of 72.8 MPa, stiffness of approximately 3.2 GPa, elongation at break of 3.2%, and impact resistance of approximately 19.7 kJ/m². Wood-fibre addition increased flexural modulus by about 117%, up to 6500 MPa, but reduced elongation below 1% and impact strength to approximately 9.6 kJ/m². Incorporating PBAT and Bio-PBS partially recovered the ductility and impact resistance lost after wood-fibre incorporation, giving elongation values of 2.1–2.8% and impact strengths of 13.3–17.3 kJ/m², while remaining below neat PLA. The study therefore provides comparative formulation screening and quantified stiffness–toughness trade-offs. It does not demonstrate non-additive ternary synergy, reactive compatibilization, a specific phase morphology, complete-formulation biodegradability, or systematic processing optimization.

title: NiMnₓCr₂_ₓO₄/rGO nanocomposites for solar-light-driven photocatalytic degradation of methyl orange: Synergistic effects of Mn substitution and rGO incorporation
source: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology
summary: Nickel chromite (NCO) and Mn-substituted nickel chromite (NMCO) were synthesized by co-precipitation and their reduced graphene oxide (rGO) composites (NCO-rGO2 and NMCO-rGO3) were prepared by ultrasonication. XRD confirmed the spinel struc
content: Nickel chromite (NCO) and Mn-substituted nickel chromite (NMCO) were synthesized by co-precipitation and their reduced graphene oxide (rGO) composites (NCO-rGO2 and NMCO-rGO3) were prepared by ultrasonication. XRD confirmed the spinel structure, with crystallite sizes ranging from 20.68 to 27.78 nm. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy supported formation of the chromite lattice and incorporation of rGO, while photoluminescence measurements indicated lower charge-carrier recombination in the composites. The optical band-gap energy decreased from 3.32 eV for NCO to 2.52 eV for NMCO-rGO3. Under natural sunlight, NMCO-rGO3 achieved 92% removal of methyl orange (MO) within 105 min. The corresponding apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant was 0.023 min⁻¹. Scavenger experiments indicated that hydroxyl radicals made the largest contribution under the tested conditions. NMCO-rGO3 retained more than 85% removal efficiency after four cycles. These findings demonstrate that combined Mn substitution and rGO incorporation can improve the solar-light photocatalytic performance of nickel chromite.

title: Marine Streptomyces biomass as a novel functional feed additive for improving the health and growth of European seabass
summary: This study investigated the production of marine-derived Streptomyces griseus and Streptomyces mutabilis using seawater-based media and evaluated their efficacy as functional feed additives for European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax). Under
content: This study investigated the production of marine-derived Streptomyces griseus and Streptomyces mutabilis using seawater-based media and evaluated their efficacy as functional feed additives for European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax). Under optimized starch nitrate seawater conditions, S. griseus and S. mutabilis produced high biomass yields (24.8 g/L and 23.9 g/L, respectively). The dry biomass was nutrient-dense, with S. mutabilis containing 19.61 ± 0.74% protein and 1.91 ± 0.2% lipids, and S. griseus containing 16.43 ± 0.52% protein and 0.46 ± 0.03% lipids. In a 60-day feeding trial, fish fed diets supplemented with 1% or 2% of either strain (D2-D5) showed no significant differences in weight gain or specific growth rate compared to the control (D1); however, survival rates significantly increased from 80% in the control group to 95% in the optimal D3 group. Whole-body composition analysis revealed significantly elevated lipid content, rising from 2.98% in the control to 4.20% in D3 and 4.80% in D5, alongside a significant reduction in ash content. Notably, the D3 group (supplemented with 2% S. griseus) emerged as the optimal treatment, exhibiting peak total protein (5.31 g/dL) and globulin (3.52 g/dL) levels alongside the lowest indicators of metabolic tissue stress, including AST (11.75 IU/mg protein), ALT (20.83 IU/mg protein), and ALP (15.01 IU/mg protein). Furthermore, D3 showed the strongest antioxidant defense compared to the control (SOD: 143.50; CAT: 18.20; TAC: 3.12%; MDA: 34.93), registering peak SOD (185.50 IU/mg protein), CAT (26.07 IU/mg protein), and TAC (5.79%) activities, coupled with the lowest MDA lipid peroxidation levels (19.91 nmol/mg protein). Histological examination confirmed that supplementation promoted hepatic lipid accumulation and enhanced intestinal morphometry, including increased villous length, muscular layer thickness, and goblet cell numbers. These results indicate that marine Streptomyces, especially S. griseus at a 2% inclusion rate, improves survival, immune status, and antioxidant capacity, making them promising functional additives for sustainable aquaculture. KEY POINTS: • Marine Streptomyces yields reached 25 g/L using sustainable seawater media. • Streptomyces biomass supplements increased seabass survival to 95% and boosted SOD/CAT. • Dietary inclusion improved villous branching and intestinal goblet cell clarity.

title: An age calculator for high-latitude Quaternary foraminifera using amino acid racemization
summary: Dating deep-sea cores from polar regions is challenging because sedimentation rates can be variable and oxygen-isotope stratigraphy can be ineffective, making amino acid racemization an important alternative. We calibrated the rate of racem
content: Dating deep-sea cores from polar regions is challenging because sedimentation rates can be variable and oxygen-isotope stratigraphy can be ineffective, making amino acid racemization an important alternative. We calibrated the rate of racemization in Neogloboquadrina pachyderma , the dominant high-latitude planktic foraminifer, using 140 independently dated samples from 21 Arctic, Nordic Seas, North Atlantic, and Southern Ocean sites spanning 2 ka to 1.4 Ma. Racemization rates among these ocean basins differ less than among individual sites. Ages are based on aspartic acid, a more precise chronometer than glutamic acid, which, however, provides an independent check on the analysis. A publicly available age calculator returns formal uncertainty intervals incorporating calibration and measurement errors. Ages carry a realistic uncertainty of roughly ± 32% (66% level), insufficient to assign a sample to a specific Marine Isotope Stage but still useful for many polar marine sediment cores. A single age picks correctly between two candidate ages 90% of the time when they differ by a factor of 2.3 (e.g., 100 versus 230 ka). An independently dated horizon in the same core can reduce the uncertainty to ± 28%. Because comparisons are more precise than absolute ages, amino acid geochronology is best applied as a down-core series.

title: Upcycled Silicon-Rich Backgrinding Waste from the Semiconductor Industry into Catalytic-Magnetic Nanocomposites for Water Remediation
summary: Wafer backgrinding process in the semiconductor industry generates large volumes of dilute backgrinding wastewater (DBGW), resulting in the loss of approximately 70% of high-purity silicon in the form of polydisperse nanosized silicon-rich
content: Wafer backgrinding process in the semiconductor industry generates large volumes of dilute backgrinding wastewater (DBGW), resulting in the loss of approximately 70% of high-purity silicon in the form of polydisperse nanosized silicon-rich colloids. The high zeta potential (−38.7 mV) of the Si colloids further confirmed their strong colloidal stability and highlights their potential for engineering valorization. In this work, silicon-rich waste recovered from semiconductor DBGW was directly upcycled as a functional support for the construction of Si-PDDA-IOMNPs nanocomposites through layer-by-layer surface functionalization with poly(diallyldimethylammonium) chloride (PDDA) and iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles (IOMNPs), resulting in an open shell core–shell architecture. The potential application of magnetically responsive particles in water treatment as adsorbents and heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysts holds great promise for effective degradation and removal of pollutants from aqueous environments. This potential dual adsorbent-catalyst role was further evaluated with the organic dye removal studies using Methylene Blue (MB) and Methyl Orange (MO) as model systems. The Si-PDDA-IOMNPs nanocomposite exhibited high removal efficiencies toward MB (100%) and MO (94.25%) in the presence of H2O2, demonstrating its potential for combined adsorption and oxidative dye removal. Sedimentation kinetics and Derjaguin–Landau–Verwey–Overbeek (DLVO) analysis further revealed that the nanocomposite possesses a substantial energy barrier (∼25.4 kBT), which suppresses aggregation and improves colloidal stability compared to bare iron oxide nanoparticles. This work demonstrates a sustainable strategy for valorizing silicon-rich semiconductor backgrinding waste into a magnetically recoverable nanocomposite with potential Fenton-like catalytic functionality, integrating pollutant removal and post-treatment magnetic separation.

title: N‐Doped Coral Carbon for Synergistic Iodine Anchoring in High‐Capacity and Long‐Life Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
summary: Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are promising energy storage candidates owing to their high capacity and environmental friendliness. However, reported cathode materials suffer from low energy density and rapid capacity decay. In this
content: Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are promising energy storage candidates owing to their high capacity and environmental friendliness. However, reported cathode materials suffer from low energy density and rapid capacity decay. In this study, a coral‐like N‐doped carbon with in situ grown surface carbon nanotubes (CNC‐CNT) was synthesized as iodine host material through the pyrolysis of bimetallic core‐shell metal‐organic frameworks. This nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon framework with well‐developed micro/mesopores enables both chemical adsorption of C–I species and physical immobilization of iodine, while providing substantial additional electric double‐layer capacitive contributions. The specific capacity reaches 690.00 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 , significantly surpassing that of the AC cathode host of 558.00 mAh g −1 . Consequently, the I2@CNC‐CNT cathode delivers stable cycling over 8000 cycles and retains 464.40 mAh g −1 even at 5 A g −1 . The pouch cell delivers an iodine‐normalized capacity of 501.33 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , yielding a material‐level energy density of ∼780 Wh kg −1 at 1.55 V including host capacitance. The host‐subtracted iodine‐redox capacity is 422.00 mAh −1 . This study presents a CNC‐CNT‐derived carbon cathode strategy with facile synthesis, which leverages its hierarchical coral‐like architecture to significantly enhance the specific capacity and cycling stability of AZIBs.

title: Heterodyne-Detected Sum-Frequency Generation Spectroscopy at Two-Dimensional Material–Water Interfaces: A Practical Guide
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Water at two-dimensional (2D) material surfaces plays a central role in catalysis, electrochemistry, and nanofluidics. Molecular-level insights into their structure and dynamics at buried 2D material/water interfaces are essential for under
content: Water at two-dimensional (2D) material surfaces plays a central role in catalysis, electrochemistry, and nanofluidics. Molecular-level insights into their structure and dynamics at buried 2D material/water interfaces are essential for understanding interfacial mechanisms and guiding the design of functional systems. Heterodyne-detected sum-frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy provides a direct probe of interfacial water, but its quantitative application to 2D materials has been limited by the difficulty of extracting the intrinsic interfacial molecular response, which requires accurate phase measurement and rigorous Fresnel-factor corrections. In multilayer 2D material geometries, this challenge is further compounded by nanoconfined water trapped between the 2D material and its supporting material, the finite nonlinear response of the 2D material itself, and its crystallographic symmetry, all of which modulate both the amplitude and phase of the measured signal. Here, we present a practical protocol that enables robust, quantitative HD-SFG measurements at thin-film 2D material/water interfaces by explicitly accounting for thin-film interference and nanoconfined water as well as the intrinsic nonlinear response of the 2D material. Using SiO2-supported hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) thin films as a model system, we systematically investigate the roles of nanoconfined water, film thickness, crystallographic orientation, and substrate effects, demonstrating quantitative and selective probing of interfacial water at hBN surfaces. We further establish an experimentally implementable phase-retrieval and Fresnel-correction scheme, based on an in situ hBN/D2O reference, that yields the intrinsic Im χyyz(2)spectrum of interfacial water at the hBN/water interface, independent of film thickness and crystal orientation. Moreover, this approach provides a strategy for probing nanoconfined water by selecting appropriate thin-film materials, paving the way for future studies of interfacial water under nanoscale confinement. This methodology establishes a general framework for interpreting HD-SFG spectra at 2D material/water interfaces and is broadly applicable to a wide range of 2D materials, including membrane systems, as well as polymer thin films, and complements existing thin-film SFG treatments by extending Fresnel-factor engineering to phase-resolved HD-SFG at 2D material/liquid interfaces.

title: Measurements of Density and Viscosity for Methyl Dodecanoate and Ethyl Tetradecanoate and Speed of Sound in Ethyl Tetradecanoate at Temperatures from (298 to 423) K and Pressures from (0.1 to 100) MPa
summary: The density and viscosity of methyl dodecanoate and ethyl tetradecanoate were measured along six isotherms at temperatures from (298 to 423) K and pressures from (0.1 to 100) MPa. For ethyl tetradecanoate, the speed of sound was also invest
content: The density and viscosity of methyl dodecanoate and ethyl tetradecanoate were measured along six isotherms at temperatures from (298 to 423) K and pressures from (0.1 to 100) MPa. For ethyl tetradecanoate, the speed of sound was also investigated in this temperature and pressure range. Density was measured using two vibrating tube instruments, at two separate laboratories, with maximum relative combined expanded uncertainties (k = 2) of 0.15% and 0.20%, respectively. Viscosity was measured using a vibrating-wire viscometer with a relative combined expanded uncertainty (k = 2) of 1.4%, and the speed of sound using a dual-path pulse-echo instrument with a relative combined expanded uncertainty (k = 2) of 0.09%. The density data were used to develop a Tait model, the viscosity data to parametrize the Tait-Andrade model, and the speed of sound data to model an empirical correlation. All models were compared with available literature data.

title: Migration of Clustered Seismicity Controlled by Fluids, Aseismic Deformation, and Lithology in the Northern Apennines
summary: The Alto Tiberina Fault (ATF) extensional system in the Northern Apennines is an ideal natural laboratory for observing seismic clustering, swarm behaviors, cluster migration, and their interplay with highly pressurized fluids (CO 2 ) in th
content: The Alto Tiberina Fault (ATF) extensional system in the Northern Apennines is an ideal natural laboratory for observing seismic clustering, swarm behaviors, cluster migration, and their interplay with highly pressurized fluids (CO 2 ) in the crust. Using a 13‐year high‐resolution earthquake catalog and density‐based clustering, we identify over 70 migrating clusters within the ATF hanging wall. Spatiotemporal analysis reveals multi‐scale migration patterns, from localized bursts to regional transients, that we characterized by both diffusive and linear fronts. Scaling relationships between migration speeds, durations, and magnitudes indicate a strong underlying influence of fluid diffusion and aseismic creep, modulated by local structural and lithological heterogeneity. Furthermore, we observe a clear positive correlation between maximum magnitude and apparent diffusivity. Notably, the 2013–2014 Gubbio swarm was preceded by a regional transient initiated in late 2012, suggesting a self‐similar process involving a large portion of the ATF hanging wall.

title: DFT-based Structural, Electronic, and Vibrational Properties of Terbutaline with Molecular Docking Analysis
summary: Terbutaline is a selective β₂-adrenergic agonist widely associated with bronchodilatory activity, but an integrated computational description of its structural, vibrational, electronic, and receptor-binding characteristics remains limited.
content: Terbutaline is a selective β₂-adrenergic agonist widely associated with bronchodilatory activity, but an integrated computational description of its structural, vibrational, electronic, and receptor-binding characteristics remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the optimized molecular structure, vibrational properties, frontier molecular orbitals, solvent-dependent electronic transitions, molecular electrostatic potential, and receptor-binding interactions of Terbutaline using density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT), and molecular docking. Geometry optimization and vibrational analysis were performed at the B3LYP/3-21G level, while electronic absorption properties were evaluated for the gas phase and aqueous solvent. Molecular docking was performed against the human β₂-adrenergic receptor (PDB ID: 4LDE) using SwissDock. The optimized structure showed structural features consistent with previously reported Terbutaline data, and the vibrational analysis identified characteristic N–H and O–H stretching modes. The calculated HOMO–LUMO gap changed only slightly from 5.91 eV in the gas phase to 5.89 eV in aqueous solvent. The principal H→L transition occurred at 241 nm in the gas phase and shifted to 243 nm in aqueous solvent, accompanied by a modest increase in oscillator strength. Docking analysis yielded a top-ranked binding affinity of −6.334 kcal/mol, with hydrogen-bonding interactions involving ASP113 and ASN312 and hydrophobic contacts involving VAL114, VAL117, and PHE290. Overall, the results provide an integrated computational characterization of Terbutaline and indicate that its polar functional groups contribute to interactions within the β₂-adrenergic receptor binding pocket. The findings should be interpreted primarily as qualitative and comparative computational insights given the B3LYP/3-21G and molecular docking approaches employed.

title: Large-Scale Synthesis of Diphenyliodonium Triflate in Green Solvent
summary: Diphenyliodonium triflate is the standard iodine(III) reagent for phenylations, yet its synthesis requires the use of dichloromethane, which is a solvent associated with serious health risks. Herein, we report a large-scale synthesis of dip
content: Diphenyliodonium triflate is the standard iodine(III) reagent for phenylations, yet its synthesis requires the use of dichloromethane, which is a solvent associated with serious health risks. Herein, we report a large-scale synthesis of diphenyliodonium triflate in the sustainable solvent ethyl acetate, utilizing a straightforward reaction setup without the need for inert conditions. The E factor of the reaction is impressively low, and the product shows excellent thermal stability.

title: Small but still important: spatio-temporal variability of the hydrochemistry of lowland spring waters and its landscape dependence in central Poland
summary: The current study aimed to identify the general spatio-temporal variability pattern of the hydrochemical properties of spring waters in the Mazovian Lowland, central Poland, and to evaluate its associations with the land cover of the spring
content: The current study aimed to identify the general spatio-temporal variability pattern of the hydrochemical properties of spring waters in the Mazovian Lowland, central Poland, and to evaluate its associations with the land cover of the spring proximity zones. Water samples were collected three times from November 2024 to May 2025 across 35 perennial, valley, or hillslope type springs, draining Quaternary porous aquifers; the chemical analysis included selected macro- and microelements, determined using IC and ICP-MS techniques. The studied springs were characterized by low discharge, belonging from VIII to V Meinzer classes (from 0.2 to 77.8 L/min). Their waters were usually slightly alkaline, with TDS ranging from 64 to 2055 mg/L, and represented various hydrochemical water types, from the most common HCO 3 -Ca to even five ionic types such as HCO 3 -SO 4 -NO 3 -Ca-Mg and Cl-SO 4 -HCO 3 -Ca-Na. The chemical composition, as captured and indicated by descriptive statistics, molar ratios, and PCA, reflected both geogenic and anthropogenic influences. Spring water in urbanized areas experienced high concentrations of Cl − , SO 4 2− , Na + , and K + , which could be explained by multidimensional human pressure across cities, while significant NO 3 − contamination was revealed in springs across the agricultural landscape, originating from intensive fertilizer applications. The correlation analysis suggested that the land cover of the spring proximity zone could partially explain its water chemical composition; road length, building area, and the contribution of total artificial areas had a significant, statistical effect on numerous macro- and microelement concentrations. Cultivated lands were associated mainly with NO 3 − concentrations, whereas forest cover contribution was negatively correlated with lower concentration values. Overall, the spring proximity zone of 500 m radius provided the best correlation for artificial areas, agricultural lands, and forests, while road length and building area appeared to be the most significant in the 100 and 250 m radius zone. The results provide a comprehensive insight into spring water chemistry across lowland, post-glacial areas, crucial in terms of the effective management of groundwater, its protection, as well as future investigations.

title: Temporal Graph Learning for Robust Detection of Coordinated Fraud in Dynamic Transaction Networks
source: International Journal of Advanced Engineering and Technology Research
summary: Coordinated fraud can produce repeated, synchronized transfers whose signatures are obscured by heterogeneous activity, missing edges, and evolving behavior. This paper studies a lightweight temporal graph learning strategy based on account
content: Coordinated fraud can produce repeated, synchronized transfers whose signatures are obscured by heterogeneous activity, missing edges, and evolving behavior. This paper studies a lightweight temporal graph learning strategy based on account-level transaction attributes, static neighborhood descriptors, and eight-bin temporal coordination statistics. Static and temporal feature variants are each trained with the same simulated edge-deletion augmentation to disentangle the effects of timing descriptors and robustness training. Experiments are conducted on a controlled, fully specified synthetic benchmark containing 4,800 accounts, approximately 15,000 transfers per run, and simulator-assigned coordinated actors; the benchmark is not a real-world labeled fraud dataset. Three independent runs use chronological, nonoverlapping train/validation/test snapshots. The edge-augmented static graph achieves test average precision 0.631, while the identically augmented temporal feature model reaches 0.602; their nonaugmented counterparts score 0.571 and 0.569, respectively. At 20% and 40% test-edge removal, augmented static-graph average precision is 0.518 and 0.389, respectively. A matched augmentation control, fixed-budget top-100 precision, and timestamp shuffling separate the roles of training robustness and within-snapshot timing. The study provides an efficient, transparent protocol for evaluating coordinated-pattern detection in evolving transaction networks.

title: AQUIFER PARAMETER VARIATION USING VERTICAL ELECTRICAL SOUNDING AND CONTOURING TECHNIQUES IN APETE-AKUFO PHASE II, AWOTAN-ASUNLE AREA OF IBADAN, SOUTH-WEST NIGERIA
source: Journal of African Advancement and Sustainability Studies
summary: Subsurface characterization is essential for evaluating groundwater potential and assess the environmental impact of dumpsites. Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) was carried out to study the subsurface condition of Apete-Akufo, Awotan-Asun
content: Subsurface characterization is essential for evaluating groundwater potential and assess the environmental impact of dumpsites. Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) was carried out to study the subsurface condition of Apete-Akufo, Awotan-Asunle dumpsite area of Ibadan, aimed at determining the subsurface resistivity beneath the dumpsite, identifying the different geoelectric layers present, evaluating the depth and extent of leachate contamination. Ten (10) Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) stations were occupied using Schlumberger electrode configuration with half-electrode spacing (AB/2) of 75m each and the field data were interpreted using Win Resist software to generate geoelectric models. The interpreted results revealed three to four geoelectric layers comprising the topsoil, weathered layer, fractured basement, and fresh basement. The top soil resistivity values range from 8.1Ωm to 800.2Ωm, the weathered layer resistivity (4.1-619.1Ωm), fractured basement resistivity ranges from 25.6Ωm to 105.6Ωm and fresh basement resistivity (25.7-1291.6Ωm) with curves types ranging from H-type to A-type and K-type across the different stations. Other aquifer properties were consequently determined; bedrock relief which ranges from 187.5 to 221.3m, Aquifer thickness (0.5 - 41.7m) and overburden thickness ranges from 2.7 to 44.5m among others. The aquifer protective capacity assessment, based on longitudinal conductance values, revealed that 10%, 20%, 60% and 10% were classified as poor, weak, moderate and good protective capacity status respectively. The location exhibiting low protective capacity will enhance the migration of contaminants into the groundwater system of the study area. Periodic groundwater quality monitoring is recommended particularly in locations with low aquifer protective capacity to minimize the impact of leachate contamination from the dumpsite.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
summary: Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a mo
content: Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni 0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
summary: Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high‐pressure liquid‐phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selecti
content: Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high‐pressure liquid‐phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selectivity, and structural robustness are difficult to optimize simultaneously. Here, we report a strategy that couples additive manufacturing with molten‐salt activation to engineer a 3D‐printed bladed agitator catalyst (AB–MSL–H 2 ). Molten‐salt treatment selectively reconstructs the alloy surface while preserving the printed architecture, generating a Ni‐enriched interface with abundant exposed metallic Ni 0 active sites. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that surface reconstruction enriches accessible Ni 0 sites to direct the desired hydrogenation pathway while suppressing isomerization, cyclization, and hydrogenolysis, whereas the integrated bladed architecture simultaneously enhances gas‐liquid‐solid mass transfer and reactant accessibility. Consequently, AB–MSL–H 2 achieves complete conversion of 2‐butyne‐1,4‐diol with a 1,4‐butanediol yield exceeding 97%. This work establishes a general strategy for transforming additively manufactured structural alloys into catalytically active reactor components through molten‐salt‐induced surface reconstruction, expanding the scope of catalyst‐reactor integration for high‐pressure liquid‐phase catalysis.

title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
summary: The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH 3 , ·OH) generated during Fe‐catalyzed oxidation with H 2 O 2 . Here we report a radical buffering strategy in
content: The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH 3 , ·OH) generated during Fe‐catalyzed oxidation with H 2 O 2 . Here we report a radical buffering strategy in which atomically dispersed Ru is co‐loaded with Fe in ZSM‐5 as an ·OH reservoir, steering intermediates toward selective Eley‐Rideal‐type coupling in the micropores. The Ru‐Fe/ZSM‐5 catalyst achieves an oxygenate productivity of 37.5 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 at 70°C with 95.7% oxygenate selectivity and 92.3% formic acid selectivity among liquid products, a 2.2‐fold improvement over Fe/ZSM‐5. Extended X‐ray absorption fine structure analysis shows that Ru and Fe exist as two independent populations of single atoms with no metal–metal bonding. Electron paramagnetic resonance and in situ infrared spectroscopy show that Fe activates CH 4 to ·CH 3 while Ru activates H 2 O 2 and holds part of the resulting ·OH. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that Ru binds ·OH more strongly than Fe (−3.130 compared to −2.738 eV), and dissociates H 2 O 2 nearly thermoneutrally (+0.077 eV). Therefore ·OH is held on Ru rather than on the Fe. This work establishes radical buffering by independent single‐atom populations in confined micropores as a design principle for controlling selectivity in radical‐mediated catalysis.

title: Dual mRNA delivery corrects physical and biochemical deficits in a mouse model of hepatic onset trifunctional protein deficiency
summary: Mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency (TFP-D) is a rare, life threatening long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorder caused by variants in either the HADHA or HADHB subunits, leading to toxic metabolite accumulation and systemic ener
content: Mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency (TFP-D) is a rare, life threatening long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorder caused by variants in either the HADHA or HADHB subunits, leading to toxic metabolite accumulation and systemic energy deficiency. Current dietary management strategies are only partially effective and fail to prevent long term morbidity and mortality. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) mediated mRNA replacement strategy to restore TFP function in a moderate severity TFP-D mouse model by delivering both Hadha and Hadhb mRNA. In cultured TFP-D mouse fibroblasts, dual mRNA delivery, but not single subunit replacement, rescued long-chain fatty acid oxidation and revealed a dominant negative effect exerted by the endogenous M404K variant Hadhb. In vivo, intravenous administration of dual mRNA-LNPs restored hepatic TFP expression, reduced circulating long-chain acylcarnitines, and improved physiological performance in aged TFP‑D mice. Notably, intravenous delivery of dual mRNA LNPs significantly rescued cold tolerance test (CTT) performance by up to 71.6% compared to untreated and healthy controls. Together, these findings establish dual subunit LNP‑mRNA delivery as a promising therapeutic strategy for TFP‑D and support its potential applicability to other long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders.

title: Entropy‐Compensated Electrolyte Enables Low‐Temperature 400 Wh Kg −1 Silicon‐Based Lithium‐Ion Batteries
summary: Electrolytes dictate the low‐temperature (LT) performance of Si‐anode lithium‐ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li + transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hin
content: Electrolytes dictate the low‐temperature (LT) performance of Si‐anode lithium‐ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li + transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hinder Li + migration, limiting Li + supply to the interface and destabilizing interfacial reactions. Herein, we propose an entropy‐compensation strategy to counteract LT‐induced solvation deterioration in Si‐anode electrolytes. Increasing the solvation entropy ( ΔS solv ) compensates for the LT‐induced increase in the Gibbs free‐energy change for ion‐cluster dissociation ( ΔG solv ), thereby raising the corresponding equilibrium constant ( K solv ) and suppressing ion pairing. Consequently, electrolytes preferentially form smaller anion‐rich ionic clusters, delivering an approximately threefold increase in ionic conductivity at −20°C. Enhanced bulk transport alleviates concentration polarization, stabilizes the interfacial solvation environment, and promotes uniform SEI‐forming reactions. Benefiting from this coupled bulk‐interfacial optimization, Ah‐level pouch cells retain 97.8% capacity after 165 cycles at −20°C and support sustained discharge at −81°C. This strategy enables high‐energy pouch cells to deliver 400 Wh kg −1 under ambient conditions and 339 Wh kg −1 at LT, while an Ah‐level pouch cell retains 80% capacity after 1150 cycles at 2 C. This work identifies ΔS solv as a critical thermodynamic descriptor for low‐temperature electrolyte design.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
summary: Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified fra
content: Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Nuclear quantum effects on ion permeation through the open transient receptor potential melastatin 7 pore: A continuum-electrostatics estimate
summary: We estimate how nuclear delocalization affects magnesium and calcium release from occupied wells in the naltriben-open pore of transient receptor potential melastatin 7 (TRPM7). We compare the equilibrium distributions of sodium, magnesium,
content: We estimate how nuclear delocalization affects magnesium and calcium release from occupied wells in the naltriben-open pore of transient receptor potential melastatin 7 (TRPM7). We compare the equilibrium distributions of sodium, magnesium, and calcium in the same open structure and fixed continuum field. Thermal quantum states extend over nearby positions, so the ion can sample more than one local environment. For the divalent ions, the model combines a Gaussian test charge in the nonlinear Poisson--Boltzmann potential, spatial dielectric self-energy, and the free-energy cost of restricting a correlated first hydration shell. The hydration shell comprises the water molecules that directly coordinate the ion. In a constriction, the wall can block access to some of these water sites. The classical and quantum calculations use the same insertion energy, pore geometry, and axial diffusivity. The leading Wigner--Kirkwood correction for a smooth ion energy $U_i$ away from the wall is $\ell_i^2\left[\nabla^2 U_i-\frac{\beta}{2}|\nabla U_i|^2\right]$, up to an additive constant, with $\ell_i^2=\frac{\beta\hbar^2}{12m_i}$ for ion mass $m_i$ and inverse thermal energy $\beta$. The length $\ell_i$ is about $0.02\,\text{\AA}$ at $310\,\text{K}$. At the point-ion magnesium basin, the refined centerline self-energy reaches $430\,\text{meV}$. Steric constraints also restrict water coordination at the $1.43\,\text{\AA}$ constriction. At $310\,\text{K}$ in the primary extended dielectric box, the deepest wells for magnesium and calcium lie at $22.75$ and $11.00\,\text{\AA}$, respectively. The quantum changes in mean passage time toward the intracellular and extracellular interfaces are $0.68\%$ and $-0.66\%$ for magnesium and $-0.10\%$ and $16.12\%$ for calcium. Calcium starts on the intracellular side of the constriction and must cross it to reach the extracellular interface. The preferred magnesium site is already on the extracellular side. A change in the dielectric boundary for magnesium or the ligand penalty for calcium can move the deepest well across the constriction and reverse the extracellular response. For comparison, the circular point-ion estimate for magnesium changes from $-37.4\%$ and $-34.5\%$ to $-8.9\%$ and $-8.6\%$ with a $0.5\,\text{\AA}$ wall inset. In the circular reference, the largest local correction occurs at the intracellular widening and depends on near-wall access and axial sampling. Its influence on escape from the occupied well is small. In a separate screened two-ion benchmark, classical repulsion changes escape barriers by tens to hundreds of meV. Isotope substitution tests the mass dependence at fixed charge and chemistry. Together, the results show how pore geometry, dielectric response, and water coordination determine which local quantum corrections affect directional release.

title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables Sn II /Sn IV Redox Catalysis
summary: Main‐group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade‐off, that is, reactive p‐block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two‐coordinate stannyliumylidene ions w
content: Main‐group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade‐off, that is, reactive p‐block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two‐coordinate stannyliumylidene ions with an accessible lone pair and vacant p‐orbital offer an attractive ambiphilic platform for engaging in redox processes. To date, most reported examples remain confined to π‐ or heteroatom‐donor‐stabilized rigid frameworks, and the isolation of a genuinely two‐coordinate acyclic stannyliumylidene has remained elusive. Herein, we report the synthesis and isolation of a two‐coordinate, acyclic, mono‐N‐heterocyclic‐carbene‐stabilized stannyliumylidene paired with a weakly coordinating [B(3,5‐(CF 3 ) 2 C 6 H 3 ) 4 ] − anion. Stripped of additional donor stabilization, the tin centre is rendered highly electrophilic while maintaining an accessible lone pair. This enhanced electrophilicity enabled capture of a stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct, the first structurally characterized ketone‐bound tetryliumylidene intermediate that is directly implicated in a catalytic cycle. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, combining experimental results with theoretical calculations, reveal an Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox manifold that drives catalytic turnover. Together, these results significantly expand the landscape of tin‐based redox catalysis and highlight that accessing stable low‐valent stannyliumylidene ions with a minimal coordination number and weaker donor stabilization is a feasible approach for unlocking transition‐metal‐like redox behaviour at the tin centre.

title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO 2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
summary: Carbon dioxide (CO 2 )‐derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO 2 ‐based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequenc
content: Carbon dioxide (CO 2 )‐derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO 2 ‐based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences. Here, we introduce terpolymerization of CO 2 with cyclosilanes and epoxides to access poly(silyl ether–ester) with perfectly alternating A‐B‐C (CO 2 ‐ alt ‐cyclosilane‐ alt ‐epoxide) sequences. This terpolymerization is enabled by the thermodynamically favored formation of Si─O bonds, providing a driving force for efficient incorporation of both silalactones and epoxides into the terpolymer backbone in an alternating fashion. A range of epoxide and silacyclobutane substrates can be incorporated into the polyester, affording structurally diverse terpolymers. Notably, these polymers are stable thermally ( T d up to 313°C) and hydrolytically (in neutral water) but can slowly degrade under acidic or basic conditions and be chemically depolymerized under mild catalytic conditions to recover the silalactone monomer.

title: Interfacial Molecular Engineering Mediated Intramolecular Inter‐Group Relay Effect Enables Efficient Acidic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ Conversion
summary: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C 2+ products at high cu
content: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C 2+ products at high current densities remains a formidable challenge due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and sluggish C─C coupling process. Here, we introduce the surface‐adsorbed bifunctional organic molecule on Cu (Cu─SBMA), which delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 90.4% for C 2+ products at 0.8 A cm −2 under acid media and pure CO 2 flow, together with a single‐pass carbon efficiency (SPCE) of 92.8% at 0.6 A cm −2 . Furthermore, under diluted CO 2 flow (15 vol% CO 2 ), Cu─SBMA still maintains a high C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 85.3% at 0.4 A cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy and DFT calculations uncover an intramolecular inter‐group relay mechanism that governs asymmetrical OC─CHO coupling toward C 2+ productions. Specifically, the quaternary ammonium (─N + (CH 3 ) 2 ─) group promotes CO 2 activation and stabilizes *CO intermediate, the adjacent sulfonate (SO 3 − ) moiety mediates protonation of *CO toward *CHO. The intramolecular inter‐group relay effect facilitates C─C coupling and suppresses HER. Our findings provide novel insights for the precise design of catalysts to regulate the reaction selectivity of complex multi‐step energy conversion process.

title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
summary: The protolignin standardization transformation into high-value-added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G-lignin-derived benz
content: The protolignin standardization transformation into high-value-added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G-lignin-derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3-alkyl guaiacol (C3-G), stoichiometric diazotization-reductive ammonification of C3-G to aminophenol C3-GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3-GAP to the benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor-selective cytotoxicity of the as-synthesized G-lignin-derived benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3-GLB-pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high-value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

title: Hierarchical cellulose-based tungsten trioxide–silicon dioxide hybrid for synergistic adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of organic contaminants
summary: The contamination of natural water sources by hazardous substances such as toxic dyes and mycotoxins has emerged as a serious health and environmental issue due to their high toxicity and resistance to conventional treatment methods.
content: The contamination of natural water sources by hazardous substances such as toxic dyes and mycotoxins has emerged as a serious health and environmental issue due to their high toxicity and resistance to conventional treatment methods.

title: FluidUrban v1.0: enhancing urban ventilation and pollutant dispersion modelling with three-dimensional dynamic adaptive meshes optimisation
summary: Simulating urban airflow and pollutant dispersion requires resolving multiscale physical processes, from large-scale meteorological forcing to highly localized building-induced turbulence. To accurately capture these multiscale urban flow f
content: Simulating urban airflow and pollutant dispersion requires resolving multiscale physical processes, from large-scale meteorological forcing to highly localized building-induced turbulence. To accurately capture these multiscale urban flow fields, this study introduces FluidUrban v1.0, an advanced modelling system built upon the Fluidity solver and centred on a three-dimensional Dynamic Adaptive Mesh Optimization (DAMO) framework. By dynamically adapting mesh resolution in response to the evolution of flow physics and scalar gradients, DAMO concentrates computational resources on critical high-gradient regions such as building wakes, shear layers and scalar sharp plumes. The model's performance is systematically evaluated against high-fidelity “WOTAN” wind-tunnel experimental data under varying surface roughness conditions and inflow directions. The results demonstrate that the FluidUrban with DAMO framework consistently outperforms traditional non-uniform fixed meshes (FIXM) by accurately capturing complex urban wind fields and pollutant concentration. For normalized wind speed, FluidUrban with DAMO achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.187, representing a notable reduction from 0.214 simulated by FIXM. In terms of wind direction, the model reduced the MAE by up to 38.4 % in medium roughness and 36.1 % in high roughness conditions, respectively, during realistic oblique inflow scenarios. Additionally, DAMO effectively mitigates the non-physical numerical dissipation observed in static meshes, significantly improving the prediction of streamwise and lateral turbulence intensities. Furthermore, for pollutant dispersion, the model effectively suppressed numerical diffusion and maintained sharp plume gradients, achieving an 89 % compliance rate with established atmospheric model evaluation standards (FB, NMSE, and MG), compared to only 50 % for FIXM. Although DAMO introduces runtime overhead for mesh regeneration, this cost is justified by significant gains in physical accuracy and multi-scale flow resolution. Following the systematic evaluation, FluidUrban v1.0 was applied to a realistic urban scenario, demonstrating its robust capability to resolve the complex flow fields and spatial heterogeneity within real urban morphologies. Thus, FluidUrban v1.0 demonstrates to be a robust aerodynamic tool for resolving the transient, small-scale flow structures critical to pollutant transport, establishing a solid foundation for the future integration of comprehensive urban physical components, including radiation, vegetation, and full energy-balance physics.

title: A survey of macroeconomic nowcasting applications
summary: Nowcasting, broadly understood as the real-time assessment of current and near-term economic conditions, is a framework of growing importance that helps inform both economic policy decision for Governments and Central banks but also shape s
content: Nowcasting, broadly understood as the real-time assessment of current and near-term economic conditions, is a framework of growing importance that helps inform both economic policy decision for Governments and Central banks but also shape strategies of private institutions. In this paper, a dataset of macroeconomic nowcasting application papers is compiled and analyzed to identify the main research themes and gaps in the literature. Results find that literature is rather concentrated in nowcasting aggregate economic measures, specifically GDP which appears as the target variable in 74% of the papers examined. In terms of modelling frameworks, even though there is no consensus about the best-performing type of model, Dynamic Factor Models seem to be widely preferred as they were used in 37.5% of the nowcasting applications. However, Machine Learning applications are being increasingly used after the COVID-19 pandemic, coupled by an increased reliance in the use of alternative sources of data, which feature in an average of 51.7% of annual publications between 2020-2026, compared with 18.6% during 2010–2019. Despite advances in the field, important challenges remain, as illustrated not only by the difficulties many nowcasting models faced during periods of economic turbulence but also more recently, by the Atlanta Fed’s toolkit’s “GDPNow” nowcasting undershoot associated with differences in the classification of gold imports. Further challenges arise from the insufficiently explored limitations and potential biases of alternative data sources, as well as difficulties in acquiring historical data vintages necessary for conducting true real-time nowcasting evaluations. Against this background, future research should focus on: (i) continuing on extending nowcasting applications to underexplored variables and economies, (ii) examining the predictive properties and limitations of alternative data, and (iii) examine the potential usefulness of evaluation frameworks that combine real-time predictor vintages with final revised estimates of target variables to assess predictive performance against their underlying economic movements while avoiding look-ahead bias, so as to avoid misguiding policy makers during periods of substantial data revisions.

title: Carbon at the Border, Cost in the Supply Chain: The CBAM in the EU and the Rearrangement of Turkish Export Logistics, 2019–2024
summary: This paper examines the interaction between the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and Türkiye’s export of iron and steel, aluminium, and cement from the beginning of the transitional regime in October 2023 and the i
content: This paper examines the interaction between the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and Türkiye’s export of iron and steel, aluminium, and cement from the beginning of the transitional regime in October 2023 and the implementation of the definitive regime starting in 2026. In addition to this, it explores whether the export performance depends only on CBAM exposure or also varies due to differences in production technology, adaptation capability of firms, logistics costs, and domestic climate policy. An ex-post descriptive-comparative research design is used here, based on bilateral UN Comtrade data of Türkiye with five CBAM-exposed exporters including Ukraine, Serbia, India, Egypt, and Brazil. Cross- sectoral and cross-temporal comparisons will be supplemented with the use of EU-5 proxy market coverage assessment, alternative destination falsification, and official data aggregations provided by the Turkish Statistical Institute and Turkish Exporters Assembly. Information on crossing the border and logistics costs will provide context for CBAM compliance of Turkish- EU logistics chain. With respect to total trade between Türkiye and the EU-27 for iron and steel exports, there is an approximate decline of 18% from 2019 to 2023; this decline is even larger, at an approximate 40% level, when it is considered only with respect to the top five countries in the EU in terms of trade. The comparative analysis performed in the paper uses Comtrade data spanning 2019-2024, and data on 2025-2026 years are presented as aggregate data for the upcoming period in the non- sectoral format of TİM/TÜİK. This decrease exceeds the one of a similarly selected group of non-EU destinations.
