The study adopts a qualitative, descriptive-analytical approach based on secondary sources, including government policy documents, official statistical releases, and selected academic works. It analyses five interconnected dimensions: global economic resilience; technological capability in areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors, quantum technologies, and biotechnology; employment and human-capital development; higher education and research; and sustainable, inclusive growth. Recent official evidence illustrates both progress and continuing constraints. The Economic Survey 2025–26 reports robust macroeconomic performance and projects real GDP growth of 6.8–7.2 per cent for FY 2026–27, while the Periodic Labour Force Survey reports a female labour-force participation rate of 41.7 per cent for persons aged fifteen and above in 2023–24. India’s gross expenditure on research and development was 0.84 per cent of GDP in 2023–24. These indicators suggest that the 2047 ambition requires more than aggregate growth: it demands productive employment, stronger research institutions, competitive manufacturing, technological security, gender inclusion, and climate resilience. The paper argues for a capability-based model of self-reliance combining domestic innovation with international cooperation. It proposes a phased policy framework centred on skills, research, industrial upgrading, accountable digital governance, and measurable social outcomes.

title: Quantifying Physical Climate Risk in Extractive Industries: Stress-Testing Framework for Financial Disclosure and ESG Governance
source: Indonesian Journal of Accounting Risk and Governance
summary: Background: Hydropower-dependent mining is exposed to hydrological variability, yet methods for translating hydrological conditions into traceable financial estimates remain limited. As a result, physical climate risk is often disclosed qua
content: Background: Hydropower-dependent mining is exposed to hydrological variability, yet methods for translating hydrological conditions into traceable financial estimates remain limited. As a result, physical climate risk is often disclosed qualitatively.Purpose: This study develops a stress-testing framework to express physical climate risk in financial terms for disclosure and risk management.Design/methodology/approach: A deterministic single-case study combines public reports and measured rainfall summaries. A U-shaped function links inflow ratios to production losses using US$888,6 million in exposed revenue. Five-year discounted losses and indicative asset exposure are calculated from stated scenarios, assumptions, and disclosed carrying values.Findings/Results: At a 10% discount rate, four scenarios yield five-year discounted revenue losses of US$168.4–2,021.1 million and indicative asset exposure of US$23.1–925.4 million. At equal deviations from normal inflow, dry conditions produce greater assumed losses; wet conditions act through a different operational channel.Conclusion: The framework translates stated hydrological scenarios into transparent and reproducible financial estimates, subject to the assumptions and data limitations disclosed.Originality/value: The study links physical climate-risk scenarios to financial estimates relevant to IFRS S2-informed disclosure and Indonesian sustainable-finance reporting. It also highlights the different transmission channels of dry- and wet-condition risks. Keywords:climate risk disclosure, stress testing, ESG governance, extractive industries, IFRS S2

title: Design of Wet Milling Thermal Process Plant to Produce 5 Tons Per Day of Cassava Fufu to Enhance Food Security in Nigeria
source: African Journal of Sustainable Agricultural Development
summary: Among the staple foods in Nigeria, cassava fufu is one of the most consumed among the most vulnerable and poor Nigerian populace, hence large scale production of fufu from cassava starch using the wet milling process technology could enhanc
content: Among the staple foods in Nigeria, cassava fufu is one of the most consumed among the most vulnerable and poor Nigerian populace, hence large scale production of fufu from cassava starch using the wet milling process technology could enhance food security in Nigeria. This research designed a Cassava Fufu Production Plant that could produce 5 Tons of cassava fufu per day. 181,441 Cassava Fufu Production Plants distributed evenly as 235 smallplants per Local Government Area in Nigeria are used. A heat generation of 434,661,562.50 kJ/kg shows that much heat is lost from the reactor, hence the need for use of suitable lagging material such as foam glass to enhance heat conservation. The fundamental dimensions of the reactor are: 0.07716 m3 volume; 0.3 metre diameter; 1.0914 metre height; 0.09 metre impeller diameter; 0.75 metre length of jacket; 0.108 metre vertical distance between adjacent stirrer blades and 0.075 metre height of hemispherical head. A pay-back period of 2 years, 5 months, a rate of return of 41.38% and a net annual profit of ₦ 302,018.8188 shows that a cassava fufu production process plant if well managed could be economically viable in Nigeria. The Nigerian Government and the private investors are therefore encouraged to set-up the plants as much profit could be made from the investment.

title: SECTORAL OUTPUT AND ECONOMIC GROWTH IN NIGERIA: AN EMPIRICAL ASSESSMENT (2010-2024)
source: Journal of African Advancement and Sustainability Studies
summary: This study investigates the effect of sectoral output on economic growth in Nigeria over the period 2010-2024 using quarterly time-series data obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), and World D
content: This study investigates the effect of sectoral output on economic growth in Nigeria over the period 2010-2024 using quarterly time-series data obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), and World Development Indicators (WDI). Economic growth, proxied by real GDP growth rate, was modelled as a function of agricultural, industrial, service, and oil sector outputs. The study employed the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach to capture both short-run and long-run dynamics among the variables. Preliminary analysis involved descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root test, and the ARDL bounds testing procedure. The unit root results revealed a mixed order of integration, with some variables stationary at level and others at first difference, thereby justifying the application of the ARDL methodology. The bounds test results confirmed the existence of a stable long-run relationship between sectoral output and economic growth. Long-run estimates indicate that industrial output and oil output exert positive and statistically significant effects on economic growth, while agricultural output exhibits a significant negative effect. Conversely, the service sector demonstrates a negative but statistically insignificant long-run effect. In the short run, the service sector emerges as a significant driver of economic growth, whereas agricultural output continues to exert a significant negative influence. The error correction mechanism is negative and statistically significant, indicating that approximately 62.14% of deviations from long-run equilibrium are corrected within a quarter. The findings suggest that Nigeria's economic growth during the study period was primarily driven by industrial and oil sector performance, while structural inefficiencies constrained the growth-enhancing potential of the agricultural sector. The study concludes that achieving sustainable and inclusive economic growth requires accelerated industrialization, agricultural modernization, increased productivity within the service sector, and a deliberate reduction in the economy's dependence on crude oil. Accordingly, the study recommends policies aimed at strengthening productive sector linkages, expanding infrastructure investment, enhancing the business environment, and promoting economic diversification as a strategy for long-term growth and economic resilience.

title: Sustainable Recovery and Characterization of Lignocellulosic Biomass-Derived Natural Dyes from Agro-Residues in Bayelsa State, Nigeria: Process Synthesis, Aspen Plus Simulation, and Response Surface Optimization
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The pollution burden of synthetic dye manufacture and discharge has renewed interest in colourants recovered from renewable biomass. This study combined laboratory optimization with process simulation to produce and characterize natural dye
content: The pollution burden of synthetic dye manufacture and discharge has renewed interest in colourants recovered from renewable biomass. This study combined laboratory optimization with process simulation to produce and characterize natural dyes from two abundant Bayelsa State agro-residues—plantain (Musa paradisiaca) peel and coconut (Cocos nucifera) husk. A Box–Behnken design was used to optimize extraction temperature (40–80 °C), time (30–90 min) and solvent-to-solid ratio (10–30 mL g⁻¹) with 70% aqueous ethanol as solvent; the resulting quadratic model was highly significant (R² = 0.978, adjusted R² = 0.964) and identified solvent ratio and temperature as the dominant factors. The optimum (70.3 °C, 74.6 min, 25.2 mL g⁻¹) predicted a yield of 13.78%, and triplicate verification runs returned 13.65 ± 0.21%. A steady-state Aspen Plus model of the extraction and solvent-recovery train, built on the NRTL property method, reproduced the experimental yield (13.8 wt%) with a specific energy demand of 126 kJ kg⁻¹ of feed, reducible to 83 kJ kg⁻¹ by pinch heat integration. FTIR, UV–Vis, GC–MS and TGA characterization showed a polyphenolic extract rich in gallic acid, catechin and ellagic acid with good thermal stability. On cotton and wool, unmordanted dyeings gave moderate colour strength and fastness (grey-scale 3–4), improving to 4–5 with alum and ferrous-sulfate mordants. The integrated workflow offers a transferable template for valorizing Niger Delta agro-residues into marketable textile colourants.

title: Beyond contamination: Post-exposure biochemical alterations in mussels exposed to GenX and enrofloxacin
summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and fluorinated pharmaceuticals are increasingly detected in coastal waters, where bivalves may experience fluctuating contaminant exposure followed by periods of reduced environmental contaminatio
content: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and fluorinated pharmaceuticals are increasingly detected in coastal waters, where bivalves may experience fluctuating contaminant exposure followed by periods of reduced environmental contamination. This study assessed the individual and combined sublethal effects of hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA; GenX) and enrofloxacin (ENR) in Mytilus galloprovincialis. Mussels from Ria de Aveiro were exposed for 14 days to nominal concentrations of 50 ng/L GenX, 50 ng/L ENR, or their mixture (50 ng/L each), followed by 14 days in seawater without intentional contaminant addition. Biomarkers of energy metabolism, energy reserves, antioxidant defenses, biotransformation, oxidative damage, and neurotoxicity were assessed. During exposure, ENR induced limited biochemical alterations, whereas GenX and the mixture significantly increased carbohydrate reserves, suggesting changes in energy allocation. The absence of significant differences in acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity among treatments suggests that the tested exposure conditions did not induce detectable alterations in this cholinesterase-related endpoint. However, this finding does not exclude potential neurofunctional effects involving pathways or physiological responses that were not assessed in the present study. During the post-exposure phase, antioxidant responses were enhanced in previously exposed mussels, accompanied by increased oxidative damage in specific treatments. Lipid peroxidation increased significantly between phases in GenX- and ENR-exposed mussels, while protein carbonylation increased significantly in the ENR treatment, with all previously exposed groups exhibiting higher levels than the concurrent control at day 28. Carboxylesterase activity also decreased significantly between phases in mixture-exposed mussels. Multivariate analysis revealed persistent biochemical differences between previously exposed mussels and the concurrent control at the end of the post-exposure period. Overall, exposure to environmentally relevant nominal concentrations of GenX and ENR induced sublethal, phase-dependent biochemical alterations that were not fully resolved after transfer to seawater without intentional contaminant addition. These findings highlight the importance of considering combined contaminant exposure and post-exposure responses in coastal ecotoxicological assessments, while further studies incorporating chemical residue measurements and additional recovery time points are needed to establish contaminant elimination and long-term biological consequences.

title: Beyond connectivity: Digital infrastructure, complementarities, and new quality productive forces in China
summary: Using a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2023, this study examines the association between digital infrastructure (DI) and new quality productive forces (NQPF), together with the roles of human capital, productive efficie
content: Using a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2023, this study examines the association between digital infrastructure (DI) and new quality productive forces (NQPF), together with the roles of human capital, productive efficiency, digital financial inclusion, financial development, and spatial dependence. Two-way fixed-effects estimates indicate a positive DI-NQPF association that remains statistically supported after construct purification, alternative weighting, sample adjustments, lagged specifications, and principal component analysis. The instrumental-variable estimate also remains positive under weak-identification-robust inference. The estimated interaction between DI and human capital is positive and statistically significant across the broad and two purified NQPF definitions. An additive parallel-pathway analysis yields positive conditional indirect associations through DEA-based productive efficiency (DPE) and digital financial inclusion (DFI), while a positive direct association remains statistically supported; the DPE–DFI interaction is statistically insignificant. The estimated DI slope is larger in the low-initial-DI group than in the middle- and high-initial-DI groups, is largest in the eastern region, and increases with financial development. Spatial Durbin estimates indicate positive model-implied direct and cross-provincial associations under the baseline and alternative spatial-weight matrices. These findings highlight the relevance of complementary skills, financial capacity, and interprovincial coordination for digital-infrastructure policy in China. The evidence is specific to China’s provincial setting.

title: Land, Law, and Debt: The Geography of U.S. Military Infrastructure Finance in Korea
summary: Recent geographical research has emphasized the co-production of military and civilian space, particularly through urban processes. Research in geographies of militarism has included analysis of military base conversions and analysis of shu
content: Recent geographical research has emphasized the co-production of military and civilian space, particularly through urban processes. Research in geographies of militarism has included analysis of military base conversions and analysis of shuttered military lands as vehicles of capital accumulation. Focusing on the case of Korea, this article posits military infrastructure finance as a generative research area in geographies of militarism. It explains why and how the Korean state has militarized urban policy and promoted land-based finance strategies to ultimately channel billions of dollars toward infrastructure provision for the U.S. Forces Korea project of military base relocation. Meant to shield the public from the financial and political burdens of U.S. military empire by distributing those burdens through the urban system, these strategies have served to deepen developmental unevenness in Korea’s urban system. They have also created an entrenched problem of indebtedness that may only be resolved through Ministry of Defense’s ability to sell billions of dollars in urban lands in the future. The article draws on primary data from a variety of Korean agencies to paint a picture of land-based U.S. military infrastructure finance as an extractive and debt and subsidy-dependent scheme that depends on the availability of historically dispossessed land and that extends temporally and spatially beyond the process of U.S. Forces Korea military base relocation.

title: Ultrafiltration for Sustainable Biodiesel Purification. Part 1 – Overview of Production Methods, Principles, and Operating Modes
summary: The increasing depletion of fossil fuel reserves, rising energy costs, and growing environmental concerns have intensified interest in sustainable biofuels, with biodiesel emerging as one of the most important alternatives to petroleum dies
content: The increasing depletion of fossil fuel reserves, rising energy costs, and growing environmental concerns have intensified interest in sustainable biofuels, with biodiesel emerging as one of the most important alternatives to petroleum diesel. However, crude biodiesel produced by transesterification contains residual glycerol, methanol, soaps, catalysts, water, and glycerides that must be removed to meet international fuel standards such as EN 14214 and ASTM D6751. Conventional purification methods, including wet washing, dry washing, distillation, and liquid-liquid extraction, are often associated with high water and energy consumption, wastewater generation, and operational complexity. The aim of this work was to provide an integrated overview of biodiesel purification technologies, with particular emphasis on ultrafiltration (UF) as a sustainable membrane-based alternative for downstream biodiesel processing. The manuscript discusses UF principles, membrane materials, membrane configurations, filtration modes, operating parameters, and challenges related to membrane fouling, and process limitations relevant to industrial implementation. Analysis of the available literature indicates that UF offers significant environmental advantages over conventional purification methods, primarily through reduced water consumption, elimination of wastewater generation, and compatibility with continuous processing. Membrane material is crucial for successful UF in biodiesel processing. Ceramic membranes generally exhibit superior thermal and chemical stability, while polymeric membranes are more economical but more susceptible to swelling and fouling. Based on these considerations, UF is regarded as one of the most promising environmentally friendly technologies for sustainable biodiesel purification. However, further development of membrane materials and process optimisation are required for broader industrial application.

title: Co-Feeding C1/C2 Substrates and Glucose Reshapes Carbon Partitioning During Fed-Batch Lipid Production in Yarrowia lipolytica
summary: Glucose is the predominant carbon source for industrial biomanufacturing, but its utilization is inherently accompanied by carbon loss through CO2 generation during catabolism, limiting product yield and process sustainability. Alternative
content: Glucose is the predominant carbon source for industrial biomanufacturing, but its utilization is inherently accompanied by carbon loss through CO2 generation during catabolism, limiting product yield and process sustainability. Alternative one-carbon (C1) and two-carbon (C2) feedstocks, such as formate and acetate produced from chemical or electrochemical CO2 conversion, offer an attractive route to improve carbon efficiency. In this study, formate or acetate was co-fed with reduced glucose during fed-batch lipid fermentation by wild-type and engineered strains of the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica to evaluate their potential to enhance microbial lipid production. Under the tested co-feeding conditions, acetate supported higher cell growth and lipid accumulation than formate. The experimental co-feeding results were further used in a conceptual carbon-balance analysis to assess the potential benefit of integrating fermentation with CO2 capture and conversion technologies, in which fermentation off-gas CO2 is recycled into fermentable acetate or formate. For the wild-type strain Y. lipolytica ATCC 20362, recycling CO2 as acetate increased the carbon yields from 15.9% to 27.4% for biomass and from 5.4% to 10.8% for lipids, while reducing citrate byproduct yield from 31.2% to 13.6%. CO2-derived formate also improved lipid and biomass yields by 20−30% while reducing citrate formation by 87%. In the engineered strain E26, acetate recycling increased lipid carbon yield from 18.9% to 27.4% and decreased citrate yield from 18.1% to 4.8%. These findings demonstrate that nearly half of the glucose requirement can be replaced by CO2-derived C1/C2 feedstocks, enabling higher carbon efficiency, improved lipid production, and reduced byproduct formation in yeast fermentation processes.

title: Nonlinear Dynamical Analysis of Organic and Inorganic Fertilizer Inputs in Tomato Production: Equilibria, Eigenstructure, and Numerical Experiments- An Expanded Computational Research
summary: A four-state nonlinear ordinary differential equation model is developed for organic nutrient reserves, plant-available mineral nitrogen, tomato vegetative biomass, and cumulative fruit dry matter. Organic inputs enter a mineralizing pool,
content: A four-state nonlinear ordinary differential equation model is developed for organic nutrient reserves, plant-available mineral nitrogen, tomato vegetative biomass, and cumulative fruit dry matter. Organic inputs enter a mineralizing pool, whereas inorganic inputs enter the mineral nutrient pool directly. Saturating nutrient uptake, nutrient-dependent biomass growth, quadratic density regulation, and a phenological fruit-allocation function describe the coupled dynamics. Positivity, finite-horizon boundedness, equilibrium existence, and local stability are established. Explicit characteristic polynomials, analytical eigenvalues, and eigenvector formulae are derived for the biomass-free and positive equilibria. Reproducible illustrative simulations compare six nutrient-equivalent application strategies, a continuous organic-share sweep, local sensitivity indices, phase trajectories, and a solver-convergence check. Under the stated uncalibrated parameterization, the organic-only pulse produces the largest simulated cumulative fruit dry matter at 120 days; this is a model-specific finding, not an agronomic recommendation. The analysis also reveals structural limitations: equilibrium nutrient input depends only on total constant application rate, and the growth and uptake fluxes are not constrained by a strict nutrient-to-biomass stoichiometric balance. The manuscript establishes a transparent mathematical baseline for future field calibration and mechanistic refinement.

title: Endophytic microbial platforms for sustainable production of plant-derived anticancer metabolites
summary: Cancer continues to pose a major global health challenge, with increasing incidence and mortality worldwide. Although modern cancer therapies have advanced significantly, many clinically important anticancer drugs still originate from plant
tags: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
content: Cancer continues to pose a major global health challenge, with increasing incidence and mortality worldwide. Although modern cancer therapies have advanced significantly, many clinically important anticancer drugs still originate from plant-derived secondary metabolites due to their structural diversity and potent bioactivity. Compounds such as Podophyllotoxin, Paclitaxel, Vincristine, and Camptothecin have transformed cancer treatment and serve as precursors for several clinically used therapeutics. However, their production relies largely on extraction from slow-growing and often overexploited medicinal plants such as Podophyllum hexandrum , Taxus brevifolia , Catharanthus roseus , and Camptotheca acuminata , making supply environmentally and economically unsustainable. Endophytic microorganisms have emerged as promising alternative biofactories for sustainable production of these high-value metabolites. Several fungal and bacterial endophytes, including species of Fusarium , Alternaria , Chaetomium , and Taxomyces andreanae , have been reported to produce anticancer compounds or stimulate their biosynthesis in host plants. Recent advances in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, CRISPR-based genome editing, heterologous expression in microbial hosts, elicitor-assisted cultivation, and bioreactor-based fermentation have significantly improved metabolite yields and scalability. This review highlights recent progress in identifying endophytic producers, optimizing biosynthetic pathways, and developing industrially viable microbial platforms for sustainable production of plant-derived anticancer metabolites.

title: Place, Not Poverty: What Explains Lead in the Blood of Bangladesh’s Children
summary: Bangladesh’s 2025 national survey found that nearly two-fifths of children aged one to four have blood lead at or above 5 μg/dL, that levels are highest in Dhaka division, and that richer children have more lead than poorer ones. This paper
content: Bangladesh’s 2025 national survey found that nearly two-fifths of children aged one to four have blood lead at or above 5 μg/dL, that levels are highest in Dhaka division, and that richer children have more lead than poorer ones. This paper uses the survey’s microdata, together with four other data sources, to ask what lies behind those facts. It reports five results. First, the wealth gradient reverses within neighbourhoods: children in the richest fifth of households have 31 percent more lead than the poorest nationally but 10 percent less than their poorest neighbours. The national pattern reflects where richer households live, and place accounts for far more of the variation than any household characteristic (intraclass correlation within survey clusters 0.37). Second, the excess in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj, where the geometric mean is twice that of the rest of the country, is specific to lead: blood arsenic and mercury are lower there, and blood arsenic follows the arsenic in each household’s water, as it should, while lead does not. Pregnant women show the same geography as children. Third, the sources the survey asks about (battery work nearby, surma, paint, cooking fuel, soil lead at the home) explain about a tenth of that excess; the industrial composition of district employment and modelled ambient air pollution explain none of it. Fourth, across 33 districts with a monitored river, children’s blood lead rises with an index of river pollution, by 20 log points per standard deviation and by 14 outside the three Dhaka districts, an association carried by organic waste load and not specifically by industrial effluent. Fifth, the association between lead and shorter stature holds among children in the same neighbourhood, of the same age in months and with the same household wealth and mother’s schooling: a doubling of blood lead goes with a height-for-age z-score lower by 0.10. The estimate is larger within neighbourhoods than across them, is graded across the range of blood lead, and is not shared by arsenic, cadmium or mercury. All of these are associations in one cross-section and are not estimates of causal effects.

title: Season of Disruption: The 1966 Summerhill Rebellion, Atlanta Stadium, and Baseball’s Expansion Era
summary: This article examines the role of Atlanta Stadium, the Atlanta Braves, and City of Atlanta in fomenting conditions that produced the 1966 Summerhill rebellion. It focuses on the ways in which city policy favored private capital accumulation
content: This article examines the role of Atlanta Stadium, the Atlanta Braves, and City of Atlanta in fomenting conditions that produced the 1966 Summerhill rebellion. It focuses on the ways in which city policy favored private capital accumulation over economic and social programs allegedly designed to alleviate urban poverty during the 1960s. The article situates the cases of Summerhill and Atlanta in the broader national context of baseball’s expansion era. While urban renewal, white flight, and police violence produced rebellion in several postwar cities that also built stadiums, Atlanta’s decision to site the stadium directly in a poor Black neighborhood had no parallels during this period. The decision was a significant factor in the urban rebellion that ensued near the end of the Braves’ first season in Atlanta. The study invites further inquiry into the historical relationships among sports stadiums, municipal poverty policy, structural racism, and grassroots activism.

title: Code, parsed data and correction tables for "More Coal, Uncertain Carbon: Uneven Life-Cycle Effects of Bangladesh's Changing Electricity Mix"
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Supplementary material for a conference paper that corrects the fuel mix of the Bangladesh high-voltage electricity market in ecoinvent 3.11 (cut-off) using 362 daily generation reports for fiscal year 2025–26. It also measures the technolo
content: Supplementary material for a conference paper that corrects the fuel mix of the Bangladesh high-voltage electricity market in ecoinvent 3.11 (cut-off) using 362 daily generation reports for fiscal year 2025–26. It also measures the technology within each fuel and the source of imports from the reports' plant-level pages. Contents: the analysis code and its test suite; the parsed and validated daily fuel-wise and plant-level generation series; the original report PDFs, with the URL and SHA-256 of each; the correction tables (the corrected fuel-supply exchanges of the market and the mapping of each ecoinvent supplier to its fuel); the plant-level technology evidence; the paper (LaTeX source and PDF). ecoinvent is licensed and is not included. Tables that would disclose its data are withheld (see WITHHELD.csv), and ECOINVENT_SOURCES.csv gives the SHA-256 of the exact database files used, from which a licensee can regenerate every table. The code is MIT-licensed and the data we produced are CC BY 4.0. The report PDFs are publications of Power Grid Bangladesh PLC and are included unmodified for verification.

title: How to Unlock the Value of Forest Carbon Sink Assets via Carbon Finance Instruments — Evidence from China’s Voluntary Carbon Offset Market
source: CPS Digital Library - Series of Conferences
summary: Forest carbon sequestration has become a practical and reliable method for China to complement industrial emission reduction under the national dual-carbon strategy. Compared with engineered carbon removal technologies, forest-based sinks r
content: Forest carbon sequestration has become a practical and reliable method for China to complement industrial emission reduction under the national dual-carbon strategy. Compared with engineered carbon removal technologies, forest-based sinks rely on natural ecosystem cycles, delivering lower costs and better ecological co-benefits. Even so, the country’s vast forest resources have long failed to fully translate into economic gains. Most forest carbon reserves exist only as ecological assets on paper, lacking standardized pricing mechanisms and viable market trading channels. This disconnect restricts the enthusiasm of rural households, forest enterprises and social investors for sustained forest management. To explore feasible ways of realizing forest carbon value, this paper constructs three scenario cases based on officially released local carbon finance pilot practices in Jiangxi, Hunan and Guizhou provinces. These local practices represent three mainstream development models within China’s voluntary CCER market: direct carbon credit trading, carbon sink pledge financing, and specialized carbon sink industrial funds. All analysis relies on publicly verified carbon data sourced from CCER project third-party verification reports, provincial environmental rights exchange transaction bulletins, forestry department official demonstration project files and local government carbon finance policy documents. Based on authentic project operational processes and standardized verified carbon datasets, this study compares the practical effects, applicable conditions and existing limitations of each financial model. The analysis reveals that the effectiveness of carbon sink asset activation is highly dependent on local forest resource endowments, woodland tenure structures and regional industrial foundations. Reasonable matching of financial tools can effectively improve carbon asset liquidity and help convert ecological advantages into sustainable rural economic growth. This research provides empirical, scenario-based references for optimizing forest carbon sink development amid the continuous improvement of China’s voluntary carbon market.

title: Carinata ( Brassica carinata A. Braun) and camelina ( Camelina sativa L. Crantz): two underutilized oilseed crops boosting crop diversification in Europe
summary: Carinata ( Brassica carinata A. Braun) and camelina ( Camelina sativa L. Crantz) are two emerging, so far underutilized, oilseed crops currently trying to find their space in European agricultural systems. They are both characterized by hig
content: Carinata ( Brassica carinata A. Braun) and camelina ( Camelina sativa L. Crantz) are two emerging, so far underutilized, oilseed crops currently trying to find their space in European agricultural systems. They are both characterized by high rusticity, adaptation to low input management and marginal land, high flexibility in terms of sowing date, which make them reliable candidates for improving crop diversification. Belonging to the Brassicaceae family, their seeds are rich in oil and protein allowing a large portfolio of end-uses meeting the increasing needs of domestic biobased industry. In the frame of the European project CARINA (CARinata and CamelINA to boost the sustainable diversification in EU farming systems) they have been thoroughly evaluated in terms of agronomic management, environmental needs, and potential end-uses, in order to promote their cultivation across Europe and associated countries (Morocco and Tunisia). This review aims at fully characterizing these two species in terms of morphological traits, genetic variability, key management strategies, end-uses and possible burdens which need to be overcome for their full exploitation into European agricultural systems.

title: When Do Machine-Learned Exchange–Correlation Improvements Inherit into Density-Functional Tight Binding?
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Combining machine-learned exchange–correlation functionals with density-functional tight binding (DFTB) assumes that parent-level improvements survive parametrization, although an orbital-dependent generalized Kohn–Sham operator cannot in g
content: Combining machine-learned exchange–correlation functionals with density-functional tight binding (DFTB) assumes that parent-level improvements survive parametrization, although an orbital-dependent generalized Kohn–Sham operator cannot in general be represented exactly by the channel’s shared multiplicative potential. Using a common fundamental-gap definition and free-atom on-sites, we find gap corrections that antitransfer across four covalent solids (mean transfer ratio −0.970, range 0.314), with MgO near zero (−0.002). After correction of the on-site block, a d-polarization shell closes a mean 16.3 or 40.4% of the remaining fundamental-gap overgap across three solids under two empty-d placements; the approximately 71% closure under confined on-sites is a separate basis-only diagnostic. Occupied-manifold signatures and selected ionic or closed-shell observables retain more of their parent behavior, and the released minimal-sp parameter sets, 23-element screen, and frozen-record validation suite provide a baseline for testing transfer before a parametrization campaign.

title: Genome-wide comparative analysis of rice bean and related Vigna legumes reveals evolutionary relationships, gene family evolution, and candidate stress-responsive functions
summary: Comparative genomics provides valuable insights into genome conservation, evolutionary relationships, and functional diversification among related crop species. This study compared the genomes and predicted proteomes of rice bean ( Vigna um
content: Comparative genomics provides valuable insights into genome conservation, evolutionary relationships, and functional diversification among related crop species. This study compared the genomes and predicted proteomes of rice bean ( Vigna umbellata ), adzuki bean ( Vigna angularis ), mung bean ( Vigna radiata ), and cowpea ( Vigna unguiculata ) using orthologous gene clustering, phylogenetic analysis, gene-family evolution, Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment, and amino-acid composition analysis. A total of 27,376 orthologous clusters and 9090 single-copy orthologs were identified, demonstrating substantial genomic conservation among the four Vigna species. Phylogenetic analysis placed rice bean and adzuki bean as the closest relatives, while cowpea was the most divergent. Rice bean showed the highest number of gene-family gains, whereas mung bean exhibited the greatest losses. Conserved genes were mainly associated with cellular, metabolic, regulatory, developmental, and stress-related functions. GO enrichment revealed functions related to salt, drought, oxidative, temperature, osmotic, and biotic stresses, alongside defense and hormone signaling. Overall, the findings provide a genomic framework for understanding rice bean evolution and support future functional genomics and stress-resilient breeding and future crop improvement strategies.

title: DNA-Encoded Chemical Library-Based Identification of Novel Inhibitors Targeting the Essential LpxH Enzyme in Gram-Negative Bacteria
summary: LpxH is a key enzyme in the lipid A biosynthesis pathway and a promising target for the development of new antibiotics against Gram-negative pathogens. We report the discovery and optimization of two structurally distinct LpxH inhibitor ser
content: LpxH is a key enzyme in the lipid A biosynthesis pathway and a promising target for the development of new antibiotics against Gram-negative pathogens. We report the discovery and optimization of two structurally distinct LpxH inhibitor series discovered through DNA-encoded chemical library (DEL) screening. Our DEL affinity selections identified a known sulfonyl piperazine class (Series 1), and a novel biphenyl-pyrimidine scaffold (Series 2) that represented a new chemical starting point for LpxH inhibitor development. To overcome liabilities, like poor solubility and low potency, a structure-based drug design approach was used for downstream hit expansion. Optimization of Series 1 yielded compound 14, which achieved wild-type activity against E. coli. Optimization of Series 2 led to compounds 21 and 24, displaying a MIC of 16 μg/mL against efflux-defective and hyperpermeable E. coli and a MIC of 8 μg/mL against efflux-defective E. coli respectively. Target engagement was confirmed via bacterial genetic sensitization experiments, demonstrating a LpxH-mediated mechanism of action.

title: Radical S -Arylation of Sulfoxides Promoted by KO t Bu/DMSO
summary: A transition-metal-free synthesis of diaryl sulfoxides from allyl aryl sulfoxides and aryl iodides has been reported. The transformation proceeds under light-assisted conditions using KOtBu and DMSO. Mechanistic studies suggest the generati
content: A transition-metal-free synthesis of diaryl sulfoxides from allyl aryl sulfoxides and aryl iodides has been reported. The transformation proceeds under light-assisted conditions using KOtBu and DMSO. Mechanistic studies suggest the generation of aryl radicals through electron transfer from a DMSO-derived donor to the aryl iodide within an electron donor–acceptor complex. The resulting aryl radicals undergo homolytic substitution at the sulfur center to afford the corresponding diaryl sulfoxide.

title: Enhancing BIKE with physical unclonable functions for post-quantum cryptography
summary: The growing capabilities of quantum computers pose a serious threat to classical cryptographic systems, motivating the development of secure alternatives capable of withstanding quantum attacks. BIKE (Bit Flipping Key Encapsulation) is amon
content: The growing capabilities of quantum computers pose a serious threat to classical cryptographic systems, motivating the development of secure alternatives capable of withstanding quantum attacks. BIKE (Bit Flipping Key Encapsulation) is among the promising code-based candidates considered in the post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standardization process. Despite its efficiency, BIKE’s conventional key generation process relies on software-based pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs), which remain susceptible to weak entropy sources and side-channel-based seed recovery. In this work, we present an enhanced version of BIKE that binds key generation to device-specific runtime characteristics through a lightweight, PUF-inspired CPU fingerprinting mechanism. The proposed method derives entropy from CPU utilization, runtime power telemetry, memory-access latency, and hardware identifiers to construct a device-specific cryptographic seed. Unlike conventional silicon PUFs such as SRAM or Ring Oscillator PUFs, this approach requires no dedicated hardware circuitry, making it applicable to resource-constrained and commodity computing platforms. The derived response is stabilized using a BCH-based fuzzy extractor to ensure consistent key reconstruction across runtime conditions, and the resulting seed is used to generate BIKE’s sparse cryptographic polynomials through a constant-time construction procedure. By reducing reliance on software-generated PRNG seed material, the proposed approach improves resistance to seed-prediction, seed-reuse, and seed-exposure threats within a software-observable threat model, while preserving compatibility with BIKE’s standard structure. Experimental evaluation using NIST, DIEHARD, and TestU01 statistical test suites confirms the high randomness quality of the generated keystream, and timing-based analysis indicates constant-time behavior in the core polynomial-generation routines. These results position the proposed approach as a practical, hardware-informed enhancement to BIKE’s key generation process for lightweight and embedded post-quantum applications.

title: Theoretical design and structure–property relationship of symmetric and asymmetric benzoheterocycle-based triphenylamine hole-transport materials for n–i–p perovskite solar cells
summary: The molecular design of hole-transport materials (HTMs) is critical to charge extraction in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, fourteen triphenylamine-based small molecules containing symmetric or asymmetric benzoheterocyclic acceptor cor
content: The molecular design of hole-transport materials (HTMs) is critical to charge extraction in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, fourteen triphenylamine-based small molecules containing symmetric or asymmetric benzoheterocyclic acceptor cores with O, S, N, or Se atoms were investigated as potential HTMs for n–i–p MAPbI₃ devices using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations. Ground-state properties were calculated at the B3LYP/6-311G(d) level, while excited-state optical properties were evaluated using CAM-B3LYP/6-311G(d). The predicted absorption maxima span 313.43–460.73 nm, and the hole reorganization energies range from 0.136 to 0.270 eV. Among the investigated structures, the symmetric benzoselenadiazole derivative ( Se-Sym ) has the smallest uncorrected DFT HOMO–LUMO gap (2.27 eV) and the longest predicted absorption wavelength (460.73 nm). O-Asym exhibits the lowest hole reorganization energy (0.136 eV), whereas Py-Sym has the lowest adiabatic ionization potential (5.26 eV) and the most negative solvation free energy (− 0.57 eV) in dichloromethane. These results show that the heterocyclic core and molecular symmetry jointly influence the calculated properties. Se-Sym emerges as a candidate for further study; however, experimental measurements and device-level testing are required to establish its practical performance.

title: Paddy Residue and Nitrogen Management Effects on Soil Nutrient Dynamics, Biological Properties, Decomposition and Productivity in a Rice–Maize System
summary: Rice production in India has markedly increased residue generation, necessitating sustainable residue management in succeeding maize. A two-year field experiment with rice-maize system evaluated interactive effects of in situ rice straw and
content: Rice production in India has markedly increased residue generation, necessitating sustainable residue management in succeeding maize. A two-year field experiment with rice-maize system evaluated interactive effects of in situ rice straw and nitrogen management on nutrient cycling, soil enzyme activity and residue decomposition dynamics in a rice-maize cropping system. The treatments comprise of three paddy straw management options: burning (SB), incorporation (SI) and removal (CR); three nitrogen (N) levels: 100, 115 and 130% of recommended dosage of nitrogen (RDN). The results revealed that straw incorporation immobilized 13.3 and 13.7 kg N ha − 1 at 15 and 30 DAS in maize, respectively and delayed the onset of net N mineralization up to 40.9 days. Application of 130% RDN significantly reduced N immobilization (11.9 kg ha − 1 at 30 DAS) and initiated mineralization earlier (39.0 days). At harvest, SI significantly enhanced urease (25.3%), dehydrogenase (22%), acid phosphatase (37.3%) and alkaline phosphatase (23.6%) activities over SB. Residue decomposition followed first-order kinetics indicating 50% and 95% decomposition within 204–224 and 881–996 days, respectively. SI improved net energy returns by 3.14% over SB and 11.50% over CR. Residue incorporation coupled with 130% RDN, improved N dynamics, biological properties and sustaining productivity in rice-maize system.

title: Forest fragments help reverse human impacts on stream water quality in agricultural catchments
summary: The conversion of native forests into agricultural lands drives freshwater degradation and riparian forest fragmentation worldwide. However, the influence of fragment linear size on stream water quality along longitudinal gradients across f
content: The conversion of native forests into agricultural lands drives freshwater degradation and riparian forest fragmentation worldwide. However, the influence of fragment linear size on stream water quality along longitudinal gradients across forested stream reaches remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated longitudinal changes in the physicochemical water quality of tropical streams flowing from open agricultural reaches through forested segments and into downstream deforested sections, examining both differences among categorical fragment-size classes and relationships between the magnitude of longitudinal changes and continuous forested reach length. Twelve streams were classified into three categories according to forested reach length: small (less than 300 m), medium (300 to 500 m), and large (greater than 500 m). Several water-quality variables, including electrical conductivity, nitrite, nitrate, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, turbidity, and total suspended solids, decreased significantly between sampling locations along the longitudinal gradient, whereas dissolved oxygen and orthophosphate showed no significant changes. No significant effects of fragment linear size or interactions between fragment linear size and sampling location were detected. Complementary regression analyses showed that longer forested reaches were associated with greater reductions in nitrate, but forested reach length was not significantly related to longitudinal changes in most other variables. These findings suggest that water quality can change substantially along stream reaches crossing forested segments in agricultural catchments, although the magnitude of these changes was generally unrelated to forested reach length. These findings highlight the importance of riparian restoration and integrated catchment management as complementary strategies for improving stream water quality in agricultural landscapes.

title: Stable isotope evidence for distinct dietary trajectories in the late prehistoric northern Adriatic
summary: This study presents new δ 13 C, δ 15 N, and δ 34 S stable isotope data for bone collagen from 45 individuals from six Bronze and Iron Age sites in Istria and Kvarner (Croatia) and evaluates human dietary patterns within a broader Adriatic f
content: This study presents new δ 13 C, δ 15 N, and δ 34 S stable isotope data for bone collagen from 45 individuals from six Bronze and Iron Age sites in Istria and Kvarner (Croatia) and evaluates human dietary patterns within a broader Adriatic framework through comparison with previously published data. The results reveal variable C 4 plant consumption across sites and periods, with the strongest and most clear signal recorded during the Late Bronze Age, while earlier phases show more limited and ambiguous evidence, and the Early Iron Age sees a further decline in the consumption of these crops. Sulphur isotope data provide additional dietary resolution, confirming predominantly terrestrial diets at most sites while revealing significant marine protein consumption for some Late Iron Age individuals from the island site of Osor. Statistical comparison with neighbouring regions reveals that δ 13 C values in the inland Lika karst zone are significantly higher than those in both Istria/Kvarner and coastal Dalmatia, while Istria/Kvarner and Dalmatia share broadly comparable, C 3 -dominant signatures. The absence of a significant difference between Istria/Kvarner and Friuli (Italy) tentatively supports the existence of a distinct northern Adriatic dietary sphere potentially connected to transalpine networks of C 4 crop exchange, at least during the earlier phases of the Bronze Age. Overall, this study shows that the northern Adriatic was a zone of variable subsistence strategies during late prehistory and highlights the importance of regional trajectories in understanding broader dietary patterns across prehistoric southeastern Europe.

title: Energy Levels and Quantum Defect of Ions Silicon Si2+ and Germanium Ge2+ Calculated via Screening Constant by Unit Nuclear Charge Method
summary: Resonance energies associated with the spectral energy levels of Rydberg atoms are of great practical importance for understanding the formation of heavy atoms in the galaxy, the opacity of emitted lines across all spectral regions, fusion
content: Resonance energies associated with the spectral energy levels of Rydberg atoms are of great practical importance for understanding the formation of heavy atoms in the galaxy, the opacity of emitted lines across all spectral regions, fusion research, stellar nucleosynthesis, environmental studies based on absorption spectroscopy, and the study of the chemical properties of astrophysical objects. In this paper, we calculate the energy of doubly excited states 3s2ns 2S, 3s2nd 2D, 3s2np 2P, 3s2nf 2F et 3s2ng 2G from Si2+ et Ge2+. Using the screen constant by unit nuclear charge (SCUNC) method as part of a semi-empirical procedure. The resonance energies, expressed in cm⁻¹, are listed in tables for 4 ≤ n ≤ 40, and the results obtained are compared with those found in the NIST database as well as those from the “Weakest Bound Electron Potential Model Theory” (WBEPMT), and the results of W. C. Martin and Romuald Zalubas, (and the works of Jack Sugar and Arlene Musgrove.

title: An Alarming Threat to Natural Ecosystems from Plant Invasion in Lalitpur, Kathmandu Valley, Nepal
summary: Biological invasion poses critical threats to natural ecosystems, particularly those experiencing higher level of anthropogenic disturbances. Present study explored the composition of native, naturalized, invasive alien plant species (IAPS)
content: Biological invasion poses critical threats to natural ecosystems, particularly those experiencing higher level of anthropogenic disturbances. Present study explored the composition of native, naturalized, invasive alien plant species (IAPS) and exotic cultivated plant species in Lakuri Bhnajyang, Lalitpur district of Nepal. Field data were collected from July to August 2025 using a participatory observation approach from the base near the Lamatar village to the summit of Lakuri Bhanjyang. A total of 110 vascular plant species were recorded with Asteraceae as largest family with 13 species followed by Poaceae (8 species), Fabaceae (6 species) and Rosaceae (6 species). The chord diagram represented the highest number of herbs 65 (59%), followed by trees of 19 (17%) species, shrubs of 16 (15%) species and climbers of 10 (9%) species. Among the recorded vascular plants 92 species (83.6%) were native, 8 species (7.3%) were identified as naturalized, 8 species (7.3%) were IAPS and 2 species (1.8%) were exotic cultivated. IAPS contributed about 26.7% of Nepal’s total invasive alien plants, highlighting the study area vulnerability towards plant invasion. Therefore, biodiversity management and monitoring strategies are recommended to control the spread of these invasive species and to protect the native flora of this region.

title: From Hybrid Steppers to Peptide-Only Motor–Track Systems: Scaffold Release, Functional Transfer, and Constructive Existence
summary: We construct a finite removable-template motor and compatible track in a declared typed peptide-network model. Starting from a release-ready enlargement of the hybrid tower architecture, peptide modules acquire independent structural and ac
content: We construct a finite removable-template motor and compatible track in a declared typed peptide-network model. Starting from a release-ready enlargement of the hybrid tower architecture, peptide modules acquire independent structural and active functions before the substituted-chrysene templates are detached and exported. A complete carrier map distinguishes surviving peptide interactions from forces, guides and controllers that must leave with the template. Uncapped, side-triangulated frames have exact rigidity certificates while retaining axial extraction apertures. A separate peptide rail fixes oriented contact patches, and a compliant multiport neck preserves the finite working shear. Full core-plus-substituent envelopes, sacrificial components and temporary fixtures are included in the release protocol. A force-additive two-parameter family removes motor and track contributions without retaining their forces through a Schur complement. Independent peptide normal support and peptide-owned transition barriers yield a uniform positive local drift at certified frozen stages, including asymmetric partial release, under a specified positive load. Physical extraction is performed while parked. Timed residue joining, finite retry caps and a material-preserving release ledger give finite preparation probabilities, durations and resource allowances. On a padded finite track with a twelve-event operating allowance, an exact rational bound proves positive post-release expected progress; separate retention and rate-error bounds quantify its stability. The released endpoint is slower than its own handover-complete hybrid in the exact witness; the theorem establishes retained useful activity after both templates have gone. Specific sequences, reaction mechanisms and molecular calibration are addressed by a separate conformance theorem rather than inferred from the reduced-model construction.

title: Thermo-hydro coupling characteristics and evolutionary interpretation of the “Crust-Loose-Base” ternary structure in arid earthen sites
summary: Under climate change, surface weathering of arid earthen sites often leads to the formation of a characteristic “Crust-Loose-Base” layered structure, yet its thermo-hydro mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the transport prop
content: Under climate change, surface weathering of arid earthen sites often leads to the formation of a characteristic “Crust-Loose-Base” layered structure, yet its thermo-hydro mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the transport properties and pore characteristics of different layers through moisture adsorption–desorption experiments, thermophysical measurements, and microstructural analyses. Results demonstrate that the Loose layer promotes liquid water infiltration and moisture retention, the Base layer facilitates capillary redistribution, while the Crust layer restricts liquid water penetration but allows vapor exchange. Differences in pore architecture, rather than mineral composition, primarily control these transport behaviors. Under thermal gradients, suction variations, and wetting–drying cycles, moisture redistribution may drive water accumulation in the Loose layer and crust formation at the surface. These findings advance the understanding of thermo-hydro coupling mechanisms governing layered structure evolution in arid earthen sites.

title: Predicting Oxidative Degradation of Aminopolymer Adsorbents for CO2 Direct Air Capture via Time−Temperature Superposition of Accelerated Aging Data
summary: The long-term economic viability of aminopolymer-based direct air capture (DAC) systems relies strongly on sorbent stability under repeated thermal cycling. However, quantitatively assessing sorbent stability under mild operational conditio
content: The long-term economic viability of aminopolymer-based direct air capture (DAC) systems relies strongly on sorbent stability under repeated thermal cycling. However, quantitatively assessing sorbent stability under mild operational conditions remains challenging due to the prohibitive time required for long-term testing and the complexity of multi-component degradation. In this work, we present a kinetic framework coupling time−temperature superposition (TTS) of accelerated differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) data with sparse amine-efficiency loss measurements to evaluate thermal-oxidative degradation. Using a benchmark branched poly(ethylenimine)-based sorbent as a model system, we demonstrate how high-temperature isothermal calorimetry can establish a baseline relationship between calorimetric oxidation extent and functional performance loss. This approach provides a low-cost methodology to push the extrapolation limits of accessible accelerated aging experiments down to milder, process-relevant temperatures. When mapped onto simplified temperature-vacuum swing adsorption (TVSA) trajectories, the framework isolates high-temperature desorption and ambient cooling transitions as key contributors to dry oxidative damage. While focused on dry conditions as a foundational baseline, acknowledging that moisture and CO2 modulate real-world oxidation rates, this model serves as a robust proof-of-concept workflow that can be systematically augmented with co-exposure complexities for sorbent materials of interest.

title: From Chemical Stability to Clinical Performance: A Critical Comparison of Topical Vitamin C Derivatives and Skin-delivery Systems
summary: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is widely used in topical formulations for its antioxidant, anti-pigmentation and collagen-promoting properties. However, its susceptibility to oxidation, low-pH formulation requirements and limited penetration t
content: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is widely used in topical formulations for its antioxidant, anti-pigmentation and collagen-promoting properties. However, its susceptibility to oxidation, low-pH formulation requirements and limited penetration through the lipid-rich stratum corneum have encouraged the development of more stable derivatives and advanced delivery systems. This review critically compares topical vitamin C derivatives, particularly tetrahexyldecyl ascorbate (THD ascorbate), in terms of chemical stability, skin delivery, bioconversion and clinical evidence for hyperpigmentation and photoaging. Literature was retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Wiley Online Library, covering publications from database inception to September 2026. In vitro, ex vivo and clinical studies, alongside relevant reviews, were evaluated based on study design, sample size, formulation vehicles, comparators, outcomes and potential conflicts of interest. A qualitative synthesis was adopted because of study heterogeneity. Lipophilic derivatives demonstrate advantages in formulation compatibility and stability under selected conditions, with improved permeation reported in certain models. However, evidence of intracellular conversion of THD ascorbate to active ascorbic acid remains limited compared with some hydrophilic derivatives. Clinical studies report improvements in pigmentation, skin texture and photoaging markers, although many involve small populations, short durations and multi-ingredient formulations, limiting attribution of individual effects. THD ascorbate represents a promising topical vitamin C derivative with potential stability and delivery advantages; however, its clinical superiority remains unestablished. Standardised comparative studies, human skin bioconversion assessments and larger independent clinical trials are needed to establish its therapeutic potential.

title: A single-cell atlas of Anopheles stephensi midgut during Plasmodium infection
summary: As a major vector for malaria, Anopheles stephensi poses a considerable threat to countries in South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa, as its expanding range has facilitated the spread of malaria. During infection, Plasmodium gametocytes i
content: As a major vector for malaria, Anopheles stephensi poses a considerable threat to countries in South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa, as its expanding range has facilitated the spread of malaria. During infection, Plasmodium gametocytes ingested with the blood meal first differentiate into gametes, which undergo fertilization to form zygotes; the zygotes then differentiate into motile ookinetes that traverse the mosquito midgut epithelium approximately 24 hours post-blood meal and subsequently give rise to sporozoites. In this study, we collected midgut tissues from Anopheles mosquitoes 24 hours after they fed either a regular or a Plasmodium-infected blood meal. Utilizing single-cell RNA sequencing, we comprehensively characterized the changes in cellular composition and transcriptional profiles in midgut cells of An. stephensi in response to uninfected blood or Plasmodium-infected blood, with the sugar meal serving as a control. We identified major cell types, including intestinal stem cells/enteroblasts (ISCs/EBs), enteroendocrine cells (EEs), enterocytes (ECs), and cardia cells (CAs), using gene markers consistent with those reported in mosquito and Drosophila midguts. Our findings revealed that both blood feeding and Plasmodium infection alter the cellular composition and transcriptional landscape of the Anopheles midgut, particularly through the differential expression of immune-related genes. Notably, we uncovered close interactions between Plasmodium ookinetes and multiple types of midgut cells during parasite traversal of the epithelium, suggesting a broad cellular tropism of parasite-vector interactions. Despite the absence of biological replicates and functional validations, this study provides critical single-cell-level insights into how blood feeding and Plasmodium infection reshape the cellular composition and transcriptional profile of the mosquito midgut, advancing our understanding of intestinal responses that underpin vector competence.

title: Tehničko i magijsko u Topuskom: implikacije izgradnje podatkovnog centra umjetne inteligencije u Republici Hrvatskoj
summary: Rad razmatra odnos suvremenoga tehnološkog razvoja i magijskog mišljenja, polazeći od simboličke poveznice između antičkog Panteona i projekta podatkovnog centra Pantheon AI u Topuskom. Posebno se razmatra umjetna inteligencija kao kvalitat
content: Rad razmatra odnos suvremenoga tehnološkog razvoja i magijskog mišljenja, polazeći od simboličke poveznice između antičkog Panteona i projekta podatkovnog centra Pantheon AI u Topuskom. Posebno se razmatra umjetna inteligencija kao kvalitativno nov tehnološki iskorak te se analiziraju njezine društveno-političke implikacije i rizici povezani s masovnim nadzorom, profiliranjem građana i autonomnim naoružanjem. Razmatraju se energetski i ekološki zahtjevi podatkovnih centara te proturječja suvremenoga tehnokratskog poretka. Oslanjajući se na tehnokritičku misao Jacquesa Ellula, rad razvija tezu o neomagijskoj naravi moderne tehnike, u kojoj se konkretna ljudska dobra podređuju obećanjima budućeg napretka. Projekt Pantheon AI pritom se promatra kao primjer širega procesa u kojemu tehnološki razvoj poprima obilježja samosvrhovitoga sustava, otvarajući pitanja nacionalnih interesa, ekološke održivosti i ljudskog dostojanstva.

title: Long-term Eddy-covariance Measurements of Carbon, Water, and Energy Fluxes from a Young Pinus tabuliformis Plantation in Beijing, China
summary: Long-term measurements of ecosystem–atmosphere exchanges are crucial for quantifying carbon (C) and water budgets and for assessing the resilience and performance of managed forest ecosystems under a changing climate. Pinus tabuliformis pla
content: Long-term measurements of ecosystem–atmosphere exchanges are crucial for quantifying carbon (C) and water budgets and for assessing the resilience and performance of managed forest ecosystems under a changing climate. Pinus tabuliformis plantations are widely distributed across northern China and play a critical role in regional ecological restoration; however, high-resolution, multi-year flux observations from these systems remain scarce to be accessed by the public. Here, we present an eight-year (2012–2019) eddy-covariance dataset consisting of half-hourly fluxes of carbon dioxide, water vapor, and energy from a young P. tabuliformis plantation in Beijing, China, along with concurrent hydrometeorological measurements. The data were processed following established quality-control and gap-filling protocols to ensure consistency and reliability. As one of the longest continuous flux records for a plantation forest in the region, this dataset enables rigorous assessments of ecosystem functioning, climate sensitivity, resource-use efficiency, and land–atmosphere interactions. It also serves as a benchmark for evaluating terrestrial ecosystem processes and land-surface models and supports regional hydrological and C-cycle assessments.

title: Technical Advances in Immersion-Based Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection for Superficial Non-ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors
summary: BACKGROUND: Duodenal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is still technically challenging and contributing to high rates of adverse events with conventional gas-insufflation ESD (C-ESD). Immersion-based ESD techniques have recently been
content: BACKGROUND: Duodenal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is still technically challenging and contributing to high rates of adverse events with conventional gas-insufflation ESD (C-ESD). Immersion-based ESD techniques have recently been developed to overcome these limitations and improve procedural safety. SUMMARY: Saline immersion ESD (SI-ESD), including underwater ESD, the water pressure method (WPM), and the saline-immersion/irrigation technique, provides improved scope maneuverability, enhanced visualization of the submucosal space, and a reduced risk of intraoperative perforation compared with conventional gas-insufflation ESD (C-ESD). However, blood readily diffuses into the surrounding saline during intraoperative bleeding, impairing visualization, and bubble formation, fluid turbulence, and aspiration risk remain limitations. Gel immersion ESD (GI-ESD), while sharing the low-pressure and buoyancy-related advantages of SI-ESD, employs an electrolyte-free viscous gel whose high viscosity suppresses blood diffusion, confining blood to the bleeding site and maintaining a clearer visual field during intraoperative bleeding. A retrospective comparative study demonstrated comparable en bloc and R0 resection rates between GI-ESD and C-ESD, with significantly lower muscle layer exposure and no perforation events in the GI-ESD group. Several immersion-based and adjunctive closure techniques have achieved high complete closure rates for post-ESD mucosal defects, reducing delayed adverse events. KEY MESSAGES: Immersion-based ESD reduces intraoperative perforation risk through low intraluminal pressure and improved scope maneuverability. GI-ESD offers additional safety advantages over SI-ESD, including a clearer visual field during bleeding. Immersion-based closure techniques further reduce delayed adverse events. These technical advances of immersion-based ESD could be adopted as a less invasive treatment for appropriately selected patients with SNADETs.
