CV, EIS, pH, and ORP analyses further confirmed that UV-PA possessed Cr(VI) reduction capability, with the highest electron transfer efficiency observed under UV+aerobic conditions. Probe compound experiments revealed that the generation of O was maximized under these conditions, effectively promoting Cr(VI) reduction. In the presence of Cr(VI), dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and total nitrogen (TN) concentrations increased to 15 mg/L and 6 mg/L, respectively, indicating that Cr(VI) accelerated the leaching of UV-PA. EEM-PARAFAC analysis showed that the leachates were mainly composed of protein-like and humic-like substances, while NO was detected only in Cr(VI)-containing systems. LC–MS results further indicated that Cr(VI) could selectively cleave PA molecular chains and promote the formation of specific organic compounds. These findings provide new insights into the interaction mechanisms and environmental behavior of combined microplastic–heavy metal pollution systems.

title: Stereoscopic photoacoustic microscopy reveals impaired glymphatic–mLV–dCLN transport after prolonged isoflurane anesthesia
summary: Anesthetic exposure is implicated in perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), but tracer transport across the glymphatic–meningeal lymphatic vessel (mLV)–deep cervical lymph node (dCLN) pathway after prolonged anesthesia remains unclea
content: Anesthetic exposure is implicated in perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), but tracer transport across the glymphatic–meningeal lymphatic vessel (mLV)–deep cervical lymph node (dCLN) pathway after prolonged anesthesia remains unclear. Dual-contrast functional photoacoustic microscopy (DCF-PAM) was used to characterize tracer transport in vivo after prolonged isoflurane anesthesia, with ex vivo validation. Prolonged anesthesia induced acute cognitive impairment, reduced early glymphatic tracer entry, decreased mLV coverage, and reduced perivascular AQP4 polarization. Bilateral dCLN ligation further impaired glymphatic transport and cognitive function. AAV-VEGF-C pretreatment was associated with greater mLV coverage, enhanced glymphatic–mLV–dCLN tracer transport, and improved cognitive impairment. These findings link glymphatic–mLV–dCLN dysfunction to anesthesia-associated lymphatic transport impairment and support further investigation of this pathway as a potential intervention target. This study represents the first application of DCF-PAM in a prolonged isoflurane anesthesia model, supporting its utility for in vivo assessment of brain transport function and neuroscience research.

title: Nonlinear Broadband Wave Energy Harvesting via Pendulum-Based Converters for Sustainable Self-Powered Marine Observation: A Review
source: Journal of Maritime Innovation and Sustainability
summary: Pendulum-based wave energy converters (WECs) offer a promising route to self-powered marine observation. A sealed buoy converts low-frequency, irregular, and multidirectional wave motion into electricity for onboard sensors and telemetry, r
content: Pendulum-based wave energy converters (WECs) offer a promising route to self-powered marine observation. A sealed buoy converts low-frequency, irregular, and multidirectional wave motion into electricity for onboard sensors and telemetry, reducing battery-replacement and vessel-access requirements. This review synthesizes evidence in four groups: built-in and miniaturized point absorbers, rotating-pendulum electromagnetic harvesters, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), and hybrid TENG–electromagnetic systems. The first two groups define the core pendulum-based scope; TENG and hybrid studies without a pendulum are included only as contextual comparators when they inform low-frequency conversion, power management, durability, or marine deployment. Rather than cataloguing devices, the review groups them by nonlinear mechanism, with emphasis on parametric excitation, rotational orbits, multistability, and bounded chaos, which can broaden the operating bandwidth under realistic sea states. On that mechanistic basis, a fluid–mechanical–electrical coupled modeling framework is outlined, together with design principles, experimental standardization, and field-validation requirements for self-powered observation buoys. Because progress is constrained less by isolated peak outputs than by the incompatibility of reported metrics, the review also sets out minimum reporting requirements for cross-study comparison. It then assesses remaining challenges in power-take-off design, energy management, durability, and the sustainability of distributed ocean observation. Together, these strands indicate how miniature pendulum WECs may move from laboratory prototypes toward energy-autonomous marine sensing infrastructure, while identifying where the evidence remains too thin to support that transition.

title: Large-scale 3D stitching montage cryo-electron tomography reveals heterogeneity and connectivity of lamellipodial actin networks
summary: Cellular processes range from local interactions among a few proteins to micrometer-scale assemblies whose coordinated components give rise to emergent properties. A prime example is the actin cytoskeleton in protrusive structures at the le
content: Cellular processes range from local interactions among a few proteins to micrometer-scale assemblies whose coordinated components give rise to emergent properties. A prime example is the actin cytoskeleton in protrusive structures at the leading edge of migrating cells, termed lamellipodia. Significant progress has been made in understanding the functional contributions of distinct actin-filament populations and associated proteins within lamellipodia. Yet, a detailed quantitative appreciation of how actin filaments form a spatially connected and interdependent network has been impeded by limitations of existing methods. Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) can visualize such biological entities at molecular resolution in native cellular environments, but its limited field-of -view constrains quantitative analysis of extended assemblies. Hence, how lamellipodial actin architectures collectively support productive migration is not completely understood. Here, we present a 3D stitching montage cryo-ET workflow that advances both methodological and biological frontiers through its application to lamellipodia. We combine large-area montage-tilt series acquisition with independent tile reconstruction, denoising, and optical flow-based three-dimensional stitching to reconstruct large regions of the leading edge up to ~ 100 μm 2 at single-filament resolution. Bridging molecular resolution and cellular-scale context allows comprehensive filament tracing and quantification of actin filament networks, providing parameters for models of force generation in motile cells. Our data reveal that the network architecture in a seemingly uniform protrusive lamellipodium is markedly heterogeneous. By mapping Arp2/3 branch junction-based connectivity, using the molecular resolution of our data, we show how branch-junction distribution and network connectivity vary as a function of filament density and distance from the leading edge. We also identify the complex coexistence of short, branched and long, unbranched filament assemblies. We provide montage 3D volumes and filament vectorizations through an interactive, open web-based resource for browsing and interrogating the data. Our work thus provides a quantitative reference for lamellipodial actin architecture and a scalable approach for large-scale cryo-ET.

title: Design of an Interactive Intelligent QA System for Power Knowledge Base Based on Language Model Combined with Intelligent Retrieval
source: Archives des sciences a multidisciplinary journal
summary: To address challenges in the power sector, such as heterogeneous knowledge sources, complex domain-specific semantic relationships, the limitations of traditional retrieval methods in handling multi-turn interactions, and the tendency of la
content: To address challenges in the power sector, such as heterogeneous knowledge sources, complex domain-specific semantic relationships, the limitations of traditional retrieval methods in handling multi-turn interactions, and the tendency of large language models (LLMs) to generate factual hallucinations—this paper proposes an interactive intelligent question-answering framework for power-domain knowledge bases. This framework integrates multi-agent knowledge construction, context-aware processing, and adaptive retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). First, an ontology-constrained, multi-agent collaborative knowledge extraction mechanism is designed; through entity localization, attribute fusion, and evidence tracing, a hybrid vector-graph knowledge base is constructed using FAISS and Neo4j. Second, the framework incorporates structured dialogue memory, context-aware query reformulation, and a two-tier keyword enhancement strategy to facilitate entity coreference resolution, semantic completion, and the propagation of domain-specific constraints across multi-turn interactions. Building on this, a multi-path retrieval mechanism is developed, incorporating semantic coverage, terminology anchoring, and document structure priors, which utilizes a lightweight language model to dynamically adjust retrieval weights and optimizes evidence ranking through cross-path consensus feedback. Finally, by integrating evidence-constrained generation, factual consistency verification, and uncertainty assessment, the framework enhances the traceability and reliability of the generated answers. The proposed framework is evaluated through the design of a multi-type power-domain QA benchmark, alongside comparative experiments, ablation studies, and robustness tests, assessing performance across dimensions such as retrieval quality, answer accuracy, multi-turn consistency, and computational efficiency.

title: Towards the Development of Sustainable Organic Thin-Film Transistors
summary: Electronic devices are used for tasks ranging from health monitoring and environmental sensing to communication and consumer electronics. As demand for these devices grows, so does the volume of electronic waste (e-waste) they leave behind,
content: Electronic devices are used for tasks ranging from health monitoring and environmental sensing to communication and consumer electronics. As demand for these devices grows, so does the volume of electronic waste (e-waste) they leave behind, most of which is exported, incinerated, or sent to landfills, where non-degradable components such as semiconductors, dielectrics, and metal electrodes can persist for years. This growing problem has motivated interest in transient electronics: devices designed to intentionally degrade after their functional lifetime. For biodegradable materials to be viable in these devices, they need to be solution-processable and capable of controlled degradation, all while maintaining the electrical performance expected of conventional electronic materials. This thesis focuses on the development of low-voltage operation sustainable organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs) that combine strong electrical performance with reduced use of non-degradable materials and engineered, controllable degradation pathways. The first study focused on integrating a biodegradable dielectric with a biodegradable substrate to build a cytocompatible and fully disintegrable low-voltage n-type OTFT. I paired a fluorinated silicon phthalocyanine (F10-SiPc) semiconductor with a bilayer poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and poly(caprolactone) (PCL) dielectric deposited on a polylactic acid (PLA) substrate. This bilayer dielectric substantially lowered the threshold voltage (VT) compared to a conventional SiO2 dielectric while maintaining comparable electron mobility (μ), and I showed that the complete device could disintegrate in phosphate-buffered saline solution within 20 days without producing degradation products toxic to cultured fibroblasts. In the second study, I report that a non-biodegradable diketopyrrolopyrrole-based semiconducting polymer (DPP2T) can be blended with the biodegradable polymers PLA and PCL to reduce the amount of active semiconductor (DPP2T) required in an OTFT by roughly 70-80%. Rather than sacrificing performance, the right PLA-PCL ratio actually improved device performance over neat DPP2T by increasing μ, lowering the VT, and improving Ion/off, while also improving long-term stability under ambient air exposure. In my last study, I built on this dielectric-and-substrate foundation to address a key limitation: once assembled, these devices dissolved into a single system, making it difficult to separate or recover individual materials. I designed a fully sustainable p-type OTFT using an imine-linked degradable semiconducting polymer (PDPP-TIT) paired with a PVA/UV-crosslinked-PCL bilayer dielectric on a PLA substrate, engineering each layer to respond to a different degradation trigger. This device also achieved a reduction in VT relative to a conventional SiO2 dielectric, and I demonstrated that the semiconductor and dielectric could be selectively dissolved under acidic conditions while the substrate degraded separately under bas

title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
summary: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (
content: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (coordination-based models like the alpha-scheme). Here, we present AdsNet, an equivariant graph neural network that directly predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass, which operates on a local graph restricted only to adsorbate atoms and its immediate surface neighbors within a cutoff radius. This local graph formulation decouples computational complexity from total system size while encoding continuous geometric features (interatomic distances and directional vectors) enabling sensitivity to subtle variations in local bonding environments. AdsNet adopts a message-passing architecture with scalar and vector node features over multiple interaction layers. Trained on AdsTraj, a dataset of 33,920 density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates (H*, C*, O*, CO*, OH*, HOCO*), the model achieves an adsorption energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/A. Analytic forces obtained via automatic differentiation enable structure relaxation through a projected gradient descent algorithm with adaptive line search, eliminating entire geometry optimizations. Additionally, AdsNet uniquely decomposes predicted adsorption energies into contributions from individual atoms within the local adsorbate graph - an interpretability feature unattainable with conventional machine-learning potentials. AdsNet thus establishes an accurate, highly efficient, and interpretable framework for large-scale adsorption energy prediction and local interface relaxation across various material surfaces.

title: Granular sludge management
summary: Die Technologie des aeroben granulären Schlamms (AGS) bietet großes Potenzial für eine effiziente und ressourcenschonende Abwasserbehandlung. Ihre großtechnische Umsetzung ist jedoch weiterhin mit Herausforderungen verbunden, insbesondere b
content: Die Technologie des aeroben granulären Schlamms (AGS) bietet großes Potenzial für eine effiziente und ressourcenschonende Abwasserbehandlung. Ihre großtechnische Umsetzung ist jedoch weiterhin mit Herausforderungen verbunden, insbesondere beim Schlammmanagement. Diese Arbeit untersucht daher die anaerobe Faulung, Entwässerbarkeit sowie die Rückgewinnung von Phosphor und alginatähnlichen Polymeren (ALE) aus AGS. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Granulatgröße und extrazelluläre polymere Substanzen (EPS) die Abbaubarkeit, Methanbildung und Entwässerbarkeit wesentlich beeinflussen. Im Vergleich zu konventionellem Belebtschlamm zeigte AGS eine geringere Abbaubarkeit und Entwässerbarkeit. Gleichzeitig erwies sich AGS als vielversprechende Quelle für die Rückgewinnung von Phosphor und ALE. Die Ergebnisse tragen zu einem besseren Verständnis des AGS-Schlammmanagements und seiner nachhaltigen Integration in bestehende Abwasserbehandlungsanlagen bei.

title: EXPORT PORTFOLIO COMPOSITION, UNCERTAINTY TRANSMISSION, AND GDP DYNAMICS: A STOCHASTIC FACTOR MODEL FRAMEWORK
source: Far East Journal of Theoretical Statistics
summary: The composition and diversity of a nation's export basket influence both growth and susceptibility to external shocks, yet standard macroeconomic models typically treat exports as a single aggregate in the national income identity. Using 46
content: The composition and diversity of a nation's export basket influence both growth and susceptibility to external shocks, yet standard macroeconomic models typically treat exports as a single aggregate in the national income identity. Using 46 years of Kenyan data (1980-2025), with the core estimation window spanning 1996-2022, this study develops and empirically tests a stochastic, export-driven GDP framework. GDP growth is decomposed into a deterministic term representing portfolio-weighted sectoral trend growth and a stochastic term representing common global shocks transmitted through sector-specific loadings. Feasible Generalized Least Squares is used to estimate five systematic factors across six HS-level export sectors: commodity-price volatility, global demand, exchange-rate movements, global economic policy uncertainty, and total factor productivity. A Student- \(t\) copula is employed to capture cross-sectoral residual dependence. The export-portfolio problem is reformulated as a Second-Order Cone Program, with Conditional Value-at-Risk adopted as a coherent measure of downside GDP risk. Four findings stand out. First, export concentration, measured by the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, is associated with materially lower GDP growth: an uncontrolled bivariate specification yields an approximate 3 percentage-point difference across Kenya's historical HHI range. Second, commodity-price volatility, not productivity, is the dominant source of systematic variance transmission, while productivity growth primarily drives trend export growth. Third, global uncertainty shocks affect the tail of the GDP distribution rather than its conditional mean. Fourth, the SOCP-optimal portfolio dominates both the historical and equal-weighted portfolios on expected growth and tail risk. Although the optimal portfolio is not less concentrated than the status quo by the HHI metric, it reallocates weight away from the highest-variance sector. Naive equal-weighting performs worst on CVaR, demonstrating that diversification that ignores sectoral risk structure can increase macroeconomic vulnerability.

title: Analisis Peran Mediasi Brand Image pada Pengaruh Green Marketing Mix terhadap Purchase Intention Konsumen pada Weavora Tas Anyaman Bamban
summary: This study aims to analyse the influence of an eco-friendly marketing mix on purchase intention, with brand image acting as a mediating variable, at the Weavora Bamban Woven Bags SME. This study specifically examines the relative role of ea
content: This study aims to analyse the influence of an eco-friendly marketing mix on purchase intention, with brand image acting as a mediating variable, at the Weavora Bamban Woven Bags SME. This study specifically examines the relative role of each dimension of green marketing in shaping consumer perceptions in the context of locally-based eco-friendly products. A quantitative approach was employed using the Partial Least Squares-based Structural Equation Modelling (SEM-PLS) method on 100 respondents selected via purposive sampling. The results indicate that eco-friendly products, eco-friendly promotions, and eco-friendly locations have a positive and significant influence on brand image and purchase intention, whilst eco-friendly pricing does not have a significant influence on either variable. Brand image proved to be the most dominant variable and fully mediated the influence of most dimensions of the green marketing mix on purchase intention. These findings reveal that, in the context of SMEs based on environmentally friendly products, purchasing decisions are not driven by price considerations, but rather by the strength of brand image built through communication and product value. Thus, this study contributes to enriching the literature on green marketing by emphasising the importance of brand image as the primary mechanism for converting sustainable marketing strategies into consumer purchase intent.

title: Tissue-specific effects of in ovo prebiotic stimulation on cytokine gene expression in broiler chickens
summary: The modulation of the immune system during the early life of broiler chickens has been shown to have a beneficial effect on disease resistance and overall health. The present study investigated the effects of in ovo administration of xylo-
content: The modulation of the immune system during the early life of broiler chickens has been shown to have a beneficial effect on disease resistance and overall health. The present study investigated the effects of in ovo administration of xylo- and mannooligosaccharides (XOS and MOS) on cytokine gene expression in two immune-relevant tissues: the spleen and cecal tonsils. The injection of fertilized eggs was conducted on embryonic day 12, with the substances xylotriose (XOS3), xylotetraose (XOS4), mannotriose (MOS3), mannotetraose (MOS4), or saline (control) utilised for this purpose. The gene expression of cytokines representing general immune regulation (IL1β, IL2, IL10), Th1 (IL8, IL12, IFNβ, IFNγ), Th2 (IL4, IL6), and Th17 (IL17) pathways was quantified in 42-day-old birds using RT-qPCR. A significant immunomodulatory effect was observed in the spleen, where XOS3 consistently increased the expression of cytokines associated with Th1-, Th2-, and Th17-mediated responses, indicating enhanced systemic immune activation. Conversely, no statistically significant differences were detected in the cecal tonsils, although numerical variation was present. This muted mucosal response is likely to reflect the inherent heterogeneity and tolerance-oriented function of gut-associated lymphoid tissue, consistent with the concept of acquired immunotolerance to commensal microbiota. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that in ovo prebiotic stimulation exerts tissue-specific effects, promoting systemic immune readiness while maintaining mucosal homeostasis, and highlight XOS3 as a particularly effective modulator of splenic cytokine expression in broiler chickens.

title: EU skilled circular migration and financial risk
summary: Purpose This study examines which institutional and labor market conditions are associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility between EU country pairs and how these conditions relate to human capital allocation risk. Design/methodolo
content: Purpose This study examines which institutional and labor market conditions are associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility between EU country pairs and how these conditions relate to human capital allocation risk. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses an annual panel of undirected EU27 country pairs from 2004 to 2020, restricted to pair-years in which both countries were EU members. The outcome is a weighted corridor-level index combining reciprocal balance and skilled flow volume. It captures balanced reciprocal skilled mobility, not repeated movement by the same individuals. Country-pair fixed effects, year effects, lagged predictors, mediation, moderated mediation and alternative outcome checks are applied. Findings Destination skill shortages are positively associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility. Qualification recognition has no statistically significant direct association with the outcome, but the recognition-to-employment-absorption pathway is positive. This indirect pathway weakens as overqualification risk rises. Research limitations/implications Aggregate pair-year flows cannot identify return or repeated movement by the same workers. The design therefore supports corridor-level inference about balanced reciprocal mobility rather than individual circular migration. The models also identify an upstream human capital allocation channel rather than credit, market, liquidity or systemic risk. Practical implications Recognition bodies, employers, sector councils and employment services should coordinate so that recognized skills are more likely to lead to qualification-matched employment. The evidence supports improving skill use and matching rather than claiming that these interventions directly reduce financial risk. Social implications Better skill matching can reduce skill waste and support more balanced skilled mobility across EU labor markets. Originality/value The study distinguishes corridor-level reciprocal skilled mobility from person-level circular migration and specifies an institutional conversion pathway linking recognition capacity to employment absorption under overqualification constraints. Its risk contribution concerns human capital allocation and labor market risk.

title: Parametric Non‐Intrusive Reduced Order Modelling via Taylor Series Neural Networks and Dynamic Identification
source: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering
summary: Numerically solving parameterised partial differential equations (P‐PDEs) is both valuable and computationally intensive, driving the development of reduced‐order models (ROMs). Recently, methods that combine latent space identification tec
content: Numerically solving parameterised partial differential equations (P‐PDEs) is both valuable and computationally intensive, driving the development of reduced‐order models (ROMs). Recently, methods that combine latent space identification techniques with deep learning algorithms (e.g., autoencoders) have shown great potential in describing the dynamical system in the lower‐dimensional latent space. In this paper, a new parametric latent identification of nonlinear dynamics neural networks, P‐TLDINets, is introduced, which relies on a novel neural network structure based on Taylor series expansion and ResNets to learn the parametric differential equations that govern the dynamics in the latent space. During the training process, Taylor series‐based Latent Dynamic Neural Network (TLDNet) and identified equations are trained simultaneously to generate a smoother latent space. In order to facilitate the parameterised study, a ‐nearest neighbours (KNN) method based on an inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation scheme is introduced to predict the identified ODE coefficients using local information. Compared to other latent dynamics identification methods based on autoencoders, P‐TLDINet eliminates the encoder‐decoder's dependence on spatial coordinates, enabling it to be a parameterised ROM. Additionally, its lightweight network structure allows high generalization capabilities with less training time. P‐TLDINet was tested on the 2D Burgers' equation and the lock‐exchange case, maintaining an error of less than 2% compared to high‐fidelity models.

title: From financial difficulty to financial resilience: the role of financial inclusion, gender, and geography in Saudi Arabia
summary: Financial resilience has become an increasingly important dimension of financial wellbeing, reflecting individuals’ capacity to cope with financial shocks and maintain economic stability over time. This study examines financial difficulty a
content: Financial resilience has become an increasingly important dimension of financial wellbeing, reflecting individuals’ capacity to cope with financial shocks and maintain economic stability over time. This study examines financial difficulty and financial resilience as interconnected positions along a financial wellbeing continuum and investigates how socio-demographic characteristics and multidimensional financial inclusion are associated with resilience outcomes in Saudi Arabia. Using microdata from the Global Findex Database 2025, the analysis employs ordered logistic and multinomial logistic regression models to examine factors associated with short, mid, and long-term financial resilience. The results indicate that financial inclusion is multidimensional, with access, use, and digital financial engagement exhibiting distinct associations with resilience outcomes. Saving behavior is consistently associated with lower perceived financial difficulty and a greater likelihood of achieving mid-term financial resilience, while long-term resilience is more strongly associated with higher income, tertiary education, urban residence, and digital financial engagement. Women are more likely to report financial difficulty than men, even after controlling for socioeconomic characteristics, although evidence regarding the interaction between gender and urbanicity is limited and should be interpreted cautiously. Income remains a significant correlate of resilience across all model specifications. The findings suggest that account ownership alone is an incomplete indicator of financial resilience. Instead, effective financial behaviors, human capital, and broader socioeconomic conditions appear to play important roles in shaping resilience pathways. Rather than implying causal relationships, the results should be interpreted as associations derived from cross-sectional data. By providing recent micro-level evidence from Saudi Arabia, this study contributes to the literature on financial inclusion and financial wellbeing and offers policy insights relevant to Vision 2030 initiatives aimed at promoting inclusive and resilient financial systems. The study’s contribution lies in distinguishing among the access, use, and digital engagement dimensions of financial inclusion and examining their associations with different resilience horizons rather than proposing a new theory of financial resilience.

title: Roles and Research Focus of AI in Mathematics Education: Insights from a Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
source: International Journal of Education in Mathematics Science and Technology
summary: In this study, we adopted a holistic approach by integrating bibliometric analysis and systematic review methods to thoroughly evaluate the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics education and its research trends. The study aim
content: In this study, we adopted a holistic approach by integrating bibliometric analysis and systematic review methods to thoroughly evaluate the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics education and its research trends. The study aims to understand the current state of the field and provide strategic direction for future research by assessing general trends, intellectual contributions, and application potential in AI-focused mathematics education research from a multidimensional perspective. In the first phase, we conducted a content analysis of 363 articles published in high-quality journals indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database, focusing on dimensions such as publishers, method types, research designs, study groups, theoretical or conceptual frameworks, data collection techniques, preferred technologies, purposes of use, and roles. Subsequently, we conducted a comprehensive and systematic evaluation of scientific productivity, citation performance, collaboration networks, conceptual structures, thematic maps, and intellectual transformations. During this process, we followed the guidelines outlined in the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA). The findings indicate that AI technologies have been increasingly utilized in mathematics education, with significant growth observed since 2015. AI-focused mathematics education research has been predominantly concentrated in countries like the USA, China, and Germany, delving into areas such as personalized learning, assessment, feedback, and pedagogical innovations. Most studies have employed quantitative and mixed methods, with middle school and undergraduate students being the primary target groups. Bibliometric analyses reveal a rapid expansion in scientific productivity and collaboration networks, while thematic trends primarily focus on personalized learning and the integration of digital tools.

title: Effective Machine Learning Methods Used for Stock Price Forecasting: A Performance Evaluation
source: American Journal of Computing and Engineering
summary: A crucial component of financial decision-making and investment planning is stock price forecasting, but it is a complicated problem because of the non-linear and unstable dynamics of the market. In this paper, the researcher outlines a fun
content: A crucial component of financial decision-making and investment planning is stock price forecasting, but it is a complicated problem because of the non-linear and unstable dynamics of the market. In this paper, the researcher outlines a functioning stock market forecasting model which aims at enhancing the degree of forecasting precision founded on the past data of the S and P500 index. The approach involves the use of systematic data gathering and a thorough preprocessing procedure, such as the management of missing data, feature scaling with standardization and chronologically dividing the dataset into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Machine learning (ML) models called Random Forest (RF) and Linear Regression (LR) are used to analyze current market trends and forecast future prices. The key error measures (R2, MSE, RMSE and MAE) are used to evaluate the performance of each model, which guarantees an accurate evaluation of forecasting reliability. The results of the experiments prove that both models provide very accurate predictions, though LR has slightly better error performance, and RF has high levels of generalization. The comparative analysis also demonstrates that proposed models are superior to the current models, such as ANN and SVM. Overall, the work offers an informative, evidence-based prediction model, which is resistant, stable, and can be used in supporting real-time financial decisions and investment policies. Keywords: Stock Price Forecasting, S&P 500 Index, Machine Learning, Financial Market Prediction, Linear Regression, Random Forest, Stock Market Analysis.

title: Sampling optimization to estimate fishing effort for small-scale fisheries using high-resolution tracking data
summary: Small-scale fisheries (SSF, vessels under 12 m) represent approximately 90% of global fisheries and over 80% of the EU fleet, employing around 100,000 people, yet their fishing effort (FE) remains poorly quantified. Unlike large-scale fleet
content: Small-scale fisheries (SSF, vessels under 12 m) represent approximately 90% of global fisheries and over 80% of the EU fleet, employing around 100,000 people, yet their fishing effort (FE) remains poorly quantified. Unlike large-scale fleets equipped with Vessel Monitoring Systems, SSF tracking is only now emerging following EU legislation mandating electronic tracking by 2030 (EU 2023/2842). However, the required temporal resolution is 30 min (Implementing Regulation C(2025)7501), despite evidence that resolutions of seconds to minutes are needed to reliably estimate SSF effort. This raises two related challenges: whether higher-resolution data should complement mandatory tracking, and how sampling can be optimised when full fleet tracking is not economically feasible, specifically, how many fishing trips are required. Using case studies from Portugal and Catalunya, we assessed the sampling effort needed to estimate total FE through three indicators: (i) spatial extent, the area of fishing grounds (km²); (ii) geographic location, where fishing occurs; and (iii) fishing intensity, the cumulative amount of effort (e.g., fishing hours). Two sampling strategies were tested for each indicator: by fishing trip and by vessel. High-resolution GPS data (30-s intervals, 2016–2023) were used for bivalve dredges (three Portuguese regions), trammel-nets (southwest Portugal) and octopus pots and traps (southern Portugal), mapped onto 500-m grids following Rufino et al. (2023) and Samarão et al. (2024) . A second case study used GPS data (3-min intervals, October 2023) from gillnetters along the Catalan coast, processed following Mendo et al. (2025). FE indicators were estimated for randomly drawn subsets of trips or vessels, repeatedly resampled from the full tracked dataset (the universe), to evaluate how estimates changed with sample size. Geographic location and spatial extent showed an asymptotic relationship with sample size, best described by a Michaelis-Menten model among six models tested, while fishing intensity showed a linear relationship. Three criteria, empirical, and two model-parameter-based (percentage and derivative plateau), were used to estimate minimum sample size. Across gears, areas and years, 100–189 tracked trips were sufficient to capture 90% of FE for both spatial extent and geographic location. The exception was the octopus trap case study, where spatial extent stabilised only at 502 trips, though geographic location did not show this delay. When sampling by vessel, the plateau was often not reached within the observed range of vessels. Model-based approaches produced more realistic minimum sample size estimates, and combining criteria gave more robust conclusions. We conclude that fishing effort sampling, including for validation purposes, should be conducted by trip rather than by vessel, with 100–189 trips distributed across the year sufficient to characterise total effort. title: Механизмы и пути влияния зелёного финансирования на высококачественное развитие китайской промышленности
summary: Введение. В условиях ориентации Китая на высококачественное развитие обрабатывающая промышленность как ядро национальной экономики сталкивается с задачами перехода от экстенсивного роста к инновационному и зелѐному развитию. Зелѐное финанси
content: Введение. В условиях ориентации Китая на высококачественное развитие обрабатывающая промышленность как ядро национальной экономики сталкивается с задачами перехода от экстенсивного роста к инновационному и зелѐному развитию. Зелѐное финансирование как инновационный финансовый инструментарий играет решающую роль в обеспечении финансирования и снижении рисков для трансформации промышленности, являясь важным драйвером еѐ устойчивого прогресса. Новизна исследования заключается в комплексном выявлении четырѐх ключевых механизмов влияния зелѐного финансирования на высококачественное развитие промышленности и эмпирическом подтверждении их эффективности на основе данных 2021–2025 гг. с углублѐнным анализом региональной неоднородности и разработкой количественно обоснованных оптимизационных путей. Материалы и методы. Исследование базируется на теориях устойчивого развития, внешних эффектов и оптимизации промышленной структуры. В работе использованы методы литературного обзора, качественного анализа механизмов и количественного анализа статистических данных за 2021–2025 гг., включая индикаторы зелѐного финансирования (кредиты, облигации, фонды) и высококачественного развития обрабатывающей промышленности (инновации, энергоэффективность, структура отрасли) в Китае, полученных из статистических ежегодников, баз данных Народного банка Китая и WIND. Проведѐн сравнительный региональный анализ по трѐм макрорегионам (восток, центр, запад). Результаты. Исследование выявило четыре механизма влияния: направление капитала (к 2025 г. объѐм зелѐных кредитов в промышленности превысил 10,5 трлн юаней, более 65% направлено на проекты интеграции цифровых и экологических технологий); инновации в зелѐных технологиях (среднегодовой темп роста заявок на зелѐные патенты в промышленности достиг 28,3%); модернизацию промышленной структуры (доля высокотехнологичной промышленности достигла 18,7%); снижение рисков (доходы от страхования экологической ответственности превысили 12 млрд юаней). Выявлена существенная региональная неоднородность: индекс зелѐного финансирования в восточных провинциях в 2,3–3,5 раза выше, чем в западных регионах. Объѐм дефицита финансирования зелѐной трансформации промышленности превышает 3 трлн юаней. Обсуждение и заключения. На основе аналитических данных разработаны количественно обоснованные оптимизационные пути: создание национальной платформы обмена зелѐной информацией с полным охватом крупных предприятий к 2026 г.; увеличение объѐма углеродного финансирования до 500 млрд юаней; формирование регионального фонда зелѐного финансирования объѐмом 500 млрд юаней для поддержки центральных и западных регионов; обеспечение доли межрегиональных зелѐных кредитов на уровне 15% к 2026 г. title: Green Finance in BRICS-T Countries: The Role of Economic Growth, Trade, Natural Resources, and Education
source: Scientific Annals of Economics and Business
summary: Current research predominantly treats green finance as an independent policy instrument and fails to provide a comprehensive framework regarding the mechanisms through which structural macroeconomic indicators shape green financial developm
content: Current research predominantly treats green finance as an independent policy instrument and fails to provide a comprehensive framework regarding the mechanisms through which structural macroeconomic indicators shape green financial development in emerging economies. Motivated by this problem, the present study examines green finance dynamics in BRICS-T countries over the 1990-2023 period based on economic growth, trade, natural resources, and education; it also includes population growth in the model as a control variable. Analyses conducted using econometric techniques (cross-sectional dependence tests, homogeneity tests, CIPS unit root tests, Westerlund-Durbin-Hausman cointegration analysis, CCE and AMG estimators, Dumitrescu-Hurlin causality tests, and Panel ARDL tests) reveal that economic growth reduces green finance in both the short and long term. Furthermore, in the long term, natural resources and population growth negatively affect green finance. On the other hand, trade and education positively support green finance, playing a critical role in the development of sustainable financial practices. Dumitrescu-Hurlin causality test results confirm unidirectional causality relationships running from green finance to natural resources, population growth, and education variables. In light of these findings, this study reveals the dynamics of green finance in emerging BRICS-T economies, offering policymakers an empirical framework for developing economic strategies aligned with environmental sustainability. Additionally, it emphasizes the necessity of aligning macroeconomic growth policies with sustainable financial development, promoting eco-friendly trade integration, and strategically utilizing educational investments to build green financial capacity.

title: What drives social entrepreneurial intention? An integrated model of cognitive, moral, and social antecedents among university students in India
summary: Social entrepreneurship is pivotal in addressing social and environmental challenges, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying social entrepreneurial intention (SEI), especially in developing nations, remain underexplored. This study, gr
content: Social entrepreneurship is pivotal in addressing social and environmental challenges, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying social entrepreneurial intention (SEI), especially in developing nations, remain underexplored. This study, grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the social entrepreneurial intention framework, investigates the cognitive, moral, normative, and experiential determinants of SEI among higher education students. Employing a quantitative methodology, a cross-sectional design was utilized, involving 349 postgraduate and undergraduate participants. The analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that opportunity recognition competency (ORC) is the most significant predictor of SEI, underscoring the importance of entrepreneurial cognition in SEI. SEI is positively correlated with social entrepreneurial self-efficacy and subjective norms, indicating the significance of perceived entrepreneurial capability and social endorsement. However, SEI does not exhibit significant associations with empathy, moral obligation, perceived sustainability values, perceived social support, perceived behavioural control, or prior experience. Notably, prior experience is indirectly linked to SEI through social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, despite its direct and total associations with SEI being non-significant. Overall, the findings suggest that opportunity recognition competency, social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, and subjective norms hold greater relative importance for SEI when antecedents are evaluated concurrently.

title: Redesigning Educational System: Evaluating the Importance of Educational Certificates Versus Work Experiences in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
source: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
summary: Rapid technological change raises an urgent question for higher education: how can universities prepare students for workplaces that may change substantially before they graduate? During several years of study, professional tools and expect
content: Rapid technological change raises an urgent question for higher education: how can universities prepare students for workplaces that may change substantially before they graduate? During several years of study, professional tools and expectations can develop faster than curricula are updated, leaving graduates to acquire essential practical skills after entering employment. The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) makes this challenge more pressing. Online courses and self-directed learning also raise questions about the value of investing in a university qualification when alternative routes offer more immediate professional training. If universities cannot demonstrate how their programmes support professional capability, they risk weakening their appeal to prospective students. This study examines the perceived gap between university preparation and workplace requirements, exploring how participants understand the contribution of educational credentials and practical experience to their professional development. It draws on 35 personal, semi-structured interviews with purposively selected participants from diverse professional and educational backgrounds. Interview material was analysed using reflexive thematic analysis supported by MAXQDA, with curriculum preferences reported separately as descriptive counts. Participants described acquiring changing technologies through work and continued learning. Their responses distinguished the value of qualifications in opening opportunities from the practical capability needed to perform effectively. AI supported faster production, but its use required independent judgement and verification. Universities need to make the practical value of higher education visible throughout students’ learning, while developing the capacity to keep learning as workplace demands change.

title: Motivators to improve the likelihood of willingness to pay for circular MSW management: The case of Fiji
summary: Household support for circular economy (CE) transitions in municipal solid waste management does not translate into fee acceptance. This study surveyed 331 participant and interviewed 11 stakeholders in Fiji to identify motivators of willin
content: Household support for circular economy (CE) transitions in municipal solid waste management does not translate into fee acceptance. This study surveyed 331 participant and interviewed 11 stakeholders in Fiji to identify motivators of willingness to pay (WTP). Neither socio-demographic variables nor CE endorsement showed stable associations with WTP likelihood. Sustainability priorities and sorting intention showed weak but significant positive associations (ρ ≈ 0.20, p < 0.001). Awareness engagement showed the strongest association, albeit weak (ρ = 0.27, p < 0.001). Intention to sort was high but unrelated to the current sorting. Stakeholders perceived household’s passive; however, our results revealed 94.9% of non-sorters would sort if bins were provided. WTP likelihood was unassociated with service access but associated positively with sorting behaviour. No-service households sorted more intensively. Degree-educated respondents were overrepresented, so findings are sample-specific. Fee design should be proportionate and transparent. Bin provision and separate collection are prerequisites for participation.
