The study provides a transparent island transition portfolio while identifying resource, dispatch, surplus, financial and emissions assumptions requiring validation before investment.

title: Future of Biofuels from Agricultural Waste Challenges, Opportunities, and Improvement Strategies
summary: Crop residues such as rice and wheat straw, maize stover, sugarcane bagasse and coconut husk are among the largest underused renewable resources in India, where roughly 500 million tonnes of agricultural biomass are generated each year and
content: Crop residues such as rice and wheat straw, maize stover, sugarcane bagasse and coconut husk are among the largest underused renewable resources in India, where roughly 500 million tonnes of agricultural biomass are generated each year and a large share is burned in the field or left to rot.This review examines how second-generation biofuels (cellulosic ethanol, biogas, bio-oil and syngas, and biodiesel from oilseed residues) can turn that waste into fuel.Drawing on published resource assessments and on indicative yield, energy, emission and cost figures compiled by the authors, it outlines the scale of the opportunity, points out where optimistic estimates diverge from what operating plants have delivered, and discusses the main barriers: scattered and seasonal feedstock, costly pretreatment and enzymes, high capital cost and weak rural infrastructure.Seven improvement strategies are then proposed: advanced pretreatment, better enzymes and microbes, integrated biorefineries, farm-scale processing, stronger supply chains, supportive policy and continued research.The analysis suggests that residue-based biofuels can contribute meaningfully to energy security, rural income and emission reduction, provided that feedstock logistics and process economics are tackled together.

title: Bio-oil Production from Rice Husk Pyrolysis using NiO/Rice Husk Ash Catalyst
summary: The rice husk pyrolysis was studied using the NiO/RHA catalysts. The NiO/RHA catalysts were prepared by impregnating the nickel oxide as active components on RHA. The NiO/RHA catalyst characteristics were analyzed by nitrogen adsorption-des
content: The rice husk pyrolysis was studied using the NiO/RHA catalysts. The NiO/RHA catalysts were prepared by impregnating the nickel oxide as active components on RHA. The NiO/RHA catalyst characteristics were analyzed by nitrogen adsorption-desorption, X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), and Energy Dispersive X-Ray (EDX). The NiO/RHA catalyst was examined for the rice husk pyrolysis in the batch experiment. Several process variables i.e., temperature (400 to 600 °C), catalyst addition, nitrogen gas ﬂow rate (100 to 300 cm 3 /min), and heating rate (10 to 30°C/min) were investigated. The Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometer (GC-MS) and FTIR analysis were carried out to determine the chemical compositions of liquid products. The experiment concluded that using the NiO/RHA catalyst increased in the liquid yield, while decreasing the char yield. It also has been found that the addition of a catalyst, ﬂow rate of nitrogen gas, and rate of heating influenced the liquid yield. The liquid yield reached at maximum when the operation conditions were the temperature of 600°C, nitrogen gas ﬂow rate of 300 cm 3 /min, and heating rate of 30 °C.min −1 .

title: Discovery of a Linked Fragment That Creates a Potent Half-Site Binder and Functional Antagonist of a Riboswitch RNA
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Fragment-based ligand discovery has identified RNA-targeted hits, but progressing these hits into potent, biology-altering leads has remained unrealized. During transcription, the bacterial thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) riboswitch samples a
content: Fragment-based ligand discovery has identified RNA-targeted hits, but progressing these hits into potent, biology-altering leads has remained unrealized. During transcription, the bacterial thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) riboswitch samples a complex structure, stabilized by TPP, that sequesters the start codon region to create a translation-inhibiting OFF state. SHAPE-informed fragment screening previously identified a quinoxaline ligand (Kd = 25 μM) that, when linked to a cobinding piperazine fragment, yielded Z1 (Kd = 0.2–0.6 μM). We used structure–activity relationships to create Z2 with ∼50 nM affinity and ligand efficiency exceeding the native ligand. Structure determination by cryo-EM reveals that every heteroatom in Z2 (n = 6) forms direct hydrogen bonds with the RNA. Z2 engages exclusively at a mini-3-helix junction to stabilize a half-open riboswitch conformation distinct from both ligand-free and TPP-bound states. Cotranscriptional folding and cell-based experiments show that Z2 competes with TPP for binding but does not stabilize the native regulatory OFF state. Z2 thus functions as an RNA-targeted antagonist, displacing the native ligand and disrupting the regulatory logic of the riboswitch. These results establish a pathway for creating high-efficiency RNA–ligand interactions and identify half-site occupancy as a mechanism for antagonizing RNA function.

title: Cardiac-targeted nanoparticles delivering bellidifolin attenuate myocardial injury via the Gal-3/TREM2 signaling axis
summary: Background Myocardial injury involves a detrimental inflammation-fibrosis cascade orchestrated by Galectin-3 (Gal-3), yet its precise downstream mechanisms remain elusive. Bellidifolin (BEL) exhibits promising cardioprotective effects but i
content: Background Myocardial injury involves a detrimental inflammation-fibrosis cascade orchestrated by Galectin-3 (Gal-3), yet its precise downstream mechanisms remain elusive. Bellidifolin (BEL) exhibits promising cardioprotective effects but is limited by poor bioavailability and lack of tissue specificity. Methods We investigated the Gal-3/TREM2 axis using wild-type and Lgals3 knockout mice in an isoproterenol (ISO)-induced model. Additionally, a cardiac-targeted nano-delivery system (BEL@HMSNs-CTP) was engineered to overcome the poor bioavailability of BEL. Results Genetic Lgals3 deletion preserved cardiac function by specifically abolishing TREM2 upregulation and ERK activation, while sparing the p38 pathway. The fabricated BEL@HMSNs-CTP exhibited uniform hollow mesoporous structures, high drug loading, and sustained release. Crucially, in vivo imaging demonstrated significantly enhanced and prolonged cardiac accumulation of CTP-modified nanoparticles compared to non-targeted controls. Therapeutically, BEL@HMSNs-CTP profoundly alleviated ISO-induced cardiac dysfunction, inflammatory infiltration, and collagen deposition. Mechanistically, it achieved a synergistic effect via cardiac-targeted inhibition of the Gal-3/TREM2 pro-fibrotic axis and its downstream ERK signaling pathway. Conclusion The Gal-3/TREM2 axis specifically drives the transition from myocardial inflammation to fibrosis. BEL@HMSNs-CTP effectively prevents adverse cardiac remodeling via precise spatial delivery, offering a promising precision nanomedicine strategy for the clinical translation of natural xanthones.

title: Piperine induces ROS-associated mitochondrial dysfunction with differential cytotoxic potential against oral cancer and non-malignant cells
summary: Oral carcinoma (OC) continues to present significant therapeutic challenges due to tumor aggressiveness, metastatic progression, and the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. The identification of anticancer agents ca
content: Oral carcinoma (OC) continues to present significant therapeutic challenges due to tumor aggressiveness, metastatic progression, and the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. The identification of anticancer agents capable of eliminating tumor cells while sparing normal tissues remains a critical unmet need. In the present study, piperine (PIP), a major bioactive alkaloid from Piper nigrum , was extracted, purified, characterized, and investigated for its anticancer efficacy against OC using integrated in vitro and computational approaches. PIP demonstrated pronounced dose-dependent cytotoxicity against KB, Hep2, Cal 27, and OECM-1 OC cells, and reported significantly lower toxicity against NOE, PBMCs, NIH3T3, L929, H9c2 cells, and erythrocytes, indicating favorable biocompatibility. Mechanistic investigations revealed that PIP induced marked intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, lysosomal alterations, chromatin condensation, membrane blebbing, and apoptotic cell death. AO/EtBr, Hoechst, H 2 DCFDA, JC-1, MitoTracker, LysoTracker, and PI staining collectively demonstrated oxidative stress-mediated mitochondrial dysfunction as a central mechanism underlying PIP-induced cytotoxicity. Furthermore, the scratch assay revealed significant suppression of OC cell migration following PIP exposure, suggesting anti-metastatic potential. In addition, PIP exhibited considerable antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities in cell-free assays. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations further supported stable interactions between PIP and cancer-associated molecular targets involved in apoptotic signaling pathways. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that PIP induces context-dependent ROS-associated mitochondrial dysfunction and cytotoxicity, with greater sensitivity against OC cells than in non-malignant oral epithelial cells, highlighting its potential for future OC therapeutic development and warranting further investigations.

title: An exploratory diagnostic model for the risk of pulmonary embolism in patients with atrial fibrillation: a Doppler ultrasound-based approach
summary: Objectives Atrial fibrillation (AF) aggravates the clinical probability of pulmonary embolism (PE), which is associated with markedly higher mortality. We developed an exploratory diagnostic nomogram to screen high-risk PE in AF patients an
content: Objectives Atrial fibrillation (AF) aggravates the clinical probability of pulmonary embolism (PE), which is associated with markedly higher mortality. We developed an exploratory diagnostic nomogram to screen high-risk PE in AF patients and to provide clinicians with interpretative information for early treatment. Design This single-center retrospective cohort study was divided into training and internal split-sample validation parts. Based on collected data, we built an exploratory diagnostic model for PE in AF patients. Setting Clinic data were collected from all patients diagnosed with AF between January 2014 and August 2022 at the First People's Hospital of Yunnan Province, China. Participants The study included 754 consecutive AF patients who were randomly classified into training ( n = 527;70%) and validation ( n = 227; 30%) cohorts according to the inclusion criteria. Among the training cohort, 65 patients were diagnosed with PE. The validation cohort included 227 AF patients with or without PE. Using data from blood tests and Doppler ultrasound, logistic regression and the Boruta algorithm were employed for feature selection, and the nomogram's performance was evaluated both in the internal training and validation sets. Results Five variables were identified as independent predictors of the recorded PE outcome: RVD (OR 1.97; 95% CI 1.22–3.17; p = 0.005), PAP (OR 1.03; 95% CI 1.02–1.04; p < 0.001), blood D-dimer level (OR 1.03; 95% CI 1.01–1.05; p = 0.001),DVT diagnosed by Doppler ultrasound (OR 5.59; 95% CI 3.31–9.47; p < 0.001), and respiratory failure (OR 1.94; 95% CI 1.15–3.25; p = 0.012). These factors were used to establish a model to identify the probability of PE in AF patients. The model demonstrated moderate-to-good discrimination, with areas under the ROC curves (AUC) of 0.839 (95% CI: 0.797–0.880) in the training cohort and 0.8 (95% CI: 0.719–0.881) in the validation cohort. The calibration intercept, calibration slope, and Brier score were 0.000, 1.045, and 0.090 in the development cohort, indicating acceptable calibration. Conclusions We developed an exploratory diagnostic model to identify PE in patients with AF.The model showed acceptable internal diagnostic performance.

title: Stand density and pruning shape leaf pressure-volume traits and their coordination with functional traits in a poplar plantation
summary: Stand density and pruning are silvicultural measures used to modify canopy structure and resource distribution in plantations. However, their effects on within-growing-season and canopy-position variation in leaf pressure-volume (PV) traits
content: Stand density and pruning are silvicultural measures used to modify canopy structure and resource distribution in plantations. However, their effects on within-growing-season and canopy-position variation in leaf pressure-volume (PV) traits, their coordination with functional traits, and the scale dependence of these relationships remain unclear. To address these questions, we investigated Populus tomentosa plantations in northern China subjected to two stand densities and three pruning intensities, using leaf samples collected monthly from top and bottom canopy positions from May to October 2024. The results showed that leaf PV traits varied markedly by month and canopy position. Canopy differences emerged mainly from August to October, with bottom canopy leaves generally showing more negative osmotic potentials than top canopy leaves. Leaf osmotic potential at full turgor ( Ψ sat ) and water potential at the turgor loss point ( Ψ tlp ) generally reached their most negative values from June to August and became less negative thereafter, whereas bulk modulus of elasticity (ϵ) showed a corresponding mid-season increase, and leaf capacitance ( C leaf ) remained relatively stable across months. Lower stand density and heavier pruning were generally associated with more negative osmotic potentials. PV traits showed significant, trait-specific associations with leaf morphology and gas exchange, whereas exploratory treatment-level analyses detected no significant relationships. Together, these findings show that stand density and pruning shape leaf PV traits, with their effects varying over the growing season and between canopy positions.

title: Rice straw ash as a sustainable pozzolanic additive in geopolymer mortars: effects on strength, permeability, and microstructure
summary: To reduce carbon emissions, interest in using agricultural residues in alkali‐activated binders is growing. This study investigates the impact of processed rice straw ash on fly ash and ground granulated blast‐furnace slag geopolymer mortar
content: To reduce carbon emissions, interest in using agricultural residues in alkali‐activated binders is growing. This study investigates the impact of processed rice straw ash on fly ash and ground granulated blast‐furnace slag geopolymer mortar. Rice straw ash, calcined at 650 °C for six hours and ball‐milled for 20 minutes, replaced 25% of the fly ash (20% of total binder). Mortar mixtures were evaluated across sodium hydroxide molarities from 7.5 M to 14 M. Incorporating rice straw ash improved workability, increasing flow diameter by 4–8 mm across all concentrations. Compressive strength increased with curing age and sodium hydroxide molarity, peaking at 41 MPa after 56 days at 14 M sodium hydroxide, compared to 36 MPa for the control. Additionally, rice straw ash mixtures demonstrated lower water absorption and reduced cumulative capillary water uptake. Scanning electron microscopy and energy‐dispersive X‐ray spectroscopy revealed that rice straw ash created a more compact, homogeneous matrix with higher silicon and aluminum signal intensities. These findings indicate rice straw ash has strong potential as a supplementary precursor in this geopolymer mortar, enhancing mechanical strength and water‐transport properties. However, further assessment of sorptivity and validation under broader exposure conditions are needed to establish long‐term durability.

title: Nano‐Fe 2 O 3 Enhances Carbon Utilization for Nitrogen Removal in Modified Basalt Fiber Bio‐Nests
summary: Nano‐Fe 2 O 3 was incorporated into modified basalt fiber (MBF) bio‐nests to enhance nitrogen removal from carbon‐limited wastewater. Under continuous‐flow conditions, nano‐Fe 2 O 3 increased NH 4 + ‐N and total nitrogen (TN) removal by 22.
content: Nano‐Fe 2 O 3 was incorporated into modified basalt fiber (MBF) bio‐nests to enhance nitrogen removal from carbon‐limited wastewater. Under continuous‐flow conditions, nano‐Fe 2 O 3 increased NH 4 + ‐N and total nitrogen (TN) removal by 22.1% and 26.5%, respectively, while reducing COD consumption per unit TN removed from 184.5 to 36.2 g COD g −1 TN. Mechanistic analyses, including metagenomics, qPCR, TEM, and electrochemical characterization, revealed findings consistent with a putative intracellular electron‐mediating role of nano‐Fe 2 O 3 . Denitrification genes ( napA , nirS , norB , nosZ ) were significantly upregulated, whereas outer‐membrane electron transport genes ( mtrABC , fccA ) were downregulated, a transcriptional pattern consistent with a redirection of electron flux from carbon oxidation toward denitrification. Cyclic voltammetry showed a shift of the EPS reduction peak from −0.394 V to −0.460 V and a lower EPS capacitance, indicating an altered redox‐mediator pool; however, these electrochemical observations alone do not uniquely demonstrate riboflavin‐like intracellular mediation. Additionally, nano‐Fe 2 O 3 promoted EPS secretion and enriched electroactive denitrifying bacteria such as Thauera and Pseudomonas spp. This study proposes a passive, cost‐effective strategy to overcome carbon limitation in biological nitrogen removal putatively by facilitating intracellular electron transfer, while emphasizing that direct evidence of intracellular Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox cycling remains to be established, offering a practical upgrade for existing infrastructure without external energy input.

title: A Computational Framework for Predicting the Mechanical Properties of Recycled CFRP Laminates
summary: The qualification of recycled carbon fiber reinforced polymers (CFRPs) requires reliable methodologies capable of linking constituent-level properties with laminate-scale mechanical performance. This work presents a multiscale property-tran
content: The qualification of recycled carbon fiber reinforced polymers (CFRPs) requires reliable methodologies capable of linking constituent-level properties with laminate-scale mechanical performance. This work presents a multiscale property-transfer framework for predicting the behavior of unidirectional CFRP laminates manufactured using recycled carbon fibers recovered through a plasma-assisted solvolysis process. Single-fiber tensile and microbond tests were conducted to characterize the tensile and interfacial properties of virgin and recycled TR30S carbon fibers. The experimentally measured constituent properties were used as input to analytical micromechanical models for the prediction of the elastic constants and strength properties of a unidirectional ply. In addition, a 3D representative volume element was used to quantify the effect of interface degradation. The resulting ply properties were implemented in laminate-level finite element models and validated against experimental tensile, compression and interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) tests performed on both virgin and recycled CFRP laminates. Sensitivity studies evaluated the influence of fiber-strength and interface-strength degradation on the laminate response. Recycling reduced laminate tensile and compressive strength by less than 20%, while the ILSS decreased by 58%. The experimental tensile and compressive strengths lay within the numerical scatter band, and with an inter-ply tiebreak interface, the ILSS of the virgin laminates was predicted within 8%, whereas that of the recycled laminates was overpredicted owing to pre-existing damage. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully transfers constituent-level degradation effects to the laminate scale and provides an efficient tool for predicting the mechanical performance of recycled composite structures.

title: Arginine depletion by lactic acid bacteria drives a save-and-sequester metabolic strategy in competing yeast
summary: Microbial interactions in complex communities are shaped by nutrient competition, yet the metabolic consequences of selective amino acid remodeling remain poorly understood. We show that Weissella confusa remodels the extracellular nitrogen
content: Microbial interactions in complex communities are shaped by nutrient competition, yet the metabolic consequences of selective amino acid remodeling remain poorly understood. We show that Weissella confusa remodels the extracellular nitrogen environment through rapid arginine depletion and ornithine enrichment, eliciting a save-and-sequester response in Saccharomyces cerevisiae . In the save module, reduced fatty acid degradation and glyoxylate metabolism preserve acyl-CoA precursors and redirect carbon toward volatile medium-chain fatty acid ethyl esters (MCFAEEs) for export, creating a carbon-overflow route that alleviates potential lipotoxic stress. In the sequester module, extracellular ornithine and aspartate, together with nitrogen redistribution and reduced nitrogen catabolism, support rebuilding and maintenance of the intracellular arginine pool. Together, these responses couple nitrogen conservation to carbon overflow and underpin the increase in MCFAEE production. This strategy links bacterial niche modification to yeast volatile output and establishes selective amino acid remodeling as a key driver of metabolic reprogramming during interspecies resource competition.

title: Forecasting the interaction among electricity consumption, population, and GDP in Egypt using a modified Lotka–Volterra model and an interaction ANN model
summary: Forecasting electric load consumption is inherently complicated due to the nonlinear dynamic relationships between electricity consumption and its underlying socio-economic determinants, particularly population and real gross domestic produ
content: Forecasting electric load consumption is inherently complicated due to the nonlinear dynamic relationships between electricity consumption and its underlying socio-economic determinants, particularly population and real gross domestic products (GDP). The main aim of this research is to develop proper and reliable models to investigate the mutual effectiveness between electric load consumption, population, and GDP for Egypt. Two different techniques, namely, a modified Lotka-Volterra (LV) model and an interaction artificial neural network (ANN) model, are used to model the reciprocating relations between these three variables up to 2040. A selected nonlinear ordinary differential equation (NODE) form is used to represent each variable in the modified LV model as a modification for the usual LV model in the literature. Two separate ANN models for population and GDP are constructed to forecast their values up to 2040, and an interaction ANN model is constructed using time, population, and GDP as input data to predict electric load consumption. Predictions of the modified LV and the ANN models are closely aligned. Results can serve as a foundation for developing or refining strategies and help in the balance between electricity supply and demand. It can guide infrastructure investments and support the integration of renewable energy sources.

title: Thermal Stress During Early Development Alters Purine and Phospholipid Metabolism in Zebrafish Larvae
summary: Global warming has continuously increased sea surface temperatures, posing significant challenges to aquatic ecosystems and the aquaculture industry. Thermal stress during early development can profoundly alter physiological, morphological,
content: Global warming has continuously increased sea surface temperatures, posing significant challenges to aquatic ecosystems and the aquaculture industry. Thermal stress during early development can profoundly alter physiological, morphological, and metabolic processes in fish, affecting growth, behavior, and survival. In this study, we investigated the effects of elevated temperature during early development of wild-type zebrafish (from < 2 h post-fertilization (hpf) to 14 days post-fertilization (dpf)) on morphological phenotypes, larval behavior, and metabolic regulation. Embryos were exposed to control (26 °C) and thermal stress (34 °C) conditions, and phenotypic and biochemical analyses were conducted from hatching through to the larval stage. Thermal stress accelerated hatching to within 48 hpf, accompanied by morphological abnormalities. At 14 dpf, larvae exposed to thermal stress exhibited significantly increased swimming velocity and distance with altered spatial occupancy patterns. Untargeted metabolomic profiling of 3 dpf larvae using UPLC-QTOF-MS revealed alterations in purine metabolism, amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism, amino acid metabolism, and lipid metabolites. Among the altered lipids, phosphatidylserines were consistently elevated, whereas phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylinositol species showed species-specific fluctuations, suggesting potential associations with membrane lipid remodeling and related cellular pathways. These findings indicate that thermal stress during early development is associated with physiological, behavioral, and metabolic changes in zebrafish, providing insights into how sustained elevated temperature alters early development and metabolism in aquatic organisms.

title: Seasonal physiological resilience and age‐dependent stress responses in artificially introduced Kandelia obovata mangrove stands
summary: Introduction Mangroves planted beyond their historical range may face seasonal cold, heat, and salinity stress. Structural monitoring alone may miss changes in leaf photosynthetic function, but physiological measures must be interpreted alo
content: Introduction Mangroves planted beyond their historical range may face seasonal cold, heat, and salinity stress. Structural monitoring alone may miss changes in leaf photosynthetic function, but physiological measures must be interpreted alongside restoration outcomes. Objectives We asked whether chlorophyll fluorescence distinguishes seasonal physiological condition among approximately 3‐, 10‐ to 12‐, and 20‐year‐old Kandelia obovata stands introduced into Yueqing Bay, Zhejiang Province, China. Methods We measured light‐adapted chlorophyll fluorescence during four seasonal field surveys from April 2024 to January 2025 and compared responses among stand age classes. Fluorescence measurements indicate how efficiently leaves use light for photosynthesis and can help detect short‐term physiological stress without destructive sampling. Results Photochemical efficiency declined in summer and winter across all age classes. The approximately 20‐year‐old stand generally maintained higher values during those seasons, whereas young stands showed the largest seasonal decline. Young leaves also carried more surface sediment, a possible contributor to the observed differences. Conclusions Seasonal fluorescence measurements can complement structural monitoring by identifying when and where introduced stands show physiological stress. Because the oldest age class was sampled at only one site and survival, growth, and recruitment were not measured systematically, these observations do not establish a long‐term restoration trajectory or validated intervention thresholds.

title: Crop-specific partitioning of ozone deposition in mediterranean agroecosystems: Contrasting stomatal and non-stomatal pathways
summary: Ground-level ozone (O 3 ) remains a significant constraint on crop productivity and a key component of atmospheric chemistry. However, its deposition pathways within agricultural systems remain poorly quantified, particularly in Mediterrane
content: Ground-level ozone (O 3 ) remains a significant constraint on crop productivity and a key component of atmospheric chemistry. However, its deposition pathways within agricultural systems remain poorly quantified, particularly in Mediterranean regions where vegetation phenology and water demand vary strongly across crops and seasons. In this study, we compare O 3 dry deposition across four representative Mediterranean crops: rice ( Oryza sativa ), citrus ( Citrus sinensis ), potato ( Solanum tuberosum ), and artichoke ( Cynara scolymus ) using eddy covariance measurements of O 3 , water vapor, and CO 2 fluxes combined with three stomatal conductance models based on CO 2 assimilation rate (Ball-Berry, modified Ball-Berry, and Medlyn) evaluated against a physically-based Evaporative/Resistive (ER) approach. Results differed among sites due to contrasting hydrological regimes and crop phenology, leading to significant crop-specific differences in both the magnitude and partitioning of ozone uptake. Rice and potato acted predominantly as stomatal sinks during active vegetation crop stages, whereas citrus and artichoke exhibited substantial and persistent non-stomatal contributions associated with vegetation canopy properties and environmental constraints on stomatal conductance. Among the tested models, the Medlyn model showed the most consistent overall agreement with ER-derived stomatal conductance, particularly under high VPD conditions. Overall, our results demonstrate that O₃ deposition in Mediterranean agroecosystems is governed by crop characteristics, irrigation management, and environmental drivers, resulting in substantial variations in the balance between stomatal and non-stomatal pathways. These findings highlight the need for crop-specific deposition parameterisations in regional and global atmospheric models and underscore the dual role of Mediterranean agriculture as both a vulnerable receptor and a dynamic sink for tropospheric ozone.

title: Bioinspired Plasma‐Programmed Supramolecular Interfaces for Proton Relay‐Driven Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
summary: Solar‐driven photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production is fundamentally constrained by inefficient proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET); asynchronous proton delivery and electron transport impede formation of key oxygenated intermediates. Herein
content: Solar‐driven photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production is fundamentally constrained by inefficient proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET); asynchronous proton delivery and electron transport impede formation of key oxygenated intermediates. Herein, we report a plasma‐programmed supramolecular proton‐relay interface COF (SPRI‐COF) for H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Inspired by cytochrome c oxidase, SPRI‐COF harnesses plasma‐programmed hydrogen bonding carbon dots (HB‐CDs) within a surface‐programmed COF (SP‐COF). Incorporating HB‐CDs transforms the parent SP‐COF framework into a hydrogen bond‐directed supramolecular composite, SPRI‐COF, wherein an interconnected proton‐relay network composed of complementary hydrogen bonds and confined water molecules is established. SPRI‐COF reveals a hydrogen bond‐rich interfacial microenvironment that facilitates proton‐coupled oxygen conversion while maintaining favorable charge‐carrier dynamics. Benefiting from interfacial polarization, altered carrier dynamics, and the hydrogen bond‐rich interfacial environment, SPRI‐COF achieves an H 2 O 2 production rate of 2387 µmol g − 1 h − 1 , approximately 4.5 times that of SP‐COF, together with improved selectivity toward the two‐electron oxygen reduction pathway. Spectroscopic characterization, electrochemical analyses, and theoretical calculations collectively support the cooperative contributions of interfacial electronic regulation, hydrogen bond‐mediated proton transfer, and *OOH (* = adsorbed) stabilization to the enhanced photocatalytic performance. This work demonstrates a plasma‐enabled supramolecular strategy for integrating local proton‐transfer regulation with interfacial electronic modulation in photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production.

title: Multi‐Stable Origami Metamaterials for Reusable Impact Cushioning
summary: Impacts in everyday and engineered settings demand cushions to limit transmitted peak force while remaining reusable. Conventional absorbers often trade these attributes: plastic systems dissipate energy irreversibly, whereas elastic system
content: Impacts in everyday and engineered settings demand cushions to limit transmitted peak force while remaining reusable. Conventional absorbers often trade these attributes: plastic systems dissipate energy irreversibly, whereas elastic systems are reusable but prone to rebound and rising peak forces as impact energy increases. Here, we propose a lightweight, multi-stable origami metamaterial that mitigates impact through configuration switching rather than material damage. We fabricate and characterize "origami ball" cells whose thickness-dominated multistability and thickness-tunable switching thresholds enable programmable mechanical responses. These measurements inform an equivalent dynamic model that captures switching sequences and predicts transmitted-force histories. Single-cell drop tests reveal adaptive attenuation: the cell deforms elastically at low energies and undergoes one or two configuration switches at high energies, creating an effective range in which transmitted force grows only marginally with impact energy. To overcome the trade-off between minimizing peak force and widening the operating range, we assemble a gradient chain metamaterial with increasing thickness, enabling staged switching that extends the slow-growth effective range, enlarges the rebound-free window, lowers peak-force ratios, and permits rapid pneumatic resetting for immediate recovery. This work establishes a design framework linking material thickness, potential wells, switching thresholds, and impact response for programmable, reusable, lightweight cushions.

title: Attribution of changes in hydrological extremes in the eastern headwaters of the Asian water tower based on a causal discovery–machine learning–spatial heterogeneity attribution framework
summary: Global change has profoundly altered hydrological regimes in the river-source basins of the eastern Tibetan Plateau, a core component of the Asian Water Tower. While previous studies have extensively documented changes in annual and monthly
content: Global change has profoundly altered hydrological regimes in the river-source basins of the eastern Tibetan Plateau, a core component of the Asian Water Tower. While previous studies have extensively documented changes in annual and monthly runoff, systematic attribution of hydrological extreme indices and their multi-factor driving mechanisms remains critically underexplored. To address this gap, we integrated runoff records from 102 gauging stations across two periods, earlier (1964–1979, period 1) and later (2006–2020, period 2), computed 62 hydrological extreme indices, and compiled explanatory variables covering extreme climate, landscape patterns, topography, vegetation, land use, and socioeconomic conditions. A three-tier framework was applied, combining temporal causal discovery (J-PCMCI+), machine-learning attribution (XGBoost-SHAP, RF, BRT), and spatial heterogeneity decomposition (OMGD), enabling systematic comparisons across all catchments as well as separately for natural and managed. The major conclusions are as follows: (1) In terms of multi-year averages, overall, runoff and most extreme indices are higher in period 1 than in period 2, while the change rate shows the opposite pattern. Yet with pronounced spatial disparities across the SYAR, SYER, and SIR basins, particularly for magnitude- and frequency-based indices, including mean and change rate. (2) Extreme climate indices exhibited strong spatial explanatory power but weak temporal predictability, with their effects substantially moderated by underlying surface conditions. In natural catchments, runoff was governed by a synergistic “climate–structure” control, where key climate indices coordinated with landscape metrics (COHESION, PD, DRD). In managed catchments, however, drivers shifted toward land use, water regulation, and ecological status, with SPI, NDVI, Water, Barren, NPP, pH, and Rwidth outweighing climatic factors. High-flow indices depended more on extreme precipitation and routing structures, whereas low-flow and baseflow indices were jointly controlled by landscape connectivity, land use, vegetation, and long-term hydrothermal regimes. (3) Landscape and land-use factors exhibited notable time-lags and directional shifts, while static attributes (topography, catchment morphology) remained stable across periods; interactive effects showed enhanced spatial explanatory power but with marked heterogeneity. Major findings reveal that runoff changes arise from synergistic climatic, landscape, and anthropogenic forcing, with responses being index-specific, scale-dependent, and catchment-type variable. Methodologically, this study provides a spatiotemporally integrated framework combining causal discovery, machine learning, and spatial attribution, offering a valuable reference for hydrological attribution research under global change. 1

title: Microstructure, mechanical, wear, fracture behavior, and machining characteristics of stir-cast A356/n-TiC composites: influence of reinforcement fraction and quenching media
summary: Stir casting was used to reinforce aluminum alloy, A356, with varying wt. % of titanium carbide (TiC) nanoparticles (0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4%). Solution treatment at 520°C for two hours, quenching in three distinct agents (brine solution, syn
content: Stir casting was used to reinforce aluminum alloy, A356, with varying wt. % of titanium carbide (TiC) nanoparticles (0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4%). Solution treatment at 520°C for two hours, quenching in three distinct agents (brine solution, synthetic oil, and hot water), and subsequent aging at 180°C for four hours was carried out. The objective was to examine how microstructure, mechanical, and machining characteristics of the stir-cast n-TiC reinforced A356 composites were affected by n-TiC reinforcement and quenching agents. It was observed that nanoparticles were uniformly distributed throughout the matrix, on the basis of microstructural studies. Among the compositions tested (0 to 4 %), 3 % n-TiC reinforcement exhibited the best mechanical performance, reaching high increase in hardness, tensile strength, and wear resistance. With a 36.2% increase in hardness, a 16.4% increase in tensile strength, and a 39.5% decrease in wear loss, brine quenching produced the greatest overall improvement of all compositions. The ANOVA findings showed that the following factors influenced the machining force, Fm (N), and surface roughness (Ra): wt. % of n-TiC, cooling/quenching agent, depth of cut (mm/min), and cutting speed (rpm). The confirmatory test results confirmed the model's validity within acceptable limits. Specifically, the errors in machining force and surface roughness (Ra) were 9.81% and 7.69%, respectively.

title: Path-dependent NOx dynamics under controlled fuel-flow forcing in an industrial diffusion flame
summary: Controlled fuel-flow forcing can reduce NOx emissions from industrial diffusion flames, but the transient response of nitrogen chemistry remains insufficiently understood. Previous experiments on the investigated furnace demonstrated NOx re
content: Controlled fuel-flow forcing can reduce NOx emissions from industrial diffusion flames, but the transient response of nitrogen chemistry remains insufficiently understood. Previous experiments on the investigated furnace demonstrated NOx reductions of up to approximately 45%. This study investigates path-dependent NOx dynamics using complementary 3-D transient CFD and 0-D chemical-kinetic analyses. CFD-predicted volume-averaged furnace temperatures agreed with measured mean temperatures within approximately 6 K, while the predicted NO concentrations reproduced the experimentally observed decreasing trend with increasing forcing frequency, with deviations of 2.67–6.53 ppm. The transient simulations further resolved phase-dependent temperature and NOx distributions. The 0-D chemical-kinetic model revealed pronounced temperature–NOx hysteresis, indicating that the instantaneous NOx state depends on the preceding thermochemical trajectory. Increasing forcing frequency reduced the temperature and NOx excursions, whereas increasing duty ratio prolonged the fuel-restricted phase and restricted the high-temperature excursion. Rate-of-production analysis showed that extended Zeldovich reactions contributed strongly to NO formation during the high-fuel phase but became negligible during the fuel-restricted phase. The 0-D model predicted NOx reductions of up to approximately 70% within the investigated operating range. This model-based reduction reflects the idealized chemical-kinetic response and should not be interpreted as experimentally validated furnace-scale emission performance.

title: Linking microbial and geochemical processes in a deep volcanic lake (Lake Albano, Central Italy)
summary: Volcanic lakes have been extensively studied for their physical-chemical mechanisms governing greenhouse gas dynamics and potential limnic eruptions. However, the role of microbial communities in these processes remains underexplored. Here,
content: Volcanic lakes have been extensively studied for their physical-chemical mechanisms governing greenhouse gas dynamics and potential limnic eruptions. However, the role of microbial communities in these processes remains underexplored. Here, we integrate geochemical, isotopic, and microbial data from Lake Albano (Central Italy), a temperate volcanic lake (167m deep), to elucidate how biological processes influence carbon cycling and water column stability. A marked stratification characterized the water column, with oxygenated surface waters and progressively anoxic deeper layers where CO₂ and CH₄ accumulated. Microbial community composition changed accordingly, shifting from predominantly aerobic and phototrophic taxa in the upper water column to anaerobic, sulfur-cycling, methanotrophic, and methanogenic groups in the hypolimnion. Functional profiles mirrored this vertical organization, indicating a transition from oxygen-dependent and phototrophic processes to anaerobic carbon- and sulfur-related metabolisms with depth. The coupling between dissolved gas distributions, isotopic signatures, and microbial functional patterns suggests that microbial processes contribute to the transformation of CO₂ and CH₄ within the water column, potentially modulating their vertical accumulation and transfer toward the surface. Overall, this study underscores the crucial role of microbial-geochemical interactions in shaping greenhouse gas dynamics and stratification stability in temperate volcanic lakes, providing novel insights into carbon cycling and ecosystem resilience.

title: Operando Pressure Monitoring, EIS, and X‐Ray Imaging of Solid‐State Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries — Insights into Chemo‐Mechanical Degradation Mechanisms
summary: In this study, we introduce a multi‐modal operando platform that combines cell stack pressure monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and x‐ray imaging to unravel the chemo‐mechanical aging processes in sulfide‐based solid‐state
content: In this study, we introduce a multi‐modal operando platform that combines cell stack pressure monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and x‐ray imaging to unravel the chemo‐mechanical aging processes in sulfide‐based solid‐state sodium‐sulfur (ssNa||S) cells. Despite their promising theoretical capacity and resource abundance, the mechanisms that limit the full performance of ssNa||S batteries are still poorly understood. To address this issue, we employ a new multi‐modal operando setup optimized for solid‐state cells. By comparing cells with different electrolytes, Na 3 PS 4 (NPS), a multiphase electrolyte Na 2 S‐P 2 S 5 ‐NaCl (NPS‐Cl), and Na 3 SbS 4 (NSbS), operando over the course of 50 cycles, we monitor slowly evolving aging effects that are found to be correlated with the electrolyte composition. For NPS, the combination of low interfacial stability against sodium and reduced ionic conductivity causes the electrochemical activity to be concentrated in localized regions, leading to sodium plating‐like behavior as the dominant degradation mechanism. In contrast, the chloride‐containing NPS‐Cl enhances the interfacial stability and mitigates dendrite formation. These findings provide valuable insights for the materials development of sulfide‐based electrolytes for ssNa||S cells and demonstrate the capability of combined operando diagnostics to resolve complex chemo‐mechanical phenomena that influence solid‐state battery performance.

title: Informing the Strategic Use of Multiple Bivalve Species Across an Estuarine Gradient to Counteract Eutrophication
summary: Eutrophication threatens estuaries worldwide, prompting significant investments in nature-based-solutions like bivalve restoration aquaculture to enhance nutrient cycling and improve water quality. However, optimizing bivalve service provis
content: Eutrophication threatens estuaries worldwide, prompting significant investments in nature-based-solutions like bivalve restoration aquaculture to enhance nutrient cycling and improve water quality. However, optimizing bivalve service provisioning in estuaries is challenging due to salinity, predation, and food availability gradients and species-specific physiological tolerances. To guide system-wide management, we conducted field experiments, biogeochemical analyses, spatial analyses, and restoration aquaculture simulations in the eutrophic Guana River (Florida, USA). Transplanting bivalves revealed that lower-intertidal oysters grow twice as fast as higher-intertidal mussels, with oyster growth peaking upstream in brackish, nutrient-enriched waters and mussel growth peaking downstream with higher salinities. Oyster and mussel coverage decreased 3- and 2-fold moving downstream. Scaling nutrient storage and assimilation rates across the estuary, we estimate bivalve N and C storage and annual assimilation services are 4.4-8.8x higher upstream where nutrient loads, oyster growth rates, and bivalve populations are greatest, with oysters providing 63%–93% of these services due to their larger population. Cumulatively, bivalves assimilate 631 kg N per year, 5% of the annual total N input and 10% of the particulate N input to this estuary. By simulating restoration scenarios, we show that concentrating oysters in high-growth upstream areas increases nutrient assimilation by 26–44%, demonstrating that nutrient removal outcomes can be maximized with deliberate spatial planning. We conclude that bivalve management and restoration aquaculture can serve as optimizable tools for countering eutrophication when incorporated with broader nutrient-reduction strategies. We summarize our workflow to support the use of shellfish for nutrient mitigation in estuaries containing multiple bivalve species worldwide.

title: Energy and operational carbon performance of a medical building in Hot-Arid Upper Egypt: A comparative simulation of conventional and sustainable scenarios
source: Journal of Sustainable Food Water Energy and Environment
summary: Climate change intensifies environmental challenges in Egypt, particularly Upper Egypt, where hot-arid conditions and energy-intensive medical buildings increase cooling demand, energy consumption, and emissions. This study aims to evaluate
content: Climate change intensifies environmental challenges in Egypt, particularly Upper Egypt, where hot-arid conditions and energy-intensive medical buildings increase cooling demand, energy consumption, and emissions. This study aims to evaluate the energy performance and operational carbon footprint of a multi-story medical building in Sohag under two scenarios: a conventional base case and a sustainable scenario. In our case study at EL Helal Medical Tower in Sohag Governorate, medical equipment and cooling represented the largest consumers of electricity; therefore, the largest source of carbon emissions. Energy performance simulations were conducted using DesignBuilder software integrated with EnergyPlus. In the base case scenario, equipment and cooling accounted for the largest share of operational energy use to operate the building, followed by lighting, DHW (domestic hot water), and heating, which represented a lower share of total consumption. Results indicated that the sustainable scenario achieved a significant reduction in annual electricity consumption of approximately 49.00%, decreasing from 1,187,523.96 kWh/year in the base case to 605,761.14 kWh/year. The photovoltaic system generated 69,239.34 kWh/year, reducing net grid electricity demand to 536,521.80 kWh/year, about 54.80%, and the reduction in total site energy was 53.20% due to a slight increase in heating energy in the sustainable scenario. The corresponding carbon footprint decreased by 54.33%, from 719.76 tCO₂/year to 328.71 tCO₂/year. The largest contribution to energy savings was observed in the cooling system (62.70%). These results demonstrate the role of integrating passive and active sustainable strategies in reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions in a hot, dry climate.

title: Home Healthcare Routing and Scheduling Considering Automated Guided Vehicles with Failure and Communication Factors: A Robust Possibilistic-Stochastic Approach
summary: Home healthcare (HHC) is a system that provides medical services at the patient’s home. One aspect of this service involves the timely delivery of medical supplies. The performance of transportation equipment significantly influences servic
content: Home healthcare (HHC) is a system that provides medical services at the patient’s home. One aspect of this service involves the timely delivery of medical supplies. The performance of transportation equipment significantly influences service completion times and energy consumption. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a two-echelon scheduling problem, utilizing automated guided vehicles (AGVs) within the home healthcare warehouse and autonomous vehicles (AVs) for delivering medical goods. AGVs transport medical goods from shelves along specific bi-directional paths to the outbound door. During transit, AGVs may encounter failures, requiring immediate repair. In the second echelon, a routing problem is formulated for delivering medical goods to patients’ homes via AVs, considering vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure communications. Given that the data includes both randomness and epistemic uncertainty, we present a robust scenario-based possibilistic-stochastic programming based on the Me criterion. We also conduct a numerical example to evaluate the robustness and efficiency of our model. The results indicate that increasing the scenario coefficient reduces the probability deviation and increases the expected value. Moreover, to adapt to real-world conditions, we simulate the proposed robust model using nominal data. The outcomes indicate the lowest average and standard deviation for constraint violations. Finally, sensitivity analyses were performed on parameters related to demand, the number of AGVs, and AVs energy capacity. The results show that increasing the number of AGVs reduces the total completion time by 9.5%.

title: Optimizing Reliability Indexes of II Practical Standard Electrical Distribution Networks Using LINGO
summary: Today, the power industry is steadily moving toward a competitive and privatized market structure across its various sectors. At the same time, both the qualitative and quantitative expectations of electrical energy consumers are continuous
content: Today, the power industry is steadily moving toward a competitive and privatized market structure across its various sectors. At the same time, both the qualitative and quantitative expectations of electrical energy consumers are continuously increasing. Therefore, one of the primary objectives of power distribution companies is to provide reliable and uninterrupted electricity to customers. Among the main factors that reduce the reliability of distribution networks and disrupt service continuity are outages occurring within the system. Outages may be classified as either momentary (temporary) or permanent. Various factors contribute to their occurrence, including short circuits in the power system, equipment failures, and malfunctions of network components. According to IEEE standard, an outage is considered to have occurred when the network voltage drops below 0.1 per unit. Outages lasting between three seconds and one minute are categorized as permanent outages. Due to the increasing sensitivity of modern electrical equipment to voltage disturbances, it is essential to adopt effective scientific and practical methods to mitigate the effects of momentary outages and enhance power quality. Practical solutions include the installation of sectionalizers, reclosers, cut-out fuses at branch points, and the creation of properly designed switching locations within the distribution network.

title: Carbono elemental de tres especies forestales del bosque reservado de laUniversidad Nacional Agraria de la selva, Tingo María
summary: El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar el contenido de carbono elemental en tres especies forestales del Bosque Reservado de la Universidad Nacional Agraria de la Selva (BRUNAS), Tingo María: Casearia ulmifolia, Hevea guianensis y Jacarand
content: El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar el contenido de carbono elemental en tres especies forestales del Bosque Reservado de la Universidad Nacional Agraria de la Selva (BRUNAS), Tingo María: Casearia ulmifolia, Hevea guianensis y Jacaranda copaia. Se recolectaron muestras de xilema de 33 árboles, 11 individuos por especie, obteniéndose 66 cilindros de madera. La densidad básica se determinó mediante el método gravimétrico y el carbono elemental con un analizador elemental orgánico; la biomasa aérea se estimó mediante un modelo alométrico y el CO2 equivalente mediante la relación estequiométrica CO2 /C. Los resultados evidenciaron diferencias significativas entre especies (p < 0,01). La mayor densidad básica se registró en H. guianensis (0,560 ± 0,008 g·cm-³), seguida de C. ulmifolia (0,532 ± 0,007 g·cm-³), mientras que J. copaia presentó el menor valor (0,304 ± 0,011 g·cm-³). El carbono elemental fue mayor en C. ulmifolia (54,6 ± 0,4 %), seguido de H. guianensis (47,9 ± 0,4 %) y J. copaia (46,2 ± 0,7 %). H. guianensis presentó la mayor acumulación en la clase de 50–60 cm, con 1400,6 kg·árbol-¹ de biomasa aérea, 670,9 kg C·árbol-¹ y 2459,9 kg CO2 ·árbol-¹. Se concluye que las especies evaluadas presentan potencial diferenciado para almacenar carbono.

title: Planning carbon removal landscapes in Africa: land use regulation, spatial justice and the governance of negative emissions
source: Journal of Property Planning and Environmental Law
summary: Purpose This paper aims to explore whether land-use planning and environmental regulations in seven African countries – Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda and Ethiopia – can effectively manage the use of land for carbon d
content: Purpose This paper aims to explore whether land-use planning and environmental regulations in seven African countries – Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda and Ethiopia – can effectively manage the use of land for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies. It examine how planning law handles competing land uses for afforestation, bioenergy with carbon capture and storage and soil carbon sequestration, and assesses whether current frameworks address spatial justice, participatory governance and fair land access. Design/methodology/approach The study uses à socio-legal approach that combines three methods: analyzing land use planning laws, environmental regulations and climate policies in the seven countries; reviewing interdisciplinary literature on land governance, legal pluralism and climate mitigation; and examining national policy documents like nationally determined contributions, spatial plans and land tenure laws. The analysis draws on spatial justice theory and legal pluralism. Since the study is based on documents rather than fieldwork, its findings reflect the legal and policy record. Further research would be needed to confirm how these laws work in practice at the community level. Findings In all seven countries, land-use planning systems are not set up to manage CDR projects effectively. There are three main problems: no clear carbon rights in property law, a gap between climate goals and planning laws and not enough protections for communities whose land rights are affected by carbon removal. These issues perpetuate land inequalities and make green grabbing more likely. The paper proposes a five-part framework for fair CDR governance, including integrating spatial justice, linking climate and planning laws, clarifying carbon rights, managing trade-offs and legally recognizing different tenure systems. Originality/value This paper contributes to the discussion on property law, planning law and climate governance by showing that African planning systems struggle with CDR due to underlying values, not just technical issues. These systems focus more on state development than on fair distribution. The article introduces the idea of spatially just carbon removal governance as a framework for analyzing and reforming these systems, building on African constitutional and international climate law and expanding research on green grabbing and spatial justice to include negative emissions.

title: A framework for holistic development of sustainability in higher education institutions
source: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
summary: Purpose Nations are implementing systematic approaches to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Higher education institutions (HEIs) can serve as powerful catalysts in supporting these efforts and driving progress towards the
content: Purpose Nations are implementing systematic approaches to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Higher education institutions (HEIs) can serve as powerful catalysts in supporting these efforts and driving progress towards the agenda. However, existing Sustainable Assessment Tools (SATs) were unable to meet the needs of developing nations’ HEIs. This study aims to analyse five major SATs and propose a holistic Environmental Social and Governance (ESG)-aligned framework for HEIs, with India as a validation case study. Design/methodology/approach A mixed method approach was used, and data were collected from sources like research articles, ranking and accreditation agencies. Five SATs (QS, UI GM, THE, USAT and STARS) were classified and analysed. The qualitative method involved mapping SAT towards 169 indicators of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). The quantitative method involved charting the proportion of the five SATs indicators and metrics towards ESG. Findings The analysis showed major contribution was towards environmental segment and less towards social and governance. Social SDGs, particularly SDG 8 (Decent work) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) received near zero coverage. The proposed framework includes segments such as social, economic and governance which also aligns with SDGs. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to analyse five SATs through both SDG and ESG charting providing an analysis for existing gaps. The expected impact was highest in the environmental segment by curbing emissions to 5.7 from 7.1 kg CO2eq. per capita per day. Incorporating the proposed framework with a ranking body, like NIRF in India will promote sustainability in HEIs and eventually contribute towards the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development of the nation.

title: Transforming Legacy Oilfield Infrastructure for Hydrogen Transport: Integrating Advanced Technologies and Green Finance
source: SPE Annual Caspian Technical Conference and Exhibition
summary: The urgent need for climate change mitigation and low-carbon energy transition creates a strategic opportunity to repurpose existing oilfield infrastructure for grey and blue hydrogen production, processing, and transportation. This study e
content: The urgent need for climate change mitigation and low-carbon energy transition creates a strategic opportunity to repurpose existing oilfield infrastructure for grey and blue hydrogen production, processing, and transportation. This study evaluates how legacy oil and gas (O&G) facilities and pipeline networks can be converted into hydrogen-ready assets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, minimize flaring, and support sustainable energy-system transformation. Repurposing legacy oil and gas infrastructure for hydrogen service is often presented as a low-cost route to early hydrogen markets, yet the decision is frequently made before material compatibility, lifecycle emissions and financing eligibility are evaluated on a common basis. This paper develops a gate-based screening method that links pipeline requalification, system performance, lifecycle greenhouse-gas intensity and financeability. Three representative asset archetypes are assessed: a documented dry-gas transmission line, an ageing gathering line with incomplete integrity records, and a former liquid-hydrocarbon line. A 200,000-trial Monte Carlo analysis propagates uncertainty in retrofit expenditure, retained energy throughput, operating-cost uplift, carbon-capture performance and upstream methane loss. For the dry-gas archetype, the median retrofit capital ratio was 0.336 relative to a new hydrogen pipeline, and the median normalized delivery burden was 0.484; all sampled cost cases remained below the new-build reference, subject to passing the structural-integrity gate. The ageing gathering line produced a median burden of 1.266 and was below the new-build reference in only 8.1% of trials. The former liquid line produced a median burden of 2.593 and did not reach cost parity. For natural-gas-derived hydrogen, median lifecycle intensity was 1.65 kg CO2e/kg H2 for integrated capture supplied by low-leakage gas, 4.01 kg CO2e/kg H2 for uncertain upstream performance, and 6.06 kg CO2e/kg H2 for partial capture and high leakage. Capture fraction and methane loss were the dominant carbon variables. The analysis also shows that the often-cited global flaring quantities are system-wide upper bounds, not project outcomes: 167 bcm was flared globally in 2025, whereas a project must be evaluated from site-specific recoverable volume, composition and operating continuity. The proposed framework provides a reproducible basis for selecting assets, defining monitoring requirements and linking finance claims to measured technical and carbon performance.

title: Synthesizing mixed-integer linear programming models from natural language descriptions
source: INFOR Information Systems and Operational Research
summary: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) is a powerful tool for solving numerous real-world decision-making problems. However, the formulation process typically requires substantial expert effort. This study investigates whether it is possib
content: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) is a powerful tool for solving numerous real-world decision-making problems. However, the formulation process typically requires substantial expert effort. This study investigates whether it is possible to automatically recognize constraints and generate accurate MILP formulations from unstructured textual descriptions. We propose a multi-stage framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) and mathematical modeling techniques. The framework comprises three stages: (1) identification of decision variables, (2) classification of objectives and constraints with fine-tuned LLMs, and (3) generation of mathematical expressions based on templates, including implicit constraints for logical relations. We conduct numerical evaluation on a new dataset of 30 problems comprising 177 paragraph-level descriptions. The proposed framework is able to generate correct models for 29 of 30 instances and 176 of 177 mathematical expressions. Compared with direct prompting and recent automatic model generation methods, including a training-based framework and an agentic system, our approach achieves 7 to 24 additional accurate models and produces consistent results across multiple trials. Error analysis shows that competing methods often fail to capture implicit constraints or logical relations. Our framework enhances the automation of MILP formulation and also offers opportunities for developing training tools for operations research practitioners and supporting automatic decision problem solving in practice.

title: QAMNet: Co-designing deep learning with complex-valued computing machines
summary: The energy consumption of inference has become critically important with the growing adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs). Analog optical neural networks (ONNs) can reduce the energy of matrix-vector multiplication below that of digital
content: The energy consumption of inference has become critically important with the growing adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs). Analog optical neural networks (ONNs) can reduce the energy of matrix-vector multiplication below that of digital electronics. However, this promise is limited by digital-to-analog (DAC) conversion: even at low bit precision b , encoding the 2 b levels of weights and inputs into the analog domain requires specialized, power-hungry electronics. Quadrature-Amplitude Modulation (QAM), the dominant format in modern telecommunications, encodes information on both the in-phase and quadrature axes of a carrier. A consequence of this two-dimensional signaling is a quadratic O ( N 2 ) → O ( N ) saving in modulation energy over intensity-only modulation. Inspired by this advantage, we introduce QAMNet, an ONN architecture and hardware that fully utilizes the complex amplitude of light with QAM to achieve superior modulation-energy scaling. Using physics-based simulations of conventional telecommunications equipment, we show that QAMNet accelerates complex-valued DNNs with accuracies indistinguishable from digital hardware. Compared to standard ONNs, QAMNet ONNs: (1) attain higher accuracy above moderate total bit precision, (2) are more accurate above low energy budgets, and (3) are optimal when hardware bit precision is limited.

title: Impacts of snowpack on winter ecosystem respiration across the Northern Hemisphere
summary: Climate-driven snowpack dynamics across the Northern Hemisphere introduce substantial uncertainty into the global carbon budget, but how winter ecosystem respiration (Reco winter ) responds to this critical driver remains unclear. In this s
content: Climate-driven snowpack dynamics across the Northern Hemisphere introduce substantial uncertainty into the global carbon budget, but how winter ecosystem respiration (Reco winter ) responds to this critical driver remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the impact of seasonal snowpack on Reco winter across the Northern Hemisphere (NH, > 30 ° N) using multi-source datasets. Our analysis revealed that in 34.71 % of NH ecosystems, snowpack (depth, density, and duration) exerted the most critical impact on respiration. Incorporating snowpack indicators progressively improved model R 2 compared with no-snowpack models. Applying a single indicator improved R 2 by 0.19–0.22 over 18.85 % –32.96 % of the study area, and the combined use of all three indicators improved R 2 by an average of 0.24 over 50.18 % of the study area, demonstrating the necessity of adopting a multi-indicator approach. By applying structural equation models, we further demonstrated that snowpack impacts Reco winter through direct, thermal, and moisture pathways, with the direction and relative contribution of each pathway exhibiting significant regional differentiation under varying hydrothermal conditions. The thermal pathway was predominantly positive across the NH (69.53 % of ecosystems), the direct pathway shifted from a negative impact in cold zones to a positive impact in warm zones, and the moisture pathway was negative in most of the study area. These findings highlight the complex and spatially heterogeneous nature of snowpack impacts on winter ecosystem carbon fluxes, and underscore the importance of adopting a multi-indicator, multi-mechanism perspective in understanding ecosystem responses to snowpack.

title: Trophic state assessment of a phosphorus-enriched pre-sanctuary estuarine reach using Carlson TSI, Bayesian network modelling, and Shannon entropy analysis
summary: Estuarine reaches immediately upstream of protected habitats intercept nutrient and pollutant loads before they reach the protected zone, yet their trophic status is rarely monitored. This study provides a field-based trophic assessment of
content: Estuarine reaches immediately upstream of protected habitats intercept nutrient and pollutant loads before they reach the protected zone, yet their trophic status is rarely monitored. This study provides a field-based trophic assessment of the Tulabhagya River reach, a 6.8-km distributary of the Godavari Delta (Andhra Pradesh, India) immediately upstream of the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary (CWS), India's second-largest contiguous mangrove forest. Water samples were collected from ten stations across 6 months (January–June 2025); total phosphorus (TP), chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), and Secchi disk depth (SDD) were measured to compute Carlson’s Trophic State Index (TSI). A Bayesian Network (BN) model was developed for probabilistic scenario analysis under four TP loading conditions, and Shannon entropy analysis quantified spatial and temporal variability across 60 station-month observations. Results confirm persistent hypertrophic conditions throughout the transect (TSI(Avg): 68.84–79.50; mean = 74.71 ± 2.69), driven by TP concentrations (mean 1733 ± 512 µg L −1 ) exceeding the eutrophic threshold by up to 31-fold. TSI(Chl-a) remained oligotrophic, near the mesotrophic threshold, evidencing turbidity-mediated phytoplankton suppression. The BN model indicated 70% eutrophic–hypertrophic probability under high-TP conditions, shifting to 77% oligotrophic–mesotrophic probability when TP was reduced to 1000 µg L −1 . Shannon entropy reached its theoretical maximum for SDD and TSI(Avg) (H = 1.585 bits). A strong relationship between TSI(TP) and TSI(Avg) (R 2 = 0.602, p < 0.001) identifies TP as the dominant trophic driver. These findings provide a probabilistic evidence base for targeted phosphorus abatement to safeguard the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary.

title: Present and future responses of near-surface wind speed to different land-use and land-cover types in China
summary: Near-surface wind speed (NSWS) is highly sensitive to land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). However, previous studies have mainly focused on overall LULCC effects, leaving the attribution of wind variations to individual land transitions
content: Near-surface wind speed (NSWS) is highly sensitive to land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). However, previous studies have mainly focused on overall LULCC effects, leaving the attribution of wind variations to individual land transitions and management poorly constrained. Here, we utilize simulations from the latest Land-Use Model Intercomparison Project to disentangle and quantify the responses of NSWS to different types of LULCC over China from 1970 to 2014. We demonstrate that the primary-to-grazing transition is the dominant factor contributing to LULCC-induced NSWS variability, followed by fertilizer use, while urbanization makes the smallest contribution among the examined LULCC types. Future projections further suggest that land-use pathways can substantially perturb wind patterns, with low-emission pathways combined with minimally regulated land use producing more pronounced alterations than high-emission pathways combined with sustainable land use. These results highlight the importance of resolving LULCC in attributing and projecting NSWS changes, with implications for climate modeling, wind-energy assessment, and land-use policy.

title: Combined Rhizophagus irregularis and Bacillus megaterium inoculation enhances root hydraulics and potassium acquisition and improves maize tolerance to drought stress and potassium deficiency
summary: In this study we investigated the effectiveness of combined inoculation with the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus R. irregularis and the PGPR B. megaterium in improving maize tolerance to combined potassium (K) deficiency and drought stress. T
content: In this study we investigated the effectiveness of combined inoculation with the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus R. irregularis and the PGPR B. megaterium in improving maize tolerance to combined potassium (K) deficiency and drought stress. Thus, maize plants inoculated with these microorganisms or maintained as uninoculated controls were cultivated either under deficient K supply (0.3 mM K) or under ample K fertilization (6 mM K). Half of plants was maintained under well-watered conditions during the entire experiment and the other half was subjected to drought stress for 15 days before harvest. Results showed that under K deficiency, the combined inoculation of R. irregularis plus B. megaterium allowed maize plants to overcome the problem of K limitation and to reach a similar biomass production than uninoculated control plants cultivated under normal K levels. This effect was observed both, under well-watered and under drought stress conditions. The mechanisms underlying these effects on plant growth include enhanced root hydraulic conductivities, improved photosynthetic capacity and efficiency of photosystem II, reduced oxidative damage to lipids, and enhanced K uptake and accumulation. This indicates that, for important crops such as maize, the inoculated microorganisms can contribute to reducing the use of chemical fertilizers under the influence of additional abiotic stresses such as drought.

title: A digital twin and XR framework for heritage access by visitors with mobility limitations
summary: Balancing heritage authenticity with accessibility presents a "double constraint" for historical sites restricted by complex topography and strict preservation laws. This study addresses this challenge by proposing a non-invasive "Scan-to-S
content: Balancing heritage authenticity with accessibility presents a "double constraint" for historical sites restricted by complex topography and strict preservation laws. This study addresses this challenge by proposing a non-invasive "Scan-to-Service" framework that integrates LiDAR, Digital Twin (DT), and Extended Reality (XR) to revolutionize inclusive smart tourism. Using Taipei’s Treasure Hill Artist Village as a testbed, we developed a high-fidelity Digital Twin and an accessibility-optimized XR interface, subsequently validating the system's efficacy through the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) model with 36 elderly and mobility-impaired participants. Empirical results demonstrate that the virtual system significantly outperforms traditional physical tourism experiences. Notably, a surge in "Technology Utilization" scores confirms that such advanced tourism technology successfully unlocks latent demand previously suppressed by physical barriers, while business model analysis indicating a user preference for pay-per-use services suggests long-term economic sustainability. By establishing a comprehensive engineering workflow, this research theoretically extends the TTF model to the domain of inclusive heritage and demonstrates how automation can empirically realize spatial justice and cultural equity for marginalized groups.

title: Unveiling carbonate dissolution in coastal sediments and its influence on seawater buffering capacity with δ 13 C DIC and 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibria
summary: Organic carbon mineralization is generally recognized as the primary source of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) released from sediments in coastal seas. The CO 2 accumulation or the formation of corrosive microenvironment induced by organic
content: Organic carbon mineralization is generally recognized as the primary source of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) released from sediments in coastal seas. The CO 2 accumulation or the formation of corrosive microenvironment induced by organic carbon degradation can promote the dissolution of calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) in sediments, complicating the efficiency of carbon burial and total alkalinity (TA) inputs to aquatic environments. However, quantitative assessments of sediment CaCO 3 dissolution and its impacts on the seawater carbonate remain poorly constrained. In this study, we selected typical high-productivity regions, mariculture farms, and applied the 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibrium approach to quantify the effluxes of DIC and TA across the sediment-water interface. The stable carbon isotope of DIC ( δ 13 C DIC ) was employed to trace DIC sources in porewater. The results showed that CaCO 3 dissolution in the sediment accounted for 29±13 % to 55±10 % of the benthic DIC effluxes. Notably, a high contribution of CaCO 3 dissolution did not coincide with strong organic carbon degradation across sites, suggesting that dynamic disturbance in the sediment, which weakened the metabolic CO 2 accumulation in porewater, was also a crucial factor affecting carbonate dissolution. According to the evaluation of the influence that benthic DIC and TA effluxes exerted on the seawater CO 2 content, the TA supplied by the CaCO 3 dissolution was identified to enhance the carbonate buffering capacity of seawater and counteracted the acidification driven by organic matter remineralization. This indicates that CaCO 3 dissolution in sediments should be involved in coastal carbon cycling and assessments on coastal ecosystem resilience under the risk of CO 2 elevation.

title: RMG-Py v4: 17 Years of Open-Source Reaction Mechanism Generation
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Kinetic modeling describes reacting chemical systems through networks of elementary reactions and their associated rate parameters. Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG-Py) automates the construction of these networks by simulating reaction fl
content: Kinetic modeling describes reacting chemical systems through networks of elementary reactions and their associated rate parameters. Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG-Py) automates the construction of these networks by simulating reaction fluxes to identify dominant chemical pathways in silico. RMG-Py v4.0.0 marks 17 years of open-source reaction mechanism generation, introducing substantial improvements in performance, usability, and chemical scope. Benchmarks demonstrate higher throughput in constructing combustion models relative to prior versions, alongside streamlined installation via Docker and binary distributions. Key new capabilities include automated library selection, improved species selection algorithms, integration with the Julia-based ReactionMechanismSimulator.jl for simulating arbitrary reactor configurations, and PySIDT-based property estimators.
