title: Explainability-based virtual metrology for surface roughness prediction in lubrication-assisted turning under variable conditions
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Accurate and rapidly deployable prediction of surface roughness is essential in lubrication-assisted hard turning because conventional physics-based simulations remain computationally intensive and do not readily capture lubrication-depende
content: Accurate and rapidly deployable prediction of surface roughness is essential in lubrication-assisted hard turning because conventional physics-based simulations remain computationally intensive and do not readily capture lubrication-dependent thermo-tribological effects. This study developed an Artificial Intelligence-based Manufacturing Process Optimization and Design (AIMPOD) framework to model surface roughness in turning of AISI D2 steel under dry, flood, cryogenic, and minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) conditions. The parametric window included cutting speed $$V=80\text {--}307.867$$ m/min, feed rate $$f=0.05\text {--}0.24$$ mm/rev, and depth of cut $$a_p=0.15\text {--}1.20$$ mm, while the measured roughness ranged from $$R_a=0.31$$ to $$1.265~\mu \text {m}$$ . Exploratory analysis showed that feed rate was the dominant variable, with the strongest correlation to roughness ( $$r=0.74$$ ), compared with depth of cut ( $$r=0.31$$ ) and cutting speed ( $$r=-0.24$$ ). Gradient Boosting was the strongest individual learner, with $$R^2_{\textrm{test}}=0.943$$ , RMSE $$=0.05~\mu \textrm{m}$$ , and MAE $$=0.03~\mu \textrm{m}$$ . The genetically weighted ensemble achieved $$R^2_{\textrm{test}}=0.9434$$ and RMSE $$=0.0492~\mu \textrm{m}$$ , closely matching the best individual model. Genetic optimization was used to determine model-combination weights rather than machining settings. Main-effect analysis further showed that dry turning produced the highest mean roughness ( $$\sim 0.90~\mu \text {m}$$ ), whereas MQL gave the lowest ( $$\sim 0.60~\mu \text {m}$$ ). The results demonstrate that explainable machine learning can provide robust and physically meaningful support for surface quality related operational decision in sustainable hard turning.

title: Data-Efficient Machine Learning-DFT Workflow for Rapid Prediction of Polyaromatic Reactivity on Bimetallic Surfaces
summary: Density functional theory (DFT) simulations have become an essential tool for studying surface reactivity at the microscale, providing guidelines for experimentalists in the design of efficient catalyst compositions across a wide range of a
content: Density functional theory (DFT) simulations have become an essential tool for studying surface reactivity at the microscale, providing guidelines for experimentalists in the design of efficient catalyst compositions across a wide range of applications. However, DFT calculations are resource-intensive and can be prohibitively time-consuming, especially when large adsorbates must be sampled across heterogeneous surfaces with many nonequivalent adsorption sites. In this work, we propose a joint ML–DFT workflow to accelerate the prediction of polyaromatic reactivity on bimetallic surfaces using carefully selected descriptors computed on related molecular fragments. To establish a proof of concept for this strategy, we focused on the hydrogenation of anthraquinone (AQ) to anthrahydroquinone (H2AQ)─a key step in the industrial production of hydrogen peroxide─on Pd-based alloys (25 and 50 at. % alloying ratios). We show that a relatively small data set (<100 samples) is sufficient to build predictive models with high accuracy and strong robustness using tree-based regression methods. Notably, despite the flexibility of these ML algorithms and the broad diversity of surface atomic arrangements and adsorbate configurations represented in our training set, overfitting could be effectively limited through careful selection of multidimensional descriptor sets and appropriate model tuning. With training mean absolute errors (train-MAEs) on the order of ∼0.15 eV for predicting AQ and H2AQ adsorption energies, as well as the AQ-to-H2AQ hydrogenation reaction energies, our model is competitive with state-of-the-art ML approaches in heterogeneous catalysis, including machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), which for certain surface classes and adsorbate types often struggle to achieve train-MAEs below ∼0.10 eV. Although developed here for polycyclic aromatic compounds, we anticipate that this strategy could be extended to other large, chemically complex molecular systems, helping bridge computational screening with experimental validation in industrially relevant catalyst design.

title: Ski Tourism Under Global Climate Change: Carbon Footprint, Energy Efficiency, and Sustainability Perspectives from Turkey and Lithuania
summary: This study aims to determine the Scope 2 electricity-related carbon emissions of Sarıkamış Ski Center in Turkey and Liepkalnis Ski Centre in Lithuania during the 2025–2026 ski season (December 2025–March 2026) and to evaluate the findings f
content: This study aims to determine the Scope 2 electricity-related carbon emissions of Sarıkamış Ski Center in Turkey and Liepkalnis Ski Centre in Lithuania during the 2025–2026 ski season (December 2025–March 2026) and to evaluate the findings from an environmental sustainability perspective through expert opinions. A mixed-methods approach was employed. In the quantitative phase, electricity consumption data were obtained for both facilities, and their associated Scope 2 electricity-related carbon emissions were calculated using country-specific electricity emission factors, while the qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with 40 experts from Turkey and Lithuania. The calculated Scope 2 electricity-related carbon emissions were 98.8408 t CO2e for Sarıkamış Ski Center and 16.7135 t CO2e for Liepkalnis Ski Centre. Because the two ski resorts differ substantially in scale and operational characteristics, these absolute emission values should not be interpreted as direct indicators of relative energy efficiency or overall environmental sustainability. These values represent only purchased-electricity-related Scope 2 emissions and should not be interpreted as the complete carbon footprints of the two ski resorts. This substantial difference was primarily associated with the higher electricity emission factor in Turkey and differences in the scale and operational characteristics of the two ski resorts. Expert opinions identified energy efficiency, renewable energy use, smart energy management, regular monitoring, and infrastructure modernization as key priorities for sustainable ski resorts. In Turkey, public support, incentives, and infrastructure renewal were emphasized, while in Lithuania greater attention was given to low-carbon energy sources and the integration of monitoring systems. Overall, the findings from these two cases indicate that regular carbon monitoring, optimized energy use, renewable energy transition, and stakeholder participation are important sustainability priorities.

title: Research on a Fault Fast Self-Healing Method Based on Distributed Energy Storage Cluster Control Strategy
summary: To address the fault self-healing bottlenecks in active distribution networks (ADNs) with high-penetration distributed energy resources, this paper proposes a fast fault self-healing method based on distributed energy storage (DES) cluster
content: To address the fault self-healing bottlenecks in active distribution networks (ADNs) with high-penetration distributed energy resources, this paper proposes a fast fault self-healing method based on distributed energy storage (DES) cluster cooperative control. The integrated framework combines voltage cooperative control and mode-adaptive frequency deviation control to enhance the operational stability and fault resilience of ADNs under both grid-connected and post-fault islanded scenarios.The voltage cooperative control strategy is functional for both grid-connected and islanded operation, while the frequency deviation control is triggered only upon feeder islanding to prevent unnecessary control intervention during normal grid operation. To achieve high-precision voltage regulation, an enhanced droop-based cooperative control approach is developed by fully considering the residual capacity of individual DES units and the inherent impedance characteristics of distribution feeders. Meanwhile, droop coefficient tuning principles are formulated to coordinate the dynamic responses of multiple DES units. This design effectively suppresses feeder-wide voltage fluctuations in grid-connected mode and maintains stable voltage profiles under islanded operating conditions.For islanded frequency regulation, a dual-hysteresis frequency control strategy is presented to improve the post-fault frequency support performance of DES clusters. Equipped with bidirectional upper and lower hysteresis comparison mechanisms, the proposed scheme accurately identifies positive and negative frequency deviations and enables DES frequency regulation loops according to preset thresholds. This strategy achieves reliable frequency restoration and precise islanding detection without relying on communication links, and it exhibits superior robustness against stochastic frequency disturbances induced by real-time power fluctuations during grid-connected operation.A distinct advantage of the proposed DES cluster control strategy is its full communication independence, which eliminates data interaction and information sharing among feeder nodes. Only local voltage and frequency measurements are utilized to implement cooperative voltage regulation for grid-connected operation and adaptive frequency stabilization for islanded operation. Integrating with feeder reclosing and automatic transfer switching technologies, the proposed method enables rapid feeder reconfiguration and efficient fault self-healing, offering a practical and effective solution for improving the operational resilience of modern active distribution networks.

title: Living labs in higher education for energy-saving behaviors: a systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: Energy transitions require not only technological innovation and policy support but also changes in everyday energy-use practices. Higher education institutions are increasingly recognized as important sites for sustainability learning beca
content: Energy transitions require not only technological innovation and policy support but also changes in everyday energy-use practices. Higher education institutions are increasingly recognized as important sites for sustainability learning because they can connect knowledge acquisition, campus operations, and behavioral change. However, a persistent gap remains between the technological potential of energy transitions and users’ actual energy-saving practices, limiting the broader societal benefits of low-carbon transformation. Although Living Labs (LLs) have been applied as real-world, user-centered environments that integrate technologies, stakeholders, and socio-material contexts, evidence regarding their effectiveness in shaping energy-saving behaviors and sustainability learning in higher education remains fragmented. This study conducts a systematic review and meta-analysis of LLs-based interventions published between 2005 and 2024 to assess their contributions to energy-related behavioral change in higher education. Following PRISMA standards, 44 studies yielding 60 effect sizes were synthesized using a random-effects model. The pooled effect size showed a moderate positive effect on pro-environmental attitudes and behaviors (Hedges’ g = 0.539), while substantial heterogeneity (I² = 97.7%) indicated that intervention outcomes were strongly shaped by contextual and methodological factors. Moderator analyses revealed significant regional variation, with East Asian LLs-based interventions showing the largest effects. Attitudinal outcomes were more responsive than behavioral outcomes, suggesting that changing pro-environmental attitudes does not automatically translate into behavioral change. Interventions incorporating structured environmental or energy education were more effective than those relying mainly on standalone nudges or norm-based strategies. Higher education students also showed stronger responsiveness than other participant groups, reflecting the importance of cognitive maturity, learning autonomy, and emerging energy citizenship. These findings clarify the role of LLs as socio-technical and pedagogical environments for bridging sustainability knowledge and energy-saving practices. The study contributes evidence-based guidance for designing multi-component, context-sensitive LLs frameworks that support behavioral foundations for low-carbon energy transitions.

title: Quantifying pixel- and patch-scale Spartina patens dynamics during salt marsh restoration using multispectral UAV imagery
summary: As a salt marsh restoration progresses, the temporal transition from low marsh to high-marsh vegetation is an ecologically important stage reflecting increased elevation and reduced tidal inundation, as well as associated changes in ecosyst
content: As a salt marsh restoration progresses, the temporal transition from low marsh to high-marsh vegetation is an ecologically important stage reflecting increased elevation and reduced tidal inundation, as well as associated changes in ecosystem functioning and services including faunal community composition, fish accessibility, coastal protection, and carbon burial. However, quantifying this transitional process is challenging because vegetation change often occurs at fine spatial scales. We used high-resolution, multispectral uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and pixel-based random forest classification to generate annual land cover maps at two managed realignment salt marsh restoration sites in the Bay of Fundy, Atlantic Canada, over three growing seasons (2020–2022). High classification accuracy (overall accuracy 90.1–95.2%) enabled detailed assessment of vegetation change, showing expansion of the foundational high-marsh zone grass Spartina patens . Patch-based analyses showed that persistent S. patens patches formed stable patch cores that gradually increased in area through time, while gains and losses were concentrated along patch edges. Most gains occurred in areas previously occupied by the low marsh cordgrass S. alterniflora , whereas direct colonization of mud was uncommon. Ancillary image-derived predictor analysis focused on the congeneric Spartina grasses showed that the most important spectral wavelength bands, vegetation indices, and textural features differed between S. patens comparisons with sparse and dense S. alterniflora. Together, our findings demonstrate that combining pixel-based UAV classifications, patch-based analyses, and evaluation of image-derived predictors improves understanding of vegetation succession and provides a transferable framework for monitoring high-marsh development in restoring salt marshes.

title: Selecting cellulolytic bacteria for ruminants: from recoverable isolates to added function in the rumen
summary: Cellulolytic bacteria initiate an important part of plant-fibre conversion in the rumen, yet activity measured in pure culture does not establish that adding a strain will increase feed utilization by an established microbial community. Thi
content: Cellulolytic bacteria initiate an important part of plant-fibre conversion in the rumen, yet activity measured in pure culture does not establish that adding a strain will increase feed utilization by an established microbial community. This critical narrative review traces the evidence needed to move from a recoverable candidate to a useful intervention. Anaerobic cultivation resolves strain physiology; genome-guided discovery expands the candidate pool; and community studies reveal how substrate access, partner identity and competition shape realized activity. These approaches address different levels of inference and should not be treated as interchangeable measures of efficacy. We distinguish primary degraders from accessory organisms whose contribution emerges in defined combinations, and propose three evidence gates: verified conversion or attributable facilitation on the intended substrate, incremental conversion in a receiving community, and a nutritional response under relevant feeding conditions. Microbial pretreatment and live supplementation share the need for traceable preparations but require different assessments of material recovery and delivered potency. Published intervention studies show why inoculant presence, in situ fibre disappearance and animal performance must be interpreted separately. The framework is a testable decision aid, not a validated predictive score. Progress will depend on matched substrate and donor comparisons, explicit failure diagnoses and prospective evaluations that retain unsuccessful candidates.

title: Designing a Three-Track Internal Carbon Pricing Governance Mechanism in the Real Estate Service Industry
summary: This study examines how internal carbon pricing (ICP) can be designed as an organisational governance mechanism in the real estate service industry, where carbon emissions are dispersed across daily operations, service processes, and employ
content: This study examines how internal carbon pricing (ICP) can be designed as an organisational governance mechanism in the real estate service industry, where carbon emissions are dispersed across daily operations, service processes, and employee behaviours rather than concentrated in production activities. While existing ICP literature has primarily focused on manufacturing and energy-intensive sectors, conventional pricing models are often less effective in real estate service settings, where carbon reduction depends more heavily on organisational coordination, managerial alignment, and behavioural change. To address this gap, this study develops an analytical framework for the real estate service industry, informed by the institutional context of Sinyi Realty and its existing carbon management arrangements. The analysis suggests that ICP in this industry cannot function effectively as a governance tool through price signaling alone; instead, it must be embedded in an integrated institutional design that links short-term motivation, medium-term accountability, and long-term transformation. More specifically, the findings indicate that an effective ICP mechanism in the real estate service industry requires three interconnected governance tracks: short-term carbon reduction incentives to encourage frontline participation and behavioural change; medium-term performance evaluation arrangements that incorporate carbon reduction outcomes into departmental accountability; and long-term reinvestment mechanisms that channel avoided carbon costs into low-carbon technologies and broader organisational transformation. By linking these three dimensions, the proposed framework transforms individual carbon-saving actions into a collective organisational asset and fosters a governance environment in which operational behaviour and corporate development are mutually reinforcing. In this sense, the three-track structure should be understood not merely as a managerial arrangement, but as a set of essential governance conditions through which ICP can become operationally effective in dispersed-emission service contexts. The study further argues that resource allocation across these governance tracks should remain dynamic, enabling organisations to shift gradually from individual mobilization toward more systemic managerial and technological transformation as carbon governance maturity evolves. By reframing ICP as an organisational governance mechanism rather than merely a pricing instrument, this study contributes to the literature on carbon management in the real estate service industry and offers a scalable analytical perspective for firms pursuing net-zero transition.

title: Exploring virulence, histopathological alterations and host immune gene expression associated with Lactococcus lactis 4NC1 infection in Labeo bata
summary: Disease outbreaks caused by emerging bacterial pathogens represent a significant challenge to sustainable aquaculture production. In the present study, a severe mortality event (>60%) affecting Labeo bata in a freshwater culture system in W
content: Disease outbreaks caused by emerging bacterial pathogens represent a significant challenge to sustainable aquaculture production. In the present study, a severe mortality event (>60%) affecting Labeo bata in a freshwater culture system in West Bengal, India, was investigated to identify the causative agent and elucidate its pathogenic mechanisms. Diseased fish exhibited hemorrhagic lesions, ulceration, and skin discoloration. The bacterial pathogen isolated from moribund fish was identified as Lactococcus lactis 4NC1 through biochemical characterization, 16S rRNA gene sequencing (GenBank strain name, CIFRI.LL-55; accession number, OR999571), and phylogenetic analysis, showing 99.86% sequence similarity with reference L. lactis strains. Antibiotic susceptibility testing revealed a multidrug-resistant phenotype with a multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) index of 0.30, indicating potential exposure to high antimicrobial selection pressure. The isolate demonstrated significantly higher biofilm-forming ability and lower swimming motility, suggesting enhanced virulence potential. Experimental challenge assays (@ 1.2 × 10^4, 1.2 × 10^5, 1.2 × 10^6, 1.2 × 10^7, and 1.2 × 10^8 CFU/fish) confirmed the pathogenicity of the isolate. Survival of L. bata declined with increasing pathogen dose and exposure duration, ranging from 100% survival at 10^4 to complete mortality at 10^8 within 24 h. At 10^7, survival decreased to 10% at 24 h, followed by complete mortality at 48 h, while 50-65% survival was recorded at doses of 10^5-10^6 during the later observation period. The estimated 96-h LD 50 was approximately 10^6 dose units, indicating a dose-dependent pathogenic effect. Histopathological examination revealed severe pathological alterations in the gills and liver, including lamellar hyperplasia, epithelial lifting, lamellar fusion, hepatocellular degeneration, vacuolation, necrosis, and inflammatory infiltration, indicating extensive tissue damage and systemic infection. To investigate host immune responses, the expression of immune- and stress-related genes was evaluated in kidney, liver, and spleen tissues. Infection significantly upregulated Hsp70, TLR4, IL-1β, iNOS , C3 , and Mx , reflecting activation of stress-response, pathogen-recognition, inflammatory, complement-mediated, and innate immune pathways. Conversely, IFN-γ, NOD1 , and MyD88 were consistently downregulated across tissues, suggesting pathogen-induced modulation of specific immune signaling pathways. Expression of IgM remained largely unchanged, indicating a predominant innate immune response during the acute phase of infection. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that pathogenic L. lactis possesses multidrug resistance and multiple virulence-associated traits capable of causing severe disease and mortality in L. bata . This study provides novel insights into the immunopathological mechanisms of lactococcosis in Indian minor carps and highlights the urgent need for improved disease surv

title: Antarctic meltwater discharge impacts the Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall
summary: Antarctic ice sheet is melting at a faster rate, resulting into an increased freshwater flux entering the Southern Ocean from the Antarctic continent. State-of-the-art coupled climate models generally lack the physical components required t
content: Antarctic ice sheet is melting at a faster rate, resulting into an increased freshwater flux entering the Southern Ocean from the Antarctic continent. State-of-the-art coupled climate models generally lack the physical components required to accurately represent the dominant sources of Antarctic ice sheet melt, which contribute to the uncertainty in climate change projections. The Southern Ocean Freshwater Input from Antarctica (SOFIA) initiative aims to systematically address this problem by quantifying the climate system response to Antarctic meltwater input in coupled models. Here, the output of nine coupled models is analysed to demonstrate that an input of 0.1 Sv freshwater flux due to Antarctic mass loss significantly increases the Indian summer monsoon rainfall (ISMR). We find a significant cooling (warming) in sea surface temperature (SST) over the equatorial Pacific (extra-tropical North Pacific) ocean as a result of the additional freshwater flux from Antarctica. The changes in Pacific Ocean SST are reminiscent of the Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO)-like structure. Then, the anomalous Antarctic freshwater flux acts to increase the ISMR via the IPO-ISMR teleconnection, which is likely to become more prominent in a warming environment. A strengthened ISMR could have profound impacts on the densely populated Indian sub-continent.

title: Fluke in the grass: variation in Fasciola hepatica and Calicophoron daubneyi metacercarial encystment among forage species
summary: Background The trematode parasites Fasciola hepatica and Calicophoron daubneyi infect grazing livestock following ingestion of metacercariae encysted on herbage. However, the influence of forage species on metacercariae encystment is poorly
content: Background The trematode parasites Fasciola hepatica and Calicophoron daubneyi infect grazing livestock following ingestion of metacercariae encysted on herbage. However, the influence of forage species on metacercariae encystment is poorly understood. The aim of this study was to determine whether the encystment of F. hepatica and C. daubneyi differed among common forage species. Methods Infected Galba truncatula snails were stimulated to shed cercariae in the presence of forage material. Single forage species assays were conducted for F. hepatica and C. daubneyi using eight and three forage species, respectively, and a mixed-forage species assay directly compared F. hepatica encystment on Italian ryegrass, Timothy and Cocksfoot. Metacercarial recovery from plant and non-plant locations was recorded with relative encystment analysed using beta-binomial models. Results Relative encystment differed among forage species with relative F. hepatica encystment lower on Timothy (OR = 0.438, P = 0.036) and Yorkshire fog (OR = 0.106, P < 0.001) compared to Italian ryegrass. In the mixed-forage assay, relative F. hepatica encystment was lower on Cocksfoot (OR = 0.519, P = 0.040) and Timothy (OR = 0.453, P = 0.015) than on Italian ryegrass. Leaf-surface analysis indicated lower surface bias for F. hepatica metacercariae encystment on Italian ryegrass and Yorkshire fog ( P < 0.05). In contrast, in the separate C. daubneyi assay, relative C. daubneyi encystment was higher on Plantain (OR = 38.305, P < 0.001) and Yorkshire fog (OR = 26.862, P = 0.001) than on Italian ryegrass. Conclusions Variation in relative encystment of F. hepatica and C. daubneyi metacercariae was seen among forage species. These findings suggest that plant–parasite interactions during the free-living metacercarial stage may influence the spatial distribution of infective stages on pasture. Semi-natural and field-based studies are needed to determine whether these differences affect transmission risk under grazing conditions.

title: Feeling the “Pinch”? On the Cost of Relying on the Forest Sink to fulfill EU LULUCF and Climate Targets
summary: Several EU Member states have recently been rocked by revelations that their LULUCF-based net forest carbon removal targets are becoming more and more difficult to achieve. Though blame for this phenomenon has frequently been leveled at gov
tags: Land use, land-use change and forestry
content: Several EU Member states have recently been rocked by revelations that their LULUCF-based net forest carbon removal targets are becoming more and more difficult to achieve. Though blame for this phenomenon has frequently been leveled at governments and the forestry sector, much of the difficulty in achieving these targets derives from the global inability to better respond to and manage the climate challenge. Tree growth is highly dependent upon the climate and our inability to adequately reduce energy and industrial sector emissions is increasingly challenging the climatic conditions under which trees grow. Depending on how important a role the LULUCF sector plays in meeting individual Member state climate commitments, as well as on how the policy itself is structured, shortfalls in emission reductions will have variable impacts on national level climate change mitigation objectives. Countries with more sizable LULUCF sector commitments are likewise frequently both more heavily invested in, and constrained by, forest growth, harvest practice and their bioeconomy ambitions. Declining growth potentially means reduced availability of renewable, material, and circular bioeconomy resources: i.e., declining carbon sequestration in the harvested wood product carbon pool, and the declining availability of biomass-based, renewable, material and energetic resources. Moreover, where declining growth and LULUCF sector targets progressively impinge upon the availability of the renewable, material forest biomass resource, one can increasingly expect significant and increasingly acute social, ecological and political conflict. As the current road to Paris grows increasingly rough and rocky, we ask what the alternative routes might be?

title: Climate Effect of Alternative Binders: Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Potential as a Carbon Sink
summary: Substituting Portland cement (PC) with alternative binders offers a promising pathway to mitigate the climate impacts of the cement industry, one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonize. While substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissio
content: Substituting Portland cement (PC) with alternative binders offers a promising pathway to mitigate the climate impacts of the cement industry, one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonize. While substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are generated during production, most alternative binders can sequester CO2 during their service life. This effect has been acknowledged from a technical perspective, yet its significant influences on the GHG footprint of alternative binders remain unresolved. In this study, we quantify the CO2 uptake of common alternative binders alongside their lifetime GHG emissions. We demonstrate that most binders can take up a larger amount of CO2 than PC during usage, due to a thermodynamically high uptake capacity or high uptake kinetics. The uptake reactions enable a dynamic CO2 loop, with 1–248% of the production emissions being recovered over a 100-year structure service life. However, when the slow reaction rate is considered, the associated climate benefits can be up to 71% lower than the theoretical apparent uptake value. Our results highlight the importance of combined CO2 uptake modeling in assessing the decarbonization potential of alternative binders, and provide a basis for justifying the capability of these binders for use as building carbon sinks.

title: Jurisdictional reference levels from direct biomass estimation: emissions, removals, and uncertainty in nine tropical jurisdictions
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Jurisdictional forest reference emission levels (FRELs) submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) are generally built from an activity-data by emission-factor (AD × EF) framework: forest is defined stru
tags: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
content: Jurisdictional forest reference emission levels (FRELs) submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) are generally built from an activity-data by emission-factor (AD × EF) framework: forest is defined structurally, land-cover change is mapped or sampled, and the area of each change class is multiplied by an average per-class carbon density from field plots. A single stock-and-change method, in which above-ground biomass and its annual change are estimated at each 30 m pixel, was applied to nine jurisdictions: Kenya, Zambia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Colombia, Cambodia, Indonesia, and the Brazilian states of Pará, Amazonas, and Mato Grosso. Each jurisdiction was analyzed over the reference period of the relevant UNFCCC submission and over a common recent five-year window. The forest domain was defined by a biomass threshold calibrated, by ecological zone, to the canopy-cover criterion of each national forest definition against an independent tree-cover layer; below-ground biomass was added per pixel from Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) 2019 default root-to-shoot ratios keyed to ecological zone and biomass tier; degradation was restricted to forest remaining forest; and gains were recovered from the same signed record as losses. The analysis drew on 2,364 field plot measurements, with plot-based calibration of the biomass maps in all nine jurisdictions, tested against held-out and remeasured plots. Over the FREL historical reference periods degradation accounted for 79% of forest emissions on an emissions-weighted basis and exceeded deforestation in eight of nine jurisdictions; reference levels diverged from the UNFCCC comparators by 0.4× to 3.9×, in directions consistent with the scope of each AD × EF submission. Map and calibration errors combined to jurisdictional uncertainties of ±2.9% to ±9.1% (95% confidence interval) against ±9% to ±25% in the submissions. Across the whole landscape, gross gains offset 62% of gross emissions over the recent window, and Kenya and Colombia were net biomass sinks.

title: Percutaneous Cryoablation in Bone Tumors: Current Applications, Technical Considerations, Clinical Outcomes, and Future Perspectives
summary: Image-guided percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as an increasingly important minimally invasive treatment option in musculoskeletal oncology. Its applications range from the definitive treatment of selected benign bone tumors to local tu
content: Image-guided percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as an increasingly important minimally invasive treatment option in musculoskeletal oncology. Its applications range from the definitive treatment of selected benign bone tumors to local tumor control and pain palliation in patients with malignant primary bone lesions and skeletal metastases. Compared with heat-based ablation techniques, cryoablation offers several potential advantages, including visualization of the ice ball during treatment, the ability to create large and irregular ablation zones, and reduced procedural pain. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the principles, technical considerations, clinical applications, efficacy, and complications of percutaneous cryoablation in the management of bone tumors, emphasizing its current role and future perspectives in musculoskeletal interventional oncology. Relevant publications addressing the use of image-guided cryoablation in benign and malignant bone tumors were reviewed, including clinical studies, prospective trials, retrospective series, systematic reviews, and international recommendations. Particular attention was given to treatment indications, procedural techniques, local tumor control, pain reduction, and complication prevention. Cryoablation has demonstrated favorable clinical outcomes in selected benign bone tumors, particularly osteoid osteoma, and in patients with painful skeletal metastases. Its role in locally aggressive benign tumors, oligometastatic disease, and selected recurrent malignant bone tumors is expanding. The ability to monitor the ice ball in real time facilitates treatment planning and protection of adjacent critical structures. However, pathological fractures, neural injuries, and incomplete tumor coverage remain important considerations. Percutaneous cryoablation represents a valuable addition to multidisciplinary bone tumor management. Appropriate patient selection, accurate imaging guidance, adequate ablation margins, and systematic protection of adjacent structures are essential for achieving optimal outcomes. Further prospective comparative studies are required to establish its long-term oncological efficacy and define its role relative to surgery and other ablative techniques.

title: When and where do forest carbon sinks respond to rocky desertification control? Insights from the Yunnan–Guangxi–Guizhou karst region in southwest China
summary: Revealing the spatiotemporal response patterns of forest carbon sinks to rocky desertification control is important for evaluating the effectiveness of ecological engineering and understanding carbon cycling mechanisms. This study focuses o
content: Revealing the spatiotemporal response patterns of forest carbon sinks to rocky desertification control is important for evaluating the effectiveness of ecological engineering and understanding carbon cycling mechanisms. This study focuses on the Yunnan–Guangxi–Guizhou Rocky Desertification (YGGRD) area by employing a comprehensive analytical framework integrating Theil–Sen Median and Mann–Kendall trend analysis, Breaks For Additive Seasonal and Trend (BFAST), and random forest–SHAP modeling. This approach identifies structural changes, spatial heterogeneity, and factors associated with forest carbon sink dynamics. The results reveal that between 2001 and 2020, the YGGRD area experienced a significant reduction in rocky desertification and a continuous increase in its forest carbon sinks, with both exhibiting spatially coordinated improvement. Forest carbon sinks predominantly exhibited monotonic increases, with BFAST-detected structural changes affecting less than 3% of the study area. These changes were temporally concentrated during 2008–2012, indicating a distinct temporal pattern in forest carbon sink dynamics. The YGGRD region is divided into a synchronous response zone, non-synchronous response zone, uncoupled response zone, and no-detectable-response zone, accounting for 19.84%, 22.63%, 27.91%, and 29.62% of the total area, respectively. Random forest and SHAP analyses further revealed differentiated driver structures across the four response zones: temperature and vegetation restoration were more prominent in the synchronous response zone; topography and moisture were more influential in the non-synchronous response zone; climatic factors were more prominent in the uncoupled response zone; and anthropogenic disturbance and ecological fragility were more prominent in the no-detectable-response zone. This study reveals the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of forest carbon sink dynamics under changing rocky desertification conditions, providing analytical insights for evaluating the benefits of degraded ecosystem restoration and carbon sink governance.

title: VISIT-4type v1.0: Forest age structure, wood harvest and land-cover transitions in a dynamic global vegetation model
summary: In dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs), representing land-use change solely through net changes in land-cover fractions can obscure forest disturbance histories and associated carbon transfers. Here we describe VISIT-4type (v1.0), whic
content: In dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs), representing land-use change solely through net changes in land-cover fractions can obscure forest disturbance histories and associated carbon transfers. Here we describe VISIT-4type (v1.0), which extends the two-type framework of the Vegetation Integrative SImulator for Trace gases (VISIT) to primary forest, secondary forest, cropland and other natural vegetation. Both forest types are resolved into six age cohorts; a transition ledger transfers carbon with changing area; wood harvest follows Land-Use Harmonization 2 (LUH2) area requests with separate fuelwood and industrial-wood pathways; and secondary-forest leaf traits are derived from the TRY database. Six model configurations under common environmental forcing are compared to quantify the contributions of these developments to differences in simulated net biome productivity (NBP) over 1850–2019. Against eddy-covariance observations, VISIT-4type reduced the per-site root-mean-square error (RMSE) of annual gross primary production (GPP), net ecosystem exchange (NEE) and ecosystem respiration at 64 %, 74 % and 74 % of forest sites (p ≤ 0.015); the median RMSE decreased from 615 to 565, 303 to 286 and 499 to 434 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹, without significant changes in correlation. Against FLUXCOM X-BASE (2001–2019), the area-weighted mean RMSE of monthly GPP and NEE decreased by 0.42 and 0.25 g C m⁻² month⁻¹, with lower errors over 46.7 % and 56.1 % of the evaluated land, concentrated in grid cells with a history of wood harvest or forest clearing. Harvested stem carbon was 44–61 % of LUH2 wood-harvest biomass, reflecting lower simulated carbon density in harvested primary forest and in the young secondary forests that dominate the harvest requests. Over 1850–2019, global mean NBP was 0.173 Pg C yr⁻¹ lower in VISIT-4type than in VISIT-2type. Wood harvest with forest age structure accounted for −0.171 Pg C yr⁻¹ of this difference, whereas land-cover structure and transitions contributed +0.026 Pg C yr⁻¹ and secondary-forest traits −0.027 Pg C yr⁻¹. Relative to 1850, the 2019 ecosystem carbon-stock difference between the two versions (−81.2 Pg C) was about 52 Pg C more negative than the cumulative NBP difference over 1851–2019 (−29.2 Pg C). About 45 Pg C of this gap arises because abandoned cropland in VISIT-2type inherits the per-area carbon of natural vegetation without a corresponding uptake flux, which are not included in its ecosystem stock. These results show that disturbed-stand carbon density and the end use of harvested wood are key controls on simulated land-use effects, and that flux evaluation needs to be complemented by forest observations that resolve stand age and successional stage.

title: Enabling Genotyping of Low-Biomass Zebra Mussel Samples via Multi-Displacement Amplification (MDA)
summary: Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)-based genotyping enables population genomic studies of the history of biological invasions, allowing for inference of source populations and routes of spread. Methods for genotyping include whole genome sequ
content: Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)-based genotyping enables population genomic studies of the history of biological invasions, allowing for inference of source populations and routes of spread. Methods for genotyping include whole genome sequencing (WGS), as well as lower-cost targeted approaches, such as microarrays, hybrid capture, or Genotyping by Sequencing (GBS). Using GBS, we previously genotyped ~2,000 adult zebra mussels collected from over 100 populations across Minnesota, the Great Lakes, and the Upper Mississippi River. The need for sufficient template DNA restricts such genotyping approaches to adult animals, while genotyping lower biomass samples, such as zebra mussel veliger larvae remains challenging. Here, we applied Multiple Displacement Amplification (MDA) to increase DNA concentration from low-biomass samples. We demonstrate that MDA yields reproducible WGS and GBS data from as little as 1 ng of starting material and genotyped single veliger larvae from MDA amplified DNA, accurately assigning them to their known source populations. Furthermore, we showed that inheritance patterns can be tracked in MDA amplified DNA from veliger larvae and demonstrated an approach for forensic genetics of juvenile zebra mussels that were found contaminating "moss balls" and sold in the aquarium pet trade. Pairing MDA with high-resolution genomic workflows overcomes biomass limitations and represents a powerful toolkit to enhance early detection, trace invasion pathways, and mitigate the spread of the invasive zebra mussel. This approach is readily generalizable to other organisms or developmental stages where limiting quantities of DNA are available.

title: Convergence, Strain, and Cross-Scale Kinetic Energy Flux at Submesoscale Fronts in the California Current System
summary: Submesoscale fronts are thought to route kinetic energy (KE) from the mesoscale toward dissipative scales, but several kinematic quantities, in particular horizontal convergence and strain, can control the direction and magnitude of that tr
content: Submesoscale fronts are thought to route kinetic energy (KE) from the mesoscale toward dissipative scales, but several kinematic quantities, in particular horizontal convergence and strain, can control the direction and magnitude of that transfer, and their relative roles remain unconstrained by observations. We estimate the cross-scale horizontal KE flux at submesoscale fronts in the California Current System using an array of four Saildrones with downward-looking ADCPs and concurrent DopplerScatt airborne surface velocity maps collected during the NASA S-MODE IOP-1 campaign. We first show that coarse-graining KE flux estimates obtained with uniform, Hann, and Gaussian kernels converge to a common profile once their e-folding energy cutoff wavenumbers are aligned, and we validate the full multi-method framework against a two-layer quasi-geostrophic model. Applied to the observations, both the Saildrone array and DopplerScatt independently show forward KE flux at scales below approximately 30\,km and inverse KE flux at larger scales. The forward flux is surfaceintensified within the mixed layer, with a localized flux reversal near the mixed-layer base that coincides with a sign change in the fine-scale-KE-weighted divergence. At the smallest resolved scales, divergence predicts the sign of the KE flux and strain modulates its magnitude, while at larger scales the strain contribution dominates the inverse flux. Both convergence and deformation contribute comparably to the frontogenetic tendency. Individual front crossings show the forward KE flux and the frontogenetic tendency spatially locked to the surface convergent zone.

title: Lead Shot in Soils at Battlefields from the 17th and 18th Centuries
source: Soil and Sediment Contamination An International Journal
summary: Effects of prolonged contact between soil and lead shots at 17th and 18th century battlefields in the southeast part of Norway have been investigated. Sampled shots were found in soil at main target areas by means of historical records and
content: Effects of prolonged contact between soil and lead shots at 17th and 18th century battlefields in the southeast part of Norway have been investigated. Sampled shots were found in soil at main target areas by means of historical records and metal detectors. The results show that the shots are almost intact after approximately 300–350 years in the soil. Corrosion crusts seem to protect the shot from extensive weathering. An X-ray diffractometry analysis indicates that the crusts are composed of cerussite, massicot/litharge, hydrocerussite, and anglesite in order of appearance. Down to some tens of centimeters below the shot, the lead content in the soil is elevated. On the basis of analyses of soil chemistry and mineralogy, it is suggested that lead retention by iron oxides and amorphous or poorly ordered carbonates dominates in these soils. At some sites, lead may also be present as phosphates and sulfates. From an environmental point of view, there is a theoretical risk that soluble lead could be transported to groundwater if the shot is situated directly upon the bedrock or in very thin soil covers. In the case when the shot is buried in thicker soil with a deeper groundwater table, there is a low risk of lead contamination of groundwater.

title: Shedding Light on Autophagy: Autophagy–Light Signalling Crosstalk Shaping Growth and Metabolism
summary: Light is both an energy source and a regulatory signal that shapes plant development, metabolism and environmental acclimation. Autophagy, a conserved degradation and recycling pathway, maintains cellular homoeostasis by reallocating resour
content: Light is both an energy source and a regulatory signal that shapes plant development, metabolism and environmental acclimation. Autophagy, a conserved degradation and recycling pathway, maintains cellular homoeostasis by reallocating resources and removing damaged components. Although these processes have often been studied separately, emerging evidence reveals that light signalling and autophagy are mechanistically intertwined. In this review, we examine how spectral cues, circadian timing, photodamage and metabolic status converge on autophagy to balance growth with cellular recycling. We highlight transcriptional and epigenetic control of ATG genes, metabolic regulation via the TOR-SnRK1 axis, selective autophagic turnover of light-signalling regulators and organelle quality-control pathways that remove damaged chloroplasts, peroxisomes and mitochondria. We further discuss how this interface contributes to darkness-associated carbon remobilisation, senescence-linked nitrogen recycling, lipophagy and possible connection with specialised metabolism. Finally, we highlight conceptual and technical gaps and propose experimental strategies, including spectral manipulation, autophagy reporters, phosphoproteomics and optogenetic approaches, to dissect the light-autophagy interface. By consolidating these insights, we provide a blueprint for testing how interactions between light signalling and autophagy affect plant stress resilience and metabolic output, and whether they contribute to developmental plasticity.

title: Formate and Acetate: A Challenging Case for Microdroplet Chemistry
summary: Recent studies reported the spontaneous formation of formate and acetate in water microdroplet sprays when exposed to CO2 gas with micromolar yields over timescales of less than seconds. Here, we used in situ Raman spectroscopy of single, o
content: Recent studies reported the spontaneous formation of formate and acetate in water microdroplet sprays when exposed to CO2 gas with micromolar yields over timescales of less than seconds. Here, we used in situ Raman spectroscopy of single, optically-trapped water droplets in CO2 gas to investigate whether this unconventional droplet reaction enables product formation on timescales longer than seconds, thus increasing the product yields to amounts potentially providing a competitive green synthesis pathway. The results show that product formation by this droplet reaction does not occur beyond the short timescales reported previously. The present study reveals that single droplets act as extremely sensitive and fast detectors for trace gas amounts of these acids down to the level of parts per trillion. In situ single-droplet Raman spectroscopy offers a fast, sensitive platform for trace gas detection of soluble acids or bases. Single-droplet studies are crucial to advance our knowledge of unusual microdroplet reactivity.

title: Nanozyme-activated microspheres modulate inflammation and angiogenesis for functional skeletal muscle regeneration
summary: The failure of skeletal muscle regeneration after volumetric muscle loss (VML) is primarily due to the impaired intrinsic regenerative capacity, a deteriorative oxidative stress microenvironment, and inadequate vascular network formation. I
content: The failure of skeletal muscle regeneration after volumetric muscle loss (VML) is primarily due to the impaired intrinsic regenerative capacity, a deteriorative oxidative stress microenvironment, and inadequate vascular network formation. In this study, we introduced a multifunctional hydrogel microsphere with myogenic, antioxidant, and pro-angiogenic properties to facilitate vascularized skeletal muscle regeneration following VML. The pro-angiogenic K 2 (SL) 6 K 2 peptide was modified with a terminal thiol group to form K 2 (SL) 6 K 2 -SH (KS) and covalently conjugated to gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) via a thiol-Michael addition reaction. Subsequently, platinum (Pt) and copper (Cu) nanoparticles were incorporated into the microspheres (GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu). In vitro , the GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu microspheres exhibited excellent biocompatibility, potent antioxidant activity, effective antibacterial function, and a robust pro-angiogenic capability. GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu microspheres significantly facilitated myogenic differentiation, enhanced the expression of intracellular antioxidant enzymes, and improved mitochondrial energy metabolism via the involvement of the NRF2 signaling pathway. In vivo , GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu microspheres were implanted in a murine tibialis anterior VML model. Four weeks post-injury, treatment with GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu microspheres effectively promoted the formation of mature myofibers, reduced fibrotic collagen deposition, and modulated the polarization of M1/M2 macrophages. Notably, a dense vascular network, prominent axonal sprouting, and acetylcholine receptor clustering were observed at the injury site of GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu-treated mice, accompanied by superior exercise performance including grip strength, running distance, and muscle force. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the therapeutic potential of GelMA-KS@Pt/Cu microspheres in cooperatively promoting vascularized skeletal muscle regeneration and facilitating early structural neural repair following VML.

title: A Precision Management Framework for Water-Nitrogen in Watermelon
source: Advances in biological sciences research/Advances in Biological Sciences Research
summary: While substantial research has been conducted on irrigation and fertilization technologies for watermelon, there is still no systematic framework that integrates stage-specific water and nitrogen demand, water-nitrogen interactions, and ful
content: While substantial research has been conducted on irrigation and fertilization technologies for watermelon, there is still no systematic framework that integrates stage-specific water and nitrogen demand, water-nitrogen interactions, and full-growth-cycle operational rules. Most existing studies only carry out multi-factor analyses and have not yet established a unified decision-making logic. To address this research gap, this paper summarizes watermelon’s stage-specific water and nitrogen demand characteristics and their physiological basis; compares the principles and applicability of response surface methodology, TOPSIS, and crop models (DSSAT, APSIM) for quantifying water–nitrogen coupling effects; analyzes how such coupling regulates plant physiological traits; and reviews advances in related regulatory measures. Based on this, we propose a precision management framework that uses stage-specific demand as the diagnostic benchmark, quantified coupling effects as the evaluation criterion for management schemes, physiological regulatory mechanisms as the scientific foundation, and regulatory technologies as the implementation pathway. Developed from watermelon’s physiological needs across growth stages, this framework provides a theoretical basis for precision water and nitrogen management.

title: Mágneses baktériumok sejten belüli zárványai és lehetséges geokémiai szerepük
summary: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) are able to sense the Earth’s magnetic field direction through chains of membrane-bound iron oxide or iron sulfide minerals, known as magnetosomes. By aligning and migrating along these magnetic field lines, the
content: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) are able to sense the Earth’s magnetic field direction through chains of membrane-bound iron oxide or iron sulfide minerals, known as magnetosomes. By aligning and migrating along these magnetic field lines, the cells are able to locate their position within optimal oxygen gradients in aquatic environments. Although the pres­ence of magnetic nanocrystals is their most distinctive characteristic, MTB may also contain intracellular granules of polyphosphate (polyP), elemental sulfur (S), and amorphous calcium carbonate (ACC). MTB-containing samples collected from Kinizsi-spring, near Nagyvázsony in autumn, winter and spring were studied using transmission electron microscopy. We investigated both the freshly collected samples and the changes that occurred over time during laboratory storage. Regarding the fresh samples, our primary aim was to obtain a preliminary overview of the cell types and their intra­cellular inclusions. It was observed that the type of inclusion – present within a given cell type – was associated with other cellular characteristics, whereas the occurrence of inclusions varied with season. These findings suggest that inclu­sion type is under genetic control but is simultaneously influenced by environmental conditions. As magnetotactic bacte­ria (MTB) continuously migrate between microoxic and anoxic zones, their polyphosphate (polyP) and elemental sulfur (S) inclusions may play an important role in the biogeochemical cycling of phosphorus and sulfur, and in shaping their distribution within aquatic environments. In the laboratory-stored samples, shifts in the dominance of different MTB cell types were observed after several months. To analyze temporal patterns in greater detail, the winter sample was divided into four equal subsamples and examined monthly over a three-month period. Over time, the dominant cell type changed within each microcosm and polyphosphate (polyP)-containing cell types generally became predominant. Electron tomography was performed on three coccoid cells, enabling the three-dimensional assessment of the spatial arrangement of intra­cellular inclusions. The distribution of inclusions was consistent with a balanced mass distribution within the cell and may facilitate swimming along magnetically guided trajectories. Some coccoid cell types contained extremely large polyP inclusions relative to their cell size. These observations highlight the potential of MTB for technological applications, particularly in the removal of phosphorus from aqueous solutions.

title: Root-Zone Conditions and Fruit Performance of Greenhouse Melon Under Nine Fertigation-Volume and Subtrate Combinations
summary: Substrate-hydroponic melon production requires coordinated irrigation and growing-medium management. This study compared nine combinations of field-capacity-derived daily nutrient-solution volume (100%, 75%, or 50% of the medium-specific no
content: Substrate-hydroponic melon production requires coordinated irrigation and growing-medium management. This study compared nine combinations of field-capacity-derived daily nutrient-solution volume (100%, 75%, or 50% of the medium-specific nominal dose) and substrate (cocopeat, rice-husk charcoal, or their 1:1 w/w mixture) in greenhouse-grown ‘Sweet Lavender’ melon. A completely randomized design comprised three independent units per combination (27 units); plant subsamples were averaged within units. Daily doses were divided equally between morning and afternoon. Substrate temperature and moisture were recorded at 05:00 and 13:00 on five dates. One-way ANOVA, Tukey HSD, exploratory Pearson correlations, and moisture permutation sensitivity tests were applied. At 42 days after transplanting (DAT), 13:00 substrate temperature reached 29.50 °C in P5 and P8 versus 26.67 °C in P1 and P7. Stem diameter at 28 DAT (p = 0.034) and root volume (p = 0.045) had significant omnibus ANOVAs but no significant Tukey pairs. Mean fruit weight ranged from 881.67 g plant⁻¹ in P8 to 1165.00 g plant⁻¹ in P1; numerical maximum total soluble solids was 14.50 °Brix in P4, P6, and P9. Moisture contrasts persisted in omnibus rank-permutation tests, but the restored Takemura DM-15 readings represent a 1–8 index, not calibrated percentage water content. No combination was superior for all traits. Interpretation remains limited by three replicates, uncalibrated moisture indices, and confounded water and nutrient delivery.

title: Enhanced Biohydrogen Production from Microalgal Biomass Through Methane Suppression in Sulfate-Reducing Bacteria-Based Bioelectrochemical Systems
summary: Bioelectrochemical systems offer a promising approach for improving biohydrogen yields. The integration of microalgal biomass in bioelectrochemical systems supports resource recovery and clean energy generation, while additives such as acti
content: Bioelectrochemical systems offer a promising approach for improving biohydrogen yields. The integration of microalgal biomass in bioelectrochemical systems supports resource recovery and clean energy generation, while additives such as activated carbon and iron may improve hydrogen production by modifying the reaction environment. However, the coexistence of methanogens and sulfate-reducing bacteria in bioelectrochemical systems can lead to substrate competition and reduce hydrogen productivity. Therefore, in the present study, the effects of activated carbon and iron on hydrogen production and methane suppression in a sulfate-reducing bacteria-based bioelectrochemical system using spent microalgal hydrolysate as feedstock were investigated. Activated carbon and iron enhanced hydrogen yields by up to 1.46-fold relative to controls fed with spent microalgal hydrolysate and completely suppressed methane after 18 cycles of bioreactor operation. Volatile fatty acid profiles revealed that the predominance of acetic acid was associated with reduced methanogenic activity. Furthermore, butyric acid was minimal, indicating a metabolic shift towards acetic-dominated pathways that favour hydrogen production by sulfate-reducing bacteria. Principal component analysis revealed significant differences in hydrogen and volatile fatty acid profiles, indicating differences in the microbial communities adapted to bioelectrochemical systems and the control bioreactor. The coefficients of the various kinetic models also confirmed the best fit for cumulative hydrogen production (R 2 =0.99). These findings support sustainable biohydrogen production from spent microalgal biomass hydrolysate using bioelectrochemical systems, with material supplements that improve hydrogen yields and suppress methane production. However, additional inputs, such as inhibitor removal, are required to achieve much higher H 2 productivity from spent microalgal biomass.

title: Modelling an Integrated Waste-to-Energy PPP for Jamaica
summary: Jamaica's municipal solid-waste system presents a linked development challenge. The country generates approximately 1.5 million tonnes of solid waste each year, but disposal continues to depend heavily on open dumps rather than fully engine
content: Jamaica's municipal solid-waste system presents a linked development challenge. The country generates approximately 1.5 million tonnes of solid waste each year, but disposal continues to depend heavily on open dumps rather than fully engineered sanitary landfills. The Riverton City and Retirement legacy disposal sites, located in St. Andrew and St. James, respectively, have long outlived their design lives and experience recurrent fires, smoke and odour. Together with collection constraints, low levels of separation and recycling, and the absence of a modern residue-management system, these conditions impose environmental, health and productivity costs. The 2022 national waste-characterisation study also found that organics account for about 39.7% of the municipal waste stream, followed by plastics, cardboard, paper and other materials (Development Bank of Jamaica [DBJ], 2022). The Auditor General's Department (2022) separately identified persistent weaknesses in the regulation, coordination, collection and disposal functions of the National Solid Waste Management Authority (NSWMA).

title: Investigating Non-Newtonian Hybrid Nanofluid Impact on a Heated Oscillating Cylinder Free Convection in a Trapezoidal Cavity
summary: Because of its many industrial uses, inquiry of natural convective heat transfer in enclosures has long garnered significant intreset. By computationally analyzing the combined impact of heated ocillated cylinder inside a trapezoidal cavity
content: Because of its many industrial uses, inquiry of natural convective heat transfer in enclosures has long garnered significant intreset. By computationally analyzing the combined impact of heated ocillated cylinder inside a trapezoidal cavity and the non-Newtonian rheology of a Cu-Al2O3 hybrid nanofluid on NCHT, the current work sets itself apart from earlier studies. The effects of the Rayleigh number 103≤Ra≤106, the oscillation amplitude of the heated cylinder 0.05h≤A≤0.3h , and the power-law index 0.7≤n≤1.3 on the average Nusselt number, Nuavg are examined using a finite-element numerical scheme.The outcomes indicate that increasing the oscillation amplitude from 0.05h to 0.3h, under conditions of Ra=105 and n=0.7, enhances the time-averaged mean Nusselt number by 28%. Moreover, the improvement in the time-averaged Nusselt number resulting from increasing the Rayleigh number from 103 to 106 is 25% greater at n=0.7 compared to the case with n=1.3.

title: A Diode-Less Inductor-Less Compact Nine-Level Switched-Capacitor Inverter with Low Total Standing Voltage Reduced Switch Rating and Inherent Inrush Current Limitation
summary: This paper proposes a novel switched-capacitor-based nine-level inverter topology with a voltage-doubling gain. The proposed structure employs eleven switches and zero diodes to generate multilevel output voltages with boosting capability,
content: This paper proposes a novel switched-capacitor-based nine-level inverter topology with a voltage-doubling gain. The proposed structure employs eleven switches and zero diodes to generate multilevel output voltages with boosting capability, while ensuring low voltage ripple and limited semiconductor voltage stress. Specifically, the maximum blocking voltage (MBV) of each switch is limited to 0.5Vmax, and the total standing voltage (TSV) is restricted to 4.5Vmax, which significantly reduces the cost and rating of the switches. By establishing fully independent charging paths and adopting a proper charging sequence, this configuration provides inherent soft-charging for the repetitive post-LDP capacitor recharging process during steady-state operation, without requiring limiting inductors or auxiliary resistors. A level-shifted modulation strategy is adopted, resulting in short and non-repetitive longest discharging periods (LDPs); capacitor C2 experiences LDPs only over two consecutive levels, while C1 undergoes an LDP at only a single level. This non-repetitive LDP sequence, together with decoupled charging loops, enables inherent voltage self-balancing without sensors or auxiliary control circuits, leading to reduced capacitance requirements and a compact overall volume. Furthermore, the topology provides a structurally scalable extension path for higher voltage levels. Analytical comparisons and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed inverter in terms of reduced component count, lower voltage stress, high efficiency, and reliable operation under various load conditions.

title: Effect of Band Gap, Absorber Layer Type, and Ga/(Ga+In) (R1C1) Ratio Variation on Thin-Film CIGS Solar Cell Efficiency
summary: Thin-film Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) solar cells are highly promising for next-generation photovoltaics due to their tunable bandgap, high absorption coefficient, and long-term stability. However, achieving maximum power conversion efficiency requ
tags: Copper indium gallium selenide solar cells
content: Thin-film Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) solar cells are highly promising for next-generation photovoltaics due to their tunable bandgap, high absorption coefficient, and long-term stability. However, achieving maximum power conversion efficiency requires complex, simultaneous optimization of material and structural parameters. Specifically, the ratio of gallium to the sum of gallium and indium, along with the absorber-layer thickness, remains critical for balancing open-circuit voltage (Voc) and short-circuit current density (Jsc). Unlike conventional approaches that rely on independent parametric sweeps, this work introduces an integrated multi-parameter optimization framework. By coupling Silvaco ATLAS device simulations with the Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO) algorithm, we simultaneously optimize the gallium content, absorber and buffer-layer thicknesses, and bandgap profiles within a unified search space. Simulation results demonstrate that, under ideal conditions with minimized non-radiative recombination, a gallium-to-total-gallium-plus-indium ratio of 0.60–0.63, paired with an absorber thickness of 4–4.5 μm, achieves a theoretical efficiency of 28.43%. This optimized configuration provides a superior trade-off between bandgap widening and photon absorption. Comparative analysis with experimental high-efficiency devices confirms the feasibility of these parameters within current fabrication windows. These findings highlight that systematic multi-parameter optimization is a powerful strategy for advancing the performance of CIGS solar cells toward their theoretical limits.
