title: Control of PMSG for a hydroelectric power factory using adaptive sliding mode control with disturbances
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: This study, calculates, and controls an electric drive system for a hydroelectric generator based on the adaptive sliding mode control (European Green Hydrogen Acceleration Center (EHGASC)) method, with a permanent magnet synchronous genera
content: This study, calculates, and controls an electric drive system for a hydroelectric generator based on the adaptive sliding mode control (European Green Hydrogen Acceleration Center (EHGASC)) method, with a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG). Here, an integral sliding mode combined with an adaptive law is designed to demonstrate how a fast control response achieves greater convergence than conventional control. An adaptive law is developed to enable the control parameters, especially the switching process, to be quickly and automatically updated online. Therefore, the disturbance affecting the controller can be effectively reduced, and noise, chattering, and nonlinear disturbances can be eliminated using the Sat(.) function for the system. Thus, a perfect control model is created, and the quality of high-speed and low-speed control, as well as angular position control, is consistently satisfactory. The EHGASC system used for the PMSG generator, as proposed by the authors in this paper, demonstrates the advantages of adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC) based on a model. The simulation results presented in the paper show faster performance and more accurate control compared to other control methods. This also forms the basis for the development, design, fabrication, establishment of intelligent controller algorithms for future hydropower plants.

title: PRIORITY AREAS AND MECHANISMS FOR ENHANCING THE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF ATTRACTING FOREIGN INVESTMENT TO UZBEKISTAN IN THE CONTEXT OF TRANSITIONING TO A GREEN ECONOMY
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This article examines the priority areas for attracting foreign investment to Uzbekistan in the context of the transition to a green economy, as well as mechanisms for improving its economic efficiency. It analyzes the role of foreign inves
content: This article examines the priority areas for attracting foreign investment to Uzbekistan in the context of the transition to a green economy, as well as mechanisms for improving its economic efficiency. It analyzes the role of foreign investment in the national economy, the sectoral and geographical structure of investment flows, and trends in capital investment directed towards renewable energy sources. Furthermore, the article identifies promising areas for attracting foreign investment, including energy storage systems, electricity grid infrastructure, industrial decarbonization, efficient water resource management, and the development of environmental technologies. Based on the research findings, a five-component mechanism aimed at enhancing the economic, environmental, and technological efficiency of green foreign investment is proposed. The article also develops scientific and practical recommendations for evaluating and monitoring investment projects. Keywords: green economy, foreign investment, foreign direct investment, investment efficiency, renewable energy sources, green finance, energy efficiency

title: The persistence of groundwater depletion in the United States across widely ranging futures
summary: Groundwater resources are essential for crop production, enabling irrigation in many arid regions of the world. With a growing dependence on groundwater to serve increasing crop demands, concerns have been raised regarding alarming rates of
content: Groundwater resources are essential for crop production, enabling irrigation in many arid regions of the world. With a growing dependence on groundwater to serve increasing crop demands, concerns have been raised regarding alarming rates of groundwater depletion at the global scale. Modeling efforts focused on projecting future groundwater depletion have been limited by key factors: exogenous assumptions of human demand for groundwater that are unresponsive to changing groundwater availability and cost, simplistic treatment of the physics of groundwater depletion, narrow application to localized contexts, and limited exploration of future uncertainties. To address these gaps, we introduce a coupled human-natural modeling approach that links a positive mathematical programming (PMP) representation of farmer crop choice and irrigation decisions with an analytic, Theis-based groundwater cost-curve model. The two components interact annually: farmer groundwater extraction drives aquifer drawdown and rising pumping costs, which in turn condition the farmers’ following year cropping and irrigation decisions. The approach enables process-rich, broad exploration of groundwater depletion futures, initially deployed for ~35,000 farm-groundwater systems across the major aquifers of the continental United States. Our results indicate persistent groundwater depletion across a range of hydrologic-economic futures, with many of the key agricultural regions of the U.S. encountering substantial depletion even in the absence of adverse hydrologic or economic change.

title: Cross-correlating blade-wake dynamics for a model wind turbine
summary: Understanding how wakes interact with wind turbine blades under varying operating and inflow conditions is essential for improving fatigue prediction and performance assessment in increasingly dense wind farms. We present an experimental in
content: Understanding how wakes interact with wind turbine blades under varying operating and inflow conditions is essential for improving fatigue prediction and performance assessment in increasingly dense wind farms. We present an experimental investigation of wake-blade coupling in a model wind turbine, focusing on the role of tip-speed ratio, λ , under varying free-stream turbulence conditions. Spatially resolved wake velocity measurements are acquired concurrently with distributed blade strain measurements using Rayleigh backscattering fibre-optic sensing, enabling direct, time-synchronised analysis of fluid-structure interaction across the blade’s span. The blades’ strain dynamics are strongly governed by λ , where variations of the operating condition of the turbine modify the amplitude, coherence, and the temporal/spectral organisation of the blade’s structural dynamics, while free-stream turbulence primarily modulates these responses. Instantaneous joint statistics reveal negligible zero-lag dependence between wake velocity and blade strain, motivating a lagged and frequency-resolved analysis. Cycle-averaged cross-correlation and cross-power spectral density analyses demonstrate that wake-induced blade response is spatially localised within the wake shear layers and organised around rotation-coherent frequencies, with the correlated energy peaking at intermediate downstream locations. These results highlight the dominant role of operating condition in shaping wake-mediated blade loading and demonstrate the value of concurrent, spatially resolved flow-structure measurements for resolving blade-exciting flow dynamics in wind-turbine wakes.

title: Twistronic control of shift current in multilayer moiré systems
summary: The bulk photovoltaic effect in non-centrosymmetric materials provides an alternative mechanism for the conversion of light into a current response compared to p-n junctions. Among its various contributions, the shift current is particularl
content: The bulk photovoltaic effect in non-centrosymmetric materials provides an alternative mechanism for the conversion of light into a current response compared to p-n junctions. Among its various contributions, the shift current is particularly attractive because it is governed by the geometric properties of electronic wavefunctions and can generate large photocurrents in low-dimensional materials. Here, we investigate the evolution of the shift current response in mono-, bi-, and trilayer H-MoS2, as well as in twisted moiré bilayers and trilayers. To describe large moiré supercells we develop a Slater-Koster tight-binding model parametrized from first-principles calculations. The resulting electronic structures and shift-current responses are compared with density functional theory calculations and Wannier-interpolated results to verify the accuracy of the approach. The model accurately reproduces the electronic structure near the band edges and captures the main spectral features of the shift current conductivity. We show that twisting breaks the crystal symmetry and activates additional conductivity tensor components that are forbidden in untwisted structures, leading to new tunable in-plane photocurrent components. Analysis of the shift distance reveals a direct connection between the twist-induced modification of the electronic wavefunctions and the increase of the nonlinear response. Our results establish the twist angle as an effective parameter for engineering shift current generation in multilayer transition-metal dichalcogenide base systems and demonstrate that tight-binding approaches provide a practical route for exploring nonlinear optical phenomena in large-scale moiré materials beyond the limits of conventional first-principles calculations.

title: Smart efficient control design for an electric delivery vehicle
source: Science and Technology for Energy Transition
summary: In the context of reducing energy consumption for transportation, a substantial contribution can be given by electric delivery vehicles. An energy-efficient thermal management system is essential, particularly for those vehicles where hot a
content: In the context of reducing energy consumption for transportation, a substantial contribution can be given by electric delivery vehicles. An energy-efficient thermal management system is essential, particularly for those vehicles where hot and cold freight boxes (food and beverages) have to managed. Within a French-German research project (Innovative Thermal Management Systems, InnoTherMS), aimed at reducing the energy consumption by 10% with respect to a baseline vehicle, a novel thermal management approach was developed. This strategy is based on the application of optimal control theory and the availability of predictive information coming from connected driver assistance systems. In this work, the developed strategy is presented and its simulation results are compared with a state-of-the-art approach, to assess the achievement of the project goals.

title: Tunable Magneto-Excitonic Coupling in an Alloyed van der Waals Antiferromagnet
summary: Unique coupling between magnetic order and photogenerated excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors offers a powerful mechanism for controlling light–matter interactions. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr, this coupling is except
content: Unique coupling between magnetic order and photogenerated excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors offers a powerful mechanism for controlling light–matter interactions. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr, this coupling is exceptionally strong and manifests distinctly in two coexisting excitonic states: the localized, Frenkel-like XA exciton and the more delocalized, Wannier–Mott-like XB exciton. Here, we reveal how chlorine incorporation reshapes the magneto-optical interplay in CrSBr1–xClx by modifying its electronic structure, excitonic properties, and magnetic interactions. Combining magneto-optical spectroscopy up to 85 T with quasiparticle self-consistent GW (QSGŴ) calculations on alloy supercells, we show that Cl insertion progressively localizes the excitonic wave functions and drives both states toward a more Frenkel-like regime, most pronounced for the Wannier–Mott-like XB. Our work connects exciton character to magneto-excitonic coupling and establishes compositional alloying as an effective strategy for engineering light–matter interactions in van der Waals magnetic semiconductors.

title: Ultra-high hydrostatic pressure combined with tea saponin micelles enhances naringin extraction from pomelo peel
summary: Pomelo peel is a citrus-processing by-product rich in naringin, a high-value bioactive flavonoid, but its dense tissue matrix and naringin’s limited aqueous solubility constrain efficient extraction. We therefore developed an aqueous proces
content: Pomelo peel is a citrus-processing by-product rich in naringin, a high-value bioactive flavonoid, but its dense tissue matrix and naringin’s limited aqueous solubility constrain efficient extraction. We therefore developed an aqueous process combining ultra-high hydrostatic pressure (UHHP) with tea saponin micelles to address both tissue disruption and solubilization. Conductor-like screening model for real solvents (COSMO-RS) calculations, followed by experimental screening, identified tea saponin as the most suitable candidate among the tested surfactants. Response surface methodology gave optimal conditions of 293 MPa, 80.8 mg/mL tea saponin, a liquid-to-solid ratio of 25 mL/g, three pressure cycles, and a holding time of 4.45 min per cycle. Under these conditions, mean naringin recovery and extraction yield reached 80.3% and 9.58 mg/g, respectively. In a laboratory-scale comparison with ethanol maceration and ultrasound- and microwave-assisted extraction, the UHHP–micellar process gave the highest yield and shorter treatment time, together with lower calculated energy use and CO 2 emissions within the laboratory-scale comparison. Scanning electron microscopy indicated marked disruption and increased porosity of the peel matrix, while Fourier transform infrared spectra showed no new major bands attributable to naringin degradation. Density functional theory calculations supported hydrogen-bonding and van der Waals interactions between naringin and the modeled tea saponin structure, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested pressure-induced micellar compaction and retention of naringin after decompression. The enhanced extraction performance is attributed to complementary contributions from tissue disruption, micellar solubilization, and noncovalent association. These findings provide a basis for further scale-up, downstream purification, and life-cycle evaluation of an aqueous route for recovering poorly soluble flavonoids from citrus-processing by-products.

title: Науковий круглий стіл «Розвиток інформаційних технологій»: Тези доповідей
summary: Збірник містить тези доповідей, представлені на науковому круглому столі «Розвиток інформаційних технологій». У доповідях розглянуто дослідження сучасних методів, алгоритмів та інформаційних технологій у різних сферах застосування. Видання
content: Збірник містить тези доповідей, представлені на науковому круглому столі «Розвиток інформаційних технологій». У доповідях розглянуто дослідження сучасних методів, алгоритмів та інформаційних технологій у різних сферах застосування. Видання призначене для науковців, викладачів, аспірантів, студентів і фахівців у галузі інформаційних технологій та суміжних напрямів.

title: Production and Antibacterial Activity of a Biosurfactant from Schizosaccharomyces pombe Grown on Waste Soybean Oil and Corn Steep Liquor
summary: Biosurfactants are microbially derived amphiphilic compounds with potential applications in environmental and industrial processes. This study evaluated biosurfactant production by the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe using waste soy
content: Biosurfactants are microbially derived amphiphilic compounds with potential applications in environmental and industrial processes. This study evaluated biosurfactant production by the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe using waste soybean oil and corn steep liquor as low-cost production substrates and assessed the antibacterial activity of the recovered extract against four selected bacterial isolates. The yeast was cultivated for 120 hours at 28°C and 150 rpm. The cell-free culture broth was acidified and extracted with ethyl acetate, followed by solvent partitioning and thin-layer chromatography (TLC). The surface-active properties and emulsification ability of the produced biosurfactants were evaluated using an oil-displacement assay and the emulsification index (E24), respectively, against vegetable, coconut, groundnut and olive oils. Antibacterial activity was evaluated by agar-well diffusion, and the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was estimated by broth serial dilution. The partially purified biosurfactant extract produced a 29 mm oil-displacement zone and E24 values ranging from 27.8% to 56.4%. TLC with iodine vapour indicated the presence of a lipid-containing fraction; this result was considered supportive of, but not sufficient to establish, a specific phospholipid structure. The extract produced measurable inhibition at 100 and 50 mg/mL against all four isolates, while inhibition remained detectable at 25 mg/mL for Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. The corresponding MIC was therefore 25 mg/mL for these two isolates under the assay conditions used. The findings provide preliminary evidence that S. pombe can produce a surface-active extract when grown on low-cost waste substrates. Further work with replicated experiments, standardised antimicrobial testing, quantitative yield determination, and chemical characterisation is required to confirm the composition, potency and application potential of the product.

title: Event-Triggered Collaborative Control Models for Microgrid Systems
source: Journal of Circuits Systems and Computers
summary: Time-triggered control approaches in microgrids rely on periodic communication between distributed controllers irrespective of system status, resulting in unnecessary communication overhead and increased energy consumption. In order to addr
content: Time-triggered control approaches in microgrids rely on periodic communication between distributed controllers irrespective of system status, resulting in unnecessary communication overhead and increased energy consumption. In order to address the drawbacks mentioned above, this research proposes the application of the Event-Triggered Collaborative Control Model (ET-CCM), which consists of RF-based event detection and FL-based collaborative learning. The RF classifier identifies critical operating conditions, such as voltage and frequency deviations, and allows for control actions, substantially minimizing unnecessary communications. Simultaneously, FL makes it possible for several microgrids to learn their global model through sharing of model parameters rather than operational data. The proposed ET-CCM is implemented and evaluated in the MATLAB environment under different operating scenarios involving renewable energy intermittency and load variations. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed model reduces communication load by approximately 30% while improving voltage regulation accuracy by about 20% compared with conventional time-triggered control. The Voltage Stability Index (VSI) increases from 0.45 to 0.38 (about 18% improvement), whereas the Frequency Regulation Error (FRE) declines from 3.5% to 2.5% (about 15% improvement). Thus, the results obtained confirm that the ET-CCM model offers improved communication efficiency, voltage and frequency regulation, increased stability and privacy-preserving collaborative control for interconnected microgrid systems.

title: A Novel Dual Interleaved Boost Converter Topology for Improved Efficiency and Dynamic Response
summary: This study proposes a Dual-Interleaved Boost Converter (DIBC) as an improvement over the conventional In-terleaved Boost Converter (IBC) to enhance voltage conversion capability and performance characteristics. The DIBC is built using a two
content: This study proposes a Dual-Interleaved Boost Converter (DIBC) as an improvement over the conventional In-terleaved Boost Converter (IBC) to enhance voltage conversion capability and performance characteristics. The DIBC is built using a two-level interleaved boost converter configuration arranged in a cascade. The per-formance of both topologies is evaluated using PSIM simulation with an input voltage of 18 V and a switching frequency of 20 kHz. The IBC is operated at a 50% duty cycle, while the DIBC uses a 70% duty cycle. The simu-lation results show that the IBC produces a steady-state output voltage of 36.00 V, while the DIBC reaches 199.97 V. Ripple analysis shows that the DIBC has an absolute output voltage of 1.030 V and a ripple current of 0.069 A, higher than the IBC's 0.241 V and 0.005 A, respectively. However, after normalizing to their respec-tive output values, the DIBC produces a ripple voltage of 0.517% and a ripple current of 0.51%, compared to 0.669% and 0.69% for the IBC. In terms of power, the IBC produces an input power of 44.00 W and an output power of 37.08 W with an efficiency of 84.27%, while the DIBC produces an input power of 2798.10 W and an output power of 2640.66 W with an efficiency of 94.37%. Transient response analysis shows that the DIBC reaches steady state in approximately 0.87 s, faster than the IBC which requires approximately 1.84 s under the test conditions used. These results indicate that the DIBC has high step-up voltage conversion capability, good normalized ripple characteristics, higher simulation efficiency, and faster steady-state response under the evaluated operating conditions. Further research is needed through non-ideal component modeling, varying operating conditions, and experimental validation to more comprehensively confirm the performance of the DIBC.

title: Analysis of IFOC-Based Sliding Mode Control with A Hyperbolic-Tangent Function for Low-Speed Induction Motor Control
summary: Compared to direct field-oriented and scalar control, indirect field-oriented control (IFOC) provides a more straightforward implementation for induction motor (IM) control. Nevertheless, IFOC control does not guarantee sufficient robustnes
content: Compared to direct field-oriented and scalar control, indirect field-oriented control (IFOC) provides a more straightforward implementation for induction motor (IM) control. Nevertheless, IFOC control does not guarantee sufficient robustness and stability, particularly at low-speed operations where the system tends to have a high steady-state error (SSE). This study explicitly addresses the issue of achieving robust and stable IM performance at low speeds using IFOC. The objective is to develop a control strategy that reduces SSE and overshoot in the rotor speed response while improving energy efficiency. To achieve this objective, sliding mode control (SMC) is augmented with a Lyapunov function to enhance robustness and stability. To minimize SSE and overshoot, a hyperbolic tangent function-based boundary layer is used. Simulation results show that under low-speed reference conditions, SSE is reduced by 1.96% in the no-load scenario and 1.92% in the loaded scenario, while overshoot is reduced by 29.93%. These improve-ments substantially reduce power consumption, including active power by 64.43%, reactive power by 40.92%, and apparent power by 53.48%. In addition, current consumption in the ABC architecture de-creased by 25.67% under no-load conditions and 22.62% under load. Nonetheless, although the boundary layer approach reduces power consumption, the robustness and stability of the system under load are not maintained under some conditions. The findings highlight the advantages and limitations of the proposed strategy and indicate the need for further research to optimize IM control.

title: Predicting Asymmetric Organocatalysis via Machine-Learning-Driven Molecular Dynamics of Chiral Deep Eutectic Solvents
summary: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) serve as sustainable, low-volatility, and bio-derived alternatives to conventional organic media, aligning with the demand for green chemical processes. Beyond their role as solvents, they offer transformative
content: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) serve as sustainable, low-volatility, and bio-derived alternatives to conventional organic media, aligning with the demand for green chemical processes. Beyond their role as solvents, they offer transformative potential as integrated catalytic platforms, yet the molecular determinants of their performance remain poorly understood. This study employs machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics combined with density functional theory to investigate the structure and dynamics of chiral deep eutectic solvents in asymmetric catalysis. Simulations reveal that overly persistent hydrogen-bond networks within DES components impede key reaction steps and intermediate formation, reducing efficiency. Conversely, more labile networks preserve molecular flexibility, facilitating substrate activation and enhancing conversion. Furthermore, these networks compete with interactions controlling substrate orientation, thus influencing stereocontrol. By connecting microscopic hydrogen-bond dynamics to macroscopic performance, this work provides atomistic insight into structure-reactivity relationships. The findings define a quantitative computational framework that uses hydrogen-bond descriptors to predict catalytic efficiency. This approach demonstrates the utility of artificial intelligence-driven methodologies for the accelerated optimization and rigorous benchmarking of catalytic systems, offering a mechanism-based strategy for the rational design of next-generation organocatalytic media.

title: Reassessing Maritime Law and Order Strategies in the Gulf of Aden: Are There Sustainable Policy Solutions?
source: International Journal for Crime Justice and Social Democracy
summary: The resurgence of piracy off the coast of Somalia indicates important limitations of counter-piracy strategies, which have prioritized militarized deterrence over addressing the root issues of modern-day piracy. These issues are ingrained i
content: The resurgence of piracy off the coast of Somalia indicates important limitations of counter-piracy strategies, which have prioritized militarized deterrence over addressing the root issues of modern-day piracy. These issues are ingrained in a legacy of colonial exploitation, Cold War geopolitics and environmental degradation. This analysis examines historical context, socio-economic factors and a critique of the dominant counter-piracy methods in place. Geospatial analysis of piracy reveals distinct patterns of nearshore attacks clustered around non-commercial ports and coastal communities, highlighting the local and opportunistic nature of piracy. Carceral approaches have failed to rehabilitate offenders, instead creating breeding grounds for extremism. A sustainable solution requires a development-focused strategy that strengthens governance and the rule of law, invests in economic infrastructure, protects Somali waters from illegal exploitation and implements effective justice programs.

title: Chitosan-lipoic acid conjugate as an adsorbent for dispersive solid-phase microextraction of Cd, Cu and Pb in infant formulas
summary: A dispersive solid-phase microextraction (d-SPME) method based on a newly synthesized chitosan-lipoic acid (Chts-Lipo) adsorbent was developed for the flame atomic absorption spectrometric (FAAS) determination of Cd, Cu, and Pb in baby food
content: A dispersive solid-phase microextraction (d-SPME) method based on a newly synthesized chitosan-lipoic acid (Chts-Lipo) adsorbent was developed for the flame atomic absorption spectrometric (FAAS) determination of Cd, Cu, and Pb in baby foodstuffs. The physicochemical properties of the Chts-Lipo adsorbent were characterized by SEM and infrared spectroscopy. The experimental variables influencing the d-SPME procedure were systematically investigated and optimized. The limits of detection were 0.15, 0.33, and 0.83 µg L − 1 for Cd, Cu, and Pb, respectively, whereas the linear working range extended from 0.5 to 400 µg L − 1 . The optimized method was validated using two standard reference materials, yielding recovery values between 90.1 and 97.2%. Subsequently, the method was applied to the analysis of sixteen different baby foodstuffs. The concentrations of Pb, Cd, and Cu ranged from 10.9 to 77.3, 3.2 to 35.7, and 62.5 to 388.0 µg kg − 1 , respectively. The environmental sustainability and practical applicability of the proposed method were assessed using the Analytical GREEnness metric (AGREE) and the Blue Applicability Grade Index (BAGI), resulting in scores of 0.67/1.00 and 67.5/100, respectively.

title: GTOpt: Open-Source Energy-System Optimization, Consistent from Minutes to Decades
summary: Planning and operating energy systems with high shares of variable renewables, storage and hydro requires models that remain consistent from daily dispatch to multi-decade expansion. This paper presents GTOpt, an open-source optimizer writt
content: Planning and operating energy systems with high shares of variable renewables, storage and hydro requires models that remain consistent from daily dispatch to multi-decade expansion. This paper presents GTOpt, an open-source optimizer written in C++26 for the expansion planning of generation, transmission, storage and demand, hydrothermal scheduling, and unit commitment and dispatch. The same formulation is used at every time scale, from 15-minute blocks to 30-year horizons. It covers DC power flow with Kirchhoff constraints and line losses, hydro cascades with water rights, batteries, unit commitment, reserves and inertia, multi-carrier chains (fuels, LNG, hydrogen, ammonia, heat) and multi-pollutant emission zones with caps and allowance banking. The time scales are coupled through optimality cuts, which carry water values and storage opportunity costs, and through feasibility cuts, which enforce reservoir and water-right limits. Three methods are provided: a monolithic LP/MIP; stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) with backward-pass apertures, multi-cut and elastic-filterfeasibility cuts; and a multi-level cascade that refines a coarse model into a detailed one while inheriting its cuts. Operating rules such as the Chilean irrigation agreements are added without code through PAMPL, an AMPL-like constraint language, and LP/MIP solvers are loaded at run time as plugins. GTOpt is validated against IEEE benchmark networks, pandapower and published SDDP benchmarks. It is also compared with the official daily schedule of the Chilean national system on 14 days, using the system operator’s PLEXOS inputs and results. The comparison shows that the line-loss model drives most of the differences: a piecewise-linear loss model with free losses inflates them to 2.5 times their physical value, whereas a tangent outer approximation with a small loss price stays within 5%.

title: Robust Multi-Task Learning and Entropy-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization for Operational Decision Support in Data-Driven Wind Turbine Digital Twins
summary: Reliable operational decision support for wind turbines requires more than accurate prediction: predictive outputs must also be translated into operational alternatives, while accounting for the limitations of data-driven models. This study
content: Reliable operational decision support for wind turbines requires more than accurate prediction: predictive outputs must also be translated into operational alternatives, while accounting for the limitations of data-driven models. This study develops an integrated, data-driven decision-support framework that combines perturbation-based robust multi-task learning with entropy-aware multi-objective optimization. Using industrial supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) data from an Aventa AV-7 wind turbine, the framework jointly predicts power output and classifies operational status into 11 classes. Robust training incorporates Gaussian input noise and random feature dropout, and predictive performance is evaluated alongside gradient-boosting baselines. Under nominal training, LightGBM achieves an RMSE of 0.0403 and an R² of 0.9996, while the robustly trained models retain R² values ranging from 0.9957 to 0.9991. The trained deep multi-task learning model is then used as a surrogate for multi-objective optimization with six metaheuristic algorithms. The optimization objectives are predicted power output and an entropy-based index calculated from the predicted operational-status probabilities. The resulting Pareto solutions are summarized through three decision-oriented policies—Safe, Knee-Point, and Max-Power—that represent different trade-offs between predicted performance and model-derived operational-status uncertainty. To assess the consistency of the optimization surrogate's power predictions, selected optimization-derived solutions are evaluated using a separately trained LightGBM regressor, yielding Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.9561–0.9926 across the six optimization algorithms. The principal contribution is the integration of joint performance and status prediction, perturbation-based robustness, status-probability entropy, Pareto search, and independent model-based assessment within a single monitoring-to-decision pipeline. The framework provides a computational basis for exploring candidate operating policies; the entropy index is not a calibrated failure probability, and the physical effectiveness of the resulting policies requires validation against measured operating responses.

title: Valorization of Brazilian Pequi Peel by Fungal Solid-state Fermentation for Protease Production, Aqueous Two-phase Recovery and Biochemical Characterization
summary: This study investigated the valorization of pequi ( Caryocar brasiliense ) peel as a substrate for protease production by Penicillium sp. 2A3, isolated from the Caatinga–Cerrado ecotone, and the subsequent recovery of the enzyme using a pol
content: This study investigated the valorization of pequi ( Caryocar brasiliense ) peel as a substrate for protease production by Penicillium sp. 2A3, isolated from the Caatinga–Cerrado ecotone, and the subsequent recovery of the enzyme using a polyethylene glycol (PEG)/sodium sulfate aqueous two-phase system (ATPS). A (2 3 ) factorial design was used to evaluate the effects of PEG molar mass (1,500–20,000 g mol⁻¹), PEG concentration (18–30%, w/w), and sodium sulfate concentration (10–13%, w/w) on the partition coefficient ( K ), recovery yield ( Y ), and purification factor ( PF ). The selected conditions, consisting of PEG with a molar mass of 20,000 g mol⁻¹, 18% PEG, and 10% sodium sulfate, resulted in a K of 2.23, a Y PEG of 164.1% in the PEG-rich phase, and a PF of 1.75. Biochemical characterization of the recovered fraction revealed optimal proteolytic activity at 40°C and pH 5.0. The enzyme exhibited differential responses to metal ions, with Mg²⁺, Na⁺, and K⁺ showing no significant effect or only slight inhibition, whereas Fe²⁺, Zn²⁺, Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺, and Ba²⁺ reduced residual activity. Inhibitor assays revealed sensitivity to EDTA, β-mercaptoethanol, and PMSF, although the results did not allow the catalytic class of the protease to be conclusively established. Overall, this study highlights the potential of pequi peel as a renewable feedstock for fungal enzyme production and demonstrates the applicability of ATPS as a recovery strategy, contributing to the valorization of agro-industrial biomass and the development of more sustainable bioprocesses.

title: A Knowledge-Augmented Large Language Model for Power System Security Risk Reasoning
source: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
summary: With the increasing complexity of modern power systems caused by renewable energy integration, distributed energy resources, and cyber–physical interactions, accurate and trustworthy security risk reasoning has become increasingly important
content: With the increasing complexity of modern power systems caused by renewable energy integration, distributed energy resources, and cyber–physical interactions, accurate and trustworthy security risk reasoning has become increasingly important. Existing data-driven methods mainly focus on risk prediction based on statistical correlations, while lacking the capability to model causal risk evolution and generate interpretable explanations. This paper proposes a knowledge-augmented large language model framework for power system security risk reasoning (KALLM-PSR). The proposed framework integrates structured power system knowledge with large language model reasoning capabilities to construct knowledge-enhanced representations, perform multi-stage risk propagation analysis, and generate reliability-aware explanations. A consistency evaluation mechanism is further introduced to improve the trustworthiness of reasoning results. Extensive experiments on IEEE 14-bus, 39-bus, and 118-bus systems demonstrate that KALLM-PSR outperforms conventional deep learning models, general large language models (LLMs), and retrieval-augmented approaches in risk identification accuracy, reasoning consistency, explanation quality, and robustness under disturbance conditions. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for intelligent and trustworthy power system security management.

title: Impacts of Marine Heatwaves
summary: This chapter examines marine heatwaves (MHWs), prolonged periods of extreme ocean warming driven by human-induced climate change and by natural climate modes such as El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). These events have transitioned from r
tags: Effects of global warming on oceans
content: This chapter examines marine heatwaves (MHWs), prolonged periods of extreme ocean warming driven by human-induced climate change and by natural climate modes such as El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). These events have transitioned from rare anomalies to a defining feature of a warming planet. Ecological consequences are catastrophic, including widespread coral bleaching, the destruction of kelp forests, and mass species mortality. The chapter identifies “winners” and “losers” in shifted food webs and notes that warming now penetrates the twilight zone, influenced by deep-reaching eddy currents. Regionally, the Indian Ocean is warming rapidly, intensifying cyclones and altering monsoon patterns, notably causing extreme rainfall in northwest India. In polar regions, MHWs trigger abrupt sea ice melt and accelerated glacier loss. Beyond ecology, these events threaten socio-economic stability through fishery closures and toxic algal blooms. To combat these threats, the text advocates mitigation strategies, including reducing global emissions and integrating renewable energy. Enhanced monitoring via Argo floats and early warning systems, such as those at Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), is essential for building coastal resilience. Ultimately, the chapter emphasizes that international collaboration and habitat restoration are vital to prevent a near-permanent heatwave state.

title: Green Growth, Sustainable Development and Climate Resilience in Nigeria: An Accounting and Financial Governance Perspective
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
summary: This paper examines how green growth can promote sustainable development and strengthen climate resilience in Nigeria through accounting and financial governance mechanisms that translate environmental objectives into measurable decisions a
content: This paper examines how green growth can promote sustainable development and strengthen climate resilience in Nigeria through accounting and financial governance mechanisms that translate environmental objectives into measurable decisions and outcomes. The paper adopts a structured qualitative literature review and documentary analysis design. The thematic content analysis was carried out to conclude from existing literature, institutional, and global accounting standards, which serve as the primary sources of data for the study. The findings show that renewable energy, resource efficiency, cleaner production, resilient infrastructure, and green innovation can support productivity, energy access, and environmental improvement. Still, their contribution depends on policy credibility, financing conditions, institutional capability, and distributional safeguards. Nigerian evidence further shows that renewable energy finance is constrained by policy and market risks, that the quality of sustainability disclosure remains uneven, and that external assurance and governance improve reporting quality. The paper finds that environmental management accounting, IFRS sustainability reporting, green budgeting, environmental-economic accounting, and credible green finance can link physical environmental performance to costs, financial statement effects, capital allocation, and accountability. It concludes that Nigeria's principal challenge is an implementation connectivity gap between climate-policy commitments, financing, accounting systems, and verifiable outcomes. The paper recommends integrated environmental data controls, climate sensitive investment appraisal, stronger implementation and assurance of IFRS S1/S2, transparent green finance accountability, and explicit reporting of distributional and resilience outcomes.

title: Oil Palm Frond-Derived Cellulose as a Sustainable Bio-Based Coagulant for Fine Silica Particle Removal: Structure-Performance Relationship and Coagulation Mechanism
summary: The growing demand for sustainable water treatment technologies has accelerated the development of renewable bio-based coagulants derived from agricultural biomass. In this study, we extracted cellulose from oil palm fronds (OPF) through se
content: The growing demand for sustainable water treatment technologies has accelerated the development of renewable bio-based coagulants derived from agricultural biomass. In this study, we extracted cellulose from oil palm fronds (OPF) through sequential dewaxing, alkaline delignification, bleaching, and acid hydrolysis, and evaluated its potential as a sustainable bio-based coagulant for removing turbidity from synthetic silica particle-containing wastewater. The structural evolution and physicochemical properties of the extracted cellulose were investigated using complementary spectroscopic, structural, morphological, surface, and thermal characterization techniques. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed the effective removal of lignin, hemicellulose, and other non-cellulosic constituents while preserving the crystalline cellulose framework. Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area and porosity analysis showed a retained mesoporous structure despite reduced surface area and pore volume. At the same time, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) confirmed enhanced thermal stability after cellulose enrichment. The coagulation–flocculation performance of raw OPF, dewaxed OPF, and extracted cellulose was evaluated by varying coagulant dosage, pH, and settling time. OPF-derived cellulose had a BET surface area of 38.17 m² g⁻¹ and achieved 94.0% turbidity removal at pH 10, with a dosage of 0.10 g and a settling time of 100 min. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed compact silica-loaded flocs, while energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) confirmed the highest localized silicon content (40.13 wt.%), demonstrating effective silica capture through adsorption, polymer bridging, and physical entrapment. These findings establish OPF-derived cellulose as an effective and sustainable bio-based coagulant with a clear structure–performance relationship for fine silica particle removal and a promising alternative to conventional chemical coagulants for wastewater treatment.

title: Predictive MPPT Algorithm using Hybrid ANFIS and LSTM for Solar Photovoltaic Systems
summary: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems have become one of the fastest-growing renewable energy sources, contributing approximately 8% of global electricity generation. However, their efficiency is significantly affected by rapidly varying environm
content: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems have become one of the fastest-growing renewable energy sources, contributing approximately 8% of global electricity generation. However, their efficiency is significantly affected by rapidly varying environmental conditions such as solar irradiance and temperature. Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is essential for maximising power extraction under these dynamic conditions. Conventional MPPT algorithms, such as Perturb and Observe (P&O), are computationally simple but often suffer from oscillations and poor performance during rapid environmental changes. Artificial intelligence techniques, including the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS), improve tracking accuracy but remain primarily reactive. This paper proposes a hybrid ANFIS-LSTM predictive MPPT architecture in which an LSTM network forecasts future irradiance and temperature from historical environmental data. These predictions are supplied to the ANFIS controller to proactively determine the optimal operating point. By combining time-series forecasting with intelligent decision-making, the proposed framework shifts MPPT from reactive to predictive-reactive control, enabling faster adaptation to changing conditions and improving the efficiency and reliability of solar PV systems.

title: Chemo-Signal–Microbiome Interactions for Soil Fertility and Carbon Sequestration
summary: Coal mining severely degrades soils through acid mine drainage, nutrient depletion, and disruption of microbial communities, while also contributing to greenhouse gas emissions. Conventional reclamation practices, such as recontouring and s
content: Coal mining severely degrades soils through acid mine drainage, nutrient depletion, and disruption of microbial communities, while also contributing to greenhouse gas emissions. Conventional reclamation practices, such as recontouring and superficial revegetation, often fail in the face of extreme physicochemical and biological inactivity, with little consideration of rhizosphere microbiomes and chemical signaling. This study evaluates the potential of chemical signals (chemo-signals), the molecular mediators of plant–microbe communication, as a novel ecological tool to rehabilitate coal mining–impacted soils of the Raniganj Coalfield (RCF), India. Specifically, it examines how plant- and microbe-derived signals, including flavonoids, strigolactones, siderophores, phytohormones, and quorum sensing (QS) molecules, can enhance microbial recruitment, nutrient cycling, potentially toxic element (PTE) sequestration, and carbon stabilization in degraded soils. Evidence demonstrates that chemo-signal–driven rhizosphere interactions improve soil fertility, accelerate vegetation establishment, and significantly increase carbon sequestration, contributing directly to climate change mitigation. The RCF case highlights both persistent challenges, such as heterogeneous spoil chemistry and recalcitrant contaminants, and emerging opportunities through tailored microbial consortia and integrated amendments. By linking rhizosphere signaling to practical restoration, this study proposes a biologically informed pathway to transform coal mining wastelands into self-sustaining ecosystems that support biodiversity, soil health, and long-term carbon storage, with implications for mining regions worldwide.

title: ANALYSIS OF THE APPLICABILITY OF THE CANADIAN CARBON BUFFER POOL FORMING MODEL
summary: The article examines the Canadian methodology for forming a carbon buffer pool, which is designed to minimize the consequences of greenhouse gas emissions. The authors pay special attention to the process of determining contributions to the
content: The article examines the Canadian methodology for forming a carbon buffer pool, which is designed to minimize the consequences of greenhouse gas emissions. The authors pay special attention to the process of determining contributions to the buffer pool, including risk mitigation measures that can reduce the volume of these contributions. The authors conclude that the Canadian experience can be applied within the framework of the Russian regulatory and legal environment, but it requires localization taking into account the specific features of forestry in Russia.

title: DATASET FOR DETERMINING GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSION CONTRIBUTIONS FROM LIVESTOCK ACTIVITY IN META, COLOMBIA
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This article presents a dataset compiled for the characterization and diagnosis of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from livestock activity in the department of Meta, Colombia. The data include a systematic review of specialized lit
content: This article presents a dataset compiled for the characterization and diagnosis of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from livestock activity in the department of Meta, Colombia. The data include a systematic review of specialized literature and the identification of critical areas with the highest estimated emissions in the region. Qualitative and quantitative variables associated with the environmental impact of extensive and intensive livestock farming were evaluated, with a focus on gases such as methane (CH₄), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and nitrous oxide (N₂O). The information gathered enables the analysis of mitigation methodologies tailored to local conditions and serves as a technical resource for the development of sustainable production strategies and public policies in the Eastern Plains (Llanos Orientales) region. Este artículo presenta un conjunto de datos recopilados para la caracterización y diagnóstico de los aportes de emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero (GEI) derivados de la actividad ganadera en el departamento del Meta, Colombia. Los datos abarcan una revisión sistemática de la literatura especializada y la identificación de zonas críticas con mayores estimaciones de emisión en la región. Se evaluaron variables cualitativas y cuantitativas asociadas al impacto ambiental de la ganadería extensiva e intensiva, enfocándose en gases como el metano (CH₄), dióxido de carbono (CO₂) y óxido nitroso (N₂O). La información recopilada permite analizar metodologías de mitigación adaptadas a las características locales y sirve como insumo técnico para la formulación de estrategias productivas sostenibles y políticas públicas en la región de los Llanos Orientales.

title: Whose shift? Demographic variation in willingness to adopt plant-rich diets and its mitigation consequences
summary: Background: Dietary transitions towards plant-rich diets are critical to reducing the environmental burden of the food system and improving public health, yet consumer adoption remains slow and uneven globally. Global dietary transition mod
content: Background: Dietary transitions towards plant-rich diets are critical to reducing the environmental burden of the food system and improving public health, yet consumer adoption remains slow and uneven globally. Global dietary transition models typically assume uniform and universal uptake of alternative diets, overlooking how willingness to change varies across countries and population groups. Modelling dietary transitions that reflect stated consumer willingness can reveal how much of the expected mitigation is achievable, for whom, and what residual gap needs to be bridged by policy action Methods: We coupled consumer adoption willingness data from a representative survey of 30,218 respondents across 31 countries with the MATILDA dietary impact model to compare dietary greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) under willingness-adjusted and population-wide adoption of the EAT-Lancet 2.0 reference diet. Random forest regression identified demographic and attitudinal predictors of adoption willingness.

title: Scientists in conservation advocacy: moving beyond the lab and taking protagonism in activism in Brazil
summary: The global environmental crisis threatens human health, ecosystem functioning, and the economy. Scientists are essential in providing evidence-based solutions and informing public policy. However, many feel unprepared or hesitant to engage
content: The global environmental crisis threatens human health, ecosystem functioning, and the economy. Scientists are essential in providing evidence-based solutions and informing public policy. However, many feel unprepared or hesitant to engage in activism or political processes. Here, we discuss how scientists can bridge the gap between research and policy implementation through dialogue with policymakers and society, public engagement, and active participation in biodiversity conservation. Scientists can enhance the science-policy interface and influence conservation decisions by actively participating in public engagement. Collaboration, political commitment, and active involvement as citizen scientists are critical to addressing environmental issues. Scientists should be encouraged to recognize their expertise as valuable contributions to public policies and advocate for change, despite the challenges of balancing research demands and societal spheres. By gradually engaging in the political process, advocating for change, and disseminating high-quality information, scientists can significantly impact biodiversity conservation and environmental sustainability.

title: Ambient Drying Enabled Energy Efficient Fabrication of Skin‐Free Aerogel Evaporators for High‐Performance Interfacial Solar Evaporation
summary: Aerogel‐based evaporators are widely explored for interfacial solar evaporation (ISE), yet their fabrication generally relies on energy‐intensive freeze‐drying, creating an inherent contradiction with the sustainable nature of solar desalin
content: Aerogel‐based evaporators are widely explored for interfacial solar evaporation (ISE), yet their fabrication generally relies on energy‐intensive freeze‐drying, creating an inherent contradiction with the sustainable nature of solar desalination. Moreover, freeze‐drying generates dense surface skin that restricts vapor escape and reduces evaporation area. Here, we report an ambient‐temperature and atmospheric‐pressure drying strategy that transforms the drying process from simple solvent removal process into structural engineering of sodium alginate (SA) aerogel evaporators. Gluconolactone‐triggered gradual Ca 2+ release enables thorough in situ crosslinking which mechanically stabilizes the gel network, while sacrificial CaCO 3 templating, CO 2 bubble evolution, and low‐surface‐tension solvent exchange preserve a skin‐free porous surface during ambient drying. Concurrently, gel domains formed within vertically oriented channels regulate water transport, establishing a balance between water supply and evaporation. The resulting aerogel achieves an evaporation rate of 2.36 kg m −2 h −1 under one sun, compared with 1.84 kg m −2 h −1 for its freeze‐dried counterpart, while reducing fabrication energy consumption by 94.8% and processing time by 55.6%, and increasing tensile strength by 537%. Life‐cycle assessment reveals a 96.5% reduction in CO 2 emissions. This work establishes low‐energy drying as a means of simultaneously programming aerogel surfaces and mass transport, providing a sustainable route toward high‐performance solar evaporators.

DUMT}$) در چارچوب فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{HIP-1155}$) و معادله مادر. حوزه‌های هدف از ۵۰ حوزه: حوزه شماره ۲۳ (مدیریت ساختمان‌های هوشمند $\text{BMS}$)، حوزه شماره ۳ (مدیریت منابع آب و فاضلاب شهری) و حوزه شماره ۱ (شبکه‌های توزیع برق هوشمند در مقیاس شهری). بیان مشکل: معماری و شهرسازی کنونی بر پایه سوداگری زمین، فروش متراژ بتنی و سیستم‌های تهویه و مدیریت ساختمان واکنشی ($\text{Reactive BMS/HVAC}$) بنا شده است. در این الگو، ساختمان‌ها بدون تطابق ترمودینامیکی با اقلیم محلی ساخته می‌شوند، گرما و آلاینده‌ها را به محیط بیرونی پمپاژ می‌کنند، فاضلاب و پسماند را به جای بازیافت درجا به شبکه‌های خطی می‌سپارند و پس از بروز نوسان دمایی یا آلودگی با تأخیر وارد عمل می‌شوند. در سطح محاسباتی نیز اتکا به تقریب‌های ناپایدار، نبودِ کران‌مندی جبری صریح روی کل $\mathbb{R}$ و خطاهای ممیز شناور استاندارد در مقیاس‌های بسیار بزرگ یا کوچک، تحلیل متابولیسم شهری را با ناپایداری مواجه می‌کند. سطح حاد بودن مشکل: این مسئله در سطح بحرانیِ چندلایه ($\text{CRITICAL-MULTILAYER}$) قرار دارد؛ زیرا هم پایداری ترمودینامیکی و هم‌ترازی متابولیک سلول‌های شهری (انرژی، آب، گرما و زیست‌توده در حوزه‌های ۱، ۳ و ۲۳) و هم دقت صوری و عددیِ مدل‌سازی در $\text{Lean 4}$ و پایتون باید هم‌زمان و بدون تناقض برقرار باشند. ۲. نوع الگوریتم و معماری سیستم نوع الگوریتم: الگوریتم ترکیبیِ اثبات صوری و محاسبه دقیق تانسور متابولیسم شهری ($\text{Formal-Verified \& Deterministic Urban Metabolism Engine - DUMT-1155}$)، مبتنی بر تکمیل مربع کامل برای نامساوی‌های درجه دو روی کل $\mathbb{R}$، بازنویسی تقسیم‌شده بر $\chi^2$ برای جلوگیری از سرریز در مقادیر بزرگ، حساب چندگانه دقیق با mpmath.workdps، حفظ علامت با np.arcsinh و اعتبارسنجی صریح ورودی و خروجی. معماری سیستم: لایه صوری $\text{Lean 4}$ ($\text{Self-Verifying Kernel}$): تعریف صریح تعاریف noncomputable برای مقادیر حقیقی، اثبات هویت تکمیل مربع کامل روی کل محور اعداد حقیقی ($\mathbb{R}$)، اثبات کران‌های مثبت و کران بالا/پایین، تعمیم فرضیات به حالت کمینه‌تر (0 ≤ rho0) و راستی‌آزمایی اصول موضوعه با #print axioms بدون sorry. لایه محاسبات علمی پایتون ($\text{High-Precision Numerical \& Validation Layer}$): استفاده از mpmath.workdps برای دقت دلخواه بدون تغییر وضعیت سراسری، جلوگیری از سرریز و خطای $\infty / \infty$ در $\chi$ بزرگ، استفاده از np.arcsinh برای نگاشت پایدار با حفظ علامت، رد ورودی‌های بولی به جای عدد صحیح و مقایسه شرطی خطای مدل نسبت به میانگین پایه (model_mae < baseline_mae). لایه متابولیسم شهری و تطابق فرمولی ($\text{Urban Metabolic \& Formula Consistency Layer}$): قفل کردن گره‌های ساختمانی و شهری (حوزه‌های ۲۳، ۳ و ۱) روی توازن انرژی، بازیافت گرما و چرخه بسته آب و راکتورهای زیستی-نوری، همراه با انطباق دقیق فرمول‌های پایتون با قضایای $\text{Lean 4}$. ۳. روش و سازوکار این نظریه (معادله مادر) در چارچوب معادله مادر برتر ($\text{Master Equation}^{1155\text{D}}$) برای نظریه ۱۱، کلان‌شهر به جای رفتار انگلی و مصرف‌کننده خطی، به یک شبکه هم‌تراز از س

title: A small ensemble of bias-adjusted CMIP6 climate simulations over North America extending to 2300
summary: ESPO-G6-post2100 is a bias-adjusted dataset covering North America featuring CMIP6 climate projections extending from 1950 up to 2300. It is meant to support climate change impact and adaptation studies for long-lived infrastructure and lon
content: ESPO-G6-post2100 is a bias-adjusted dataset covering North America featuring CMIP6 climate projections extending from 1950 up to 2300. It is meant to support climate change impact and adaptation studies for long-lived infrastructure and long-term planning decisions. It includes 17 simulations from eight different Earth System Models driven by five ScenarioMIP scenarios. The small ensemble size and the fact that most simulations are driven by either extremely low or extremely high greenhouse gas concentration pathways raises challenges for the delivery of robust and actionable climate products post-2100. The dataset is registered at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22132713 (Lavoie et al., 2026).

title: Assessment of a Diverse Pea Panel for Seed Quality, Yield, and Trait Trade‐Offs in Organic Trials
summary: Background and Objectives Increasing the consumption of legume‐based proteins is important for human nutrition and the environment. This study assessed the yield and seed quality of 18 pea accessions, mostly landraces of diverse geographica
content: Background and Objectives Increasing the consumption of legume‐based proteins is important for human nutrition and the environment. This study assessed the yield and seed quality of 18 pea accessions, mostly landraces of diverse geographical origins, intercropped with wheat on five farms in a participatory organic farming framework. Findings Genotype accounted for 40.2%–72.6% of the variance in seed protein, calcium, magnesium, and zinc contents, as well as in PA2 albumin, vicilin, and convicilin (7S globulins) abundances, with weaker environmental effects. In contrast, environment accounted for 51.5%–59.5% of the variance in iron content, 11S globulin abundance, and 7S/11S ratio. Data integration revealed trade‐offs between yield and seed quality traits, some being environment‐specific (e.g., iron content). Favorable trait associations were also identified, notably between yield and PA2 albumins. Conclusions Outstanding pea landraces were identified as rich in sulfur‐containing seed proteins or micronutrients, with positive associations between some seed components and yield. A negative correlation was observed between protein content and yield, highlighting the necessary compromises to develop the cultivation of landraces under organic systems. Significance and Novelty This study uncovers both trade‐offs and positive associations between yield and seed quality, and provides genetic resources for developing peas with improved nutritional value under agroecological systems.

title: Direct Solar Storage and On‐Demand Power via Threshold‐Matched Silicon Photovoltaics and Dual‐Ion Batteries
summary: Direct integration of photovoltaics with batteries is attractive for energy‐autonomous mobile platforms, but mismatched photovoltaic output and battery charging requirements, limited high‐rate capability, and low‐temperature degradation can
content: Direct integration of photovoltaics with batteries is attractive for energy‐autonomous mobile platforms, but mismatched photovoltaic output and battery charging requirements, limited high‐rate capability, and low‐temperature degradation can necessitate intermediate power electronics and restrict burst‐power delivery. Here, a threshold‐matched silicon photovoltaic–dual‐ion battery (PV–DIB) architecture is demonstrated by directly coupling a voltage‐ and current‐tailored crystalline‐silicon photovoltaic module with a high‐voltage dual‐ion battery pouch cell. Under one‐sun illumination, the photovoltaic module supplies ≈72 mA at the battery charging threshold, enabling direct charging without intermediate power‐conversion hardware. This matching establishes two complementary operating regimes: solar‐sustained operation when photovoltaic current meets the load demand and on‐demand battery assistance when the load exceeds the photovoltaic input. The integrated system delivers a maximum power density of 11,430 W kg −1 at 40.83 mA cm −2 , maintains stable operation under drone‐relevant dynamic load profiles, and the DIB retains 5,088 W kg −1 at −10°C. Indoor and outdoor flight demonstrations validate direct solar energy storage and burst‐power delivery, establishing threshold matching as a practical design strategy for power‐electronics‐minimized, energy‐autonomous mobile systems.

title: Controlled Localization of Dual Oxides in SSZ‐13 Zeolites Promoting Catalytic Performances in Chloromethane‐to‐Olefins Conversion
summary: Chloromethane‐to‐olefins (CMTO) conversion over small‐pore zeolites offers a route for valorizing C1 feedstocks, but its practical performance is limited by rapid catalyst deactivation associated with restricted diffusion and polyaromatic a
content: Chloromethane‐to‐olefins (CMTO) conversion over small‐pore zeolites offers a route for valorizing C1 feedstocks, but its practical performance is limited by rapid catalyst deactivation associated with restricted diffusion and polyaromatic accumulation. In this study, the spatial functions of MgO and SnO 2 within SSZ‐13 are systematically controlled to improve catalytic activity, stability, and light‐olefin selectivity. Structural characterization confirms selective localization of the oxides on the external surface, within the micropores, or in combined configurations without significant disruption of the CHA framework. External MgO promotes CH 3 Cl activation and methyl spillover to the zeolite surface, accompanied by the formation of Si–O–CH 3 species, whereas internal SnO 2 is associated with reduced accumulation of recoverable naphthalene‐related species. The optimized M ext S int /SSZ‐13 catalyst, containing external MgO and internal SnO 2 , achieves a maximum CH 3 Cl conversion of 98.3% and maintains >94% conversion after 8 h, with the lowest deactivation rate of 0.010% min −1 and high light‐olefin selectivity. TGA and GC‐MS analyses show an association between catalyst deactivation and the accumulation of recoverable naphthalene‐related species, while FT‐IR spectroscopy supports MgO‐assisted CH 3 Cl activation and methyl transfer. These findings demonstrate that spatial division of complementary catalytic functions within zeolite architectures provides an effective strategy for simultaneously enhancing CMTO activity, selectivity, and stability.

title: A New Variable-Exponent Predefined-Time Sliding Mode Control for the Energy Management of Battery-Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles
summary: Despite recent improvements to battery-powered electric vehicles, they face limitations related to limited driving range, long charging times, and accelerated battery degradation under demanding duty cycles. In addition, existing methods fo
content: Despite recent improvements to battery-powered electric vehicles, they face limitations related to limited driving range, long charging times, and accelerated battery degradation under demanding duty cycles. In addition, existing methods for addressing these issues may be impractical in real-world applications. This study addresses this gap by investigating a robust energy management approach for a fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) with hybrid power sources. In this system, the fuel cell serves as the main power source, whereas a lithium-ion battery and an ultracapacitor provide additional support to handle load variations and transient conditions. The fuel cell is connected to the DC link through a DC–DC boost converter, whereas the battery and ultracapacitor are interfaced via bidirectional converters to allow flexible power exchange. A fourth-order dynamic model that accounts for model uncertainties and voltage fluctuations is developed to accurately represent system behavior. In addition, a new variable-exponentbased predefined-time sliding mode control strategy is introduced. This controller is designed to coordinate power sharing among multiple sources and effectively regulate the DC-link voltage across different operating conditions. Simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme. The results demonstrate that the system achieves fast response, stable voltage regulation, and reliable energy distribution. The proposed method guarantees predefined-time stability, i.e., the system states reach their desired values within a predefined time regardless of initial conditions. In addition, the controller improves robustness against uncertainties and reduces the effect of disturbances, making it suitable for practical FCEV applications

title: Durable Superhydrophobic Surface Engineering for Agricultural and Food-Contact Systems
summary: Agricultural machinery, storage silos, food-processing pipelines, and packaging substrates operate under harsh coupled mechanical, tribological, chemical, electrochemical, and biological stressors that bare metallic or polymeric bulk materi
content: Agricultural machinery, storage silos, food-processing pipelines, and packaging substrates operate under harsh coupled mechanical, tribological, chemical, electrochemical, and biological stressors that bare metallic or polymeric bulk materials cannot withstand alone. Engineered superhydrophobic surface–substrate systems—combining controlled micro-/nanoscale topography with low-surface-energy chemistry to sustain a Cassie–Baxter air plastron (static water contact angle θs > 150°, sliding angle α < 10°)—impart emergent wear resistance, corrosion protection, drag reduction, and multi-foulant repulsion across pre-harvest and post-harvest environments. This review examines contemporary surface engineering advances (predominantly 2023–2026) through a process–structure–property lens. Subtractive monolithic texturing (nanosecond/femtosecond laser processing, reactive-ion etching, interference lithography) is critically compared against additive and hybrid deposition routes (nanodiamond composites, sol–gel/mesoporous silica, electrodeposition, electrospinning, cellular armor, and fluorine-free bio-dispersions). Tribological soil/mud anti-adhesion on tillage and harvesting components, electrochemical impedance corrosion protection on magnesium, aluminum, galvanized, and stainless alloys, and turbulent slip hydraulics are evaluated alongside a quantitative cross-study benchmark of bacterial log10 reductions (0.7 to 6.5 log_{10}) separating passive anticontact ceilings from dual-functional synergy. Finally, multiscale surface characterisation, non-destructive examination (plastron tracking, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, X-ray computed tomography), and quality-control protocols for PFAS-free food-contact compliance are established.

title: Anaerobic Parameterization Lowers Inferred Carbon Inputs but Yields Regionally Inconsistent RothC Performance Under Regional Input Scenarios for Chinese Paddy Soils
source: Advances in biological sciences research/Advances in Biological Sciences Research
summary: Anaerobic corrections to RothC remain insufficiently tested across paddy regions. Standard and modified RothC were compared using paired 1980s–2010s soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks at 104 Chinese sites. Published decomposition multipliers
content: Anaerobic corrections to RothC remain insufficiently tested across paddy regions. Standard and modified RothC were compared using paired 1980s–2010s soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks at 104 Chinese sites. Published decomposition multipliers of 0.2 in assigned flooded months and 0.6 otherwise were applied without refitting. Simulated and observed stocks were standardized to 0–20 cm, and external precipitation and reference evapotranspiration were re-extracted from matched-period monthly climate products. Mean inferred carbon inputs were 4.67 and 1.75 t C ha ⁻1 yr ⁻1 . In a leakage-free benchmark of 1,469 external cropland profiles, modification reduced pooled root mean square error from 24.37 to 22.80 t C ha ⁻1 (6.4%) and mean bias from +8.93 to +7.33 t C ha ⁻1 . Both pooled R 2 values remained negative, and RMSE increased in Northeast China. Literature budgets contextualize inferred inputs without validating site-level additions. The correction strongly changes model-equivalent input requirements but provides only modest aggregate stock improvement; regional application requires independent carbon budgets, water-management records, and repeated SOC observations.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
summary: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors p
content: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO 2 /H 2 O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.

title: Governed Synchronization of Adaptive Digital Twins for Industrial Biomanufacturing: Application to Penicillin Fermentation
summary: Digital twins are increasingly used in biomanufacturing to support real-time monitoring and decision-making. However, maintaining long-term synchronization between the digital twin and the physical twin remains a significant challenge becau
content: Digital twins are increasingly used in biomanufacturing to support real-time monitoring and decision-making. However, maintaining long-term synchronization between the digital twin and the physical twin remains a significant challenge because biological processes continuously evolve due to batch-to-batch variability, process drift, and measurement uncertainty. Existing approaches rely on repeated model retraining or high-dimensional adaptive models, increasing computational complexity and reducing interpretability and industrial deployability. This work proposes a Governed Adaptive Digital Twin (GADT) framework for industrial penicillin fermentation that relies on a validated symbolic process model synchronized through a low-dimensional governed adaptation layer. The structural model is developed offline using multi-gene genetic programming (MGGP), while online synchronization is achieved by adaptively updating only two interpretable parameters, gain and bias, using normalized prediction error. The adaptation process incorporates scheduling, innovation filtering, guardrail constraints, parameter bounding, and batch lifecycle management to ensure robust industrial operation. The proposed framework was evaluated using pseudo-online streaming data generated from 90 simulated fed-batch fermentation campaigns based on the industrial-scale IndPenSim benchmark, labelled as representing approximately three years of simulated production campaigns in the IndPenSim benchmark. Compared with a conventional digital twin, the proposed GADT achieved higher prediction accuracy and trajectory-level synchronization while effectively compensating for long-term process drift without recursive model correction or structural model retraining. Ablation studies further demonstrate that the proposed governance mechanisms are essential for stable and physically consistent adaptation. The results demonstrate that governed synchronization, rather than continuous structural model evolution, enables sustained digital twin performance and provides an interpretable, computationally, industrially deployable architecture for adaptive digital twins in biomanufacturing.

title: Editorial: Utilizing well-instrumented critical zone sites: infrastructure, data integration, and advancements in earth system research
summary: Critical Zone (CZ) science brings together disciplines such as hydrology, soil science, geochemistry, ecology, and earth-surface processes to understand Earth's shallow skin as an interconnected system. By examining interactions among water
content: Critical Zone (CZ) science brings together disciplines such as hydrology, soil science, geochemistry, ecology, and earth-surface processes to understand Earth's shallow skin as an interconnected system. By examining interactions among water, rocks, soils, the atmosphere, and living organisms, CZ science research advances our understanding of the processes that govern ecosystem functioning and inform applications ranging from water-resource management to sustainable agriculture and carbon cycling (Brantley et al., 2007;Banwart et al., 2013;Stolze et al., 2024). Addressing these complex interactions requires observations that capture the spatial heterogeneity and temporal dynamics of CZ processes across a range of scales (Kumar et al., 2023). Open-source monitoring infrastructure, innovative sensing, and low-cost instrumentation can expand access to environmental data and reveal dynamics and subsurface heterogeneity that might otherwise remain unresolved. This Research Topic brings together five contributions that illustrate these complementary advances, spanning environmental monitoring networks, soil moisture and CO₂ flux measurements, soil carbon dynamics, and subsurface flow pathways. Below, we synthesize these contributions, highlighting their methodological innovations and the scientific insights they offer.Of the five publications in this Research Topic, three focus on how open-source infrastructure, innovative sensing techniques, and low-cost instrumentation can improve the spatial and temporal resolution of CZ observations while expanding access to environmental data. Dessimond et al. present the Environmental Sensing and Data Network (ESDN), a multisite environmental monitoring infrastructure in eastern North Carolina that integrates legacy and modern sensors using LoRaWAN telemetry, a self-hosted ThingsBoard Internet of Things (IoT) platform, and cloud-based data archiving. Since its deployment in mid-2024, the network has expanded to 110 sensors and 14 communications gateways across diverse settings, including urban and suburban neighborhoods, agricultural lands, forests, and coastal wetlands, supporting applications ranging from flood and groundwater monitoring to soil moisture, nutrient cycling, and community science. By supporting diverse sensors while reducing reliance on proprietary platforms, recurring telemetry fees, and vendor-specific systems, the ESDN offers a flexible alternative to conventional commercial monitoring systems. Such networks have the potential to lower technical and financial barriers to environmental monitoring and broaden participation among educators, community organizations, and local stakeholders.Susanto et al. developed a hybrid inversion approach that combines signal processing and numerical modeling to estimate soil moisture from passively heated fiber-optic distributed temperature sensing (FO-DTS).
