title: Mangrove Ecosystem Quality Index: Combining Field-Based Vegetation Structure and Water Quality to Assess Mangrove Ecosystem Condition in Segara Anakan, Cilacap, Indonesia
summary: Comprehensive mangrove health assessments require evaluating both historical vegetation structure and dynamic water quality, yet these domains are rarely integrated into a single field-based index. This study develops the Mangrove Ecosystem
content: Comprehensive mangrove health assessments require evaluating both historical vegetation structure and dynamic water quality, yet these domains are rarely integrated into a single field-based index. This study develops the Mangrove Ecosystem Quality Index (MEQI) to address this gap, applying it to 45 sampling points in the Segara Anakan lagoon, Indonesia. The MEQI combines a Vegetation Structure Index (ISV) and a Water Quality Index (IWQ), each comprising six parameters weighted empirically through principal component analysis (PCA). Point-level scores were mapped utilizing inverse distance weighting on a hexagonal grid. Results indicate an average MEQI of 51.76, with 2 stations classified as Very Good, 26 as Good, 15 as Moderate, and 2 as Poor. Spatially, ecosystem health was strongest in the north-central and western sectors but degraded along the eastern arm due to anthropogenic loads. Notably, evaluating the sub-indices independently revealed a statistically significant divergence: vegetation structure (average ISV 40.77) was substantially more degraded than water quality (average IWQ 62.75). Relying solely on the composite MEQI risks a masking effect, where functional aquatic conditions obscure historically degraded vegetation. The PCA weights highlighted carbon stock, biomass, pH, and dissolved oxygen as primary ecosystem drivers. The MEQI serves as a practical, field-deployable tool that robustly complements remote-sensing approaches like the Mangrove Ecosystem Health Index (MEHI). For effective conservation, managers must utilize such integrated indices to periodically monitor the disparate recovery timelines of structural and aquatic mangrove dimensions.

title: An Injectable Hydrogel With Dynamic Anchoring of Salvianolic Acid B Enables Sustained Co‐Delivery With Bevacizumab for Retinal Trifunctional Recovery in Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is driven by oxidative stress, pathological angiogenesis, and retinal neurodegeneration, yet current anti‑VEGF therapies fail to address upstream oxidative damage or neuronal injury and require frequent injections.
content: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is driven by oxidative stress, pathological angiogenesis, and retinal neurodegeneration, yet current anti‑VEGF therapies fail to address upstream oxidative damage or neuronal injury and require frequent injections. Moreover, the distinct pharmacokinetic behaviors of small molecules and biologics hinder their synchronized delivery. Herein, an injectable hydrogel exploiting salvianolic acid B (SaB) as a dynamic molecular anchor is developed for sustained co‑delivery with bevacizumab (Bev). Through multivalent dynamic boronate ester interactions, SaB functions simultaneously as a therapeutic cargo and a dynamic network participant, restricting its rapid diffusion and reducing the release-rate mismatch with Bev to enable sustained co-delivery for over 6 weeks. Sustained SaB scavenges reactive oxygen species, activates Nrf2/HO‑1 signaling and suppresses the ROS/MAPK/HIF-1α/VEGF cascade, thereby reduces endogenous VEGF production, whereas Bev continuously neutralizes extracellular VEGF. By integrating upstream oxidative stress regulation with downstream angiogenic inhibition, this strategy achieves trifunctional retinal recovery characterized by oxidative stress alleviation, pathological angiogenesis suppression, and retinal neuroprotection. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats, a single intravitreal injection effectively suppresses pathological angiogenesis, reduces oxidative damage, preserves retinal structure and function, and exhibits excellent ocular biocompatibility. This SaB-enabled dynamic anchoring hydrogel provides a promising long-acting co-delivery strategy for multifactorial DR therapy.

title: Rhizosphere Resource–Niche Coupling Mediates A Respiratory Trade‐Off in Microbial Carbon Use Under Contrasting Agricultural Management
summary: The rhizosphere constitutes a critical hotspot for terrestrial carbon transformation, yet the mechanistic linkage between contrasting agricultural management and coordinated shifts in rhizosphere resources, microbial niches, and carbon-use
content: The rhizosphere constitutes a critical hotspot for terrestrial carbon transformation, yet the mechanistic linkage between contrasting agricultural management and coordinated shifts in rhizosphere resources, microbial niches, and carbon-use strategies remains poorly resolved. Here, we established a unified resource-niche coupling framework and validated it using a seven-year field experiment with crop rotations of contrasting diversity and two fertilization regimes (mineral vs. manure). We quantified rhizosphere vs. bulk soil effects across three resource axes: resource quantity, microbial stoichiometric demand, and enzyme-based carbon-processing allocation. Fertilization dominated the stoichiometric-demand axis, enriching labile metabolites (amino acids, peptides, lipids), accelerating bacterial community turnover, and driving high respiration investment per unit microbial biomass alongside carbohydrate-specialized carbon use. By contrast, diversified crop rotation affected resource quantity and carbon-processing strategy axes, accumulating polyphenolic and glycosylated secondary metabolites, expanding fungal niche breadth, and homogenizing substrate utilization across carbon substrates. We identified a community-level trade-off between respiratory intensity and substrate-use evenness associated with rhizosphere resource-niche coupling: mineral fertilization favored respiration-intensive carbon use, whereas crop diversification promoted more balanced substrate utilization. This unifying mechanistic framework predicts rhizosphere carbon partitioning under agricultural management and offers actionable guidance for climate-smart farming to strengthen long-term soil carbon retention.

title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO 2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
summary: Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design
content: Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady‐state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO 2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO 2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO 2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO 2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo‐ and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

title: Thermal Dynamics as a Non‐Invasive Indicator for Cycle Life Prediction of LiFePO 4 /Graphite Batteries Under Fast‐Charging
summary: Resistance‐induced overpotential and the associated heat generation are critical factors affecting cycle life of lithium‐ion batteries under fast‐charging conditions. In this study, we propose a temperature‐based prognostic approach for the
content: Resistance‐induced overpotential and the associated heat generation are critical factors affecting cycle life of lithium‐ion batteries under fast‐charging conditions. In this study, we propose a temperature‐based prognostic approach for the early prediction of battery cycle life, focusing on LiFePO 4 /graphite cells cycled under a fixed family of multistep fast‐charging protocols at 30°C. The charging process was segmented into four state‐of‐charge (SoC)‐resolved constant‐current regions (CC1–CC4). Voltage and temperature analyses revealed that the initial SoC region (CC1) is particularly sensitive to overpotential development, where a high current density is associated with a premature transition to the constant‐voltage (CV) mode and intensified heat generation. At advanced stages of cycling, temperature behavior exhibited correlations with cycle life consistent with voltage responses. Based on these observations, temperature evolution during the early cycles (third to 10th) was employed to construct a cycle life prediction model. Among the CC‐resolved regions, temperature‐related features from CC1 and CC4 showed higher predictive relevance than those from CC2 and CC3. These results suggest that non‐invasively measured surface temperature can serve as a physically meaningful indicator for early‐stage cycle life prognosis under the studied fast‐charging conditions. The proposed framework provides an interpretable approach for battery health monitoring and fast‐charging protocol design.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
summary: Phenazine-based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one-step two-electron redox reaction. However, the highly co
content: Phenazine-based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one-step two-electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the π-π interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2'-(phenazine-2,3-diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low-capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot-scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large-scale energy storage applications.

title: Optimizing Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Performance of MoSe₂ through Strategic Transition-Metal Doping: A Density Functional Theory Analysis
summary: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising candidates for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) because of their high specific surface areas and mechanical flexibilities. However, the catalytic activities
content: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising candidates for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) because of their high specific surface areas and mechanical flexibilities. However, the catalytic activities of pristine TMDs are limited by the chemical inertness of their basal planes. In this study, spin-polarized density functional theory calculations are performed to investigate the effects of 3d- and 4d-transition-metal doping on the HER performance of the MoSe2 basal plane. Transition-metal doping in MoSe2 confirms the thermodynamic stability of the resulting systems; specifically, doping with early transition metals offers the highest lattice stability, whereas doping with late transition metals induces greater electronic perturbations. The adsorption energetics reveal that pristine MoSe2 provides the weakest binding energy toward H (1GH∗ = 1.40 eV), whereas Zn doping gives the strongest binding energy (1GH∗ = −0.40 eV). Moreover, doping of Cd and Ag in the nearest-neighbor configuration drastically reduces the Gibbs free energy of H adsorption to near-optimal values of – 0.02 and –0.16 eV, respectively. Finally, electronic structure analysis and d-band center scaling indicate that these dopants trigger a semiconductor-to-metal transition and optimize the orbital hybridization between the metal d-states and H s-orbitals. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the development of high-performance, earth-abundant electrocatalysts for sustainable, green H2 production.

title: Are fungi and their enzymes effective for biodegradable microplastics in wastewater? Linking particle retention to polymer-carbon conversion
summary: Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) can persist through wastewater treatment and be transferred from water to sludge without substantial polymer degradation, posing potential risks to aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Fungi can colonize bi
content: Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) can persist through wastewater treatment and be transferred from water to sludge without substantial polymer degradation, posing potential risks to aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Fungi can colonize biodegradable polyester particles and produce extracellular enzymes capable of depolymerization, but their effectiveness in continuous municipal wastewater treatment remains uncertain. This critical review examines the relationships among particle retention, fungal enzyme activity, polymer hydrolysis, and the fate of released carbon. We distinguish physical capture from depolymerization, assimilation, and mineralization, drawing on evidence from fungal cultures, isolated enzymes, and mixed microbial systems. Three potential treatment configurations are evaluated: recoverable fungal pellets, attached fungal growth, and enzymatic hydrolysis of concentrated BMP fractions. Their feasibility depends on sustained particle–enzyme contact, catalytic activity under non-sterile conditions, and downstream utilization or recovery of hydrolysis products. We propose evaluation criteria incorporating polymer-specific inventories across effluent, sludge, and retained solids; isotope-based carbon tracing; matched experimental controls; and energy and material accounting. This framework identifies the evidence needed to determine whether fungal interventions achieve genuine reductions in residual polymer discharge rather than merely transferring biodegradable microplastics between environmental compartments.

title: Oxygen Vacancies as a Reaction Switch for Cocatalysts‐Free CO 2 Photoreduction on CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 Hybrid Without Sacrificial Agent
summary: Photocatalysis offers an energy‐efficient and renewable approach of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion into sustainable fuels and chemicals. However, the cutting‐edge photocatalysts mostly rely on sacrificial electron donors, whereas noble‐m
content: Photocatalysis offers an energy‐efficient and renewable approach of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion into sustainable fuels and chemicals. However, the cutting‐edge photocatalysts mostly rely on sacrificial electron donors, whereas noble‐metal cocatalysts hinder the progress of this field to real‐world applications. Developing photocatalysts that could work in the absence of sacrificial agents as well as noble‐metal cocatalysts is highly desirable, but remains challenging. As such, this work demonstrates a Z‐scheme photocatalyst having abundant oxygen vacancies (OVs) in a flower‐shaped CeO 2 /Manganese oxide (Mn 3 O 4 ) hybrid to facilitate the CO 2 photoreduction via exposure to visible light. The CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 hybrid with OVs promotes visible light absorption and charge carrier separation. The optimized 9CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 catalyst yields 12 μmol h −1 of CO and 2.2 μmol h −1 of CH 4 without any noble‐metal catalysts or sacrificial agents, which is ∼13 times greater than that of pristine Mn 3 O 4 . The 9CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 catalyst exhibits robust structural stability with fully regenerable activity. While per‐hour yield declines due to intermediate adsorption, mild thermal treatment at 425 K completely restores catalytic performance over multiple cycles. The optimized photocatalytic efficiency of 9CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 is primarily due to its expanded range of light‐absorption capacity and effective charge carrier retention, as demonstrated by ultraviolet–visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, photoluminescence analysis, transient photocurrent spectra, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Therefore, this discovery has the potential to facilitate the fabrication of photocatalysts for CO 2 reduction to biofuels and synthetic compounds.

title: Exploiting the Potential of Large Language Models in NLP : A Survey of Methods and Applications
source: Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have proven to be a revolutionary concept in the field of natural language processing (NLP). The development of transformer‐based models and the advances in related directions, such as large‐scale pre‐training,
content: Large language models (LLMs) have proven to be a revolutionary concept in the field of natural language processing (NLP). The development of transformer‐based models and the advances in related directions, such as large‐scale pre‐training, instruction tuning, preference optimization, retrieval augmentation, and parameter‐efficient adaptation, have led to the creation of extremely capable and versatile language models. At the same time, the rapid growth of the LLM makes it hard to track and understand the relationships between different models, their training procedures, adaptation methods, applications, and evaluation techniques. This survey presents a unified taxonomy of LLMs organized around three core dimensions: architectural paradigms, training methodology, and fine‐tuning and adaptation techniques. In addition, the survey examines LLM capabilities across major NLP tasks and analyzes the evaluation techniques used to assess their performance, robustness, and generalization. This distinction between core taxonomy dimensions and complementary analytical dimensions provides a structured perspective on the development, adaptation, application, and evaluation of LLMs. For each category, the paper analyzes the current trends, advantages, and limitations and provides a taxonomy of the main approaches and directions. Moreover, this paper also discusses the key limitations of the state‐of‐the‐art LLMs. Altogether, the study provides a holistic view of the LLM that can help understand the research directions in the LLM field.

title: Astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D regulates hippocampal memory through extracellular matrix remodeling
summary: Astrocytes contribute to hippocampal cognitive functions, but how astrocyte-derived factors regulate memory formation remains unclear. Here, we identify astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D (CtsD) as a regulator of hippocampal learning and memory
content: Astrocytes contribute to hippocampal cognitive functions, but how astrocyte-derived factors regulate memory formation remains unclear. Here, we identify astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D (CtsD) as a regulator of hippocampal learning and memory. Proteomic profiling of hippocampal astrocytes upon learning identified candidates predicted to be secreted, among which we focused on CtsD, whose extracellular brain functions are unknown. Neutralizing extracellular CtsD or astrocyte-selective CtsD knockdown (aCtsD-KD) impaired hippocampal long term potentiation (LTP) and memory acquisition, suggesting an extracellular role for astrocytic CtsD. In aCtsD-KD mice, these deficits were accompanied by alterations in excitatory transmission and synaptic structures. aCtsD-KD also caused abnormal extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, and its partial digestion by chondroitinase ABC rescued the memory deficit, indicating that astrocytic CtsD-dependent ECM degradation contributes to hippocampal memory. Together, our findings suggest a CtsD-dependent astrocyte-matrix-synapse axis regulating hippocampal memory.

title: FlexibleCommunity: An Incentive-Based Dynamic Flexibility Management Simulator
summary: This paper introduces FlexibleCommunity, an incentive-based energy management simulator for investigating demand-response strategies of communities and generating high-resolution datasets capturing both explicit and implicit participation.
content: This paper introduces FlexibleCommunity, an incentive-based energy management simulator for investigating demand-response strategies of communities and generating high-resolution datasets capturing both explicit and implicit participation. The simulator can be configured to represent an arbitrary number of buildings, enabling scalable modeling of communities with heterogeneous dwellings equipped with price-responsive heating systems of varying types and capacities. It also integrates photovoltaic (PV) systems, electric vehicles (EVs), and battery storage to represent multiple flexibility mechanisms. FlexibleCommunity includes stochastic occupant behavior to improve realism and capture uncertainty in energy use patterns. The generated datasets contain time-series data on energy consumption, price signals, weather conditions, and solar irradiance, supporting applications such as load forecasting and flexibility assessment. To improve accessibility, it includes a graphical user interface (GUI) for configuration, visualization, and dataset generation.

title: Developing Actual Occupancy Profiles for Mosques
summary: Building occupancy profiles are essential for optimizing energy performance, yet standardized data for mosques remains scarce despite their unique, intermittent usage patterns. This study addresses this gap by evaluating a cost-effective, r
content: Building occupancy profiles are essential for optimizing energy performance, yet standardized data for mosques remains scarce despite their unique, intermittent usage patterns. This study addresses this gap by evaluating a cost-effective, real-time occupancy monitoring system using Raspberry Pi and computer vision. By capturing headcount data at 30-second intervals, the system demonstrated high responsiveness in tracking complex dynamics within a mosque environment. The analysis reveals that weekend attendance generally exceeds weekday levels, with weekdays showing sharper post-prayer declines due to professional and academic obligations. A primary divergence occurs during the Friday Jummah congregation, which reached a peak of 110 occupants, saturating the hall’s capacity. This surge exhibited a wider temporal footprint than standard prayers due to the mandatory pre-prayer sermon (Khutbah). Quantitative results show that weekday occupancy peaked at 60 during the Maghrib prayer, while weekend peaks reached 75. On average, worshippers arrived 5 minutes before the prayer and departed 20 minutes after, resulting in a total stay of 25 minutes. These findings validate the system’s ability to provide high-resolution, empirical data, offering a foundation for demand-controlled environmental management and more energy-efficient operational strategies in religious facilities.

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no
content: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

title: Effect of spring maize hybrids on ruminal degradation kinetics of dry matter, fiber and protein in silages
summary: Increasing the role of home-grown forages in animal feeds is of utmost importance for a more appropriate recycling and re-utilization of nutrients, and to reduce dependency on imported concentrated ingredient and provide long-term sustainab
content: Increasing the role of home-grown forages in animal feeds is of utmost importance for a more appropriate recycling and re-utilization of nutrients, and to reduce dependency on imported concentrated ingredient and provide long-term sustainability to dairy production systems.However, with agricultural land shrinking and food sector competition increasing, efficient use of available land and feed resources is critical.In this regard, silage production from whole crop maize and optimizing its utilization in animal ration can play a key role by ensuring continuous and uniform supply of good quality forage throughout the year and optimizing animal productivity.In this context, current research was designed to investigate the rumen fermentation kinetics of dry matter (DM) and nutrients of maize silages produced from different genotypes of spring maize.Ten maize genotypes were cultivated for silage production in sixty plots within two fields with three replicates per field, using Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD), at the research fields of Livestock Research and Development Station Surezai Peshawar.The maize were grown under uniform growing condition using standard agronomic practices.Crop growth was monitored, and samples were taken from a 1 m long strip of two adjacent rows of each plot when the DM content reached 335 g/kg.The samples were chopped into small (1-1.5 cm) particles and fermented in 1.5 L silos.The silos were packed layer by layer and the compacted and closed air tightly.After 60 days silos were opened and subsamples were collected for in situ studies.The samples were air-dried in oven, ground (2 mm particle size) and stored for in situ trial.Samples (5 g) of each silage were incubated in the rumen of a cannulated cow for 0, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, and 36 hours to determine in situ fermentation kinetics.The residues and samples were analysed for DM, crude protein (CP), and neutral detergent fibre (NDF).The degradation rate of DM (Kdm) of maize genotypes varied from 1.99% in (P-3025W) to 5.72% (CS200).The effective rumen degradable DM (EDDM) varied from 44.05% in (P-30k08) to 36.22% in (CS200).The kd of CP (Kdcp) of maize hybrids ranged from 2.50% in (M-Garanan) to 8.83% (Azam).The effective rumen degradable CP (EDcp) ranged from 72.32% in P-2Y10 to 36.35% in 3025W.The kd-NDF of maize genotypes ranged from 1.56% (P-3025W) to 7.32% (M-Gorilla).The effective rumen degradable NDF (EDNDF) fraction varied from 36.07%(P-3025W) to 14.12% (P-2Y10).The results of this study revealed that the degradation of DM, CP, and NDF of maize silage in the rumen differed depending on maize cultivars, indicating that there is a higher potential for utilising this knowledge in ration design to improve livestock productivity.

title: Conscious coins: an interpretive structural approach to understanding behavioral drivers of green cryptocurrency investment
summary: Purpose This study systematically aims to explore and structures the key enablers driving green cryptocurrencies adoption. Design/methodology/approach The study uses interpretive structural modelling approach to delve into the complex inter
content: Purpose This study systematically aims to explore and structures the key enablers driving green cryptocurrencies adoption. Design/methodology/approach The study uses interpretive structural modelling approach to delve into the complex interplay between psychological, technological, financial and regulatory factors, revealing both direct and indirect influences on investment decisions. Findings Drawing on a comprehensive literature review and insights from 20 domain experts, the research identifies 19 critical factors influencing green cryptocurrency adoption. These factors are organised into a five-tier hierarchical structure, uncovering their causal relationships and classifying them according to their influence levels. Research limitations/implications The present research is constrained by expert-driven analysis, which may affect the objectivity of the findings. Further quantitative validation of the identified factor interrelationships is warranted. The exclusion of demographic and psychographic influences restricts user segmentation insights, while the static view limits generalisability. Practical implications From a practical perspective, the study provides actionable recommendations for businesses, policymakers and environmental advocates by helping to promote sustainable practices, address key barriers and foster a more resilient green cryptocurrency ecosystem. Social implications The study emphasises that advancing green cryptocurrency adoption can drive a collective shift towards sustainable digital finance, fostering eco-conscious investment behaviour, enhancing financial literacy on environmental responsibility and reinforcing the social norm of aligning technological innovation with sustainability values. Originality/value The findings contribute to the broader theoretical discourse on sustainable digital finance by integrating micro- and macro-level influences within a unified framework. Furthermore, the study introduces a novel conceptual model grounded in the means-end chain theory, offering deeper insights into the dynamics of green cryptocurrency investments.

title: Green finance investments in the era of geopolitical uncertainty: moderation and mediation effects
summary: Purpose This study investigates the effects of environmental knowledge, corporate social responsibility (CSR) scepticism and media intervention on willingness to invest in green finance products (WGF) through the mediation of greenwashing p
content: Purpose This study investigates the effects of environmental knowledge, corporate social responsibility (CSR) scepticism and media intervention on willingness to invest in green finance products (WGF) through the mediation of greenwashing perception. Furthermore, the study examines the moderating role of geopolitical uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 372 Islamic Bank customers via a questionnaire and evaluated using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study reported a positive relationship between environmental knowledge, CSR scepticism, media intervention and greenwashing perception. In addition, the results show a negative relationship between greenwashing perception and WGF. Furthermore, geopolitical uncertainty negatively moderated the relationship between greenwashing perception and WGF. Practical implications This study proposes pragmatic approaches for Islamic banks to enhance the adoption of green finance and effectively tackle greenwashing amid geopolitical uncertainty. By implementing focused sustainability education, individuals are empowered to make well-informed investment decisions and better understand greenwashing. Engaging in collaborative media initiatives and employing transparent marketing strategies can bolster trust among environmentally conscious customers, increasing their involvement in sustainable banking. Originality/value The article makes novel contributions by examining Islamic banking customers' opinions on green finance and their reactions to greenwashing amid geopolitical uncertainties. By incorporating variables such as environmental knowledge, CSR scepticism and media intervention, the study will provide insights into the behaviours related to sustainable finance in the context of Islamic banking. This study introduces innovative theoretical viewpoints to sustainable finance research through multi-theoretical frameworks.

title: Credible CSR and credit ratings: how state-led CSR enhances firm creditworthiness
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether participation in China’s large-scale, government-led corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative, the Targeted Poverty Alleviation (TPA) campaign, affects firm credit ratings. It also explores
content: Purpose This study aims to examine whether participation in China’s large-scale, government-led corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative, the Targeted Poverty Alleviation (TPA) campaign, affects firm credit ratings. It also explores the mechanisms through which such participation enhances creditworthiness. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel dataset of 1,177 listed firms in China from 2009 to 2021, the authors use coarsened exact matching (CEM) to construct a matched sample and then apply a staggered difference-in-differences (DiD) framework to estimate the causal effect of TPA participation on credit ratings. We also conduct mediation analyses to identify the roles of environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance and media reputation, and perform robustness checks including PSM-DiD, placebo tests and heterogeneity analyses. Findings Firms participating in the TPA campaign receive higher credit ratings. The effect is stronger among non-state-owned enterprises, firms in underdeveloped regions, and those rated by international joint-venture agencies. Greater investment intensity in the program further amplifies the benefit. Improved ESG performance and media favorability partially mediate the relationship, suggesting that rating agencies value the reputational and sustainability signals conveyed through government-aligned CSR. Research limitations/implications This study addresses the “credibility gap” in CSR by shifting focus from voluntary actions to high-visibility, state-monitored mandates like China’s TPA campaign. It demonstrates that in emerging markets, institutional legitimacy and political alignment are vital nonfinancial determinants of credit risk. Future research should examine how macroeconomic risks moderate this relationship and explore other firm-level outcomes. In addition, testing the generalizability of these findings in different institutional contexts is essential. Finally, as data improves, explicitly comparing the differential impacts of voluntary versus government-led CSR on firm performance will provide deeper insights into corporate sustainability and creditworthiness. Practical implications The findings provide insights for firms seeking to improve creditworthiness and for policymakers aiming to align CSR incentives with development goals in emerging economies. For corporate managers, the findings demonstrate that aligning CSR strategies with national development goals can yield tangible financial benefits, specifically improved credit ratings and reduced borrowing costs. For investors and credit rating agencies, the study highlights that government-endorsed CSR provides a more reliable and externally validated benchmark for assessing a firm’s long-term stability and operational risk than opaque, self-reported composite CSR scores. Social implications The research underscores the effectiveness of public-private collaborations in addressing key social challenges, such as extreme poverty. By mobilizi

title: Searching for nearby supermassive black hole binaries with GRAVITY
summary: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with <16.5% for <9.2%. We compared these results with predictions from the Horizon-AG
content: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with <16.5% for <9.2%. We compared these results with predictions from the Horizon-AGN simulation, finding comparable binary fractions. We also noted that the expected fraction strongly depends on the assumed distribution of individual SMBH accretion rates within binaries, which is currently unresolved in cosmological models. Our results demonstrate the potential of infrared interferometry to identify parsec-scale binary AGN candidates. Moreover, the results motivate future + observations to expand the sample and follow up on known candidates in order to help confirm their nature and distinguish genuine binaries from asymmetric nuclear structures. on Very Large Telescope Interferometer. We investigated parsec-scale asymmetric emission by modeling the squared visibilities and closure phases with a single circular Gaussian component plus a background point source for the central AGN, and we searched for additional compact companions through grid-based binary models. The robustness of the search was validated using injection--recovery simulations and point-spread-function diagnostics. We identified several features in the initial significance maps, but only one candidate of the 20, NGC 3783, showed a persistent compact asymmetry, corresponding to an observed incidence of 5%. If NGC 3783 is interpreted as a binary AGN, the Poissonian one-sided 1σ upper limit we derived is f_ ̊m bin binaries among bright nearby AGN (K<12.5) at separations of sim1--100 pc.
