title: Structural Inertia of Energy Inefficiency: Can Islamic Finance Close the Energy Efficiency Gap in Java's Provincial Economies, Indonesia?
summary: Java faces a dilemma between the demand for high economic growth and a chronic dependence on fossil energy. This study examines the persistence of the energy efficiency gap across five provinces in Java from 2017 to 2023 and tests the role
content: Java faces a dilemma between the demand for high economic growth and a chronic dependence on fossil energy. This study examines the persistence of the energy efficiency gap across five provinces in Java from 2017 to 2023 and tests the role of Islamic finance in narrowing it. Energy efficiency is measured using the Slack-Based Measure Data Envelopment Analysis (SBM-DEA) with undesirable output. The persistence of the gap and its determinants are estimated using the one-step System Generalised Method of Moments (GMM). The results reveal pronounced performance polarisation among provinces. DKI Jakarta, East Java, and West Java reach the best-practice level, whereas Banten and Central Java remain locked at low efficiency levels. The energy efficiency gap is highly persistent, with a coefficient of 0.748. The adjustment rate is only 25.2% per year, with a half-life of approximately 2.4 years. Green sukuk significantly narrows the gap, while economic growth has no significant effect. These findings indicate that Islamic finance can help close the energy-efficiency gap but operates within strong structural inertia. Energy policy should therefore be differentiated across provinces, and green sukuk allocation should target provinces with the widest gaps.

title: Viscophoretic Nanoparticle Transport
summary: Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and sets the diffusivity of suspended particles. When viscosity varies in space, diffusivity does too; under isothermal conditions, stochastic thermodynamics predicts a particle drift term v =
content: Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and sets the diffusivity of suspended particles. When viscosity varies in space, diffusivity does too; under isothermal conditions, stochastic thermodynamics predicts a particle drift term v = ∂xD(x) arising from position-dependent viscosity. Here, we impose steep, stable viscosity gradients in a microfluidic channel and directly image nanoparticle motion at the single-particle level using high-resolution microscopy. We find viscous-gradient-driven drift velocities that exceed Stokes–Einstein-based estimates, and we quantify this discrepancy through simultaneous measurements of local diffusivity and drift extracted from the same trajectories. We then illustrate how such controlled gradients enable passive focusing in a phoretic trap that combines viscophoresis with diffusiophoresis. Our measurements provide a quantitative single-particle characterization of viscous-gradient-driven transport that is of importance in any system and any application exhibiting viscosity gradients, from membrane separation processes to inter- and intracellular biomolecular transport.

title: Ozone decrease observed in the upper atmosphere following the 11 May 2024 Mother's Day and the 8 June solar storms
summary: On 11 May 2024, a succession of coronal mass ejections merged and struck the Earth, inducing large-scale perturbations in the magnetosphere. During this event, satellite observations revealed that an extreme geomagnetic storm occurred along
content: On 11 May 2024, a succession of coronal mass ejections merged and struck the Earth, inducing large-scale perturbations in the magnetosphere. During this event, satellite observations revealed that an extreme geomagnetic storm occurred alongside a moderate solar proton event (SPE). Simultaneously, atmospheric ozone and temperature were measured by the AURA/MLS instrument. In this work, we present the first observations of the effect of the extreme storm of May and the subsequent SPE of 8 June on ozone concentration and temperature throughout the atmosphere. The observations of the MLS instrument show that the event of May led to stronger depletion of O 3 in the mesosphere and lower thermosphere (MLT) than in June and that noticeable depletion mainly occurred in the Southern Hemisphere. This difference is explained by the type and intensity of energetic particle precipitation (EPP) that occurred during the two events, with both protons and electrons in May and only protons in June. In May, mesospheric ozone depletion peaked at 60 % at 80 km and reached 30 % at 75 km, lasting for 5 d. The SPE of June also caused a decrease of mesospheric ozone that lasted for 2 d down to 70 km. Below 60 km, no significant changes in ozone volume mixing ratio (vmr) were observed after either event.

title: Generalized Wright Analysis: Stochastics and Applications
summary: In this paper, we investigate the stochastic counterpart of the generalized Wright analysis introduced in Beghin et al.~ in Integral Equations and Operator Theory, 97, 2025. We define a new class of non-Gaussian and non-Markovian processes,
content: In this paper, we investigate the stochastic counterpart of the generalized Wright analysis introduced in Beghin et al.~ in Integral Equations and Operator Theory, 97, 2025. We define a new class of non-Gaussian and non-Markovian processes, called the generalized Fox-H process, which extends well-known processes such as fractional Brownian motion and generalized grey Brownian motion. We study their joint probability density and covariance, showing the stationarity of their increments. In addition, this process has H{\"o}lder continuous paths and is represented as a time-change of fractional Brownian motion. We characterize the generalized Fox-$H$ noise as an element in the distribution space $(\mathcal{S})^{-1}_{\mu_\Psi}$. We conclude by establishing the existence of local times and discussing their anomalous diffusion properties. MSC Classification: 33E12 , 60E05 , 60G18 , 60G20 , 60G22

title: Combining geodetic data and summer MODIS albedo anomalies for annual glacier mass balance estimation
summary: Annual glacier mass balance time series are essential for understanding the impacts of climate change on glacierized regions. Satellite-based observations enable consistent and regionally comprehensive monitoring of glacier mass balance. Wh
content: Annual glacier mass balance time series are essential for understanding the impacts of climate change on glacierized regions. Satellite-based observations enable consistent and regionally comprehensive monitoring of glacier mass balance. While geodetic methods yield robust estimates over decadal timescales, their application at annual resolution is limited by measurement uncertainty. In this study, we propose an approach that combines 20 years geodetic mass balance data with glacier-wide average summer albedo anomalies from MODIS to produce reliable annual glacier mass balance estimates for land-terminating glaciers. We generated time series from 2000 to 2019 for 2748 glaciers across three regions: the European Alps, Scandinavia, and Svalbard. Validation against 1108 available in-situ mass balance measurements yielded root mean square errors (RMSE) of 0.44, 0.72, and 0.39 m w.e. and coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.62, 0.54, and 0.44 for the European Alps, Scandinavia, and Svalbard, respectively. These results demonstrate the method's effectiveness and its potential for application in other glacierized regions.

title: Sub-shot-noise emission statistics of a CW-excited single photon source
summary: Shot noise sets a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of classical optical measurements, with coherent emitters achieving the lowest possible shot-noise level. Emission from sub-Poissonian light provides a pathway to surpass this limit, an
content: Shot noise sets a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of classical optical measurements, with coherent emitters achieving the lowest possible shot-noise level. Emission from sub-Poissonian light provides a pathway to surpass this limit, and single-photon sources provide a natural platform for generating such light. However, it is commonly assumed that off-resonance continuously excited solid-state single-photon sources exhibit Poissonian statistics over large exposure periods, owing to their strong coupling to the host lattice. In this work, a theoretical model of a continuously driven two-level single-photon source is developed, treating both excitation and radiative decay as stochastic processes. The analysis demonstrates that photon emission can display sub-Poissonian statistics when excitation and decay rates are comparable, showing that continuous excitation does not inherently preclude nonclassical emission. The model is further extended to include finite detection efficiency and detector dead time, illustrating how these practical non-idealities can affect the experimental observation of sub-Poissonian statistics.

title: Metal-dependent thermodynamics of histidine-mediated protein immobilization revealed by quantum chemical calculations
summary: Quantum chemistry and experiment show that His-mediated enzyme immobilization is governed by first-shell metal–imidazole thermodynamics, coordination number and Fe 3+ hydrolysis, reproducing the observed order Ni 2+ > Zn 2+ > Co 2+ > Fe 3+
content: Quantum chemistry and experiment show that His-mediated enzyme immobilization is governed by first-shell metal–imidazole thermodynamics, coordination number and Fe 3+ hydrolysis, reproducing the observed order Ni 2+ > Zn 2+ > Co 2+ > Fe 3+ .

title: Mitigating numerical stiffness in least-squares formulations of elliptic PDEs for physics-informed neural networks
summary: Residual-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combine interior PDE and boundary residuals using mean squared errors (MSE). For elliptic boundary value problems, these formulations can show numerical stiffness causing slow training
content: Residual-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combine interior PDE and boundary residuals using mean squared errors (MSE). For elliptic boundary value problems, these formulations can show numerical stiffness causing slow training. We study a residual formulation that combines an H 0 − 1 interior residual with an H 1 / 2 boundary residual for nonzero Dirichlet boundary data. For finite-dimensional test spaces in H 1 ( Ω ) , we introduce two finite-dimensional approximations, the subspace-induced negative-order Sobolev seminorm (SINOS) and its dual counterpart (D-SINOS), and quantify their stiffness through a stiffness ratio defined with respect to the H 1 -norm. We establish continuity and coercivity estimates for both formulations and show that, for polynomial spaces of degree n , the stiffness ratios of SINOS and D-SINOS grow at most as O ( n 2 ) and O ( 1 ) , respectively. Numerical experiments recover rates of n 2.00 and n 0.05 , compared with n 6.95 and n 5.68 for MSE and L 2 -based residual losses. PINN experiments for the Poisson equation, a stationary convection–diffusion–reaction problem, and the stationary incompressible Navier–Stokes equations show that SINOS achieves consistently strong convergence and accuracy, while D-SINOS improves over MSE but does not attain the performance of SINOS. These results demonstrate that negative-order Sobole

title: Suppressing cavity frequency noise using a Kerr nonlinearity
summary: Resonance-frequency fluctuations can limit the sensitivity and stability of superconducting microwave cavities used for qubit readout, optomechanical displacement sensing, and magnetic flux detection. Here, we demonstrate the suppression of
content: Resonance-frequency fluctuations can limit the sensitivity and stability of superconducting microwave cavities used for qubit readout, optomechanical displacement sensing, and magnetic flux detection. Here, we demonstrate the suppression of resonance-frequency fluctuations by locking a noisy nonlinear superconducting microwave cavity to a strong pump tone. The Kerr nonlinearity of this system, whereby the resonance frequency depends on the intracavity field amplitude, gives rise to an intrinsic feedback mechanism that enables passive stabilization without active external feedback. Using two-tone spectroscopy, we experimentally characterize the intrinsic nonlinear feedback mechanism and investigate its temporal stability through Allan deviation analysis. The frequency fluctuations of the locked cavity mode are reduced by nearly two orders of magnitude, reaching the 1/f noise floor, without continuous frequency tracking or active control. Kerr locking provides a general approach for self-stabilizing nonlinear microwave resonators by suppressing low-frequency cavity noise while preserving sensitivity to signals outside the locking bandwidth. This approach may benefit a broad range of systems, including superconducting quantum interference device-based resonators, optomechanical devices, and parametric amplifiers.

title: Effective neutrino mass and apparent phantom crossing
summary: Recent cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses have reached, and in some analyses fallen below, the minimum value implied by the normal mass ordering, suggesting a possible tension with neutrino-oscillation measurements. We i
content: Recent cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses have reached, and in some analyses fallen below, the minimum value implied by the normal mass ordering, suggesting a possible tension with neutrino-oscillation measurements. We investigate whether this discrepancy can be alleviated in a mass-varying-neutrino (MaVaN) cosmology in which a canonical pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson (pNGB) drives late-time cosmic acceleration and controls the masses of massive neutrinos through an exponential coupling. Using current cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and type Ia supernova data, we reconstruct the neutrino-mass evolution and show that the cosmologically inferred effective neutrino mass can fall below the present-day normal-ordering floor while remaining consistent with oscillation constraints. The same interaction produces a distinctive late-time signature, with 96% of the posterior expansion histories exhibiting a crossing of the apparent phantom divide, wapp = −1, at zcross = 0.90+0−0.2813 within 68% C.L. The underlying scalar field nevertheless remains canonical, with wϕ ≥−1. Our results therefore show that neutrino mass variation can simultaneously alleviate the apparent neutrino-mass tension and generate the phantom-crossing behavior favored by current cosmological data, without introducing a phantom field or violating the null energy condition.

title: The Digitalization–Fraud Paradox: Asymmetric Effects of Strategic Digital Orientation
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping organizational governance, yet its ethical implications for corporate misconduct remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how strategic digital orientation (SDO), defined as a firm’s strategi
content: Digital transformation is reshaping organizational governance, yet its ethical implications for corporate misconduct remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how strategic digital orientation (SDO), defined as a firm’s strategic commitment to developing and integrating digital capabilities, is associated with corporate fraud. Using 34,320 firm-year observations of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2022, we construct a multidimensional measure of SDO through textual analysis of Management Discussion and Analysis disclosures and measure corporate fraud using complementary regulatory databases. The results provide robust evidence of an asymmetric relationship between SDO and corporate fraud. Firms exhibiting relatively low to intermediate levels of SDO are associated with higher observed fraud risk, whereas the positive association weakens at higher levels of SDO. Moderation analyses show that internal control quality and innovation capability weaken the positive association between SDO and fraud, potentially by reducing governance misalignment associated with digital transformation. Mediation analyses reveal multiple competing governance mechanisms—audit quality, information asymmetry, technology intensity—with indirect effects that are statistically significant but economically modest. These findings are consistent with an asymmetric ethical risk framework in which technological opacity, accountability diffusion, and governance lag create ethical vulnerabilities that are partially offset by stronger monitoring and governance capabilities at higher levels of SDO. This research contributes to business ethics research by demonstrating how digital transformation reshapes accountability structures, redistributes moral responsibility, and generates asymmetric patterns of misconduct risk across firms exhibiting different levels of SDO.

title: ArchaeoBench: a large-scale archaeological question-answering benchmark for large language models
summary: Despite the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in data-intensive disciplines, archaeology lacks public, large-scale benchmarks, and its spatio-temporally fragmented knowledge resists integration into model parameters. Here we in
content: Despite the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in data-intensive disciplines, archaeology lacks public, large-scale benchmarks, and its spatio-temporally fragmented knowledge resists integration into model parameters. Here we introduce ArchaeoBench, a hierarchically structured benchmark built from 63 official excavation reports across 20 Chinese provinces, comprising over 9.2 million training question-answer pairs and 1,698 evaluation questions spanning multiple cognitive levels. Fine-tuning seven open-source LLMs on this benchmark yields substantial gains, approaching commercial baselines on several question types, whereas chain-of-thought prompting brings only marginal improvements on fact- and text-grounded questions, suggesting that archaeological question answering is constrained primarily by access to reliable domain knowledge rather than reasoning depth. Motivated by this finding, we propose a knowledge-graph-based retrieval-augmented generation framework that injects curated structured evidence to enhance spatio-temporal and cultural-linkage reasoning. ArchaeoBench converts excavation reports into reusable, machine-readable knowledge infrastructure for the discipline.

title: Dimensions of Brand Activism as Predictors of Customer Purchase Intention: A Study of Multinational Brands in Nigeria
summary: The research evaluated the effect of brand activism on customer purchase intention toward multinational companies’ products in South-West Nigeria. The research adopted a cross-sectional survey research design. The study's population was lim
content: The research evaluated the effect of brand activism on customer purchase intention toward multinational companies’ products in South-West Nigeria. The research adopted a cross-sectional survey research design. The study's population was limited to customers of multinational companies in South-West Nigeria. The sample size of 384 participants was selected for the study. It was determined using the Cochran formula. The study used the judgmental sampling technique. The data for this study were generated from the primary source through the use of a structured questionnaire. The study used internal consistency reliability. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical techniques in order to arrive at a conclusion. The findings revealed that value-driven communications have a positive and significant effect on customer purchase intention (β = 0.139, p < 0.05), indicating that ethical and value-based messaging can influence consumers, though with a relatively modest impact. Brand authenticity emerged as the strongest predictor of customer purchase intention (β = 0.721, p < 0.05), underscoring the critical role of perceived sincerity, consistency, and credibility in shaping consumer trust and emotional attachment. In contrast, woke-washing was found to have a negative and significant effect on customer purchase intention (β = −0.080, p < 0.05), suggesting that consumers penalize brands perceived to engage in superficial or insincere activism. The study concludes that while value-driven communications are important, authentic and consistent brand activism is far more influential in driving purchase intentions, whereas woke-washing undermines trust and weakens brand–consumer relationships. It therefore recommends that multinational companies align activism messages with tangible actions, prioritize authenticity, and ensure transparency and long-term commitment to social causes to enhance customer purchase intention.

title: ESG Information Credibility and Retail Investors’ Allocation Intention: The Roles of Sustainability Awareness and Greenwashing Perception
source: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
summary: Purpose – This study examines the relationship between ESG information credibility and retail investors’ ESG investment allocation intention, considering sustainability awareness and greenwashing perception as potential mediators.Design/met
content: Purpose – This study examines the relationship between ESG information credibility and retail investors’ ESG investment allocation intention, considering sustainability awareness and greenwashing perception as potential mediators.Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among Indonesian retail investors from January to April 2026. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4, including direct, indirect, serial mediation, and predictive analyses using PLSpredict.Finding/Results – ESG information credibility is positively associated with investment allocation intention, sustainability awareness, and greenwashing perception. Sustainability awareness positively relates to greenwashing perception but not significantly to allocation intention. Unexpectedly, greenwashing perception positively relates to allocation intention. Mediation through sustainability awareness is insignificant, whereas mediation through greenwashing perception and serial mediation are statistically significant. However, these indirect associations do not confirm the hypothesized mechanisms because key relationships differ from their predicted directions.Originality/Value – This study highlights the complex relationships among ESG credibility, sustainability awareness, greenwashing perception, and investment intentions. It challenges conventional assumptions about greenwashing as an investment deterrent and emphasizes the distinction between statistical mediation and theoretical confirmation, providing directions for further research on investor behavior and ESG information exposure. intentions.

title: Digital Trade Transitions: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Economic Networks and Innovation Ecosystems
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INNOVATIONS & RESEARCH ANALYSIS
summary: Digital trade has emerged as an innovative economic strategy that transcends traditional and cross-border electronic commerce. Research Objectives: This research performs an extensive bibliometric examination to review and synthesize availa
content: Digital trade has emerged as an innovative economic strategy that transcends traditional and cross-border electronic commerce. Research Objectives: This research performs an extensive bibliometric examination to review and synthesize available research at the convergence of digital commerce, international economic networks, and innovation systems. Methodology: Employing the Scopus database, the study investigates a collection of 877 academic publications from 2010-2026 adhering to PRISMA guidelines. To extract the data, four crucial phrases “International Business”, “Global Trade”, “Economic Integration” and “Innovation” are utilised. Through performance analysis and scientific mapping methodologies, using VOSviewer software, the researcher examined prominent cited authors, disciplines, top universities, significant journals, citation analysis, bibliographic network of leading nations and keyword clusters over time. Key Findings: The results indicate a notable increase in scholarly production 158 in 2025 regarding digital trade, propelled by technological upheaval in this domain. Top Scopus subject areas include ‘Business, Management and Accounting’ having 383 documents, ‘Social Sciences, 267’, ‘Economics, Econometrics and Finance’, 261 and so on. Co-citation of most cited authors include Porter M.E., Goto M., Teece D.J. among top most productive and quoted writers with highest link strength. United States lead with 105 documents, China 86, India 66 followed by other 107 nations. Most frequent keywords are ‘International Trade’ with 361 occurrences, ‘Innovation’, 166, ‘Sustainable Development’ 126, ‘Global Market’, 72 and so on. The research reveals a significant transformation from company-focused evaluations of digital trade adoption to knowledge dissemination and sustainable economic integration, unveiling a vibrant and swiftly evolving domain. Implications: The bibliometric identification of AI, blockchain, and platform-based business models as dominant clusters offers a clear directive for MNEs. The findings have serious implications for policymakers, business strategies, and innovators. Further studies need to be done to look at the impact of digital trade shift on specific industries such as green energy technology, FinTech, and Industry 5.0.

title: Gendered Experiences of Crop Loss in Rice Farming, India
summary: This study examines the gendered impacts of rice crop loss in Odisha, India, drawing on evidence from 409 farming households across eight rice-producing districts. Using household surveys, focus group discussions, and key informant intervie
content: This study examines the gendered impacts of rice crop loss in Odisha, India, drawing on evidence from 409 farming households across eight rice-producing districts. Using household surveys, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews, the research explores how crop loss affects livelihoods, food security, health, education, migration, and household wellbeing. The study identifies significant gender disparities in exposure to crop loss impacts and access to recovery resources, with women disproportionately affected by increased unpaid labour, food insecurity, financial stress, and limited access to insurance, compensation, and advisory services. The findings highlight the need for gender-responsive policies and interventions to strengthen resilience, improve equitable access to support systems, and promote inclusive recovery among rice-farming households.

title: Financing Green Residential Retrofits: An Ex Ante Cost–Benefit Analysis of Energy Affordability in Thessaloniki
summary: This study appraises external-wall insulation for lower-income apartment households in Thessaloniki under financing assumptions drawn from Greece’s Exoikonomo 2025 programme. It adapts the C40 Healthy and Efficient Retrofitted Buildings (HE
content: This study appraises external-wall insulation for lower-income apartment households in Thessaloniki under financing assumptions drawn from Greece’s Exoikonomo 2025 programme. It adapts the C40 Healthy and Efficient Retrofitted Buildings (HERB) model using regional household profiles, census floor areas and Greek multifamily archetypes. Under the engineering benchmark, discounted retail bill savings do not cover installation costs for either insulation package. The lower-cost package can exceed break-even in the partial economic appraisal when avoided direct carbon emissions are valued at European Investment Bank shadow prices, depending on rebound and the costs included. Grants improve household financial returns, but the higher-cost package has negative mean household returns at the lower ordinary grant rate. At a binding grant ceiling, the lower-cost package reaches more dwellings and delivers greater aggregate bill savings. Targeting the higher-cost package by affordability-gap relief yields a slightly larger reduction in the gap. The estimates describe conditional programme outcomes rather than observed energy-poverty reduction.

title: Global Labor Market and Artificial Intelligence (AI) WILL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) CAUSE JOB CUTS?
source: Innovative Research in the Modern World
summary: This article investigates whether the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models will lead to widespread job cuts across the global economy. Drawing on contemporary labor economics and international instituti
content: This article investigates whether the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models will lead to widespread job cuts across the global economy. Drawing on contemporary labor economics and international institutional forecasts, it distinguishes between task-level automation and full occupational displacement, analyzing vulnerable routine and clerical professions alongside emerging AI-augmented roles. The paper further examines skills transformation in language and knowledge industries, cross-country disparities between advanced and emerging economies, and risks of wage polarization, demonstrating that proactive reskilling, inclusive governance, and human-AI collaboration are essential to prevent structural unemployment.

title: Financing Broader Sustainable Transition: Green Finance Policies and Cross-Regional Green Innovation Spillovers Along Supply Chains
summary: In the pursuit of sustainable development, whether green finance policies can transcend geographical boundaries and reshape resource allocation to generate cross-regional green innovation spillovers along supply chains deserves in-depth inv
content: In the pursuit of sustainable development, whether green finance policies can transcend geographical boundaries and reshape resource allocation to generate cross-regional green innovation spillovers along supply chains deserves in-depth investigation. This study conducts an empirical analysis using a difference-in-differences (DID) approach. The results show that: (1) the establishment of green finance pilot zones in the regions where upstream supply chain firms are located significantly promotes green innovation among downstream firms outside the pilot zones, confirming the existence of a cross-regional spillover effect of green finance policies. (2) The establishment of green finance pilot zones significantly alleviates financing constraints for firms within the pilot zones. Supported by a "push-pull" theoretical framework, credit transmission among supply chain firms provides a channel for capital flows, enabling the incentive effects generated by green finance policies to spill over to downstream firms outside the pilot zones. (3) Further analysis reveals that the cross-regional green innovation spillover effect driven by positive corporate credit transmission is influenced by multiple factors at the firm, supply chain, and environmental levels. These findings not only provide theoretical insights into corporate green transformation but also offer empirical support for leveraging green finance policies to achieve broader sustainable development goals (SDGs).

title: A Formal Model of Wealth–Power Feedback with Eight Classes: Thresholds of Elite Capture, Class Mobility and Policy Counter-Levers, with an Illustrative Calibration for Urban Punjab
summary: This paper develops a dynamic political-economy model in which wealth and political power reinforce one another across an ordered structure of eight economic classes. Each class converts population, wealth and organisational capacity into p
content: This paper develops a dynamic political-economy model in which wealth and political power reinforce one another across an ordered structure of eight economic classes. Each class converts population, wealth and organisational capacity into political power; power is converted into policy rents through a contest whose decisiveness is a property of institutions; and rents, together with power-dependent privileged returns, feed back into the distribution of wealth. Class mobility responds to the concentration of power, closing a second loop between who governs and who can rise. The model yields a single summary statistic, the Wealth–Power Feedback Index , which combines the wealth elasticity of power (), the decisiveness of rent contests (), the share of wealth reallocated through politics (), the strength of market income (), the privileged-return premium () and the rate at which captured rents are clawed back and redistributed (). We prove that a pluralist steady state exists for all parameter values, that it is stable if and only if in the symmetric benchmark, and that when the rent elasticity exceeds one in the purely political economy, the plural steady state is unstable and a single class absorbs the rent stream. We further prove that concentration of power shifts the stationary class distribution downward in the sense of first-order stochastic dominance, hollowing out the upper and middle classes. An illustrative calibration to a stylised eight-class urban Punjab economy shows that the observed distribution can sit on a knife-edge (), that heterogeneity in organisational capacity lowers the capture threshold relative to the symmetric benchmark, and that a rent levy that does not reduce can rotate rather than dissolve elite dominance. Institutional reforms that lower the decisiveness of discretionary allocation and the money-to-influence elasticity are the most robust counter-levers. The framework provides a formal backbone for an eight-class approach to socio-economic public policy and a programme for empirical estimation.

title: Environmental Improvements in Developing Economies: A Multi Sectoral Analysis of Policy, Technology, and Community Action in Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: This PhD seminar paper critically examines the multifaceted landscape of environmental improvements in Nigeria, positioning it as a representative case study for developing economies grappling with the dual pressures of rapid development an
content: This PhD seminar paper critically examines the multifaceted landscape of environmental improvements in Nigeria, positioning it as a representative case study for developing economies grappling with the dual pressures of rapid development and ecological degradation. Moving beyond a purely technical assessment, the paper employs a multi sectoral lens to analyze interventions across renewable energy adoption, sustainable waste management, water resource restoration, innovative infrastructure, and ecological reclamation. Through an in-depth analysis of six distinct case studies, ranging from urban solar PV integration to the great green wall reforestation program in northern Nigeria, the paper evaluates the efficacy, scalability, and socio-economic impacts of current environmental strategies. The research adopts a socio-technical systems approach, integrating insights from Ecological Modernization Theory, Integrated Sustainable Waste Management, and Environmental Justice frameworks. The findings reveal a complex picture: while innovative pilot projects and policy frameworks demonstrate significant potential for positive impact, their success is often undermined by systemic barriers including inconsistent policy enforcement, infrastructural deficits, high upfront costs, and insufficient community engagement. Successful interventions, such as the Sokoto River restoration project and the waste-to-wealth road technology demonstrate the critical importance of aligning technological innovation with robust governance, community participation, and institutional champions. The paper argues for a paradigm shift towards integrated, community-centered approaches that synergize technological innovation with robust governance and local empowerment to achieve durable environmental improvements. It concludes with a set of evidence-based policy recommendations spanning governance strengthening, innovative financing, human capital development, and enhanced monitoring frameworks.

title: Gender just policies for urban development: Depletion of resettled women domestic workers in Mumbai
summary: This paper examines the sustained gendered consequences of urban resettlement in Mumbai, India, through a case study of women domestic workers resettled in the Lallubhai Compound. Using a feminist social reproduction lens that reveals deple
content: This paper examines the sustained gendered consequences of urban resettlement in Mumbai, India, through a case study of women domestic workers resettled in the Lallubhai Compound. Using a feminist social reproduction lens that reveals depletion through social reproduction, it analyses how resettlement to historically under-resourced areas farther from their workplaces, based on the World Bank-endorsed Resettlement and Rehabilitation (R&R) policy, reshaped the livelihoods and social reproduction strategies of resettled domestic workers’ households. The paper shows how women have absorbed the material and embodied consequences of inadequate infrastructure necessary for social reproduction and the lack of viable livelihood opportunities at the resettlement site, resulting in a cumulative depletion of their capacities. It argues that urban policies can advance equitable development and gender-just outcomes only by recognising women’s social reproductive labour as foundational to urban life, rather than transferring its costs onto informal workers’ households in ways that deepen, rather than redress, urban inequities.

title: Impact of E-Logistics Service Quality on Customer Satisfaction and Loyalty in Sri Lanka
summary: The increase in online purchases has significantly increased the need for e-logistics services. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the impact of e-logistics service quality on customer satisfaction and loyalty. However, i
content: The increase in online purchases has significantly increased the need for e-logistics services. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the impact of e-logistics service quality on customer satisfaction and loyalty. However, it was discovered that there has not been much research on the quality of e-logistics services in Sri Lanka. The present study aims to fill this gap in the literature. In order to conduct this research Order Accuracy (OA), Timeliness (T), Order Discrepancy Handling (ODH), and Information Quality (IQ) have been taken as the variables of the e-logistics service quality. A structured questionnaire was employed to collect data from 304 Sri Lankan individuals who make online purchases. The results were analyzed using the SPSS Statistical Software. While timeliness was found to have no direct impact on customer loyalty, information quality, order discrepancy handling, and order accuracy were discovered to have a significant positive relationship with customer loyalty. According to the mediation analysis using the Sobel test, customer satisfaction partially mediates the nexus between order accuracy and customer loyalty, information quality and customer loyalty, and order discrepancy handling and customer loyalty while customer satisfaction fully mediates the relationship between timeliness and customer loyalty. Moreover, the finding of the research revealed that order accuracy is the most influential e-logistics service quality factor. This research provides implications for the e-commerce industry to overcome managerial inefficiencies in the delivery of high-quality e-logistics services and raise the level of customer loyalty towards the organization.

title: Pathways to Cleaner Air and Heat Adaptation by 2050: Reducing environmental exposure, strengthening climate resilience, and accelerating sustainable development
summary: Cleaner air and heat adaptation should be pursued as interconnected development priorities rather than as separate environmental policy objectives. Across 46 pages, this H Heuristics research report develops an environmental exposure reduct
content: Cleaner air and heat adaptation should be pursued as interconnected development priorities rather than as separate environmental policy objectives. Across 46 pages, this H Heuristics research report develops an environmental exposure reduction framework—decomposing expected harm into hazard, exposure, and vulnerability—and evaluates ten pathway clusters spanning clean power, zero-emission transport, clean cooking, industrial and agricultural reform, waste and fire management, urban greening and blue infrastructure, cool roofs and passive design, efficient and equitable cooling, heat-health early warning, and workplace protections. Applying the Development Multiplier and the six H Heuristics concepts, it maps synergies, trade-offs, illustrative scenarios to 2050, financing architectures, regional pathways, and a 2026–2050 implementation roadmap.

title: Cocoa bean shells at regulatory-compliant inclusion levels in finishing beef cattle diet: effects on physiological status, methane emissions, meat quality, and productive performance
summary: This study aimed to evaluate whether the inclusion of cocoa bean shells (CBS) in finishing diets could improve physiological status and meat quality of an autochthonous cattle breed without negatively affecting animal performance and carcas
content: This study aimed to evaluate whether the inclusion of cocoa bean shells (CBS) in finishing diets could improve physiological status and meat quality of an autochthonous cattle breed without negatively affecting animal performance and carcass traits. Thirty Sardo-Bruna cattle (15 females and 15 males) were assigned to three dietary treatments: a control diet without supplementation (CON), a control diet supplemented with 150 g · animal -1 · d -1 of CBS (LCBS), and a control diet supplemented with 300 g · animal -1 · d -1 of CBS (HCBS). The trial lasted six months, during which body weight (BW) was recorded monthly, and average daily gain (ADG) was calculated to assess growth performance. Blood samples were collected during the experimental period and at slaughter to assess hematological, biochemical, and serum protein parameters. At slaughter, carcass weight and yield were recorded, and samples of Longissimus thoracis et lumborum muscle were collected for the evaluation of proximate composition, fatty acid (FA) profile, cooking loss, and drip loss. Meat color and pH were also evaluated. CBS supplementation did not affect blood parameters, except for eosinophils and calcium concentration, which showed a non-linear response with differences detected only in the LCBS group. CBS inclusion did not affect proximate composition, pH, cooking loss, or drip loss. However, dietary treatment modified the FA profile. Polyunsaturated FA omega-3 (PUFA n-3) were higher (P = 0.01) in the HCBS group compared to the CON and LCBS groups [0.59, 0.38, and 0.43 g/100 of FA methyl esters (FAME)]. The color measured in the Rectus abdominis muscle revealed a difference only for the b* parameter, which was lower in LCBS compared to CON and HCBS groups (P = 0.03). CBS supplementation did not affect BW, ADG, and carcass traits. Overall, the inclusion of CBS at the tested levels did not improve the physiological status but induced favorable changes in the meat FA profile. Moreover, the absence of detrimental effects on animal health, growth performance, slaughter yield, and carcass characteristics supports the potential use of CBS as a viable by-product ingredient in finishing diets for beef cattle.

title: Implementing hybrid telehealth for cardiometabolic disease in a pioneering Latin American digital hospital: a retrospective cohort study
summary: Hybrid telehealth has emerged as a promising strategy for chronic disease management, yet evidence from long-term implementation in resource-constrained health systems remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world effectivene
content: Hybrid telehealth has emerged as a promising strategy for chronic disease management, yet evidence from long-term implementation in resource-constrained health systems remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world effectiveness of a clinician-led hybrid telehealth programme compared with conventional in-person care among adults with chronic cardiometabolic diseases, focusing primarily on therapeutic goal attainment and secondarily on clinical complications, healthcare utilisation, and mortality. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 542 adults with chronic cardiometabolic diseases receiving either hybrid telehealth or conventional in-person care. The primary outcome was therapeutic goal attainment, defined as the simultaneous achievement of all disease-specific therapeutic targets applicable to each patient’s diagnosed conditions during the final year of follow-up. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to estimate the average treatment effect in the overlap population. Hybrid telehealth was associated with a higher probability of simultaneously achieving all applicable disease-specific therapeutic targets compared with conventional in-person care (66.4% vs. 13.3%; RR 5.00, 95% CI 2.81–8.89). Lower cumulative occurrence of incident complications (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.13–0.48) and Non-communicable disease (NCD)-related hospitalisation (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.08–0.32) was also observed. However, no statistically significant differences were found in all-cause hospitalisation (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.50–1.09), all-cause emergency visits (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.69–1.27), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.03–1.19). Findings were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses, although unequal follow-up duration and limited propensity-score overlap warrant cautious interpretation. Among patients in the overlap population, hybrid telehealth was associated with improved therapeutic goal attainment and lower cumulative occurrence of selected cardiometabolic complications and NCD-related healthcare utilisation. However, no statistically significant differences were observed in all-cause healthcare utilisation or mortality. These observational findings suggest potential benefits of hybrid telehealth for long-term cardiometabolic disease management but require confirmation in prospective studies with comparable follow-up periods and broader patient populations.

title: The Sabrinal El-rakhawi Vision Geoeconomic Engineering and Sustainable Development for Tebessa Province, Algeria A Foresight Approach to Regional Planning, Border Economics, and the Valorization of Strategic Wealth
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Sabrinal El-rakhawi Vision presents a transformative geoeconomic framework for Tebessa Province, Algeria, converting it from a resource-dependent periphery into a sustainable industrial and knowledge hub. This comprehensive study diagno
content: The Sabrinal El-rakhawi Vision presents a transformative geoeconomic framework for Tebessa Province, Algeria, converting it from a resource-dependent periphery into a sustainable industrial and knowledge hub. This comprehensive study diagnoses the structural paradox of the resource curse, where immense phosphate and iron wealth coexists with chronic underdevelopment. Through advanced spatial analysis, original econometric modeling including the Elrakhawi Computable General Equilibrium Model and the Elrakhawi Regional Resilience Index, and strategic foresight, the book offers scientifically rigorous solutions. The vision encompasses seven innovative frameworks: industrial transformation through green mining and fourth industrial revolution technologies, border reengineering via Special Economic Zones, environmental sustainability through water security master plans and green hydrogen production, knowledge economy development, cultural heritage valorization, and digital governance. The implementation roadmap spans 2026 to 2050 across three phases, with innovative financing mechanisms including green bonds and public-private partnerships. Three future scenarios project outcomes from continued decline to continental leadership. This work represents a civilizational manifesto grounded in geoeconomic engineering, demonstrating that integrated scientific approaches can reverse structural failures and transform territories into engines of sustainable prosperity.

title: From ashes to agency: informal-settlement fires, intergenerational power, and democratic survival in Gauteng, South Africa
summary: Introduction Recurrent fires in South Africa's informal settlements are governed as technical emergencies, despite being produced and experienced through unequal infrastructures, insecure tenure, and uneven state protection. This study exam
content: Introduction Recurrent fires in South Africa's informal settlements are governed as technical emergencies, despite being produced and experienced through unequal infrastructures, insecure tenure, and uneven state protection. This study examines how young and older residents of fire-prone informal settlements in the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality interpret risk, respond to emergencies, negotiate recovery, and convert disaster experience into civic action. Methods We used an interpretivist narrative design combining semi-structured interviews, focus-group discussions, participant-generated photographs, ethnographic observation, and stakeholder interviews. The focal sample comprised 22 residents aged 15–35 years or 60 years and older, recruited through an environmental citizenship programme and selected for direct experience of fire-related loss, injury, or displacement. Thematic analysis integrated deliberative-democratic criteria inclusion, reason-giving, and legitimacy with a combative account of conflict and emotion as constitutive of democratic politics. Results Across prevention, response, and recovery, residents described a consistent governance asymmetry: households and neighbors generated situated risk knowledge, evacuation plans, warning networks, bucket chains, and mutual aid, whereas formal intervention was often delayed, reactive, or insufficiently responsive to local priorities. Fire also produced a trauma-to-agency pathway. Indignation at institutional abandonment, grief over irreplaceable homes and routines, fear of recurrence, and hope for change motivated fire-safety education, environmental activism, and claims for municipal accountability. The findings challenge protectionist models that cast young and older residents as passive beneficiaries. Discussion Effective fire governance requires institutionalized co-production, accessible intergenerational preparedness, legitimate space for emotional testimony and disagreement, and sustained investment before predictable high-risk seasons. A deliberative combative model offers a more realistic basis for democratic and effective disaster governance under conditions of structural inequality.

title: Effects of Cross-Regional Ecological Compensation on Industrial Ecologization: Evidence from the Wei River Basin, China
summary: To examine how interregional compensation arrangements may reconcile upstream conservation responsibilities with downstream development interests, the policy implemented in the Wei River Basin is employed, for identification purposes, as a
content: To examine how interregional compensation arrangements may reconcile upstream conservation responsibilities with downstream development interests, the policy implemented in the Wei River Basin is employed, for identification purposes, as a quasi-natural institutional shock. Industrial ecologization is quantified using a super-efficiency SBM model incorporating undesirable outputs, while the policy effect is identified within a difference-in-differences framework using panel observations for 79 prefecture-level cities in the Yellow River Basin over 2005–2024. A significant improvement in industrial ecologization was observed in treated areas following the introduction of horizontal ecological compensation, and the estimated effect remained positive across a range of robustness and endogeneity checks. The results are consistent with green finance development, R&D human capital, and industrial intelligence being potential mechanisms. Contemporaneous interaction estimates are positive for environmental pollution control intensity and government attention to the digital economy, whereas interactions using their pre-policy averages are not statistically significant. Subgroup estimates are positive across the regional and income groups considered, while formal tests do not indicate statistically significant differences between the corresponding group coefficients. Beyond its conventional functions in water-environment governance and interregional interest coordination, the policy also provides an institutional foundation for advancing industrial ecologization.

title: The Green Finance Ecosystem in India: Current Landscape and Roadmap for Sustainable Development
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INNOVATIONS & RESEARCH ANALYSIS
summary: India stands at a key stage in its commitment to sustainable development while pursuing ambitious economic growth. Over past few years country has reinforced commitment to sustainability and targeted of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.
content: India stands at a key stage in its commitment to sustainable development while pursuing ambitious economic growth. Over past few years country has reinforced commitment to sustainability and targeted of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070. To source half of its electricity from renewables by 2030, the country will need an investment of approximately $2.5 trillion (around ₹162.5 lakh crore) across the 2015–2030 period, averaging roughly $170 billion (about ₹11 lakh crore) per year. With an increasing focus on ESG initiatives and generating 50% of its electricity from renewable energy sources by 2030, the nation will require US$ 2.5 trillion (around Rs. 162.5 lakh crore) between 2015 and 2030, or US$ 170 billion (approximately Rs. 11 lakh crore) annually. Driven by convergence of policy initiatives and the imperative to meet ambitious climate targets, the role of green finance has emerged and fundamentally reshaping the investment ecosystem beyond long established wealth maximization objective. This encompasses a wide array of financial instruments, including loans, debt mechanisms, and investments, all channelled towards encouraging the development of green projects or minimizing the environmental impact of existing initiatives. This paper is an endeavor to give a comprehensive analysis of the current green finance landscape. The paper will study the various financial instruments, regulatory framework and key players that constitutes India’s unique green finance ecosystem.

title: Greening building construction in Africa: opportunities for firm upgrading in the case of Rwanda
source: German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS)
summary: Rwanda does not lack green building policy instruments. Its main challenge is implementation and turning them into a functioning market. Its relatively advanced policy framework includes a revised Building Code, the Green Building Minimum C
content: Rwanda does not lack green building policy instruments. Its main challenge is implementation and turning them into a functioning market. Its relatively advanced policy framework includes a revised Building Code, the Green Building Minimum Compliance System (GBMCS), sustainable public procurement instruments, one of Africa’s first green taxonomies and complementary green finance instruments. Yet adoption of green practices in construction remains limited because policy has not consistently translated into market demand, firm capabilities, enforceable requirements or finance accessible to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). This report explores the underlying issues based on two complementary firm surveys (with 854 firms across two separate waves), 88 semi-structured interviews and two focus group discussions across a broad set of stakeholders relevant to the Rwandan construction industry between 2023 and 2026. Analyses focus on interlocking stabilised soil blocks (ISSBs), improved adobe/rukarakara, residential solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and solar water heaters (SWHs) as case studies of value chains contributing to green building.

title: A Roadmap to the World Health Organization
summary: This chapter explains why the World Health Organisation (WHO) remains indispensable to global health governance while repeatedly facing constrains in fulfilling its mandate. It argues that WHO’s achievements and persistent governance diffic
content: This chapter explains why the World Health Organisation (WHO) remains indispensable to global health governance while repeatedly facing constrains in fulfilling its mandate. It argues that WHO’s achievements and persistent governance difficulties arise from a durable institutional bargain wherein member states endorse ambitious global health objectives with incomplete delegation of authority, finance and implementation. Drawing on the evolution, institutional design, performance, and reform of the WHO from its historical origins to 2026, the chapter shows how the incomplete delegation shapes both organisational capacity and political legitimacy. The analysis integrates perspectives from global public goods and collective action, principal-agent and common-agency theory, historical institutionalism, legitimacy theory, and the literature on orchestration in international organizations. Particular attention is given to three enduring features of WHO governance: the decentralized regional structure, the growing dependence on voluntary and often earmarked financial contributions, and its use of legal and normative instruments with limited enforcement mechanisms. It shows that many apparent institutional weaknesses also reflect underlying governance trade-offs: decentralization can improve regional responsiveness while complicating coordination; voluntary finance expands resources while constraining agenda autonomy; and sovereignty-preserving legal instruments facilitate broad participation while limiting compliance. The paper evaluates these dynamics across WHO’s normative standard-setting and health intelligence, emergency response, country-level technical cooperation, and coordination within an increasingly fragmented global health system. The chapter further assesses major reform episodes, including post-Ebola emergency reforms, sustainable-financing initiatives, the 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations, the adoption of 2025 Pandemic Agreement, and the renewed U.S. withdrawal process. It concludes that WHO’s central challenge is not to eliminate the tension between national sovereignty and collective health governance, but to manage it more effectively through stronger financial resilience, more coherent institutional authority, and legitimacy preserving accountability.

title: When Structural Synergy Does Not Translate into Resilience: Governance and Functional Insularity in Island Systems
summary: Interconnected territorial systems may benefit from cross-sectoral synergies, yet greater integration does not necessarily translate into greater resilience. This study develops a conceptual and mathematical framework for examining how inst
content: Interconnected territorial systems may benefit from cross-sectoral synergies, yet greater integration does not necessarily translate into greater resilience. This study develops a conceptual and mathematical framework for examining how institutional conditions modulate the contribution of structural synergy to systemic resilience. It introduces Functional Insularity as an operational state in which a territory must sustain essential functions under constrained access to external support, and proposes the Composite Resilience Index (CRI) to represent the interaction between baseline structural capacity, latent cross-sectoral synergy, and institutional transmission. The framework is operationalized using Sustainable Development Goal indicators for five island jurisdictions: Malta, the Dominican Republic, Cuba, Fiji, and Haiti. A sensitivity analysis explores how alternative assumptions about structural capacity, synergy, and institutional conditions affect modelled resilience. A comparison using the World Bank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators further examines the sensitivity of the resulting institutional profiles to alternative governance measures. The results illustrate contrasting modelled configurations, while the governance comparison reveals heterogeneous agreement across cases, highlighting the importance of measurement choices and model assumptions. The study contributes a framework for investigating why similar levels of structural integration may yield different resilience outcomes under different institutional conditions. Although the empirical application is conducted at the national level and does not directly measure urban resilience, the concept of Functional Insularity offers a basis for future research on urban systems whose essential services depend on interconnected infrastructures, resource flows, and institutional coordination. Further independent validation is required before the CRI can be used as a predictive or operational resilience indicator.

title: The Knowledge–Action Gap in Sustainable Personal Finance: An Empirical Investigation
summary: Prominent discussions on environmental and social responsibility and sustainable finance practices still stand as an important subject of relevant academic research, particularly in light of the emerging economy characterized by value in In
content: Prominent discussions on environmental and social responsibility and sustainable finance practices still stand as an important subject of relevant academic research, particularly in light of the emerging economy characterized by value in India. Such research as the present one delves into the knowledge, the practice behaviour, and the principal factors influencing the sustainable finance use by individual stakeholders in India. This paper uses a organized questionnaire survey method and employs chi-square data analysis. It concludes statistically. There is a important association among education level and the level of cognizance about green financial products when it is used in a similar time frame. The study also separates them by time frame, showing that awareness- building initiatives are solely insufficient to encourage involvement in green financial instruments. The study identified education, institutional role, and information access as the major drivers of sustainable financial behaviour and established the existing knowledge-action gap as the primary problem faced by policymakers, financial services providers, and educational stakeholders. The study contributes to extant green finance literature by providing verifiable and practical recommendations for regulators, educational bodies, and financing intermediary institutions that would hasten the implementation of predicable personal finance sustainability policy in India.

title: Beyond the Breach: Reassessing Cyber-Incident Coverage Under India's Insurance Framework
source: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
summary: In India, the rising pace of technological innovation in the digital space has led to an increase in cyber incidents, including unauthorised access, data breaches, ransomware attacks, malware attacks, cyber extortion and the disruption of d
content: In India, the rising pace of technological innovation in the digital space has led to an increase in cyber incidents, including unauthorised access, data breaches, ransomware attacks, malware attacks, cyber extortion and the disruption of digital services. Indian cyber law deals with many aspects of these incidents under the Information Technology Act, 2000, in particular through the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), and under the newer data protection and cybersecurity regulations. Yet the law on these incidents remains fragmented, without a comprehensive classification that can be applied across cybersecurity, data protection, cyber insurance and related legal purposes. This study assesses the sufficiency of the current Indian regime and examines whether a standardised system of legal classification of cyber incidents could ensure consistency in their handling. It follows a doctrinal approach, studying section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the CERT-In Directions, together with other relevant provisions on data protection and cyber insurance regulation. A comparative study of the European Union, the United Kingdom, Singapore and Australia is conducted to identify effective mechanisms for classifying and reporting cyber incidents and for regulating cyber insurance. The study finds, first, that India’s framework covers many kinds of incident but defines and reports them under separate, unconnected concepts, none of which grades incidents by severity, so that its alignment with the perils of cyber insurance policies is incidental; second, that the four comparator jurisdictions grade incidents by significance, disruption, designation or impact, and that several of those features can be adapted to India, although none of them links policy terms to reporting categories; and third, that the absence of a common classification widens India’s cyber protection gap through incomparable data, policy terms unconnected to regulatory categories, and the lack of a defined event on which public risk-sharing could rest. The study therefore suggests strengthening the regime under section 70B through a standard classification of cyber incidents based on CERT-In, and standardising cyber insurance policy terminology and disclosures under IRDAI’s oversight.

title: Weather and Climate Systems
summary: This chapter examines the fundamental dynamics of weather and climate, distinguishing between short-term atmospheric states and long-term regional averages. It identifies latitude, atmospheric circulation, and ocean currents as primary driv
content: This chapter examines the fundamental dynamics of weather and climate, distinguishing between short-term atmospheric states and long-term regional averages. It identifies latitude, atmospheric circulation, and ocean currents as primary drivers of global climate patterns. The chapter emphasizes that anthropogenic factors, such as fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, have become the dominant causes of contemporary climate change, resulting in sea-level rise, extreme weather, and biodiversity loss. The text details profound geoeconomic consequences, noting that global GDP could have been 37% higher had historical warming not occurred. India faces acute risks, including a potential 20% reduction in rice yields by 2050 and the loss of 4.5% of GDP by 2030 due to heat-induced labor productivity declines. Additional threats include resource scarcity, supply chain disruptions, and climate-induced migration. To foster resilience, the chapter advocates for mitigation strategies such as industrial symbiosis, green bond financing, and climate-conscious urban planning. It highlights India's comprehensive policy framework, specifically the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and its eight specialized missions. Finally, the Panchamrit commitments and the Green Hydrogen Mission are presented as essential pillars for India's transition to a sustainable, low-carbon economy.

title: Corruption Perceptions, the Pendleton Act, and Sovereign Borrowing Costs
summary: Significant research suggests that systems of bureaucratic patronage tend to promote corruption and reduce the efficient production of publicly provided goods. However, much less work has been done to consider how market actors perceive suc
content: Significant research suggests that systems of bureaucratic patronage tend to promote corruption and reduce the efficient production of publicly provided goods. However, much less work has been done to consider how market actors perceive such selection processes and especially reforms implemented to reduce such corruption. This study rectifies this by evaluating how the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act impacted federal borrowing costs. If patronage resulted in increased corruption and bureaucratic inefficiency, this should be reflected in relatively higher bond yields. If the Pendleton Act was successful in curbing this behavior, then this should be rewarded by market actors in the form of lower borrowing costs. Using interrupted time series analysis with and without control, we find that the passage of the Pendleton Act did, in fact, result in lower borrowing costs for the federal government of between 63 and 84 basis points depending on specification. Implications are discussed.

title: Gambling for Retirement: The Hidden Costs of Savings Lotteries in a Nationwide Experiment
summary: Governments increasingly encourage socially desirable behavior with probabilistic incentives. We study such "Pigouvian lotteries'' in a retirement-savings field experiment with 387,000 workers in Colombia's public pension system. The lotter
content: Governments increasingly encourage socially desirable behavior with probabilistic incentives. We study such "Pigouvian lotteries'' in a retirement-savings field experiment with 387,000 workers in Colombia's public pension system. The lotteries induce sharp bunching at qualification thresholds, but workers mostly meet them by retiming rather than increasing deposits, leaving overall savings largely unaffected. Lotteries further crowd out valuable life and disability insurance and disproportionately reward wealthier savers. A welfare analysis shows that, once we account for these unintended consequences, lotteries reduce welfare. Our findings illustrate that behavioral spillovers across time and choice domains can reverse the verdict on behavioral public policies.

title: ESG Data Governance for Sustainable Business: Ownership, Authority, and the Strategic Role of HR
summary: The growing institutionalization of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting raises questions about how organizations allocate authority over ESG information. While existing research addresses reporting requirements and data go
content: The growing institutionalization of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting raises questions about how organizations allocate authority over ESG information. While existing research addresses reporting requirements and data governance structures, the organizational processes through which ESG data ownership emerges remain insufficiently theorized. This conceptual paper develops an integrated framework in which ESG data ownership is understood as the institutionally recognized allocation of governance authority over the definition, interpretation, validation, and use of ESG information. It identifies four interacting mechanisms through which this authority is formed: authority claiming, allocation of decision rights, interpretative alignment, and institutional stabilization. The framework distinguishes finance‐centered, sustainability‐centered, and matrix governance configurations as alternative outcomes of formation processes shaped by institutional and organizational conditions. Drawing on contrasting governance traditions in France and Germany, it highlights the context‐dependent nature of these arrangements. Particular attention is given to human resources (HR), whose expertise in producing and interpreting social ESG information does not necessarily translate into recognized decision‐making authority. By explaining how distributed functional expertise and competing authority claims are translated into institutionally recognized decision rights, the framework advances an understanding of how different governance configurations and positions of HR emerge.
