title: Comunicación, innovación y energía con propósito: Análisis de startups lideradas por mujeres
source: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual
summary: Este artículo analiza el papel de la comunicación estratégica, la innovación y el liderazgo en startups españolas de climate-tech lideradas por mujeres. A partir de una revisión bibliográfica y un estudio de seis casos, se examinan las brec
content: Este artículo analiza el papel de la comunicación estratégica, la innovación y el liderazgo en startups españolas de climate-tech lideradas por mujeres. A partir de una revisión bibliográfica y un estudio de seis casos, se examinan las brechas de género en financiación, liderazgo y visibilidad mediática, así como las ventajas competitivas asociadas al emprendimiento femenino orientado a la sostenibilidad. Los resultados muestran que estas startups presentan alta legitimidad moral y cognitiva, pero desigual legitimidad mediática y pragmática. Se concluye que la comunicación digital constituye una palanca clave para mejorar la eficiencia de su marca y la contribución a los ODS.

title: Whither EU borrowing?
summary: The EU has emerged as a sovereign-style bond issuer following the Next Generation EU scheme decided during the Covid emergency in 2020. But NGEU did not settle the issue of whether the EU should develop into a permanent borrower. That debat
content: The EU has emerged as a sovereign-style bond issuer following the Next Generation EU scheme decided during the Covid emergency in 2020. But NGEU did not settle the issue of whether the EU should develop into a permanent borrower. That debate was bound to reemerge as NGEU was drawing to a close. Over the past year, various proposals by proponents of a permanent EU borrowing capacity have been formulated. This policy perspective analyzes their rationales and asks which one is more likely to overcome the resistance of Germany and the frugal member states.

title: Unleashing the Power of Constraints: Green Power Trading and Corporate Investment Efficiency
summary: Using a difference-in-differences (DID) design with annual data from 2018 to 2025, we investigate how China’s green power trading policy influences investment efficiency among wind and photovoltaic power enterprises covered by the policy. R
content: Using a difference-in-differences (DID) design with annual data from 2018 to 2025, we investigate how China’s green power trading policy influences investment efficiency among wind and photovoltaic power enterprises covered by the policy. Results show that green power trading significantly improves investment efficiency, mitigating both over- and under-investment. We provide evidence consistent with the alleviation of financing constraints and the strengthening of decision-making constraints as potential channels underlying this improvement. Consistent with these mechanisms, the policy has a stronger association with investment efficiency in less marketized regions and in firms characterized by greater managerial discretion. Further evidence shows that environmental prioritization by local governments undermines the policy’s effectiveness in restraining overinvestment. This study offers micro-level evidence validating the effectiveness of the green power trading policy and presents a pathway to resolve the investment efficiency challenges that have hindered the sustainable growth of the renewable energy generation sector.

title: COVID‐19 induced lockdown and economic activity: Evidence from zoning restrictions in India
summary: We estimate the economic impact of COVID‐19 lockdowns in India, which classified the districts into red, orange, and green zones based on case severity. By analyzing data on household income, consumption expenditure, and unemployment, we as
content: We estimate the economic impact of COVID‐19 lockdowns in India, which classified the districts into red, orange, and green zones based on case severity. By analyzing data on household income, consumption expenditure, and unemployment, we assess the relative impact of these restrictions. Our findings show that while income levels in red zones recovered by July 2020, consumption expenditure remained below pre‐pandemic levels until August. Additionally, unemployment increased across all districts between May and August 2020. We further investigate economic activity through ATM withdrawals and Point of Sale (POS) transactions, finding a significant slowdown in both metrics in red zones, particularly in April and May, with ATM withdrawals remaining subdued until August. In contrast, POS transactions began to recover in red zones from June 2020. These results provide valuable insights into the differential economic effects of lockdown restrictions and the pace of recovery across regions.

title: Government Policy, Organizational Responses, and Sustainable Performance: An Organizational Perspective
summary: Sustainable performance is increasingly important for enterprises operating under growing environmental, technological, and institutional pressures. Drawing on stakeholder theory and dynamic capabilities theory, this study examines an integ
content: Sustainable performance is increasingly important for enterprises operating under growing environmental, technological, and institutional pressures. Drawing on stakeholder theory and dynamic capabilities theory, this study examines an integrated model of the relationships among government policy, environmental compliance, digital adoption, innovation capability, ethical leadership, and sustainable performance. Using cross‐sectional survey data based on the organizational perceptions of 303 senior managers, board members, and business owners in Vietnam, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) to examine the proposed direct and indirect relationships. The results show significant positive associations between government policy and both environmental compliance and digital adoption, as well as between environmental compliance and digital adoption and ethical leadership. Digital adoption, innovation capability, and ethical leadership are positively associated with sustainable performance, while digital adoption has a positive relationship with innovation capability. Environmental compliance has no statistically significant direct association with sustainable performance but shows significant indirect associations through digital adoption and ethical leadership. Overall, the findings clarify how policy‐related perceptions, organizational responses, capabilities, and leadership are statistically associated with multidimensional sustainable performance in an emerging‐market context. Given the cross‐sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causal or temporal relationships.

title: Do thematic ETFs transmit shocks, or do they contain them? A diagnostic for composition overlap in connectedness systems
summary: Connectedness studies of thematic assets routinely place exchange-traded funds and the securities they hold in a single vector autoregression. Because a fund is by construction a linear combination of its holdings, a generalized variance de
content: Connectedness studies of thematic assets routinely place exchange-traded funds and the securities they hold in a single vector autoregression. Because a fund is by construction a linear combination of its holdings, a generalized variance decomposition cannot distinguish shock transmission from shared composition. We quantify the distortion in a nine-asset system spanning AI equities, AI-themed ETFs, cryptocurrencies and safe-haven assets over January 2019 to July 2026. Estimated conventionally, the system returns a connectedness index of 52.8% and identifies the two ETFs as dominant net transmitters at +18.4% and +13.0%, while the three included equities span 71% and 64% of the funds’ return variation. Three counterfactual designs each reduce the index to approximately 37% and eliminate the funds’ net-transmitter position, a result stable across VAR lag orders one to eight. Comparison against direct equity exposure bounds any genuine ETF premium at 3.2 percentage points, roughly one-sixth of the conventional estimate. Across twenty fund configurations, overlap and inflation correlate at 0.984, and broad-market benchmarks prove as exposed as thematic funds. The block structure, frequency composition and regime dependence survive the diagnostic; connectedness rises from 39.3% in calm conditions to 68.8% under extreme stress and steepens once overlap is removed.

title: EMERGING MARKET FINANCE IN A FRAGMENTING GLOBAL ECONOMY: BANKING RESILIENCE, DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION, AND INVESTMENT REALIGNMENT (2024–2026)
source: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
summary: The global economic landscape in the mid-2020s is undergoing profound structural change, marked by geopolitical fragmentation, deglobalization, and rapid digital transformation.Within this context, emerging markets have transitioned from be
content: The global economic landscape in the mid-2020s is undergoing profound structural change, marked by geopolitical fragmentation, deglobalization, and rapid digital transformation.Within this context, emerging markets have transitioned from being peripheral participants to central anchors of global economic resilience.This study examines the evolving financial and investment ecosystems of key emerging regions-India, Brazil, and Southeast Asia-during the 2024-2026 period.Using a mixed-methods synthesis of secondary data from international financial institutions, central banks, and investment reports, the research evaluates banking sector stability, foreign direct investment (FDI) dynamics, and the disruptive role of fintech and artificial intelligence.The findings reveal that strengthened monetary frameworks, improved asset quality, and institutional credibility have enhanced emerging market resilience to global shocks.Simultaneously, supply-chain realignment under the "China Plus One" strategy has redirected capital flows toward ASEAN and India, while Brazil illustrates how digital finance can coexist with high interest rates.However, rising unsecured retail credit, fiscal vulnerabilities, and regulatory fragmentation present new systemic risks.The study concludes that sustainable growth in emerging markets will depend on balancing digital financial innovation with prudent regulation and maintaining strong domestic financial institutions to attract long-term investment in a fragmented global economy.

title: Integrated Vector, Canine, and Human Evidence Reveal a Stable Dog‐Maintained Cycle of Leishmania Infantum in a Historically Endemic Area From Spain
summary: INTRODUCTION: Leishmaniosis, caused by Leishmania infantum, is a major zoonotic vector-borne disease in southern Europe. Dogs act as the primary domestic reservoir of the parasite. However, there is growing evidence that transmission cycles
content: INTRODUCTION: Leishmaniosis, caused by Leishmania infantum, is a major zoonotic vector-borne disease in southern Europe. Dogs act as the primary domestic reservoir of the parasite. However, there is growing evidence that transmission cycles involving wild lagomorphs may contribute to both epidemic and endemic human cases in certain settings. Nevertheless, the ecological and epidemiological mechanisms sustaining long-term endemic transmission in stable foci remain poorly understood. This study used an integrated One Health approach combining vector, canine, and human data to investigate transmission dynamics in a long-established endemic area with low human case incidence. METHODS: An eco-epidemiological study was conducted in Crevillente Municipality in southeast Spain, between 2021 and 2022. Sand flies were collected using CDC light traps and analysed to determine species composition, Leishmania infection by real-time PCR, parasite identification, and blood meal sources. Dogs were tested for anti-Leishmania antibodies using ELISA. Human blood donors were assessed for Leishmania infection by PCR and for anti-Leishmania antibodies and antibodies against Phlebotomus perniciosus saliva as markers of parasite and vector exposure, respectively. RESULTS: A total of 11,375 sand flies were collected, predominantly Sergentomyia minuta and Phlebotomus perniciosus, and displayed marked seasonal and spatial variation. High Leishmania infection rates were detected in confirmed vector species, with L. infantum identified in most samples. Blood meal analysis revealed that the primary feeding sources were dogs and humans, while rabbits and hares were detected but infrequently. Canine seroprevalence was high (43%) and associated with rural exposure. In humans, infection markers were low (3% PCR, 4% serology), despite high exposure to sand fly bites (38% seroprevalence for anti-saliva antibodies). CONCLUSIONS: The study characterizes a Mediterranean endemic focus with intense circulation of L. infantum in vectors and dogs, widespread human exposure to sand flies, but low levels of asymptomatic human infection and no reported clinical disease during the decade preceding the study. The findings support a predominantly domestic transmission, with dogs representing the main identified reservoir host and lagomorph-derived blood meals being relatively infrequent. The potential contribution of lagomorphs to local parasite circulation warrants further investigation. The detection of Leishmania DNA in non-confirmed vector species, including sequences consistent with the L. donovani/L. infantum complex, further highlights the need for continued surveillance of Leishmania diversity and transmission dynamics.

title: India's Global South Leadership in the 21st Century: Challenges, Opportunities, and Strategic Implications
source: International Journal of Science and Social Science Research
summary: India has emerged as one of the most influential voices of the Global South in the twenty-first century, advocating for a more inclusive and equitable international order. Through initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summit, its G2
content: India has emerged as one of the most influential voices of the Global South in the twenty-first century, advocating for a more inclusive and equitable international order. Through initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summit, its G20 Presidency, development partnerships, humanitarian assistance, digital public infrastructure, and climate diplomacy, India has sought to redefine its role from that of a developing nation to a leading partner of developing countries. India's leadership derives from a combination of historical solidarity, democratic values, developmental experience, and strategic autonomy. However, challenges such as geopolitical competition with China, resource limitations, regional security concerns, and balancing relations with major powers continue to influence India's effectiveness as a representative of the Global South. Drawing upon qualitative analysis of official policy documents, scholarly literature, and contemporary diplomatic initiatives, the study explores India's contributions to South-South cooperation, global governance reforms, sustainable development, and strategic diplomacy. And it concludes that while India's leadership has gained unprecedented international recognition, its long-term credibility will depend upon translating diplomatic aspirations into sustained developmental partnerships and institutional reforms that genuinely address the concerns of developing nations.

title: Corporate Activism and Social Change: A Semiotic Perspective on Actors, Practices, and Meaning
summary: The book examines how companies and other business actors engage with contested social, political, economic, and environmental issues, and under what conditions such involvement can be understood as activism. Rather than treating corporate
content: The book examines how companies and other business actors engage with contested social, political, economic, and environmental issues, and under what conditions such involvement can be understood as activism. Rather than treating corporate activism simply as public stance-taking, it develops a relational and processual perspective centered on contested change. Across five chapters, the book maps the conceptual landscape of business activism, examines stakeholder expectations and the conferral of legitimacy, explains how firms assume and sustain activist positions, analyzes how those positions are communicated, and develops a framework for evaluating whether corporate interventions contribute to observable social change. Particular attention is given to distinguishing communication from commitment, stakeholder response from legitimacy, and corporate outputs from social impact. The book is written for academics and students across a broad range of business disciplines, including management, marketing, communication, organization studies, business ethics, and corporate social responsibility. It provides readers with conceptual tools for interpreting corporate activism more precisely, assessing its legitimacy and organizational consistency, and evaluating what companies can credibly claim to have changed, which will also appeal to practitioners responsible for corporate affairs, sustainability, communication, branding, and public policy.

title: A Guidebook for Planning Project Management
summary: A Guidebook for Planning Project Management by Rakesh Singh is a professional guidebook focused on the relationship between planning and project management. It is intended to introduce readers to the importance of systematic planning, organ
content: A Guidebook for Planning Project Management by Rakesh Singh is a professional guidebook focused on the relationship between planning and project management. It is intended to introduce readers to the importance of systematic planning, organised project processes and coordinated implementation in the delivery of projects. Effective project management requires a clear understanding of objectives, scope, resources, schedules, responsibilities and implementation priorities. Planning provides the foundation for organising these elements and supporting informed decisions throughout the project lifecycle. The book's subject is relevant to professionals and students working in planning, architecture, infrastructure, construction and related fields. It may also serve as a useful introductory reference for readers seeking to understand the role of project planning in professional practice. The guidebook connects the broad areas of planning and project management, highlighting the importance of structured approaches, coordination and effective project delivery.

title: Bauxite residue deposition in Corinth Gulf, Greece: a potential REE resource
summary: The Parnassus-Ghiona Unit in Greece represents a Mesozoic carbonate platform hosting at least three bauxite strata (B1, B2 and B3). Currently, this area is among Europe’s most active bauxite mining districts, primarily exploiting the Al-ric
content: The Parnassus-Ghiona Unit in Greece represents a Mesozoic carbonate platform hosting at least three bauxite strata (B1, B2 and B3). Currently, this area is among Europe’s most active bauxite mining districts, primarily exploiting the Al-rich B3 strata. In addition to their importance as a critical raw material for aluminium production within the European Union, bauxites may also represent potential sources of rare earth elements (REEs), depending on the degree of REE enrichment. Historically, bauxite residue (BR) was discharged into the Corinth Gulf via pipelines. Seabed mapping of Antikyra Bay revealed two BR layers: a surficial layer 2 cm thick and a sub-seafloor layer up to 4 cm thick, with a total estimated volume of 1.96 × 106 m3. Mineralogical analysis identifies the BR as being composed of calcite, hematite, quartz, katoite, cancrinite, clinochlore and clay minerals, with trace REE-bearing phases (cerianite, synchysite, bastnäsite and monazite). Geochemical analyses indicate REE concentrations ranging from 484 to 771 mg/kg, with notable enrichment in Ce, La, Nd and Sc (45–73 mg/kg). Ga ranges from 13 to 20 mg/kg with an average concentration of 17 mg/kg. This study evaluates the spatial distribution and mineralogical deportment of these elements to assess the economic potential of this secondary resource.

title: Rethinking Human Resource Practices ( HR Practices) From a Sustainable Approach: A Measure Integrating People, Planet, and Profit
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: As business complexity increases, Sustainable Human Resource Management (Sustainable HRM) is now both a legal and ethical obligation, forming a baseline for responsible corporate conduct. Despite growing recognition of sustainability as ess
content: As business complexity increases, Sustainable Human Resource Management (Sustainable HRM) is now both a legal and ethical obligation, forming a baseline for responsible corporate conduct. Despite growing recognition of sustainability as essential, the HRM field has very limited validated tools for measuring and implementing sustainable practices. While frameworks like the triple bottom line (TBL) promote a balance among economic, social, and environmental factors, validated empirical measurements of those factors facilitate practical application. This study addresses this issue by advancing and providing evidence of the validity and reliability of a sustainable HR practices scale (S‐HRP scale) aligned with the TBL framework, operationalizing three key dimensions: performance‐enhancement practices (profit), employee‐support practices (people), and green HR practices (planet). The research utilizes data gathered from Spain, encompassing a cross‐sector sample of 741 employees (2021) and a data cohort from the social economy sector (1589 at the end of 2022; 562 in mid‐2023). The study conducted comprehensive statistical analyses, including exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, reliability analyses, a heterotrait–monotrait ratio analysis, nomological validity testing, and cross‐lagged structural equation modelling on the longitudinal subsample, to ensure the scale's structural integrity. The results suggest that a three‐bundle model with 10 individual HR practices provided a better fit than the other tested models, and all psychometric results are robust. Cross‐lagged analyses on the matched two‐wave subsample showed that all bundle‐level predictors of employee outcomes retained significant directional influence after 6 months, providing strong evidence of predictive validity. By confronting the gap between theoretical paradigms and practical applications, this research offers organizations a useful tool that not only enhances academic discussions but also provides practitioners with a validated tool to foster significant, data‐driven advancements in sustainable HRM.

title: Import exposure and food production instability amid global economic shocks: trend–residual decomposition (FIPP) evidence from Indonesia and Malaysia
summary: This study examines the empirical association between import exposure and short-run food production instability in Indonesia and Malaysia during 2010–2024, a period marked by successive global economic shocks. It addresses an empirical gap
content: This study examines the empirical association between import exposure and short-run food production instability in Indonesia and Malaysia during 2010–2024, a period marked by successive global economic shocks. It addresses an empirical gap in production-side instability measures linked to trade-exposure channels in a Southeast Asian comparative setting. Annual World Bank data are decomposed into long-run trends and short-run instability. Food production is measured using the Food Production Index (FPI), while instability is captured by the Fluctuation of Food Production Index (FIPP), calculated as the squared residual from a country-specific linear trend. Three hypotheses are tested: H1 proposes a positive association between import exposure and FIPP; H2 proposes a negative association between export performance and FIPP; and H3 proposes that decomposed trade measures provide stronger identification of external channels than aggregate trade balance. Panel FGLS with AR(1) correction and year effects indicates that food imports are positively associated with instability, whereas food exports are negatively associated when trade is decomposed. A robustness specification using ln(FIPP + 1) shows a positive association with GDP growth. Country-specific VAR(1) models serve as complementary diagnostics, providing IRF and FEVD evidence on short-horizon dynamics. The findings are interpreted as empirical associations rather than causal effects because panel FGLS cannot distinguish demand-side transmission from supply-side coping responses. Moreover, the small cross-section (N = 2) limits inferential strength; therefore, the results should be regarded as illustrative rather than definitive.

title: Dialektika Sakralitas dan Pragmatisme: Epistemologi Preferensi Pembiayaan Syariah dan Konvensional Pada Masyarakat Desa
summary: The use of Islamic financing products in rural communities is not always accompanied by a proper understanding of Sharia contracts. This study aims to identify the understanding of the Muslim community in Trajumas Village, Pekalongan Regenc
content: The use of Islamic financing products in rural communities is not always accompanied by a proper understanding of Sharia contracts. This study aims to identify the understanding of the Muslim community in Trajumas Village, Pekalongan Regency, regarding Islamic and conventional financing products, as well as the factors influencing their preferences in using these products. This qualitative research, conducted using a case study approach, employs semi-structured interview data collected from ten users of the People's Business Credit (Kredit Usaha Rakyat/KUR), Islamic motorcycle leasing, and weekly installment bank loans. The findings reveal that none of the informants understand the fundamental differences between Islamic and conventional financing systems. Their preferences are shaped by urgent financial needs, ease of access, perceptions of low costs, and social environmental influences. The contribution of this study highlights the importance of strengthening widespread Sharia contract literacy initiatives by Islamic financial institutions among rural Muslim communities.

title: Automotive Repair SMEs’ Marketing Performance: Digital Transformation, Knowledge Antecedents, Social Media Mediation, Market Turbulence Moderation
source: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
summary: Purpose – This study examines knowledge capabilities as antecedents of digital transformation and its relationship with marketing performance, considering social media marketing as a mediator and market turbulence as a moderator among Indon
content: Purpose – This study examines knowledge capabilities as antecedents of digital transformation and its relationship with marketing performance, considering social media marketing as a mediator and market turbulence as a moderator among Indonesian automotive repair MSMEs. Design/methodology/approach – A cross-sectional survey involved 227 owners and managers. Responses were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.0 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Findings/Results – Absorptive capacity (p = 0.402) and knowledge management capability (p = 0.061) were not significantly associated with digital transformation. Digital transformation was positively associated with marketing performance (p = 0.005), with significant mediation through social media marketing (p < 0.001). Market turbulence negatively moderated this relationship (p = 0.022), contrary to the proposed direction. Originality/Value – The study integrates knowledge capabilities, digital transformation, social media marketing, and market turbulence in a conventional service sector, identifying a marketing mechanism and an environmental constraint on digital transformation’s benefits.

title: How Do Employees Navigate Destructive Leadership Behaviour? A Focus on SMEs
summary: Destructive leadership has detrimental effects on employee and organizational performance, yet we know little about how employees respond to such leadership behaviour, particularly in small‐ and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs), where close
content: Destructive leadership has detrimental effects on employee and organizational performance, yet we know little about how employees respond to such leadership behaviour, particularly in small‐ and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs), where close interpersonal relationships and limited organizational support constrain employees’ responses. Drawing on Leader‐Member Exchange (LMX) theory, we examine the coping strategies employees adopt to navigate destructive leadership behaviour and the mechanisms that shape these strategies. We conducted 26 semi‐structured interviews with employees across diverse SMEs and job roles and analysed the data thematically. We identify three coping strategies: (i) adaptation, (ii) resistance and (iii) exit. Employees’ choice among these strategies depends on their assessment of their tolerance of personal and professional risks and their perceived power to influence or change their situation. These evaluations determine whether employees accommodate their leaders’ destructive behaviour, resist it or disengage entirely by leaving the organization. Our findings extend LMX theory by highlighting employees’ active role in evaluating their interactions and adapting their responses according to the associated risks and their power to influence or change their situation. The study also highlights the contextual dynamics of SMEs and offers insights for organizations seeking to recognize the effects of destructive leadership and support employees.

title: A quantitative analysis of determinants and severity of rural poverty: a household level cross-sectional study in Rushinga rural district in Zimbabwe
summary: Alleviating all forms of poverty is a priority for developing countries like Zimbabwe, but understanding the factors driving household-level rural poverty is vital for achieving the UN SDGs. This study compares the characteristics of poor a
content: Alleviating all forms of poverty is a priority for developing countries like Zimbabwe, but understanding the factors driving household-level rural poverty is vital for achieving the UN SDGs. This study compares the characteristics of poor and non-poor households, estimates ward-level poverty incidence, depth and severity, and examines the household- and location-level factors associated with consumption poverty in Rushinga Rural District, Zimbabwe. Therefore, a multi-stage sampling technique was used to systematically collect cross-sectional data from 300 participants in three wards. The Foster-Greer-Thorbecke (FGT) poverty class index was used to measure the severity of poverty, and a binary logistic model, along with its associated odds ratios and marginal effects, was used to estimate the determinants of poverty based on per capita food consumption expenditure. The indices showed significant variation in incidence, gap, and inequality when aggregated at the ward level, indicating a geographical poverty trap in the district. The logistic model results further revealed that spatial location, dependency ratio, marital status, total monthly income, asset endowment, access to extension services and maize yield were significantly associated with rural poverty. The study identifies key household and location-specific socio-economic factors associated with rural poverty using household-level data and binary logit estimation.

title: Niche-Controlled Proliferation of Leukemic Stem Cells: Insights from Integrative Modeling Approaches
summary: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a severe disorder of the blood forming system typically treated with cytotoxic drugs. It is still incompletely understood how interaction between leukemia and the stem cell niche regulates stem cell prolifera
content: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a severe disorder of the blood forming system typically treated with cytotoxic drugs. It is still incompletely understood how interaction between leukemia and the stem cell niche regulates stem cell proliferation and quiescence, thereby influencing AML progression, treatment outcome and resistance formation. To this end we analyzed two unique models of AML progression that explicitly describe the reversible, niche-mediated induction of quiescence for normal and leukemic cells. Through analytical reformulation we identify structurally different mechanisms regulating stem cell proliferation: quiescence-independent proliferation, in which stem cells can re-enter the cell cycle and divide without first passing through a quiescent state, while the other assumes quiescence-dependent proliferation, in which subsequent cell division requires prior passage through a quiescent state. Despite this mechanistic difference, we show that both models share key dynamic features and describe disease dynamics equally well when fitted to 275 clinical remission time courses. Based on these findings, we derive a unified model integrating both modes of proliferation regulation. Using this framework, we show that leukemic clones may rely on quiescence-dependent and quiescence-independent mechanisms to varying extents, thereby exhibiting distinct dynamics during disease progression and treatment. We conclude that the regulation of normal and leukemic stem cell proliferation can be linked to niche-induced quiescence induction. While both concepts allow to sufficiently describe clinically available time course data, their complementary roles in leukemia progression but also in normal and stress hematopoiesis need to be further delineated.

title: Authority bias in Human-AI decision making: The effects of AI appraisals and journal cues in abstract screening
summary: Human-AI collaboration is increasingly embedded in decision-making tasks, including systematic reviewing workflows such as title and abstract screening. Yet humans as final arbiters remain susceptible to peripheral cues, leaving these hybri
content: Human-AI collaboration is increasingly embedded in decision-making tasks, including systematic reviewing workflows such as title and abstract screening. Yet humans as final arbiters remain susceptible to peripheral cues, leaving these hybrid workflows vulnerable to systematic bias. This paper examined how two authority cues, namely AI appraisals and journal prestige, influence screening judgments. Across three preregistered experiments, we employed an identical 3 × 3 mixed design in which participants were randomly assigned to receive AI recommendations, AI disapprovals, or no AI appraisal, while evaluating abstracts presented with prestigious journal labels, non-prestigious journal labels, or no journal information. Across Western graduate students, Asian bachelor’s-degree holders, and Western professionals (total N = 977), AI appraisals produced robust and symmetric shifts in screening decisions: recommendations increased erroneous inclusion of irrelevant abstracts, whereas disapprovals increased erroneous exclusion of relevant abstracts. Journal information produced weaker and more asymmetric effects. Prestigious labels increased erroneous inclusion of irrelevant abstracts, whereas non-prestigious labels did not increase erroneous exclusion of relevant abstracts. Comparisons with the no-journal-information condition further suggested that the availability of journal information may itself influence inclusion decisions. These findings show that AI appraisals and journal information can both bias abstract screening, but through distinct patterns of influence, highlighting the need to design AI-aided screening systems that support independent evaluation of task-relevant information.

title: Istidamah al-Mawarid al-Tabi’iyyah in Artificial Intelligence Era: Study on Water Resource Governance for Data Centers
source: Advances in Social Science, Education and Humanities Research/Advances in social science, education and humanities research
summary: Data center water consumption grows in step with artificial intelligence workloads, and the Annual and Sustainability Report published by PT DCI Indonesia for fiscal year 2025 shows this pattern at facility scale in Indonesia. This study as
content: Data center water consumption grows in step with artificial intelligence workloads, and the Annual and Sustainability Report published by PT DCI Indonesia for fiscal year 2025 shows this pattern at facility scale in Indonesia. This study asks whether Islamic legal doctrine can supply a normative ceiling that secular efficiency-based regulation currently lacks. This is a normative-juridical study using statutory, comparative, and conceptual approaches. Comparative analysis covers the water governance regimes of Singapore, the Netherlands, and the United States. Conceptual analysis draws on istidamah al-mawarid al-tabi’iyyah, maqasid al-syari’ah (hifz al-nafs), la darar wa la dirar, and mizan. All quantitative data are drawn from PT DCI Indonesia’s Annual and Sustainability Report 2025; a 2026 projection for the E2 Surabaya facility is calculated from the company’s own disclosed water-to-electricity ratio. Disclosed water usage across DCI’s facilities rose 161% between 2023 and 2025, from 233,586 m 3 to 610,833 m 3 . Applying DCI’s 2025 water-to-electricity ratio to E2 Surabaya’s 9 MW installed capacity projects approximately 134,700 m 3 of water consumption for April-December 2026 under a full-load scenario. None of the three secular regimes examined impose an absolute consumption ceiling comparable to what la darar wa la dirar would require, pointing toward a hybrid governance model combining an absolute threshold, waqf-linked conservation financing, and mandatory pre-approval harm assessment.

title: Eggshell microstructure and age-related structural changes in emus (Dromaius novaehollandiae)
summary: The emu ( Dromaius novaehollandiae ) eggshell exhibits distinctive microstructural features that remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding the organization of its structural layers and the effects of bird age. This study aimed to
content: The emu ( Dromaius novaehollandiae ) eggshell exhibits distinctive microstructural features that remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding the organization of its structural layers and the effects of bird age. This study aimed to characterize emu eggshell microstructure and evaluate the effects of bird age on the thickness and relative contribution of its structural components. Eggshell samples from 19 emus (nine males and ten females) assigned to two age groups (2 and 7 years) were examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Five morphologically distinct layers were identified: crystalline, porous-reticular, palisade, supra-mammillary, and mammillary. The supra-mammillary layer was identified as a distinct structural region between the palisade and mammillary layers. No cuticle was observed, and deep, predominantly conical pore-like structures were identified within the mineralized shell. However, their continuity with the external surface and their three-dimensional connectivity could not be established from the two-dimensional images examined. Eggs from older emus had thinner eggshells. The absolute thicknesses of the palisade and supra-mammillary layers were greater in eggs from younger birds, whereas the mammillary layer was thicker in eggs from older birds. The crystalline and porous-reticular layers were not significantly affected by age. Shell membranes were thicker in eggs from younger birds, although their relative contribution, approximately 11% of the measured thickness, did not differ significantly between age groups. Dry matter and mineral matter contents were also similar between age groups. The observed outer eggshell surface and the distinct organization of the mineralized layers highlight the structural characteristics of the emu eggshell. Overall, these findings expand current knowledge of emu eggshell ultrastructure and demonstrate that bird age is associated with differences in specific structural components of the eggshell.

title: The growth energy emissions trilemma: evidence from BRICS
source: International Journal of Energy Sector Management
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the equilibrium relationship between economic growth, foreign direct investments (FDI), trade openness, fossil fuel energy use and CO2 emissions for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) co
content: Purpose This study aims to examine the equilibrium relationship between economic growth, foreign direct investments (FDI), trade openness, fossil fuel energy use and CO2 emissions for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) countries over a period from 1990 to 2022. Design/methodology/approach Panel data tests are done using the first- and second-generation unit root tests, Pedroni and Johansen Fisher panel co-integration tests, fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) for long-run coefficient and the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality test. Findings There is evidence of cointegration in the long run among the variables. According to the FMOLS estimates, fossil fuel energy consumption (elasticity = 0.847) and inward foreign direct investments (elasticity = 0.031) have a positive and significant effect on CO2 emissions, while trade openness has a negative but insignificant effect. Causality from GDP per capita to CO2 emissions (p < 0.05), and inward FDI to CO2 emissions (p < 0.10) is one-sided. Research limitations/implications The limitation of availability of data restricts the study period from 1990 to 2022. The study uses aggregate data on fossil fuels without differentiating the types of fossil fuels used. Further studies should consider the analysis with country-level asymmetry, structural break models and extended BRICS membership. Originality/value Built on the basis of the hypotheses of Environmental Kuznets Curve, this research attempts to combine the economic, energy, trade and environmental factors in one panel model for BRICS economies. This paper provides the long-run elasticity analysis and causality directions for green policymaking, filling the gap in literature that reports only about cointegration without the effect size estimates.

title: How green finance reduces agricultural carbon emissions: incentivizing green technology innovation and constraining traditional technology inputs
summary: Can China peak its carbon emissions by 2030 as scheduled? As agricultural decarbonization has become increasingly important in the transition toward carbon neutrality, the role of green finance in supporting low-carbon agricultural developm
content: Can China peak its carbon emissions by 2030 as scheduled? As agricultural decarbonization has become increasingly important in the transition toward carbon neutrality, the role of green finance in supporting low-carbon agricultural development deserves further attention. Using province-level panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2007 to 2022, this study constructs a composite Green Finance Index and employs a two-way fixed-effects model to systematically examine the impact and mechanism of green finance on total agricultural carbon emissions. The results show that higher levels of green finance are significantly associated with lower agricultural carbon emissions. Mechanism analyses reveal a dual-channel pathway: green finance promotes green technology innovation while constraining traditional technology inputs, both contributing to emissions abatement. Moreover, rural digitalization attenuates the marginal impact of green finance, indicating an important boundary condition. Heterogeneity analyses show that the abatement effect is stronger in eastern China. Overall, green finance supports the agricultural low-carbon transition by incentivizing green technology innovation and curbing traditional technology inputs, yet its mitigation effects are significantly moderated by rural digitalization. Policy efforts should strengthen the additionality and precision of green finance and align it with rural digitalization to enhance mitigation outcomes.

title: Long C–N quasi banana bond in an organic molecule: a quadripartite computational investigation
summary: -)-bridged pyridinium phenolate-based zwitterion. The optimized structure of the molecule showed an unusual conformation. Thus, to ascertain that the molecule is not broken, but rather that the C-N bond is merely elongated, a quadripartite
content: -)-bridged pyridinium phenolate-based zwitterion. The optimized structure of the molecule showed an unusual conformation. Thus, to ascertain that the molecule is not broken, but rather that the C-N bond is merely elongated, a quadripartite approach ((1) PES, NBO and methodologies, (2) metamerism, (3) extended bridges and (4) chemical perturbation) was undertaken. The molecule was found to have an elongated C-N bond and a quasi-banana bond type (CAM-B3LYP: 1.610 Å). It is suggested that a very small contribution from the unfavourable quinonoid fragments could be responsible for this behaviour, with support from the nature of the donor/acceptor. Compared with earlier literature (amines and ammonium salts, with C-N bond lengths in the range of 1.469 Å-1.499 Å), this work reports an elongated C-N heteronuclear bond for a simple purely organic molecule. This work shows the significance of quinonoid contribution in the bond elongation of a simple organic molecule. With an ongoing quest in the scientific community for obtaining longer C-C bonds, this work opens new challenges to the quest for longer C-N bonds in organic molecules, a relatively less explored area.

title: Electrodialysis Reversal Brine as a Feedwater Blend to Decarbonize Island Seawater Reverse Osmosis
summary: The decarbonization of seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination is a critical challenge in isolated regions with limited water resources. This study evaluates an industrial symbiosis strategy for the island of Tenerife (Canary Islands,
content: The decarbonization of seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination is a critical challenge in isolated regions with limited water resources. This study evaluates an industrial symbiosis strategy for the island of Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain) by utilizing brackish water brine (BWB) from an electrodialysis reversal (EDR) plant as the feedwater blend with seawater (SW) at different SW/BWB ratios. The results identify an SW/BWB ratio of 5 as the operational threshold, at which the annual carbon footprint reaches 2570 ± 4 tons of CO2/year, representing a 10.3% reduction (292.6 ± 4.6 tons of CO2/year) relative to a baseline SWRO plant of equal capacity operating on seawater alone, while maintaining technically and economically viable conditions. Under these conditions, the specific carbon footprint and OPEX are 1.46 kg CO2/m3 and 0.34 EUR/m3, respectively. Below this threshold, high antiscaling agent demand leads to increases in OPEX of up to 39.7%, rendering the operation unfeasible. At higher ratios, the carbon footprint reduction falls below 10%. Dynamic blending during peak emission hours offers no advantage over constant operation, as the carbon footprint reductions achieved during high-emission periods are offset by operating on seawater alone during low-emission hours. Beyond decarbonization, this strategy valorizes a residual stream that would otherwise be discharged. These findings are transferable to other isolated regions characterized by dependence on fossil fuels for electricity generation, brackish water desalination infrastructure, and additional seawater reverse osmosis capacity required to meet drinking water demand.

title: Biowaste-based microbial protein for sustainable circular food systems and climate mitigation
summary: Agriculture production and waste management is a major source of global greenhouse gas emissions. These emissions, however, can be mitigated by a circular bioeconomy approach that upcycles biowaste into high-value microbial protein capable
content: Agriculture production and waste management is a major source of global greenhouse gas emissions. These emissions, however, can be mitigated by a circular bioeconomy approach that upcycles biowaste into high-value microbial protein capable of displacing animal feed like soybean protein. Here, we assess the global climate mitigation potential of scaling up methanotrophic microbial protein production using biogas derived from animal manure and food waste. We find that biowaste-based microbial protein has a carbon footprint of < 6 kg CO2e kg-1 protein, similar to that of chicken and farmed fish. Its global production potential amounts to 97 Mt of protein by 2050, enough to replace 55% of global soybean protein demand and spare 79 Mha of soybean cropland in 2050. Combining avoided emissions from conventional waste management and soybean production with carbon removal on spared cropland could deliver 30 to 56 Gt CO2e of cumulative climate mitigation by 2050. The magnitude of these benefits depends strongly on how quickly the microbial protein is scaled up and how the spared soybean cropland is managed. Our study demonstrates the great potential of biowaste-based microbial protein for sustainable circular food systems and climate mitigation.

title: How Efficient Are China’s and the EU’s Carbon Markets? A Comparative Analysis Using the Adjusted Market Inefficiency Magnitude
source: Scientific Annals of Economics and Business
summary: This paper examines the time-varying efficiency levels in the European Union’s and China’s carbon markets, including China’s pilot markets. A comparative analysis of these markets' efficiency levels is conducted using the recently developed
content: This paper examines the time-varying efficiency levels in the European Union’s and China’s carbon markets, including China’s pilot markets. A comparative analysis of these markets' efficiency levels is conducted using the recently developed Adjusted Market Inefficiency Magnitude (AMIM). Our findings indicate that China's national carbon market remained inefficient during its first two years of operation, lagging considerably behind the efficiency levels observed in the European Union’s carbon market. Additionally, China’s pilot markets have generally exhibited inefficiency, with some exceptions: Shanghai showed efficiency between 2016 and early 2020, while Tianjin and Beijing have demonstrated efficiency since mid-2020. Notably, our results provide no evidence of a substantial deterioration in the efficiency of the Chinese carbon markets during the period encompassing the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings are relevant to emission-intensive industries, policymakers, and investors engaged in carbon and energy markets. The study discusses the impact of market inefficiency on low-carbon development, providing policy recommendations to enhance the effectiveness and maturity of China’s carbon markets.

title: The Planet Doesn't Give a Damn: Advancing Climate Action in an Age of Pushback and Skepticism
summary: The Planet Doesn’t Give a Damn is a call for strategic realism. We are standing at a historic turning point. Economic stagnation, geopolitical instability, and growing public skepticism about climate policy reinforce one another, creating a
content: The Planet Doesn’t Give a Damn is a call for strategic realism. We are standing at a historic turning point. Economic stagnation, geopolitical instability, and growing public skepticism about climate policy reinforce one another, creating a dangerous cycle of hesitation and vulnerability. This book demonstrates that, approached strategically, climate action is a way to tackle these challenges hand in hand: modernizing our economy, strengthening our security, and restoring confidence in Europe’s climate future. This book offers more than a description of climate change or policy analysis. It shares the reflections behind major decisions, dilemmas that rarely make it into official statements, and encounters with remarkable individuals, businesses, and institutions already shaping a cleaner, more competitive Europe. It is both an insider’s account and a testament to the people proving progress is possible. In an accessible style, it explains how climate change works, why change can feel uncomfortable from a psychological and geopolitical perspective, why the transition to clean energy is vital, and how Europe can set the standard for future industries. Using everyday examples and personal stories, Wopke Hoekstra translates complex technical and geopolitical issues into relatable content anyone can understand.

title: Influence of Ca2+ and HCO3- and Their Ratios in Water on the Aggregation Behavior of Photosynthetic Bacteria in Karst Regions
summary: Photosynthetic bacteria (PSB) for organic wastewater treatment represents an innovative approach in anaerobic microbial metabolism and has been applied in aquaculture wastewater. To extend the application scope of this process, the effects
content: Photosynthetic bacteria (PSB) for organic wastewater treatment represents an innovative approach in anaerobic microbial metabolism and has been applied in aquaculture wastewater. To extend the application scope of this process, the effects of different water bodies must be examined. The water body in karst regions is rich in Ca2+, Mg2+, and HCO3-, which may strongly influence the behavior of PSB, particularly their aggregation and extracellular polymeric substances (EPS). The ratios among these ions vary between water bodies. This study investigates the impact of varying ion ratios on the aggregation behavior of PSB, focusing on PSB biomass, EPS, and bacterial micro-morphology. The results demonstrate that different Ca2+/HCO3- ratios markedly affect PSB aggregation behavior. The addition of Ca2+ and HCO3- shortened the lag phase of PSB, and a higher Ca2+ proportion (Ca2+/HCO3- mass ratio of 4:3) resulted in the strongest aggregation and sedimentation. SEM-EDS analysis revealed Mg- and P-rich crystalline precipitates around the PSB, while Ca was enriched on the bacterial aggregates, suggesting that mineral precipitation and Ca2+ bridging jointly facilitated PSB flocculation. The addition of Ca2+ and HCO3- reduced the protein content of loosely bound EPS (LB-EPS), which may promote bacterial flocculation. Three-dimensional excitation-emission matrix (3D-EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy showed that ion addition increased the proportion of hydrophobic tryptophan-like proteins in LB-EPS, which may further favor PSB flocculation. These findings suggest that the water in karst regions may be conducive to organic wastewater treatment using PSB, and that the Ca2+/HCO3- ratio is a key factor regulating PSB aggregation and solid–liquid separation.

title: Unveiling corporate digital responsibility disclosure practices in the banking sector: An exploratory analysis of CDR governance
source: The International Journal of Digital Accounting Research
summary: Corporate Digital Responsibility (CDR) has emerged as an important framework for addressing the ethical, governance, and accountability challenges associated with digital transformation. However, the current body of knowledge on CDR remains
content: Corporate Digital Responsibility (CDR) has emerged as an important framework for addressing the ethical, governance, and accountability challenges associated with digital transformation. However, the current body of knowledge on CDR remains limited, particularly in the context of the global banking industry. This study explores the developing domain of CDR disclosures in the banking sector. Employing an exploratory qualitative analysis, it examines the extent and nature of CDR disclosures in the annual reports of the top 100 global banks from 2021-2023 and provides qualitative insights into how governance-related CDR aspects are disclosed, drawing from a sample of annual reports and supplementary web-based documents such as codes of conduct and customer privacy. Leveraging stakeholder theory, this study demonstrates how digital responsibility emerges as both an instrumental strategy to mitigate risks and a normative commitment to ethical digital practices, providing a foundation for future work on how ethical governance structures can be embedded into digital business models.

title: Climate Performance and Carbon Accounting of Residue-Based Bioethanol: A Critical Review of Life-Cycle Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Policy Implications
summary: Residue-based bioethanol can contribute to transport decarbonization, but its climate performance depends on feedstock management, conversion technology, energy supply, coproduct treatment, and carbon-accounting choices. This critical integ
content: Residue-based bioethanol can contribute to transport decarbonization, but its climate performance depends on feedstock management, conversion technology, energy supply, coproduct treatment, and carbon-accounting choices. This critical integrative narrative review examines life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions, carbon balances, mitigation options, and policy implications across agricultural and agro-industrial residue pathways. Reported results vary substantially: specific rice-straw pathways show 77–89% lower emissions than gasoline, whereas one corn-stover assessment reports 97 g CO2-eq/MJ for loose biomass and 48 g CO2-eq/MJ for pelleted biomass, compared with 93 g CO2-eq/MJ for gasoline. These estimates reflect different assessment contexts and cannot be treated as directly comparable or universal mitigation rates. Across pathways, process energy and chemical inputs, methane leakage, soil-carbon effects, alternative residue uses, and coproduct allocation can materially influence results. Credible climate claims therefore require transparent functional units and system boundaries, verified inventories, sensitivity analysis, and region-specific supply-chain data. The biogenic origin of a feedstock alone does not establish carbon neutrality or net greenhouse gas savings.

title: Standardization landscape for positive energy districts: mapping SDOs, gaps, and recommendations for interoperability
summary: Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for urban decarbonization, yet their implementation requires integration across energy systems, buildings, mobility, and information and communication technologies,
content: Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for urban decarbonization, yet their implementation requires integration across energy systems, buildings, mobility, and information and communication technologies, for which no coherent international standardization framework currently exists. This conceptual analysis examines the PED standardization landscape using a three-layer interoperability model encompassing technical, governance, and social dimensions. The initial standard inventory was primarily sourced from the IEC Technology Report Positive Energy Districts, supplemented by documents from SET Plan IWG 3.2, JPI Urban Europe, and IEA framework definitions. PED-relevant standards were defined as documents addressing energy, the built environment, mobility, digital infrastructure, or urban governance within district-scale decarbonisation. The analysis drew on the inventory documented in the IEC Technology Report, supplemented by the framework documents noted above. Standards were coded against the three-layer interoperability framework using the definitions and decision rules described in the Methods. Because the analysis is based on a documented inventory rather than an independent systematic search, statements about coverage and absence refer to that inventory. The findings reveal a pronounced asymmetry: technical interoperability is extensively but fragmentedly covered, governance interoperability is selectively addressed at a high level, and social interoperability is almost entirely absent. This imbalance reflects institutional path dependencies, including the historical division of standardization work, the technical composition of SDO epistemic communities, and an epistemology privileging codifiable, measurable aspects of systems. Technical interoperability is thus necessary but insufficient for PED success, which also requires governance and social interoperability that current standards do not provide. To address these gaps, the paper proposes orchestrative standardization, characterized by cross-domain mapping, process orientation, multi-level integration, and stakeholder-oriented design, and identifies the recently established ISO/IEC JTC 4 as a critical institutional opportunity. Theoretical contributions include a three-layer interoperability model extending beyond the technical focus of most interoperability research, orchestrative standardization as a framework for supporting sociotechnical system transitions, and institutional theory’s value for understanding standards landscapes. The paper concludes with implications for standards policy and practice, emphasizing the need for a formal PEDs standards roadmap translating identified gaps into priority work items with assigned responsibilities and timelines.

title: Just Because You Can, Does Not Mean You (Always) Should: The Ethical Implications of Using Generative AI in Chemistry Education
summary: The proliferation of accessible generative AI platforms continues to accelerate in society. With this growth, educators are looking to understand how to best train their students to engage in their work and society with this new technology.
content: The proliferation of accessible generative AI platforms continues to accelerate in society. With this growth, educators are looking to understand how to best train their students to engage in their work and society with this new technology. Most research in this realm has focused on training students to consider when and how to use generative AI, with newer work focused on the impacts on learning. Yet, there has been little exploration of training educators and educational researchers on when and how to use generative AI. While there are some nascent ethical codes emerging, individual exploration of whether, when, and how to use AI in our role as educators deserves attention. In this manuscript, we describe three frameworks of normative ethics, namely, utilitarianism, deontology, and virtue ethics, and explore instructor use cases for generative AI. We do not intend this work to advocate for a specific stance on the use of AI but to invite the reader and our community to engage with the question of their own ethical stance in the context of their own use of the new technology.

title: A comparative MEP and GEP framework for predicting long-term carbon reduction efficiency degradation in office buildings in Pakistan
summary: Carbon reduction efficiency (CRE) of office buildings in hot climates erodes with ageing and heat stress, yet its long-term decline is rarely predicted with transparent models. This study compares Multi-Expression Programming (MEP) and Gene
content: Carbon reduction efficiency (CRE) of office buildings in hot climates erodes with ageing and heat stress, yet its long-term decline is rarely predicted with transparent models. This study compares Multi-Expression Programming (MEP) and Gene Expression Programming (GEP) for predicting CRE degradation in 156 office buildings from Lahore (composite climate, n = 78) and Multan (hot-dry climate, n = 78). We introduce Thermal Performance Resilience (TPR), a 0–1 index that combines envelope stability, mechanical efficiency retention and environmental resistance from annual degradation rates, so that higher values indicate slower CRE decline. Eleven envelope, mechanical, operational and climatic predictors were used to derive TPR equations. On independent test buildings, MEP reached R 2 = 0.90 (Lahore) and 0.88 (Multan), against 0.87 and 0.85 for GEP, with MEP equations 28% smaller and obtained in 49% less time. Wall thermal resistance was the most informative predictor in both cities (18–20% relative importance). Relating TPR to the decay constants of 24 buildings with 8–15 years of records gives scenario-based 20-year retention of about 62% (95% prediction interval: 48–81%) for Heat-Proof buildings and 35% (27–44%) for Standard buildings. These projections are extrapolated beyond the longest record, are not validated, and reflect predictive associations rather than causal effects.

title: Decoupling urban expansion from CO2 emissions in China: the role of urban form and spatial spillover
summary: Decoupling urban expansion from CO2 emissions is crucial for guiding sustainable city planning and achieving carbon neutrality in China's urban landscapes. This study employs the Tapio decoupling model and spatial econometric analyses to ex
content: Decoupling urban expansion from CO2 emissions is crucial for guiding sustainable city planning and achieving carbon neutrality in China's urban landscapes. This study employs the Tapio decoupling model and spatial econometric analyses to examine the relationship between urban land use and carbon emissions (CEs) in China from 2010 to 2019. Our findings indicate that weak decoupling of CEs from urban land expansion was the most common state among the 150 sample cities (33.33%), reflecting an emergent pattern of low-carbon urban development. Despite this, emissions in cities with expansive negative decoupling increased by 112.52%, highlighting the need for carbon mitigation. In contrast, emissions in strongly decoupled cities decreased by 15.50%, indicating sustainable progress. Emissions were influenced by urban compactness, fragmentation, shape regularity, and centrality, and their spatial variation calls for targeted carbon reduction strategies. Notably, spatial spillover from compact urban growth can hinder nearby cities' emission reduction, suggesting a need for regionally coordinated planning. These insights suggest that a multidimensional strategy, potentially incorporating a polycentric urban form, is essential for effective urban carbon reduction planning.

title: Advances in Biological Funneling of Lignin: Chassis Domestication, Multi-input Autonomous Dynamic Regulation, a nd Integrated Bioplastic Manufacturing
summary: Lignin is the most abundant renewable aromatic polymer in nature. Agro-forestry residues and pulp industries generate over 300 million tons of industrial lignin annually, yet more than 95 % is merely incinerated for low-grade heat recovery,
content: Lignin is the most abundant renewable aromatic polymer in nature. Agro-forestry residues and pulp industries generate over 300 million tons of industrial lignin annually, yet more than 95 % is merely incinerated for low-grade heat recovery, wasting high-value aromatic carbon resources. Biological funneling addresses the structural heterogeneity of lignin monomers by converting diverse H-, G- and S-type hydroxycinnamic acids into a single central intermediate, protocatechuic acid (PCA). Traditional static constitutive metabolic engineering suffers from aromatic cytotoxicity, imbalanced upstream-downstream flux, massive intermediate accumulation and poor adaptability to fluctuating industrial hydrolysates. In 2026, a Shandong University team reported in Nature Communications a layered multi-input autonomous biological-funneling system in Corynebacterium glutamicum, integrating ALE-driven chassis domestication, six endogenous aromatic-responsive transcription-factor biosensors and a two-tier cascade positive-negative feedback circuit, achieving 99.89 % molar conversion of mixed lignin-derived aromatics. Fed-batch fermentation produced 53.40 g L⁻¹ PCA, 51.90 g L⁻¹ cis,cis-muconic acid (CCM) and 38.33 g L⁻¹ β-ketoadipic acid, and the strain directly utilized non-detoxified corn-stover alkaline pretreatment liquor. This review systematically compares lignin pretreatment-fractionation technologies and four major microbial chassis, reviews the three regulatory generations, and dissects the molecular mechanisms and fermentation performance of this landmark work. Synthetic routes to high-value lignin-derived chemicals (PCA, CCM, β-KA, PDC) and full-chain biorefinery bottlenecks with corresponding optimization strategies are summarized, providing theoretical references for green lignin biorefinery.

title: Grid-forming SVG DC-side hybrid capacitor series topology and capacity design method
summary: Introduction Grid-forming (GFM) static var generators (SVGs) require adequate DC-side energy storage to provide transient active-power support during grid-frequency disturbances. This study aims to reduce supercapacitor requirements while m
content: Introduction Grid-forming (GFM) static var generators (SVGs) require adequate DC-side energy storage to provide transient active-power support during grid-frequency disturbances. This study aims to reduce supercapacitor requirements while maintaining the transient support capability of GFM SVGs. Methods A series hybrid DC-side topology combining supercapacitors and electrolytic capacitors with a bidirectional partial-power DC/DC converter is proposed. An 800 V direct-connected all-supercapacitor system serves as the benchmark. An energy-equivalent synchronization method and a coordinated engineering sizing procedure are developed for realizable commercial-cell banks and the partial-power converter. Results Using identical 3.0 V/50 F cells, the benchmark and proposed systems require 297s1p and 75s1p supercapacitor banks, respectively. This represents a 74.75% reduction in supercapacitor cell count and the corresponding aggregate cell mass and geometrical volume relative to the specified benchmark. The selected DC/DC converter is rated at 2.114 kW, equivalent to 21.14% of the 10 kW SVG rating. Under the investigated consecutive disturbances with finite rates of change of frequency (RoCoF), the proposed system’s individual decline-stage peak support is approximately 1.52% lower than that of the benchmark. At the time of the benchmark system’s peak, the proposed system’s support is approximately 16.44% lower. The maximum normalized pointwise active-power difference reaches 30.23% during frequency recovery. The proposed system crosses the adopted 10% threshold 1 ms earlier; this is reported only as a diagnostic timing comparison. Discussion Under the investigated operating conditions, the proposed topology substantially reduces supercapacitor-cell requirements while using a converter rated at 21.14% of the SVG rating. It maintains comparable individual peak-support magnitudes and bidirectional energy-exchange characteristics, although the two systems have different peak timing and instantaneous active-power trajectories, particularly during frequency recovery.

title: Shaping eco-friendly headlines over time: A BERTopic analysis of political orientation in news coverage
summary: This study extends research on partisan environmental communication to Korea by examining the persistent lexical frame “eco-friendly.” Using approximately 6700 Korean news headlines published between 2010 and 2024, a single BERTopic model c
content: This study extends research on partisan environmental communication to Korea by examining the persistent lexical frame “eco-friendly.” Using approximately 6700 Korean news headlines published between 2010 and 2024, a single BERTopic model created a shared topic space for comparisons across political orientations and over time. The analysis identified 19 interpretable topics spanning corporate, technological, consumer, and public-policy domains. Although conservative and progressive outlets covered broadly similar themes, their topic distributions differed significantly. Corporate management was 8.09% more prevalent in conservative coverage, whereas institutional catering and school meals were 6.15% more prevalent in progressive coverage. Positive sentiment predominated in both groups, although adjusted sentiment associations were sensitive to the treatment of neutral headlines and limitations in classifier validity. Overall, political orientation was associated with selective emphasis within a broadly shared eco-friendly agenda rather than with distinct environmental discourses.

title: Stabilizing Soil Organic Carbon Fractions as a Negative Emission Pathway in China: Mechanisms, Policy Drivers, and Systemic Innovations
summary: Background: Agricultural soil carbon sequestration can contribute to China’s climate mitigation, but total soil organic carbon (SOC) gains alone do not establish durable net greenhouse-gas re-moval. This critical narrative review integrates
content: Background: Agricultural soil carbon sequestration can contribute to China’s climate mitigation, but total soil organic carbon (SOC) gains alone do not establish durable net greenhouse-gas re-moval. This critical narrative review integrates evidence on particulate organic carbon (POC) and mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC) dynamics, regional soil constraints, agricultural management, carbon governance, and digital monitoring. Methods: A structured comparison of published management effects distinguishes carbon concentrations from stocks and Chi-na-specific evidence from global analogues. Key Findings: POC and MAOC provide comple-mentary information about management response and persistence, although neither fraction de-fines a fixed permanence class. Paddy soils illustrate why fraction measurements must be eval-uated alongside methane, nitrous oxide, crop yield, and water management. Mineral saturation deficits and high-resolution maps can guide sampling and prioritization, but do not independently establish additionality, detect stock changes, or authorize credit issuance. Conclusion: A condi-tional pathway from regional monitoring pilots to methodology evaluation were discussion, with safeguards for food production, farmer participation, uncertainty, and reversal liability. Frac-tion-informed assessment may strengthen future China Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) methodologies and ecological compensation, yet its financial benefits and institutional feasibility require empirical testing. The review connects soil mechanisms with governance and identifies evidence needed before agricultural carbon gains can support credible removal assets.

title: Intelligent manufacturing advances carbon emission reduction in supply chains in Industry 6.0
summary: With increasing global concern about climate change, governments worldwide are vigorously promoting emission reduction policies to reduce carbon emissions across all industries and achieve carbon neutrality as soon as possible. Manufacturin
content: With increasing global concern about climate change, governments worldwide are vigorously promoting emission reduction policies to reduce carbon emissions across all industries and achieve carbon neutrality as soon as possible. Manufacturing has consistently ranked among the top carbon emitters, thus urgently requiring industrial transformation and upgrading to reduce carbon emissions. Smart manufacturing is a powerful technology capable of driving this transformation, and Industry 6.0 further accelerates this process. This paper primarily explores how smart manufacturing can effectively promote carbon emission reduction across all links of the supply chain within the context of Industry 6.0. This research transcends the enterprise-level perspective, constructing a comprehensive framework integrating technology, operations, and governance mechanisms to explain carbon emission reduction throughout the entire supply chain. First, this paper identifies key shifts in carbon management under Industry 6.0, including a shift in responsible entities from the enterprise level to the network level, from static accounting to real-time monitoring, and from compliance-driven to optimization-driven approaches. Second, this paper analyzes three core mechanisms: data-driven carbon governance, end-to-end process optimization, and collaborative governance structures. Third, this paper further explores how smart manufacturing supports these mechanisms through technological empowerment, spillover effects, coordination effects, and blockchain-based smart contracts. Carbon reduction in the Industry 6.0 era is a systemic outcome resulting from the coordinated interaction between digital technologies and supply chains. It expands the role of smart manufacturing from improving operational efficiency to sustainable transformation and provides a theoretical basis for data-driven carbon governance in the supply chain.

title: Strengthening Indonesia’s Environmental Law for AI Data Centers: Developing Ecological Threshold Standards through a Comparative Analysis with Singapore
summary: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has accelerated hyperscale data center construction in Indonesia, yet the electricity and cooling water these facilities demand are not governed by enforceable ecological thresho
content: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has accelerated hyperscale data center construction in Indonesia, yet the electricity and cooling water these facilities demand are not governed by enforceable ecological thresholds. This study examines the adequacy of Indonesian environmental law in governing AI data centers and develops a framework of ecological threshold standards through a functional comparison with Singapore. It applies prescriptive doctrinal legal research with statutory, conceptual, case, and comparative approaches, and draws on peer-reviewed empirical findings to establish the ecological burden. These findings show that workload-level water use varies more than 10,000-fold, that global data center water use could grow more than sevenfold by mid-century without mitigation, and that reduction measures alone cannot deliver climate neutrality. Indonesia recognizes carrying capacity, environmental approval, energy management, and green building, but has not converted them into measurable duties for high-density computing. Singapore combines building-level energy benchmarks, tropical operating standards, water reporting, and capacity allocation, although its power usage effectiveness (PUE) target is not yet a statutory ceiling. The study proposes an eleven-element ecological compliance standard and an eight-stage procedural mechanism, each classified as law in force, strengthening through interpretation, or proposed reform. Only PUE receives an initial numerical value; the other thresholds remain to be set after baseline measurement.

title: A national grid-level dataset of wind and solar capacity deployment pathways in China to 2060
summary: China’s rapid clean energy expansion is essential for addressing climate challenges and rising electricity demand, yet a pronounced spatial mismatch remains between renewable energy resources and major electricity demand centers. Translatin
content: China’s rapid clean energy expansion is essential for addressing climate challenges and rising electricity demand, yet a pronounced spatial mismatch remains between renewable energy resources and major electricity demand centers.
