Translating national climate and energy targets into spatially explicit and actionable deployment pathways is therefore critical for renewable energy planning and long-term decarbonization. This study constructs a 10-km-resolution gridded dataset of China’s wind and solar installed capacity pathways through 2060. Existing capacities are mapped, technically installable areas are identified, and terrain-adjusted capacity densities are estimated. A GIS-based Analytic Hierarchy Process framework integrates resource potential, infrastructure, and environmental characteristics to rank the deployment priority of each grid cell. Provincial rollout sequences are further developed under a policy scenario and an IPCC AR6 low-carbon scenario. The dataset bridges national capacity targets and grid-level deployment, providing spatially explicit support for implementing China’s 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution targets and 2060 carbon neutrality goal. It can support renewable energy spatial planning, transmission and infrastructure coordination, carbon-neutrality pathway assessment, and industrial development strategies. The dataset and analytical framework may also provide a transferable reference for other countries facing similar spatial mismatches between renewable energy resources and electricity demand.

title: Regional Disparities, Distributional Dynamics, and Barriers to the Development of Agricultural Product Cold-Chain Logistics in China
summary: Amid China's ongoing agricultural modernization and green transition, high-quality agricultural product cold-chain logistics plays a critical role in ensuring food safety and promoting sustainable agricultural development. Using provincial
content: Amid China's ongoing agricultural modernization and green transition, high-quality agricultural product cold-chain logistics plays a critical role in ensuring food safety and promoting sustainable agricultural development. Using provincial panel data from 30 Chinese provinces during 2018 and 2024, this study employs the entropy-weighting method, Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition, kernel density estimation, and the obstacle degree model to examine the temporal evolution, regional disparities, distributional dynamics, and key barriers to agricultural product cold-chain logistics development. Four main findings emerge. First, the national development level increased steadily, although substantial regional disparities persisted, with the eastern region consistently outperforming the central, western, and northeastern regions. Second, the overall Dagum Gini coefficient declined with fluctuations. Between-region disparities constituted the largest source of inequality, followed by within-region disparities and transvariation density. Third, the national kernel density distribution shifted rightward and became more dispersed. The eastern distribution moved rightward and became more concentrated, while an emerging development gradient appeared in the central region. The western region remained at a relatively low level with pronounced internal disparities, whereas growth rates varied substantially within the northeastern region. Fourth, infrastructure was the dominant barrier. Insufficient and spatially uneven infrastructure supply remained the primary constraint. Although the obstacle degree of economic synergy declined, regional disparities persisted. Development capacity improved only slowly, indicating insufficient endogenous momentum. Technological capacity had the lowest obstacle degree. These findings provide an empirical basis for formulating region-specific policies to promote more balanced and high-quality development of agricultural product cold-chain logistics in China.

title: UHPLC–MS-based characterization of the pharmacokinetics and in-vivo metabolic profile of oleanonic acid in rats
summary: Background: Oleanonic acid (ONA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid with significant hypoglycemic and neuroprotective activities, shows promise as a multi-target anti-diabetic candidate. However, its pharmacokinetic behavior and metabolic fate in-
content: Background: Oleanonic acid (ONA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid with significant hypoglycemic and neuroprotective activities, shows promise as a multi-target anti-diabetic candidate. However, its pharmacokinetic behavior and metabolic fate in-vivo remain incompletely characterized, limiting dose optimization and clinical translation. Objective: To investigate the pharmacokinetic profile, absolute bioavailability and metabolic pathways of ONA in rats following oral and intravenous administration. Methods: In-silico ADME predictions (SwissADME, GLORYx) were initially performed to guide the experimental design. Healthy male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were administered ONA either orally (36.66 mg/kg) or intravenously (3.75 mg/kg). A validated UHPLC–MS/MS method was utilized for pharmacokinetic quantification, while UHPLC–Q–Exactive Orbitrap HRMS was employed for comprehensive metabolite profiling in biological matrices. Results: Ten metabolites were identified, with the parent compound and metabolites predominantly detected in feces. After oral administration, ONA exhibited a Cmax of 441.43 ± 111.09 ng/mL at tmax 1.3 h, t1/2 of 1.38 ± 0.61 h, an AUC0-∞ of 1027.29 ± 399.45 h·ng/mL and absolute bioavailability of 12.6%. Intravenous administration showed rapid systemic clearance (CLobs = 4.64 ± 0.86 L/h/kg), a large apparent volume of distribution (Vobs = 10.13 ± 5.16 L/kg) and an AUC0-∞ of 831.20 ± 154.99 h·ng/mL, consistent with extensive tissue distribution of lipophilic triterpenes. Conclusion: ONA exhibits low oral bioavailability, rapid clearance and extensive metabolism in rats. Fecal excretion represents a major detectable elimination route for ONA and its metabolites. These findings provide essential ADME information to support the rational development and formulation optimization of ONA-based therapeutics.

title: Reactivity and Permeability Dynamics of a Fe0/ Sand/ Pozzolan/ Charcoal Filter Bed for Water Treatment
summary: This experimental study focuses on optimizing the proportions of constituent materials in a quaternary reactive zone (RZ) based on zero-valent iron (Fe°) for water decontamination. The system investigated combines Fe° (25%), pozzolan (Pz, 2
content: This experimental study focuses on optimizing the proportions of constituent materials in a quaternary reactive zone (RZ) based on zero-valent iron (Fe°) for water decontamination. The system investigated combines Fe° (25%), pozzolan (Pz, 25%), sand (S), and natural charcoal (C) in varying proportions. Three (03) filtration systems were tested: (1) 25%Fe°/45%S/25%Pz/05%C; (2) 25%Fe°/35%S/25%Pz/15%C; (3) 25%Fe°/25%S/25%Pz/25%C. Methyl orange (OM) at 2 mg/L and pH 5.2 served as the tracer micropollutant. The parameters monitored over forty (40) days included residual iron, decontamination rate, conductivity, flow rate, redox potential, and pH. The results indicate that all three systems initially release Fe²⁺ (3.4 to 5.1 mg/L) through anodic corrosion of Fe°. The system containing 25% C maintains lower and more stable concentrations (maximum 3.4 mg/L), indicating better-distributed corrosion. The highest decontamination efficiency is observed in the 25%Fe°/25%S/25%Pz/25%C system, which is more performant and durable, with a decontamination rate between 98–100% and low, stable conductivity. This system also exhibits a low flow rate and high reactivity based on its potential values. All three systems raise pH values due to the buffering effect of charcoal.

title: MultiCat-KG: An Intelligent System Integrating Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model for Recommendation of Tandem Reaction Pathways Across Electro-, Photo- and Thermocatalysis
summary: Catalysis plays a central role in modern chemistry and chemical engineering, but it faces challenges, such as limited product selectivity, side reactions, greenhouse gas emissions, and high energy consumption. Coupling photo-, electro-, and
content: Catalysis plays a central role in modern chemistry and chemical engineering, but it faces challenges, such as limited product selectivity, side reactions, greenhouse gas emissions, and high energy consumption. Coupling photo-, electro-, and thermocatalysis provides a strategy for green and efficient conversion, offering fewer steps, reduced separation requirements, lower emissions, and improved atom economy. However, data on multicatalytic processes remain scattered across extensive literature, while complex mechanisms and inconsistent descriptions of reaction conditions limit efficient knowledge utilization. To overcome these bottlenecks, this work proposes a multicatalysis knowledge graph (MultiCat-KG), a framework integrating large language models (LLMs) and knowledge graphs (KGs) to provide a data-driven solution. We first designed a catalysis-specific ontology to define domain concepts and relationships, followed by a cross-domain data extraction workflow using published journal literature to structure, clean, and integrate data on reactions, intermediates, catalysts, and conditions. By aligning these data with the ontology, we constructed a KG covering photo-, electro-, and thermocatalysis to enable path retrieval and recommendation. Results show that MultiCat-KG can identify known high-value pathways and suggest promising candidates for coupling scenarios such as thermoelectrocatalysis and photothermocatalysis. An interactive interface enables efficient querying and decision making, providing a scalable data infrastructure for green catalysis research.

title: Anti‐Site Defects Enable Cr 4+ Heavy Doping for Efficient and Thermally Stable NIR‐II Luminescent Ceramics
summary: Near‐infrared‐II (NIR‐II) photons hold great promise for non‐invasive optical imaging, food analysis, and optical communication. However, designing broadband NIR‐II materials with high efficiency and thermal stability remains a significant
content: Near‐infrared‐II (NIR‐II) photons hold great promise for non‐invasive optical imaging, food analysis, and optical communication. However, designing broadband NIR‐II materials with high efficiency and thermal stability remains a significant challenge. Here, a highly efficient and thermally stable NIR‐II luminescent ceramic Li 1.975 Na 0.025 MgGeO 4:Cr 4+ (LNMGOC) with a quantum efficiency of 62.1% and emission retention of 69.8% at 423 K is demonstrated via a pre‐oxidation/post‐reduction valence control strategy in an all‐tetrahedral matrix. The optimal Cr 4+ doping reaches 8% with absorption efficiency up to 73.2%, far exceeding the typical doping level of 1–4% in congeners. Defect formation energy calculation reveals that intrinsic anti‐site defects ( and ) suppress Cr 3+ occupation at [MgO 4], promoting Cr 3+ → Cr 4+ conversion and Cr 4+ incorporation into size‐matched [GeO 4], which enables high‐concentration Cr 4+ doping. This mechanism is further validated by marked luminescence quenching arising from reduced anti‐site defect concentration at Na + /K + substitution level above 5%. Benefiting from superior thermal stability and thermal conductivity, LNMGOC ceramic delivers 0.49 W NIR‐II output under 14 W·mm −2 saturated laser pumping, and realizes effective optical imaging and organic component detection. This work establishes an intrinsic defect‐mediated strategy for Cr 4+ stabilization and heavy doping toward high‐efficiency, thermally stable NIR‐II luminescent materials.

title: Pore‐Confined Ag Nanoclusters for Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction to Ethanol via Enhanced CO Binding and Intermediate Confinement
summary: Silver-based catalysts have attracted extensive research interest for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, their selectivity is typically limited to CO due to the inherently weak binding strength with the *CO interme
content: Silver-based catalysts have attracted extensive research interest for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, their selectivity is typically limited to CO due to the inherently weak binding strength with the *CO intermediate. Here, we develop a catalyst of ultrafine silver nanoclusters confined within nitrogen-doped mesoporous carbon (Ag-in) via a pore-confinement strategy for efficient electrochemical CO2-to-ethanol conversion. The Ag-in catalyst achieves a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 15.3% for ethanol at -1.25 V vs. RHE in a flow cell, with a production rate of 99.4 µmol h-1 cm-2. In contrast, the control catalyst with silver nanoparticles supported predominantly on the exterior surface of the mesoporous carbon (Ag-out) shows no detectable ethanol production during CO2RR. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this unique selectivity arises from the low-coordinated silver nanoclusters with an increased d-band center and enhanced *CO binding affinity, along with the promoted CO concentration in the vicinity of Ag catalytic sites due to the confinement effect of mesoporous carbon. This work not only presents a novel approach for efficient ethanol production from electrochemical CO2RR but also paves the way for the development of non-copper-based catalysts for carbon-neutral energy conversion processes.

title: An Analytical Study of Risk and Return in Public and Private Mutual Funds
summary: Introduction: Mutual funds are a very important financial market scheme in the current economy as it deals with multiple investments and market shares. It can boost the economy of developing nations by a significant amount. Aim: The study a
content: Introduction: Mutual funds are a very important financial market scheme in the current economy as it deals with multiple investments and market shares. It can boost the economy of developing nations by a significant amount. Aim: The study aims to know the value of Mutual funds in the improvement level of sectors in private and public. Literature Review: Mutual funds have many advantages like liquidity, diversification of markets, management by experts in finances, bulk transactions in billions of dollars and most importantly work through a cost-efficient process. Methodology: Primary quantitative method is used to collect data and relevant information from the survey questionnaire. 55 participants took part in the survey and their responses were recorded. Findings: It was found that mutual funds have huge benefits in terms of an economic boost for developing nations and it provides ample opportunities to invest for a hefty return. Discussion: Transaction challenges and risks are the most important in terms of issues seen in mutual funds markets. Despite all the risks, the mutual funds market is an emerging asset of economies in developing economic nations. Conclusion: Mutual funds in private and public sectors have huge potential in terms of market boost and economic advancements.

title: Spherulite-size modulation of electrical insulation performance in polypropylene
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Polypropylene (PP) is a promising recyclable insulating material for next-generation high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) cables, owing to its melt recyclability, thermal stability and favourable DC dielectric performance. While cooling-rate
content: Polypropylene (PP) is a promising recyclable insulating material for next-generation high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) cables, owing to its melt recyclability, thermal stability and favourable DC dielectric performance. While cooling-rate regulation is known to modify PP crystallization morphology and space-charge behaviour, the microstructural mechanism by which spherulite size simultaneously governs charge transport, electrical breakdown and mechanical fracture remains insufficiently understood. In this work, PP films with varying spherulite sizes were prepared by controlling the cooling rate during non-isothermal crystallization. DC breakdown strength, volume conductivity and tensile properties were characterized. Local trap parameters in crystalline interiors and interspherulitic amorphous boundaries were extracted in situ using atomic force microscopy (AFM)-assisted nanoscale isothermal surface-potential decay, and were incorporated into an electrical breakdown coupled with molecular displacement model based on two-dimensional Voronoi morphology. The results show that spherulite refinement markedly increases the characteristic DC breakdown field and reduces volume conductivity, while tensile testing further reveals concurrent improvements in tensile strength and elongation at break. Local measurements reveal that amorphous boundaries have a lower deep-trap density than spherulite interiors, rendering them relatively high-conductivity regions. Nevertheless, macroscopic conductivity is governed not by local conductivity alone, but by the long-range connectivity of these amorphous pathways. Large spherulites form continuous boundary networks, which promote charge migration, field distortion and electron-energy accumulation. In contrast, refined spherulites divide the amorphous phase into shorter and more tortuous pathways, effectively suppressing continuous charge transport, molecular-chain displacement and through-crack propagation. This topology-induced confinement mechanism accounts for the concurrent improvement in DC insulation strength and mechanical toughness of PP.

title: System-level optimization of seawater-based water supply and cooling for large-scale green hydrogen and ammonia production under variable renewable operation
summary: As green hydrogen and ammonia projects expand in arid coastal regions, coupled demands for process water (PW) and cooling water (CW) increasingly constrain cooling system (CS) selection and water supply infrastructure sizing. To address thi
content: As green hydrogen and ammonia projects expand in arid coastal regions, coupled demands for process water (PW) and cooling water (CW) increasingly constrain cooling system (CS) selection and water supply infrastructure sizing. To address this research gap, a transferable methodology for designing and techno-economically evaluating cooling and water supply systems for large-scale seawater-based production is presented. It combines time-resolved renewable power and ammonia production modelling, CS performance models, water treatment plant (WTP) sizing, PW and CW storage simulation, and cost assessment. It is applied to the 1.5 GW Phase 1 Murchison Green Hydrogen Project in Western Australia as a case study, using hourly ERA5 climate data for 2015–2024. The investigated CS options include once-through seawater cooling (OTSC), dry cooling (DC), wet cooling towers (WCT), and adiabatic hybrid coolers (AHC). Storage-based optimization substantially reduced the required peak treatment capacities, lowering WTP capacity by 12.4% (to 273 m 3 /h) for PW and CW capacity by 20.6% (to 1,127 m 3 /h) for WCT, and 63.0% (to 636 m 3 /h) for AHC. These reductions translated directly into lower PW-related capital expenditure, operational expenditure, and levelized cost of water (−8.7%, −4.2%, and − 7.3%, respectively). On an integrated cost basis, WCT achieved the lowest levelized cost of cooling (5.96 USD/MWh th ), below DC (38.0%), AHC (44.7%), and OTSC (73.6%). A simplified cost-allocation sensitivity showed that neglecting water treatment and marine infrastructure requirements can alter the CS ranking. The analysis further indicated that CS and water supply make a non-negligible contribution to the total levelized cost of hydrogen, accounting for 2.0–7.4%.

title: Sustainable Cold Chain Logistics for Fisheries: A Systematic Review of Facility Location–Allocation and Coastal Spatial Planning
summary: Abstract* Fishery products are prone to quality deterioration during post-harvest handling and distribution. Therefore, the development of a sustainable cold chain requires the integration of facility planning, distribution efficiency, coas
content: Abstract* Fishery products are prone to quality deterioration during post-harvest handling and distribution. Therefore, the development of a sustainable cold chain requires the integration of facility planning, distribution efficiency, coastal zone management, and socio-ecological considerations. This study aims to synthesize these approaches and identify gaps in their integration. A systematic review was conducted through a literature search in the Scopus database, with reporting guided by PRISMA 2020. The initial search yielded 396 records; 222 records were retained after applying the publication year restriction of 2016–2026. Screening for document type, language, and access resulted in 134 records for title and abstract evaluation. A total of 37 publications proceeded to the eligibility assessment stage, and 12 publications were reported in a qualitative-thematic synthesis based on four research questions. The synthesis identified four main themes: location-allocation optimization and low-emission distribution; coastal spatial-ecological planning; facility accessibility and socioeconomic resilience; and carbon traceability and accountability. The results show that technical, ecological, and social approaches make complementary contributions, but their integration into a single fisheries cold chain planning model has not been comprehensively demonstrated in the reviewed literature. This study proposes a Coastal Cold Chain Integration Triad Framework that links spatial-ecological suitability, facility location-allocation optimization, and socio-ecological resilience and supply chain integrity. This framework provides a conceptual basis for research and planning in sustainable fisheries logistics, with a need for further empirical testing.

title: Synergistic Mechanisms and Integrated Design Strategies of Adsorption–Catalysis Bifunctional Materials for Emerging Pollutant Removal
summary: Emerging pollutants, though present at trace levels in aquatic environments, pose persistent ecological risks that conventional treatment fails to fully mitigate. Despite the booming development of bifunctional materials integrating adsorpt
content: Emerging pollutants, though present at trace levels in aquatic environments, pose persistent ecological risks that conventional treatment fails to fully mitigate. Despite the booming development of bifunctional materials integrating adsorption and catalysis, a critical disparity persists-their exceptional lab-scale performance rarely translates into practical water treatment. This review critically deconstructs this efficiency-viability gap, attributing it primarily to the intrinsic spatiotemporal mismatch between adsorption kinetics and catalytic turnover, alongside severe matrix interference. Subsequently, we systematically re-evaluate recent advances across carbon, metal oxide, metal-organic frameworks (MOF), and layered double hydroxides (LDH) systems, not merely by cataloging their structures, but by interrogating their failure mechanisms under realistic conditions. Finally, we propose a paradigm shift from material-centric optimization to process-driven interfacial engineering, outlining data-driven and modular strategies to bridge the gap between promise and practice.

title: Avrupa Yeşil Mutabakatı Çerçevesinde Türkiye’nin İklim Değişikliği Uyum Sürecine Yönelik Bir Değerlendirme
summary: İklim değişikliği, çevresel, ekonomik ve toplumsal etkileri nedeniyle uluslararası gündemin temel başlıklarından biri olmaya devam etmektedir ve ülkelerin bu alanda ulusal ve uluslararası düzeyde çeşitli politika ve uygulamalar geliştirmele
content: İklim değişikliği, çevresel, ekonomik ve toplumsal etkileri nedeniyle uluslararası gündemin temel başlıklarından biri olmaya devam etmektedir ve ülkelerin bu alanda ulusal ve uluslararası düzeyde çeşitli politika ve uygulamalar geliştirmelerine zemin hazırlamaktadır. Avrupa Yeşil Mutabakatı (AYM) aday ülke statüsündeki Türkiye açısından iklim politikalarının Avrupa Birliği (AB) hedefleriyle uyumlaştırılması sürecine yeni bir boyut kazandırmıştır. Bu çalışma, Türkiye’nin iklim değişikliğine yönelik politika ve düzenlemelerini AYM kapsamında geliştirilen AB iklim politikaları bağlamında ele alarak Türkiye’nin uyum sürecini değerlendirmektedir. Çalışmada literatür taramasına dayalı betimsel bir inceleme yapılmıştır. Bu kapsamda; başta AYM olmak üzere AB’nin iklim değişikliğine yönelik politika ve düzenlemeleri ile Türkiye’nin 7552 sayılı İklim Kanunu, ilgili politika belgeleri, stratejileri ve eylem planları incelenmiştir. Bulgular, Türkiye’nin AYM öncesinde de iklim değişikliğiyle mücadele ve yeşil dönüşüm alanlarında çeşitli çalışmalar yürüttüğünü; AYM’nin yayımlanmasının ardından ise bu alanlardaki politika ve hukuki düzenlemelerin AB iklim politikalarıyla uyumu doğrultusunda gelişmeye devam ettiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Bununla birlikte, belirlenen hedeflerin uygulamaya daha güçlü biçimde yansıtılması, kaydedilen ilerlemenin somut göstergelerle izlenmesi ve kurumlar arası koordinasyonun geliştirilmesi, uyum sürecinin güçlendirilmesi açısından öne çıkan başlıca alanlar arasında yer almaktadır. Genel olarak çalışma, Türkiye’nin iklim politikalarının AB politikalarıyla yakınlaşma yönünde ilerleme kaydettiği ancak mevcut politika ve uygulamaların etkinliğinin artırılmasının AYM hedefleriyle daha kapsamlı bir uyumu destekleyebileceği sonucuna ulaşmaktadır.

title: Exploring motivations, challenges and strategic actions in setting Science-based Targets (SBTs) by New Zealand firms
summary: This study critically examines the extent to which corporate emissions reduction targets are grounded in science-based principles. It explores the motivations, challenges and strategies that shape such target setting. The study adopts a mix
content: This study critically examines the extent to which corporate emissions reduction targets are grounded in science-based principles. It explores the motivations, challenges and strategies that shape such target setting. The study adopts a mixed-methods design. It combines longitudinal content analysis of over 500 organisational reports from New Zealand’s 50 largest listed firms over ten years (2012–2021) with 29 interviews with senior managers from 23 of those firms in 2019. Drawing on achievement goal theory, we identify four distinct clusters of firms: mastery approach, performance approach, mastery avoidance, and performance avoidance, and map each cluster to observable target-setting practices. Mastery avoidance is the most prevalent approach which reflects an absence of science-based targets driven by a lack of know-how, a lack of technology, constraints on the needed changes in assets, or a lack of external guidance. The next common cluster is a performance approach where firms manage stakeholders’ relationships through supplier engagement targets, participation in policy processes, and the use of third-party verification to enhance credibility. Performance avoidance is much less popular which is characterised by reliance on offsetting; the adoption of feasible targets aligned with current capabilities and cautious external disclosure. Finally, mastery-oriented firms develop absolute science-based targets and undertake substantive operational and business model change to achieve their targets. Overall, the study contributes to accounting and sustainability literatures by explaining how firms adopt (or avoid) setting science-based targets, and how they operationalise these targets to make progress on their climate mitigation journey.

title: Mapping Sustainability Indicators in Higher Education Institutions: A Multi-Framework Analysis Based on the UNEP Sustainable University Framework
source: Mindanao Journal of Science and Technology
summary: Universities play a pivotal role in advancing global sustainability agendas through education, research, and institutional governance. Yet, most existing sustainability assessment frameworks remain fragmented and overly focused on environme
content: Universities play a pivotal role in advancing global sustainability agendas through education, research, and institutional governance. Yet, most existing sustainability assessment frameworks remain fragmented and overly focused on environmental performance. This study adopts a hybrid review approach combining database searches with official framework documents, followed by directed content and mapping analysis to classify 463 sustainability indicators from eight global and regional higher-education frameworks. Databases included Science Direct, MDPI, and official institutional manuals, with defined inclusion and exclusion criteria, a 2015–2024 time span, and an English-language restriction. Two researchers independently coded all indicators using a predefined codebook and aligned them with the UNEP Sustainable University Framework (UNEP-SUF), covering four dimensions—Environment & Climate (EC), Teaching & Research (TR), People & Society (PS), and Administration & Governance (AG)—with inter-coder reliability of κ = 0.75. Results reveal a significant imbalance: EC (48.81%), AG (22.03%), PS (17.06%), and TR (12.10%), indicating that sustainability measurement remains predominantly environmental and operational. UI GreenMetric and FAS-EUC showed a higher concentration of environmental indicators, whereas STARS offered more equitable representation across dimensions. Pielou’s evenness index evaluated dimensional proportionality, while frequency counts confirmed EC dominance. As a technical foundation for campus sustainability, the UNEP-SUF supports an indicator-based assessment and decision-support method for Science and Technology (S&T) applications in campus infrastructure management, enabling HEIs to address structural imbalances across all four dimensions. Future work requires weighted scoring and empirical validation to strengthen generalizability.

title: Organizing the area of Human Biometeorology in Brazil – insights from the third Human Biometeorology Symposium
summary: This short communication provides an overview of the Third Brazilian Symposium on Human Biometeorology, held in August 2026 in São Paulo, Brazil. By synthesizing key insights from oral presentations, round tables, and keynote lectures, this
content: This short communication provides an overview of the Third Brazilian Symposium on Human Biometeorology, held in August 2026 in São Paulo, Brazil. By synthesizing key insights from oral presentations, round tables, and keynote lectures, this summary highlights critical research gaps and emerging opportunities in the field. This third edition further solidified the national working group's collaborative efforts, establishing the symposium as a leading, long-term venue for advancing human biometeorology research.

title: Evaluation of waste-to-fuel potential in Ukraine
summary: The article discusses the problem of the impact of household waste on the environmental condition of Ukraine, as well as ways to solve it. Today, in the world, in particular in Ukraine, there is a significant danger of the lithosphere, atmo
content: The article discusses the problem of the impact of household waste on the environmental condition of Ukraine, as well as ways to solve it. Today, in the world, in particular in Ukraine, there is a significant danger of the lithosphere, atmosphere and hydrosphere pollution by household and industrial waste. The role of the negative waste impact on the environmental condition of Ukraine in the formation of the degree of environmental hazard hasn’t been sufficiently studied. Over the past 100 `years, mankind has increased energy resources more than 1000 times, while increasing the volume of industrial and agricultural products. This, in turn, led to an increase in the amount of waste. The main objectives of the work were to justify the use of household waste as a raw material for alternative fuels in Ukraine and to determine the contribution to the formation of the economic hazard degree due to environmental pollution with solid household waste. The negative impact of waste on Ukraine’s environmental condition has been studied. The shortcomings of the actual solid waste disinfection methods were analyzed. The method of household waste processing for the purpose of obtaining alternative energy sources was substantiated. It has been established that the most effective method of reducing emissions of biogas (landfill gas) from solid household waste landfills into the atmosphere was its collection and use. The economic indicators of landfill gas production and recycling projects are quite profitable, especially when the landfill is located close to an industrial gas consumer. The development of technologies for the production and use of landfill gas is very promising for Ukraine from both an environmental and an economic point of view. State regulation in the field of waste processing is of high importance, since it will not only improve the environmental condition of our country, but can also significantly affect the improvement of the energy situation in Ukraine. Research results can be applied in the field of environmental protection. The results of this work can be applied by expert environmentalists, as well as energy engineers and experts in the field of the production and rational use of alternative energy sources.

title: Vis-NIR and MIR Sensor Synergy enables Robust Assessment of Spatio-Temporal Soil Property Alterations
summary: Understanding how intensive agricultural management affects the spatial organisation and temporal stability of soil properties is important for long-term experimentation and digital soil monitoring. We investigated changes between 2011 and
content: Understanding how intensive agricultural management affects the spatial organisation and temporal stability of soil properties is important for long-term experimentation and digital soil monitoring. We investigated changes between 2011 and 2021 at the 15-ha Crop Research Unit Merbitz (Central Germany) and assessed the performance and transferability of Vis-NIR, MIR and synergistic spectroscopy for predicting seven soil properties. Samples were collected on a 25-m grid (n = 480 per year). PLS, Cubist and Random Forest were evaluated with algorithm-specific feature-selection methods, varying calibration proportions, and vertical (topsoil-subsoil) and temporal transfer. Field-scale spatial organisation remained broadly persistent over the decade, while the individual soil properties changed to different degrees. In particular, topsoil SOM showed an increased relative contribution of small-scale or unstructured variability, whereas other properties retained more persistent spatial patterns. Spectra were more similar between years in the topsoil than in the subsoil, although both depths showed substantial temporal continuity Predictive performance was dependent on the spectral dataset, property and depth. The synergistic dataset significantly outperformed MIR in both depths and outperformed Vis-NIR in the topsoil. CaCO₃ was predicted best (RPD up to 5.54), whereas SOM and topsoil texture fractions were difficult to predict. Cubist achieved the highest mean predictive performance, and feature selection maintained comparable performance with fewer wavelengths. Gains from larger calibration proportion were property-dependent and limited for weakly predicted properties. CaCO₃ retained comparatively high performance under both vertical and temporal transfer, whereas SOM, pH H2O and texture fractions were more sensitive to transfer. These results indicate that persistent spatial and spectral characteristics can support, but do not guarantee transferability, which depends on the stability of the spectral-property relationship. Overall, the findings support property-specific calibration and transferability assessment as important components of efficient long-term spectroscopy monitoring.

title: Multi-Fault Detection Method for Lithium-Ion Batteries Using a Dual-Branch Feature Fusion Network
summary: To ensure the safe service of electric vehicles, accurate diagnosis of low state-of-charge (SOC) and micro internal short-circuit (ISC) faults in power batteries under real-world conditions is essential. This paper proposes a dual-branch fe
content: To ensure the safe service of electric vehicles, accurate diagnosis of low state-of-charge (SOC) and micro internal short-circuit (ISC) faults in power batteries under real-world conditions is essential. This paper proposes a dual-branch feature extraction and classification decision-based multi-fault diagnosis method that integrates fused features of microscopic and macroscopic. Firstly, time series features and macroscopic statistical features that can reflect battery faults are extracted preliminarily. The dual branch feature extraction model with raw time-series data and statistical features as inputs to further explore potential fault features is constructed. Then, automatic recognition of normal, low-SOC faults, and ISC faults through feature fusion and classification decision-making. Finally, compared with the four classic models, the dual-branch fusion model proposed in this study achieves the best performance: accuracy, balanced accuracy, and macro-average F1 are 92.86%, 96.67%, and 93.481%, respectively.

title: Does economic prosperity lead to environmental sustainability in developing economies? evidence from the environmental Kuznets Curve
summary: This study examined whether economic prosperity contributes to environmental sustainability in developing economies, drawing on empirical evidence from Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) theory. The study employed a quantitative explanatory
content: This study examined whether economic prosperity contributes to environmental sustainability in developing economies, drawing on empirical evidence from Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) theory. The study employed a quantitative explanatory research design using panel data from 45 developing economies across Africa, Asia, and Latin America spanning 1996–2023. Data were sourced from World Bank Development Indicators and International Energy Agency statistics. The analysis used the panel Augmented Mean Group (AMG) and Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG) estimators. The study found the following: an insignificant linear relationship between economic prosperity and environmental sustainability; prosperity reduces pollution intensity in developing countries; no evidence of an inverted-U relationship; however, a U-shaped relationship is found in low-income countries; and finally, economic prosperity reduces carbon emissions in developing countries while increasing them in low-income countries beyond the estimated turning points. The findings underscore the need for governments of developing countries to establish renewable energy mandates requiring progressive increases in clean energy share. They should redirect fossil fuel subsidies toward clean energy investment and green technology development.

title: Electrochemical Technologies for Cement Clinker Synthesis in the Context of Carbon Neutrality: Principles, Applications, and Progress
summary: Clinker production accounts for approximately 7–8% of global anthropogenic CO₂ emissions, of which about 60% originates from the process emissions of limestone decomposition. These emissions can hardly be eliminated by conventional energy-e
content: Clinker production accounts for approximately 7–8% of global anthropogenic CO₂ emissions, of which about 60% originates from the process emissions of limestone decomposition. These emissions can hardly be eliminated by conventional energy-efficiency measures, so achieving carbon neutrality calls for transformative production technologies. Electrochemical technologies employ electrons as clean reagents to achieve the directional conversion of substances under ambient conditions and have been validated industrially in chlor-alkali production, water electrolysis, and lithium-ion batteries. Based on an analysis of the structural dilemmas faced by the cement industry in energy consumption, environmental pollution, and carbon emissions, this paper introduces the fundamentals and core advantages of electrochemical technologies and reviews their applications in cement clinker synthesis. It covers the reaction mechanisms of low-temperature pH-gradient electrolysis, high-temperature molten-salt electrolysis, electrochemical conversion of silicate minerals, and direct electrosynthesis of active phases, as well as the evolution of cement electrolyzer configurations and key materials. The application prospects are assessed through life-cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, and industrialization cases. The electrochemical route can reduce carbon emissions by more than 75% and even achieves carbon negativity when coupled with non-carbonate silicate feedstocks, representing a transformative direction for the deep decarbonization of the cement industry.

title: The Ecological Limits of Growth‐Led Development
summary: Whether economic growth can improve ecological balance without exceeding regenerative capacity is a central sustainable‐development question. This study examines how economic growth and the renewable energy transition relate to ecological b
content: Whether economic growth can improve ecological balance without exceeding regenerative capacity is a central sustainable‐development question. This study examines how economic growth and the renewable energy transition relate to ecological balance through the load capacity factor (LCF). The analysis draws on a balanced panel of 94 countries over the period 1996–2020. The LCF is computed as the ratio of per capita biocapacity to the per capita consumption‐based ecological footprint. Long‐ and short‐run relationships are assessed with CS‐ARDL, variation across the conditional distribution with the method of moments quantile regression (MMQR), and predictive direction with a bootstrap panel Granger test. The findings do not support the expectation that economic growth improves ecological balance of its own accord beyond a certain income level. The quadratic income term is insignificant in every long‐run and distributional specification, and the load capacity curve hypothesis is not confirmed. The income coefficient declines significantly toward the upper quantiles of the conditional distribution, yet most quantile‐level coefficients are statistically indistinguishable from zero. The results for renewable energy are sensitive to the estimation approach. While standard mean‐group estimates yield no significant long‐run relationship, sensitivity estimates that trim extreme country coefficients, the MMQR results, and alternative specifications produce a recurring positive pattern. The predictive direction analyses point to short‐run, one‐way temporal precedence from income and renewable energy toward the LCF, and the findings are not interpreted as structural causality. The results indicate that sustainability cannot be treated as an automatic by‐product of economic growth and that energy, consumption, and ecosystem policies need to be designed in an integrated manner.

title: When Does Mineral Wealth Advance SDG 7 and SDG 13? Conditional and Nonlinear Evidence From Ghana's Clean Energy Transition
summary: To achieve the SDGs, particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), countries must move rapidly toward clean energy systems, especially in developing countries with abundant mineral resources. Although mineral
content: To achieve the SDGs, particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), countries must move rapidly toward clean energy systems, especially in developing countries with abundant mineral resources. Although mineral resources can finance and supply inputs for renewable energy production, overreliance on extraction may hinder progress toward these goals. This study investigates whether, and under what conditions, mineral resource dependence impedes Ghana's clean energy transition, using a quantile‐on‐quantile regression (QQR) approach from 1990Q1 to 2023Q4. Drawing on Resource Curse Theory and the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis, this study analyses the relationships among mineral rents, economic growth (ECG), urbanisation (URB) and energy intensity (ENT) across the full range of CET. The findings reveal an interactive, nonlinear relationship: mineral resource rent activity positively affects CET at initial and middle phases of transition but limits progress at advanced transition levels. In contrast, CET is associated with ECG and URB in all scenarios, underscoring its role in inclusive and sustainable development. ENT exhibits bidirectional effects, supporting CET in specific conditions. URB and ECG, however, show weak associations with CET, suggesting policy tolerance or structural constraints. These findings further explain how structural factors affect CET in resource‐rich economies. The paper offers policy recommendations tailored to varying levels of CET maturity, including specialised reforms in city planning, fiscal openness and energy regulation.

title: Reaction‐Pathway Regulation for Degradation‐Insensitive Direct Regeneration of Spent LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 Cathode Materials
summary: (NCM523) cathode materials with different degradation states, we show that this limitation originates from competition among relithiation, structural recovery, and thermal decomposition during calcination. As the balance of these competing
content: (NCM523) cathode materials with different degradation states, we show that this limitation originates from competition among relithiation, structural recovery, and thermal decomposition during calcination. As the balance of these competing reactions shifts with degradation state, cathodes evolve along distinct reaction trajectories. Recognizing that these reactions are governed by the reactants, we regulate the regeneration reaction through the lithium-source reactant, causing cathode materials with different degradation states to pass through the same type of low-symmetry, synthesis-derived intermediate structure during calcination. This redirects regeneration toward a reconstruction pathway with favorable thermodynamics and improved ion diffusion, enabling rapid Li replenishment, long-range cation ordering, and structural restoration. Consequently, practical NCM523 black mass is regenerated into cathodes that deliver higher capacity and better capacity retention than those regenerated via the conventional pathway, and a 1.3 Ah pouch cell with the regenerated cathode retains 80.2% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles. This reconstruction pathway also enables direct upcycling of degraded NCM523 toward higher-Ni compositions. Broadly, this work provides a mechanistic framework for reducing degradation-state dependence in direct regeneration of spent cathode materials.

title: From baseload to backup: how capacity payments are redefining coal's role in China's power system
summary: Driven by high variable renewable energy penetration, eroding coal-plant viability in China’s energy-only markets threatens grid reliability, prompting a nationwide capacity-payment rollout. A key question is whether this mechanism can shif
content: Driven by high variable renewable energy penetration, eroding coal-plant viability in China’s energy-only markets threatens grid reliability, prompting a nationwide capacity-payment rollout. A key question is whether this mechanism can shift coal from baseload to backup without distorting competition or crowding out renewables. Combining a seasonally adjusted staggered difference-in-differences design with a multi-agent non-cooperative equilibrium model under carbon and green-certificate constraints, we quantify causal behaviors and welfare impacts across 31 provinces (2020–2025). Estimates show capacity payments provide a robust dynamic incentive, raising coal generation by about 3.13 TWh per month, peaking in the third month, consistent with peak-shaving and reliability provision rather than baseload operation. Effects are spatially heterogeneous: incentives strengthen in import-dependent load centers (Guangdong: +4.21 TWh/month) but weaken in transmission-constrained export regions (Shanxi: −0.18 TWh/month). Equilibrium simulations indicate that although the policy internalizes coal’s reliability value, it reduces photovoltaic revenues by 8.7%, suggesting a “green squeeze” in resource-rich areas, while total social costs fall by 2.3% through optimized fixed-cost recovery. These findings reframe capacity remuneration as a strategic “system regulator” that balances security, decarbonization, and affordability during the transition.

title: Lignified Wood: A Sustainable High‐Performance Alternative to Structural Alloys
summary: Developing high‐performance sustainable structural materials remains challenging. Here, we introduce a “lignin reintegration” strategy that returns lignin to wood to construct ultra‐strength and dimensionally stable materials. Without remov
content: Developing high‐performance sustainable structural materials remains challenging. Here, we introduce a “lignin reintegration” strategy that returns lignin to wood to construct ultra‐strength and dimensionally stable materials. Without removing native lignin or using petroleum‐derived resins, uncondensed aldehyde‐protected lignin (APL) was infiltrated into rotary‐cut wood veneers and subsequently hot‐pressed. During thermal densification, APL undergoes recondensation by formation of stable C–C crosslinks to reinforce intercellular interfaces at the nanoscale. Meanwhile, thermoplastic reflow of lignin promotes microfibril rearrangement, pore filling, and interfacial reconstruction, enabling hierarchical reinforcement across multiple length scales. The resulting lignified wood (LW) achieves a flexure strength of 382–405 MPa, along with ultralow water absorption and thickness swelling (< 1%) and outstanding hardness/puncture resistance. This process transforms lignin from a passive structural constraint into an active thermoplastic reinforcement phase, offering a scalable, sustainable, and chemical‐minimized route for next‐generation bio‐based structural materials.

title: Breaking the Voltage–Charge Trade‐Off in Bi‐Characteristic Current Triboelectric Nanogenerators via Charge‐Migration Engineering
summary: The energy output of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) requires the simultaneous buildup of load voltage and extraction of transferred charge. In emerging bi‐characteristic current TENGs (BC‐TENGs), however, these two quantities are mutu
content: The energy output of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) requires the simultaneous buildup of load voltage and extraction of transferred charge. In emerging bi‐characteristic current TENGs (BC‐TENGs), however, these two quantities are mutually constrained under practical loads: increasing the load voltage elevates the electrode potential, suppresses charged‐particle migration, and reduces the transferred charge. Here, we identify this load‐coupled voltage–charge trade‐off as a key energy‐extraction bottleneck in BC‐TENGs and establish an equivalent circuit model linking the external load to internal charged‐particle migration. This framework reveals that load‐induced electrode‐potential elevation reduces the effective potential drop across the migration region, weakens the driving electric field, and limits charge extraction under high‐voltage conditions. Guided by this mechanism, carbon‐particle‐assisted charge‐migration engineering is introduced into the porous polyurethane migration region to intensify the local electric field and lower the effective migration threshold. By optimizing carbon particle loading and spatial distribution, the device preserves triboelectrification while suppressing direct neutralization between oppositely charged residual regions. The optimized BC‐TENG delivers a ∼9‐fold enhancement in output energy and achieves an energy density of ∼19.73 J m −2. This work elucidates the influence of external load on the operating mechanism of BC‐TENGs, advances their theoretical framework, and provides guidelines for maximizing their energy output.

title: MASA Continuum: A Geopolitical Framework for Maghreb-Sahel Connectivity and Morocco-Algeria Rivalry
source: Journal of International and Prospective Studies
summary: The Maghreb and the Sahel are frequently examined through separate regional frameworks, obscuring the relationships connecting them. This article develops the MASA Continuum (Maghreb-Sahel-Africa) as a geopolitical framework for analyzing t
content: The Maghreb and the Sahel are frequently examined through separate regional frameworks, obscuring the relationships connecting them. This article develops the MASA Continuum (Maghreb-Sahel-Africa) as a geopolitical framework for analyzing these relationships and their implications for Morocco–Algeria rivalry. The analysis identifies the potential significance of Atlantic–Saharan–Sahelian connectivity for Morocco’s regional positioning, while emphasizing that infrastructure completion, partner-state agency, insecurity, and Algerian adaptation condition its strategic effects. Three prospective trajectories illustrate these contingencies. The article contributes a relational framework for studying cross-regional connectivity and middle-power rivalry, rather than a predictive model of an inevitable regional hierarchy.
