title: Avaliação da P+L (Produção Mais Limpa) e Priorização de Alternativas Ambientais Sustentáveis por meio do AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process): estudo de caso em uma empresa de Data Center
summary: A digitalização expandiu os Data Centers, intensificando o consumo de recursos, a geração de resíduos e as emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Este artigo avaliou a aplicação da Produção Mais Limpa (P+L) em um Data Center brasileiro e utili
content: A digitalização expandiu os Data Centers, intensificando o consumo de recursos, a geração de resíduos e as emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Este artigo avaliou a aplicação da Produção Mais Limpa (P+L) em um Data Center brasileiro e utilizou o método Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) para priorizar alternativas ambientais. A pesquisa, de natureza exploratória e abordagem qualitativa, adotou estudo de caso (entrevista por meio de questionário semiestruturado e análise documental) e aplicação do AHP. Os dados documentais indicaram PUE de 1,42, WUE de 0 L/kWh e 91,72% dos resíduos desviados de aterros. O AHP priorizou práticas ambientais da logística reversa e rastreabilidade, virtualização de servidores, energia renovável e eficiência térmica, otimização dos sistemas de arrefecimento, reuso e monitoramento de água, sistemas de contenção e detecção de vazamentos de emissões e energia de baixo carbono.

title: The Clinical-Industrial Paradigm: A Methodological Architecture Based on Hierarchical Bioethics for the Design of Health Products
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: The design of health products and devices has traditionally been guided by criteria of function, ergonomics, manufacturability and cost, while their environmental and distributive consequences, as well as their consequences for user autonom
content: The design of health products and devices has traditionally been guided by criteria of function, ergonomics, manufacturability and cost, while their environmental and distributive consequences, as well as their consequences for user autonomy, are usually assessed late or in a fragmentary way. This article proposes the Clinical-Industrial Paradigm, a conceptual methodological framework that transfers Diego Gracia's hierarchical principlism to the conceptual phase of industrial design in order to identify, prioritize and prevent the harms of products before they materialize. The research was qualitative and theoretical-conceptual and was carried out in three stages: a scoping review of 30 documents on design methodology, bioethics, circular economy, artificial intelligence governance and human rights; the construction of the framework from that synthesis; and its examination in three scenarios. The result was a three-phase sequence with explicit passage criteria: first, an ethics-of-minimums filter that evaluates distributive justice and non-maleficence, including environmental non-maleficence, before formal alternatives are generated; second, a beneficence oriented morphological synthesis that cannot reverse the achievements of the first phase; and third, a verification of autonomy and cognitive usability, with a plan for monitoring the product throughout its life cycle. When applied to the scenarios of single-use devices, neonatal equipment for low-resource settings and artificial intelligence-based diagnostic systems, the framework made visible harms that conventional approaches tend to overlook and steered decisions toward reprocessable, frugal and explainable solutions. These results come from a conceptual analysis rather than an empirical validation; studies with experts and real design cases are needed to evaluate its applicability, its reliability and its effect on professional practice.

title: Leveraging green opportunities to harmonize energy transition and ecological preservation in GCC economies
summary: This study examines the relationship between renewable energy transition and ecological conditions in the Gulf Cooperation Council economies, with particular emphasis on the moderating roles of green technology innovation and information an
content: This study examines the relationship between renewable energy transition and ecological conditions in the Gulf Cooperation Council economies, with particular emphasis on the moderating roles of green technology innovation and information and communication technology. Ecological footprint and load capacity factor are employed to capture environmental demand and carrying capacity dimensions. Using the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimator and the Method of Moments Quantile Regression approach as a robustness check, the findings indicate that renewable energy transition, green technology innovation, and ICT improve ecological conditions by enhancing load capacity factor and reducing ecological footprint. In contrast, population density and natural resource rents exert adverse environmental effects. The results support the inverted U-shaped Environmental Kuznets Curve within the ecological footprint framework and the U-shaped load capacity curve within the load capacity factor framework. Furthermore, the interaction effects reveal that advancements in green innovation and ICT amplify the ecological gains from renewable energy transition. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological innovation and digital infrastructure into energy transition strategies to strengthen ecological sustainability in GCC economies.

title: How much enhanced weathering carbon removal can croplands sustain?
summary: Regional and global scoping models are the main quantitative basis for projections of gigaton-scale carbon dioxide removal (CDR) from enhanced weathering on croplands (EW). Their CDR fluxes often reach about 4–12 t ha-1 yr-1, several times
content: Regional and global scoping models are the main quantitative basis for projections of gigaton-scale carbon dioxide removal (CDR) from enhanced weathering on croplands (EW). Their CDR fluxes often reach about 4–12 t ha-1 yr-1, several times higher than long-term liming studies suggest croplands can sustain at near-neutral pH. Because CDR from EW generally rises with pH, and pushing pH too high can cause adverse agronomic effects, these fluxes raise the question of whether croplands can sustain them without alkalizing. Scoping models simplify EW’s geochemistry to estimate CDR at large scales, and most do not track pH, leaving this question open. As a case study, we analyze the only scoping model we are aware of that reports the quantities needed to probe the carbonate chemistry linking CDR and pH. Closing the carbonate system reveals a trade-off: sustaining the model’s CDR fluxes on U.S. croplands would push pH above 8 nearly everywhere, whereas holding pH near neutral reduces CDR by more than 80 percent. Because this trade-off is governed by carbonate chemistry, it broadly applies to scoping models that project high CDR fluxes. In soils, buffering by reserve acidity can obscure this trade-off, dampening the pH response to weathering by neutralizing alkalinity that could otherwise become CDR. Models that omit this alkalinity loss, or do not simulate the pH response to EW, risk overestimating the CDR that croplands can sustain. We argue that carbonate system closure and soil acid-base balance are necessary constraints on estimates of CDR at scale. Although the pH threshold for agronomically acceptable EW deployment will vary among soils and crops, a provisional pH limit of 7.5 provides a useful ceiling for model projections. As in agricultural liming, sustaining CDR at a stable pH requires balancing the alkalinity supply from weathering with acid production and drainage.

title: Ownership Type and Corporate Green Innovation
summary: Corporate green innovation supports the transition to a low-carbon economy, but it remains unclear how green innovation differs across ownership types and what accounts for those differences. Using data on Chinese A-share listed firms from
content: Corporate green innovation supports the transition to a low-carbon economy, but it remains unclear how green innovation differs across ownership types and what accounts for those differences. Using data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2024, we apply the entropy weighting method to construct a composite index covering green innovation inputs, green innovation outputs, sustainability performance, and environmental performance. We examine the association between ownership type and green innovation, the role of financing constraints, and variation across regions and industries. State-owned enterprises score significantly higher on the composite index than non-state-owned enterprises. They also face significantly weaker financing constraints, which may help explain their green innovation advantage. The estimated advantage is statistically significant in eastern China and in manufacturing, while the estimates for central and western China and for non-manufacturing are statistically insignificant. These findings provide evidence for allocating green finance resources and tailoring policies to support green innovation.

title: Consolidation of Soft Ground Improved by Biodegradable Prefabricated Vertical Drains with Time-Dependent Discharge-Capacity Decay: A Field-Validated Finite-Element Study
summary: Biodegradable prefabricated vertical drains (PVDs) are an emerging green alternative to conventional plastic drains, but their core material degrades during service, so the drain discharge capacity decays with time and the well-resistance e
content: Biodegradable prefabricated vertical drains (PVDs) are an emerging green alternative to conventional plastic drains, but their core material degrades during service, so the drain discharge capacity decays with time and the well-resistance effect intensifies; consolidation analyses that assume a constant discharge capacity therefore cannot reproduce the true field behaviour. Unlike previous analyses that assume an exponential or polynomial decay, this paper calibrates the discharge-capacity decay directly from laboratory tests and embeds it in a field-validated finite-element (FE) consolidation model. Laboratory accelerated-degradation and longitudinal discharge-capacity tests provided the measured decay data; after comparison with an exponential model, a logistic function with upper and lower asymptotes was selected to describe the decay, and was converted, via Darcy’s law and the equivalent-hydraulic-radius method, into a time-dependent decay function of the drain permeability. Because general-purpose FE codes cannot vary a parameter continuously in time, a staged-assignment method was proposed that discretises the continuous decay curve into successive stages and updates the drain permeability stage by stage. Using the Soft-Soil constitutive model for the non-linear compressibility of dredged silty clay, the model was validated against field settlement and excess-pore-pressure measurements at Meishan Port, Ningbo, and then applied to sensitivity analyses of the drain spacing, decay rate and decay amplitude and a 1000-day long-term prediction, providing a calibratable and field-verifiable reference for the design-parameter selection of biodegradable-PVD ground improvement.

title: Advances in RuO 2 -based heterostructures as high-performance electrocatalysts toward electrochemical water splitting
summary: The global pursuit of carbon neutrality has deepened people's understanding of green hydrogen, thereby accelerating the growing demand for this clean energy carrier. Among the existing production strategies, water electrolysis remains the o
content: The global pursuit of carbon neutrality has deepened people's understanding of green hydrogen, thereby accelerating the growing demand for this clean energy carrier. Among the existing production strategies, water electrolysis remains the only commercially viable way to produce zero-carbon-emission green hydrogen. Ru-based materials, especially ruthenium oxide (RuO2), exhibit great potential in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) of water electrolysis due to their high intrinsic activity and comparative cost advantages. However, RuO2 is prone to oxidative dissolution during water electrolysis, leading to structural instability and activity decay. This stability issue has become a key bottleneck restricting its practical application. Constructing heterojunction catalysts provides a feasible path to surpass the performance limitations of single-component materials. By forming interfacial coupling between RuO2 and functional materials, including metals, metal oxides, and nonmetallic compounds, the adsorption energy of reaction intermediates is optimized, thereby enhancing catalytic activity while inhibiting the dissolution of active components and improving structural stability. This review provides a systematic overview of recent advances in RuO2-based heterojunction electrocatalysts for water electrolysis across both acidic and alkaline environments. This review specifically elucidates the design and synthesis strategies and discusses the related mechanisms for performance improvement. Furthermore, this review analyzes the remaining challenges in the synergistic tuning of the activity and stability of RuO2-based heterojunction catalysts and outlines prospective research directions to address these gaps.

title: Percentile-based cooling load sizing and thermal comfort assessment for a UAE residential villa: A TRNSYS case study
summary: The residential sector in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) accounts for a substantial share of national electricity demand, with air conditioning responsible for nearly 80% of building energy consumption. This study addresses the persistent c
content: The residential sector in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) accounts for a substantial share of national electricity demand, with air conditioning responsible for nearly 80% of building energy consumption. This study addresses the persistent challenge of oversizing cooling systems in hot–humid climates by developing and validating a simulation-based framework for a two-story villa in Dubai. The building was modeled in TRNSYS with geometry and envelope properties defined according to UAE building codes. Model adequacy was assessed through external calibration against published UAE residential measurements and complementary E20 cooling-load cross-validation. An integrated simulation–statistical approach was applied to identify percentile-based cooling design capacities using the 97 th percentile of annual load–frequency distributions, rather than conventional maximum-load sizing. The calibrated simulation predicted an annual cooling-demand reduction of 12,737.64 ton·h (17.2%) relative to maximum-load sizing. Using the adopted COP of 3.5 and the Dubai Electricity and Water Authority emissions factor, this corresponds to an estimated electrical-energy saving of 12.80 MWh/year and an estimated avoided emission of 5.17 tCO₂/year. Thermal comfort evaluation using the Predicted Mean Vote (PMV) model under peak summer conditions confirmed compliance with ASHRAE Standard 55, with PMV values maintained between −0.5 and +0.5. Benchmarking through the ASHRAE Building Energy Quotient (bEQ) framework further indicated an improvement in Building Performance Score from 237.8 to 196.5, although both configurations remained above the median benchmark of 100. The novelty of the framework lies in integrating 97th-percentile HVAC sizing with PMV-based thermal-comfort verification, ASHRAE bEQ benchmarking, and quantified electrical-energy savings and CO₂-emission reductions for a hot–humid UAE residential villa. Beyond the UAE context, the methodology demonstrates a transferable framework for aligning HVAC system sizing with actual demand in hot–humid climates, supporting energy efficiency, emission reduction, and improved thermal comfort globally.

title: Climate Policy Without Commitment
summary: Private investments in abatement technology often precede the policy that determines how much firms must abate. Motivated by this observation, we study a simple model in which the regulator sets abatement policy only after firms invest in a
content: Private investments in abatement technology often precede the policy that determines how much firms must abate. Motivated by this observation, we study a simple model in which the regulator sets abatement policy only after firms invest in a technology that determines their abatement costs. We show that, despite the regulator's inability to commit, cap-and-trade always implements the first-best outcome. Under a — practically common — policy of emissions standards, however, firms' green investments become strategic complements: if some firms invest heavily, abatement becomes cheaper and the regulator tightens the standard, inducing other firms to invest more as well. This strategic interaction is entirely policy-induced. We establish when this feedback generates equilibrium multiplicity, with a "green'' and a "brown'' equilibrium existing in parallel. The policymaker can eliminate the brown equilibrium by subsidizing investment. Investment subsidies are credible because they are paid if and when firms invest, thus circumventing the commitment problem. However, eliminating the brown equilibrium necessarily induces overinvestment relative to the first best. We characterize when the welfare gain from equilibrium selection outweighs this cost. These results are relevant because regulatory standards are pervasive in climate policy, including vehicle-emissions standards, energy-efficiency requirements, fuel-blending mandates, and technology mandates such as the phase-out of internal combustion engines.

title: Isolation of Cultivable Fishery By-products-derived Microorganisms with Carotenoid Production
summary: Fishery by-products are generated in increasing amounts during seafood processing, and management strategies that favor resource recovery over disposal or low-value use are needed. In this study, we examined fishery by-products as a source
content: Fishery by-products are generated in increasing amounts during seafood processing, and management strategies that favor resource recovery over disposal or low-value use are needed. In this study, we examined fishery by-products as a source of cultivable microorganisms with potential for carotenoid production. Bacteria and haloarchaea were isolated from the intestines and gills of hairtail, flatfish, and mackerel and identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. In total, 85 isolates (84 bacteria and one haloarchaeon) were obtained, and the 84 bacterial isolates were assigned to 28 families and 41 genera. Moraxellaceae was the most frequently recovered family and Pseudomonas the most frequently recovered genus. Thirty-seven isolates were selected on the basis of colony pigmentation and reports on related taxa, and 12 of them (11 bacteria and one haloarchaeon) showed carotenoid-associated profiles by HPLC-DAD-MS. Tentative assignments, based on retention time, absorption spectra, and nominal mass, included C 40 xanthophylls and ketocarotenoids as well as C 50 carotenoids. Related isolates sometimes showed similar profiles, as with the nostoxanthin-like profiles of three Sphingomonadaceae isolates, but this was not a general pattern across taxa. These results suggest that fishery by-products can serve as a source of diverse cultivable microorganisms with carotenoid production, which merit structural confirmation via high-resolution mass spectrometry and quantitative evaluation.

title: Enhanced luminescence and ultra-stability of WLEDs combined with urchin-like Ca 1− x Sr x WO 4:Ln 3+ with hierarchical structure through charge self-compensation combined with 3D printing
summary: Although rare-earth tungstates exhibit significant advantages in luminescence, the common problem of charge imbalance in traditional Ln3+ doping systems poses a serious challenge for further improving luminescence intensity and color purity
content: Although rare-earth tungstates exhibit significant advantages in luminescence, the common problem of charge imbalance in traditional Ln3+ doping systems poses a serious challenge for further improving luminescence intensity and color purity. Based on this, a charge self-compensation strategy is proposed by optimizing the charge balance state within the crystal lattice at the atomic scale, which effectively suppresses lattice defects and significantly reduces non-radiative transition processes, thereby greatly improving the luminescence intensity and stability. Detailed calculations and analysis based on density functional theory (DFT) were conducted on the crystal structure, band structure, density of states (DOS), and charge density distribution by constructing different doping structure models. The luminescence efficiency and stability have been improved by enhancing the hybridization of material orbitals. Compared with the corresponding uncompensated samples, the integrated emission peak area of Ca1−xSrxWO4:Ln3+ is enhanced by up to 2.96-fold after charge compensation. In addition, the three-dimensional (3D)-printed phosphor-resin composites exhibit robust storage stability, with their integrated emission peak areas remaining above 95% of the initial values after six months of storage. Finally, white light-emitting diodes (WLEDs) manufactured using optimized phosphors achieved better color quality with a color rendering index (CRI) of 95, highlighting their potential in high-quality solid-state lighting and indoor photovoltaic applications.

title: Lexicographic Energy-Efficient Scheduling in Semiconductor Assembly and Test Hybrid Flow Shops
summary: The hybrid flow shop scheduling problem (HFSP) is a widely used model for energy-efficient multi-stage manufacturing, yet semiconductor studies rarely combine discrete assembly and packaging, batch burn-in processing and speed-adjustable te
content: The hybrid flow shop scheduling problem (HFSP) is a widely used model for energy-efficient multi-stage manufacturing, yet semiconductor studies rarely combine discrete assembly and packaging, batch burn-in processing and speed-adjustable testing within a single four-stage formulation. Most also treat energy consumption as a Pareto trade-off with time-related objectives, which is less suitable for make-to-order production, where late delivery can cause revenue loss and customer attrition. This study addresses both gaps. A four-stage Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model determines job sequencing, machine assignment, burn-in batch formation and final-test speed selection under a lexicographic objective that minimizes total tardiness (TT) before total energy consumption (TEC). An Extended Teachers’ Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (E-TTLBO) algorithm is proposed with a four-string chromosome encoding and a greedy batch-packing decoder that constructively enforces oven-capacity feasibility during the search. Its performance is benchmarked against MILP solutions generated by IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio on small-scale instances, with optimality certified for a subset of cases. Across 18 instance configurations with 5 to 100 jobs, the proposed algorithm achieves an LR of at least 80% in 17 configurations against the Lexicographic Genetic Algorithm (Lex-GA) and in 16 configurations against Simulated Annealing (SA). In Phase 2, E-TTLBO lowers TEC by 8.8% to 21.7% relative to the Phase-1 tardiness-minimizing schedule, averaged over ten replications per configuration, with no increase in tardiness in any of the 180 runs. The average solution time remains below 110 s for the largest tested instances. These results indicate that energy savings from speed reduction and batch consolidation can be achieved without compromising delivery performance in semiconductor production.

title: Intelligent Large-Scale IoT: A Survey on Architectures, Learning, and Autonomous Decision-Making
summary: The rapid emergence of large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) systems leads to massive heterogeneous data generation, which raises significant challenges in scalability, semantic interoperability, security, and autonomous decision-making. Exi
content: The rapid emergence of large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) systems leads to massive heterogeneous data generation, which raises significant challenges in scalability, semantic interoperability, security, and autonomous decision-making. Existing state-of-the-art surveys primarily focus on individual technologies such as Deep Learning (DL), Federated Learning (FL), or IoT security, in isolation, providing limited insight into their integration for realizing intelligent IoT ecosystems. To address this gap, this survey presents a comprehensive data-to-decision framework that encompasses the entire intelligent IoT pipeline, including data acquisition, communication architectures, distributed intelligence, semantic interoperability, security, and autonomous decision-making. Specifically, this survey includes both centralized and distributed intelligence paradigms, including DL, FL, and Automated Machine Learning (AutoML), together with semantic interoperability methods based on knowledge graphs and learning-based security mechanisms. Additionally, we investigate intelligent decision-making approaches, with particular emphasis on Reinforcement Learning (RL) and multi-agent systems for enabling autonomous IoT operations. A systematic analysis of existing approaches is provided, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and integration challenges. Finally, we identify key research gaps and outline promising future directions, including foundation models, edge-native generative artificial intelligence, digital twins, continual learning, and trustworthy autonomous IoT systems.

title: A Geometry-Constrained Multi-View Triangulation Framework for Real-Time 3D Breathing-Zone Localization in AI-Driven Indoor Exposure Assessment
summary: Person-centered exposure assessment to indoor air pollutants requires resolving the inhalation interface (the mouth–nose region localization) of every occupant in three-dimensional (3D) space, but current vision and radar systems either lac
content: Person-centered exposure assessment to indoor air pollutants requires resolving the inhalation interface (the mouth–nose region localization) of every occupant in three-dimensional (3D) space, but current vision and radar systems either lack the vertical accuracy to localize the breathing zone or fail under multi-person occlusion. This work proposes a purely vision-based, geometry-constrained multi-view triangulation framework that produces a continuous stream of 3D breathing-zone coordinates suitable for direct coupling with pollutant concentration fields and downstream artificial intelligence (AI) health-effects models. Six synchronized RGB cameras feed a per-view YOLOv8-pose detector augmented with a head-top inference rule for back-facing occupants, after which a reference-camera-anchored two-view triangulation generates 3D hypotheses that must clear four geometric gates (reprojection, viewing-angle, cheirality, and room-bound) and an appearance-consistency gate built on re-identification (ReID) features before being clustered by appearance-aware Hungarian assignment with a tunable consensus radius. A constant-velocity Kalman tracker maintains stable global identities through an N-of-M candidate-confirmation buffer that suppresses single-frame ghost matches, a cross-view identity-voting and appearance re-acquisition layer that prevents identity fragmentation when a target is briefly lost, and a missing-candidate-revival pool that recovers identity continuity across short occlusions. The full system is implemented as a modular Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) pipeline of five independent nodes, enabling horizontal scaling and a clean perception/analytics boundary suitable for privacy-aware deployment. Evaluation in a six-camera indoor laboratory against an independent LiDAR reference reports a planar root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 183.1 mm and a vertical (breathing-zone height) RMSE of 101.7 mm against an independent reference, for a combined 3D RMSE of 209.5 mm, in real time. An ablation shows all five mechanisms are individually necessary—removing any one significantly increases the ghost rate—with missing-candidate revival the dominant contributor, followed by the N-of-M buffer and the inferred-keypoint gate for phantom-track suppression, the appearance-consistency gate for false-pairing reduction and improved MOTA, and the identity-voting layer with a smaller ghost-suppression role; the mechanisms improve the false-positive rate and track-count fidelity rather than reducing identity switches. The resulting 3D breathing-zone stream provides the missing perception layer for AI-driven inhalation-dose modeling, enabling the transition from station-level concentration averaging to truly per-person exposure-response analysis.

title: Posthumanism, Politics, Democracy: Quick Thoughts on (De/Re)Constructions of the Future
source: Word and Text - A Journal of Literary Studies and Linguistics
summary: This article asks what a posthumanist politics that does not hold itself above the raw processes of democratic participation might entail. It does so on the basis of cues arising from 2026 work within posthumanism, essayism, fiction and cur
content: This article asks what a posthumanist politics that does not hold itself above the raw processes of democratic participation might entail. It does so on the basis of cues arising from 2026 work within posthumanism, essayism, fiction and curation: Cary Wolfe’s Jagged Ontologies, Rebecca Solnit’s The Beginning Comes after the End, Ian McEwan’s What We Can Know and Are We Still Up to It?: Art and Democracy (Herrenchiemsee Palace / Pinakothek der Moderne, Munich). The discussion develops through reference to further pertinent perspectives, particularly arising from N. Katherine Hayles’s Bacteria to AI: Human Futures with Our Nonhuman Symbionts (2025), Anton Jäger’s Hyperpolitics: Extreme Politicization without Political Consequences (2025) and Judith Butler’s Notes toward a Performative Theory of Assembly (2015). Its conclusions turn on the intractability of the relation between the political imperatives of posthumanist thought and the compromises of democratic choice.

title: Clinical Deterioration Following Inadvertent Lacosamide Administration in an Unrecognized Lacosamide Overdose
summary: Introduction Lacosamide is increasingly used off-label for the treatment of status epilepticus and refractory status epilepticus. However, lacosamide overdose may also present with refractory seizures and cardiac sodium channel blockade, cr
content: Introduction Lacosamide is increasingly used off-label for the treatment of status epilepticus and refractory status epilepticus. However, lacosamide overdose may also present with refractory seizures and cardiac sodium channel blockade, creating diagnostic uncertainty when serum concentrations are not available in real time. We describe a patient with initially unrecognized lacosamide overdose who received additional lacosamide for presumed refractory status epilepticus and subsequently developed worsening seizures, ventricular dysrhythmias, and cardiac arrest. Case A 58-year-old male with focal epilepsy treated with lacosamide and lamotrigine presented after a witnessed seizure. Prehospital and emergency department electrocardiograms demonstrated wide-complex tachycardia with QRS prolongation and a terminal R’ wave in lead aVR. He received benzodiazepines and levetiracetam, was intubated for hypoxia, and was administered intravenous lacosamide 400 mg for presumed status epilepticus. After transfer to the neurocritical care unit, he was restarted on enteral lacosamide 250mg twice daily. He subsequently developed recurrent convulsions, hypotension, non-sustained and sustained ventricular tachycardia, and cardiac arrest approximately 24 hours after presentation. A suicide note and a half-empty lacosamide bottle were later discovered. Lacosamide was discontinued, and treatment included sodium bicarbonate, vasopressors, high-dose midazolam, ketamine, clobazam, and intravenous lipid emulsion. The earliest lacosamide concentration, obtained 60 minutes after arrival and before hospital-administered lacosamide, resulted on hospital day 5 at 110.4 mcg/mL. The peak concentration was 117.0 mcg/mL at 24.5 hours. QRS narrowing occurred after administration of several sodium bicarbonate boluses. The patient was discharged on hospital day 10 without permanent neurologic sequelae. Conclusion In patients prescribed lacosamide who present with refractory seizures, particularly in the presence of QRS widening or other evidence of sodium channel blockade, lacosamide toxicity should be considered before administering additional lacosamide. Alternative antiseizure agents may be prudent until overdose can be reasonably excluded.

title: Be Epic, Escape the Vape: Confidence Club for Youth Prevention
summary: The Be Epic, Escape the Vape youth prevention program includes prevention programming for youth, caregivers, teachers, and community members in rural Utah. The four-session youth Confidence Club with CATCH My Breath vape prevention curricul
content: The Be Epic, Escape the Vape youth prevention program includes prevention programming for youth, caregivers, teachers, and community members in rural Utah. The four-session youth Confidence Club with CATCH My Breath vape prevention curriculum components has been delivered at least once annually in three counties. Results of youth self-report post-surveys showed that youth increased their confidence, knowledge, and behavioral intentions for refusing e-cigarettes.

title: Optimization of laccase production by the birds nest fungus, Cyathus sp.
summary: This study aimed to isolate and optimize laccase production by Cyathus spp., collected from decaying wood in Kisii County, Kenya. The fungal isolate was characterized using morphological and molecular approaches and screened for laccase pro
content: This study aimed to isolate and optimize laccase production by Cyathus spp., collected from decaying wood in Kisii County, Kenya. The fungal isolate was characterized using morphological and molecular approaches and screened for laccase production using 2,2′-azino-bis (3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) and α-naphthol, while the effects of incubation time, initial pH, supplemental carbon and nitrogen sources, chemical inducers, and surfactants were assessed using a one-factor-at-a-time method under stationary submerged fermentation. Laccase activity was determined using ABTS as substrate and analyzed statistically using one-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey's post hoc test at P < 0.05. Laccase production increased progressively with incubation time and reached a maximum activity of 8.92 IU/mL on day 18. Among the tested pH values, pH 8.0 produced the highest activity, reaching 9.32 IU/mL on day 12. Glucose was the most effective supplemental carbon source, producing 21.01 and 21.14 IU/mL at 10 and 50 mM, respectively, on day 7. Among nitrogen sources, 80 mM yeast extract produced the highest activity of 35.1 IU/mL on day 12, while 80 mM peptone produced 21.7 IU/mL on day 7. For inducers, 0.25 mM CuSO₄ produced 8.74 IU/mL on day 7, whereas 0.25 mM MnSO₄ produced the highest activity of 9.48 IU/mL on day 12. Surfactants generally reduced laccase activity relative to the control, although 0.4% Triton X-100 produced activity comparable to the control on day 12. The outcomes demonstrate that culture conditions strongly affect laccase production by Cyathus spp. and provide preliminary data for further optimization using multivariate experimental designs and scale-up studies.

title: SAUDI ARABIAS TRANSFORMATION INTO A GLOBAL LOGISTICS HUB: OPPORTUNITIES AND IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGES UNDER VISION 2030
summary: Vision 2030 commits Saudi Arabia to becoming a global logistics hub that links Asia, Europe and Africa, and it set the goal of raising the country to 25th place in the international Logistics Performance Index. This paper examines what the
content: Vision 2030 commits Saudi Arabia to becoming a global logistics hub that links Asia, Europe and Africa, and it set the goal of raising the country to 25th place in the international Logistics Performance Index. This paper examines what the evidence says about the opportunities that support this ambition and the challenges that stand in the way of implementing it. It is based on a systematic integrative review of 30 refereed journal articles published from 2020 to 2025, two of which anchor the analysis: a spatial optimisation study of regional logistics hubs in the Kingdom and an analysis of Gulf economic diversification with Saudi Arabia as its case. Eighteen articles concern Saudi Arabia or the Gulf directly, and twelve provide international evidence on logistics performance, hub location, connectivity and port competition. The review identifies four groups of opportunity: geography and trade integration, sector-specific hubs for energy, aviation and religious tourism, trade facilitation, and the use of new technology in mobility and logistics. It also identifies four groups of challenge: a persistent gap between target and actual logistics performance in a competitive Gulf region, shortfalls in skills and the matching of national talent to logistics jobs, environmental pressures that rise with logistics activity, and governance and procurement arrangements that are still being reformed.

title: The Pristine Survey. XXX. Mapping substructures in the inner and outer halo with blue horizontal branch stars
summary: Blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars serve as good standard candles and kinematic tracers of the Milky Way halo. The halo displays various overdensities and kinematical substructures of different shapes and sizes. Our objective is to investig
content: Blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars serve as good standard candles and kinematic tracers of the Milky Way halo. The halo displays various overdensities and kinematical substructures of different shapes and sizes. Our objective is to investigate the substructure in three dimensions and the bulk motion of the halo up to distances well exceeding the limit of the parallaxes. Gaia We selected BHB stars in the łeft(u-CaHK̊ight) _ 0-$(g-r) _ 0$ colour-colour diagram with a hierarchical Bayesian mixture model of three populations: BHB stars, blue straggler stars, and outliers. Using CaHK photometry derived from XP spectra and the Pristine survey, we provide both a shallow and a deep catalogue of BHB stars of 7,057 and 8,824 stars, respectively, where the deep catalogue is restricted to the deeper Pristine footprint compared to the shallower with XP. Using the shallow catalogue, we trace to larger distances 6D substructures identified earlier within a 2.5 kpc from the Sun, including accepted populations; namely, Gaia-Enceladus, Thamnos, Helmi streams, Sequoia, and other smaller halo substructures such as ED-3, ED-4, and ED-6. The deep catalogue provides reliable distance measurements for a more detailed 3D mapping of the Sagittarius stream and of the Pisces Overdensity. We add new candidate BHB stars with line-of-sight velocities to existing catalogues and confirm previously reported differences between the northern and southern Galactic hemispheres, likely due to the infall of the Large Magellanic Cloud. Gaia Gaia This research demonstrates that probabilistic photometric classification can effectively identify distant candidate BHB stars, and can provide catalogues of these stars that enhance our understanding of the 3D and 6D structures in the halo of the Milky Way.

title: DeepLINK-T: deep learning inference for time series data using knockoffs and LSTM with applications to metagenomic data
summary: High-dimensional longitudinal time series data is prevalent across various real-world applications. Many such applications can be modeled as regression problems with high-dimensional time series covariates. Deep learning has been a popular
content: High-dimensional longitudinal time series data is prevalent across various real-world applications. Many such applications can be modeled as regression problems with high-dimensional time series covariates. Deep learning has been a popular and powerful tool for fitting these regression models. Yet, the development of interpretable and reproducible deep-learning models is challenging and remains underexplored. This study introduces a novel method, Deep Learning Inference using Knockoffs for Time series data (DeepLINK-T), focusing on the selection of significant time series variables in regression while controlling the false discovery rate (FDR) at a predetermined level. DeepLINK-T combines deep learning with knockoff inference to control FDR in feature selection for time series models, accommodating a wide variety of feature distributions. It addresses dependencies across time and features by leveraging a time-varying latent factor structure in time series covariates. Three key ingredients for DeepLINK-T are 1) a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) autoencoder for generating time series knockoff variables, 2) an LSTM prediction network using both original and knockoff variables, and 3) the application of the knockoffs framework for variable selection with FDR control. Extensive simulation studies have been conducted to evaluate DeepLINK-T's performance, showing its capability to control FDR effectively while demonstrating superior feature selection power for high-dimensional longitudinal time series data compared to its non-time series counterpart. DeepLINK-T is further applied to three metagenomic data sets, validating its practical utility and effectiveness, and underscoring its potential in real-world applications.

title: Drone-Based Antenna Beam Calibration in the High Arctic
summary: Precision calibration is a critical requirement for future ultra-low-frequency observations of the early universe. The Array of Long Baseline Antennas for Taking Radio Observations from the Seventy-Ninth Parallel (ALBATROS), a radio interfe
content: Precision calibration is a critical requirement for future ultra-low-frequency observations of the early universe. The Array of Long Baseline Antennas for Taking Radio Observations from the Seventy-Ninth Parallel (ALBATROS), a radio interferometer located in the Canadian high Arctic, is designed to map Galactic foreground emission as a pathfinder for these future experiments. Accurate antenna beam characterization at these frequencies is therefore essential, yet remains uniquely challenging. We present PteroSoar, a custom-built drone platform equipped with a calibrated radio-frequency transmitter that enables controlled, in-situ measurements of low-frequency antenna beams. As an initial demonstration, we produce a two-dimensional beam map of an LWA antenna at 50 MHz to a precision of approximately [Formula: see text] near zenith. We identify the dominant sources of systematic uncertainty, including timing imprecision, and outline hardware and software improvements that are expected to reduce beam measurement uncertainties to below [Formula: see text]. This target is sub-dominant to the [Formula: see text] amplitude variability introduced by ionospheric scintillation at these frequencies, providing a practical pathway toward precision beam calibration for ALBATROS and other ultra-low-frequency radio experiments.

title: D-lactate enhances inflammatory and cytotoxic functions of Th1 cells through stereospecific control of mitochondrial ROS
summary: CD4 + T lymphocytes with cytotoxic activity are an understudied T helper (Th) cell population with the capacity to orchestrate immune responses and kill target cells in a TCR-restricted manner. Particularly, the mechanisms that promote the
content: CD4 + T lymphocytes with cytotoxic activity are an understudied T helper (Th) cell population with the capacity to orchestrate immune responses and kill target cells in a TCR-restricted manner. Particularly, the mechanisms that promote the differentiation of cytotoxic Th cells remain elusive. Here, by supplementing Th1 cells with different lactate stereoisomers, we identify a previously unrecognized stereospecific adaptation that reinforces cytotoxic and proinflammatory programs. Although both D- and L-lactate impacted histone acetylation and metabolic activity, only D-lactate increased IFN-γ and TNF-α production and most potently promoted cytotoxic function. D-lactate also selectively enhanced mTORC1 and ERK1/ERK2 signaling, although these changes were not sufficient to fully explain the distinctive phenotype. Instead, the decisive feature of D-lactate supplementation was a reduction in mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), associated with electron transport chain (ETC) remodeling and enhanced glyoxalase-dependent buffering. Together, these findings identify a stereospecific lactate redox axis promoting cytotoxic Th1 cell differentiation.

title: Time-resolved single-cell phenotyping identifies two major classes of antimicrobial peptides with shared principles and key trade-offs
summary: Cationic antimicrobial peptides are a broad family of host defence molecules that neutralize bacteria by permeabilizing one or more membranes and/or inhibiting intracellular targets. However, the relative timings of these effects and their
content: Cationic antimicrobial peptides are a broad family of host defence molecules that neutralize bacteria by permeabilizing one or more membranes and/or inhibiting intracellular targets. However, the relative timings of these effects and their impact at the population level remain poorly understood. Here we present a time-resolved single-cell pipeline for quantifying these effects in Escherichia coli. Applying this pipeline to 18 diverse peptides and peptidomimetics reveals shared activities, but with different kinetics, defining two classes with opposite trade-offs. Class I peptides cause abrupt growth arrest coupled with inner-membrane permeabilization and ribosome/DNA reorganization, conferring fast, multipronged action. However, rapid intracellular absorption by the first permeabilized cells depletes the extracellular pool, rendering these peptides ineffective against dense populations, including biofilms. Class II peptides act more gradually, with delayed or absent inner-membrane permeabilization, limiting their speed of action. However, this results in slower intracellular absorption and greater efficacy at high cell densities and against biofilms. These opposing trade-offs point to important immunological and therapeutic implications.

title: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
summary: Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Current understanding of these processes largely derives from in vitro flat plates, hydroponics and gnotobiotic platforms. However, fungal-plant interactions largely occur
content: Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Current understanding of these processes largely derives from in vitro flat plates, hydroponics and gnotobiotic platforms. However, fungal-plant interactions largely occur in soil – a disordered and granular 3D environment with heterogeneous elasto-viscoplastic properties – whose inherent opacity precludes direct visualisation of the infection. How the physical structure of such natural habitats influences interkingdom interactions remains unknown. Here, we introduce an optically transparent 3D jammed granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments. This platform supports long-term co-culture of plants and fungi, while being compatible with classical physiological assays. We accomplish a direct cellular-level visualisation of the plant-fungal interface. Specifically, host-derived signals prior to the physical contact trigger hyphal reorientation towards the root tips. Using spatiotemporally resolved transcriptomics we discover distinct pathogen-host ex- and in-planta signalling modules, which are associated with granular heterogeneous environments. Together, our findings establish an experimental platform for dissecting fungal development and pathogenesis with unprecedented microscopic and molecular resolution.

title: New processes to counteract sedimentation of coarse dust particles are required for climate models to agree with aircraft observations
summary: Recent observations reveal coarse (diameter > 2.5 µm) mineral dust particles are transported unexpectedly great distances from their Saharan source. Transport models represent this coarse dust transport poorly, having important feedbacks on
content: Recent observations reveal coarse (diameter > 2.5 µm) mineral dust particles are transported unexpectedly great distances from their Saharan source. Transport models represent this coarse dust transport poorly, having important feedbacks on Earth's radiative budget, carbon and hydrological cycles, and human health. We carry out sensitivity tests on the trans-Atlantic transport and deposition processes governing the long-range evolution of mineral dust size distribution in a climate model (HadGEM3-GA7.1). We test the sensitivity of coarse particle transport (up to 63.2 µm diameter) to sedimentation, convective and turbulent mixing, impaction scavenging, and dust shortwave absorption by removing or scaling the magnitude of these processes. Reductions in sedimentation velocity of 50 %–95 % bring modelled coarse particle transport into better agreement with in-situ aircraft observations with the required reduction increasing with transport distance. Other tested processes do not result in the multiple order of magnitude changes in transported dust mass required for agreement with observations. We infer that additional process/es which are misrepresented or missing in the model must be acting to counteract particle sedimentation. Convective and turbulent mixing have minimal impact on coarse particle transport in the model but are key in controlling the vertical distribution of dust in the Saharan air layer and marine boundary layer. Impaction scavenging dominantly impacts fine dust concentration. This study adds to the growing body of evidence pointing to processes involved in coarse mineral dust transport and deposition which are not represented accurately or at all in models, which counteract the sedimentation of coarse particles in the real-world.

title: A new ridge filter design method for PBS-IMPT
summary: Background Adopting the new ridge filter (RF) design method enables the use of a single proton beam energy to achieve plan quality comparable to IMPT while reducing treatment time. Purpose The study enhances the RF design, significantly imp
content: Background Adopting the new ridge filter (RF) design method enables the use of a single proton beam energy to achieve plan quality comparable to IMPT while reducing treatment time. Purpose The study enhances the RF design, significantly improving its dose modulation capability and further demonstrates the ability to complete more complex plan. Methods A PTV-based optimization method (Monte Carlo calculation + IPOPT solver) was used to first create a standard IMPT plan as reference. RF hexagon was then assembled based on the optimized spot weights according to the new design method. The dose distribution through the RF was compared with that of the reference plan and previous design to validate the new design. The study also evaluated the modulation capability of RF in a simultaneous integrated boost (SIB) plan and analyzed relevant FLASH parameters (DADR, total treatment duration). Results For both the standard IMPT plan and the simultaneous boost plan, the dose distribution through RF hexagon was highly comparable to the reference, with gamma passing rates exceeding 97%. Compared to RF square, the RF hexagon shows a closer similarity to the reference. The entire PTV and ~85% of the oar volume received DADRs higher than 40 Gy/s when the beam intensity reached 1.0 × 10 10 protons/s. When the beam intensity surpassed 5×10 11 protons/s, the total treatment time was reduced to less than 2.66 second. Conclusion Compare to square RF, the new RF design improve its dose modulation capability at single spot. Furthermore, the RF’s performance in the simultaneous boost plan confirms that the new design exhibits modulation capability for more complex dose distributions (versus single-target dose plan).

title: Plasma waveguides for high-intensity laser pulses
summary: Fundamental to many applications of laser pulses in science and technology is an extended interaction length with matter that significantly exceeds the distance over which the pulse would normally diffract and transversely spread. At low in
content: Fundamental to many applications of laser pulses in science and technology is an extended interaction length with matter that significantly exceeds the distance over which the pulse would normally diffract and transversely spread. At low intensity, the interaction could simply be the linear refraction provided by a glass optical fiber to keep the pulse from spreading. At higher pulse intensities, however, the goal extends beyond diffraction-free pulse transport: an extended interaction length of high intensity light can give rise to bright secondary sources of photons and, at relativistic intensities, beams of high energy charged particles. Since these applications require laser intensities well above the threshold for ionization of atoms, new methods for overcoming pulse diffraction in a plasma have been developed. Chief among them are plasma waveguides  optical fibers composed of plasma, with characteristic mode structure. This article reviews the methods and theory of plasma waveguides, highlighting the recent development of meter-scale plasma waveguides that have been instrumental to the laser acceleration of high-charge electron beams to energies ~10 GeV.

title: Coupled degradation and mechanical performance of additively manufactured poly(L-lactic acid) esophageal stents: Influence of strut thickness
summary: Achieving predictable degradation for bioresorbable esophageal stents remains a significant challenge. The influence of strut thickness (0.8 and 1.6 mm) on the coupled chemical degradation and mechanical stability of additively manufactured
content: Achieving predictable degradation for bioresorbable esophageal stents remains a significant challenge. The influence of strut thickness (0.8 and 1.6 mm) on the coupled chemical degradation and mechanical stability of additively manufactured poly (L-lactic acid) (PLLA) esophageal stents is investigated via accelerated in vitro degradation (50°C, 90 days). Molecular weight, crystallinity, thermal transitions, and mechanical properties are assessed via gel permeation chromatography, differential scanning calorimetry, and mechanical testing (three-point bending and radial compression). Molecular weight decreases by approximately 90% over 90 days, with a similar half-life (t 1 / 2 ≈ 25 days) for both thicknesses, indicating bulk-dominated hydrolysis and autocatalytic degradation. At the number-average molecular weight (M n) half-life, both designs show substantial reductions in flexural and radial performance; however, crystallinity evolution and mechanical loss are strongly thickness-dependent. Thinner stents provide greater initial flexibility but undergo rapid embrittlement and mechanical failure by day 52, whereas thicker designs retain structural integrity longer despite lower initial compliance. Correlation analysis reveals that load-bearing capacity strongly correlates with M n, while radial stiffness associates with crystallinity. Consequently, strut thickness is a critical design parameter governing the degradation-performance profile of additively manufactured PLLA stents. These findings quantify the trade-off between initial flexibility and long-term stability, informing the optimization of bioresorbable, patient-specific esophageal stents.

title: Tailoring lignin glass transition for enhanced PBAT biocomposite performance
summary: Lignin represents a promising sustainable bio-filler for polymer composites, yet its inherent structural heterogeneity and poor compatibility with polymer matrices often restrict its practical application. To overcome these challenges and a
content: Lignin represents a promising sustainable bio-filler for polymer composites, yet its inherent structural heterogeneity and poor compatibility with polymer matrices often restrict its practical application. To overcome these challenges and achieve structural homogeneity, a green fractionation approach was applied to kraft lignin, avoiding chemical modification and facilitating solvent recovery. The lowest molecular weight fraction (KL10) exhibited the most pronounced end-group effects, resulting in high free volume and a significantly reduced glass transition temperature (T g) of 110 °C, compared to 172 °C for unfractionated lignin (UKL). Under the thermal processing temperature, this lowered T g allows KL10 to undergo a glass-rubbery transition, promoting liquid-like chain mobility. Consequently, the interfacial adhesion and homogeneity of the poly(butylene adipate- co -terephthalate) (PBAT) composite with KL10 were superior to those of the PBAT composite with solid-like UKL and higher molecular weight fractions. Computational analysis of model PBAT-lignin interactions further suggests that a competition between lignin-PBAT and lignin-lignin hydrogen bonds drives these observed correlations between properties and dispersion effectiveness of lignin. This study demonstrates that green fractionation effectively tailors the T g and reduces molecular heterogeneity of lignin, enhancing polymer-filler interfacial adhesion for melt processing and advancing the feasibility of sustainable biocomposites.

title: Agricultural Fallowing Drives Extreme Anthropogenic Dust and Visibility Degradation During the October 2021 Dust Event in California’s Central Valley
summary: Anthropogenic dust aerosols from agricultural land affect regional air quality, visibility, and radiation, yet they are often ignored in atmospheric models. Here, we investigate the role of fallow croplands in driving anthropogenic dust emi
content: Anthropogenic dust aerosols from agricultural land affect regional air quality, visibility, and radiation, yet they are often ignored in atmospheric models. Here, we investigate the role of fallow croplands in driving anthropogenic dust emissions during the 11 October 2021, wind‐driven dust event over California’s Central Valley (CV). The simulation without fallow‐cropland erodibility fails to reproduce the dust event, whereas the simulation including it produces 90 t of cumulative dust emissions within the CV, reproducing the observed aerosol optical depth of 0.6–0.8 and PM 10 concentrations of 1,000–1,200 μg m −3. Fallow‐cropland‐emitted dust reduces surface net radiation by 30 W m −2, leading to near‐surface cooling of 0.2°C and a model‐diagnosed visibility reduction up to 1,000 m across the CV. These results highlight the important role of agricultural fallowing in regulating regional dust emissions, particularly as climate‐driven drought and groundwater sustainability policy may expand fallowed cropland areas in the coming decades.

title: Research on rectification and photoelectric properties of planar heterojunctions based on armchair SiC nanoribbon
summary: 金属与半导体构成的异质结由于具有快速响应、低正向压降和易于制造等特点是现代电子和光电子器件的基本结构单元。本文构建了扶手椅型碳化硅纳米带(aSiCNR)分别与边缘C原子双氢钝化aSiCNR(2CH2-aSiCNR)或边缘Si原子双氢钝化aSiCNR(2SiH2-aSiCNR)构成的平面异质结，并利用第一性原理计算方法研究其电子输运性质与光电特性，旨在从原子构型与电子结构层面揭示异质结整流机制及光电响应的本质。aSiCNR边缘C原子或Si原子被双氢原子钝化后，将对应原子的轨道杂
content: 金属与半导体构成的异质结由于具有快速响应、低正向压降和易于制造等特点是现代电子和光电子器件的基本结构单元。本文构建了扶手椅型碳化硅纳米带(aSiCNR)分别与边缘C原子双氢钝化aSiCNR(2CH2-aSiCNR)或边缘Si原子双氢钝化aSiCNR(2SiH2-aSiCNR)构成的平面异质结，并利用第一性原理计算方法研究其电子输运性质与光电特性，旨在从原子构型与电子结构层面揭示异质结整流机制及光电响应的本质。aSiCNR边缘C原子或Si原子被双氢原子钝化后，将对应原子的轨道杂化方式从sp2杂化转变为sp3杂化，显著调整其能带结构，并将其从半导体转变为金属。2CH2-aSiCNR/aSiCNR平面异质结的负偏压电流大于正偏压电流，呈现反向整流，最大整流比超过1011。2SiH2-aSiCNR/aSiCNR平面异质结呈现正向整流，最大整流比可以达到1032。因此，通过对不同类型边缘原子进行双氢钝化可以实现异质结整流特性的反转。2CH2-aSiCNR/aSiCNR平面异质结在蓝紫光以及近紫外光区呈现显著的光生电流，最高值达到1.5 A/m2。该平面异质结仅在近紫外(3.2 eV)存在一个光生电流峰，光电响应度（Rph）可以达到27.9 mA/W，因此在近紫外光的环境气体分析、生物荧光检测及紫外保密通信等领域具有重要的应用潜力。

title: All-Electron Dynamical Bethe-Salpeter Equation for Extended Systems with Atom-Centered Orbital Basis
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) for the two-particle Green’s function is the most widely used approach for taking into account the particle-hole (exciton) interaction in electronic excitation in the context of the many-body theory
content: Solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) for the two-particle Green’s function is the most widely used approach for taking into account the particle-hole (exciton) interaction in electronic excitation in the context of the many-body theory based on Green’s function. In BSE calculations, the static approximation to the screened Coulomb interaction kernel is commonly employed. However, when the excitonic character is significant, as typically indicated by a large exciton binding energy, dynamical screening effects become non-negligible, rendering the static approximation questionable. Because of the large computational cost due to the dense Brillouin-zone integration necessary for convergence, solving the dynamical BSE for extended systems remains a significant challenge, especially when combined with a GW calculation for calculating quasi-particle energies. In this work, we formulate the plane-wave-based effective dielectric function method [Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. B 107, 235205 (2023)] for the dynamical BSE calculation using atom-centered orbitals as basis functions. We implement this approach in our recently developed all-electron numerical atom-centered orbital (NAO) implementation of BSE@GW [Zhou et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 21, 291 (2025)] for extended systems. We validate our all-electron NAO-based implementation of the dynamical BSE method, and then discuss its realistic application to a molecular crystal of naphthalene by performing the dynamical BSE@G0W0 calculation.

title: Research on Active CO2 Fire Extinguishing Technology for Initial Annular Pool Fires in Storage Tanks
summary: To improve the efficiency of extinguishing initial fires in the annular gaps of storage tanks, this study designs an automatic trigger carbon dioxide active fire extinguishing system. The core innovation of the system lies in the use of mol
content: To improve the efficiency of extinguishing initial fires in the annular gaps of storage tanks, this study designs an automatic trigger carbon dioxide active fire extinguishing system. The core innovation of the system lies in the use of molten material (EVA hot-melt adhesive) to seal the spray holes, which melt upon heating during the early stage of a fire and automatically release high-pressure carbon dioxide, responding quickly. Two key engineering parameters, namely the layout of the spray holes and the installation height, were experimentally studied for their impact on fire suppression performance. The experiment found that reducing the spray height from 30cm to 20cm could significantly shorten the time to extinguish the flame, with the optimal condition (8 holes, 20cm high) taking only 15 seconds. At the same time, increasing the number of spray holes from 4 to 8 can further reduce the fire extinguishing time by 14.3% to 25%, because the porous arrangement forms a more uniform inert gas cover. Both simulations and experiments have confirmed that low-position, porous jetting enables the carbon dioxide jet to penetrate the flame plume more effectively and act directly on the combustion reaction zone, thereby maximizing its cooling and suffocation effects. This study provides direct guidance on parameter optimization for tank safety design and demonstrates the feasibility and efficiency of an active fire extinguishing device for initial annular pool fires.

title: Synthesis of a hydroxy-functionalized poly(m-xylylene) via visible-light-driven reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde using perylene as a photoredox catalyst
summary: A visible-light-driven synthesis of hydroxy-functionalized poly(m -xylylene) was developed via the reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde, an aromatic dialdehyde. In this system, perylene served effectively as a photoredox catalyst under b
content: A visible-light-driven synthesis of hydroxy-functionalized poly(m -xylylene) was developed via the reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde, an aromatic dialdehyde. In this system, perylene served effectively as a photoredox catalyst under blue-light irradiation. It was found that selecting Hantzsch ester capable of activating the aldehyde substrate through hydrogen bonding is crucial for achieving sufficient polymer growth. MALDI-TOF MS analysis of the resulting polymers enabled detailed structural characterization of the polymer chain ends, revealing that their structures vary depending on the type of electron donor used. The obtained hydroxy-functionalized poly(m -xylylene)s exhibited glass transition temperatures above 100°C, suggesting that hydrogen bonding between hydroxyl groups restricts polymer chain mobility.

title: Pulsations along the asymptotic giant branch (AGB): a global view
summary: In three preceding articles, we studied the relation between the light curves of Mira variables and their stellar properties. Clear relations were revealed between the evolution of the stars along the AGB and parameters such as the width of
content: In three preceding articles, we studied the relation between the light curves of Mira variables and their stellar properties. Clear relations were revealed between the evolution of the stars along the AGB and parameters such as the width of the light pulse or the deviation of its ascending branch from a sine wave. However, the restriction to Mira variables prevented a complete picture to be drawn. The present article overcomes this deficiency by reviewing a large sample of semi-regular and irregular variables. It gives evidence for two families of stars having different progenies. The first family enters the AGB already pulsating with amplitudes at the scale of one magnitude. It keeps cooling down and expanding, while pulsating with increasing amplitudes and periods and decreasing width of the light pulse; its progeny is dominated by Mira variables. The second family enters the AGB before displaying significant pulsations; some of its progeny may leave the AGB without experiencing strong Third-Dredge-Up events; others may instead become Mira variables pulsating with a broader light pulse than those of the first family. The possible transition from oxygen-rich to carbon-rich is studied and described. Comments on the interpretation of these results in the context of current state-of-the-art knowledge are presented. While the stars of the first family tend to have larger initial masses than the stars of the second family, details of the properties of the convective envelope seem also to play a role in defining which of the two families a star belongs to.
