title: Stability and optoelectronic properties of oligothiophene molecules confined in boron-nitride nanotubes: A many-body theoretical approach
summary: We investigate the structural and optoelectronic properties of oligothiophene (nT) molecules encapsulated in boron-nitride (BN) nanotubes using density functional theory, many-body $GW$ and Bethe-Salpeter equation approaches. We show that t
content: We investigate the structural and optoelectronic properties of oligothiophene (nT) molecules encapsulated in boron-nitride (BN) nanotubes using density functional theory, many-body $GW$ and Bethe-Salpeter equation approaches. We show that the binding energy is maximized for tube diameters of approximately 10 \AA{}, decreasing gradually for larger diameters. The nT molecules can slide along the tube with a corrugation potential smaller than room temperature thermal energy, promoting their head-to-tail aggregation. Regarding the electronic properties, we find that hybridization with the tube electronic states has a much smaller effect than that of screening, which can close the nT photoemission gap by as much as an eV. A simple model for the polarization of the BN tube demonstrates how these polarization effects decrease with increasing nT molecule length and BN tube diameter. Compared to the gas phase optical properties, structural relaxation, hybridization, and screening can redshift the absorption onset by up to 250 meV for isolated intercalated nTs. Additionally, the study of a head-to-tail sexithiophene dimer reveals an exciton-exciton interaction that splits the absorption onset into a lowest bright exciton, separated by approximately 75 meV from a dark peak. This suggests possible collective effects upon the formation of nT chains inside BN tubes. Our results confirm and clarify experimental data, mitigating the conclusion that insulating BN tubes just act as a protecting environment for encapsulated molecules.

title: Primary sources and secondary formation of brown carbon in urban Shanghai: insights from bihourly measurements of brown carbon and organic tracers
summary: Brown carbon (BrC) is a significant component of atmospheric carbonaceous aerosols and has important influence on climate, atmospheric chemistry, and air quality. Our knowledge about its sources and atmospheric evolution is limited due to t
content: Brown carbon (BrC) is a significant component of atmospheric carbonaceous aerosols and has important influence on climate, atmospheric chemistry, and air quality. Our knowledge about its sources and atmospheric evolution is limited due to the challenges of accurate estimation of its mass concentrations. To address this gap, we examined concurrent measurements of bihourly BrC and a suite of organic molecular and elemental tracers in urban Shanghai from March to August 2020. BrC was determined by synergistically applying the Bayesian inference (BI) model to multi-wavelength aethalometer and total carbon (TC) measurements. BrC constituted 38 %–40 % of TC, with pronounced seasonal differences in diurnal evolution. The source apportionment analysis resolved 15 source factors and among them 7 were secondary sources, namely, secondary nitrate and sulfate formation processes, aromatic secondary organic aerosol (SOA), α -pinene SOA, β -caryophyllene SOA, isoprene SOA, oxygenated cooking OA, and secondary biomass burning. Secondary BrC accounted for 42 % and 49 % of total BrC in spring and summer, respectively. Seasonal contrast of the BrC contributions from primary and secondary sources were noticed. The formation mechanisms of secondary BrC were investigated by isolating events with continuous increment in secondary BrC concentrations, and the analysis suggested the diversity of oxidative pathways governing secondary BrC production. This study demonstrated the potential applicability of coupling the BI framework with online measurements of organic and elemental tracers for robust, chemically resolved BrC source apportionment. Our field observations provide the first high-time-resolution source apportionment of BrC mass in Shanghai and offer new insights into the primary sources and secondary formation of BrC in the urban atmosphere.

title: Evolution of Electrically Induced Damage in Bearing Contacts
summary: In this investigation, a thrust ball-on-flat electric discharge test rig was used to examine the progression of electrically induced bearing damage. Tests were conducted at Hertzian contact pressures of 2, 3, and 4 GPa under a constant lamb
content: In this investigation, a thrust ball-on-flat electric discharge test rig was used to examine the progression of electrically induced bearing damage. Tests were conducted at Hertzian contact pressures of 2, 3, and 4 GPa under a constant lambda ratio of 6 and a fixed electrical power of 3 W per rolling element. Specimens were tested with and without electrical power at increasing cycle counts and examined using optical microscopy, optical surface profilometry, and near-surface yield-strength measurements. Surface discoloration observed after 5e6 cycles indicated evidence of localized heating and tempering of the material caused by electrical power. The electrothermal process reduced the near-surface yield strength by 16%. Two distinct damage modes were observed in the running track: (i) central track deformation and (ii) discharge-induced pitting. The results demonstrate that, at 4 GPa, the threshold for permanent surface deformation was reached at a cycle count approximately two orders of magnitude lower with electrical power than without. Pit initiation and growth were evaluated using a defined pitting criterion (50 μm width x 1 μm depth) and mapped using S–N diagrams. The results showed that electrothermally induced material softening promoted earlier pit initiation and subsequent pit growth. Accordingly, the presence of electrical power reduced the cycles to failure by up to 80% relative to tests conducted without electrical power.

title: Multifunctional BN-enabled Li7La3Zr2O12 composite electrolytes with enhanced toughness and ionic conductivity
summary: The development of mechanically robust and ionically conductive solid electrolytes is essential to ensure fast electrochemical kinetics, dendrite suppression, enhanced safety, and stable cycling performance in solid-state lithium batteries.
content: The development of mechanically robust and ionically conductive solid electrolytes is essential to ensure fast electrochemical kinetics, dendrite suppression, enhanced safety, and stable cycling performance in solid-state lithium batteries. However, simultaneously achieving these properties remains a critical challenge. Here, we report an ultrafast sintering strategy to fabricate hexagonal boron nitride (BN)-reinforced Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12 (LLZO) composite electrolytes with well-balanced ionic conductivity and mechanical strength. The optimized LLZO/BN composite demonstrates enhanced densification, reduced grain-boundary resistance, improved ionic conductivity, and a substantial increase in toughness compared to pristine LLZO and a conventionally sintered LLZO. Only a 0.5 wt% addition of BN resulted in a 12-fold increase in toughness from ~ 5.8 MJ/m 3 to ~ 70 MJ/m 3 and approximately a 2.5-fold enhancement in ionic conductivity, from 0.44 × 10 − 5 S/cm to 1.1 × 10 − 5 S/cm. This study reveals that BN not only acts as a sintering aid to promote densification but also reacts with Li 2 CO 3 to form Li 3 BO 3 , thereby reducing interfacial resistance and facilitating Li-ion transport. This work demonstrates that fast sintering combined with BN is a scalable and efficient approach to synthesize mechanically robust and electrochemically improved garnet electrolytes for practical solid-state battery applications.

title: Neutron dynamics in the fusion of neutron-rich O ions with 12 C
summary: The fusion excitation function for $^{21}$O + $^{12}$C was measured for the first time and compared to the fusion of less neutron-rich isotopes. The impact of valence neutrons in the d$_{5/2}$ shell on the fusion excitation function is exam
content: The fusion excitation function for $^{21}$O + $^{12}$C was measured for the first time and compared to the fusion of less neutron-rich isotopes. The impact of valence neutrons in the d$_{5/2}$ shell on the fusion excitation function is examined. The experimental data manifest a clear dependence of the extracted barrier height, V$_B$, and barrier position, R$_B$ on neutron excess. To assess the role of dynamics the experimental data are compared with both density constrained frozen Hartree Fock (DCFHF) and density constrained time-dependent Hartree Fock (DCTDHF) theories.

title: Partially biodegradable phosphorylated sugarcane bagasse based poly (AA-co-AM) hydrogel as a soil conditioner for drought stress mitigation and supplementary nitrogen delivery in lupine (Lupinus termis L.)
summary: Background The excessive application of conventional mineral NPK fertilizers has led to severe environmental and agricultural challenges, including nutrient leaching, soil degradation, and ecological risks. Addressing these challenges requi
content: Background The excessive application of conventional mineral NPK fertilizers has led to severe environmental and agricultural challenges, including nutrient leaching, soil degradation, and ecological risks. Addressing these challenges requires sustainable alternatives that efficiently regulate soil moisture and nutrient availability. This study developed a partially biodegradable hydrogel composite derived from agricultural waste (sugarcane bagasse) to serve the dual purpose of water retention and improved nutrient retention. The hydrogel was synthesized by functionalizing sugarcane bagasse via phosphoric acid phosphorylation, followed by free-radical graft copolymerization with acrylamide (AM) and acrylic acid (AA). Subsequently, pot experiments were conducted to evaluate the efficacy of Phosphorylated Sugarcane Bagasse Based Poly (AA- co -AM) hydrogel on lupine grown under drought conditions. The hydrogel was applied at 0, 0.1% and 0.2% (W/W) in pots subjected to either well-water conditions (100% field capacity, FC) or water deficit (50% FC). Results FTIR and SEM analyses confirmed the successful grafting of monomers onto the bagasse and the formation of an interconnected porous network. The incorporation of acrylic acid (AA) significantly enhanced the material’s water swelling capacity, reaching up to 2900%. A specific hydrogel formulation with an AM: AA ratio of 1:1 exhibited a 25% weight loss in soil over 4 weeks, which was primarily attributed to the decomposition of the natural bagasse fraction. Elemental analysis revealed a high nutrient loading efficiency, which was particularly pronounced for nitrogen in AM-dominant matrices. In a two-season pot trial conducted under deficit irrigation (50% FC), soil amendment with the H1-type hydrogel at 0.1–0.2% (w/w) significantly improved the growth of lupine (Lupinus termis L.) compared with unamended, drought-stressed controls, the hydrogel-treated plants exhibited increased shoot length by 86.13% (44.42 cm), enhanced chlorophyll a by 117.28%, chlorophyll b by 272.16% and carotenoid contents by 920.88%, and higher fresh by 314.38% and dry biomass by 429.94% (23.92 g and 8.32 g, respectively). Additionally, the application of the hydrogel successfully mitigated drought stress, as evidenced by reduced levels of malondialdehyde, hydrogen peroxide, proline, and total soluble sugars, alongside decreased activities of antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT and POX). Conclusion This study successfully bridges the gap between agricultural waste valorization and sustainable fertilizer management. The sugarcane bagasse-based hydrogel composite effectively enhances soil water retention and mitigates the negative physiological impacts of drought stress while improving nutrient availability. Consequently, this partially biodegradable hydrogel represents a scalable and sustainable strategy to optimize nutrient use efficiency, reduce reliance on conventional mineral fertilizers, and promote resilient agricultural practi

title: Coupling network reconstruction-driven charge transport transition: Capacity breakthrough and wide-temperature sodium storage in Na 3 VCr(PO 4) 3 cathodes
summary: NASICON-type sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) cathode material Na3VCr(PO4)3 (NVCP) theoretically offers the advantage of high energy density. However, its practical capacity is severely restricted, rendering the theoretical potential unrealized.
content: NASICON-type sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) cathode material Na3VCr(PO4)3 (NVCP) theoretically offers the advantage of high energy density. However, its practical capacity is severely restricted, rendering the theoretical potential unrealized. The root cause underlying this capacity limitation remains unclear to date, posing a fundamental obstacle to the material's practical application. Through the deep synergy of theoretical calculations and experiments, this study reveals that the electron state localization induced by insufficient V–Cr d–d orbital hybridization in NVCP is the core bottleneck constraining the intrinsic kinetics of charge transfer. To address this, we propose a "coupling network modulation" strategy, employing Mo6+ with a 4d0 empty orbital as a probe to implement precise intervention in the local bonding environment. The preferential occupation of Mo6+ at the Cr site efficiently reconstructs the Cr–O–V bonding topology and enhances V–Cr orbital overlap, boosting the bulk electronic conductivity by two orders of magnitude. Simultaneously, the strong covalent Mo–O bonds pin the lattice framework, significantly improving strain resistance and effectively suppressing structural degradation during long-term cycling. Consequently, the optimized Na2.91VCr0.97Mo0.03(PO4)3 delivers an initial specific capacity of 105.2 mAh·g−1, achieving a 21.1% gain in specific energy, and exhibits excellent performance across a wide temperature range of −60 to 50 °C. This work clarifies the root cause of NVCP performance failure at the electronic structure level. It thereby establishes a novel strategy for performance modulation based on local bonding reconstruction, offering theoretical guidance for designing high-energy and wide-temperature SIBs cathode.

title: Geometry-driven confinement and iodine evolution in robust metal–organic frameworks for adsorptive iodine storage
summary: Efficient volatile iodine uptake and release is crucial for nuclear waste remediation and aerospace propulsion. However, current sorbents often face a trade-off between high capacity and facile regeneration, as strong host–guest interaction
content: Efficient volatile iodine uptake and release is crucial for nuclear waste remediation and aerospace propulsion. However, current sorbents often face a trade-off between high capacity and facile regeneration, as strong host–guest interactions can hinder low-energy iodine release. Here, we report a reticular chemistry strategy combining geometry-driven confinement and structural retrofitting to address this challenge. In MOF-521, favorable geometric matching between one-dimensional rhombic channels and I2 molecules promotes dense iodine confinement, achieving an intrapore packing density of 3.18 g·cm−3 and utilizing approximately 65% of the available pore space. Comprehensive investigations integrating single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Raman and XPS spectroscopy, electrical conductivity measurements, and theoretical calculations reveal a dual-stage synergistic capture mechanism. Initial iodine incorporation involves speciation evolution and charge redistribution, followed by progressive geometry-confined physical filling and dense iodine organization. SCXRD further resolves ordered iodine assemblies with short I···I contact, highlighting the role of spatial confinement in promoting dense packing. However, such confined packing also contributes to framework deformation during desorption. Replacing monodentate formate with ditopic fumarate yields MOF-521-Fum with a distinct wwq topology. This structural retrofit maintains a high intrapore packing density of 2.79 g·cm−3, raises the decomposition temperature by 200 °C, enables complete iodine desorption, and achieves 96% capacity retention after four cycles. These findings highlight geometry-driven confinement and targeted structural regulation as complementary strategies for balancing dense iodine storage and reversible release.

title: Tracking the effects of noncovalent interactions in liquids using vibrational spectroscopy and computational chemistry
summary: Noncovalent intermolecular interactions are fundamental to a wide range of chemical phenomena. Among these, hydrogen and halogen bonding interactions are particularly influential in the liquid phase, where they have profound implications fo
content: Noncovalent intermolecular interactions are fundamental to a wide range of chemical phenomena. Among these, hydrogen and halogen bonding interactions are particularly influential in the liquid phase, where they have profound implications for biological activity, solution-phase synthesis, and materials self-assembly. Computational chemistry has emerged as an invaluable tool in unraveling the underlying mechanisms of experimental observations in systems involving hydrogen and halogen bonds. This review explores the role of these interactions in nitrogen-containing building blocks and small molecules, highlighting the complementary use of density functional theory (DFT) to interpret and explain experimental findings. In the case of azabenzenes, for instance, charge transfer establishes a strong connection between hydrogen and halogen bond acceptors and the surrounding solvent network. For molecules with large dipole moments, such as trimethylamine N-oxide, the organization and dynamics of the neighboring solvent network are largely dictated by the local hydrogen-bonding structure. In systems with delocalized protons, such as triazoles, the formation of extended hydrogen-bonded networks is driven by entropy and free energy considerations. This work provides a reference for understanding the effects of hydrogen and halogen bonding in pure and mixed liquids, underscoring the synergistic potential of combining experimental techniques and theoretical modeling to uncover the origins of macroscopic properties.

title: Mechanism-informed kinetic modelling of arc-induced ablation and carbon-deposition propensity in gassing polymers
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Gassing polymers are widely used in low-voltage switching devices because their arc-induced ablation products promote arc cooling and post-arc dielectric recovery. However, ablation may also generate carbonaceous precursors and residues tha
content: Gassing polymers are widely used in low-voltage switching devices because their arc-induced ablation products promote arc cooling and post-arc dielectric recovery. However, ablation may also generate carbonaceous precursors and residues that deteriorate insulation performance. To link short-timescale atomistic reactions with long-timescale product evolution, this work develops a mechanism-informed chemical-kinetic framework for arc-induced polymer ablation. For PA66, reaction pathways extracted from multi-configuration ReaxFF molecular dynamics are parameterized through database matching, rate-rule estimation, and quantum-chemical calculations, and then incorporated into reaction mechanism generator calculations. A skeletal mechanism with 81 species and 191 reactions is reduced from a detailed mechanism containing 148 species and 967 reactions, while preserving the key product evolution over 1000–5000 K and 1–10 atm. The kinetic analysis shows that H 2 is favoured at intermediate temperatures, whereas C 2 H 2 and other unsaturated carbon precursors accumulate during deeper decomposition. A yield-sooting-index-weighted carbon-deposition propensity index, S CSI, is further proposed and applied to PA6, PA66, PA46, and POM. Experiments under three arc currents and three arcing durations show that S CSI correlates inversely with post-arc partial-discharge inception voltage (PDIV) under severe ablation, while the correlation weakens under mild conditions. Cleaning experiments further show that PDIV recovers markedly after removal of retained surface residues, indicating that carbonaceous contamination is a major contributor to severe post-arc dielectric degradation. The proposed framework provides a quantitative link between atomistic ablation chemistry, carbon-deposition propensity, and post-arc dielectric performance.

title: Enhanced gemcitabine delivery via metformin-derived carbon dots for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma therapy
summary: carbodiimide coupling was confirmed through comprehensive optical, structural, and morphological analyses. A novel approach has been implemented to overcome the challenges associated with GEM quantification in highly photoactive drug carrie
content: carbodiimide coupling was confirmed through comprehensive optical, structural, and morphological analyses. A novel approach has been implemented to overcome the challenges associated with GEM quantification in highly photoactive drug carriers using circular dichroism spectroscopy. Cell viability assays indicate that MetCDs conjugation substantially improves GEM's therapeutic index by increasing tumor-cell toxicity while minimizing off-target effects. Confocal imaging studies further support these results, revealing selective and markedly higher intracellular accumulation of MetCDs in PDAC cells relative to non-malignant pancreatic ductal cells. Overall, this work presents a novel nanocarrier platform that expands GEM's therapeutic window and offers a promising strategy to overcome chemoresistance in aggressive PDAC.

title: Emerging perovskite quantum dots for optoelectronic sensing–memory–computing neuromorphic systems
summary: With the explosive development of artificial intelligence (AI), unprecedented demands have been imposed on modern computing hardware. Conventional von Neumann architectures suffer from inherent data throughput and energy efficiency bottlene
content: With the explosive development of artificial intelligence (AI), unprecedented demands have been imposed on modern computing hardware. Conventional von Neumann architectures suffer from inherent data throughput and energy efficiency bottlenecks due to physical isolation between computation and memory units. In this context, a brain-inspired neuromorphic computing system enabled by emerging optoelectronic synaptic devices (OSDs) has emerged as a highly promising and transformative alternative, offering a viable pathway toward next-generation intelligent computing systems featuring parallelism, low power consumption, and high efficiency comparable to biological neural networks. Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) exhibit exceptional optoelectronic properties, making PQDs-based OSDs (PQDs-OSDs) a research hotspot. This review summarizes recent advances in PQDs-OSDs including the material characteristics and synthesis methods of PQDs, as well as the device structures, working mechanisms, and applications of PQDs-OSDs. We systematically introduce the applications of PQDs-OSDs in brain-inspired computing and artificial vision. Furthermore, the critical challenges of stability and scalability are comprehensively discussed, providing fundamental insights for advancing the application of PQDs-OSDs in optoelectronic sensing-memory-computing neuromorphic systems.

title: A Highly Sensitive Electrochemical Sensor Based on B, N Co-Doped Porous Carbon/Cobalt Composite for Trace Determination of Bosutinib in Biological and Pharmaceutical Samples
summary: A novel electrochemical sensor was constructed using a boron–nitrogen co-doped porous carbon composite containing cobalt species (C 2 BN/Co@PCS) for the sensitive determination of bosutinib (BOS). The nanocomposite was synthesized utilizing
content: A novel electrochemical sensor was constructed using a boron–nitrogen co-doped porous carbon composite containing cobalt species (C 2 BN/Co@PCS) for the sensitive determination of bosutinib (BOS). The nanocomposite was synthesized utilizing phenylboronic acid, an inorganic salt mixture, and ZIF-12, yielding a hierarchical porous structure with high surface area, abundant active sites, and enhanced electrical conductivity. The structural properties were confirmed by XRD, Raman, XPS, SEM, TEM, and nitrogen adsorption analyses. The electrochemical behavior of the C 2 BN/Co@PCS/GCE was investigated using cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The modified electrode exhibited a significant increase in electroactive surface area (0.191 cm 2 vs 0.094 cm 2), enhanced redox response, and reduced charge-transfer resistance (1600 Ω vs 3900 Ω), indicating improved electron-transfer kinetics. Differential pulse voltammetry was used for BOS quantification, yielding a linear range of 0.1–4.0 µM and a detection limit of 0.013 µM. The proposed sensor also demonstrated excellent selectivity, as evaluated against a range of potentially interfering species, including inorganic ions and biologically relevant electroactive molecules. The sensor exhibited good repeatability and reproducibility. Its practical applicability was evaluated using tablet formulations and commercially obtained human plasma and urine samples. Recovery experiments yielded values ranging from 96.99%–103.7%. Overall, the developed sensor offers a rapid, sensitive, and reliable platform for BOS detection in complex matrices.

title: Phosphate-modified ZSM-5 catalyst converting beverage wastewater to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural and electrochemical upgrading
summary: Converting sugars in beverage wastewater into 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) provides a sustainable waste valorisation pathway. A heterogeneous phosphate-modified ZSM-5 catalyst was examined as an alternative to the conventional homogeneou
content: Converting sugars in beverage wastewater into 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) provides a sustainable waste valorisation pathway. A heterogeneous phosphate-modified ZSM-5 catalyst was examined as an alternative to the conventional homogeneous sulphuric acid catalyst for selective 5-HMF production from beverage wastewater under hydrothermal conditions. Treating ZSM-5 with KH 2 PO 4 introduces surface phosphate species while preserving zeolite crystallinity and the pre-existence of acidic and basic active sites. The KH 2 PO 4 -modified ZSM-5 catalyst delivered a 5-HMF yield of 23.6%, compared to 18.0% for neat ZSM-5 when treating beverage wastewater at 160 °C for 45 min. The improved performance is attributed to a favourable acid-base synergy that suppressed side reactions. The 5-HMF-containing post-reaction stream was then fed into an alkaline electrolyser. Electrolysis delivered a high hydrogen Faradaic efficiency (98 ± 2%) and complete 5-HMF conversion into products including 2,5-FDCA (∼30% yield), laevulinic acid and formic acid. This integrated approach demonstrates the potential to simultaneously valorise beverage wastewater and produce hydrogen and value-added chemicals, offering an alternative to conventional wastewater treatment and disposal.

title: Controlling fragmentation pathways in boron toward borophene-like nanoflakes: impact on morphology, properties, and surface accessibility
summary: In this study, we investigated how successive fragmentation, centrifugation, and drying method affect the morphology, structure, and electrochemical behavior of boron-derived nanoflakes. Bulk boron was first ultrasonicated for 24 h (physica
content: In this study, we investigated how successive fragmentation, centrifugation, and drying method affect the morphology, structure, and electrochemical behavior of boron-derived nanoflakes. Bulk boron was first ultrasonicated for 24 h (physical route) and then subjected to dichromate-assisted treatment (chemical route). AFM analysis showed that the mean thickness decreased from 15.0 nm for the starting boron to 10.1 nm after ultrasonication and 4.9 nm after chemical treatment, together with a narrower thickness distribution. TEM and XRD analyses revealed that crystalline features were retained after fragmentation, despite changes in diffraction peak widths. Subsequent centrifugation yielded thinner nanoflake fractions with mean thicknesses ranging from 2.15 to 2.98 nm. Compared with conventional drying, freeze-drying slightly increased the apparent AFM thickness while maintaining a comparable BET surface area. However, t-plot analysis suggested an increased contribution from non-microporous surfaces after freeze-drying. The freeze-dried sample also exhibited the most favorable cathodic polarization response among the investigated materials. Overall, these findings demonstrate that fragmentation and post-processing conditions can influence the morphology, surface characteristics, and electrochemical behavior of boron-derived nanoflakes.

title: Engineering the topology of multienzyme glycoside hydrolase complexes reveals distinct effects on soluble and insoluble polysaccharide degradation
summary: Background: Plant cell walls are structurally complex, and certain anaerobic microorganisms cope with this complexity by producing a wide range of glycoside hydrolases (GHs) organized into multienzyme complexes, the cellulosomes, to release
content: Background: Plant cell walls are structurally complex, and certain anaerobic microorganisms cope with this complexity by producing a wide range of glycoside hydrolases (GHs) organized into multienzyme complexes, the cellulosomes, to release oligosaccharides as a carbon source. Owing to their intrinsic flexibility, determining how the spatial organization within these assemblies influences catalysis remains a major challenge. Results: We used the Jo–In protein pair, which spontaneously forms a covalent isopeptide bond, to hold fused enzymes in rigid, defined arrangements. Three cellulosomal GHs from Acetivibrio thermocellus (At Cel8A, At Cel9R and At Xyn11A) were assembled into a library of 12 tri-enzymatic Jo-In complexes. Toward soluble polysaccharides, the assemblies largely preserved the activity of the free enzymes, whereas their efficiency varied markedly on insoluble substrates such as wheat bran and wheat straw. Mass spectrometry revealed that the oligosaccharide product profiles depended more on the substrate type than on the assembly architecture, although “cellulolytic” and “xylanolytic” assemblies produced distinct oligosaccharides on wheat straw. SAXS revealed similar global dimensions but different interdomain arrangements, with no significant correlation between interdomain distances and product profiles. Conclusions: Enzyme topology affects the kinetics of insoluble biomass degradation, although it has little effect on activity on soluble substrates. These effects are predicted neither by soluble-substrate activity nor by pairwise interdomain distances alone, indicating that parameters such as enzyme orientation, accessibility and conformational freedom must also be considered. The Jo-In platform provides a framework to separate these contributions in the design of programmable multienzyme complexes.

title: Geometric constraint enables Z-type indylene ligand character
summary: Through the use of chelation-enforced geometric constraint, a T-shaped nickel(0)–indylene complex is accessed. Computational comparison of B, Al, Ga, and In derivatives sheds light on why this unique structure is observed for In.
content: Through the use of chelation-enforced geometric constraint, a T-shaped nickel(0)–indylene complex is accessed. Computational comparison of B, Al, Ga, and In derivatives sheds light on why this unique structure is observed for In.

title: Single source precursors for the aerosol assisted chemical vapour deposition of tantalum oxide
summary: -O coordination mode (5) is also presented, highlighting the structural versatility of the triethanolamine ligand system and its ability to support both mononuclear and multinuclear tantalum centres. Thermogravimetric analysis of the precur
content: -O coordination mode (5) is also presented, highlighting the structural versatility of the triethanolamine ligand system and its ability to support both mononuclear and multinuclear tantalum centres. Thermogravimetric analysis of the precursor complexes indicated that all possessed volatility at raised temperatures. Amorphous tantalum oxide with a band gap of 4.9 eV was successfully deposited by AACVD.

title: Glow discharge plasma-induced thermo-mechanical enhancement of GO/MWCNT reinforced hybrid glass–carbon fibre epoxy composites with alternating laminating configuration
summary: Hybrid FRP composites fabricated with alternating glass–carbon fibre laminates exhibited optimum inter laminar shear strength (ILSS) and glass transition temperature (T g ) at 0.3 wt% graphene oxide (GO) and 0.2 wt% multiwall carbon nanotub
content: Hybrid FRP composites fabricated with alternating glass–carbon fibre laminates exhibited optimum inter laminar shear strength (ILSS) and glass transition temperature (T g ) at 0.3 wt% graphene oxide (GO) and 0.2 wt% multiwall carbon nanotube (MWCNT) dispersion, respectively. The optimized hybrid composites were subsequently subjected to direct current glow-discharge plasma treatment under air and argon gaseous environments, power levels (10–50 Watt), and exposure durations (5–35 mins). Both GO- and MWCNT-reinforced composites showed significant improvements in inter laminar shear strength (ILSS) and surface hardness as plasma power increased. The MWCNT-filled composite treated with argon plasma at 50 W for 15 min showed the greatest enhancements in ILSS (246.7%), Vickers hardness (53.3%), and glass-transition temperature (Tg) (75.8%). Thermo-gravimetric analysis revealed that the highest thermal activation energy, 31.35 kJ mol −1 , was obtained for the MWCNT-based composite following air-plasma treatment at 50 W for 15 min. In comparison, the GO-filled FRP composite subjected to argon-plasma irradiation at 50 W for 15 min exhibited an 8% increase in thermal activation energy. Plasma treatment of the GO- and MWCNT-reinforced composites also resulted in improved surface wettability, as evidenced by the reduction in contact angle. Despite the inherently hydrophobic nature of carbonaceous nanofillers, the lowest contact angle of 96.9° was observed for the MWCNT-filled FRP composite irradiated with argon plasma at 50 W for 10 min. Fourier transformation infrared spectra of MWCNT-filled composites showed the emergence of additional absorption peaks at lower wave numbers after plasma exposure, indicating enhanced chemical interactions and post-curing effects due to formation of oligomers. Furthermore, scanning electron microscope fractographic observations suggested directional curing and improved interfacial strengthening induced by plasma-assisted post-curing.

title: Germination, growth and osmotic adjustment substances of maize (Zea mays L.) varieties exhibit stage-specific response characteristics under continuous salt concentration gradients
summary: Introduction Soil salinization severely threatens global irrigated agriculture, and maize is highly sensitive to salt stress. To clarify the stage-specific responses of different maize cultivars to salt stress, this study investigated the e
content: Introduction Soil salinization severely threatens global irrigated agriculture, and maize is highly sensitive to salt stress. To clarify the stage-specific responses of different maize cultivars to salt stress, this study investigated the effects of varying salinity levels. Methods A sand culture experiment was conducted with four major maize cultivars (Xianyu335, Xinyu24, Jinli1982, and Denghai605) under six NaCl concentration gradients (distilled water CK1, Hoagland nutrient solution CK2, 70, 140, 210, and 280 mmol L ⁻¹) with three replicates for 14 days. Results Salt stress inhibited germination in a concentration-dependent manner, with germination potential being the most sensitive parameter (dropping to zero at 70 mmol L ⁻¹). Seedling growth and biomass decreased significantly with increasing salt concentration. Physiologically, seedlings could adapt to stress at 70–140 mmol L ⁻¹ through osmotic adjustment and antioxidant defense, but this defense mechanism failed beyond 210 mmol L ⁻¹. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed a distinct “growth-defense” trade-off (cumulative contribution rate of 81.7%), in which JL1982 exhibited the most dramatic trajectory shifting from high growth to high defense, whereas DH605, XY24, and XY335 clustered together with relatively stable patterns. Further analysis of individual indicators revealed that Xianyu335 showed the strongest salt tolerance at germination, whereas Denghai605 was the most sensitive, and Xinyu24 and Jinli1982 grew better under moderate salinity. Discussion Overall, the germination stage was more sensitive to salt stress than the seedling stage. This study provides a theoretical basis for cultivar selection and salt-tolerant cultivation in saline-alkali lands.

title: Monitoring Forest Habitats Based on Sustainable Development Goals in the Protection of Northern Iran
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: The Hyrcanian forests of northern Iran are ecologically rich ecosystems that support biodiversity and local livelihoods. This study explores the sustainable utilization of Non-Timber Forest Products (NWFPs), focusing on hazelnut (Corylus av
content: The Hyrcanian forests of northern Iran are ecologically rich ecosystems that support biodiversity and local livelihoods. This study explores the sustainable utilization of Non-Timber Forest Products (NWFPs), focusing on hazelnut (Corylus avellana) in the Fandoglu Forest of Namin, Ardabil Province. Physiographic factors such as elevation, slope, and aspect, along with soil characteristics including texture, pH, electrical conductivity, organic carbon, and total neutralizing value, were analyzed across two vegetation zones using systematic random sampling. Vegetation distribution was assessed through linear transects and circular plots. The findings revealed that hazelnut thrives in lower elevations (1400–1500 meters), gentle slopes (0–12%), and northern/eastern aspects with loamy soils and high humidity. In contrast, steeper and rockier terrains favored more resilient species like Carpinus betulus and Parrotia persica. The study highlights the critical role of physiographic and edaphic conditions in species distribution and identifies optimal habitats for hazelnut growth. Despite the promising potential for sustainable harvesting, signs of degradation due to human activities particularly uncontrolled tourism underscore the need for integrated management, community involvement, and ecological capacity assessment. Sustainable exploitation of NWFPs can strengthen local economies while preserving the biodiversity of these valuable forest ecosystems.

title: Research on Core Loss Prediction Models and Multi-Condition Optimization Based on Data-Driven Methods
summary: As a core component in power conversion equipment, the core loss characteristics of magnetic components have a direct impact on the overall operational efficiency of power electronic systems. Under non-sinusoidal excitation conditions such
content: As a core component in power conversion equipment, the core loss characteristics of magnetic components have a direct impact on the overall operational efficiency of power electronic systems. Under non-sinusoidal excitation conditions such as triangular and trapezoidal waves, as well as under dynamic temperature variations, the loss prediction error of the traditional Steinmetz empirical equation is relatively large. To address the limitations of traditional loss models in prediction accuracy, this paper first extracts relevant feature parameters based on flux density data and constructs an excitation waveform classification model; subsequently, temperature variables are introduced into the Steinmetz equation to propose a modified Steinmetz equation; on this basis, a data-driven method is used to achieve high-precision prediction of core losses; finally, to balance magnetic energy transfer characteristics, the trained neural network model is coupled with an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm, taking both core loss minimization and magnetic energy transfer maximization as dual optimization objectives, and parameter optimization under constraints is conducted. The research results show that the modified Steinmetz equation achieves a goodness of fit (R 2) of 0.9908, and compared to the original model, its loss prediction capability under variable temperature conditions is significantly improved; the neural network model achieves a goodness of fit (R 2) of 0.9982 and a mean squared error (MSE) of 134,018.16 on the test set; after optimization with the coupled improved particle swarm algorithm, the optimal parameter combination balancing low core losses and high magnetic energy transfer characteristics is obtained.

title: Assessing economic impacts of Compound Coastal Water Events
summary: This study investigates the often undercounted and hard-to-value economic consequences of Compound Coastal Water Events (CCWEs) in rural Eastern North Carolina (ENC), a region facing significant deep uncertainty due to future conditions. Mo
content: This study investigates the often undercounted and hard-to-value economic consequences of Compound Coastal Water Events (CCWEs) in rural Eastern North Carolina (ENC), a region facing significant deep uncertainty due to future conditions. Moving beyond traditional, risk-focused analyses that often miss long-term and indirect costs, this research adopts a deep resilience approach to evaluate the cumulative impacts of flooding. Drawing on data from two focus group workshops with local planners, emergency managers, and public officials, the analysis reveals that a comprehensive understanding of economic consequences requires examining five interconnected categories that represent a more systemic view of the problem: (1) Human Capital and Social Costs (loss of livelihoods, health impacts, social capital erosion), (2) Natural Resource Costs and Ecosystem Services (agricultural productivity, ecosystem damage, disaster relief and recovery), (3) Infrastructure and Public Services (infrastructure damage, public service disruption, emergency response costs), (4) Business and Investments (property value reductions, business closures and relocation, investor confidence), and (5) Other Indirect and Long-Term Impacts (e.g., insurance costs, supply chain disruptions, economic multiplier effects). The findings highlight the challenges of operationalizing these concepts, particularly the difficulty of capturing these less tangible costs in traditional economic models. The research emphasizes the urgent need for improved tools and methods for community resilience planning that can account for deep uncertainty and facilitate a transition from narrowly siloed, incremental adjustments to more holistic and integrative solutions that promote deep resilience. This study aims to provide evidence to support a more comprehensive framework for assessing the true economic burden of CCWEs and to inform a new generation of more effective, cross-sectoral resilience strategies. These categories of economic impacts require additional study in areas affected by other types of complex hazards.

title: What satellite building height data reveal about urban form and horizontal expansion in Ghana
summary: Urban expansion in sub-Saharan Africa is commonly measured through changes in built-up extent, while nationally comparable evidence on building height remains limited. We examine both dimensions across 296,668 built-up 500 m grid cells in G
content: Urban expansion in sub-Saharan Africa is commonly measured through changes in built-up extent, while nationally comparable evidence on building height remains limited. We examine both dimensions across 296,668 built-up 500 m grid cells in Ghana using two 2018 Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) products: Average Net Building Height (ANBH), which estimates height over built pixels, and Average Gross Building Height (AGBH), which combines height with built coverage and therefore measures volumetric density. The two rasters are mutually consistent, but their distributions differ substantially. Within Ghana, 38.5% of pixels with a positive ANBH signal fall within the 2.50–2.55 m interval, and 14.6% of footprint cells have no GHSL height signal. An independent satellite product, WSF3D, shows 2.5–5.0 m of height variation among cells that ANBH places within a 1.8 cm interquartile range, and cell-level agreement between the two height estimates is weak (Spearman ρ = 0.18). A model of log(1 + ANBH) using only pre-2018 predictors explains 23.5% of the variance; built coverage in 2010 remains its strongest predictor under spatially clustered standard errors and a spatial error specification. A four-class classification of ANBH against pre-2018 horizontal expansion agrees with expansion more than expected by chance (κ = 0.28), but almost entirely because cells without a height signal fall in its lowest class; among cells with a signal, agreement is at chance level. National analyses of building height should distinguish net height from gross built density, and absent signal from low height, before drawing substantive conclusions.

title: Streets as workplace environments: Exploring the impact of environmental design on street vendors in Indian cities
summary: Street environments are workplaces for vendors, characterised by a complex interplay among the built environment, ecology, and society. These conditions directly shape vendors’ livelihoods. Existing studies on street vendors are limited in
content: Street environments are workplaces for vendors, characterised by a complex interplay among the built environment, ecology, and society. These conditions directly shape vendors’ livelihoods. Existing studies on street vendors are limited in their focus, solely on policy, climate or management lenses, and holistic environment-based enquiries are scarce. This paper explores how the environmental design of Indian streets shapes street vendors' experiences. It employs a qualitative, multi-method approach across two cities: the small- to mid-sized city of Roorkee in northern India and the regional urban centre of Bhopal in central India. The core methodology comprises four phases: literature review and context identification; development of a conceptual framework and pilot study; empirical field observations and semi-structured interviews with vendors to gain deeper insights; and an overall narrative-based analysis across the two cities. The study proposes and demonstrates the use of a conceptual framework to understand how street environmental design shapes vendors’ experiences. The key emergent themes are environmental stressors as perceived by vendors and coping strategies involving interaction with street design elements. This paper highlights that street vending is not merely an urban informal practice but also an avenue of understanding how everyday environmental design shapes human livelihoods and well-being.

title: Decentralized Gravity-Fed GRP Tank Systems for Flash-Flood Harvesting in Ungauged Tributaries of the Hatta Catchment, UAE: A Conceptual Design and Feasibility Study
summary: Flash floods in the Hatta catchment (Dubai, United Arab Emirates) are short and intense, and most of their water is held by large dams downstream, while small hillslope tributaries near farms and houses remain unused. This study sizes a dec
content: Flash floods in the Hatta catchment (Dubai, United Arab Emirates) are short and intense, and most of their water is held by large dams downstream, while small hillslope tributaries near farms and houses remain unused. This study sizes a decentralized, electricity-free system of prefabricated glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) sectional tanks placed on rock terraces on both banks of small ungauged tributaries. The tanks fill by gravity through a screened lateral intake, spill in cascade, and drain passively within 24 h to recharge wells, ponds, households and farms. The design combines published rainfall frequencies, the curve number (CN) method, a stochastic rainfall model and structural checks under the Dubai Building Code. The 10-year design day (80 mm, CN = 80) yields 346 m³ of runoff per hectare, or 13 standard 4 × 4 × 2 m modules per hectare. A 5-year design (7 modules per hectare) still captures 79% of the long-term runoff and is the economic optimum. A full module applies about 21 kPa to the rock, one tenth of the 200 kPa allowable pressure; buoyancy of an empty, flooded tank (four 25 mm rock anchors) and planar sliding on joints dipping more than about 23° govern siting. A small undammed wadi in Hatta town is proposed for a pilot station.

title: Laboratory Polyvinyl Chloride Combustion and Wildland–Urban Interface Fire Ash Analysis: Chemical Markers and Atmospheric Implications
summary: Wildfires at the wildland–urban interface (WUI) involve the combustion of man-made materials, producing smoke with chemical composition distinct from wildland fires. However, uncertainties remain on the composition and impacts of these emis
content: Wildfires at the wildland–urban interface (WUI) involve the combustion of man-made materials, producing smoke with chemical composition distinct from wildland fires. However, uncertainties remain on the composition and impacts of these emissions. We report emissions from the laboratory combustion of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC), a widely used plastic in the built environment. Trace gases (CO2, CO, CH4, HCl) were quantified and aerosol chemical composition was measured using soot-particle aerosol mass spectrometry between 650 and 950 °C to probe smoldering and flaming conditions. Hydrogen chloride was efficiently produced at all temperatures with a median (25th–75th percentile) emission factor of 72 (53–108) g kg–1, while black carbon content increased under flaming combustion. Organic aerosol was enriched with polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) during smoldering combustion, which are human and environmental toxins. Chemical signatures in ash collected downwind of the Eaton Fire, which burned nearly 10 000 structures, showed distinct signatures of PAHs and trace metals. This included unique markers such as CuCl+ and Cu2Cl+, consistent with laboratory PVC combustion results. Our combined laboratory and field results quantify an important source of airborne toxics and reactive chlorine, highlighting the need for comprehensive measurements of WUI fire emissions to constrain their atmospheric and health-relevant impacts.

title: Alkali Metal Cation Regulation of the Interfacial Microenvironment for Selective Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Glyoxylic Acid
summary: Electrochemical C–N coupling offers a potentially sustainable approach to glycine synthesis from glyoxylic acid (GX) and nitrate (NO3–), but competing reactions limit the selectivity under high current densities. Alkali metal cations can in
content: Electrochemical C–N coupling offers a potentially sustainable approach to glycine synthesis from glyoxylic acid (GX) and nitrate (NO3–), but competing reactions limit the selectivity under high current densities. Alkali metal cations can influence glycine electrosynthesis through modulation of the electrode–electrolyte microenvironment. However, their role in glycine electrosynthesis has remained largely unexplored. Here, the effect of alkali metal cations was systematically investigated using oxide-derived Bi. Notably, glycine selectivity follows the order of Na+ > K+ > Li+ > Cs+ at 200 mA cm–2, with Na+ providing an optimal balance among the consecutive reaction steps and achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 61.1% and a partial current density of 122.2 mA cm–2. A preliminary technoeconomic analysis further suggests potential economic viability at high current densities. Control experiments show that Na+ favors both the formation of NH2OH and the reduction of oxime to glycine. Together with in situ spectroscopy, these results suggest that cation-dependent interfacial electrostatic and hydration environments contribute to glycine selectivity. This work identifies alkali metal cations as effective interfacial regulators for controlling complicated electrochemical C–N coupling and provides insights into the rational design of selective glycine electrosynthesis.

title: Reconstructing Structural Dynamic Cooperativity Suppresses Conduction Loss in Linear Aliphatic Polymer Dielectrics at Elevated Temperatures
summary: Linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics show increased conduction loss at elevated temperatures as thermally activated structural fluctuations modulate electronic states and facilitate charge transport. We examine how aromatic side groups with
content: Linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics show increased conduction loss at elevated temperatures as thermally activated structural fluctuations modulate electronic states and facilitate charge transport. We examine how aromatic side groups with different π‐electron delocalization affect structural dynamic cooperativity and charge transport. Side‐group modification alters intermolecular interactions and local dynamic constraints, shifting long‐range cooperative motion to localized heterogeneous fluctuations. This transition coincides with reduced collective structural fluctuations and improved local electronic‐state stability, consistent with suppressed phonon‐assisted carrier transport. As a result, the furan‐modified polymer exhibits a statistical electronic energy fluctuation descriptor of 0.132 eV and nearly two orders of magnitude higher volume resistivity. It achieves a discharged energy density of 8.38 J cm −3 at 120°C, approximately 45 times that of pristine polymer while maintaining a charge‐discharge efficiency above 90%. It also retains an efficiency above 93% over 5 × 10 5 charge‐discharge cycles at 200 MV m −1. Although the higher glass transition temperature of the furan‐modified polymer may also contribute to its performance near 120°C, its advantage is already evident at 25°C and 80°C, well below the glass‐transition regime. This work highlights structural dynamic cooperativity as a descriptor linking molecular dynamics and charge transport in linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics.

title: Spatiotemporal reconstruction and influencing factors of rubber plantation dynamics in Xishuangbanna since the 1950s
summary: To characterize the long-term spatiotemporal dynamics and spatial differentiation of rubber plantations in Xishuangbanna, this study integrated multi-source data and employed historical backcasting, random forest classification, spatial gra
content: To characterize the long-term spatiotemporal dynamics and spatial differentiation of rubber plantations in Xishuangbanna, this study integrated multi-source data and employed historical backcasting, random forest classification, spatial gradient analysis, and GeoDetector to reconstruct rubber plantation distributions from the 1950s to 2025. The results showed that: (1) Rubber plantation area followed a nonlinear trajectory of “slow growth–rapid expansion–post-peak adjustment,” increasing from approximately 5.5 × 10 3 hm 2 in the 1950s to 486.24 × 10 3 hm 2 in 2015, before declining to 400.85 × 10 3 hm 2 in 2025, a mapped decrease of 17.6% from its peak. (2) Rubber plantation expansion exhibited a pronounced mountainward shift. The proportion of plantations at elevations of 900 m and above reached 36.1% in 2015, accompanied by an increase in the proportion located on slopes of 25° and above. Plantations also gradually extended away from areas near farms, settlements, and roads, indicating a transition from densification in lowland core areas to outward expansion onto peripheral mountain slopes. (3) From 1976 to 2025, elevation consistently had the highest q value among the individual factors. Two-factor combinations generally had higher q values than their corresponding individual factors, with the combination of elevation and current protected-area boundaries showing the highest joint q values from 2010 to 2025. These findings reveal the long-term expansion, mountainward shift, and stage-specific changes in the spatial correlates of rubber plantations in Xishuangbanna, providing a basis for spatial management and ecological risk identification in mountainous rubber-producing areas.

title: The Synthesis, Characterization and Spectroscopic Study of Glutaraldehydiphenyl Hydrazone as Chromogenic Reagent for Spectrophotometric Determination of Selected Toxic Heavy Metals (Pb, Cr, Cd and as) in Water and Biological Samples
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CHEMISTRY AND CHEMICAL PROCESSES
summary: In this work, synthesis, characterization and spectrophotometric study of glutaraldehydiphenyl hydrazone (GDP), a chromogenic reagent for determination of selected heavy metals in water and soil samples has been carried out. The results obt
content: In this work, synthesis, characterization and spectrophotometric study of glutaraldehydiphenyl hydrazone (GDP), a chromogenic reagent for determination of selected heavy metals in water and soil samples has been carried out. The results obtained showed product yield of 79.0%, nitrogen content of 18.91% and melting points of 129-131ºC. Infrared spectra data obtained showed absorptions bands at regions around 3492.5, 3451 for –NHR groups and stretches at 3085 and 1604 for -CH and C=N respectively. The nuclear magnetic resonance (13C-NMR) spectrum showed peaks around 111.0-141.0 for aromatic carbons, 129.3ppm for cyano carbon atom and 40.0, 39.2 and 31.7ppm for three methylene carbons. The 1HNMR spectrum revealed peaks at 1.64-1.69 ppm for multiplet –CH2- protons, 2.214-2.386 ppm for quartet –CH2- protons, 7.331- 7.345 ppm for -CH protons, 7.015 ppm for –NH signal and 6.59-7.34 ppm for aromatic protons. The spectral analysis of the glutaraldehydiphenyl hydrazone complexes revealed wavelength ranging between 360.0 (Cr) to 395.0 nm for (Pb and As) as maximum absorption at a working pH of 6.5 to 7.5 at 37°C. The reagent showed a molar absorptivities (L mol-1 cm-1) ranging from 2.213 x 104 (Pb) to 2.460 x 104 (As), a mole ratio of metal to ligand of 2:1, detection limits (µg/g) ranging from 0.3432 (As) to 0.5250 (Pb) and the metal-ligand complex was stable for 0-48 hours. Additionally, the compounds Beer’s law validity ranges from 0.001 to 100 (mgL-1). The spectrophotometric results were compared with atomic absorption spectroscopy results and the results were satisfactory with good precision for the GDH method.

title: Circadian coding of chemosensation: a peripheral-central oscillator framework for insect olfaction and gustation
summary: Chemical cues guide major aspects of insect life, yet their detection and behavioral relevance vary throughout the day. Although circadian regulation of insect olfaction and gustation has been increasingly reported, the mechanisms by which
content: Chemical cues guide major aspects of insect life, yet their detection and behavioral relevance vary throughout the day. Although circadian regulation of insect olfaction and gustation has been increasingly reported, the mechanisms by which local sensory clocks interact with central timing and physiological-state signals remain fragmented. Here, we systematically synthesized molecular, electrophysiological, behavioral, and ecological evidence for the temporal regulation of insect chemosensation for the first time. Comparison of olfaction and gustation reveals a shared organizational principle but distinct adaptive functions: olfactory rhythms primarily align long-range chemical detection with external ecological opportunities, whereas gustatory rhythms more directly couple contact chemosensation to feeding and metabolic state. On the basis of these findings, we propose a Peripheral–Central Dual Oscillator (PCDO) framework: (i) cell-autonomous peripheral clocks are necessary; (ii) central clocks do not generate primary sensory rhythms but integrate sensory timing with physiological state, memory, and ecological context; and (iii) olfactory and gustatory modalities share conserved clock effectors but are predominantly biased toward external ecological windows and internal metabolic/feeding control, respectively. This hierarchical yet flexible organization enables insects to optimize mate searching, host detection, feeding, oviposition, and predator avoidance within species-specific temporal niches. We further emphasize that both modalities are state-dependent and can serve external or internal functions; the olfactory–gustatory contrast is therefore a difference in predominant function, with exceptions arising through distinct routes, time scales, and molecular substrates of state gating. Circadian chemosensation therefore represents a temporal computation that enables insects to determine not only which chemical signals are available but also when those signals should influence behavior.

title: Ecological Silviculture and Climate Adaptation in Western Frequent-Fire Forests
summary: Ecological silviculture offers a holistic management approach for the long-term stewardship and climate adaptation of frequent-fire conifer forests in the interior of western North America. This forest type is increasingly vulnerable to hig
content: Ecological silviculture offers a holistic management approach for the long-term stewardship and climate adaptation of frequent-fire conifer forests in the interior of western North America. This forest type is increasingly vulnerable to high-severity wildfires and insect outbreaks owing to legacies of past harvest and fire exclusion, combined with increasingly hotter and drier climate conditions. Ecological silviculture in this forest type seeks to move forests towards an open canopy, multi-age spatial mosaic that emulates the natural forest development cycle perpetuated by frequent low-severity fires, and then maintain forests in this condition with multi-age treatments. We build on prior descriptions of ecological silviculture for frequent-fire forests by explicitly integrating climate change adaptation. We summarize the mechanistic rationale for why the primary adaptation strategy in most locations remains restoring the inherent resilience and adaptive capacity of forest conditions perpetuated by frequent fire. We then define strategies to direct transitions to new species assemblages or vegetation types and describe how this approach can be used to adapt moist forests to future conditions. We present operational guidelines for long-term application of ecological silviculture to a range of common conditions, including (i) dense stands arising from fire suppression and past harvest; (ii) sites recently burned in moderate- and high-severity fires; and (iii) stands developing after fuel reduction or shelterwood treatments that require another entry. Ecological silviculture is well suited to landowners who seek to restore and sustain a high level of resistance and adaptive capacity to high-severity fire, insect outbreaks, and drought while managing for multiple social, ecological, and economic objectives over time.

title: Wild calanoid copepods are more sensitive to chronic anthropogenic noise than their cultured conspecifics
summary: Anthropogenic underwater sound is a growing global stressor, yet its chronic effects on zooplankton species remain poorly understood. This study examined the behavioral responses and survival rates of the calanoid copepod Calanus finmarchic
content: Anthropogenic underwater sound is a growing global stressor, yet its chronic effects on zooplankton species remain poorly understood. This study examined the behavioral responses and survival rates of the calanoid copepod Calanus finmarchicus to long-term noise exposure, specifically comparing wild-caught individuals with laboratory-reared ones. Both groups were exposed to wind farm noise playback for 20 days while incubating in a natural environment. We have observed a marked difference in survival rates over time of sound exposure only in wild copepods, while cultured copepods seemed to be rather unaffected by the increased noise levels. These findings suggest that cultured copepods may have acclimatized to chronic noise, due to the acoustic environment in rearing tanks. Unlike previous studies, our results did not indicate a significant effect of noise exposure on the average swimming speed of Calanus spp., regardless of the origin. These different responses underscore the importance of considering population origin in behavioral and physiological assays and suggest that wild populations should be preferred over cultured animals when investigating responses to environmental stimuli to obtain the most ecologically relevant results.

title: Bio‐geochemical signature of lobe progradation and switching in the Po Delta: Identifying cryptic stratigraphic surfaces in prodelta successions
summary: Major facies shifts within Holocene deltaic successions can be readily identified in sediment cores. However, at a finer scale, distinguishing partially overlapping delta lobes within lithologically homogeneous prodelta successions is not s
content: Major facies shifts within Holocene deltaic successions can be readily identified in sediment cores. However, at a finer scale, distinguishing partially overlapping delta lobes within lithologically homogeneous prodelta successions is not straightforward. Based on integrated sedimentological, micropaleontological (benthic foraminifers and ostracods) and geochemical (XRF Core Scanner) analyses of two 40 m‐long cores, located ~15 km apart in the modern Po Delta, this study provides a tool for the high‐resolution analysis of along‐strike stratigraphic variability, enabling delineation of subtle discontinuities associated with delta‐lobe boundaries. Facies stacking patterns reveal a pronounced asymmetry between a thin transgressive systems tract (TST; ~3 m), comprising a condensed succession of bay, transgressive barrier and inner‐shelf deposits, and a significantly thicker highstand systems tract (HST; up to 35 m), characterised by the superposition of prodelta, delta‐front and delta‐plain facies. The maximum flooding surface (~7000 cal yrs bp) marks minimal Po River influence on the shelf. Within the HST, abrupt environmental changes tracked by meiofauna shifts and associated variations in geochemical proxies of sediment provenance highlight stratigraphic surfaces that lack a clear lithological expression and mark lobe abandonment and activation. The ratio of opportunistic – sensitive (mainly epiphytic) taxa to organic enrichment and the Ni/Ca ratio, respectively, track variations in organic matter (OM) fluxes and Po‐derived sediment supply across delta‐lobe boundaries. Delta‐lobe switching is marked by an abrupt increase in OM‐sensitive taxa and a negative shift in Ni/Ca values, whereas renewed progradation is associated with an increase in OM‐opportunistic taxa and relatively stable Ni/Ca values. The subsurface stratigraphic architecture of prodelta lobes is consistent with Po Delta evolution inferred from outcropping beach ridges, demonstrating the effectiveness of this integrated approach in identifying cryptic stratigraphic surfaces and improving the interpretation of mud‐dominated prodelta successions.

title: Beaver ponds on the peatland-rich Taiga Plains act as sinks for methylmercury
summary: Beaver ponds occupy key hydrological landscape positions where they can influence downstream water quality, but the net effect of beaver ponds may depend on climate, landscape, and beaver pond characteristics. Methylmercury (MeHg) is a toxi
content: Beaver ponds occupy key hydrological landscape positions where they can influence downstream water quality, but the net effect of beaver ponds may depend on climate, landscape, and beaver pond characteristics. Methylmercury (MeHg) is a toxin of concern and previous studies have found that beaver ponds often are net sources of MeHg due to increased microbial MeHg production in flooded soils. Here we studied the influence of beaver ponds on MeHg on the Taiga Plains in western Canada, a region with discontinuous permafrost, widespread peatlands, and many long-established large beaver ponds. We sampled inflow and outflow of 21 beaver ponds over two summers, and our objectives were: 1) determine if the beaver ponds were net sinks or sources of MeHg, and 2) infer dominant hydrological and biogeochemical controls on MeHg concentrations leaving the beaver ponds using ancillary water quality parameters (including oxygen, pH, 18O, and deuterium) and information on dissolved organic matter (DOM) characteristics. Most beaver ponds in this study were net MeHg sinks, especially those which received inflow with high MeHg concentrations (> 0.6 ng MeHg L-1) and those that had longer pond water residence times as indicated by evaporative isotopic enrichment. Losses of MeHg were closely associated with losses of aromatic and photosensitive DOM, suggesting that photochemical processes were the dominant processes causing beaver ponds to act as MeHg sinks. A few beaver ponds acted as minor but consistent net sources of MeHg, and these ponds were either newly established beaver ponds or ponds with decreasing dissolved oxygen. The dominant sink function of beaver ponds on the Taiga Plains was however likely due to the widespread peatlands, which deliver high concentrations of DOM and MeHg to the ponds, and the relatively dry climate, which causes long water residence times which increases the influence of photochemical processes. Our results suggest that beaver ponds in this region may counteract some increase in delivery of MeHg from thawing and warming peatlands.

title: Flood invasion evolution and sustainability‑oriented risk assessment of metro-led underground spaces under extreme rainfall scenarios
summary: Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall, posing growing flood intrusion risks to urban underground spaces and challenging the resilience and flood protection performance of existing metro station designs
content: Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall, posing growing flood intrusion risks to urban underground spaces and challenging the resilience and flood protection performance of existing metro station designs, which is critical for sustainable transportation infrastructure development. Taking Changban Metro Station in Guangzhou, China, as a case study, this study combined a coupled 1D–2D surface flood model with a 3D numerical model of flood propagation inside the station to investigate flood intrusion under rainfall events with different return periods. The spatiotemporal characteristics of flood propagation, including flow paths, arrival time, inundation depth, discharge, and velocity, were analyzed to assess the flood risk of the existing station design under intensifying rainfall conditions. Results show that both peak inflow and intrusion duration increase markedly with rainfall return period. Under the 100‑year rainfall scenario, peak inflow is 35 times that under the 5‑year scenario, while intrusion duration is 3.4 times longer. Flood propagation exhibits clear vertical and horizontal patterns, with faster spread on upper levels and in near‑field areas, and slower spread on lower levels and in far‑field areas. The platform level is identified as the most vulnerable zone and may experience substantial inundation even under low‑return‑period rainfall. Flood hazard evolves from planar inundation to linear contraction and finally point‑like residual water, while both hazard extent and duration expand with rainfall intensity. These findings highlight the need for adaptive design and retrofitting measures to improve the flood resilience of metro stations under extreme rainfall conditions, supporting climate‑mitigated structural design and sustainable construction of underground transportation infrastructures.

title: Microbially mediated soil carbon and nitrogen cycling after prescribed pile burning
summary: Prescribed fires are effective tools for mitigating catastrophic wildfires and inducing positive ecological changes, but their impacts on soil biogeochemistry, particularly C and N cycling, remain poorly resolved. Post-fire trajectories of
content: Prescribed fires are effective tools for mitigating catastrophic wildfires and inducing positive ecological changes, but their impacts on soil biogeochemistry, particularly C and N cycling, remain poorly resolved. Post-fire trajectories of C and N are strongly governed by soil microbial communities, whose composition and functional potential are also altered by burning and subject to successional dynamics. While previous studies show prescribed fires can shift community composition and increase soil organic matter pools, few studies couple microbial community dynamics with geochemical transformations at high temporal resolution. Here, we investigate interactions between microbial community assembly and ash-derived C and N transformation over time after prescribed pile burns in California chaparral and coast live oak woodland soils. Using an approach that integrates high-resolution temporal measurements of soil geochemistry (soluble organic matter pools, inorganic N speciation, pH), in-field CO 2 flux measurements, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, we observe significant changes to soluble organic C and N pools and bacterial and archaeal community composition immediately post-fire. In the months following fire, both gradually recovered toward pre-fire conditions, with acceleration during the following wet season, returning to baseline conditions within 1 year, in contrast to decadal wildfire legacies. Shifts in microbial families coincided with measured changes in N speciation and ash-derived C loss; however, these processes appear to be strongly modulated by post-fire moisture dynamics. We complemented this year-long field study with a controlled laboratory incubation, revealing that under sufficient soil moisture, burned soils exhibited higher respiration rates and greater declines in soluble C and N compared to low-moisture and unburned controls. Collectively, our results illustrate the potential for post-fire microbial succession to rapidly regulate C and N cycling after prescribed fires, mediated by a changing moisture regime. Our findings provide insights for evaluating the ecological impacts of prescribed fire and guiding land management practices.

title: Effect of cultivation conditions on C-phycocyanin extractability following pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment of Arthrospira platensis
summary: Microalgae and cyanobacteria, such as Arthrospira platensis (A. platensis), are a promising, sustainable source of proteins and bioactive compounds, including the blue protein-pigment complex phycocyanin. Pulsed electric fields (PEF) are a
content: Microalgae and cyanobacteria, such as Arthrospira platensis (A. platensis), are a promising, sustainable source of proteins and bioactive compounds, including the blue protein-pigment complex phycocyanin. Pulsed electric fields (PEF) are a potentially energy-efficient technology for protein and phycocyanin extraction. However, the need to replace the cultivation medium before treatment because of its high conductivity limits its industrial application. Reduced salt cultivation could therefore enhance the technical viability of PEF treatment. Nevertheless, the influence of medium composition on the relation between growth, phycocyanin content, and sensitivity to PEF treatment remains unclear. Arthrospira platensis was cultivated for seven or 14 days in media with 5%, 20%, 50%, or 100% of the standard SOT medium carbonate concentration. The modified media also contained reduced nitrate and selected salts, while the pH was maintained at 9.5 through a controlled CO 2 supply. After cultivation, the biomass was washed, resuspended in standardized buffer, and subjected to PEF treatment at 20 kV/cm with a specific energy input of 25 or 75 kJ/kg. After 7 days, there was no significant difference in biomass concentration or phycocyanin content between the tested media. However, PEF-mediated phycocyanin extraction was strongly affected by the cultivation medium. The highest C-phycocyanin recoveries relative to the ultrasound reference were 96.6% and 90.8% for biomass cultivated in 5% and 20% SOT medium, respectively, compared to 52.7% and 50.6% for biomass cultivated in 50% and 100% SOT medium. After 14 days, the advantage of reduced-salt cultivation was less pronounced. Phycocyanin content was lower in the reduced-salt media, indicating nutrient limitation. Cultivation in salt-reduced media for 7 days, therefore, provided the most favorable conditions for PEF-assisted phycocyanin recovery under the applied conditions. The present findings provide a basis for further investigations into PEF-assisted C-phycocyanin extraction directly in the cultivation medium, where lower electrical conductivity could reduce the generator peak power required to maintain a given electric field strength.

title: Beyond BET Surface Area: Accessible Porosity and Interfacial Binding Govern Batch and Fixed-Bed Phenol Capture by Porous Carbons
summary: The rational design of carbonaceous adsorbents for organic pollutant remediation requires moving beyond surface-area-centric metrics toward understanding carbon–water interfacial thermodynamics and structural accessibility. In this work, KO
content: The rational design of carbonaceous adsorbents for organic pollutant remediation requires moving beyond surface-area-centric metrics toward understanding carbon–water interfacial thermodynamics and structural accessibility. In this work, KOH-activated rice straw biochars (KRBCs) were developed via controlled KOH activation to systematically elucidate the mechanistic balance between pore structure, surface functionalities, and phenol (PhOH) uptake capacity. The moderately activated carbon (KRBC-2) demonstrated superior performance with an ultrafast adsorption equilibrium achieved within 10 min and a maximum Langmuir capacity of 164.008 mg·g–1 at 298 K. Intriguingly, overactivated carbon with higher BET surface area displayed inferior kinetic uptake, proving that accessible porosity and carbon-skeleton integrity─rather than raw surface area─dominate interfacial mass transport and site availability. Reversibility and thermodynamic studies demonstrated that PhOH sorption was spontaneous, exothermic, and highly sustainable (>90% efficiency after consecutive regeneration cycles). XPS and DFT calculations comprehensively revealed that the adsorption is driven by a multimodal mechanism: planar graphitic domains and nanoconfined pores induce strong π–π electron donor–acceptor and dispersion stabilization, whereas oxygen-containing polar sites contribute supplemental hydrogen bonding and local charge polarization. Overall, this study establishes a quantitative, experimentally constrained picture of PhOH adsorption at porous carbon interfaces, highlighting that moderate KOH activation optimizes pollutant accessibility while avoiding structural overdestruction.
