title: Translating culture into design studio pedagogy: a systematic review and integrated conceptual framework
summary: Introduction This study provides an overview of how culture is interpreted in architectural design education, addressing the fragmentation of pedagogical strategies used to translate abstract cultural constructs into the design studio. Meth
content: Introduction This study provides an overview of how culture is interpreted in architectural design education, addressing the fragmentation of pedagogical strategies used to translate abstract cultural constructs into the design studio. Methods Employing a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines, 319 records published between 2015 and 2026 were identified across Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. After applying strict eligibility criteria, 50 peer-reviewed studies were synthesised using bibliometric and thematic analyses. Results The findings are organised into three core thematic pillars derived from the research questions: cultural operationalisation, instructional delivery, and evaluation models. The relationships among these pillars informed the development of the Integrated Matrix of Cultural Pedagogy (IMCP), a novel conceptual framework that systematically links how culture is defined, taught, and assessed. Discussion By bridging the persistent gap between cultural theory and tangible design output, the IMCP framework equips design educators, researchers, and curriculum boards with a data-grounded, flexible structure to audit and deliver culturally responsive education. Ultimately, this review provides a robust foundation for future empirical research and the global restructuring of context-aware design curricula.

title: A Coupled Critical Shear Crack and Local Bond–Slip Model for Predicting the Shear Capacity of CFRP-Strengthened Reinforced Concrete Beams
summary: Externally bonded carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) sheets are widely used to strengthen reinforced concrete (RC) beams in shear. However, predicting the CFRP contribution is difficult, since concrete cracking, stirrup action, and CFRP
content: Externally bonded carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) sheets are widely used to strengthen reinforced concrete (RC) beams in shear. However, predicting the CFRP contribution is difficult, since concrete cracking, stirrup action, and CFRP debonding interact at the critical crack. This study presents a mechanics-based model for slender U-wrapped beams with a/d ≥ 2.5. The concrete contribution follows a critical shear crack theory (CSCT)-type criterion, and the crack angle follows the AASHTO strain relation. The CFRP is modeled as discrete crack bridges with a Lu-type bond–slip law, and its contribution is the peak of the summed bridge response, without an assumed effective strain. For 31 external rectangular beams, obtained by screening a published 172-beam database, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 12.01%, compared with 21.31% for ACI 440.2 and 16.07% for fib Bulletin 14, and it remained between 9.9% and 14.0% when each program was removed in turn. For an independent six-beam series, the MAPE was 3.71% for the total capacity and 14.78% for the CFRP contribution. The main limitation is that the concrete and CFRP terms are not evaluated at the same crack opening, and enforcing this compatibility would reduce the predictions by 27–33% on average. T-beams, anchored beams, and other configurations are reported separately.

title: Contrasting maize straw pre-decomposition strategies alter soil nutrient status, root metabolism, and rhizosphere microbial communities in an acidic red soil
summary: Introduction Straw decomposition products may serve as organic amendments for acidic soils, but their effects depend on the decomposition strategy. Methods Maize straw was pre-decomposed for 150 d with either effective microorganisms (EM) o
content: Introduction Straw decomposition products may serve as organic amendments for acidic soils, but their effects depend on the decomposition strategy. Methods Maize straw was pre-decomposed for 150 d with either effective microorganisms (EM) or lime, and the resulting products were applied to an acidic red soil planted with maize. The pot experiment comprised three treatments: unamended control (CK), the EM-mediated straw decomposition product (EM-SDP), and the lime-mediated straw decomposition product (Lime-SDP). We assessed maize growth, soil properties, root metabolomic profiles, and rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities. Results Both amendments promoted maize growth and altered root metabolic and rhizosphere microbial profiles. Lime-SDP treatment primarily alleviated soil acidity and increased total K, whereas EM-SDP treatment was associated with higher soil organic matter and greater N, P, and K availability. Root metabolic profiles were also strongly reconfigured, with treatment explaining 46.7% of the total metabolomic variation (R 2 = 0.467, exact P = 0.0036), with the dominant response shared by both amendments. Treatment explained 30.5% of bacterial and 34.3% of fungal community variation based on Aitchison distances (both P = 0.0036). Terpenoid-related features were the only chemical class significantly enriched among the shared metabolic responses. Exploratory path model analysis showed that EM-SDP was associated with the major soil physicochemical gradient, Lime-SDP with root-metabolome variation, and both amendments with the first Aitchison PCoA axis of the fungal community (β = 0.739 and 0.876, respectively). Discussion These findings highlight distinct soil, root metabolic, and rhizosphere microbial responses to contrasting straw pre-decomposition strategies in the acidic red soil.

title: Activation controlled pore engineering and ion transport in polyetherimide-derived carbon for high performance supercapacitors
summary: Activated porous carbons are promising electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors due to their tunable surface characteristics and charge-storage properties. This work examines the effect of \(ZnCl_{2}\) activation on the stru
content: Activated porous carbons are promising electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors due to their tunable surface characteristics and charge-storage properties. This work examines the effect of \(ZnCl_{2}\) activation on the structural, surface, and electrochemical properties of carbon materials derived from PEI (polyetherimide). Both non-activated and activated samples were compared using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy dispersive X-ray analysis and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller analysis. Activation with \(ZnCl_{2}\) altered the surface properties and porous structure of the carbon materials. The electrodes were used to fabricate all-solid-state supercapacitors with an optimized solid polymer electrolyte based on polyethylene oxide ( \({S}_{0a}-7\) ), that contained \(5 \: wt.\%\) sodium thiocyanate and \(30 \: \text{w}\text{t}.\%\) tributylmethylphosphonium iodide. It exhibited an ionic conductivity of \(\sim7.9\times{10}^{-5} \: \text{S} \: \text{c}\text{m}^{-1}\) and an electrochemical stability window of \(\sim3.7 \: \text{V}\) . Supercapacitors were investigated via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and cyclic voltammetry techniques. Due to its enhanced porosity and larger ion-accessible surface area, the activated electrode demonstrated a significantly higher specific capacitance \(\sim 166 \: \text{F} \: \text{g}^{-1}\) compared to \(\sim 60.8 \: \text{F} \: \text{g}^{-1}\) for the non-activated electrode, calculated from CV measurements at a scan rate of \(5 \: \text{m}\text{V} \: \text{s}^{-1}\) within a potential window of \(-1\) to \(+1 \: \text{V}\) . These results demonstrate the potential of \(ZnCl_{2}\) -activated porous carbon derived from polyetherimide as an electrode material for next-generation solid-state supercapacitors.

title: Upcycling Waste Plastics into Conductive Materials: Conversion Methods, Applications, and Pathways to Circularity
summary: The escalating global production of plastics, coupled with persistently low recycling rates, demands innovative valorization strategies. Upcycling waste plastics into conductive materials offers a dual-strategy solution that addresses both
content: The escalating global production of plastics, coupled with persistently low recycling rates, demands innovative valorization strategies. Upcycling waste plastics into conductive materials offers a dual-strategy solution that addresses both environmental pollution and the growing demand for energy-storage and electronic applications. By examining four feedstock classes (hydrocarbon, oxygen-containing, nitrogen-containing, and halogenated polymers) and three conversion pathways (pyrolytic, non-pyrolytic, and hybrid), the review traces how waste plastics are transformed into advanced functional materials and how polymer structure governs carbon yield, porosity, and heteroatom retention. Plastic-derived hard carbons reach reversible capacities of roughly 300 to 450 mAh/g in sodium-ion and potassium-ion anodes, while several activated and heteroatom-doped porous carbons exceed 400 F/g in supercapacitors, and carbon nanotube and graphene additives together with conductive polymer composites further broaden the application range. These upcycled materials also enable high-performance sensors, electromagnetic interference shielding, and energy-harvesting devices. However, critical gaps including the absence of standardized testing protocols, the difficulty of scaling complex multi-step routes, and limited techno-economic and life-cycle validation for advanced chemical recycling continue to hinder commercialization. Addressing these challenges is essential to transitioning plastic upcycling from laboratory research to viable real-world deployment and to establish it as a core component of the circular economy.

title: Multi-year field study links local bio-inoculants and plant extracts to improved soybean yield and rhizosphere functions
summary: Soybean productivity in Cameroon (0.60 t ha⁻¹) remains below the global average (2.76 t ha⁻¹), partly due to poor soil fertility in acidic tropical soils, which drives reliance on chemical inputs that may pose environmental risks. A field s
content: Soybean productivity in Cameroon (0.60 t ha⁻¹) remains below the global average (2.76 t ha⁻¹), partly due to poor soil fertility in acidic tropical soils, which drives reliance on chemical inputs that may pose environmental risks. A field study was conducted from 2021 to 2023 in Buea, Cameroon, using a randomized complete block design with four replications to evaluate the effects of microbial inoculants and plant extracts on soybean productivity. Soybean grain yield, 1000-grain weight and nodulation were assessed across all cropping periods from 2021 to 2023. Soil microbial biomass, acid phosphatase, urease and soil physicochemical properties were assessed in August 2021 and April 2022, while plant N, P, K uptake, total root bacteria and qPCR analyses for Kosakonia radicincitans colonization and nifH abundance were assessed only in April 2022 as cumulative indicators. Thirteen management options were tested: a no-input control, chemical input, microbial consortia (Bacteria and Fungi), plant extracts ( Mucuna and Piper ), and their combinations. Across three years, bio-inputs produced grain yield and 1000-grain weight similar to chemical input ( P > 0.05) and significantly higher than the control ( P < 0.05). Maximum yield was 6.9 t ha⁻¹ for M + EF in 2022, compared to 3.1 t ha⁻¹ in the control. Soybean yield and 1000-grain weight correlated positively ( P < 0.05) with effective nodules, acid phosphatase, urease, microbial biomass, total nitrogen, available phosphorus, and organic matter. Quantitative PCR conducted in the 2022 season only confirmed root colonization by Kosakonia radicincitans in inoculated treatments and higher nifH abundance, suggesting greater genetic potential for biological nitrogen fixation. Plant extracts alone performed comparably to microbial inoculants ( P > 0.05). Combinations significantly increased rhizosphere pH, microbial biomass, enzyme activities, effective nodules, and root bacteria compared to chemical input or control ( P < 0.05). Overall, locally produced bio-inoculants and plant extracts enhanced rhizosphere functions and soybean yield, offering viable sustainable alternatives to chemical inputs.

title: Great Expectations: Remodeling the emissions assumptions behind CDR policies
summary: How much carbon dioxide removal (CDR) will the world need if emissions do not decline as rapidly as assumed in many of today's climate policy scenarios? Great Expectations: Remodeling the emissions assumptions behind CDR policies explores t
content: How much carbon dioxide removal (CDR) will the world need if emissions do not decline as rapidly as assumed in many of today's climate policy scenarios? Great Expectations: Remodeling the emissions assumptions behind CDR policies explores this question through a new comparative framework called TIER (Temperature Impact from Emissions and Removals). Using the FaIR climate model and 841 calibrated climate configurations, TIER evaluates 121 combinations of emissions-reduction and carbon dioxide removal pathways through 2200, examining their implications for global temperatures, peak warming, temperature overshoot, climate restoration, and the consequences of delayed action. An applied version of this framework, TIER-A, explores how established CDR deployment scenarios from the third edition of the State of Carbon Dioxide Removal report might perform under alternative CMIP7 emissions pathways. The findings suggest that future CDR requirements could be substantially higher than commonly cited estimates if anticipated emissions reductions fail to materialize. The report makes the case for evaluating CDR needs across a wider range of possible emissions futures and for developing more ambitious, scalable, and affordable removal solutions alongside continued emissions reduction efforts. Developed by the Science Communication Institute for the Vancouver Process, this report is intended to inform international climate policy discussions and encourage further research. The accompanying dataset includes model inputs, numerical outputs, figures, computational code, historical validation results, and reproduction instructions.

title: Decannulation and noninvasive ventilation: the respiratory support loop
summary: Liberation from an artificial airway through decannulation and liberation from mechanical ventilatory support are fundamentally distinct clinical objectives that have historically been conflated. In complex critical care populations, includ
content: Liberation from an artificial airway through decannulation and liberation from mechanical ventilatory support are fundamentally distinct clinical objectives that have historically been conflated. In complex critical care populations, including patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), obesity hypoventilation syndrome, neuromuscular diseases, high cervical spinal cord injury, and stroke, ventilatory muscle pump failure often persists beyond the need for an invasive airway. Traditional sequential weaning pathways, progressing from invasive mechanical ventilation to a spontaneous breathing trial, decannulation, and complete liberation, may unnecessarily prolong tracheostomy dependence, increase hospital-acquired pulmonary infections, impair swallowing, and delay the restoration of speech. This review introduces the Respiratory Support Loop (RSL), a cyclical model integrating non-invasive ventilation (NIV) as an active bridging strategy between liberation from invasive ventilation and decannulation. Once upper airway patency, swallowing safety and effective cough clearance have been established, decannulation can proceed while NIV supports respiratory muscle function during periods of increased demand, particularly overnight. We propose a multidomain readiness assessment covering six physiological domains: neurological status; upper airway anatomy; swallowing safety; cough effectiveness; respiratory muscle strength; and gas exchange. The review presents practical protocols for NIV with a downsized, capped tracheostomy tube in situ, the management of peristomal air leakage and phenotype-specific weaning pathways. The review incorporates a critical appraisal of the evidence using GRADE certainty ratings, Cochrane systematic reviews and the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS) for cohort studies. The evidence reviewed supports the use of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) as a bridging strategy and targeted respiratory muscle training. However, it should be noted that the evidence for sequential NIV-supported weaning is predominantly observational. Decannulation decisions should be based on multidimensional clinical readiness rather than on capping trials or oxygenation measurements in isolation. Persistent compensated hypercapnia should not be considered an absolute contraindication to decannulation. Every patient discharged through this pathway should have a clearly defined, phenotype-specific plan for long-term respiratory support.

title: Coordination‐Driven Spiral Self‐Assembly of Helical Mesoporous Polymer Nanospheres and Derived MoS 2 /Carbon Colloidal Nanospheres for Fast Lithium Storage
summary: Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied
content: Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. Herein, we develop a coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly (CSS) strategy that converts achiral building blocks into helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres (HMPSs) with continuous spiral surface textures and internal helical mesopores. Interfacial Mo–S coordination drives micellar spiral organization without chiral additives, enabling systematic regulation of pore size, morphology, and composition. Subsequent carbonization transforms HMPSs into helical mesoporous MoS 2 /C nanospheres (HMMoS 2 /C) containing uniformly dispersed monolayer MoS 2 while retaining the helical mesostructure. Finite‐element simulations and density functional theory calculations reveal that the helical mesoporous architecture facilitates rapid Li + diffusion, local ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, thereby improving Li‐storage kinetics. Consequently, HMMoS 2 /C delivers a reversible capacity of 1776.3 mAh g − 1 at 0.3 A g − 1 after 150 cycles, a high‐rate capacity of 752.7 mAh g − 1 at 10 A g − 1, and outstanding long‐term cycling stability. This work establishes coordination‐driven self‐assembly as a versatile route to helical mesoporous materials for energy storage.

title: Glucose-Assisted Synthesis of Hierarchical Zeolite Y for CO₂ Capture: Adsorption Isotherms, Selectivity, and Isosteric Heat
summary: In this study, a glucose modified hierarchical Zeolite Y adsorbent was developed for high-performance CO2 capture. Glucose as a soft templating agent was used to modify the pore structure and surface chemistry for preparing the multifunctio
content: In this study, a glucose modified hierarchical Zeolite Y adsorbent was developed for high-performance CO2 capture. Glucose as a soft templating agent was used to modify the pore structure and surface chemistry for preparing the multifunctional adsorbent with improved adsorption performance. The synthesized materials were characterized by XRD, FTIR, TGA, SEM-EDX and N2 adsorption-desorption analysis. Results confirmed the retention of the crystalline zeolite Y structure after modification and the successful introduction of additional oxygen-containing surface functionalities and improved pore accessibility. The unmodified zeolite had the highest BET surface area (862 m2.g-1). The modified samples (with slightly lower surface areas) exhibited better adsorption behavior. The highest CO2 adsorption capacity was observed for the glucose modified zeolite YS/0.2 of 4.88 mmol.g-1 at 273 K and 4.52 mmol.g-1 at 298 K in comparison with the unmodified zeolite, which was 3.65 and 3.15 mmol.g-1, respectively. Moreover, the CO2/N2 selectivity of the YS/0.2 was still high at 11.08 and 11.63 for CO2/N2 and 5.34 and 7.91 for CO2/CH4 at 273 and 298 K, respectively. The raw zeolite showed the highest heat of adsorption (27.53 kJ.mol-1). The YS/0.2 showed the highest of CO2 uptake due to the improvement of pore accessibility and mass transfer characteristics. The CO2 adsorption data were well described by the Langmuir model (R2 = 0.986) and the predicted monolayer capacity (5.15 mmol.g-1) was close to the experimental uptake (4.88 mmol.g-1) indicating adsorption on relatively uniform sites. The adsorption followed the Freundlich model (R2= 0.959) indicating adsorption on a heterogeneous surface and the Toth model gave the best overall fit (R2= 0.999) and confirmed the heterogeneous nature of the adsorption. The results indicate that the glucose-modified adsorbents are multifunctional, simple, cheap and sustainable for carbon capture.

title: Forecasting biomass electricity production in Greece with SARIMA and SARIMAX models – A methodological approach
summary: Biomass supports grid stability because, unlike wind and solar, it can be dispatched and stored on demand. Yet mid-term forecasts of biomass electricity generation remain scarce, particularly for national systems with limited installed capa
content: Biomass supports grid stability because, unlike wind and solar, it can be dispatched and stored on demand. Yet mid-term forecasts of biomass electricity generation remain scarce, particularly for national systems with limited installed capacity such as Greece. This study compares univariate SARIMA and exogenous SARIMAX models for monthly biomass electricity generation in Greece over 2014–2026, testing deterministic against stochastic seasonality and the role of installed capacity as an exogenous regressor. A SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1) 12 model outperforms deterministic alternatives in short-term forecasts, while adding installed capacity in a SARIMAX(1,0,0)(0,1,1) 12 improves accuracy over the extended horizon, reflecting a cointegrating long-run relationship between capacity and output. An ex-post adjustment for zero-price hours and mandatory renewable energy curtailment suggests that recent regulatory shifts can also be captured within the SARIMAX framework, further improving forecast accuracy. These findings underline the value of combining technical and regulatory information in forecasting for grid operators and policymakers.

title: Millennial‐Scale Persistence and Long‐Term Dormancy of Bloom‐Forming Cyanobacteria in the Baltic Sea Revealed by Viable Resting Stages and Sedimentary Ancient DNA
summary: Blooms of filamentous diazotrophic cyanobacteria (Nostocales) have occurred in the Baltic Sea for millennia but are expected to intensify under ongoing climate warming and eutrophication, with consequences for ecosystem health. Nostocales f
content: Blooms of filamentous diazotrophic cyanobacteria (Nostocales) have occurred in the Baltic Sea for millennia but are expected to intensify under ongoing climate warming and eutrophication, with consequences for ecosystem health. Nostocales form resting stages (akinetes) that are preserved in sediments, enabling reconstruction of past bloom dynamics. We investigated past and contemporary variability in the abundance of bloom-forming Nostocales by analysing akinetes and sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) metabarcoding from central Baltic Sea sediments, spanning ~7200 calibrated years before present (cal yr BP). Akinete viability was assessed by dead-cell staining and fluorescence microscopy. Akinetes were present back to ~3580 cal yr BP, with 98% remaining viable for up to 200 years and the oldest viable akinete persisting up to ~1450 years, highlighting resilience in hypoxic Baltic Sea sediments. SedaDNA extended the Nostocales record back to ~7150 cal yr BP. Both parameters showed a significant increase in Nostocales abundance since the 1990s, likely driven by past anthropogenic nutrient inputs before and ongoing climate warming in the Baltic Sea. The findings highlight the value of a multi-parameter approach, while discrepancies between akinete and sedaDNA records underscore the complexity of reconstructing past cyanobacterial abundance from sedimentary archives.

title: Reviving the Oasis Heritage: Thermodynamic Analysis and Regulatory Bottlenecks of Contemporary Rammed Earth under the Scope of RPCT 2011
source: Global Journal of Researches in Engineering
summary: In response to the climate emergency, reviving vernacular building cultures is a critical paradigm. This paper investigates the transferability of vernacular architecture from Southern Moroccan oases—characterized by rammed earth (pisé) and
content: In response to the climate emergency, reviving vernacular building cultures is a critical paradigm. This paper investigates the transferability of vernacular architecture from Southern Moroccan oases—characterized by rammed earth (pisé) and high-density urban morphology (ksour)—into contemporary practice. While their bioclimatic efficiency is documented, a major gap remains regarding practical operationalization under modern industrial needs, the Moroccan Earthen Buildings Seismic Code (RPCT 2011), and market realities. Using triangulation, this research combines morpho-typological analyses in the Drâa and Ziz valleys, stakeholder field surveys ( _n_ =24), and a meta-analysis of local geo-resources. Quantitative findings corroborate the thermodynamic superiority of optimized contemporary rammed earth (10– 12 hours thermal lag) and ksour morphology, which reduces global radiative load by 35%. However, a complex triple trade-off restricts the sector: strict altimetric limits (maximum R+1) under RPCT 2011, lack of insurance frameworks, and an economic distortion making optimized rammed earth 1.5 to 2 times more expensive than concrete due to labor intensity. Furthermore, life cycle assessment (LCA) shows that hydraulic binders compromise the material’s initial ecological reversibility, while interviews highlight the fragility of this orally transmitted craft, which faces demographic extinction. Ultimately, the paper advocates for a technological hybridization strategy based on decentralized industrialization (prefabricated components), supported by normative updates and adapted public procurement frameworks to establish raw earth as a sustainable, sovereign, and economically viable pillar of architectural modernity in Morocco.

title: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Working Papers
summary: Applied economists use subaggregate variation to estimate macroeconomic effects without establishing whether relationships aggregate consistently.We develop an aggregation-consistent exposure framework.For linear models, two requirements un
content: Applied economists use subaggregate variation to estimate macroeconomic effects without establishing whether relationships aggregate consistently.We develop an aggregation-consistent exposure framework.For linear models, two requirements uniquely yield a two-slope exposure specification: coalition responses must be invariant to within-coalition treatment allocation, and the response to a unit increase in a coalition's average treatment must vary linearly with coalition size.Conventional time fixed-effects regressions identify the relative-exposure slope; the aggregate-exposure slope captures responses to a common exposure increase.Applications to carbon taxes, state exposure to oil supply shocks, and federal income-tax shocks show that relative and aggregate effects can differ substantially.

title: Food Processing Innovation, Productive Employment, and Poverty Reduction in Afghanistan: An Integrative Narrative Review
source: Journal of Strategic Innovation in Economics and Business
summary: Agrarian economies like Afghanistan face a persistent paradox: abundant agricultural endowments coexist with entrenched poverty and underemployment due to raw exports and severe post-harvest losses, yet scholarship rarely integrates food pr
content: Agrarian economies like Afghanistan face a persistent paradox: abundant agricultural endowments coexist with entrenched poverty and underemployment due to raw exports and severe post-harvest losses, yet scholarship rarely integrates food processing innovation with labor quality and fragile-state constraints. Anchored in Global Value Chain (GVC) governance theory and dynamic capabilities, this review examines how food processing innovation drives productive employment and poverty reduction in Afghanistan. We conducted an integrative narrative review across Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, Persian repositories, and multilateral libraries, prioritizing 2021–2026 literature, and thematically synthesized 51 core publications using qualitative credibility appraisal. Findings indicate that although agriculture generates 33.7% of Afghanistan’s gross domestic product versus 16.1% for industry, only 23.5% of reviewed studies examine Afghanistan directly. Comparative evidence demonstrates that agro-industrial jobs alleviate poverty durably only when formal, stable, and productivity-enhancing rather than precarious. In Afghanistan, interlocking deficits in credit, energy, cold chains, skills, and export certification exclude small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) from higher-value markets, rendering capital-intensive frontier processing technologies unviable in isolation. Instead, staged upgrading—prioritizing shared cold chains, hygienic packaging, and electronic marketing before moderate non-thermal processing—yields the highest inclusive-growth returns under binding transit and energy constraints. Theoretically, this review extends GVC governance and dynamic capabilities through a four-layer ecosystem framework tailored to fragile agrarian states. Practically, it guides SME managers toward capability-sequenced innovation and urges policymakers to bundle rural infrastructure with SME finance, accredited laboratories, and workforce training.

title: From imaging to immunotherapy: luminescence-based strategies for reprogramming the tumor microenvironment
summary: Photoluminescence (PL)-based nanotheranostics integrate real-time imaging with light-activated therapy, offering a route to reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Clinical translation, however, remains hindered by poo
content: Photoluminescence (PL)-based nanotheranostics integrate real-time imaging with light-activated therapy, offering a route to reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Clinical translation, however, remains hindered by poor light penetration, the diminished oxygen-dependent reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and unresolved safety and manufacturing challenges. This review presents a stepwise framework organized around four progressive dimensions: precision imaging guidance for treatment planning and dosimetry; deep-tissue excitation strategies, including X-ray-excited persistent luminescence and chemiluminescence resonance energy transfer, that circumvent physical light barriers; biochemical TME reprogramming through Type I photosensitizers, which retain activity under hypoxia rather than being oxygen-independent, together with oxygen-supplying systems that further sustain ROS generation under hypoxia; and the downstream induction of immunogenic cell death and pyroptosis that converts localized therapy into systemic antitumor immunity. We distinguish photodynamic therapy (PDT) from photothermal therapy (PTT) and combination modalities throughout, and we critically appraise the evidence base, noting the predominance of single subcutaneous models, small cohort sizes, inconsistent ROS reporting, and the near-absence of abscopal and survival endpoints. We further propose a two-tier prioritization framework that separates platform-intrinsic potential from treatment-dependent achievability, making explicit which parameters must be measured at which stage of development rather than assigning weights to incommensurable quantities. Future work should prioritize NIR-II activatable systems, harmonized GMP manufacturing, and prospective clinical validation linking photophysical parameters to survival outcomes.

title: Angle‐Triggered Structural‐Color Anti‐Counterfeiting Enabled by Film‐Covered Photonic Crystals
summary: Photonic crystal structural colors provide attractive optical features for anti‐counterfeiting, but their practical use is often limited by background dependence, slow responsiveness, or poor durability. Here, we report a pure optical‐path
content: Photonic crystal structural colors provide attractive optical features for anti‐counterfeiting, but their practical use is often limited by background dependence, slow responsiveness, or poor durability. Here, we report a pure optical‐path modulation strategy that enables transparent concealment and angle‐triggered decryption in two‐dimensional photonic crystals. The film‐covered photonic crystal (FCPC), fabricated by self‐assembly and magnetron sputtering, remains invisible under ambient light on different backgrounds but immediately reveals bright structural colors along the forward diffraction path. The flower color code and FCPC bilayer label exhibit effective readout windows of approximately 3° and 5°, respectively, under the tested conditions. An indium tin oxide (ITO) overlayer increases the optical path length of the diffracted light, producing a predictable structural‐color redshift and programmable color output across the visible spectrum. Using this optical‐path control, we achieve transparent concealment and angle‐triggered decryption in two different scenarios: color‐code matching and pattern recognition. The strategy combines optical concealment, rapid readout, background independence, mechanical flexibility, and scalable fabrication, providing a high‐security optical authentication platform for information encryption.

title: Amorphous SiOC nanofibers: A multifunctional platform integrating electromagnetic wave transparency, thermal insulation, and mechanical resilience for extreme environments
summary: Amorphous SiOC ceramics show promise potential for high-temperature electromagnetic wave (EMW) transmission owing to their light weight, low dielectric loss, and thermal/oxidation resistance. However, bulk SiOC suffers from inherent brittle
content: Amorphous SiOC ceramics show promise potential for high-temperature electromagnetic wave (EMW) transmission owing to their light weight, low dielectric loss, and thermal/oxidation resistance. However, bulk SiOC suffers from inherent brittleness and poor designability, limiting applications on complex structural surfaces. Herein, flexible amorphous SiOC nanofiber membranes were fabricated via electrospinning by precisely regulating precursor-solution viscosity and conductivity to minimize defects and create free surfaces for stress release. The resulting three-dimensional nanofiber network endows the membranes with exceptional compressive resilience (retaining >95% of initial maximum stress after 500 cycles at 50% strain), ultralow thermal conductivity (<0.04 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹), fire resistance (structural integrity maintained after 5 min flame exposure), and excellent recyclability (negligible mass and adsorption-capacity loss after ten pollutant adsorption–elimination cycles). Moreover, the amorphous SiOC phase yields an ultralow dielectric constant (ε′ ≈ 1.0) and loss tangent (tan δ < 0.0023), enabling >99% EMW transparency across the entire X band; this transparency remains above 98% after cyclic compression and high-temperature treatment. These findings offer valuable insights into the design of multifunctional wave-transmitting materials for harsh environments.

title: A SHAP-Augmented Machine Learning Framework for Optimizing Iron-Carbon Micro-Electrolysis of PVA Wastewater
summary: While iron-carbon micro-electrolysis (ICME) is effective for treating polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) wastewater, its optimization remains notably constrained by two limitations of Response Surface Methodology (RSM): RSM's poor extrapolation capabi
content: While iron-carbon micro-electrolysis (ICME) is effective for treating polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) wastewater, its optimization remains notably constrained by two limitations of Response Surface Methodology (RSM): RSM's poor extrapolation capability and inability to reveal underlying governing mechanisms beyond local experimental domains. To break this bottleneck, this study establishes a triple-integrated paradigm that synergistically combines the experimental rigor of RSM, the predictive power of machine learning, and the mechanistic insights from SHAP interpretability analysis. A high-fidelity dataset of 1,423 samples was constructed via Box-Behnken design augmented with literature data. Among seven machine learning (ML)algorithms evaluated, XGBoost achieved superior predictive performance for COD removal rate(test set R² = 0.8045, RMSE = 6.06, MAPE = 11.25%), demonstrating robust generalization. Crucially, SHAP analysis decoded insights inaccessible to RSM: it identified the Fe/C ratio as the dominant structural factor governing system efficiency and delineated pH 2–3 as the optimal window for synergistic Fe/C ratio - pH interactions. The core innovation lies in the three-tiered methodological integration: RSM provides a rigorous experimental foundation; machine learning enables global, high-accuracy prediction; and SHAP transforms the "black-box" model into a discovery tool for extracting condition-dependent rules. This paradigm shifts the optimization strategy from local empirical tuning to system-level intelligent design, enabling a translatable framework for real-time control and the scale-up process of complex wastewater treatment.

title: Knowledge-guided supervisory architecture with an LLM-compatible interface for robust energy management of integrated storage under renewable uncertainty
summary: Introduction High renewable penetration couples forecast errors, storage dynamics, and grid constraints. We study a knowledge-guided supervisory architecture that maps operational context to bounded uncertainty margins, carbon and peak weig
content: Introduction High renewable penetration couples forecast errors, storage dynamics, and grid constraints. We study a knowledge-guided supervisory architecture that maps operational context to bounded uncertainty margins, carbon and peak weights, degradation multipliers, and reserve targets. Methods A worst-corner rolling linear program coordinates battery, hydrogen, and thermal storage, followed by deterministic realized-balance repair. A large language model (LLM)-compatible interface is proposed, but the experiments use deterministic numeric context rules and do not execute retrieval, language-model inference, or a text parser. The synthetic 7-day comparison gives all model predictive control (MPC) controllers the same issued grid-event notices and emergency recourse. Results Each MPC controller achieves numerical zero unserved energy. Relative to fixed robust MPC, the adaptive supervisor decreases nominal peak import from 439.86 to 414.81 kW but increases evaluation cost from 3,160.73 to 3,337.12 USD and service-normalized emissions from 145.28 to 148.01 kg CO 2 /MWh. Four additional randomized scenarios show the same mean cost-peak trade-off, without establishing universal superiority. Isolated ablations and notice-recourse controls show that zero shortage is not unique to adaptive reasoning. All 57 released trajectories pass physical and accounting checks. Discussion Exact-projection and recursive-feasibility statements remain conditional theoretical results, not certificates for the implemented heuristic.

title: Unprecedented evaluation of macaúba (Acrocomia aculeata) oils from commercial sources: chemical profile and bioactivity
summary: The interest in macaúba (Acrocomia aculeata) oil is primarily driven by studies using experimental or non-commercial samples, while little is known about the quality and functionality of products available to consumers. This study provides
content: The interest in macaúba (Acrocomia aculeata) oil is primarily driven by studies using experimental or non-commercial samples, while little is known about the quality and functionality of products available to consumers. This study provides an unprecedented evaluation of commercial macaúba oils, focusing on their fatty acid profile, acidity index, phenolic compounds, antioxidant capacity, carotenoid content, and antimicrobial potential. Gas chromatography analysis revealed a predominance of monounsaturated fatty acids, particularly oleic acid, with nutritional indices favorable to cardiovascular health. However, both samples exhibited linoleic acid levels at higher concentrations than those reported in the literature, raising concerns regarding raw material variability or possible adulteration. Despite relevant concentrations of carotenoids and moderate antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, the oils presented a low phenolic content, limited antioxidant activity, and acidity values above acceptable limits, indicating quality deterioration. These findings highlight the importance of monitoring commercial macaúba oils to ensure authenticity, technological quality, and consumer safety, while reinforcing their potential as a sustainable alternative to conventional vegetable oils.

title: Fabrication of Rice Husk Biochar under Varying Pyrolysis Conditions for Soil Amendment and Enhanced Agronomic Traits of Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)
summary: Rice husk, an abundant agricultural residue that is mostly wasted or burned, has potential as a biochar feedstock. This study examined how pyrolysis temperature affects the physicochemical and structural properties of rice husk biochar (RHB
content: Rice husk, an abundant agricultural residue that is mostly wasted or burned, has potential as a biochar feedstock. This study examined how pyrolysis temperature affects the physicochemical and structural properties of rice husk biochar (RHB), and how RHB influences the germination, growth, and yield of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.). RHB was produced by slow pyrolysis at 250, 350, and 450°C for 2 h. It was characterized in terms of proximate and chemical properties, morphology, elemental composition, and structure using SEM, EDAX, and XRD. Pot experiments assessed wheat germination, early seedling development, growth, and yield under control and RHB treatments. As pyrolysis temperature increased, biochar yield fell from about 69% at 250°C to 40% at 450°C. Moisture content also decreased, while ash and fixed carbon contents rose. RHB improved early seedling development, and the 450°C biochar produced the fastest shoot and root growth. The 450°C treatment also gave the greatest plant height, leaf number, dry weight, and leaf area index. It produced the most spikes and spikelets and the highest grain and stover yields. Pyrolysis temperature therefore markedly changed RHB properties, and these changes shaped wheat establishment, growth, and yield. Temperature-optimized RHB is a promising way to recycle residue for sustainable wheat production and agricultural waste management.

title: Ultrastable Chromium Pyrazolate Polyhedra With Amorphization‐Enhanced Microporosity for Corrosive Guest Capture
summary: The chemical stability of porous coordination solids is commonly rationalized using hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) considerations, which have largely excluded chromium(III)‐pyrazolate architectures owing to their incompatibility and the kinetic
content: The chemical stability of porous coordination solids is commonly rationalized using hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) considerations, which have largely excluded chromium(III)‐pyrazolate architectures owing to their incompatibility and the kinetic inertness of Cr(III). Here, we report the first porous chromium(III) pyrazolate metal–organic polyhedron. The material exhibits extraordinary chemical robustness, remaining chemically intact over a pH window spanning 13.7 units (pH < 0 to 13). The protonation tendency of azolate ligands is largely suppressed upon coordination to Cr(III), leading to resistance to acidic environments. Remarkably, even after amorphization induced by prolonged boiling in water (Cr(III)‐MOP‐A), the discrete Cr–pyrazolate cages persist, as evidenced by XPS and EXAFS, accompanied by an approximately twofold increase in the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area. This unexpected robustness originates from a ligand‐field‐dominated stability regime in which the d 3 electronic configuration of Cr(III) maximizes crystal‐field stabilization energy, leading to unusually strong Cr–N (pyrazolate) bonding that overrides HSAB‐based expectations. Such robustness enables efficient and recyclable adsorption of highly corrosive guests, including water vapor, SO 2, and NH 3. Notably, the amorphous MOP achieves the highest SO 2 uptake reported among metal–organic polyhedra, exceeding the previous benchmark by 74%, together with outstanding SO 2 /CO 2 selectivity that is corroborated by dynamic breakthrough experiments.

title: Development and pilot-scale validation of high-loading NMC811 composite cathodes for quasi-solid-state lithium metal batteries
summary: Introduction Quasi-solid-state lithium metal batteries offer higher energy density and improved safety, yet most demonstrations stop at the coin-cell scale, leaving their compatibility with conventional manufacturing largely unproven. Bridg
content: Introduction Quasi-solid-state lithium metal batteries offer higher energy density and improved safety, yet most demonstrations stop at the coin-cell scale, leaving their compatibility with conventional manufacturing largely unproven. Bridging this gap requires composite cathodes that combine high active-material loading with standard wet processing. Ni-rich NMC811 composite cathodes based on a polymeric catholyte were developed for pilot-scale production. Methods The thermal stability of the catholyte plasticizer under electrode-drying conditions was assessed by thermogravimetric analysis, and the catholyte fraction was tuned to maximize active-material content. Electrodes were evaluated in lithium-metal cells, then transferred to a roll-to-roll pilot coating line and assembled into single-layer pouch cells at an areal capacity of 2.5 mAh cm -2. Results The widely used plasticizer fluoroethylene carbonate evaporates almost entirely during drying, whereas its replacement by the ionic liquid PYR14TFSI yields a catholyte that withstands industrial drying without compositional drift. Optimizing the catholyte fraction increases the active-material content while preserving rate capability. Pilot-coated electrodes retain the microstructure and electronic conductivity of their lab-scale counterparts, and the resulting pouch cells cycle stably with Coulombic efficiency close to 100%, ultimately matching and exceeding coin-cell performance. Discussion These results demonstrate a viable route for quasi-solid-state composite cathodes from laboratory to pilot-scale manufacturing.

title: Prussian blue nanozyme-based colorimetric biosensor for rapid visual quantification of β-galactosidase-positive foodborne bacteria in bottled water and milk
summary: Infections caused by foodborne pathogens pose a serious challenge to global public health. Conventional detection approaches suffer from inherent drawbacks, e.g., time-consuming, operationally complex, high-cost, and instrument-dependent. T
content: Infections caused by foodborne pathogens pose a serious challenge to global public health. Conventional detection approaches suffer from inherent drawbacks, e.g., time-consuming, operationally complex, high-cost, and instrument-dependent. Thus, to develop a rapid, sensitive, convenient, and cost-effective novel visual sensor for bacterial detection remains an urgent need. Herein, we rationally designed a novel sensing strategy based on β-galactosidase-positive bacteria (β-gal) can interact with a peroxidase-like nanomaterials, i.e., Prussian blue nanoparticles (PB NPs). The PB NPs-based β-galactosidase detection approach enables highly specific recognition toward β-galactosidase-positive bacteria with the linear range from 8 × 10 1 to 8 × 10 7 CFU/mL (R 2 = 0.9984). Generally, PB NPs firstly catalyze H 2 O 2 -mediated oxidation of colorless 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) and yield a blue signal (oxidized TMB, ox-TMB). Upon the trigger of target bacteria, p-aminophenyl-β-D-galactopyranoside (PAPG) is subsequently hydrolyzed into reductive p-aminophenol (PAP), which suppresses ox-TMB, i.e., the blue signal is negatively correlated with the bacterial concentration. The turnaround time from sample generation to measurement has been reduced by half. The novel approach achieves real-time and sensitive detection for β-galactosidase-positive bacteria flora, showing excellent feasibility, robustness, and great potential for practical applications.

title: Effects of stand types on soil active organic carbon pool and driving factors in the dry-hot valley region of Sichuan Province, China
summary: Active organic carbon, as the core driver of soil nutrient cycling, is vital for enhancing soil carbon sequestration by directly participating in soil biochemical processes and transforming into stable organic carbon. Increasing soil carbon
content: Active organic carbon, as the core driver of soil nutrient cycling, is vital for enhancing soil carbon sequestration by directly participating in soil biochemical processes and transforming into stable organic carbon. Increasing soil carbon storage (SCS) promotes forest growth and ecosystem health by enhancing soil fer tility, water-holding capacity, and nutrients. To clarify the specific effects of different stand types on the soil active organic carbon pool in the dry-hot valley region, this study examined three typical forests: Pinus yunnanensis pure forest (YC), Pinus yunnanensis–Alnus cremastogyne mixed forest (YQ), and Camellia sinensis–Alnus cremastogyne mixed forest (CQ). We analyzed the soil active organic carbon pool, SCS and physicochemical properties at 0–20 cm depth and used redundancy analysis to identify key driving factors. Results showed that active organic carbon content and SCS decreased with soil depth across all stands, with the order CQ > YQ > YC, and significant differences were observed among stands and layers (p < 0.05). Soil organic carbon (SOC) and SCS was highest in the CQ, with significant differences between the 0–10 cm and 10–20 cm layers (p < 0.05). Easily oxidizable organic carbon and dissolved organic carbon also varied significantly among stands (p < 0.05), with differences diminishing with depth, while light fraction organic carbon and microbial biomass carbon differed significantly in both depth intervals. Total nitrogen showed a significant positive correlation with the SOC, SCS and was the main driver of active organic carbon pool variation (p < 0.05). The CQ demonstrated strong carbon fixation ability, indicating that introducing nitrogen-fixing tree species positively enhances the soil active organic carbon pool. Thus, incorporating nitrogen-fixing species in mixed afforestation is recommended to improve SCS, providing a valuable reference for ecological restoration and carbon sequestration in the dry-hot valley regions.

title: Surfactant-lipase-microwave-assisted extraction of Schizandrin A, Schizandrin B, and essential oil from Schisandra chinensis: process optimization, enrichment, and antioxidant activity
summary: Schizandrin A, Schizandrin B and Schisandra chinensis essential oil have excellent antioxidant, hepatoprotective and anti-inflammatory activities. This study first optimized their simultaneous extraction by surfactant-lipase-microwave-assis
content: Schizandrin A, Schizandrin B and Schisandra chinensis essential oil have excellent antioxidant, hepatoprotective and anti-inflammatory activities. This study first optimized their simultaneous extraction by surfactant-lipase-microwave-assisted extraction via Box-Behnken design, and turbid point enrichment with NaCl dosage, equilibrium time and temperature as factors. The optimal surfactant-lipase-microwave-assisted and turbid point enrichment conditions were determined, under which Schizandrin A and Schizandrin B extraction rates reached 96.34 and 96.45%. Their yields and Schisandra chinensis essential oil's oxygenated terpenoids content (16.61%) were 1.76, 2.05 and 1.21 times those of ethanol reflux extraction. Network pharmacology predicted that Schizandrin A and Schizandrin B may produce antioxidant effects via SRC, PTGS2, EGFR regulating cancer and MAPK pathways. All three exhibited in vitro chemical radical-scavenging capacity, with respective IC50 values for DPPH/ABTS/superoxide anion. Surfactant-lipase-microwave-assisted extraction represents an organic-solvent-reduced efficient extraction strategy, and the three components are potential natural antioxidants. This study investigates the combined use of surfactant-lipase-microwave-assisted extraction to simultaneously obtain Sch A, Sch B, and essential oil from Schisandra chinensis, providing fundamental technical data for its subsequent high-value utilization in functional food applications.

title: Interrupting Epitaxial Inheritance Through Phase Evolution Enables Grain Refinement in Additive Manufacturing
summary: The formation of columnar grains through epitaxial growth remains a major challenge in metal additive manufacturing (AM), as the resulting crystallographic texture can contribute to direction-dependent mechanical response, including variati
content: The formation of columnar grains through epitaxial growth remains a major challenge in metal additive manufacturing (AM), as the resulting crystallographic texture can contribute to direction-dependent mechanical response, including variations in strength and deformation behavior depending on the loading direction. In this work, we investigate the role of phase evolution pathways in disrupting epitaxial grain propagation during AM of 17 − 4 PH stainless steel (PH 17 − 4 SS). Owing to its sensitivity to cooling rate and alloy chemistry, PH 17 − 4 enables controlled tuning of phase fractions, i.e., ferrite, austenite, and martensite, under different processing conditions. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveals that variations in processing conditions produce different phase evolution behaviors that modify the crystallographic template inherited during subsequent deposition, suppressing epitaxial grain propagation. Insights gained from operando XRD are then used to fabricate bulk multilayer specimens to tailor microstructural properties such as grain size and crystallographic texture. These findings establish phase evolution as a promising strategy for grain refinement by disrupting epitaxial grain growth in metal AM.

title: Na/Fe-Modified Natural Bentonite as a Photo-Fenton-like Catalyst for Abamectin Degradation in Water and Soil
summary: Abamectin is an environmental contaminant of serious concern. In this study, a naturally occurring bentonite from the Ardabil mine was modified with Fe(II) and evaluated as a heterogeneous photo-Fenton catalyst for abamectin degradation. Ch
content: Abamectin is an environmental contaminant of serious concern. In this study, a naturally occurring bentonite from the Ardabil mine was modified with Fe(II) and evaluated as a heterogeneous photo-Fenton catalyst for abamectin degradation. Characterization (XRD, FTIR, BET, SEM, EDS) confirmed successful iron incorporation and a mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 34.92 m² g⁻¹. Operating under UV/H₂O₂, the system overcame acidic limitations, achieving optimal efficiency at natural neutral pH (pH = 7.0) with 0.03 g catalyst, 100 mg L⁻¹ abamectin, and 20 µL H₂O₂. Degradation followed pseudo-first-order kinetics (k = 0.0089 min⁻¹, R² = 0.964 at 25°C). COD removal reached 73.9%, achieving significant mineralization accompanied by improved biodegradability (BOD₅/COD 0.125 → 0.135). The catalyst remained highly stable over six consecutive cycles, with negligible iron leaching. Applicability was further examined with a commercial abamectin formulation and in soil pot experiments exposed to sunlight. These findings establish the low-cost Na/Fe-modified bentonite as a robust, recoverable catalyst for remediating persistent pesticide-contaminated environments.

title: Compositionally tuned electrospun spinel nanofibers: phase-specific redox chemistry and battery-type charge storage in CoFe₂O₄, CuCo₂O₄ and CuNi₂O₄
summary: Electrospun spinel oxides are attractive battery-type electrode materials, but comparisons among compositions are often confounded by changes in precursor chemistry, morphology and thermal treatment. Here, CoFe₂O₄, CuCo₂O₄ and CuNi₂O₄ nanof
content: Electrospun spinel oxides are attractive battery-type electrode materials, but comparisons among compositions are often confounded by changes in precursor chemistry, morphology and thermal treatment. Here, CoFe₂O₄, CuCo₂O₄ and CuNi₂O₄ nanofibers were prepared under identical PVP/DMF electrospinning, pre-oxidation and calcination conditions. Phase-specific X-ray diffraction peak groups were indexed separately against the corresponding reference cards rather than forced onto a common set of reflections. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identified Co²⁺/Co³⁺ and Fe³⁺ in CoFe₂O₄, Cu²⁺ and Co²⁺/Co³⁺ in CuCo₂O₄, and Cu²⁺ and Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ in CuNi₂O₄, together with lattice and surface oxygen species. In 1 mol L⁻¹ KOH, the electrodes delivered specific capacitances of 484, 406 and 220 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹ for CuCo₂O₄, CoFe₂O₄ and CuNi₂O₄, respectively. CoFe₂O₄ exhibited the best relative rate retention, reaching approximately 54% at 4 A g⁻¹, compared with approximately 49% for CuNi₂O₄ and 41% for CuCo₂O₄. Cyclic-voltammetry analysis showed battery-like Faradaic behavior with composition-dependent surface and diffusion contributions. A CuCo₂O₄//activated-carbon device retained 99.93% of its initial capacitance and a coulombic efficiency of 99.96% after 5000 cycles. The comparison shows that cation composition controls the balance among accessible redox centers, charge-transfer resistance and ion transport more strongly than fiber diameter alone.

title: Use of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria cultivated from mine water combination with compost for the restoration of mine area soil
summary: Northwest China hosts numerous open-pit coal mines. Mining activities have rendered pristine ecosystem vulnerable and generate large volumes of mine water, which can cause water pollution if left untreated. To address these issues, this stu
content: Northwest China hosts numerous open-pit coal mines. Mining activities have rendered pristine ecosystem vulnerable and generate large volumes of mine water, which can cause water pollution if left untreated. To address these issues, this study focused on indigenous nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (NFC) selected from local soil. It examined key factors affecting NFC cultivation, such as mine water type, mine water dilution rate, inoculation concentration, and light intensity The cultivated NFC were then combined with compost derived from the fermentation of local agricultural and livestock waste for mine soil remediation. Experimental results revealed that NFC exhibited better physiological activity when cultured using raw mine water (HL-1), Among the tested strains, NFC No. 1 (Nostoc sp. HL) was selected for its outstanding performance across multiple indicators, including pH, Fv/Fm, dry weight (DW), and chlorophyll a concentration. Additionally, a pot experiments was conducted using NFC combined with compost under six different treatments: CK (control), C (compost alone), M1 (0.1 g/m 2 NFC), M2 (1 g/m 2 NFC), CM1 (0.1 g/m 2 NFC + compost), and CM2 (1 g/m 2 NFC + compost). The results indicated that the combined application of 1g/m 2 NFC and compost (CM2) significantly promoted the growth of Elymus dahuricus (E. dahuricus), enhanced its antioxidant enzyme activity, increased its nutritional content, and elevated soil SOM, TN, and AK content. CM2 treatment also increased the abundance of beneficial bacterial phyla, such as Bacillota and Bacteroidota, while reducing the oligotrophic taxa abundance of Acidobacteriota and Gemmatimonadota. In summary, the combined use of NFC and compost as restoration agents represents a highly promising practice for the ecological restoration of open-pit coal mine soil.

title: Rod-shaped crystalline microstructures from β-cyclodextrin/hydroxyethyl cellulose hydrogen-bond networks as light-extraction templates for OLEDs
summary: Conventional optical structures for enhancing the light-extraction efficiency of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) require toxic solvents, non-recyclable synthetic resins, and high-cost, complex fabrication processes. These factors incr
content: Conventional optical structures for enhancing the light-extraction efficiency of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) require toxic solvents, non-recyclable synthetic resins, and high-cost, complex fabrication processes. These factors increase the environmental impact of these structures and hinder the development of sustainable next-generation display technologies. To address these limitations, in this study, an eco-friendly light-extraction template for OLEDs was developed, with deionized water as the sole solvent and incorporating the naturally derived oligosaccharide β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and water-soluble polymer hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC). Through chemical interactions between the β-CD and HEC, rod-shaped crystal structures with suppressed aggregation formed on the template surface. Both the crystal morphology and distribution varied with the presence or absence of HEC. Furthermore, a shift in the O–H stretching band observed in the FT-IR spectra indicated that the hydrogen-bonding and hydration environment was modified upon mixing the β-CD and HEC. The proposed template was replicated in PDMS to obtain the rod-shaped crystalline structure (RCS) w/ HEC film, which was laminated onto an OLED device through an index-matching oil layer. This device exhibited a 60% enhancement in light-extraction efficiency over the entire emission hemisphere. These results demonstrate that a light-extraction microstructure of practical performance can be obtained from a master template prepared in water alone, without organic solvents or a separate patterning step, thereby offering a viable platform for next-generation OLED displays and lighting.

title: Triacontanol enhances cytokinin-mediated in vitro shoot proliferation and biomass accumulation in two cherry rootstocks
summary: Efficient micropropagation of cherry rootstocks is frequently constrained by low shoot regeneration and limited biomass accumulation. This study evaluated the synergistic effects of the biostimulant triacontanol (TRIA) and the cytokinin 6-b
content: Efficient micropropagation of cherry rootstocks is frequently constrained by low shoot regeneration and limited biomass accumulation. This study evaluated the synergistic effects of the biostimulant triacontanol (TRIA) and the cytokinin 6-benzyladenine (BA) on in vitro shoot proliferation, biomass production, and growth behavior in two commercial cherry rootstocks, CAB-6P and Gisela 6. Shoot-tip explants were cultured on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium supplemented with varying concentrations of TRIA (2, 4, and 6 μg L−¹) and BA (0.5, 1, and 2 mg L−¹), alongside plant growth regulator (PGR)-free controls (0 μg L−1 TRIA + 0 mg L−1 BA). Growth parameters including shoot number, length, multiplication percentage, fresh weight (FW), dry weight (DW), and dry matter content (DW%) were assessed after six weeks. Significant genotype-dependent TRIA × BA interactions were observed across all evaluated traits. Supplementation with optimized TRIA–BA combinations markedly improved shoot proliferation, multiplication efficiency (100%), and biomass accumulation compared to PGR-free controls. For CAB-6P, maximum shoot proliferation (20.1–23.0 shoots/explant) peaked under intermediate-to-high BA (1 mg L−1) alone and combined with targeted TRIA concentrations (4–6 μg L−1), whereas Gisela 6 responded most strongly (16.0 shoots/explant) to lower BA combined with higher TRIA (0.5 mg L−1 BA + 6 μg L−1 TRIA). Biomass accumulation (FW and DW) improved under combined treatments: CAB-6P peaked at 6 μg L−1 TRIA + 2 mg L−1 BA, while Gisela 6 peaked at 4 μg L−1 TRIA + 1 mg L−1 BA. Across both rootstocks, increasing cytokinin levels enhanced shoot multiplication and biomass while concurrently suppressing excessive shoot elongation, which was greatest in the PGR-free control treatments (CAB-6P: 17.83 mm, Gisela 6: 20.19 mm). Further analysis confirmed strong positive associations among shoot proliferation and biomass accumulation (number, multiplication %, FW, and DW), alongside an inverse physiological relationship between intensive shoot multiplication and elongation. TRIA acts as an effective growth-promoting supplement that synergistically enhances BA-mediated shoot proliferation and biomass accumulation in a genotype-dependent manner. Optimizing TRIA–BA combinations successfully improves in vitro shoot regeneration efficiency, providing a reliable strategy for the commercial micropropagation of cherry rootstocks

title: A practical toolbox for acquisition and processing of MAS NMR spectra obtained by heteronuclear cross relaxation under dynamic nuclear polarization (SCREAM-DNP)
summary: Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) significantly enhances the sensitivity of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) through polarization transfer from unpaired electron spins to nuclear spins. Recent developments aim at achieving site-specific si
content: Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) significantly enhances the sensitivity of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) through polarization transfer from unpaired electron spins to nuclear spins. Recent developments aim at achieving site-specific signal enhancement, yet conventional approaches face challenges including paramagnetic relaxation enhancement (PRE) and the need for precise molecular positioning of paramagnetic species. Specific cross-relaxation enhancement by active motions under DNP (SCREAM-DNP) offers an alternative strategy enabling site-specificity through highly mobile functional groups. Under typical DNP conditions of 100 K, heteronuclear resonances from rapidly rotating moieties such as methyl groups appear through an indirect route via proton spin-diffusion and heteronuclear Overhauser effect in competition with direct DNP; these contributions may be separated through spectral filtering. This work provides a comprehensive overview of the entire SCREAM-DNP workflow, encompassing pulse sequence design, data acquisition and post-processing steps using Bruker TopSpin format. Furthermore, we introduce 𝚂𝙲𝚁𝙴𝙰𝙼𝙻𝙰𝙱 (v0.3.0), a Python package designed to enable reproducible, standardized, and transparent analysis of SCREAM-DNP data.

title: Targeted observations could substantially reduce aerosol radiative forcing uncertainty over China
summary: Aerosol radiative forcing remains one of the key uncertainties in climate models, limiting the accuracy of projections and weakening global action to mitigate climate risks. Previous studies combining observations with a perturbed parameter
content: Aerosol radiative forcing remains one of the key uncertainties in climate models, limiting the accuracy of projections and weakening global action to mitigate climate risks. Previous studies combining observations with a perturbed parameter ensemble of the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1) identified and constrained the key causes of uncertainty, reducing global-mean aerosol forcing uncertainty by nearly 70 %. However, some regions remain highly uncertain after constraint, particularly over densely populated and industrialized East Asia. Here, we aim to further constrain the remaining uncertainty caused by aerosol-cloud forcing, quantify the constraint potential of novel observations, and guide future measurement strategies. We map regions over mainland China that remain highly uncertain after observational constraint, identify observation combinations that share causes of uncertainty with ΔFaci and provide complementary information for constraint, then test their constraint potential using synthetic constraints. These synthetic constraints further reduce the remaining uncertainty by around 30 % over eastern coastal China and by around 50 % over central China. Our results also identify a lack of useful observations over the Tibetan Plateau in western China, providing clear priorities for future observational constraint. These results show that constraining aerosol forcing depends less on the number or spatial coverage of observations and more on making complementary collocated measurements at times and locations that directly target the key causes of model uncertainty. Our framework links diagnosis of remaining model uncertainty with observational strategy and subsequent constraint, providing actionable guidance for future aerosol observations and iterative model evaluation.

title: Medium‐Entropy Metallene Enables Sequential Hot‐Carrier Nanocatalytic Triaptosis Induction for Suppressing Tumor Growth and Metastasis
summary: Triaptosis, a newly recognized cell death modality driven by endosomal dysfunction and persistent vacuolization, holds promise for tumor therapy. However, its clinical translation has been hindered by the lack of spatiotemporally controllab
content: Triaptosis, a newly recognized cell death modality driven by endosomal dysfunction and persistent vacuolization, holds promise for tumor therapy. However, its clinical translation has been hindered by the lack of spatiotemporally controllable strategies to disrupt endosomal homeostasis. Herein, we engineer ultrathin PdCuCo medium‐entropy metallene catalysts (PCC MEMCs) as a new class of sono‐activatable catalytic biomaterials that induce triaptosis for tumor therapy. Upon ultrasound irradiation, lattice oscillations in PCC MEMCs generate non‐equilibrium hot carriers that execute two synergistic catalytic functions. These high‐energy hot carriers directly drive interfacial electron transfer with H 2 O and O 2 to produce hydroxyl radicals and superoxide anions, with sufficiently energetic carriers further converting triplet oxygen to singlet oxygen. Simultaneously, these hot carriers accelerate the intrinsic enzyocatalytic reactions by lowering surface adsorption barriers and enhancing charge transfer. This sequential nanocatalysis triggers a massive oxidative burst and substantial depletion of antioxidants, leading to VPS34 oxidation, PI(3)P depletion, and disruption of early endosomal processing. Consequently, persistent vacuolization and membrane collapse induce triaptosis, effectively suppressing tumor growth and metastasis. Collectively, this work establishes a sono‑activatable hot‑carrier sequential nanocatalytic paradigm, offers a distinct nanotherapeutic strategy against tumors via triaptosis induction, and broadens the biomedical scope of medium‐entropy metallenes toward sonocatalytic therapy.

title: Controlling Factors of Ultra-Deep Tight Sandstone Reservoirs in the Lower Cretaceous Bashijiqike Formation, Kuqa Depression, Western China
summary: The mechanisms of pore preservation and the compaction processes of ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs have been extensively studied. Specifically, this study examines how sedimentary, diagenetic, tectonic, evaporite, overpressure, and ga
content: The mechanisms of pore preservation and the compaction processes of ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs have been extensively studied. Specifically, this study examines how sedimentary, diagenetic, tectonic, evaporite, overpressure, and gas-charging processes interact to control reservoir quality and develops an integrated genetic model for high-quality ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs. To address this gap, this study takes the ultradeep tight sandstone of the Bashijiqike Formation (buried at depths exceeding 8000 m) in the Kelasu structural belt of the Kuqa Depression, Western China, as a case study. A multidata set analysis was conducted by integrating petrophysical property measurements, thin-section observations, core descriptions, and individual-well productivity data. By comparing wells under different geological conditions, this study identifies the controlling factors and formation mechanisms responsible for the development of ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs. The results show that sedimentary processes serve as the primary control on reservoir quality: conglomerate-rich sediments with high mud content inhibit primary porosity development, whereas well-sorted sandstones in the central part of underwater distributary channels preserve grain-supported fabrics, forming the initial material basis for high-quality reservoirs. Diagenetic processes further modify these primary differences: an alternating alkaline-to-acidic diagenetic environment first enhances compaction resistance through early carbonate cementation and then generates secondary porosity through late-stage dissolution, thereby directly controlling the formation of high-quality ultradeep tight sandstones. External factors provide additional modifications: thick overlying evaporite layers not only seal overpressure but also retard thermal evolution through their high thermal conductivity, delaying late-stage cementation, while alkaline fluids released during gypsum metamorphic reactions help maintain an alkaline diagenetic state over an extended period. Consequently, the rapid and high-saturation natural gas charging induces reservoir overpressure, which effectively lowers the porosity threshold for effective reservoir development.

title: An indicator-free electrochemical magnetoresistance nano aptamer-biosensor for the ultra-sensitive determination of B-Raf proto-oncogene
summary: Introduction To address the long assay time and high cost associated with BRAF determination, a type of indicator-free electrochemical magnetoresistance nano aptamer-biosensor (ECMRNABS) was designed and constructed for the ultra-sensitive
content: Introduction To address the long assay time and high cost associated with BRAF determination, a type of indicator-free electrochemical magnetoresistance nano aptamer-biosensor (ECMRNABS) was designed and constructed for the ultra-sensitive determination of BRAF. Methods Initially, α-Fe 2 O 3 /Fe 3 O 4 magnetic heterogeneous nanorods were prepared via hydrothermal combined with the calcination–reduction procedure and coated with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) to yield α-Fe 2 O 3 /Fe 3 O 4 @Au magnetic nanocomposites. Subsequently, aptamer (Apt) was immobilized on α-Fe 2 O 3 /Fe 3 O 4 @Au, and bovine serum albumin (BSA) was employed to block non-specific binding sites to form α-Fe 2 O 3 /Fe 3 O 4 @Au-Apt/BSA ECMRAS for the determination of BRAF, and the analytical performances were evaluated by differential pulse voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry. Results and Discussion The ECMRNABSs revealed excellent sensitivity of 62.94 µA/(pMcm 2) and a linear relationship (R 2 = 0.993), a large linear range (10 pM–1 μM), a lower LOD (0.44 pM), reliable reproducibility (RSD = 1.04%), receivable stability (RSD of 0.73% in 10 days), credible selectivity, and the determination capacity of the spiked human serum samples (recoveries of 94.6%–106.6% with RSD ≤ 2.6%), supporting the preliminary feasibility of the ECMRNABSs for BRAF determination in serum samples.

title: MTDDAPT: Multi-Modal Text Distribution-Aware Deep Adversarial Prompt Tuning for Robust Vision-Language Representation Learning
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs), such as CLIP, have achieved competitive performance in open-vocabulary visual recognition, but they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples. This vulnerability may affect the reliability of AI-based visual p
content: Vision-language models (VLMs), such as CLIP, have achieved competitive performance in open-vocabulary visual recognition, but they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples. This vulnerability may affect the reliability of AI-based visual perception models when image inputs are perturbed. Existing robustness-oriented adaptation methods mainly optimize model weights or prompts, while the geometry of class-level textual representations remains underexplored during adversarial adaptation. In this work, we investigate clean accuracy and adversarial robustness of VLMs from the perspective of multi-modal text distribution optimization. We propose Multi-modal Text Distribution-Aware Deep Adversarial Prompt Tuning (MTDDAPT), which builds on multi-modal adversarial prompt coupling with frozen encoders and further introduces explicit distribution-aware regularization over class-level textual embeddings. Specifically, MTDDAPT uses a Gaussian-kernel-based inter-dispersion objective to enlarge inter-class separation in the normalized text embedding space, while PGD-based adversarial training optimizes deep textual prompts and text-to-visual projection mappings, thereby adapting the projected visual prompts. Across three visual recognition datasets, MTDDAPT consistently outperforms hand-crafted prompts, achieving average improvements of 19.51 and 11.44 percentage points in clean accuracy and robust accuracy, respectively. In the 16-shot setting, MTDDAPT further improves clean accuracy by 34.71 percentage points over hand-crafted prompts and achieves an average robust accuracy improvement of 22.32 percentage points across PGD, TPGD, and CW attacks. These results suggest that explicit text distribution-aware regularization can complement multi-modal prompt coupling and improve robust vision-language representation learning under adversarial image perturbations.

title: Flexible Hybrid Technique for a Fully Fuzzy Mixed Integer Programming: Case Study for a Distribution Supply Chain
summary: Many researchers have studied uncertainty models using fuzzy set tools and techniques. One approach in fuzzy mathematical optimization is full fuzzy linear programming, in which all parameters, including the continuous decision variables, a
content: Many researchers have studied uncertainty models using fuzzy set tools and techniques. One approach in fuzzy mathematical optimization is full fuzzy linear programming, in which all parameters, including the continuous decision variables, are fuzzy. Many real-world problems involve mathematical models that include integer variables, specifically binary variables, as well as continuous fuzzy variables. Such models, called fuzzy mixed-integer programming models, have not been comprehensively studied so far.
