In this research, a hybrid method is developed for a fully fuzzy mixed-integer programming model with binary variables. The main part of this model includes the objective function and constraints. The objective function expressed as a trapezoidal fuzzy number, is converted into a crisp multi-objective form. For the constraints, we first convert the left- and right-hand side values into intervals using the well-known fuzzy alpha-cut technique. Then, we convert it into crisp form by defining a value called the degree of constraint satisfaction, which ranges from zero to one. To investigate this problem operationally, we consider a three-level supply chain with factories, warehouses, and retailers, and we implement a mixed model to design the supply chain. The solutions proposed in this research enable the decision-maker to select an optimal solution from a range of values-rather than being limited to a single solution based on the latest information regarding current uncertain conditions. The results from solving the aforementioned problem indicate the hybrid method’s appropriate performance, and the sensitivity analysis on the problem’s key parameters also confirms its reliability.

title: Epistemic Decolonisation in IPE: A Pedagogical Intervention and the Case for a Khaldun–Yunus Framework
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: This study examines the pedagogical effects of integrating Ibn Khaldun’s Muqaddimah into an undergraduate International Political Economy (IPE) curriculum as part of a broader effort towards epistemic decolonisation. A convergent mixed-meth
content: This study examines the pedagogical effects of integrating Ibn Khaldun’s Muqaddimah into an undergraduate International Political Economy (IPE) curriculum as part of a broader effort towards epistemic decolonisation. A convergent mixed-methods design combined end-of-semester survey data (N = 36) with thematic analysis of open-ended responses at a Malaysian university. All students reported some shift in their understanding of the origins of economic thought, and most questioned its exclusively Western foundations, and qualitative results suggest emerging awareness of knowledge hierarchies and receptivity towards Islamic ethical principles across religious backgrounds. Situating these findings within the history of IPE, the paper advances a Khaldun–Yunus framework, arguing that Ibn Khaldun’s concepts of ʿumran (civilisational flourishing) and taʿawun (mutual cooperation) provide the moral and macro-institutional grounding that Muhammad Yunus’s enterprise-based approach to poverty lacks, and specifying the conditions under which that approach is consistent with Khaldunian principles in light of left-structuralist critiques of microfinance. Because the instrument relied on post-only self-report, the findings indicate perceived rather than measured change; a pre-test/post-test design is set out for subsequent iterations.

title: Beyond SAF Certification: Reconciling ISCC CORSIA and ISCC EU through Life-Cycle Carbon Accounting, Feedstock Eligibility and Double-Counting Prevention in International Aviation
source: Journal of Environmental Sustainability and Renewable Systems
summary: The international expansion of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) has exposed a critical distinction between sustainability certification, quantified life-cycle greenhouse gas reductions, and legal recognition of those reductions. This qualita
content: The international expansion of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) has exposed a critical distinction between sustainability certification, quantified life-cycle greenhouse gas reductions, and legal recognition of those reductions. This qualitative literature review examines the relationship between ISCC CORSIA and ISCC EU, emphasizing their different regulatory purposes, life cycle assessment methods, feedstock criteria, and controls against duplicate environmental claims. Drawing on 64 journal articles published during 2020-2026 and authoritative ICAO and European Union documents, the review synthesizes six themes: certification non-equivalence, carbon-intensity methodology, feedstock eligibility, chain-of-custody integrity, market implications, and institutional interoperability. The analysis identifies a recurrent governance error: treating possession of a recognized certificate as sufficient proof that the same emissions benefit can be claimed under multiple compliance or voluntary frameworks. It proposes a three-gate model that separates qualified physical fuel, regime-specific life-cycle calculation, and exclusive claim entitlement. Particular attention is given to the differentiated legal treatment of palm-derived materials, including palm fatty acid distillate, palm oil mill effluent, and empty palm fruit bunches. A linked physical-batch and claims-ledger architecture, supplemented by minimum evidence datasets and transparent regulatory mapping, is advanced as a practical alternative to automatic certificate equivalence. The review concludes that cross-border SAF recognition depends on auditable data exchange, explicit jurisdiction specific eligibility decisions, and prevention of double issuance, double use, and double claiming, rather than universal acceptance of any one sustainability certificate.

title: Beyond Double Charging: Reconciling CORSIA and the EU Emissions Trading System through Climate Policy Coherence, Environmental Integrity and Equitable Aviation Governance
source: Journal of Environmental Sustainability and Renewable Systems
summary: The evolving relationship between the International Civil Aviation Organization’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) poses a complex challenge
content: The evolving relationship between the International Civil Aviation Organization’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) poses a complex challenge for climate governance. This article uses a critical qualitative literature review of peer-reviewed research published from 2020 through 2026, interpreted alongside authoritative ICAO and European Union materials. It distinguishes overlapping financial obligations from administrative duplication, carbon-credit double claiming, and legitimate concurrent regulation. The thematic synthesis finds that a common global framework improves predictability but does not independently guarantee emissions additionality, while regional cap-and-trade can strengthen carbon-price incentives yet potentially alter competition among air routes and transit hubs. The European Commission’s July 2026 aviation proposal, envisaging expanded geographical application from 2029 if adopted, sharpens these tensions. The article develops an operator–route–year diagnostic framework, assesses carbon-market integrity and distributional effects, and proposes a five-part compatibility architecture covering legal-scope mapping, auditable cost deductions, registry safeguards, competition and equity review, and recurrent ICAO–EU dialogue. For Indonesia and other international aviation economies, the preferred approach combines support for CORSIA-centered multilateral coordination with evidence based engagement on environmental ambition, transparent economic burdens, and direct emissions-reduction investment. The conclusions are interpretive and policy-oriented, not estimates of the future proposal’s realized impacts.

title: Properties of chromium and manganese in Tycho's supernova remnant with XRISM/Resolve
summary: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants (SNRs) gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especiall
content: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants (SNRs) gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. We analyzed /Resolve high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy observations of five regions of Tychos's supernova remnant, which were performed during the performance-verification phase and the AO1 phase. Gaussian line modeling was first used to determine the spatial distribution and intensity of Cr and Mn Kα lines. We then modeled the emission of the Cr, Mn and Fe plasma in each pointing with two nonequilibrium ionization shock models to reproduce both the front- and rear-emitting sides of the shocked ejecta shell. Mass ratios of Cr/Fe, Mn/Fe, and Mn/Cr are compared with expectations from different Type Ia supernova models from 1D and 3D numerical simulations. XRISM The unprecedented spectral resolution of /Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even on small scales, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe-bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim; some are observed in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe, and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 M_⊙ sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. XRISM Overall, the best agreement is found for models with metallicities too high to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronization such as carbon simmering for a Chandrasekhar-mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar-mass, double-detonation models with a white-dwarf mass lower than 1M_⊙ are suggested.

title: Social business and the three zeros: applying ethical and triple bottom line principles to create prosperity, opportunity and a sustainable planet
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how social businesses (SBs) ethically operationalize stakeholder relationships and contribute to the broader aspirations of Zero Poverty, Zero Unemployment and Zero Net Carbon Emissions, while generating i
content: Purpose This study aims to examine how social businesses (SBs) ethically operationalize stakeholder relationships and contribute to the broader aspirations of Zero Poverty, Zero Unemployment and Zero Net Carbon Emissions, while generating interconnected social, economic and environmental value relevant to SDGs 1, 7, 8 and 13. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Normative Stakeholder Theory (NST) and the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) as complementary analytical perspectives, this study adopts a qualitative comparative multiple-case design involving Grameen Bank (GB), Grameen Shakti (GS) and Grameen Telecom Trust (GTT) in Bangladesh. Data comprise 56 semi-structured interviews, eight field observations and six organizational documents. The analysis examines how normative stakeholder responsibilities are translated into organizational practices and how these practices generate multidimensional value. Findings The cross-case analysis proposes ethical stakeholder operationalization as an organizational mechanism linking normative stakeholder responsibility with SB practices and multidimensional value creation. Stakeholder recognition, voice, participation, empowerment, fairness, accountability, co-creation and management of competing interests are reflected in practices involving financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, capability development, employment opportunities, renewable energy and environmental responsibility. TBL provides an analytical lens for examining social, economic and environmental value, while the Three-Zero framework (TZF) provides broader societal aspirations rather than organizational performance targets. Research limitations/implications The qualitative multiple-case design and focus on three Grameen initiatives in Bangladesh limit transferability to other institutional, sectoral and geographical contexts. This study develops an empirically grounded analytical pathway rather than establishing universal causal effects. Future research should examine the proposed mechanism across different countries, sectors, organizational forms and institutional settings. Practical implications The framework can serve as a preliminary diagnostic aid for SB managers and development organizations seeking to assess whether stakeholder responsibilities are embedded in organizational practices, while identifying stakeholder tensions, implementation constraints and multidimensional value creation. Social implications The findings of this study suggest that ethically grounded SB practices can provide organizational pathways toward poverty reduction, employment opportunities and environmental sustainability. This study highlights the potential contribution of stakeholder-inclusive SB to sustainable development while distinguishing organizational contributions from broader societal outcomes. Originality/value This study specifies ethical stakeholder operationalization as a linking mechanism among established perspectives rather than simply combining them. NST

title: An analysis of renewable energy cost sharing in sustainable supply chains under uncertain conditions
summary: Greenhouse gas is one of the major concerns for policymakers and academicians in the modern era. Renewable energy helps to reduce emissions if the industry supply chain is used optimally. Further, there is little understanding of how renewa
content: Greenhouse gas is one of the major concerns for policymakers and academicians in the modern era. Renewable energy helps to reduce emissions if the industry supply chain is used optimally. Further, there is little understanding of how renewable energy implementation cost and stock dependence simultaneously impact supply chain (SC) profit. Thus, we propose a duopoly sustainable supply chain considering renewable implementation and stock-dependence demand under uncertain environments. A mathematical model is developed for a sustainable supply chain under three scenarios: (i) Renewable energy effort by manufacturer and cost-shared by the retailer (Model M) (ii) Renewable energy effort by retailer and cost-shared by the manufacturer (Model R), and (iii) Renewable energy effort by both retailer and manufacturer and cost-shared by the manufacturer and retailer (Model C). Nash equilibrium was used to find optimal strategies for players under different integrated channels. The result finds that Model M is comparatively better than the other two models as cost-sharing increases. The result additionally establishes that the total profit decreases as the cost of sharing increases in Model C and Model R, whereas it increases in Model M.

title: Carbon home bias
summary: We undertake a global analysis of institutional investor portfolios and find widespread underweighting of companies with higher carbon emissions, both in levels and intensities. This underweighting is largely driven by foreign companies wit
content: We undertake a global analysis of institutional investor portfolios and find widespread underweighting of companies with higher carbon emissions, both in levels and intensities. This underweighting is largely driven by foreign companies with high carbon emissions, both at the intensive (tilting) and extensive (exclusion) margins. Domestic firms with high emissions are overweighted but by a smaller magnitude. These results reveal a bias for domestic companies with high carbon emissions. The carbon home bias is stronger in settings where institutions have tighter business connections, in countries with weaker social norms regarding climate crisis, and where the political environment is more polarized.

title: Inventory Productivity and Carbon Emissions in Retailing
summary: Problem definition: Higher inventory productivity is thought to be associated with lower carbon emissions and waste. We test this conventional wisdom using granular emissions data from CDP. Methodology/results: Pairing emissions data with f
content: Problem definition: Higher inventory productivity is thought to be associated with lower carbon emissions and waste. We test this conventional wisdom using granular emissions data from CDP. Methodology/results: Pairing emissions data with firms’ financials, we show that most of the emission reduction benefits emerge organically with the scale of operations. Using causal inference techniques, we show that, absent the scale, an external shock to inventory productivity results in higher emission intensity in aggregate across scopes, in Scope 3, and its category of purchased goods and services. The effect on Scope 2 emissions is negative and null in Scope 1. The effect is concentrated in the non-essential retail segments, excluding food and beverage, and health and personal care retailers. Managerial implications: All else kept equal, a higher inventory productivity trades off associated profitability benefits with upstream carbon emissions, particularly in the Scope 3 category of purchased goods and services, underscoring the need for holistic implementation of lean practices. We explore the feasibility of carbon pricing as a mechanism to shift the retailers’ calculus to the dual objective of profit maximization and minimization of environmental impact.

title: Soil re-engineering in Western Australia, Part II: benchmarking crop performance on an Arenosol and a Kurosol
summary: Context Soil constraints, including subsoil acidity, compaction and low fertility, limit crop productivity and water-use efficiency (WUE) in Western Australia (WA) and around the world. Conventional shallow soil amelioration (SSA), generall
content: Context Soil constraints, including subsoil acidity, compaction and low fertility, limit crop productivity and water-use efficiency (WUE) in Western Australia (WA) and around the world. Conventional shallow soil amelioration (SSA), generally targeting the upper 10–30 cm of the soil profile, often provides modest or short-lived benefits. Soil profile re-engineering (SPR), involving deep mixing with amendments to 80-cm depth, may address multiple constraints, but the longevity of its productivity benefits and economic outcomes remain poorly understood. Aim This study assessed the persistence of soil improvements and crop responses to SPR across four rain-fed cropping seasons and at two sites. Methods Eight treatments, including an untreated control, shallow surface amendments and four re-engineering approaches, were evaluated in a partially randomised block design on two contrasting soils: an Arenosol and a Kurosol in the central grainbelt of WA. Measurements included soil physicochemical properties, root development, grain yield, WUE and nitrogen (N) and potassium (K) uptake. Key results All SPR treatments substantially reduced soil strength and increased soil pHCa and cation exchange capacity (CEC). Treatments incorporating clay were associated with greater volumetric water content, while those incorporating compost increased soil organic carbon (SOC). These improvements were observed across the amended soil profile. The SPR treatments substantially increased grain yield across crops and seasons, with the largest response for canola at Bolgart in 2022, where yield increased from approximately 0.50 t ha−1 in the control to 2.64 t ha−1 under SPR (+432%). Calculated WUE showed corresponding treatment responses, with the largest absolute increase of 9.8 kg mm−1 for barley at Bolgart in 2024, from approximately 3.5 kg mm−1 in the control to 13.3 kg mm−1 under SPR. The SSA treatments generally produced smaller or no yield gains compared to the control. The N and K uptake increased proportionally with yield. Regression tree analysis identified CEC, soil strength and SOC as important predictors of yield response across both soils, with clay content also contributing for the Arenosol and pHCa for the Kurosol. The models explained up to 80.4% of the variation in grain yield. Benefits from SPR persisted for at least four cropping seasons and are expected to continue for several years. Conclusions and implications Although soil profile re-engineering may not be economically scalable at present, it provides a valuable benchmark for designing targeted, cost-effective amelioration strategies to enhance the resilience and productivity of rainfed cropping systems in semi-arid environments in WA.

title: Drivers of reduced permafrost cooling efficacy of equatorial stratospheric aerosol injection in the Eastern Arctic compared to a moderate emission pathway
summary: The Arctic is warming about four times faster than the global average, with permafrost thaw representing a potential global climate tipping element. Given the insufficient rate of carbon emission reductions, stratospheric aerosol injection
content: The Arctic is warming about four times faster than the global average, with permafrost thaw representing a potential global climate tipping element. Given the insufficient rate of carbon emission reductions, stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) has emerged as a strategy to abate climate warming. However, its effects on permafrost thaw drivers remain uncertain. The G6sulfur and G6solar experiments, part of the Geoengineering Model Intercomparison Project (GeoMIP6), aim to offset the warming in the high-emission scenario (ssp585) to achieve global-mean near-surface air temperatures comparable to those in the moderate-emission scenario (ssp245), through the injection of stratospheric aerosols near the equator (G6sulfur) or a reduction in top-of-atmosphere solar irradiance (G6solar), respectively. Analyzing both experiments, we find that G6sulfur alters atmospheric circulation, modifying winds, cloud properties, and the North Atlantic Oscillation, which affect temperature patterns and longwave radiation. These changes shift the relative importance of mechanisms driving summer permafrost thaw, resulting in a robust east–west dipole in thaw depth (+0.769 m, 6/6 models): increased thaw in the Eastern Hemisphere (+0.491 m) and a significant but less model-consistent reduction in thaw in the Western Hemisphere (−0.278 m), compared to the ssp245 scenario targeted by the intervention. While both G6sulfur and G6solar slow permafrost decline by 2080–2099 relative to ssp585 (+4.61 × 10 6 and +5.37 × 10 6 km 2 respectively), neither preserves as much permafrost area as ssp245 (−1.08 × 10 6 km 2 for G6sulfur and −0.32 × 10 6 km 2 for G6solar). By altering the drivers of permafrost dynamics, G6sulfur creates spatial variations in thaw patterns, resulting in an overall reduction in permafrost area compared to ssp245. Our findings underscore the need to better understand and optimize SAI deployment to avoid unintended regional impacts.

title: Measuring ESG risk in supply networks
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) rating is a way for investors to prioritize investments in companies with good corporate behavior. However, ESG ratings are vulnerable to manipulation in a number of ways. In this paper we study h
content: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) rating is a way for investors to prioritize investments in companies with good corporate behavior. However, ESG ratings are vulnerable to manipulation in a number of ways. In this paper we study how trade with badly rated companies can affect a target company’s own rating. To do this, we introduce a scoring framework to account for the effect of bad actors deep in the supply chain. This scoring framework is flexible enough to reflect different rater’s opinions and preferences for ESG assessment. These scores allow updating of the target’s ESG rating, identification of influential neighbors, and assessment of vulnerability of the target to bad behavior in their supply network. We study these metrics on synthetic ESG interaction networks, a real inter-company network and the international trade network.

title: Can we teach generative artificial intelligence the design language of engineered living materials?
summary: Engineered living materials (ELMs) are rapidly expanding as a new family of materials. Here, an ontology and a useful codification scheme for describing all kinds of ELMs are presented, and their different components are systematically orga
content: Engineered living materials (ELMs) are rapidly expanding as a new family of materials. Here, an ontology and a useful codification scheme for describing all kinds of ELMs are presented, and their different components are systematically organized, classified, codified, and explained. The methodical application of the ontology to a set of 100 relevant examples of materials helps to demonstrate its utility and adaptability as a comprehensive classification tool. Furthermore, the usability of the codification by generative artificial intelligence is explored and validated, checking that both natural language and the codification are understandable for contextualizing and describing ELMs. AI adequately classifies and codifies the materials, which highlights the synergy between generative AI tools and the design of ELMs. This perspective is expected to provide a universal language to facilitate communication and discoveries in the field.

title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity toler
content: Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH > 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

title: How Elite Communication Shapes the Emerging Politics of AI Regulation
summary: Artificial intelligence is often treated as a legal or technical object of regulation. Yet whether meaningful regulation emerges will also depend on politics: how AI enters mass politics, which risks become salient to voters, and which elit
content: Artificial intelligence is often treated as a legal or technical object of regulation. Yet whether meaningful regulation emerges will also depend on politics: how AI enters mass politics, which risks become salient to voters, and which elites are trusted to define the need for action before the issue hardens into a polarized partisan conflict. This article examines those early dynamics through a preregistered survey experiment with a behavioral component. We expose US respondents to competing media frames about AI’s risks and benefits, which are attributed to different elite sources. The findings show that the early politics of AI regulation is not organized around a simple pro- versus anti-regulation divide. Instead, it turns on the institutional form regulation takes, the uneven political legibility of different AI harms, and partisan differences in trusted messengers. Broad support for oversight coexists with sharper disagreement over whether government should lead, and elite cues matter differently across partisan groups. These patterns suggest that AI regulation remains politically open rather than fully sorted and that its future trajectory may depend on which harms, institutions, and messengers come to organize public debate.

title: Particulate Nitrate Photolysis Alters the Atmospheric Chemistry Response to Marine Cloud Brightening Sea Salt Aerosol Emissions
summary: Marine cloud brightening (MCB) aims to inject sea salt aerosols (SSA) into the marine boundary layer to increase cloud reflectivity. Limited work has explored how SSA emissions for MCB could impact tropospheric chemistry, and updates to our
content: Marine cloud brightening (MCB) aims to inject sea salt aerosols (SSA) into the marine boundary layer to increase cloud reflectivity. Limited work has explored how SSA emissions for MCB could impact tropospheric chemistry, and updates to our understanding of MCB and atmospheric chemistry suggest the need for further investigation. Using the 3‐D global atmospheric chemistry model GEOS‐Chem, we explore how a range of SSA emissions scenarios for MCB influence concentrations of tropospheric reactive halogens (Br y, Cl y, and I y) and oxidants (ozone, OH, and NO x), and methane lifetime. Contrary to previous studies, we show enhanced SSA for MCB increases tropospheric oxidant concentrations and shortens methane lifetime (≤15%). Sensitivity simulations demonstrate that increased tropospheric oxidant concentrations and decreased methane lifetime is driven by the treatment of particulate nitrate photolysis. However, the particulate nitrate photolysis mechanism remains poorly constrained, highlighting an important source of uncertainty in evaluating the atmospheric chemistry impacts of MCB.

title: Indolo[3,2,1- jk]carbazole-based narrowband multi-resonance polycyclic organic systems for high-performance OLEDs
summary: ]carbazole (ICz)-based systems offer a compelling alternative by leveraging intrinsic carbon-nitrogen electronegativity differences to induce MR-features, eliminating the need for B-incorporation for narrow emission. Despite their promise,
content: ]carbazole (ICz)-based systems offer a compelling alternative by leveraging intrinsic carbon-nitrogen electronegativity differences to induce MR-features, eliminating the need for B-incorporation for narrow emission. Despite their promise, ICz-based MR-emitters face key limitations, including inefficient triplet exciton utilization, poor spin-orbit coupling, restricted emission beyond the blue region (>450 nm), aggregation-induced quenching, low EQE and suboptimal device stability. These challenges are closely tied to the molecular architecture of N-PAHs, such as π-conjugation, N-atom positioning and number, and core/peripheral modifications. Thus, understanding the molecular design and structure-function relationships is essential to develop efficient ICz-MR emitters. This review consolidates recent progress in ICz-based MR-emitters, emphasizing strategies to mitigate the above said challenges. By correlating molecular structure with photophysical behavior and device performance, it provides critical insights into overcoming current bottlenecks. The discussion concludes with forward-looking perspectives aimed at developing scalable, high-performance OLED technologies based on this emerging class of emitters.

title: Local leakage effects of establishing protected areas in multi-use forests
summary: Strengthening protection of multi-use lands used for forestry production is a central pillar for achieving global area-based conservation targets. However, there are concerns that this can lead to ‘leakage’ effects or the displacement of re
content: Strengthening protection of multi-use lands used for forestry production is a central pillar for achieving global area-based conservation targets. However, there are concerns that this can lead to ‘leakage’ effects or the displacement of resource extraction activities to unprotected lands, which can undermine biodiversity goals. To assess this risk, we applied a causal inference framework to New South Wales, Australia, which has a long-running program of converting government-owned multi-use land into protected areas. We estimated the historical leakage effects arising from displaced harvesting activities and isolated them from other drivers of forest clearing. Our results show that these leakage effects were small when averaged across the years and rarely exceeded the amount of clearing that the new protected area helped avoid. Leakage effects were statistically significant and increased clearing in nearby areas in the early years of the program (2001), when large amounts of forests were added to the national parks estate each year. However, these estimated effects were much smaller in later years (2006–2011) when fewer protected areas were created annually. Overall, our findings suggest that despite the potential for conservation to shift activities and cause local leakage, strengthening protection on multi-use land still delivered net-positive conservation outcomes. Our findings highlight that while strengthening protection on multi-use lands can deliver conservation outcomes, there is a strong need for similar programmes to be accompanied by monitoring and evaluation that includes estimates of local leakage effects.

title: Emotional framing and visual image in carbon pricing persuasion: the mediating role of message elaboration
source: Journal of responsible production and consumption.
summary: Purpose Drawing on the emotions-as-frames model (EFM), this study aims to examine the interaction between emotional framing and visual imagery in carbon pricing persuasion, focusing on the mediating role of message elaboration. Design/metho
content: Purpose Drawing on the emotions-as-frames model (EFM), this study aims to examine the interaction between emotional framing and visual imagery in carbon pricing persuasion, focusing on the mediating role of message elaboration. Design/methodology/approach This study used a 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design (emotion: hope vs fear; visual image: present vs absent) with a sample of 300 participants. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to test for main and interaction effects while controlling for climate change knowledge. The PROCESS macro was used to test for mediation. Findings The results indicated that fear framing was more persuasive than hope framing for behavioral intentions. The presence of a visual image in a fear-framed message showed a significant main effect on attitudes toward the climate change message. Furthermore, significant interaction was found between hope-framed messaging and visual imagery for attitudes toward the climate change message. Message elaboration, through evaluative processing, mediated the relationship between the emotional frames and the outcome variables. These effects remained robust after controlling for climate change knowledge. Practical implications This study offers important contributions and provides a messaging framework for policy practitioners and communication specialists, suggesting that emphasizing risks through fear-framed messages paired with relevant visuals is most effective for driving behavioral intentions for carbon pricing. Originality/value This study advances the EFM by examining the interaction between emotion and a visual image, while accounting for the mediating role of message elaboration and the stability of these effects across varying levels of climate change knowledge.

title: The effects of pasture species richness and functional group proportions on in vitro ruminal fermentation and methane emissions
summary: Context Introducing multispecies pastures has the potential to reduce enteric methane emissions and improve ruminant production compared with offering monocultures in temperate livestock grazing systems. Aims This study evaluated the effect
content: Context Introducing multispecies pastures has the potential to reduce enteric methane emissions and improve ruminant production compared with offering monocultures in temperate livestock grazing systems. Aims This study evaluated the effect of increasing species richness and functional group proportions in multispecies samples on methane and rumen fermentation parameters by using both ANKOM and rumen simulation technique (RUSITEC). Methods and Results The in vitro batch culture (ANKOM system) was used to evaluate the effect of increasing species richness (3, 5 and 7 species) and varying functional group proportionality (ratios of grass:legume:herb; dry matter (% DM): even (33:33:33) vs grass heavy (66:17:17) vs legume heavy (17:66:17) vs herb heavy (17:17:66) in a 3 × 4 factorial design. These mixtures were compared with a control monoculture perennial ryegrass (PRG) for methane emissions and fermentation parameters. The herb heavy mixture reduced methane by 11% as a proportion of total gas production, without affecting total volatile fatty acids yield while reducing ammonia nitrogen concentration compared with PRG. The herb heavy mixture was subsequently evaluated in the RUSITEC over 21 days to determine the effect of increasing species richness within the herb component (66% DM of the mixture), while other pasture species (grass and legumes) remained constant (4, 5 and 6 species in total). The four species mixture with only one herb lowered methane as a proportion of total gas production by 17% and also lowered total volatile fatty acid yield and ammonia nitrogen concentration compared with PRG. Conclusion The anti-methanogenic potential of these multispecies samples was driven by the higher inclusion rate of certain herbs. Including multiple species of varying mitigating potential had a diluting effect rather than a synergistic effect on methane reduction in both ANKOM and RUSITEC systems. However, increasing species richness exhibited synergistic effects on total volatile fatty acid production, indicating potential fermentation benefits. Implications Herb heavy multispecies samples showed promising in vitro methane reduction compared with PRG. However, combining multiple herbs had no synergistic effect for methane reduction over burnet (Sanguisorba minor Scop.) alone. Further in vivo validation is required prior to application in temperate dairy grazing systems.

title: A policy readiness evaluation framework for circular timber reuse: reframing timber construction
summary: Purpose This paper develops and demonstrates the framework for circular timber construction (FCTC) to assess how well Australian policy settings support timber deconstruction and reuse. It addresses the gap between broad circular-economy co
content: Purpose This paper develops and demonstrates the framework for circular timber construction (FCTC) to assess how well Australian policy settings support timber deconstruction and reuse. It addresses the gap between broad circular-economy commitments and the specific regulatory, economic, technical and market conditions needed to make reclaimed timber reuse practical in residential construction. Design/methodology/approach This original framework-development study combines systematic literature and policy review methods. Bibliometric mapping, thematic coding, comparative policy analysis and cognitive mapping were used to derive a 34-domain framework. Five experts then assessed each domain against centrality, clarity, coverage, operationalisability and applicability to the Australian policy context using a rapid modified Delphi-informed expert validation process. The FCTC was subsequently demonstrated through an illustrative documentary scoring exercise applied to selected Australian policies. Findings The reviewed Australian instruments address circular economy, waste, procurement and timber-related functions unevenly. In the illustrative scoring matrix, monitoring, policy review and procurement appear across the largest numbers of documents, while grading and defect-acceptance provisions are concentrated in a specialised timber standard. The assessment identifies uneven documentary coverage of the framework domains; it does not establish policy effectiveness or provide a comprehensive national readiness assessment. Research limitations/implications The study relies on published academic and grey literature, so emerging local initiatives or unpublished policy practices may not be fully captured. The scoring exercise is illustrative, not a validated national audit. Future research should extend validation through inter-rater calibration, sensitivity analysis, pilot use by policy and industry users and broader assessment across federal, state, territory and local policy settings. Practical implications The FCTC provides policymakers, regulators, industry bodies and practitioners with a structured tool for identifying gaps in circular timber policy. It can support benchmarking, guide code and deconstruction-process reforms, and identify practical actions such as reclaimed timber grading pathways, pre-deconstruction audits, procurement pilots and regional recovery hubs. Originality/value The paper contributes a timber-specific policy-readiness framework that extends beyond general circular construction assessment. By integrating regulatory recognition, reuse standards, incentives, traceability, deconstruction planning and market enablement, it frames timber circularity as a policy-coordination challenge rather than only a technical or recovery issue.

title: Household Composting in the Urban Environment: Experiences and Challenges of a Community
summary: The increasing generation of urban solid waste poses a major environmental challenge, as conventional management methods such as sanitary landfilling negatively impact the environment. Within this context, household composting emerges as an
content: The increasing generation of urban solid waste poses a major environmental challenge, as conventional management methods such as sanitary landfilling negatively impact the environment. Within this context, household composting emerges as an effective and sustainable solution for managing organic waste. This study investigates the extent to which citizens’ stated intention to participate in a composting program, previously recorded, was actually implemented. The research was based on a quantitative methodology using a structured questionnaire distributed to participants of the initial phase. A pilot test was carried out, and the data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and the Chi-square test. The results indicated that only about one-third of those who had initially expressed intention ultimately implemented composting. The participants in this study encountered several practical challenges in the process of composting, with the most frequently reported issues being the presence of insects or animals and the emergence of unpleasant odors. Nevertheless, the majority expressed willingness to continue the practice, reflecting an overall positive perception of composting. Statistically significant correlations were found only with gender and age, while other demographic characteristics did not show notable influence. These findings can contribute to the design of targeted policies that promote both the intention and the practice of household composting.

title: Renewable Energy Revolution
summary: This chapter will discuss how renewable energy technologies would be extremely significant in realizing a low-carbon future. As the globe faces the pressing necessity to reduce the impact of climate change and switch to using renewable ener
content: This chapter will discuss how renewable energy technologies would be extremely significant in realizing a low-carbon future. As the globe faces the pressing necessity to reduce the impact of climate change and switch to using renewable energy, solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, and biomass seem to be the most important sources of this energy. The chapter gives a broad outlook on familiarizing themselves with such types of technologies with a focus on their developments, integration issues, and how they contribute to the emissions of the greenhouse gases. Efficiency of solar panels, the evolution of offshore wind farms, development of energy storage mechanisms, and how to electrify all these different regions through the use of renewable energy are the most critical ones. The chapter also relates to the question of policy frameworks, economic, and the magnitude it would contribute towards global energy security through the use of renewable energy technologies. By examining the current trends as well as the future opportunities brought about by renewable energy, this chapter will attempt to provide a clear picture of how the presence of renewable energy would lead to a shift towards a sustainable and low-carbon economy.

title: Microplastic fibres from textiles: evaluation, exposure pathways, and impacts on human health
summary: Textile microplastic fibres (TMFs) are new indoor and occupational contaminants that are being emitted during the various stages of the textile life cycle, during the production of fibres, the manufacturing of garments, wearing, washing, dr
content: Textile microplastic fibres (TMFs) are new indoor and occupational contaminants that are being emitted during the various stages of the textile life cycle, during the production of fibres, the manufacturing of garments, wearing, washing, drying and building up in household dust. This review is focused on their sources, sampling and analytical methods, human health risks, risk assessment strategies and strategies of mitigation. The most common textile polymers found in indoor and outdoor air include polyester, nylon, acrylic, polypropylene, elastane and blended fabrics. The size, shape and aerodynamic characteristics of the fibres are major factors in the dynamics of their flight, deposition and inhalation potential. Indoor environments are significant exposure spaces since fibres are continually shed from clothing, carpets, upholstery and bedding, and normal activities like walking, cleaning and vacuuming can resuspend deposited fibres. Inhaled TMFs could lead to respiratory irritation, mucociliary dysfunction, oxidative damage, inflammation and activation of epithelial and immune cells. The possibility of smaller microplastics and nanoplastics crossing biological barriers, with potential immunological, cardiovascular, and metabolic effects, is limited as of yet in humans. Inconsistencies in sampling protocols, contamination-control procedures and criteria for polymer identification limit current exposure assessment. The source-to-exposure approach should include low-shedding textile design, safer and more durable finishes, HEPA filtration, wet cleaning, laundry filtration, minimizing tumble drying, and increased occupational and regulatory control measures. Harmonised monitoring protocols, realistic models of chronic inhalation exposures, epidemiological research using biomarkers, mixture-toxicity assessment, and field trials of intervention are important areas of future research. TMFs should be considered as a complex issue in the environment and public health that demands synergy among the textile engineering, indoor air science, toxicology and policy fields.

title: A Descriptive Assessment of Green-Port Implementation and Air Quality at Palaran Container Terminal, Samarinda
source: Edunity Kajian Ilmu Sosial dan Pendidikan
summary: This article evaluates changes in air quality at Palaran Container Terminal, Samarinda, during 2022-2026 using annual measurements of sulfur dioxide (SO2), ozone (O3), carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and dust particulate matte
content: This article evaluates changes in air quality at Palaran Container Terminal, Samarinda, during 2022-2026 using annual measurements of sulfur dioxide (SO2), ozone (O3), carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and dust particulate matter (less than 100 micrometers). The program toward green-port implementation began in 2023, while the sampling point was located at the container-port entrance, an area with heavy vehicle traffic. All numerical results or measurement limits were below the quality standards reported in the source document. Descriptively, CO, NO2, and particulate matter decreased from 2022 to 2026, whereas SO2 and O3 increased; the 2026 values remained below 42% of their respective standards. The year 2022 is treated as the pre-program period and 2023-2026 as the period after program initiation, but this pattern does not establish a causal effect of green-port implementation because intervention intensity, replication, adequate meteorological conditions, vehicle-activity data, and a comparison group were unavailable. The literature indicates that shore power, equipment electrification, vessel-speed reduction, and low-sulfur fuels are relevant interventions to evaluate at Palaran Terminal. Further studies should combine green-port implementation logs, terminal and vehicle activity data, meteorological observations, and repeated monitoring at multiple points.

title: Forecasting and Modelling the Impact of Ionophore Withdrawal on Poultry Health and Welfare, Economics and Carbon Footprint
summary: Coccidiosis is one of the most important endemic diseases of poultry, causing intestinal damage, impaired nutrient absorption, dysbiosis, and predisposing broilers to necrotic enteritis and secondary bacterial infections, with major consequ
content: Coccidiosis is one of the most important endemic diseases of poultry, causing intestinal damage, impaired nutrient absorption, dysbiosis, and predisposing broilers to necrotic enteritis and secondary bacterial infections, with major consequences for productivity, welfare and food safety. Modern broiler production relies on robust control of this disease to sustain performance and mitigate animal and human health impacts. Ionophore coccidiostats have been central to managing coccidiosis for more than 45 years, providing effective prevention via the feed route. Ionophore coccidiostats are antimicrobials that are mechanistically distinct from antimicrobials used in human medicine and classified as not medically important by major regulatory authorities.This review evaluates the likely consequences of removing access to ionophore coccidiostats and relying primarily on vaccination and management measures in large populations of broilers to prevent coccidiosis. The food safety and animal welfare benefits of including ionophore programmes, which help to reduce the frequency and severity of intestinal lesions, wet litter, contact dermatitis, and associated respiratory problems are considered.Economic modelling suggests that using ionophore coccidiostats to control coccidiosis reduces production costs by improving feed efficiency, while life-cycle assessment shows that improved feed efficiency also decreases greenhouse gas emissions per unit of liveweight. Finally regulatory assessments and approvals, along with recent genomic and environmental reviews, confirm that ionophores can continue to be used safely with regard to public health, the environment and effective for coccidiosis control, preventing outbreaks. Concurrently, the collective evidence demonstrates ionophore coccidiostats contribute to substantial sustainability benefits in broiler production.

title: Ammonia Production via Plastic Gasification–Reforming: Interpretable Machine Learning and Techno-Economic–Environmental Assessment
summary: Converting waste plastics into ammonia offers a route to recover chemical value from discarded materials, but selecting suitable operating conditions requires balancing production yield, cost, and environmental performance. This study integ
content: Converting waste plastics into ammonia offers a route to recover chemical value from discarded materials, but selecting suitable operating conditions requires balancing production yield, cost, and environmental performance. This study integrates process simulation and interpretable machine learning to evaluate ammonia production through polyethylene and polypropylene gasification coupled with steam methane reforming. A validated Aspen Plus model generated 1800 observations spanning five feedstock and operating variables. Six regression models were assessed using independent testing and five-fold cross-validation. Gradient boosting provided the highest predictive accuracy, achieving a test R 2 of 0.99941 and an average absolute percentage error of 0.15848%. Permutation importance and SHAP analysis identified the steam-to-plastic ratio and ammonia synthesis pressure as the dominant predictors, together accounting for 87.86% of the mean normalized importance. These findings guided the selection of eight configurations for economic and environmental assessment at a plastic feed rate of 1000 kg/h. Configurations operating at 57 bar achieved the lowest levelized ammonia costs of $0.235–0.238/kg and net present values of $173.5–177.2 million. Across the proposed designs, carbon intensities ranged from 14.0 to 15.3 kg CO 2 -eq/kg NH 3, compared with 19.5 kg CO 2 -eq/kg NH 3 for the simulated conventional SMR benchmark under the adopted accounting assumptions. However, SMR achieved higher energy efficiency and net present value, revealing a trade-off between the assessed environmental burden and financial return. Design 8 offered a favorable balance among the plastic-based alternatives. The framework supports transparent screening of operating choices while identifying utility consumption and acid-gas removal as priorities for further process improvement.

title: A Climate‐Adaptive Window Enabling All‐Day Anti‐/Deicing and Dynamic Thermal Management
summary: Transparent anti-/deicing materials have traditionally focused on maximizing solar harvesting to achieve efficient ice mitigation under cold conditions. However, this approach can introduce overheating risks during warm periods, creating a
tags: Thermal management of electronic devices and systems
content: Transparent anti-/deicing materials have traditionally focused on maximizing solar harvesting to achieve efficient ice mitigation under cold conditions. However, this approach can introduce overheating risks during warm periods, creating a challenge in balancing anti-/deicing and thermal management. Here, we report a climate-adaptive window consisting of a spectrally selective optical switch, a hybrid Joule-heating and a highly transparent superhydrophobic coating. Guided by an energy-balance framework for full spectrum design, the window simultaneously achieves high luminous transmittance (65.2%), strong near-infrared absorption (76.1%), and large solar modulation capability (36.0%), enabling dynamic thermal regulation while preserving robust anti-/deicing functionality. The synergistic interplay of photo-electrothermal heating, thermal retention, and superhydrophobicity extends icing delay by 11-fold and realizes rapid all-day deicing at -20°C. Under hot conditions, the thermochromism reduces the average indoor temperature by 15.2°C, substantially reducing building cooling demand and boosting greenhouse seedling biomass relative to conventional configurations. By integrating solar modulation with transparent anti-/deicing functionality, this work paves the way for the development of next-generation climate-adaptive windows.
