title: Aridity-dependent asymmetry in vegetation drought sensitivity associated with CO₂ emissions over China during 2001–2022
summary: Whether rising atmospheric CO₂ alleviates or exacerbates vegetation drought stress remains vigorously debated, with contrasting predictions from stomatal-conductance fertilisation and warming-driven evapotranspiration enhancement. Here we t
content: Whether rising atmospheric CO₂ alleviates or exacerbates vegetation drought stress remains vigorously debated, with contrasting predictions from stomatal-conductance fertilisation and warming-driven evapotranspiration enhancement. Here we test this competing hypothesis across China's climatic gradient from 2001 to 2022 by integrating two vegetation indicators (Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI, structural) and Gross Primary Productivity (GPP, functional)) with multi-scale (1- to 24-month) Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), using a combined framework of optimal timescale identification, moving-window trend detection, and relative-importance attribution. Results show a pronounced aridity-dependent shift in vegetation response timescale: arid and semi-arid regions respond to short-term (1–6 months) water deficits, whereas humid regions are regulated by long-term (12–24 months) water accumulation. Over the 22-year period, the areal percentage of water-limited vegetation increased significantly (0.250%·yr−1 for EVI, p = 0.034; 0.383%·yr−1 for GPP, p = 0.038), while water-surplus areas showed no significant change. In attribution analysis, atmospheric CO₂ ranked as the leading statistical contributor in 33% of national pixels, exceeding precipitation, temperature, and solar radiation (21–24%). Its relative importance increased sharply along the aridity gradient, reaching 35–40% in northern dry basins (Yellow River and Inland River Basins), where higher anthropogenic CO₂ emissions were statistically associated with exacerbated water stress rather than alleviation. These results imply that the net statistical contribution of the CO₂ emission variable to vegetation drought sensitivity shifts from neutral to positive as aridity increases, challenging the prevalent assumption of CO₂ fertilisation as a universal drought mitigator and providing observational constraints for carbon–water coupling models in the East Asian monsoon region.

title: TERRITÓRIOS DE FOGO E QUALIDADE DO AR: MODELAGEM EXPLORATÓRIA DE PM2,5 E DESAFIOS DA GOVERNANÇA SOCIOAMBIENTAL EM MANAUS (2023–2025)
summary: A ocorrência de queimadas na Amazônia e a circulação atmosférica de poluentes suscitam questões sobre a relação entre os territórios de ocorrência do fogo e as áreas potencialmente afetadas pela deterioração da qualidade do ar. Este estudo
content: A ocorrência de queimadas na Amazônia e a circulação atmosférica de poluentes suscitam questões sobre a relação entre os territórios de ocorrência do fogo e as áreas potencialmente afetadas pela deterioração da qualidade do ar. Este estudo objetivou analisar exploratoriamente as relações entre a distribuição espacial e temporal das detecções de fogo no Amazonas, as condições meteorológicas e as concentrações indicativas de material particulado fino (PM₂,₅) em Manaus, entre 2023 e 2025, discutindo suas implicações para a governança dos riscos socioambientais. Adotou-se delineamento observacional, ecológico e quantitativo, com dados do INPE, da estação meteorológica INMET A101 e de três sensores PurpleAir. A caracterização descritiva compreendeu 515 dias elegíveis, enquanto a modelagem exploratória utilizou 406 dias, com validação temporal e comparação de quatro modelos. Registraram-se 19.601 detecções de fogo em 2023, 25.499 em 2024 e 4.545 em 2025. As medianas anuais indicativas de PM₂,₅ foram de 11,29, 10,46 e 4,70 µg/m³, respectivamente, observadas sob cobertura temporal desigual. A inclusão de indicadores de fogo e interação direcional não proporcionou melhoria preditiva robusta em relação aos controles meteorológicos e temporais. Os resultados não permitem confirmar ou refutar o transporte atmosférico de fumaça nem atribuir fontes emissoras específicas. Conclui-se que a distinção entre ocorrência territorial do fogo, condições meteorológicas e concentrações ambientais é fundamental para a interpretação dos riscos e para o aprimoramento do monitoramento integrado e da governança socioambiental.

title: When is the cleanest, and the cheapest, time to use electricity? Carbon intensity, prices and load shifting on the GB grid, 2019–2025 (code, results and working paper)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Code, processed results and working paper (draft v0.3) for a study of when electricity use in Great Britain is cleanest and cheapest, 2019–2025. Using public half-hourly data (NESO Carbon Intensity API; Elexon FUELHH generation and MID whol
content: Code, processed results and working paper (draft v0.3) for a study of when electricity use in Great Britain is cleanest and cheapest, 2019–2025. Using public half-hourly data (NESO Carbon Intensity API; Elexon FUELHH generation and MID wholesale prices; Octopus Agile household prices), the study measures how the daily shape of carbon intensity and prices has changed, simulates flexible demand under fixed, forecast-based and price-based schedules (testing fixed rules out of sample), compares carbon and cost savings on the same days, and estimates the implied abatement cost of carbon-aware over cheapest scheduling. Marginal emission factors are estimated as a robustness check. The analysis can be reproduced with four commands; see README.md.

title: Economics and market impacts of offshore power hubs in the North Sea
summary: TenneT proposed the North Sea Wind Power Hub concept, which connects multiple offshore wind farms to a central hub equipped with interconnections to neighbouring countries (Energinet et al., 2021). The intention is to reduce overall costs;
content: TenneT proposed the North Sea Wind Power Hub concept, which connects multiple offshore wind farms to a central hub equipped with interconnections to neighbouring countries (Energinet et al., 2021). The intention is to reduce overall costs; however, previous studies have largely examined hypothetical configurations rather than the specific proposal from system operators, and they have focused on construction costs rather than system-wide implications. A bottom-up capital cost estimate is developed here in order to compare the hub approach against conventional point-to-point offshore wind connections. Using a pan-European electricity market model for 2030, the resulting impacts on regional electricity prices, wind generation value, fossil fuel generation and carbon emissions are quantified. Two hub configurations are considered: a smaller hub with 12 GW of connected capacity and a larger hub with 30 GW of installed capacity.

title: Data-driven environmental genomics across a soil-salinity gradient reveals candidate loci and population-structure confounding in hexaploid Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus)
summary: Introduction Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus) is a hexaploid, clonally propagated perennial cultivated on marginal saline land. Its tolerance to salinity varies among cultivars. We examined genetic associations with agronomic trai
content: Introduction Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus) is a hexaploid, clonally propagated perennial cultivated on marginal saline land. Its tolerance to salinity varies among cultivars. We examined genetic associations with agronomic traits and collection-site salinity. Methods We evaluated plant height and yield in 72 accessions grown in a common field. We used genome-wide association analysis (GWAS) for both traits and genotype–environment association analysis (GEA) for collection-site salinity. We evaluated population structure using principal components and sparse non-negative matrix factorization. Results Height and yield differed among collection-site salinity classes (Kruskal–Wallis P = 8.8 × 10⁻⁷ and 6.4 × 10⁻⁶, respectively). Cross-validation supported three ancestral clusters. Kinship-controlled GWAS identified no genome-wide-significant locus for either trait. In the GEA, the kinship-only model showed substantial inflation (λ = 3.294), with 926 loci exceeding the Bonferroni threshold. With 15 principal components, the test statistics were deflated (λ = 0.481), and six loci exceeded the threshold. Sequence searches identified stress-related homologs for four of these loci, including a U-box E3 ubiquitin ligase and succinate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH1). Discussion The common-field design suggests that trait differences among salinity classes reflect differences among accessions. The GEA results provide candidates for follow-up and show how strongly the inferred associations depend on the adjustment for population structure.

title: Environmental PFOSA Exposure Activates NF-κB and Disrupts Lysosomal Gb3 Metabolism in Renal Tubular Cells
summary: Ammonium perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOSA), a widely distributed surfactant salt of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS), bioaccumulates in aquatic systems and biota, exerting multi-system toxicity. Although hepatotoxicity, immunotoxicity,
content: Ammonium perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOSA), a widely distributed surfactant salt of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS), bioaccumulates in aquatic systems and biota, exerting multi-system toxicity. Although hepatotoxicity, immunotoxicity, and neurotoxicity are well characterised, the molecular mechanisms underlying PFOSA-induced renal injury remain poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate the intracellular mechanisms linking environmentally relevant PFOSA exposure to renal tubular cell death. Human renal proximal tubular epithelial (HK2) cells were exposed to PFOSA (0.5–5 µM). Cell viability, apoptosis, acute kidney injury (AKI) biomarkers, and transcriptomic changes were assessed using CCK-8, flow cytometry, TUNEL staining, RT-qPCR, RNA sequencing, and ELISA. PFOSA induced concentration- and time-dependent cytotoxicity (IC 50 = 4.937 µM), doubled the early apoptotic fraction, and elevated AKI biomarkers including kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) and N-acetylglucosaminidase (NAGLU). RNA sequencing revealed dual mechanisms: (i) NF-κB p50/p52 upregulation coupled with transcriptional suppression of anti-apoptotic BIRC2/5 and down-regulation of FAS/HRK, shifting the balance toward TP53-driven apoptosis; and (ii) a putative RPL36A–HNRNPH2 read-through fusion associated with GLA silencing, resulting in lysosomal globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation and apoptotic amplification. These findings establish NF-κB reprogramming and GLA–Gb3 lysosomal dysregulation as novel molecular nodes of PFOSA nephrotoxicity at environmentally relevant concentrations, offering potential dual-target therapeutic strategies against PFAS-induced renal injury.

title: The radiant perspective
summary: Pragmatic climate assessment must override ideological reflexes: Europe cannot meet its urgent decarbonization goals without nuclear energy. Serving as a vital low-carbon provider of stable baseload electricity, nuclear power successfully c
content: Pragmatic climate assessment must override ideological reflexes: Europe cannot meet its urgent decarbonization goals without nuclear energy. Serving as a vital low-carbon provider of stable baseload electricity, nuclear power successfully counteracts the natural intermittency of renewables. Europe must proactively maintain its existing fleet, reject the high-emission trap of premature shutdowns, and orchestrate a unified continental deployment of factory-built Small Modular Reactors (SMRs).

title: Enhanced β-decay rates and the role of underlying nuclear structure at the neutron drip line
summary: Nuclei are bound collections of protons and neutrons whose stability reflects a delicate balance of the forces inside matter. When many extra neutrons are added, this balance shifts: traditional arrangements can reorganize, allowing new sha
content: Nuclei are bound collections of protons and neutrons whose stability reflects a delicate balance of the forces inside matter. When many extra neutrons are added, this balance shifts: traditional arrangements can reorganize, allowing new shapes to compete and previously high-energy configurations to emerge at low energies. Measurements at the limits of nuclear binding are scarce but essential for testing descriptions of this evolution. How far toward these neutron-rich limits does nuclear structure continue to influence β-decay half-lives, even as the decay energy becomes very large? Here we report the first β-decay half-life measurements of 31 F and 37 Na, nuclei at or near the neutron-rich limits of binding. The measured half-lives of 1.31 +0.25 −0.21 ms for 31 F and 1.65 +0.33 −0.27 ms for 37 Na are the two shortest directly measured β − -decay half-lives by central value, with 31 F the shortest. Large-scale shell-model calculations indicate that these rapid decays depend not only on the large energy available for decay but also on shell evolution that places accessible transition strength at lower daughter excitation energies, where phase space remains large. These measurements replace extrapolated lifetimes with experimental benchmarks and show that, even at the neutron-rich limits of binding, exceptionally rapid β decays retain sensitivity to internal nuclear structure.

title: Dynamic Separation of CO2/CO/N2 from Blast Furnace Gas Using Twin-Tower Vacuum Pressure Swing Adsorption with Multiobjective Optimization
summary: Decarbonizing blast furnace gas (BFG) while recovering CO is essential for mitigating industrial emissions and valorizing carbon resources. Here, we integrate experiments with process simulation to elucidate CO2/CO/N2 separation over 13X ze
content: Decarbonizing blast furnace gas (BFG) while recovering CO is essential for mitigating industrial emissions and valorizing carbon resources. Here, we integrate experiments with process simulation to elucidate CO2/CO/N2 separation over 13X zeolite in a twin-tower vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) process. Adsorption analyses reveal that CO loading is markedly lower than CO2 loading; coadsorbed CO marginally depresses CO2 purity yet exerts negligible influence on recovery. Raising the feed CO2 concentration from 10% to 30% increased CO2 purity from 48% to 70% and recovery from 44% to 93%. Meanwhile, the CO concentration in the vacuum-desorption CO2 product decreased, while CO recovery, defined as the percentage of feed CO entering this stream, remained near 5%. Higher feed flow rates enhance purity but compromise recovery owing to accelerated CO2 breakthrough, and product CO concentration varies sensitively with temperature, pressure, and flow rate. Notably, surrogate-assisted multiobjective optimization disentangles the competing effects and pinpoints balanced operating windows, disclosing that flow rate predominantly governs purity whereas CO2 concentration dictates recovery. These findings establish quantitative structure–performance relationships and deliver actionable guidance for configuring BFG VPSA operating windows for selecting BFG VPSA operating conditions based on CO2 capture performance and CO contamination of the CO2 product.

title: Posthuman Motherhood and Uneven Futurity in S.B. Divya’s Machinehood
source: Word and Text - A Journal of Literary Studies and Linguistics
summary: S.B. Divya’s Machinehood (2021) is a techno-dystopian speculative fiction that analyses how maternal care and agency are reorganised in an AI-driven future. The article argues that Machinehood employs bio-augmentation, AI mediation, and dig
content: S.B. Divya’s Machinehood (2021) is a techno-dystopian speculative fiction that analyses how maternal care and agency are reorganised in an AI-driven future. The article argues that Machinehood employs bio-augmentation, AI mediation, and digital surveillance to establish that technology does not automatically empower mothers, but instead, pre-digital hierarchies of gender, class, and colonial power in technologically enhanced forms. Drawing from Haraway’s cyborg, Braidotti’s nomadic subject, Butler’s grievability and Ferrando’s question of whether the posthuman is a post-woman, this article analyses how the novel’s three maternal characters represent three distinct modalities of futurity: conditional, precarious and denied. Nithya, the bio-augmented working mother, inhabits a conditional future where her caregiving is algorithmically devalued relative to her market productivity. Welga, the prosthetically enhanced protector, occupies a precarious future that is structured by the asymmetry between her visible physical labour and the systemically invisible emotional labour. Ao Tara, the posthuman ‘dakini’ – a sacred female embodiment of enlightened energy – faces a denied future since her mode of being is illegible to the Earth’s governance systems, which end up classifying her not as a mother but as a threat. In the light of such an imbalance, the article argues that the novel exposes how technological augmentation and biopolitical governance produce uneven futurity rather than liberation.

title: The Rural Online Initiative: Short-term Outcomes of Remote Work Skills Training for the Young Workforce
summary: The Certified Remote Work Professional® (CRWP) course aims to prepare young people for long-term career success by including remote work and professional skills in occupational training. USU Extension’s Rural Online Initiative piloted the c
content: The Certified Remote Work Professional® (CRWP) course aims to prepare young people for long-term career success by including remote work and professional skills in occupational training. USU Extension’s Rural Online Initiative piloted the course with 53 participants at Washington County’s Career Tech High School. Pre- and post-tests showed significant knowledge gains in all nine modules, and participants reported stronger abilities in productivity, teamwork, problem-solving, and digital communication. Most (93%) viewed remote work favorably, and 90% felt more empowered to seek remote employment. Of 25 follow-up respondents, 18 reported new or better jobs. These short-term outcomes suggest the course can help Utah’s young workforce reach higher-paying careers without leaving their communities.

title: Evolution of energy storage: from passive backup to intelligent energy assets
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: Energy storage is undergoing a fundamental transformation from passive backup devices into intelligent energy assets that actively support modern power systems. This evolution is driven by advances in electrochemical storage technologies, p
content: Energy storage is undergoing a fundamental transformation from passive backup devices into intelligent energy assets that actively support modern power systems. This evolution is driven by advances in electrochemical storage technologies, power electronics, artificial intelligence, digital communication, and distributed energy management, enabling storage systems to operate as adaptive and value-generating components of future energy infrastructures. This editorial presents a conceptual framework describing four stages of energy storage evolution: passive backup, monitored storage, smart storage, and intelligent energy assets. Building upon this progression, it discusses the enabling technologies, system architecture, and emerging applications that support increasingly autonomous and data-driven energy management. The integration of battery technologies with intelligent energy management systems, advanced analytics, and interoperable communication networks enables energy storage to provide services beyond energy balancing, including renewable integration, grid flexibility, market participation, and resilience enhancement. The editorial further argues that future energy storage systems should be evaluated not only by energy capacity and efficiency but also by their intelligence, adaptability, interoperability, sustainability, and system value. This perspective positions intelligent energy storage as a strategic foundation for flexible, resilient, and carbon-neutral electrical energy systems.

title: Effect of nano urea, GA3, boron and calcium on growth, yield, and quality of strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) cv. winter dawn
summary: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is a high-value fruit cultivated globally for its adaptability. Optimizing pre-harvest nutrition and growth regulators is critical for maximizing its growth, yield, and quality. A field experiment was
content: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is a high-value fruit cultivated globally for its adaptability. Optimizing pre-harvest nutrition and growth regulators is critical for maximizing its growth, yield, and quality. A field experiment was conducted during 2024–25 to evaluate the effects of nano urea, GA 3, boron, and calcium on strawberry cv. ‘Winter Dawn’ under a naturally ventilated polyhouse at Prof. Rajendra Singh (Rajju Bhaiya) University, Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The study followed a Randomized Block Design (RBD) with seven treatments and three replications. Results revealed significant variations among treatments. Foliar application of T 7 [GA 3 150 ppm) + Boron (0.6%) + Calcium nitrate (1.0%)] at 25, 50, and 75 days after planting (DAP) recorded the maximum vegetative and yield attributes, including plant height (19.10 cm), plant spread (19.44 cm E–W, 22.16 cm N–S), leaf number (18.60), fruit weight (15.46 g), yield plant⁻ 1 (320.47 g), and the highest benefit–cost ratio (1:2.74). Conversely, treatment T 6 [Nano urea (0.2%) + Boron (0.6%) + Calcium nitrate (1.0%)] maximized fruit quality parameters, yielding the highest TSS (10.27°Brix), ascorbic acid (61.10 mg/100 g), and total sugar (7.20%).

title: Halogen-bond/hydrogen-bond donor hybrid catalysts for carbon dioxide fixation
summary: Hydroxymethyl-functionalized iodotriazolium halides were developed as highly active catalysts for the cycloaddition of carbon dioxide to epoxides.
content: Hydroxymethyl-functionalized iodotriazolium halides were developed as highly active catalysts for the cycloaddition of carbon dioxide to epoxides.

title: Between sustainability strategy and financial practice: archetypes of financial agency in Norwegian salmon farming
source: Journal of responsible production and consumption.
summary: Purpose This paper aims to clarify the role of financial actors in sustainability transitions by developing and applying an archetype framework of financial agency logics. In transition studies, finance is often treated as a resource that f
content: Purpose This paper aims to clarify the role of financial actors in sustainability transitions by developing and applying an archetype framework of financial agency logics. In transition studies, finance is often treated as a resource that flows towards promising innovations, rather than as a domain of agency shaping sustainability-related decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts an abductive qualitative research design. An archetype framework is developed through engagement with sustainability transition theory and sustainable finance literature, and empirically explored through 13 semi-structured interviews with financial actors involved in Norwegian salmon farming production, complemented by 55 documents, including annual reports, sustainability strategies, investment guidelines and policy-related documents. Findings The findings reveal a misalignment between sustainability ambitions articulated in strategies and the logics guiding investment practices. While sustainability is commonly framed in line with sustainable logics, decision-making remains dominated by conventional orientations prioritising short-term profitability and narrowly defined risk. Transformative logics appear mainly in discursive commitments. Financial actors selectively mobilise overlapping logics depending on context, rather than conforming to a single archetype. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to a single sector and national context. Future research should test and refine the framework across sectors and geographies and examine how financial instruments and policy mixes shape the mobilisation of financial logics. Practical implications The framework offers a diagnostic lens for practitioners and policymakers to examine how sustainability ambitions are interpreted and filtered within financial decision-making. Originality/value The paper introduces a novel archetype framework that operationalises financial agency in sustainability transitions, responding to a call for more knowledge on the role of finance.

title: Between Memory and Modernity: Indigenous Climate Adaptation Practices in the Himalayan Agriculture of Jammu and Kashmir
summary: The local sustainability of regional Himalayan agriculture critically depends on climate change by virtue of the survival dependence of smallholder farmers on regionalized environmental expertise. The paper examines farmers’ perceptions and
content: The local sustainability of regional Himalayan agriculture critically depends on climate change by virtue of the survival dependence of smallholder farmers on regionalized environmental expertise. The paper examines farmers’ perceptions and adaptation responses under the influence of environmental conditions, Indigenous Knowledge (IK), and psychological bias in Shopian, Ganderbal, Bandipora, Rajouri, Samba, and Kathua districts. The primary data was collected by conducting 60 in-depth interviews and corresponding surveys by means of a mixed-method approach. Surveys used reflective thematic analysis and descriptive statistics for analysis. The results of the analysis suggest that farmers’ perceptions of climate depend on geographical and climatic conditions and that IK provides a pragmatic kit and culture repository of adaptation responses. Psychological biases of availability, recency, and optimism bias, respectively, shape how such knowledge is perceived and used, and on occasions limit time adaptation. The study establishes the potential for a hybrid adaptation model of indigenous wisdom and scientific intervention. A reduction of cognitive biases, policymakers and strategists of development will incorporate climate-resilient practices more relevantly and accessibly and ensure productive agriculture and culture preservation in the region.

title: Nature-Derived Materials for Energy Conversion: A Review
summary: Nature-derived materials are increasingly investigated as alternatives to conventional functional materials for energy conversion and storage because they combine renewable or waste-based sourcing with hierarchical structures and tunable su
content: Nature-derived materials are increasingly investigated as alternatives to conventional functional materials for energy conversion and storage because they combine renewable or waste-based sourcing with hierarchical structures and tunable surface chemistry. This review examines biomass and agricultural residues, biopolymers, marine-derived resources, natural clay minerals, and mineral-rich wastes, with emphasis on how processing modifies pore architecture, interfaces, conductivity, ion transport, and thermal behavior. Applications considered include triboelectric energy harvesting, electrochemical storage, solar and thermal-energy systems, hydrogen generation, and bioelectrochemical technologies. Biomass-derived carbons emerge as particularly versatile electrode materials because carbonization and activation can tailor porosity and heteroatom chemistry, whereas biopolymers provide flexible substrates, separators, binders, and biodegradable components. Natural clays offer ion-exchange capacity, confinement effects, and stable inorganic frameworks. Across these applications, however, feedstock variability, moisture sensitivity, durability, processing energy, reproducibility, cost, and end-of-life management remain major barriers to scale-up. The review therefore proposes a materials-selection perspective in which functional performance is assessed together with processing intensity, circularity, durability, economic feasibility, and environmental compatibility. Market deployment will depend on standardized feedstocks, scalable low-energy processing, life-cycle validation, and policy frameworks supporting circular material flows.

title: Does Macro-Financial Uncertainty Matter for Energy-to-Carbon Downside Risk?
summary: This study examines whether macro-financial uncertainty shapes the downside risk that the European carbon market inherits from energy markets, and whether it does so by making carbon prices more volatile or by tightening their dependence on
content: This study examines whether macro-financial uncertainty shapes the downside risk that the European carbon market inherits from energy markets, and whether it does so by making carbon prices more volatile or by tightening their dependence on fuel and clean-energy markets. Using daily data from 2017 to 2026, we estimate event-conditioned CoVaR for EU allowance futures with asymmetric score-driven copulas for Brent crude oil, TTF gas, Rotterdam coal, and clean-energy equities, and decompose each downside spillover into carbon conditional volatility and a standardized conditional-quantile gap. The spillovers are then related to six lagged macro-financial indicators in persistence-controlled linear and penalized additive models, with inference based on a bootstrap that re-estimates both stages. Equity-market uncertainty emerges as the most notable correlate: higher VIX is associated with larger carbon losses when the oil market is in distress. This association is suggestive and sensitive to model specification: its additive-model interval narrowly excludes zero, and AIC and BIC favor different Brent copulas. VIX is also associated with higher carbon volatility, whereas uncertainty does not strengthen the dependence of carbon on gas and coal. Therefore, macro-financial uncertainty appears to reach the carbon market mainly through the scale of carbon-price risk rather than through tighter energy–carbon linkages.

title: Edible Dandelions: A Gastrophysical Approach
summary: Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) is an edible weed with a long history of medicinal use. With a global spread, this versatile plant has several desirable sensory properties. Because the nutraceutical properties of plants are rarely subject
content: Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) is an edible weed with a long history of medicinal use. With a global spread, this versatile plant has several desirable sensory properties. Because the nutraceutical properties of plants are rarely subject to robust clinical testing, a more effective route to increasing the use of this weed in the diet may be to emphasize its culinary and gastrophysical potential. Indeed, by adopting a gastrophysics, rather than nutraceutical, lens, this review leads to several testable predictions about how the desirability of this edible weed (leafy green, flower, and edible root) can be enhanced. This review synthesises information from plant biology, phytochemistry, sensory research, and gastrophysics, positioning edible dandelions as a sustainable and versatile food resource, with potential relevance for climate-resilient food systems under conditions of global environmental change. The plant’s ecological resilience, bolstered by apomictic reproduction and phenotypic plasticity, facilitates its extensive range and potential as a climate-resilient crop, although this remains to be tested directly. The phytochemical composition of the plant underpins its known bioactivity, as well as its unique bitter taste and herbal scent character. Preclinical investigations have shown a wide range of health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity, but these findings derive mainly from in vitro and animal models; the experimental results have yet to be validated in human clinical trials. The culinary value of the dandelion plant is well-known. From the standpoint of gastrophysics, flavor-matching and visual presentation, especially vivid coloured flowers, can provide powerful opportunities to improve consumer acceptance. This review proposes that sensory-oriented food design should complement nutritional and pharmacological research, with particular emphasis on reproducible preparation methods, consumer acceptance and safety. In particular, dandelion can be used in salads, drinks (tea and soft drinks), and fermented foods.

title: Resource efficiency in the SME sector in the European Union: An analysis of Slovakia's position
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) represent a significant part of the business sector in the European Union, both because of their number and their contribution to economic performance. At the same time, their role is becoming incre
content: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) represent a significant part of the business sector in the European Union, both because of their number and their contribution to economic performance. At the same time, their role is becoming increasingly important in the context of growing pressure for sustainability and the transition towards a circular economy. The aim of this paper is to examine selected resource-efficiency measures implemented by SMEs in EU Member States and to assess the relative position of Slovak SMEs. The analysis is based on secondary data from Flash Eurobarometer 549 “SMEs, resource efficiency and green markets” and applies descriptive statistical and comparative analysis. Nine resource-efficiency measures are classified into basic and advanced practices, for which corresponding implementation scores are calculated. The results show that Slovak SMEs perform above the EU average in basic resource-efficiency measures, while their position is less favourable in advanced practices. The main gaps are observed in renewable energy use, sustainable product design, and the sale of residual materials and waste. The findings show that Slovakia's implementation gap is concentrated primarily in more advanced and systemic practices rather than in resource efficiency generally, highlighting the need for more targeted support for the transition towards more comprehensive circular economy practices.

title: Creating a Green Zone
summary: A single, universally agreed global carbon price remains an unrealistic near-term prospect, but Europe can weaponize its massive market scale to shape global behavior. By integrating its economic weight with like-minded international tradin
content: A single, universally agreed global carbon price remains an unrealistic near-term prospect, but Europe can weaponize its massive market scale to shape global behavior. By integrating its economic weight with like-minded international trading partners, the Union can establish a robust Green Trade Zone. Linking entry into this marketplace of half a billion affluent consumers to strict compliance with carbon, circularity, and biodiversity standards makes sustainable commercial operations an irresistible global entry ticket.

title: A Study on the International Marketing Issues and Countermeasures of Industrial Vacuum Cleaners For Company A
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: With the acceleration of global trade integration, competition in the European industrial vacuum cleaner market has become increasingly fierce. As a Chinese OEM/ODM manufacturer of industrial vacuum cleaners, Company A faces both opportunit
content: With the acceleration of global trade integration, competition in the European industrial vacuum cleaner market has become increasingly fierce. As a Chinese OEM/ODM manufacturer of industrial vacuum cleaners, Company A faces both opportunities and challenges in exploring the European market. Taking Company A’ s operations in Europe as the research object, this paper uses Porter’s Five Forces Model to analyze its macro and competitive environment, and summarizes its marketing status, advantages and problems. The study finds that although Company A has advantages in production capacity, certifications and customization, it still suffers from weak independent design, unstable quality, high cost pressure, unbalanced parts pricing, single channel, insufficient digital marketing, and inadequate technical and after-sales service. This paper puts forward optimization strategies from four aspects: product, price, channel and service, so as to enhance Company A’ s competitiveness and market share in Europe, and provide practical reference for similar Chinese manufacturing enterprises to expand overseas markets, with strong theoretical and practical significance.

title: Pathological mechanisms and therapeutic strategies for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury: a review of current status, challenges, and future perspectives
summary: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) constitutes a secondary pathology in ischemic stroke (IS), with its underlying mechanisms encompassing oxidative stress, hyperactivated inflammatory responses, calcium overload, excitatory amino a
content: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) constitutes a secondary pathology in ischemic stroke (IS), with its underlying mechanisms encompassing oxidative stress, hyperactivated inflammatory responses, calcium overload, excitatory amino acid toxicity, cellular death, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. Specific drugs and therapeutic strategies for CIRI remain in the exploratory phase, with clinical treatment primarily focused on alleviating complications and expanding the eligible patient population. This review systematically outlines the pathological mechanisms of CIRI, potential targets, and its therapeutic strategies. At present, mechanical revascularization techniques remain the primary means of restoring cerebral blood flow. Preclinical and early clinical evidence suggests that antioxidants, anti-inflammatory agents, excitatory amino acid antagonists, neuroprotective agents, and traditional Chinese herbal medicines may mitigate neuronal injury and promote neurological recovery; however, robust clinical evidence remains limited. Emerging therapies such as stem cell therapy, nanotechnology, and gene therapy show potential in preclinical models through multi-targeted, multi-pathway interventions, but their clinical efficacy requires further validation. Moreover, the clinical translation of CIRI presents certain challenges. This review aims to provide new insights into the prevention and treatment of CIRI by examining the current research status and clinical application prospects of these diverse strategies.

title: Transforming Forest Dependence into Sustainable Livelihood Pathways: Evidence from Community Forest Associations in Kenya
summary: A key challenge for developing countries is to reconcile forest conservation with the need of forest-dependent communities to earn a living. Participatory forest management, implemented in Kenya through Community Forest Associations (CFAs),
content: A key challenge for developing countries is to reconcile forest conservation with the need of forest-dependent communities to earn a living. Participatory forest management, implemented in Kenya through Community Forest Associations (CFAs), is promoted as a way to improve forest governance while supporting rural livelihoods. This study examines whether CFA participation is associated with household income and forest-resource income among forest-adjacent households. Using survey data from 2,513 households, of which 1,904 had complete observations, we apply an endogenous switching regression (ESR) model to account for selection associated with voluntary participation and to estimate counterfactual outcomes for members and non-members. CFA participation is associated mainly with institutional and resource-access factors, including participation in the Plantation Establishment and Livelihood Improvement Scheme (PELIS), forest grazing group membership, access to credit, and proximity to roads. Estimated treatment effects suggest that CFA membership is associated with 22.3% higher household income and 7.5% higher forest-resource income than the counterfactual of non-participation. These estimates are imprecise, statistically insignificant at conventional levels, and diagnostic tests fail to detect selection on unobservables, so they are best interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects. The findings suggest that CFAs might be able to contribute to livelihood support if participation is coupled with tangible incentives and supportive complementary institutions.Enhanced role for participatory forest management in sustainable rural livelihoods can be achieved by strengthening CFA governance, expanding PELIS and forest-based enterprises and improving market and service linkages.

title: Ad Hoc Window Protection Materials Performance Under Fire Exposure
summary: Windows are a critical vulnerability of buildings exposed to large outdoor fires impacting the built environment, such as wildland-urban interface fires. Failure of windows during such incidents provides potential pathways for smoke, flames
content: Windows are a critical vulnerability of buildings exposed to large outdoor fires impacting the built environment, such as wildland-urban interface fires. Failure of windows during such incidents provides potential pathways for smoke, flames, and embers into a structure. During these events, structure loss may be reduced if homeowners and/or emergency responders have readily available options to fashion ad hoc protection for at-risk windows. This study evaluated the performance of six commercially available materials — plywood, fiber cement board, intumescent wrap, metal mesh, carbon fiber blanket, and foil-faced fiberglass fabric — installed over residential windows and exposed to a full-scale post-flashover compartment fire from an adjacent structure at varying separation distances. The time relative to flashover and the heat load (time-integrated heat flux) to the exterior surface were quantified at the first observed instances of smoke and flame on the back side of the windows and formation of an opening through the assembly large enough for ember intrusion. Heat flux measured on the back side of the windows was evaluated against a threshold value (20 kW/m $$^2$$) for non-piloted ignition of common household combustibles. All window protection materials improved flame and ember resistance to exterior fire exposure compared to unprotected windows. Foil-faced fiberglass fabric provided the most consistent protection across all exposure conditions. Ad hoc window protections can provide improved resistance to exterior fire, flame, and ember hazards when installed over residential windows and may be a practical mitigation strategy for homeowners and emergency responders.

title: Impact of ESG Rating Disparities on Equity Financing Costs: An Empirical Analysis of the A-Share Market in China
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: This paper selects A-share listed companies in China from 2019 to 2023 as the research sample and constructs an ESG rating divergence indicator based on the ratings of three domestic agencies—Huasheng, Shangdao Ronglv, and Menglang—to empir
content: This paper selects A-share listed companies in China from 2019 to 2023 as the research sample and constructs an ESG rating divergence indicator based on the ratings of three domestic agencies—Huasheng, Shangdao Ronglv, and Menglang—to empirically examine the impact of ESG rating divergence on the cost of equity capital. Using a panel fixed-effects model, the study finds that domestic ESG rating divergence significantly increases the cost of equity capital, with a coefficient of 0.0163 and a p-value of 0.022, confirming Hypothesis H1. Furthermore, the effect exhibits source heterogeneity: domestic divergence exerts a significant positive effect, whereas foreign divergence, constructed based on Bloomberg, FTSE Russell, and MSCI ratings, shows no significant impact (−0.0012, p=0.847). When both types of divergence are included simultaneously, domestic divergence remains significant (0.0180, p=0.028), while foreign divergence remains insignificant (−0.0019, p=0.757), confirming Hypothesis H2 and indicating that domestic divergence is the key factor affecting financing costs, while foreign rating information has limited transmission efficiency in the Chinese market. The main conclusions remain robust across multiple robustness tests, including sample screening relaxation and winsorization. This paper expands the existing literature on the economic consequences of ESG rating divergence and provides empirical support for promoting the unification of ESG rating standards, optimizing corporate information disclosure, and guiding investors to rationally interpret rating divergence.

title: From Carbon Revenue to Financial Resilience: Rethinking Risk Allocation in REDD+
summary: REDD+ mobilizes public and private finance for forest conservation, yet community benefits and conservation functions can become vulnerable when they depend on uncertain carbon revenues. This forum paper argues that the central financial pr
content: REDD+ mobilizes public and private finance for forest conservation, yet community benefits and conservation functions can become vulnerable when they depend on uncertain carbon revenues. This forum paper argues that the central financial problem is not carbon-market participation itself, but how revenue uncertainty is transmitted through REDD+ financing arrangements and how resulting losses are allocated. It develops a framework linking financial exposure, risk transmission and allocation, and financial resilience. Revenue exposure concerns dependence of project income on a financing source, expenditure exposure concerns which functions rely on that income, and liquidity exposure concerns mismatches between revenue timing and expenditure commitments. Market shocks do not automatically become community losses because outcomes depend on reserves, alternative finance, contracts, expenditure priorities, and institutional decisions. The paper extends benefit-sharing analysis from the distribution of gains to the allocation of downside risk and identifies four complementary resilience mechanisms comprising financing diversification, reserves and liquidity management, contractual risk sharing, and transparent financial governance. Financial resilience is distinct from carbon integrity, but can help sustain the community institutions and conservation activities on which durable mitigation outcomes partly depend.

title: Designing cross-jurisdictional ecological compensation: a supply–flow–equity framework for the Poyang Lake Basin, China
summary: Introduction Cross-jurisdictional compensation needs an explicit beneficiary boundary, an auditable allocation rule, and transparent equity assumptions. We examine a city-level negotiation framework for the Poyang Lake Basin and three selec
content: Introduction Cross-jurisdictional compensation needs an explicit beneficiary boundary, an auditable allocation rule, and transparent equity assumptions. We examine a city-level negotiation framework for the Poyang Lake Basin and three selected downstream Yangtze cities. Methods For 2000, 2010, and 2020, InVEST annual water yield is compared with allocated water demand. Eleven services are valued using land-cover equivalent factors. ESV-based gravity and break-point weights allocate a water-replacement payment base, adjusted by a land-cover habitat proxy, relative payer income, and an Engel-based social proxy. Official nine-class CLCD coding is used consistently. Sensitivity, geographic-detector, and scenario-uncertainty analyses accompany the calculation. Results All 24 basin cities have positive modeled water balances in each year. The three downstream cities enter as an assumed beneficiary set, rather than as independently measured local deficits. Basin ESV rises from 1,876.6 to 4,042.5 and 5,400.5 × 10 8 CNY under year-specific nominal inputs. Compensation totals are 54.13, 75.77, and 65.79 × 10 8 CNY. Depth-normalized water validation has 10.9% mean absolute relative error, with 12 of 15 comparisons within ± 20%. Ranks of pair-level allocation shares are similar under most tested gravity variants but change when ESV density replaces total mass. Discussion The framework makes conditional bilateral payment assumptions reviewable. Its outputs are negotiation scenarios, not traced physical service flows or validated fiscal entitlements. Unverified price and downstream-proxy inputs, administrative catchment boundaries, and the weak social-proxy contribution limit interpretation.

title: Salutogenic urban housing in hot-arid climates: Daylight as a catalyst for health and resilience
summary: This paper provides a critical, integrated examination on the built environment of hot-arid Levantine cities, specifically evaluating its unintended, long-term impacts on human health. Gropius championed a functionalist architecture of stan
content: This paper provides a critical, integrated examination on the built environment of hot-arid Levantine cities, specifically evaluating its unintended, long-term impacts on human health. Gropius championed a functionalist architecture of standardization, extensive glazing, and flat roofs designed to maximize “sun, light, and air”. However, the uncritical export and imposition of these modernist models and the rush to residential towers as a solution for densification in the Middle East created a profound climate and cultural mismatch, disrupting centuries of indigenous building traditions. Employing a critical environmental-health reading grounded in contemporary public health metrics, this study revisits Gropius’ core principles against four measurable health domains: thermal stress, air quality, circadian/light health, and psychosocial wellbeing. The analysis reveals that modernist architectural features intended to promote hygiene and efficiency in temperate zones actively exacerbate heat accumulation, severe glare, dust infiltration, and social isolation when transplanted to hot-arid climates. This paper argues that contemporary therapeutic architecture in the Levant must move beyond functionally desolate urban planning and reconcile modern production needs with the nuanced, climate and human-responsive logic of traditional regional typologies, proposing a guideline for “Contextualized Housing Adaptation”.

title: From Himalayan transboundary glacier hazards and European heatwaves to actionable climate finance: quantified allocation, tiered governance and a COP31 implementation pathway for the Global Climate Responsibility and Resilience Fund
summary: Glacier-related hazards along the Nepal–China border and European heatwaves in 2026 expose climate risks that cross national and sectoral boundaries. Climate-finance targets leave unresolved how responsibility should be allocated, recipient
content: Glacier-related hazards along the Nepal–China border and European heatwaves in 2026 expose climate risks that cross national and sectoral boundaries. Climate-finance targets leave unresolved how responsibility should be allocated, recipients prioritized, projects delivered and outcomes verified. This Perspective proposes the Global Climate Responsibility and Resilience Fund (GCRRF) to connect these functions within a common institutional framework. The proposal draws on an August 2026 policy interview, contrasting risk examples and existing research on climate equity, loss and damage, and energy systems. Under its contributor baseline, historical cumulative national emissions and historical cumulative per capita emissions each receive 35%. Consumption-adjusted per capita emissions over the preceding five years and ability to pay each receive 15%. Recipient priority assigns 65% to economic and social losses and 35% to sea-level and low-elevation exposure. Supplementary tracks address inland mountain regions and transboundary basins, while ecological appraisal considers ecosystem condition and natural forest carbon stocks. Open procurement, capacity building, long-term operation and maintenance, and monitoring, reporting and verification connect allocation rules to project delivery and performance assessment. The weights define policy baselines for sensitivity testing. Implementation would require international authorization, informed by phased pilot assessments. The COP31 process could initiate these pilots, with reproducible calculation, public scrutiny and independent evaluation informing subsequent refinement.

title: Corporate Organizational Structure and Decarbonization
summary: We examine how organizational structure affects carbon emissions. Using the introduction of the Market Stability Reserve (MSR) in the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), we show that more centralized firms reduce emissions more when incre
content: We examine how organizational structure affects carbon emissions. Using the introduction of the Market Stability Reserve (MSR) in the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), we show that more centralized firms reduce emissions more when increases in carbon prices make capital-intensive abatement economically viable. In particular, the decline in emissions is larger for installations linked to legal entities with larger portfolios of regulated installations and lower when the regulated installations are dispersed across more legal entities under the same ultimate owner. The results are stronger among organizations with layered ownership structures, ultimate owners located within the EU ETS, and in sectors where abatement requires coordinated capital investment. Overall, our evidence indicates that cap-and-trade systems are more effective when the organizational structure of the firm facilitates coordination. Corporate decarbonization is therefore not only a regulatory challenge, but also an organizational one.

title: AI Disclosure Credibility and Corporate Financial Misconduct: Evidence from Green Digital Infrastructure in China
summary: Can green digital infrastructure discipline corporate misconduct, and can discrepancies between corporate AI talk and observable AI action reveal residual financial risk? We address these questions by linking 33,356 firm-year observations f
content: Can green digital infrastructure discipline corporate misconduct, and can discrepancies between corporate AI talk and observable AI action reveal residual financial risk? We address these questions by linking 33,356 firm-year observations for 4,662 Chinese listed firms in 259 cities to the staggered rollout of the National Green Data Center program, enforcement records, annual-report AI disclosures, digital-capital investment, AI patents, audit information, innovation, and city conditions. A cohort-stacked difference-in-differences design indicates that program exposure is associated with a 1.71 percentage-point reduction in next-year punitive violations, equivalent to 50.5% of the treated firms’ pre-treatment risk. The estimate remains negative with direct controls for three overlapping digital policies. Re-estimation around official list publication gives + 0.54 percentage points for 2018 (p = 0.336) and − 1.25 percentage points for newly exposed cities on the 2021 list (p = 0.014). We then construct an expanding-window AI disclosure-action benchmark that distinguishes narrative intensity from observable AI investment and patenting. Positive unexplained AI language is associated with subsequent recorded misconduct under two-stage bootstrap inference. Rolling OLS residuals and raw AI intensity provide comparable in-sample fit. In later-period classification tests, raw AI talk and the disclosure-action gap provide modest additional ranking information beyond financial variables, while the integrated model identifies 31.4% of recorded violations in the highest-risk decile. The findings connect digital infrastructure with corporate financial discipline and characterize the information in conditional AI language for risk-oriented monitoring.

title: Plant-protein films and composites: effects of composition, fractionation and processing on functionality and sustainability – A review
summary: Plant-protein isolates, concentrates and other fractions are increasingly used to produce films, coatings and composites, although their functionality depends on protein composition, fractionation route, processing conditions and formulatio
content: Plant-protein isolates, concentrates and other fractions are increasingly used to produce films, coatings and composites, although their functionality depends on protein composition, fractionation route, processing conditions and formulation. This review examines the influence of these factors on film formation, functional properties, applications and environmental impact, treating protein purity as an application-dependent design variable and distinguishing direct material comparisons from extraction–functionality studies and environmental or economic assessments. Residual carbohydrates, lipids, phenolics, minerals and insoluble particles can influence aggregation, plasticisation, interfacial adhesion, rheology, thermal response, moisture sensitivity and degradation. Selected studies show both benefits and penalties of purification, while recent dry, mild aqueous and membrane fractionation studies reveal trade-offs among purity, recovery and functionality. Composite-grade purity is defined here as a compositional specification suitable for a stated material and process. Minimum-sufficient purity is the lowest tested protein content that meets all predefined requirements within a specified formulation and processing window. An operational framework links feedstock selection and fractionation to protein functionality, formulation, service performance and separate life-cycle and techno-economic assessments. Ingredient-level impact data and feedstock prices do not establish finished-material sustainability, and low purity is not inherently optimal. The evidence supports application-specific testing rather than a universal purity threshold.

title: Red, blue and far-red light regimes shape vegetative growth and flowering responses in wild rocket: potential implications for vertical farming and speed breeding
summary: This study compared vegetative growth and flowering incidence in wild rocket (Diplotaxis tenuifolia) under contrasting spectral and photon-supply conditions. Two varieties, Dragon’s Fire and Saturn, were exposed for four weeks to ambient-li
content: This study compared vegetative growth and flowering incidence in wild rocket (Diplotaxis tenuifolia) under contrasting spectral and photon-supply conditions. Two varieties, Dragon’s Fire and Saturn, were exposed for four weeks to ambient-light Control and four LED regimes: R70:B30, R50:B50, red-blue-far-red (RBF) and low-photon white (LFW), supplying total photon fluxes of 215, 160, 230 and 50 µmol m -2 s -1, respectively, including far-red where present. RBF supplied red:blue:far-red photon fluxes in a 155:60:15 ratio. The white LED treatment served as a reference with deliberately constrained photon supply. Light regime affected shoot fresh weight and stomatal conductance (both p < 0.001), whereas total phenolic content did not differ significantly among light treatments (p > 0.05). The red-blue treatments supported the strongest vegetative performance. Mean shoot fresh weight was 3.47 and 2.63 g plant -1 under R70:B30 and R50:B50, respectively, compared with 0.75 g plant -1 under RBF and 0.62 g plant -1 under LFW. However, the red-blue treatments did not differ significantly for shoot fresh weight within either variety. RBF produced the highest mean stomatal conductance (g s; 6.273 and 9.080 mm s -1 in Dragon’s Fire and Saturn, respectively) but weak biomass accumulation and flowering, despite receiving the highest photon flux. Under R70:B30 and R50:B50, mean flowering incidence ranged from 16.07 to 21.21% in Dragon’s Fire and from 31.90 to 38.49% in Saturn. No flowering occurred under LFW, although this was accompanied by a substantial biomass penalty. PCA separated the red-blue treatments from RBF and LFW. Shoot fresh weight was positively associated with flowering incidence across treatments and varieties (R 2 = 0.621). Overall, wild rocket responded to the complete light regime rather than spectral composition or photon supply independently.

title: Local lens, global vision
summary: This chapter introduces the groundbreaking work of four South Asian women architects from two different generations – Minnette de Silva (Sri Lanka), Yasmeen Lari (Pakistan), Marina Tabassum (Bangladesh), and Anupama Kundoo (India). It highl
content: This chapter introduces the groundbreaking work of four South Asian women architects from two different generations – Minnette de Silva (Sri Lanka), Yasmeen Lari (Pakistan), Marina Tabassum (Bangladesh), and Anupama Kundoo (India). It highlights their contributions to critical regionalism and sustainable architecture. They all integrate local materials, building traditions, and modernist principles to challenge dominant architectural norms and address socio-ecological challenges. De Silva pioneered regional modernism in Sri Lanka by merging local with modern design, while Lari changed her approach from brutalist urban projects to zero-carbon humanitarian architecture in Pakistan. Tabassum’s designs emphasize climate responsiveness and cultural identity in Bangladesh, whereas Kundoo’s innovative material research fosters affordable and eco-viable solutions in India. Their increasing global recognition, ranging from exhibitions and media coverage to prestigious awards, underscores their influence in reshaping architecture’s social purpose. Despite their diverse approaches, it can be argued that these architects collectively embody a form of architectural activism that bridges local practices with global discourse, thereby inspiring future generations.

title: The Future of Sustainable Transportation
summary: The chapter explains the innovative role of electric and autonomous vehicle technologies in contemporary transportation. Electric vehicles (EVs) and autonomous vehicles (AVs) have become essential solutions as cities and governments globall
content: The chapter explains the innovative role of electric and autonomous vehicle technologies in contemporary transportation. Electric vehicles (EVs) and autonomous vehicles (AVs) have become essential solutions as cities and governments globally struggle with the issue of company carbon emissions and making their urban environments more mobile. This chapter provides an in-depth exploration of the current EV technologies, such as the enhancement of battery performance, charging infrastructure, and market adoption. It also discusses the evolution of AVs and points to sensor technology innovations, artificial intelligence, and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication. The combination of these technologies in the chapter describes how sustainable transportation systems can make a difference in terms of greenhouse gas emissions, reduce traffic congestion, and improve overall efficiency. The chapter also covers the policy implications, infrastructure needs, and the social effects of changing to electric transport and autonomous transport. The chapter will critically analyze how these technologies are defining the future of sustainable mobility by reviewing the prevailing trends, challenges, and prospects in detail to establish the appropriate futures.

title: As Tendências Mundiais da Regulamentação Técnica e a Competitividade da Indústria Química Brasileira.
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Twenty-one years separate the defense of this thesis, on March 8, 2005, at the School of Chemistry of the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), from this revised edition. In rereading it, I tried to resist two oppositetemptations: re
content: Twenty-one years separate the defense of this thesis, on March 8, 2005, at the School of Chemistry of the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), from this revised edition. In rereading it, I tried to resist two oppositetemptations: rewriting it in light of what we know today, and treating it as a museum piece. I chose to preserve its content in full, limiting the revision to the spelling, punctuation and grammar of the Portuguese and English texts, and to offer, in this prologue, a candid assessment of what the workanticipated correctly and what it failed to see.The first innovation concerned the source. In 2005, the notifications of technical regulations submitted to the World Trade Organization under the Agreement on Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) were treated mainly as diplomatic paperwork. This thesis turned them into an empirical base: 4,501 texts notified between 1996 and 2002 were read, classified and analyzed one by one in order to extract patterns of regulatory behavior across countries.Treating the Enquiry Points as a systematic observatory of regulatory trends, rather than merely as a consultation channel, was an unusual methodological choice at the time, and it has since become common practice in studies of technical barriers.The second innovation concerned the method. The infometric approach developed at Siquim made it possible to build a matrix of some 30,000 regulatory and foreign trade data points, cross-referencing 292 items ofBrazil’s chemical trade list with more than 90 American and European regulations and programs. The effort to map the Mercosur Common Nomenclature (NCM) onto CAS numbers — a bridge between the language ofcustoms and the language of chemistry — anticipated, by hand, what is now done with integrated databases and text-mining tools. The notion of a product’s “regulatory susceptibility,” measured in hits, is a direct forerunner of the regulatory exposure analyses that have become routine in thecompliance departments of major chemical companies.The third concerned rigor. The hypotheses were stated in testable form and confronted with data: that emerging countries regulate by drawing on requirements first adopted by developed countries, and that developedcountries concentrate their exports to Brazil in less regulated areas, while Brazil tends to export products subject to stricter regulatory control in its destination markets. Both were tested with careful sampling, representativeness checks and an explicit statement of limitations —something not always found in industrial policy studies of that period.Its most evident success was the diagnosis regarding REACH. When this thesis was written, the European regulation was still a proposal under discussion; it would be adopted in December 2006 and enter into force in June 2007.
