title: Modeling Hedging of Renewable Energy Price Fluctuations: Risk Management Strategies with Forward Contracts, Futures Contracts, Options, and Energy Swaps
source: African Journal of Mathematics and Statistics Studies
summary: This paper explores a scientific approach using the technology of modelling and analysis of risk management strategies for renewable energy price fluctuations to achieve economic growth. It investigates the application of forward contracts,
content: This paper explores a scientific approach using the technology of modelling and analysis of risk management strategies for renewable energy price fluctuations to achieve economic growth. It investigates the application of forward contracts, futures contracts, options, and energy swaps in mitigating the financial risks associated with price volatility in renewable energy markets. The paper presents mathematical formulations for each of these instruments, provides solutions, and offers a comprehensive analysis of their effectiveness in hedging risk. Numerical simulations demonstrate the application of these models in real-world scenarios, highlighting their role in stabilising energy markets with positive consequential economic growth.

title: Challenges in Achieving High Energy Density in Lithium-Ion Batteries: Anode Materials and Silicon Modification Strategies
summary: Due to the development of electric cars, portable electronic devices, and energy storage, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have experienced an increase in energy density demand. However, restrictions associated with the design of classical elec
content: Due to the development of electric cars, portable electronic devices, and energy storage, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have experienced an increase in energy density demand. However, restrictions associated with the design of classical electrodes hinder the improvement of batteries' characteristics. The present review article examines three types of anode materials, namely, graphite, graphene, and silicon, as well as their distinct features. First, despite low cost and reliable cycling ability, the capacity of graphite is limited by 372 mAh g⁻¹. Second, high conductivity and lithium storage capacities are provided by graphene, but there is a possibility of aggregation of its sheets that can cause instability. Last but not least, silicon attracts special attention owing to its potential capacity of 3579 mAh g⁻¹. But the constant expansion of silicon makes it harmful for the structure of the electrode and solid electrolyte interphase. In order to resolve these issues, three modification approaches, i.e., structural engineering, composite with carbon materials, and modification of the interface, are proposed. Experimental data support positive outcomes related to the use of such modifications and improvement of the electrode capacity and performance. At last, the drawbacks of silicon-containing anodes, namely production difficulties, electrode swelling, and gap between the experiment and industrial practice, are discussed.

title: GUT FEELINGS: THE ROLE OF INTESTINAL MICROBIOME IN TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS AND ITS COMPLICATIONS
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Diabetes, particularly type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), is a complex metabolic disorder influenced by an interplay of genomic, nutritional, and lifestyle factors, with a significant rise in prevalence linked to modern lifestyles. The increa
content: Diabetes, particularly type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), is a complex metabolic disorder influenced by an interplay of genomic, nutritional, and lifestyle factors, with a significant rise in prevalence linked to modern lifestyles. The increasing burden of T2DM, affecting over 422 million individuals globally, is associated with insulin resistance (IR), chronic inflammation, and various organ dysfunctions, leading to severe complications such as diabetic cardiovascular disease and kidney disease. Recent advances in microbiome research have unveiled the gut microbiome's pivotal role as an endocrine organ, influencing metabolic health through mechanisms related to digestion, immunity, and metabolic regulation. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the shifts in gut microbiome composition throughout the progression of T2DM and associated conditions, examining the causal relationships between intestinal microbiota and metabolic dysregulation. Key findings highlight the role of specific microbial taxa in modulating inflammation and glucose metabolism, as well as the therapeutic potential of microbiome-targeted interventions, including dietary modifications, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation. Additionally, we explore the molecular interactions between host factors and microbiota that contribute to dysbiosis in T2DM, emphasizing the impact of microbial metabolites on systemic inflammation and metabolic pathways. By elucidating these intricate relationships, this review aims to contribute to the understanding of how microbiome modulation may offer novel therapeutic strategies for managing T2DM and its complications.

title: Trade-offs in the Energy Transition: Local Public Health Gains and Socioeconomic Costs of U.S. Coal Facility Retirements
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Retirement of coal-fired power stations and industrial coal plants is a crucial characteristic of the US energy transition process. While reduction in fossil fuel consumption provides climate and air-quality benefits nationwide, local commu
content: Retirement of coal-fired power stations and industrial coal plants is a crucial characteristic of the US energy transition process. While reduction in fossil fuel consumption provides climate and air-quality benefits nationwide, local communities hosting these facilities face uneven socio-economic, fiscal and public health outcomes. This paper analyses local socio-economic and public-health consequences of US coal-related facility shutdowns from the perspective of negative externality environmental economic theory and with the help of comparative case studies of Huntley Coal-Generating Station and Shenango Coke Works. By using peer-reviewed scholarly literature and secondary empirical evidence published in governmental reports, the paper aims to address two main research questions. First, what is the mixture of benefits and concentrated local costs of coal infrastructure shutdown? Secondly, what makes it so hard to prove the empirical link between environment policy, environmental conditions in the locality and health results and what case study evidence can be gained from a natural experiment?

title: Rice Cultivation in India: Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Emerging Opportunities and Challenges in Voluntary Carbon Markets
source: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change
summary: Rice cultivation is an important source of agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly methane, while also supporting food security and rural livelihoods. This study examines trends in rice area, production, GHG emissions, and
content: Rice cultivation is an important source of agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly methane, while also supporting food security and rural livelihoods. This study examines trends in rice area, production, GHG emissions, and emissions intensity in India and globally during 1970–2023 and describes rice-related project activity in voluntary carbon registries using a June 2026 database snapshot. The analysis draws on the FAOSTAT rice-commodity farm-gate emissions series, World Development Indicators, the Berkeley Voluntary Registry Offsets Database, and registry project information. Descriptive comparisons and log-linear compound growth-rate estimates indicate that farm-gate GHG emissions attributed to rice production in India rose from 119.77 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (Mt CO₂e) in 1970 to 164.24 Mt CO₂e in 2023, while output increased more rapidly and emissions per kilogram of paddy declined. In 2023, rice accounted for 20.69% of the agricultural GHG total used in the analysis. The registry compilation identified 77 India-associated rice-emission-reduction projects, but approximately 0.03 million credits had been issued by the reporting cut-off. Issued credit volumes were small relative to the number of listed projects and should not be equated with technically achievable mitigation or future financial returns. Heterogeneous crediting methodologies, additionality and measurement requirements, uncertain demand, and project-level verification costs constrain implementation. The findings indicate opportunities for improved water management through carbon credits, subject to robust emission accounting, crop-yield safeguards, and transparent distribution of benefits.

title: Growth and yield assessment of mint (Mentha spicata L.) plants in response to integration of organic and chemical fertilizers in sandy soils
summary: The combined application of organic and chemical fertilizers is an effective strategy to enhance soil properties, crop growth, and overall yield. This study evaluated the growth characteristics, essential oil yield, and chemical composition
content: The combined application of organic and chemical fertilizers is an effective strategy to enhance soil properties, crop growth, and overall yield. This study evaluated the growth characteristics, essential oil yield, and chemical composition of mint (Mentha spicata L.) grown under various organic and inorganic fertilizer treatments in sandy soil. The experimental treatments consisted of treatment 1 (unfertilized control) (T1) control (unfertilized); treatment 2 (100% NPK + seaweed extract) (T2) 100% nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) + 3 mL L − 1 seaweed extract (SW); treatment 3 (6 tons [6 Mg]/fed Biochar + 50% NPK + seaweed extract) (T3) 6 tons [6 Mg]/fed biochar + 50% NPK + SW; treatment 4 (6 tons [6 Mg]/fed Compost + 50% NPK + seaweed extract) (T4) 6 tons [6 Mg]/fed compost + 50% NPK + SW; treatment 5 (6 tons [6 Mg]/fed Biochar + 25% NPK + seaweed extract) (T5) 6 tons [6 Mg]/fed biochar + 25% NPK + SW; and treatment 6 (6 tons [6 Mg]/fed Compost + 25% NPK + seaweed extract) (T6) 6 tons [6 Mg]/fed compost + 25% NPK + SW. Results indicated that all fertilization treatments significantly improved growth traits, herb yield, essential oil yield, photosynthetic pigments, and nutritional content compared to the unfertilized control. The highest values across all studied parameters were recorded under treatment T4, followed closely by T2 and T3. These findings suggest that integrating compost or biochar at 6 tons [6 Mg]/fed with 50% NPK and SW (T4 or T3) is a viable approach to optimizing mint growth and yield in sandy soils.

title: Private demand cannot scale carbon sequestration
summary: Scenarios meeting international climate change targets assume tens of gigatons of annual anthropogenic carbon sequestration by mid-to-late century. Ecosystems of voluntary carbon markets, corporate climate pledges, and sustainable banking i
content: Scenarios meeting international climate change targets assume tens of gigatons of annual anthropogenic carbon sequestration by mid-to-late century. Ecosystems of voluntary carbon markets, corporate climate pledges, and sustainable banking initiatives assume private capital is key to delivering this. Yet voluntary carbon markets currently provide only tens of megatons of sequestration, and vintages are declining. We argue that private incentives can contribute at most marginally to multi-gigaton- scale sequestration demand. Carbon sequestration is a public good. Marketing incentives driving carbon credit demand are small and disconnected from scaling, expected storage, and costs. Scaling demand through public pressure would be unprecedented, and public pressure seems to be declining. Scaling demand through financial firms faces antitrust and fiduciary duty challenges, illustrated by the Net-Zero Banking Alliance’s collapse. Sequestration projects’ monetizable co-benefits, when existing, may not scale with sequestration. Governments should accelerate interventions to facilitate carbon sequestration, de-emphasize high-sequestration scenarios in climate outlooks, or both.

title: Evaluating and Improving Access to the Bus Station as an Initial Step Toward a Sustainable Public Transport Strategy
summary: In the Sultanate of Oman, net emissions totaled approximately 90 Mt CO2e, with five sectors accounting for ~95% of net emissions—industry, oil and gas, power, transport, and buildings. Unless Oman acts now, emissions are projected to rise b
content: In the Sultanate of Oman, net emissions totaled approximately 90 Mt CO2e, with five sectors accounting for ~95% of net emissions—industry, oil and gas, power, transport, and buildings. Unless Oman acts now, emissions are projected to rise by 16% to 104 Mt CO2e by 2050. As a result, Oman's national strategy prioritizes behavioural change to reduce car use. To achieve this, the strategy encourages residents to use public transportation and plans for an equitable distribution of bus stops, the only public transport option in Oman. Therefore, this study investigates the accessibility and distribution of bus stops in Al-Maabilah South, Muscat, Oman. Al-Maabilah South is a mixed-use, rapidly expanding metropolitan area that requires urban services and everyday transportation. To examine how various factors affect bus use, the study used a mixed-methods approach, including a literature review, a case study, resident surveys, and interviews with transportation industry specialists. The results reveal uneven bus stop distribution, long walks, inadequate pedestrian pathways, poor facilities, and low safety, all of which hinder bus use. The population's needs and the current public transportation infrastructure are clearly at odds. The study recommends improving bus stop distribution, enhancing pedestrian facilities, and developing the public transportation system to support sustainable transport solutions aligned with Oman Vision 2040's goals.

title: From Agent to Swarm and Decentralized Collaboration: Rethinking Power System Collaboration Driven by Large Language Models
summary: With the increasing deployment of renewable energy and distributed energy resources, the power system is becoming more complex and distributed in its operation. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have attracted much attention due to the
content: With the increasing deployment of renewable energy and distributed energy resources, the power system is becoming more complex and distributed in its operation. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have attracted much attention due to their strong domain knowledge and flexible decision-making abilities, and various forms of multi-agent and decentralized methods have also been introduced to support distributed intelligent organizations. However, the application of these methods to problems in power systems has not been fully realized. Organization structure and coordination mode are the two research topics examined in this paper's theoretical exploration of LLM-based agents. This paper studies the application of LLMs in power-system agents and multi-agent systems, and analyzes the development of swarm and decentralized collaboration based on LLMs in this field. The relationship between the two research directions and the basic conditions under which they can be applied in power system scenarios are investigated. Based on the above analysis, this paper outlines the current research landscape and provides a theoretical basis for future research on integrated intelligent collaboration in complex power system environments.

title: Regional Environmental Governance and Sustainable Consumption: A System Transformation Perspective from China's National Ecological Civilization Pilot Zones Policy-Based Evidence from the Regression Control Method
summary: Regional environmental governance is increasingly recognised as an important driver of sustainability transitions because it can simultaneously influence production systems, market incentives, and the conditions under which consumers make d
content: Regional environmental governance is increasingly recognised as an important driver of sustainability transitions because it can simultaneously influence production systems, market incentives, and the conditions under which consumers make decisions. However, while its environmental and economic outcomes have been widely examined, considerably less is known about how environmental governance facilitates sustainable consumption through broader regional system transformation. Using panel data from 29 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities) in China from 2004 to 2023, this study exploits the first batch of the first National Ecological Civilization Pilot Zones (NECPZs) established in Fujian, Jiangxi, and Guizhou to evaluate the policy effects of regional environmental governance on sustainable consumption. The results show that NECPZs' implementation significantly enhanced regional green consumption, and the results remain robust to a temporal placebo test and optimal subset selection. Mechanism analysis further suggests that regional environmental governance promotes sustainable consumption by facilitating production-side structural transformation and improving environmental conditions. These findings provide empirical evidence that regional environmental governance extends beyond environmental protection to reshape the broader regional systems that support sustainable consumption. They also offer policy insights for integrating production-side transformation with consumption-side strategies to advance sustainable production and consumption.

title: Issue Construction and Value Oriented Guidance in People’s Daily Reports on “Synergy Between Compu-ting Power and Electricity”
source: Journal of Computer Science and Frontier Technologies
summary: Against the backdrop of mounting anxiety over computing power related energy consumption triggered by the expansion of generative artificial intelligence, syn-ergy between computing power and electricity has evolved into a major com-pound i
content: Against the backdrop of mounting anxiety over computing power related energy consumption triggered by the expansion of generative artificial intelligence, syn-ergy between computing power and electricity has evolved into a major com-pound issue bearing on China’s layout of new quality productive forces and its green low carbon transition. Taking relevant news reports from the People’s Daily media matrix as research samples, this study integrates the is-sue construction theory and Gamson’s “interpretive package” theory to explore how mainstream media construct this issue. The analysis reveals that in theme selection, media coverage focuses on strategic coordination, spatial restructuring and technological rationality. In framing, media employ framing devices such as metaphors, illustrative cases and slogans, together with reasoning devices in-cluding causal attribution, consequence prediction and moral principles to form interpretive packages. These packages realize the figurative translation and le-gitimacy justification of sophisticated technical content. In terms of val-ue oriented guidance, media transcend social subsystems and build a four dimensional value guidance path targeting governments, enterprises, media outlets and individuals, facilitating the transformation of policy intentions into nationwide strategic consensus. This research provides academic references for journalistic practices concerning major strategic issues during the 15th Five Year Plan period and for enhancing China’s discourse power in green digital govern-ance.

title: Arsenic Contamination of Soil and Its Impact on Plantation Crop Production
source: Asian Journal of Research in Agriculture and Forestry
summary: Arsenic (As) contamination of agricultural soils is an increasingly important constraint on the sustainability of plantation cropping systems, particularly tea (Camellia sinensis), coffee (Coffea spp.), rubber (Hevea brasiliensis), cocoa (T
content: Arsenic (As) contamination of agricultural soils is an increasingly important constraint on the sustainability of plantation cropping systems, particularly tea (Camellia sinensis), coffee (Coffea spp.), rubber (Hevea brasiliensis), cocoa (Theobroma cacao), and perennial spice and fruit crops. Although arsenic occurs naturally in many soils, its accumulation is often intensified by geogenic enrichment, contaminated irrigation water, mining and industrial deposition, and historical use of arsenical pesticides and phosphate fertilizers. In plantation systems, long cropping cycles, permanent root systems, repeated agrochemical use, and dependence on shallow groundwater can promote gradual arsenic loading and exposure. Arsenic reduces plantation productivity by inhibiting root development, disrupting the uptake of water and nutrients, degrading chlorophyll and photosynthetic machinery, generating reactive oxygen species and altering carbon assimilation and hormone signalling. These effects can lower vegetative growth, reduce leaf, bean, latex, or fruit yields, and compromise produce quality and market acceptance. The severity of the impact depends on arsenic speciation, soil pH, redox status, iron and aluminium oxides, organic matter, microbial activity, and crop genotype. Tea is particularly relevant because acidic plantation soils, high root-zone exposure, and repeated leaf harvesting create conditions in which arsenic can accumulate in foliage; studies report arsenic partitioning predominantly in roots, with lower but measurable transfer to leaves. Management should therefore combine source control, irrigation-water testing, site-specific soil monitoring, avoidance of unnecessary phosphate inputs, iron- and silicon-based immobilization where appropriate, organic amendments, tolerant or low-accumulating planting material, and phytoremediation in severely affected areas. This review synthesizes current evidence on arsenic sources, soil–plant dynamics, physiological effects, plantation-crop responses, food-safety implications, and practical mitigation strategies. It concludes that plantation systems require long-term, landscape-scale monitoring and integrated management rather than single-point remediation.

title: Effects of poultry manure and seaweed extract on growth and yield of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)
summary: The continuous use of chemical fertilisers has adversely affected soil condition and reduced the efficiency of nutrient use, resulting in lower wheat yields over time. A field study was performed during the rabi season of 2024–25 at the Agr
content: The continuous use of chemical fertilisers has adversely affected soil condition and reduced the efficiency of nutrient use, resulting in lower wheat yields over time. A field study was performed during the rabi season of 2024–25 at the Agricultural Research Farm, Lovely Professional University, Punjab, using a split-plot design, with four levels of poultry manure (PM) (0, 5, 10 and 15 tonnes per hectare (t ha-1)) as main plot treatments and four levels of seaweed extract (SE) (0, 0.25 %, 0.75 % and 1 %) as subplot treatments, forming 16 treatment combinations with 3 replications. The study showed that applying PM at 15 t ha-1 significantly enhanced growth parameters including plant height, number of tillers and dry matter accumulation, while seaweed extract at 1 % enhanced crop vigour. The integrated application of 15 t ha-1 poultry manure and 1 % SE recorded the highest grain yield (61.21 quintals per hectare (q ha-1)), straw yield (56.09 q ha-1) and harvest index (52.21 %), with a significant interaction between poultry manure and SE (p < 0.05). These findings indicate a synergistic effect between PM and SE. The use of organic manure combined with biostimulants significantly enhanced yield attributes such as spike length and grain formation, leading to higher wheat productivity. This study indicates that the use of PM along with SE can be considered as an environmentally friendly approach for improving yield in wheat cultivation.

title: Bioprotective potential of Sargassum muticum extracts against Stemphylium vesicarium in tomato
summary: Stemphylium vesicarium, the pathogen responsible for brown spot disease, poses a significant challenge to pear production and threatens a variety of crops, including onion, parsley, and sunflower. While synthetic fungicides remain the prima
content: Stemphylium vesicarium, the pathogen responsible for brown spot disease, poses a significant challenge to pear production and threatens a variety of crops, including onion, parsley, and sunflower. While synthetic fungicides remain the primary control method, their environmental risks, association with microbial resistance, and potential health effects underscore an urgent need for sustainable alternatives. This study explores the potential of Sargassum muticum (Yendo) Fensholt, an invasive seaweed, as a valuable source of bioactive compounds for the development of sustainable plant-protective products for controlling S. vesicarium infections. Native to East Asia and now widespread along European coastlines, S. muticum represents an abundant and underutilized biomass resource rich in minerals, phytohormones, and phenolic acids, including salicylic acid, which may contribute to the observed protective effect following extract application, making it a promising source for eco-friendly agricultural applications. The findings reported here, obtained through controlled infection assays with Solanum lycopersicum L., suggest that treatments with S. muticum extracts, particularly root irrigation and potential seed priming, may have beneficial effects on plant growth, potentially associated with milder disease symptoms. These results support the valorization of invasive seaweed biomass as a source of bio-based agricultural products and contribute to the development of environmentally friendly strategies for the sustainable management of S. vesicarium infections and other crop diseases.

title: Fast-Charging Sodium Solid-State Batteries Enabled by closo -Hydridoborate Anode Interlayers for Sulfide Electrolytes
summary: Sodium solid-state batteries may offer high-power operation through highly conductive sulfide solid electrolytes but remain limited by unstable electrode|electrolyte interfaces. Bilayer separators can decouple interfacial requirements if el
content: Sodium solid-state batteries may offer high-power operation through highly conductive sulfide solid electrolytes but remain limited by unstable electrode|electrolyte interfaces. Bilayer separators can decouple interfacial requirements if electrochemical compatibility, contact quality, and charge transfer are ensured. Here, the closo-hydridoborate Na4(B10H10)(B12H12) is identified as an effective interlayer material for sulfide electrolytes. Time-dependent impedance measurements reveal that Na3PS4 bilayer cells still suffer from severe instability, while Na3SbS4 and Na2.9P0.9W0.1S4 bilayers are stabilized by the hydridoborate interlayer. For the latter cells, the interface resistance is easily dominated by poor mechanical contact but can be eliminated under moderate stack pressure. Incorporating Na4(B10H10)(B12H12) enables stable cycling of Na2.9P0.9W0.1S4-based cells with a TiS2-based cathode and Na15Sn4/Na3Sn anode, delivering >90% capacity retention over 250 cycles and capacitor-like charging from 0–50% SOC in 30 s (82 mA cm–2) at 80 °C. The results identify closo-hydridoborate interlayers as key enablers for high-power sodium sulfide solid-state batteries.

title: Why High-Emission Industries, Value-Chain Adoption, and Sustainable Development Goals Are Not Driving Circular Economy Research: A Knowledge-Economy Systematic Review
summary: The circular economy (CE) is central to sustainability agendas, yet it remains largely theoretical and unevenly implemented. A deeper, often overlooked problem is epistemic: CE still lacks consensual definitions and a stable taxonomy of its
content: The circular economy (CE) is central to sustainability agendas, yet it remains largely theoretical and unevenly implemented. A deeper, often overlooked problem is epistemic: CE still lacks consensual definitions and a stable taxonomy of its circular strategies (the “Rs”), even as their application across value chains and economic sectors expands. This systematic literature review (SLR), reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and guided by 15 research questions, analyzes 114 first-quartile, peer-reviewed articles retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus, and reframes this unevenness as a knowledge-economy problem: how circular knowledge is created, diffused, codified, absorbed, and applied. The review finds that (1) CE is an emerging, weakly consolidated field; (2) plural definitions and 14 Rs signal weak conceptual codification; (3) the Rs cluster in the design and disposal stages of the value chain; (4) the regions and industries producing most CE research are not the highest greenhouse-gas (GHG) emitters; and (5) no validated instrument exists to assess CE. We therefore caution that scaling certification under the emerging ISO 59,000 series—like prior reliance on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), international agreements, and ISO 14,001—cannot substitute for the missing epistemic and taxonomic consensus and risks institutionalizing an unsettled construct. The world’s heaviest polluters do not lead CE research; knowledge capacity does. Advancing CE therefore depends on the interdisciplinary management of circular knowledge, not on goals or certification alone.

title: From climate anxiety to green stagnation: The impact of climate policy uncertainty on urban green trade
summary: Amid escalating global climate governance and the imperative of sustainable development, green trade has emerged as a pivotal mechanism for mitigating climate change. This study examines the causal effect of climate policy uncertainty (CPU)
content: Amid escalating global climate governance and the imperative of sustainable development, green trade has emerged as a pivotal mechanism for mitigating climate change. This study examines the causal effect of climate policy uncertainty (CPU) on the development of urban green trade using a panel dataset of Chinese customs and urban economic statistics. Employing a two-way fixed-effects model, we find that CPU exerts a statistically significant inhibitory effect on green trade. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that this adverse impact is amplified in cities excluded from low-carbon pilot programs and environmental protection priority lists, underscoring the moderating role of institutional preparedness. Mechanism investigations indicate that the CPU impedes green trade primarily through three channels: deteriorating resource allocation efficiency, restricting green finance, and attenuating trade openness. Furthermore, we document that strengthening environmental regulation intensity and marketization levels effectively buffer the deleterious effects of CPU. These findings offer critical policy insights for refining climate policy frameworks and accelerating the transition toward a green economy.

title: The Legal Regulation of Food Waste Management: A Comparative Study of the United States, France, and South Korea
source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
summary: Food waste has become a pressing global challenge with significant environmental, economic, and social implications, demanding urgent and coordinated legal responses. The author conducts a comparative analysis of the rules and laws governin
content: Food waste has become a pressing global challenge with significant environmental, economic, and social implications, demanding urgent and coordinated legal responses. The author conducts a comparative analysis of the rules and laws governing food waste reduction and food waste management in the United States, France, and South Korea, three jurisdictions that have adopted distinctive regulatory approaches to this pressing global issue. By examining the legal frameworks, policy instruments, and enforcement mechanisms employed in each country, the study identifies both common principles and divergent strategies in addressing food waste. The comparison encompasses key aspects such as reduction targets, disposal restrictions, recycling requirements, and liability allocation. Drawing on these existing rules and their implementation outcomes, the author proposes development suggestions for future global food waste-related laws, aiming to inform the formulation of more effective and harmonized legal responses to food waste at the international level and to support sustainable food systems worldwide.

title: The power of a price
summary: The EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) stands as a highly successful, market-based engine for industrial decarbonization. By capping total pollution and making allowances tradable, the market dynamically drives emissions cuts where they are
content: The EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) stands as a highly successful, market-based engine for industrial decarbonization. By capping total pollution and making allowances tradable, the market dynamically drives emissions cuts where they are most cost-effective. To support industries facing severe geoeconomic disadvantages, the ETS must reinforce reciprocity by reinvesting revenues into carbon contracts for difference to de-risk green innovations.

title: GREEN FINANCE PATHWAYS FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE NEW WESTERN LAND-SEA CORRIDOR: FROM PRODUCT OVERLAY TO AN INSTITUTIONAL CLOSED LOOP
source: Journal of trends in financial and economics.
summary: The green finance needs of the New Western Land-Sea Corridor exhibit pronounced scenario specificity: emission abatement centers on the gradual upgrading of existing high-carbon assets rather than incremental purely green projects; funding
content: The green finance needs of the New Western Land-Sea Corridor exhibit pronounced scenario specificity: emission abatement centers on the gradual upgrading of existing high-carbon assets rather than incremental purely green projects; funding must be matched to long-lived assets such as shipbuilding and shoreline retrofitting; and environmental benefits must be accounted for and certified along cross-border transport chains. Building on a review of three strands of literature—corridor effects, financial supply, and the micro-level mechanisms of green finance—this paper constructs a coupled analytical framework of “funding supply–risk governance–industrial guidance” and, drawing on nine representative cases along the corridor and across borders, identifies four obstacles: the gradient fracture between green standards and transition finance; the maturity–risk mismatch between cross-border capital and corridor assets; data silos in carbon accounting infrastructure; and the structural weakness of local financial supply along the corridor. The study argues that the solution lies not in stacking green products but in building an institutional closed loop of “standard coordination–product adaptation–infrastructure support–cross-border circulation,” underpinned by cross-regional institutional coordination. Further progress in corridor green finance hinges on whether carbon footprints can become the language of credit, whether digital bills of lading can carry green information, and whether transition finance can offer a verifiable way out for high-carbon segments.

title: The Impacts of Green Finance on Carbon Balance Capacity with Environmental Governance Pressure
summary: This study utilizes provincial panel data from 2011 to 2022 in China to examine the influence of green finance on carbon balance capacity under varying levels of environmental governance pressure. A panel threshold model is applied to captu
content: This study utilizes provincial panel data from 2011 to 2022 in China to examine the influence of green finance on carbon balance capacity under varying levels of environmental governance pressure. A panel threshold model is applied to capture nonlinear effects across regions and governance contexts. The empirical results demonstrate that green finance significantly enhances carbon balance capacity, particularly when governance pressure is moderate, which strengthens its positive impact. The strength of this relationship differs across provinces with diverse industrial structures, degrees of market segmentation, and functional zones. Further investigation shows that green finance promotes carbon balance mainly by facilitating industrial structure greening and encouraging green technological innovation. Moreover, environmental governance pressure moderates these mediating mechanisms, shaping how effectively green finance operates. Overall, expanding green finance, optimizing governance pressure, and advancing industrial and technological transformation are crucial to improving carbon balance capacity and achieving national carbon reduction objectives.

title: Financing constraints and energy-price incentives shape community-heating investment and domestic carbon accounts: a synthetic-community analysis for Jinan, China
summary: Public money for community heating is limited, and its carbon effect depends on how it is paid, not only how much. Support can relax initial financing, change marginal energy prices or merely move payments, yet evaluations rarely separate t
content: Public money for community heating is limited, and its carbon effect depends on how it is paid, not only how much. Support can relax initial financing, change marginal energy prices or merely move payments, yet evaluations rarely separate these channels, and carbon accounts can mistake a change of payer for a change of demand. This modelling study separates them: capital support of equal public present value tests the financing channel, annual support of the same present value, which pays 34% more undiscounted, serves as an accounting check of the payer channel, and a current-rule energy reimbursement tests the marginal-price channel; each is followed into dated domestic supply-chain carbon accounts (domestic fossil CO 2 plus on-site gas combustion, undiscounted). The experiment uses a financing-constrained investment model of a synthetic, uncalibrated 17-building community in Jinan, China, checked by 10-min redispatch, so its numbers illustrate mechanisms rather than estimate the effects of Jinan’s policies. Fixed support changed the heating system only when it relaxed a binding limit on initial finance. With private finance hard-capped at half the reference investment, all-capital support reduced the 20-year carbon account by 1.9–2.5 kt across ±30% installed costs and ±20% retail prices, and by about 2,550 t in the reference case. Under the same cap, a fully repaid interest-free loan of equal public cost reduced the account by 6.9 kt, whereas with costlier unlimited finance instead of a cap, the same support left the design unchanged. The reimbursement, which subsidized gas far more than electricity, favoured gas capacity that outlasts the subsidy and raised the 20-year account by 115–141 t; under the documented rule this increase would reverse with a 24% higher electricity-purchase footprint (5% in the 2023 structure), so its sign is uncertain for a Shandong project. A fixed subsidy therefore changes heating investment and carbon only if paid before a quantity-constrained financing decision; a change of payer alone leaves purchases unchanged. Programmes facing such constraints should support investment at the financing decision, compare dated payments rather than present values alone, and check how reimbursements shift relative fuel prices before claiming carbon savings.

title: Low-Carbon Electricity Technologies for Decarbonizing Aluminum Alloy Wheel Manufacturing: A Life Cycle Assessment
summary: This study assesses electricity-related greenhouse gas emissions from aluminum alloy wheel manufacturing at Jajce Alloy Wheels d.o.o., Bosnia and Herzegovina, within a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment covering raw materials, inbound tra
content: This study assesses electricity-related greenhouse gas emissions from aluminum alloy wheel manufacturing at Jajce Alloy Wheels d.o.o., Bosnia and Herzegovina, within a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment covering raw materials, inbound transport and manufacturing. Plant-level data and Ecoinvent datasets were used, with results expressed per kilogram of finished product. A descriptive comparison of the 2023 residual-mix and 2024 market-based hydro–wind inventories was complemented by a solar photovoltaic sensitivity analysis holding the 2024 electricity demand and non-electricity inputs constant. Reported electricity-related emissions decreased from 1.864 to 0.030 kg CO2e/kg between the annual inventories, a reduction of about 98.4%, despite higher electricity demand per kilogram. However, differences in annual activity data and background database versions prevent attribution of this change solely to electricity procurement. Total manufacturing emissions decreased from 2.81 to 1.27 kg CO2e/kg, whereas the cradle-to-gate footprint increased from 7.88 to 10.3 kg CO2e/kg alongside a higher raw-material contribution. Under the selected photovoltaic factor, electricity-related emissions were 0.189 kg CO2e/kg, yielding indicative total manufacturing emissions of approximately 1.43 kg CO2e/kg. This sensitivity result is conditional on equivalent electricity delivery boundaries and does not establish a general ranking of renewable technologies. The market-based results reflect renewable electricity procurement documented through Guarantees of Origin, not demonstrated physical grid emission reductions or additional renewable generation. The study illustrates the importance of technology-specific electricity factors and of distinguishing electricity-related results from total manufacturing and cradle-to-gate footprints.

title: Urban Expansion and Land Use/Land Cover Change in the Greater Tamale Area, Ghana, 2000–2025: A Landscape-Metric Analysis with Institutional Perspectives
summary: This study examines urban expansion and land use/land cover (LULC) change in the Greater Tamale Area (GTA), Ghana, between 2000 and 2025, with a projection to 2030. Multi-temporal Landsat data (Landsat 5 TM, Landsat 7 ETM+, Landsat 8 OLI an
content: This study examines urban expansion and land use/land cover (LULC) change in the Greater Tamale Area (GTA), Ghana, between 2000 and 2025, with a projection to 2030. Multi-temporal Landsat data (Landsat 5 TM, Landsat 7 ETM+, Landsat 8 OLI and Landsat 9 OLI-2) were used to classify six epochs into five LULC classes using Maximum Likelihood Classification, with overall accuracies ranging from 87.0% to 96.0% (Kappa 0.825 0.946) compared to independently sampled reference data for each epoch. Built-up area increased from 7,375 ha in 2000 to 24,737 ha in 2025, a 235% increase, while vegetation cover declined by 74% (26,319 ha to 6,931 ha), bare soil declined by 89%, and agricultural land expanded by 68% (29,896 ha to 50,315 ha). The Urban Expansion Intensity Index rose from 0.68%/year (2000 2005) to 2.56%/year (2020 2025). Landscape-level FRAGSTATS metrics reveal an increase in the Largest Patch Index (17.3% in 2000 to 48.4% in 2025) as agricultural and built-up patches merged and a decrease in Simpson's Evenness Index (0.92 in 2000 to 0.70 in 2025) as there was a greater focus on more dominant patches that were larger in size and less frequent across the landscape. The key proximate drivers of expansion identified by the semi-structured interviews with all the nine planning, parks, and traditional landowners are unregulated release of customary land prior to formal planning approval, conversion of urban-core green space, and peri-urban land value increases. With ongoing trends, the built-up area is projected to be around 25,199 ha by 2030. The proposed study model aims to integrate the three key elements urban consolidation zones, protected agricultural and ecological buffers, and regulated peri-urban corridors to enable compact growth in Greater Tamale and other similar cities in Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: From grown to programmed: Optogenetic control of bioactive composition in plants
summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine recognized discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.A landmark 2005 study showed that channelrhodopsin-2 could control neural activity with millisecond precision.This wo
content: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine recognized discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.A landmark 2005 study showed that channelrhodopsin-2 could control neural activity with millisecond precision.This work proved one concept.Light can serve as a precise and programmable switch for specific cellular processes.For most people, light and plants simply mean photosynthesis.Plants use light to acquire energy.But for medicinal and edible plants, can light become a defined input for controlling bioactive composition?Native light regulation has already given us a positive answer.Mulberry stays poor in flavonoids indoors until a low-dose ultraviolet-B (UV-B) supplement arrives [1] .Chinese bayberry raises quercetin only when UV-B reaches it [2] .Dendrobium officinale shifts its flavonoids and polysaccharides with the light level [3] .These examples show that light shapes plant composition.But they also point to a fundamental weakness.Native light regulation is inherently systemic.It cannot precisely tune a single target.To overcome this lack of target specificity, we need a method with a fundamentally different logic.If native light regulation nudges the plant's own photoreceptors and relies on its inherent networks, it asks the plant a question in its own language.Then optogenetics introduces an exogenous light-sensitive switch.We wire this switch directly to a chosen gene.It creates an independent control channel to drive that gene on demand.Conventional agronomy relies entirely on the first approach.It treats light as a continuous, fluctuating environmental input.We measure it, we shade it, and we hope for the best.But this approach only tunes the average, whole-plant condition.It cannot provide a discrete control channel to switch on one specific gene without disturbing the rest of the network.The industrial problem persists: We keep turning a continuous environmental knob without a direct, targeted dial.

title: SALCAfuture – an expert research tool for the generation of life cycle inventories for agricultural products, foodstuffs, and farms
summary: Introduction Agricultural production systems are highly diverse and complex, posing major challenges for life cycle assessment (LCA). SALCAfuture was developed as an expert tool to generate comprehensive life cycle inventories for agricultu
content: Introduction Agricultural production systems are highly diverse and complex, posing major challenges for life cycle assessment (LCA). SALCAfuture was developed as an expert tool to generate comprehensive life cycle inventories for agricultural products, farms, and food systems. Methods This paper presents the concept, methodological foundations, and technical implementation of SALCAfuture. The tool implements the Swiss Agricultural Life Cycle Assessment (SALCA) method and integrates state-of-the-art emission models within a modular, web-based architecture, performing best under Swiss and Western European agricultural conditions due to its current parametrisation. Key features include flexible data collection, specific modelling of emission pathways, and interfaces for linking foreground data with background databases in LCA software. Results The results demonstrate that SALCAfuture enables consistent, transparent, and reproducible LCA calculations across multiple levels of agricultural production, namely farm, animal, field, and crop. Differences in data availability and specifications across these levels are dynamically integrated through flexible data-collection strategies and specific allocation rules (e.g., crop-related mapping of management inputs). Discussion The modular design of SALCAfuture ensures adaptability to diverse research questions and future methodological developments. SALCAfuture thus provides a robust foundation for high-quality environmental assessments in agricultural research.

title: High-speed railway expansion and county economic marginalization: evidence from China
summary: The economic impacts of high-speed railway (HSR) connection on regional development remain contested in the literature. From the perspective of county economic status, this study investigates the county-level effects of HSR connection in Ch
content: The economic impacts of high-speed railway (HSR) connection on regional development remain contested in the literature. From the perspective of county economic status, this study investigates the county-level effects of HSR connection in China and addresses the salient practical challenge of the persistent marginalization of county economy and the weak endogenous development momentum. Using county-level panel data spanning 1999 to 2023, we find that HSR connection has significantly reduced county economic status. Heterogeneity analysis yields three key findings. First, temporally, the negative effect only materialized after 2008, when China initiated large-scale, standardized and networked HSR development. Second, geographically, the negative effect is present only in the eastern and northeastern regions, especially with a stronger negative shock in the northeast, whereas no such effect is observed in the central and western regions. Third, regarding county characteristics, the effect is more pronounced in counties with larger population sizes but absent in those with extremely small ones; it is also typically confined to counties with low industrialization levels, and non-natural-resource-based as well as non-tourism-oriented counties. Mechanism tests demonstrate that HSR connection erodes counties’ endogenous development momentum and perpetuates their economic marginalization mainly through the outflows of labor and capital, as well as the loss of land factors driven by cropland abandonment. Further moderating effect analysis reveals that the location of HSR stations moderates these negative effects. A shorter distance between the HSR station and the county center reinforces the labor and capital outflow channels, thus amplifying the negative effect. However, this moderating effect does not extend to the land factor loss mechanism associated with cropland abandonment.

title: Techno-Economic (TEA) and Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) Assessments of Lignin-Derived Products for a Sustainable Bioeconomy
summary: Lignin, the most abundant natural source of aromatic compounds, represents an underutilized feedstock for the transition from a fossil-based economy to a sustainable circular bioeconomy. This chapter provides a comprehensive guide to the te
content: Lignin, the most abundant natural source of aromatic compounds, represents an underutilized feedstock for the transition from a fossil-based economy to a sustainable circular bioeconomy. This chapter provides a comprehensive guide to the techno-economic analysis TEA) and life cycle assessment of lignin valorization pathways, ranging from well-known commodity applications to high-value emerging opportunities. This chapter presents a systematic framework for evaluating economic feasibility and environmental performance, addressing main methodological challenges such as system boundary definition, co-product allocation, and biogenic carbon accounting. A detailed analysis of valorization routes, including aromatic chemicals (e.g., BTX), carbon fiber, phenolic resins, and bio-based materials, emphasizes the strategic trade-offs between technical maturity, market value, and production volume. Current market projections (2024–2034) and sensitivity analyses recognize capital expenditure and feedstock costs as primary economic drivers, while carbon credit mechanisms and supportive regional policies are assessed as important enablers for overcoming commercialization barriers. Overall, this work offers a pathway for de-risking investment and accelerating the deployment of lignin-based technologies.

title: Schumpeter à l'Européenne
summary: This chapter examines the fundamental Darwinism of economic evolution and the Schumpeterian logic of creative destruction that comes with innovation. Corporations operate within market realities and respond to financial incentives; they can
content: This chapter examines the fundamental Darwinism of economic evolution and the Schumpeterian logic of creative destruction that comes with innovation. Corporations operate within market realities and respond to financial incentives; they cannot be treated as NGOs. Policymakers should focus on stabilizing long-term predictability, establishing robust boundary conditions like the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and actively rewarding forward-leaning green frontrunners while intentionally phasing out brown capitalism.

title: A New Analytical Framework for Industrial Hydrogen Emissions Quantification: Validation and First Results
summary: Hydrogen is anticipated to play a significant role in decarbonizing various industrial sectors, yet hydrogen emissions to the atmosphere contribute to climate warming. To maximize the climate benefits of replacing fossil fuels with hydrogen
content: Hydrogen is anticipated to play a significant role in decarbonizing various industrial sectors, yet hydrogen emissions to the atmosphere contribute to climate warming. To maximize the climate benefits of replacing fossil fuels with hydrogen, emissions must be managed along the entire value chain; however, their true scale is still poorly understood. We present a novel analytical framework that quantifies industrial hydrogen emissions using high-precision gas analyzers and a safe, climate-neutral tracer gas, and validate and demonstrate its performance in an industrial setting. Under optimal conditions, our technique can detect hydrogen releases of only a few grams per hour. Measurements from a conventional hydrogen processing site indicate emissions representing 0.2–0.3% of total production. Engineering estimates indicate that operational venting, particularly from pressure-swing adsorption and trailer filling, could account for as much as ∼1.5% of production if released without combustion. This framework enables accurate, sensitive, and field-deployable quantification of H2 emissions, providing essential data for the industry, policymakers, and the research community to better constrain the climate footprint of hydrogen technologies.

title: Technology–augmented credit creation in supply chain finance: dynamic synergy of AI, blockchain, and data assetization
summary: The coupling of blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and data assetization (DA) offers a transformative pathway for supply chain finance (SCF) to alleviate financing constraints of small and medium–sized enterprises (SMEs). This study
content: The coupling of blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and data assetization (DA) offers a transformative pathway for supply chain finance (SCF) to alleviate financing constraints of small and medium–sized enterprises (SMEs). This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game model integrating blockchain–based certification, AI valuation correction, and dynamic incentive–penalty mechanisms for DA–backed SCF financing. We advance a Technology–Augmented Credit Creation (TACC) framework that extends the information production dimension of intermediation theory through a dynamic information cost function, where blockchain credibility and AI valuation precision synergistically reduce information production costs via the supermodular cost complementarity coefficient. Using system dynamics rate–in–tree modeling with Logistic time–varying parameters calibrated through Latin Hypercube sampling and Sobol global sensitivity analysis, we simulate technology diffusion paths and strategic evolution across three typological scenarios varying in data–density and network–externality intensity. Our findings reveal five structural results: (1) blockchain–AI synergy generates supermodular information cost reductions beyond additive predictions; (2) once the information cost coefficient crosses its critical threshold, the endogenous pledge ratio jumps discontinuously, transforming the static haircut into a dynamic, information–contingent risk premium; (3) technology–mediated intermediation follows a non–monotonic three–phase trajectory (productivity paradox → synergy dividend → mature synergy); (4) network externalities induce path–dependent tipping points that separate synergy convergence from coordination–failure lock–in; and (5) the mechanism core is parsimonious, with three structural parameters explaining 45.8% of outcome variance. These results underpin differentiated, threshold–anchored governance pathways across data–density scenarios. The contributions are threefold: extending banking intermediation theory through TACC; introducing the dynamic synergy accumulation mechanism; and establishing a conditional policy mapping protocol with explicit implementation actors and monitoring thresholds, offering actionable insights for hybrid intelligent systems and multi–agent collaborative governance in SCF risk management practice.

title: Mitigating severe salinity stress in Vicia faba L. via exogenous proline: a climate resilience intervention
summary: Saline irrigation can constrain faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) production in the Nile Delta. A single-season greenhouse pot experiment evaluated plant height, pod number, and leaf and seed nutrient concentrations in the Giza 843 cultivar. The f
content: Saline irrigation can constrain faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) production in the Nile Delta. A single-season greenhouse pot experiment evaluated plant height, pod number, and leaf and seed nutrient concentrations in the Giza 843 cultivar. The five treatments comprised a freshwater control (0.33 dS m −1 ) and irrigation at 6 or 12 dS m −1 , each with or without weekly foliar proline at 500 mg L⁻ 1 . At 12 dS m⁻ 1 , mean pod number was 33.67 with proline and 30.00 without proline. Based on the unrounded pot means, the difference represented a 12.22% increase relative to the untreated saline group and 91.67% recovery of the pod-number deficit relative to the freshwater control. The simultaneous 95% Tukey confidence interval for the difference ranged from − 0.50 to 7.83 pods. At the same salinity, mean leaf potassium and calculated leaf crude protein concentrations were 2.01% and 21.85% with proline, compared with 1.56% and 11.68% without proline. Calculated seed crude protein concentration was 23.91% with proline and 21.57% without proline. The absence of a freshwater-plus-proline treatment limits inference about whether these responses were specific to salinity. Field trials with independent harvest measurements are needed to assess whether the observed responses translate into higher seed yield.

title: The Bright and Dark Sides of CEO Personality in Corporate Sustainability: A Critical Review
summary: Following PRISMA, we review 47 studies on CEO traits and sustainability using the Dark Triad, Positive Self‐regard, and institutional isomorphism frameworks. Narcissism is associated with CSR engagement and greenwashing; hubris with conditi
content: Following PRISMA, we review 47 studies on CEO traits and sustainability using the Dark Triad, Positive Self‐regard, and institutional isomorphism frameworks. Narcissism is associated with CSR engagement and greenwashing; hubris with conditional green innovation; and overconfidence with mixed CSR outcomes and greater decoupling. Machiavellianism is linked to manipulation risks, while psychopathy is negatively associated with sustainability orientation. Core self‐evaluation and related attributes generally support stakeholder‐oriented engagement. Coercive, normative, and mimetic isomorphism help explain these relationships under different governance and financial conditions. The review distinguishes substantive engagement from symbolic compliance and identifies research priorities concerning endogeneity, personality measurement, and cross‐country differences.

title: People Analytics and Employee Retention: A Descriptive Study of Data-Driven Approaches to Understanding and Reducing Employee Turnover
summary: Employee retention is a strategic concern because departures can disrupt operations, weaken institutional knowledge, increase recruitment and training costs, and affect team morale. Traditional practices such as exit interviews, engagement
content: Employee retention is a strategic concern because departures can disrupt operations, weaken institutional knowledge, increase recruitment and training costs, and affect team morale. Traditional practices such as exit interviews, engagement surveys and retrospective turnover reports remain useful but may not identify emerging risks in time. People analytics combines workforce data, statistical analysis and, where appropriate, machine-learning techniques to support better HR decisions. This paper examines the contribution of people analytics to employee retention through a descriptive and conceptual review of the academic literature. It discusses turnover theories, workforce data, analytical methods, HR applications and the ethical conditions required for responsible implementation. It proposes a framework in which data quality and analytical capability support the identification of retention drivers, insights inform fair and targeted interventions, and evaluation supports continuous improvement. The review argues that predictive signals must be interpreted alongside organisational context and employee voice: a model may estimate resignation risk, but it cannot independently establish why an employee may leave or which intervention is appropriate. The paper therefore recommends a human-centred approach that combines descriptive, diagnostic and predictive analysis with managerial judgement, transparency, privacy safeguards and evaluation.

title: Who cares wins? ESG, power, and the climate politics of corporate landlordism
summary: This paper examines the ethical contradictions of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) investment logics in build-to-rent (BTR) and affordable housing development through a study of two large, corporate landlords in the UK. As part of
content: This paper examines the ethical contradictions of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) investment logics in build-to-rent (BTR) and affordable housing development through a study of two large, corporate landlords in the UK. As part of a wider ascendance of ESG, these investment logics are being increasingly integrated into rental housing development. In such instances ESG is integral, and not merely epiphenomenal to financialization processes. Within much of the financial services industry, ESG is understood as a neutral, technical calculus for optimizing returns through neoliberal logics of disclosure, risk pricing and efficient markets. Yet ESG practices in housing blur the lines between risk management and ethics, collapsing any distinction between protecting profits for investors and ‘doing good’ for society or the environment. Through our empirical cases, we demonstrate that in the field of housing, ESG is bound up with the emergence of a new kind of landlord, one that both governs and profits through the integration of ESG logics and techniques. Our analysis shows how ESG functions as a kind of governmentality that reimagines landlord tenant relations by weaving emerging asset management logics into domains of household social reproduction and local environmental governance. As such we offer an understanding of ESG as power, by showing how power flows through the quasi-ethical claims associated with institutional investment in housing. At stake here is the very notion of what ethics is , as ESG discourse collapses the difference between caring for life and caring for capital.

title: Исследование сущности инновационного потенциала АПК как фактора повышения продовольственной безопасности
summary: Введение. В статье определена экономическая сущность инновационного потенциала АПК и его влияние на стабильность продовольственной безопасности. Автор подчеркивает, что инновации в аграрном производстве не только обеспечивают страну достато
content: Введение. В статье определена экономическая сущность инновационного потенциала АПК и его влияние на стабильность продовольственной безопасности. Автор подчеркивает, что инновации в аграрном производстве не только обеспечивают страну достаточным количеством продуктов, но и делают ее менее зависимой от импорта, создавая конкурентную продукцию и улучшая качество жизни населения. Материалы и методы. Методологическую основу исследования составили системный, сравнительный и структурно-функциональный анализ. Визуализация результатов обеспечивалась графическим методом. При разработке предложений использовался метод экономического обоснования. Результаты исследования. Предложено авторское определение инновационного потенциала АПК как совокупности имеющихся ресурсов, а также организационных и правовых возможностей, характеризующих способность и готовность отрасли разрабатывать инновации, осуществлять инновационную деятельность и получать экономический эффект от ее осуществления. Выделены ключевые составляющие инновационного потенциала, а также факторы, оказывающие на него существенное влияние. Обсуждение и заключения. Результаты исследования подтверждают, что развитие АПК на основе инновационного подхода позволит уменьшить издержки на производство сельскохозяйственной продукции, завоевать и удержать доминирующие позиции на рынке, наращивать доходность, расширять финансовую привлекательность и тем самым обеспечить продовольственную безопасность. Introduction. The article defines the economic essence of the innovation potential of the agro-industrial complex and its impact on the stability of food security. The author emphasizes that innovations in agricultural production not only ensure an adequate food supply for the country but also reduce its dependence on imports by creating competitive products and improving the population's quality of life. Materials and Methods. The methodological basis of the study consisted of methods of systems, comparative, and structural-functional analysis. Graphical methods were used to visualize the results, while the method of economic justification was employed in developing the proposals. Results. The authors propose a definition of the innovation potential of the agroindustrial complex as the aggregate of available resources, as well as organizational and legal capabilities, characterizing the sector's capacity and readiness to develop innovations, engage in innovation activities, and derive economic benefits from them. The key components of innovation potential are identified, along with the factors that significantly influence it. Discussion and Conclusions. Research findings confirm that developing the agroindustrial complex through an innovative approach will make it possible to reduce agricultural production costs, capture and maintain dominant market positions, boost profitability, enhance financial attractiveness, and thereby ensure food security.

title: Comparative Architecture and Economics of Terrestrial, Orbital, and Lunar Data Centers
summary: Artificial intelligence is adding accelerator capacity faster than utilities can deliver energized land and grid interconnection, which has made the physical placement of compute a strategic question. Existing studies treat terrestrial powe
content: Artificial intelligence is adding accelerator capacity faster than utilities can deliver energized land and grid interconnection, which has made the physical placement of compute a strategic question. Existing studies treat terrestrial power demand, orbital data centers and lunar surface infrastructure separately, and published estimates differ by an order of magnitude because their system scopes are not stated. This study develops the Terrestrial–Orbital–Lunar AI Infrastructure (TOLAI) reference architecture and evaluates the three domains on a common thermal, economic and workload-placement basis. A radiative heat-rejection model gives a lower bound of 1,516 kg per megawatt on orbital radiator mass. After scope normalization, three of four published estimates fall within a band of 21,100–33,300 kg/MW, while one operator figure lies below the radiator-only floor. A discounted ten-year cost model places orbital infrastructure at 2.44 times terrestrial cost, within the 2.11–3.40 range reported independently; Monte Carlo analysis over sixteen parameters gives a median of 2.25 with a 90% interval of 1.39–3.66, and parity is reached in under 1% of draws. A Compute Geography Score, tested against joint perturbation of weights and scores, places terrestrial infrastructure ahead in every workload profile with probability 98.2% or higher. Orbital parity therefore requires simultaneous progress in launch price, spacecraft lifetime, system mass and hardware qualification cost, and the Moon is better understood as a prospective manufacturing platform than as a computing location.

title: Structural Analysis of AlyQ7 Reveals Two Distinct −1 Subsite Architectures for Substrate Recognition and Ca2+ Dependence in PL7 Alginate Lyases
source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
summary: Polysaccharide lyase family 7 (PL7) alginate lyases are well characterized, yet the structural basis of their catalytic mechanisms remains incompletely understood. AlyQ7, a PL7 enzyme from the marine bacterium Saccharobesus litoralis, exhib
content: Polysaccharide lyase family 7 (PL7) alginate lyases are well characterized, yet the structural basis of their catalytic mechanisms remains incompletely understood. AlyQ7, a PL7 enzyme from the marine bacterium Saccharobesus litoralis, exhibited optimal activity toward polyguluronate at pH 8.0–9.0, 30 °C, 100 mM NaCl and 3 mM CaCl2, and generated dimers, trimers and tetramers endolytically. Docking analyses using an AlphaFold model of AlyQ7 and the crystal structure of AlyQC, a characterized PL7 alginate lyase from Persicobacter sp. CCB-QB2, suggested that conserved Asp/Glu residues at the −1 subsite may contribute to substrate recognition through Ca2+ coordination. Comparative structural and phylogenetic analyses of characterized PL7 alginate lyases further revealed two distinct −1 subsite architectures: an electronegative subsite containing conserved Asp/Glu residues and an electropositive subsite containing conserved Arg/Lys residues. These contrasting substrate-recognition strategies provide a structural framework for guiding PL7 enzyme characterization, rational engineering and tailored biotechnological applications.

title: Can Central Environmental Protection Inspection Promote Corporate Green Transformation?
summary: Whether stringent environmental oversight can induce substantive green transformation in highly polluting enterprises is central to evaluating the effectiveness of China's environmental governance. Taking the implementation of the Central E
content: Whether stringent environmental oversight can induce substantive green transformation in highly polluting enterprises is central to evaluating the effectiveness of China's environmental governance. Taking the implementation of the Central Environmental Protection Inspection (CEPI), launched in 2016, as the policy setting, this study constructs a text‐based measure of corporate green transformation based on annual reports and employs a double machine learning framework to identify the policy effect. The results show that CEPI significantly promotes green transformation among heavily polluting enterprises. Mechanism tests indicate that this effect operates through two complementary channels: CEPI alleviates agency conflicts and managerial short‐termism by improving internal controls, while also strengthening external supervision and market discipline. Heterogeneity analyses show that the effect is stronger among state‐owned enterprises, firms located in central and western regions, and enterprises with higher levels of executive shareholding. Further analysis finds no significant deterioration in the operating performance of regulated enterprises, suggesting that green transformation does not necessarily impose a material short‐term performance penalty. Repeated rounds of CEPI have strengthened the sustainability of firms' green transformation, but have also led to significant declines in local fiscal revenue and tax revenue.

title: Финансовая система Российской Федерации в условиях технологической трансформации: переход к интеллектуальной архитектуре
summary: Введение. Технологическая трансформация изменяет архитектуру финансовой системы Российской Федерации, охватывая государственные и муниципальные финансы, банковский сектор, финансовые рынки, финансы организаций и домохозяйств. Актуальность и
content: Введение. Технологическая трансформация изменяет архитектуру финансовой системы Российской Федерации, охватывая государственные и муниципальные финансы, банковский сектор, финансовые рынки, финансы организаций и домохозяйств. Актуальность исследования обусловлена необходимостью теоретического осмысления новых свойств финансовой системы, формируемых под влиянием финтеха, включая способность прогнозировать риски, адаптировать параметры и обеспечивать непрерывное взаимодействие участников. Цель работы заключается в обосновании концепции интеллектуальной финансовой системы, разработке Индекса финтех-трансформации и выявлении характера воздействия финансовых технологий на качественные характеристики системы. Исследование основано на трудах отечественных и зарубежных учѐных, нормативных правовых актах и аналитических материалах Банка России, Федерального казначейства, ФНС России, МВФ, Всемирного банка и Совета по финансовой стабильности. Применены системный, структурно-функциональный и институциональный подходы, методы сравнительного анализа, систематизации, классификации, контент-анализа, концептуального моделирования и матричного анализа. Результаты исследования. Систематизированы звенья финансовой системы Российской Федерации и применяемые в них финтех-инструменты. Сформулировано понятие интеллектуальной финансовой системы и выделены еѐ признаки: предиктивность, адаптивность, проактивность надзора, бесшовность, верифицируемость и инклюзивность. Предложена архитектура Индекса финтех-трансформации, включающего пять компонентов: проникновение цифровых продуктов, регуляторное признание, инфраструктурный охват, пользовательское принятие и глубину функциональной трансформации. Разработана матрица влияния технологий на прозрачность, открытость, стабильность и устойчивость финансовой системы. Обсуждение и заключения. Установлено, что RegTech и SupTech оказывают наиболее широкое положительное воздействие, тогда как BNPL, DeFi и BigTech-финансы наряду с расширением доступности формируют кредитные, концентрационные и инфраструктурные риски. Сделан вывод о необходимости сочетания количественной оценки технологической зрелости с качественным анализом еѐ последствий для отдельных звеньев и финансовой системы в целом. Эмпирическая апробация индекса и формирование сопоставимой системы частных показателей определены как направления дальнейших исследований с использованием открытых статистических данных. Technological transformation is reshaping the architecture of the financial system of the Russian Federation, encompassing public and municipal finance, the banking sector, financial markets, corporate finance, and household finance.
