title: Graphene Oxide-Based Composite Scaffolds for Bone Tissue Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review on Synthesis, Fabrication Methods, Mechanical Performance, In Vitro Biological Activity, and In Vivo Regenerative Cascades
summary: Bone regeneration in cases of extensive damage remains challenging due to the bone’s limited capacity for self-healing. Graphene Oxide (GO) is a two-dimensional carbon material containing numerous oxygen-functional groups (hydroxyl, epoxy,
content: Bone regeneration in cases of extensive damage remains challenging due to the bone’s limited capacity for self-healing. Graphene Oxide (GO) is a two-dimensional carbon material containing numerous oxygen-functional groups (hydroxyl, epoxy, carboxyl) that holds potential as a nanofiller scaffold in bone composites because it can enhance mechanical properties while actively modulating cellular behavior. However, the existing evidence remains scattered across various types of matrices and heterogeneous testing protocols. This systematic review aims to compile evidence on GO-based composite scaffolds used in bone tissue engineering, covering synthesis, fabrication techniques, physicochemical characterization, mechanical properties, in vitro osteogenic activity, and in vivo regeneration outcomes. The search was conducted in PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Scopus (n = 1,590), plus gray literature (n = 62). After removing duplicates, screening titles and abstracts, and evaluating the full texts, 97 studies met the inclusion criteria. GO is generally synthesized using a modified Hummers method, and this approach consistently enhances the tensile and compressive strengths of the scaffolds. Furthermore, this method also helps improve osteoblast adhesion, ALP activity, the expression of osteogenic genes such as Runx2, BMP-2, and OCN, as well as the in vitro biomineralization process. In vivo, GO-based scaffolds increased bone volume to total volume (BV/TV) by 1.5 to 2 times compared to controls in various matrix types, supporting the integration of angiogenesis and osteogenesis, and promoting macrophage polarization from M1 to M2. These three aspects exhibit dose-dependent response patterns, with the best effects observed at low to moderate GO concentrations, while adverse effects (cytotoxicity, pro-inflammatory responses) occur at higher doses. GO-based scaffolds are a promising option for bone regeneration; however, further validation in large-scale preclinical models is required, and long-term toxicology studies remain necessary to support their translation into clinical trials.

title: Оценка ресурсного потенциала сельскохозяйственных предприятий Ульяновской области на основе анализа основных фондов
summary: Введение. Аграрный сектор российской экономики выполняет функцию одного из ведущих системообразующих факторов, определяющих общую макроэкономическую конъюнктуру. Значимость данной отрасли не ограничивается лишь продовольственным снабжением
content: Введение. Аграрный сектор российской экономики выполняет функцию одного из ведущих системообразующих факторов, определяющих общую макроэкономическую конъюнктуру. Значимость данной отрасли не ограничивается лишь продовольственным снабжением внутреннего рынка: она непосредственно влияет на социальное благополучие сельских территорий и поддерживает устойчивость множества смежных производственно-технологических цепочек. Ключевым звеном, обеспечивающим товарный выход в этой сфере, выступают сельскохозяйственные предприятия, сосредоточивающие преобладающий объѐм производимой продукции. В этом контексте укрепление имущественно-производственной базы таких организаций и гарантированная непрерывность воспроизводственных контуров приобретают статус важнейших приоритетов государственной аграрной политики, рассчитанной на долгосрочную перспективу. При этом центральным элементом всего ресурсного обеспечения аграрных товаропроизводителей остаются их основные фонды, без которых невозможна сколько-нибудь эффективная хозяйственная деятельность. Материалы и методы. Прикладные расчѐты выполнены на основе публичных данных сельскохозяйственных организаций Ульяновской области. Использован комплекс методов: расчѐтно-конструктивный, наблюдение, статистическая группировка, динамические ряды, аналитическое выравнивание, анализ и синтез, экспертная оценка, графический. Оценочная процедура базируется на аккумулировании эмпирических данных, экспертизе количественных и качественных параметров, последующем ранжировании, группировке и установлении корреляционных зависимостей по итогам расчѐтных вычислений. Результаты исследования. Цель настоящего исследования заключается в анализе совокупного объѐма, компонентной структуры и уровня отдачи от использования основного капитала в сельскохозяйственных организациях Ульяновской области. Для реализации поставленной цели в динамике за 2013–2024 гг. изучены стоимостные изменения основных средств, их состав, а также показатели фондообеспеченности, фондовооружѐнности, фондоотдачи, фондоѐмкости и рентабельности фондов. Обсуждение и заключения. Для реализации поставленной цели в работе решались следующие задачи: обобщены теоретические положения об основных фондах как составляющей ресурсного потенциала аграрных организаций; проведена оценка состава, структуры и динамики основных средств сельхозпредприятий региона; проанализирована эффективность их использования и выявлены факторы, оказывающие на неѐ влияние в аграрном секторе. The importance of this industry is not limited only to the food supply of the domestic market: it directly affects the social well-being of rural areas and supports the stability of many related production and technological chains. title: Cone calorimeter assessment and machine-learning prediction of heat-release behavior in corn straw and rosewood biomass pellets
summary: Biomass pellets derived from agricultural and woody residues are increasingly used as renewable solid fuels, making their response to external thermal loading important for both energy utilization and thermal safety. In this study, corn str
content: Biomass pellets derived from agricultural and woody residues are increasingly used as renewable solid fuels, making their response to external thermal loading important for both energy utilization and thermal safety. In this study, corn straw (CS) and rosewood (RW) pellets were evaluated by cone calorimetry under external heat fluxes of 40, 50, and 60 kW m −2 to characterize ignition behavior, heat-release characteristics, and combustion-gas evolution. The critical heat flux (CHF), heat release rate intensity (HRRI), fire growth rate index (FIGRA), fire performance index (FPI), flashover potential (X), and CO and CO 2 evolution were analyzed. Back-propagation (BP), long short-term memory (LSTM), and gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural networks were further compared for time-resolved HRRI prediction. RW exhibited a higher estimated CHF than CS (24.20 versus 13.04 kW m −2 ), whereas its peak HRRI values were higher throughout the tested heat-flux range (290.6-363.8 kW m −2 versus 276.7-303.1 kW m −2 ). FIGRA generally increased and FPI decreased with increasing heat flux, while all X values remained below 10 under the adopted criterion. The recurrent models achieved substantially better internal hold-out performance than the BP model, with GRU obtaining R 2 > 0.996 and RMSE < 0.018. The results reveal differences in estimated ignition threshold and post-ignition heat-release intensity and show that recurrent models incorporating preceding measured HRRI values can support data-assisted characterization of transient biomass-pellet combustion. These findings provide experimental evidence to inform comparative thermal-safety assessments of densified biomass fuels under radiant heating.

title: Agroforestry restoration led by Awajún Indigenous women: biodiversity patterns, carbon stocks and soil quality in degraded landscapes of the Peruvian Amazon
summary: Agroforestry systems (AFS) can serve as restoration strategies that integrate production, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation; however, integrated empirical assessments of restoration-oriented AFS remain scarce in the A
content: Agroforestry systems (AFS) can serve as restoration strategies that integrate production, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation; however, integrated empirical assessments of restoration-oriented AFS remain scarce in the Amazon. This study assessed biodiversity, carbon stocks and soil quality in AFS managed by Awajún Indigenous women in the Peruvian Amazon. Between 2022 and 2024, we compared a 2-year-old restoration AFS (SAF-R), an 8-year-old cacao AFS (SAF-C) and a reference primary forest (FP). SAF-R stored 101.44 Mg C ha⁻¹, 5.2% more than SAF-C (96.39 Mg C ha⁻¹), with soil organic carbon (SOC) accounting for 96.7% of the total; in the absence of a baseline, the fraction attributable to restoration could not be quantified. FP stored 152.02 Mg C ha⁻¹. Tree diversity was higher in SAF-R (Shannon H′ = 2.74; 63 species, including 17 morphospecies) than in SAF-C (H′ = 2.34; 72 species, including 36 morphospecies). Over two years, SAF-R soil organic matter increased by 40.1% and available phosphorus by 34.3%, while exchangeable aluminum decreased by 57.1%; these trends require longitudinal monitoring. The exploration of the convergence between Awajún traditional ecological knowledge and agroecological principles, through the Multiple Evidence Base approach, suggests that AFS led by Indigenous women are promising strategies for multifunctional restoration, with relevance to restoration policies, REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) mechanisms, and nature-based solutions.

title: Surfactant and sensitizer-reductant assessment for enhancing solar energy conversion and storage by employing photogalvanic cells
summary: Sensitizer, reductant and surfactant were used in an authentic investigation plan concerning photogalvanic cells (PG cells) for solar energy. The use of direct sunlight for the studies was both advised and required. The purpose of the resea
content: Sensitizer, reductant and surfactant were used in an authentic investigation plan concerning photogalvanic cells (PG cells) for solar energy. The use of direct sunlight for the studies was both advised and required. The purpose of the research is to improve solar energy conversion into electricity and storage using PG cells. Several parameters were examined in two PG cells using the Alizarin Red-S + Ascorbic acid + NaLS ( PG a System ) and Brilliant Yellow + Ascorbic acid + NaLS ( PG b system ), respectively. The PG a system's Voc and PP have been calculated to be 1075.00 mV and 912.00 mV, respectively. The PG b system's Voc and PP were, respectively, 1120.00 mV and 924.00 mV. The fill factor and conversion efficiency for the PG a system were found to be 0.2731 and 1.8970%, respectively. Fill factor and conversion efficiency for the PG b system have been found to be 0.3422 and 2.1562%, respectively. The impacts of solar energy were investigated by varying the various parameters. With regard to enhancing electrical production and solar energy storage in particular, PG b has shown experimentally that it is an effective system as the desired subject of study based on the aforementioned values.

title: Fire-induced soil water repellency, CO2 efflux and organic carbon storage in sub-Saharan African savanna soils: implications for climate-smart land management
summary: How does fire-induced soil water repellency (SWR) mediate post-fire soil CO 2 efflux and soil organic carbon (SOC) storage in tropical African savannas, and what fire-smart management can conserve SOC? Seasonal bush burning is deeply embedd
content: How does fire-induced soil water repellency (SWR) mediate post-fire soil CO 2 efflux and soil organic carbon (SOC) storage in tropical African savannas, and what fire-smart management can conserve SOC? Seasonal bush burning is deeply embedded across sub-Saharan derived savannas, yet the integrated effects of fire on soil physical, biogeochemical and carbon-cycling processes remain poorly quantified: only 17.0% of global fire-soil research originates from sub-Saharan Africa, and no studies have quantified the SWR–CO 2 –SOC interaction chain in the Nigerian derived savanna. Tropical savannas are prioritised because they store more terrestrial carbon than the atmosphere and vegetation combined, support over one billion people dependent on rain-fed agriculture, and experience fire as an annual management tool rather than an episodic disturbance. Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is emphasised because SOC underpins CSA’s productivity, resilience and mitigation pillars, yet fire-induced SWR introduces uncertainty into the persistence of CSA-induced SOC gains. This review synthesises evidence from 135 unique peer-reviewed studies on three mechanistically coupled soil responses to fire — SWR, CO 2 efflux and SOC storage — established in temperate and Mediterranean literature but under-quantified in tropical Africa. Systematic searches across six bibliographic sources using five Boolean search blocks identified 1,150 records, of which 820 remained after duplicate removal. Inclusion required peer-reviewed quantitative evidence on fire-induced SWR, post-fire CO 2 efflux or SOC effects in tropical, subtropical or semi-arid savanna contexts. Of 360 full-text records assessed, 180 met these criteria; cross-domain deduplication removed 40 duplicate entries across thematic domains, and five methodological references were retained in the inventory but excluded from the evidence corpus, yielding 135 unique studies in the final corpus. Synthesised evidence demonstrates that fire-induced hydrophobicity creates persistent water-repellent layers at 1–3 cm depth, reducing infiltration and increasing surface runoff. SWR dampens post-rainfall Birch-effect CO 2 pulses by restricting matrix wetting, though patchy SWR can enhance efflux by juxtaposing wettable and repellent zones. Fire alters SOC through combustion losses, aggregate destabilisation and erosion-driven export; pyrogenic carbon (PyC) partially offsets these losses, contributing up to 14% of SOC in tropical savannas. A mediation-moderation framework is proposed: fire regime characteristics alter SWR, which mediates effects on CO 2 efflux and SOC storage, moderated by soil texture, slope, rainfall intensity and land use. Priority gaps include: absence of standardised Water Drop Penetration Time (WDPT) and Molarity of Ethanol Droplet (MED) SWR data for Nigerian-derived savannas; lack of continuous CO 2 efflux monitoring in West African savannas; unquantified PyC contributions in West African agricultural soils; unv

title: Plastic Flows and Footprints in Norway’s Sea-Based Aquaculture Sector: A Material Flow Perspective
summary: Marine plastic pollution is an increasing environmental concern, yet aquaculture’s contribution remains poorly quantified despite its rapid expansion and reliance on plastic infrastructure. Limited data on plastic stocks, flows, losses, and
content: Marine plastic pollution is an increasing environmental concern, yet aquaculture’s contribution remains poorly quantified despite its rapid expansion and reliance on plastic infrastructure. Limited data on plastic stocks, flows, losses, and end-of-life (EOL) management constrain effective mitigation and circularity strategies. This study presents a system-wide assessment of plastic use and management in Norway’s sea-based Atlantic salmon aquaculture industry. A static Material Flow Analysis (MFA), informed by data from equipment manufacturers, suppliers, operators, and waste-management stakeholders, quantifies plastic stocks and flows across equipment deployment, use, repair, replacement, environmental losses, and end-of-life treatment. The results indicate annual marine plastic losses of approximately 2737 t, corresponding to 1.2–1.7 kg per tonne of salmon produced. Feed pipes, walkway components, and consumable ropes dominate leakage. Approximately 37,400 t of end-of-life plastics are collected annually, with 42% directed to incineration with energy recovery, 22% landfilled, and limited recovery through recycling. These findings highlight substantial opportunities to strengthen collection, recycling, and resource recovery. This first comprehensive national-scale assessment establishes a quantitative baseline for monitoring and policy development. It demonstrates MFA’s utility for identifying leakage hotspots and supporting Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and circular economy strategies to reduce plastic pollution from aquaculture.

title: Global research on cashless payments: a scopus-based bibliometric analysis
summary: Cashless payments encompass digital services, instruments, and infrastructure enabling transactions without physical cash. This study maps publication growth, productivity, citation performance, collaboration, and thematic patterns in Scopu
content: Cashless payments encompass digital services, instruments, and infrastructure enabling transactions without physical cash. This study maps publication growth, productivity, citation performance, collaboration, and thematic patterns in Scopus-indexed empirical research on cashless payments. The analysis included 1,959 publications and used biblioMagika for bibliometric performance analysis and metadata cleaning, complemented by Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer for co-word analysis and network visualization. Dictionary-based Excel extraction identified mentions of theory, method, technology, and application in titles, abstracts, and keywords, followed by joint manual review. Mean publication-level citations per year complemented cumulative citation indicators for selected authors, institutions, and journals. Publication output expanded substantially after 2019; India recorded the highest publication count, while the United States accumulated the most citations. Co-word analysis identified three clusters: adoption and behavioral foundations of mobile payments; user perceptions, trust, and continued use; and digital payment technologies, financial inclusion, and fraud detection. Mobile wallets, payment applications, cards, contactless technologies, and acceptance-oriented frameworks appeared prominently, while surveys were the most frequently identified research design. The findings describe the reviewed dataset rather than the field as a whole or its intellectual maturity. They suggest opportunities to integrate behavioral, technological, and inclusion perspectives and connect stated intentions with observed usage, service outcomes, and consumer protection across payment contexts.

title: Multi-objective fuzzy solid transportation problem optimization approach for cost-efficient CNG cascade replenishment
summary: The growth of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) use in Maharashtra has increased the burden of replenishing daughter booster stations from pipeline-connected mother stations with mobile high-pressure cascades. Because CNG is a flammable, pressur
content: The growth of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) use in Maharashtra has increased the burden of replenishing daughter booster stations from pipeline-connected mother stations with mobile high-pressure cascades. Because CNG is a flammable, pressurised commodity, this last-mile allocation must balance operating cost, delivery time and transport security risk, which frequently conflict. This study formulates cascade replenishment as a multi-objective fuzzy solid transportation problem in which the third index distinguishes standard cascade trucks from secured, escorted carriers. Imprecise coefficients are represented as triangular fuzzy numbers and converted to crisp values by an accuracy-parameterised ranking whose midpoint coincides with the credibilistic expected value. The integer model is solved exactly for a Pune-region case study with three mother stations, four daughter stations and two carrier types. We enumerate its complete non-dominated set and use it to assess a weighted-sum/ε-constraint frontier. The best-compromise plan is obtained by an exact fuzzy max–min (Zimmermann) programme and cross-checked with TOPSIS and five other multi-objective methods. Constructive integer feasibility, an explicit Lipschitz bound for stability under fuzziness, and invariance of the recommendation under round-trip time and tariff scaling are proved. Sensitivity, Monte Carlo, credibility chance-constrained, scalability and electric-truck analyses show where the recommendation is robust and where it depends on the data. The framework provides CNG distributors with a transparent decision-support tool for security-aware cascade dispatch.

title: Grapevine physiological response to winter pruning and techniques to mitigate rising pruning costs
summary: Winter pruning is crucial for ensuring long-term grape production, managing yield, and enhancing fruit composition. In established vineyards, cane pruning, the most labour-intensive and costly vineyard operation after harvest, poses serious
content: Winter pruning is crucial for ensuring long-term grape production, managing yield, and enhancing fruit composition. In established vineyards, cane pruning, the most labour-intensive and costly vineyard operation after harvest, poses serious challenges because it is a complex manual task requiring skilled labour. Extensive research on pruning, including its principles and effects on grapevine physiology, has been conducted over centuries across wine-growing regions worldwide; however, the application of these principles in commercial vineyard operations remains limited. It also examines the potential for automation in vineyard management and investigates the physiological responses of grapevines to winter pruning. This review provides valuable insights for researchers, viticulturists, and industry stakeholders by bridging the gap between traditional viticultural practices and emerging technology-driven solutions.

title: The effect of storage tank capacity on a solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC)–compressed CO2 energy storage (CCES) combined cycle energy storage and power generation system
summary: CO₂ with its low critical temperature and pressure and high energy storage density, is considered a promising large-scale energy storage technology. However, due to the ineffective utilization of substantial amounts of low-grade waste heat,
content: CO₂ with its low critical temperature and pressure and high energy storage density, is considered a promising large-scale energy storage technology. However, due to the ineffective utilization of substantial amounts of low-grade waste heat, compressed CO₂ energy storage demonstrates relatively lower efficiency compared to chemical energy storage. Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs) exhibit high efficiency, the capability to utilize low-temperature waste heat, and the generation of high-temperature waste heat. These characteristics synergize with compressed CO₂ energy storage to enable mutual utilization of high- and low-temperature waste heat, offering a novel approach for integrating energy storage and power generation systems. This paper proposes a novel SOFC-CO₂ combined cycle energy storage and power generation system, detailing its architecture and operating principles, presenting thermodynamic models for key components, and analyzing the impact of storage tank capacity on system performance. The results demonstrate that the SOFC-CO₂ system effectively enables cascaded utilization of high- and low-temperature waste heat, significantly enhancing the efficiency of both the compressed CO₂ and SOFC systems, and provides a viable technical solution for long-duration compressed gas energy storage.

title: How Price Signals Reshape Renewable Energy Investment and Revenue Logic: A Case Study of China’s Electricity Market
summary: China’s renewable energy sector is entering a new phase of market-oriented transformation. As renewable energy pricing reform deepens and electricity market participation expands, price signals are playing a greater role in project investme
content: China’s renewable energy sector is entering a new phase of market-oriented transformation. As renewable energy pricing reform deepens and electricity market participation expands, price signals are playing a greater role in project investment, revenue formation and asset operations. This paper examines how these changes reshape the investment and revenue logic of renewable energy projects in China from a market-participant perspective. The study adopts a qualitative case-study approach combining policy, institutional and market-mechanism analysis. It examines the evolution of China’s renewable energy pricing framework and the transmission of national reform through provincial electricity markets into project-level price, contract and settlement arrangements. Provincial market data and anonymised project settlement materials are used as supporting evidence to illustrate how market conditions are reflected in project revenues and risks. The analysis shows that market reform does not change the basic financial principles of project valuation, but changes the revenue assumptions underlying investment decisions. Project value increasingly depends on generation profiles, market prices, contract structures, mechanism coverage and settlement rules. Revenue is therefore no longer adequately represented by a single on-grid tariff, but by a constrained combination of market electricity revenue, revenue stabilisation arrangements and other settlement components. This also changes the focus of asset management. Generation volume and equipment availability remain fundamental, while forecasting, contract management, production–trading coordination, settlement analysis and risk management increasingly affect the value and cash flow realised by renewable energy assets. The paper characterises China’s current renewable energy market as a hybrid transition in which stronger market-based price discovery coexists with revenue stabilisation mechanisms. The findings provide practical implications for policymakers, investors and market participants seeking to balance effective price signals, project risk management and the predictability required for long-term renewable energy investment.

title: Grading the evidence linking gut microbiota-associated metabolites to osteoarthritis: a five-axis translational maturity framework for phenotype-stratified trial design
summary: Existing syntheses of the gut-joint axis in osteoarthritis (OA) catalogue metabolite-pathway pairs and appraise individual associations, but they do not record how far each pair has advanced from association through causal chain to clinical
content: Existing syntheses of the gut-joint axis in osteoarthritis (OA) catalogue metabolite-pathway pairs and appraise individual associations, but they do not record how far each pair has advanced from association through causal chain to clinical efficacy, nor the trial-design requirements that follow from that position. Gut microbiota-associated metabolites act as systemic messengers: short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), secondary bile acids, tryptophan-derived indoles and urolithins are sensed through the farnesoid X receptor (FXR), the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) and the G-protein-coupled receptors GPR43 and GPR109A, and modulate epithelial barrier integrity and the lipopolysaccharide (LPS)–TLR4-NLRP3 innate immune axis, linking intestinal dysbiosis to joint inflammation and cartilage degradation. This narrative review makes three contributions. First, it proposes a microbiota-associated metabolite pool disequilibrium framework, centred on ferroptosis and on nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)/NLRP3 signalling, that maps protective and pathogenic pools onto four operationally defined OA phenotypes. Second, it replaces a single ordinal hierarchy with five independent axes, namely certainty of the human association, causal transfer, mechanistic completeness, human intervention efficacy and human target engagement, which are never summed. Third, it sets out four recurrent design considerations for metabolite-directed trials: delivery, stratification, endpoint selection and confounder control. Applied to the 18 claims identified across 55 included studies, the matrix shows that the glycoursodeoxycholic acid (GUDCA)–FXR–glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) cascade is the only chain reaching complete mechanistic dissection, yet it remains untested on both human axes, and that no claim combines an efficacy signal with direct human target engagement. The metabolite ratios discussed here are candidate research biomarkers requiring prospective validation, not decision rules.

title: Структурно-логическая модель учета производственной логистики в условиях цифровой трансформации бухгалтерского учета
summary: Введение. Цифровая трансформация экономики и переход к обществу знаний инициируют смену парадигмы бухгалтерского учета от традиционной регистрационноретроспективной к когнитивной. В условиях высокой автоматизации, роботизации и поточного ха
content: Введение. Цифровая трансформация экономики и переход к обществу знаний инициируют смену парадигмы бухгалтерского учета от традиционной регистрационноретроспективной к когнитивной. В условиях высокой автоматизации, роботизации и поточного характера производства границы между подсистемами учета размываются, а фактор создания добавленной стоимости дематериализуется. Традиционные методы калькулирования, разработанные для дискретного производства, теряют объективность, что создает методологические трудности при расчете финансового результата и распределении прямых и косвенных затрат как составляющих затрат производственной логистики. Целью статьи является разработка структурно-логической модели учета затрат производственной логистики, обеспечивающей объективное формирование финансового результата в условиях когнитивной парадигмы бухгалтерского учета. Материалы и методы. Материалами исследования выступили нормативноправовые акты РФ (в т.ч. ПБУ 10/99, программа «Цифровая экономика РФ»), концепции экономической добавленной стоимости (EVA), а также современные научные труды, посвященные эволюции учетных парадигм и когнитивной функции учета. В работе применены методы системного анализа, структурно-логического моделирования, процессного подхода и сравнительного анализа традиционных и когнитивных подходов к ведению учета. Результаты исследования. Выявлены концептуальные факторы цифровой трансформации учета на примере затрат производственной логистики, способствующие формированию ее структурно-логической модели учета в условиях современного формата бухгалтерского учета, что важно сегодня в свете интеграции разнородных экономических входящих и прогнозного моделирования будущих результатов. Автором предложена трехуровневая структурно-логическая модель учетного обеспечения производственной логистики, которая интегрирует современные IT-инструменты (ИИ, Big Data) для объединения всех технологических и сервисных потоков в эффективную модель учета. Обсуждение и заключения. Разработанная модель дополняет действующие нормативные акты в сфере бухгалтерского учѐта, предлагая гибкий алгоритм учѐтноаналитического обеспечения учѐта затрат для непрерывных производств в условиях автоматизации и роботизации. Внедрение процессной (а не продуктовой) ориентации учета позволяет синхронизировать материальные потоки посредством детального межцехового и внутрицехового учета. Практическая значимость модели заключается в переходе от условного математического расчета к формированию экономически обоснованного финансового результата от продаж. Использование предложенного подхода обеспечит предприятиям прозрачность движения добавленной стоимости, более объективное распределение ресурсов между центрами ответственности и рост общей эффективности производственно-логистических операций. title: A data-efficient machine-learning approach for modeling the photodynamics of all- trans hexatriene based on multireference configuration interaction calculations
summary: Accurate simulations of excited-state photodynamics of polyenes remain challenging due to the high computational cost of multireference electronic-structure methods required to describe the coexistence of ionic and covalent states. In this
content: Accurate simulations of excited-state photodynamics of polyenes remain challenging due to the high computational cost of multireference electronic-structure methods required to describe the coexistence of ionic and covalent states. In this work, active learning together with machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIP) trained on multireference configuration interaction with single and double excitations (MR-CISD) level energies and gradients, is used to enable efficient and accurate nonadiabatic molecular dynamics for all-trans-hexatriene. A compact yet representative training set is constructed by reducing an initial pool of ∼850 k configurations to ∼3 k geometries while preserving the regions of configurational space relevant for the dynamics. The resulting model reproduces the topology of the excited-state potential energy surfaces and yields a physically consistent relaxation mechanism, characterized by a sequential S2 → S1 → S0 pathway and time constants in good agreement with experimental data. Analysis of representative trajectories provides mechanistic insight into the structural factors governing nonadiabatic transitions, and identifies a notably broader and more diffuse structural distribution associated with the S1 → S0 transition in comparison to the more localized S2 → S1 decay pathway. Analysis of the torsional angles around the CC double bonds reveals preferential isomerization at the central C3C4 bond, providing semi-quantitative evidence for the initiation of cis-trans photoisomerization in the hot ground state. The MLIP simulations trained at high-level MR-CISD are extremely efficient, enabling 200 trajectories running up to 800 fs in short time, whereas direct on-the-fly multireference dynamics simulations would be practically impossible at this MR level.

title: The Ultimate Experiment for the Future: Analysing Utopia in Kim Stanley Robinson’s Aurora
source: Word and Text - A Journal of Literary Studies and Linguistics
summary: Frederic Jameson wrote that ‘the best utopias are those that fail the most comprehensively’. By that standard, Kim Stanley Robinson’s Aurora is a perfect example of utopian literature. Divided into seven parts, the novel consists of seven a
content: Frederic Jameson wrote that ‘the best utopias are those that fail the most comprehensively’. By that standard, Kim Stanley Robinson’s Aurora is a perfect example of utopian literature. Divided into seven parts, the novel consists of seven attempts to capture utopia. As each section represents significant changes to the setting, each takes on a new utopian experiment, offering an avenue for critique and change. Aurora’s first experiments exist off Earth, relying on small communities, science, and a careful balance with the environment. In the final experiment, Robinson returns to Earth, arguing that the true path forward entails working carefully to rebuild the planet. In this article, I will outline these seven utopian experiments, their failures, and why, by Jameson’s standards, they are successful. The result of this analysis will explore potential pathways for the future as well as expand upon science fiction’s role in determining these possibilities.

title: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
summary: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in diffe
content: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines. However, so far, a concrete mechanism by which parallel timelines can be created has never been satisfactorily formulated in a way that makes the relationships between the timelines clear. In this paper, we propose such a mechanism based on the Everett (many-worlds) interpretation of quantum mechanics. The timelines in our model are variants of the “worlds” of the Everett interpretation that can connect to each other via the time machine. They are created by the entanglement of the time machine with the environment and the resulting decoherence; therefore, we call them “entangled timelines” or E-CTCs. As the entanglement gradually spreads out to additional systems, the timelines spread out as well, providing a local and well-defined mechanism for branching timelines. The E-CTC model is similar to Deutsch’s familiar D-CTC model but differs from it mainly by imposing a different consistency condition, based on pure states, which allows the information about the entanglement to be preserved. These differences allow us to create a clearer practical definition of the timelines and avoid some of the surprising consequences of the D-CTC model’s non-linear evolution.

title: Developmental bias explains the evolutionary trend towards simple leaf shapes
summary: The relative influence of developmental bias and natural selection on evolutionary outcomes remains a central, unresolved question in evolutionary biology. Here, we combine large-scale phylogenetic trees with herbarium data to confirm that,
content: The relative influence of developmental bias and natural selection on evolutionary outcomes remains a central, unresolved question in evolutionary biology. Here, we combine large-scale phylogenetic trees with herbarium data to confirm that, across the evolutionary history of angiosperms, transitions from complex to simple leaf shapes have occurred at a significantly higher rate than the reverse. To investigate whether this directional trend reflects an underlying developmental bias, we simulate evolutionary transitions by introducing random mutations into a well-established computational model of leaf development. Despite excluding selection, the transition rates produced by the model closely align with those observed in the phylogenetic data. This agreement indicates that a strong developmental bias, reflecting the relative ease with which gene regulatory networks generate simple over complex leaves, has played a major role in shaping the evolution of leaf morphology. Our findings echo recent work showing that similar biases towards simplicity influence the evolution of molecular structures, including RNA secondary structures and protein quaternary assemblies. Together, these results suggest that a developmental bias favouring simplicity may be a widespread and general feature of evolutionary systems.

title: Atomically Resolving Magnetic Triple- q State in Antiferromagnetic Mn Monolayer Interfaced with Bismuthene
summary: Two-dimensional bismuthene with its unique honeycomb lattice and strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC) is anticipated to have an impact on monolayer (ML) noncollinear antiferromagnets. Here, we have systematically investigated the magnetic tripl
content: Two-dimensional bismuthene with its unique honeycomb lattice and strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC) is anticipated to have an impact on monolayer (ML) noncollinear antiferromagnets. Here, we have systematically investigated the magnetic triple-q (3Q) state in bismuthene-covered (1 × 1)-Mn/Ag(111) by exploiting spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy (SP-STM) and density-functional theory (DFT). The characteristic checkerboard and stripe spin contrasts of noncollinear 3Q spin texture have been atomically resolved by SP-STM. Furthermore, the magnetic switching between magnetic checkerboard and stripe patterns and the absence of their rotational domains have been revealed in field-dependent SP-STM measurements. By considering higher-order Heisenberg exchange interactions along with SOC, the magnetic 3Q3 state turns into the lowest-energy ground state of bismuthene/(1 × 1)-Mn/Ag(111), where a uniaxial magnetic anisotropy arises from a local shift of atomic Mn spin relative to bismuthene lattice site. Our experimental and theoretical results therefore uncover the important role of bismuthene in the noncollinear antiferromagnetism of an AFM monolayer.

title: From naïve certainty to intellectual humility: how an AI-SSI curriculum reshapes high school students’ socioscientific orientations
source: Disciplinary and Interdisciplinary Science Education Research
summary: This study examines the effects of an ENACT model-guided, Artificial Intelligence-related Socioscientific Issues (AI-SSI) curriculum on high school students’ socioscientific orientations (SO). While SSI-based pedagogy is recognized for enha
content: This study examines the effects of an ENACT model-guided, Artificial Intelligence-related Socioscientific Issues (AI-SSI) curriculum on high school students’ socioscientific orientations (SO). While SSI-based pedagogy is recognized for enhancing scientific literacy and moral development, its specific effects within the domain of AI ethics remain underexplored. Employing a mixed-methods pretest-posttest design, this research investigated the influence of a 10-week AI-SSI intervention on 45 Chinese tenth-graders’ SO. Findings revealed significant pre-to-post declines in self-reported SO across all four dimensions --- ecological worldview, social and moral compassion, socioscientific accountability, and scientific evidence views. However, qualitative interview data suggest that these declines reflect epistemic development and the emergence of intellectual humility: students transitioned from simplistic, absolutist views toward more nuanced, conditional, and critical understandings of AI-SSI dilemmas. These findings imply that initial decreases in self-reported competencies may signal deeper epistemic development, including enhanced critical reasoning and more calibrated self-awareness of complexity. This study underscores the need for assessment strategies that can capture such intricate cognitive transformations. Overall, the findings suggest that AI-SSI instruction, when implemented under supportive conditions, has the potential to foster intellectual humility and nuanced ethical reasoning—dispositions that are important for navigating an AI-saturated world. These findings offer preliminary implications for AI-SSI, civic literacy, and responsible innovation.
