title: Beyond hydraulic diffusion: reaction front propagation and timescales in metamorphic (de)volatilization processes
summary: Metamorphic (de)volatilization reactions play fundamental roles in many geodynamic processes and are frequently associated with propagating reaction fronts, yet the mechanisms controlling front propagation remain poorly constrained. Here, w
content: Metamorphic (de)volatilization reactions play fundamental roles in many geodynamic processes and are frequently associated with propagating reaction fronts, yet the mechanisms controlling front propagation remain poorly constrained. Here, we derive new analytical solutions for fluid pressure-driven (de)volatilization reaction fronts in porous rocks. The solutions predict that reaction-zone width increases with the square root of time, a scaling that arises from mass conservation across the moving reaction front rather than from classical hydraulic pore-pressure diffusion. Front propagation is governed by an effective diffusivity that depends on both hydraulic and chemical parameters, including reaction-induced density changes. Unlike conventional hydraulic diffusivity, which neglects reaction-induced density variations and generally predicts much faster propagation, the effective diffusivity captures the retardation of reaction fronts caused by density changes, with larger reaction-induced density changes producing slower propagation. In addition to a single-front formulation, we derive an analytical solution for two simultaneously propagating, coupled reaction fronts. The fronts are dynamically linked through mass conservation, preventing independent propagation and causing the leading front to advance faster than the trailing front. Both the single- and two-front solutions closely match numerical simulations. Application of the two-front model to published gypsum dehydration experiments shows that accounting for pore-water to pore-vapor transitions yields more realistic permeability estimates than single-front models. Application to natural metamorphic reactions predicts permeabilities between 10 −18 and 10 −24 m 2, consistent with independent experimental, geophysical, and geological estimates. By analogy, the analytical framework can also be extended to chemically controlled reaction fronts governed solely by chemical diffusion. The analytical solutions provide a quantitative framework for estimating the timescales of natural and experimental (de)volatilization processes involving propagating reaction fronts.

title: Omics insights: In situ tools shed light on deep-sea microbial activities
summary: Extreme conditions, including darkness, elevated hydrostatic pressure, low temperature, and limited nutrient availability create unique deep-sea environments. Previous studies on deep-sea organisms/microorganisms have not only revealed the
content: Extreme conditions, including darkness, elevated hydrostatic pressure, low temperature, and limited nutrient availability create unique deep-sea environments. Previous studies on deep-sea organisms/microorganisms have not only revealed the metabolic characteristics of various deep-sea life forms and their dynamic communities but also contributed to the development and utilization of deep-sea biological resources. Genomic studies of deep-sea organisms heavily rely on high-quality samples. However, environmental alterations during sample retrieval, from the deep sea to the research vessel, lead to microbial community changes and RNA degradation. Hence, various automatic devices are developed for in situ fixation of samples and extraction of nucleic acids in the deep-sea environment, with subsequent processing conducted onboard. In recent years, in situ metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metaproteomics (omics) have become powerful tools for exploring the metabolic activities and periodicity of the deep-sea inhabitants, which can provide insights into survival mechanisms, element cycles, and dynamic changes of the “microbial dark matter” in the deep ocean. This paper reviews the necessity of deep-sea in situ omics, outlines the development of ecological monitoring equipment for omics research in the deep sea, and discusses its applications in revealing novel genes and active substances in the deep sea, as well as understanding the distribution and ecological functions of deep-sea microorganisms. These in situ omics approaches are poised to revolutionize deep-sea research, enabling more accurate models of ecosystem dynamics.

title: A multi-species stem taper and volume model for 41 tree species groups from 150 years of forest experiments
summary: Stem taper and volume models are typically developed only for commercially important and data-rich species. Many species of increasing interest for forest inventory and carbon accounting lack specific models, and stem taper and volume are i
content: Stem taper and volume models are typically developed only for commercially important and data-rich species. Many species of increasing interest for forest inventory and carbon accounting lack specific models, and stem taper and volume are instead estimated using a presumed similar species. This study presents a multi-species stem taper and volume modelling system, demonstrated on a dataset of 743,045 stem sections from 41,129 trees in 41 species groups measured across 150 years of Danish forest experiments. Six candidate functions were assessed, and the Kozak (2004) Model 02 was selected and extended with species-level random effects, per-species optimisation of the inflection point parameter, and variance and autocorrelation structures. To our knowledge, species-level random effects have not previously been used in taper modelling. The mixed-effects design delivered species-specific taper predictions for every group, including the most data-sparse, within a single operational model. The final model generalised well to unseen plots in the 23 sufficiently replicated species groups, and stem volumes produced by numerical integration of the fitted taper curve agreed with section-based Smalian volumes. Volume predictions cover the stem only, so modelling branch volume is a natural next step, enabling estimation of total aboveground biomass. The framework is expandable to new species or regions and allows the estimation of merchantable volume to any top-diameter limit in mixed-species forests.

title: The JWST Early Release Science Program for Direct Observations of Exoplanetary Systems. VIII. Patchy Forsterite and Enstatite Clouds in the Atmosphere of VHS 1256 b, Retrieval Lessons Learned and Outlook to the Future
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope defines a new era for the data-driven approach to retrieval modeling, which has become a cornerstone tool for the statistical inference of exoplanetary and brown dwarf properties. The Early Release Science pro
content: The James Webb Space Telescope defines a new era for the data-driven approach to retrieval modeling, which has become a cornerstone tool for the statistical inference of exoplanetary and brown dwarf properties. The Early Release Science program #1386 observations of VHS 1256 b represent a huge jump in data quality, data quantity, and spectral coverage for such objects. VHS 1256 b is a young, planetary-mass and extremely variable companion that populates the enigmatic L/T cohort of substellar atmospheres. In this first retrieval analysis of the full 1–18 μ m data set, we apply the Brewster retrieval framework to the NIRSpec and MIRI spectroscopic observations of VHS 1256 b, exploring a variety of cloud species and structures. Using ΔBIC, we find that the data are best described by a forsterite (Mg 2 SiO 4) and enstatite (MgSiO 3) cloud combination. Our analysis shows a strong preference for patchy silicate cloud coverage, which aligns with VHS 1256 b’s extensive and well-documented spectral variability. Our retrieval is able to place constraints on the abundances of H 2 O, CO, CO 2, CH 4, as well as NH 3. We also show that the retrieved parameters are sensitive to the data used and the relative signal-to-noise ratios between data from different instruments. We conclude with the next steps for the wider retrieval community to better understand young and cloudy exoplanetary atmospheres.

title: Beyond the Carbon Ceiling: Neural Econometric Decoupling of GCC Energy Portfolios—Bridging Growth Theory and Deep Learning
summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states have to find a way to balance their reliance on hydrocarbon resources and their ambitious aims on moving to renewable energy (for instance, the Saudi Vision 2030). Despite the policies in place, the
content: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states have to find a way to balance their reliance on hydrocarbon resources and their ambitious aims on moving to renewable energy (for instance, the Saudi Vision 2030). Despite the policies in place, the implementation of renewable energy technologies in the region is relatively low, indicating that more needs to be understood about the reasons behind the use of renewable energy. The present research analyzes the macroeconomic determinants of renewable energy consumption as a share of total final energy consumption, expressed as a fraction in [0, 1], sourced from WDI/IEA, in the six GCC states over 2000–2024 using a combination of panel econometric techniques and machine learning. Panel data were constructed from data from the World Bank and the International Energy Agency. The econometric results show that R&D expenditure and trade openness are the two most important determinants of renewable energy consumption, which jointly explain about 53.5% of the variation (adjusted R2 = 0.535), rising to about 63% under pooled OLS (adjusted R2 = 0.629); the difference reflects the absorption of cross-country heterogeneity by the fixed effects rather than a difference in the estimated associations. A complementary machine learning exercise yields the same ranking of predictors, with R&D expenditure as the most important predictor followed by trade openness. No statistically meaningful relationship was found among GDP, foreign direct investment, inflation, and renewable energy consumption in the final models due to the structural characteristics of GCC economies. Among the machine learning models, XGBoost was the strongest tree-based specification (out-of-sample RMSE = 0.031, R2 = 0.451), with random forest a close second (RMSE = 0.032, R2 = 0.425); a deep neural network delivered a modest exploratory improvement (RMSE = 0.029, R2 = 0.479) without altering the ranking of determinants. All models outperformed the OLS, random-walk, country-mean, and AR(1) benchmarks on the identical test window. Sub-period analysis also indicates that the relationships between R&D expenditure and trade openness became stronger after 2015, which coincides with the introduction of national energy transition strategies in the GCC. The study implies that innovation in terms of technology as well as the open nature of economy could promote energy transition in the region, whereby a high number of investments in research and development are required as well as deeper international trade linkages, which might support the acceptance of the green energy approach. The analysis establishes conditional associations, not causal effects.

title: An effective topology-transfer nuisance for Genie-based neutrino-argon semi-inclusive analyses: a methodological proposal with MicroBooNE-constrained diagnostic
summary: Liquid-argon TPC oscillation analyses increasingly split samples into proton-tagged (Np) and proton-less (0p) topologies at the $$\sim 35\,\text {MeV} $$ ∼ 35 MeV tracking threshold, but the standard Genie Reweight library contains no dial
content: Liquid-argon TPC oscillation analyses increasingly split samples into proton-tagged (Np) and proton-less (0p) topologies at the $$\sim 35\,\text {MeV} $$ ∼ 35 MeV tracking threshold, but the standard Genie Reweight library contains no dial that transfers events across this boundary. We propose a single empirical nuisance parameter $$f_\textrm{mig}$$ f mig that fills this gap as a per-event reweight on nominal Genie output, implementable without event regeneration. The parameter is presented as a methodological diagnostic: an effective topology-transfer surrogate that absorbs an unspecified combination of near-threshold proton mismodelling effects (proton-side FSI, nucleon-momentum distribution, RES $$Q^2$$ Q 2 shape, MEC kinematic shape), rather than a measurement of any single microscopic mechanism. As a physically motivated reference scale, the residual position-dependent mean-field energy loss absent from Genie ’s cascade is estimated from the $$^{40}$$ 40 Ar density profile to be a few percent, consistent with proton-transparency differences reported between cascade and transport generators on MicroBooNE data. The primary empirical constraint is a direct scan on the MicroBooNE simultaneous CC 0 p / Np differential cross-section release with no sector-weight regularisation: $$\hat{f}_\textrm{mig} = 0.093 \pm 0.024$$ f ^ mig = 0.093 ± 0.024, $$3.8\sigma $$ 3.8 σ (Wilks) / $$3.2\sigma $$ 3.2 σ (empirical). A supporting NC $$\Delta $$ Δ radiative sideband fit gives $$\hat{f}_\textrm{mig} = 0.050^{+0.029}_{-0.022}$$ f ^ mig = 0. 050 - 0.022 + 0.029, conditional on sector-weight priors. Both datasets share flux/detector systematics and are corroborating rather than statistically independent. A useful diagnostic by-product is that introducing $$f_\textrm{mig}$$ f mig relieves a compensatory CCRES sector-weight suppression in migration-blind fits. The extracted parameter is best understood as a flux-integrated effective nuisance direction for the MicroBooNE BNB configuration, suitable as a candidate Genie dial in future LArTPC analyses pending detector-level validation.

title: Testing gravitational-wave signal from verification binaries with space-based gravitational-wave detectors
summary: Space-based detectors will open the millihertz band to survey . (VBs) is a key to verifying the performance of space-based detectors because its parameters are known from electromagnetic observations and it is expected to be a detectable so
content: Space-based detectors will open the millihertz band to survey . (VBs) is a key to verifying the performance of space-based detectors because its parameters are known from electromagnetic observations and it is expected to be a detectable source of . We evaluated 73 VBs, computing their detection prospects and parameter estimation precision for individual detectors and networks. Among single detectors, DECIGO shows the highest sensitivity, detecting 71 sources at signal-to-noise ratio ρ ≥ 5, compared to 42 for LISA, 32 for Taiji, and 27 for TianQin, while the full TianQin + LISA + Taiji + DECIGO network improves this to 73 detectable sources. For parameter estimation, individual detectors achieve median precisions on the order of ∼ 10 − 2 − 10 − 1 M ⊙ for chirp mass, ∼ 1 kpc for distance, ∼ 1 − 17 deg for inclination and ∼ 10 − 4 − 10 − 2 deg 2 for sky localization. The complete TianQin + LISA + Taiji + DECIGO network enhances these constraints substantially, reducing the median uncertainties to approximately ∼ 10 − 2 M ⊙ in chirp mass, ∼ 10 − 2 kpc in distance, ∼ 1 deg in inclination and ∼ 10 − 4 deg 2 in sky localization. The upcoming space-based detectors, especially their networks, have outstanding observational capabilities for , which will advance our research on multi-messenger astronomy and deepen our understanding of in the Milky Way. Space-based detectors, such as TianQin, LISA, Taiji, and DECIGO, will open the millihertz frequency band, promising to detect tens of thousands of Galactic . Among these, , which are systems already observed electromagnetically, are crucial for validating detector performance. Our results demonstrate that among single detectors, DECIGO offers the highest detection sensitivity, identifying 70 sources at ≥ 5, followed by LISA with 41, Taiji with 31, and TianQin with 26. In parameter estimation, DECIGO provides the best median sky localization precision with ∼ 3.9 × 10 − 3 deg 2 , but exhibits larger average uncertainties for chirp mass and distance due to its sensitivity to fainter populations. Taiji achieves the tightest constraints on chirp mass with median σ ℳ = 1.47 × 10 − 2 M ⊙ and distance with median σ d = 0.172 kpc . However, multi-detector networks (e.g., TianQin+LISA+Taiji+DECIGO) significantly enhance the detection count, especially for faint sources, and dramatically improve parameter estimation. For instance, such a network can localize sources to ∼ 10 − 5 deg 2 and measure chirp masses with $$0.01% precision for high-SNR systems like J0806. This work underscores the scientific necessity of operating a coordinated network of space-based observatories to maximize the scientific return from Galactic binary populations.

title: Selenoxanthylyl radicals – characterization and conPET catalysis
summary: Selenoxanthylium photocatalysts are designed based on their ground-state properties to enable low-energy photon photocatalysis, although reductive quenching of their excited state generates persistent selenoxanthylyl radicals. Herein, we re
content: Selenoxanthylium photocatalysts are designed based on their ground-state properties to enable low-energy photon photocatalysis, although reductive quenching of their excited state generates persistent selenoxanthylyl radicals. Herein, we report the characterization of selenoxanthylyl radicals by EPR, cyclic voltammetry, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and TD-DFT calculations, together with their application in consecutive photoinduced electron-transfer (conPET) catalysis.

title: Momentum-space mismatch enables non-Hermitian valley filtering
summary: Valley-selective transport is central to valleytronics, but existing valley filters are largely tailored to specific materials or lattice geometries, motivating the search for a common microscopic ingredient. Here we identify the momentum-s
content: Valley-selective transport is central to valleytronics, but existing valley filters are largely tailored to specific materials or lattice geometries, motivating the search for a common microscopic ingredient. Here we identify the momentum-space mismatch between the band-touching nodes of a system and its dissipative reservoir as a route to node-selective non-Hermitian skin effects (NHSE). When the two are coupled, the mismatch is encoded in the retarded self-energy, producing node-dependent dissipation and contrasting quasiparticle lifetimes. The resulting effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian exhibits opposite point-gap spectral winding at the two nodes, giving rise to a node-resolved NHSE with strongly asymmetric dissipation rates: one node decays rapidly into the reservoir while the other survives over the device, yielding a nearly valley-polarized outgoing current. We demonstrate this mechanism in a minimal one-dimensional dimer chain and in two-dimensional systems hosting genuine Dirac valleys, including π -flux rectangular and honeycomb lattices. In all cases, transport calculations yield nearly 100% valley polarization, while remaining gate-tunable and robust against disorder and edge imperfections. Our results show that momentum-space mismatch provides a route to non-Hermitian valley filtering.

title: Chemomechanical and thermomechanical weakening in muscovite mica and related materials: a review
summary: Muscovite mica is a critical mineral in geoscience and materials science due to its layered structure that underlies its beneficial properties. In this review, we highlight recent advancements in the chemomechanical and thermomechanical wea
content: Muscovite mica is a critical mineral in geoscience and materials science due to its layered structure that underlies its beneficial properties. In this review, we highlight recent advancements in the chemomechanical and thermomechanical weakening of muscovite mica and related materials, focusing on the stages and mechanisms of degradation with and without mechanical stimuli at the macroscale and microscale, as well as analytical and atomistic models that provide mechanistic and interfacial-structure context for the reported trends. By synthesizing published findings across fluid environments and temperatures, we discuss how interlayer bonding and stress-corrosion kinetics influence structural evolution. Finally, we consider the integration of in-situ testing and machine learning to accelerate discovery, providing essential insights for geological fault modeling and the engineering of advanced layered materials. Overall, this review emphasizes microscale mechanical test methods and simulations as means to better elucidate bulk mechanical behavior and structural changes in mica under extreme environmental conditions.

title: Single‐Device Bidirectional Photonic Synapses: From Polarity Switching to Adaptive Neuromorphic Computing
summary: Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single-device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses
content: Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single-device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses within the same physical element, provide a compact platform for adaptive photonic computing. However, the diverse architectures, regulation strategies, and physical mechanisms reported for BPS have hindered systematic understanding and quantitative comparison. Here, we establish a unified Structure-Regulation-Mechanism-Function (S-R-M-F) framework to organize single-device BPS from device architecture and polarity regulation to physical mechanisms, synaptic functions, quantitative benchmarks and neuromorphic applications. We further distinguish physical photoresponse polarity from its functional interpretation in synaptic computing and highlight key considerations including energy consumption, reproducibility, variability, and system-level scaling. Finally, we identify the transition from empirically observed PPC-NPC switching toward predictive, deterministic, programmable and reproducible operation as a key direction for future BPS development, with physics-informed modeling and closed-loop control offering promising routes toward adaptive photonic neuromorphic hardware.

title: Band-dependent charging governs electrochemical energetics in two-dimensional materials
summary: Accurately predicting the electrochemical energetics of two-dimensional (2D) materials as electrode potential varies is critical for understanding interfacial processes underlying electrocatalysis and rechargeable batteries. However, the co
content: Accurately predicting the electrochemical energetics of two-dimensional (2D) materials as electrode potential varies is critical for understanding interfacial processes underlying electrocatalysis and rechargeable batteries. However, the conventional single-quadratic model (CSQM), widely used for metallic/semimetallic systems, cannot capture distinct charging behaviors arising from separated valence and conduction bands in semiconductors. Here, we reveal band-dependent charging as a general feature of 2D materials and establish its connection to their intrinsic electronic characteristics. We therefore develop a dual-quadratic model (DQM) that separately captures valence- and conduction-band charging behaviors, enabling continuous prediction of potential-dependent energetics across metallic, semimetallic, and semiconducting 2D materials. Using only 6 discrete grand canonical density functional theory (GC-DFT) calculations, the DQM predicts potential-dependent adsorption energy profiles matching densely sampled GC-DFT benchmarks (RMSE ~ 0.055 eV), whereas the CSQM exhibits errors of up to 80%. These findings establish band-dependent charging as a governing principle of electrochemical energetics in 2D materials.

title: Comprehensive spa care as a multimodal intervention for healthspan-related outcomes: A scoping review
summary: Population ageing has increased interest in interventions that maintain function and wellbeing across the life course. This scoping review mapped evidence on spa care as a comprehensive multimodal intervention relevant to healthspan-related
content: Population ageing has increased interest in interventions that maintain function and wellbeing across the life course. This scoping review mapped evidence on spa care as a comprehensive multimodal intervention relevant to healthspan-related outcomes. A protocol was developed a priori, and database searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus on 27 May 2026 for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Adult studies focusing on spa care, balneotherapy, thermal medicine or spa rehabilitation and addressing healthy ageing, functional health, frailty-related outcomes, psychosocial, or physiological and metabolic outcomes were eligible. Ten studies were included. The evidence covered musculoskeletal function and pain, sarcopenia-related indicators, psychosocial wellbeing and sleep, selected metabolic and inflammatory markers, cardiovascular safety, and drinking cures. Several studies evaluated multicomponent spa or spa-rehabilitation programmes, whereas others examined individual spa-related components, including drinking cures or balneotherapy added to standard care. Most findings indicated short-term improvements in symptoms, function, wellbeing or selected biomarkers, but the studies were heterogeneous in population, design, intervention content and follow-up. No study directly assessed healthspan, mortality, biological age, lifespan, or long-term chronic disease incidence. The evidence therefore supports a cautious interpretation of spa care as a clinically relevant, potentially healthspan-oriented field rather than a proven longevity intervention. Future research should distinguish comprehensive spa programmes from individual components, use longer follow-up, standardised healthspan-related outcomes and detailed reporting of intervention components.

title: Proton Relays Versus Direct Transfer in Polyketide Cyclisations: Solution Rejection, Bioinspired Complexes, and Enzyme-Pocket Rescue
summary: Nature builds the polycyclic cores of tetracycline and aromatic polyketide antibiotics by folding linear polyketide chains through regioselective aldol and Claisen cyclisation cascades.Whether the proton transfers driving these cascades pro
content: Nature builds the polycyclic cores of tetracycline and aromatic polyketide antibiotics by folding linear polyketide chains through regioselective aldol and Claisen cyclisation cascades.Whether the proton transfers driving these cascades proceed by direct collision with a base or by hopping along hydrogen-bonded solvent wires (a Grotthuss proton relay) remains unresolved.Here we test when proton relays fail and when they prevail in a three-seed pilot diagnostic evaluation across 1,142 reaction paths spanning solution models, bioinspired complexes, and an enzyme active site.In unconstrained solution, a free base approaches the carbon acid to direct contact, making direct proton transfer outcompete multi-water wires whose assembly and charge separation impose an energetic cost.This outcome reverses once direct contact is blocked or the proton wire is preorganised.Screening three bioinspired levers shows that Grotthuss relays dominate when the base is held at least 5 Å from the carbon acid, when a bifunctional shuttle bridges donor and carbonyl oxygen simultaneously, or when the wire is preorganised on a rigid triol ring.Translating these rules into unconstrained, non-peptide catalysts reveals that chelating a diketone to MgCl 2 or ZnCl2 with a bulky pyridine base (2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylpyridine) keeps the base off the carbon acid, allowing a single bridging water to lower the median barrier (suggestive at three seeds).Finally, a 241-atom cluster of TcmN (PDB 3TVQ) confirms that the enzyme pocket blocks direct carbon-acid transfer to Asp57 unless bridged by a cavity water, while a two-water wire shuttles protons to His128.

title: From economic recovery to strategic necessity: Shifting government and media narratives legitimating extractivism in Greece
summary: This paper examines how extractive development has been publicly legitimated across changing political-economic conjunctures in Greece. It compares three fields: gold-copper mining in Skouries/Halkidiki, offshore hydrocarbon exploration aro
content: This paper examines how extractive development has been publicly legitimated across changing political-economic conjunctures in Greece. It compares three fields: gold-copper mining in Skouries/Halkidiki, offshore hydrocarbon exploration around Crete, and antimony and critical-raw-material development in Chios. A qualitative longitudinal analysis combines a purposive sample of 31 articles from the national mainstream news outlets Kathimerini and Proto Thema with 23 government-related texts and supplementary corporate, movement and licensing material. The findings identify cumulative layering and re-hierarchisation of justificatory repertoires. Investment, employment and growth persist, but legal certainty, energy security, sovereignty, green transition, supply security and technological autonomy become progressively more central. A parallel change concerns modal force, understood here as the degree of necessity attributed to extraction: extraction moves from being framed mainly as an economic opportunity, through crisis-era necessity, towards a strategic and technological requirement. Government-media convergence is particularly visible after 2019 and around energy security after 2022, while environmental and democratic counter-frames remain visible, especially in Kathimerini. The paper argues that successive crises amplify particular legitimating rationales and reshape the terms on which extractive futures are contested.

title: Hybrid Nanofluid-Assisted Minimum Quantity Lubrication for Machining of Ti-6Al-4V Research Framework and Hypothesis Development
source: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology
summary: The conventional fluids have been in use for a very long period in the manufacturing industry for cooling and lubrication of various machines involved in the machining processes. However, in the recent past, the focus on enhancing productiv
content: The conventional fluids have been in use for a very long period in the manufacturing industry for cooling and lubrication of various machines involved in the machining processes. However, in the recent past, the focus on enhancing productivity and sustainability has been growing and therefore there is a demand for more innovative lubrication processes. The soluble machine oils are often utilized for cooling purpose but the focus nowadays lies on alternative lubrication techniques. This paper deals with the use of alternative lubrication processes with the objective of guiding future research related to sustainable machining. Nanofluids along with minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) technique are being in trend and their use is discussed in this paper. In addition, the review of the work done by other researchers with regard to machining of difficult-to-machine super alloys with the same technique is presented and along with-it research framework and hypotheses are proposed.

title: The CO-N2 intermolecular potential energy surface revisited
summary: We developed a new ab initio ground-state intermolecular potential-energy surface (IPES) for the CO-N2 complex evaluated veryefficiently with the use of the AutoPES program. The global minimum of the potential corresponds to a planar geomet
content: We developed a new ab initio ground-state intermolecular potential-energy surface (IPES) for the CO-N2 complex evaluated veryefficiently with the use of the AutoPES program. The global minimum of the potential corresponds to a planar geometry characterized by the center-of-mass distance R = 4.153 \AA\ and the angles theta1 = 109.9 degrees and theta2 = 162.2 degrees between the COand N2 axes and the vector R, with a binding energy of De = 118.2 cm-1. The accuracy of the potential was assessed by calculating the rovibrational energy levels of the complex. The root-mean-square deviations from the experimental values are 0.096 cm-1 for CO-orthoN2 and 0.065 cm-1 for CO-paraN2. Additionally we compared the potential to those previously available. The most accurate one is that in [Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 20, 12636, (2018)], obtained from about 10,000 interaction energies calculated with the CCSD(T) method and Dunning's aug-cc-pVQZ basis set extended with midbond functions. The level of agreement with experiment of the rovibrational energy levels calculated with the latter potential was among the best reported in the literature for weakly bound systems, so we took this potential as a reference. The present AutoPES potential has a global minimum close to that of the reference potential, but it was not able to achieve the accuracy of the latter in providing the rovibrational transitions.

title: Mechanical and fire‐resistant properties of a binder incorporating recycled brick powder for 3D printing at elevated temperatures
summary: 3D‐printed concrete is susceptible to fire damage due to its numerous interfaces. A binder system based on calcium aluminate cement and recycled brick powder was developed to enhance the fire resistance of 3D‐printed concrete. A series of o
content: 3D‐printed concrete is susceptible to fire damage due to its numerous interfaces. A binder system based on calcium aluminate cement and recycled brick powder was developed to enhance the fire resistance of 3D‐printed concrete. A series of orthogonal experiments, including the dosages of recycled brick powder, nano‐silica, and sodium sulfate at four levels, was conducted. The setting time, workability, early‐age strength, mechanical properties, and fire‐resistant performance of this binder were systematically investigated. The results revealed that under the activation of sodium sulfate, the binder system retains excellent compressive strength and fire resistance even at a recycled brick powder content of 15 wt%. The early‐age compressive strength at 6 h increased by up to 78.9%. However, excessive dosages reduce workability, leading to a decline in both mechanical and fire‐resistant performance. An optimized mix proportion that balances various properties was proposed, and the 3D‐printed concrete exhibited excellent printability and buildability, achieving a compressive strength over 70 MPa and retaining nearly 70% of its strength after exposure to 1100°C.

title: Overstory structure drives seedling traits via soil mediation: implications for plantation regeneration in semiarid rocky mountain restoration
summary: Introduction Understanding how forest vertical stratification interacts with belowground processes to regulate seedling functional traits is critical for advancing forest regeneration theory and guiding ecological restoration in semiarid mo
content: Introduction Understanding how forest vertical stratification interacts with belowground processes to regulate seedling functional traits is critical for advancing forest regeneration theory and guiding ecological restoration in semiarid mountainous regions. Methods This study examined how overstory structure, understory vegetation, soil properties, and seedling traits are interrelated across contrasting slope aspects in Quercus variabilis plantations in semiarid rocky mountainous regions. These components were quantified in sunny- (southwest-facing) and shady-slope (northeast-facing) stands, and their relationships were analyzed using Spearman’s rank correlation, random forest (RF) and partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM). Results Compared with sunny-slope stands, shady-slope stands exhibited more complex overstory structure (greater species composition, size differentiation, and mingling), denser understory vegetation, and seedlings with larger leaf areas and higher leaf nitrogen concentration, whereas their soil had lower pH, total phosphorus (TP) and ammonium nitrogen. RF and Spearman analyses consistently identified soil pH and TP (%IncMSE = 9.5 and 9.0) as the dominant predictors of seedling leaf traits, followed by overstory species diversity and mingling. PLS-PM (GoF = 0.649) further revealed that overstory structure promoted understory vegetation development but reduced soil pH and TP. Soil was the only factor with a significant direct effect on seedling traits (β = -0.839, P < 0.01), and the strongest total effect of overstory structure (0.613) on seedling traits was transmitted predominantly through the indirect overstory-soil-seedling pathway (indirect effect = 0.490) rather than through direct overstory effects (0.123) or understory mediation. Discussion These results suggest that overstory structure regulates seedling functional traits mainly through soil-mediated indirect pathways rather than through direct effects or understory vegetation under contrasting aspects, highlighting aboveground-belowground coupling as a key mechanism shaping seedling functional trait variation. Coordinating stand-structure regulation with soil management may nonetheless represent a promising, though untested, option for facilitating the natural regeneration of plantations in semiarid mountainous regions.

title: Repurposing Lignite Power Plants into Long-Duration Thermal Energy Storage Systems: A Techno-Economic Assessment for Greece
summary: The rapid expansion of renewable energy sources, particularly solar photovoltaics and wind, has introduced significant variability into modern power systems. Greece, endowed with high solar irradiance and steadily increasing wind capacity,
content: The rapid expansion of renewable energy sources, particularly solar photovoltaics and wind, has introduced significant variability into modern power systems. Greece, endowed with high solar irradiance and steadily increasing wind capacity, is already experiencing frequent periods of excess electricity generation during daylight hours, alongside deficits during nighttime or low-wind conditions. This imbalance highlights the growing need for effective and scalable energy storage solutions. This paper examines the feasibility of converting decommissioned lignite-fired power plants into long-duration thermal energy storage facilities. The core concept involves utilizing surplus renewable electricity to generate thermal energy, storing it at high temperatures, and subsequently reconverting it into electricity through existing steam turbine infrastructure. A detailed techno-economic comparison is carried out between such thermal storage systems and lithium-ion battery storage, focusing on storage durations of 10 and 20 hours. The analysis incorporates lifecycle costs, system efficiency, infrastructure reuse potential, and recycling considerations. The results suggest that although thermal storage systems exhibit lower round-trip efficiency than batteries, they become economically competitive—and in some cases advantageous—at longer storage durations. This is primarily due to their lower material costs and minimal replacement requirements over their operational lifetime. The study concludes that repurposing lignite assets into thermal storage facilities could play a meaningful role in supporting Greece’s transition toward a high-renewable and low-carbon energy system.

title: In silico repurposing of FDA approved drugs as novel inhibitors of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1) via docking and ADMET analysis
summary: New Delhi metallo‑β‑lactamase‑1 (NDM‑1) is a globally disseminated carbapenemase that hydrolyses almost all clinically used β‑lactams, leaving few effective treatment options and driving urgent efforts to identify clinically actionable inhi
content: New Delhi metallo‑β‑lactamase‑1 (NDM‑1) is a globally disseminated carbapenemase that hydrolyses almost all clinically used β‑lactams, leaving few effective treatment options and driving urgent efforts to identify clinically actionable inhibitors. Despite intense discovery programs, no clinically approved standalone metallo-β-lactamase inhibitor is currently available, although therapeutic strategies such as cefiderocol and aztreonam/avibactam combinations have demonstrated clinical utility against infections caused by NDM-producing organisms. In this study, 50 FDA‑approved drugs spanning β‑lactams, β‑lactamase inhibitors, metal chelators, antibacterial agents with diverse mechanisms, and non‑antibiotic scaffolds were systematically screened against NDM‑1 (PDB ID: 4EXS) using AutoDock Vina. The docking protocol was validated by redocking of the co‑crystallized ligand, and a grid centered on the catalytic Zn(II) cluster was used to capture active‑site binding. Ligand ranking combined binding energy (Δ G ≤ −6.0 kcal/mol) with stringent Zn‑coordination criteria based on donor atom identity and Zn–ligand distances, followed by in silico ADMET and toxicity prediction and detailed interaction analysis. Docking identified glipizide and belinostat as the most promising leads, each showing strong bidentate coordination to both Zn(II) ions, favorable binding energies, and extensive hydrogen‑bonding and aromatic interactions with key catalytic residues. Linezolid and avibactam were retained as secondary candidates owing to near‑bidentate or asymmetric Zn engagement and acceptable safety profiles, whereas nitrofurantoin and other Zn‑coordinating hits were deprioritized due to predicted hepatotoxicity, mutagenicity, or poor pharmacokinetics. Collectively, this integrative, mechanism‑guided repurposing workflow reveals glipizide and belinostat, chemically and pharmacologically distinct from previously reported repurposed NDM‑1 inhibitors, as translationally realistic lead candidates and provides a generalizable framework for prioritizing Zn‑dependent β‑lactamase inhibitors.

title: Photothermal Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution via a Traceless Carboxylate Directing Group
summary: Intermolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution remains challenging for arenes lacking strong electron-withdrawing groups. Here, we report a photothermal amination–decarboxylation strategy that uses an ortho-carboxylate as a traceless act
content: Intermolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution remains challenging for arenes lacking strong electron-withdrawing groups. Here, we report a photothermal amination–decarboxylation strategy that uses an ortho-carboxylate as a traceless activating group. Under red-light irradiation, inexpensive carbon black enables amination of 2-bromobenzoic acids followed by decarboxylation, providing formal amination products of electronically neutral and electron-rich aryl bromides without transition-metal catalysis. The method accommodates primary aliphatic amines, anilines, and cyclic secondary amines, and its synthetic utility is demonstrated through preparative-scale synthesis and access to pharmaceutically relevant compounds. Competition experiments, substituent correlations, and density functional theory calculations support hydrogen-bond-assisted substitution and implicate steric constraints in the unusual preference for primary over secondary amines. Changing the leaving group from bromide to fluoride reverses this selectivity. Time-course measurements and reactions of a preformed intermediate support sequential substitution and decarboxylation. These findings establish a removable carboxylate activation strategy for extending intermolecular photothermal C–N bond formation beyond strongly activated electrophiles.

title: Algorithms for Computing Full Pressure–Temperature Phase Diagrams of Mixtures with Solid–Liquid–Vapor Equilibrium
summary: Solid formation in cryogenic applications, such as liquefied natural gas and liquid hydrogen processing, poses operational risks and requires reliable prediction of solid–liquid–vapor equilibrium (SLVE). However, complete pressure–temperatu
content: Solid formation in cryogenic applications, such as liquefied natural gas and liquid hydrogen processing, poses operational risks and requires reliable prediction of solid–liquid–vapor equilibrium (SLVE). However, complete pressure–temperature (p–T) phase diagrams covering all single-phase and coexistence regions remain rarely available. This work presents a comprehensive set of algorithms for automatically generating full p–T phase diagrams, including the entire SLVE domain. Using a cubic Yang–Frotscher–Richter equation of state and a classical solid fugacity model, a global sweep with adaptive refinement efficiently identifies all relevant phase boundaries. Binary diagrams can be generated within tens of seconds and ternary diagrams within a few hundred seconds on a standard laptop. The examples studied also reveal previously unreported complex phase-transition behaviors, particularly in ternary mixtures. An extensible software package is provided to support reproducible calculations and further development.

title: Remediation and immobilization of hexavalent chromium in contaminated soil using Cordia africana leaf-derived biochar
summary: Soil pollution from hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) poses severe risks to ecosystems and food security due to its high mobility and toxicity. This study evaluated the capacity of Cordia africana leaf-derived biochar to remediate and immobilize
content: Soil pollution from hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) poses severe risks to ecosystems and food security due to its high mobility and toxicity. This study evaluated the capacity of Cordia africana leaf-derived biochar to remediate and immobilize Cr(VI) in contaminated silty clay soil. The biochar, produced via controlled pyrolysis, exhibited a highly porous structure with a specific surface area of 698.813 m²/g and surface functional groups including hydroxyl, carboxyl, and aromatic rings. Batch incubation experiments were conducted for 30 days in soil contaminated with 100 mg/kg of Cr(VI), which had an initial extractable baseline of 97.08 mg/kg. The biochar application showed a clear dose-dependent reduction in extractable soil chromium. Increasing the biochar dosage from 1% to 3% enhanced the Cr(VI) removal efficiency from 55.91% to 82.22%, leaving a residual concentration of 17.78 mg/kg. Higher applications up to 4% resulted in a plateau effect, yielding a marginal maximum removal of 82.80%. Pot culture trials using Eragrostis tef confirmed the practical efficacy of the treatment. The unamended control soil caused complete plant mortality due to extreme phytotoxicity. A 1% biochar amendment enabled plant survival, though tissues accumulated 13.75 mg/kg of chromium. Increasing the amendment to 2% and 3% significantly lowered tissue accumulation to 6.32 mg/kg and 4.53 mg/kg, respectively. A 4% application further reduced tissue accumulation to 4.28 mg/kg. This leaf-derived biochar provides an effective physical and chemical barrier that successfully immobilizes chromium, offering a sustainable, low-cost strategy to protect crops from heavy metal toxicity.

title: Metabolic Implications of Metal Toxicity: The Omics Paradigm Approach
summary: Metal toxicity poses significant risks to human health and the environment, with far-reaching implications for metabolic processes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying metal-induced metabolic disturbances is crucial for develo
content: Metal toxicity poses significant risks to human health and the environment, with far-reaching implications for metabolic processes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying metal-induced metabolic disturbances is crucial for developing effective interventions and therapeutic strategies. Omics approaches, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, offer comprehensive insights into the metabolic implications of metal toxicity. This review paper highlights the importance of omics techniques in elucidating how metals disrupt cellular pathways and processes, leading to metabolic alterations. By identifying biomarkers of metal exposure and toxicity, omics studies contribute to the early detection and assessment of metal-induced metabolic disturbances. Furthermore, these approaches facilitate the discovery of potential therapeutic targets for mitigating the adverse effects of metal toxicity on metabolism. Through a review of relevant literature, this paper provides insight into the metabolic pathways affected by metal toxicity, its impacts on metabolism, and the role of omics approaches in studying metal-induced metabolic disturbances. It further emphasizes the significance of integrating omics technologies into research on metal toxicity to advance our understanding of its metabolic implications and inform strategies for protecting human health and the environment. Key therapeutic targets and intervention strategies are outlined, together with the principal limitations and challenges of omics approaches. By adopting a multidimensional understanding of metal toxicity through the omics approach, humanity is gradually moving closer to a future of proactive measures that safeguard ecosystems and populations from the deleterious effects of metal toxicity, thereby ensuring a healthier and more sustainable world for generations to come.

title: Seasonal hydrological influences on pCO2 dynamics in a groundwater-connected urban lake
summary: Lakes occupying a small fraction of the Earth’s surface, yet emit an estimated 0.11–0.57 PgC yr -1 to the atmosphere as CO 2 , comparable to the fluxes of net terrestrial uptake and ocean absorption. Small water bodies have long been undere
content: Lakes occupying a small fraction of the Earth’s surface, yet emit an estimated 0.11–0.57 PgC yr -1 to the atmosphere as CO 2 , comparable to the fluxes of net terrestrial uptake and ocean absorption. Small water bodies have long been underestimated in global carbon budgets due to their high spatial and temporal variability, and the governing mechanisms of lake carbon dynamics are still poorly understood. To better the understanding, we conducted a site study with eight sampling campaigns between October 2024 and November 2025 in Ziyang Lake (~ 0.136 km 2 with mean depth of 1.5–2.0 m), a typical shallow urban lake in Wuhan, China, for physicochemical parameters and carbon-related parameters of both surface water and adjacent groundwater. Lake pCO 2 and CO 2 flux sensitively responded to hydrological forcing including seasonal groundwater input and rain event. The lake acted as a CO 2 sink during the wet season (with CO 2 flux of -24 ± 10 mmol m -2 d -1 ), and a spatially heterogeneous source during the dry season (13 ± 52 mmol m -2 d -1 , ranging from − 35 to 184 mmol m -2 d -1 ). Following a rain event, the lake shifted to a strong source (63 ± 31 mmol m -2 d -1 ). Surface water pCO 2 ranged from 31 to 2,476 µatm and showed no significant correlations with biological drivers (DO, temperature, Chl‑a), indicating that internal metabolism was not the primary control. The difference between groundwater head and surface water level (Δh) exhibited a seasonal reversal: negative Δh during the wet season (-7.9 ± 1.2 cm) suppressed the input of high-CO 2 groundwater, keeping pCO 2 low (162 ± 111 µatm), while positive Δh during the dry season (2.2 ± 5.6 cm) enabled groundwater discharge that elevated pCO 2 (573 ± 587 µatm). Using TA‑DIC as a conservative tracer, we estimated that localized groundwater contributed to only 1–5% of water volume. This is, however, enough to increase pCO 2 by 50–650% relative to baseline, shifting lake water from carbon sinks to sources. In the single rain event captured, the wet-season sink was temporarily overridden, producing a pCO 2 spike of 1,089 ± 328 µatm. We treat terrestrial flushing, and enhanced shallow groundwater input as plausible mechanisms for that pulse. Our findings suggest that hydrological forcing mediated by seasonal groundwater input and rain events has critical impact on carbon dynamics in shallow urban lakes, with implications for carbon budget estimation for small water bodies.

title: Degradation of Drugs of Abuse and Associated Microbial Community Shifts in Freshwater Systems
summary: Drugs of abuse (DAs) are frequently detected in surface waters due to their incomplete removal during wastewater treatment and continued discharge from point and nonpoint sources. Despite growing evidence of ecological effects at environmen
content: Drugs of abuse (DAs) are frequently detected in surface waters due to their incomplete removal during wastewater treatment and continued discharge from point and nonpoint sources. Despite growing evidence of ecological effects at environmentally relevant concentrations, the environmental fate of many DAs in river systems remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we evaluated the degradation of eight commonly detected DAs and metabolites (amphetamine, benzoylecgonine, buprenorphine, codeine, fentanyl, ketamine, methamphetamine, and tramadol) spiked at environmentally relevant concentrations in river microcosms designed to distinguish hydrolysis, abiotic degradation, biodegradation, and sorption processes. Microcosms were incubated under dark, aerobic conditions for 9 days, and first-order kinetics were used to quantify individual degradation rate constants. Overall removal was limited, ranging from 12% (tramadol) to 21% (buprenorphine), indicating high persistence under the microcosm conditions. Hydrolysis and abiotic degradation contributed minimally to attenuation, whereas biodegradation accounted for the largest estimated contribution (k = 0.0044–0.016 d–1), with sorption providing a secondary estimated contribution for more hydrophobic compounds. Principal component analysis indicated that attenuation behavior was associated with physicochemical properties, including hydrophobicity and ionization; compounds such as buprenorphine and fentanyl showed stronger associations with sorption and hydrolysis, while ketamine attenuation was more strongly influenced by ionization than sorption. Parallel taxonomic analysis revealed temporal shifts in microbial community composition, although Pseudomonadota (formerly Proteobacteria) and Bacteroidota (formerly Bacteroidetes) remained dominant throughout the incubation. Dynamic community restructuring was observed in biologically active microcosms based on taxonomic profiling, although changes could not be linked directly to drug presence. Overall, degradation rates in river water were 1–4 orders of magnitude lower than those reported for wastewater or sludge matrices, suggesting greater persistence and prolonged ecological exposure in freshwater systems. These findings improve understanding of the environmental fate of DAs and support risk assessment efforts for bioactive contaminants in aquatic ecosystems.

title: Linking Methane Emission Reductions To Design and Operational Changes at a US Landfill
summary: Landfills are a major contributor to anthropogenic methane emissions in the United States; therefore, there is a need for methane monitoring tools that can guide stakeholder decisions in the sector. We use remote sensing instruments to moni
content: Landfills are a major contributor to anthropogenic methane emissions in the United States; therefore, there is a need for methane monitoring tools that can guide stakeholder decisions in the sector. We use remote sensing instruments to monitor methane point source emissions at a municipal solid waste landfill in Monterey, California, as it undergoes changes to its gas collection and control system and to the work face (where new waste is added). We use the spatial information from the observations to attribute emissions and verify that site changes at new waste areas, like well installation and intermediate cover application, can reduce emissions over short time scales, indicating that these practices are promising solutions for reducing emissions and that airborne and satellite remote sensing instruments can be used to track mitigation progress at high-emitting landfills, but further study is needed to assess long-term emission trends and applicability to diverse landfills in the United States.

title: Contrasting climatic and anthropogenic influences on vegetation productivity stability across spatiotemporal scales in China’s drylands
summary: Gross primary productivity (GPP) stability is crucial for dryland carbon sinks, yet how climatic and anthropogenic proxy factors are associated with stability across spatiotemporal scales remains poorly understood. Using satellite-derived a
content: Gross primary productivity (GPP) stability is crucial for dryland carbon sinks, yet how climatic and anthropogenic proxy factors are associated with stability across spatiotemporal scales remains poorly understood. Using satellite-derived annual GPP from 1982 to 2018, we combined ensemble empirical mode decomposition with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify interannual, trend, and overall stability and assess variable importance, nonlinear associations, and local contributions. Results showed that: (1) Variable importance was strongly timescale-dependent. Interannual stability was most strongly associated with shortwave radiation trend (SRAD_SLOPE) and mean population density (POP_MEAN); trend stability with temperature variability (TEM_CV), SRAD_SLOPE, and POP_MEAN; and overall stability with SRAD_SLOPE and TEM_CV. Locally, SRAD_SLOPE (34.27%) and POP_MEAN (21.85%) were the main variables of interannual stability, TEM_CV (44.22%) of trend stability, and SRAD_SLOPE (50.68%) and TEM_CV (24.32%) of overall stability. (2) Associations varied across dimensions. Increasing precipitation was associated with higher trend stability but lower interannual and overall stability; SRAD_SLOPE was negatively associated with all three dimensions; and elevation, represented by the digital elevation model (DEM), showed opposite associations with trend stability and the other two dimensions. POP_MEAN showed a nonlinear association with trend stability, while forests and croplands were more closely associated with interannual and trend stability, respectively. Among land-cover trajectory types, no-significant-change trajectories in forests and grasslands were associated with higher interannual stability, whereas decrease-to-increase trajectories were associated with higher trend stability across all land-cover types. (3) Local SHAP patterns were spatially heterogeneous. SRAD_SLOPE and TEM_CV showed broadly similar patterns across dimensions, whereas PPT_SLOPE and DEM showed contrasting patterns between trend and interannual stability. These findings highlight the need to consider both temporal dimensions and spatial context when attributing dryland GPP stability and may inform future carbon-sink management.

title: Assessment of ultramafic mine tailings in Ontario as resource-scale carbon sinks
summary: Mine tailings rich in Mg- and Ca-bearing silicates represent an immediately available feedstock for permanent CO 2 mineralization because they are already excavated and finely processed. However, national-scale assessments of sequestration
content: Mine tailings rich in Mg- and Ca-bearing silicates represent an immediately available feedstock for permanent CO 2 mineralization because they are already excavated and finely processed. However, national-scale assessments of sequestration capacity remain limited, particularly for Canadian mining jurisdictions. Here we present a quantitative screening evaluation of ultramafic-hosted tailings in Ontario, using whole-rock oxide capacity metrics, and discuss the broader applicability of this framework to other Canadian provinces. Lithological analysis indicates that serpentinite-hosted residues exhibit the highest theoretical capacity ( ∼ 51 g CO 2 /100 g), followed by peridotite ( ∼ 47 g CO 2 /100 g) and komatiite ( ∼ 39 g CO 2 /100 g). Site-level estimates for nine Ontario operations span approximately 0.02 to 4.5 Mt CO 2 under partial conversion (20%–50%), with individual large operations reaching up to 9 Mt CO 2 under idealized full conversion. Spatial clustering of reactive deposits in northern mining belts suggests the feasibility of regional mineralization hubs capable of serving multiple emission sources. Beyond carbon storage, carbonated tailings are compositionally consistent with magnesite-bearing supplementary cementitious materials, suggesting an integrated pathway linking mine waste management with decarbonization of the built environment. These findings demonstrate that Canadian ultramafic tailings constitute a large, ready-made carbon sink and provide a practical framework for prioritizing sites for characterization, pilot testing, and deployment within national climate mitigation strategies.

title: To wards S u s t a i n a b l e We t l a n d M a n a g e m e n t : A F o c u s o n Ramsar Sites and Conservation Policies
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Wetlands are critical ecosystems that provide essential ecological, social, and economic benefits. However, they are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic activities and climate change. Ramsar sites, designated wetlands of international
content: Wetlands are critical ecosystems that provide essential ecological, social, and economic benefits. However, they are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic activities and climate change. Ramsar sites, designated wetlands of international importance, represent a cornerstone for wetland conservation. This review article highlights the ecological, legal, and policy frameworks for the protection and sustainable management of Ramsar wetlands, with a focus on India. Challenges such as biodiversity loss, pollution, and habitat degradation are addressed alongside strategies for improved governance and technological interventions. By integrating conservation policies, economic valuation, a n d international collaboration, this article underscores the need for adaptive management to ensure the wise use of wetlands for future generations.

title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
summary: Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their
content: Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

title: Dataset for: Probing pod photosynthesis and its potential contribution to pod yields
summary: Publication Title: Probing pod photosynthesis and its potential contribution to pod yields Authors: Yuyang Ding, Mauricio Tejera Nieves, Liana G. Acevedo-Siaca Study objectives: to determine how bean pods contribute to overall bean pod yiel
content: Publication Title: Probing pod photosynthesis and its potential contribution to pod yields Authors: Yuyang Ding, Mauricio Tejera Nieves, Liana G. Acevedo-Siaca Study objectives: to determine how bean pods contribute to overall bean pod yields. This was assessed by combining pod shading treatments, leaf level gas exchange measurements, and chlorophyll fluorescence imaging of bean pods under fluctuating light. The data set consists of Excel sheets with data on destructive harvest traits, chlorophyll fluorescence imaging of pods and leaves (FluorCam), leaf-level gas exchange data (Li-6800), leaf level chlorophyll fluorescence and leaf greenness measurements (LSA2050). Treatment abbreviations are as follow: Control (CK), Shade (S), and Transparent Plastic (P). Abstract: Common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) pods contribute to whole-plant carbon assimilation via photosynthesis in the pod wall. However, the specific contribution of pod photosynthesis to yield and its relevance on source-sink dynamics remain unknown. In this study, pods were individually shaded using opaque and transparent bags to investigate pod- specific photosynthetic traits and possible secondary effects at leaf-level, relative to an unshaded control treatment. Plants with shaded pods displayed a compensatory effect of leaf photosynthetic capacity: the net CO2 assimilation rate in saturating light (Asat) increased by 6%, while both leaf chlorophyll content and the quantum yield of PSII (ΦPSII) also increased significantly relative to the control. In contrast, the shaded pods exhibited lower photoprotective capacity, a lower induced amplitude of non-photochemical quenching (NPQ), slower NPQ induction kinetics, and lower Fv/Fm values. Furthermore, few significant correlations were found between leaf- and pod-level photosynthetic traits. Contrary to expectations, shading significantly increased the total aboveground biomass (14%; P < 0.001), number of pods per plant (24%; P < 0.001), and total dry weight of pods (18%; P < 0.05), while reducing the average dry weight of each shaded pod (22-29%), relative to the control plants. In general, the shading of individual pods stimulated the production of additional pods in the plant. However, when only comparing treated pods, the shaded pods were significantly smaller relative to the control. These findings suggest that pod photosynthesis likely influences pod yields and has downstream effects on source-sink dynamics in the plant, including in untreated foliar tissues.

title: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose-based dissolving microneedle platform enabling efficient transdermal delivery of a poorly water-soluble drug
summary: This study aimed to develop an optimal microneedle based on hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) matrix for the effective transdermal delivery of dexibuprofen (DXI). After evaluating the mechanical strength and drug solubility of various bi
content: This study aimed to develop an optimal microneedle based on hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) matrix for the effective transdermal delivery of dexibuprofen (DXI). After evaluating the mechanical strength and drug solubility of various biocompatible polymers, HPMC was selected as the optimal microneedle matrix. HPMC not only provided sufficient mechanical strength for the microneedle but also enhanced the solubility of DXI. Various microneedle formulations with different DXI-to-HPMC weight ratios were developed and comprehensively evaluated in terms of physicochemical and mechanical properties, skin insertability, solubility, in vitro drug release, ex vivo skin permeability, in vivo pharmacokinetics, and post-insertion skin safety. Among them, the optimal HPMC-based microneedle with a DXI:HPMC weight ratio of 1:1.25 (w/w) was selected. The selected formulation demonstrated excellent mechanical strength and insertability. The HPMC-based microneedle system enhanced drug solubility, release rate, and skin permeability, achieving a 13-fold increase in relative bioavailability compared with the needleless film. Histological evaluation based on H&E staining showed that the skin structure recovered within 3 days, with no obvious histological signs of irritation or inflammation. These findings suggest that HPMC-based microneedles may serve as a useful transdermal delivery platform for improving the solubility and relative bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs such as DXI.

title: Comprehensive overview of surface and interfacial engineering for enhanced heat transfer in solar thermal systems
summary: Surface engineering and characterization play a central role in determining the thermal efficiency and durability of solar thermal energy systems. Although numerous studies have explored materials and coatings for solar thermal applications
content: Surface engineering and characterization play a central role in determining the thermal efficiency and durability of solar thermal energy systems. Although numerous studies have explored materials and coatings for solar thermal applications, the interaction between surface properties and heat transfer mechanisms remains not fully understood. The present review highlights the pivotal role of surface engineering for optimizing the thermal performance of solar energy technologies, from non-concentrating collectors to concentrated solar power and thermal energy storage systems. By analysing developments in surface coatings, micro/nano-texturing and surface-functionalized fluids, this overview shows that tailored surface morphology and interfacial properties (such as roughness, absorbance, emissivity and chemical composition) enables improved control of heat transfer processes. These engineered surfaces, in direct interaction with working fluids, critically influence convective and radiative transfer, as well as the effectiveness of phase change processes. Special attention is given to selective and textured absorbers, direct-absorption fluids and nanostructured surfaces, with emphasis on the trade-offs between optical performance, heat transfer enhancement and long-term durability under realistic operating conditions. Finally, technological gaps and emerging research directions are identified to support the development of more efficient and reliable solar thermal systems.

title: Seasonally Asynchronous Hydrological Buffering and C:N:P Stoichiometric Regulation by Alpine Wetlands in a Small Alpine Catchment on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau
summary: Alpine wetlands on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau (QXP) serve as critical yet poorly quantified regulators of hydrological processes and biogeochemical fluxes at the catchment scale. However, how the seasonal hydrological switching of these wet
content: Alpine wetlands on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau (QXP) serve as critical yet poorly quantified regulators of hydrological processes and biogeochemical fluxes at the catchment scale. However, how the seasonal hydrological switching of these wetlands controls the export and stoichiometry of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P), and thereby the nutrient status of downstream oligotrophic lakes, remains poorly quantified. This study addresses this gap through integrated meteorological, hydrological, and water-quality monitoring conducted across the early (EGS), middle (MGS), and late (LGS) growing seasons in a subbasin containing extensive alpine wetlands of the Niyaqu catchment on the QXP. The wetland attenuated inflows above approximately 4.75 m 3 s -1 and supplemented outflow below this threshold. Net storage gains occurred mainly in MGS, whereas net releases dominated EGS and LGS. The mean outlet baseflow index was 84.60%, compared with 76.94% at the inlet, consistent with enhanced delayed-flow contributions. Solute responses were element-specific and seasonally asynchronous. Carbon export increased by 28.08%, 56.91%, and 48.59% during EGS, MGS, and LGS, respectively. Nitrogen export decreased only in MGS (5.72%) but increased in EGS and LGS, whereas phosphorus export decreased by 31.91%, 46.92%, and 34.89%, respectively. Consequently, load-based C:P, C:N, and N:P ratios were higher at the outlet than at the inlet in all seasons; C:P and N:P increases were greatest in EGS and LGS. These results identify seasonal hydrological switching as a key control on the timing and stoichiometry of wetland solute export. The decoupling of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus responses shows that hydrological buffering of alpine wetlands cannot be assumed to imply uniform nutrient retention. By revealing how hydrological switching propagates into element cycles, this study provides a mechanistic basis for protecting the water quality of downstream oligotrophic lakes and for climate-resilient watershed management in the Asian Water Tower region.

title: Resilient Net Community Production in a Warming North Pacific Ocean (2001–2019)
summary: Net community production (NCP)─carbon fixation remaining after autotrophic and heterotrophic respiration─regulates surface fCO2, air–sea CO2 exchange, and the ocean’s vertical carbon gradient. However, sparse measurements limit our understa
content: Net community production (NCP)─carbon fixation remaining after autotrophic and heterotrophic respiration─regulates surface fCO2, air–sea CO2 exchange, and the ocean’s vertical carbon gradient. However, sparse measurements limit our understanding of its long-term variability at basin scales. We estimated North Pacific NCP at 1° × 1° resolution for 2001–2019 from the warming-period (wp) drawdown of dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) in the surface mixed layer. CT was reconstructed from more than 3.3 million surface fCO2 observations and empirically estimated total alkalinity using carbonate-system thermodynamics, with corrections for salinity, net air–sea CO2 exchange, vertical diffusion, and CaCO3 production. Mean NCP was 1.3 ± 0.1 Pg C wp–1 and exhibited no long-term trend despite 0.6 °C of basin-wide warming, which is expected to suppress biological production by strengthening stratification and limiting nutrient supply. This apparent stability masked opposing trends: declining NCP in the western deep-mixed-layer region was offset by increasing NCP in the tropics, potentially supported by enhanced nitrogen fixation. Thus, basin-wide stability reflected regional compensation rather than a uniform response to warming. Nevertheless, a projected NCP decline of approximately 0.16 Pg C yr–1 by 2100 is equivalent in magnitude to approximately 30% of the basin’s current net air–sea CO2 uptake.

title: Recycled tyre-derived steel cord fibres improve the strength, durability and material carbon intensity of vibro-pressed concrete
summary: Vibro-pressed (dry-cast) concrete products such as paving blocks and kerbs pair a low water content with intense mechanical compaction, which makes them dense and impermeable but also brittle and weak in tension. We asked whether steel cord
content: Vibro-pressed (dry-cast) concrete products such as paving blocks and kerbs pair a low water content with intense mechanical compaction, which makes them dense and impermeable but also brittle and weak in tension. We asked whether steel cord recovered from end-of-life tyres could compensate for that brittleness while lowering the material carbon footprint. Four mixes were manufactured on a full-scale production line with mixing water held at 140 kg m⁻³; because cement was replaced one-for-one by mass with cord, the effective w/c ratio increased from 0.314 in the reference to 0.368 at the highest dosage. Fibre content, cement content and effective w/c therefore changed together, so all reported trends describe formulation-level (production-recipe) effects rather than isolated fibre-dose effects. Cord was dosed at 0, 5, 10 and 15% of the reference cement mass (0, 22, 44 and 66 kg m⁻³), and fourteen physical, durability and mechanical responses were measured after 28 days with five replicates per series. Relative to the reference, the 15% formulation raised compressive strength by 21.8%, flexural strength by 40.4% and impact energy by 66.9%, while reducing water absorption, abrasion, freeze–thaw mass loss and drying shrinkage. One-way ANOVA showed formulation-level differences for thirteen of the fourteen responses. Splitting tensile strength measured on the as-produced paving blocks rose by 35.8%, and every block met the EN 1338 requirements. A screening life-cycle assessment restricted to a material greenhouse-gas proxy (cement, aggregate and fibre) showed lower material greenhouse-gas intensity with increasing cement substitution. Balancing performance, cost and environmental value, the 10% dosage is identified as optimal.

title: Nutrient Recycling is a Critical Process in Closed Ecological Systems
summary: Permanent space colonies will approach being Closed Ecological Systems; recycling of essential elements will minimize transport from Earth: Food to Metabolism to Wastes to Recycle to Food, etc. Marine Closed Ecological Systems have been rep
content: Permanent space colonies will approach being Closed Ecological Systems; recycling of essential elements will minimize transport from Earth: Food to Metabolism to Wastes to Recycle to Food, etc. Marine Closed Ecological Systems have been reported to remain photosynthetically active for decades. In contrast, our freshwater, chemically defined Closed Ecological Systems tend to run down, and grazers die out in about a year. Our 259 mL Closed Ecological Systems, consisting of 3 species of green algae (Ankistrodesmus, Scenedesmus and Selenastrum), the grazers (Daphnia magna), and unidentified microorganisms, have been studied under a variety of conditions. Our earlier studies have shown that high nutrient concentrations, including those associated with algal cultures, harm Daphnia. In an initial experiment, we tested lower concentrations of algal suspension (10%, 5%, and 1%); lower concentrations reduced chlorophyll a (an estimate of algal abundance) but did not statistically change the persistence of Daphnia populations. In general, the systems declined, which we assume was caused by nutrient limitation. For the following observations, supplements of C, N, P, C + N, N + P, and C + N+P were tested after the initial algal- Daphnia interactions (day 38). The introduction of C and P had no significant effect. The addition of N had mixed effects; if Daphnia grazing was low (3 replicates), chlorophyll a increased significantly; if Daphnia grazing was high (2 replicates), chlorophyll a remained low. Adding N together with C, P, or C + P all resulted in increases in chlorophyll a. Despite variability, some N compounds appear to fail to recycle and persist in forms unavailable for algal regrowth. Although it is often assumed that sewage treatment or artificial wetlands recycle all complex molecules into those needed for food production, evidence suggests otherwise. The European Space Agency developed a recycling system that began with anaerobic digestion of human waste, with eventual food production. In contrast, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration has tended to store or dispose of waste but is currently studying waste recycling. Improved waste recycling methods will greatly benefit Earth’s ecosystems.

title: Bottom-up nanostructured thermal radiation protective coatings for nuclear environments: interface density, interface order, and chemical disorder engineering
