summary: Protective coatings for nuclear and high-temperature systems must control heat transfer while retaining structural, chemical, and irradiation stability as their nanoscale architectures evolve during service. This review evaluates coating de
content: Protective coatings for nuclear and high-temperature systems must control heat transfer while retaining structural, chemical, and irradiation stability as their nanoscale architectures evolve during service. This review evaluates coating design through three coupled forms of nanostructure control: interface density, interface order, and chemical disorder. Nanocrystal-derived processing can generate grain boundaries, interparticle contacts, heterophase interfaces, and pores that increase thermal resistance and shorten diffusion distances to irradiation-defect sinks. Retention of these advantages depends on the stability of the interface network against sintering, coarsening, gas accumulation, and environmental attack. Studies of mesocrystal assembly, oriented attachment, nanocrystal superlattices, and epitaxial multilayers delineate how interface coherency, periodicity, spacing, and connectivity can suppress or enhance heat transport; however, direct evidence from thick refractory mesocrystal coatings remains scarce. Chemical disorder modifies lattice transport and defect migration through mass and size variance, bond heterogeneity, vacancy chemistry, and short-range order. Selected high-entropy oxides combine low lattice thermal conductivity with high-temperature stability, whereas high-entropy carbides, nitrides, borides, and carbonitrides provide complementary mechanical, ablation, erosion, and irradiation resistance, with strongly composition-dependent oxidation behavior. Recent irradiation studies reveal contrasting effects of chemical short-range order, which can improve radiation resistance in selected compositions or accelerate species-specific defect diffusion and segregation in others. These findings do not support a universal sluggish-diffusion mechanism. Durable performance requires stable interface networks, deliberately selected boundary structures, and compositionally controlled disorder validated under coupled thermal, irradiation, mechanical, and chemical loading.

title: Tree Species Identity Outweighs Provenance in Shaping Soil Organic Carbon Storage in an Arid Industrial Plantation, Northern Persian Gulf
summary: Soils beneath planted trees are a durable carbon sink, yet species-selection guidance for hyper-arid plantings rests on evidence from mesic forests and on the assumption that native species outperform introduced ones. In the hyper-arid Sout
content: Soils beneath planted trees are a durable carbon sink, yet species-selection guidance for hyper-arid plantings rests on evidence from mesic forests and on the assumption that native species outperform introduced ones. In the hyper-arid South Pars industrial zone on the northern Persian Gulf coast, we sampled soils beneath three trees each of three native (Phoenix dactylifera, Ziziphus spina-christi, Prosopis cineraria) and three introduced species (Eucalyptus camaldulensis, Callistemon viminalis, Conocarpus erectus) at 0–10 and 10–30 cm, and partitioned variation in soil organic carbon between species identity and provenance with split-plot analysis of variance, multivariate variance partitioning, exact permutation tests and mixed models. Species identity explained 46% of multivariate soil dispersion and 77% of variance in log-transformed carbon, whereas provenance explained 12% and could not be separated from species-within-category variation. Phoenix dactylifera held 2.46% carbon versus 0.59% under Conocarpus erectus, a 4.2-fold range not sorted by provenance. Carbon declined 33% from 0–10 to 10–30 cm in 17 of 18 trees with parallel species profiles, and covaried negatively with clay, consistent with input rather than mineral limitation; indicative 0–30 cm stocks spanned 20.6–98.4 Mg carbon per hectare. Species-specific organic inputs, not provenance labels or mineralogical capacity, govern soil carbon in this input-limited system, extending the species-identity rule of mesic forests to the hyper-arid extreme. Plantation and agroforestry programmes in arid regions should therefore select at the species level, prioritising high-input taxa such as date palm and jujube, rather than applying native-versus-introduced rules.

title: Regional screening of subsurface resource interactions in the northern Perth Basin, Western Australia
summary: Sedimentary basins can host multiple subsurface resources, creating potential for direct competition where activities target the same pore space and for pressure or fluid interaction where they occupy separate but connected intervals. In th
content: Sedimentary basins can host multiple subsurface resources, creating potential for direct competition where activities target the same pore space and for pressure or fluid interaction where they occupy separate but connected intervals. In the onshore northern Perth Basin, Western Australia, these relationships may involve petroleum production, carbon geological storage (CGS), underground gas storage (UGS), geothermal development and groundwater abstraction. Regional spatial overlap can identify where potential resources interactions warrant closer assessment, but these resources may still be vertically and hydraulically separated. This study provides a data-driven framework for evaluating potential subsurface resource interactions and identifying potential risks and opportunities for regulators, industries and communities. The project uses a Geographic Information System (GIS)-based multi-criteria and hierarchy evaluation process to assess the suitability of different resources and quantify their spatial interactions with focus on petroleum and CGS operations and potential conflicts with groundwater usage. The overlap of suitable petroleum and CGS resources is most pronounced in the Permian succession, particularly on the Dongara, Beharra Springs and Donkey Creek terraces and in the northwestern Dandaragan Trough. Candidate areas where CGS could follow petroleum production and reservoir depletion extend south along the Cadda Terrace and Coomallo Trough. CO 2 source–sink proximity screening identifies a western basin corridor, particularly between Dongara and Leeman, where prospective CGS areas lie relatively close to potential future gas-related CO₂ sources. The potential for vertical interaction between resources was also examined by considering faults and petroleum wells as possible vertical pathways between deep formation and to shallow groundwater aquifers. Water bore density was used as a proxy for evaluating the competition for groundwater. While groundwater resources are typically hydraulically isolated from deeper resources development activities by thick intervening shale aquitards, potential impacts of petroleum and CGS operations on groundwater resources are possible in heavily faulted areas in a central-western corridor inland of Dongara and extending south along the Cadda Terrace and Coomallo Trough. The presented framework provides a regional basis for more targeted, field-scale assessments and identification of resource development synergies, options for sequential development, and cumulative groundwater management.

title: A three-stage metabolic switch links root-zone water status to phloem fiber growth and defense in Salix suchowensis
summary: How woody plants adjust bark-fiber development to groundwater-table gradients—and the underlying root-zone soil moisture regimes—is central to understanding riparian tree acclimation and the developmental regulation of bark secondary walls.
content: How woody plants adjust bark-fiber development to groundwater-table gradients—and the underlying root-zone soil moisture regimes—is central to understanding riparian tree acclimation and the developmental regulation of bark secondary walls. Eight- to ten-year-old Salix suchowensis plants were compared at groundwater table depths of 1.2 (CK), 0.6 (T1), 0.5 (T2), 0.4 (T3) and 0.3 m (T4), integrating fiber morphology, growth traits, and cell-wall cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin with widely targeted metabolomics and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Fiber development followed a threshold-type, three-stage response. The deep-water control set the baseline (wall-to-lumen ratio, RR, 0.65); the adequate-water state (T1/T2) defined a wall-construction window, with fiber length peaking at T1 and RR falling to 0.52–0.56; the shallow-water state (T3/T4) shifted development toward wall thickening and defense, with RR reaching 0.92 at T4. Wall components peaked in strict succession: cellulose at T1 (418 mg g − 1, + 18.8%) before falling 38.8% by T4; lignin transiently at T3 (199 mg g − 1, + 68.7%); and hemicellulose latest at T4 (464 mg g − 1, + 39.8%). Carbon was redirected from glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway through the shikimate–phenylpropanoid network toward flavonoids, tannins, salicinoids and hemicellulose. WGCNA independently identified a cellulose-associated module (ME5, r = + 0.94) and a hemicellulose-associated module (ME9, r = − 0.89). The ordered carbon-sink succession from cellulose to lignin and then to hemicellulose and terminal defense adds metabolite-level timing to the growth–differentiation balance framework and reveals root-zone water status as a physiological switch governing bark development between structural growth and chemical defense.

title: Sustainable antifouling marine coatings based on thiosemicarbazide Schiff-base Cu(II) and Zn(II) complexes: experimental evaluation and DFT insights
summary: The development of more sustainable antifouling coatings has become imperative due to increasingly stringent regulations on conventional biocidal marine paints that release toxic substances into aquatic ecosystems. In this study, a novel an
content: The development of more sustainable antifouling coatings has become imperative due to increasingly stringent regulations on conventional biocidal marine paints that release toxic substances into aquatic ecosystems. In this study, a novel antifouling coating system was developed based on a synthesized thiosemicarbazide Schiff-base ligand and its transition-metal complexes, namely Cu(II) and Zn(II) derivatives, as sustainable antifouling additives. The prepared compounds were incorporated into marine coating formulations by replacing 50% of the conventional cuprous oxide (Cu 2 O) pigment content, and their performance was compared with that of the reference Cu 2 O-based formulation obtained from an international marine paint manufacturer. The novelty of this work lies in the development of thiosemicarbazide-based Cu(II) and Zn(II) complexes as multifunctional antifouling additives capable of reducing the reliance on conventional copper-based biocides. The formulated coatings exhibited excellent mechanical and chemical properties and were evaluated under natural seawater exposure for six months. The results of antifouling study demonstrate that the Zn(II)-Schiff-base complex-containing formulation (F4) exhibited antifouling performance comparable to the reference Cu 2 O-based formulation (F1), whereas the Cu(II)-complex-containing formulation (F3) showed moderate antifouling performance. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations revealed that metal coordination reduced the HOMO–LUMO energy gap and enhanced electrophilic character, supporting the experimentally observed improvement in antifouling performance. Overall, this study presents a promising strategy for the design of next-generation sustainable marine coatings by combining reduced-biocide formulations with functional Schiff-base metal complexes. The synergistic experimental and theoretical investigation provides new insights into the development of high-performance antifouling coatings and potential to reduce reliance on conventional biocides in marine coating systems.

title: Where Does the Fluorine Go? A Systematic Evidence Audit of Fluorine Fate and Carbon’s Role in PFAS Photocatalysis
summary: Carbon-containing photocatalysts are proposed for treating per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), but performance is usually reported as parent-compound loss, which does not distinguish adsorption, transformation and C–F bond cleavage.
content: Carbon-containing photocatalysts are proposed for treating per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), but performance is usually reported as parent-compound loss, which does not distinguish adsorption, transformation and C–F bond cleavage. We searched Scopus and Web of Science and audited 115 studies (121 experiments), coding fluorine in six measurable reservoirs and an unresolved fraction, recalculating defluorination and grading evidence for carbon’s electronic role. No study quantified fluorine in all reservoirs: 35 studies measured no fluoride, 12 extracted PFAS from the spent catalyst, one quantified catalyst-bound fluoride and none measured volatile products. Eight of nine numerical fluorine balances covered only the aqueous phase (42–93% recovery); the one including the catalyst recovered 2.35%. Removal exceeded defluorination by a median of 55.8 percentage points when removal included dark adsorption (n = 19) and by 10.4 points when degradation was reported (n = 11); the baseline was not stated for 33 of 63 paired values. Four of twelve recalculable defluorination values did not reproduce, one exceeding the theoretical maximum. The strongest evidence for carbon’s electronic role was correlative charge-carrier data in 67 studies and assertion, calculation or scavenger tests in 40; direct electron transfer to PFAS was shown for two intrinsically photoactive catalysts, neither compared with a carbon-free material. Sixty studies compared carbon-free or carbon-only materials, but none normalized performance to adsorbed PFAS. Carbon’s sorptive functions are well documented; its independent contribution to C–F activation in carbon-supported composites is untested. We propose a four-level reporting standard that separates removal, defluorination, fluorine closure and mechanistic claims.

title: Rewiring versus optimization: how to connect the two philosophies of improving photorespiration?
summary: Main conclusion Synthetic bypasses as well as optimized expression of native photorespiratory enzymes improve plant performance through overlapping mechanistic principles, yet their full benefits emerge from similar and distinct features su
content: Main conclusion Synthetic bypasses as well as optimized expression of native photorespiratory enzymes improve plant performance through overlapping mechanistic principles, yet their full benefits emerge from similar and distinct features such as relief of metabolic constraints and energetic savings. Abstract The long-standing view on photorespiration as a wasteful and dispensable evolutionary relic has shifted substantially in recent years. Photorespiration is now recognized as an essential metabolic process that not only recycles 2-phosphoglycolate (2PG) to sustain oxygenic photosynthesis, but also impacts on metabolic homeostasis, redox balance, environmental acclimation, and stomatal regulation. Nevertheless, its associated CO2 loss, energetic costs, and metabolic constraints have motivated extensive efforts to improve plant productivity through genetic engineering of photorespiration. Two principal strategies have emerged: (i) introducing synthetic bypasses that reroute photorespiratory flux, particularly inside the chloroplast, and (ii) optimizing the native pathway by engineering expression of key enzymes such as 2PG phosphatase (PGLP1) and glycine decarboxylase (GDC). Although these approaches differ fundamentally in design, they produce overlapping physiological and metabolic outcomes, suggesting a partially shared mechanistic basis. One possibility is that both alleviate negative feedback from photorespiratory intermediates on carbon fixation and downstream carbon utilization. However, important differences between the strategies point to potential trade-offs in energy balance and additional, unresolved effects. Here, we propose an integrative framework in which synthetic rerouting and optimization of the native pathway are viewed not as competing strategies, but as complementary approaches. We evaluate their respective advantages and limitations and discuss how combining their strengths could contribute to the development of crops with improved performance under future climates.

title: A Chain of Multiple Cryptic N-Fe-Mn-CH4 Redox Couplings in Methanogenic Lake Sediments
summary: Approximately 30% of methane (CH4) emissions originate from freshwater sediments, typically oxygen- and sulfate (SO42-)-depleted, limiting their ability to regulate CH4 release. Here, we unravel a chain of triple cryptic N-Mn/Fe-CH4 redox c
content: Approximately 30% of methane (CH4) emissions originate from freshwater sediments, typically oxygen- and sulfate (SO42-)-depleted, limiting their ability to regulate CH4 release. Here, we unravel a chain of triple cryptic N-Mn/Fe-CH4 redox couplings in natural, unpolluted reduced methanogenic lake sediments, which impact their cycles while sustaining complex aerobic and anaerobic microbial communities. Sediment profiles revealed an unexpected increase in nitrite (NO2-) along with elevated Fe2+, Mn2+, active NC10 bacteria, and aerobic methanotrophs and decreased CH4 levels. Sediment incubations amended under anoxic conditions with labeled ammonium (15NH4+) produced 15NO2- and 15N2, indicating anaerobic NH4+ oxidation, likely coupled to Mn(IV)/Fe(III) reduction. We further identified a sink for NO3-/NO2- coupled to Fe2+ oxidation, with Fe2+ partly derived from Fe(III)-dependent CH4 oxidation. The activity of NC10 bacteria and Methylococcales suggests an additional NO2- sink via NO2- disproportionation and potentially dark oxygen production, thereby facilitating aerobic CH4 oxidation under anoxic conditions. These coupled cycles likely dominate sulfate-depleted, organic- and Mn/Fe-rich methanogenic freshwater sediments, including many eutrophic lakes and wetlands that are expected to expand under global warming.

title: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
summary: Understanding how plants integrate developmental programs with temperature-responsive growth remains a central challenge in plant biology. Here, we uncover a mechanism by which a canonical leaf senescence regulator directly governs thermomo
content: Understanding how plants integrate developmental programs with temperature-responsive growth remains a central challenge in plant biology. Here, we uncover a mechanism by which a canonical leaf senescence regulator directly governs thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis. We show that ORESARA1 (ORE1), best known for orchestrating leaf senescence, promotes warm temperature-induced hypocotyl and petiole elongation and the expression of warmth-responsive genes IAA19 and YUC8 . Mechanistically, ORE1 acts upstream of PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 4 (PIF4), the central transcriptional hub for thermomorphogenesis. ORE1 does not alter PIF4 transcript abundance but specifically stabilizes PIF4 protein under warmth by physically interacting with PIF4 in the nucleus to enhance its deubiquitination. We identify the deubiquitinase UBP12/UBP13 as an essential component of this pathway; however, PIF4 does not bind UBP12/UBP13 directly. Biochemical and genetic analyses demonstrate that ORE1 functions as a molecular scaffold, recruiting PIF4 to an ORE1-UBP12/UBP13 complex to position UBP12/UBP13 for PIF4 deubiquitination. This UBP12/UBP13-ORE1-PIF4 module establishes a paradigm where a senescence factor regulates thermomorphogenesis by orchestrating deubiquitinase-mediated tuning of PIF4 proteostasis.

title: CACNA2D2 Regulates Mitochondrial Function to Attenuate Fibrosis and Atrial Fibrillation via the cGAS-STING Pathway
summary: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is thought to be driven by atrial fibrosis. A previous study has identified the expression of calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit alpha2del
content: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is thought to be driven by atrial fibrosis. A previous study has identified the expression of calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit alpha2delta2 (CACNA2D2) is significantly downregulated in patients with AF, but its functional role remains unclear. METHODS: We analyzed CACNA2D2 expression levels using public databases and clinical samples. Fibroblast-specific Cacna2d2 knockout and overexpression models were established to assess its role in atrial fibrosis through in vivo electrophysiological recordings, histopathologic analysis, in vitro mitochondrial function assays, and biochemical studies. We also evaluated the role of Cacna2d2 in doxorubicin/myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis models. RESULTS: We observed α2δ2 (encoded by CACNA2D2) expression was significantly reduced in patients with AF and Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced AF mouse models. Fibroblast-specific knockout of Cacna2d2 exacerbated Ang II-induced atrial fibrosis, increasing AF susceptibility and duration, whereas overexpression reversed these effects. In cardiac fibroblasts, Cacna2d2 overexpression blocked induction of ACTA2 (α-SMA) and COL1A1 (Col1). Mechanistically, Cacna2d2 localized to mitochondria when overexpressed in fibroblasts, blocked TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta)-induced reactive oxygen species production and inhibit the leakage of mitochondrial DNA through the BAX/BAK channel, suppressing the activation of the cGAS-STING pathway. Notably, exogenous supplementation of Cacna2d2-overexpressing mitochondria significantly suppressed TGF-β-induced α-SMA and Col1 expression in fibroblasts. Cacna2d2 knockdown increased mortality and α-SMA expression, aggravating cardiac fibrosis in doxorubicin-treated mice, whereas its overexpression attenuated myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced hepatic fibrosis. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrates that Cacna2d2 exerts antifibrotic effects by preserving mitochondrial function and preventing mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING pathway activation, identifying Cacna2d2 as a promising novel target for fibrotic diseases, including AF.

title: Why does water quality improvement fail to persist after external nutrient loading reduction? Evidence of internal loading dominance from Yilong Lake
summary: External nutrient loading reduction is the primary strategy for mitigating eutrophication in lakes. However, many lakes do not exhibit sustained water quality improvement after strict external pollution control; instead, water quality often
content: External nutrient loading reduction is the primary strategy for mitigating eutrophication in lakes. However, many lakes do not exhibit sustained water quality improvement after strict external pollution control; instead, water quality often deteriorates abruptly following short-term recovery, a phenomenon closely linked to lake internal nutrient loading. Using Yilong Lake as a representative case, we constructed a process-based dynamic model using a Bayesian hierarchical framework, based on multi-year in situ monitoring data covering external nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) loadings as well as in-lake water quality from 2014 to 2023. The results demonstrated that despite substantial reductions in external N and P loadings over the 2014–2023 period, in-lake bulk nutrient concentrations underwent a sharp rebound after 2018. Model simulations showed the average external TN loading was 6.71 mg N/m 3 /day and the external TP loading was 0.48 mg P/m 3 /day, while the internal N flux reached 7.57 mg N/m 3 /day and the internal P flux reached 1.52 mg P/m 3 /day, confirming the dominant role of internal nutrient loading. Importantly, this shift coincided temporally with the large-scale decline of submerged macrophytes, which triggered a positive feedback loop of internal nutrient release, algal blooms, declining transparency, and further macrophyte loss, and ultimately offset the effectiveness of external nutrient reduction. We emphasize that shallow lake management must shift from sole external load reduction to a synergistic strategy combining external and internal control, together with ecosystem structural restoration.

title: Sex-specific reproductive costs and water relations in Ilex paraguariensis: insights from flower and fruit removal experiments
summary: Females of dioecious species often bear higher reproductive costs than males, but the physiological basis of these costs, whether they are carbon- or water-driven, and their modulation by the light environment remain poorly understood, part
content: Females of dioecious species often bear higher reproductive costs than males, but the physiological basis of these costs, whether they are carbon- or water-driven, and their modulation by the light environment remain poorly understood, particularly in species cultivated across contrasting light regimes. We investigated sex-specific photophysiological responses and reproductive water costs in I. paraguariensis (yerba mate), a dioecious tree cultivated for its caffeine-rich leaves in monocultures under high solar radiation and shaded agroforestry systems. In a branch-level experiment, we removed flowers from selected branches of female and male plants at anthesis in both cultivation systems and compared gas exchange during fruit ripening between treated and control branches on the same individuals. In a second experiment involving whole plants in monoculture, we removed all fruits from female plants with naturally low or high fruit load and monitored midday leaf water potential, gas exchange, and leaf shedding over 21 days. At the branch level, flower-removed branches of female plants showed higher stomatal conductance and photosynthesis than fruit-bearing branches, but this difference was confined to the monoculture. Males showed no local responses. Whole-plant fruit removal decreased stomatal conductance in high-load plants, slowed the rate of midday leaf water potential deterioration over time, improved water status by day 21, and reduced leaf shedding independently of initial fruit load, indicating a hydraulic strategy to balance water demand with supply. Our results show that reproductive costs in Ilex paraguariensis are sex-specific and light-dependent, and that in females they involve a water-driven component detectable under progressive water stress. These findings highlight the need to integrate photophysiology and hydraulic traits for climate-resilient management and suggest that agroforestry may buffer drought effects on female plants.

title: Touching corals in crises: “Feel Good” fragmentations of tentacular submarine restorations
summary: Human‐coral contact zones are full of impressions, of touching relays of power and precarity. At in‐water reef restoration nurseries on the Great Barrier Reef, Australia, restoration diver‐practitioners fragment, and cultivate thermally tol
content: Human‐coral contact zones are full of impressions, of touching relays of power and precarity. At in‐water reef restoration nurseries on the Great Barrier Reef, Australia, restoration diver‐practitioners fragment, and cultivate thermally tolerant Acropora corals for adaptive resistance to climate induced marine heat stress. As this handsy work activates a biopolitical governance of life, it is animated by a tentacular submarine. Based on novel subaquatic ethnographic fieldwork that is oriented by embodied methodologies, this article examines how cross‐species touchings in crises are generative of affective charge for restoration divers that forges “epistemic fragmentations.” Storied by a coral fragmentation or “fragging” narrative, this work interrogates how “feeling good” about interventionist touchings of reef‐dwelling beings, stirs up an uneasy, marine situated knowledge of making life in the Anthropocene. With reparative touchings impressed with power, extraction and control, this writing offers a tentacular reimagining of reef restoration biopowers—a “tentacular biopolitics”—and presses for a posthuman feminist reading of biopolitical intervention; one that becomes in touch with the more‐than‐human marine. This subaqueous ethnography thinks through how humans can better live with, make life and care for ocean companions.

title: Quasi conservative behaviour of dissolved and particulate glacial silicon in a subantarctic fjord (Kerguelen Island)
summary: Glacial meltwaters deliver substantial amounts of dissolved and reactive particulate material to coastal environments, but the transformation of glacier derived silicon (Si) during transport and their impact on coastal ecosystems remain poo
content: Glacial meltwaters deliver substantial amounts of dissolved and reactive particulate material to coastal environments, but the transformation of glacier derived silicon (Si) during transport and their impact on coastal ecosystems remain poorly understood. Accelerating glacier retreat may alter the magnitude and composition of exported material and its biogeochemical impacts downstream. Here, we investigate the influence of direct glacial inputs from the Kerguelen subantarctic Islands (Southern Ocean) on estuarine and coastal waters. We report dissolved silicon (DSi) and alkaline extractable particulate silicon (AlkExSi) concentrations and their silicon isotopic compositions (δ30SiDSi and δ30SiAlkExSi). Glacial freshwater exhibits higher DSi (41.8 µmol L−1) and AlkExSi (68 µmol L−1) concentrations as well as lighter isotopic signatures (δ30SiDSi = −0.06 to +0.58 ‰; δ30SiAlkExSi = −0.13 ± 0.04 ‰) than the surrounding seawater. Along the salinity gradient, both concentrations decrease rapidly over a few kilometres, until reaching respectively 11 and 1.2 µmol L−1 at the seawater end-member, following predominantly conservative mixing. AlkExSi concentrations are strongly correlated with suspended particulate matter (SPM) concentrations. Mineralogical characterization shows that both coarse (> 3 µm) and fine (0.2–3 µm) size fractions are very similar in their composition, which is dominated by primary minerals derived from basalt (feldspars, pyroxene) and clay minerals (smectite). SPM concentrations decreased first by 10 % below the conservative mixing line at salinities <2, while SPM and AlkExSi concentrations then follow conservative mixing downstream the estuary. Surface δ30SiDSi compositions are conservative throughout the estuary despite relatively high AlkExSi concentrations. This suggests negligible glacial AlkExSi dissolution within the estuarine Si budget, likely due to the short surface layer residence time (~10 days). We estimate glacial Si flux to be 3.7 x 104 ± 2.0 x 104 mol Si km−2 melt season−1 for DSi and 3.9 x 104 ± 2.7 x 104 mol Si km−2 melt season−1 for AlkExSi over the studied watershed. These specific fluxes are similar to global river average but lower than glacial rivers. This suggest that glacial AlkExSi is unlikely to represent a significant source of dissolved Si sustaining the phytoplankton bloom on the northeastern Kerguelen Plateau, highlighting the importance of the various characteristics of every estuary in regulating the contribution of glacial Si to coastal waters.

title: Broadleaf companion species shape ecosystem carbon storage in underplanted Pinus massoniana plantations
summary: Broadleaf underplanting can increase forest carbon (C) storage, but whether companion species differ in their contributions to tree and soil C stocks remains unclear. We compared pure Pinus massoniana stands (PM) with stands underplanted wi
content: Broadleaf underplanting can increase forest carbon (C) storage, but whether companion species differ in their contributions to tree and soil C stocks remains unclear. We compared pure Pinus massoniana stands (PM) with stands underplanted with Osmanthus fragrans (PO) or Schima superba (PS) 11 years earlier in subtropical China. We quantified vegetation and litter C stocks, soil C stocks to 60 cm on an equivalent soil mass basis, and soil nutrients, microbial biomass, potential enzyme activities, and topsoil fungal communities. Ecosystem C stocks were 50.8% higher in PO and 68.5% higher in PS than in PM. Retained pines accounted for most of the higher live tree C in both mixtures relative to PM. Compared with PO, PS stored 11.8% more ecosystem C, 12.5% more soil organic carbon (SOC), and 4.8 times as much C in broadleaf trees, despite lower litter C. P. massoniana and total live tree C stocks did not differ significantly between the mixtures. Mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC) accounted for over 96% of the SOC stock differences between each mixture and PM, while particulate organic carbon (POC) stocks did not differ significantly among treatments. MAOC concentrations were higher throughout the sampled profile, with the largest proportional differences at 40–60 cm. After accounting for treatment and soil layer, microbial biomass C was more strongly associated with MAOC than with POC. These results favor S. superba over O. fragrans for ecosystem C storage at this site, with its advantage reflected in broadleaf tree C and MAOC.

title: Geochemical Stability of a Sediment-Water System in a Reclaimed Post-Gold Mining Watershed: A PHREEQC-Based Scenario Assessment From North Sulawesi, Indonesia
summary: Post-gold-mining reclamation areas commonly undergo prolonged geochemical adjustment, yet the processes governing long-term metal stability within sediment-water systems remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the geochemi
content: Post-gold-mining reclamation areas commonly undergo prolonged geochemical adjustment, yet the processes governing long-term metal stability within sediment-water systems remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the geochemical processes controlling dissolved metal behavior in a reclaimed post-gold-mining watershed in North Sulawesi, Indonesia. Long-term surface-water monitoring data collected between 2017 and 2023 were integrated with a pH-REdox-EQuilibrium C (PHREEQC)-based geochemical scenario assessment to evaluate sediment-water geochemical stability through changes in pH and dissolved metal mobility. River pH remained within a slightly alkaline to near-neutral range throughout the monitoring period. Dissolved concentrations of Cr, Fe, Mn, Pb, and Zn showed only minor temporal variation, whereas the representative PHREEQC scenarios indicated greater geochemical sensitivity for aluminum and arsenic. In particular, the representative PHREEQC scenarios suggested greater arsenic mobility under changing pH conditions, indicating that arsenic may be more responsive than the other evaluated elements to sediment-water geochemical adjustment. The PHREEQC-based geochemical scenario assessment supported the interpretation that pH buffering plays an important role in regulating sediment-water interactions. Collectively, the findings suggest that pH-related geochemical processes contribute to the long-term geochemical stability of reclaimed sediment-water systems, while arsenic may serve as a sensitive indicator of early geochemical change. The integrated approach provides a process-based framework for environmental monitoring and adaptive post-mining management, extending reclamation assessment beyond conventional compliance-based evaluation in tropical mining watersheds.

title: Dual-atom Cu/Ni-Loaded SAPO-34 Facilitates Acetic Acid Production under Non-Thermal Plasma Catalysis
summary: Directly using CO 2 for the efficient C-C coupling with methane into valuable chemicals under atmospheric conditions provides an appealing pathway for the greenhouse gases resourcefulness utilization, but owing to the chemical inertness of
content: Directly using CO 2 for the efficient C-C coupling with methane into valuable chemicals under atmospheric conditions provides an appealing pathway for the greenhouse gases resourcefulness utilization, but owing to the chemical inertness of methane and the low activity of CO 2, this remains a significant challenge. Nonetheless, non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a distinctive approach for achieving thermodynamically unfavorable reactions at mild conditions by virtue of its non-equilibrium characteristics. Herein, we first report an NTP-assisted catalysis for the efficient CC coupling of methane and CO 2 to yield acetic acid over a novel Cu 1 Ni 1 @SAPO-34 heteronuclear diatom catalysts under ambient conditions (20 °C, 1 atm), which achievement a remarkable 1204.22 μmol·g cat -1 ·h -1 productivity and 26.49 % selectivity of acetic acid with acids account for up to 90.02 % of the liquid oxygenates selectivity. Advanced structural microscopic technology revealed that Cu and Ni dual-metal uniformly dispersed on SAPO-34 zeolites in the form of heteronuclear diatoms, which can powerfully promote the reactants dissociation to form some free radicals (e.g. CH 3 *, CO 2 *, etc.). Furthermore, in-situ spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated the synergistic effect between Cu and Ni diatoms facilitate the occurrence of efficient C-C coupling to generate acetic acid which resulting in significantly en-hancement the selectivity and production of acetic acid.

title: Beyond a Single Southern Annular Mode Pattern: Identifying Southern Hemisphere Circulation Classes With a Convolutional Autoencoder
source: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation
summary: The Southern Annular Mode (SAM), the dominant mode of extratropical atmospheric variability in the Southern Hemisphere (SH), is conventionally represented as a single empirical orthogonal function (EOF) whose polarity and amplitude vary ove
content: The Southern Annular Mode (SAM), the dominant mode of extratropical atmospheric variability in the Southern Hemisphere (SH), is conventionally represented as a single empirical orthogonal function (EOF) whose polarity and amplitude vary over time. Although highly informative, this framework favors high‐variance patterns and therefore may obscure differences among circulation patterns with similar SAM polarity. Here, we combine a convolutional autoencoder with hierarchical clustering of ERA5 monthly mean sea level pressure anomalies to develop a class‐based representation of SH circulation that does not prioritize such high‐variance patterns. Across 10 random initializations, the framework consistently identifies coherent SAM+ and higher‐amplitude SAM− classes. In nine of the 10 initializations, it also identifies a more frequently occupied, lower‐amplitude SAM− like class. This class is strongly correlated with empirical orthogonal function in the SAM− direction and differs significantly from zero over much of the domain, but is substantially more regionally asymmetric than the higher‐amplitude, strongly annular SAM− class. Transitions between the two SAM− like classes tend to occur more often than expected from their overall frequencies, although this enrichment is not statistically significant, whereas direct transitions between higher‐amplitude SAM− and SAM+ occur less often than expected. Seasonal analyses further reveal lower‐amplitude, non‐annular structures whose frequency and form vary throughout the year. These results suggest that SAM− variability may comprise both higher‐amplitude annular events and lower‐amplitude, regionally asymmetric events. The autoencoder framework therefore complements the conventional SAM index by distinguishing differences in amplitude, spatial structure, and temporal organization that are compressed within a single EOF pattern.

title: Effect of Betel Leaf Extract (Piper betle L.) and Dietary Protein Level on Performance and Carcass Traits of Local Ducks
summary: The restriction of antibiotic growth promoters has increased interest in phytogenic feed additives in poultry production. This study evaluated the effects of betel leaf (Piper betle L.) extract and dietary protein level on performance, carc
content: The restriction of antibiotic growth promoters has increased interest in phytogenic feed additives in poultry production. This study evaluated the effects of betel leaf (Piper betle L.) extract and dietary protein level on performance, carcass traits, and income over feed cost of male local ducks. A total of 135 male local ducks were assigned to a 3 × 3 factorial completely randomized design with three replications. The treatments consisted of betel leaf extract levels of 10, 20, and 30 ml and dietary protein levels of 13%, 15%, and 17%. Observed variables included feed intake, body weight gain, feed conversion ratio, slaughter weight, carcass weight, carcass percentage, and income over feed cost. Betel leaf extract significantly affected feed conversion ratio and slaughter weight (P < 0.05), whereas dietary protein level and the interaction between both factors had no significant effect on the measured variables. Among the tested extract levels, 20 ml produced the best feed conversion ratio and slaughter weight. Meanwhile, the combination of 20 ml betel leaf extract and 13% dietary protein produced the highest income over feed cost. In conclusion, betel leaf extract at 20 ml improved feed efficiency and slaughter weight, while its combination with 13% dietary protein provided the best economic return in male local ducks

title: Strain-resolved HiFi assemblies reveal seep microbiome adaptive divergence and interactions with viruses
summary: While seep-associated microbes have been broadly characterized, their strain-level genomic divergence, adaptive evolution, and virus – host interactions remain largely obscured. Here we employ HiFi sequencing to investigate microbial divers
content: While seep-associated microbes have been broadly characterized, their strain-level genomic divergence, adaptive evolution, and virus – host interactions remain largely obscured. Here we employ HiFi sequencing to investigate microbial diversity in Haima cold-seep sediments. We recover 214 complete and 79 high-quality single-contig microbial genomes. This dataset comprises 191 species, 46 of which exhibit strain-level diversity. Anaerobic methane-oxidizing archaea (ANMEs) that act as the primary marine methane sink are specifically investigated, and the ANME-1b lineage shows substantial intra-species genetic and functional diversity. Evolutionary analyses indicate that ANME-1b is under purifying selection and harbors an open pangenome potentially mediated by mobile genetic elements. We identify 18,594 viral operational taxonomic units, including nine putatively novel viral families associated with ANMEs. Extensive gene exchange between these viruses and ANME hosts may contribute to genetic divergence among ANME populations. These results provide a critical strain-level genome dataset, which facilitates illuminating their genomic and functional divergence and the driving forces that govern them.

title: Carbon flux dynamics and drivers during the initial years after boreal forest clearcutting
summary: Background Boreal forests are pivotal in the global carbon cycle, yet their carbon balance is highly sensitive to disturbance and management. Clearcutting, the dominant harvesting method within rotation forestry in managed boreal forests, a
content: Background Boreal forests are pivotal in the global carbon cycle, yet their carbon balance is highly sensitive to disturbance and management. Clearcutting, the dominant harvesting method within rotation forestry in managed boreal forests, alters carbon, water, and energy exchanges. We used a unique decade-long eddy covariance dataset from a southern boreal forest in Sweden, spanning eight years before and two years after clearcutting, to quantify changes in carbon and energy fluxes and identify shifts in their environmental controls. Results As a result of clearcutting, annual total gross primary productivity (GPP) was reduced by 61% and ecosystem respiration (Reco) by 28%; hence net ecosystem exchange (NEE) increased (towards more positive) by 131% relative to pre-clearcut conditions. Albedo and Bowen ratio increased, while the ratio of evapotranspiration to precipitation declined. Clearcutting also altered the relationships between carbon fluxes and environmental drivers. To capture both the magnitude of driver effects and the temporal dynamics, we combined mixed effect statistical modelling and machine learning. Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMM) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted that, after clearcutting, the influence of light on NEE substantially weakened, while soil temperature and soil moisture became more influential drivers of ecosystem carbon exchange. Conclusions Our results improve understanding of post-disturbance ecosystem functioning and can help improve the representation of post-clearcut dynamics in ecosystem models, thereby supporting more reliable carbon budget assessments and better-informed forest management under climate change.

title: Tidal controls on soil and water CO 2 and CH 4 emissions in an Amazon estuarine floodplain forest
summary: Amazon estuarine floodplain forests are periodically inundated by macrotides, creating dynamic redox conditions that regulate CO2 and CH4 emissions. However, few studies have simultaneously measured soil and water fluxes within the same tid
content: Amazon estuarine floodplain forests are periodically inundated by macrotides, creating dynamic redox conditions that regulate CO2 and CH4 emissions. However, few studies have simultaneously measured soil and water fluxes within the same tide-influenced system across seasons. We investigated how tidal phase (flood vs. ebb), compartment (water vs. soil), season (rainy vs. dry), and tide type (spring vs. neap) affect CO2 and CH4 emissions in a floodplain forest near Belém. Fluxes were measured hourly over complete tidal cycles using closed static chambers and automated GHG analyzers at the soil–atmosphere and water–atmosphere interfaces, across eight campaigns (four per season) covering spring and neap tides. Soil dominated CO2 emissions, while water dominated CH4 emissions. Ebb tide increased emissions relative to flood tide, especially for water CH4 and CO2. The compartment × tidal phase interaction was significant for CO2 but not for CH4; season and tide type had no effect. CO2 and CH4 are functionally decoupled between compartments, with tidal phase acting as a short-term driver. Integrated soil–water sampling across diurnal and tidal cycles is essential to quantify GHG balances in these ecosystems.

title: Spatiotemporal Profiles, Pollution Sources and Ecological Risk Assessment of Poly-and Perfluoroalkyl Substances in Sediments of Lake Victoria, East Africa
summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants with potential bioaccumulative and ecotoxicological effects. Yet little is known about their occurrence, sources, and ecological risks in Lake Victoria sediments. PFAS c
content: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants with potential bioaccumulative and ecotoxicological effects. Yet little is known about their occurrence, sources, and ecological risks in Lake Victoria sediments. PFAS contamination may threaten the lake’s ecological integrity and socio-economic importance. To address these gaps, we investigated PFAS occurrence and distribution in Lake Victoria sediments, elucidated their potential sources, and associated ecological risks. Sediment samples were collected in September/October 2017, May 2019 and September/October 2019 and extracted on an ultrasonic bath, cleaned up by solid phase extraction and analyzed for PFAS using liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry. Total PFAS (∑PFAS) levels ranged from < 6.78 to 1021 ng/kg dw in September/October 2017, 165 to 1004 ng/kg dw in May 2019, and < 1.98 to 593 ng/kg dw in September/October 2019. Intra-region PFAS spatial distribution was site-dependent with the highest concentrations observed at sites near urban centers. PFAS in the core sediment implied a significant post depositional redistribution of PFAS in Lake Victoria. In general, there was no significant lake-wide spatial structure exhibited by the PFAS concentration. Despite the low PFAS concentration, Principal Component Analysis-Multiple Linear Regression (PCA-MLR) suggested that the primary source of PFAS into Lake Victoria was atmospheric deposition. PFAS in Lake Victoria posed moderate to negligible ecological risks except for PFBA. Occurrence of PFAS in Lake Victoria shows that contamination pressures are persistent and that continuous monitoring and mitigation are necessary to protect the ecological and socio-economic functions of the lake.

title: Carbon-Smart Agriculture and Farm Profitability: A Systematic Literature Review of Economic and Environmental Trade-offs
summary: Carbon-smart agriculture is promoted as a way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while sustaining farm income, yet evidence on when this dual benefit materializes remains fragmented. This study synthesizes the conditions under which carbon-
content: Carbon-smart agriculture is promoted as a way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while sustaining farm income, yet evidence on when this dual benefit materializes remains fragmented. This study synthesizes the conditions under which carbon-smart practices are profitable or unprofitable and the economic–environmental trade-offs involved. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of 15 publications (2021–2026) was analyzed using thematic content analysis and a synthesis matrix; quantitative results are reported in their original units. Adoption studies reported higher farm income, for example 20.3% higher income per hectare in southern Ethiopia and about 40% in drought-prone India. Modeling studies indicated that regional emissions from irrigated cropping in Australia could fall by up to 50% without reducing total gross margins, and that carbon sequestration on farmland could generate up to USD 375 billion in additional producer revenue at USD 160 per tCO₂e. These benefits are conditional on input-use efficiency, practice combinations, transition and verification costs, farm characteristics, and credible carbon payment systems, and capital-intensive practices tend to be viable only with incentives. Economic and environmental benefits should be assessed jointly rather than assumed to coincide. The evidence is dominated by observational studies of climate-smart agriculture in general, and carbon-specific farm-level cost data remain scarce.

title: Marine Meteorology: An Introduction
summary: Earth's surface is 71% water, and the ocean plays a critical role in shaping global weather patterns and climate systems. Many weather disturbances start over Earth’s land area but are greatly modified by the ocean. This book provides a com
content: Earth's surface is 71% water, and the ocean plays a critical role in shaping global weather patterns and climate systems. Many weather disturbances start over Earth’s land area but are greatly modified by the ocean. This book provides a comprehensive exploration of marine meteorology, examining the complex interactions between the atmosphere and ocean that drive weather at sea. This interdisciplinary text bridges meteorology, oceanography, and ocean engineering to explain the fundamental principles governing atmospheric behavior in marine environments and their far-reaching impacts on maritime operations, coastal infrastructure, and marine ecosystems. It includes real-world examples and problems throughout, reinforcing core concepts of phenomena unique to the marine boundary layer. Features Explains the theories, practices, and complexities of weather over the marine environment. Provides highly quantitative coverage of weather and ocean phenomena from the Arctic to the tropics. Integrates discussions and examples of long-standing traditional approaches to basic weather fundamentals with high-quality satellite data. Explains meteorological analysis focused on the atmospheric components utilizing the most recent datasets. Draws on the author’s latest research in the field and his vast teaching experience. Features case studies and questions at the end of each chapter. Designed for upper-level undergraduate and graduate courses, this primary textbook equips students in meteorology, oceanography, ocean engineering, and related fields with essential knowledge for understanding and predicting weather in the marine environment. Professionals from such areas can also use this book as an insightful resource for understanding and forecasting weather phenomena.

title: Quenching or Accelerating Large‐Scale Surface Reconstruction by the Lightest Element: Facet‐Dependent Hydrogen‐Induced Reconstruction (HIR)
summary: Adsorbate-induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd-Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to under
content: Adsorbate-induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd-Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to undergo hydrogen-induced surface reconstruction (HIR) that exposes Pd active sites. However, the kinetic origin of HIR remains unknown because hydrogen is difficult to image. Here, using large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we resolve the kinetics of H-driven reconstruction. On Pd-covered Ag surfaces, reconstruction initially involves Pd-Ag exchange at domain peripheries and Ag atoms popping up to encapsulate exposed Pd. This process is faster on (100) than on (111). Hydrogen suppresses reconstruction on (111) above 0.3 ML, but accelerates Pd dispersion and encapsulation on (100) mediated by transient Pd-H pair formation. This facet dependence arises from hydrogen-induced kinetic hindrance of edge Pd diffusion away from Pd domains on (111). Analysis of MD-derived surface structures further shows that the Pd3 triangular surface pattern favors selective acetylene hydrogenation, confirming HIR's role in determining active-site structure. These findings provide the first evidence for facet-dependent, large-scale surface reconstruction induced by the lightest element and establish HIR as a key determinant of catalytic activity and selectivity.

title: GRA-based multi-objective optimization for sustainable EDM using triple component surfactant infused condensate water dielectric
summary: The electric discharge machining (EDM) has emerged as promising choice for producing high precision and intricate profiles in advance engineering materials like AA6083. It is pertinent to mention that EDM performance is mainly dependent on
content: The electric discharge machining (EDM) has emerged as promising choice for producing high precision and intricate profiles in advance engineering materials like AA6083. It is pertinent to mention that EDM performance is mainly dependent on the characteristics of the dielectric. The traditional dielectric i.e. kerosene or mineral oil based, produces toxic fumes which is a serious concern for the environment and operator,s health. The application of water based dielectric is a viable choice if the issue of unstable discharge and low dielectric strength may be overcome. Therefore, the objective of this research work is to propose a novel approach combining nanopowder, non-ionic surfactant and air-conditioner (AC) condensate water, as triple component dielectric to keep the procedure eco-friendly. The aforementioned unique combination of condensate water with nano-additives in non-ionic surfactant has never been comprehensively investigated so far in EDM of AA6083. Taguchi,s experimental design was used for performing the experimentation. Based on the findings it has been concluded that inclusion of nano-additives in the presence of Span 20 surfactant in water has significantly improved spark stability and ensure better flushing of debris. Al 2 O 3 outperformed SiC in terms of nanopowder, resulting in higher material removal rate (MRR), lower tool wear rate (TWR), superior surface finishing, and improved dimensional precision. Lesser powder concentration (0.5 g/L) has been found suitable for both nanopowders in terms of MRR, surface roughness and overcut. Interestingly, high surfactant concentration provides high MRR, low TWR and overcut whereas, low surfactant concentration (4 g/L) yielded better surface finish. The process has also been optimized using grey relational analysis (GRA) multi-objective optimization approach. A significant enhancement in material removal rate (MRR) i.e. 4.79 fold (378.57% ) was noted if process is carried out at optimal settings. Remarkably, the magnitude of tool wear rate (TWR), surface roughness (SR), and overcut (OC) reduce by 3.89 fold, 1.98 fold and 2.79 fold respectively, if the proposed combination is used instead of non-optimal settings in surfactant infused nano powder mixed EDM.

title: The Classification of Compensation for Environmental Damage within the Liability of Environmental Offenders: Establishing the Status of Preferential Creditors
summary: Climate change and environmental degradation demand a legal shift from an anthropocentric to an ecocentric paradigm, including in bankruptcy law, which has so far been designed to settle commercial debts. This study examines the position of
content: Climate change and environmental degradation demand a legal shift from an anthropocentric to an ecocentric paradigm, including in bankruptcy law, which has so far been designed to settle commercial debts. This study examines the position of environmental compensation claims in the distribution of the bankruptcy estate under Law No. 37 of 2004 and formulates a reconstruction of that framework. The problem arises when a corporation held liable for environmental damage under the polluter pays principle in Law No. 32 of 2009 is declared bankrupt. The state is not notified, misses the verification deadline, and must pursue a renvoi procedure, because the law has no mechanism to inform public creditors holding final environmental judgments. Environmental claims are also left in the concurrent creditor class, which cannot accommodate the intergenerational public interest in ecological restoration. This normative legal study uses statutory, conceptual, case-based, and comparative approaches, drawing on Canada, the United States, the European Union (especially Germany and France), Australia, the United Kingdom, and China. The study finds that bankruptcy should not be used to force a polluter into insolvency, because a dispute over environmental damage cannot meet the “simple proof” requirement. Bankruptcy is instead a forum for recognizing established claims. The study proposes an “ecological preferential claim” model that distinguishes obligations by the time they arose. Once a debtor is bankrupt, pre-petition claims supported by a final judgment or a direct link to the pollution source rank immediately after tax claims, while post-petition remediation costs are treated as estate debts. Wages and separatist creditors’ rights remain intact. The study recommends amending the Bankruptcy Law, requiring curators to register environmental judgments without separate litigation, strengthening the prosecutor’s role, reforming restoration fund governance, and aligning the model with national climate accountability.

title: A snapshot review on inverted thermal degradation for frugal cellulose fiber processing
summary: Natural fibers are often the basis for neoteric materials for energy storage, agriculture, environmental remediation, and catalysis. Thermal processing, such as Inverted Thermal Degradation ( i TD ), has emerged as a vital processing method
content: Natural fibers are often the basis for neoteric materials for energy storage, agriculture, environmental remediation, and catalysis. Thermal processing, such as Inverted Thermal Degradation ( i TD ), has emerged as a vital processing method. Understanding the mechanisms governing combustion propagation, however, remains challenging. Existing theoretical frameworks rely on idealized conditions, despite combustion being a highly coupled, nonlinear reaction. This discrepancy has limited the predictive understanding of thermal degradation and perception of combustion as an uncontrollable runaway reaction. Advancing understanding of the thermodynamic and kinetic processes underlying i TD is critical in the development of carbonaceous materials, particularly, the influence of intrinsic and extrinsic heterogeneities on the reaction pathways. Nonequilibrium thermodynamics can provide a framework by defining combustion through interconnected transport and reaction phenomena, enabling the identification and manipulation of governing parameters. This offers a pathway toward achieving predictive control of i TD and the rational design of materials with tailored structures and functionalities.

title: Observational insights on sediment dynamics along the Singapore Strait
summary: Accurate characterization of offshore sediment is fundamental to advancing coastal management, engineering, and environmental resilience. While sediment properties exert a critical influence on coastline stability, they remain inadequately
content: Accurate characterization of offshore sediment is fundamental to advancing coastal management, engineering, and environmental resilience. While sediment properties exert a critical influence on coastline stability, they remain inadequately understood along complex urban coastlines where anthropogenic modifications intersect with natural hydrodynamic processes. This limitation is particularly important in narrow tropical straits, where strong tidal currents, monsoon variability, complex bathymetry and coastal modification interact over short spatial scales. Here we present a new year-long observational record of seabed sediment characteristics, geochemical properties, and water column parameters obtained from nearshore and offshore sites across the Singapore Strait. Utilizing monthly field survey data collected from October 2023 to October 2024, alongside high-resolution ocean reanalysis, we examine sediment–hydrodynamic variability. Our results indicate pronounced spatial heterogeneity in sediment properties, including a general westward-coarsening grain-size gradient, and marked nearshore-offshore contrasts in sediment texture and geochemical composition. Sediment and turbidity variability also differ substantially among sites experiencing broadly similar seasonal climate forcing. Our results suggest that monsoon forcing provides an important seasonal background, while local forcing strongly modulates sediment behaviour at individual sites experiencing similar climatic conditions. Our study highlights the critical need for sustained, spatially resolved high-resolution observational data with potential to improve existing model-based approaches in monitoring coastal change with implications for sustainable coastal management, marine habitat conservation, and climate adaptation strategies.

title: OTIMIZAÇÃO DA IRRIGAÇÃO SUPLEMENTAR NA ESTAÇÃO SECA PARA O ESTABELECIMENTO INICIAL DE Euterpe precatoria Mart. NO SUDOESTE DA AMAZÔNIA
summary: OPTIMIZING DRY-SEASON SUPPLEMENTAL IRRIGATION FOR EARLY ESTABLISHMENT OF Euterpe precatoria Mart. IN THE SOUTHWESTERN AMAZON MÁRCIA CHAVES DA SILVA1; CLEYTON SILVA DE ARAÚJO1; LEONARDO PAULA DE SOUZA1; AURENY MARIA PEREIRA LUNZ2; JARDERSON
content: OPTIMIZING DRY-SEASON SUPPLEMENTAL IRRIGATION FOR EARLY ESTABLISHMENT OF Euterpe precatoria Mart. IN THE SOUTHWESTERN AMAZON MÁRCIA CHAVES DA SILVA1; CLEYTON SILVA DE ARAÚJO1; LEONARDO PAULA DE SOUZA1; AURENY MARIA PEREIRA LUNZ2; JARDERSON CASSIMIRO CARNEIRO1 E ROMEU DE CARVALHO ANDRADE NETO 3 1 Center for Biological and Natural Sciences, Federal University of Acre, BR-364 Highway, km 04, Distrito Industrial, Rio Branco, AC, 69915-900, Brazil. email: marcia.chaves@sou.ufac.br; cleytonsdearaujo@gmail.com; leonardo.souza@ufac.br; jarderson.carneiro@ufac.br. ORCID (https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1348-9875; https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9273-7322; https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4522-8020; https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6908-9400). 2 Embrapa Acre, Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation, BR-364 Highway, km 14, Rio Branco/Porto Velho, P.O. Box 321, Rio Branco, AC, 69900-970, Brazil. email: aureny.lunz@embrapa.br. ORCID (https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2697-7509). 3 Embrapa Coastal Tablelands, Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation, Avenida Governador Paulo Barreto de Menezes, 3250, Jardins, Aracaju, SE, 49025-040, Brazil. email: romeu.andrade@embrapa.br. ORCID (https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8238-7020). 1 ABSTRACT Euterpe precatoria establishment in upland areas of the southwestern Amazon is constrained by seasonal water limitation. A field experiment conducted in Rio Branco, Acre, Brazil, during the 2022 dry season evaluated five daily supplemental irrigation levels applied by microsprinklers (0, 8, 16, 24, and 32 L plant⁻¹ day⁻¹) in a banana-intercropped system. Treatments were arranged in a randomized complete block design with four replicates. Irrigation was managed from May to October 2022, and plant morphology was assessed monthly from June to October, corresponding to 5–9 months after planting. Mixed-effects models were used to characterize temporal growth responses and estimate irrigation optima. Mortality reached 25% under rainfed conditions, whereas no mortality was recorded in any irrigated treatment. Growth responses varied with time and were nonlinear across the irrigation gradient, with most stem and canopy traits reaching fitted maxima near 20–24 L plant⁻¹ day⁻¹ at 9 months after planting. Stem diameter reached 25.9 mm at approximately 22.0 L plant⁻¹ day⁻¹, crown diameter reached 85.8 cm at 20.8 L plant⁻¹ day⁻¹, and leaf number reached 5.09 leaves plant⁻¹ at 24.0 L plant⁻¹ day⁻¹. At the highest irrigation level, plants were taller but also showed the highest height:stem diameter ratio, indicating that vertical growth increased more strongly than radial growth toward the upper end of the irrigation gradient. Overall, the results identify 20–24 L plant⁻¹ day⁻¹ as an operational supplemental irrigation range for early dry-season establishment of E. precatoria under the conditions evaluated. Keywords: açaí palm, seedling establishment, water stress, microsprinkler irrigation, canopy development. SILVA, M. C. da; ARAÚJO, C. S. de; SOUZA, L. P. de; LUN

title: Biomaterial-enabled monitoring of gastrointestinal leakage and anastomotic compromise: material mechanisms and postoperative observation
summary: Responsive biomaterials can translate postoperative chemistry and physiology into signals of tissue condition, local fluid exposure and loss of containment. This critical review examines how network design, tissue interfaces and readout arc
content: Responsive biomaterials can translate postoperative chemistry and physiology into signals of tissue condition, local fluid exposure and loss of containment. This critical review examines how network design, tissue interfaces and readout architecture determine the meaning and duration of those observations. Three overlapping functions organize the synthesis: current-state monitoring, exposure recording and single-use alarms. Transport, binding and reaction govern whether a material follows present conditions or retains earlier exposure; tissue remodeling, protection and reader access determine its functional observation window. In sensing seals, adhesion and barrier structure also redirect the fluid supplying the signal. Within-study comparisons distinguish partitioning from mobility, retained responsiveness from calibration accuracy, and interfacial attachment from bulk mechanics. Gastrointestinal experiments demonstrate physiological recording, delayed interrogation of persistent material changes and accessible fluid sampling, while emerging human evidence remains heterogeneous in surgical setting and acquisition protocol. We derive task-matched design priorities: preserve the temporal meaning of the signal, maintain target and reader access, and evaluate the assembled device under the mechanical and chemical conditions of its intended site. Clinical translation requires a defined confirmatory-care pathway and evidence that usable information improves assessment without delaying indicated treatment.

title: Primary school student teachers’ scientific literacy on biodiversity loss: The use and evaluation of source texts
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of Environmental and Science Education
summary: Finding reliable information is increasingly difficult as false information spreads on the Internet, necessitating scientific literacy for both students and teachers. This study examines the source texts used by 71 first-year primary school
content: Finding reliable information is increasingly difficult as false information spreads on the Internet, necessitating scientific literacy for both students and teachers. This study examines the source texts used by 71 first-year primary school student teachers when presented with ten different texts in an electronic learning environment and how they evaluated those sources. The participants were tasked with summarizing texts on biodiversity loss and assessing their reliability and usefulness. Of the ten texts, four were relevant, four irrelevant, and two contained false information. The analysis indicated that whilst all student teachers utilized at least one relevant source, irrelevant texts and false texts were also incorporated. Evaluations revealed uncertainty regarding the reliability and usefulness of the sources, emphasizing the need to consider multiple factors rather than only isolated aspects in the source texts. The study concludes with suggestions for enhancing scientific literacy in teacher education programs.

title: From physical principles to next generation of process-based simulations of water flow in arable soils
summary: Computational process-based models have become essential tools for understanding and predicting water flow in arable soils, supporting applications ranging from irrigation management to assessments of crop yield and agricultural systems sus
content: Computational process-based models have become essential tools for understanding and predicting water flow in arable soils, supporting applications ranging from irrigation management to assessments of crop yield and agricultural systems sustainability. Most hydrological models are built upon the Richards equation and its constitutive hydraulic functions, which provide a physically based approach for simulating soil water movement under variably saturated conditions. Despite significant advances in numerical methods and computational efficiency, challenges regarding soil heterogeneity and dynamics, hydraulic parameterization, root water uptake, boundary condition representation, model calibration, and predictive uncertainty remain. This review synthesizes the current state of process-based simulations of soil water flow with a particular focus on agricultural systems. First, the physical and numerical foundations of soil water flow modeling are examined, including the governing equations, solution strategies, and their associated limitations. Then, direct and indirect methods for determining or estimating soil hydraulic properties are discussed. Subsequently, the representation of root water uptake and boundary conditions is evaluated, highlighting the trade-offs between physical realism, data requirements, and computational feasibility. Attention is given to model calibration procedures and parameter uncertainty. Emerging developments involving remote sensing, hybrid physical-statistical models, physics-informed neural networks, and operator-learning frameworks are also discussed as potential pathways toward next-generation hydrological modeling. Overall, advances in hydrological modeling are expected to improve the accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency of simulations by integrating multi-source observations, strengthening process representation, quantifying predictive uncertainty, and enabling scalable modeling strategies to support decision-making across diverse agricultural environments.

title: Vertical and Spatial Patterns of Microplastics in Norwegian Sea Shelf Sediments May Influence and Be Influenced by Infaunal Benthic Species Richness and Polychaeta Subcommunity Structure
summary: The vertical and spatial distribution of microplastics in seabed sediments may be influenced by benthic fauna and bioturbation processes, which may themselves be affected by microplastic contamination. We investigated microplastic accumulat
content: The vertical and spatial distribution of microplastics in seabed sediments may be influenced by benthic fauna and bioturbation processes, which may themselves be affected by microplastic contamination. We investigated microplastic accumulation in sediments and sediment cores from biodiverse areas of the Norwegian Sea and the mid-Norwegian Continental Shelf. Comprehensive analytical procedures for microplastic identification were paired with radiometric dating, X-ray imaging, grain size measurements, and benthic fauna community analysis. Microplastics (≥43 μm) were quantified in 20 of 23 samples, with concentrations in surface sediments (0–2 cm) from 23 to 1310 particles/kg dry weight and the highest concentrations in the sediment cores at 2–4 cm depth. Signs of benthic activities including bioturbation were evident. Microplastic concentration in surface sediments showed strong, significant negative relationships with macrofaunal abundance and taxa richness. A 10-fold increase in microplastic concentration corresponded to a 37.2% decrease in total abundance and a 22.3% decrease in taxa richness. Multivariate analyses identified Polychaeta as the community group most strongly associated with microplastic concentration, with an effect comparable to that of water depth. The abundance-weighted proportion of deposit feeders was also negatively related to microplastic levels, suggesting a role for faunal sediment reworking in microplastic redistribution. However, the mechanistic direction of this relationship could not be resolved in the present study. Our findings highlight the need to couple field observations at the community level with controlled mesocosm experiments to disentangle sediment reworking as a driver of microplastic distribution from the toxicological effects of microplastics, and associated pollutants such as plastic chemicals, on deep sea biota.

title: Moonlighting proteins in chloroplasts: known functions and unexplored roles
summary: Chloroplasts are dynamic organelles that play central roles in photosynthesis, metabolism, cellular homeostasis and environmental responses. Their functional diversity is reflected in a dynamic proteome in which individual proteins may perf
content: Chloroplasts are dynamic organelles that play central roles in photosynthesis, metabolism, cellular homeostasis and environmental responses. Their functional diversity is reflected in a dynamic proteome in which individual proteins may perform multiple functions, a phenomenon known as protein moonlighting. Protein moonlighting, which is defined as the ability of a single polypeptide to perform distinct but physiologically relevant functions, is an important mechanism for increasing the functional capacity of the chloroplast proteome without additional genes being required. Although protein moonlighting has been extensively studied in other cellular compartments, its significance in chloroplasts remains incompletely understood. This review summarizes the mechanisms underlying chloroplast protein moonlighting and highlights established, potential and predicted examples in plants and other photosynthetic organisms. The described moonlighting proteins illustrate how chloroplast proteins can connect photosynthesis and metabolism with protein homeostasis, chloroplast and nuclear gene expression, genome organization, stress responses and chloroplast development. Particular attention is given to the distinction between experimentally validated moonlighting functions and proposed activities that require further investigation. In addition, the potential influence of diurnal and circadian regulation on protein multifunctionality is discussed. Despite growing evidence for functional diversification within the chloroplast proteome, establishing the mechanistic independence and physiological relevance of additional protein functions remains a major challenge. However, understanding these functions may provide new insights into chloroplast regulation and plant adaptation to environmental stresses.

title: Bubble-manipulated glioma ecosystem platform for investigating cell migration behavior and therapeutic response prediction
summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a dismal prognosis. Although 3D-engineered cellular microenvironments better recapitulate in vivo configurations than 2D monolayer cultures, most current glioma models are used for
content: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a dismal prognosis. Although 3D-engineered cellular microenvironments better recapitulate in vivo configurations than 2D monolayer cultures, most current glioma models are used for mechanistic investigations rather than clinical treatment decision-making. Here, we report a modular 3D-engineered scaffold platform with tailored geometries that accommodate diverse cellular combinations. We select glioma stem cells (GSCs), endothelial cells, and THP-1-derived macrophages and design scaffold niches based on their growth characteristics, achieving successful colonization. Using optothermally generated bubble microrobots, we precisely manipulate and assemble these cellularized scaffolds into complex, reconfigurable 3D glioma microenvironments. This bubble-manipulated glioma ecosystem (BMGE) platform enables investigation of multicellular interactions and cell migration, sustains patient-derived cells with in vivo-like features, and provides prognostically relevant insights for eight patient cases. The BMGE platform offers high biomimicry and practical utility for understanding glioblastoma progression and accelerating personalized treatment strategies.

title: Quality, land-use efficiency and economics of high-density cotton in paired-row pigeonpea intercropping under different nitrogen and growth regulator management
summary: The experiment was carried out to examine the performance of paired-row pigeonpea in a high-density cotton intercropping system and to evaluate the quality and economics of high-density cotton grown with paired-row pigeonpea. The space betw
content: The experiment was carried out to examine the performance of paired-row pigeonpea in a high-density cotton intercropping system and to evaluate the quality and economics of high-density cotton grown with paired-row pigeonpea. The space between the two paired rows of pigeonpea was effectively used to grow high-density cotton.
