The trial was conducted at the Agricultural Research Station (ARS) Tandur, Vikarabad during kharif 2023–24 and 2024–25 and was laid out in a split-plot design with 3 replications. The main plots comprised paired rows of pigeonpea between high-density cotton spacing, while the subplots consisted of 6 treatments with varying levels of nitrogen and growth regulators. Among the main plots, the high-density cotton spacing of 60 × 15 cm (M1) significantly recorded the highest mean maximum gross returns (243347), net returns and benefit–cost (B : C) ratio (2.68), as well as land equivalent ratio (LER) of (1.36). However, the superior fibre quality parameters were observed with the higher density cotton spacing of 100 × 15 cm (M3) during 2023–24, 2024–25 and in the mean results. Among the subplots, the highest mean gross returns (243589), net returns (155015), B : C ratio (2.74) and LER of (1.38) were recorded and the maximum quality parameters were obtained with the application of 125 % recommended dose of nitrogen (RDN) + mepiquat chloride 50 ppm at the square formation and flowering stage (S3). This treatment was statistically comparable to the application of 100 % RDN + mepiquat chloride 50 ppm at the square formation and flowering stage (S2), which produced mean gross returns (213855), net returns (136907), B : C ratio (2.55) and LER of (1.31). The application of 125 % RDN + cycocel 60 ppm at the square formation and flowering stage (S6) also showed comparable performance, with mean gross returns (227144), net returns (138970), B : C ratio (2.57) and LER of 1.28 across 2023–24, 2024–25 and the mean data.

title: Engineering Kluyveromyces marxianus for high-titer succinic acid production at elevated temperature and low pH from sugarcane bagasse hemicellulose hydrolysate and crude biodiesel glycerol
summary: Succinic acid is a high-priority platform chemical, yet industrial biomanufacturing is constrained by fermentation cooling duty, stoichiometric base neutralisers, and downstream calcium sulfate (gypsum) sludge. Here, thermotolerant, acidoto
content: Succinic acid is a high-priority platform chemical, yet industrial biomanufacturing is constrained by fermentation cooling duty, stoichiometric base neutralisers, and downstream calcium sulfate (gypsum) sludge. Here, thermotolerant, acidotolerant yeast Kluyveromyces marxianus was engineered for reductive tricarboxylic acid (rTCA) succinic acid production from non-food residues at 42°C and pH 3.65. Integrating Actinobacillus succinogenes PEP carboxykinase (AsPCK), Corynebacterium glutamicum malate dehydrogenase (CgMDH), native fumarase (KmFUM1), Trypanosoma brucei NADH-dependent fumarate reductase (TbFRD), and Schizosaccharomyces pombe dicarboxylate exporter (SpMAE1) established the synthetic conduit. Sequential CRISPR/Cas9 disruption of KmADH1, KmGPD1, KmSDH1, and KmACH1 suppressed ethanol and glycerol overflow and converted acetate excretion into net uptake, raising succinic acid titre by 97.6% (2.51 to 4.96 g/L) and product-carbon selectivity from 7.0% to 64.3% C-mol on hydrolysate. Non-calcium Amberlite XAD-16N detoxification of sugarcane bagasse hemicellulose hydrolysate (SBH) avoided upstream gypsum, while Acidothermus cellulolyticus xylose isomerase (AcXI) with KmXKS1, KmTAL1, and KmTKL1 enabled pentose assimilation. In 2.5 L bioreactors (42°C, pH 3.65, KOH titration), the strain produced 23.50 g/L in batch (18 h) and 58.42 g/L in fed-batch (72 h; 0.379 g/g yield; 0.811 g/L/h). Glycerol-fed cultures combining Klebsiella pneumoniae glycerol dehydrogenase (KpGDH) and KmDAK1 with rTCA amplification expanded whole-cell NADH by 145.2% (1.15 to 2.82 µmol/g DCW), reaching 71.20 g/L on pure glycerol (0.486 g/g) and 65.18 g/L on crude biodiesel glycerol (0.463 g/g). KOH titration at pH 3.65 eliminates gypsum (0 vs 1,458 kg/t) and cuts base/acid demand by 78.0%, while 42°C operation removes mechanical chilling (113.7 kWhₑ/t) and saves 20.9% cooling water.

title: Cultivating Sustainability: Agricultural Value Added Per Worker, Forest Resources and Carbon Emissions in Six Emerging and Developing Economies
summary: This study examines the conditional associations of agricultural value added per worker (AVA), forest area, and per capita carbon dioxide emissions in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Mexico over 1990–2021. The BENIVM
content: This study examines the conditional associations of agricultural value added per worker (AVA), forest area, and per capita carbon dioxide emissions in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Mexico over 1990–2021. The BENIVM countries constitute a purposively selected, structurally heterogeneous comparison group. AVA is measured as agriculture, forestry, and fishing value added per worker, an accounting‐based indicator of labour productivity rather than total factor productivity or technological efficiency. Country‐specific dynamic autoregressive distributed lag (NDARDL) simulations and kernel‐based regularised least squares (KRLS) characterise temporal adjustment and nonlinear marginal associations. ARDL/NDARDL estimates associate higher AVA with lower emissions in five countries but with higher emissions in Mexico; the forest‐area coefficients are negative in these national dynamic models. However, KRLS and pooled panel sensitivity estimates do not consistently reproduce these relationships. Income, trade, and foreign‐investment associations are likewise context‐dependent. The contribution lies in documenting this empirical heterogeneity, not in methodological novelty or causal identification. Additional parsimonious first‐difference regressions and a residual dependence diagnostic offer short‐run sensitivity evidence but do not establish causal effects or overcome omitted‐energy concerns. Policy implications are distinguished from broader interventions requiring separate evaluation.

title: Aqua Regia in Platinum-Group Metal Processing: Reaction Chemistry, Chloride Speciation, Dissolution Mechanisms, Selectivity, and Recovery Challenges—A Critical Review
source: Journal International Review of Research Studies
summary: Aqua regia remains an important benchmark lixiviant for platinum-group metals (PGMs), yet the shorthand HCl:HNO₃ = 3:1 obscures its time-dependent oxidant chemistry and the decisive influence of support materials and chloride speciation. Th
content: Aqua regia remains an important benchmark lixiviant for platinum-group metals (PGMs), yet the shorthand HCl:HNO₃ = 3:1 obscures its time-dependent oxidant chemistry and the decisive influence of support materials and chloride speciation. This critical review examines aqua-regia formation, oxidation–complexation coupling, dissolution mechanisms for Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os, operating conditions, feed-matrix effects, kinetic interpretation, co-dissolution, separation, and reagent management. A curated body of 145 cited publications spanning 2010–2026 provides the documentary basis, supplemented by qualitative process-chemistry analysis. The literature indicates that a nominal acid ratio is not a transferable measure of leaching severity: absolute concentration, acid age, oxidant volatilization, accessible metal surface, matrix consumption, and reactor configuration must also be stated. The markedly different responses of individual PGMs and the speciation dependence of downstream separation preclude a universal maximum-extraction flowsheet. The review proposes a reporting framework linking effective oxidant availability and free chloride activity to metal-specific dissolution, impurity loading, and refined-metal yield, and identifies in situ speciation, gas quantification, selective rhodium recovery, and integrated techno-economic evaluation as priorities.

title: Programmable Interfacial Evolution in Seawater Iodine Batteries Guided by an Electrochemical Vector‐Coupled Free‐Energy Descriptor
summary: Interface, as predominant electrochemical reaction region at the metal anode, has to face challenging issues in harsh seawater environment. Highly reactive soluble halogen intermediates can facilitate the multiple electron transfer process
content: Interface, as predominant electrochemical reaction region at the metal anode, has to face challenging issues in harsh seawater environment. Highly reactive soluble halogen intermediates can facilitate the multiple electron transfer process during electrochemical reaction, but the severe shuttle behaviors and cascade corrosion would become more serious in chlorine enriched seawater electrolyte. Conventional solution focused on static interfacial regulation with strong confinement, the lack of dynamical electrochemical response results in irreversible active iodine loss, further accelerate the battery failure. Given that, we proposed a novel theoretical descriptor to qualify electrochemical vector coupled free energy landscape, denoted as 𝒢 ev (E, Δ G 0). By coupling electric filed with free energy, the electrochemically programming interface with dynamic self‐adaptive halogen regulation (AHR) can be described quantitively. Taking an α‐aminoketone‐contained bio‐interface as an example, along with the polarization variation over electrochemical reaction, the interface enables reversible capture to release shift of halogen intermediates, and thus realize reversible modulation of Cl‐coordinated iodine species by leveraging thermodynamic gating mechanism. An emergency power supply system based on seawater‐activated flexible fiber batteries could well operate in underwater portable situation. Our work unveils a novel research perspective on interface regulation strategies, to build an initiative adaptive interface rather than conventional ways.

title: Active Site Migration in Heterogeneous Hydrogenation by Coupling N‐Doped Carbon and Platinum
summary: In heterogeneous hydrogenation, porous carbon supports are usually treated as passive dispersants or electronic scaffolds for metal nanoparticles. Here, we show that in specifically designed N‐doped carbon electrically coupled to Pt, the op
content: In heterogeneous hydrogenation, porous carbon supports are usually treated as passive dispersants or electronic scaffolds for metal nanoparticles. Here, we show that in specifically designed N‐doped carbon electrically coupled to Pt, the operative reduction locus can shift between catalyst components. Using p‐nitrophenol (pNP) hydrogenation as a model reaction, we decouple hydrogen activation from substrate reduction in unbiased electrochemical and thermochemical configurations. While Pt/C is required for hydrogen activation, the nitrogen‐doped TCNQ900 carbon acts as an efficient pNP reduction interface once supplied with ‐derived electrons and protons. Electrochemical measurements show that coupling to TCNQ900 displaces Pt/C from its / equilibrium along its hydrogen oxidation polarization curve, establishing a mixed‐potential‐driven electron flux toward the carbon phase. Under high ‐activation capacity, Pt‐centered (thermochemical) and carbon‐centered reductions (electrochemical) operate in parallel, increasing the overall rate. Under ‐activation‐limited conditions, electrical coupling relocates the dominant reduction locus from Pt/C to TCNQ900 with little change in total rate. We describe this reversible redistribution of catalytic function as active‐site migration. These results show that carbons can be chemically designed to serve not as passive supports, but as electronically coupled reduction interfaces that redirect hydrogenation pathways in multicomponent catalysts.

title: Different responses to manganese toxicity and its mitigation through association with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus in sunflower and eggplant
summary: Manganese (Mn) toxicity is a widespread constraint in plant production; however, limited information is available on the role of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) in enhancing Mn tolerance. In this study, eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) an
content: Manganese (Mn) toxicity is a widespread constraint in plant production; however, limited information is available on the role of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) in enhancing Mn tolerance. In this study, eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) and sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) were inoculated with Rhizophagus intraradices and exposed to 800 μM Mn for four weeks under greenhouse conditions. Based on biomass production and leaf symptoms, sunflower exhibited greater tolerance to Mn toxicity than eggplant. Mn toxicity symptoms appeared as small black spots associated with leaf trichomes in sunflower, whereas in eggplant, brown spots and speckles developed on the leaf blades without the involvement of stellate trichomes. Under Mn stress, leaf phenolics and anthocyanins increased in sunflower but declined in eggplant. AMF colonisation was higher in sunflower and associated with improved chlorophyll content, enhanced photosynthetic light reactions, and more efficient carbohydrate allocation to the fungal partner compared with eggplant. Although Mn stress reduced root colonisation more strongly in eggplant, biomass production was improved to a similar extent in both species upon AMF inoculation. Photosynthetic light reactions and leaf chlorophyll, carotenoid, phenolic, and macronutrient concentrations were significantly higher under combined Mn toxicity and AMF inoculation than under Mn stress alone, with the effect particularly pronounced in sunflower. The most consistent impact of AMF colonisation was a reduction in Mn accumulation in leaves and roots, likely due to Mn immobilisation in the rhizosphere. Overall, our findings highlight the strong potential of AMF to mitigate Mn toxicity by both reducing Mn accumulation in roots and leaves and enhancing internal detoxification mechanisms.

title: Production of ultra-low ash coal from low-rank coal by mild organic acid leaching: screening and optimization of acid treatment
source: International Journal of Coal Preparation and Utilization
summary: Low-rank coals are potential feedstocks for high-value carbon products, but their mineral matter limits applications requiring high purity. This study investigated the production of ultra-low ash coal from Soma, Turkey, through an integrate
content: Low-rank coals are potential feedstocks for high-value carbon products, but their mineral matter limits applications requiring high purity. This study investigated the production of ultra-low ash coal from Soma, Turkey, through an integrated physical beneficiation and organic acid leaching route. Following float–sink separation, the <1.30 specific gravity fraction containing 6.78% ash was selected as the leaching feed. Formic, acetic, citric, and oxalic acids were compared, with formic acid showing the highest demineralization performance and reducing ash to 0.92% and 0.90% at 1 and 2 M, respectively. Plackett–Burman screening identified temperature, acid concentration, and liquid-to-solid ratio as the dominant operating variables, whereas stirring speed and leaching time had limited effects. These variables were optimized using a Box–Behnken design. The developed models showed high predictive accuracy, with R2 values of 0.9799 for ash content and 0.9853 for ash removal efficiency. Optimum conditions of 1.12 M formic acid, 75°C, and 40 mL/g yielded a validated product containing 0.70% ash at 91.14% removal efficiency. XRD, SEM–EDS, and FTIR analyses confirmed preferential removal of Ca-bearing carbonate minerals, while the carbonaceous matrix was largely preserved and residual ash was mainly associated with acid-resistant silicate/aluminosilicate phases.

title: Low‐carbon cotton: Understanding and managing greenhouse gas emissions in production fields
summary: Conventional cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) production is among the most carbon‐intensive agricultural systems worldwide. Enhancing its environmental sustainability requires a clear understanding of how management practices influence greenh
content: Conventional cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) production is among the most carbon‐intensive agricultural systems worldwide. Enhancing its environmental sustainability requires a clear understanding of how management practices influence greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. This review synthesizes the literature to identify management practices that drive GHG emissions, knowledge gaps, and climate‐smart strategies in cotton systems. Studies report that conservation tillage can reduce carbon dioxide (CO 2) emissions by limiting soil disturbance, whereas its effects on nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions may vary, with increases reported mainly under wetter soil conditions. Elevated nitrogen fertilizer rates generally increase CO 2 and N 2 O emissions. However, organic fertilizer sources reduced N 2 O emissions by 26% on average while increasing CO 2 emissions by 14%, compared with synthetic sources. Urease and nitrification inhibitors showed promise to reduce N 2 O emissions in some studies. Among different irrigation techniques, drip irrigation emitted 68% less N 2 O on average than furrow or flood irrigation. However, irrigation studies are concentrated in arid regions of northwestern China, and tillage studies in the southern United States. Cover cropping during fallow periods, along with organic amendments, inhibitors, and precision nitrogen management, can significantly reduce emissions. Rotating cotton with other crops such as corn (Zea mays L.) or sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] can enhance carbon sequestration and help mitigate GHG emissions. Long‐term comparative studies across regions and systems are still needed to fully assess the mitigation potential of these practices in cotton‐based agriculture.

title: Genomic Determinants of Taxis in Pelagic SAR324 Bacteria From the Cold, High‐Pressure Deep Ocean
summary: In the deep pelagic ocean, organic matter is typically scarce, making taxis potentially essential for heterotrophic microorganisms to locate and acquire it. We analysed SAR324 single amplified genomes and identified a predicted core chemose
content: In the deep pelagic ocean, organic matter is typically scarce, making taxis potentially essential for heterotrophic microorganisms to locate and acquire it. We analysed SAR324 single amplified genomes and identified a predicted core chemosensory domain architecture consistent with the F7 and F8 classes, associated with flagellar-driven taxis. The absence of a canonical standalone CheY and the identification of a predicted dual-domain REC-CHD response regulator suggest that second messengers may serve as the primary signalling output for taxis. Recruitment of SAR324 taxis sequences across global ocean metagenomes revealed a cluster with higher read coverage below 2800 m than in shallower depths. This deep cluster exhibits distinct nucleotide and predicted amino-acid compositions in genes involved in flagellar-based taxis, including chemoreceptors MCP, flagellar biosynthesis protein FlhG, the motor switch component FliN, and hook-length control protein FliK. These compositional shifts, together with depth-structured synonymous codon usage patterns, are consistent with structural and/or translational adaptation of the flagellar machinery to extreme hydrostatic pressure. Higher read recruitment in free-living than in particle-attached deep-sea metagenomes suggests that SAR324 is predominantly free-living. These findings suggest that SAR324 employs taxis as a foraging strategy specifically adapted to the physical and nutritional constraints of the deep ocean.

title: A Perspective on Hydrothermal Catalysis for Chemical Recycling of Polyolefin‐Rich Plastic Waste
summary: Polyolefins dominate global plastic production, yet most post-consumer polyolefin waste is too mixed, wet, or contaminated for mechanical recycling. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts such waste in hot, compressed water into hydrocarb
content: Polyolefins dominate global plastic production, yet most post-consumer polyolefin waste is too mixed, wet, or contaminated for mechanical recycling. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts such waste in hot, compressed water into hydrocarbon oils compatible with existing refineries and steam crackers, without pre-drying. Water under hydrothermal conditions acts as a heat transfer medium, pseudo-organic solvent, ionic catalyst, and purification phase, suppressing char and aromatics while partitioning heteroatoms into the aqueous phase. However, polyolefin degradation in hot water still proceeds through unselective radical scission, producing broad, waxy product distributions. This Perspective identifies catalysis as the key to achieving selective and scalable chemical recycling of polyolefins by HTL. Hydrothermal catalysis is distinct from catalytic pyrolysis, as water alters acid-site chemistry, interfacial reactivity, and hydrogen availability while accelerating zeolite dealumination, support dissolution, and metal sintering. Catalyst design principles are discussed, including acid, metal, and bifunctional sites for selective chain scission and strategies for hydrothermal stability. Process integration of HTL oil with steam cracking, fluid catalytic cracking, and gasification is assessed, together with techno-economic and policy factors favoring olefins over fuels. Finally, research priorities are outlined, including long-duration catalyst testing, mechanistic studies in hot compressed water, reactor scale-up, and coupled techno-economic and life cycle assessment.

title: Sugar‐Epigenetic Crosstalk in Plant Stress Response
summary: Sugar signaling is increasingly recognized as a central regulator of plant growth and stress adaptation, but whether it actively encodes persistent epigenetic memory remains unclear. A growing body of literature proposes that this signaling
content: Sugar signaling is increasingly recognized as a central regulator of plant growth and stress adaptation, but whether it actively encodes persistent epigenetic memory remains unclear. A growing body of literature proposes that this signaling reshapes chromatin to generate lasting transcriptional states, or 'stress memory.' However, the supporting evidence falls into several distinct levels of mechanistic rigor that are rarely separated, making it difficult to distinguish direct sensor-to-modifier action from indirect, permissive, or correlative effects. We propose that sugar-epigenetic coupling should be treated as a stratified regulatory layer with explicit evidence criteria. This review summarizes current mechanistic understanding of how epigenetic change is coupled to sugar signaling in plants and outlines a framework researchers can apply toward crop improvement. It first examines SnRK1, TOR, HXK1 and other key regulators relevant to crop improvement. It then details how sugar signaling integrates with epigenetic mechanisms, including histone modification and DNA methylation, to modulate the expression of stress-associated genes. With particular focus on recent findings, we highlight the bidirectional interplay between metabolic status and chromatin state. The review also considers how such an integrated regulatory network may allow plants to balance growth and defense, accumulate stress memory and undergo transgenerational adaptation to environmental stress. We argue that the value of these sugar-epigenetic links should ultimately be judged not by the number of co-occurring marks, but by whether validated mechanisms provide explanatory or decision-relevant information beyond existing signaling and transcriptomic data. Clarifying which of these links are mechanistically established versus inferred may help guide efforts to engineer climate-adapted, stress-resilient, resource-efficient crops, although translating even the best-supported mechanisms into field-ready applications remains an open challenge.

title: Does metal (Ni and Mn) accumulation shift plant position along the leaf economics spectrum?
summary: Soils are major drivers of plant physiology, function, and diversity, shaping plant performance and ecosystem productivity. Serpentine (ultramafic) systems, where edaphic specialists (metallophytes) evolve under high metal concentrations, l
content: Soils are major drivers of plant physiology, function, and diversity, shaping plant performance and ecosystem productivity. Serpentine (ultramafic) systems, where edaphic specialists (metallophytes) evolve under high metal concentrations, low nutrient availability, and limited water retention, host stress-tolerant species that express resource-conservative strategies, as predicted by the leaf economics spectrum. We investigate how leaf metal contents, from excluder to hyperaccumulator plant strategies, correlate with other leaf functional and anatomical traits. We sampled 56 woody species on ultramafic soils of New Caledonia, including 13 Ni- and five Mn-hyperaccumulators, spanning a gradient of Ni and Mn foliar metal concentrations. We measured leaf functional traits (LA, LDMC, LTh, SLA) and four anatomical traits (including epidermis and cuticle thickness, and mesophyll tissue structure). All taxa fell on the conservative side of global trait spectra. Within this conservative range, higher leaf Ni concentration was associated with more acquisitive leaves, with higher SLA, lower LDMC, thinner cuticles and a less dense mesophyll, and explained 26% of species variation along the main trait axis. These relationships held when phylogeny, locality and habitat were accounted for. Ni-hyperaccumulators were shifted towards the acquisitive side of trait space, but overlapped with non-hyperaccumulators and were as functionally diverse. In contrast, leaf Mn concentration was unrelated to any traits. In the woody flora of New Caledonia, Ni accumulation forms a continuous axis of functional variation aligned with the leaf economics spectrum, with hyperaccumulators at its upper end. Ultramafic soils promote functional structuring linked to variation in Ni accumulation and tolerance. Transpiration-driven uptake and elemental defence may link Ni accumulation to leaf construction.

title: Vegetation Structural Configuration and Cultural Ecosystem Services in linpan Rural Green Spaces
summary: Rural green spaces provide important cultural ecosystem services (CES). However, rapid urbanisation and rural transformation are altering vegetation structures and affecting inhabitants’ everyday interactions with these spaces. The relation
content: Rural green spaces provide important cultural ecosystem services (CES). However, rapid urbanisation and rural transformation are altering vegetation structures and affecting inhabitants’ everyday interactions with these spaces. The relationships between vegetation structural configuration (VSC), cultural ecosystem benefits, and actual spatial use remain insufficiently understood. Therefore, this study examines these relationships in two Linpan rural green spaces on the Chengdu Plain, China. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach was employed, combining questionnaire data from 190 respondents, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), 570 behavioural observations, and spatial mapping. Exploratory factor analysis identified two VSC dimensions: Woody Structural Configuration (WSC) and Vegetation Layering and Naturalness (VLN), while cultural ecosystem benefits were represented by Experiences, Capabilities, and Identities. Both VSC dimensions were positively associated with all three benefit dimensions at both study sites, with WSC showing stronger associations, particularly with Capabilities. Behavioural and spatial analyses further revealed that recreation was the dominant form of CES use and that cultural practices were concentrated in vegetation settings associated with inhabitants’ everyday activities. By integrating perceptual, behavioural, and spatial evidence, the findings support a conceptual synthesis linking VSC preferences, cultural ecosystem benefits, cultural practices, and actual spatial use. This study extends the application of the Ecosystem Services Cascade Model by providing a spatially explicit interpretation of ecosystem structure and highlights the importance of maintaining diverse, accessible, and functionally meaningful vegetation configurations in rural green space planning.

title: Applications of Simple Methods in Property Correlations
summary: Thermo physical and chemical property estimation methods are vital for the equipment design and process development. In this context, we present the utility of simple methods for the calculation of important properties of relevance to chemi
content: Thermo physical and chemical property estimation methods are vital for the equipment design and process development. In this context, we present the utility of simple methods for the calculation of important properties of relevance to chemistry and chemical engineering. The methods developed include the study of a large variety of organic and inorganic compounds and vegetable oils. Index Terms: Group contribution methods, vapor pressure, viscosity, nonlinear optical materials the paper deals with(1) Application of dimensionless numbers in chemical engineering. (2) Extension of group contribution methods.(3) Application of vapor pressure and viscosity vs. temperature methods. (4) Modeling two photon absorption cross sections of organic compounds used to replace very expensive organometallic compounds. (5) Use of molar refraction in the estimation of several oil properties.

title: Data-Driven Emulation of a Double Gyre Ocean Circulation Using Operator Inference
summary: Ocean general circulation models are indispensable tools for climate research, yet their high computational cost limits many-query applications, including uncertainty quantification, large-ensemble forecasting, and scenario-based evaluation
content: Ocean general circulation models are indispensable tools for climate research, yet their high computational cost limits many-query applications, including uncertainty quantification, large-ensemble forecasting, and scenario-based evaluations of oceanic response to changing atmospheric forcing. Machine learning enables rapid emulation, but purely data-driven, “black-box” neural networks often lack interpretability and generalize poorly to unseen forcing conditions. In this work, we construct a physics-motivated, data-driven Operator Inference reduced-order model (OpInf ROM) capable of evolving the full threedimensional prognostic ocean state over decade-long simulation horizons. Applied to an idealized double-gyre basin driven by seasonally cycling wind and buoyancy forcing, the OpInf ROM combines learned quadratic dynamics with atmospheric forcing operators constructed from known surface forcing fields. To ensure physical consistency, linear constraints on the reduced operators enforce basin-integrated heat and salt budget closure. Evaluated on a wind-stress amplitude held out from training, the OpInf ROM accurately reproduces decadal-mean surface and interior states, the vertical thermohaline structure, and the scaling of gyre transport with forcing amplitude. The conservation constraints prevent spurious net heat and salt sources, ensuring internally consistent tracer budgets even when predicted tracer changes differ from the full-order model. Although the OpInf ROM progressively damps high-frequency mesoscale eddy variability, its computational speedup of over five orders of magnitude enables rapid evaluation of mean-state ocean sensitivity to variable atmospheric forcing. Plain Language Summary Numerical ocean models are vital for understanding how ocean currents transport heat and regulate global climate. However, their high computational cost makes it difficult to explore how oceans might respond to changing atmospheric conditions. Machine learning can speed up simulations, but purely data-driven models often fail when tested under new climate conditions. In this study, we developed a data-driven model that combines machine learning with known physical laws to simulate a decade of ocean circulation in a simplified ocean basin. We also enforce conservation of heat and salt, ensuring that changes in their total amounts are consistent with exchanges at the ocean surface. The model stays stable and accurately captures the average climate over ten years, though it gradually smooths out rapid, small-scale eddy features over time. Notably, it runs more than 100,000 times faster than a traditional ocean model and correctly predicts how ocean currents change under new wind patterns. This enables rapid exploration of “what-if” climate scenarios, making large-ensemble forecasting and uncertainty quantification computationally feasible.

title: Korean pine nut shell extract reduces in vitro rumen methane production and modulates fermentation, protozoa, and methanogenic archaeal profiles
summary: Korean pine nut shells are an underutilized by-product with potentially bioactive constituents. However, integrated evidence linking pine nut shell extract (PNSE) chemistry with dose-dependent changes in rumen methane, fermentation, microbi
content: Korean pine nut shells are an underutilized by-product with potentially bioactive constituents. However, integrated evidence linking pine nut shell extract (PNSE) chemistry with dose-dependent changes in rumen methane, fermentation, microbial profiles, and substrate digestibility remains limited. We characterized PNSE and evaluated graded-dose responses in a 24-h in vitro rumen fermentation system. Untargeted UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS profiling showed that PNSE contained diverse putatively annotated bioactive features, mainly terpenoids/steroids and flavonoids, together with alkaloids, phenolic acids, and saponins. In the dose-screening experiment, PNSE supplementation at 20–140 g/kg DM altered VFA profiles, particularly acetate, butyrate, branched-chain VFAs, and the acetate-to-propionate ratio, without significant overall treatment effects on pH, microbial crude protein, total gas production, apparent CO₂ production, or propionate concentration. Nevertheless, propionate exhibited a significant positive linear dose response. Compared with the control, CH 4 production was reduced by 13.5%, 20.8%, and 21.1% at 100, 120, and 140 g/kg DM, respectively, while NH 3 -N concentration was reduced by 28.1%, 30.5%, and 36.7%, respectively. Although 120 and 140 g/kg DM showed stronger methane inhibition, they reduced in vitro dry matter digestibility, whereas 100 g/kg DM maintained IVDMD. Further analyses showed that PNSE altered bacterial and methanogenic archaeal community structures, reduced protozoal abundance, and changed selected ELISA-based enzyme-related indicators and indicated exploratory fatty acid variation. Overall, PNSE may mitigate in vitro rumen methanogenesis, possibly in association with changes in fermentation patterns, protozoa, and microbial community profiles. These findings suggest that PNSE may be considered a candidate plant-derived additive for further evaluation in ruminant methane mitigation, although independent in vivo studies are required to confirm its efficacy, safety, optimal dose, and practical applicability.

title: An Enhanced Osprey Optimization Algorithm for Benchmark Function Evaluation and FOPID Tuning for BLDC Motor Control
summary: This paper introduces an Enhanced Osprey Optimization Algorithm (EOOA), designed to circumvent the limitations of the original Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA), such as premature convergence and unstable search dynamics, particularly in
content: This paper introduces an Enhanced Osprey Optimization Algorithm (EOOA), designed to circumvent the limitations of the original Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA), such as premature convergence and unstable search dynamics, particularly in high-dimensional or nonlinear optimization problems. The proposed enhancement incorporates a velocity-driven search mechanism that reinforces global exploration while preserving effective local exploitation, thereby improving convergence reliability and overall search stability. To validate its effectiveness, EOOA is rigorously tested on 20 benchmark functions and compared against several state-of-the-art metaheuristics, including Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Bald Eagle Search (BES), African Vultures Optimization Algorithm (AVOA), and the original OOA. The comparative results are further analyzed using Friedman and Wilcoxon statistical tests, confirming the superiority of EOOA in terms of solution quality, robustness, and ranking significance. Specifically, EOOA consistently obtained the lowest average rank and the highest accuracy rate (90.34%), thereby approving its superiority when faced to the other mentioned algorithms. Accordingly, OOA demonstrated strong competitiveness (87.18%), while BES (84.08%) and AVOA (82.62%) occupied mid-tier positions. HHO exhibited moderate effectiveness (80.40%), and PSO recorded the weakest performance (75.38%). To highlight its practical relevance, EOOA is applied to the tuning of a fractional-order PID (FOPID) controller for brushless direct current (BLDC) motor speed regulation. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the EOOA-FOPID controller achieves faster dynamic response, reduced overshoot, and enhanced tracking accuracy compared with competing approaches. Moreover, the proposed controller exhibits strong robustness against parameter variations in stator resistance (Rs) and inertia (J), as well as resilience under band-limited white noise disturbances. Collectively, these findings establish EOOA as an effective and reliable optimization paradigm for both theoretical benchmarks and real-world engineering applications.

title: Non-IID Data Challenges in Federated Learning for Distributed Systems: A Systematic Review
summary: Federated learning is a distributed machine learning framework, that enhances privacy and security against malicious behavior, including data poisoning and model poisoning. Nevertheless, federated learning models tend to have worse performa
content: Federated learning is a distributed machine learning framework, that enhances privacy and security against malicious behavior, including data poisoning and model poisoning. Nevertheless, federated learning models tend to have worse performance than centralized models, particularly when the data is non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) on local devices. Moreover, the non-IID data negatively impacts the outcome of the model, causing slower convergence, lower accuracy, and even leading to model bias. These challenges limit the applicability of the federated learning model and exhibit constrained convergence and generalization. In order to help researchers better understand and study the challenges of non-IID data settings in federated learning, this article presents a systematic review of existing research by analyzing beyond 50 related works and providing substantial solutions to address certain challenges in non-IID data. Unlike existing literature, this survey introduces a sophisticated, comprehensive taxonomy that systematically categorizes non-IID data challenges across statistical dimensions, critically evaluates mitigation strategies, and outlines open research trajectories for federated learning. The review discussed the taxonomy of the non-IID data challenges with their statistical properties, such as label, temporal, and quantity. Moreover, the review describes popular solutions to mitigate the challenges, ensure personalized federated learning and a domain adaptation technique in distributed and edge-based intelligent systems, including internet of things (IoT) and communication networks, and outlines promising future research directions.

title: Multi-Scale Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting with Graph-Based Super-Resolution of Numerical Weather Prediction
summary: Short-term wind power forecasting up to 72 h ahead is essential for reliable power system operation and efficient electricity market participation under high renewable penetration. However, operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) pro
content: Short-term wind power forecasting up to 72 h ahead is essential for reliable power system operation and efficient electricity market participation under high renewable penetration. However, operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) products are substantially coarser than the spatial and temporal scales governing turbine-level inflow variability. In contrast, turbine-level refinement of coarse NWP for multi-step forecasting remains largely unexplored. To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-scale short-term wind power forecasting framework that combines graph-based NWP super-resolution with transformer-based temporal forecasting. First, a graph learning module refines coarse NWP data into turbine-level wind speed representations by incorporating turbine layout topology and wind-direction-aware spatial interactions. Second, a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) performs parallel multi-horizon forecasting across turbines using the refined wind speeds, historical power measurements, and turbine-specific static covariates. Farm-level forecasts are subsequently obtained through hierarchical aggregation. Case studies on two real-world wind farms with contrasting terrain characteristics demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative baselines, delivering a 34.1% decrease in normalized mean absolute error (NMAE) and a 28.6% gain in normalized continuous ranked probability score (NCRPS). The results indicate that turbine-level refinement of coarse NWP inputs before temporal forecasting significantly improves short-term forecasting performance, providing an effective and scalable solution for multi-scale wind power forecasting.

title: A Lightweight Four-Credential Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for AI-Enabled Edge-IIoT: Transcript-Bound Resistance to Replay and Impersonation
summary: Edge intelligence places model inference and data aggregation on edge nodes deployed outside tightly controlled premises. The edge node therefore decides who may query a deployed model and whose measurements may reach its input. We present
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Edge intelligence places model inference and data aggregation on edge nodes deployed outside tightly controlled premises. The edge node therefore decides who may query a deployed model and whose measurements may reach its input. We present an authentication and key agreement scheme using a password, smart card, biometric, and Cognitively Evaluable Authentication Factor (CEAF). CEAF is a session-dependent knowledge credential derived from a fresh challenge and checked against edge-side state. The hash–XOR exchange uses nonces and timestamps, while version-bound two-record state tolerates one lost authentication message without re-registration. The ROR analysis separates password and biometric guessing, transcript collisions, forgery, and CEAF-response enumeration. Sensitivity analysis shows how the residual guessing probability changes with the segment count and the admitted-attempt budget. The main protocol provides session-key independence but neither perfect forward secrecy nor key opacity from the edge node. The analytical unit-cost estimate is 0.4588 ms; a host reference implementation measured 0.0226 ms for the summed software roles on an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, excluding communication and I/O. The construction is a pre-inference access-control mechanism for edge-intelligent IIoT, not a model-level defense. In particular, because Q1 is a transcript-bound hash, exposure of the smart card, password, and biometric permits offline enumeration of the CEAF response from a recorded login; the scheme does not claim offline resistance under that compromise.
