title: High-power PV applications using hybrid battery-supercapacitor storage: state-of-the-art solutions for fast transients and power quality
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: High-power photovoltaic (PV) systems introduce grid stability challenges due to rapid irradiance fluctuations, leading to fast transients, voltage deviations, and frequency instability. Conventional battery-only storage has limited response
content: High-power photovoltaic (PV) systems introduce grid stability challenges due to rapid irradiance fluctuations, leading to fast transients, voltage deviations, and frequency instability. Conventional battery-only storage has limited response capability and degrades more rapidly under frequent dynamic stress. Hybrid battery–supercapacitor energy storage systems (HESS) offer a promising solution by combining high energy density with fast transient response. This paper reviews hybrid architectures and control strategies for fast transient mitigation in high-power PV applications. Passive, semi-active, and fully active topologies are examined with respect to dynamic performance and implementation complexity. Control methods, including frequency-based power decomposition, ramp-rate control, and adaptive coordination, are analyzed for their effectiveness in improving voltage and frequency stability. Comparative analysis shows hybrid systems reduce direct current-link (DC-link) voltage deviation, battery current ripple, and electrochemical stress while enhancing multi-time-scale response capability. Key research gaps include degradation-aware control, grid-forming integration, and large-scale validation. Hybrid battery–supercapacitor systems are essential for stable, reliable, and resilient renewable-based power systems in future energy networks worldwide today.

title: Explainable convLSTM-based solar irradiance and wind speed forecasting for hybrid renewable energy systems in India
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Accurate forecasting of solar irradiance and wind speed is essential for the reliable integration and operation of hybrid renewable energy systems. This study develops an explainable ConvLSTM-based forecasting framework using five years of
content: Accurate forecasting of solar irradiance and wind speed is essential for the reliable integration and operation of hybrid renewable energy systems. This study develops an explainable ConvLSTM-based forecasting framework using five years of hourly data (2016-2020) from the National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB) for a selected location in Tamil Nadu, India. The dataset includes global horizontal irradiance (GHI), wind speed, temperature, solar radiation variables, solar zenith angle, temporal features, and lagged renewable-resource variables. Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and ConvLSTM models are developed and comparatively evaluated to capture nonlinear and temporal dependencies. A 24-hour sliding window is used to provide temporal context. Model performance is assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R²). ConvLSTM achieves the best overall performance, with an MAE of 7.64, RMSE of 11.28, and R² of 0.95. Learning-curve and predicted-versus-actual analyses indicate stable convergence and good predictive agreement. Feature-importance and SHAP analyses identify lagged renewable-resource and meteorological variables as important contributors to the predictions. Transfer learning is further incorporated to assess regional adaptability. The proposed framework combines forecasting accuracy, temporal learning, interpretability, and transferability, supporting renewable-resource management, grid balancing, and hybrid renewable-energy integration in India.

title: Interpretable early warning of statistics induced query plan regression in real-time analytical workloads
source: International Journal on Information Technologies and Security
summary: Analytical databases under continuous ingest accumulate a divergence between the data distribution assumed by the query optimiser and the data actually stored, and plans degrade silently when that divergence crosses a plan-selection boundar
content: Analytical databases under continuous ingest accumulate a divergence between the data distribution assumed by the query optimiser and the data actually stored, and plans degrade silently when that divergence crosses a plan-selection boundary. This paper asks whether such regressions can be predicted before execution and attributed to a repairable cause. Three PostgreSQL databases receive identical drifting data under different statistics policies, so regression is measured as a latency ratio against a fresh-statistics reference rather than assumed. Across 1,620 query instances the optimiser’s own cost estimate predicts nothing, whereas a two-predicate rule reading the catalogue and the unexecuted plan matches a gradient-boosted model, identifying all thirty held-out regressions without false positives. Repairing the attributed column resolves every regression, while repairing a second drifted column resolves none.

title: Hybrid renewable systems in smart grids through enhanced control strategies
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: The potential for improving sustainability and dependability has led to an extensive amount of interest in the integration of renewable energy sources (RES), especially hybrid RES (HRES), into smart grids. However, there are still several o
content: The potential for improving sustainability and dependability has led to an extensive amount of interest in the integration of renewable energy sources (RES), especially hybrid RES (HRES), into smart grids. However, there are still several obstacles to overcome, such as improving power quality, maintaining grid stability, and increasing energy efficiency. To improve energy extraction and stability in smart grids, this research highlights a unified control synergy between MPPT and inverter regulation. This research presents an integrated method for successful integration of HRES into smart grids that includes traditional and improved control mechanisms in order to overcome these issues. The suggested system makes use of modern control techniques to maximize energy production and maintain grid stability, such as pulse width modulation (PWM) for inverter control and the perturb and observe (P&O) algorithm for maximum power point tracking (MPPT). The development and application of a complete control system that combines the benefits of enhanced and conventional control techniques is the primary contribution. The findings highlight how integrated control techniques may help move RES closer to integration into smart grids, which will lead to more dependable and sustainable energy in the future.

title: An intelligent weather-aware energy management framework for resilient smart-grid operation using adaptive battery control
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Extreme weather conditions such as heatwaves and high-temperature events can adversely affect the stability, reliability, and operational performance of modern smart grids. This paper presents an intelligent energy management framework for
content: Extreme weather conditions such as heatwaves and high-temperature events can adversely affect the stability, reliability, and operational performance of modern smart grids. This paper presents an intelligent energy management framework for weather-aware smart-grid operation using real-world meteorological data and renewable-energy integration. Hourly temperature, solar irradiance, and wind-speed data were obtained from the NASA POWER Data Access Viewer for Chennai, India, from 2020 to 2024. The framework integrates temperature-dependent load demand, solar-energy generation with PV efficiency degradation, adaptive grid-stress thresholds, and battery energy management for charging, discharging, and idle operation. The proposed system was evaluated using grid-stress analysis, normalized voltage assessment, and renewable-energy contribution before and after intelligent energy management. Simulation results showed a reduction in average grid stress from 90.47 to 90.43 and a 9.09% reduction in peak grid stress from 109.97 to 99.97. The normalized voltage indicator increased from 0.81906 to 0.81914, while renewable-energy support reduced modelled grid dependency during solar availability. Overall, the proposed framework provides a computationally efficient supervisory approach for weather-aware, renewable-integrated, battery-assisted smart-grid energy management.

title: Cascade sliding mode control of dual-input DC converter
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Hybrid energy systems for electric vehicles, renewable microgrids, and uninterruptible power supplies require multi-input converters that maintain tight output regulation under variable source voltages, battery internal impedance, and load
content: Hybrid energy systems for electric vehicles, renewable microgrids, and uninterruptible power supplies require multi-input converters that maintain tight output regulation under variable source voltages, battery internal impedance, and load disturbances. This work presents a cascade sliding mode controller for a dual-input single-inductor DC converter operating across buck and boost regions, with the key novelty of a mode-adaptive feed-forward duty cycle, derived from steady-state volt-second balance, that cancels source impedance disturbances without observers or auxiliary hardware. The control architecture combines an outer proportional-integral voltage regulator with an inner current sliding surface enforced by a boundary-layer saturation function. Controller gains are obtained through a two-stage automated search of 164 total trials. Simulation over sixty milliseconds with a load step from 3.5 to 1.8 Ω yields ripple of 0.044% (reported throughout as the median of the per-5 ms-window peak-to-peak output voltage over the steady-state interval, normalized to Vref), steady-state voltage error of 0.003%, current settling time of 2.79 ms, and conversion efficiency of 95.35%. Introducing realistic source impedances of 0.05 and 0.20 Ω degrades ripple by less than 0.02 percentage points. Lyapunov analysis confirms reaching condition validity across 99.6% of the sampled state space.

title: Observer-based sliding mode control for high-gain boost converters in renewable systems
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Robust output-voltage regulation of high-gain capacitor-based boost converters is complicated by coupled internal energy-transfer dynamics, uncertain duty-to-output gain, source and load variations, and sensitivity to switching noise. To ad
content: Robust output-voltage regulation of high-gain capacitor-based boost converters is complicated by coupled internal energy-transfer dynamics, uncertain duty-to-output gain, source and load variations, and sensitivity to switching noise. To address these effects using the output voltage as the sole measured feedback variable, a linear extended-state-observer-assisted integral super-twisting sliding-mode controller (LESO-ISTSMC) is developed from the exact duty-affine output channel of the full averaged model. A second-order LESO estimates the lumped output-channel disturbance from the measured voltage and applied duty ratio, while a tanh-regularized super-twisting law, duty projection, and model-consistent anti-windup feedback produce a continuous commanded-duty correction before PWM realization; under the invariant-region condition stated explicitly in Assumption 1, regional Lyapunov analysis establishes bounded closed-loop signals and an explicit practical regulation bound. Experiments on a TMS320F28379D platform show that, relative to a conventional sign-based sliding-mode controller (CSMC), LESO-ISTSMC reduces normalized reference-centered RMS voltage deviation by 59.75-63.14% over 30-80 V and load-step voltage-dip magnitude by 71.4-85.0% following a 50% load increase. During 48–108 V reference steps at an approximately 24-V input, the converter exhibits well-damped transitions and a mean efficiency of 92.40%, supporting the practical realizability of the output-feedback architecture over the tested operating region.

title: Spectral machine learning framework for power system contingency assessment
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This study proposes a fast static-security screening framework for contingency assessment in renewable-integrated power systems. The IEEE 118-bus system is modified by adding a 50 MW photovoltaic unit and an 80 MW wind generator. The framew
content: This study proposes a fast static-security screening framework for contingency assessment in renewable-integrated power systems. The IEEE 118-bus system is modified by adding a 50 MW photovoltaic unit and an 80 MW wind generator. The framework combines DC load-flow-based N-1/N-2 screening, AC power-flow validation, fast Fourier transform (FFT) spatial spectral feature extraction, and support vector machine (SVM) classification. The DC model is used as a preliminary screening engine rather than a full substitute for AC power flow, and its limitations are evaluated through case-by-case AC/DC validation, line-resistance sensitivity, and reactive-load sensitivity. Results identify lines 65-68, 38-65, and 8-5 as the most critical N-1 contingencies, while the combined outage of 65-68 and 23-24 gives the most severe N-2 case. FFT energy shows strong rank consistency with angle-deviation severity and complements LOI and L-index indicators. The SVM achieves 83.18% accuracy on a grouped holdout of unseen contingencies and 83.06% under grouped K-fold cross-validation. Stochastic renewable and ramp-event analyses show corridor-dependent severity changes. Scalability tests demonstrate practical screening capability while indicating the need for filtering and parallelization in very large systems.

title: Integrated PV-driven DC–DC converter with hybrid energy storage system for electric vehicle applications
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This work introduces a power conversion architecture for grid-connected electric vehicle (EV) applications using a photovoltaic (PV) power generation system, a single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC) DC-DC converter, an interleaved
content: This work introduces a power conversion architecture for grid-connected electric vehicle (EV) applications using a photovoltaic (PV) power generation system, a single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC) DC-DC converter, an interleaved KY converter, and a hybrid energy storage system. The SEPIC converter is connected to the PV array; the output voltage is controlled by varying the PV array input voltage under different conditions of solar insolation, and a constant DC-link voltage is achieved. The interleaved KY converter offers high voltage gain, low output-current ripple, high dynamic response, and high conversion efficiency. A cascaded fuzzy logic controller (CFLC) is designed to control the operation of the converter by using an outer voltage-control loop to generate the reference current and an inner current-control loop to calculate the optimal duty ratio for interleaved phases. The hybrid energy storage system is comprised of a battery and supercapacitor to assist EV charging, regenerative braking, as well as peak-power demands, while minimizing the stress on the battery. Moreover, a bidirectional DC-DC converter provides the possibility for vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and controlled bidirectional power transfer between the EV and the utility grid. The effectiveness of voltage regulation, power-flow management, stress on storage elements, and stable charging and discharging operation is confirmed by MATLAB/Simulink results. The proposed architecture is flexible for applications related to renewable energy integration and EV charging and grid interaction.

title: Solar-based street light with automatic control unit
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: Street lighting is essential for providing safety and visibility on roads during nighttime. However, traditional street lighting systems consume a large amount of electrical energy and often operate even when lighting is not required. To ov
content: Street lighting is essential for providing safety and visibility on roads during nighttime. However, traditional street lighting systems consume a large amount of electrical energy and often operate even when lighting is not required. To overcome this problem, a solar-based street light with an automatic control unit is proposed. In this system, a solar panel collects sunlight during the daytime and converts it into electrical energy, which is stored in a rechargeable battery. The stored energy is then used to power the street lights at night. An light dependent resistor (LDR) is used to detect the surrounding light intensity and automatically switch the street lights ON when it becomes dark and OFF during daylight. A controller unit manages the operation of the system and ensures proper coordination between all components. Light-emitting diode (LED) lights are used as the light source because they consume less power and provide better efficiency. The proposed system helps reduce electricity consumption, minimize energy wastage, and promote the use of renewable energy sources. It is an economical, reliable, and environmentally friendly solution for modern street lighting systems in cities, highways, and rural areas.

title: Baseline stability-oriented proximal policy optimization for energy storage in microgrids
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy in microgrids introduces power variability and supply-demand imbalance, making energy storage system (ESS) control important for stability-oriented operation. This study develops a reproducible
content: The increasing penetration of renewable energy in microgrids introduces power variability and supply-demand imbalance, making energy storage system (ESS) control important for stability-oriented operation. This study develops a reproducible baseline stability-oriented ESS control framework using proximal policy optimization (PPO) in a simplified PV, load, and ESS microgrid environment. The control problem is formulated as a continuous-action Markov decision process, where the agent observes load demand, PV generation, state of charge, net imbalance, and previous ESS command to generate bounded charge/discharge actions. The reward function penalizes residual power imbalance, SOC deviation, and abrupt command variation. The framework is implemented using MATLAB/Simulink and a function-based reinforcement learning environment, and a rule-based controller is included as a benchmark. Training results show that PPO improves episode reward from approximately -72.63 to an average reward of about -2.51 after 300 episodes. During evaluation, the simplified voltage-response indicator remained within 0.9985-1.0016 p.u, keeps SOC within 49.4830-50.0000%, and generates bounded ESS commands. Compared with the rule-based benchmark, PPO demonstrates feasible and bounded operation, although the rule-based controller achieves lower average residual imbalance in the simplified deterministic profile. These results establish a transparent baseline for future stability-oriented DRL-based ESS control studies.

title: Active clamp technique for voltage stress mitigation in flyback converters
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Flyback converters are widely used in isolated low- to medium-power DC-DC conversion systems due to their simple structure, low component count, and inherent galvanic isolation. However, transformer leakage inductance causes severe drain-so
content: Flyback converters are widely used in isolated low- to medium-power DC-DC conversion systems due to their simple structure, low component count, and inherent galvanic isolation. However, transformer leakage inductance causes severe drain-source voltage overshoot and high-frequency ringing during switch turn-off, leading to increased voltage stress, switching losses, electromagnetic interference, and reduced reliability. Passive RC snubbers are commonly used to suppress voltage spikes, but they dissipate leakage energy as heat, limiting converter efficiency, especially at higher switching frequencies. To address this limitation, this study experimentally investigates an active clamp flyback converter using a silicon carbide MOSFET (12M1H090) as the primary switching device. Three converter configurations are evaluated under comparable operating conditions: a conventional flyback converter, an RC-snubber-based flyback converter, and an active clamp flyback converter. The results show that the conventional flyback converter produces a peak drain-source voltage of approximately 380 V. At the same time, the active clamp configuration reduces the voltage stress to approximately 140 V. With optimized clamp capacitor, resonant inductance, and a 550 ns deadtime interval, zero-voltage switching is achieved, resulting in reduced switching stress. These findings demonstrate that coordinated tuning of active clamp parameters provides an effective approach for mitigating voltage stress and improving performance in high-frequency SiC-based flyback converters for microgrid, renewable energy, and auxiliary power supply applications.

title: Frequency and voltage droop control of parallel inverters for integrating renewable energy sources in microgrids
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: In recent years, microgrids are employed exceedingly in distribution power utilities for securing the system's practicality for both islanded and tied modes. The voltage and frequency limits preservation represents the essential challenge i
content: In recent years, microgrids are employed exceedingly in distribution power utilities for securing the system's practicality for both islanded and tied modes. The voltage and frequency limits preservation represents the essential challenge in load sharing between the DGs. This paper exhibits a simple and efficient frequency control approach for grid-connected two-distribution sources (DG’s) employing droop-logic alongside a traditional PI controller to produce a two-step active and reactive power reference value generation is the main goal in this strategy. The proposed approach allows direct active and reactive power control for two parallel DGs, joined in a microgrid. The proposed algorithm is designed to track the active power reference value based on the grid frequency deviation to enable decentralized power sharing between DG units and improve the system's response to load demands. The MATLAB/Simulink model simulation results confirm the enhancement in power sharing, controllability, and transient response of the power flow due to demand changes. The parallel inverters are governed to supply the demand power and transport the excess to the grid utility.

title: Adaptive neural network - based red-tailed hawk optimization for renewable energy integration and power quality enhancement using UPQC
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) into modern power systems can cause voltage fluctuations, harmonic distortion, reactive power imbalance, and instability under nonlinear loading conditions. This paper proposes a
content: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) into modern power systems can cause voltage fluctuations, harmonic distortion, reactive power imbalance, and instability under nonlinear loading conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive neural network-based red-tailed hawk optimization (ANN-RTHO) approach for renewable energy integration and power quality enhancement in a meshed hybrid microgrid using a unified power quality conditioner (UPQC). Photovoltaic (PV) and wind energy sources are integrated through adaptive power electronic converters connected to a low-voltage DC (LVDC) network. The artificial neural network (ANN) predicts variations in solar irradiance, wind speed, load demand, and DC-link voltage, while the RTHO algorithm determines optimal maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operating points and UPQC control signals. The UPQC compensates for voltage disturbances, harmonic currents, reactive power, and DC-link voltage variations under linear and nonlinear loads. The proposed method is evaluated using MATLAB/ Simulink under different operating conditions. Simulation results show improved MPPT efficiency, reduced total harmonic distortion (THD), enhanced DC-link voltage stability, and faster dynamic response compared with conventional control methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the ANN-RTHO strategy for intelligent control and reliable operation of renewable energy-based hybrid microgrids.

title: Placement of solid-state circuit breaker at microgrid for different types of faults
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: A direct current (DC) microgrid is a localized electrical network that uses DC for power distribution and integrates renewable energy sources, such as solar panels and batteries, with electronic loads, reducing conversion losses. DC microgr
content: A direct current (DC) microgrid is a localized electrical network that uses DC for power distribution and integrates renewable energy sources, such as solar panels and batteries, with electronic loads, reducing conversion losses. DC microgrids improve reliability, reduce transmission losses, and support off-grid and remote applications. Solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) enhance protection and control by rapidly interrupting current, minimizing arc formation, and improving system resilience. Fast fault isolation is essential to maintaining DC microgrid stability and efficiency. Distributed energy resources (DERs) and loads are connected to the DC mains through power electronic converters. The proposed system consists of three DC feeders, each supplying three loads through individual breakers. A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) power from the main grid into DC when DER power is unavailable, while DERs and batteries directly supply DC power. This study analyzes different microgrid fault conditions and applies intentional islanding to improve the reliability and resilience of DERs in a low-voltage direct current (LVDC) system. The proposed system is modeled and analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink.

title: Study on adaptive control of solar panel array systems based on the changing direction of the sun throughout the day
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This paper presents the research, calculations, and design of an automatic electric drive control system for a solar panel array (ACDSPA) with a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) using an adaptive control method that takes into acco
content: This paper presents the research, calculations, and design of an automatic electric drive control system for a solar panel array (ACDSPA) with a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) using an adaptive control method that takes into account disturbances. Here, the optimal adaptive controller is designed to demonstrate greater convergence than conventional control. Based on the adaptive law developed, control parameters, especially self-tuning parameters during the control process, are updated quickly online. Therefore, disturbances and nonlinearity can be better reduced for the intelligent electric drive system (IEDS). A reference model based on Lyapunov theory is then created to track angular position errors. The adaptive law control system with model reference proposed by the authors in this paper combines the advantages of adaptive model-based control methods to control this IEDS system. Simulation results show faster performance and more accurate control compared to other control methods. This also provides a basis for future research, design, fabrication, and algorithm development of an intelligent controller AI for the ACDSPA auto-tracking system and renewable energy battery systems in the future.

title: DECISION-CENTRIC PROCESS MINING AND AUTOMATION PRIORITISATION FOR SAUDI PUBLIC AND FINANCIAL SERVICES UNDER VISION 2030: INTEGRATING BUSINESS PROCESS MANAGEMENT, ROBOTIC PROCESS AUTOMATION, AND BENEFIT-RISK ANALYSIS
summary: Digital transformation programmes increasingly possess event traces but lack defensible methods for deciding which workflows should be automated, redesigned or retained under human control. This critical review examines how business process
content: Digital transformation programmes increasingly possess event traces but lack defensible methods for deciding which workflows should be automated, redesigned or retained under human control. This critical review examines how business process management, process mining, robotic process automation and benefit risk analysis can jointly improve prioritisation in Saudi public administration and financial services, while extending the analysis to electricity utility interfaces. Thirty DOI-identified scholarly works published between 2021 and 2025 are synthesised through an explicit thematic appraisal covering data quality,decision discovery,technical suitability,value measurement, governance and contextual transferability. The proposed decision-centric framework separates evidence about process behaviour from normative decisions about public value, legal authority and operational risk. It introduces auditable eligibility gates, scenario-sensitive prioritisation, human decision rights and post-deployment monitoring. Application pathways are developed for permits, banking onboarding, electricity connections, metering disputes and grid-related service requests.

title: Revisiting Hubbert linearization: a dynamic regression approach for analyzing hydrocarbon production trajectories
summary: The effect of geological constraints on future hydrocarbon production is often underestimated in energy policies due to unreliable or incomplete reserve data. An alternative is to rely on production data, on the premise that production traj
content: The effect of geological constraints on future hydrocarbon production is often underestimated in energy policies due to unreliable or incomplete reserve data. An alternative is to rely on production data, on the premise that production trajectories of non-renewable resources reflect underlying geological factors. Curve-fitting techniques, such as Hubbert linearization, have long been used to estimate ultimate recovery and forecast future production, but their typical application provides only a snapshot of the current situation, making it difficult to capture the influence of fluctuating human factors on oil extraction. They have therefore often proved unsatisfactory, resulting in repeated revisions. Here, we introduce a new dynamic Hubbert linearization framework that transforms the conventional single linear regression into a comprehensive diagnostic tool. Our contribution rests on four key elements: (1) systematic backward regressions over multiple time windows (e.g., 10–40 years), thus generating up to several dozens of estimates of ultimate recovery (U est) and logistic growth rate (r est) per year; (2) a visualization mapping all U est and r est over time, generating a diagnostic “fingerprint” that reveals characteristic temporal patterns of the production profile; (3) the interpretation of the fingerprint, allowing the detection of production above or below trends, and the distinction between transient deviations and sustained changes in logistic trends and its parameters; and (4) the introduction of the apparent depletion level (cumulative production/U est) as a practical peak-warning indicator. Applied to three contrasting production profiles, conterminous US conventional oil, Norwegian offshore oil, and Barnett shale gas, this dynamic approach resolves long-standing limitations of static curve-fitting by extracting persistent production trends from time-dependent noise and market fluctuations.

title: Achieving Robust Extrapolation in Materials Property Prediction via Decoupled Transfer Learning
summary: Machine learning (ML) has revolutionized materials property prediction, yet can exhibit substantial performance degradation when extrapolating beyond training distributions—precisely the capability required for discovering unprecedented mat
content: Machine learning (ML) has revolutionized materials property prediction, yet can exhibit substantial performance degradation when extrapolating beyond training distributions—precisely the capability required for discovering unprecedented materials. In the end-to-end graph neural networks (GNNs) baselines examined here, joint optimization couples learned representations to target-property distributions, and predictions tend to remain near the training-property range. We demonstrate that decoupled transfer learning—separating pretrained GNN feature extractors from simple regressors—addresses this challenge. Pretrained features provide transferable structural knowledge, while simple regressors enable smooth extrapolation by maintaining learned trends beyond training boundaries. Benchmarked on layered intercalation compounds through four rigorous extrapolation scenarios and a temporal Materials Project split, our framework achieves 68% error reduction [root-mean-square error (RMSE): 0.881 versus 2.778 eV/atom] versus end-to-end GNNs for extrapolation. Failure analysis reveals extrapolation succeeds for continuous chemical space but fails for discontinuous space, establishing clear design principles. Validated on Fermi energy prediction, this framework is immediately deployable using existing pretrained models, requiring no architectural innovations—transforming ML-driven materials discovery.

title: SolarFCD: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Solar Fault Classification in Photovoltaic Systems
summary: The increasing global deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems needs robust, scalable, and automated inspection technologies capable of detecting a wide range of panel flaws under a variety of operating situations. The lack of comprehe
content: The increasing global deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems needs robust, scalable, and automated inspection technologies capable of detecting a wide range of panel flaws under a variety of operating situations. The lack of comprehensive, multi-modal, publicly available annotated datasets is a major obstacle preventing advancement in this field. We introduce SolarFCD, a harmonized multi-modal dataset of solar panel defects created by methodically combining and reconciling three publicly accessible datasets covering two imaging modalities. Following near-duplicate removal, the dataset comprises 3,742 unique real images, expanded to 6,651 through targeted augmentation of the three under-represented classes; augmentation was applied to the training and validation partitions, and all test images are unique real observations. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test splits at an 80:10:10 ratio through methodical label mapping, near-duplicate removal, and targeted augmentation of minority classes. Sixteen classification architectures from five design families were trained and assessed on the dataset to provide repeatable benchmark baselines. With an accuracy of 86.93%, precision of 88.79%, recall of 88.72%, and F1-score of 88.27%, ResNet101V2 performed the best overall. Per-class results showed balanced detection across all four defect categories within a narrow performance band. To promote open and repeatable research in automated PV inspection and solar energy operations and maintenance, the dataset, annotation files, and baseline code are made openly available.

title: Modeling the influence of sensory overload on visitor conservation at urban heritage destinations
summary: Historic urban centers attract visitors with dense sensory richness, yet that same richness may reduce the attention tourists need for small conservation acts such as putting litter in bins or keeping to protected boundaries. Existing susta
content: Historic urban centers attract visitors with dense sensory richness, yet that same richness may reduce the attention tourists need for small conservation acts such as putting litter in bins or keeping to protected boundaries. Existing sustainable-tourism research explains these acts mainly through attitudes, awareness and intentions, and rarely examines the tourist’s momentary cognitive state during the visit. This conceptual paper proposes the sensory–mindfulness–stewardship (SMS) model to address that gap. Drawing on recent research on embodied experience, mindfulness, restoration and crowding in tourism, it proposes that the auditory, visual and spatial atmosphere of a heritage site may influence a visitor’s momentary mindful state (a short-lived condition of calm, present-focused attention); that this state helps explain eco-preservation behavior (small on-site acts that protect the site) beyond attitudes and awareness; and that ‘restorative cognitive pathways’ (brief, designed recovery points along visitor routes) may buffer the effect of sensory overload. Crowding, cultural distance and time pressure are treated as conditions that may strengthen or weaken these effects. Six propositions are derived (P2 has two parts). We distinguish links that have partial empirical support from those that remain theoretical, set out candidate indicators, including physiological measures as complements to self-report and observation, and outline a staged validation design. The paper is theory-building and reports no new data. Because much of the supporting evidence comes from questionnaire studies in China, the propositions are offered for testing in other regions and with other methods.

title: Comprehensive predictive models for offshore wind farm performance: integrating reliability, energy production and cost analysis for current and next-generation installations
summary: Offshore wind is moving to larger turbines, deeper water and floating foundations while developers remain under pressure to reduce the levelised cost of energy (LCOE). This article presents a transparent, reproducible scenario model that li
content: Offshore wind is moving to larger turbines, deeper water and floating foundations while developers remain under pressure to reduce the levelised cost of energy (LCOE). This article presents a transparent, reproducible scenario model that links turbine reliability, availability, energy yield and LCOE, and it quantifies how much of a projected cost reduction comes from reliability and turbine scale and how much comes from exogenous cost and financing assumptions. Subsystem failure rates representative of a 97-turbine onshore fleet of 1.5 MW turbines are translated offshore with published stress factors and extrapolated to 8 MW and 15 MW ratings with explicit scaling laws. A Monte Carlo failure-and-repair simulation (10,000 turbine-years, fixed seed) returns availability, which enters the net capacity factor and hence the LCOE. Four scenarios are analysed: the onshore reference (S1), its offshore translation (S2), a 640 MW fixed-bottom farm (S3) and a 900 MW floating farm (S4). Central LCOE values are 119, 79.5 and 65.8 €/MWh for S2–S4, with input-uncertainty 90% intervals of 102–141, 68–95 and 56–88 €/MWh. A Shapley decomposition attributes the 53 €/MWh reduction from S2 to S4 to gross capacity factor (− 17.8), O&M cost per MW (− 15.4), CapEx per MW (− 14.1) and financing terms (− 13.8), partly offset by lower availability (+ 7.4). WACC, capacity factor and CapEx are the three most influential inputs in every offshore scenario, with failure rate fourth. The ranking S4 < S3 holds for mechanical scaling exponents up to about 0.8 but only if floating CapEx stays below 2.7 M€/MW; S3 and S4 are therefore conditional projections, not forecasts.

title: MeteoSynth: A Python Package for Non-Parametric Stochastic Weather Series Generation in Renewable Energy and Building Performance Simulations
summary: Evaluating renewable energy system performance and building energy demand typically relies on single-year historical profiles or Typical Meteorological Years (TMYs). However, deterministic weather series fail to capture inter-annual variabi
content: Evaluating renewable energy system performance and building energy demand typically relies on single-year historical profiles or Typical Meteorological Years (TMYs). However, deterministic weather series fail to capture inter-annual variability, extreme operational events, and provide distribution information necessary for performance assessment, control optimization, and Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA). To address these limitations, this paper introduces MeteoSynth, an open-source Python package designed for high-throughput, non-parametric generation of physically consistent synthetic time series for individual environmental variables. The package is variable-agnostic: any continuous hourly series can be modeled once its physical support and units are declared. This paper, like the package defaults, focuses on solar irradiance, air temperature, and wind speed. These three were chosen mainly because their physical constraints differ: temperature may take negative values, wind speed is non-negative, and irradiance is non-negative and also collapses to a degenerate zero state every night. Together they show how the generator handles each of these cases in general, and the limitations that remain are also examined. A second and practical reason is that the European Commission’s Photovoltaic Geographical Information System (PVGIS) supplies all three for any location. The present release is a parallel univariate generator: each variable is simulated independently, so the variables share the diurnal and seasonal cycle but not their day-to-day departures from it. Joint multivariate generation is identified as the main next development step. MeteoSynth models diurnal weather dynamics using time-inhomogeneous first-order Markov chains governed by two-dimensional Kernel Density Estimation (2D KDE). To ensure physical validity and calendar continuity, the framework incorporates features such as prevention of non-physical negative values with minimal domain distortion, a robust degenerate state classification engine to handle zero-variance night-time solar irradiance, a climatological circular rolling-window calendar (366-day calendar) that eliminates New Year boundary jumps while accommodating leap years, and date-aligned cross-midnight transition models ensuring multi-day series continuity. It additionally offers optional integration with the PVGIS database, a user-friendly API supporting both rapid monthly subsetting and high-accuracy rolling-window training, and an optimized ensemble engine capable of generating thousands of synthetic weather realizations in a single calendar walk, such that generating a single synthetic year and large ensembles of 1000 to 100,000 years takes virtually the same amount of execution time due to internal model-reuse optimizations.

title: Sustainable Climate Mitigation and Biodiversity Improvement by Natural/Renaturalized Ecosystems
summary: After Chap. 6 showed that technological processes for climate stabilization are unsustainable, the key question immediately arises: what alternative do we have? Quantitative data reveal that nature’s role in various natural—and renaturalize
content: After Chap. 6 showed that technological processes for climate stabilization are unsustainable, the key question immediately arises: what alternative do we have? Quantitative data reveal that nature’s role in various natural—and renaturalized—environments is greatly underestimated. These ecosystems have the capacity to sequester CO2 at levels both necessary and sufficient for meaningful climate change mitigation. Simultaneously, they can stabilize and restore biodiversity. Thus, it is crucial that society and policymakers recognize this immense natural potential, which can address both biodiversity loss and climate change without causing environmental harm. We should not focus on technological fixes that would damage the biosphere, but rather on leveraging the ecosystems’ capabilities.

title: Potential Increase in Spatial Overlap Between Humans and Large Carnivore Species Under Future Climate Change Scenarios in the Sanjiangyuan Region, China
summary: Climate change‐driven resource scarcity is likely to intensify human–wildlife conflicts (HWC) through increased spatial overlap between humans and wildlife. Therefore, assessing wildlife habitat suitability under climate change and evaluati
content: Climate change‐driven resource scarcity is likely to intensify human–wildlife conflicts (HWC) through increased spatial overlap between humans and wildlife. Therefore, assessing wildlife habitat suitability under climate change and evaluating species vulnerability are essential for improving in‐situ conservation planning. This study predicts climate change impacts on habitat suitability for four large carnivores, including the snow leopard Panthera uncia, wolf Canis lupus, brown bear Ursus arctos, and Eurasian lynx Lynx lynx, in the Sanjiangyuan Region of China, assessing their vulnerability and protection gaps. Our findings showed: (1) under current conditions, the Sanjiangyuan region offered the largest suitable habitat for wolves, followed by snow leopards and Eurasian lynx, with brown bears having the smallest area; (2) by 2030S (SSP126), snow leopards and wolves faced the most severe impacts, with ~7.73% and ~6.40% of their habitat becoming vulnerable; (3) future climate change was expected to significantly affect brown bears, potentially increasing high, medium, and low suitability habitats by ~4.5, ~5.6, and ~2.8 times by 2070S; (4) Eurasian lynx habitat was projected to increase slightly, most notably by 2070S under SSP126 (RScf = 22.50%); (5) Spatial overlap between human and large carnivore activities is projected to be concentrated primarily in the central and southern Sanjiangyuan region under future climate scenarios, with climate change potentially expanding risks for human‐brown bear and human‐Eurasian lynx conflicts; (6) Protection gaps for all four species were concentrated in northeastern Tanggulashan Town, southern Qumalai County, and southeastern Zhiduo County. These findings offer crucial data for large carnivore conservation, national park planning, and the formulation of evidence‐based strategies to mitigate HWC.

title: Small Collisions, Big Impact: The Sensitivity of Atmospheric Temperatures to Collision-Induced Absorption
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Collision-induced absorption (CIA) data are relevant to determining atmospheric temperatures and, in turn, the habitability of a diverse set of planetary atmospheres. However, these data remain sparse across broad wavelength and temperature
content: Collision-induced absorption (CIA) data are relevant to determining atmospheric temperatures and, in turn, the habitability of a diverse set of planetary atmospheres. However, these data remain sparse across broad wavelength and temperature ranges. Nevertheless, multiple, sometimes disagreeing, sources of experimental and theoretical data can be available for the same CIA pair. In this paper, we assess the impact of these varying sources on atmospheric temperatures and the limitations that the available data coverage can introduce. In order to inform future measurements and calculations, we test additional cases with extrapolated wavelength and temperature ranges. We first introduce a measure of the importance of CIA opacities depending on pressure and temperature by calculating the Rosseland mean with and without each CIA pair’s contribution. Secondly, we employ each CIA source in a radiative transfer model of idealised atmospheres which maximise the effect of the CIA pair of interest. Our findings highlight the uncertainties related to the current data. Temperature differences between CIA data sources range from ∼10 K when sources overlap in wavelength and temperature coverage to >100 K when spectral gaps or temperature limits differ. Spectral windows or narrow temperature coverage can also hinder the model’s convergence of the temperature profile. This work aims to provide guidance on the selection of CIA opacity datasets for atmospheric modelling and to identify the wavelength and temperature regimes in which further laboratory measurements and theoretical calculations are most urgently needed. We publish all our findings in detail in the form of an accessible website.

title: Silicon-Modified Biochar in Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agroecosystems
summary: Silicon-rich and silicon-modified biochars (Si-BCs) are amendments for sustainable soil management, contaminant remediation, and climate-resilient agriculture. This review examines four production routes: direct pyrolysis of silicon-rich bi
content: Silicon-rich and silicon-modified biochars (Si-BCs) are amendments for sustainable soil management, contaminant remediation, and climate-resilient agriculture. This review examines four production routes: direct pyrolysis of silicon-rich biomass, pre-pyrolysis modification, co-pyrolysis with silicon-rich feedstocks, and post-pyrolysis modification. It assesses how feedstock composition and processing affect silicon speciation, structural accessibility, dissolution kinetics and silicon transfer to the soil–plant system. It highlights analytical limitations and the distinction between total, extractable and plant-available silicon. Evidence is synthesized on Si-BC effects on soil structure, water retention, nutrient dynamics, microbial communities and plant tolerance to abiotic stress. The review also examines mechanisms of potentially toxic element immobilisation and transformation, as well as potential greenhouse gas mitigation and carbon sequestration. Outcomes depend on biochar properties, soil conditions and management; differences in experimental designs and evaluation methods hinder comparison and generalization. Research priorities include standardized characterisation and silicon-release protocols, controlled studies separating silicon-specific effects from those of the biochar matrix and co-introduced constituents and long-term field validation. Life-cycle impacts, production costs, scalability and environmental safety also require assessment. Overall, total silicon content alone is a poor predictor of performance; silicon speciation, accessibility and release kinetics govern its effective transfer from biochar to the soil–plant system.

title: The Netherlands
summary: Overview Cases of Human Rights Violations and Mass Atrocities Related to This JurisdictionIn the Netherlands, the legal responsibility of companies for human rights violations has increasingly been made the subject of litigation in civil co
content: Overview Cases of Human Rights Violations and Mass Atrocities Related to This JurisdictionIn the Netherlands, the legal responsibility of companies for human rights violations has increasingly been made the subject of litigation in civil courts.In particular, the question has been raised to what extent a parent company based in the Netherlands can be held liable for damage having occurred in the ambit of a daughter company's activities in other countries.Although case law is scarce, important developments have taken place in relation to claims regarding oil company Shell's responsibility for the consequences of oil spills for the local community in the Niger delta.In a judgment of 29 January 2021 in the case of Nigerian farmers Oguru and Efanga, joined by the NGO Milieudefensie ('Friends of the Earth'), the Court of Appeal of the Hague ruled that not only daughter company Shell Nigeria was liable in tort towards farmers whose land has been damaged, in particular for not having installed a leak detection system (LDS) on the oil pipeline.1 The Court also established a duty of care in tort law for the holding 1 Court of Appeal of The Hague, 29 January 2021, ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2021:132 (Oguru and Efanga), paras 6.35-43 and 7.24-29.On the same day, the Court of Appeal in the case of Dooh established that daughter company Shell Nigeria was liable in tort for damage caused by shutting down a leaking pipeline too late; Court of Appeal The Hague, 29 January 2021, ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2021:1827, para 6.11.Finally, in the case of Akpan, the court of first instance had established liability of Shell Nigeria for damage resulting from it not having taken sufficient measures to prevent sabotage of an oil well; District Court of The Hague, 30 January 2013, ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2013:BY9854, an appeal to which was lodged with the Court of Appeal of The Hague, 29 January 2021, ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2021:134.Eventually, in December 2022, the parties reached an outof-court settlement, based on which

title: DAVLATLARNING EKOLOGIK JINOYATLARGA DOIR JAVOBGARLIGI MASALASI: VOQELIK VA ISTIQBOLLAR
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Ushbu maqolada xalqaro huquq va milliy qonunchilik doirasida davlatlarning ekologik javobgarligi institutining nazariy-huquqiy asoslari hamda amaliy mexanizmlari tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotda transchegaraviy ekologik zarar yetkazilgan taqdird
content: Ushbu maqolada xalqaro huquq va milliy qonunchilik doirasida davlatlarning ekologik javobgarligi institutining nazariy-huquqiy asoslari hamda amaliy mexanizmlari tahlil qilinadi. title: Estimation of Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Fogera Dairy Cattle Breeding Program at Andassa Livestock Research Center in Ethiopia Using Gleam-I Model
summary: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emission from livestock systems is gaining more attention because of its potential impacts on climate change and food security. In this study, GHG emission from the Fogera dairy cattle breeding program of Andassa Livest
content: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emission from livestock systems is gaining more attention because of its potential impacts on climate change and food security. In this study, GHG emission from the Fogera dairy cattle breeding program of Andassa Livestock Research Center, Ethiopia, were estimated using a model called GLEAM-i and a potential mitigation option (scenarios) was evaluated. The study used data collected from 2014 to 2024 to estimate GHG emissions, quantity of proteins produced, and emission intensity. The overall emission was increasing from 538.6 to 896.03 t CO-eq over the study period mainly because of expanding herd size and productivity. Among the gases, CH 4 comprised the bulk of emissions (> 80%). Although the overall emission was rising during the study period, the quantity of proteins produced increased from around 2,800 to nearly 8,000 kg while emission intensity showed a decreasing trend, indicating the efficiency of producing more proteins per unit of GHG emitted. Two scenarios were evaluated against the business-as-usual system. Scenario 1 increased the quantity of proteins produced by 19.99% and reduced emission intensity by 8.49%. Moreover, scenario 2 increased the quantity of proteins produced by 49.96% and decreased emission intensity by 22.38%. Even though the overall emission for the scenarios was slightly higher than the base, the increase in the quantity of proteins produced was considerably higher compared to the GHG emission. Improving feed quality, herd performance, and manure management would improve productivity and minimize emission per unit of milk produced. Scenario 2 resulted in the best performance and is a feasible option for climate-smart production in Ethiopia. So further, to reduce GHG emissions while increasing productivity, the study suggests scaling up Scenario 2 practices, with a focus on feed optimization, selective breeding, and better manure management.

title: Training future sustainable culinary professionals through game-based learning: development and preliminary evaluation of a carbon-reducing culinary board game
summary: Introduction This study aimed to develop an educational board game that integrates carbon-reducing culinary competence and to evaluate its content validity and students’ self-reported player experiences in foodservice education. Methods Usi
content: Introduction This study aimed to develop an educational board game that integrates carbon-reducing culinary competence and to evaluate its content validity and students’ self-reported player experiences in foodservice education. Methods Using the ADDIE instructional design model, we translated competency indicators across three dimensions (knowledge, attitudes, and skills) into game mechanics for Carbon-Reducing Culinary Helper. Experts in sustainable foodservice education, culinary instruction, board game design, and industry practice reviewed the game’s content. During playtesting, 82 undergraduate students in hospitality and culinary-related programs completed the Player Experience Inventory (PXI). PXI scores were compared between students with and without prior knowledge of sustainability. Results Item-level content validity indices ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, indicating satisfactory content validity. The ten PXI dimensions showed high internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.893 to 0.960. Students generally reported positive player experiences. No statistically significant differences in player experience were found between students with and without prior knowledge of sustainability. Discussion The expert ratings and positive player experiences support the game’s potential as a supplementary tool for foodservice education, education on sustainable food practices, and professional training for foodservice practitioners. The development process illustrates how competency indicators can be translated into game mechanics for sustainability-oriented foodservice education.

title: Bridging the Energy Gap: Performance Benchmarking and Optimisation Potential of Biogas Recovery at a Sewage Treatment Plant in Delhi, India
summary: Anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge offers a dual opportunity for energy recovery and greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation, yet large sewage treatment plants (STPs) in India often operate well below their energy recovery potential. This study e
content: Anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge offers a dual opportunity for energy recovery and greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation, yet large sewage treatment plants (STPs) in India often operate well below their energy recovery potential. This study evaluates biogas generation and energy recovery at a 564 MLD municipal STP in Delhi, India, which employs Anaerobic-Anoxic-Oxic biological treatment with anaerobic sludge digestion and gas-engine based combined heat and power (CHP) generation. Thirteen months of operational data (October 2025 to October 2026), supported by a site visit, were analysed. Biogas production averaged 16,524 Nm³/day, ranging from 14,442 Nm³/day (July 2026, monsoon minimum) to 18,269 Nm³/day (November 2025), with a coefficient of variation of 7.39%, indicating stable digester performance. Biogas-derived electricity averaged 35,062 kWh/month and met 33.0% of plant electricity demand (Energy Self-Sufficiency Index, ESI = 0.330), against a best-practice benchmark of 0.80. ESI showed clear seasonal behaviour, from 0.269 in July to 0.403 in November, linked to monsoon dilution of organic loading. A comparison of theoretical and recorded energy output indicates a large recovery gap, attributed to flaring, engine downtime and biogas quality variation. Current biogas use saves about Rs. 33.66 lakh per year and avoids about 301 tCO₂e/year; raising ESI to 0.50 through optimisation would save an additional Rs. 20 lakh per year and increase avoided emissions to about 503 tCO₂e/year. Five optimisation measures are prioritised, and a replicable benchmarking framework for large Indian STPs is proposed.

title: Sustainable Biogas Production Through Anaerobic Digestion: Environmental Trade-Offs, Process Optimisation and Circular Economy Pathways
summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) supports sustainable organic waste management, renewable energy generation and resource circularity. However, optimisation strategies prioritising methane yield may overlook energy requirements, fugitive emissions a
content: Anaerobic digestion (AD) supports sustainable organic waste management, renewable energy generation and resource circularity. However, optimisation strategies prioritising methane yield may overlook energy requirements, fugitive emissions and resource recovery, potentially compromising overall environmental performance. This study critically examines the sustainability implications of AD optimisation research and identifies opportunities to integrate environmental, economic, and circular economy considerations into biogas production. A bibliometric and thematic review of 413 Scopus-indexed publications (2020–2025) was conducted using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix, complemented by a critical synthesis of optimisation approaches and sustainability-related findings. Research output increased from 40 publications in 2020 to 120 in 2025, representing a threefold increase, with a reported annual publication growth rate of 24.57%. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified 45 frequently occurring keywords, organised into five interconnected research clusters: feedstock management, co-digestion, process optimisation and pretreatment, modelling and intelligent control, and sustainability and circular economy integration. The critical synthesis identifies energy–climate synergies and trade-offs, including reductions in processing energy and modelled emissions, as well as competing electricity-generation and climate outcomes across optimisation configurations. Although hybrid optimisation frameworks are increasingly discussed, consistent integration of life-cycle assessment, techno-economic evaluation, methane-loss mitigation and full-scale environmental validation remains an important research priority. This review proposes a conceptual multi-objective optimisation framework that integrates methane recovery, net energy performance, greenhouse gas emissions, economic viability, operational stability, and nutrient recovery; however, it requires further independent validation. These findings provide sustainability-oriented priorities for researchers, engineers and policymakers seeking to develop resource-efficient, environmentally responsible and economically viable biogas systems.

title: Söylem Analizi Bağlamında İklim Diplomasisinde Türkiye’nin Rolü
summary: Günümüzde varoluşsal bir tehdit olarak nitelendirilen iklim değişikliği, ulusal çıkar ve uluslararası iş birliği tartışmalarını beraberinde getirmiş, söz konusu tartışmalar ise “iklim diplomasisi” özel alanının ortaya çıkmasını sağlamışt
content: Günümüzde varoluşsal bir tehdit olarak nitelendirilen iklim değişikliği, ulusal çıkar ve uluslararası iş birliği tartışmalarını beraberinde getirmiş, söz konusu tartışmalar ise “iklim diplomasisi” özel alanının ortaya çıkmasını sağlamıştır. Bu bağlamda devletler, hükümet liderleri, çıkar grupları, çevreci örgütler, Birleşmiş Milletler (BM), Avrupa Birliği (AB) gibi birçok aktör müzakerelerin yürütülmesinde, iklim değişikliğine yönelik kuralların oluşturulmasında ve uygulanmasında önemli rol oynamıştır. Müzakere sürecinde aktörler finans, kayıp ve hasar gibi konuları tartışarak uyum ve azaltım temelli politikalar geliştirmeye çalışmıştır. Türkiye'de bu aktörlerden biri olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır. Nitekim Türkiye’nin iklim değişikliğine yönelik politika belgelerinde de azaltım ve uyum konusu ön plana çıkmış, BM Taraflar Konferansları’ndaki söylemlerinde iklim değişikliği tehdit olarak belirtilmiştir. Bu çalışma Türkiye’nin iklim diplomasisindeki rolünü incelemektedir. Bu doğrultuda Türkiye’nin 1995-2025 yılları arasında gerçekleşen BM Taraflar Konferansları’ndaki resmî söylemleri analiz edilmiştir. Yorumsamacı söylem analizinin kullanıldığı çalışmanın araştırma sorularını iklim diplomasisinde Türkiye’nin rolünün ne olduğu ve diplomatik söylemlerinde tehdit kavramının nasıl temsil edildiği hususları oluşturmaktadır. Araştırmada iklim diplomasisinde Türkiye’nin uluslararası toplum içerisinde yer alma amacı taşıdığı, iklim değişikliğine yönelik uyum sağlamaya çalıştığı ve ulusal çıkar temelinde iş birliği r olü üstlendiği saptanmıştır.

title: Sandbags and river dikes
summary: Because past greenhouse gas emissions have already triggered irreversible changes in global weather systems, mitigation alone is no longer enough to protect societies. Passive adaptation must give way to active climate resilience by design.
content: Because past greenhouse gas emissions have already triggered irreversible changes in global weather systems, mitigation alone is no longer enough to protect societies. Passive adaptation must give way to active climate resilience by design. By embedding strict climate-proofing criteria into all public investments and capitalizing on the booming global adaptation market, communities can proactively manage escalating hazards like floods and urban heatwaves.

title: Increasing Spatial Unevenness of Dry‐Wet Conditions With Global Warming
summary: Despite little change in total rainy‐season precipitation across the Northern Hemisphere, extreme dry and wet events have become more frequent, indicating intensifying spatial unevenness of dry‐wet conditions. This observed pattern is consi
content: Despite little change in total rainy‐season precipitation across the Northern Hemisphere, extreme dry and wet events have become more frequent, indicating intensifying spatial unevenness of dry‐wet conditions. This observed pattern is consistent with expectations from climate process understanding and evidence from climate models. However, a systematic hemispheric‐scale quantitative assessment of this unevenness remains lacking. To fill this gap, this study examines it through changes in extreme‐event occurrence, distributional shifts, and direct unevenness indices. Observations show that the land area affected by extremes increased by about 1 percentage point per decade, with particularly strong increases in densely populated regions such as the Mediterranean and East Asia. Multi‐model ensemble projections indicate that this tendency will persist and strengthen under higher‐emission scenarios, with increasing divergence toward both drier and wetter extremes. Emission reductions cannot fully prevent this trend but can substantially limit its amplification, highlighting the importance of mitigation and low‐carbon transitions.

title: Environmental standardization in the sustainable blue economy: An integrated environmental management perspective
summary: The Sustainable Blue Economy has become a central objective of international and European marine policy, but its implementation at organisational level remains uneven. This paper examines how environmental standards can support that transit
content: The Sustainable Blue Economy has become a central objective of international and European marine policy, but its implementation at organisational level remains uneven. This paper examines how environmental standards can support that transition when they are used in combination rather than as separate certification tools. The analysis draws on a structured literature and document review, supported by a Scopus search and transparent screening criteria, together with 17 ISO standards and selected European schemes. The instruments are grouped according to the management tasks they support, from establishing responsibilities and measuring impacts to operational improvement and external reporting. On this basis, the paper proposes an integrated standards-to-action framework for blue-economy organisations. Its practical use is illustrated through ship-generated waste management, where ISO 14001, ISO 21070 and ISO 16304 address different but connected parts of the ship-port interface. The analysis shows that no single standard examined covers the full chain from policy objective to documented action. Standards cannot by themselves ensure ecological sustainability or social justice, but they can provide a more coherent basis for planning, monitoring and reporting environmental action.

title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Exposure to Environmental Heat and Cold Among Women of Reproductive Age, 1990-2021
summary: Background: The health impacts of extreme temperature exposure on women of reproductive age remain unclear. This study assesses the global burden of extreme heat and cold exposure (EHCE)-related diseases among women aged 15–49 years from 19
content: Background: The health impacts of extreme temperature exposure on women of reproductive age remain unclear. This study assesses the global burden of extreme heat and cold exposure (EHCE)-related diseases among women aged 15–49 years from 1990 to 2021. Methods: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 data, we analyzed EHCE-related incidence, prevalence, mortality, and DALYs. Temporal trends were assessed using joinpoint regression analysis to estimate annual average percentage changes (AAPC), stratified by age, region, country, and socio-demographic index (SDI). Results: Global EHCE-related burden declined overall from 1990–2021, with fluctuations. Younger women (15–19 years) had highest disease risk but smallest incidence reduction (AAPC=-1.00), while women aged 40–44 showed largest incidence decline (AAPC=-1.43) yet highest mortality. Higher SDI correlated with increased incidence and prevalence; high-SDI countries showed smallest declines (incidence AAPC=-0.34), whereas high-middle SDI countries had steepest reductions (incidence AAPC=-2.14). Regionally, Eastern Europe (AAPC=-2.44) and East Asia (AAPC=-1.85) had largest incidence declines, while high-income Asia-Pacific showed increasing prevalence (AAPC=0.20). Most countries decreased incidence, though France (AAPC=1.83) recorded increases. Conclusion: Persistent disparities across age groups and SDI levels necessitate integrated climate adaptation strategies—including early warning systems and targeted healthcare—and inclusion of women's health in climate policy frameworks.

title: Climate Cooperation under Heterogeneity Enforcement versus Technology Sharing
summary: This contribution investigates under what policy and institutional conditions climate cooperation among heterogeneous sovereign countries can be preserved and sustained over time, in a repeated strategic environment with non-perfect complia
content: This contribution investigates under what policy and institutional conditions climate cooperation among heterogeneous sovereign countries can be preserved and sustained over time, in a repeated strategic environment with non-perfect compliance. We focus on the 19 sovereign members of the G20 - which account for about three-quarters of global greenhouse gas emissions - and the study examines whether alternative policy mechanisms can overcome free-riding incentives coming from the asymmetry between domestic costs and global benefits. The analysis employs a repeated-game framework where countries choose between cooperation and defection during an infinite horizon. We compare two different institutional configurations, C0 and C1: i) C0, a benchmark regime combining sanctions (τ) and monetary transfers as incentives (ρ); and ii) C1, a technology-sharing regime reducing mitigation costs ex ante through a calibrated knowledge spillover (δ_club). The dynamic evaluation of these configurations is conducted via Monte Carlo simulations (T = 5,000, R = 300), assuming a three-period tolerance rule, and it provides the common basis for the cross-regime comparison. Results suggest that without enforcement, cooperation collapses immediately. The technology-sharing regime achieves comparable cooperation rates (coop_rate_avg ≈ 0.985) and collapse probabilities (prob_collapse ≈ 0.030) with less than half the policy intensity (τ = 0.22 vs τ + ρ = 0.5) and no transfers. The main contribution of our analysis is to show that policy design can matter as much as enforcement strength. These findings support designing climate clubs as cooperative structures that reduce individual mitigation costs, and not as agreements based primarily on punishment or redistribution.

title: Parents’ promotion of their children’s pro-environmental attitudes and behaviours: a scoping review
summary: Parents play a central role in shaping children’s awareness of climate change and fostering pro-environmental attitudes and behaviours, yet parents’ perspectives are still underrepresented in the literature. This scoping review identified t
content: Parents play a central role in shaping children’s awareness of climate change and fostering pro-environmental attitudes and behaviours, yet parents’ perspectives are still underrepresented in the literature. This scoping review identified the literature about parents’ promotion of their children’s pro-environmental attitudes and behaviours, i.e., “green parenting”. This review particularly focused on definitions of green parenting, parents’ pro-environmental constructs, theoretical frameworks that informed the studies and were mentioned in the studies, measurement approaches to parental pro-environmental constructs, and psychosocial influences related to green parenting. Following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) scoping review guidelines (PRISMA-ScR), we systematically searched five databases for English- and Spanish-language studies involving parents of children aged 0–12 years. Forty-one studies, representing 10,124 parents—predominantly mothers—met the inclusion/exclusion criteria. This review has demonstrated that research on green parenting has grown in recent years. Definitions addressed parents’ pro-environmental personal orientations, behaviours, and parenting role. However, the scientific literature lacks theory-driven and reliable and valid measures of parent pro-environmental constructs. Current evidence broadly suggests that parents’ pro-environmental attitudes and behaviours were associated with children’s pro-environmental attitudes and behaviours; however, theoretical and methodological limitations across the literature show that the field is not yet positioned to inform evidence-based parenting recommendations. Addressing these limitations through more rigorous and theory-based research is needed to determine how parents can best promote climate resilience and sustainable practices in their children, families, and communities.

title: Oxygen‐Stacking Reconstruction of Spent LiCoO 2 for Fast Li‐Ion Kinetics and High‐Voltage Stability
summary: Recycling spent LiCoO 2 battery cathodes is essential for securing the sustainable supply of lithium and cobalt, yet current recycling methods mainly produce metal salts, precursors, or conventionally regenerated cathodes, making the recove
content: Recycling spent LiCoO 2 battery cathodes is essential for securing the sustainable supply of lithium and cobalt, yet current recycling methods mainly produce metal salts, precursors, or conventionally regenerated cathodes, making the recovery of high‐value LiCoO 2 with enhanced electrochemical performance remain challenging. To address this challenge, we systematically investigate and compare conventionally regenerated O3‐type LiCoO 2 (O3‐R‐LCO) and O2‐type LiCoO 2 produced through a hydrometallurgy‐assisted ion‐exchange upcycling strategy (O2‐UP‐LCO). The upgraded O2‐UP‐LCO preserves the local CoO 6 framework while exhibiting enlarged Li‐layer spacing and a more open interlayer structure compared with O3‐R‐LCO. Multiscale characterizations further reveal that the distinct oxygen stacking in O2‐UP‐LCO enables fast Li + transport and stable interfacial reaction kinetics, despite reversible phase transitions during cycling. Benefiting from these structural and kinetic advantages, O2‐UP‐LCO delivers 201 mAh g −1 even at 20C in coin cells and achieves an energy density of 486 Wh kg −1 at 1C in a 2 Ah‐level pouch cell. In contrast, O3‐R‐LCO suffers from restricted Li + diffusion and increased interfacial impedance at high voltage, accompanied by aggravated particle cracking after cycling. Overall, this work provides a polymorph‐upgrading strategy for efficient recovery of spent LiCoO 2 material.

title: Carbon Emission Factor Dataset for China’s Road Infrastructure Construction
summary: Road infrastructure construction is a major contributor to global resource consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Accurate life-cycle carbon accounting is therefore essential to support the green and low-carbon transition of transport in
content: Road infrastructure construction is a major contributor to global resource consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Accurate life-cycle carbon accounting is therefore essential to support the green and low-carbon transition of transport infrastructure. However, existing carbon emission factor data for road construction are dispersed across diverse sources, including international guidelines, national greenhouse gas inventories, life-cycle assessment datasets, industry standards, and academic literature. These data may exhibit substantial heterogeneity, inconsistent system boundaries, incomplete metadata, and limited comparability. To address these challenges, this study systematically integrates multi-source heterogeneous data to establish a standardised and traceable carbon emission factor dataset for road infrastructure construction in China. A data-processing workflow comprising literature parsing, information extraction, and manual review was adopted. Large language models were used to assist in extracting key information from unstructured literature, while each record was manually verified and subsequently standardised and classified using a coding framework to ensure data reliability. The resulting data resource provides a reliable foundation for life-cycle inventory development, carbon footprint assessment of road infrastructure, and the selection of low-carbon construction materials.

title: Operationalising Solidarity in Global Health Law
