summary: Global crises reveal that nationalism, rather than solidarity, dominates international responses. This stems from a gap between solidarity as a normative legal concept and as a tangible practice. Current global health law remains constraine
content: Global crises reveal that nationalism, rather than solidarity, dominates international responses. This stems from a gap between solidarity as a normative legal concept and as a tangible practice. Current global health law remains constrained by a state-centric model, treating solidarity as discretionary charity rather than a binding imperative. Recent legal scholarship suggests using obligations erga omnes (obligations owed to the global community as a whole) to foster “subaltern internationalism” among states, but these top-down developments often lack connection to the interpersonal, communal, and national practices necessary for equity. This article argues that global health solidarity must be integrated across four tiers: interpersonal, communal, national-institutional, and international. International principles only achieve sustainability when anchored by bottom-up political will and domestic legal integration. The article explores a long-term structural approach via EU refugee law, demonstrating how communal narratives translate abstract norms into binding mechanisms. It then applies a practical approach to the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing framework, asserting that pathogen data sharing must be legally inseparable from equitable distribution. These approaches transform solidarity from a discretionary diplomatic gesture into a functionally operationalised practice, ensuring top-down obligations are structurally anchored in the domestic capacities required for global health justice.

title: Tunable Spinel Ferrite Nanoparticles for High Frequency Power Magnetics and Thermal Management
summary: Soft ferrites are the material of choice for inductive cores in high frequency power electronics, and spinel ferrite nanoparticles extend their functionality to electromagnetic interference (EMI) suppression and thermal management. This cri
content: Soft ferrites are the material of choice for inductive cores in high frequency power electronics, and spinel ferrite nanoparticles extend their functionality to electromagnetic interference (EMI) suppression and thermal management. This critical review of the 2019–2026 literature links composition, cation distribution, and microstructure to magnetic, electrical, and thermal performance using quantitative benchmarks. Mn–Zn ferrites combine high permeability with a DC resistivity of only a few Ω m, whereas Ni–Zn ferrites exceed 10⁵ Ω m, have a coercive field of 200–300 A/m instead of 5–15 A/m, and shift the permeability response by about one order of magnitude toward higher frequency. In a Mn–Zn ferrite, sintering at 1360 °C for 7 h instead of 1325 °C for 3 h increased the grain size from 11.4 to 19.8 µm and the core loss at 100 kHz by about 40%, whereas 3000–4000 ppm CoO flattened the temperature dependence of permeability and loss. At the nanoscale, the saturation magnetization of NixFe3−xO4 fell from 40.16 to 21.97 emu/g as the Ni:Fe ratio increased. The review derives a frequency map of loss mechanisms and a selection guide for Mn–Zn and Ni–Zn ferrites from published benchmarks and compares heat-management pathways on one metric: Fe₃O₄ composites raised polymer thermal conductivity by 22–46%, Fe₃O₄ ferrofluids by more than 200% under a field, while a CoFe₂O₄ nanofiber example showed an entropy change of 1.71 J/(kg K) near 32 K. A gap persists between material-level data and device-level metrics such as loss density at MHz frequencies. A prioritized research agenda is proposed.

title: Beyond the Circularity Illusion in Fast Fashion: A System Dynamics Evaluation of Circular Economy Strategies
summary: In the last two decades, the rise of fast fashion, characterized by overproduction and short product lifecycles, has exacerbated the environmental impacts of the fashion sector at a global level. Driven by policy and market pressures, major
content: In the last two decades, the rise of fast fashion, characterized by overproduction and short product lifecycles, has exacerbated the environmental impacts of the fashion sector at a global level. Driven by policy and market pressures, major fast fashion companies have started implementing circular economy (CE) initiatives, including recycling programs, reuse, and repair services, and the use of recycled materials. Even if such actions could be particularly relevant in fast fashion due to the sectors' high product volumes and extensive vertical integration, few studies focus specifically on evaluating in a holistic way all actions carried out by fast fashion companies. In detail, a comprehensive systemic analysis of the potential long‐term environmental benefits of CE strategies adoption in this sector is still lacking, as most studies focus on isolated actions or short‐term qualitative assessments. This study aims at addressing this gap by developing a system dynamics (SD) model to evaluate the long‐term environmental performance of CE strategies in fast fashion. The SD model captures the behavior of a fast fashion company under circular and linear scenarios, enabling comparative analysis and supporting decision‐making processes on a long‐term horizon. By integrating multiple CE interventions across the value chain, the study contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of their environmental implications. Results suggest that implementing different CE actions in a structured and holistic way can contribute to reducing the environmental burden of fast fashion, although broader business model innovations are required to achieve more substantial and long‐lasting effects.

title: Correlating CO 2 reduction selectivity with ML-quantified morphology of surface Cu and cracks in gas diffusion electrodes
summary: Gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) enable Cu-catalyzed CO 2 electroreduction (CO 2 RR) at industrially relevant current densities, but their porous, multicomponent architecture evolves during operation, affecting selectivity and stability in p
content: Gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) enable Cu-catalyzed CO 2 electroreduction (CO 2 RR) at industrially relevant current densities, but their porous, multicomponent architecture evolves during operation, affecting selectivity and stability in poorly understood ways. We use machine learning clustering of post-mortem electron micrographs to quantify the morphology of surface Cu and cracks of three types of copper-carbon paper GDEs at different stages of CO 2 RR selectivity decay. Pixels are grouped by lightness to identify bright regions associated with agglomerated or rough Cu catalyst and dark regions associated with cracks that extend through the Cu layer in the gas diffusion layer. For each class, we quantify the average patch area, average total area, and average boundary length. These descriptors correlate with C 2 H 4, CO, and H 2 Faradaic efficiencies at least as strongly as conventional observables such as electrode resistance and potential, and gas or liquid pressure. Larger average Cu patch areas correlate with lower C 2 H 4 and CO selectivity in nanoparticle electrodes, consistent with detrimental nanoparticle agglomeration. In contrast, both larger average Cu patches and a larger total area of rough Cu correlate with higher C 2 H 4 and CO selectivity in sputtered electrodes, consistent with a larger electrochemically active Cu surface area. Across electrode types, larger crack patches are associated with higher C 2 H 4 and CO selectivity relative to H 2, consistent with cracks providing preferential drainage pathways that limit flooding. Without a Nafion overcoat, larger crack patches combined with a smaller total crack area are associated with higher C 2 H 4 and CO selectivity, whereas Nafioncoated electrodes retain selectivity despite more extensive cracking. Our findings identify morphological parameters that can guide the design of more selective and stable CO 2 RR electrodes.

title: Rhizosphere as a potential signalling hub for plant adaptation and restoring degraded arid soil
summary: Arid and semi-arid soils are exposed to various interacting biotic and abiotic stresses that impair soil fertility, plant growth, and ecosystem productivity. The combined effects of salinity, elevated temperatures, drought, and nutrient def
content: Arid and semi-arid soils are exposed to various interacting biotic and abiotic stresses that impair soil fertility, plant growth, and ecosystem productivity. The combined effects of salinity, elevated temperatures, drought, and nutrient deficiencies can significantly alter beneficial and pathogenic soil microbial communities, triggering interconnected responses at the rhizosphere, physiological, and molecular levels. At the root–soil interface, hormonal signalling, root system architecture, carbon allocation, and microbial interactions collectively shape soil resilience and plant adaptation. This review provides an overview of rhizosphere responses to multiple stresses and the underlying root-mediated mechanisms, with particular emphasis on soil aggregation, mycorrhizal associations, root exudation, soil organic carbon dynamics, microbial communities, and root turnover. We further highlight the role of phytohormone networks, including jasmonic acid, auxins, and cytokinins, in coordinating stress signalling, root growth, and rhizosphere microbial interactions under stress conditions. Integrating physiological traits and hormone-associated metabolic reprogramming with root phenotyping, proteomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics could provide deeper insights into the phenotype–hormone–metabolome axis. Overall, we propose that combining organic amendments, precision agriculture, deep-rooted perennial systems, and multi-omics approaches could provide a framework for restoring arid soils and developing stress-resilient crops.

title: Adapting to the new abnormal: multinational corporations’ foreign subsidiary investment and country resilience to climate change
summary: As climate change (CC) increasingly disrupts infrastructure, supply chains, labor availability, and public services, multinational corporations (MNCs) face growing uncertainty when selecting locations for foreign expansion. We examine wheth
content: As climate change (CC) increasingly disrupts infrastructure, supply chains, labor availability, and public services, multinational corporations (MNCs) face growing uncertainty when selecting locations for foreign expansion. We examine whether host-country CC resilience has become an important determinant of international investment and how firm capabilities shape this relationship. Drawing on socio-ecological resilience theory and the resilience and turbulence framework, we analyze Global Fortune 500 firms investing across 155 countries between 2003 and 2017. We find that MNCs establish more wholly owned subsidiaries in countries with higher CC resilience, indicating that resilience is emerging as a strategic location-specific advantage. This relationship is stronger for firms with well-developed ESG capabilities and prior experience operating in resilient countries, but weaker for firms with greater financial slack. Our findings suggest that managers should incorporate CC resilience into location decisions alongside traditional economic and institutional criteria while considering their firms’ resource and capability profile to assess how effectively they can leverage host-country CC resilience. For policymakers, the results indicate that strengthening CC resilience can improve not only adaptation to CC but also national competitiveness in attracting MNC foreign direct investment. Overall, CC resilience is becoming a strategic determinant of where MNCs choose to invest.

title: IQLIM O'ZGARISHIGA QARSHI KURASHISHDA PARIJ BITIMINING XALQARO HUQUQIY AHAMIYATI
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Mazkur ilmiy maqolada iqlim o'zgarishiga qarshi kurashishda Parij bitimining xalqaro-huquqiy ahamiyati, uning xalqaro iqlim huquqi tizimidagi o'rni hamda asosiy huquqiy qoidalari tahlil qilinadi. Xususan, Parij bitimining maqsadlari, davlat
content: Mazkur ilmiy maqolada iqlim o'zgarishiga qarshi kurashishda Parij bitimining xalqaro-huquqiy ahamiyati, uning xalqaro iqlim huquqi tizimidagi o'rni hamda asosiy huquqiy qoidalari tahlil qilinadi. Xususan, Parij bitimining maqsadlari, davlatlarning iqlim o'zgarishiga qarshi kurashish bo'yicha xalqaro-huquqiy majburiyatlari, milliy darajada belgilanadigan hissalar va ularni amalga oshirishning huquqiy mexanizmlari o'rganiladi va bitim ijrosini ta'minlashda xalqaro hamkorlik mexanizmlarining huquqiy ahamiyati yoritiladi hamda O'zbekiston Respublikasining Bitimdagi ishtiroki hamda 2026-yil 9–20-noyabrda Antalya(Turkiya)da o'tkazilgan COP31 sammiti natijalari ilmiy-huquqiy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. Maqolada Parij bitimining xalqaro iqlim huquqini rivojlantirishdagi o'rni hamda uning qoidalarini amalga oshirish bilan bog'liq huquqiy muammolar va ularni takomillashtirish istiqbollari bo'yicha ilmiy-amaliy takliflar beriladi.

title: Unstable Antarctic ice sheets in the news media: a 10-year headline analysis
summary: For most people, Antarctic encounters are mediated through texts such as online and print news articles. One of the Antarctic issues appearing in the news media in recent years is ice sheet instability and its implications for future global
content: For most people, Antarctic encounters are mediated through texts such as online and print news articles. One of the Antarctic issues appearing in the news media in recent years is ice sheet instability and its implications for future global sea level rise – an issue also of central concern to the scientific community. Drawing on the Thomson Reuters Westlaw print media database, we used sentiment analysis and reflexive thematic analysis to examine headlines of news stories from 2013, 2018 and 2023 that featured Antarctic ice sheets and sea level rise. Unsurprisingly, we found that negative sentiment dominated these news headlines and increased over time. After excluding words with a weak or neutral sentiment, we further identified an evolution of sentiment language from 2013, when “loss” was the dominant sentiment word, to 2023, when “collapse” was the dominant sentiment word. We categorised the headlines into 10 themes: violence, juggernaut, scale, heroism, fragility, dread, uncertainty, mystery, hope, culpability. Headlines coded to violence, scale, fragility, dread and juggernaut increased over time, while those coded to uncertainty, mystery and culpability decreased over time. For scientists and communicators who interact with media frequently, understanding and awareness of these themes may be useful for anticipating how particular words, phrases, or language use are likely to be thematically contextualised.

title: An insight into the catalytic decomposition of ozone by microbial charcoal-loaded composite materials: the effects and mechanism
summary: Ozone (O 3), which is produced through both natural processes and anthropogenic activities, presents considerable risks to human health and the environment. The effective decomposition of O 3 at ambient temperature utilizing catalysts repre
content: Ozone (O 3), which is produced through both natural processes and anthropogenic activities, presents considerable risks to human health and the environment. The effective decomposition of O 3 at ambient temperature utilizing catalysts represents a promising avenue for mitigation. While microbial carbon materials had shown promise in electrocatalysis and energy storage applications, their utilization as supports for O 3 decomposition catalysts remained largely unexplored. This research involved the synthesis of a microbial carbon-loaded manganese (Mn)/cobalt (Co) catalytic material, designated as Mn2Co1-MC, utilizing microbial biomass residue. The catalyst was activated via pyrolysis at 800 °C, resulting in exceptional O 3 decomposition performance, with a removal efficiency of 88.78 ± 1.32% at an O 3 concentration of 4673 ± 234 ppm. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), and in-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (in-situ DRIFTS) collectively indicated changes in surface oxygen species and metal oxidation states during catalysis. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further suggested that water vapor might competitively adsorb at oxygen vacancy sites. Taken together, these findings were consistent with a plausible deactivation mechanism involving the occupation of oxygen vacancies by water vapor, though direct real-time observation of this process remained challenging.

title: Engineering synthetic microbial communities for black-soil fertility: black-soil-prioritized functional targets, assembly principles, and the colonization gap
summary: Black soils support productive croplands, but intensive cultivation threatens their organic reserves and structure. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs), defined consortia assembled to deliver a target function, offer a tractable appro
content: Black soils support productive croplands, but intensive cultivation threatens their organic reserves and structure. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs), defined consortia assembled to deliver a target function, offer a tractable approach to microbiome intervention. This review develops a black-soil-centered framework, with particular emphasis on cultivated Mollisols of Northeast China and comparable cold-region soils. It prioritizes four fertility functions: necromass-mediated carbon stabilization, seasonally matched nitrogen cycling, organic-phosphorus mobilization, and aggregate maintenance. These functions are shared with other agricultural soils; their priority depends on local constraints, with cold and freeze–thaw tolerance matched to the intended deployment season. Against the resident microbiota and local pH, carbon, mineral and seasonal constraints, the review then evaluates candidate assembly principles, including keystone selection, priority effects, metabolic coexistence, functional redundancy and community coalescence, while separating black-soil observations, mechanisms demonstrated in other systems and proposed design tests. Finally, it examines field establishment and separates colonization, persistence and functional benefit, which need not vary together. Direct field evidence integrating these targets with strain-resolved monitoring in black soils remains limited in the studies reviewed. A practical research agenda links standardized strain and site characterization to controlled, multi-site and multi-season evaluation, followed by an omics-to-design feedback loop, with prespecified functional endpoints, evaluation periods and meaningful effect targets. The framework provides hypotheses for local testing; conceptual links and proposed screening conditions are not validated causal pathways or universal performance thresholds.

title: D1.5 Recommendations for wetland restoration
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Executive summary: This deliverable synthesizes past peatland restoration projects, analysing their goals, methodologies, and outcomes. A comprehensive database was developed from various sources, focusing on European peatlands. The study e
content: Executive summary: This deliverable synthesizes past peatland restoration projects, analysing their goals, methodologies, and outcomes. A comprehensive database was developed from various sources, focusing on European peatlands. The study explores restoration goals, wetland types, restoration measures, monitoring variables, and stakeholder engagement.The report evaluates restoration success, highlighting factors like water level restoration, vegetation recovery, and peat formation. Challenges include varying restoration effectiveness, the complexity of peatland classification, and the influence of global change. The study emphasizes the importance of long-term monitoring, stakeholder involvement, and standardized restoration practices.The findings underscore the need for tailored restoration approaches, considering the specific ecological conditions and degradation status of each site. Effective peatland restoration is essential for climate change mitigation, biodiversity conservation, and the preservation of crucial ecosystem services. The deliverable also identifies knowledge gaps and suggests directions for future research and restoration.

title: A remote sensing approach for in-season nitrogen and yield prediction
summary: Vegetation indices (VIs) provide valuable insights that can be used for optimizing corn production across diverse agroecological environments. This study evaluated the reliability of Sentinel-2-derived VIs for monitoring nitrogen (N) uptake
content: Vegetation indices (VIs) provide valuable insights that can be used for optimizing corn production across diverse agroecological environments. This study evaluated the reliability of Sentinel-2-derived VIs for monitoring nitrogen (N) uptake, estimating above‑ground biomass (AGB), and predicting final yield. Validation of VI‑based estimates was performed using field data from three commercial farms selected for their distinct pedoclimatic characteristics. VI performance varied across environmental regimes, reflecting differences in canopy development and field‑scale heterogeneity. For early‑season N uptake (V5–V6), simple indices such as the chlorophyll index green (CIg) performed exceptionally well in environments with more uniform canopy development (R² up to 0.91) but showed reduced reliability under more heterogeneous conditions (R² < 0.53). Incorporating bivariable models improved robustness across environments, with the MERIS terrestrial chlorophyll index (MTCI) + Advanced Vegetation Index (AVI) combination emerging as the most stable and transferable predictor overall (R² ≈ 0.70). For AGB estimation, the red‑edge‑based MTCI was the strongest single predictor across environments, while bivariable models substantially enhanced accuracy in fields characterized by greater spatial variability (R² up to 0.83). Yield prediction at the R1 growth stage was strongly correlated with CIg (R² = 0.80), but moderately with MTCI, (R² = 0.63). A pooled, multi‑environment yield model achieved an overall R² of 0.64. Although predictive strength declined in some environments, precision remained high (SE < 1.03 Mg ha⁻¹), supporting the utility of Sentinel‑2–based VIs for generating reliable spatial yield maps and delineating intra‑field management zones.

title: Beyond ‘Green Intensive Care Units’, climate-smart critical care: A resource-conscious paradigm for sustainable intensive care unit
source: World Journal of Critical Care Medicine
summary: Intensive care units (ICUs) are resource-intensive healthcare environments with substantial environmental footprints arising from energy consumption, medical supplies, pharmaceuticals, water usage, and high waste generation.Simultaneously,
content: Intensive care units (ICUs) are resource-intensive healthcare environments with substantial environmental footprints arising from energy consumption, medical supplies, pharmaceuticals, water usage, and high waste generation.Simultaneously, climate change threatens critical care delivery through heightened patient surges and infrastructure disruptions.Integrating environmental sustainability with clinical safety and operational resilience is thus paramount.The objective of the review is to propose an integrative framework for climate-smart critical care that bridges environmental sustainability, high-value clinical practice, climate resilience, and context-specific implementation.This narrative review examines major ICU environmental hotspots and outlines strategies to reduce avoidable resource consumption without compromising patient safety.We introduce the "Resilience Quartet" as vital interdependent system ensuring continuity of life-sustaining care.A practical four-stage implementation approach emphasizes baseline assessments, localized prioritization, standardized indicators, and iterative evaluation.The implementation priorities must reflect local infrastructure, affordability, environmental hotspots, and operational vulnerabilities.Resource conservation should not be equated with environmental benefit and the interventions must be balanced against clinical safety, infection control, and economic outcomes.Climate-Smart Critical Care expands upon traditional Green ICU initiatives by unifying environmental footprint reduction, high-value care, operational resilience, and contextual feasibility into a single decision-making model.Successful execution demands multidisciplinary engagement, and rigorous evaluation across diverse global healthcare settings.

title: Kinetic windows for abiogenesis
summary: The origin of life on Earth occurred within a narrow window delimited by cessation of intense late accretion bombardment at about 4.4 Ga on the one hand, and younger evidence gleaned via molecular phylogenetic studies, isotopic biosignature
content: The origin of life on Earth occurred within a narrow window delimited by cessation of intense late accretion bombardment at about 4.4 Ga on the one hand, and younger evidence gleaned via molecular phylogenetic studies, isotopic biosignatures and morphological traces on the other. Molecular clock analyses tentatively place the median age for the Last Universal Common Ancestor LUCA population of all contemporary DNA life at about 4.2 Ga. Cryptic isotopic biosignatures go back as far as 4.1 Ga in Hadean zircons and more robustly in Eoarchean rocks at about 3.83 Ga. Morphological remains including microfossils and microbially mediated sedimentary structures are almost as ancient, around 3.5 Ga. To make better sense of this early and rapid timeline and its implications for a biosphere on Hadean Earth, we parameterize the kinetic windows for that transition from non-living to living chemistry, abiogenesis. Here, we reinforce the finding that before the LUCA, a RiboNucleic Acid RNA and RiboNucleoProtein RNP World could have persisted for less than 130 Myr. Furthermore, we show that conditions which define the kinetic windows for early Earth stand out compared to other worlds in our Solar System considered as candidates for abiogenesis. Specifically, these are sustained stable liquid water from 4.4 Ga, wet-dry cycling on dry land under an atmosphere, effective crustal recycling to rejuvenate disequilibrium chemistry, available key elements for synthesis and growth, mechanisms to concentrate prebiotic reaction products without also destroying them, and sufficient spatial scales for subsequent evolution and diversification. We argue that the steps from abiogenesis to DNA required chemistry coordinated with environmental conditions overlapping in time with each transition from prebiotic synthesis to cellular life governed by distinct rate limiting processes operating over geologically short timescales. Our analysis suggests that if DNA life had not emerged, an informationally deficient and thermally unstable RNA biosphere would eventually have gone extinct.

title: Powering green energy through public–private partnerships in Pakistan
summary: The transition towards green energy is critical for Pakistan’s pursuit of climate justice, particularly in the context of its surging energy demands, financial constraints, and recurrent climate challenges. The existing literature on Pakist
content: The transition towards green energy is critical for Pakistan’s pursuit of climate justice, particularly in the context of its surging energy demands, financial constraints, and recurrent climate challenges. The existing literature on Pakistan’s energy sector has largely focused on policy frameworks and technical feasibility of renewable projects and very limited empirical attention has been paid to the phase-wise Critical Success Factors (CSFs) that shape the actual implementation of Public–Private Partnerships (PPPs) in green energy projects. Therefore, this qualitative study aims to fill the research gap and explore the CSFs of PPPs vis-à-vis green energy transition in Pakistan. The study takes the Atlas Solar Power Project, Layyah, as a case study and classifies the PPP process into three integrated phases (Pre-Installation, Installation, and Post-Installation). Theoretically, this study integrates Triple-Helix, Stakeholder and Resource Dependence theories to evaluate the dynamics of collaborative governance in PPP-enabled green energy transition. It also contributes meaningfully to Sustainable Development Goal 7 by synchronizing PPPs with Pakistan’s quest for reliable, affordable, and clean energy. The data were collected through semi-structured interviews with key stakeholders involved in the project, conducted over a four-month period. The interview data is analysed using thematic analysis through NVivo 15 to derive key themes. This study identifies distinct policy, regulatory, and coordination gaps that are critical for the success of this model. These findings offer valuable insights for policymakers, future researchers, and private investors with a focus on the renewable sector.

title: Extreme heat and informal urban workers’ health – lessons for Latin America and the Caribbean from South Asia
summary: Background Extreme heat events are becoming more frequent and intense, posing substantial public health risks. In Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), 82% of the population resides in urban areas and over half of workers (51.7%) are infor
content: Background Extreme heat events are becoming more frequent and intense, posing substantial public health risks. In Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), 82% of the population resides in urban areas and over half of workers (51.7%) are informally employed. To address the heat-related health risk of informal urban workers, LAC can learn from other Global South regions facing similar challenges of informality, multidimensional poverty, precarious labor conditions, and rising temperatures. Analysis We conducted an exploratory review of academic and grey literature on urban heat responses in LAC and South Asia, the Global South region with the most documented and evaluated experience. Each response was assessed for whether it reaches informal urban workers, the structural barriers to doing so and recommendations to overcome them. Policy Options Responses fall into four domains, each addressing a distinct gap for informal workers in LAC: satellite-based diagnostic visualization, to map where they live and work; heat action planning and early warning, to deliver alerts through channels they use; governance innovations, to assign institutional responsibility for tackling their heat risk; and exposure reduction interventions spanning household, transit, and worksite settings. Conclusion South Asian experiences show that resource-constrained cities can implement effective heat responses but these will not reach informal workers unless they are designed to include them for the start. This requires political commitment, multi-level and multi-sectoral coordination, and the meaningful participation of informal workers in intervention design.

title: Empirical Review of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) as an Energy Alternative in Nigeria: Opportunities and Challenges
source: British Journal of Multidisciplinary and Advanced Studies
summary: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) has emerged globally as a cleaner, more economical alternative to conventional fossil fuels, particularly in transportation and industrial applications. In the context of Nigeria, where reliance on petroleum-bas
content: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) has emerged globally as a cleaner, more economical alternative to conventional fossil fuels, particularly in transportation and industrial applications. In the context of Nigeria, where reliance on petroleum-based fuels continues to dominate energy consumption, CNG presents a promising pathway to energy diversification, economic efficiency, and environmental sustainability. This study examined the potential of CNG as an alternative fuel in Nigeria’s transport and industrial sectors, with particular attention to energy consumption patterns, economic advantages, infrastructural demands, and key implementation challenges. A descriptive survey design was employed, targeting energy sector stakeholders, transport operators, and policymakers. A total of 300 respondents were selected using stratified random sampling. Data were gathered through structured, close-ended questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistical tools, including frequency and percentage analysis via SPSS. Findings revealed that over 86% of respondents acknowledged the urgent need to shift from petroleum dependence. Economic benefits of CNG adoption included reduced transportation costs, lower fuel subsidy burdens, and job creation. However, major obstacles identified were high capital investment, inadequate infrastructure, low public awareness, and policy inconsistency. The study concludes that CNG is a viable solution to Nigeria’s energy challenges and recommends robust government investment in infrastructure, targeted awareness campaigns, policy coherence, and active stakeholder collaboration to facilitate CNG adoption.

title: Patent landscape and technological forecasting for biosurfactant use in agricultural biocontrol: innovation, protection strategies, and future perspectives
summary: MAIN CONCLUSION: Patent-based forecasting shows that agricultural biosurfactant technologies are growing exponentially, following a strain-to-formulation development chain. The new Strategic International Protection Index reveals the Compos
content: MAIN CONCLUSION: Patent-based forecasting shows that agricultural biosurfactant technologies are growing exponentially, following a strain-to-formulation development chain. The new Strategic International Protection Index reveals the Compositions category is closest to market-ready products. The growing search for more sustainable agricultural alternatives has prompted the development of microbial bioproducts, especially biosurfactants and lipopeptides, as substitutes for conventional agrochemicals. Although commercial and scientific interest in these products has increased, studies concerning their technological evolution, innovation trends, and future outlook are still limited. This patent-based technological prospecting study considered four categories related to protection of the strain, production processes, compositions, and applications. Technological forecasting was also carried out, using indicators, such as the maturity stage of the defined categories, Technological Diffusion Speed (TDS), Patent Power (PP), Expansion Potential (EP), and a new proposed indicator, the Strategic International Protection Index (SIPI), that expresses market perspectives and the effort to protect technologies internationally. There is a balance between patents coming from research institutes and industries, indicating good technology transfer to the market, with more than 200 patent documents from China. The Strains and biological material category had the steepest S-curve and the highest number of patent documents, in combination with the highest TDS. In comparison, PP and EP values were the highest for Compositions and formulation category, followed by the Applications and uses and Production process and fermentation categories. The SIPI was also the highest for the Compositions and formulation category, followed by the Applications and uses, Production process, and Strains and biological material categories. These findings are consistent with the research and development chain of events, with the technologies most likely to hit the market in the next few years.

title: Global hydrological impacts of pine and eucalyptus afforestation: a meta-analysis of paired catchment studies
summary: Climate change and population growth pose major challenges to global water resources by altering temperature and precipitation patterns and increasing pressure on ecosystems. Afforestation has been widely promoted as a strategy to mitigate
content: Climate change and population growth pose major challenges to global water resources by altering temperature and precipitation patterns and increasing pressure on ecosystems. Afforestation has been widely promoted as a strategy to mitigate these impacts; however, its hydrological effects remain uncertain due to inconsistent findings across studies. To provide a robust and quantitative assessment, this study applied a global meta-analysis of paired-catchment experiments to evaluate the impacts of afforestation with pine ( Pinus spp.) and eucalyptus ( Eucalyptus spp.) on surface runoff, streamflow, and evapotranspiration. A systematic literature search across ten information sources identified 810 records, of which 19 studies met the inclusion criteria and were retained for the quantitative meta-analysis, encompassing 30 paired-catchment observations for runoff, 11 for streamflow, and 16 for evapotranspiration. Using a random-effects model, the meta-analysis revealed that afforestation with pine and eucalyptus reduced surface runoff by 35% and streamflow by 51%, while increasing evapotranspiration by 20% compared to non-forested controls. These results demonstrate that afforestation can substantially alter watershed water balance, primarily by enhancing evapotranspiration and reducing water yield. The findings highlight the importance of species selection in afforestation programs and emphasize the need to integrate hydrological considerations into forest management and land-use planning to support sustainable water resource management under changing climatic conditions.

title: How eco-anxiety shapes sustainable behaviour: implications for urban planning and design
summary: Eco-anxiety is the chronic fear of environmental cataclysm. This qualitative study investigates how individuals experiencing eco-anxiety perceive and engage with urban built environments – specifically, how eco-anxiety shapes attitudes towa
content: Eco-anxiety is the chronic fear of environmental cataclysm. This qualitative study investigates how individuals experiencing eco-anxiety perceive and engage with urban built environments – specifically, how eco-anxiety shapes attitudes towards urban form and density, as well as transport and mobility. The research thematically analyses 265 user-generated comments from Reddit forums on eco-anxiety. The central finding is the prioritization of controllability and visibility in sustainable actions over their environmental effectiveness. This leads many eco-anxious individuals to reject urban living altogether. The discussion focuses how to address this anti-urban sentiment and how to move beyond individual guilt towards systemic action.

title: An algorithm for identifying abnormal power limitation data in photovoltaic power generation based on denoising of expansion corrosion morphology
summary: Power curtailment anomalies unique to the photovoltaic power generation sector arise from uncertain and sudden mandatory wind and photovoltaic power curtailment operations. Because such data exhibit no discernible patterns, conventional ano
content: Power curtailment anomalies unique to the photovoltaic power generation sector arise from uncertain and sudden mandatory wind and photovoltaic power curtailment operations. Because such data exhibit no discernible patterns, conventional anomaly detection algorithms that rely on assumptions regarding data distributions or empirical models cannot identify them effectively. To improve the recognition rate of photovoltaic power curtailment anomalies, a power curtailment anomaly detection algorithm based on mathematical morphology denoising is proposed. The algorithm treats power curtailment anomalies as noise signals superimposed on the original data and imposes no requirements on the distribution characteristics of the original data. It only converts the original data into binary images and adaptively identifies power curtailment anomalies through basic mathematical morphology denoising operations, such as dilation and erosion. Simulations based on field-collected data show that, compared with conventional anomaly detection algorithms, the proposed algorithm significantly improves the recognition rate of power curtailment anomalies, thereby verifying its applicability to power curtailment anomaly detection.

title: Toward adaptive yet comparable greenhouse gas measurements across global rice systems
summary: Toward adaptive yet comparable greenhouse gas measurements across global rice systems, Minamikawa, Kazunori, Adviento-Borbe, M. Arlene, Radanielson, Ando M., Hasegawa, Toshihiro, Li, Tao, Valdivia, Roberto O., Mencos Contreras, Erik, Karl,
content: Toward adaptive yet comparable greenhouse gas measurements across global rice systems, Minamikawa, Kazunori, Adviento-Borbe, M. Arlene, Radanielson, Ando M., Hasegawa, Toshihiro, Li, Tao, Valdivia, Roberto O., Mencos Contreras, Erik, Karl, Kevin

title: Oxygen Diffusion Rapidly Quantifies Water Vapor Permeability and Pore- Networks of Building Materials
summary: The ability of a building material to transmit water vapor is essential for indoor air quality, prevention of fungal growth, and overall livability. Today's slow and tedious methods to quantify material moisture performance is a barrier for
content: The ability of a building material to transmit water vapor is essential for indoor air quality, prevention of fungal growth, and overall livability. Today's slow and tedious methods to quantify material moisture performance is a barrier for designing healthy buildings including new sustainable and/or bio-based materials. In this study, we investigated the theoretical relation between water vapor permeability (WVP) and oxygen gas diffusivity (OGD) in porous media and verify this theoretical relation between OGD and WVP for 12 building materials spanding from dense, low porosity to light, highly-porous materials. Measurement time for OGD was typically 50–100 times quicker than for WVP (e.g., from 240 hours to 3 hours) using a newly-developed, high-precision oxygen diffusion chamber compared to using standard Dry-Cup measurements of WVP on the same material samples. As an additional benefit of the OGD method, pore-network characteristics like tortuosity and the Archie's Law coefficient for pore connectivity can be derived from the measurements. The Archies Law coefficient varied from A = 2 (highly connected pores) for fired brick to A = 250 (almost non-connected pore network) for styrofoam (expanded polystyrene) providing a rapid, highly sensitive measure of pore connectivity for oxygen, radon, and water vapor mobility through building materials.

title: FROM TREE BARK ALGAE TO ALGAE TREES: BIODIVERSITY-DRIVEN APPROACHES TO ATOM-ECONOMICAL SUSTAINABILITY
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Biodiversity plays a fundamental role in sustaining ecological balance and promoting innovative solutions for environmental sustainability. Tree bark ecosystems harbour diverse communities of subaerial algae, cyanobacteria, fungi, and bacte
content: Biodiversity plays a fundamental role in sustaining ecological balance and promoting innovative solutions for environmental sustainability. Tree bark ecosystems harbour diverse communities of subaerial algae, cyanobacteria, fungi, and bacteria that contribute to nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, and air-quality regulation. Studies have demonstrated that algal diversity varies with tree species and environmental conditions, with open-canopy habitats supporting richer biodiversity. Inspired by the remarkable photosynthetic efficiency of microalgae, engineered “Algae Trees” have emerged as climate-smart technologies for urban environments. These vertical photobioreactors utilize microalgal biodiversity to capture atmospheric carbon dioxide, reduce particulate pollution, and enhance urban ecological resilience. The concept aligns closely with the principles of green chemistry, particularly atom economy, which emphasizes the efficient conversion of inputs into useful outputs with minimal waste generation. Through photosynthesis, microalgae transform carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight into biomass and oxygen, exemplifying a near atom-economical biological process. Integrating natural biodiversity with atom-economy-driven technologies offers a sustainable framework for climate mitigation, pollution control, and circular bioeconomy development. Such approaches demonstrate how ecological diversity and resource-efficient design can work synergistically to address environmental challenges while promoting long-term sustainability and ecosystem health.

title: Using Managed Aquifer Recharge to Defer High‐Capital‐Cost Investments and Avoid Lock‐In in Semi‐Arid Australia
source: Australian Journal of Agricultural and Resource Economics
summary: Water‐scarce regions must plan long‐lived infrastructure under uncertain inflows, drought risk and future demand. Single‐decision‐point benefit–cost analyses (BCAs) can understate the value of flexibility when large, irreversible water‐supp
content: Water‐scarce regions must plan long‐lived infrastructure under uncertain inflows, drought risk and future demand. Single‐decision‐point benefit–cost analyses (BCAs) can understate the value of flexibility when large, irreversible water‐supply investments are assessed without explicitly representing future decision opportunities. This study re‐examines the 2016 decision to construct the A$491 million Murray River pipeline for Broken Hill, New South Wales and asks whether a managed aquifer recharge (MAR) first strategy could meet the city's long‐term water‐supply objective at lower expected cost while avoiding premature commitment to irreversible capital investment. We develop a stochastic real‐options benefit–cost framework over a 30‐year planning horizon. Across 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations, the historical single‐decision‐point pipeline policy is compared with an adaptive MAR‐first policy in which the pipeline is retained as a contingent option and exercised only if available supply falls below 2.5 GL for two consecutive years. The three possible adaptive outcomes are evaluated jointly as one decision strategy, weighted by their simulated frequencies. The model incorporates probabilistic supply and demand variation, capital and operating costs, salinity and greenhouse‐gas externalities, and lower‐tail reliability using Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR). The adaptive MAR‐first policy has an expected present value of costs (EPVC) of A$372.1 million, compared with A$621.4 million for the benchmark pipeline policy, an expected saving of A$249.3 million (40.1%). The pipeline is exercised in approximately 5% of adaptive‐policy futures and remains unexercised in approximately 95%. Mean annual available supply is 9.58 GL/year under the adaptive policy compared with 7.70 GL/year under the benchmark. In the lowest‐yield 5% of simulated outcomes, average annual available supply is 2.52 GL/year under the benchmark policy and approximately 5.20 GL/year under the adaptive policy. Both values remain below the representative 7.5 GL/year demand benchmark, meaning that extreme drought conditions can still produce supply shortfalls; however, the smaller gap under the adaptive policy indicates substantially reduced lower‐tail shortfall exposure. The results show that MAR‐led sequencing can improve the cost‐reliability trade‐off while reducing expected lifecycle cost and premature capital commitment under deep uncertainty.

title: Quantifying the factors behind the decision to produce second-generation ethanol in Brazil: a Fuzzy-QFD decision-support model.
summary: Second-generation (2G) ethanol is a strategic route for decarbonizing the energy matrix through lignocellulosic residues, yet its consolidation in Brazil remains limited and the corporate decision to produce it is poorly understood quantita
content: Second-generation (2G) ethanol is a strategic route for decarbonizing the energy matrix through lignocellulosic residues, yet its consolidation in Brazil remains limited and the corporate decision to produce it is poorly understood quantitatively. To address this gap, this study develops and applies a Fuzzy Quality Function Deployment (Fuzzy-QFD) decision-support model that quantifies how strongly each factor and barrier is weighed in the decision to produce 2G ethanol, and how this weighting differs among production-system actors. Nine critical factors and twelve expected-quality groups were derived from two systematic reviews and structured as a House of Quality; linguistic judgments from 40 stakeholders spanning the Triple Helix (industry, academia, and government) were encoded as triangular fuzzy numbers, aggregated (with competence-based coefficients applied to the correlation judgments), and defuzzified into crisp values that populated the matrix. The analysis is framed by the Triple Bottom Line and the Sustainable Development Goals. Industrial Efficiency ranked first (about 11% of relative importance), indicating that 2G ethanol is treated as a commodity whose competitiveness depends on process optimization rather than product properties, while Technology emerged as the structural driver of the model. Although Environmental Sustainability shared the highest declared importance with Technology, it showed limited operational influence, suggesting a gap between sustainability commitments and their translation into decision-making, with implications for SDG 13. The priorities are associative rather than causal and reflect the evaluated stakeholders, part of whom validated document-informed drafts. The model provides a replicable tool that converts subjective judgments into impact coefficients for each decision actor.

title: INTRODUCTION AND INCREASE OF BIODIVERSITY OF FOREST ECOSYSTEMS AS ADAPTATION MECHANISMS TO MITIGATE THE CONSEQUENCES OF CLIMATE CHANGE
summary: The article discusses the general introduction to the issue of increasing sustainable forestry. Humanity is facing an emergency climate situation, and it is necessary to develop approaches to the management of forest ecosystems. They must b
content: The article discusses the general introduction to the issue of increasing sustainable forestry. Humanity is facing an emergency climate situation, and it is necessary to develop approaches to the management of forest ecosystems. They must be reliable and capable of producing results, despite the great uncertainty about the conditions that forests will face in the future. Forestry must preserve the values recognized in previous concepts, such as maintaining the health of ecosystems and biodiversity in the long term, and address the urgent issue of climate change by increasing the amount of carbon stored in both forests and long-lived forest products.

title: Active Thermal Protection via TBBPA-Embedded Electrospun Separators
summary: Despite their safety benefits, most flame-retardant strategies rely on soluble additives that alter interfacial chemistry, destabilize the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and ultimately compromise battery performance. Here, in contrast
content: Despite their safety benefits, most flame-retardant strategies rely on soluble additives that alter interfacial chemistry, destabilize the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and ultimately compromise battery performance. Here, in contrast to conventional soluble-additive approaches, tetrabromobisphenol-A (TBBPA) is incorporated into electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVdF-HFP) fibers to provide a flame-retardant separator with electrochemical compatibility under the conditions investigated. Structural and chemical characterizations support TBBPA incorporation within the electrospun PVdF-HFP matrix, while electrochemical measurements indicate preserved effective ionic conductivity and sustained graphite||Li half-cell operation at room temperature and 60 °C. Post-mortem X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicates limited but detectable additive migration at 60 °C, with lower TBBPA-related accumulation on graphite than for direct addition to the electrolyte. The contribution is the combination of self-extinguishing behavior in qualitative tests on electrolyte-soaked membranes and improved electrochemical compatibility relative to direct additive addition.

title: E-waste Plastics in Concrete: A Systematic Review of Applications, Mechanical Performance, and Critical Research Gaps
summary: The increasing generation of electronic waste (e-waste), particularly plastic fractions, poses a significant environmental challenge due to their complexity and limited recyclability. In parallel, the construction industry has been actively
content: The increasing generation of electronic waste (e-waste), particularly plastic fractions, poses a significant environmental challenge due to their complexity and limited recyclability. In parallel, the construction industry has been actively seeking more sustainable alternatives to reduce the consumption of natural resources and mitigate environmental impacts. This study presents a systematic literature review on the incorporation of plastics derived from e-waste into cementitious concretes, aiming to identify their main applications, evaluate their mechanical and durability performance, and highlight existing research gaps. A total of 42 studies published between 2011 and 2025 were analyzed. The results indicate that e-waste plastics are predominantly used as a replacement for coarse aggregate, followed by fine aggregate, and to a lesser extent as fibers. A reduction in compressive strength and tensile strength is generally observed with increasing replacement ratios, particularly above 10–20%, mainly due to the low interfacial bonding and reduced stiffness of polymers. Conversely, the use of fibers may improve tensile behavior when optimized contents are adopted. Furthermore, a scarcity of studies addressing the modulus of elasticity and long-term performance was identified, along with inconclusive findings regarding durability. From a sustainability perspective, only one study conducted a life cycle assessment, highlighting a significant research gap. Although promising, the use of these residues requires more integrated and standardized investigations to ensure their structural and environmental feasibility.

title: Chemicals matter: sustainability assessments of foodware and food packaging with the Understanding Packaging Scorecard
summary: Food sector decision-makers need transparent, science-based tools to evaluate the human and environmental impacts of foodware and packaging. Existing assessment tools often focus on specific materials only or overlook chemical safety. The o
content: Food sector decision-makers need transparent, science-based tools to evaluate the human and environmental impacts of foodware and packaging. Existing assessment tools often focus on specific materials only or overlook chemical safety. The open-access Understanding Packaging (UP) Scorecard addresses this gap by comparing generic products across six impact areas, including chemical migration into foodstuffs. Improved final product testing methods would further strengthen chemical safety assessment and support more informed decisions in practice.

title: Enhancing Outdoor Comfort in Delhi: Urban Heat Island Mitigation with Future Climate Projections
summary: For rapidly warming cities such as Delhi, the real test of an Urban Heat Island (UHI) mitigation strategy is not whether it cools streets today, but whether it still does so under the hotter climate those streets will face decades from now.
content: For rapidly warming cities such as Delhi, the real test of an Urban Heat Island (UHI) mitigation strategy is not whether it cools streets today, but whether it still does so under the hotter climate those streets will face decades from now. The surface warming in Delhi due to urbanization is the result of the replacement of vegetation with built-up areas, and with hot surfaces increasing cooling loads, heat management is crucial in sustainable urban development and planning. The current research analysed high albedo pavements as a potential UHI mitigation strategy in a medium-density plotted housing neighbourhood, with respect to the outdoor thermal comfort levels under present-day conditions as well as those projected for the late twenty-first century. New Friends Colony was selected as a representative case study, combining on-site measurements with the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) and ENVI-met microclimate simulations driven by Energy Plus Weather (EPW) data. For the year 2082, the future urban form was extrapolated based on the past trends in green cover increase, along with the rise of the building density and height. The scenario included an approximately 2 °C increase in mean air temperature. Reflective pavements were considered in both cases. It was found out that under present-day conditions, reflective pavements reduced surface temperatures and heat stress levels according to UTCI levels. However, in the case of the future scenario, the increase in the heat level led to a shift in UTCI category towards higher levels, indicating that only these strategies would be insufficient for mitigating the future heat level. Thus, the maintenance of outdoor comfort requires a proactive approach with a number of strategies involving reflective pavements and surfaces, greenery and permeability.

title: From Policy to Practice: Regulatory Considerations for Offshore Wind Energy in Malaysia’s Renewable Energy Sector
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Offshore wind power has potential to help Malaysia achieve its goals, in energy advancement. This study delves into how the rules and guidelines governing offshore wind energy development are applied in Malaysia and looks at the impact of e
content: Offshore wind power has potential to help Malaysia achieve its goals, in energy advancement. This study delves into how the rules and guidelines governing offshore wind energy development are applied in Malaysia and looks at the impact of existing policies in this area like the Renewable Energy Act of 2011 and the National Renewable Energy Policy and Action Plan are examined to see how well they support offshore wind initiatives, in practice. The research also compares the structures of countries that have well established offshore wind sectors to provide a broader perspective. Key issues, like assessing effects and meeting standards while collaborating with stakeholders are reviewed to pinpoint deficiencies in the existing system. The article stresses the importance of protocols support from the government and the integration of cutting-edge technologies to promote the expansion of offshore wind energy in Malaysia. The research results end with suggestions for enhancing Malaysia’s structure to encourage the progress of wind energy while maintaining a well-rounded approach, toward economic advancement, sustainable environment and energy protection.

title: Geometry‐Guided Anisotropic Pore Stretching for Enhanced SF 6 Packing in an Al‐Based Metal–Organic Framework
summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are attractive adsorbents for recovering sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) from SF6/N2 mixtures, yet improving pore utilization without compromising SF6/N2 discrimination remains challenging. Herein, we design an Al-
content: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are attractive adsorbents for recovering sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) from SF6/N2 mixtures, yet improving pore utilization without compromising SF6/N2 discrimination remains challenging. Herein, we design an Al-based MOF, QUST-5, constructed from the one-dimensional Al(OH)2O4 chain and tetracarboxylate linker 4,4',4″,4‴-(pyrazino[2,3-g]quinoxaline-2,3,7,8-tetrayl)tetrabenzoic acid for efficient SF6/N2 separation. Guided by pore geometric analysis in this frl topology of Al-based MOF, the linker backbone is extended along one direction while the local SF6-matched confinement environment is retained. This anisotropic pore stretching preserves the high-affinity single-SF6 confinement environment of the Al-TCPA-type benchmark while introducing an additional dual-SF6 packing motif in QUST-5. At 298 K, QUST-5 shows high SF6 uptake of 2.50 mmol/g at 10 kPa, high SF6/N2 (10/90 mixture) selectivity of 760 at 100 kPa, and superior SF6 packing densities of 1.09 and 1.76 g/cm3 at 10 and 100 kPa, outperforming the parent Al-TCPA and most representative MOFs. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient SF6/N2 separation, and stability tests show retention of crystallinity and porosity after thermal, aqueous, humid, and chemical treatments. Computational simulations further identify a retained high-affinity SF6 site and an additional packing-enabled dual-SF6 site. These results highlight pore stretching as a useful design strategy for improving SF6 packing efficiency in MOF adsorbents.

title: HFC-134a Upcycling via Alkaline Hydrolysis
summary: As hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) are gradually phased out by global regulations, there is an increasing need for efficient destruction methods to treat the now waste refrigerants and legacy material. Current methods such as incineration and pla
content: As hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) are gradually phased out by global regulations, there is an increasing need for efficient destruction methods to treat the now waste refrigerants and legacy material. Current methods such as incineration and plasma are energy intensive, produce corrosive and/or toxic compounds, and may generate other fluorinated gas emissions. Continuous flow alkaline hydrolysis (AH) is a commercial method for the treatment of perfluoroalkyl substances. This work explores the AH process for the treatment of HFC-134a, an HFC commonly used in large scale refrigeration and vehicle air conditioning. We demonstrate not only >90% destruction and defluorination, but also the conversion of the waste refrigerant to glycolate and fluoride salts, useful compounds for various industries. We also analyze the kinetics and propose a mechanism for the conversion, providing insight into optimization of continuous flow AH in scalable HFC upcycling.

title: Energy supply, institutional quality and environmental quality in West Africa
summary: The study investigated energy supply, institutional quality and environmental quality in West Africa. This study used secondary data collected from World Development Indicator and World Governance Indicator between 2015 and 2024. Different
content: The study investigated energy supply, institutional quality and environmental quality in West Africa. This study used secondary data collected from World Development Indicator and World Governance Indicator between 2015 and 2024. Different estimation methods were used in analyzing the obtained data. This study considered static panel, panel autoregressive distributed lag model (Panel ARDL), generalized method of moment and panel quantile regression. These set of estimation techniques were used to check the consistencies in the results obtained. The findings from the Panel ARDL model revealed that, energy supply has a positive statistically significant effect on environmental quality with a coefficient value of 0.0016 and at 5% significance level suggesting that, improved electricity which can resuscitate the production activity of a country which in turn improves the quality of the environment. Moreover, the study findings showed that the institutional quality and environmental quality were significantly positively correlated at 5% level of significance with coefficient value of 0.0567. The result also showed that gross domestic product has positive and significant relationship with environmental quality with coefficient value of 0.2311 and at 5% level of significance supporting the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis which assumes that economic indicators influence the level of the environment. The study revealed that energy supply and institutional quality are factors that affect the quality of environment in West Africa. Thus, the study recommends that the governments should develop and enact policies to support sustainable economic growth. Governments need to invest in green infrastructure, renewable energy and environmentally friendly technologies to enhance environmental quality while promoting economic growth.

title: Metamaterial perfect absorbers: Principles and applications
summary: Metamaterial perfect absorbers (MPAs) use subwavelength structural engineering to manipulate electromagnetic coupling, field distributions, and energy dissipation enabling strong absorption within the structures. Compared with conventional
content: Metamaterial perfect absorbers (MPAs) use subwavelength structural engineering to manipulate electromagnetic coupling, field distributions, and energy dissipation enabling strong absorption within the structures. Compared with conventional absorbers that rely primarily on intrinsic material loss, MPAs provide substantially greater flexibility in tailoring spectral, polarization, and angular responses. In this Tutorial, we provide a unified physical framework for understanding the operation and design of MPAs. Impedance matching, field localization, material dissipation, and critical coupling are discussed as interconnected aspects of the absorption process, clarifying how incident energy is coupled into the structure, redistributed, and ultimately dissipated within it. On this basis, representative MPA configurations are examined to illustrate the effects of geometry, material composition, electromagnetic coupling, and structural symmetry on the resulting absorption characteristics. These design principles are further connected to application-specific functions, including microwave scattering and interference suppression, tailored thermal emission, energy harvesting, photodetection, optical sensing, and structural coloration. Emphasis is placed on how engineered absorption and field localization are translated into useful energy-transfer, conversion, or signal-transduction pathways. Practical considerations associated with fabrication tolerance, dynamic tunability, system integration, and inverse design are finally discussed to bridge fundamental absorption physics and implementable absorber systems.

title: Planning and techno-economic assessment of renewable-energy infrastructure supporting animal welfare and precision livestock farming: A feedlot case study
summary: Animal welfare motivated this planning-level assessment of elevated photovoltaic (PV) canopies and four vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) for a nominal 400.00 m 2 feedlot pen near Lethbridge, Alberta. The structure was intended to support
content: Animal welfare motivated this planning-level assessment of elevated photovoltaic (PV) canopies and four vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) for a nominal 400.00 m 2 feedlot pen near Lethbridge, Alberta. The structure was intended to support shade, renewable electricity and precision-monitoring equipment. The quantitative case used 20.00 ft × 50.00 ft and 10.00 ft × 31.00 ft canopy plans, with calculated shade and reduced-order airflow indicators. The canopies had a combined plan area of 121.70 m 2 , or 30.43% of the reference pen area. The capped gross projected-shade area index averaged 31.18% over June–August at solar-hour indices 08:00–17:00 and 32.94% at indices 09:00, 15:00 and 17:00. These indices excluded shadow overlap and clipping to pen or bedding boundaries. The annual hybrid scenario total was 7.58 MW h, combining calculated PV output with a prescribed 0.94 MW h wind contribution. With an installed-cost allowance of CAD $75,500 and an assumed annual shade benefit of CAD $6000, the 25-year appraisal yielded NPV of CAD $907, IRR of 6.03% and simple payback of 12 years. The concept therefore shows that a feedlot can treat renewable-energy infrastructure as a multifunctional asset, improving thermal comfort for the animals, supporting precision livestock monitoring and producing electricity from the same structure.

title: Case‑based Reasoning for Fire Accident Analysis and Loss Prevention: Evidence from Greenhouse Facilities
summary: From an accident analysis perspective, greenhouse fires are low-frequency, high-uncertainty events where conventional statistical and physics-based models offer limited support. Greenhouse facilities face increasing fire risk due to electri
content: From an accident analysis perspective, greenhouse fires are low-frequency, high-uncertainty events where conventional statistical and physics-based models offer limited support. Greenhouse facilities face increasing fire risk due to electrification, combustible materials, and complex operations. To support systematic analysis of fire accidents in process-like production environments, this study proposes a Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) framework with a multidimensional case representation integrating environmental, facility, and incident attributes.Using 101 validated greenhouse fire cases (2005–2024), the entropy weight method determines indicator importance across 13 variables. Local similarity combines discrete and continuous approaches, while global aggregation retrieves highly similar cases. Results show that ignition source, personnel presence, and accident severity dominate similarity. Recurring vulnerabilities include electrical ignitions, lack of firefighting infrastructure, and noncompliant facility use. Reverse validation confirms framework stability and reproducibility.Rather than predicting fire dynamics, the framework enables structured learning from historical accidents under data constraints, transforming empirical data into actionable knowledge for accident prevention and loss mitigation.

title: Place-based governance and local public procurement: engaging small and medium enterprises in low carbon, inclusive transitions
summary: Public procurement is increasingly recognised as a pivotal yet underexploited mechanism for advancing local low carbon and inclusive transitions in the United Kingdom (UK). Recent reforms, such as the Procurement Act 2023, create new opport
content: Public procurement is increasingly recognised as a pivotal yet underexploited mechanism for advancing local low carbon and inclusive transitions in the United Kingdom (UK). Recent reforms, such as the Procurement Act 2023, create new opportunities for local authorities to embed environmental and social objectives into procurement processes, while enhancing the inclusion and participation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and voluntary, community and social enterprises (VCSEs). Given local governments’ responsibility for planning, transport, development and some infrastructure, local authorities are well positioned to shape place-based climate action, despite lacking a formal energy mandate. In the absence of statutory requirements, however, the extent to which carbon reporting, energy demand reduction and wider environmental criteria are incorporated into public procurement is largely discretionary, resulting in uneven expectations and support for SMEs and VCSEs across the UK. Drawing on qualitative interviews, this paper examines how the UK’s evolving local procurement practices can engage SMEs and VCSEs in these areas. Our findings reveal that public procurement is shifting from a compliance-focused function to a more relational governance mechanism that facilitates early dialogue, bidirectional learning, and potential new entry routes for SME engagement in decarbonisation. However, these developments remain uneven across place and are shaped by significant capacity disparities within both SMEs/VCSEs and local authorities alike. While procurement may encourage the normalisation of carbon reporting, our findings reveal that it also risks amplifying inequalities between regions and between SMEs with differing resources and levels of readiness. We argue that whilst public procurement is evolving, it has significant potential to support just and place-based low-carbon transitions; yet its effectiveness depends on addressing structural capacity gaps and ensuring more consistent and supportive landscapes.

title: U-Net Semantic Segmentation of Sentinel-2 Imagery for Landfill Detection and European Inventory Validation
summary: The waste sector accounted for 19 % of the global anthropogenic methane emissions in the previous decade, according to emission inventories. To evaluate these emission inventories, correctly located facilities are necessary. The quality of
content: The waste sector accounted for 19 % of the global anthropogenic methane emissions in the previous decade, according to emission inventories. To evaluate these emission inventories, correctly located facilities are necessary. The quality of these locations affects downstream applications, such as atmospheric transport modelling and satellite tasking for emissions monitoring. Despite this importance, comprehensive knowledge of locations of solid waste disposal (landfills) sites across the European continent remains limited. This study introduces a method to investigate the locations and spatial extent of landfills. To do so, we use a U-Net model, trained on Sentinel-2 satellite bands using a limited manually labelled dataset of European landfill and non-landfill sites in order to perform pixel-level segmentation and a corresponding image-level classification. When tested onto 873 methane-reporting landfill sites from the TNO-GHGco inventory, largely based on the European Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) reporting, our model had a 79 % accuracy in detecting correct landfill locations and a 92 % recall, indicating that few true landfill locations were missed. Notably, this study detected a mismatch between reported coordinates and imagery-detected extent for at least 51 landfills, here representing ~6 % of the data, suggesting that these erroneous landfill locations could be corrected in the official IEPR register. By correctly segmenting and confirming more than 638 landfills, 462 more than the traditional CORINE land cover map, this method offers an avenue for routine validation of reported landfill locations from space. However, false positive rates associated with misreporting were high in France, likely driven by red-edge similarities between landfills and croplands, though this effect may extend beyond this region. The model exhibits a moderate Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.25, due, in parts, to the number of false positives likely driven by spectral overlap and indicating the U-Net performs best at identifying correctly reported landfills. These findings underline the importance and challenge of refining landfill location data for European methane reporting and of routinely detecting both correctly reported locations and misreporting to minimise (future) satellite mistargeting. The U-Net algorithm we present fills a critical monitoring gap, paving the way for methane source attribution, activity monitoring and infrastructure location validation through satellites to support subsequent methane measurement campaigns.

title: SWOT flood data builds a foundation to assess the devastation or value of floods
summary: For all of human history, floods have caused widespread devastation, loss of life, and displacement of people. Floods are also vital for the survival of many different ecosystems in zones that rely upon the delivery of floodwaters as their
content: For all of human history, floods have caused widespread devastation, loss of life, and displacement of people. Floods are also vital for the survival of many different ecosystems in zones that rely upon the delivery of floodwaters as their primary water source. Devastation caused by extreme flood events is regularly reported but we rarely hear of the benefits brought by floods. Management of floodwaters, either to mitigate the ensuing devastation or to provide environmental benefits, requires knowledge of where and how much floodwater lies upstream. However, many river systems lack adequate gauging stations to provide such information. Here we outline a novel methodology utilising Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite data to obtain high accuracy estimates of floodwater depth and volume in two extreme floods. There were 3.89 km 3 of floodwaters in the devastating floods in the Punjab region of Pakistan over 3–5 September 2025, which displaced over two million people. This was only ~ 8% of the volume of the ~ 45 km 3 floodwaters in Southwest Queensland over 28 March to 1 April 2025 which led to the filling of Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre over 700 km away and generated a boom of wildlife that only results from extreme flood events. Data from the SWOT satellite provides a new capability to quantify floodwater depth and volume in places where observations are currently unavailable. This information is vital for understanding flood severity and the resulting destruction as well as for the environmental management of sensitive, flood-dependent ecosystems.

title: Environmental Stringency and International Trade
summary: This paper presents a novel analysis of the impact of environmental regulations aimed at reducing emissions in international trade in goods. Using a panel dataset of OECD and non‐OECD countries spanning from 2007 to 2018, we estimate a grav
content: This paper presents a novel analysis of the impact of environmental regulations aimed at reducing emissions in international trade in goods. Using a panel dataset of OECD and non‐OECD countries spanning from 2007 to 2018, we estimate a gravity model of trade using a Poisson pseudo‐maximum likelihood estimator with high‐dimensional fixed effects, controlling for potential confounding factors. Our empirical analysis integrates emissions intensity data with detailed international trade information at the industry level, considering both market‐based and non‐market‐based environmental policies. We estimate models for disaggregated trade flows, distinguishing between dirty and non‐dirty industries, and among heterogeneous groups of countries. Our findings indicate that stricter environmental regulations tend to increase imports of OECD countries from non‐OECD countries mostly in pollution‐intensive industries.

title: Tick narratives: Stakeholder perspectives on tick‐related risks and attributions in UK Agri‐Environmental Policies
summary: Research on the relationship between conservation and greening initiatives and tick‐borne disease risks in Europe is limited but growing. While several studies have investigated the socio‐ecological drivers of tick population dynamics and l
content: Research on the relationship between conservation and greening initiatives and tick‐borne disease risks in Europe is limited but growing. While several studies have investigated the socio‐ecological drivers of tick population dynamics and linked disease risks and the potential societal benefits of biodiversity and land management schemes separately, few have explored the associated disbenefits and trade‐offs, particularly from a socio‐epidemiological perspective.
