This issue becomes particularly acute in the context of increasingly complex economic ties, growing volumes of processed information, and stricter requirements from external users for the quality of financial data, which determines a heightened interest in building reliable internal control systems. Materials and Methods. The methodological framework of the study comprised methods of systems, process, and comparative analysis, as well as scientific abstraction, generalization, and synthesis. title: From frontplane to backplane: materials, devices, and circuits for active-matrix light-emitting displays
summary: Active-matrix (AM) light-emitting displays rely on the coordinated operation of frontplanes, backplanes, and pixel-driving circuits. This review provides an integrated perspective on the materials, devices, and circuits that underpin AM dis
content: Active-matrix (AM) light-emitting displays rely on the coordinated operation of frontplanes, backplanes, and pixel-driving circuits. This review provides an integrated perspective on the materials, devices, and circuits that underpin AM displays, focusing on the transition from individual device performance to system-level operation. Self-emissive frontplane technologies, including organic light-emitting diodes, quantum-dot light-emitting diodes, and micro-light-emitting diodes, are reviewed in terms of efficiency, operational stability, and pixelation. Backplane transistors based on Si, metal oxides, one- and two-dimensional semiconductors, organic semiconductors, and metal-halide perovskite are subsequently reviewed through representative device, circuit, and display demonstrations, highlighting their electrical characteristics, processing requirements, application-specific advantages, and remaining limitations. We then connect frontplane and backplane characteristics through pixel-circuit architectures, ranging from fundamental transistor–light-emitting-diode coupling to circuits incorporating switching, storage, and compensation functions. Representative demonstrations further illustrate the progression from individual transistor–emitter operation toward array-level AM displays. Finally, challenges associated with electrical matching, device-to-device fabrication compatibility, and pixel uniformity are discussed, highlighting the need for co-design of frontplanes, backplanes, pixel circuits, and fabrication processes toward scalable, high-resolution, and reliable next-generation AM displays.

title: Surface‐State Engineered Copper Phosphide as a Durable Peroxymonosulfate Activator for Wastewater Treatment: From Activity Enhancement to Scale‐Up Demonstration
summary: Copper phosphide (CuxP), composed of earth-abundant elements, has been explored for advanced oxidation processes but suffers from ion leaching in acidic media and negligible activity under neutral and alkaline conditions, limiting its pract
content: Copper phosphide (CuxP), composed of earth-abundant elements, has been explored for advanced oxidation processes but suffers from ion leaching in acidic media and negligible activity under neutral and alkaline conditions, limiting its practical applicability. Here, we present a surface-state engineering strategy that systematically tunes the overlayer thickness and oxygen vacancy (OV) density of CuxP through controlled Ar pretreatment. The optimized catalyst (1 h pretreatment) achieved ∼80% phenol removal within 10 min and ∼30% total organic carbon abatement, while maintaining high activity and stability across a wide pH range. This enhanced performance is attributed to the interplay between a moderately thin overlayer (∼1.4 nm) and an optimal OV concentration. Density functional theory calculations indicated that surface oxygen deficiency influences peroxymonosulfate (PMS) adsorption and activation energetics, consistent with observed catalytic trends. Mechanistic studies confirmed sulfate radicals (SO4•-) as the dominant reactive species. A continuous-flow system with CuxP-based filters sustained ∼85% phenol removal over 300 min of continuous operation, while a scaled-up configuration (25 cm2 × 4 substrates) achieved ∼93% phenol removal after 120 min. These results demonstrate the preliminary practical applicability and scale-up potential of the optimized catalyst in wastewater treatment and highlight the importance of controlled surface-state engineering in developing efficient and durable PMS-activated systems.

title: Smart Integrated Hybrid Circular Treatment System for Sustainable Industrial Wastewater Management and Water Reuse
summary: Rapid industrialization has increased industrial wastewater generation. Such wastewater contains toxic organic compounds, heavy metals, suspended solids, and other persistent pollutants. If these substances are not properly removed, they ca
content: Rapid industrialization has increased industrial wastewater generation. Such wastewater contains toxic organic compounds, heavy metals, suspended solids, and other persistent pollutants. If these substances are not properly removed, they can affect the environment and public health. Conventional treatment methods may consume large amounts of energy and water. They may also generate considerable sludge and provide limited water recovery. This study proposes an Integrated Hybrid Circular Treatment System (IHCTS) for industrial wastewater treatment and reuse. This study aims to develop and evaluate an Integrated Hybrid Circular Treatment System (IHCTS) for sustainable industrial wastewater treatment and water reuse. The proposed system integrates advanced oxidation, biological treatment, membrane filtration, and adsorption-based polishing to improve pollutant removal and treated-water recovery. It also incorporates data-driven monitoring and machine learning-based process optimization to support operational stability, reduce membrane fouling, and improve energy efficiency. The system combines advanced oxidation, biological treatment, membrane filtration, and adsorption-based polishing. A data-driven monitoring layer is included to examine wastewater characteristics, predict membrane fouling, and adjust operating conditions. Machine learning is used to assist process control and select appropriate treatment conditions. The proposed system achieved COD, BOD, TSS, and heavy metal removal efficiencies of 96.8%, 95.1%, 97.2%, and 94.8%, respectively. The water recovery ratio reached 93.6%. The membrane fouling index was 0.21, while the specific energy consumption was 1.86 kWh/m³. These results show that the IHCTS can improve pollutant removal and water recovery while reducing membrane fouling and energy consumption. The system therefore provides an approach for industrial wastewater treatment and reuse.

title: Is Spare Capacity Worth Its Embodied Carbon? Distributionally Robust Capacity Planning for Carbon-Aware Cloud Data Centers under Grid-Decarbonization Uncertainty
source: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
summary: Carbon-aware scheduling shifts flexible work into hours when the grid is cleaner, but it can only do so if servers are idle at those hours, so most evaluations implicitly assume that spare capacity exists. Spare servers are not free: their
content: Carbon-aware scheduling shifts flexible work into hours when the grid is cleaner, but it can only do so if servers are idle at those hours, so most evaluations implicitly assume that spare capacity exists. Spare servers are not free: their manufacturing (embodied) emissions are incurred at purchase, while the operational savings they enable accrue over a lifetime whose length is uncertain, against grids whose future carbon intensity is uncertain too. We formulate the decision of how much spare capacity to build, and where, as a two-stage distributionally robust program. The first stage chooses slack in each region and pays its embodied carbon; the second stage, for every operating year and decarbonization pathway, solves a linear program that shifts flexible load into low-carbon hours subject to capacity and idle power. Ambiguity over pathways and server lifetimes is a total-variation ball around nominal scenario weights, and the inner supremum is dualized so that the whole problem is one linear program. We show that each scenario’s incremental carbon is convex in the slack vector and give a break-even condition comparing embodied intensity with the worst-case expected marginal operational savings. On a four-region, 100 MW case study, the 1.7× load provisioning assumed in prior carbon-aware scheduling studies adds 68 kt CO₂e over the hardware lifetime, because the embodied carbon of 44.5 MW of extra servers is never recovered. The stochastic optimum builds 4.7 MW of slack in the solar-rich region only, with an expected lifetime saving of just 0.6 kt, and the robust optimum builds none once the ambiguity radius reaches 0.25. Spare capacity pays robustly only for low-embodied hardware (≤ 1,000 t CO₂e per MW), which points to server reuse and burst capacity as the carbon-efficient source of scheduling slack.

title: Plant Developmental Responses to Plasma-Synthesized Nitrate: Concentration- and pH-Dependent Effects on Root Architecture, Reproduction and Drought Tolerance
summary: Sustainable nitrogen fertilization requires alternatives that can reduce dependence on centralized, fossil-intensive ammonia production while providing nitrogen in a biologically effective form with reduced environmental impact. Although re
content: Sustainable nitrogen fertilization requires alternatives that can reduce dependence on centralized, fossil-intensive ammonia production while providing nitrogen in a biologically effective form with reduced environmental impact. Although research on nitrogen fertilizer synthesis through thermal and non-thermal plasma routes is advancing rapidly, a comprehensive understanding of plant responses to plasma-derived fertilizers remains somewhat elusive, given the limited evidence available to date. Here, we evaluated the plant response to nitrate synthesized by an atmospheric-pressure catalytic thermal-plasma system using Cicer arietinum (chickpea) as a model crop. Soil and hydroponic experiments were combined to investigate nitrate- and pH-dependent responses from root development to reproduction and drought tolerance. Nitrate availability produced pronounced, reproducible, non-monotonic changes in root architecture and root–shoot coordination. Nitrogen limitation promoted a remarkably extensive exploratory root phenotype, whereas intermediate nitrate availability supported comparatively coordinated root and shoot development. Increasing nitrate beyond this range progressively altered root organization and restricted root-system expansion. Importantly, vegetative vigour and reproductive progression were not equivalent: under the experimental conditions, plants supplied with 35 ppm nitrate exhibited the most advanced transition toward fruit initiation, whereas higher nitrate concentrations exhibited delayed reproductive development. Root anatomical observations further revealed nitrate-associated structural differentiation. pH additionally modulated nitrate-associated root development and drought response substantially. Collectively, these findings identify a concentration- and pH-dependent developmental window for plasma-synthesized nitrate and provide a multi-scale framework linking fertilizer chemistry with root architecture, biochemical state, reproductive development and stress response.

content: Введение. Современный аграрный сектор подвержен воздействию целого комплекса рисков, влияние которых на сельскохозяйственное производство различно. title: Socio-technical transitions in rural electrification: a comparative analysis of government-led and private-led microgrid systems in Thailand
summary: Expanding reliable electricity access to remote communities remains challenging, often necessitating decentralized solutions like microgrids over costly grid extensions. While microgrid research heavily emphasizes technical feasibility and
content: Expanding reliable electricity access to remote communities remains challenging, often necessitating decentralized solutions like microgrids over costly grid extensions. While microgrid research heavily emphasizes technical feasibility and cost-effectiveness, the socio-technical conditions shaping long-term system viability remain underexamined. In Thailand, remote communities—particularly in mountainous and island areas—continue to rely on decentralized energy solutions implemented through different approaches; however, there is limited understanding of how implementation approaches influence the outcomes and long-term sustainability of a microgrid system. To address this gap, this study presents a qualitative comparative analysis of two rural microgrid cases in Thailand: a government-led system (System A) and a private-led system (System B). By examining social dynamics, institutional factors, and implementation models through a socio-technical lens, this research provides vital insights into energy transition dynamics. Findings indicate the government-led system benefits from robust initial public investment and policy support, yet faces long-term operational hurdles, including limited revenue generation, constrained technical capacity, and administrative turnover. Conversely, the private-community model demonstrates greater operational continuity, driven by adaptive financial arrangements, sustained maintenance commitments, and participatory governance involving residents in system management—though it also necessitates dedicated budgets to foster community engagement through events. Notably, both systems remain vulnerable to users’ expectations of future grid arrival. Ultimately, this comparison highlights how specific implementation arrangements dictate the sustainability of decentralized energy systems, providing valuable insights to inform broader rural electrification strategies in geographically constrained communities worldwide.

title: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
summary: Oxygen minimum zones, subsurface regions of the ocean severely depleted in dissolved oxygen, today extend over more than 30 million km 2. Although these areas are expected to expand in the future in response to warming, the magnitude of deo
content: Oxygen minimum zones, subsurface regions of the ocean severely depleted in dissolved oxygen, today extend over more than 30 million km 2. Although these areas are expected to expand in the future in response to warming, the magnitude of deoxygenation is poorly constrained. Here we present a quantitative spatio-temporal reconstruction of oxygen minimum zone changes in the subarctic and eastern North Pacific over the last 55 thousand years based on 2,569 individual foraminiferal assemblage measurements from 11 sedimentary cores. We find that the extent of oxygen minimum zones in the eastern North Pacific expanded in response to warming during Dansgaard–Oeschger events during the last glacial period and through the last deglaciation. However, re-oxygenation events and oxygen minimum zone contraction also occurred in the last glacial period when overturning circulation weakened in the North Atlantic during Heinrich events. Our findings, supported by Earth system simulations confirming a strong coupling between millennial-scale changes in North Atlantic circulation and North Pacific oxygen minimum zone extent, imply a complex future response of the oxygen minimum zone extent, with global circulation changes potentially mitigating the direct effects of warming.

title: Государственная финансовая поддержка формирования инновационного потенциала агропромышленного комплекса России

content: Введение. Создание условий для повышения технико-технологического уровня аграрного производства на основе внедрения передовых инновационных технологий невозможно без отлаженного механизма финансового содействия и системы мер, выражающихся в программных мероприятиях по государственной поддержке, которая опирается на внедрение передовых технологий в селекции, генетике, цифровизации. Материалы и методы. Информационно-аналитической основой исследования выступили труды российских ученых по проблемам инновационного развития сельского хозяйства, нормативно-правовые акты в сфере научно-технологического развития аграрного сектора, данные Росстата и Министерства сельского хозяйства России. В работе использовались общенаучные методы и приемы, среди которых системный подход, методы анализа и синтеза, логического обобщения и монографический метод. Результаты исследования. С помощью льготного инвестиционного кредитования со стороны государства, направленного на создание элитного семеноводства, модернизацию селекционно-семеноводческих центров и другие мероприятия, обеспечение сельхозтоваропроизводителей семенами отечественной селекции достигло в 2024 году 67,6%. Обсуждение и заключения. content: Введение. Переориентация экспортных потоков российского АПК на фоне геополитической напряжѐнности и санкционных ограничений требует пересмотра сложившихся приоритетов. Традиционные рынки сбыта частично утрачены, новые – требуют адаптации логистики, ценовых и качественных параметров поставок. В этих условиях обоснование трѐх ключевых направлений – зернового, масложирового и мясного экспорта – становится не просто аналитической, а стратегической задачей. Материалы и методы. Использованы методы динамического анализа, балансового моделирования и сравнительной оценки географической структуры экспортных потоков. Результаты. Under these conditions, substantiating three key directions – grain, oil and fat, and meat exports – becomes not merely an analytical but a strategic task. Materials and Methods. title: Squaraine‐Based Building Blocks for Functional Porous Materials
summary: Squaric acid (SA) and its derivative squaraine (SQ)—collectively featuring a unique four‐membered ring scaffold with distinctive electronic configuration, aromaticity, and rich chemical reactivity—have emerged as a compelling class of build
content: Squaric acid (SA) and its derivative squaraine (SQ)—collectively featuring a unique four‐membered ring scaffold with distinctive electronic configuration, aromaticity, and rich chemical reactivity—have emerged as a compelling class of building blocks for functional porous materials. By integrating SA/SQ units into the backbone of porous architectures, the exceptional electronic and optical properties inherent to these moieties are synergistically combined with the advantages of porous frameworks, such as high specific surface areas, tunable pore structures, and well‐defined channels. This review systematically summarizes recent research progress on SA‐ and SQ‐based porous materials across several key application fields, including gas adsorption and separation, catalysis, battery energy storage, and fluorescence sensing, among others. Finally, the key challenges currently facing SA/SQ‐based porous materials are outlined, alongside prospects for future development.

title: Semi‐Digital and Conventional Protocols for Masking Orthodontic Appliances and Fabricating Customized Mouthguards: A Step‐by‐Step Clinical Guide
summary: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Custom-fit ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) mouthguards are recommended for athletes participating in contact sports, particularly those undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. This clinical guide describes step-by-step co
content: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Custom-fit ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) mouthguards are recommended for athletes participating in contact sports, particularly those undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. This clinical guide describes step-by-step conventional and semi-digital workflows for fabricating custom-fit EVA mouthguards in orthodontic patients, including a patient-specific virtual block-out approach for orthodontic components. TECHNIQUE: The conventional workflow involves bracket block-out with utility wax, alginate impression, and fabrication of a dental stone model. The semi-digital workflow integrates intraoral scanning, CAD-based virtual planning of patient-specific orthodontic relief, and fabrication of a 3D-printed resin model for subsequent thermoforming. The clinical application of both workflows is illustrated in an athlete undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. RESULTS: Both workflows provided clinically satisfactory adaptation and retention. The semi-digital workflow eliminated the need for intraoral wax block-out and allowed orthodontic relief to be planned virtually, simplifying selected clinical and laboratory procedures while facilitating control of the internal geometry of the mouthguard. CONCLUSIONS: The semi-digital workflow represents a clinically applicable and reproducible alternative for fabricating custom-fit EVA mouthguards in patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. Virtual planning of orthodontic relief may facilitate individualized adaptation of the mouthguard to the orthodontic appliances, although clinical assessment and periodic reassessment remain essential throughout active orthodontic treatment.

title: Cognitive Biases as Obstacles to Sustainable Behavior or Untapped Potential for the Greater Good: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Cognitive biases often influence people’s behavior, actions, and decisions. While these biases may lead to closed-mindedness and resistance to change, they may also encourage pro-environmental behavior. Although research on cognitive biases
content: Cognitive biases often influence people’s behavior, actions, and decisions. While these biases may lead to closed-mindedness and resistance to change, they may also encourage pro-environmental behavior. Although research on cognitive biases and sustainability has increased in recent years, the evidence remains fragmented across sustainability domains, limiting a comprehensive understanding of their influence on sustainable decision-making. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic literature review following the PRISMA methodology to synthesize existing research on cognitive biases influencing decision-making in sustainability contexts. This study investigates how cognitive biases shape sustainable decision-making, whether they act as obstacles or can also serve as positive leverage for achieving sustainability goals and facilitating sustainability transitions. The findings reveal 58 cognitive biases reported across 41 studies that influence sustainable behavior and decision-making across multiple sustainability domains. While some biases contribute to unsustainable habits, others can be leveraged to encourage more sustainable actions and support the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). For policymakers and municipal waste authorities, the study provides important targets for intervention. For sustainability practitioners, the four-module framework shows how different biases can be addressed at different stages of decision-making. For researchers, the review highlights important research gaps and provides a basis for future interdisciplinary studies.

title: Targeting the KRAS4B / PDE6δ complex reveals differential lipid metabolic responses in pancreatic cancer cells
summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains among the most lethal malignancies, with a global 5‐year survival rate of less than 10%. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer and provides tumor cells with multiple advantages, incl
content: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains among the most lethal malignancies, with a global 5‐year survival rate of less than 10%. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer and provides tumor cells with multiple advantages, including metabolic plasticity and resistance to therapy. Together with the significant toxicity associated with current pharmacological treatments, these features highlight the need for new molecules with improved efficacy–toxicity profiles. In this study, mass spectrometry–based untargeted metabolomics and cheminformatics analyses were performed to profile early metabolic changes in wild‐type and mutant KRAS pancreatic cancer cell models treated with the KRAS4B–PDE6δ complex stabilizers C14 and P8 and the indirect KRAS inhibitor deltarasin. All compounds were tested at their half‐maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50) after one hour of treatment. Overall, compared with C14, deltarasin and P8 modulated the greatest number of metabolites across cell lines. Stratification of dysregulated metabolites by lipid, nitrogen, and carbohydrate metabolism revealed compound‐specific and cell‐line‐dependent differences. More metabolites were dysregulated in cancerous cells than in noncancerous cells for all the compounds, with P8 preferentially affecting nitrogen metabolism and deltarasin lipid metabolism. Focused lipid enrichment analysis revealed that glycerophospholipid and cholesterol metabolism were primarily modulated by all compounds; notably, P8 additionally altered various peptide metabolites. Taken together, our findings suggest that the compounds C14, P8, and deltarasin might induce alterations in cell membranes, thus mediating their antineoplastic effects in PDAC.

title: Tuning Alkyl Chain Length of Sulfonate Additives to Balance Solvation/Interfacial Chemistry for Highly Stable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
summary: Aqueous zinc batteries are promising for grid‐scale energy storage but are plagued by sluggish desolvation kinetics and water‐induced parasitic reactions. However, additives with short chains are adept at solvation tuning but offer limited
content: Aqueous zinc batteries are promising for grid‐scale energy storage but are plagued by sluggish desolvation kinetics and water‐induced parasitic reactions. However, additives with short chains are adept at solvation tuning but offer limited interfacial protection, whereas those with long chains offer hydrophobic protection but hinder ion transport. Herein, we systematically vary the alkyl chain length of sodium sulfonates to elucidate how chain length balances Zn 2+ solvation and interfacial chemistry. The medium‐chain sodium butanesulfonate (C4) additive overcomes the limitations of additives with short and long alkyl chains. C4 weakly coordinates with Zn 2+ to modulate solvation, and its sufficient interfacial adsorption constructs a water‐depleted electric double layer to suppress side reactions. Finally, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell with the designed electrolyte achieves an ultra‐long cycle life of 3500 h under conditions of 0.5 mA cm– 2 /0.25 mAh cm −2, and the Zn||Cu asymmetric cell achieves a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 1800 cycles (3 mA cm −2 /1 mAh cm −2). This work indicates that alkyl chain length is a key parameter governing solvation and interfacial chemistry regulation, offering guidance for electrolyte design in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries.

title: Recovery Dynamics in Soft‐Lattice Perovskite Solar Cells Compared with Space‐Grade GaAs Solar Cells under Proton Irradiation
summary: Metal‐halide perovskites (MHPs) exhibit defect healing under proton irradiation in contrast to the irreversible degradation observed in conventional III‐V solar cells. Here, we report a side‐by‐side comparison of proton‐induced damage and s
content: Metal‐halide perovskites (MHPs) exhibit defect healing under proton irradiation in contrast to the irreversible degradation observed in conventional III‐V solar cells. Here, we report a side‐by‐side comparison of proton‐induced damage and subsequent recovery in mixed‐cation perovskite solar cells (PSCs) versus industry‐standard space‐grade gallium arsenide (GaAs) devices. PSCs were exposed to space‐relevant 0.075 MeV and 1.0 MeV protons at equivalent displacement doses ∼9 × 10 12 MeV/g, with representative devices retaining 50% and 77% of initial power conversion efficiency (PCE), respectively, when first tested post‐irradiation. Notably, 1.0 MeV irradiation suppressed the structural and optical signatures of PbI 2, consistent with enhanced ionization‐driven defect repair. Over 24 h of room‐temperature dark storage, both devices recovered to ∼90% of pre‐irradiation PCE, likely owing to slow lattice reconfiguration, interface re‐passivation, and hole transporter re‐doping. By contrast, comparable‐thickness GaAs devices subjected to approximately equivalent displacement doses retained only ∼22% and ∼17% of their initial PCE under corresponding 0.075 and 1.0 MeV conditions without spontaneous recovery. These results demonstrate that PSCs are dynamic architectures possessing multi‐pathway radiation tolerance mechanism, whereas rigid, covalent GaAs lattices lack room‐temperature defect recovery. This comparative study underscores the unique promise of engineered lattice softness for space photovoltaics and other radiation‐intensive applications.

title: Solid‐State Aluminum‐Ion Batteries: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Perspective for Multivalent Energy Storage
source: Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews Energy and Environment
summary: Solid‐state aluminum‐ion batteries (SS‐AIBs) are promising future energy storage technology for the abundance of aluminum, its low cost, and high volumetric density. Traditional AIBs are limited by corrosive electrolytes, slow multivalent i
content: Solid‐state aluminum‐ion batteries (SS‐AIBs) are promising future energy storage technology for the abundance of aluminum, its low cost, and high volumetric density. Traditional AIBs are limited by corrosive electrolytes, slow multivalent ion transport, and non‐stable electrode‐electrolyte interfaces. The development of SS‐AIBs provides a disruptive solution to these issues as it will allow the combination of intrinsic safety, design flexibility, and thermal stability of solid electrolytes with the positive redox chemistry of aluminum. This review will bring together the growing literature on SS‐AIBs, including inorganic ceramics, polymer‐based, and hybrid electrolytes, and will clarify mechanistic insights into Al 3+ transport across the solid matrix and interfaces. The strategies to suppress dendrite growth, increase ionic conductivity, and stabilize electrode architecture are evaluated based on the knowledge in solid‐state batteries. Techno‐economic and sustainability studies show the potential of SS‐AIBs in grid storage and flexible electronics with high safety and cost‐efficiency. This could be achieved by combining the progress in solid‐state ionics modeling of computations and interface engineering, to establish SS‐AIBs as a feasible class of next‐generation lithium‐free storage technology. We also outline the key challenges and research opportunities that are essential for transitioning SS‐AIBs from laboratory‐scale prototypes to scalable, commercially relevant multivalent energy storage systems.

title: Biophysics and Biochemistry of Superhydrophobic Coatings for Microbiological Hygiene on Food and Food-Contact Surfaces: Mechanisms, Coating Architectures, and Translational Outlook
summary: Microbial contamination, cross-contamination, and biofilm formation on abiotic food-contact equipment and biotic food surfaces remain leading causes of foodborne illness and post-harvest food loss worldwide. Conventional chemical sanitation
content: Microbial contamination, cross-contamination, and biofilm formation on abiotic food-contact equipment and biotic food surfaces remain leading causes of foodborne illness and post-harvest food loss worldwide. Conventional chemical sanitation and thermal clean-in-place (CIP) protocols face persistent limitations once bacterial cells anchor within surface microcrevices and secrete protective extracellular polymeric substances (EPS). Superhydrophobic coatings—engineered through the synergy of low surface energy and hierarchical micro/nanoscale roughness to stabilize a Cassie–Baxter composite solid–liquid–vapor interface—offer a fundamentally distinct, physics-driven line of defense. Rather than relying solely on chemical eradication, these surfaces maintain an interfacial air cushion (plastron) that restricts true solid–liquid contact area, elevates free-energy barriers to bacterial adhesion, attenuates attractive Lifshitz–van der Waals interactions, amplifies hydrodynamic slip, and promotes low-shear self-cleaning. This review synthesizes the multiscale biophysics governing bacterial repellency on superhydrophobic interfaces in food systems, integrating recent post-2024 advances in wetting thermodynamics, gas-permeability-controlled plastron dissolution kinetics, non-mean-field interfacial electrostatics, turbulent slip nonlocality, flow-coupled active bacterial hydrodynamics, droplet impact kinematics, and lipid–membrane biophysics. Particular attention is given to how amphiphilic food lipids, proteins, and surfactants adsorb onto the air–water meniscus, alter interfacial dilatational rheology and line tension, and dictate the finite Cassie-to-Wenzel transition time beyond static water contact angles. We establish a mechanistic taxonomy of five major coating design architectures—nanotextured and nanodiamond-reinforced metals, silica aerogels and optically transparent topographies, polymeric food-contact and post-PFAS cellulosic substrates, edible wax/triterpenoid/lipid-derived produce coatings, and dual-functional or stimuli-responsive "defense-in-depth" systems—benchmarked against slippery liquid-infused and covalently attached liquid-like surfaces. Finally, we critically evaluate translational barriers—including mechanical abrasion, CIP durability, cold-chain micro-condensation, splash-mediated aerosol cross-contamination, nanoparticle and micro/nanoplastic migration, and landmark 2025–2026 regulatory mandates (US FDA PFAS phase-outs and EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation [PPWR] fluorine limits)—and outline a strategic roadmap toward durable, fluorine-free, AI-designed hygienic biointerfaces.

title: Hydrated L‑Carnitine‑Sulfamide Deep Eutectic Electrolyte Enabling Stable Ni Deposition and Reversible Four‑Electron Iodine Redox in Ni‑I 2 Batteries
summary: Novel aqueous nickel‑iodine batteries show great potential due to the abundant reserves of iodine and the low‐dendrite nature of nickel. Nevertheless, their practical performance is severely limited by sluggish iodine conversion kinetics, p
content: Novel aqueous nickel‑iodine batteries show great potential due to the abundant reserves of iodine and the low‐dendrite nature of nickel. Nevertheless, their practical performance is severely limited by sluggish iodine conversion kinetics, polyiodide shuttling, severe hydrolysis of I +, strong electrostatic shielding of Ni 2+, as well as persistent corrosion and passivation. Herein, a hydrated eutectic electrolyte consisting of L‑carnitine, sulfamide, Ni(OTf) 2 and H 2 O is rationally designed to reconstruct the electrolyte hydrogen‑bonding environment and Ni 2+ solvation structure, synergistically boosting interfacial ion transport at both electrodes. L‑carnitine and sulfamide regulate the ordered hydrogen‑bond network of H 2 O and rearrange Ni 2+ solvation shells. The zwitterionic L‑carnitine forms a hydrophobic hybrid interphase on the anode, homogenizing Ni 2+ deposition and inhibiting corrosion and passivation. At the cathode, abundant functional groups (COO −, OH, S═O) strongly interact with polyiodides, alleviating the shuttle effect and accelerating four‑electron reversible I − /I 0 /I + conversion. Therefore, the Ni||Ni cell stably operates for over 4000 h (0.2/1/5 mA cm −2), and the Ni‐I 2 battery delivers a superior capacity of 322 mA h g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 with stable cycling of 1500 cycles (0.3 A g −1). Finally, the conceptual pouch cell exhibits 100 cycles and supplies power to the model small fan.

title: Hydrated Proton‐Lattice Synergy‐Mediated Super‐Nernstian pH Sensing in H 0.95 MoO 3 for Translational Biofluid Monitoring and In Vivo Pathological Tracking
summary: Maintaining pH homeostasis in biofluids is critical for normal physiological function, with even minor deviations (±0.1–0.2 pH units) serving as early biomarkers for various pathologies such as diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and wound in
content: Maintaining pH homeostasis in biofluids is critical for normal physiological function, with even minor deviations (±0.1–0.2 pH units) serving as early biomarkers for various pathologies such as diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and wound infection. Current clinical pH monitoring relies heavily on ex vivo sampling and benchtop analysis, suffering from sampling randomness, analytical delays, and the inability to capture dynamic physiological pH fluctuations. Here, we develop a flexible biosensing system based on metalloid H 0.95 MoO 3 nanobelts fabricated by modulating selective hydronium intercalation. This system resolves the long‐standing trade‐off between full physiological pH range coverage (1–11) and high precision in narrow sub‐ranges, achieving super‐Nernstian sensitivity (66.69 mV/pH), rapid response (3–4 s), and robust anti‐interference capability against biological interferents. Moreover, it also features tunable lifespan via tailored encapsulation to adapt to diverse clinical scenarios and inherent biocompatibility for seamless in vitro/in vivo deployment. Multi‐scale characterizations and theoretical analyses clarify the underlying proton–electron coupled sensing mechanism, supported by a surface site‐binding model explaining the super‐Nernstian sensitivity. Integrated with wireless Bluetooth transmission, the system enables in situ real‐time and high‐precision monitoring of saliva, sweat, diabetic wound exudate, gastric fluid, and interstitial fluid pH, providing a versatile tool for advancing precision medicine and smart diagnostics.

title: Annual performance optimization of a solar-integrated gas turbine cycle: A comparative assessment of PINN vs. classical solvers and multi-objective analysis
summary: Attaining the best performance of any proposed system is the main aim of academics, researchers, and interested companies. This can be attained by carrying out many comprehensive studies and experimental works that aim to maximize the depen
content: Attaining the best performance of any proposed system is the main aim of academics, researchers, and interested companies. This can be attained by carrying out many comprehensive studies and experimental works that aim to maximize the dependence on sustainable energy sources, integrate the up-to-date technologies, and minimize all other energy sources. This study presents a comprehensive annual performance and economic optimization of a solar-integrated gas turbine cycle tailored for Mosul, Iraq, where an average DNI of 607 W/m² offers significant solar potential. A thermodynamic model with variable-temperature properties is developed and validated against the literature. The NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm was employed to find the optimal design that balances three conflicting objectives: maximizing thermal efficiency, minimizing CO₂ emissions, and minimizing Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) to analyse system performance. A comparative analysis showed that Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer no computational or accuracy advantage over a classic Runge-Kutta solver for the 1D heat exchanger ODE, and thus the latter is adopted. The results show that the optimized hybrid system achieves a thermal efficiency of 45.10%, comparable to 44.73% for the conventional system, with a 6.45% reduction in CO₂ emissions to 414.1 kg/MWh, and a 1.36% reduction in LCOE from 37.41 to 36.91 $/MWh. The PINN model achieved high accuracy with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.1341 K. A Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis was performed to quantify uncertainty in the key performance indicators. Sensitivity analyses were also conducted to evaluate the impact of key parameters on system performance.

title: Genomic burden and selection shape genetic immune escape across cancers
summary: Immune evasion can arise from genetic alterations and reversible regulatory programs, but how these mechanisms jointly shape tumor states across cancers remains unclear. Here, we integrated 11 genomic and 39 bulk-derived non-genomic escape
content: Immune evasion can arise from genetic alterations and reversible regulatory programs, but how these mechanisms jointly shape tumor states across cancers remains unclear. Here, we integrated 11 genomic and 39 bulk-derived non-genomic escape features across 10,616 tumors from The Cancer Genome Atlas to construct a pan-cancer immune escape atlas. Overall, 90% of tumors harbor at least one escape feature. Genomic escape features were linked more consistently to tumor mutational and copy-number burdens than to immune infiltration and showed clonal enrichment and evidence of positive selection. Mutations in antigen presentation machinery and mutations in the interferon γ (IFN-γ) signaling pathway were associated with attenuated immunoediting. Genomic escape subgrouping further stratified evolutionary and immunological phenotypes and outcomes in immune checkpoint blockade cohorts, whereas non-genomic subgrouping showed weaker outcome stratification. These findings position genomic escape as a coordinated evolutionary shift and provide a framework for context-specific tumor phenotyping.

title: A Review on Climate-Resilient Rainwater Management Systems for Island Agro-Ecosystems: Insights from the Andaman Islands
summary: The Andaman archipelago presents an acute hydro-climatic conundrum. Annual rainfall is quite high(>3,000 mm) throughout a long monsoon season, but there are severe agricultural droughts andmoisture deficiencies between the months of January
content: The Andaman archipelago presents an acute hydro-climatic conundrum. Annual rainfall is quite high(>3,000 mm) throughout a long monsoon season, but there are severe agricultural droughts andmoisture deficiencies between the months of January to April. The islands’ steep and undulatingtopography, small coastal valleys and tight geological strata dominated by shattered Andaman Flyschand ophiolite suites severely constrain regional groundwater storage, with more than 80% ofprecipitation emptying fast into the sea as runoff. Therefore, the regional agriculture has been limitedto a monsoon-driven single-crop paddy cycle followed by dry season fallow and root zone salinizationin low lying coastal regions. Pioneering research conducted by the Central Agricultural ResearchInstitute (ICAR-CARI, now CIARI) in Port Blair has addressed this paradox through landconfiguration engineering, micro-catchment harvesting, and integrated farming architectures. Thispaper analyzes the operational hydraulics, soil salinity abatement, and agronomic productivity ofCARI-developed technologies. The investigation examines both in-situ and ex-situ conservationstrategies suitable for the islands' vulnerable ecosystems. The Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) systemof the low-lying seasonally inundated valley floors is a dual-purpose intervention. Raised beds providefree drainage for high value vegetable crops during torrential rains, while depressed furrows act aswater reservoirs for integrated paddy-cum-pisciculture and subsequent dry season irrigation. In themid-slope and highland plantation areas, the ex-situ rainwater gathering using dugout farm ponds andcheck dams traps the crucial surface runoff. Critical civil engineering countermeasures such asinstallation of UV stabilized 500-micron high density polyethylene (HDPE) liners to arrest heavylateral seepage through fractured subgrades and hydraulic design of stone pitched emergencyspillways capable of discharging cyclonic cloud bursts are studied. Furthermore, the use of capturedrainwater in gravity fed low head drip and micro-sprinkler systems prevents secondary capillarysalinity in the root zone, maintains high-value spices and vegetables during the dry period andincreases cropping intensity to more than 200%. The results offer a comprehensive site-specific waterinfrastructure pathway for improving agrarian climate resilience and local food self-sufficiency in theAndaman Islands.

title: Environmental Significance of Plants and Their Role in Sustainable Development: A Research Review of Ecosystem Services, Urban Greening and Environmental Conservation in India
summary: Plants are fundamental components of natural ecosystems and play a significant role inmaintaining ecological balance, environmental stability, and sustainable development. Theycontribute to atmospheric regulation, carbon sequestration, oxyg
content: Plants are fundamental components of natural ecosystems and play a significant role inmaintaining ecological balance, environmental stability, and sustainable development. Theycontribute to atmospheric regulation, carbon sequestration, oxygen production, soil conservation,water-cycle regulation, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation. However, rapidurbanization, industrialization, population growth, deforestation, and increasing anthropogenicactivities have intensified environmental problems, including air, water, and noise pollution, habitatdegradation, and the depletion of natural vegetation. These challenges have created an urgent need foreffective plant conservation and sustainable environmental management strategies.Nagpur, popularly known as the Orange City of Maharashtra, is geographically situated inthe eastern part of Maharashtra in central India. The region forms part of the Deccan Plateau and ischaracterized by a tropical climatic regime, with distinct summer, monsoon, and winter seasons. Itsgeographical setting, seasonal rainfall patterns, surrounding agricultural landscapes, naturalvegetation, and proximity to forest ecosystems provide considerable ecological significance.However, expanding urban infrastructure, transportation networks, industrial activities, and changingland-use patterns have placed increasing pressure on the city's natural vegetation and environmentalresources. In this context, the present review examines the ecological and environmental significanceof plants, emphasizing their role in mitigating pollution, regulating urban microclimates, conservingbiodiversity, maintaining soil fertility, and supporting ecosystem services. Particular attention is givento the importance of urban forests, roadside plantations, green belts, parks, and native plant species inimproving environmental quality in Nagpur and other rapidly developing urban centres. The reviewalso highlights the need for conserving mature trees, promoting regionally suitable native vegetation,undertaking systematic afforestation, restoring degraded habitats, and incorporating greeninfrastructure into urban planning. Furthermore, environmental awareness, community participation,and sustainable management of plant resources are discussed as essential approaches to addressingcontemporary environmental challenges. Overall, the review emphasizes that plant conservation andscientifically planned urban vegetation management are indispensable for achieving ecologicalresilience, climate adaptation, and sustainable development at local, regional, and global levels.

content: The p resent paper describes ‘Green Steel’ makingprocess, related issues of manufacturing and infrastructurebesides makeshift challenges during transition period. Greensteel making consists of the new technologies, clean energysource and the application of artificial intelligence. title: Coastal women and seashells collection business along western Indian Ocean in Tanzania: A livelihood opportunity
source: African Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: This study investigated seashell collection as a livelihood opportunity for coastal women in Kigamboni Municipal Council, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. It examined the socioeconomic factors influencing women’s participation, the uses of seashell
content: This study investigated seashell collection as a livelihood opportunity for coastal women in Kigamboni Municipal Council, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. It examined the socioeconomic factors influencing women’s participation, the uses of seashell products, and the structural constraints affecting the sustainability of the seashell business. Using a mixed-methods approach and a descriptive research design, data were collected from 91 respondents through structured questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and focus group discussions. The business was dominated by women aged 21 to 50 years (93%), most of whom had primary-level education (76%). Participation was primarily driven by the need to meet basic household needs (76%), finance children’s education (79%), and respond to limited opportunities for formal employment (85%). Cowrie shells were the most preferred commodity (87%) because of their diverse uses in decoration, jewellery, arts and crafts, and construction. Major challenges included market instability (79%), limited business skills and training (89%), inadequate equipment and protective gear (88%), and an insufficiently supportive business environment (73%). A regression model was used to examine the relationship between women’s engagement in the seashell business (dependent variable) and the selected independent variables. The model was statistically significant, F(7, 83) = 18.92, p < 0.001, R² = 0.614. Barriers to formal employment (β = 0.382, p < 0.001), provision for basic household needs (β = 0.267, p < 0.001), and financing children’s educational requirements (β = 0.233, p = 0.007) positively predicted women’s engagement in the seashell business, whereas market instability (β = −0.168, p = 0.030) and lack of business skills and training (β = −0.198, p = 0.026) negatively predicted engagement. Seashell collection and trading therefore constitute an important but precarious livelihood option for coastal women. Local value addition, entrepreneurial training, improved market networks, access to finance, and affordable protective equipment are needed to strengthen the resilience of the business and enhance its contribution to women’s economic empowerment.

title: The impact of taxation on economic growth from 2000 to 2019: A quantitative analysis on time-series data of Mauritius
summary: This study assessed the influence of tax revenue on economic growth, using a time series framework. The study also relied on unit root test, autocorrelation test, heteroskedasticity test, variance inflation factor and multiple regression an
content: This study assessed the influence of tax revenue on economic growth, using a time series framework. The study also relied on unit root test, autocorrelation test, heteroskedasticity test, variance inflation factor and multiple regression analysis with a logarithmic model. The dependent variable was the gross domestic product whilst the independent variables included personal income tax, value added tax, excise tax, inflation and government revenue. This quantitative research covered the period beginning 2000 and ending 2019. The research also employed an ex-post facto research design and annualised time series data published by the World Bank and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. The results including the test of hypothesis have been discussed in the study and the related findings warrant among other recommendations a reduced compliance costs to encourage investment and productivity. The negative or inverse effect of inflation rate on gross domestic product requires that the central bank maintain a repo rate that promote revenue mobilisation but does not impede economic growth. A combination of key fiscal and monetary policy is necessary to engender economic growth whilst ensuring financial stability. The collaborative effort between the tax authorities and financial regulators is necessary in achieving these objectives.

title: ENGINEERING MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR ENHANCING INDUSTRIAL COMPETITIVENESS, OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE, AND SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS PERFORMANCE IN AUSTRALIA
summary: Australian industrial firms compete from a high-cost, geographically distant base and have recently absorbed severe disruption to supply, labour and demand. Engineering management, the discipline that plans, organises and controls technical
content: Australian industrial firms compete from a high-cost, geographically distant base and have recently absorbed severe disruption to supply, labour and demand. Engineering management, the discipline that plans, organises and controls technical operations, is central to how they respond,yet evidence on which of its strategies improve competitiveness, resilience and sustainable business performance together remains fragmented. This review synthesises 30 journal articles, all peer reviewed and dated 2020 to 2025, selected through a systematic integrative design and anchored by a scientometric review of construction engineering and management research produced by Australia-based academics and a multiple case study of competitive manufacturing in high-cost environments. Twelve of the articles draw on Australian data, including surveys of 598, 447, 204 and 117 firms or managers. The synthesis yields three findings. First, competitiveness in high-cost settings rests on a broad operations capability base spanning quality, cost, time, flexibility and innovation, supported by formal planning and access to finance. Second, operational resilience is built through manager-level capabilities that create visibility, responsiveness and flexibility, through digital technologies that work mainly by enabling incremental innovation, and through the capacity to exploit and explore at once.

title: REIMAGINING INDUSTRIAL LEADERSHIP IN THE ERA OF INDUSTRY 5.0: HUMAN-CENTRED ENGINEERING, DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION, AND SUSTAINABLE MANUFACTURING PERFORMANCE
summary: Industry 5.0 asks manufacturers to place human well-being, resilience and sustainability alongside efficiency as goals of digital transformation. Whether that ambition changes how factories are designed and led, or remains a policy label at
content: Industry 5.0 asks manufacturers to place human well-being, resilience and sustainability alongside efficiency as goals of digital transformation. Whether that ambition changes how factories are designed and led, or remains a policy label attached to familiar technologies, is an open question. This review examines what Industry 5.0 means for industrial leadership, drawing together evidence on human-centred engineering, digital transformation and sustainable manufacturing performance. A systematic integrative approach was applied to 30 journal studies dated 2020 to 2025, anchored by a systematic review asking whether Industry 5.0 is genuinely human-centred and an interview study of the transition to Industry 5.0 in Spanish supply chain management. The corpus spans reviews, interview and case research, surveys with structural modelling, laboratory and field experiments, and system design studies. Four findings emerge. First, the human-centred turn is real in policy and research agendas, yet implementation remains largely techno-centred and the voice of workers is often missing from engineering practice. Second, human-centred engineering at the workstation, including collaborative robots, ergonomic monitoring, human digital twins, exoskeletons and augmented reality, can reduce physical and cognitive strain and support skill development, but outcomes depend on the mode of interaction, workstation design and acceptance.

title: BUILDING SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE IN AUSTRALIA AGAINST GLOBAL DISRUPTIONS
summary: Australia depends on long international supply routes for fuel, medicines, manufactured goods and inputs to agriculture and construction, while its own exports of food, energy and minerals travel the same routes in the opposite direction. T
content: Australia depends on long international supply routes for fuel, medicines, manufactured goods and inputs to agriculture and construction, while its own exports of food, energy and minerals travel the same routes in the opposite direction. The pandemic, extreme weather, trade tensions and attacks on shipping have shown how quickly these links can break. This paper examines how supply chain resilience can be built in Australia against such disruptions, linking firm-level strategies with sector and national exposure. The evidence base is a systematic integrative review of 30 refereed articles from 2020 to 2025, built around a major review of supply chain disruptions and resilience and a review of resilience from a network modelling perspective. Thirteen of the studies examine Australian supply chains or national exposure directly;the remainder supply the conceptual and international evidence against which Australian findings are read. The synthesis shows that Australian exposure arises from four sources: pandemic shocks to supply and demand, compound natural disasters intensified by climate change, geopolitical restrictions on trade, and concentration in strategic resources such as critical minerals, liquid fuels and medicines.

title: Deep calibration of interest rate models
summary: For any financial institution it is a necessity to be able to apprehend the behaviour of interest rates. Despite the use of Deep Learning that is growing very fastly, for many reasons (expertise, ease of use, etc.) classic rates models such
content: For any financial institution it is a necessity to be able to apprehend the behaviour of interest rates. Despite the use of Deep Learning that is growing very fastly, for many reasons (expertise, ease of use, etc.) classic rates models such as CIR, or the Gaussian family are still being widely used. In the current paper, we propose to calibrate the five parameters of the G2++ model using Neural Networks. The G2++ model is a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model in which the short rate is represented as the sum of a deterministic shift and two correlated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck factors. Our first model is a Fully Connected Neural network and uses only covariances and correlations of Zero-Coupon and Forward rates. We show that covariances are more suited to the problem than correlations due to the effects of the unfeasible backpropagation phenomenon that we analyze in this paper. The second model is a Convolutional Neural Network using only Zero-Coupon rates with no transformation. Our numerical tests show that our calibration based on deep learning outperforms the classic calibration method used as a benchmark. Besides, our Deep Calibration approach is designed to be systematic. To illustrate that feature, we applied it to calibrate the popular CIR intensity model.

title: Positive Outcomes of Corporate Social Responsibility for Companies and Society
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: To explore the complicated field of corporate social responsibility (CSR), this study performs a thorough narrative review of the literature. It achieves this by clarifying the benefits that CSR could bring to society as well as to companie
content: To explore the complicated field of corporate social responsibility (CSR), this study performs a thorough narrative review of the literature. It achieves this by clarifying the benefits that CSR could bring to society as well as to companies. According to the study, corporate social responsibility (CSR) goes beyond philanthropy and serves as an imperative strategy that improves a company's competitive advantage, reputation, and brand image. The study highlights the several benefits companies may achieve, such as enhanced staff morale, reduced risk, increased market share, and sustained financial prosperity. The article also explores the social impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR), presenting it as a driving force behind improving living standards, advancing equity, and aiding in protecting the environment. The study acknowledges that the CSR concept has flaws despite its many advantages. It highlights the significance of a conscious choice in interacting with social responsibility concerns and suggests a full review of both advantages and limitations. The study presents itself as a review of the complications surrounding corporate social responsibility (CSR), recognizing criticisms such as worries about misleading practices and the difficulties in measuring societal impact.

title: Common Noise by Random Measures: Constructing Mean-Field Equilibria for Competitive Investment and Hedging
summary: We construct Nash equilibria in mean-field portfolio games of optimal investment and hedging under relative performance concerns with exponential utility preferences. Common noise dynamics are modeled by integer-valued random measures, for
content: We construct Nash equilibria in mean-field portfolio games of optimal investment and hedging under relative performance concerns with exponential utility preferences. Common noise dynamics are modeled by integer-valued random measures, for instance Poisson random measures, in addition to Brownian motions. Agents differ in individual risk aversions, competition weights, and initial capital endowments, while their contingent claim liabilities depend on both common and idiosyncratic risk factors. Mean-field equilibria are characterized by solutions to McKean-Vlasov backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, for which we prove existence and uniqueness of solutions, without assuming mean-field interaction to be small. Moreover, we show how the equilibrium can be constructed from the optimal strategy of a single-agent optimization problem (without mean-field interaction) via an appropriate projection. Using successive changes of measure, our derivation provides a decomposition of the equilibrium strategy into three components with clear interpretations. Finally, we show how a limiting mean-field game of quadratic (instead of utility-based) hedging with relative performance concerns arises for vanishing risk aversion.

title: Calibration techniques for marked Hawkes processes with external excitation for cyber-attack frequency modeling
summary: Modeling cyber-attacks frequency and spread is crucial for the insurance industry to evaluate risk and adapt mitigation strategies. In the literature, Hawkes processes have been widely adopted to model the self-exciting behavior of cyber-at
content: Modeling cyber-attacks frequency and spread is crucial for the insurance industry to evaluate risk and adapt mitigation strategies. In the literature, Hawkes processes have been widely adopted to model the self-exciting behavior of cyber-attacks. This paper investigates a larger class of Hawkes processes by adding external excitation to capture vulnerabilities discoveries and stochastic marks to account for the magnitude and variability of their impacts on the contagion dynamics. Parametric estimation methods are developed and compared for both exponential and Erlang kernels, without resorting to stationarity assumptions. Our results exhibit that while the Mean Squared Errors (MSE) method faces identifiability issues, the likelihood method provides more reliable parameter estimation: the deterministic likelihood method performs well in low variance settings for the random marks, while the Monte Carlo one excels in high variance. This emphasizes the need to choose suitable calibration techniques based on the underlying contagion variability.

title: A general theory of risk sharing
summary: We introduce a new paradigm for risk sharing that generalizes earlier models based on discrete agents and extends them to allow for sharing risk within a continuum of agents. Agents are represented by points of a measure space and have pote
content: We introduce a new paradigm for risk sharing that generalizes earlier models based on discrete agents and extends them to allow for sharing risk within a continuum of agents. Agents are represented by points of a measure space and have potentially heterogeneous risk preferences modeled by risk measures on a separable probability space. We derive the dual representation of the value function using a Strassen-type theorem for the weak-star topology and provide a characterization of the acceptance set using Aumann integration. These results are illustrated by explicit formulas when risk preferences are within the family of entropic and expected shortfall risk measures and applications to Pareto efficiency in large markets.

title: Selective suppression and biasing of chemokine receptors CCR9 and ACKR4 through targeting CCL25 with de novo miniproteins
summary: Chemokines and their receptors mediate cell migration and coordinate immune responses, while dysregulation can lead to inflammation. Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. Most drug discovery efforts ta
content: Chemokines and their receptors mediate cell migration and coordinate immune responses, while dysregulation can lead to inflammation. Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. Most drug discovery efforts target the receptors, whereas natural regulatory mechanisms modulate immune responses by directly binding to or modifying the chemokine ligands. Despite this insight, development of effective chemokine-directed modulators has remained elusive. Recent advances in de novo protein design offer an unprecedented opportunity to produce high-affinity binders that efficiently block protein-protein interactions. We implemented a computational workflow leveraging the BindCraft platform to generate miniprotein binders against CCL25, the chemokine ligand for the receptors CCR9 and ACKR4, and implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases. The unbiased development results in several miniproteins designed to block the receptor N-terminus from wrapping the chemokine and preventing productive engagement. Thus, these proteins suppress CCL25-mediated effector coupling and halt MOLT-4 lymphoblast migration. Another class of miniprotein, represented by VUP25111, is predicted to bind CCL25 along the chemokine β1 strand and retained receptor binding. This complex inhibited arrestin recruitment to CCR9, but not to ACKR4, indicating receptor specificity. Additionally, G protein recruitment to CCR9 was unimpeded by VUP25111, suggesting that the miniprotein biased the native agonist towards G proteins. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of differentially targeting CCL25 to suppress CCR9 signaling and new tools to resolve the structural basis of chemokine receptor activation and bias.

title: Probing the Memory of a Superconducting Qubit Environment
summary: Achieving fault tolerance with superconducting quantum processors requires qubits to operate within the regime of threshold theorems based on the Born-Markov approximation. This approximation, which models dissipation as constant energy dec
content: Achieving fault tolerance with superconducting quantum processors requires qubits to operate within the regime of threshold theorems based on the Born-Markov approximation. This approximation, which models dissipation as constant energy decay into a memoryless environment, breaks down when qubits couple to long-lived two-level systems (TLSs) that become polarized during operation and retain memory of past qubit states. Here, we show that non-Poissonian quantum jump traces carry the information required to distinguish long-lived TLSs from the standard Markovian bath. By fitting the Solomon equations to measured quantum jump dynamics arising naturally from thermal fluctuations, we can disentangle the qubit’s coupling to the two environments. Sweeping the qubit frequency reveals distinct peaks, each associated with a TLS that outlives the qubit, providing a handle to understand their microscopic origin.

title: The retraction epidemic in science across publishers, fields, and countries
summary: Retractions are considered a proxy signal of problems in the scientific record. Prior studies have documented a rise in retractions, but the functional form of this growth, once the expansion of scientific output is accounted for, has not b
content: Retractions are considered a proxy signal of problems in the scientific record. Prior studies have documented a rise in retractions, but the functional form of this growth, once the expansion of scientific output is accounted for, has not been quantified. We use one of the largest open bibliographic databases to develop incidence metrics normalized by population cohorts: retractions per publication and per active author by year of publication. Applying an epidemiological framework that models counts with exposure, we find evidence of exponential growth in retraction incidence, with approximately a 5-year doubling time at both the paper and author levels. These patterns vary significantly across scientific disciplines, publishing organizations, and national research systems. While scientific output is becoming more democratized globally, retractions are concentrated in fewer countries, creating a “concentration” paradox that calls for targeted monitoring. Despite exponential growth, the absolute incidence remains low (0.20% in 2023), allowing for corrective intervention. Incidence-based monitoring provides a framework for evaluating policies that safeguard research integrity at scale.

title: Structured parameterization and non-stabilizerness in hypergraph QAOA
summary: The QAOA admits several parameterization schemes, from the original single-angle formulation (SA-QAOA) to the more expressive multi-angle (MA-QAOA) and automorphic-angle (AA-QAOA) variants, which trade expressiveness against the cost of cla
content: The QAOA admits several parameterization schemes, from the original single-angle formulation (SA-QAOA) to the more expressive multi-angle (MA-QAOA) and automorphic-angle (AA-QAOA) variants, which trade expressiveness against the cost of classical optimization. We introduce the kA-QAOA, which assigns one cost-layer angle to all terms of the same k-body interaction order. This makes it suited to optimization problems on hypergraphs, where multi-body interactions arise naturally, for example from clauses in Boolean satisfiability or from tooling constraints in scheduling. In noiseless statevector simulations of 3-uniform cyclic sign-alternating hypergraphs (n <= 15) and random-coefficient hypergraphs (n = 12), kA-QAOA reaches approximation ratios comparable to MA-QAOA with fewer variational parameters and fewer optimizer calls to the quantum circuit. On the cyclic family, the reduction in calls grows with system size. We also find that all variants traverse a transient magic barrier, and that the barrier of kA-QAOA is on average lower than that of MA-QAOA, while the circuits themselves are gate-for-gate identical.

title: Benchmarking and resource analysis for augmented-Lagrangian quantum Hamiltonian descent
summary: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) is a continuous optimization algorithm based on simulating a time-dependent quantum Hamiltonian whose potential energy encodes the objective function and whose kinetic energy promotes exploration through qu
content: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) is a continuous optimization algorithm based on simulating a time-dependent quantum Hamiltonian whose potential energy encodes the objective function and whose kinetic energy promotes exploration through quantum interference and tunneling. While QHD is formulated for unconstrained optimization, many real-world optimization problems are constrained and highly nonconvex. In this paper, we benchmark AL-QHD, a hybrid framework that embeds QHD within the Augmented Lagrangian Method (ALM), thereby solving a sequence of unconstrained subproblems while using ALM to enforce constraints. We evaluate AL-QHD on standard nonconvex test functions and use iterative refinement to improve solution accuracy at fixed per-run qubit cost. A finite-shot supplement replaces exact-probability feedback by measurement outcomes and scans 100–10,000 shots per readout, quantifying the empirical tradeoff between solution quality, reliability, and measurement cost across complete adaptive runs. Separately from the optimization benchmarks, we estimate gate-level resources for AL-QHD circuit constructions using ACOPF-derived symbolic models extracted from the synthetic Texas7k network dataset. These models contain 2–198 buses and 6–538 active variables and are used solely for resource estimation; we do not execute AL-QHD optimization on these models or solve the full Texas7k network. Resource estimates on Texas7k-derived ACOPF instances show steep hard-gate scaling, reaching ∼ 4.46 × 10 7 entangling gates in a NISQ-oriented model and ∼ 9.42 × 10 8 T gates in a fault-tolerant model at ∼ 5.3 × 10 2 active variables. These results suggest that AL-QHD is a useful framework for studying constrained nonconvex optimization with QHD, but that practical ACOPF-scale applications under the implementation analyzed here would likely require large-scale fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

title: Portfolio allocation under heterogeneous scales and multifractality
summary: Cross-correlations between financial signals are neither scale-free nor amplitude-independent: they vary with the time scale over which they are measured and with the magnitude of the fluctuations that dominate the average. We exploit this
content: Cross-correlations between financial signals are neither scale-free nor amplitude-independent: they vary with the time scale over which they are measured and with the magnitude of the fluctuations that dominate the average. We exploit this structure to construct a portfolio allocation model in which the risk functional is the signed fluctuation function of multifractal cross-correlation analysis (MFCCA), indexed by a scale s and a fluctuation order q. Unlike MFDCCA-type criteria, which rectify local detrended covariances before aggregation, MFCCA retains their sign, so that co-moving and counter-moving components contribute to risk with opposite signs; for q = 2 the resulting quadratic form coincides with the detrended fluctuation function of the portfolio series itself, recovering the mean–variance criterion as a scale-dependent limit. Using two-component ARFIMA and Markov-switching multifractal processes, we show that prescribed multiscale and multifractal dependence is transmitted into the optimal weights, and that sign preservation contributes more to the reduction of tail risk than aggregation over fluctuation orders. Applied to financial multi-assets, the criterion lowers drawdown, Value-at-Risk, and expected shortfall relative to the mean–variance benchmark at every required return, in and out of sample, without any loss in realized portfolio return. The construction maps signed multiscale interaction structures onto resource-allocation decisions, which is applicable to complex financial systems whose components interact across heterogeneous scales with amplitude-dependent coupling.

title: Does Financial Inclusion Improve the Welfare of Informal-Worker Households? Evidence from Ghana
summary: Informal workers lack employment-based protection against income shocks, yet evidence on whether financial inclusion improves their welfare is limited. Using the seventh round of the Ghana Living Standards Survey (2016/17), this study exami
content: Informal workers lack employment-based protection against income shocks, yet evidence on whether financial inclusion improves their welfare is limited. Using the seventh round of the Ghana Living Standards Survey (2016/17), this study examines 9,867 households headed by informal workers. Comparisons within enumeration areas show that inclusion is associated with 0.235 log points higher consumption per adult equivalent, an 8.5-percentage-point lower probability of poverty, an 11.7-point lower probability of moderate or severe food insecurity and more durable assets. The results are robust across doubly robust, entropy-balancing, and preference-adjusted specifications. Households that actively use their accounts gain more than those with dormant accounts. Among unbanked informal-worker household heads, 74 per cent cite insufficient or irregular income as the main reason for exclusion, while fewer than 6 per cent cite distance, procedures or lack of awareness. Inclusion policies for informal workers therefore need to address income irregularity, not only access.

title: High Article Processing Charges and the Expansion of Predatory Publishing in the Generative AI Era: Implications for Research Integrity and Global Scholarly Inclusion
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Applied Science
summary: The transition to open access publishing was intended to democratize knowledge, yet the dominance of article processing charge models has created new financial stratifications that disproportionately affect researchers in low- and middle-in
content: The transition to open access publishing was intended to democratize knowledge, yet the dominance of article processing charge models has created new financial stratifications that disproportionately affect researchers in low- and middle-income countries. Concurrently, generative artificial intelligence has lowered barriers to manuscript production while amplifying editorial overload and predatory publishing vulnerabilities. This critical review examines the interconnected dynamics among article processing charge inflation, generative artificial intelligence-driven publication pressures, predatory publishing expansion, and global scholarly inequality, with alignment to Sustainable Development Goals 4, 9, 10, 16, and 17. The review is based on a purposive selection of interdisciplinary literature in scholarly communication, higher education, information science, research ethics, and science policy. Literature was selected through reference snowballing and thematic relevance to the five research objectives rather than systematic database searching. Findings indicate that global spending on article processing charges has escalated significantly, with average charges for high-impact journals exceeding several thousand United States dollars, creating conditions that increase susceptibility to predatory journals. The rise of generative artificial intelligence further complicates scholarly communication through accelerated manuscript production, paper mills, and concerns regarding epistemic reliability. Predatory publishing should be understood not merely as a problem of unethical journals but as a structural consequence of inequitable academic publishing systems intensified by artificial intelligence-era publication pressures. Policy reforms centered on diamond open access models, ethical artificial intelligence governance, research integrity education, and strengthened international collaboration are proposed.

title: Integrin-guided development of defined supramolecular hydrogels for human kidney tubuloid culture
summary: Tubuloids are epithelial organoids derived from tissue or urine that model tubular nephron segments of the kidney. Their use in preclinical research is limited by dependence on basement membrane extract (BME), a batch-variable animal-derive
content: Tubuloids are epithelial organoids derived from tissue or urine that model tubular nephron segments of the kidney. Their use in preclinical research is limited by dependence on basement membrane extract (BME), a batch-variable animal-derived matrix that reduces reproducibility. Here, we evaluate defined supramolecular ureido-pyrimidinone (UPy) hydrogels as an alternative matrix for tubuloid culture.
