Farmer organisations are best understood not as casualties of digital disintermediation but as contingent intermediaries whose value depends on organisational capability, governance and the rules that structure platform markets.

title: No-strings charity no more
summary: Europe must dismantle its fragmented, purely altruistic model of development aid, which yields a dangerously low geopolitical return on investment. While global rivals like China successfully leverage infrastructure lending to cement long-t
content: Europe must dismantle its fragmented, purely altruistic model of development aid, which yields a dangerously low geopolitical return on investment. While global rivals like China successfully leverage infrastructure lending to cement long-term geostrategic leverage, Europe must transition to Clean Trade and Investment Partnerships (CTIPs). By linking climate finance directly to local value creation, green procurement, and strict operational prerequisites, the Union can convert economic weight into tangible global influence.

title: Assessing the Dynamic Effects of Macroeconomic factors and Financial Inclusion on Poverty: Evidence from an ARDL Approach
summary: Background Poverty is still a hot topic in economic growth, especially in developing countries such as Indonesia. In recent years, the advancement of digital infrastructure play an important role to poverty alleviation. Aims This research i
content: Background Poverty is still a hot topic in economic growth, especially in developing countries such as Indonesia. In recent years, the advancement of digital infrastructure play an important role to poverty alleviation. Aims This research investigated the shortrun and longrun effects variables on poverty levels in Indonesia, This research was conducted in Indonesia, using data from 2001 to 2024 obtained from various sources. Methods This research adopts a quantitative methodology with an exploratory–causal research design to investigate the dynamic relationships among variables. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag model is employed due to estimating dynamic relationships. The aim to examine the short-term and long-term relationships between variables Result The findings indicate that in the long run, per capita income, inflation, and internet penetration have a significant impact on poverty levels. However, internet penetration shows a unidirectional relationship with increasing poverty, while financial inclusion is not significant. The short run shows a delayed effect of each variable on poverty, except that internet penetration has no significant effect. Conclusion This study analyzes the impact of each variable on poverty reduction in Indonesia in the short and long term. Per capita income, inflation, and internet penetration are important variables for long-term poverty reduction. Implication The results of this study contribute to the literature that shows the importance for the government to increase revenue, maintain price stability and improve digital infrastructure followed by skills development, and productive internet use among vulnerable populations.

title: Food security effects of the initiative to reduce fertilizer use while improving input-use efficiency
summary: This study uses panel data for 253 Chinese cities at or above the prefecture level from 2010 to 2019. Policy timing is defined by each city’s year of first local rollout of the Fertilizer Zero-Growth Action (the Action). A staggered differe
content: This study uses panel data for 253 Chinese cities at or above the prefecture level from 2010 to 2019. Policy timing is defined by each city’s year of first local rollout of the Fertilizer Zero-Growth Action (the Action). A staggered difference-in-differences model estimates the effect of the Action on food security. The Action significantly improves grain production outcomes. This finding remains robust across a series of tests. Tests of input-reduction effects show that the Action significantly reduces fertilizer application intensity. Mechanism tests show that it significantly promotes agricultural technological progress and the development of agricultural socialized services. These findings provide empirical evidence for understanding the technology supply and production organization channels. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects in areas with greater fiscal support for agriculture. Effects are also more pronounced in areas with mean annual precipitation above 400 mm and low terrain ruggedness. No significant difference in policy effects is found between the two groups defined by the 800 mm precipitation threshold. This study examines fertilizer reduction policies from a food security perspective. It further analyzes how agricultural technological progress, agricultural socialized services and differences in natural endowments relate to policy outcomes. The findings provide empirical evidence for coordinating fertilizer reduction with grain production and improving policies tailored to local conditions.

title: Review article: Power grid resilience under compound typhoon–rainstorm hazards
summary: Power grids are vulnerable to the combined effects of strong winds, heavy rainfall, and flooding during extreme typhoons. This review examines failure mechanisms, resilience assessment, and enhancement strategies, with particular attention
content: Power grids are vulnerable to the combined effects of strong winds, heavy rainfall, and flooding during extreme typhoons. This review examines failure mechanisms, resilience assessment, and enhancement strategies, with particular attention to how assessment results inform engineering decisions. Three findings emerge. First, typhoon impacts extend from component damage to cascading outages and delayed restoration, whereas many assessment models still represent individual hazards or failure mechanisms separately. Second, probabilistic and data-driven methods provide complementary approaches to resilience assessment, but a comparison of published vulnerability curves reveals differences in thresholds, model assumptions, and evidence bases across regions, which limit direct comparison and require local validation before model transfer. Third, resilience measures span pre-disaster hardening and preparation, emergency isolation and network reconfiguration, and post-disaster restoration, with nature-based solutions offering additional opportunities for risk reduction. Their effectiveness depends on whether they address the failure mechanisms and recovery constraints identified by the assessment. Future research should strengthen the representation of compound hazards, improve the traceability and comparability of vulnerability evidence, and evaluate coordinated interventions across the disaster cycle. Digital twins, artificial intelligence, and multi-source data can support this work when their predictions are validated and linked to feasible operational decisions.

title: Beyond “No Bed Syndrome”: reframing hospital bed shortages as a patient-flow and health-system coordination problem in Ghana
summary: Ghana's “No Bed Syndrome” describes a recurring pattern in which patients seeking emergency or referred care are reportedly turned away because a receiving facility is said to have no bed. Existing evidence suggests the problem cannot be re
content: Ghana's “No Bed Syndrome” describes a recurring pattern in which patients seeking emergency or referred care are reportedly turned away because a receiving facility is said to have no bed. Existing evidence suggests the problem cannot be reduced to a simple count of physical beds. This Perspective develops a clinically and operationally grounded interpretation of No Bed Syndrome and proposes a feasible pathway for testing the mechanisms that may produce admission failure. Drawing on a targeted, non-systematic synthesis of Ghana-specific literature, patient flow is used as the primary organising framework, with the WHO health-system building blocks locating upstream system constraints and governance and the legal-institutional environment treated as contextual determinants rather than separate causal models. We argue that No Bed Syndrome is best understood as a multidimensional patient-flow problem involving genuine bed scarcity, staffed or functional-capacity shortages, delayed discharge, referral failure, poor visibility of available capacity, and potentially discretionary admission decisions; the last of these remains an untested hypothesis in Ghana. We further show that the primary text of Ghana's Health Institutions and Facilities Act, 2011 (Act 829) does not support the frequently repeated attribution of a vicarious-liability rule to section 25, which is in fact an interpretation provision, and we separate institutional exposure to negligence risk from the untested hypothesis that liability concerns influence bed-denial decisions. We propose a phased, monitored patient-flow intervention that makes functional capacity visible, documents admission and transfer decisions, strengthens referral coordination, and protects equitable access, offering a more defensible route to reform than assuming that bed construction or digital scale-up alone will resolve the problem. Mechanisms are graded as Ghana-supported, contextual or hypothetical, and the roadmap identifies implementation risks and priority pilot indicators. Reframing No Bed Syndrome as a system-performance problem at the intersection of capacity and flow shifts the policy conversation from counting beds toward strengthening the processes that convert physical resources into timely, equitable care.

title: The role of fiscal policy in addressing environmental degradation in Iraq: Reality and proposals
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAhmed Abdulzahra Hamdan - Corresponding author, email: ahmed.ah@uomustansiriyah.edu.iqAbstractThe significance of this study lies in the critical impact of environmental degradation on human well-being a
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAhmed Abdulzahra Hamdan - Corresponding author, email: ahmed.ah@uomustansiriyah.edu.iqAbstractThe significance of this study lies in the critical impact of environmental degradation on human well-being and climate change, as well as the vital role of fiscal policy as a key economic instrument for addressing this challenge. The paper aims to assess the current readiness of the financial, legal, and institutional aspects, which are essential to implement green fiscal policy. The study adopts a deductive approach to analyze the environmental situation and the legal and institutional framework of fiscal policy. The main findings indicate a substantial deterioration in Iraq’s environmental conditions during 1970–2024. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions increased from 23,561,141 (tCO₂e) in 1970 to 238,670,397 (tCO₂e) in 2024, driven primarily by the oil industry and unsustainable patterns of individual energy consumption. In addition, greenhouse gas emissions rose significantly from 103,520,899 (tCO₂e) in 1970 to 413,276,421 (tCO₂e) in 2024. The study also revealed a significant institutional gap: the absence of legislation prevents the government from imposing environmental taxes; weak coordination between the Ministry of Environment and the Ministry of Finance; and no link between environmental and tax laws. Currently, environmental objectives are supported only through public regulations and limited fines, which contribute indirectly to environmental protection. The study concludes that Iraq lacks a green fiscal policy, placing it behind many countries in addressing environmental challenges and highlighting the need for comprehensive legal and institutional reforms.

title: Impact of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Digital Payments on India's Economic Growth: Macroeconomic Channels, Financial Inclusion, and Structural Formalization
summary: The rapid proliferation of digital payment architectures, anchored by the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), has triggered a structural paradigm shift in the Indian economy. Evolving over a decade from its launch in 2016 by the National Paym
content: The rapid proliferation of digital payment architectures, anchored by the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), has triggered a structural paradigm shift in the Indian economy. Evolving over a decade from its launch in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) into the world's largest real-time retail payment mechanism, UPI now processes nearly half of the globe's real-time digital transaction volume, crossing 241 billion annual transactions with an aggregate turnover exceeding ₹314 lakh crore (~US$ 3.8 trillion) in FY 2025-26. This paper investigates the empirical and theoretical transmission channels through which UPI and retail digital payments propel India's macroeconomic expansion and structural modernization. Grounded in monetary economics (velocity of money formulation), Transaction Cost Economics, and Financial Intermediation Theory, this study analyzes how digital payment public infrastructure (DPI) accelerates gross domestic product (GDP) growth. Specifically, the paper delineates four primary macroeconomic transmission mechanisms: (1) drastic reductions in transaction friction and cash-handling logistical costs, which historically consumed 1.5% to 2% of GDP; (2) structural formalization of the informal sector and unprecedented expansion of fiscal tax buoyancy (evidenced by record GST revenues); (3) democratization of micro-credit through the digital financial footprint of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) leveraging Credit-on-UPI and the Account Aggregator framework; and (4) friction-free public welfare distribution via Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) under the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity. Concurrently, the paper critically interrogates emergent systemic vulnerabilities: the zero-Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) sustainability dilemma, fintech duopolistic market concentration, escalating cyber-fraud vectors, and digital exclusion in marginalized regional cohorts. Finally, the study outlines strategic policy interventions to preserve infrastructural resilience, bolster digital literacy, integrate Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC e-Rupee), and expand UPI's cross-border geoeconomic footprint.

title: Telehealth as an alternative pathway for low-acuity acute care: clinical appropriateness, economic value, patient acceptance, and public-health implications
summary: The rapid expansion of telehealth has created opportunities to reconsider how patients with low-acuity acute conditions access care and whether virtual services can reduce reliance on emergency departments (EDs). This narrative review evalu
content: The rapid expansion of telehealth has created opportunities to reconsider how patients with low-acuity acute conditions access care and whether virtual services can reduce reliance on emergency departments (EDs). This narrative review evaluates the role of telehealth as an alternative acute-care pathway, integrating evidence on clinical appropriateness, healthcare utilization, economic outcomes, access and equity, safety and quality, and patient acceptance. Available evidence indicates that telehealth can safely resolve selected low-acuity conditions and facilitate triage for others, but the proportion of ED encounters that can realistically be substituted by virtual care is substantially smaller than retrospective estimates of non-emergent ED use suggest. Economic studies generally demonstrate lower resource utilization and patient-level costs for virtual care, although evidence for healthcare-system cost savings remains heterogeneous and depends on whether telehealth genuinely substitutes for higher-cost care rather than generating additional or duplicative encounters. Similarly, broad telehealth expansion does not consistently reduce ED utilization; targeted models positioned at the point of acute-care decision-making appear more promising for achieving meaningful substitution. Population-level Medicare data demonstrate both the rapid expansion of telemedicine and persistent differences in utilization across demographic and geographic groups, underscoring the importance of digital access and health equity. Patient behavior represents an additional determinant of effectiveness: awareness, perceived symptom severity, trust in virtual assessment, convenience, cost, prior experience, and clinician recommendation influence willingness to select telehealth for acute symptoms. Taken together, the evidence supports an integrated model in which telehealth serves not as a universal replacement for emergency care but as an accessible clinical entry point that directs patients toward virtual resolution, targeted in-person evaluation, or emergency escalation based on clinical need. Public-health strategies should therefore prioritize appropriate triage, equitable access, patient trust and awareness, interoperable care pathways, and episode-level outcomes rather than telehealth volume or ED avoidance alone.

title: Depth-dependent transcriptomic responses to thermal stress, including transcriptional frontloading, provide preliminary insights into the deep refugia hypothesis in a Mediterranean coral
summary: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) pose significant threats to marine biodiversity, including Mediterranean octocorals. The deep refugia hypothesis considers mesophotic populations as sources for recolonization and restoration of shallow coral populat
content: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) pose significant threats to marine biodiversity, including Mediterranean octocorals. The deep refugia hypothesis considers mesophotic populations as sources for recolonization and restoration of shallow coral populations threatened by MHWs. Using a common-garden experiment, we tested whether transcriptomic responses to thermal stress differ between shallow and mesophotic populations of Corallium rubrum and looked for underlying processes, including transcriptional frontloading. Six individuals from one shallow (15 m) and one mesophotic (48 m) population were exposed to thermal stress in aquaria, with samples collected at day 0, 5, and 10 for RNA sequencing. We revealed 2670 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in response to heat stress. Mild transcriptomic responses were observed in the shallow population (692 DEGs), characterized by heat shock proteins (HSPs) and developmental regulation, whereas stronger responses were observed in the mesophotic population with more than twice as many DEGs (1645), associated with stress and wound healing mechanisms. Temporal transcriptional shifts were larger in the mesophotic compared to the shallow population. Among the upregulated DEGs found in the mesophotic population under thermal stress, 314, including HSPs, showed high expression in the shallow compared to the mesophotic population under control conditions, suggesting transcriptional frontloading. These results suggest that the mesophotic population examined here may have limited potential to serve as a source for the restoration of the shallow population, providing preliminary insights into the deep refugia hypothesis in C. rubrum. Our findings underscore the importance of incorporating population-specific thermal responses into coral restoration strategies.

title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
summary: CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase with a well-established role in regulating gene expression, but its cytoplasmic functions remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we identified ALIX, a cytoplasmic protein acting with the ESCRT-III machi
content: CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase with a well-established role in regulating gene expression, but its cytoplasmic functions remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we identified ALIX, a cytoplasmic protein acting with the ESCRT-III machinery in numerous membrane remodeling events, as a partner and substrate of CARM1. We demonstrate that CARM1 methylates arginine residues within the proline-rich motif of ALIX. At the molecular level, ALIX methylation impairs SH3-dependent association with CD2AP, CIN85, and endophilin-A2 that are required for cytokinesis. Using a mutant of ALIX that is unable to bind these proteins, we further show that these interactions are essential for ALIX functions during cytokinesis. Mechanistically, ALIX methylation controls the levels of CD2AP at the cytokinetic midbody, which are known to be critical for successful cytokinesis. Altogether, this work highlights the significance of arginine methylation as a regulatory post-translational modification important for the final step of cell division, by modulating interactions between proline-rich domains and their SH3-containing partners.

title: Tackling Neoliberal Common Sense Through the US Municipal Public Banking Movement
summary: We argue that US public banking campaigns offer important lessons in challenging financialized logics and neoliberal “common sense.” Drawing on primary research on the Municipal Bank of Los Angeles, we show how local public banking campaign
content: We argue that US public banking campaigns offer important lessons in challenging financialized logics and neoliberal “common sense.” Drawing on primary research on the Municipal Bank of Los Angeles, we show how local public banking campaigns go beyond Occupy Wall Street in California and divestment initiatives by engaging with state actors and institutions to articulate alternative progressive economic imaginaries. This article is a contribution to the SPE special theme “Public Banks in North America.”

title: Transitions in bullying exposure over time: A person-based analysis examining how role conflict and clarity relate to face-to-face and cyberbullying target profiles
summary: Person-centred methods have been used in workplace bullying literature to identify different target groups. In this study, we use these methods to determine whether target groups are identifiable based on whether people experience face-to-f
content: Person-centred methods have been used in workplace bullying literature to identify different target groups. In this study, we use these methods to determine whether target groups are identifiable based on whether people experience face-to-face or cyberbullying behaviours. Using data collected from a sample of 748 employees at two time points separated by six months, we find that bullying targets seem to experience face-to-face and cyber acts concurrently, rather than separately. Indeed, latent profile analysis shows three categories of victimhood: “No Bullying”, “Infrequent Bullying”, and “Regular Bullying”. We then explore predictors of profile membership, finding that role conflict was significantly associated with membership of the “Infrequent” and “Regular” profiles both cross-sectionally and over time. In contrast, role clarity only showed cross-sectional associations with membership of the Infrequent Bullying profile. In a final set of analyses, we investigate whether latent changes in role stressors influence transitions of people across profiles over time. We find that role clarity changes were linked to transitions between the “No Bullying” and “Infrequent Bullying” profiles, whereas role conflict change was associated with movement between the “Regular Bullying” and “Infrequent Bullying” profiles. These findings imply that enhancing role clarity may prevent bullying, whereas reducing role conflict may de-escalate bullying.

title: The Costs and Benefits of Guest Worker Programs: Experimental Evidence from the India-UAE Migration Corridor,
source: Journal of the European Economic Association
summary: We estimate the returns to temporary, legal migration using a randomized experiment with Indian applicants for construction jobs in the UAE. Individuals who migrate doubled their earnings. However, migrants paid substantial upfront costs to
content: We estimate the returns to temporary, legal migration using a randomized experiment with Indian applicants for construction jobs in the UAE. Individuals who migrate doubled their earnings. However, migrants paid substantial upfront costs to labor intermediaries and reported significant falls in well-being. We extrapolate linear marginal treatment effects for workers who declined the offer and find they would have similar pecuniary returns to migration but would experience larger drops in well-being. We estimate that accounting for the fall in well-being and the intermediary costs reduce the welfare gains of temporary migration to the UAE to one-half of the pecuniary gains alone.

title: Demographic group differences and reliability of the virtual reality version of the Beijing performance-based functional ecological test (BJ-PERFECT VR) in Chinese healthy adults
summary: Introduction The Beijing Performance-based Functional Ecological Test physical version (BJ-PERFECT PROP) is an ecologically valid, performance-based cognitive assessment tool tailored to Chinese cultural contexts. It demonstrates satisfacto
content: Introduction The Beijing Performance-based Functional Ecological Test physical version (BJ-PERFECT PROP) is an ecologically valid, performance-based cognitive assessment tool tailored to Chinese cultural contexts. It demonstrates satisfactory reliability and validity. To enhance portability and accessibility, the BJ-PERFECT has been successfully adapted into a virtual reality (VR) format and subsequently validated in both healthy participants and schizophrenia patients. Methods In our study, we explored demographic group differences and proportional scores for the BJ-PERFECT VR based on a census-stratified sample of 726 healthy Chinese adults recruited across six geographic regions, with demographic factors of age, gender, years of education, and childhood residence. Test-retest reliability of BJ-PERFECT VR was also assessed in 54 participants. Results Analyses revealed that age and rural residence were negatively associated with GFSS scores (F=30.209, p<0.001; F=13.379, p<0.001, respectively), whereas education level showed a positive association (F=5.597, p=0.004). No significant sex differences were observed. Rural residence was associated with lower scores than urban residence (GFSS, F=13.379, p<0.001, Partial η²=0.036). GFSS showed a highly significant practice effect (Z = 3.848, p < 0.001), with borderline test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.709). The vast majority of participants (N=580) experienced minimal simulator sickness symptoms after using the BJ-PERFECT VR (IPQ=3.1±1.0, SSQ=0.2(0, 0.6)). Discussion The BJ-PERFECT VR exhibits borderline to moderate reliability, offering substantial potential for broader application in both research and clinical neuropsychiatric settings.

title: Patient Capital, Resource Allocation Efficiency and Firm‐Level Total Factor Productivity: Micro‐Level Evidence From China and Implications for the Chinese Financial Market
summary: This paper uses panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2012 to 2024 to investigate the impact of patient capital on the total factor productivity (TFP) of enterprises and its underlying mechanisms. The results demonstrate that pati
content: This paper uses panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2012 to 2024 to investigate the impact of patient capital on the total factor productivity (TFP) of enterprises and its underlying mechanisms. The results demonstrate that patient capital exhibits a significant positive association with firm‐level TFP overall. Further endogeneity tests indicated that the two‐stage least squares (2SLS) estimation confirmed that both stable equity and relational debt have robust causal enabling effects on the improvement TFP of enterprises. The test results of the propensity score matching method (PSM) and the high‐dimensional fixed effects model further support the above causal inference conclusion. Mechanism analyses reveal that patient capital promotes TFP by improving resource allocation efficiency. Specifically, it reduces agency costs, eases financing constraints, and optimises human capital allocation. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that stable equity has a stronger productivity‐enhancing effect among highly financialised firms and in western China, while relational debt has a stronger effect among less financialised firms and in eastern and central regions. Evidence from China suggests that, in emerging Asia‐Pacific markets, fostering long‐term equity investment and relationship‐based lending can help mitigate market speculation and support high‐quality growth in the real economy.

title: Lightweight domain analysis reveals spatiotemporal patterns and sources of composite pollutants in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
summary: The unique urban-rural industrial distribution and land-sea interaction in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) give rise to widespread multi-medium composite pollutants across aquatic, soil and atmospheric media. Complex po
content: The unique urban-rural industrial distribution and land-sea interaction in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) give rise to widespread multi-medium composite pollutants across aquatic, soil and atmospheric media. Complex pollution sources and scattered monitoring records further cause severe data fragmentation and multi-source heterogeneity, hampering quantitative analysis of pollutant migration, fate and regional pollution risk. Conventional simulation tools lack targeted domain constraints for coastal composite pollution and cannot achieve refined identification of pollutant spatiotemporal characteristics. To fill this gap, this study establishes GBA-PolluteGPT, a lightweight text-based domain analytical model built on the ChatGLM3-6B backbone, integrating parameter fine-tuning, environmental dataset auxiliary constraint and a spatiotemporal pollutant knowledge reasoning framework. Operating on documentary and monitoring textual materials, the model combines authoritative regional environmental monitoring data with standardized environmental logic constraints to enhance the recognition of pollutant distribution patterns and knowledge-level source identification and tracing. Comparative validation shows that the proposed model achieves 91.67% accuracy in identifying spatiotemporal distribution and source signals of composite pollutants, outperforming the vanilla base model and all general-purpose LLMs on domain-specific objective accuracy. This lightweight, low-cost analytical framework supports regional pollutant source tracing, spatiotemporal pollution risk evaluation, and precise prevention and control of multi-medium composite pollutants in coastal bay areas.

title: Mapping the impact of the digital economy on employment quality and income distribution: A bibliometric analysis
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleLei Wu - Corresponding author, email: w1424052330@gmail.comAbstractFunctioning as the central force for reshaping labor markets, the role of the digital economy in employment quality and income distribut
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleLei Wu - Corresponding author, email: w1424052330@gmail.comAbstractFunctioning as the central force for reshaping labor markets, the role of the digital economy in employment quality and income distribution has drawn global attention. This paper aims to map existing research trends in the digital economy, employment quality, and income distribution. The analysis employs systematic and bibliometric methods to analyze 75 publications from Web of Science and Scopus between 2021 and 2025. Using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, ArcGIS, and Bibliometrix in R, the systematic analysis covers publication distribution, most-cited works, author co-citation, theme evolution, and keyword co-occurrence. The results reveal increasing attention to the field, with Eurasian countries contributing the most, especially China, Romania, and Turkey. Moreover, Sustainability and Heliyon serve as the dominant platforms in this domain. The most cited work and author co-citation prove the early impact of digital technology on employment. Keyword co-occurrence analysis displays four research themes, covering the foundation of the digital economy, employment, sustainable development and income, and the labor market. Additionally, current literature highlights that scholars have examined the impact of the digital economy on employment quality and income distribution from various perspectives, such as positive effects, negative effects, heterogeneity, and impact mechanisms. Nonetheless, the conclusions lack consistency and quantitative assessment. Consequently, this study proposes four future research directions, including the non-linear impact of the digital economy on employment quality and income distribution, the mechanisms by which the digital economy influences the two variables, the development of a digital economy development imbalance index, and quantitative studies on digital policies.

title: Closing Windows: Fertility Decline and the Timing of Preventive War
summary: A state whose relative military power is growing may postpone an attack to improve its chances of victory. Fertility decline can weaken this incentive by reducing the future gains in relative power. I study a challenger choosing whether and
content: A state whose relative military power is growing may postpone an attack to improve its chances of victory. Fertility decline can weaken this incentive by reducing the future gains in relative power. I study a challenger choosing whether and when to attack after bargaining has failed. Military power combines technology and manpower, with past births providing a comparatively predictable baseline for future recruitment over a finite horizon. Holding initial relative power fixed, I show that faster own cohort decline can make immediate attack optimal even though the chances of victory would continue to improve. Near the transition to immediate attack, faster own decline advances attack and faster defender decline delays it, provided the respective country depends partly on manpower. Technology that reduces the challenger's reliance on manpower delays attack under the same condition. A common increase in cohort-decline rates leaves timing unchanged when both countries are equally technology-intensive. The results concern the timing of a war option rather than the net effect of ageing on war initiation. The mechanism is a demographic analogue of the green paradox.

title: Biopsy-confirmed celiac disease in Palestinian children and young adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus: prevalence and associated factors
summary: Background Celiac disease (CD) is more common in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) because of shared autoimmune mechanisms and underlying predispositions. CD can be asymptomatic despite the presence of intestinal histologic chan
content: Background Celiac disease (CD) is more common in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) because of shared autoimmune mechanisms and underlying predispositions. CD can be asymptomatic despite the presence of intestinal histologic changes, and therefore, early recognition of these predisposed patients allows early intervention and helps avoid complications. Despite the well-recognized association between T1DM and CD, no national screening program for CD exists in Palestine. Purpose This study aimed to determine the prevalence of CD and its associated demographic and clinical factors in Palestinian children and young adults with T1DM. Methods A cross-sectional study included 494 children and young adults (aged 1–33 years) with T1DM receiving care at three Palestinian Diabetes Institute centers between 2015 and 2020. Demographic data and information related to diabetes management, laboratory results, and family history were extracted from medical records. CD screening was performed by measuring anti–tissue transglutaminase antibody (anti-TTG Ab IgA) and total IgA levels. Patients with positive serology underwent duodenal biopsy. Univariate and Firth’s penalized logistic regression analyses were conducted. Results CD serology was positive in 75 patients (15.2%), and celiac disease was confirmed in 39 patients (7.9%) via biopsy. The sensitivity and specificity values were 89.7% and 91.2%, respectively, although these are upper-bound estimates that assume that non-biopsied seronegative participants were free of CD. Autoimmune thyroid disorders were detected in 5.5% of this population, primarily Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. Associated thyroid disease was related to biopsy-confirmed CD in univariate analysis (p < 0.05). In Firth’s penalized binary logistic regression, age, gender, and a family history of immune diseases did not predict CD, but having a related thyroid disease was associated with higher odds of biopsy-positive CD (AOR 5.12, 95% CI 1.65–13.90; p = 0.007). Conclusion This is the first study to indicate the prevalence of CD and its associated risk factors among Palestinian pediatric patients with T1DM. Approximately 8% of Palestinian children and young adults living with T1DM had biopsy-confirmed CD—a prevalence comparable with that in global reports. These results highlight the need for national CD screening guidelines in Palestinian patients with T1DM to facilitate early diagnosis and prevent long-term complications.

title: Global Regimes of Financialization: Power, Interdependence and Diversity in Finance-led Capitalism
summary: Since the early 1970s, the rise of financialization, or finance-led capitalism, has become the defining feature of the global political economy, reshaping states, markets, firms and societies worldwide. Yet, this transformation has taken ma
content: Since the early 1970s, the rise of financialization, or finance-led capitalism, has become the defining feature of the global political economy, reshaping states, markets, firms and societies worldwide. Yet, this transformation has taken markedly different characteristics across countries and regions. This raises a key question: how can we make sense of the coexistence of systemic coherence and empirical divergence in financialization? To address this question, the book advances a novel conceptual framework—Global Regimes of Financialization—arguing that financialization operates as an integrated global system of asymmetric financial interdependencies among three regimes—Hegemonic, Dependent and Patrimonial financialization—in which national economies play distinct and complementary roles, and wield different forms of financial power. Drawing on historical analysis and comparative evidence from case studies of the United States and the United Kingdom, the European Union, Latin America, the Baltic States, the Gulf Cooperation Council, Russia and China, the book traces the emergence and co-evolution of these regimes from the origins of the modern global financial system to the contemporary era of polycrisis. By placing financial hierarchy, interdependence and diversity at the centre of the analysis, Global Regimes of Financialization offers a ground-breaking perspective on the evolution of global capitalism and the forces shaping its future. This book will be of great interest to readers in comparative and international political economy, economic geography and contemporary economic history.

title: Chronic evoked seizures differentially worsen cognitive function and long-term neuropsychiatric comorbidities in Alzheimer's disease-related genotypes
summary: Variants in one of three deterministic risk genes - amyloid precursor protein (APP), presenilin 1 (PSEN1), or presenilin 2 (PSEN2) - lead to early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), which also carries a high risk of spontaneous seizures. Sei
content: Variants in one of three deterministic risk genes - amyloid precursor protein (APP), presenilin 1 (PSEN1), or presenilin 2 (PSEN2) - lead to early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), which also carries a high risk of spontaneous seizures. Seizures may worsen AD-related behavioral comorbidities, including depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment. Using the corneal kindling model of secondarily generalized focal seizures in two distinct aged male and female EOAD-associated mouse models, we assessed the interaction between investigator-initiated chronic seizures and EOAD genotype on AD-related behavioral comorbidities. Genotypes were selected to model amyloid-b; independent and dependent AD risk factors and included: PSEN2-N141I (amyloid-b; independent model) versus wild-type (PSEN2 control) mice, and APP/PS1 (amyloid-b dependent model) versus wild-type littermates (Tg-). Sham and fully kindled mice then underwent behavioral assessment in the saccharin preference test of anhedonia-like behavior, the Barnes maze test of spatial learning and memory, and a 67-hour home cage monitoring of circadian activity. EOAD genotype only significantly affected kindling acquisition of aged APP/PS1 females. However, there was no significant genotype or kindling effect on saccharin preference, suggesting no adverse impact on anhedonia-like behavior. Cognitive performance in the Barnes maze was significantly worsened by seizures exclusively in APP/PS1 female mice. However, seizures generally worsened Barnes maze performance of male PSEN2-N141I and PSEN2 control mice. Finally, chronic seizures consistently worsened exploratory behavior patterns during home cage circadian activity monitoring exclusively in APP/PS1 male and female mice. This study reveals the AD-related heterogeneity of seizure-evoked behavioral consequences on spatial working memory and circadian behaviors.

title: Implementing Academic Entrepreneurship to Advance Excellence in Entrepreneurship Education: Strategies for Building an Outstanding, Character-Driven, and Globally Engaged Universitas Bina Mandiri Gorontalo
source: International Journal of Management Research and Economics
summary: This article develops an integrative conceptual framework for implementing academic entrepreneurship to advance excellence in entrepreneurship education at Universitas Bina Mandiri Gorontalo. Using a purposive conceptual review and theory s
content: This article develops an integrative conceptual framework for implementing academic entrepreneurship to advance excellence in entrepreneurship education at Universitas Bina Mandiri Gorontalo. Using a purposive conceptual review and theory synthesis, it integrates perspectives on entrepreneurial universities, academic entrepreneurship, entrepreneurial learning, and stakeholder collaboration. The synthesis follows conceptual clarification, cross-perspective comparison, and framework integration, resulting in four interconnected domains: institutional foundations; teaching and learning processes; value creation mechanisms; and outputs, outcomes, and impacts. The framework proposes that institutional entrepreneurial support becomes educationally meaningful through authentic projects, mentoring, reflection, partner participation, and evidence-based assessment. Collaboration enables knowledge application, while multidimensional evaluation provides feedback for institutional improvement. Its conceptual originality lies in connecting established institutional, pedagogical, and value-creation perspectives through entrepreneurial learning rather than claiming new theoretical constructs. Academic integrity, equitable access, social responsibility, and global engagement operate across the domains. The framework provides implementation priorities for curriculum development, faculty support, partnerships, and evaluation, but its relationships remain theoretically proposed and require empirical validation.

title: Status, stakes and agency: A thematic analysis of plant protection perceptions among farmers and farm advisors
summary: Adverse trends such as the polycrisis, unfavourable economic and environmental conditions, and declining societal appreciation are factors that increase the number of farmers who fall under the workload or abandon their profession, thereby
content: Adverse trends such as the polycrisis, unfavourable economic and environmental conditions, and declining societal appreciation are factors that increase the number of farmers who fall under the workload or abandon their profession, thereby risking future food production. The listed extrinsic pressures are relatively well‐recognised, whereas farmers' intrinsic reasons and the socially informed themes associated with food production need better recognition. We draw on Clifford Geertz's concept of deep play to study farmers' and farm advisors' plant protection perceptions. The concept describes high‐stakes activities in which participation would be irrational in the event of potential failure. The data consist of four semi‐structured focus group interviews with Finnish farmers and farm advisors (n = 16). The interview themes included the sociocultural context of plant protection, farmers' and farm advisors' perceptions and identities, and their plant protection decisions. We used thematic analysis to examine the data. Our results show that farmers' and advisors' plant protection perceptions include considering themes of (1) status and cultural embeddedness, (2) existential and symbolic stakes and (3) strategic agency within symbolic systems. These themes are used in the creation of the ‘deep task’ concept, which describes plant protection as a socially meaningful activity in addition to being a technical procedure and an agronomic practice. The concept draws from the idea of high stakes in working life and describes characteristics of professions driven by a calling or a duty. Understanding agriculture and food production as a socially informed action is necessary to promote sustainable plant protection and effectively encourage and support farmers in their deep task of providing for life. title: Multi-level Marketing and Youth Employment in Nigeria: A case study of Kedi Health-Care Nigeria Limited (2006 – 2025)
summary: The main objective of the study is to assess the effectiveness of Multi-level Marketing (MLM) on youth employment in Nigeria, by taking Kedi Health Care industries Nigeria limited as a case study. The study is premised on the assumption tha
content: The main objective of the study is to assess the effectiveness of Multi-level Marketing (MLM) on youth employment in Nigeria, by taking Kedi Health Care industries Nigeria limited as a case study. The study is premised on the assumption that, MLM is a veritable means of mass employment opportunity in the country. Qualitative means of secondary data are utilized and descriptive method is employed in the analysis. It’s finally concluded that, MLM is not only a veritable means of youth employment but also a general means of livelihood to many people that can enhance the sustainable development initiatives in Nigeria. Some of the recommendations include: that domestic companies have to embrace MLM as a best method of distribution of goods and services and mass employment, governments have to incorporate MLM business in their youth employment initiatives and sustainable development programs, and youth organizations have to consider MLM business as a an alternative to unemployment problems in the country, among others.

title: Mapping Challenge-Based Learning in Sustainability Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Intellectual Structure, and Emerging Themes
summary: Background Challenge-Based Learning (CBL) is gaining increasing attention as a pedagogical approach that connects learning with complex, real-world challenges. Although research on CBL in education continues to evolve, a comprehensive mappi
content: Background Challenge-Based Learning (CBL) is gaining increasing attention as a pedagogical approach that connects learning with complex, real-world challenges. Although research on CBL in education continues to evolve, a comprehensive mapping of publication trends, scholarly contributions, thematic developments, and intellectual structure is still needed. This study aims to analyze the evolution and knowledge structure of CBL in education, as well as to identify future research opportunities. Methods This study employs a bibliometric analysis approach, examining 163 documents published between 2016 and 2026 across 86 publication sources. The analysis includes performance analysis, keyword co-occurrence, thematic mapping, citation and co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling to identify research trends, conceptual structures, and intellectual foundations. Results The research results show an annual publication growth rate of 30.66%, peaking at 49 documents in 2025. Mexico, the Netherlands, and Spain are the countries with the highest contributions, while Sustainability stands out as the most productive publication source. Dominant themes include challenge-based learning, sustainable development, engineering education, and higher education. Thematic analysis identifies sustainability and education as driving themes, whereas design thinking, co-creation, the circular economy, and student engagement emerge as relatively new topics. Co-citation analysis reveals three reference clusters and two author clusters, which together form the intellectual structure of the research. Conclusion Research on CBL (Challenge-Based Learning) in sustainability education is growing rapidly and is characterized by an increasingly diverse conceptual and intellectual structure. Although this research remains dominated by engineering and higher education contexts, evolving themes point to opportunities to expand the integration of CBL with sustainability competencies, interdisciplinary approaches, and action-oriented learning. These findings provide a bibliometric foundation for guiding future research on CBL in sustainability education.

title: Optimization path of seawater breeding validation improvement in China in the context of the ‘blue granary’ strategy
summary: Against the backdrop of China’s Big Food Vision and the rapid expansion of offshore and deep-sea aquaculture, developing and supplying new marine varieties is essential for advancing the ‘blue granary’ strategy and promoting high-quality gr
content: Against the backdrop of China’s Big Food Vision and the rapid expansion of offshore and deep-sea aquaculture, developing and supplying new marine varieties is essential for advancing the ‘blue granary’ strategy and promoting high-quality growth in marine aquaculture. China has a mature approval system for new marine aquaculture varieties, with increasing approvals. However, the sector still faces a structural paradox of rising domestic output while relying on imported germplasm, particularly for key farmed species such as Pacific white shrimp. Therefore, the central issue is not whether an approval system exists but whether the current institutional framework can effectively identify and promote varieties that meet the needs of modern marine aquaculture. The study uses data from the China Fishery Statistical Yearbook (2011–2024), current regulatory documents, and relevant domestic and international scholarship. It combines a literature review, institutional comparison, and policy text analysis to examine the operational characteristics and practical constraints of China’s approval system for new marine varieties and how institutional bottlenecks—by shaping approval efficiency, the assessment of regional adaptability, and mechanisms of market diffusion—ultimately hamper commercialization. The findings show that significant shortcomings persist in the approval body configuration, testing procedures, regional suitability evaluation, post-approval oversight, and approval–market extension relationship. These shortcomings create a clear gap between formal approval and successful market uptake, which weakens breeding incentives, slows diffusion of new varieties, and undermines the competitiveness of domestically developed germplasm. This study makes three contributions: First, it shifts attention from aquatic seed industry development to institutional approval of marine varieties. Second, it identifies the internal pathways through which institutional efficiency shapes commercialization outcomes. Third, it contends that international experience should be adapted to China’s specific stage of marine aquaculture development and institutional context, rather than transferred wholesale. Accordingly, the study proposes a classified approval framework, differentiated approval procedures, and a strengthened system of regulation and public support to enhance the conversion efficiency of new marine varieties, bolster China’s capacity for autonomous marine germplasm security, and support implementation of the ‘blue granary’ strategy.

八大重点任务之三：坚持改革攻坚，增强高质量发展动力活力
用改革的办法解决发展中的问题（八大重点任务看落实）
2026年是“十五五”开局之年，我国坚持改革攻坚，增强高质量发展动力活力。这一年，改革有破有立，立中有破、破中有立实现了动态平衡，各项改革举措在系统集成中释放出更大效能。
破卡点、堵点。加快制定全国统一大市场建设条例，以法规的制度刚性破除阻碍全国统一大市场建设卡点、堵点。今年以来，各地市场监管部门公平竞争审查抽查发现并督促废止、修改妨碍统一市场和公平竞争的违规文件1万余件，约谈相关政府部门59次；31个省份全面开展地方标准清理，截至6月底已废止地方标准7400余项。公平竞争审查“长牙带刺”，标准区域壁垒加快破除，全国统一大市场建设纵深推进。
破“内卷”。今年《政府工作报告》关于整治“内卷式”竞争的表述，从去年“综合整治”调整为“深入整治”，“反内卷”迈入“深水区”。10月16日国务院常务会议原则通过价格法（修正草案），依法依规治理低价无序竞争。在新能源汽车、锂电池和光伏产业等行业，开展标准提升行动，发布相关国家标准72项，助力淘汰落后产能，引领行业提质升级。
破失信。加紧清理拖欠企业账款，9月，国办印发关于加强中小企业回款难问题治理有关工作的通知，提出建立健全大型企业账款监测机制，对故意拉长账期的大型企业，进行约谈并督促整改，拒不改正的，依法依规联合惩治，被认定为严重失信的，依法依规实施失信惩戒。
立效率。制定和实施进一步深化国资国企改革方案。新一轮战略性重组不再单纯追求企业体量，而是明确同类业务横向整合、产业链上下游纵向整合，规范化解同质化竞争、重复建设问题，提升国有资本整体配置效率。
立公平。完善民营经济促进法配套法规政策。多地密集出台民营经济专项地方性法规，多省份民营经济促进条例先后施行，填补区域立法空白，优化民营经济发展环境，保证各类经济组织公平参与市场竞争。
立共赢。平台经济正深度嵌入日常生活。今年以来，监管部门叫停外卖平台“补贴大战”，在同城货运领域进行反垄断合规整改，查处在线旅游平台垄断大案等，推动平台企业和平台内经营者、劳动者共赢发展。
当前，我国经济发展中老问题、新挑战仍然不少，外部环境变化影响加深，国内供强需弱矛盾突出，重点领域风险隐患较多。改革的担子更重、挑战更大。容易的、皆大欢喜的改革已经完成了，好吃的肉都吃掉了，剩下的都是难啃的硬骨头。
惟其艰难，更显勇毅。发展中的问题要在发展中解决，要敢于啃硬骨头，敢于涉险滩，坚持改革攻坚，定能推动经济社会高质量发展不断取得新成效，不断满足人民日益增长的美好生活需要。（林丽鹂）

title: Gross primary productivity of forest ecosystems in a subtropical city and its decadal climatic and environmental drivers
summary: Vegetation plays a vital role in modulating climate and the carbon cycle on land through processes like photosynthesis, also known as gross primary production (GPP). The significant presence of vegetation in Hong Kong, covering over 70 % of
content: Vegetation plays a vital role in modulating climate and the carbon cycle on land through processes like photosynthesis, also known as gross primary production (GPP). The significant presence of vegetation in Hong Kong, covering over 70 % of the land area, highlights the potential for terrestrial carbon sink to contribute to achieving carbon neutrality in such a metropolitan city. Meanwhile, the terrestrial ecosystem is also influenced by climatic and environmental factors. This study investigates the historical spatiotemporal dynamics of GPP in the subtropical forests of Hong Kong and the key drivers behind its trend and interannual variability between 2002 and 2018. We used the Terrestrial Ecosystem Model in R-Hong Kong (TEMIR-HK), a localized process-based ecophysiological model, to evaluate the changes in GPP induced by changing CO 2 concentration, temperature, ozone (O 3) concentration, and changing leaf area index (LAI) shaped by these factors as well as land use. Simulation results indicate an increasing trend of GPP, with an average annual GPP of 1.75 TgC yr −1, which is around 15 % of the annual total anthropogenic carbon emission from Hong Kong, suggesting a limited but indispensable potential of forestry to achieve city-level carbon neutrality. Model simulations of GPP show satisfactory results when spatially comparing with satellite-derived GPP dataset (R =0.89), with slight difference of +8.7 % on average. Factorial simulations reveal LAI changes dominate both trend (+0.0134 TgC yr −2) and interannual variability (2.77 × 10 −2 TgC yr −1) of GPP in Hong Kong. This result highlights that local-scale reforestation could influence GPP trend over the whole city and emphasizes the importance on the accuracy of LAI input in ecosystem-scale photosynthesis modelling. This work contributes to improving the scientific understanding on subtropical forest ecosystems, and highlights the potential, though limited, of Hong Kong forests to play their parts in working toward carbon neutrality targets.

title: Pathways to circular and regenerative urban agriculture through stakeholder-informed approaches
summary: Conventional agriculture typically relies on linear production systems that degrade soil and undermine sustainable resource management and contribute to climate change. Urban and peri-urban agriculture can facilitate the closure of nutrient
content: Conventional agriculture typically relies on linear production systems that degrade soil and undermine sustainable resource management and contribute to climate change. Urban and peri-urban agriculture can facilitate the closure of nutrient loops left open in conventional systems, as its proximity to nutrient rich residues and waste provides a local supply for nutrient recovery and reincorporation into agricultural soils. Realizing this shift requires systemically restructuring how food, waste, and land are governed. This study applies the Three Horizons framework to structure stakeholder discussions across present conditions, emerging opportunities, and desired futures. Using grounded theory qualitative analysis, our study inductively derives seven cross-sectoral themes alongside barriers, stakeholder actions, and transformation pathways for advancing healthy soils and sustainable urban and peri-urban agriculture through carbon and nutrient circularity. Our results demonstrate the need for distributed leadership and intersectoral collaboration to enable circular practices such as decentralized and proximity-based waste management, community-led agricultural food networks, and environmental stewardship through procurement and land policy. These actions converge into three interlinking pathways that scale circularity and address system complexity: 1) localized material and knowledge flows; 2) socio-economic reconfiguration through communities and markets; and 3) policy and planning integration for resilience. These findings highlight that advancing circularity requires not only technical innovation but also participatory governance, market realignment, and regulatory adaptation. By integrating stakeholder perspectives into transformation design, the results demonstrate how a transformation to healthy soils for sustainable urban and peri-urban agriculture can be positioned as foundational infrastructure for regenerative urban and regional futures.

title: Fifty-five crowdsourced designs assessing carbon pricing support in the USA
summary: A carbon price is an effective and cost-efficient policy to mitigate emissions, yet low public acceptance and limited political support remain major barriers to its widespread implementation. This crowdsourced ‘many-designs’ project present
content: A carbon price is an effective and cost-efficient policy to mitigate emissions, yet low public acceptance and limited political support remain major barriers to its widespread implementation. This crowdsourced ‘many-designs’ project presents results from 55 behavioural interventions on real-world support for carbon pricing, independently developed by international research teams. By implementing all designs simultaneously with almost 20,000 US residents, this preregistered study shows very small positive but statistically significant effects of behavioural interventions on a set of design-specific proxies of real-world support (Cohen’s d = 0.06; 99.5% confidence interval (CI) 0.001 to 0.124) and on 4 out of 5 common measures of stated support (Cohen’s d values 0.06–0.08; 99.5% CIs from 0.006 to 0.112 and from 0.020 to 0.133; between 1.7 and 2.4 percentage points in increased support across outcomes), including the willingness to endorse a carbon price that internalizes the social costs of US$120 per ton of CO 2 emissions (d = 0.06; 99.5% CI 0.012 to 0.118). Furthermore, the results reveal low-to-medium between-study heterogeneity (τ = 0.07–0.12). Lastly, we identify strong overconfidence among research teams regarding the expected effects of their interventions and those of their peers, indicating a miscalibration of community expectations.

title: Sensitive Determination of Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 Using a Dual-Emission Ratiometric Fluorescent Probe Composed of Sulfur Quantum Dots and Gold Nanoclusters
summary: Coomassie Brilliant Blue (CBB) is widely used for protein staining, but its residues may pose environmental and biological risks, creating a need for simple and sensitive detection methods. In this work, a dual-emission ratiometric fluoresc
content: Coomassie Brilliant Blue (CBB) is widely used for protein staining, but its residues may pose environmental and biological risks, creating a need for simple and sensitive detection methods. In this work, a dual-emission ratiometric fluorescent probe was constructed from sulfur quantum dots (S-QDs; blue emission at 430 nm) and BSA-templated gold nanoclusters (Au NCs; red emission at 640 nm). CBB preferentially attenuated the Au NC emission through the inner filter effect (IFE). The fluorescence intensity ratio(F 430 / F 640) exhibited a linear correlation with CBB concentration from 0.1 to 100 µM (R 2 = 0.991). The limit of detection was calculated to be 0.01 µM (3 σ), around six times lower than that of the single-emission Au NC probe, accompanied by improved calibration sensitivity. The spectral overlap between CBB absorption and Au NC emission, together with the nearly unchanged fluorescence lifetime, supported IFE as the predominant sensing mechanism and indicated that dynamic quenching was not dominant. The probe was applied to CBB determination in a BSA model matrix and two real samples, and the results agreed well with those obtained by HPLC-MS/MS. By using the S-QD emission as an internal reference, the ratiometric strategy reduced common-mode signal fluctuations and improved measurement reliability, providing a potential approach for CBB determination in food-related and biological matrices.

title: GREEN ECONOMY IN THE WESTERN BALKANS COMPARED TO EU COUNTRIES
source: International Congress From Research to Application
summary: This paper examines the state and advancement of the green economy in the Western Balkans countries compared to European Union (EU) countries. Through a comparative analysis, the study identifies challenges, opportunities, and policy approa
content: This paper examines the state and advancement of the green economy in the Western Balkans countries compared to European Union (EU) countries. Through a comparative analysis, the study identifies challenges, opportunities, and policy approaches for fostering sustainable economic growth in these regions. The analyses are based on data from international organizations, academic studies, and policy reports, providing an overview of environmental, social, and economic indicators.

title: The system value of flexible electricity demand in a 100% renewable European energy system
source: International Journal of Sustainable Energy Planning and Management
summary: Flexible and energy-intensive technologies such as power-to-X, smart electric vehicle charging, and energy storage, including thermal storage, are expected to play a critical role in providing system flexibility in renewable energy systems.
content: Flexible and energy-intensive technologies such as power-to-X, smart electric vehicle charging, and energy storage, including thermal storage, are expected to play a critical role in providing system flexibility in renewable energy systems. However, the role and potential of flexible demands in households and industries remain less certain and have not yet been thoroughly investigated. Based on holistic energy system modelling in EnergyPLAN, this study explores the potential of households, industry and electric vehicles to contribute flexibility and the benefits observed at the system level. It is found that there are tangible benefits observed in terms of improved system efficiency, peak power plant operation, and cost savings. Total primary energy savings up to 4.4% (theoretical upper bound, 100% flexible demand on a 4-week basis). Within a plausible range, savings of 2.0-2.9% are identified in a renewable energy system, compared with only 0.5-0.7% in a baseline system.

title: Reserving carbon storage for unavoidable emissions replaces fossil fuels with carbon cycles in climate-neutral scenarios
summary: European climate-neutrality strategies rely on geological carbon storage but leave open which emissions can use it. A conditional approach reserves storage for unavoidable emissions, such as from cement and waste incineration, whereas a tec
content: European climate-neutrality strategies rely on geological carbon storage but leave open which emissions can use it. A conditional approach reserves storage for unavoidable emissions, such as from cement and waste incineration, whereas a technology-open approach allows it wherever it lowers costs. Here we compare both approaches in climate-neutral scenarios of a European energy and industry model with regional detail for Germany, endogenous industrial processes, refineries and CO 2 pipelines. In the technology-open approach, the system keeps fossil oil and gas and stores four times the unavoidable emissions. In the conditional approach, fossil fuel use is 97 % lower, steelmaking moves away from fossil gas and refineries turn from emission sources into sinks. Pipeline routes barely change, but capacity halves. System costs rise by 2.8 %, mostly for wind and solar expansion. This cost gap shrinks with higher fossil prices, more biomass or costlier direct air capture. The conditional approach is far less exposed to fossil price shocks, which sharply raise fuel costs in the technology-open approach.

title: Toward plasma-assisted fuel synthesis from CO₂ and water: Ethanol detection with Fe-loaded LTA zeolite
summary: Fe-loaded Linde type A (LTA) zeolite was examined in a material screening study of in-liquid plasma treatment of CO₂-supplied water. Among the materials screened, Fe/LTA gave the highest quantified ethanol amount. At a nominal Fe amount of
content: Fe-loaded Linde type A (LTA) zeolite was examined in a material screening study of in-liquid plasma treatment of CO₂-supplied water. Among the materials screened, Fe/LTA gave the highest quantified ethanol amount. At a nominal Fe amount of 10 mmol, treatment at 4 kV and 50 kHz for 15 min with a CO₂ flow rate of 2.0 L min⁻¹ yielded recovered amounts of 68.33 µg ethanol and 2.43 µg acetone. Estimated limits of quantification of 0.372, 0.342 and 0.112 mg L⁻¹ for acetone, methanol and ethanol, respectively, were applied to individual liquid fractions; methanol was at or below its estimated limit. Ethanol accounted for 95.9% of the uncorrected quantified carbon subtotal for these three compounds. Selected-ion monitoring chromatograms showed a response near the ethanol-standard retention time for Fe/LTA under CO₂ with plasma. This response was more prominent than those in the displayed plasma-off, Ar-plasma, bare-LTA and pure-water control traces. These findings identify Fe/LTA as a material of interest for aqueous plasma processing toward fuel synthesis from CO₂ and water.

title: Effect of QPQ treatment on microstructure and properties of 42CrMo4 steel
summary: QPQ treatment is a composite salt bath surface modification technology widely used to improve the wear and corrosion resistance of ferrous components. In this work, 42CrMo4 steel specimens were subjected to QPQ treatment to investigate the
content: QPQ treatment is a composite salt bath surface modification technology widely used to improve the wear and corrosion resistance of ferrous components. In this work, 42CrMo4 steel specimens were subjected to QPQ treatment to investigate the evolution of microstructure, microhardness, wear performance and corrosion resistance. The cross-sectional microstructure of the modified layer was characterized using optical microscopy (OM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). The results show that a dense compound layer and diffusion layer are formed on the steel surface after QPQ treatment. The surface microhardness is significantly enhanced compared with the untreated substrate. Wear tests demonstrate that the friction coefficient and wear rate decrease obviously, owing to the hard nitride compound layer. Electrochemical corrosion tests reveal that the corrosion resistance is improved effectively. This work indicates that QPQ treatment can simultaneously optimize the wear and corrosion properties of 42CrMo4 steel, which provides technical support for the application of 42CrMo4 gears in heavy-load mechanical equipment.

title: Investigating Surfactant-Induced Modulation of Electron–Hole Mobility Asymmetry in Graphene/hBN Heterostructures
summary: In this work, noncovalent surfactants (sodium octyl sulfate and sodium cholate) functionalization is demonstrated as an effective and reproducible strategy for engineering carrier-selective transport in graphene/hexagonal boron nitride (hBN
content: In this work, noncovalent surfactants (sodium octyl sulfate and sodium cholate) functionalization is demonstrated as an effective and reproducible strategy for engineering carrier-selective transport in graphene/hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) heterostructures. Temperature-dependent electrical measurements revealed that sodium octyl sulfate (SOS) promotes electron-dominated conduction, whereas sodium cholate (SC) induces hole-selective transport. These opposite transport behaviors were consistently observed across multiple devices and were quantitatively confirmed through normalized mobility asymmetry factors and mobility ratio analyses. The results indicate that surfactant adsorption modifies carrier scattering, electrostatic screening, and charge-transfer interactions at the graphene interface, leading to distinct electron–hole transport asymmetries. The persistence of these effects over the investigated temperature range indicates that the observed carrier selectivity originates from stable interfacial interactions rather than thermal fluctuations. Furthermore, the magnitude of the transport asymmetry exceeded device-to-device variability, indicating that it originates from surfactant adsorption rather than from fabrication-related variability. The findings establish molecular functionalization as a scalable, solution-based approach for tuning charge transport symmetry in graphene-enabled devices without significantly disrupting their lattice structure. This capability provides new opportunities for optimizing graphene-based electronics, sensors, and low-power devices. Furthermore, the asymmetry analysis framework developed in this work provides a quantitative basis for assessing carrier-selective transport in graphene/hBN devices and may be extended to other van der Waals heterostructures in future work.

title: Interfacial design and spin effects in room temperature magnetic photocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen production
summary: Photocatalytic water splitting is a promising route to sustainable hydrogen, but charge recombination and sluggish oxygen evolution still limit its efficiency. Adding a magnetic or spin degree of freedom to the catalyst is a growing strateg
content: Photocatalytic water splitting is a promising route to sustainable hydrogen, but charge recombination and sluggish oxygen evolution still limit its efficiency. Adding a magnetic or spin degree of freedom to the catalyst is a growing strategy for addressing both. This review examines room-temperature magnetic (“quantum magnet”) materials for hydrogen production, and covers four areas. First, we survey the materials: spinel ferrites, magnetic insulators and spin-polarized oxides, and above-room-temperature two-dimensional magnets such as Fe 3 GaTe 2. Second, we analyze interface and heterojunction designs that couple a magnetic component to a light-absorbing semiconductor. Third, we compare the synergies between magnetism and photocatalysis, from Lorentz-force and spin-polarization effects to field-free chirality-induced spin selectivity. Fourth, we benchmark reported performance across ferrite photocatalysts, field-assisted systems, oxygen-evolution photo anodes and existing reviews. Magnetic-field gains are real but moderate, mostly in the 1.3–3× range. Across the few comparable studies the gain rises with field strength (1.33× at 108 mT, 1.5× at 140 mT, 2.97× at 500 mT), but the systems differ too much to separate field from material, and interface engineering alone often provides comparable gains. Two gaps are evident: few studies include controls that separate magnetic effects from thermal and mass-transport effects, and field-free spin routes and two-dimensional room-temperature magnets have not yet been shown to evolve hydrogen. We close with priorities for standardized reporting and for the design of scalable, low-field or field-free photocatalytic devices.

title: Porphyrin Covalent Organic Frameworks as Interatomic Catalytic Messengers in Electrocatalysis: Recent Advances and Mechanistic Insights
summary: The development of efficient, stable, and structurally programmable electrocatalysts is essential for advancing the global energy transition and achieving carbon‐neutrality goals. Porphyrins provide an ideal scaffold for atomically disperse
content: The development of efficient, stable, and structurally programmable electrocatalysts is essential for advancing the global energy transition and achieving carbon‐neutrality goals. Porphyrins provide an ideal scaffold for atomically dispersed metal sites, owing to their tunable M‐N 4 coordination, adjustable electronic structures and extended conjugation. Porphyrin‐based covalent organic frameworks (Por‐COFs), which combine these molecular properties with structural designability, high surface area and chemical stability, can act as catalytic messengers that bridge atomic‐level metal active sites and reactive interfaces to mediate electron redistribution, proton transfer, intermediate stabilization and interfacial charge transfer, and consequently promote efficient electrocatalytic conversion. Herein, the structural features of Por‐COFs for electrocatalysis are outlined first, and then the molecular design strategies, including porphyrin monomer functionalization, topological regulation and covalent bond engineering are examined systematically. Subsequently, the mechanisms for enhancing the activity, selectivity and stability of the CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR), hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), oxygen evolution reaction (OER), oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), electrocatalytic nitrogen cycle (NO 3 RR, NO 2 RR and NRR) and 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation reaction (HMFOR) by applying these design principles are discussed. Finally, the key challenges in practical applications are identified and the future development directions are proposed. This review provides a comprehensive overview from precise molecular design to efficient electrocatalysis, offering insights for the industrial translation of Por‐COF‐based systems.

title: Mechanistic Understanding of Water-Assisted CO2 Mineralization in Forsterite from Molecular Simulations
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Forsterite has significant potential for permanent CO2 mineral storage, but coupled interfacial mechanisms governing water activation, Mg2+ release, and early stage magnesium carbonate formation remain incompletely understood. Reactive mole
content: Forsterite has significant potential for permanent CO2 mineral storage, but coupled interfacial mechanisms governing water activation, Mg2+ release, and early stage magnesium carbonate formation remain incompletely understood. Reactive molecular dynamics simulations investigated CO2-water-forsterite interfacial behavior across temperature, pressure, fluid composition, and protonation conditions. Under simulated conditions, water enables sustained surface reactivity by promoting Mg–O bond disruption, proton transfer reactions associated with aqueous CO2 speciation, and Mg2+ dehydration, a key kinetic barrier to Mg-carbonate association. Dry forsterite exhibits lower initial CO2 adsorption and shows limited sustained carbonate formation relative to water-containing systems, indicating that water-mediated surface activation is necessary for sustained carbonation. Fluid composition has a nonmonotonic effect on near-surface Mg-carbonate formation: an intermediate water-to-CO2 ratio produces the highest near-surface carbonate density, whereas CO2-rich conditions disrupt the interfacial hydration network and suppress cluster growth. Elevated temperature and pressure jointly enhance Mg-carbonate association, with pressure sensitivity increasing at higher temperatures. Protonation conditions alter carbonate speciation and cluster morphology: alkaline conditions favor rapid formation of larger, more connected Mg-carbonate clusters, whereas acidic conditions yield smaller, less connected aggregates. These results clarify molecular-scale controls on forsterite carbonation and provide mechanistic guidance for designing reservoir and engineered CO2 mineral storage systems.

title: Urban digitalization for cleaner development: nonlinear effects on CO2 emission intensity under China’s dual-transition policies
summary: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between digital empowerment and urban carbon emission intensity using panel data for 295 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2006 to 2023. A two-way fixed-effects model with a quadratic specif
content: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between digital empowerment and urban carbon emission intensity using panel data for 295 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2006 to 2023. A two-way fixed-effects model with a quadratic specification is employed, and the inverted U-shaped relationship is further verified using the turning point and the Lind-Mehlum U-test. The results show that digital empowerment initially increases carbon emission intensity but reduces it after a threshold is crossed. The findings remain robust after controlling for industrial structure, excluding 2020–2022, and using lagged explanatory variables. Mechanism analysis provides the strongest support for the energy-intensity channel, while evidence for virtual agglomeration is partial and the results for artificial intelligence are measurement-sensitive. Evidence for the digital-infrastructure channel is interpreted more cautiously because of its potential overlap with the digital empowerment index, although a reconstructed index excluding infrastructure-related components provides additional support. Moreover, complementary policy-based analyses using the Broadband China pilot, including conventional TWFE and stacked difference-in-differences specifications, show a significant reduction in carbon emission intensity, with parallel-trend and placebo tests providing additional support for the credibility of the policy-based evidence.

title: A sustainable cellulose-based solid acid catalyst for efficient 5-ethoxymethylfurfural production from biomass-derived HMF
summary: The development of effective and sustainable catalysts for biomass conversion is essential for advancing green fuel technologies. In this work, a solid acid catalyst was prepared by immobilizing 4-(chloromethyl)benzoic acid onto cellulose t
