content: The development of effective and sustainable catalysts for biomass conversion is essential for advancing green fuel technologies. In this work, a solid acid catalyst was prepared by immobilizing 4-(chloromethyl)benzoic acid onto cellulose through covalent bonding between the aryl chloride moieties and the hydroxyl groups of cellulose. The resulting material, designated as BA-cellulose, was thoroughly characterized via various techniques, confirming successful functionalization and high acid site density. The catalytic activity of BA-cellulose was assessed in the etherification of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) with ethanol to yield 5-ethoxymethylfurfural (EMF), a promising renewable biofuel. Reaction factors such as catalyst loading, reaction temperature, and reaction time were optimized. The catalyst revealed high activity, selectivity, and excellent reusability over multiple cycles without significant loss of performance. The catalyst was also employed for the efficient production of EMF from renewable carbohydrate sources. It is worth to mention that this work aligns with the principles of green chemistry by utilizing a biodegradable support and minimizing hazardous waste. The developed system offers potential for scalable application in biomass valorization and biofuel production.

title: A Combined Life Cycle Assessment and Multi-Scenario Photovoltaic Modelling Framework for Assessing Building Decarbonization in Nusantara
summary: Indonesia’s new capital, Nusantara, aims for net-zero emissions (NZE) by 2045, placing stringent decarbonization pressures on high-density residential developments. In tropical climates, operational cooling has historically dominated buildi
content: Indonesia’s new capital, Nusantara, aims for net-zero emissions (NZE) by 2045, placing stringent decarbonization pressures on high-density residential developments. In tropical climates, operational cooling has historically dominated building emissions; however, modern energy-efficient designs and aggressive decarbonization timelines necessitate a re-evaluation of whole-life carbon impacts. This study introduces an integrated BIM-LCA-GSA framework to conduct a 20-year cradle-to-grave Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of a newly constructed 12-storey residential building in Nusantara. The baseline results reveal total emissions of 1.73 × 10 7 kg CO 2 e, demonstrating that Embodied Carbon (EC) from building materials (50.4%) has surpassed Operational Carbon (OC) (49.6%) as the primary emission hotspot over the 20-year horizon. To mitigate these impacts, two façade-integrated Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) scenarios were modeled. The optimal 93.0 kWp BIPV system successfully reduced overall building emissions by 10.5% and achieved a financial payback period of 16.3 years, proving its techno-economic viability without feed-in tariffs. Furthermore, variance-based Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA) confirmed that operational electricity and structural material manufacturing govern the vast majority of output variance. The findings underscore that achieving NZE requires robust policies mandating both operational efficiency and structural material decarbonization.

title: A RULE-BASED ARCHITECTURAL DECISION FRAMEWORK FOR DAYLIGHT-RESPONSIVE FACADE DESIGN INSPIRED BY VERNACULAR SHADING SYSTEMS
summary: Building façades play a critical role in regulating the interaction between indoor and outdoor environments, making daylight-responsive design an essential component of sustainable architecture. This study proposes a rule-based architectura
content: Building façades play a critical role in regulating the interaction between indoor and outdoor environments, making daylight-responsive design an essential component of sustainable architecture. This study proposes a rule-based architectural decision framework inspired by vernacular shading systems to support façade design through explicit computational decision rules. Mashrabiya and breeze block patterns commonly found in Türkiye were examined, and three geometric configurations (square, circular, and hexagonal) with two opening sizes (20×20 cm and 5×5 cm) were selected as the primary design parameters. Annual daylight performance was evaluated using Spatial Daylight Autonomy (sDA) through parametric simulations conducted in Rhino, Grasshopper, and Honeybee for three representative climatic regions in Türkiye: İstanbul, Adana, and Erzurum. The simulation results reveal consistent relationships between climatic conditions, pattern geometry, opening size, and daylight performance. Larger openings perform more effectively under temperate climatic conditions, smaller openings provide better daylight performance in hot climates, and square geometries demonstrate superior performance in cold climates. These recurring relationships were formalised into explicit architectural decision rules that associate predefined input parameters with climate-responsive façade design recommendations. Rather than presenting simulation outcomes as isolated findings, the proposed framework transforms vernacular design knowledge into a reproducible architectural decision-support approach for early-stage façade design.

title: Configuration and Evolution of China’s Marine Carbon Inclusion Policy: A Stage-Theme-Instrument Analysis (2015-2026)
summary: As an emerging governance arrangement in China, marine carbon inclusion refers to integrating blue carbon into the voluntary carbon market and adopting economic incentives to promote the sustainable management of marine carbon ecosystems, t
content: As an emerging governance arrangement in China, marine carbon inclusion refers to integrating blue carbon into the voluntary carbon market and adopting economic incentives to promote the sustainable management of marine carbon ecosystems, thereby linking public low-carbon actions with the realisation of marine carbon-sink value. It incorporates dispersed emission-reduction activities and marine ecological conservation practices into an institutional framework through which their carbon contributions can be quantified, incentivised, and potentially linked to value-realisation mechanisms. Focusing on China’s marine carbon inclusion policies, this study develops a three-dimensional analytical framework comprising policy stages, themes, and instruments. Based on a quantitative analysis of 65 policy documents, this study examines policy evolution, configuration, and patterns of instrument adoption. The study further identifies key areas for policy refinement, aiming to consolidate the policy system and improve the allocation of policy resources. The study finds that China’s marine carbon inclusion policy has evolved through successive phases, from promoting the concept to building institutions and finally to implementing and governing the system. A notable finding is that China’s policy instruments tend to focus on specific themes and stages, but there remains a need for better coordination across different policy areas. China’s marine carbon inclusion policy also faces an insufficient level of institutionalisation, uneven policy attention, and an imbalanced instrument structure. The study recommends strengthening national strategic planning, improving thematic coordination, optimising the mix of policy instruments, and establishing clearer mechanisms for marine carbon-sink value realisation.

title: Regulatory Dimensions of Digital Sovereignty in the Energy Sector
summary: Digital sovereignty has become the loadstar of EU industrial policies. But it does not have a widely agreed meaning. This Article explores this apparent paradox with regard to the twin transition in the energy sector. The main argument is t
content: Digital sovereignty has become the loadstar of EU industrial policies. But it does not have a widely agreed meaning. This Article explores this apparent paradox with regard to the twin transition in the energy sector. The main argument is that the multiple meanings of digital sovereignty allow the EU and the Member States to implement regulatory measures that shape their industrial policies. A distinction between the collective and the individual dimension of digital sovereignty is proposed to analyze the contents of such regulatory choices in two domains: cybersecurity and data protection. Reference is made to both EU horizontal legislation and to legislation in the energy sector. The Article advances four recommendations, related to the joint assessment of the collective and individual dimensions, the geopolitical relevance of sustainability standards, the mechanisms to control supply chains, and the conflicting sovereignty claims in the energy sector. The Article also contributes to the wider debate about the regulation of digital technologies.

title: Ancestors of Arylmalonate Decarboxylase Show Increased Activity, Stability, and Stereoselectivity
summary: Bacterial arylmalonate decarboxylase (AMDase) generates a wide spectrum of α-chiral carboxylic acids in high optical purity, including several non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and chiral building blocks. However, extant AMDase from Bor
content: Bacterial arylmalonate decarboxylase (AMDase) generates a wide spectrum of α-chiral carboxylic acids in high optical purity, including several non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and chiral building blocks. However, extant AMDase from Bordetella bronchiseptica (BbAMDase) and related enzymes of the same family have three main limitations: (i) low operational and thermal stability, (ii) limited substrate spectrum regarding the size of the smaller substituent on the α-C-atom, and (iii) low stereoselectivity towards α-alkenyl-α-alkyl malonic acids. To address these limitations, we expanded the structural diversity of the AMDase family by ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). The phylogenetic analysis of the decarboxylase revealed conserved structural in the hydrophobic active-site cavity, a catalytic motif crucial for activity and selectivity. AMDase ancestors showed higher stability, activity, and, in one case, also stereoselectivity than BbAMDase. While variation of amino acids of the hydrophobic pockets had increased activity and expanded substrate scope in previous work, this structural motif was found to be remarkably conserved throughout the reconstructed ancestors. The substrate scope of the ancestors towards a set of arylmalonic and alkenylmalonic acids was very similar to that of BbAMDase. Inversion of the stereoselectivity by switching the catalytic cysteine residues (G74C/C188G, numbering according to BbAMDase) was successful for ancestor N5, but reduced the activity of evolutionary more distant N131. This shows that a direct transfer of mutations between related enzymes might not be possible even if the active site cavities are conserved. Ancestor N131 exhibited a 294-fold improvement in half-life time and a 1.8-fold increased specific activity (25.1 U mg–1) toward 2-methyl-2-phenyl malonate in a preparative scale application. Computational analysis provided a potential explanation for improved stability by an increase in surface Glu side chains, which form a protective hydration shell that enhances solubility and mitigates aggregation. Ancestor N31 formed 2-methyl-but-3-enoic acid from its corresponding malonic acid in high optical purity (99.7% eeR).

title: The Role of IS in Trust Building: Affordances for the Global Hydrogen Supply Chain
summary: The urgent demand for green energy has raised interest in the viability of global hydrogen supply chains connecting potential sources in the Global South and Australia with customers in the Northern Hemisphere. As technical, logistical, and
content: The urgent demand for green energy has raised interest in the viability of global hydrogen supply chains connecting potential sources in the Global South and Australia with customers in the Northern Hemisphere. As technical, logistical, and economic uncertainties in these emerging supply chains give rise to trust concerns, the role of information systems in building trust must be assessed. Previous research has acknowledged the importance of interorganizational trust, but the types of trust concerns in supply chains remain underexplored. Motivated by advancing the impact of information systems on sustainable, trusted energy supply chains, this study identifies and clusters trust concerns as relational contexts using the case of hydrogen supply chains. By matching trust-building techniques as functional enablers, we provide specific advice on how these concerns can be mitigated. Empirical evidence was sourced through 19 semi-structured interviews with supply chain experts from Germany and Australia, which we analyzed using the Gioia methodology. We identified five affordances for trust building (transparency and traceability, economic risk coordination, scenario planning, knowledge sharing and learning, and communication). This paper advances the body of knowledge on interorganizational trust and outlines the potential for information systems to elevate hydrogen as a reliable energy source in the future.

title: The Green "Trojan Horses": A Corpus-Assisted Critical Discourse Analysis of News Coverage of Chinese Electric Vehicles and Trade Measures in North America and Europe
source: Lingue Culture Mediazioni - Languages Cultures Mediation (LCM Journal)
summary: As countries accelerate electric vehicle (EV) adoption, restrictions on Chinese imports have intensified debates over sustainability, industrial policy, and international relations. This study adopts corpus-assisted critical discourse analy
content: As countries accelerate electric vehicle (EV) adoption, restrictions on Chinese imports have intensified debates over sustainability, industrial policy, and international relations. This study adopts corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis to examine coverage of Chinese EVs in newspapers from the United States, Canada, Ireland, and the United Kingdom. Keyword, headline, and concordance analyses are used to investigate how newspapers frame environmental objectives in relation to competition, protectionism, and broader geopolitical interests. Left-leaning outlets generally foreground climate concerns, whereas centre-right newspapers place greater emphasis on regulatory costs, industrial competitiveness, and security risks. Across editorial orientations, China is portrayed as both a key partner in electrification and a potential economic and geopolitical threat. Sustainability thus emerges as a politically contested policy objective.

title: A dynamic material flow analysis–system dynamics model of Japan’s special steel supply chain: toward decision support for critical mineral supply resilience
summary: Critical minerals are essential for clean-energy technologies and established industrial materials. Japan’s special steel industry uses alloying elements such as nickel, chromium, and molybdenum, and disruptions in their supply may affect d
content: Critical minerals are essential for clean-energy technologies and established industrial materials. Japan’s special steel industry uses alloying elements such as nickel, chromium, and molybdenum, and disruptions in their supply may affect downstream industries. An auditable representation of special steel product flows is therefore needed to support future supply-risk and resilience assessments. Using publicly available fiscal year (FY) statistics, we develop a dynamic material flow analysis–system dynamics (DMFA–SD) model of Japan’s special steel product flows. The model separates order backlog, work-in-process, and makers’ finished-goods inventory, represents yield losses and production and shipping decisions, and is evaluated using historical fit, naive benchmarks, and observed annual balance residuals. The analysis explicitly distinguishes model consistency from agreement with observed statistics. In-sample correlations for production (FY1994–2023), shipping and makers’ inventory (FY2009–2023) are 0.960, 0.935 and 0.602, respectively, with corresponding mean absolute percentage errors of 5.25%, 3.66% and 5.50%. Production for FY1994–2008 is estimated from hot-rolled production using a later-period mean yield. Production and shipping perform similarly to orders-based benchmarks, limiting evidence for additional feedback contributions. An audit of published flows gives a mean balance residual of 1.18% of production for the makers’ inventory boundary, compared with 4.90% when imports are routed through total inventory. In an illustrative one-year constraint limiting production starts to 80% of orders, doubling inventory coverage reduces accumulated excess backlog by 64%. The resulting model is an auditable baseline for exploring aggregate supply constraints, rather than a validated forecast or element-specific resilience assessment.

title: BARQAROR IQTISODIY O'SISHNI TA'MINLASHDA "YASHIL" IQTISODIYOT VA QAYTA TIKLANUVCHI ENERGIYA MANBALARIGA INVESTITSIYALARNI JALB ETISH MEXANIZMLARI
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Mazkur ilmiy maqola barqaror iqtisodiy o'sishni ta'minlash sharoitida "yashil" iqtisodiyotga o'tish va qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalariga (QTEM) investitsiyalarni jalb etishning samarali mexanizmlarini tadqiq etishga bag'ishlangan. Tadq
content: Mazkur ilmiy maqola barqaror iqtisodiy o'sishni ta'minlash sharoitida "yashil" iqtisodiyotga o'tish va qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalariga (QTEM) investitsiyalarni jalb etishning samarali mexanizmlarini tadqiq etishga bag'ishlangan. Tadqiqotda ekologik barqarorlik va iqtisodiy samaradorlik o'rtasidagi uzviy bog'liqlik, "yashil" obligatsiyalar, davlat-xususiy sheriklik (DXSh) loyihalari hamda xalqaro moliya institutlari resurslaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi. Natijalar uglerod izini kamaytirish va energiya samaradorligini oshirishda innovatsion moliyaviy vositalarning muhim rolini ko'rsatadi. Xulosa qismida O'zbekistonda "yashil" investitsiya muhitini yanada yaxshilash bo'yicha ilmiy-amaliy tavsiyalar beriladi. Kalit so'zlar: barqaror iqtisodiy o'sish, "yashil" iqtisodiyot, qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalari, "yashil" investitsiyalar, "yashil" obligatsiyalar, davlat-xususiy sheriklik, energiya samaradorligi, uglerod neytralligi.

title: Sustainability for Sale: Discursive Legitimation in Instagram Branded Content
source: Lingue Culture Mediazioni - Languages Cultures Mediation (LCM Journal)
summary: This study examines how sustainability is discursively legitimized in branded content on Instagram, applying van Leeuwen’s (2007) framework of authorization, moral evaluation, rationalization, and mythopoesis to a corpus of 8,113 English-la
content: This study examines how sustainability is discursively legitimized in branded content on Instagram, applying van Leeuwen’s (2007) framework of authorization, moral evaluation, rationalization, and mythopoesis to a corpus of 8,113 English-language posts (July 2021 - June 2022). This corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis combines frequency-based lexical examination with qualitative analysis of a purposive sample. All four strategies recur and frequently combine within posts. Moral evaluation is the most pervasive, drawing on evaluative language, naturalness and purity, safety and harm-avoidance. Authorization relies heavily on certification and other markers of expertise. Rationalization grounds sustainability claims in purposes, benefits, processes, and consequences, but these claims routinely leave their evidential basis unspecified. Mythopoesis is carried by narrative structures that link sustainability-related actions to positive outcomes. Taken together, these patterns show that Instagram’s affordances of brevity and affective engagement systematically compress legitimation across all four strategies, while the platform’s commendation logic privileges concise forms of credibility, value, rationalization, and narrative reward.

title: Effect of crystallinity and morphology on the photocatalytic CO 2 reduction activity of MAPbBr 3
summary: , representing a 2.8-fold improvement over Sample 2, which exhibited smaller, more aggregated particles and lower crystallinity. Systematic characterizations indicate that the improved photocatalytic performance is associated with enhanced
content: , representing a 2.8-fold improvement over Sample 2, which exhibited smaller, more aggregated particles and lower crystallinity. Systematic characterizations indicate that the improved photocatalytic performance is associated with enhanced light absorption, a slightly reduced bandgap, and more favorable charge carrier dynamics in Sample 1.

title: Heterogeneous Valuation Effects of Structural Oil Shocks Across Clean Energy Technologies
summary: This paper investigates the differential valuation responses of clean energy assets to structural oil shocks by decomposing transmission into cash-flow and discount-rate channels. Existing literature establishes that oil shocks influence cl
content: This paper investigates the differential valuation responses of clean energy assets to structural oil shocks by decomposing transmission into cash-flow and discount-rate channels. Existing literature establishes that oil shocks influence clean energy returns and that connectedness varies with market conditions, but the fundamental question of how these shocks transmit through valuation mechanisms remains underexplored. Using a structural vector autoregression framework to identify oil supply, aggregate demand, and oil-specific demand shocks, combined with local projection methods at the firm level, we examine whether the adverse valuation effects of oil shocks operate primarily through expected cash flows or through changes in discount rates and financing costs. Our analysis of publicly listed clean energy firms across major equity markets from 2005 to 2025 reveals that supply-driven oil shocks generate opposing forces: they improve expected competitiveness for renewable energy technologies while simultaneously increasing financing costs through inflation and interest rate channels. Demand-driven shocks, by contrast, operate predominantly through cash-flow expectations without commensurate discount-rate effects. We further document substantial heterogeneity across clean energy subsectors, with capital-intensive technologies such as solar and storage exhibiting greater sensitivity to discount-rate transmission, while biofuels and fuel cells show stronger cash-flow responses. These findings have important implications for energy finance risk assessment, suggesting that aggregate connectedness measures obscure economically meaningful variation in transmission mechanisms that matters for portfolio construction and policy design.

title: A modified Delphi study identifies candidate indicators for assessing smart sports venues in China
summary: Smart sports venues integrate digital technologies with sports infrastructure, yet transparent approaches to assessing venue-wide smart development remain limited. We developed an expert-informed indicator framework through a two-round modi
content: Smart sports venues integrate digital technologies with sports infrastructure, yet transparent approaches to assessing venue-wide smart development remain limited. We developed an expert-informed indicator framework through a two-round modified Delphi process. Twelve experts participated in Round 1, and six additional specialists joined in Round 2, giving an 18-member second-round panel. The process yielded a framework of 6 domains, 24 categories and 72 indicators. Retained indicators received high ratings (95.4% of 1,296 ratings were 4 or 5), although ceiling effects limited discrimination. Kendall’s W for the final items was 0.248, indicating weak-to-moderate concordance; round-level values of 0.266 and 0.329 represent separate estimates because panel composition changed. Among the 12 experts participating in both rounds, item rankings were weakly correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.177), cautioning against using the current ordering to prioritize indicators. An exploratory subgroup comparison found no detectable difference between original and newly recruited experts (mean difference = 0.112, exact p = 0.667), but low power precluded establishing equivalence. The framework provides a research-oriented starting point for venue assessment in China. It has not been tested in real venues; pilot studies and reliability and validity testing are required before practical use.

title: “Blamestorming” in Central‐Local Government Relations? A Discourse Analysis of Blame amid English Local Government Failure
summary: This article explores how blame manifests in central‐local government relations in conditions of failure. The financial challenges facing English local government have reached a tipping point in recent years, illustrated by sharp increases
content: This article explores how blame manifests in central‐local government relations in conditions of failure. The financial challenges facing English local government have reached a tipping point in recent years, illustrated by sharp increases in central government intervention, local government “bankruptcy”, and requests for “exceptional financial support”. We report on the assembly of a new, comprehensive dataset of central‐local intervention in fiscal distress between 2020 and 2026, comprising 51 Best Value Notices, Inspections, External Assurance Reviews (EAR), and Section 114 Notices. We employ Hood's blame framework in a discourse analysis of these documents, illuminating the presentational, agency, and policy strategies used to attribute blame. We find these four document types, rather than a cohesive architecture for intervention, operate as distinct discursive regimes which locate blame. The article illustrates a current system which is characterized by traditions of central control and assurance, with the current statutory and fiscal intervention approaches creating further challenges to sectoral improvement, fiscal sustainability, and locally led devolution. The article illustrates the complex and incohesive nature of current statutory and fiscal intervention instruments and cautions that the preoccupation with blame may prove counterproductive to sectoral improvement and fiscal sustainability.

title: Making science more relevant: pre-service science teachers’ perspectives on adopting a systems thinking approach
source: Disciplinary and Interdisciplinary Science Education Research
summary: Systems thinking (ST) has been recognized as an important epistemic tool for understanding complex societal challenges, yet teacher education programs give limited emphasis to systems thinking’s role in supporting science relevance. This qu
content: Systems thinking (ST) has been recognized as an important epistemic tool for understanding complex societal challenges, yet teacher education programs give limited emphasis to systems thinking’s role in supporting science relevance. This qualitative case study explored pre-service science teachers’ perceptions of the role of ST in enhancing the relevance of secondary science content with particular reference to socioscientific issues (SSIs). Data were generated from reflective journals, Canvas discussion board posts, classroom discussions, and semi-structured interviews, and were analyzed thematically, framed by systems theory and SSI in science education. The fimdings suggest that the participants viewed ST as a useful framework for linking scientific ideas to real-world, ethical, environmental, and societal issues. They also considered SSIs such as the Flint water crisis, climate change, genetic engineering, and renewable energy as meaningful contexts in which ST could help students recognize the relevance of science. At the same time, participants identified perceived challenges to integrating ST, including pedagogical inexperience, student cognitive demand, time constraints, and curriculum pressures. The study does not demonstrate improvements in teaching competence or student outcomes, but it provides preliminary empirical insights into how pre-service science teachers make sense of ST and SSI integration, indicating the need to emphasize the role of systems thinking in teacher preparation programs.

title: Elucidating conformational preference of substituted azobenzenes with intramolecular symmetry-adapted perturbation theory
summary: The cis-trans energy difference in the azobenzene molecule, an important photochemical switch, can be modulated by incorporating substituent groups. In particular, aliphatic substituents act as dispersion energy donors, enhancing the nonbon
content: The cis-trans energy difference in the azobenzene molecule, an important photochemical switch, can be modulated by incorporating substituent groups. In particular, aliphatic substituents act as dispersion energy donors, enhancing the nonbonded attraction between the two aromatic rings in the cis configuration. On the other hand, the trans isomer remains favored by its lack of geometric distortion, that is, there is a deformation energy penalty to form the cis structure. In this work, we investigate the energetic balance between deformation and nonbonded interaction for 15 unsubstituted and substituted azobenzenes with accurate ab initio calculations. To obtain reliable intramolecular interaction energies and their decomposition into dispersion and other physical effects, we employ the intramolecular symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (ISAPT) approach in the novel SIAO1 variant recently introduced by us. The deformation energy is computed by considering intermediate, auxiliary one-ring systems that preserve molecular deformation but involve little to no intramolecular interaction. The sum of the two effects is compared to the conformational cis-trans energy differences from the reference domain-based local pair natural orbital coupled-cluster calculations, DLPNO-CCSD(T). We observe a very good correlation with the reference data, indicating that the energetic balance of substituted azobenzenes can indeed be explained by the interplay of nonbonded interaction and molecular deformation.

title: Rock-Eval® Thermal Analysis Meets Machine Learning for Accurate Initialization of a Soil Carbon Model
summary: In recent years, a growing number of policies related to soil organic carbon (SOC) have been developed, creating an urgent need for tools capable of simulating and predicting changes in SOC stocks. Models dividing SOC into different kinetic
content: In recent years, a growing number of policies related to soil organic carbon (SOC) have been developed, creating an urgent need for tools capable of simulating and predicting changes in SOC stocks. Models dividing SOC into different kinetic pools are frequently used to estimate changes in SOC stocks. Accurate and robust initialization of these pools’ sizes is a recurring obstacle for generating reliable simulations, calling into question their use as an actionable basis for these policies. In this study, we used an exceptional set of data including time series from 25 temperate long-term field experiments around the world to demonstrate that thermal stability and elemental stoichiometric composition of organic matter, as determined by Rock-Eval® thermal analysis, correlate with biogeochemical stability and that it is possible to use this information to initialize a compartmental model of SOC dynamics. First, we capitalized on the relative simplicity of the AMG model to optimize the initial allocation of carbon (C) between two kinetic pools (stable C and active C), resulting in the best fit between observations and AMG simulations. Second, we ensured that some SOC characterization results obtained using Rock-Eval® thermal analyses were correlated to the proportion of stable SOC sensu AMG. Third, we developed a data-driven support vector machine (SVM) model to estimate the proportion of stable SOC sensu AMG using only Rock-Eval® parameters. Fourth, we demonstrated that implementing our initialization method in AMG produced more accurate simulations compared to the default initialization. We argue that future adaptations of this approach can be used to initialize other compartmental models of similar complexity. Thus, our study represents a major game changer in the initialization of compartmental models, which are needed in the rapidly developing monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) sector.

title: Framing forest security: the climate-security nexus and policy alignment in the EU and Baltic States
summary: This paper investigates how climate security is framed in official European Union policy documents and national climate adaptation plans in the Baltic States – Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. It also examines the perspectives of stakeholder
content: This paper investigates how climate security is framed in official European Union policy documents and national climate adaptation plans in the Baltic States – Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. It also examines the perspectives of stakeholder involved in forest governance to understand how policy narratives align with perceived local risks and security concerns. The study adopts a multi-level frame analysis to investigate the new EU Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change and the Political Guidelines for the Next European Commission 2024–2029, with this analysis complemented by 25 semi-structured interviews with forestry stakeholders across the Baltic States. The findings reveal differences across governance levels in emphasis of climate security and forest resources, as EU-level framing prioritizes climate resilience, energy, and ecosystems broadly, while national strategies highlight forests in relation to energy independence, economic stability, and regional security. This gap contrasts with stakeholder views, which see forests as central to national self-sufficiency and socio-environmental stability. The study concludes with a call for stronger integration of natural resource governance in EU-level security frameworks and improved stakeholder engagement in climate-security planning.

title: A Swedish model for a just transition? Challenges to procedural justice in the transition of the Swedish transport sector
summary: The transport sector is undergoing substantial transformation. Electrification and digitalisation are challenging established practises and structures, and raise questions about workers’ opportunities to participate in, and influence proces
content: The transport sector is undergoing substantial transformation. Electrification and digitalisation are challenging established practises and structures, and raise questions about workers’ opportunities to participate in, and influence processes that affect their work. Against this background, we investigate how transport actors in Sweden perceive the ongoing transitions, and explore the procedural justice challenges that transport workers experience in relation to them. Sweden is an informative case because the Swedish model institutionalises worker representation and collective bargaining. Drawing on the literature, we identify three institutional principles that can be understood as expressions of procedural justice: the autonomy of the social partners; inclusive representation of affected workers; and negotiated resolution and legitimate contestation. Data are drawn from a survey of transport sector stakeholders, and two focus groups consisting of transport workers and union representatives in Lund and Stockholm. Our results show that most of our sample do not see the technological transitions in the sector as inherently negative, although they raised considerably more procedural justice concerns related to digitalisation than electrification. Digitalisation, and the associated expansion of the gig economy, raised concerns about workers’ autonomy and surveillance, and were seen as challenging established forms of union organisation, representation and collective bargaining. Our findings show that socio-technical transformations can put established procedural justice institutions under pressure, when workers fall outside their traditional scope. They also reveal potential tensions between institutional principles, notably the observation that securing inclusive representation may require greater state intervention, and potentially constrain the autonomy of the social partners.

title: Multiscale Degradation Classification and Grading of Black Soil and Green Farmland Assessment Technology - Proposing an Evaluation Method for the Vulnerability and Causative Threshold of Ecosystems under Drought Stress
summary: Drought significantly threatens terrestrial ecosystems health, through influencing both photosynthesis and respiratory processes. However, whether these processes have changed in response to intensified drought and the driving mechanisms re
content: Drought significantly threatens terrestrial ecosystems health, through influencing both photosynthesis and respiratory processes. However, whether these processes have changed in response to intensified drought and the driving mechanisms remain unclear, even though the inconsistent responses may indicate an increased potential for unstable carbon sinks. The knowledge gap would hinder accurate prediction of the size of China’s future terrestrial ecosystems carbon sink under increasing extreme droughts, thus impacting the realization of China’s carbon neutrality goal.

title: A Practice‐Based View of Circular Economy Practices in an Emerging Economy: A Multiple Case Study
summary: Manufacturing organizations are facing increasing sustainability issues, including waste generation, greenhouse gas emissions, environmental degradation, employee health and safety risks, and excessive utilization of hazardous chemicals and
content: Manufacturing organizations are facing increasing sustainability issues, including waste generation, greenhouse gas emissions, environmental degradation, employee health and safety risks, and excessive utilization of hazardous chemicals and non‐renewable resources. To address these issues, the circular economy (CE) is recognized as a sustainable business model. Though firms are increasingly adopting commonly available, imitable, and publicly known CE practices, there is a scarcity of research examining the adoption patterns and implementation diversity of these practices shaping sustainable performance in manufacturing firms. Accordingly, this study aims to investigate the operationalization of CE practices in the process manufacturing industry in Pakistan for achieving sustainable performance. Using a multiple case study approach, 19 semi‐structured interviews were conducted with corporate managers and senior executives in the textile, packaging, leather, and paint and coating industries in Pakistan. Building on the practice‐based view (PBV), this study highlighted various CE practices under the cleaner production, product stewardship, and digital practices in the critical process manufacturing sector. The findings provide fresh empirical insights into the CE literature by illustrating the adoption patterns, underlying reasons for heterogeneity in the implementation of CE practices, and sustainable performance. Overall, the findings can guide practitioners, researchers, and policymakers to understand the execution of CE practices for sustainable performance in the critical process industry.

title: EPSO: Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization BP Neural Network Model
summary: China has vigorously developed wind power generation with suitable geographical conditions, reducing fossil fuel consumption, promoting the implementation of carbon neutrality, and driving the development of related economies. This article
content: China has vigorously developed wind power generation with suitable geographical conditions, reducing fossil fuel consumption, promoting the implementation of carbon neutrality, and driving the development of related economies. This article proposes a combined prediction model based on an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm (namely EPSO) and a BP neural network for short-term wind power prediction. This model aims to optimize neural network parameters through intelligent algorithms to improve prediction accuracy. This algorithm incorporates four improvement strategies. Firstly, Bernoulli mapping is used to expand the search range in the solution space. Secondly, quantum mechanics strategies are employed to further enrich population diversity and expand the optimization range. Finally, new adaptive inertia weights are introduced to balance exploration and development. Again, introducing new nonlinear learning factors enables individuals to better advance towards their own optimal position while also approaching the group’s optimal position. Finally, the Gaussian mutation perturbation strategy is introduced to improve the local convergence problem caused by the decrease in population diversity in the later stages of iteration. To verify the effectiveness of the model, this paper compared the EPSO algorithm with 11 other optimization algorithms, and the results proved its superiority. Meanwhile, the proposed combination optimization model was compared with other regression prediction models, and the results also showed that it has better predictive performance.

title: Disclosure as a Signal, Innovation as Validation: Climate Disclosure by China's Heavily Polluting Firms and Green Investor Engagement
summary: Using a sample of heavily polluting firms listed on China's A‐share market, this study develops an integrated framework linking signal transmission to legitimacy restoration in the context of China's carbon‐peaking and carbon‐neutrality goa
content: Using a sample of heavily polluting firms listed on China's A‐share market, this study develops an integrated framework linking signal transmission to legitimacy restoration in the context of China's carbon‐peaking and carbon‐neutrality goals and green finance system. Climate risks disclosure of high‐pulluting enterprises (CDHPE) serves both as a compliance baseline and as a costly signal. Mandatory disclosure establishes a general obligation, while voluntary disclosure beyond the minimum requirements, subject to regulatory scrutiny, enforcement and performance review, can serve as a credible and difficult‐to‐imitate signal of transition. The study develops a Chinese‐language CDHPE dictionary using a CBOW word‐embedding model trained on annual reports from A‐share‐listed firms and combines data from multiple sources to identify green investors. The empirical results show that CDHPE significantly increases green investor entry and participation. A one‐standard‐deviation increase in CDHPE raises the probability of entry by 4.47 percentage points (approximately 13.5%) and participation intensity by 5.65%. Reduced information asymmetry, restored corporate credibility and increased environmental investment partially mediate this relationship. The effect is stronger among firms facing greater profit pressure or weaker media oversight, non‐state‐owned firms and firms without ESG certification. Further analysis shows that CDHPE and green investor participation jointly promote high‐quality green innovation. CDHPE's effect on innovation quality, measured by patent citations (4.85%), exceeds its effect on innovation quantity, measured by patent applications (2.95%). This pattern may help counter the quantity‐over‐quality bias in patent incentives. CDHPE also increases green investor shareholdings by 3.93%. Theoretically, the study extends signalling theory beyond a static sender–receiver model to a dynamic process of signal transmission, capital inflow, innovation validation and legitimacy restoration. It also extends dual legitimacy theory by identifying how firm‐level signals contribute to legitimacy restoration. The policy implications support coordinating mandatory disclosure with third‐party carbon verification, enforcement by the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, green‐credit assessments and media oversight. Such coordination can help translate disclosure commitments into credible actions and financing for the low‐carbon transition.

title: A‐Site Vacancies and Cu‐Doping in Lanthanum‐Based Perovskite Anodes for Selective H 2 O 2 Oxidation to O 2: A Descriptor‐Based Approach
summary: The electrochemical oxidation of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2) to oxygen (O 2) is crucial for controlling reactive oxygen species and for the durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Herein, density functional theory (DFT) calculati
content: The electrochemical oxidation of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2) to oxygen (O 2) is crucial for controlling reactive oxygen species and for the durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Herein, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to study the hydrogen peroxide oxidation reaction (HPOR) on LaMO 3 (M═Co, Mn, Fe, Ni) for eighteen lanthanum‐based perovskites, such as A‐site vacancy, oxygen‐layer‐truncated, and Cu‐substituted LaM 1‐x Cu x O 3‐τ structures. Electronic descriptor analysis revealed that defect engineering decreases d‐orbital occupancy up to the Fermi level(O e) while increasing the d‐orbital density of states at the Fermi level(D π (E F)) compared to the pristine surface, thereby enhancing catalytic activity. AIMD simulations reveal the structural stability. The Co1 site in La 0.8 Co 0.91 Cu 0.09 O 3‐τ showed the highest HPOR activity, with an overpotential of 0.49 V after DFT+U correction. The OOH adsorption free energy (ΔG OOH) showed a volcano‐type correlation with catalytic activity (R 2 > 0.84; RMSE = 0.12). The electronic descriptor dxz_fermi has a good correlation with ΔG OOH (R 2 = 0.73). The MLR model with three electronic descriptors gave R 2 = 0.85 and cross‐validation Q 2 = 0.80, which allowed for efficient screening of electrocatalysts. The results provide design principles for advanced peroxide‐oxidation electrocatalysts.

title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
summary: Band-filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid-band shift of the
content: Band-filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid-band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π-conjugated electron-donating molecules are covalently linked to form one-dimensional pore channels. The introduction of a well-defined amount of electron-accepting molecules without disrupting the framework structure enabled the first successful demonstration of the deliberate band-filling control while elucidating the charge state through various spectroscopic measurements. Enhanced electronic itinerancy facilitated by host-guest charge transfer was evidenced by spectroscopic, transport, and magnetic measurements in support of theoretical calculations. The present study opens a new avenue for exploring more advanced electronic organic solids based on band-filling engineering.

title: RAPID FRESHNESS ASSESSMENT OF REFRIGERATED NILE TILAPIA USING A LOW-COST ELECTRONIC NOSE
source: Carpathian Journal of Food Science and Technology
summary: Background: Rapid and non-destructive evaluation of fish freshness is essential for ensuring product quality and reducing postharvest losses.Electronic nose (E-nose) technology has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional analytic
content: Background: Rapid and non-destructive evaluation of fish freshness is essential for ensuring product quality and reducing postharvest losses.Electronic nose (E-nose) technology has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional analytical methods for monitoring fish spoilage through volatile organic compounds (VOCs).Objective: This study developed and evaluated a low-cost metal oxide semiconductor (MOS)based electronic nose for monitoring quality deterioration and predicting the freshness of refrigerated Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).Methods: The system was built using an Arduino Mega 2560 integrated with six MOS gas sensors (MQ3, MQ4, MQ5, MQ8, MQ9, and MQ135).Sensor responses were recorded over five days of refrigerated storage and compared with conventional physicochemical (TVB-N, peroxide value, pH, and thiobarbituric acid) and microbiological quality indicators (total plate count, coliforms, Escherichia coli, Staphylococci, Salmonella, and Vibrio).Results: Progressive deterioration was confirmed by increases in TVB-N (7.90-16.18mg/100 g), peroxide value (0.78-4.05 meq O₂/kg), pH (6.14-7.14),TBA (1.07-1.57mg MDA/kg), and total plate count (3.68 × 10⁴-8.92× 10⁶ CFU/g).All MOS sensors exhibited increasing responses throughout storage, with MQ135 (195-920) and MQ3 (153-620) showing the highest sensitivity to spoilage-related VOCs.MQ135 demonstrated a strong association with TVB-N, microbial growth, and pH, whereas MQ3 closely reflected lipid oxidation.The developed E-nose correctly classified fresh, semi-fresh, and spoiled fish with 90% accuracy, confirming its capability for freshness discrimination.Conclusion: The proposed MOSbased electronic nose provides a rapid, inexpensive, and non-destructive approach for monitoring Nile tilapia freshness and offers strong potential for real-time quality control and shelf-life prediction in seafood processing, storage, and distribution.

title: A sensor-informed multi-objective weekly scheduling framework for smart residential buildings considering thermal comfort, energy cost, carbon emissions, and relative air quality
summary: Residential buildings have significant potential for energy savings through intelligent scheduling of flexible appliances and environmental control systems. This study develops a simulation-based, sensor-informed multi-objective optimizatio
content: Residential buildings have significant potential for energy savings through intelligent scheduling of flexible appliances and environmental control systems. This study develops a simulation-based, sensor-informed multi-objective optimization framework for weekly residential energy management by integrating IoT-based environmental sensing, simplified building thermal simulation, NSGA-II, and TOPSIS. Seven objectives are simultaneously considered: thermal discomfort, electricity cost, total electricity consumption, three-hour rolling energy, CO 2 emissions, user discomfort, and a relative indoor-air-quality penalty. Environmental measurements of temperature, relative humidity, and an MQ135-based air-quality indicator are incorporated into the framework, while appliance operating constraints are explicitly modeled. Optimization is performed over a 168-hour horizon using ten independent NSGA-II runs. The representative optimized solution (Seed = 32768) reduces weekly electricity consumption from 1,293.6 to 753.414 kWh (41.8%) and electricity cost from 7,242,900 to 4,080,507 IRR (43.7%), while reducing three-hour rolling energy from 32.70 to 22.83 kWh (30.2%). CO 2 emissions decrease by 42.0%, and the relative air-quality penalty decreases by 73.5%, while the mean PPD increases from 7.96% to 15.54% and user discomfort reaches 0.679. A comprehensive benchmark against MOPSO, MOEA/D, and SPEA2, evaluated using hypervolume, IGD, and spread indicators, confirms the competitive performance of NSGA-II. Convergence analysis demonstrates the progressive stabilization of the optimization process. The findings demonstrate the potential of sensor-informed multi-objective scheduling for residential energy-management decision support.

title: Action-Conditioned Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
summary: We study spatio-temporal forecasting in networked systems under specified actions. The challenge is to capture the action's effects without predicting spurious changes in unaffected regions. However, direct supervision and evaluation of the
content: We study spatio-temporal forecasting in networked systems under specified actions. The challenge is to capture the action's effects without predicting spurious changes in unaffected regions. However, direct supervision and evaluation of these effects require paired futures with and without the action, whereas observational trajectories reveal only the realized future. We introduce PairST, a benchmark comprising six datasets across traffic, power transmission and water distribution, with paired reference and intervened futures simulated from the same system state. These pairs enable separate evaluation of affected-region forecast accuracy and quiet-region response error. We further propose ActionST, which forecasts the intervened future by writing an explicit response onto an intervention-independent reference forecast. Specifically, node-time addressing constructs a query for each response position, a state-conditioned response writer computes candidate responses, and a graph-aware locality gate controls their strength. Experiments on six datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ActionST at new action targets, with the lowest mean absolute error on five datasets and the best average rank. Our source code and the PairST benchmark are available at https://github.com/yutong-xia/ActionST.

title: Citizen-informed scenarios to shape energy demand reduction strategies
summary: Growing evidence has demonstrated the important role that energy demand reduction can play in achieving net zero. Despite this, the adoption of such measures in government strategies often remains limited, in part based on perceived public
content: Growing evidence has demonstrated the important role that energy demand reduction can play in achieving net zero. Despite this, the adoption of such measures in government strategies often remains limited, in part based on perceived public resistance to change. Using a novel combined deliberative-modelling approach, which fills a key gap in the literature, we find this is unfounded. Citizens both recognise the importance of and support demand-side interventions to achieve the UK's net-zero goals. This support, however, is conditional. If policy interventions can make demand-side choices practical and fair, we find citizens are prepared to reduce energy demand by at least 37% between 2025 and 2050, providing 20% of the abatement required to meet net-zero targets. Policymakers could thus unlock a wide range of demand reduction measures by acting on a more comprehensive understanding of public views and needs. Moreover, our approach offers a powerful framework, applicable in other contexts, to underpin policymaking with socially-informed quantitative modelling.

title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
summary: Perovskites are promising materials for chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) due to their compositional flexibility and tunable redox properties. However, cation substitution opens a vast compositional space, making screening for new
content: Perovskites are promising materials for chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) due to their compositional flexibility and tunable redox properties. However, cation substitution opens a vast compositional space, making screening for new high-performing materials computationally demanding. Here, an autonomous active-learning framework combining a Wasserstein autoencoder (WAE) with a deep ensemble surrogate model was used to search for perovskites with a high hydrogen production capacity (HPC). In seven independent runs of 50 cycles, the mean HPC of the acquired compositions rose from 0.41 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$ in the starting set to 2.05 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$, and the best compositions reached 2.65-2.99 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$. All runs enriched Sn on the B-site, mostly combined with Ti and with Mg, Ce, K and Y on the A-site. Twenty diverse candidates (2.22-2.84 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$) were then selected by a multi-objective ranking that also accounts for raw-material price, supply resilience and potential environmental and health impacts. The approach links materials discovery with practical deployment constraints, and the methodology is transferable to other chemical looping processes.

title: A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance
summary: As part of the energy transition, underground hydrogen (H2) storage in porous media has emerged as an alternative solution for large-scale energy storage to salt caverns. Assessing the feasibility of such systems and ensuring their operatio
content: As part of the energy transition, underground hydrogen (H2) storage in porous media has emerged as an alternative solution for large-scale energy storage to salt caverns. Assessing the feasibility of such systems and ensuring their operation requires accurate modeling of the geochemical processes that may alter the composition of the stored gas. This results in a highly nonlinear coupled system of partial differential equations, ordinary differential equations, and algebraic constraints, calling for robust and specialized numerical strategies. In this work, we adopt a Globally Implicit Approach (GIA), as sequential solution algorithms are known to introduce splitting errors due to the decoupling of flow and geochemical processes. In addition, most splitting-based methods implicitly assume the persistent presence of the liquid phase, an assumption that may be violated during gas injection or withdrawal owing to aqueous phase vaporization and mineral precipitation in the vicinity of wells. We extend Coats' formulation to multiphase reactive transport with a rigorous and fully implicit management of aqueous phase disappearance and reappearance. The proposed approach introduces new molar concentration unknowns for basis species that track the re-appearance of the aqueous phase and guarantee the nonsingularity of the Jacobian matrix. Additionally, the appearance of the liquid phase is managed using a multiphase flash calculation algorithm. The proposed algorithm is validated against the CO2 storage benchmark problems. Finally, the approach is applied to an underground H2 storage in an aquifer under cyclic injection and withdrawal conditions.

title: Enabling MHz XFEL rates for fixed-target SFX using a rotating Round-chip
summary: Serial femtosecond crystallography (SFX) is the method of choice at X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) for obtaining structural information on biological and chemical reactions with high temporal and/or spatial resolution. While SFX methods
content: Serial femtosecond crystallography (SFX) is the method of choice at X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) for obtaining structural information on biological and chemical reactions with high temporal and/or spatial resolution. While SFX methods are in demand among the user community, the efficiency of SFX data collection is often limited by the efficiency of sample delivery, leading to high sample consumption. This bottleneck is particularly relevant for the European XFEL (EuXFEL), which delivers X-ray pulses at MHz repetition rate (within the 600 µs pulse train), making efficient sample exchange while minimizing sample consumption between adjacent pulses particularly challenging. In this study, we present a fixed-target sample delivery method that allows replenishment of samples at MHz rates with high sample efficiency using a Round-chip in combination with high-speed rotation. We discuss the mechanical constraints for the choice of materials, including comparison of stiff freestanding materials versus thinner lower background materials which require mechanical support to facilitate manual handling and exchange. Consideration is also given to the centrifugal effects on the chip and the samples. This study also provides validation for sealing of the double foils to maintain hydration of sensitive samples, and practical implementation of the Round-chip design for successful data collection at the SPB/SFX instrument of EuXFEL. Using the Round-chip, we successfully collected diffraction data from lysozyme crystals, achieving a quality comparable with other sample delivery methods implemented at EuXFEL. We demonstrate that the Round-chip approach is viable and represents a highly desirable sample delivery strategy for MHz-repetition-rate SFX experiments, offering the potential for efficient sample consumption with consistently high hit rates. The potential for automation of sample preparation and exchange at the instrument and, if combined with photoactivation, for time-resolved data collection would further facilitate access and use of SFX by the wider user community.

title: Particulate Delivery of Small Molecule Mast Cell Activator VAP-1185 for Use as a Vaccine Adjuvant

title: Effects of base fluid and pipe geometry on hybrid PV/T-PCM system efficiency
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Hybrid photovoltaic/thermal systems integrated with phase change materials (PV/T-PCM) can improve electrical performance while recovering thermal energy by regulating photovoltaic operating temperature. However, base-fluid properties and co
content: Hybrid photovoltaic/thermal systems integrated with phase change materials (PV/T-PCM) can improve electrical performance while recovering thermal energy by regulating photovoltaic operating temperature. However, base-fluid properties and collector-pipe geometries are often investigated separately, limiting understanding of their combined effects. This study presents a systematic literature review of research published between 2010 and 2024 to examine the individual and combined influences of working-fluid selection and pipe geometry on PV/T-PCM performance. Relevant studies were retrieved from Scopus using a predefined search protocol and assessed against established inclusion and exclusion criteria. The findings indicate that advanced working fluids, particularly nanofluids and encapsulated phase change material slurries, can enhance heat transfer, while optimized pipe and PCM-container geometries can improve heat extraction and temperature uniformity. Studies combining fluid and geometry enhancements report promising performance improvements; however, these results depend on system configuration and operating conditions and should not be treated as universal benchmarks. Key challenges include fluid instability, PCM degradation, increased pumping-power requirements, economic feasibility, and the lack of standardized evaluation methods. This review provides an integrated perspective to support the design and further development of efficient and reliable PV/T-PCM systems.

title: An adaptive fuzzy-SMC based active voltage balancing circuit for high rating EV battery pack
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: In order to increase the lifespan and charge/discharge cycles of the battery, the state of charge (SOC) of each cell in the battery pack of the electric vehicle (EV) has to be maintained the same. Especially in high-rating battery pack EVs
content: In order to increase the lifespan and charge/discharge cycles of the battery, the state of charge (SOC) of each cell in the battery pack of the electric vehicle (EV) has to be maintained the same. Especially in high-rating battery pack EVs with larger storage capacity and higher voltage, cell voltage balancing is mandatory. With equal voltages of the cells, charging or discharging also happens in a balanced structure, maintaining the SOC of all cells at the same value. In order to achieve this, passive or active voltage balancing circuits are needed. In this paper, an active balancing circuit is proposed with a full bridge controlled by an adaptive fuzzy-SMC voltage regulator. In this regulator, the gains of the sliding mode control (SMC) are varied by fuzzy logic control with two input variables. Here, the sliding variable in the controller is the error signal generated by the comparison of the reference and measured signals. The gains of the SMC Ki and Kq are varied by the fuzzy control with 25 rules base for each gain. The SMC is tuned as per the response of the voltage balancing circuit, keeping the ripple of the battery current very low. A comparative analysis is done with different regulators, including conventional proportional-integral (PI) and adaptive neuro fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) regulators. The peak overshoot, settling time, and the ripple in the battery current are compared to validate the optimal regulator for the active voltage balancing circuit.

title: Hybrid battery–supercapacitor storage for PV-based microgrids and smart grids: state-of-the-art applications and open challenges
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: This paper presents a structured review of hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) for photovoltaic (PV)-based microgrids and smart grids. The review focuses on system architectures, energy management strategies (EMS), and application scenario
content: This paper presents a structured review of hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) for photovoltaic (PV)-based microgrids and smart grids. The review focuses on system architectures, energy management strategies (EMS), and application scenarios. The aim is to provide an application-oriented and integrated perspective. The results show that hybrid systems are most beneficial in PV-based microgrids with high variability and frequent transients. From an architectural perspective, semi-active configurations are suitable for rural and medium-scale systems. In contrast, active architectures are more appropriate for grid-connected systems that require high controllability. In terms of EMS, rule-based and filter-based strategies are well-suited for rural microgrids. Optimization-based and intelligent methods perform better in grid-connected systems with higher computational capability. Furthermore, hybrid systems become economically viable when the reduction in battery degradation and replacement costs offsets the additional investment in power electronics and control complexity. This condition is typically observed in systems with high PV penetration and strict power quality requirements. The main contribution of this review is a unified framework linking HESS architectures, EMS strategies, and application conditions. These insights offer practical guidance for the design and deployment of efficient and resilient HESS in next-generation PV-based microgrids.

title: Electric load forecasting using LSTM and Bi-LSTM: a systematic literature review
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Future electricity load forecasting plays a critical role in modern power systems to ensure operational efficiency, planning, and grid stability. Conventional statistical methods used for forecasting often fail to capture nonlinear and temp
content: Future electricity load forecasting plays a critical role in modern power systems to ensure operational efficiency, planning, and grid stability. Conventional statistical methods used for forecasting often fail to capture nonlinear and temporal fluctuations in electricity demand, especially under high variability conditions. Deep learning methods are widely used for forecasting, especially long short-term memory (LSTM) and bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) methods, which are strong alternatives for forecasting due to their superior sequence modeling capabilities compared to others. This literature review identifies key research gaps, including the lack of standard benchmarks, the underutilization of contextual features, poor model interpretability, and challenges in real-time deployment. This literature review analyzes key datasets, model architectures, evaluation metrics, and performance comparisons with mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) as the primary benchmark. The analysis results from various sources show that Bi-LSTM generally outperforms standard LSTM in capturing forward and backward dependencies, albeit with higher computational demands. Future research directions are expected to be able to overcome the limitations of forecasting models and improve the adaptability and transparency of LSTM-based forecasting models in smart grid applications.

title: THOR: A GPU-accelerated and MPI-parallel radiative transfer code
summary: Emission and absorption line features are important diagnostics for the physics underlying extragalactic astronomy. The interpretation of observed signatures involves making comparisons against forward-modeled spectra from galaxy formation
content: Emission and absorption line features are important diagnostics for the physics underlying extragalactic astronomy. The interpretation of observed signatures involves making comparisons against forward-modeled spectra from galaxy formation simulations as well as more simplified geometries, while including the complex scattering radiative transfer (RT) of resonant emission lines. Here, we present þor, a modern C++ RT code focused initially on resonant emission lines. þor is a high-performance, distributed-memory, multi-target code that uses the message passing interface (MPI) for parallel execution. It runs on CPUs, GPUs, and other accelerators, yielding large ∼ 10-50 speed-ups compared to previous CPU-only codes. Our code supports multiple grid-based and grid-less data structures, enabling comparisons across different hydrodynamical codes as well as toy model geometries. We demonstrate its science capabilities with a number of example use cases across scales: (i) Lyman-alpha RT on simple shell-like gas distributions; (ii) Lyman-alpha RT applied to a high-resolution, high-redshift (z ∼ 6) cosmological hydrodynamical galaxy formation simulation; (iii) magnesium-II halos, namely, scattering and emission from the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of a z ≃ 1 galaxy drawn from a cosmological magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) simulation; (iv) the large-scale cosmic web in gas emission, a 6144^3 volume element RT scaling calculation; and (v) synthetic absorption spectra of the Lyman-alpha forest. We employed extensive verification and benchmarking to validate our approach and its computational efficiency. x

title: A cross-week analysis of urinary extracellular vesicles after respiratory tract exposure intervention in a cohort of isocyanate-exposed workers
summary: Background Urinary extracellular vesicles (EVs) are an accessible source of diverse molecular cargo with potential for noninvasive biomonitoring; however, the feasibility of recovering and characterizing their RNA and protein content from o
content: Background Urinary extracellular vesicles (EVs) are an accessible source of diverse molecular cargo with potential for noninvasive biomonitoring; however, the feasibility of recovering and characterizing their RNA and protein content from occupationally collected urine is not well established. This study aimed to evaluate whether urinary EVs isolated from field-collected samples could provide biologically informative molecular signatures and compared three EV cargo classes, RNA reads mapping to protein-coding transcripts (EV-mRNA-derived fragments), non-coding RNAs, and proteins, for their ability to distinguish paired sampling conditions and support exploratory biological interpretation. Methods Paired spot urine samples were collected from five workers in a fabric coating factory with well-characterized inhalation exposure to methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) on Monday morning before and Friday afternoon after a one-week respiratory-protection intervention. EVs were characterized by morphology, size, concentration, marker expression, and proteomic composition. Total EV-RNA was profiled using a small-RNA sequencing workflow without size selection, enabling analysis of diverse RNA species and comparison of molecular cargo classes. Results Urinary EVs were successfully isolated and characterized from occupational field samples. Among the three cargo classes evaluated, EV-mRNA-derived fragments provided the clearest discrimination between pre- and post-intervention sampling conditions and generated candidate signatures for exploratory biological interpretation. The pre-intervention EV-mRNA-derived fragment signature showed nominal associations with inflammatory airway-related pathways and with hypersensitivity pneumonitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease profiles in the Integrated Human Lung Cell Atlas. These findings provide biological context but do not establish tissue origin, disease causation, or exposure specificity, particularly given the possibility of uncharacterized workplace co-exposures. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of urinary EV isolation and multi-cargo molecular characterization from occupationally collected urine samples. While EV-mRNA-derived fragments emerged as the most informative cargo class for distinguishing sampling conditions and generating biologically interpretable signatures, larger longitudinal studies are needed to validate these observations and define their utility for exposure-related biomonitoring.

title: How Cost-Effective Were Subsidies for Solar Energy in Germany?
summary: We study Germany’s photovoltaic subsidy program, estimating a dynamic model of new technology adoption which accounts for heterogeneity in residential ownership structures. We find that homeowner and landlord investors heavily discount futu
content: We study Germany’s photovoltaic subsidy program, estimating a dynamic model of new technology adoption which accounts for heterogeneity in residential ownership structures. We find that homeowner and landlord investors heavily discount future benefits, highlighting the suboptimality of the feed-in tariff structure and the inefficient use of government funds. Our estimates suggest that administrative costs associated with tenant electricity contracts discourage landlords from investing in new energy technologies. Our analysis suggests that policy design should prioritize upfront investment subsidies over feed-in tariffs to promote renewable energy adoption. Reducing administrative costs associated with tenant electricity programs is key to unlock investments by landlords and expand tenants’ access to solar energy, thereby enhancing cost-effectiveness.

title: Exchange between ocean and Greenland fjords regulated by recirculating meltwater in glacial troughs
summary: The Greenland Ice Sheet is rapidly losing mass due to climate warming, contributing significantly to global sea level rise and altering ocean circulation and ecosystems. Yet, the processes controlling interactions between glacial fjords and
content: The Greenland Ice Sheet is rapidly losing mass due to climate warming, contributing significantly to global sea level rise and altering ocean circulation and ecosystems. Yet, the processes controlling interactions between glacial fjords and the adjacent continental shelf and slope are not fully understood, particularly the role of bathymetric troughs in modulating water exchange between the fjords and boundary current system. Here we present high-resolution shipboard, reanalysis, and numerical model data across several deep troughs in West Greenland, revealing a recurring anticyclonic recirculation of glacial meltwater within the inner Uummannaq trough, which isolates the glacial fjord from subsurface Atlantic Water inflow and thus limits oceanic heat penetration. This circulation—driven by seasonal meltwater discharge and modulated by wind forcing—contrasts with the adjacent Jakobshavn trough, where more efficient exchange prevents such retention. The presence of recirculating freshwater correlates with enhanced nutrient concentrations and isotopic signatures, suggesting broader biogeochemical impacts. Analogous recirculation patterns are also present in some East Greenland fjords where ice loss has been comparatively reduced. Our findings emphasize the critical role of fjord-shelf topography and regional dynamics in modulating Greenland’s glacial melting, freshwater export, and nutrient delivery, highlighting the need for improved representation of these processes in climate models.

title: Low-pressure operation of all-solid-state batteries enabled by an organic electrode
summary: All-solid-state batteries offer enhanced safety and high energy density. However, their practical application is challenged by the need for high external pressures, often tens of MPa, to maintain intimate solid–solid contact and preserve io
content: All-solid-state batteries offer enhanced safety and high energy density. However, their practical application is challenged by the need for high external pressures, often tens of MPa, to maintain intimate solid–solid contact and preserve ion/electron percolation pathways during cycling. In this work, we demonstrate that low-modulus, low-hardness, creep-compliant, low-strain organic active materials that readily deform in response to external pressures and microstructural changes enable stable cell operation under low stack pressures. Using bis-tetraaminobenzoquinone (TAQ) as a model compound, we show its low modulus (8.4–15.3 GPa), low hardness (0.33–0.76 GPa), and moderate creep compliance ( m = 0.038–0.073), quantified by nanoindentation of both pristine and lithiated TAQ, enable adaptive deformability under low stack pressures. TAQ-based solid-state cells achieve stable cycling and promising rate performance at external pressures as low as 1 MPa, retaining 80.3% capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5C. Operando and post-mortem electron microscopy reveal that TAQ electrodes maintain high structural integrity at pressures as low as 0.2 MPa. These findings establish a materials design strategy centered on mechanically adaptive materials to enable solid-state battery operation under practically relevant pressure conditions.

title: Characterizing ocean flows with the scattering transform
summary: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a use
content: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a useful statistical descriptor of these flows, it cannot always distinguish between different types of motion. We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics.
