Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

title: Precession-forced asymmetric continental heating shapes ENSO variability
summary: Geological records and climate modeling evidence indicate that the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is strongly modulated by Earth's axial precession, yet the mechanisms remain unclear due to interactions among multiple forcings. Using h
content: Geological records and climate modeling evidence indicate that the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is strongly modulated by Earth's axial precession, yet the mechanisms remain unclear due to interactions among multiple forcings. Using high-resolution climate simulations, we reconstruct ENSO variations across a full precessional cycle. Our results reveal that ENSO is more active when perihelion coincides with austral summer and aphelion with boreal summer, consistent with the orbital configuration of the present-day climate. Through diagnostics of background mean climate evolution and ENSO-related feedback processes, we propose that precession-scale modulations in ENSO variability are governed by east–west asymmetric continental warming. When perihelion occurs during austral summer and aphelion during boreal summer, pronounced warming emerges over Australia (east of the Indo-Pacific Intertropical Convergence Zone, ITCZ), whereas relative cooling prevails over the Afro–Eurasian continents (west of the Indo-Pacific ITCZ). This east–west thermal contrast drives an eastward shift of the ITCZ and its coupled Walker circulation, accompanied by weakened trade winds, a shallower ocean mixed layer, and enhanced upper-ocean stratification. These changes reduce the thermal inertia of the warm pool, allowing even moderate climate noise to trigger the Bjerknes feedback (including wind and thermocline feedbacks), ultimately magnifying ENSO variability under precessional phases analogous to the modern configuration. Conversely, when perihelion falls in boreal summer and aphelion in austral summer, cooling over Australia and warming over Afro–Eurasian continents force westward displacements of the ITCZ and Walker circulation, strengthen trade winds, force a deeper mixed layer and reduced upper-ocean stratification, suppressing the Bjerknes feedback, thereby dampening ENSO activity during precessional phases corresponding to the Early Holocene. Proxy records from the Indo-Pacific region support these shifts in climatic regimes. This mechanism of zonal asymmetric continental warming establishes a physical link between astronomical precessional forcing and ENSO behavior, and may provide insights to improve assessments of long-term tropical climate variability.

title: Mapping unsolved lipidomes accelerates lipid discovery in major bacterial pathogens
summary: Pathogenic bacteria use specialized lipids to promote virulence. Unlike genomes, the scope of lipids in many bacterial pathogens remains undefined. Here we report a discovery lipidomics platform to generate a resource of mass-defined unname
content: Pathogenic bacteria use specialized lipids to promote virulence. Unlike genomes, the scope of lipids in many bacterial pathogens remains undefined. Here we report a discovery lipidomics platform to generate a resource of mass-defined unnamed lipids in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). From a pool of 312 qualified but unknown features, we developed quality metrics to prioritize mass spectrometry signals consistent with genuine undiscovered lipids for chemical identification. Leveraging this list for molecular discovery, we identified a family of lysine lipoamino acids in Mtb that was also broadly conserved among mycobacteria. Identification and disruption of the biosynthetic gene, lysX, attenuated Mycobacterium marinum infection of zebrafish, demonstrating a role in virulence. Recognition and deletion of the orthologous virulence gene, mprF, in Staphylococcus aureus identified the same lipoamino acids. This lipidomic map of mass-defined unknown molecules represents a resource for immediate follow-up in Mtb and established a discovery framework applicable to any bacterial pathogen.

title: Defining physiological limits for speed breeding in forage legumes: generation time reduction in Medicago sativa and Medicago truncatula
summary: Climate change and the increasing demand for animal products require faster breeding cycles in forage crops, yet progress remains slow in perennial and autotetraploid legumes such as Medicago sativa. Speed breeding (SB) offers a promising s
content: Climate change and the increasing demand for animal products require faster breeding cycles in forage crops, yet progress remains slow in perennial and autotetraploid legumes such as Medicago sativa. Speed breeding (SB) offers a promising strategy to shorten generation time, but its application in forage legumes is still limited by an incomplete understanding of reproductive performance and physiological constraints. Here, we evaluated how photoperiod, light intensity, and light quality interact to accelerate complete reproductive cycles in alfalfa (Medicago sativa) and its diploid relative M. truncatula under controlled conditions. Flowering, pod development, time to seed harvest, seed set, and germination were assessed across independent and combined SB treatments, together with photosynthetic performance to identify physiological trade-offs. Extended photoperiods, moderate-to-high irradiance (450 µmol m −2 s −1), and blue-red light supplementation significantly accelerated reproductive development in both species, although these parameters differed between diploid and autotetraploid backgrounds. A combined SB regime (20/4 h photoperiod at 450 µmol m −2 s −1) reduced time to harvest by 17% in M. sativa and 28% in M. truncatula while maintaining viable seed production. Chlorophyll fluorescence analysis revealed higher photosynthetic plasticity in M. sativa, indicating species-specific physiological limits to SB intensification. Together, these results identify specific photoperiod, light quality and light intensity combinations that reduce generation time in M. sativa cv. ‘Chaná’ and M. truncatula cv. ‘Caliph’ without compromising seed viability, and reveal species-specific physiological limits that should be considered when designing SB protocols for these forage legumes.

title: Controlling Polypyrrole Morphology and Electronic Properties Through Nucleation and Growth Mechanisms
summary: The nucleation and growth mechanisms (NGMs) of polypyrrole (PPy) films formed on ITO from pyrrole in acetonitrile containing 0.1 mol L−1 LiClO4 were analyzed. Deconvolution of the i–t transient recorded at 1.1 V yielded a fit with R2 = 0.99
content: The nucleation and growth mechanisms (NGMs) of polypyrrole (PPy) films formed on ITO from pyrrole in acetonitrile containing 0.1 mol L−1 LiClO4 were analyzed. Deconvolution of the i–t transient recorded at 1.1 V yielded a fit with R2 = 0.999, identifying contributions from two-dimensional instantaneous nucleation (NI2D), three-dimensional progressive nucleation controlled by charge transfer (NP3Dct), and three-dimensional progressive nucleation controlled by diffusion (NP3Ddif). Based on the NGM analysis, 1, 2, and 3 s pulse chronoamperometry was selected and applied over ten cycles. Charge densities increased from 4.43 to 14.93 and 25.28 mC cm−2, respectively, as the electrosynthesis time increased. SEM micrographs showed an evolution from compact films to deposits with greater three-dimensional development, while XRD confirmed that PPy retained its amorphous character. The HOMO level shifted slightly from −5.40 to −5.36 eV, while the optical band gap decreased from 3.58 ± 0.04 to 3.35 ± 0.05 eV. TD-DFT calculations showed a reduction in excitation energy as pyrrole oligomer conjugation increased. Under these experimental conditions, the identified mechanisms enabled the selection of electrosynthesis times and the correlation of the growth progression with the morphology and electronic structure of the films.

title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
summary: The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling ph
content: The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp 2 -hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
summary: Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using p
content: Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the mdx mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

title: Little Red Dots: One Photometric Tag Concealing Diverse Spectroscopic Flavors of Massive Star Formation and Black Hole Activity
summary: We compile JWST/NIRSpec prism and MIRI data for 249 Little Red Dots (LRDs) at 2.3 < z < 9.3, forming a representative spectroscopic subset of NIRCam-selected LRDs. We derive a median stacked spectrum covering rest-frame 0.09–1.2 μ m, with M
content: We compile JWST/NIRSpec prism and MIRI data for 249 Little Red Dots (LRDs) at 2.3 < z < 9.3, forming a representative spectroscopic subset of NIRCam-selected LRDs. We derive a median stacked spectrum covering rest-frame 0.09–1.2 μ m, with MIRI photometry extending the spectral energy distribution to 4 μ m. 49 49 Downloadable from Zenodo: doi: 10.5281/zenodo.22206191. Four additional stacks for subsamples defined by optical-to-UV luminosity ratios show that LRDs form a heterogeneous population spanning diverse continuum slopes and line properties. Assuming LRDs host supermassive black holes (BHs) surrounded by dense gas clouds, and stars accompany this core, we infer masses of M BH ∼ 10 6.0−6.5 M ⊙ and M ⋆ ∼ 10 8.3 M ⊙, corresponding to BH-to-stellar mass ratios of 1%–2%. The stacks show ubiquitous UV and optical Fe II emission, indicating a direct view of the broad-line region and high (but sub-Eddington) accretion (λ Edd = 0.6 ± 0.2). We find a significant stellar contribution in the far-UV, reaching ∼80% in the bluest systems. Possible Wolf–Rayet features (He II λ 4687, nitrogen lines) are identified, tracing a young (3–7 Myr) compact starburst event. We also detect strong Balmer breaks and atypical Balmer, Paschen, [O III], and optical and near-infrared He I line ratios, and an absorption at ∼4550 Å (probably linked to Fe II), all consistent with radiative-transfer effects in high-density gas with warm temperatures (4000–7000 K). We find a diversity of LRD flavors modulated by the luminosity ratio between a short (≲20 Myr) and intense phase of BH activity, the most extreme stage lasting ∼3–7 Myr, characterized by near-Eddington-limit radiation, and a nuclear and compact starburst dominated by massive stars (even supermassive, M SMS ∼ 10 5 M ⊙), all embedded in dense gas with modest dust content producing a variety of optical depths.

title: The Yersinia pestis effector YopM binds the human pyrin death domain to inhibit inflammasome activation and effector-triggered immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Bacteria in the genus Yersinia use type III secretion to inject several effectors into phagocytes to disrupt signaling. Two effectors disrupt host signaling by inactivation of RhoA, triggering pyrin inflammasome assembly in infected phagocy
content: Bacteria in the genus Yersinia use type III secretion to inject several effectors into phagocytes to disrupt signaling. Two effectors disrupt host signaling by inactivation of RhoA, triggering pyrin inflammasome assembly in infected phagocytes and protective immunity. A third protein, YopM, counteracts effector-triggered immunity by binding to and inactivating pyrin. Prior evidence suggested that gain of function codon changes in the pyrin gene MEFV that cause Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and provide resistance to Yersinia pestis were selected to evade YopM binding. YopM was shown to bind an N-terminal region of human pyrin, which includes the eponymous pyrin domain (PYD), however, the interaction mechanism was undefined. Using bacterial two-hybrid assay, protein biochemistry, and X-ray crystallography, we determined that YopM binds to the PYD, which has few validated FMF amino acid variants. We show that YopM binds PYD R42, a “Site 2” amino acid important for positive and negative regulation of pyrin and that binding to the R42W variant is reduced. YopM amino acid change variants defective for PYD binding failed to inhibit the pyrin inflammasome in human monocytes infected with Yersinia. In addition, PYD binding was dispensable for YopM to inhibit the inflammasome in murine macrophages, suggesting this effector uses a distinct mechanism to target mouse pyrin. These results define that Y. pestis YopM binds to human PYD to promote pathogenesis, and because Site 2 variants that evade YopM binding have low gain of function inflammasome activity, these data may explain why most validated FMF codon changes are in other domains of pyrin.

title: Chronobiology reveals the hidden temporal organization of European beech forest phenology
summary: Biological timing is a core organizing principle across life on Earth, aligning internal physiology with environmental cues. However, whereas animal chronobiology considers seasonal behavior rhythmically, plant phenological dynamics are com
content: Biological timing is a core organizing principle across life on Earth, aligning internal physiology with environmental cues. However, whereas animal chronobiology considers seasonal behavior rhythmically, plant phenological dynamics are commonly analyzed as transition dates. Here, we extend chronobiological concepts to plant phenology by applying actigraphic metrics to annual vegetation photothermal activity. Using satellite time series of beech forests, we quantify fragmentation, consolidation and amplitude of their seasonal rhythm across Europe, and how their annual rhythms are regionally organized. A marked spring–autumn asymmetry emerges: spring green-up is event-driven and decoupled from photothermal peak activity, whereas autumn decline is cumulative and tightly synchronized with the rest phase and the overall annual rhythm. Consistently, beech forests segregate into chronotypes differing in timing and consolidation of rest–activity phases. These findings reveal a previously hidden rhythmic dimension of intraspecific phenological strategies, providing an ecosystem-scale characterization of the emergent temporal organization of vegetation activity.

title: Four-Dimensional Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Nanoscale Phase Mapping of the Lithium-Metal Surface Passivation Layer
summary: Mapping microstructural features is vital to developing next-generation materials in renewable energy applications. However, the nanometer-scale dimensions, chemical heterogeneity, and beam sensitivity of these materials make their structur
content: Mapping microstructural features is vital to developing next-generation materials in renewable energy applications. However, the nanometer-scale dimensions, chemical heterogeneity, and beam sensitivity of these materials make their structural characterization exceptionally challenging. Here, we present a data acquisition and analysis workflow for four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) applied to a beam-sensitive lithium-metal filament sample with a surface passivation layer. By combining data dimensionality reduction with unsupervised machine-learning approaches, we perform real-space clustering to enhance signal-to-noise ratios across large data sets. Automated Bragg reflection analysis was then used to identify distinct crystallographic phases within the surface passivation layer. This approach enables nanoscale phase mapping of dominant species across large fields of view with nanometer-level lateral resolution. We identify lithium oxide and lithium hydroxide as the predominant crystalline phases in the lithium-metal surface passivation layer.

title: Copper derived from deep-sea hydrothermal vent minerals facilitates hydrogen cyanide formation from glycine in alkaline aqueous environment
summary: In prevailing origin of life scenarios, hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is a key molecule for forming life’s essential building blocks, as demonstrated by HCN-centric prebiotic chemistry. However, whether HCN can be in-situ generated near deep-sea h
content: In prevailing origin of life scenarios, hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is a key molecule for forming life’s essential building blocks, as demonstrated by HCN-centric prebiotic chemistry. However, whether HCN can be in-situ generated near deep-sea hydrothermal vents (HVs) has remained unexplored. Here, we show that a Cu-rich natural HV mineral reacts with glycine to generate HCN under alkaline, anaerobic conditions. Using 13 C-isotopic labelled glycine, in-situ generation of HCN from glycine is confirmed, reaching concentration of 451.42 nM at 25 °C in 24 hours. HCN yield increases threefold at 10 °C. Copper leaching, and HCN generation from a glycine-CuCl 2 mixture, or from synthetic Cu(Gly) 2 in an anaerobic alkaline solution, indicate that copper(II) functions as an oxidant in this process. Because glycine can be generated through multiple pathways, our findings integrate cyanide chemistry into alkaline Cu-bearing HV environments, expanding the chemical diversity accessible within alkaline vent environments and potentially analogous systems beyond Earth.

title: Drivers of aerosol variability in the high Arctic: insights from integrated observations at Gruvebadet and Zeppelin (Ny-Ålesund)
summary: This paper summarizes the main results from the scientific project “Boundary layer Evolution Through Harmonization of Aerosol measurements at Ny-Ålesund research stations” (BETHA-NyÅ), in which aerosol measurements of two Arctic atmospheric
content: This paper summarizes the main results from the scientific project “Boundary layer Evolution Through Harmonization of Aerosol measurements at Ny-Ålesund research stations” (BETHA-NyÅ), in which aerosol measurements of two Arctic atmospheric observatories located near Ny-Ålesund (Svalbard) at different elevations were harmonized: at the Gruvebadet atmospheric laboratory (61 m a.s.l.) and Zeppelin observatory (472 m a.s.l.). This approach allows for a better understanding of how atmospheric layering may affect the variability of aerosol observations in the Ny-Ålesund area. From February 2022 to March 2023, a coordinated sampling campaign enabled a direct comparison of optical, chemical, and physical aerosol properties, integrated with meteorological data from the Amundsen-Nobile Climate Change Tower. Results reveal a strong seasonal coherence between the two sites for two topical markers such as sulfate and ammonium, with clear evidence of the winter–spring Arctic Haze phenomenon. Local differences emerged mainly for biogenic tracers (e.g., arabitol and mannitol) which were detected at higher concentrations at Gruvebadet compared to Zeppelin observatory, highlighting the role of near-surface sources and aerosol stratification. The analysis of trace elements, lead isotopic ratios, and organic markers helped us to distinguish natural from anthropogenic contributions, confirming the dominant role of long-range transport and the persistence of isotopic signatures consistent with Eurasian sources. The systematic comparison across the two observatories demonstrates the robustness of the harmonized protocol and emphasizes the importance of an integrated monitoring network for evaluating the evolution of atmospheric processes in the Arctic.

title: Yoda molecules agonize PIEZO2
summary: Mammalian PIEZO proteins (PIEZO1 and PIEZO2) act as essential mechanosensitive channels. PIEZO1 is thought to be selectively activated by Yoda molecules (Yoda1 and Yoda2). Although a molecular mechanism for PIEZO1 activation by Yoda1 exists
content: Mammalian PIEZO proteins (PIEZO1 and PIEZO2) act as essential mechanosensitive channels. PIEZO1 is thought to be selectively activated by Yoda molecules (Yoda1 and Yoda2). Although a molecular mechanism for PIEZO1 activation by Yoda1 exists, the origin of Yoda1 selective agonism remains obscure. Here, using electrophysiology and calcium imaging in transfected cells, we show that Yoda1 agonizes PIEZO2, but with a distinct efficacy profile compared to PIEZO1. Yoda1 increases single-channel open probability and macroscopic stretch sensitivity of PIEZO2 currents as efficaciously as reported for PIEZO1, but it elicits weak PIEZO2-dependent calcium influx in the absence of external stimulus, an effect detectable only under non-physiological conditions. Yoda1 slows down inactivation of indentation-evoked PIEZO2 currents, but to a lower extent compared to PIEZO1. The Yoda1 analog Dooku1, which does not modulate PIEZO1, slows down PIEZO2 inactivation similarly to Yoda1. Two PIEZO1 agonists unrelated to Yoda1 but thought to populate the same binding site in PIEZO1 have no effect on PIEZO2 inactivation, suggesting that their PIEZO1 selectivity is better than Yoda1. PIEZO2 inactivation is also modulated by Yoda1’s more potent analog Yoda2. Using mutagenesis and molecular dynamics simulations, we show that Yoda2’s benzoic acid group forms a transient salt-bridge with a conserved arginine in the Yoda binding site (R1724/R2029 in mouse PIEZO1/PIEZO2), explaining the higher potency of this analog for both channels. Together, our study re-evaluates the PIEZO1 selectivity of Yoda molecules and highlights a complex modulatory landscape toward distinct functional properties of PIEZO channels.

title: Data-driven moving-window Bayesian inference for transient CO2–temperature network models of buildings
summary: In this work, we propose a CO 2 –temperature network model that links multi-zone mass transport and thermal dynamics through shared latent drivers, airflow and occupancy. The thermal component is formulated as a resistance-capacitance (RC)
content: In this work, we propose a CO 2 –temperature network model that links multi-zone mass transport and thermal dynamics through shared latent drivers, airflow and occupancy. The thermal component is formulated as a resistance-capacitance (RC) network augmented with airflow-driven convective exchange, while the CO 2 component is governed by inter-zonal convective transport. To calibrate the model and track time-varying operating conditions based on sparse sensing, we introduce a moving-window Bayesian inference procedure that jointly estimates thermal parameters, airflow and occupancy trajectories. The estimation also provides room-specific sensor noise levels, yielding posterior predictive forecasts with credible intervals. The framework is assessed using a controlled synthetic benchmark and a scaled physical validation experiment using CO 2 and temperature sensing. In both settings, the posterior provides locally accurate reconstructions and adapts after abrupt regime changes, with widened posterior uncertainty indicating periods of model–data mismatch. A temperature-only calibration further shows that the CO 2 observations accelerate post-transition temperature-forecast recovery in the synthetic benchmark and more strongly constrain the shared source and airflow parameters in the scaled experiment. Overall, coupling CO 2 -informed airflow with thermal dynamics provides a physically interpretable framework for transient multi-zone temperature prediction under limited sensing.

title: Paragenetic Formation of Aqueous Alteration Minerals Under Volcanically Active, Oxidative Weathering Conditions on Mars
summary: The chemical weathering of the Martian basaltic crust produces a complex assemblage of aqueous alteration minerals. These alteration minerals can provide critical constraints on the composition of the aqueous and atmospheric systems that pr
content: The chemical weathering of the Martian basaltic crust produces a complex assemblage of aqueous alteration minerals. These alteration minerals can provide critical constraints on the composition of the aqueous and atmospheric systems that produce them. Alteration minerals discovered on Mars include massive global deposits of phyllosilicates, sulfates, and iron (oxyhydr)oxides and localized detections of carbonates and halides. These deposits are rarely monomineralic and are the result of complex geological and geochemical processing of the surface material. Several physicochemical parameters influence and determine the type of alteration mineral produced, including temperature, composition of the atmosphere, amount and composition of the alteration fluid, availability of oxidants, and the protolith. Here, we take a thermodynamic modeling approach to study the alteration of the average crust using the “Mazatzal” basalt at 25°C under volcanically active oxidative conditions. We simulated alteration under variable compositions of CO 2 and S‐bearing species at water‐to‐rock ratios between 0.1 and 10 6. Our results indicate that the alteration is strongly influenced by system acidity and the presence of S‐bearing gases. The alteration assemblage mostly comprised of phyllosilicates and sulfates; minor alteration phases included simpler silicates, oxides, and carbonates; chloride minerals did not form under modeled conditions. Our model assemblages are compared with alteration assemblages observed on Mars and are used to suggest potential pathways of their formation.

title: Interaction‐Rich Odorant Receptor Neighborhoods and Olfaction‐Dependent Subsocial Behavior in a Parasitoid Wasp
summary: Insect social behaviors are closely linked to olfaction; yet the genomic mechanisms shaping chemoreceptor expansion and behavior remain poorly understood. The subsocial ectoparasitoid wasp Sclerodermus guani relies on olfaction to coordinat
content: Insect social behaviors are closely linked to olfaction; yet the genomic mechanisms shaping chemoreceptor expansion and behavior remain poorly understood. The subsocial ectoparasitoid wasp Sclerodermus guani relies on olfaction to coordinate host‐seeking, reproduction, and maternal care, providing a tractable system to investigate these relationships. Here, we present a chromosome‐level genome assembly for S. guani and integrate chromatin conformation, transcriptomics, electrophysiology, and functional genetics to examine the organization and behavioral significance of odorant receptors (ORs). We identify 148 ORs marked by tandem expansion and sex‐biased antennal expression. These ORs preferentially occupy interaction‐rich topologically associating domains characterized by elevated interaction frequency, identifying a distinctive higher‐order genomic context for this expanded sensory receptor family. To functionally characterize this structurally organized receptor family, we generated a heritable null mutation in the OR co‐receptor (Orco). Orco mutants displayed severe impairments in host‐seeking, mating, oviposition, and maternal care. Strikingly, mutants frequently laid eggs on conspecific larvae, indicating a loss of kin recognition and raising the possibility that OR‐mediated olfaction contributes to parasitism and maternal care in this lineage. Together, these findings suggest that genome architecture may bias chemosensory gene diversification and that OR signaling is necessary for coordinated subsocial behavior in S. guani.

title: Impact of the equation of state on core collapse supernovae: I. The low- T / | W | instability
summary: Rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae are promising sources of multimessenger emission, as non-axisymmetric dynamics in the newly formed proto-neutron star can leave characteristic imprints on both gravitational waves and neutrinos. We
content: Rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae are promising sources of multimessenger emission, as non-axisymmetric dynamics in the newly formed proto-neutron star can leave characteristic imprints on both gravitational waves and neutrinos. We present three-dimensional neutrino-magnetohydrodynamics simulations of the collapse of a rapidly rotating 35 M ⊙ progenitor, performed with five different finite-temperature nuclear equations of state, to investigate how dense-matter physics affects the development of the low- T / | W | instability and its associated multimessenger signatures. We find that the low- T / | W | instability develops in all equation of state (EOS) models considered, indicating that its occurrence is robust for this rapidly rotating progenitor. However, its onset time, dominant azimuthal structure, lifetime, and characteristic multimessenger frequencies vary among models, reflecting differences in the evolving proto-neutron star structure and rotation profile. The instability produces large-scale spiral modes that generate quasi-periodic gravitational wave emission and modulate the neutrino luminosities, especially along directions close to the equatorial plane. The dominant gravitational wave frequency associated with the instability correlates with the effective stiffness and compactness of the proto-neutron star: models with more compact/stiffer configurations emit at higher frequencies. This suggests that, in rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae, the frequency of the low- T / | W | instability-driven gravitational wave signal may provide a diagnostic of the dense-matter EOS, complementary to the information carried by the neutrino signal.

title: Microbial exometabolite responses to root exudates from tallgrass prairie plants
summary: Root exudates influence soil microbial community assembly and function, yet plant species-specific effects on microbially-driven metabolic transformations remain insufficiently characterized under controlled conditions. Here, we present a m
content: Root exudates influence soil microbial community assembly and function, yet plant species-specific effects on microbially-driven metabolic transformations remain insufficiently characterized under controlled conditions. Here, we present a multi-omic dataset of exudate–microbe interactions across six plant species, including tallgrass prairie species (Helianthus pauciflorus, Carex brevior, Eragrostis spectabilis, Astragalus canadensis, and Panicum virgatum) and a model grass (Brachypodium distachyon), generated using an in vitro incubation experiment. Sterile root exudates were used to amend a soil-mimicking medium inoculated with a native tallgrass prairie soil microbiome. The dataset includes full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing for microbial community profiling, untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics for exometabolomic profiling, and optical density measurements of microbial growth. We describe the axenic plant growth protocols, experimental design, data acquisition, processing workflows, and technical validation. This dataset provides a resource for investigating microbially mediated exometabolite transformations across diverse plant species to help understand rhizosphere processes, microbiome assembly, and ecosystem function.

title: Autochthonous Weissella cibaria paraprobiotics modulate inflammatory responses induced by heat-inactivated Aeromonas hydrophila in tambaqui
summary: This study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Weissella cibaria paraprobiotics (strains M14, I10, or their combination/MIX) for 60 days on growth performance, intestinal morphology, and immunoinflammatory responses in juv
content: This study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Weissella cibaria paraprobiotics (strains M14, I10, or their combination/MIX) for 60 days on growth performance, intestinal morphology, and immunoinflammatory responses in juvenile tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum). Heat treatment at 70 °C for 10 min resulted in no detectable bacterial growth under the culture conditions tested, while preserving gross cellular morphology. In contrast, exposure to 100 °C for 10 min caused evident morphological alterations, including increased surface roughness and visible surface disruption. Following the experimental induction of coelomitis using heat-inactivated Aeromonas hydrophila, paraprobiotic supplementation modulated innate immune and hematological responses. Increased serum lysozyme activity was observed in the M14 and MIX treatments, whereas myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity was higher in the I10 and MIX treatments. All supplemented groups exhibited reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which may reflect modulation of inflammatory responses or reduced phagocyte activation. Hematological alterations included changes in circulating leukocyte and thrombocyte profiles, with treatment-specific responses. The MIX treatment was associated with lower hepatic histopathological scores. Before the inflammatory challenge, the I10 treatment showed increased total leukocyte and thrombocyte counts, while neutrophilia and lymphopenia were observed in the supplemented groups. Furthermore, fish supplemented with I10 exhibited lower proximal intestinal mucosal fold height and width. No significant differences in zootechnical performance were observed among treatments. Overall, the findings suggest that heat-inactivated W. cibaria modulated innate immune and hematological responses 12 h after coelomitis induction in juvenile tambaqui. Future studies should investigate different doses of each strain in the formulation, evaluate inflammatory responses at multiple time points, and assess protection against bacterial infection through challenges with live bacteria.

title: Revisiting the Climate Benefits Provided by Wood through Future-Oriented Material and Energy Displacement
summary: Displacement factors (DFs) quantify climate benefits of wood-based products relative to non-wood alternatives. Existing DFs are typically static whereas economy-wide decarbonization motivates a forward-looking assessment. Previous work focu
content: Displacement factors (DFs) quantify climate benefits of wood-based products relative to non-wood alternatives. Existing DFs are typically static whereas economy-wide decarbonization motivates a forward-looking assessment. Previous work focuses on semifinished materials and lacks harmonized, transparent modeling. This study provides an open-access, unit-process-based database of future-oriented DFs for 81 wood-product-material-variants across six end-use categories. It uses time-explicit life cycle assessment (LCA), which links processes to the technology landscape as they occur, under three decarbonization scenarios for 2020–2070. Wood-based products showed positive DFs in 2020, with weighted averages from near-zero for furniture to 1.04 kg C/kg C for chemicals and textiles, though lower than previous estimates. DFs declined over time for all products except chemicals, most steeply under climate-ambitious scenarios. Wood sustained the highest benefit in the least ambitious scenario. The decline was driven by faster decarbonization of non-wood products that contain proportionally more fossil-intensive components. Time-explicit LCA yielded lower DFs for long-lived products as end-of-life processes were assigned to more decarbonized future years, an effect not captured by conventional or prospective LCA. Energy-related DFs approached near-zero by 2070. The findings support redirecting wood flows from energy toward long-lived material applications and caution against harvest intensification justified on displacement arguments alone.

title: Hybrid Ag/(Au)–ZnTCPP/ZnTSPP nanoparticles on solid substrates: a versatile platform for optical and electrochemical sensing of environmental and biological targets
summary: In this work, gold and silver nanoparticles functionalized with zinc complexes of tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (ZnTCPP) or tetrakis-(4-sulfonatophenyl) porphyrin (ZnTSPP) were synthesized via a sonochemical route and immobilized onto
content: In this work, gold and silver nanoparticles functionalized with zinc complexes of tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (ZnTCPP) or tetrakis-(4-sulfonatophenyl) porphyrin (ZnTSPP) were synthesized via a sonochemical route and immobilized onto solid substrates as Color Catcher® (CC) polymeric sheets or on-plastic Screen Printed Electrodes, SPEs, to develop an innovative colorimetric and electrochemical sensor for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) or dopamine screening in water and biological samples, respectively. Structural and morphological analyses (XRD, UV-Vis, Raman, XPS, FE-SEM, and TEM) confirmed the successful formation of ZnTCPP–metal nanocomposites with distinct plasmonic and SERS properties. The CC@Ag/(Au)–ZnTCPP/ZnTSPP sensors exhibited a visible colour shift from green to dark pink upon PFOA coordination, associated with spectroscopic changes in the Soret and Q-bands. The sensor demonstrated potential for integration into low-cost flow-through monitoring devices for PFOA presence monitoring. Quantitative colorimetric responses followed Langmuir and sigmoidal adsorption models for Au- and Ag-based systems, respectively, and detection limits of 0.0048 mM (AuNPs) and 0.0105 mM (AgNPs). Furthermore, the application of a dual-mode colorimetric and fluorimetric virtual sensor array based on CC@Au–ZnTSPP has permitted lowering the PFOA LOD to 0.006 nM (2.24 ng/L) in tap water. The ZnTCPP/ZnTSPP–AuNPs incorporated into conductive PANI and PPy films on screen-printed electrodes showed enhanced electrocatalytic activity for dopamine detection. The PANI/ZnTSPP–AuNPs films performed for DA anodic striping in synthetic urine samples with LOD and LOQ of 0.025 µM and 0.087 µM respectively, highlighting the multifunctionality of these nanohybrid materials for environmental and bioanalytical sensing applications.

title: Widely targeted metabolomics analysis of the main bioactive compounds in macadamia green husk processed by different drying methods
summary: Post-harvest drying strongly affects the bioactive composition of plant by-products, yet the metabolic response of macadamia green husk (MGH) to different drying methods remains poorly characterized, limiting the rational selection of dryin
content: Post-harvest drying strongly affects the bioactive composition of plant by-products, yet the metabolic response of macadamia green husk (MGH) to different drying methods remains poorly characterized, limiting the rational selection of drying protocols for this abundant nut-processing waste. The main challenge is that drying-induced changes are compound-specific and cannot be resolved by conventional colorimetric methods. This study aimed to elucidate how different drying methods reshape the metabolome and bioactive quality of MGH and to provide a scientific basis for application-oriented drying protocols. Three drying methods, namely sun-drying (SMH), hot-air drying at 60 °C (HMH), and vacuum freeze-drying (FMH), were systematically compared using widely targeted metabolomics combined with biochemical assays. Unlike previous studies that mainly reported total phenolic and flavonoid contents, this study identified 1,292 metabolites across 12 subclasses, with phenolic acids (17.72%), flavonoids (17.03%), amino acids and derivatives (14.01%), and lipids (11.46%) as the dominant fractions. FMH best preserved heat-sensitive antioxidants, yielding the highest total phenolic content (TPC, 243.74 ± 8.94 mg/g). It also showed the strongest antioxidant activity, with DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) radical scavenging activity of 77.04 ± 1.17% and ABTS+ (2,2′-azino-bis (3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) radical cation) scavenging activity of 82.56 ± 1.47%. HMH significantly enhanced extractable flavonoids via cell wall disruption, and flavonoid-biosynthesis-associated metabolites were notably enriched in HMH. SMH uniquely promoted accumulation of terpenoids (195.23 ± 33.48 mg/g), with metabolites related to glycerolipid metabolism showing prominent enrichment in SMH. Correlation analysis indicated that antioxidant capacity was primarily driven by phenolics, while flavonoids and polysaccharides also showed notable associations with antioxidant performance. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting application-oriented drying protocols: FMH for high-antioxidant extracts, HMH for flavonoid-enriched materials, and SMH for terpenoid-rich products. This work facilitates the targeted valorization of MGH as a sustainable source of functional ingredients within a circular economy framework.

title: First divertor exposure experiments of a renewable boron pebble aggregate in DIII-D
summary: Boron pebble aggregate was tested for the first time as a high-heat-flux granular plasma facing material in a tokamak divertor. Exposures of up to q∥ = 80 MW/m² incident heat flux were conducted in the DIII-D tokamak. Single protruding rods
content: Boron pebble aggregate was tested for the first time as a high-heat-flux granular plasma facing material in a tokamak divertor. Exposures of up to q∥ = 80 MW/m² incident heat flux were conducted in the DIII-D tokamak. Single protruding rods of pebble aggregate composed of sintered amorphous boron pebbles bound with carbon binder were mounted in the Divertor Material Evaluation System (DiMES) sample holders and exposed to L-mode lower single null (LSN) plasmas. Under these heat loads, significant boron dust emission from the boron spheres was observed, and this dust dominates the divertor boron ionization source. Only about half of the released boron was recovered locally as mm-sized particles, with the rest presumably lost mainly as dust into the plasma and vacuum chamber. Preliminary estimates suggest that the rate of surface recession of ~1 cm/s in the pebble conglomerate within the plasma divertor is consistent with the recession rates observed in laser bench tests subjected to normal incidence heat loads. Although core performance was not adversely affected by the high boron dust emission, future work will need to improve the boron pebble aggregate design to reduce boron dust emission at high heat loads.

title: Natural-Based Biocomposites of Chitosan, β-Cyclodextrin, and Potato Peel Waste for the Adsorptive Removal of Sunset Yellow and Diclofenac
summary: This study aimed to prepare and evaluate the adsorptive potential of biocomposites produced from potato peel waste (PPW), β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), and chitosan (CS) in different proportions for removing Sunset Yellow FCF (SY) and diclofenac p
content: This study aimed to prepare and evaluate the adsorptive potential of biocomposites produced from potato peel waste (PPW), β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), and chitosan (CS) in different proportions for removing Sunset Yellow FCF (SY) and diclofenac potassium (DCP) from aqueous solutions. The biocomposites (BC) were characterized by FTIR, XRD, SEM, EDS, and TGA, which confirmed the successful crosslinking and the synergistic integration of the three components, producing materials rich in –OH and –NH 2 groups, in addition to an amorphous character, different morphological surfaces, and sufficient thermal stability. Adsorption experiments revealed that pH significantly influenced removal efficiency, with optimal performance at pH 4 for both contaminants (> 90% for SY and > 83% for DCP). For SY, the general-order kinetic model provided the best fit, while the Sips isotherm model most accurately represented the equilibrium data, with q m values ranging from 18.70 to 221.89 mg g⁻ 1. For DCP, the pseudo-second-order model best described the kinetic behavior, with k LDF values ranging from 0.0017 to 0.0052 min-1, while the Sips model again best fit the equilibrium isotherms (q m 151.11 to 757.29 mg g −1). Among the materials, BC-5 exhibited favorable adsorption characteristics toward both contaminants, with capacities of 221.89 mg g⁻ 1 for SY and 151.11 mg g⁻ 1 for DCP. In addition, BC-5 showed good regeneration potential, maintaining effective adsorption performance over 5 consecutive reuse cycles for SY and 4–5 cycles for DCP. These findings highlight the potential of PPW/β-CD/CS biocomposites as reusable adsorbents for treating aqueous systems containing dyes and emerging pharmaceutical contaminants.

title: Technical note: A decoupled in situ framework for aerosol multi-wavelength optical properties: application for lidar retrievals
summary: Accurate constraints on aerosol complex refractive index (CRI), single scattering albedo (SSA), and lidar ratio (LR) are essential for improving lidar-based aerosol retrievals and reducing radiative-effect uncertainties. However, their cons
content: Accurate constraints on aerosol complex refractive index (CRI), single scattering albedo (SSA), and lidar ratio (LR) are essential for improving lidar-based aerosol retrievals and reducing radiative-effect uncertainties. However, their consistent derivation from in situ observations remains challenging because size distribution, absorption, and humidity effects are coupled. Here we present a decoupled inversion framework that integrates SMPS–OPC size distributions, AE33-derived absorption coefficients, and ambient relative humidity observations from the Vipava Valley (Slovenia) in April 2016 to derive dry-state homogeneous-equivalent CRI and RH-corrected lidar-relevant SSA and LR at 355, 532, and 1064 nm. The framework reconstructs a continuous particle size distribution through instrument-response-aware SMPS–OPC geometric alignment and retrieves the reference real refractive index. AE33-derived absorption constraints and a singly subtractive Kramers–Kronig (SSKK) relation are then used to derive the dry-state CRI spectrum, after which SSA and LR are recalculated through an RH-corrected wet-state forward optical calculation. Under the assumed AE33 reference scenario with an effective multiple-scattering correction factor of C eff =5, mean dry-state n values were 1.449, 1.441, and 1.437, and mean k values were 0.0309, 0.0235, and 0.0190 at 355, 532, and 1064 nm, respectively. The RH-corrected mean SSA values were 0.855, 0.841, and 0.760, and the corresponding mean LR values were 86.53, 57.59, and 39.81 sr. Increasing C eff from 1.57 to 5 decreased median RH-corrected LR 355 from 137.3 to 84.3 sr and increased median SSA 355 from 0.646 to 0.867. These conditional, site-specific estimates link dry in situ retrievals with RH-corrected lidar-relevant optical properties.

title: Poly (aniline‑2-sulfonic acid) core-shell gold nanoparticles decorated as a non-enzymatic electrochemical sensor for Dopamine determination
summary: A novel non-enzymatic electrochemical sensing platform was developed for the sensitive and selective determination of dopamine (DA) based on a magnetic Fe 3 O 4 @ZnO core–shell nanocomposite functionalized with poly(aniline-2-sulfonic acid)
content: A novel non-enzymatic electrochemical sensing platform was developed for the sensitive and selective determination of dopamine (DA) based on a magnetic Fe 3 O 4 @ZnO core–shell nanocomposite functionalized with poly(aniline-2-sulfonic acid) and decorated with gold nanoparticles (Fe 3 O 4 -ZnO–PA2S–Au). The structural, morphological, and optical characteristics of the synthesized nanocomposite were systematically confirmed by FT-IR, XRD, SEM, TEM, EDX mapping, and DRS. The synergy between the semiconducting magnetic core–shell framework, the π\piπ-conjugated conducting polymer backbone, and the catalytic Au relays significantly facilitated electron-transfer kinetics and enlarged the electroactive surface area. Under optimized square wave voltammetry (SWV) conditions, the modified carbon paste electrode exhibited a wide linear dynamic range of 5.0 to 64.0 µM, a high sensitivity of 50.29 µA⋅µM − 1 (R 2 = 0.998) with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.19 µM and a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 0.64 µM (S/N = 3). Furthermore, differential pulse voltammetry (SWV) demonstrated clear peak separation and robust discrimination against common physiological interferents (Glucose, urea and metal ions). The proposed sensor provides a promising, cost-effective, and highly reproducible analytical tool for clinical diagnostics and neurological monitoring.

title: Stream-driven Ignition of a Realistic Undisturbed Helium Shell on a White Dwarf
summary: The dynamically driven double-degenerate double-detonation (D 6) model has emerged as a promising progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae. In this model, a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) in a close double WD binary undergoes a double-det
content: The dynamically driven double-degenerate double-detonation (D 6) model has emerged as a promising progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae. In this model, a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) in a close double WD binary undergoes a double-detonation triggered by dynamical mass transfer from its companion. The mass transfer stream directly impacts the surface of the primary WD, potentially igniting a helium detonation in the surface layer. The resulting shock converges in the core, triggering a carbon detonation that ultimately unbinds the star. While previous studies have demonstrated the viability of this mechanism, the conditions under which the helium shell ignites remain uncertain. We perform two-dimensional simulations using FLASH to study the feasibility of helium detonation ignition driven by stream impact on a carbon–oxygen WD with a realistic, unmixed composition profile left at the end of the previous helium-shell burning phase before the WD was formed. We model WDs with masses of 0.8, 0.9, and 1.0 M ⊙ and vary stream properties for each case. We find that stream impact leads to helium ignition in all cases, with ignition occurring at varying distances from the impact point. Ignition consistently occurs near the core–shell transition, highlighting the importance of a realistic WD profile. However, the ignition mechanism differs between models and can arise from interactions of neighboring hot, mixed regions rather than a single point. Ultimately, all but one sustain a propagating detonation capable of traversing the WD surface, which is suggestive of the D 6 model’s viability as a progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae.

title: Electromagnetically driven thermal dissipation scaling in plasma centrifuges for mass separation
summary: Electromagnetically driven centrifuges (EMDCs) rotate fluids using the Lorentz force, but their separative performance is limited by thermal dissipation that is coupled to electromagnetic forcing. This follows because local centrifugal stre
content: Electromagnetically driven centrifuges (EMDCs) rotate fluids using the Lorentz force, but their separative performance is limited by thermal dissipation that is coupled to electromagnetic forcing. This follows because local centrifugal strength is characterized by λ=mV_θ^2/2k_B T, which compares directed kinetic energy that drives species separation to thermal energy that smooths concentration gradients and counteracts separation. In this work, we develop a two-temperature magnetohydrodynamic model to determine how radial geometry, current density, and magnetic field strength control the coupled evolution of rotation and heating that dictates λ. The model is benchmarked against argon velocity, temperature, and pressure measurements spanning current density up to 15 kA/m2, magnetic field up to 0.57 T, feed pressures of 0.5-3 Torr, and annulus sizes of 1-5 cm. A separate Ar/Kr experiment provides evidence of mass-dependent radial compositional redistribution and is used to evaluate whether the model captures the expected separation mechanism under low-field conditions. The results show that volumetric Lorentz forcing sustains elevated λ, and therefore greater local compositional shifts throughout a larger radial portion of the fluid volume than wall-bounded shear centrifuges, despite producing a lower peak λ. Simulations of a 40Ar/36Ar isotopic mixture demonstrate that, when electromagnetic force and geometry are jointly optimized, EMDCs can approach or match the separative performance of shear-driven centrifuges operating near material speed limits while requiring lower area-averaged values of λ, and can sustain greater radial compositional shifts than the SDC reference over much of the annulus. These results challenge assertions that viscous dissipation constrains weakly ionized plasma centrifuges to λ<1, and indicate that enhanced radial mass separation can be achieved by broadening the radial region over which λ remains elevated rather than maximizing its peak or area-averaged value.

title: A determination of the backscattering probability of low-energy antiprotons
summary: It is commonly assumed that antiprotons impinging on a material surface annihilate promptly with the nuclei of the material. However, at kinetic energies of a few keV, this assumption may not hold. As with low-energy protons, electrons or p
content: It is commonly assumed that antiprotons impinging on a material surface annihilate promptly with the nuclei of the material. However, at kinetic energies of a few keV, this assumption may not hold. As with low-energy protons, electrons or positrons that can be reflected from a target, they may undergo large-angle Coulomb scattering before annihilation occurs, thereby appearing to be “backscattered” from the material surface. This backscattering fraction, largely unknown, is a crucial ingredient to the determination of the production cross-section of antihydrogen atoms in the GBAR experiment. This paper presents a determination of the probability that 4 and 6 keV antiprotons backscatter on the surface of a Micro-Channel Plate detector used for beam imaging at GBAR. No evidence for backscattering has been found and an upper limit of $$14\%$$ 14 % at $$68\%$$ 68 % confidence level has been set on this probability. The impact of backscattering on the determination of the number of antiprotons that participate in antihydrogen production in GBAR is also addressed.

title: A review on design of floating offshore wind farm control systems
summary: Floating wind energy is growing rapidly, as it enables energy generation in deep water and avoids near-coastal development barriers. In floating offshore wind farms (FOWFs), inter-turbine aerodynamic interference known as the wake effect ra
content: Floating wind energy is growing rapidly, as it enables energy generation in deep water and avoids near-coastal development barriers. In floating offshore wind farms (FOWFs), inter-turbine aerodynamic interference known as the wake effect raises the levelized cost of energy (LCOE). Wind farm control (WFC) mitigates this effect by coordinating turbines at the farm level. Designing a WFC system, however, requires choosing a WFC strategy, model dependency, and communication topology, choices that jointly determine the feasibility and performance of the resulting system. To map the current research landscape and identify unexplored gaps, this paper presents a systematic review of current studies on WFC design for FOWFs across four dimensions: WFC strategy, model dependency, communication topology, and simulated environmental conditions. The analysis reveals that turbine repositioning is the most mature and highest-gain strategy, whereas wake mixing has yet to be demonstrated at large scale. Moreover, attention is uneven across objectives, with most studies concentrating on power maximization and load minimization, leaving power tracking largely untouched. Additionally, reviewed studies are either model-based or built on precomputed look-up tables designed only for ideal wind conditions, and 85\% adopt a centralized communication scheme. No study combines a model-free scheme with a noncentralized topology. Therefore, the field has not yet tested the architectures or the conditions most relevant to utility-scale deployment. Building on these findings, we summarize unique FOWF control challenges and recommend research directions toward feasible, effective WFC systems for commercial-scale floating wind.

title: A global simplified process-based greenhouse-gas model for rice paddies
summary: Background: Rice paddies are important agricultural sources of methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O), yet quantifying these emissions remains challenging in regions with limited monitoring capacity. Most process-based biogeochemical models
content: Background: Rice paddies are important agricultural sources of methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O), yet quantifying these emissions remains challenging in regions with limited monitoring capacity. Most process-based biogeochemical models require extensive information on soil properties, hydrology, management practices, and environmental conditions limiting large-scale assessments, mitigation planning and cost-efficient CO2-eq calculations.Objectives: This work develops and evaluates a simplified, process-based framework to simulate daily CH4 and N₂O emissions from rice agriculture using minimal inputs. It integrates three coupled models: water balance, CH₄ emissions, and N₂O emissions.,Methods: For calibration and validation, a global dataset of 355 field trials, including water level measurements and CH4 and N2O flux observations, from 30 studies published between 2000 and 2025 was collected.Results: The water model reproduced daily water dynamics, with reasonable performance, driving greenhouse gas (GHG) simulations. CH4 and N₂O models performed with a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 2.65 kg CH₄ ha⁻¹ d⁻¹ and 0.09 kg N₂O ha⁻¹ d⁻¹ and normalized RMSE (NRMSE) of 1.05 and 1.02 in the validation dataset, values comparable to established biogeochemical models. While extreme peaks were sometimes underestimated, results indicate that major temporal patterns and magnitudes of CH4 and N2O emissions can be captured using a low-input framework. The framework provides a practical tool for large-scale GHG budgeting, carbon farming applications, and the evaluation of mitigation strategies in rice agriculture.

title: Effects of Prefabricated Hole-Edge Delamination Parameters on the Tensile Response and Damage Evolution of Composite Single-Bolt Double-Shear Joints
summary: Composite single-bolt double-shear joints with prefabricated hole-edge delamination are systematically investigated through experimental and numerical approaches. Tensile tests are conducted on specimens with delamination diameters of 0, 12
content: Composite single-bolt double-shear joints with prefabricated hole-edge delamination are systematically investigated through experimental and numerical approaches. Tensile tests are conducted on specimens with delamination diameters of 0, 12, 20 and 28 mm. A three-dimensional progressive damage model incorporating the Hashin-type failure criterion and Camanho degradation model is developed using a UMAT subroutine, with cohesive elements introduced to simulate delamination. Numerical predictions agree well with experiments, with errors within 10%. Parametric studies reveal that delamination location, shape, and orientation all significantly affect joint performance. Small delaminations propagate extensively beyond their initial region, whereas large delaminations exhibit limited propagation beyond the prefabricated defect. The ultimate load decreases by 5.7% as the delamination diameter increases from 0 to 28 mm. The proposed method provides a reliable tool for damage-tolerant design of composite bolted joints.

title: Emulsifier-assisted two-step hydrodeoxygenation of biocrude to produce fuel oil
summary: High oxygen content and poor miscibility of hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) biocrude in petroleum fractions limit its incorporation into refinery fuel streams. To tackle this processability issue, this study investigates decanol-assisted tw
content: High oxygen content and poor miscibility of hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) biocrude in petroleum fractions limit its incorporation into refinery fuel streams. To tackle this processability issue, this study investigates decanol-assisted two-step hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of a mixture of refinery distillate and HTL biocrude-ethanol blend. The study compares catalyst types and different approaches to upgrading biocrude-refinery-distillate blends. The approaches include direct blending, decanol addition, intermediate decanol-added mild-HDO treatment and thermal mixing of mild-HDO mixture with refinery distillate before final HDO. Performance of each strategy was assessed by liquid product yield, oxygen removal and fuel quality. Two-step HDO using NiMo/γAl 2 O 3 catalyst achieved higher liquid yield (77 wt%) than CoMo/γAl 2 O 3 (65 wt%), without decanol. Direct decanol addition increased the yield to 85.4 wt% with oxygen content of 2.6 wt%. The best performance was obtained by thermally mixing the mild-HDO biocrude intermediate with refinery distillate before two-step HDO. The liquid product yield was 93.6 wt%, containing 1.7 wt% oxygen, 85.4 wt% carbon, and HHV of 45.3 MJ/kg. The findings show that decanol bridges the polar and non-polar compounds, while staged hydrotreatment stabilizes reactive oxygenates at 180 °C before deoxygenating them at 320 °C, to produce a homogeneous biocrude-containing refinery-distillate blend.

title: Influence of Applied Potential on Albumin Adsorption and Electrochemical Accessibility at Gold and Graphitic Carbon Interfaces
summary: Biofouling is a complex and dynamic interfacial process that limits continuous and long-term sensing. Unlike passive surfaces, electrochemical sensors operate under electrical control, yet the relationship among applied potential, protein a
content: Biofouling is a complex and dynamic interfacial process that limits continuous and long-term sensing. Unlike passive surfaces, electrochemical sensors operate under electrical control, yet the relationship among applied potential, protein adsorption, and sensor performance remains insufficiently understood. Here, bovine serum albumin (BSA) adsorption on gold and graphitic carbon electrodes was investigated at different applied potentials. Cyclic voltammetry with redox probes of different interfacial sensitivities and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy were used to evaluate electrochemical accessibility and charge-transfer behavior, while electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring was used to monitor BSA adsorption in situ under potential control and estimate the associated acoustically coupled mass. Positive polarization resulted in greater suppression of redox responses and higher charge-transfer resistance, with both effects generally more pronounced on gold than on graphitic carbon electrodes. This behavior is consistent with favorable interactions involving the negatively charged BSA molecules. In contrast, the potential dependence of the estimated acoustically coupled mass was more evident for graphitic carbon than for gold. These contrasting trends suggest that the amount of retained material cannot solely explain the changes in the electrochemical response following biofouling. A conceptual model is proposed to illustrate possible electrostatic and material-specific interactions that may influence the properties of protein-modified interfaces and consequently their electrochemical accessibility and sensor performance.

title: Technology and production of painted pottery at Mahtoutabad, Southeastern Iran, in the late 5th–early 4th millennia BCE
summary: This study focuses on the analysis of painted pottery from the earliest levels of the site of Mahtoutabad (Mahtoutabad I), located in the Halil Rud valley (Kerman province, south-eastern Iran), dated to the late 5th-early 4th millennium BCE
content: This study focuses on the analysis of painted pottery from the earliest levels of the site of Mahtoutabad (Mahtoutabad I), located in the Halil Rud valley (Kerman province, south-eastern Iran), dated to the late 5th-early 4th millennium BCE. The majority of the pottery presents remarkable polychrome decoration combining black, red, and white colors. This study aims to reconstruct the technological characteristics of this ware, so far unique in the area, combining macroscopic investigation with scientific techniques for a holistic understanding. The ceramic body is analyzed using ceramic petrography, X-Ray Fluorescence and X-Ray Powder Diffraction, while the painted coatings using micro-X-Ray Diffraction, Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy-Dispersive Spectrometry (SEM–EDS), and micro-X-Ray Fluorescence. This study offers the first systematic technological investigation of Mahtoutabad I pottery, one of the earliest investigated polychrome productions. It provides insights into the pottery production in the wider area and reveals inter- and intra-regional connections across time in the Chalcolithic period.

title: Structural, Optoelectronic, and Thermoelectric Properties of Transition-Metal-Based Dichalcogenides MoX2 (X = S, Se, Te) as Semiconductors for Photoelectronic Applications
summary: Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) MoX2 with (X = S, Se, Te) are systematically investigated using density functional theory (DFT) combined with Boltzmann transport theory within the relaxation-time approximation. The structural, optoe
content: Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) MoX2 with (X = S, Se, Te) are systematically investigated using density functional theory (DFT) combined with Boltzmann transport theory within the relaxation-time approximation. The structural, optoelectronic, and thermoelectric properties are analyzed using the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) and GGA-modified Becke–Johnson (GGA-mBJ) potential. The optimized structures and formation energies confirm that MoX2 compounds are thermodynamically stable in the hexagonal symmetry with the P63/mmc phase. Electronic band-structure and density of states calculations reveal semiconducting characteristics, with indirect band gaps decreasing from (X = S to Te) as the chalcogen atomic size increases. The calculated optical parameters, including dielectric function, absorption coefficient, optical conductivity, refractive index, reflectivity, and energy-loss function, show pronounced optical absorption in the visible–ultraviolet region, suggesting that MoX2 may have potential for photoelectronic, photovoltaic, and photodetection applications. Thermoelectric analysis further reveals that chalcogen substitution strongly affects the charge-carrier transport and thermoelectric efficiency. The studied MoX2 materials exhibit low electronic thermal conductivity and enhanced electrical transport properties, leading to favorable thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT = 1.083, 0.991, and 0.988) for MoS2, MoSe2, and MoTe2, respectively. The present findings highlight the potential of these layered MoX2 compounds for future photoelectronic, thermoelectric, and energy-conversion technologies.

title: Nitrogen-loud Quasars from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. II. Broad-line Region Metallicity and Relative Nitrogen Enrichment
summary: Whether the unusually strong nitrogen emission in nitrogen-loud (N-loud) quasars reflects high overall metallicity, enhanced nitrogen abundance relative to other elements, or both, has long been debated. We analyze the broad-line region (BL
content: Whether the unusually strong nitrogen emission in nitrogen-loud (N-loud) quasars reflects high overall metallicity, enhanced nitrogen abundance relative to other elements, or both, has long been debated. We analyze the broad-line region (BLR) abundances of 121 N-loud quasars at 2.13 ≤ z ≤ 3.90 selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 and construct a control sample of normal quasars matched in redshift, continuum luminosity, and virial black hole mass. Within the N-loud sample, metallicities inferred from N v /C iv span ∼3–50 Z ⊙ and are systematically higher than those inferred from the nitrogen-independent (Si iv + O iv])/C iv and Al iii /C iv diagnostics, which agree closely and mainly span ∼1–20 Z ⊙. Compared with the matched controls, the N-loud quasars show systematically higher metallicities in both N v /C iv and (Si iv + O iv])/C iv, with median values approximately 3 times those of the controls. Notably, the discrepancy between the metallicities inferred from N v /C iv and (Si iv + O iv])/C iv becomes more pronounced toward the high-metallicity end of the N-loud sample, suggesting additional nitrogen enrichment beyond the overall metal enrichment. Together, these results indicate that N-loud quasars have both high overall BLR metallicity and enhanced relative nitrogen abundance, suggesting that relative nitrogen abundance is at least partially decoupled from overall metallicity. N-loud quasars therefore provide a high-metallicity laboratory for understanding how nuclear environments can produce unusual abundance patterns and offer a complementary view of how nitrogen enrichment arises across cosmic time.

title: Heteropolar Photo-redox Junctions Based on Covalent Organic Frameworks for Overall H2O2 Photosynthesis
summary: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production from water and air offers a promising technology for solar-to-chemical conversion, yet it remains constrained by the sluggish kinetics of the water oxidation reaction (WOR) and oxygen reduc
content: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production from water and air offers a promising technology for solar-to-chemical conversion, yet it remains constrained by the sluggish kinetics of the water oxidation reaction (WOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Herein, we propose a heteropolar photo-redox junction system for efficient overall H2O2 photosynthesis by integrating the nonpolar tetraphenylpyrene and polar thiadiazole units into a single covalent organic framework (TT-COF), which serve as the WOR and ORR modules, respectively. The polarity difference between the two modules induces local charge polarization within TT-COF, promoting the formation of a built-in electric field to accelerate charge carrier separation and migration, thereby significantly boosting the photocatalytic kinetics of the two-electron WOR and ORR. TT-COF achieves a H2O2 production rate of 1968 μmol g–1 h–1 from water and air, which is 7.4 times higher than that of its polar-module-free counterpart (265 μmol g–1 h–1). This work provides an effective strategy for improving the overall H2O2 photosynthesis performance by modulating the molecular polarity of the building blocks of COFs.

title: The oxidation of drug molecules using the peroxygenase activity of a bacterial family of cytochrome P450 enzymes
summary: We use the natural peroxygenase activity of two CYP105 enzymes to biocatalytically oxidize the drug molecules papaverine and diclofenac to generate and characterize their metabolites.
content: We use the natural peroxygenase activity of two CYP105 enzymes to biocatalytically oxidize the drug molecules papaverine and diclofenac to generate and characterize their metabolites.

title: Correlating the distribution of site energies, activation energies and saddle point energies in the energy landscape of a lithium borate glass
summary: Long range transport of ions in a solid electrolyte is subject to the potential energy landscape in which local hopping of ions occurs. Here, the distributions of site energies, saddle point energies and activation energies are quantified.
content: Long range transport of ions in a solid electrolyte is subject to the potential energy landscape in which local hopping of ions occurs. Here, the distributions of site energies, saddle point energies and activation energies are quantified.

title: Stepwise Reduction of a Porphyrin Nanowire: Minimal Structural Reorganization up to the Open-Shell Tetraanion
summary: π-Conjugated porphyrin oligomers serve as molecular wires: they exhibit high single-molecule conductance and excellent cycling kinetics as organic active electrode materials. These applications require systems in which charge/discharge cycl
content: π-Conjugated porphyrin oligomers serve as molecular wires: they exhibit high single-molecule conductance and excellent cycling kinetics as organic active electrode materials. These applications require systems in which charge/discharge cycles cause minimal changes in molecular geometry. Here, we use a butadiyne-linked porphyrin dimer as a model compound to show that its chemical reduction with alkali metals leads to subtle changes in the bond lengths in the resulting multiply charged anions, as revealed crystallographically. The pattern of covalent bond lengths is largely retained across the crystallographically characterized charge states. π-Bond delocalization function (π-BDF) analysis shows that successive reduction increases π-electron delocalization within the porphyrin cores, while the involvement of the butadiyne linker is strongly charge- and spin-state-dependent. The previously unknown, structurally characterized tetraanion has an open-shell singlet diradical ground state with a thermally accessible triplet state, as confirmed by DFT calculations. The two open-shell states retain nearly identical covalent-delocalization topologies and differ primarily in the organization and coupling of their two unpaired electrons. Prolonged reaction with lithium metal leads to demetallation of these zinc porphyrins and cleavage of the butadiyne, forming an acetylene-appended porphyrin monomer.

title: Human appearance preferences as emergent properties of generalised learning
summary: The tendency to find some individuals or personal features more visually or aesthetically appealing than others (appearance preferences) is a widespread human experience. The underlying causes of why some people or features in particular ar
content: The tendency to find some individuals or personal features more visually or aesthetically appealing than others (appearance preferences) is a widespread human experience. The underlying causes of why some people or features in particular are considered attractive has been variably conceptualised as being the product of cultural power structures, a by-product of broader cognitive processes, and a reflection of 'innate' appearance preferences and processes shaped by sexual selection. Evolutionary-adaptationist and cognitive processing perspectives both prompted the development of a large literature attempting to understand why some specific traits are considered attractive. More recently, however, questions have emerged regarding the validity of the proposed 'adaptive' benefits of some of these traits within an evolutionary framework. Simultaneously, cross-cultural research has demonstrated that while some underlying cognitive processes may be similar across populations, specific appearance preferences are more variable than some 'functional' adaptationist hypotheses predict. The current paper outlines what key challenges exist for an approach to appearance preferences that focuses on specific functional mating adaptations, and how cognitive and cultural processes may provide a more robust explanation of current cross- and intra-cultural data without a requirement for sexual selection to have played a role. It then argues that a large portion of human appearance preferences - including those previously thought to be human universals - may in fact be a by-product of broader perceptual and learning processes interacting with cultural-evolutionary feedback. Finally, new predictions, and remaining challenges to this integrated cognitive-cultural model, are put forward for further consideration.

title: Generation of a polarized pair-photon fireball via a laser-driven nonlinear-linear QED cascade
summary: Relativistic, polarized pair-photon fireballs are central to understand the microscopic energy transfer of high-energy astrophysical outflows, yet generating an dense fireball in the laboratory, especially via an ultraintense laser, remains
content: Relativistic, polarized pair-photon fireballs are central to understand the microscopic energy transfer of high-energy astrophysical outflows, yet generating an dense fireball in the laboratory, especially via an ultraintense laser, remains a formidable challenge. Here, we propose a novel method of laser-driven nonlinear-linear quantum electrodynamics (NL-QED) plasma, that dramatically lowers the laser intensity threshold for high-density pair-photon fireball creation. By coupling polarization-resolved linear Breit-Wheeler and Compton processes with strong-field nonlinear radiation, we find that a self-organized NL-QED cascade is ignited in the laser-driven hole boring at intensities of ∼ 10 22 W / c m 2 , accessible with current 10-PW-class laser facilities. Consequently, we demonstrate the generation of a pair-photon fireball with a high-density gamma-ray bath (maximum average density n γ ¯ ≈ 4.2 × 10 21 c m − 3 ) and a pair plasma (maximum average density n ± ¯ ≈ 1.3 × 10 16 c m − 3 ), which has energy-resolved polarization. Our method provides a comprehensive framework for studying laser-driven QED plasma and its application in laboratory astrophysics, probing multi-process QED physics.
