title: Water-driven porous silicon as a platform for blue materials
summary: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface
content: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on the most accessible chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and transport speed by combining large and small pores and thereby allows functions to be scaled from thin planar films to three-dimensional components. Surface modification becomes a design variable that tunes the interaction between water and the pore wall. It can be set locally and, with switchable coatings, on demand. Finally, pores only a few molecules wide alter the properties of water itself. In the absence of a bulk-like volume, water can become dielectrically anisotropic and highly conductive. Altogether, these steps turn porous silicon from a responsive material into an adaptive, water-driven material.

title: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures of BAs/MoSeTe and BAs/MoTeSe for photocatalytic and photovoltaic applications
summary: within deformation-potential theory, and Se vacancies produce larger band offsets than Te vacancies, consistent with more effective spatial separation of photoexcited carriers. Optical absorption spans the visible and ultraviolet regions, w
content: within deformation-potential theory, and Se vacancies produce larger band offsets than Te vacancies, consistent with more effective spatial separation of photoexcited carriers. Optical absorption spans the visible and ultraviolet regions, with heterostructure formation broadening the spectral response relative to the constituent monolayers. The estimated power conversion efficiencies of approximately 25%, calculated within a Shockley-Queisser-type framework, place these systems among the most promising 2D heterostructures for photovoltaic energy conversion.

title: Remote sensing as a tool for assessing landslide impacts on coastal waters at Porchat Island (SE Brazil)
summary: On April 29, 2025, a water pipeline rupture on Porchat Island (São Vicente, southeastern Brazil) triggered a mass movement that released sediment into adjacent coastal waters. Effects of urban infrastructure failures on coastal water qualit
content: On April 29, 2025, a water pipeline rupture on Porchat Island (São Vicente, southeastern Brazil) triggered a mass movement that released sediment into adjacent coastal waters. Effects of urban infrastructure failures on coastal water quality are rarely documented with imagery of adequate spatial and temporal resolution. We used Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope, processed in ACOLITE, to estimate turbidity, suspended matter concentration (SMC), chlorophyll-a, and Secchi disk depth before and after the rupture, relating the sediment plume to meteoceanographic conditions. In Sentinel-2 images, median SMC in the waters adjacent to the island increased from 9.0 to 19.0 g/m³ and median Secchi depth decreased from 2.07 to 1.03 m, whereas changes in Santos and São Vicente bays were smaller. In PlanetScope images, SMC increased the day after the rupture, most markedly near the island and in Santos Bay, and by May 2 had fallen below the pre-event levels of April 27, which were already elevated after the late-April rainfall. Chlorophyll-a varied among dates without a clear response. As no in situ data were available, results are interpreted as relative changes. PlanetScope’s daily revisit showed the sediment plume shrinking from 7.50 km² on April 30 to 2.02 km² on May 2 and dispersing toward central Santos Bay under waves from the southeast and south quadrants. This case shows that an infrastructure failure can cause marked but apparently temporary changes in the optical properties of coastal waters, and indicates that high-frequency, high-resolution remote sensing is useful for rapid impact assessment and for supporting coastal monitoring.

Also, by analyzing the desorption processes by Ba 4d and, to some extent, by O 1s core levels, following different initial adsorption temperatures, the evolution of binding energies (for Ba 4d) and intensity (for surface O 1s components) was different, suggesting the preliminary trapping of water or hydroxyl radicals on the surface when methane is dosed below room temperature. title: Partial Fragmentation of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS)
summary: We present time-series observations of the long period comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) obtained in 2025–2026, bracketing the comet’s fragmentation in early 2025 November. We show that a simple radiation pressure model can explain many of the comet’
content: We present time-series observations of the long period comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) obtained in 2025–2026, bracketing the comet’s fragmentation in early 2025 November. We show that a simple radiation pressure model can explain many of the comet’s properties: the rapid fading after fragmentation, the increasing mean particle size in the projected photometry aperture, and the time dependence of the surface brightness profile. Small dust particles (≲100 μ m) dominate the coma, with average dust velocity ∼a few ×1 m s −1. The nucleus radius is estimated at ∼0.5 km and the dust properties are consistent with, but do not prove, an origin in nucleus rotational breakup, followed by being swept down the tail by radiation pressure.

title: Axially chiral P,olefin ligands for palladium-catalyzed asymmetric allylic amination with phthalimides
summary: Axially chiral P,olefin ligand enables enantioselective Pd-catalyzed allylic amination with phthalimide. DFT suggests that Pd–C bond asymmetry linked to the phosphine trans influence contributes to stereoselectivity through reduced distorti

title: Streamwise measurements of a hypersonic shock layer radiation
summary: A simultaneous spectroscopic and visualization system was developed to study hypersonic shock layer radiation along a streamwise line-of-sight (LOS). The system was implemented to observe emissions ahead of a projectile traveling at approxi
content: A simultaneous spectroscopic and visualization system was developed to study hypersonic shock layer radiation along a streamwise line-of-sight (LOS). The system was implemented to observe emissions ahead of a projectile traveling at approximately 7 km s −1 in a controlled argon environment at the JAXA/ISAS two-stage light gas ballistic range facility. Experimental conditions were designed to establish equilibrium flow within the shock layer, enabling comparison of the measured emission spectra with equilibrium radiation models. For this comparison, stagnation point radiation was extracted from the experimental data with the aid of a co-axial visualization system. Radiation calculations were performed using the SPRADIAN07 radiation code, with equilibrium flow properties obtained using the NASA CEA code. The dominant thermochemical structure in the shock layer was analyzed by streamlining the radiative transfer within a piecewise layer model. Parameterized layer properties were iteratively refined until the calculated spectra matched the experimental spectra. The findings demonstrate that the current measurement method provides useful diagnostic information for estimating the dissociating, partially ionizing, and ablating structure of hypersonic shock layers in addition to reducing uncertainty associated with LOS measurements.

title: Melt-electrowritten gelatin-functionalized PCL scaffolds loaded with human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells for intrauterine adhesions treatment
summary: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a common refractory gynecological disease characterized by endometrial fibrosis and cavity obliteration that often leads to infertility. In this study, we developed a tissue-engineered construct combining 3D p
content: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a common refractory gynecological disease characterized by endometrial fibrosis and cavity obliteration that often leads to infertility. In this study, we developed a tissue-engineered construct combining 3D printed PCL scaffolds, surface gelatin conjugation and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUCMSCs) for IUA treatment. PCL scaffolds were fabricated by melt electrowriting (MEW) and subjected to sequential surface modification: NaOH hydrolysis (PCL-N), gelatin coating (PCL-NG), and 1-Ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide/N-hydroxysuccinimide (EDC/NHS) crosslinking (PCL-NGE). Physicochemical characterization confirmed the successful surface modification. In vitro cytocompatibility was assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, live/dead staining, and cytoskeleton staining. The results demonstrated that the PCL-NGE scaffold exhibited superior cytocompatibility toward hUCMSCs, significantly promoting their metabolic activity, adhesion, and spreading. The PCL-NGE-hUCMSCs constructs were then implanted into a rat IUA model, and the histopathological assessment revealed that the PCL-NGE-hUCMSCs group markedly restored endometrial thickness, increased glandular density, and substantially reduced collagen deposition and fibrosis compared to the IUA model group. These findings suggest that gelatin-functionalized PCL scaffolds fabricated using MEW and loaded with hUCMSCs may represent a potential strategy for endometrial regeneration and IUA treatment.

title: Surface Component Regulation for Durable Li-Rich Layered Cathodes
summary: Lithium-rich layered oxides (LLOs) represent appealing high-capacity and low-cost cathode candidates for advanced lithium-ion batteries. Nevertheless, severe capacity fading and voltage decay triggered by interfacial side reactions and irre
content: Lithium-rich layered oxides (LLOs) represent appealing high-capacity and low-cost cathode candidates for advanced lithium-ion batteries. Nevertheless, severe capacity fading and voltage decay triggered by interfacial side reactions and irreversible phase transformations under high-voltage cycling greatly hinder their practical implementation. Herein, a weak acid ammonium salt-assisted precursor regulation strategy is employed to regulate the surface composition of Co-free LLOs. This modification helps alleviate interfacial and structural degradation during cycling. Benefiting from this modification, all treated samples achieve high capacity retention over 95% after 200 cycles at 1 C, distinctly outperforming the pristine counterpart. This precursor surface engineering strategy offers a facile route to stabilize LLO cathodes toward high-energy-density battery applications.

title: Mixed Conductivity of Polypyrrole/Polyvinyl Alcohol Composite Determined by Impedance Spectroscopy
summary: A comprehensive study of doped polypyrrole/polyvinyl alcohol (PPy/PVA) composites on cellulose substrate was conducted in the temperature range of 28 °C–70 °C. An electrical approximation circuit consisting of three series-connected circuit
content: A comprehensive study of doped polypyrrole/polyvinyl alcohol (PPy/PVA) composites on cellulose substrate was conducted in the temperature range of 28 °C–70 °C. An electrical approximation circuit consisting of three series-connected circuits is used for quantitative analysis of impedance spectra. This model approximates with high accuracy the experimental temperature dependences of the impedance, phase angle, and permittivity of the PPy/PVA composite. It was found that the phase shifts at low frequencies are determined by energy losses in the ionic component, while at higher frequencies they are determined by the combined ionic and electronic losses. The static polarization is also determined by the polarizability of ions, whereas at frequencies above 4 Hz, it is governed by the combined polarizability of both ions and polarons. The temperature dependences of the diffusion coefficients of ions and polarons were derived from impedance spectra. It was established that two groups of ions are present in the composite: the diffusion coefficients of the first group are practically independent of temperature, while those of the second group depend on temperature according to the Arrhenius law, with activation energy of 1.5 eV. Polaron diffusion coefficients can be well explained by a model of defect-mediated diffusion.

title: 3-step-CVD-MoS 2 film formation from PVD-Mo film via oxygen and sulfur-vapor anneals
summary: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2) is a promising candidate channel material for future logic transistors. In this study, a 3-step CVD method with high industrial scalability is investigated, wherein a molybdenum film deposited by sputtering unde
content: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2) is a promising candidate channel material for future logic transistors. In this study, a 3-step CVD method with high industrial scalability is investigated, wherein a molybdenum film deposited by sputtering undergoes oxygen annealing followed by sulfur vapor annealing to synthesize an MoS 2 film via a vapor-phase reaction. The successful formation of the MoS 2 film was confirmed using cross-sectional TEM, Raman spectroscopy, in-plane XRD, and XPS. The MoS 2 film deposited by the 3-step CVD also exhibited higher crystallinity than the directly sulfurized Mo film. Furthermore, back-gate field-effect transistors fabricated with these films demonstrated n-type semiconducting characteristics.

title: Stokes phenomenon in the adiabatic evolution of discrete-time non-Hermitian systems
summary: The adiabatic dynamics of non-Hermitian systems gives rise to rich phenomena originating from complex energy spectra and exceptional points (EPs). However, investigations of the Stokes phenomenon induced by gain and loss—which stem from the
content: The adiabatic dynamics of non-Hermitian systems gives rise to rich phenomena originating from complex energy spectra and exceptional points (EPs). However, investigations of the Stokes phenomenon induced by gain and loss—which stem from the imaginary parts of dynamical phases—remain limited in discrete-time settings. In this work, we consider a two-mode traceless symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian subjected to discrete-time periodic driving, with its parameters evolving along a rhombic trajectory in parameter space. We generalize the parallel transport condition to eliminate geometric phases and adopt a discrete adiabatic criterion, enabling us to quantitatively reveal how the number of discrete evolution steps affects adiabaticity. Within this framework, we observe the Stokes phenomenon under specific conditions—namely, non-Hermiticity, periodic driving, adiabatic evolution, and a sufficiently large running accumulated imaginary phase along the path—although we do not claim that these conditions are universally necessary. Under these conditions, the eigenstate amplitudes display characteristic behavior: exponential suppression of the subdominant eigenstate accompanied by violent oscillations of the dominant eigenstate. This behavior is closely associated with the dynamical switching of the exponentially dominant eigenstate, driven by the competition between the imaginary parts of the dynamical phase factors. This study extends the investigation of the Stokes phenomenon to discrete non-Hermitian systems, demonstrates it as a characteristic feature of the non-Hermitian adiabatic dynamics studied here, and provides a theoretical foundation for its experimental observation.

title: Electrodeposited ZnCo Processed by Microwave Plasma Generated Using a Household Microwave Oven
summary: This study investigates the effect of microwave plasma post-treatment on electrodeposited ZnCo-based material on carbon cloth. Compared with conventional direct current (DC) or radio frequency (RF) plasma systems, microwave plasma offers ad
content: This study investigates the effect of microwave plasma post-treatment on electrodeposited ZnCo-based material on carbon cloth. Compared with conventional direct current (DC) or radio frequency (RF) plasma systems, microwave plasma offers advantages such as electrodeless discharge and rapid surface modification. In this work, a modified household microwave oven was used to generate microwave plasma in a vacuum-sealed tube, providing a simple and low-cost route for microwave plasma post-treatment of materials. Surface and structural analyses, including water contact angle measurement, SEM, EDS, XRD, and XPS, show that microwave plasma treatment modifies the surface morphology, elemental distribution, and near-surface chemical states of the electrodeposited layer. XRD suggests the presence of Zn/Co oxide-related phases, while XPS reveals an increased Co 3+ -related contribution and a higher fraction of hydroxyl-/adsorbate-related oxygen species after plasma treatment. These results indicate that microwave plasma treatment mainly affects the surface/interface characteristics of the Zn–Co-based electrode. When assembled into flexible symmetric supercapacitor devices, the sample processed by microwave plasma for 3 s exhibits higher CV-derived device capacitance, lower fitted interfacial resistance, and improved long-term cycling response compared with the as-deposited sample. The devices also maintain functional charge-storage behavior under bending deformation. These findings suggest that household microwave-generated plasma can serve as a rapid and low-cost surface modification strategy for Zn–Co-based flexible electrodes, showing potential for flexible supercapacitor applications.

title: Photocatalytic activity of green-synthesized PANI/ZnO nanocomposite under solar irradiation: water remediation application
summary: A morphologically modified PANI/ZnO NCs was synthesized using Solanecio gigas (S. gigas) leaf extract as a reducing and capping agent for the photocatalytic degradation of crystal violet (CV) under sunlight irradiation. Additionally, PANI a
content: A morphologically modified PANI/ZnO NCs was synthesized using Solanecio gigas (S. gigas) leaf extract as a reducing and capping agent for the photocatalytic degradation of crystal violet (CV) under sunlight irradiation. Additionally, PANI and ZnO NPs were synthesized for comparison. All synthesized nanomaterials were characterized using UV–Vis, FT-IR, SEM, and XRD. The blue shift in the absorption peak of PANI/ZnO NCs suggests modifications in their optical and electronic properties, potentially associated with interfacial interactions and heterojunction formation between PANI and ZnO. FT-IR analysis revealed red-shifted absorption bands, suggesting possible hydrogen-bonding interactions between PANI and ZnO. Morphological analysis indicated that the composite exhibited surface features combining the rough texture of ZnO NPs with the relatively smooth morphology of PANI. Furthermore, XRD patterns exhibited overlapping diffraction peaks corresponding to the constituent phases, while the estimated crystallite size of the PANI/ZnO NCs (5.577 nm) was smaller than that of pristine ZnO NPs (9.455 nm), suggesting a reduction in crystallite growth upon composite formation. The effects of key photocatalytic parameters were investigated, and a solution pH of 11, photocatalyst dosage of 0.12 g, and an initial CV concentration of 20 ppm were determined to be optimum. The PANI/ZnO NCs exhibited higher photocatalytic activity, achieving 98.25% degradation compared to ZnO NPs with 92.76% under optimal conditions after 60 min of sunlight exposure. Kinetics studies indicated that the degradation rate fit well with the PFO kinetics (R 2 = 0.968) for PANI/ZnO NCs. The composite demonstrated good catalytic activity with four cycles of reusability time compared to non-coated ZnO NPs. These findings highlight the potential of S. gigas leaf extract-assisted PANI/ZnO NCs as effective and sustainable nanocatalysts with promising applications in photocatalytic decomposition of organic contaminants for environmental remediation.

title: Continuous-wave and passively Q-switched Er:KGd(WO 4) 2 channel waveguide laser near 1.5 μm
summary: We demonstrate continuous-wave (CW) and passively Q-switched operation of femtosecond-laser-inscribed Er:KGd(WO 4) 2 (Er:KGdW) channel waveguide (WG) lasers operating near 1.5 μm. Depressed-cladding WGs with core diameters of 40 and 60 μm w
content: We demonstrate continuous-wave (CW) and passively Q-switched operation of femtosecond-laser-inscribed Er:KGd(WO 4) 2 (Er:KGdW) channel waveguide (WG) lasers operating near 1.5 μm. Depressed-cladding WGs with core diameters of 40 and 60 μm were fabricated in the same gain crystal and systematically characterized under CW operation using output couplers with transmissions ranging from 0.5% to 15%. The 60-μm WG exhibited the best performance, delivering a maximum output power of 39.8 mW at 1534.7 nm with a slope efficiency of 24.1%. Caird analysis indicated a low passive loss of only 0.11 dB/cm, confirming the high optical quality of the fabricated WG. Passive Q-switching was subsequently achieved in the same quasi-monolithic cavity by spin-coating single-walled carbon nanotubes onto the output coupler, which served as a saturable absorber. Stable pulse operation was obtained with pulse durations as short as 136 ns, repetition rates continuously tunable up to 529 kHz, pulse energies of up to 64 nJ, and peak powers of up to 0.47 W. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first demonstration of a passively Q-switched Er:KGdW WG laser and highlights the potential of this platform for compact, efficient, eye-safe pulsed laser sources operating in the 1.5-μm spectral region.

title: Interlayer sliding induced thermal conductance oscillation in van der Waals contact graphene/h-BN heterostructures
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) field-effect transistors (FETs) face a fundamental thermal-management challenge because heat generated in atomically thin channels must efficiently cross the van der Waals (vdW) interface into the supporting substrate.
content: Two-dimensional (2D) field-effect transistors (FETs) face a fundamental thermal-management challenge because heat generated in atomically thin channels must efficiently cross the van der Waals (vdW) interface into the supporting substrate. Yet, how atomic-scale interfacial arrangement governs the transmission channels of heat-carrying phonons remains poorly understood. Here, using atomistic nonequilibrium Green’s function calculations combined with mode-resolved phonon transmission analysis, we investigate interfacial phonon transport in sliding graphene/h-BN vdW heterostructures. We reveal a pronounced oscillatory thermal conductance governed by two distinct characteristic length scales: a short-period oscillation of 0.5 unit cell (uc) and a long-period modulation of approximately 8 uc. The short-period oscillation originates from periodic changes in atomic arrangement and the resulting variation in local interlayer vdW coupling. In contrast, mode-resolved analysis reveals that the long-period modulation is accompanied by a wavevector-dependent evolution and redistribution of the transmission contributions from heat-carrying phonons. In particular, the characteristic wavelengths of the dominant ZA phonons associated with the first high-transmission region are approximately 7.1-9.1 uc, comparable to the 8 uc sliding length of the long-period conductance modulation. These results reveal that interfacial phonon transport in vdW heterostructures can be governed by two distinct structural and vibrational length scales: an atomic-arrangement scale controlling local interlayer coupling and a phonon-wavelength scale associated with the redistribution of heat-carrying transmission channels. Our findings establish a microscopic connection between interfacial atomic arrangement, momentum-resolved phonon transmission, and thermal conductance, providing a physical basis for stacking engineering of heat dissipation in 2D FETs.

title: Tree species diversity and three-dimensional canopy structure jointly shape soil bacterial and fungal diversity in mangroves
summary: Global climate change and human activities are driving widespread degradation of mangrove ecosystems, threatening the multiple ecosystem functions and services they provide. Previous studies have shown that tree species diversity and three-
content: Global climate change and human activities are driving widespread degradation of mangrove ecosystems, threatening the multiple ecosystem functions and services they provide. Previous studies have shown that tree species diversity and three-dimensional canopy structure can shape soil microbial communities. However, their interactive effects and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood in mangrove wetlands, where salinity, periodic inundation, and anoxia impose strong environmental constraints. We surveyed 29 plots in the Beibu Gulf, China, integrating tree inventories, UAV- and terrestrial LiDAR-derived canopy metrics, soil chemical properties, and high-throughput sequencing of bacterial and fungal communities. Tree species diversity explained 16.0% and 30.1% of the variation in fungal Shannon diversity and Chao1 richness, respectively. Mediation analyses indicated that foliage height diversity (FHD) and leaf area index (LAI) were indirectly associated with bacterial and fungal diversity through soil nutrient pathways. The interaction between tree species diversity and FHD was evident for fungal diversity but not bacterial diversity, with fungal diversity peaking at relatively high levels of both variables. These findings reveal group-specific associations between aboveground vegetation and belowground biodiversity, with fungal communities showing stronger responses than bacterial communities to variation in canopy structure and soil nutrient conditions. Our results suggest that mangrove restoration in the Beibu Gulf should coordinate tree species composition with canopy development and evaluate soil nutrient status and microbial recovery alongside vegetation attributes, rather than maximizing species diversity or canopy structural complexity in isolation. However, the generalizability of these findings remains to be tested across broader spatial, climatic, and vegetation compositional gradients.

title: Electrocatalytic Coal Depolymerization to Graphene Quantum Dots via Bridge Bond Cleavage and Aromatic Radical Evolution
summary: The direct depolymerization of coal into high‐value carbon nanomaterials represents a promising route for its utilization, yet achieving selective conversion under mild conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrocatalytic str
content: The direct depolymerization of coal into high‐value carbon nanomaterials represents a promising route for its utilization, yet achieving selective conversion under mild conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrocatalytic strategy for the targeted depolymerization of coal macromolecules into graphene quantum dots (GQDs). Using a multivalent copper‐based catalyst in a swollen coal‐water slurry, the anodic coal oxidation reaction (COR) exhibits a low onset potential of ‐0.21 V RHE and a peak current density of 0.94 A cm −2 at 1.6 V RHE. Under optimized pulsed potential conditions (E H = 1.1 V RHE and E L = −0.8 V RHE), coal is selectively converted into GQDs with an average size of 1.33 nm and a yield of 10.1 wt% within 12 h. Mechanistic studies reveal that COR proceeds via two elementary reactions on Cu‐based active sites: (i) bridge bond cleavage followed by competitive (ii) condensation and oxidation of derived aromatic radicals. Furthermore, we constructed a COR||HER hybrid system for the efficient co‐production of GQDs and hydrogen. This work presents an electrocatalytic method for coal molecular engineering, demonstrating its potential for producing both chemicals and clean energy from coal.

title: Nitrate prevents hypoxia-induced bone loss by restraining the gut Prevotella denticola–glutamine–ASCT2–α-ketoglutarate osteoclastogenic axis
summary: Chronic hypoxia causes progressive bone loss, but its mechanisms remain unclear and effective interventions are limited. Given its potential to regulate bone and gut homeostasis, we investigated whether inorganic nitrate protects against hy
content: Chronic hypoxia causes progressive bone loss, but its mechanisms remain unclear and effective interventions are limited. Given its potential to regulate bone and gut homeostasis, we investigated whether inorganic nitrate protects against hypoxia-induced bone loss. In mice exposed to 10% O₂ for 3 months, nitrate preserved trabecular microarchitecture, improved bone formation and reduced osteoclast-associated bone resorption. Fecal microbiota transplantation from nitrate-treated donors improved bone phenotypes in hypoxic recipients, supporting a transferable gut-associated component of protection. Metagenomic and metabolomic analyses identified hypoxia-induced enrichment of Prevotella denticola and glutamine-related metabolic abnormalities, both attenuated by nitrate. P. denticola supplementation aggravated hypoxic bone loss and increased serum glutamine. Nitrite, a downstream metabolite of nitrate, inhibited P. denticola growth, reduced glutamine synthetase activity and decreased extracellular glutamine in vitro. To examine the functional relevance of these metabolic changes, we assessed glutamine supplementation and transport. Glutamine supplementation exacerbated hypoxic bone loss, while hypoxia increased ASCT2 expression and intracellular glutamine accumulation during osteoclast differentiation. Pharmacological transport inhibition and deficiency of the ASCT2-encoding gene Slc1a5 suppressed osteoclastogenesis; Slc1a5-deficient mice retained more trabecular bone under hypoxia. [U-¹³C₅]glutamine tracing and rescue experiments implicated α-ketoglutarate (α-KG) as a downstream mediator of ASCT2-associated glutamine metabolism. α-KG restored osteoclastogenesis in Slc1a5-deficient cells and reduced H3K27me3 enrichment at the Nfatc1 transcription start site, supporting an epigenetic link. These findings implicate a P. denticola-associated glutamine–ASCT2–α-KG pathway in hypoxic bone loss. They suggest that nitrate may preserve gut–bone homeostasis by modulating microbial and metabolic changes under chronic hypoxia.

title: On the geomechanical signatures of tailings: a case of monazite tailing
summary: The need to source for rare earth elements and the development of renewable and nuclear energy is of utmost importance worldwide. One of the significant source for these elements are monazite ore and they are mined and processed. The materi
content: The need to source for rare earth elements and the development of renewable and nuclear energy is of utmost importance worldwide. One of the significant source for these elements are monazite ore and they are mined and processed. The materials left after processing the ore to obtain the pure elements are termed tailings and their disposal and handling are problematic due to their adverse impacts on social, economy and environment of human as well as the entire ecosystem. This paper presents the geomechanical signatures of monazite tailings through the conduction of index and physical tests, compositional tests, one-dimensional compression tests as well as the prediction of behaviour using measured parameters. The specimens have varying particle sizes and well graded in nature. The tailings are non-clayey and non-plastic and could be classified as silty sand. Fabric seems to be less heterogeneous and isotropic with inter particle and inter cluster voids. Silica is the dominant chemical compositions followed by alumina and potassium oxide in significant percentages. Quartz is the major mineral and the other compositions are orthoclase and albite. The characteristics of monazite tailings are similar to some tailings and also differ from some tailings and this shows the cumbersome nature of this inevitable artificial material. The monazite tailings compression paths are fairly similar with variable initial specific volumes. The specimen’s characteristics is initial state-dependent which could be termed transitional behaviour. The non-convergent behaviour is significant with m value of 0.73. Although, the prediction using artificial intelligence (AI) shows transitional behaviour in monazite tailings, it could not be satisfactorily predicted using AI model developed for iron tailings. However, the AI model developed for iron tailings could be used to predict transitional behaviour in tin and columbite tailings.

title: Iodinated Heptamethinecyanine Dye / Dextran-Polyacrylamide Polymer / Gold Nanorods Nanohybrid with Plasmon Enhanced NIR Optical Response for Potential Bioimaging and Biosensing Applications
summary: Multifunctional hybrid nanoplatforms operating within the near-infrared (NIR) biological transparency window hold immense potential for various biomedical applications. In this work, we report the synthesis and optical investigation of wate
content: Multifunctional hybrid nanoplatforms operating within the near-infrared (NIR) biological transparency window hold immense potential for various biomedical applications. In this work, we report the synthesis and optical investigation of water-soluble 3-component nanohybrids based on iodinated heptamethine cyanine dyes (2I-HITC and 4I-HITC), a star-like dextran-graft-polyacrylamide copolymer matrix (D6-PAA), and plasmonic gold nanorods (AuNRs) with longitudinal surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) at 660 nm (AuNR660) and 745 nm (AuNR745). The D6-PAA polymer matrix effectively reduces hydrophobic dye aggregation as well as encapsulates dye molecules and AuNRs. Spectral tuning of the LSPR of AuNRs to match the NIR absorption and emission bands of the dyes led to strong plasmon-enhanced photoluminescence (SEPL) and Raman scattering (SERS). The optical response exhibited a non-monotonic concentration dependence dictated by the competition between plasmonic enhancement and non-radiative Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) quenching. Due to weaker FRET quenching and stronger local electromagnetic field hot spots, the 2I-HITC/D6-PAA/AuNR745 nanohybrid achieved the highest enhancement factors for both PL (26.8-fold) and SERS (25.4-fold under 785 nm excitation). Theoretical calculations using Boyd’s local-field enhancement model strongly corroborated the experimental SERS results, confirming the spatial proximity of the functional components within the polymer matrix. These findings highlight the three-component 2I-HITC/D6-PAA/AuNR745 nanohybrid as a potential platform for high-sensitivity NIR fluorescence bioimaging and diagnostic SERS sensing.

title: Suppression of herbaceous weed germination and growth by extracts of Acacia dealbata
summary: Weeds are major constraints to agricultural production, and increasing concerns associated with intensive herbicide use and herbicide resistance highlight the need to identify new sources of compounds for weed management. In this context, i
content: Weeds are major constraints to agricultural production, and increasing concerns associated with intensive herbicide use and herbicide resistance highlight the need to identify new sources of compounds for weed management. In this context, invasive plants may provide bioactive metabolites with phytotoxic properties. In this study, the effects of methanolic extracts from the stems, leaves, flowers, and pods of silver wattle (Acacia dealbata Link) on the seed germination and early growth of herbaceous weeds were evaluated. The extracts significantly inhibited germination, radicle elongation, and hypocotyl growth, although the responses varied according to weed species and donor organ. Common lambsquarters (Chenopodium album L.) showed the highest germination percentage under extract exposure, whereas large crabgrass (Digitaria sanguinalis (L.) Scop.) was the most sensitive species. Jimsonweed (Datura stramonium L.), spurred anoda (Anoda cristata (L.) Schltdl. ), and yellow foxtail (Setaria pumila (Poir.) Roem. & Schult.) also showed substantial inhibition depending on the extract applied. Radicle development was particularly affected, indicating that roots are a major target of silver wattle phytotoxins. Anatomical analyses of D. stramonium and A. cristata radicles revealed reduced or inhibited root hair formation, rhizodermal and cortical damage, root apex alterations, and disorganization of the vascular cylinder. Overall, the species- and organ-dependent phytotoxicity demonstrated here highlights silver wattle aerial biomass as a promising source of bioactive compounds for further development and evaluation in weed management strategies.

title: Mobility-weighted heat exposure reveals priority corridors for climate-resilient cycling
summary: (150 words) Urban overheating threatens efforts to expand low-carbon active mobility, yet cities lack scalable methods to identify where heat most affects cyclists. This study integrates high-resolution biometeorological modeling with segme
content: (150 words) Urban overheating threatens efforts to expand low-carbon active mobility, yet cities lack scalable methods to identify where heat most affects cyclists. This study integrates high-resolution biometeorological modeling with segment-based cycling mobility data to distinguish between heat hazard and actual heat exposure. Using a building and tree-resolving machine-learning model (HTC-NN), hourly Universal Thermal Climate Index rasters are generated at 1 m spatial resolution for Freiburg, Germany, during a summer cycling campaign in 2023. Recorded cycling activity data are used to estimate the cumulative exposure cyclists experience along cycling segments. Results show substantial intra-urban variability in heat hazard, but exposure patterns differ when accounting for cyclist activity. Heavily used corridors produced high exposure even under moderate hazard. Existing tree canopy reduced cumulative cyclist heat exposure by 29%, with benefits depending on shade, urban form, and cycling activity. This framework supports targeted, climate-resilient active transport planning.

title: Diagnosing the environmental performance gap of manufacturing enterprises in Uzbekistan through a threshold-based indicator system: instrument design and a first enterprise-level application
summary: Whether Uzbek manufacturing can respond to the national green agenda depends on capacities that country-scale indices miss. This brief report presents a threshold-based diagnostic instrument for the environmental performance gap of manufact
content: Whether Uzbek manufacturing can respond to the national green agenda depends on capacities that country-scale indices miss. This brief report presents a threshold-based diagnostic instrument for the environmental performance gap of manufacturing enterprises and a first application to a textile enterprise, Toshbuloq Teks LLC. The instrument combines twenty indicators in five blocks: energy and resource efficiency, capital and technology, investment and finance, environmental costs and impact, and governance. Each indicator carries a norm with pre-crisis and crisis bands, every boundary is documented, and observed values become distance-to-target scores aggregated into sub-indices and an overall index. In 2024, seventeen of the twenty indicators fall in the crisis band and none reaches its norm; the overall index equals 62.2 on a hundred-point scale, so the enterprise stands on average at 62 percent of its norms. Tightening every boundary by up to twenty percent raises the crisis count to twenty; under loosening, no indicator attains its norm up to ten percent and a majority remains in crisis up to five percent. The index stays within 61.3–63.3 when any single indicator is excluded and within 57.7–69.3 in ninety percent of random re-weightings. An equal-weight integral index of the enterprise’s energy economics over 2016 to 2024 rises from 0.128 to 0.716 and falls to 0.469, consistent with operational gains that were not institutionally anchored. The deepest gaps concern capital renewal and environmental monitoring rather than energy performance; whether they are binding is a hypothesis for multi-enterprise validation; the findings describe one enterprise, not Uzbek manufacturing.

title: Molecular topography evolution: saddle-to-cylinder adaptation of carpyridines on metals
summary: The intrinsic curvature of non-planar macrocycles plays a crucial role in directing supramolecular self-assembly and tuning functional properties. Here, we demonstrate a topographic reconfiguration of metal-free carpyridines - a prototypica
content: The intrinsic curvature of non-planar macrocycles plays a crucial role in directing supramolecular self-assembly and tuning functional properties. Here, we demonstrate a topographic reconfiguration of metal-free carpyridines - a prototypical class of saddle-shaped molecules - on coinage metal supports, Au(111) and Ag(111). Integrating scanning probe microscopies, X-ray spectroscopies and density functional theory reveals insights into interfacial behaviour and structural adaptability. While the carpyridines remain non-planar upon adsorption, their shape changes to a cylindrical geometry. Columnar stacking is suppressed and the formation of well-ordered two-dimensional carpyridine arrays is enabled, whose packing is tuned by peripheral substituents. The adsorption configuration and interfacial electronic structure of the carpyridines differ significantly from those observed in typical free-base porphyrins. This work elucidates the balance between conformational rigidity and adaptability in curved macrocycles on coinage metal supports, with broad implications for thin-film growth, shape-assisted self-assembly, and tuning of topography-related molecular properties.

title: Generational development of a self-contained dual-axis solar power system—A design evolution
summary: This paper describes a multi-year engineering development of a self-contained solar power system that uses dual-axis tracking to ensure improved efficiency. This system is designed to operate in remote and rugged environments with minimal h
content: This paper describes a multi-year engineering development of a self-contained solar power system that uses dual-axis tracking to ensure improved efficiency. This system is designed to operate in remote and rugged environments with minimal human intervention. The iterative design process yielded three generations of systems that were increasingly productive and responsive to design issues identified during development. The generations are labeled T1V1, T1V2, and T1V3, and this nomenclature is used throughout the manuscript. Across the three generations, the systems scaled dramatically at each generation (from 1.58 to 9.28 kW to 18.56 kW of photovoltaic capacity, and from 9.6 to 16.13 to 32.2 kWh of battery storage), while preserving a 48 V direct current (VDC) bus and maintaining the underlying dual-axis tracking approach. A comparison test was used to establish performance metrics and yielded approximately 30% greater incident solar energy and 39% greater delivered electrical energy than the equivalent fixed-tilt array. Field tests at a test facility exposed mechanical and electrical design issues that had to be addressed. Among the most significant issues were tracker binding and emergency stop contacts. The second generation (T1V2) was evaluated over 245 days of operation, including during the winter in a mid-latitude location. The third generation added a containerized shipping configuration and other changes to improve performance. This paper discusses the three-generation design evolution and focuses on improvements that had the most significant impact on performance and reliability.

title: Ion‐Pair Decoupler Tunes Solvation Chemistry for Room‐Temperature Polymer Electrolytes With Built‐In Flame Retardancy
summary: Solid‐state polymer electrolytes for high‐energy lithium‐metal batteries are severely constrained by low room‐temperature ionic conductivity. However, mainstream approaches focus on regulating the aggregate structure and flexibility of poly
content: Solid‐state polymer electrolytes for high‐energy lithium‐metal batteries are severely constrained by low room‐temperature ionic conductivity. However, mainstream approaches focus on regulating the aggregate structure and flexibility of polymer chains while neglecting the ionic solvation microenvironment, which caps ionic conductivity gains at a marginal level. Here, an innovative ion‐pair decoupling strategy is proposed to reshape the Li + solvation chemistry within polymer matrices and to facilitate rapid ionic conduction. The ion‐pair decoupler, diethyl phosphoramidate, promotes the dissociation of lithium salt into a configuration dominated by solvent‐separated ion pairs by coordinating with Li + via its electron‐rich P = O groups and anchoring TFSI ‒ through hydrogen bond donors. Consequently, the ionic conductivity of the engineered electrolyte increases 24.6‐fold at 25°C. Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling over 850 h, and Li||LiFePO 4 cells deliver a high‐capacity retention rate of 96.5% after 400 cycles at 25°C. Furthermore, the designed electrolyte exhibits excellent self‐extinguishing flame‐retardant properties by combining gas‐phase radical scavenging and condensed‐phase char‐forming mechanisms. Thus, a single molecular design simultaneously serves as an ion‐pair decoupler and an intrinsic flame retardant, establishing solvation‐chemistry tuning as a new paradigm for safe, room‐temperature solid polymer electrolytes.

title: Perovskite materials for biomedical sensing, imaging, and therapy: recent advances and translational challenges
summary: Perovskite-structured materials encompass chemically distinct families whose optical, electronic, piezoelectric, catalytic, and magnetic properties have prompted growing interest in biomedicine. This review critically examines recent progre
content: Perovskite-structured materials encompass chemically distinct families whose optical, electronic, piezoelectric, catalytic, and magnetic properties have prompted growing interest in biomedicine. This review critically examines recent progress in metal-halide perovskites, oxide perovskites, and related perovskite-type materials for X-ray detection and imaging, biosensing, cancer theranostics, implant-associated infection control, drug-delivery research, bioinspired devices, light-emitting devices, and biomechanical energy harvesting. Rather than treating these materials as a single platform, we distinguish their composition-dependent functions and translational constraints. Metal-halide perovskites offer strong X-ray attenuation, tunable emission, and solution processability, but their moisture sensitivity and potential release of lead or other ions remain major barriers to in vivo use. Oxide perovskites generally provide greater chemical robustness and enable piezoelectric, catalytic, magnetic, and photothermal functions, although their biodegradation, clearance, and long-term tissue responses require further study. Across both families, most biomedical evidence remains at the proof-of-concept or small-animal stage. Reproducible synthesis, stability in physiological media, standardized toxicity testing, device integration, sterilization, and regulatory evaluation are therefore priorities. A material-class-resolved framework is essential for comparing performance and identifying applications with credible routes toward clinical translation.

title: CHARACTER BEHAVIOR EVENT PREDICTION MODEL BASED ON FUSION OF TRAJECTORY AND ENVIRONMENTAL FEATURES
source: Journal of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of predicting human behavior events by integrating trajectory and environmental features. Existing methods often neglect structured associations between trajectories and scenes or decouple trajectory regre
content: This paper addresses the challenge of predicting human behavior events by integrating trajectory and environmental features. Existing methods often neglect structured associations between trajectories and scenes or decouple trajectory regression from intention classification. To overcome these limitations, we propose an end-to-end framework comprising dual-stream encoding, cross-modal fusion, and multimodal decoding. The dual-stream encoder separately models historical trajectories using a two-layer Transformer and scene environments via a static scene branch (ResNet-50 extracting 64 spatial tokens from semantic segmentation) and an interaction graph branch (two-layer GCN modeling up to 30 neighboring agents). Cross-modal fusion uses trajectory global features as Query and scene tokens/interaction nodes as Key/Value, enabling soft alignment of environmental elements through cross-attention, with residual connections and layer normalization. The multimodal decoder, based on a conditional variational autoencoder, simultaneously predicts future 12-step trajectories and six behavior classes (straight, turn left/right, stop, interact with person/vehicle), jointly optimized by weighted negative log-likelihood and cross-entropy loss. Experiments on ETH/UCY, SDD, and nuScenes demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: on ETH/UCY, ADE=0.61m, FDE=1.10m, behavior accuracy=89.7%; on nuScenes, ADE=0.43m, accuracy=95.6%; on SDD, ADE=0.90m. Ablation studies confirm the importance of each component, with attention visualization showing dynamic focus shifts. The full model has 28M parameters, runs at 115 FPS (8.7ms per sample), while a lightweight version achieves 189 FPS with ADE=0.64m. This work highlights the value of structured environment fusion and joint trajectory-intention decoding for accurate, rational, and generalizable human behavior prediction.

title: Artificial Reefs: Computational Fluid Dynamics Informed Insights into Particle Interception
summary: Artificial reefs (ARs) are increasingly deployed to support coral restoration, yet how their geometry influences larval settlement remains poorly quantified. Here, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of AR structures were perform
content: Artificial reefs (ARs) are increasingly deployed to support coral restoration, yet how their geometry influences larval settlement remains poorly quantified. Here, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of AR structures were performed and analysed with Lagrangian particle tracking to estimate collision probability on the structures. A suite of AR designs and reference geometries were simulated and oriented at varying angles to the flow to test whether structure‑ and vertex‑scale geometric metrics can be used as predictors of collision probability. Results show that rotating structures broadside to the flow (90°) lowers collision odds. A larger frontal area consistently reduced the likelihood of particle interception, while greater surface packing, the degree of indentation and rugosity, increased it. Surfaces on ARs that were oriented more directly toward the oncoming flow captured more particles, but the highest collision probability occurred at 2–4° rather than 0°. Convex features consistently intercepted more particles than concave ones, though the benefit of curvature showed diminishing returns, with collision probability rising to a peak near a relative curvature of 0.13 before falling off at higher curvatures. Collisions were overwhelmingly concentrated within the first few centimetres of any highly curved surface, dropping steeply with distance. Surface slope relative to the seabed had no detectable effect. Our findings reveal a systematic trade-off between flow deflection and surface trapping that operates from the whole reef down to the centimetre scale. When prioritising initial settlement, simulation results suggest that effective ARs should balance compact from with edge‑richness and convex‑curved surfaces. Demonstrating the necessity of validating these insights against real world cases to determine if particle modelling informed AR design translates to real world conservation gains.

title: Interface‐Enhanced PMMA ‐Based Sandwich Composites Containing KH ‐570 Modified Hollow Glass Microspheres and Silicate Fiber Fabrics
summary: Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)‐based lightweight composites containing hollow glass microspheres (HGM) offer potential for lightweight panels and buoyancy‐assisted components. HGM/PMMA cores, standalone PMMA laminates reinforced with unid
content: Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)‐based lightweight composites containing hollow glass microspheres (HGM) offer potential for lightweight panels and buoyancy‐assisted components. HGM/PMMA cores, standalone PMMA laminates reinforced with unidirectional basalt‐fiber (BF) and glass‐fiber (GF) fabrics, and corresponding sandwich composites were fabricated using a reactive PMMA/MMA binary resin. HGM and both fabrics were treated with γ‐methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (KH‐570). Incorporating 10 wt% HGM reduced the core density from 1.18 to 0.89 g/cm 3. At this loading, 4 wt% KH‐570 relative to HGM increased the tensile and flexural strengths from 34.7 to 51.6 MPa and from 45.9 to 68.1 MPa, respectively, while reducing 120 h water absorption from 0.76% to 0.28%. FTIR and XPS confirmed the presence of KH‐570‐derived groups on HGM, while SEM revealed fewer interfacial gaps and reduced microsphere debonding. Fabric treatment increased the 90° tensile strength from 25.5 to 34.8 MPa for BF/PMMA and from 39.8 to 49.2 MPa for GF/PMMA. The treated BF‐ and GF‐faced sandwich composites had densities of 0.90 and 1.06 g/cm 3, respectively. The treated GF‐faced composite achieved tensile and flexural strengths of 325 and 426 MPa, respectively. KH‐570 treatment increased flatwise tensile strength by 101.4% for BF‐faced and 120.2% for GF‐faced sandwiches.

title: High-resolution BIOCLIM and ENVIREM grids for Europe in the last 21,000 years: downscaled CCSM3 simulations compared to pollen-based reconstructions
summary: High-resolution paleoclimatic data are essential for understanding how past climate changes have shaped modern biodiversity and for developing robust models to predict future biotic responses. Here, we introduce a comprehensive dataset of p
content: High-resolution paleoclimatic data are essential for understanding how past climate changes have shaped modern biodiversity and for developing robust models to predict future biotic responses. Here, we introduce a comprehensive dataset of paleoclimate grids for Europe covering the last 21,000 years, from the Last Glacial Maximum to the present. This dataset goes beyond the commonly used set of 19 bioclimatic (BIOCLIM) variables by incorporating an additional 16 environmental (ENVIREM) variables, which have been identified as biologically relevant factors influencing the ecological or physiological processes that determine species distributions. The complete set of 35 variables is provided at a high spatial resolution of 30 arc-seconds in transient 100-year temporal steps. These variables were calculated from monthly temperature and precipitation simulations of the Community Climate System Model version 3, which were statistically downscaled and debiased using a change-factor approach based on high-resolution baseline climate data. Technical validation against alternative paleoclimate databases confirms high spatial and temporal congruence across the dataset, with minor discrepancies limited to variables dependent on the identification of the wettest quarter of the year. Additionally, we evaluated temperature and precipitation simulations against pollen-based reconstructions from the Temperature 12k database across 137 sites in Europe. The comparison shows that model-proxy agreement is highly variable across both time and space and depends on whether annual means or seasonal variables are considered. This open-access dataset, freely available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5119958 (Divíšek, 2021), enables the integration of transient climate dynamics into paleoecological and biogeographical models, enhancing their capacity to track biotic responses to past climate changes.

title: Size structure, regeneration and co-occurrence patterns of an endangered Eastern Arc tree, Cola clavata
summary: Background and aims. Knowledge of the population status of narrowly distributed trees is fundamental to their conservation, yet it is lacking for most threatened plants of the Eastern Arc Mountains. We assessed the size structure, regenerat
content: Background and aims. Knowledge of the population status of narrowly distributed trees is fundamental to their conservation, yet it is lacking for most threatened plants of the Eastern Arc Mountains. We assessed the size structure, regeneration, elevational distribution and co-occurring species of the endangered forest tree Cola clavata (Malvaceae: Sterculioideae) in Kambai Forest Reserve, East Usambara Mountains, Tanzania. Material and methods. Trees and seedlings were recorded in 51 nested circular plots across low (< 600 m), middle (600–900 m) and high (> 900 m) elevation zones. Size-class distributions were analysed by log-linear regression and a weighted Weibull model, spatial pattern by Morisita's index, elevational distribution by Fisher's exact and Kruskal–Wallis tests, and co-occurrence by phi coefficients and one-sided Fisher's exact tests. Key results. Cola clavata occurred at 175.9 stems ha −1 and 0.46 m 2 ha −1 basal area, ranking sixth of 136 tree species by importance value. Stem density declined steeply with diameter (slope −0.137, R 2 = 0.79), and the Weibull model (c = 1.31) described a strongly right-skewed distribution, consistent with an inverse-J population. Stems of 15 cm diameter at breast height and above made up 2.4% of stems but 55% of basal area. Seedlings (171.6 ha −1) and saplings (156.0 ha −1) were abundant, but density fell tenfold from saplings to poles, and juveniles were clumped. The species was rare in the low zone (one of 16 plots) compared with the middle and high zones combined (12 of 32 plots; odds ratio 0.12, p = 0.036). Englerophytum natalense and Lecaniodiscus fraxinifolius co-occurred with C. clavata more often than expected by chance (adjusted p = 0.026). Conclusion. The Kambai population is self-replacing but concentrated at mid-elevations, the forest zone most heavily cleared across the Eastern Arc, and its few large trees deserve strict protection.

title: Risk-Constrained Wastewater Control under Missing Sensor Measurements: Analysis of an Original Hourly Dataset with Dhaka-Relevant Ecological Conditions
summary: Intermittent instrumentation failure is a persistent obstacle to dependable wastewater control, and its consequences are most severe in catchments where receiving waters are already ecologically degraded. This study analyzes an original hou
content: Intermittent instrumentation failure is a persistent obstacle to dependable wastewater control, and its consequences are most severe in catchments where receiving waters are already ecologically degraded. This study analyzes an original hourly operational dataset spanning 90 consecutive days to examine how incomplete dissolved oxygen measurements influence treatment performance, effluent release decisions, and receiving-water oxygen condition under circumstances comparable to those of Dhaka, Bangladesh. The dataset comprises 2,160 hourly records for each of three control strategies, giving 6,480 strategy-level records in total, and it carries a full set of process, effluent, and receiving-water variables. Dissolved oxygen measurements were absent or stale during 20.83 percent of time steps. Three strategies were assessed on the identical hourly record: fixed feedback control at a constant aeration setting of 0.62, imputation-based control that acted on the most recent dissolved oxygen estimate, and risk-constrained control that adjusted aeration according to both the estimated concentration and its accumulated uncertainty. Under risk-constrained control, the release gate withheld wastewater whenever estimation uncertainty exceeded 0.55 mg/L or estimated dissolved oxygen fell below 1.75 mg/L. Mean effluent biochemical oxygen demand declined from 25.28 mg/L under fixed feedback control to 22.43 mg/L under risk-constrained control, a reduction of approximately 11.3 percent, while the share of time steps exceeding the 20 mg/L benchmark fell from 84.82 to 69.82 percent. Mean receiving-water dissolved oxygen rose from 4.84 to 5.02 mg/L, and the proportion of hours with river dissolved oxygen below the 4 mg/L screening threshold declined from 13.38 to 7.13 percent, a relative reduction of approximately 46.7 percent. These ecological gains carried a measurable operational cost, because wastewater was withheld from release during 11.62 percent of time steps, equivalent to 251 of the 2,160 hours. The evidence indicates that treating outage duration as an explicit uncertainty term, rather than substituting a single best estimate, offers a defensible basis for coupling treatment control with release safety in data-scarce settings.

title: Dispersive Magnetic Solid-Phase Cleanup Technique for Analysis of Multiclass Herbicides in Fresh Produce Prior to UPLC-MS Detection
summary: A magnetic nanocomposite (Fe 3 O 4 @NH 2 -GO) was synthesised, characterised, and evaluated as a dispersive magnetic solid-phase extraction (D-MSPE) sorbent for the removal of matrix interferants from squash leaves, ripe avocado, and ripe m
content: A magnetic nanocomposite (Fe 3 O 4 @NH 2 -GO) was synthesised, characterised, and evaluated as a dispersive magnetic solid-phase extraction (D-MSPE) sorbent for the removal of matrix interferants from squash leaves, ripe avocado, and ripe mango extracts prior to the analysis of 17 multiclass herbicides using ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS). The work evaluates Fe 3 O 4 @NH 2 -GO as a reusable cleanup sorbent for determining multiclass herbicides in fresh produce with different physicochemical characteristics; specifically, pigment-rich squash leaves, lipid-rich avocados, and sugar-rich mangoes. The nanocomposite was characterised using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Raman spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and nitrogen adsorption–desorption isotherms. After optimizing the D-MSPE procedure, the limits of detection (LODs) ranged from 0.004 to 0.621 µg∙kg −1, and limits of quantification (LOQs) from 0.013 to 1.88 µg∙kg −1. The method was evaluated by spiking samples with 7.5, 15, and 30 µg∙kg −1 and yielded recoveries of 25.93–95.80%, 33.77–79.03%, and 20.56–99.24% in squash leaves, avocado, and mango samples, respectively. The intra-day precision, expressed as relative standard deviation (RSD), was below 18%. Reusability studies over six cycles showed relatively stable recoveries. Comparisons using the quick, easy, cheap, effective, rugged, and safe (QuEChERS) method yielded LODs from 0.013 to 0.695 µg∙kg⁻ 1 and LOQs from 0.040 to 1.226 µg∙kg⁻ 1, with recoveries of 24.39–70.65%, 32.14–62.66%, and 54.03–88.63% in squash leaves, avocados, and mangoes, respectively, and RSD values below 16%. These results demonstrate that Fe 3 O 4 @NH 2 -GO is an effective reusable cleanup sorbent for multiclass herbicide analysis in complex food matrices.

title: Homoleptic ruthenium(II)-N-heterocyclic carbene complexes with metal-to-ligand charge transfer phosphorescence lifetimes up to 11 μs
summary: [Ru(tpy)2]2+ (tpy = 2,2’:6’,2’’-terpyridine) and its derivatives are weakly emissive or non-emissive with extremely short metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) lifetimes. [Ru(tpy)2]2+ possesses a 3MLCT lifetime of about 0.25 ns. Herein we
content: [Ru(tpy)2]2+ (tpy = 2,2’:6’,2’’-terpyridine) and its derivatives are weakly emissive or non-emissive with extremely short metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) lifetimes. [Ru(tpy)2]2+ possesses a 3MLCT lifetime of about 0.25 ns. Herein we report a series of homoleptic Ru(II)-N-heterocyclic carbene (Ru(II)-NHC) complexes ([Ru(LH)2](PF6)2, [Ru(LPhMe2)2](PF6)2, [Ru(LPhOMe)2](PF6)2, and [Ru(LNaph)2](PF6)2) which are structurally analogous to [Ru(tpy)2]2+, however, display phosphorescence in deaerated acetonitrile solution at room temperature with record 3MLCT lifetimes up to 11.2 μs which is longest among any homoleptic Ru(II) complexes reported to date. Transient absorption spectroscopy and time-dependent density functional theory calculations have unambiguously supported these results. The homoleptic Ru(II)-NHC complexes possess higher 3MLCT state energies (2.35-2.58 eV) compared to both benchmark [Ru(bpy)3]2+ (bpy = 2,2’-bipyridine, 2.13 eV) and [Ru(tpy)2]2+ (2.07 eV) complexes, and their polypyridyl derivatives. They have been used as photosensitizers in challenging visible light induced [2+2] cycloaddition reactions, and dearomative cascade catalysis via energy transfer processes. Such photoreactions have not been accessible previously by using benchmark [Ru(bpy)3]2+ photosensitizer or its derivatives.

title: SILEX atmospheric layer classification: flight-by-flight manual and K-Means (v2)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Flight-by-flight classification of the atmospheric layers sampled during the SILEX aircraft campaign (15 July–3 August 2025, France), produced as part of a PhD thesis within the EUBurn project. The dataset consists of an OpenDocument Spread
content: Flight-by-flight classification of the atmospheric layers sampled during the SILEX aircraft campaign (15 July–3 August 2025, France), produced as part of a PhD thesis within the EUBurn project. The dataset consists of an OpenDocument Spreadsheet (.ods) file containing two sheets, corresponding to two versions of the atmospheric layer classification: Sheet 1 – Classification_v1: Manual classification Potential plumes were identified based on information from the SILEX flight logbook and peaks in black carbon (BC) mass concentration. They were then classified according to their particle size distributions as: Fossil fuel plumes (modal diameter: 40–150 nm); French biomass burning plumes (modal diameter: 100–200 nm); Long-range transport (LRT) plumes (modal diameter > 200 nm, originating far from local sources). HYSPLIT back-trajectories were used to investigate the origin of long-range transport plumes. The manual classification includes the following categories: Airport, Background, Local Plume, LRT Plume, Diluted and Mix. Sheet 2 – Classification_v2: Unsupervised K-Means classification An unsupervised K-Means clustering approach was developed to refine and provide a more specific classification of the atmospheric plumes. The results were cross-validated against the manually identified plumes from Version 1. The clustering algorithm uses the following input variables: UHSAS particle size distribution parameters (N_total and V_total); SP2 black carbon (BC) mass concentration; CO/CO2, CH4/CO and O3/CO ratios. All input variables were log-transformed and standardised before clustering, with BC weighted by a factor of 3. Separate K-Means models were fitted for two atmospheric domains: Local air (K = 2); Other air (K = 4). This resulted in six clusters (C0–C5). Cluster labels were interpreted and cross-validated against the manually flagged plumes. Version 2 includes only in-plume measurements, classified as either Local Plume or Long-Range Transport (LRT) Plume. Flights 23, 28, 30 and 31 retain their manual classification because no plumes were identified by the K-Means algorithm during these flights. Data availability and file structure The spreadsheet also contains a flight details sheet for each flight, providing information on the measurements performed and the atmospheric layers sampled. The K-Means background clusters from Version 2 are not included in this dataset but are available upon request from the author. All data are provided in OpenDocument Spreadsheet (.ods) format. Related thesis: Characterization of aerosols released by wildfires in Europe and their regional climate impact, Université de Toulouse / Météo-France – CNRM (in preparation). Funding: EUBurn project. Code and documentation: https://github.com/leticiaerthalc/SILEX_EUBURN/

title: Earnings Management of Oil & Gas Firms After the Russian Invasion of Ukraine
summary: Political crises often lead to sharp increases in energy prices and, consequently, in the profits of oil and gas companies. However, exceptionally high profits may be perceived as unethical, creating reputational and legitimacy concerns tha
content: Political crises often lead to sharp increases in energy prices and, consequently, in the profits of oil and gas companies. However, exceptionally high profits may be perceived as unethical, creating reputational and legitimacy concerns that can influence firms’ financial reporting behavior. Yet, there is no evidence whether European oil & gas firms manage earnings after sudden political crises, and whether their responses differ across countries. Using a difference-in-differences design, this study documents that European oil & gas firms engaged in significant income-decreasing earnings management—through both accrual-based and real activities—following the Russian invasion of Ukraine. This effect is particularly pronounced in the third quarter of 2022 and the first quarter of 2023. We further find that (real) earnings management by oil & gas firms is more pronounced in countries that implemented windfall profit taxes and in institutional environments characterized by stronger democratic governance. At the firm level, the effect is concentrated among oil & gas firms with relatively low sustainability scores, which exhibit significantly greater income-decreasing earnings management than control firms. These findings suggest that earnings management decisions were driven not only by tax considerations but also by legitimacy and reputational concerns. This study contributes to the literature by providing cross-country evidence that exploits variation in taxation regimes and institutional settings, and by explicitly examining the role of legitimacy and reputational concerns in shaping corporate reporting behavior.

title: Tuning the Photoluminescent Response of Carbon-Based Nanoparticles Through Solvothermal Synthesis Temperature
summary: Carbon-based nanoparticles (CNPs) were synthesized through a solvothermal process using citric acid and urea as precursors at 120, 150, and 180 °C to investigate the influence of synthesis temperature on their structural organization and op
content: Carbon-based nanoparticles (CNPs) were synthesized through a solvothermal process using citric acid and urea as precursors at 120, 150, and 180 °C to investigate the influence of synthesis temperature on their structural organization and optical properties. Characterization by bright-field transmission electron microscopy (BF-TEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, and photoluminescence (PL) revealed temperature-dependent changes in the organization of the carbonaceous structures, with increased continuity of the lamellar features and no appreciable changes in nanoparticle size or the main surface functional groups identified by FTIR. Raman analysis showed the most pronounced spectral changes between 120 and 150 °C, followed by smaller variations at 180 °C, suggesting a progressive reorganization of the sp2 carbon domains. These structural variations were accompanied by changes in emission peak positions, relative intensities, and spectral broadening, indicating a temperature-dependent redistribution of emissive states. The results suggest that solvothermal synthesis temperature plays an important role in modulating the structural organization and photoluminescent response of carbon-based nanoparticles, providing insights into the relationship between carbon structure and optical properties.

title: Energy Storage Properties of Natural Clinoptilolite-Based Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Improved Capacity and Stability via Magnesiothermic Reduction
summary: In this work, we investigate the morphology, chemical composition, and electrochemical performance of natural clinoptilolite subjected to thermal and chemical treatment. Magnesiothermic reduction of this natural zeolite resulted in an incre
content: In this work, we investigate the morphology, chemical composition, and electrochemical performance of natural clinoptilolite subjected to thermal and chemical treatment. Magnesiothermic reduction of this natural zeolite resulted in an increase in the Si/O ratio and the formation of a new crystalline silicon phase. SEM observations showed that the original particle morphology was largely preserved, whereas EDS and XRD confirmed changes in the elemental and phase composition, respectively. The suggested partial reduction of SiO2 was additionally confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), which revealed a substantial decrease in the surface aluminum content and densification of Si species on the modified surface. Electrochemical studies showed that the clinoptilolite-based materials can be used effectively as negative electrodes in lithium-ion batteries. Cyclic voltammetry indicated stable electrochemical properties, with a predominantly capacitive contribution at higher scan rates and a greater contribution from diffusion-controlled processes at lower scan rates. In turn, galvanostatic tests confirmed the high specific capacity, reaching 668 mAh/g for the material after magnesiothermic reduction, with a capacity retention of ∼94% after 1000 cycles. The results indicate the potential use of the tested materials as negative electrodes with high specific capacity and long-term cyclic stability.

title: Lagrangian inference of turbulent diffusivity in stratified shear flows
summary: We infer various measures of turbulent diffusivity using Lagrangian particles and tracers in direct numerical simulation (DNS) of stratified shear flows prone to Kelvin–Helmholtz instability and Holmboe wave instability. Irreversible mixing
content: We infer various measures of turbulent diffusivity using Lagrangian particles and tracers in direct numerical simulation (DNS) of stratified shear flows prone to Kelvin–Helmholtz instability and Holmboe wave instability. Irreversible mixing in density-stratified flows is often diagnosed in terms of a buoyancy-sorted coordinate using a model developed by Winters & D’Asaro (1996 J. Fluid Mech. vol. 317, pp. 179–193). DNSs are typically not able to capture mixing of weakly diffusive tracers with high Schmidt numbers. We show that Lagrangian particles can be used to diagnose mixing in terms of a buoyancy-sorted coordinate and that this method can be used to diagnose mixing for tracers with large Schmidt numbers. We also investigate the degree to which the evolution of a passive tracer field in sorted density coordinates can be inferred from the effective diffusivity diagnosed from the density field. This works well when the passive scalar and density have the same diffusivity. Otherwise the tracer eddy term derived by Penney et al. (2020 J. Fluid Mech. vol. 900, A26) arising from correlations between tracer fluctuations and the buoyancy field can become important. Comparison of the passive scalar tracer field, averaged in buoyancy-sorted coordinates, with a Gaussian profile shows that mixing induced by the Kelvin–Helmholtz instability can be appropriately modelled using a constant diffusivity. Conversely, a passive tracer in a flow subject to Holmboe wave instability can only be appropriately modelled using an empirically determined spatio-temporally varying diffusivity.

title: Durability of Marine‐Service Carbon‐Fiber‐Reinforced Polymer Composites: Scenario‐Resolved Moisture Transport, Multiscale Damage, and Engineering Implications
summary: Marine‐service carbon‐fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP) durability depends on how exposure boundaries govern moisture transport and the evolution of the polymer matrix, interphase, and fiber–matrix interface. This review connects surface/spla
content: Marine‐service carbon‐fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP) durability depends on how exposure boundaries govern moisture transport and the evolution of the polymer matrix, interphase, and fiber–matrix interface. This review connects surface/splash‐zone, shallow/nearshore, and mid‐to‐deep‐sea scenarios with material‐state changes, multiscale damage, and performance selectivity. Moisture transport is boundary and state dependent: temperature, exposed surfaces, thickness, sizing, defects, sustained loading, and hydrostatic pressure affect apparent uptake kinetics and local moisture gradients. Matrix plasticization, swelling, and chemical change interact with interphase evolution and loss of interfacial load transfer. Direct interface tests, local nanomechanical measurements, and thermomechanical characterization help distinguish these processes from laminate‐scale damage. Longitudinal tensile retention consequently provides an incomplete measure of durability; compression, interlaminar response, fracture, fatigue, impact tolerance, and joint performance probe different vulnerabilities. Fickian, Langmuir, and broader non‐Fickian descriptions are assessed according to observed transport behavior and material state, while accelerated aging is bounded by mechanism consistency. Engineering interpretation proceeds through state‐dependent properties, damage modeling, and validation at the relevant laminate, detail, or component scale. The resulting evidence translation framework preserves marine‐service relevance while identifying material‐specific limits on durability prediction and engineering use.

title: The fishing cat in the Kingdom of Water: first review of presence, population size, distribution and conservation in Cambodia
summary: The fishing cat Prionailurus viverrinus in Southeast Asia is threatened by habitat destruction and poaching. In Cambodia, despite the availability of suitable habitat in extensive wetlands, evidence of the species’ presence is scarce. This
content: The fishing cat Prionailurus viverrinus in Southeast Asia is threatened by habitat destruction and poaching. In Cambodia, despite the availability of suitable habitat in extensive wetlands, evidence of the species’ presence is scarce. This study presents the results of surveys for fishing cats at four wetland sites, a review of all records of presence and an assessment of the extent of predicted suitable habitat in Cambodia. We also report on threats to fishing cat survival and a population estimate to inform the species’ categorization on the IUCN Red List.
