Camera-trap surveys showed a decline in frequency of captures during 2017–2023. More recent records from 2021–2023 confirmed a breeding population in the mangrove wetlands of south-west Cambodia. There were no records of presence on the Tonle Sap Lake floodplain in central Cambodia (2021–2022) or along the Mekong River (2022), apart from a single photographic record south-east of Tonle Sap Lake in 2022. The presence of wetlands and high levels of precipitation were predictors of fishing cat presence, and 17% of Cambodia’s wetlands are predicted to offer suitable habitat. We identified 19 protected areas as priority sites for conservation action and population monitoring. High priority sites (c. 5% of Cambodia was identified as highly suitable habitat) are located along the coast and moderately suitable areas (c. 12.5% of Cambodia) on the Tonle Sap floodplain. Poaching and deforestation are the main threats to fishing cats in Cambodia. We extrapolated the size of the fishing cat population from available data and estimated 34–67 individuals in Cambodia, which is low and warrants urgent and effective conservation action.

title: Crystallinity determination for cellulose nanomaterials using powder X-ray diffraction coupled with Rietveld analysis: An interlaboratory comparison
summary: Cellulose nanomaterials are slowly gaining ground in the manufacturing realm. As part of ongoing efforts to provide quality assurance measures for reproducible production of cellulose nanomaterials, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) can be an
content: Cellulose nanomaterials are slowly gaining ground in the manufacturing realm. As part of ongoing efforts to provide quality assurance measures for reproducible production of cellulose nanomaterials, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) can be an accessible and relatively easy technique to use to establish percent crystallinity measurements as a quality control and assurance standard of these materials. An interlaboratory comparison (ILC) was undertaken to test a protocol for data acquisition and determination of percentage crystallinity and crystallite size for cellulose nanomaterials using PXRD coupled with peak fitting of the diffraction pattern by Rietveld analysis. Parameters such as the exact unit cell dimensions and crystallite size were adjusted by the software to minimize the difference between the calculated and observed patterns by the least-squares method. The significant differences in these values for the nanocellulose samples derived from wood pulp compared to the parameters from the tunicate structure that provides our ideal pattern arise in part because of biosynthetic mechanisms that result in the crystallites of different sizes and shapes. This paper outlines the methodological approach along with comparison of the results and site-dependent variability. Conclusions are made as to the most practical and technically consistent steps for quantifying the crystallinity of nanocellulose.

title: Operation of a high-rate reactor for biogas production: Integration of sugarcane vinasse and cattle manure
summary: Biogas has emerged as a promising solution for the anaerobic treatment of organic waste, offering energy, economic, and environmental benefits. This study evaluated the co-digestion of sugarcane vinasse and cattle manure (5:1 v/m) in an ana
content: Biogas has emerged as a promising solution for the anaerobic treatment of organic waste, offering energy, economic, and environmental benefits. This study evaluated the co-digestion of sugarcane vinasse and cattle manure (5:1 v/m) in an anaerobic structured bed reactor (AnSTBR) for methane production optimization. The reactor operated under mesophilic conditions (35°C) for 332 days across five phases with progressively increasing organic loading rates (OLR), including assessment under reduced alkalizing-agent use. At an OLR of 12.0 kg COD m⁻³ d⁻¹, methane yield reached 297.5 ± 60.2 NmL CH₄ g⁻¹ COD removed, with a volumetric production rate of 4,103.5 ± 816.9 NmL CH₄ L⁻¹ d⁻¹. Higher OLRs (18 kg COD m⁻³ d⁻¹) further enhanced methane production while maintaining operational stability under controlled conditions. The AnSTBR demonstrated robustness in processing agroindustrial waste at high organic loads with reduced chemical input, confirming its potential as an efficient and sustainable technology for biogas generation from vinasse-based co-digestion systems.

title: Semi-transparent agrivoltaics above Riesling vines: three-year assessment of ripening dynamics, cluster health, yield, and must quality
summary: Introduction Climate change poses major challenges to viticulture, including accelerated phenological development, increased berry sugar content, declining acidity, drought stress, and sunburn damage. Agrivoltaics (APV), which combines grap
content: Introduction Climate change poses major challenges to viticulture, including accelerated phenological development, increased berry sugar content, declining acidity, drought stress, and sunburn damage. Agrivoltaics (APV), which combines grape production with photovoltaic electricity generation, may offer an adaptation strategy by modifying the microclimate and reducing climate-related stresses. This study evaluated the effects of a semi-transparent, tracking APV system on Riesling (Vitis vinifera L.) in the cool-climate Rheingau region of Germany. Methods An APV facility was installed in winter 2022/2023, and differences between APV and control plots were investigated over three consecutive growing seasons (2023–2025). The effects of APV on grape ripening, berry composition, sunburn damage, disease-related yield losses, and overall yield were assessed under varying annual climatic conditions. Results APV effects varied considerably among vintages. Compared with the control, APV significantly reduced sunburn damage to grape clusters and delayed, but did not prevent, ripening. Total acidity, particularly malate, and assimilable nitrogen concentrations were enhanced under APV. Reduced leaf wetness and altered cluster architecture may have contributed to lower Botrytis -mediated yield losses. Yields under APV were comparable to those of the control in two of the three years, whereas yield reductions occurred in 2024, a year with below-average radiation. Discussion Semi-transparent APV systems show potential as an adaptation strategy for cool-climate viticulture by reducing sunburn damage and modifying grape composition while maintaining yields under favorable conditions. However, shading may limit productivity in years with insufficient solar radiation, and changes in microclimatic conditions may alter disease pressure. These findings provide initial evidence of the benefits and limitations of APV systems for Riesling production and highlight the need to account for vintage-specific climatic conditions when assessing their suitability for viticulture.

title: Applications of self-healing nanomaterials in aerospace and marine industry: a review
summary: The demand for low-maintenance and long-lasting structural materials for extreme environments has generated a growing interest in the development of self-healing nanomaterials. They are emerging as the next generation’s solution for sectors
content: The demand for low-maintenance and long-lasting structural materials for extreme environments has generated a growing interest in the development of self-healing nanomaterials. They are emerging as the next generation’s solution for sectors in aerospace and marine engineering. Conventional protective coatings and structural polymers, including passive barrier layers and bulk thermoplastics such as PEEK, are limited by their inability to self-repair damages, resulting in degradation, corrosion, and costly repeated maintenance. Self-healing nanomaterials on the other hand are engineered through the integration of vitrimers, nanocontainers, and multifunctional nanofillers including graphene nanoplatelets, carbon nanotubes, halloysite nanotubes, and mesoporous silica. These newly engineered materials are capable of autonomous damage recovery and prolonged service life under harsh conditions which are inaccessible to traditional systems. In aerospace applications, aromatic thermosetting copolyester (ATSP) vitrimers make use of interchain transesterification reactions to achieve consistent healing efficiencies above 98%, elastic recovery above 75%, and structural integrity above 330 °C, which outperforms PEEK across operation temperatures of cryogenic to high temperatures. Nanocontainer-based coatings further provide localised, trigger-responsive corrosion protection for fuselage panels, engine casings, cryogenic pressure vessels, and spacesuits. In marine applications, self-healing anti-corrosion coatings exploit pH-responsive nanocarriers for autonomous restoration of barrier upon damage. They can be used on ship hulls, propellers, and offshore structures exposed to continuous chloride-rich seawater. Slippery lubricant-infused porous surfaces (SLIPS) reinforced with nanostructured silica and TiO₂ resulting in superior antifouling performance and corrosion resistance, with optimised porous nanostructures having corrosion current densities as low as 1.138 × 10⁻⁷ A cm⁻², while high-viscosity lubricants have the greatest durability and biofouling resistance under seawater exposure. Beyond these two sectors, there is emerging potential of their use in other sectors such as energy storage, radiation shielding, and biomedicine. Future development prioritises multifunctional, environmental sustainability, recyclability and scalable manufacturing to support next-generation high-performance and efficient systems.

title: Potential of Biogas Recovery from Industrial Wastewater and CO2-Equivalent Emission Mitigation
summary: Industrial wastewater from agro-industry is a large but under-exploited resource of renewable energy, while, when untreated, a relevant source of methane emissions. This study reviews and compares the potential for biogas recovery from palm
content: Industrial wastewater from agro-industry is a large but under-exploited resource of renewable energy, while, when untreated, a relevant source of methane emissions. This study reviews and compares the potential for biogas recovery from palm oil mill effluent (POME) in Thailand and quantifies the carbon dioxide equivalent (CO 2 e) emissions of the following three anaerobic treatment technologies: the up flow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactor, the continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR), and the anaerobic covered lagoon (ACL). Two comprehensive software applications were developed for visualizing the information for six full-scale mill sites, based on wastewater flow, chemical oxygen demand (COD), COD removal efficiency, methane-emission estimates according to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines and electricity-related emissions; analytic hierarchy process (AHP) decision criteria were also applied. Hydraulic loading ranged from 327 to 579 m 3 d −1 (99,582 to 170,647 m 3 yr −1). Influent COD was approximately 5,556 mg L −1 for the UASB/CSTR dataset and 60,819–69,887 mg L −1 for the ACL sites, with COD removal efficiencies of approximately 90% (UASB), 80% (CSTR), and 60% (ACL). Baseline methane emissions were estimated at 54,698 t CO 2 e yr −1 (UASB), 26,249 t CO 2 e yr −1 (CSTR), and 19,075–23,844 t CO 2 e yr −1 (ACL). With biogas capture and utilization, emissions decreased to 5,383 and 6,512 t CO 2 e yr −1 for the UASB and CSTR—reductions of approximately 90% and 75%, respectively—whereas the ACL sites achieved only 26–33%. The AHP ranked the UASB first (global weight 0.351), essentially tied with the ACL (0.343), with a consistency ratio of 0.026 (< 0.10). These findings indicate that high-rate anaerobic systems coupled with effective biogas utilization can convert agro-industrial wastewater into a renewable energy resource while substantially reducing greenhouse-gas emissions in Thailand.

title: Novel engineering economic evaluation method for optimal distribution transformer sizing
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Selecting the appropriate transformer size is crucial. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation method is required. This study proposes a novel engineering economic approach to assess transformer performance and suggests the most suitable tran
content: Selecting the appropriate transformer size is crucial. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation method is required. This study proposes a novel engineering economic approach to assess transformer performance and suggests the most suitable transformer size for obtaining optimal economic and operational efficiency. The method considers energy losses throughout the transformer’s service life, balancing initial investment, energy expenses, and operational performance to ensure reliable operation with low losses. The approach was implemented on 500 kVA, 1,000 kVA, and 1,250 kVA three-phase distribution transformers operating at 50 Hz and voltage levels of 22 kV-400/230 V. The analysis indicates electricity cost, demand charge, initial transformer price, and power losses as the primary factors affecting total and environmental costs. Results indicate that higher interest rates result in a lower present worth factor and a lower cost to own the transformer. Using two 500 kVA units in parallel to supply a 1,000 kVA load obtains a lower cost than using a single 1,000 kVA transformer, whereas the 1,250 kVA transformer provides the lowest overall cost and best economic performance. The proposed method effectively evaluates transformer performance and indicates the optimal transformer size under given operating and economic conditions.

title: Dynamic Adjustments in Environmental Input-Output Models: Incorporating Quantity and Price Traverse Disequilibrium
source: BCU Open Access Repository (Birmingham City University)
summary: This paper extends the traditional Leontief Input-Output (I-O) model by introducing a traverse disequilibrium framework that captures simultaneous quantity and price adjustments over time. Unlike standard static I-O models, this approach in
content: This paper extends the traditional Leontief Input-Output (I-O) model by introducing a traverse disequilibrium framework that captures simultaneous quantity and price adjustments over time. Unlike standard static I-O models, this approach incorporates continuous-time adjustments in production, prices, and resource utilization. The analysis models how sectors respond to demand fluctuations through inventory accumulation and production adjustments, allowing for temporary imbalances between supply and demand. The model is further extended to include price-setting mechanisms. In this framework, sectors adjust markups in response to cost fluctuations and inventory deviations, and biophysical resource utilisation, leading to physical constraints and cost-push inflation. Calibrated using Brazil's Input-Output matrix and land-use data, the framework is applied to sectoral shocks, including demand surges and price rigidities, to assess their sectoral and macroeconomic impacts. The results highlight the importance of adjustment speeds in shaping economic dynamics, showing that rigid price and quantity settings amplify inventory cycles, while fast quantity adjustments increase output volatility. Sectoral interdependencies create cascading effects, demonstrating how price, and quantity shocks propagate across industries. Additionally, the dependence on environmental services illustrates how pressures on scarce resources feedback into prices and quantities.

title: A Break with “Business as Usual”? IMF Contradictions on Tackling Climate Change and What Are Seen (and Not Seen) as Viable Decarbonization Options
summary: This article explores the International Monetary Fund (IMF)’s economic ideas regarding tackling climate change. It unearths a broad repertoire of Fund climate policy thinking, fusing neoclassical “completing the market” ideas about carbon p
content: This article explores the International Monetary Fund (IMF)’s economic ideas regarding tackling climate change. It unearths a broad repertoire of Fund climate policy thinking, fusing neoclassical “completing the market” ideas about carbon pricing with Keynesian or Schumpeterian calls for wide-ranging public policy interventionism. The resultant amalgam betrays cognitive dissonance, captured in the IMF’s climate policy trilemma, as the IMF highlights ecological “tipping points” and calls for dramatic decarbonizing transformations to “business as usual,” yet retains unwavering commitments to economic growth and fiscal discipline. Before 2025, navigating mandate restrictions, IMF climate policy mobilized around helping countries achieve Paris Agreement emissions reduction undertakings. Yet limited traction with governments, Fund knowledge limits, and ongoing contestation within mainstream climate economics hindered IMF efficacy. Fund climate policy efforts abruptly halted when a climate change–denying US president openly hostile to Bretton Woods institutions unleashed a period of “greenhushing,” sending climate policy within global economic governance into stealth mode.

title: Mechanistic optimisation of biochar-modified concrete for simultaneous carbon dioxide reduction and strength enhancement
summary: The production of Portland cement accounts for approximately 8% of global anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions. Incorporating biogenic carbon into concrete can reduce clinker use and valorise agricultural and forestry residues. In this st
content: The production of Portland cement accounts for approximately 8% of global anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions. Incorporating biogenic carbon into concrete can reduce clinker use and valorise agricultural and forestry residues. In this study, hardwood (HW) and cocoa pod husk (CP) biochars treated at pyrolysis temperatures (PTs) of 300°C (T300) or 700°C (T700) were evaluated. The biochars were incorporated at rates of 0% to 3.0% by weight of cement across 25 mix designs and concrete specimens were tested at 7, 14 and 28 days. The use of 1.5% HW pyrolysed at 700°C led to the highest 28-day compressive strength (39.0 MPa), exceeding that of the control (35.0 MPa) by 11.4%. For this mix, water absorption decreased to 5.20% (5.70% for the control). After post-heating exposure (600°C, 2 h) this mix retained 80% of strength (70% for the control). The key contribution was the feedstock × PT interaction: at a dosage of 1.5%, the T700 − T300 strength difference was +0.2 MPa for HW but +5.2 MPa for CP. The empirical response model gave R2 = 0.68 and a leave-one-out root mean square error of 1.61 MPa. Analysis of variance identified PT (partial η2 = 0.38), quadratic dosage (0.21) and feedstock × dosage interaction (0.18) as dominant effects. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy and thermogravimetric analysis supported pore-refinement and aromatised-carbon mechanisms. However, isothermal calorimetry, mercury intrusion porosimetry and quantitative XRD investigations are needed to confirm the mechanisms.

title: Integration of post-combustion CO 2 capture and flare gas recovery (PSA) for feed optimization and blue methanol production
summary: Methanol complexes face growing pressure to reduce carbon emissions, improve feedstock efficiency, and meet increasingly strict environmental and sustainability requirements. In the first part, an amine-based post-combustion absorption unit
content: Methanol complexes face growing pressure to reduce carbon emissions, improve feedstock efficiency, and meet increasingly strict environmental and sustainability requirements. In the first part, an amine-based post-combustion absorption unit with a design capacity of 20 ton/hr CO 2 is proposed. The captured CO 2 is injected into the pre-reformer inlet after purification and compression. In the second stage, pressure swing adsorption is evaluated for recovery of at least 4,056 Nm 3 /h of H 2 from the flare stream. Four operating scenarios were assessed, combining CO 2 injection with and without hydrogen injection under two operating objectives: increasing methanol production, and reducing natural gas consumption at constant production. The most favourable scenario for increasing production is CO 2 injection at the pre-reformer inlet combined with hydrogen injection, which yields approximately 294 t/d of additional methanol at a return on investment of 42.8 %. Under constant production without loop hydrogen injection, natural gas consumption can be reduced by approximately 6,700 Nm 3 /h at a return on investment of 23.2 %. In addition, PSA-recovered hydrogen from flare gas alone increases methanol production by 28.8 ton/day, corresponding to approximately USD2.56 million per year in additional revenue. This study shows that integrated carbon management and flaring convert emissions into economic value and pave the way for the production of blue methanol.

title: THE ORGANISM CITY ALGORITHMIC MORPHOLOGICAL URBAN PLANNING Legal and Economic Governance of Living Urban Systems and Predictive Spatial Intelligence
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: DRAFT LAW ON ADAPTIVE CONSTRUCTION AND MORPHOLOGICAL GOVERNANCE This groundbreaking legislation transforms urban planning from static, rigid frameworks into dynamic, living systems. It establishes the Living Digital Twin as the binding regu
content: DRAFT LAW ON ADAPTIVE CONSTRUCTION AND MORPHOLOGICAL GOVERNANCE This groundbreaking legislation transforms urban planning from static, rigid frameworks into dynamic, living systems. It establishes the Living Digital Twin as the binding regulatory reference, replacing fixed building codes with Performance-Based Codes and the Digital Morphological Protocol. Key innovations include:- Adaptive Density Coefficient: Building rights dynamically calculated based on real-time infrastructure capacity and environmental performance.- Temporal Zoning: Spaces automatically change function across day/night cycles via Spatial Smart Contracts.- Algorithmic Urban Acupuncture: Surgical intervention clearing only 5% of dense areas to create green lungs, preserving 96% of residents.- Vertical Transfer of Development Rights: Building rights transferred from cleared properties to additional floors elsewhere.- Dynamic Resource Pricing: Tariffs fluctuate instantaneously based on network capacity, protecting vulnerable groups with social lifelines.- Digital Urban Endowment: Rehabilitated green spaces permanently protected from future construction. The law mandates automated licensing via smart contracts within 72 hours, establishes criminal penalties for digital manipulation, and creates an Independent Algorithmic Audit Committee ensuring spatial justice. It applies to new cities, rehabilitation zones, and regulatory sandboxes, achieving metabolic balance, zero carbon emissions, and equitable urban development through predictive intelligence and bio-inspired design.

title: Shifts in Bacteria–DOM Interactions Accompany Changes in Methane Emissions with Weakening Glacial Influence in Proglacial Lakes
summary: Proglacial lakes formed by glacial retreat are increasing in number and may feed back on climate change if they contribute to aquatic greenhouse gas emissions. However, this potential feedback depends on how microbial processing of dissolve
content: Proglacial lakes formed by glacial retreat are increasing in number and may feed back on climate change if they contribute to aquatic greenhouse gas emissions. However, this potential feedback depends on how microbial processing of dissolved organic matter (DOM) responds to climate change-related processes, such as weakening glacial influence, and on the potential consequences of these responses for methane (CH4) emissions. We investigated nine proglacial lakes on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau to characterize bacterial communities and DOM pools along a gradient of weakening glacial influence, and to assess how shifts in bacteria–DOM interactions are associated with CH4 emissions. We found that bacterial community assembly and DOM assembly were decoupled, with different responses to the same environmental pressures. With weakening glacial influence, the DOM pool in proglacial lakes may increasingly comprise relatively recalcitrant DOM components. Meanwhile, DOM production or transformation may become less dependent on specific bacteria–DOM interactions, while DOM degradation becomes increasingly specialized. Together, these shifts could favor the accumulation of substrates for methanogenesis and were associated with changes in methanogenic community composition and reduced potential resource competition between methanogens and bacteria, which may contribute to higher CH4 emissions from proglacial lakes. These findings reveal associations between weakening glacial influence and shifts in microbial carbon processing, providing new insights into potential climate feedbacks from expanding proglacial lakes.

title: De weg van de minste weerstand? Navigeren door publieke voorkeuren voor koolstofbeprijzingsbeleid
summary: Carbon pricing is widely recognised as one of the most efficient and cost-effective instruments for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Despite strong economic arguments and growing empirical evidence, its implementation remains limited in p
content: Carbon pricing is widely recognised as one of the most efficient and cost-effective instruments for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Despite strong economic arguments and growing empirical evidence, its implementation remains limited in practice. Carbon prices often remain below levels consistent with climate targets, while many sectors and countries still lack carbon pricing mechanisms. One of major barriers to the implementation and expansion of carbon pricing policies is public acceptability, which constitutes an important condition for the political feasibility and successful implementation of climate policies. This dissertation examines how carbon pricing policies can be designed and communicated in ways that are acceptable to citizens, with a specific focus on Belgium. The dissertation addresses the overarching question of which factors influence public attitudes towards and preferences for carbon pricing policies, and how and to what extent these factors shape support for such policies. More specifically, it investigates the role of policy design through revenue recycling and policy packaging, perceived policy impacts, communication and information, and heterogeneity in attitudes and preferences across societal subgroups. The findings show that policy design plays a central role in shaping support for carbon pricing. Revenue recycling is a key determinant of public acceptability, with attitudes depending not only on whether revenues are recycled, but also on how they are used. Carbon pricing is also evaluated more positively when embedded within a broader policy package and when revenue use is clearly specified. Regarding perceived policy impacts, the dissertation confirms that perceived fairness, perceived environmental effectiveness, and perceived financial impacts are among the most important drivers of public attitudes towards carbon pricing. With respect to communication and information, the findings show that their effects vary considerably. While information about financial impacts has relatively limited effects on policy preferences, framing carbon pricing as part of a broader policy package can substantially enhance public acceptability. Finally, the dissertation demonstrates that public preferences are heterogeneous. Citizens differ systematically in their climate attitudes, policy preferences, and responses to information. As a result, policy designs that maximise average support are not necessarily those that are most effective in reducing opposition across societal groups. Overall, the dissertation shows that public resistance to carbon pricing is neither inevitable nor universal. Support depends on how policies are designed, communicated, and implemented, as well as on the broader context in which they are introduced. The main conclusion is that the path of least resistance towards carbon pricing policies does not lie in lowering climate ambition, but in designing and communicating carbon pricing packages that are perceived

title: Radiotracers Used in Nuclear Medicine for Prostate Cancer Diagnosis and Follow-Up
summary: Prostate cancer is the most common cause of cancer in males worldwide.Currently, imaging in prostate cancer has acquired great importance in staging, re-staging, treatment selection, and recurrence assessment.Molecular imaging with positron
content: Prostate cancer is the most common cause of cancer in males worldwide.Currently, imaging in prostate cancer has acquired great importance in staging, re-staging, treatment selection, and recurrence assessment.Molecular imaging with positron-emission tomography has enabled a personalized approach for these purposes.In addition to these clinical needs, there are growing perspectives and a challenge for new molecular imaging techniques, not only to detect metastatic disease, but also to provide relevant information on tumor biology and prognosis, and one of the greatest challenges for non-radioisotope imaging techniques is the ability to detect recurrence in patients with low levels of prostate-specific antigen.(crea- tivecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).

title: A Possible Role of LjSEN1 in Molybdenum Distribution toward Bacteroids in Lotus japonicus
summary: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF) in legume root nodules depends on nitrogenase activity in bacteroids, which requires Mo and iron for the Fe-Mo cofactor. These metals must be supplied from host cells to bacteroids across the peribacteroid
content: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF) in legume root nodules depends on nitrogenase activity in bacteroids, which requires Mo and iron for the Fe-Mo cofactor. These metals must be supplied from host cells to bacteroids across the peribacteroid membrane (PBM), but the mechanisms underlying Mo transport to bacteroids remain unknown. A Lotus japonicus symbiotic mutant, sen1, forms small nodules with impaired nitrogen fixation. The causal gene, SEN1 (LjSEN1), encodes a membrane protein belonging to the vacuolar iron transporter (VIT)/VIT-like (VTL) family. Although Fe transport has been proposed for LjSEN1 based on studies of its orthologues, this activity has not been directly shown for LjSEN1 itself. Here, we show that heterologous expression of LjSEN1 in yeast promotes Mo accumulation and increases sensitivity to molybdate toxicity, suggesting that LjSEN1 can transport molybdate in yeast. Similar Mo accumulation phenotypes were observed for the orthologous proteins MtVTL8 and GmVTL1a, suggesting the possibility that Mo transport activity is a shared property of this VTL clade. In sen1 mutant nodules, Mo accumulation was increased in host cell fractions but reduced in bacteroid fractions, suggesting altered Mo distribution within nodules and supporting a role for LjSEN1 in Mo transfer toward bacteroids. Immunolocalization analyses support the idea that LjSEN1 is associated with the symbiosome membrane region of rhizobium-infected cells. Together, these results point to LjSEN1 as a candidate Mo transporter involved in supplying Mo to bacteroids via PBM and suggest that VTL proteins may contribute to the transport of multiple metals, including Mo and Fe.

title: Green energy consumption in public transportation: a bibliometric analysis of current trends and future directions
summary: Purpose Given its considerable carbon footprint, the green energy use in public transportation requires a fundamental transformation towards environmentally sustainable energy options. To achieve this transition, comprehensive research is n
content: Purpose Given its considerable carbon footprint, the green energy use in public transportation requires a fundamental transformation towards environmentally sustainable energy options. To achieve this transition, comprehensive research is needed. This study aims to provide critical insights for academics, policymakers and industry stakeholders to guide sustainable transportation strategies. The research also emphasizes a global shift toward integrated, technology-driven and sustainable mobility solutions by identifying knowledge gaps and areas for future investigation. Design/methodology/approach This study employed bibliometric analysis as its primary methodology. A systematic search of Scopus and Web of Science (WoS) databases yielded a total of 1,513 publications. Data analysis and visualization were facilitated through RStudio and VOSviewer software. Findings The findings suggest the need for interdisciplinary collaboration, enhanced international cooperation and policy-driven research to accelerate the adoption of green energy in public transport. The analysis shows an average publication age of 4.78 years suggests that most contributions are relatively recent, pointing to increasing scholarly attention in recent years. While the average citation count per document is 13.87, which is relatively modest, it suggests a moderate level of impact. The study analysis reveals that China leads in research output. Thematic mapping highlights the growing importance of “smart city” and “sustainable transport” as pivotal to advancing this domain. Research limitations/implications The implications of this study are profound, highlighting the need for a concerted effort to transition towards green energy consumption in public transportation. The study emphasizes the importance of efficient energy utilization, particularly in urban transportation. Implementing effective strategies, greenhouse gas emissions can be reduced, sustainable development can be promoted and an eco-friendly transportation sector can be created. However, international collaboration and publication consistency require improvement. Future research should prioritize global partnerships, seamless renewable energy integration and innovative technologies. Originality/value This paper contributes to the literature by providing the first comprehensive bibliometric analysis specifically focused on green energy consumption in public transportation. It offers valuable insights into current research dynamics, identifies emerging trends and highlights areas where further exploration is necessary to promote sustainable and efficient energy solutions in the sector.

title: GEOS-Chem-hyd: enabling source-oriented sensitivity analysis with GEOS-Chem
summary: Effective environmental policymaking requires accurate quantification of how changes in emissions impact air quality. Chemical transport models, such as GEOS-Chem, are widely used for such analysis. Traditional methods to compute the relati
content: Effective environmental policymaking requires accurate quantification of how changes in emissions impact air quality. Chemical transport models, such as GEOS-Chem, are widely used for such analysis. Traditional methods to compute the relative influence of a change in emissions, or the sensitivity of pollutant concentrations to a change in emissions, with these models often suffer from numerical inaccuracies, especially when evaluating nonlinear atmospheric processes. To overcome these limitations, we integrated a novel sensitivity analysis approach leveraging hyperdual numbers into GEOS-Chem, making GEOS-Chem-hyd. The hyperdual step method accurately calculates first- and second-order sensitivities simultaneously and avoids common numerical errors associated with traditional finite difference methods. The real concentrations as well as first- and second-order sensitivities with respect to emissions calculated with GEOS-Chem-hyd align with the values calculated with GEOS-Chem version 14.0.0-rc.3 within expected error. GEOS-Chem-hyd is applied to assess how changes in emissions of nitrogen oxides can alter ozone, particulate matter, ammonium, and biogenic organic aerosol concentrations, demonstrating regional differences and nonlinear influences. As an example of regional variations, the relative influence of increasing nitrogen oxide emissions was to decrease biogenic organic aerosol concentrations in most areas, except in portions of the boreal forests in Siberia. The nonlinear influence of emissions of nitrogen oxides on ozone, ammonium, and biogenic organic aerosol was evidenced by second-order sensitivities on the same order of magnitude as the first-order sensitivities. GEOS-Chem-hyd incurs approximately four times greater computational costs than GEOS-Chem, which is competitive with the three GEOS-Chem model executions required for less accurate second-order sensitivities using the central finite difference method. GEOS-Chem-hyd provides a framework for efficient assessment of the influence of new scientific modules, which are easily incorporated into the sensitivity analysis framework, and supports informed emission control policy development through accurate, source-oriented sensitivity analysis.

title: ISEFlow: a flow-based neural network emulator for improved sea level projections and uncertainty quantification
summary: Ice sheets are the primary contributors to global sea level rise, yet projecting their future contributions remains challenging due to the complex, nonlinear processes governing their dynamics and uncertainties in future climate scenarios.
content: Ice sheets are the primary contributors to global sea level rise, yet projecting their future contributions remains challenging due to the complex, nonlinear processes governing their dynamics and uncertainties in future climate scenarios. This study introduces ISEFlow, a neural network-based emulator of the ISMIP6 ice sheet model ensemble designed to accurately and efficiently emulate sea level contributions from both ice sheets while quantifying the sources of projection uncertainty. By integrating a normalizing flow architecture to capture data coverage uncertainty and a deep ensemble of recurrent neural network models to assess emulator uncertainty, ISEFlow separates uncertainties arising from training data from those inherent to the emulator. Compared to existing emulators such as a Gaussian Process-based emulator modeled after emulandice and LARMIP, ISEFlow achieves substantially lower mean squared error and improved distribution approximation while maintaining faster prediction times. This study investigates the drivers of increased emulation accuracy and emission scenario distinction and finds that the inclusion of all available climate forcings, ice sheet model characteristics, and higher spatial resolution significantly enhances emulation accuracy and the ability to capture the effects of varying emissions scenarios compared to other emulators. We include a detailed analysis of the importance of input variables using Shapley Additive Explanations, and highlight which climate forcings and model characteristics have the largest impact on sea level projections. ISEFlow offers an additional tool for efficient, accurate exploration of future sea level projections.

title: West Antarctic ice retreat temporarily halted with transient rheology in future climate projections
summary: Projections of sea-level change and Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) stability under anthropogenic climate change hinge upon accurately describing physical feedbacks that link ice dynamics (marine and terrestrial) with the gravitational, rotationa
content: Projections of sea-level change and Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) stability under anthropogenic climate change hinge upon accurately describing physical feedbacks that link ice dynamics (marine and terrestrial) with the gravitational, rotational and deformational response of the solid Earth to ice and ocean loading changes. The marine West Antarctic Ice Sheet (WAIS) is vulnerable to runaway grounding line retreat. However, the rapid viscoelastic rebound of the bedrock in response to ice retreat has been shown to stabilize its grounding line, aided by the low-viscosity mantle beneath the WAIS. Such bedrock deformation is typically modelled using idealised Maxwell viscoelasticity. However, rock deformation experiments show that additional “transient” creep mechanisms, which are not captured by the Maxwell model, occur over societally relevant (∼ decadal-centennial) timescales. Here, we simulate future AIS evolution, coupled with self-consistent solid Earth deformation and sea level change, for various emissions scenarios (RCP 2.6, 4.5, 8.5), incorporating transient deformation. This more complete treatment of solid Earth deformation delays grounding line retreat as compared to Maxwell projections, with differences of tens of kilometres persisting for decades at Pine Island and Thwaites Glaciers. Though transient deformation slows glacier retreat, it is unable to prevent the bulk of ice loss and sea-level rise on longer, centennial timescales. Even still, deviations in AIS meltwater flux with transient deformation could impact climate model predictions.

title: Breast cancer Mexican consensus 2025. Early breast cancer management
summary: Breast cancer, in early stages, has specific surgical, RT, and systemic management.This type of cancer includes ductal carcinoma in situ and breast cancers in stages I, IIA, IIB, and IIIA.This eleventh update of the Mexican Breast Cancer Co
content: Breast cancer, in early stages, has specific surgical, RT, and systemic management.This type of cancer includes ductal carcinoma in situ and breast cancers in stages I, IIA, IIB, and IIIA.This eleventh update of the Mexican Breast Cancer Consensus addressed the management of early stages.The dissemination of this consensus contributes to the updating and homogeneity of breast cancer management criteria.This article aims to present the update in the multidisciplinary management of breast cancer.

title: Climpact Typology: towards a relational climate impact classification of open space
summary: The climate impact of open space plays a significant role in adapting urban and rural spaces to climate change. Depending on open space’s material and immaterial characteristics, its climate impact may differ. Thus, understanding the locall
content: The climate impact of open space plays a significant role in adapting urban and rural spaces to climate change. Depending on open space’s material and immaterial characteristics, its climate impact may differ. Thus, understanding the locally specific relationship between landscapes and climate elements, such as radiation, wind, and precipitation, is crucial for leveraging the role of open spaces in climate-adaptive strategies. In this study, we introduce the Climpact Typology. A hybrid method for classifying cadastral land use data according to the climate impact of each parcel’s open space. In three steps, ranging from qualitative description through operative mapping to quantitative classification of open space using agglomerative clustering, we reveal eight Climpact Attributes and classify 26.818 parcels in Salzgitter, Germany, into ten novel Climpact Types. The Climpact Typology aims to bridge comparability and spatial relationality within a single framework and provides a practical, spatial-planning-oriented understanding of open spaces beyond anthropogenic land use to support climate-adaptive design and planning processes.

title: Quantum Teleportation Toward the Quantum Internet: A Concise Review
summary: Quantum networks play a pivotal role in quantum information science, as they not only provide a secure communication platform for remote access to quantum computers but also serve as the strategic core for achieving large‐scale quantum info
content: Quantum networks play a pivotal role in quantum information science, as they not only provide a secure communication platform for remote access to quantum computers but also serve as the strategic core for achieving large‐scale quantum information processing, forming the foundational infrastructure for the future global‐scale quantum internet. Quantum teleportation, which enables the transmission of unknown quantum states over long distances by employing quantum entanglement together with classical communication, is essential for the distribution of quantum resources in the construction of the global‐scale quantum internet. To realize a global‐scale quantum internet, quantum repeater protocols represent one of the most promising approaches for enabling quantum communication between any nodes. This concise review presents representative experimental demonstrations of quantum teleportation for constructing quantum networks across different physical platforms. Along this trajectory, the review discusses current challenges, open issues, and future perspectives toward a scalable and practical quantum internet.

title: Year-round aerosol variability across monsoon regimes at a near-equatorial Indian Ocean receptor
summary: Year-round observations of aerosol characteristics remain scarce over the equatorial Indian Ocean, particularly at receptor locations far from South Asian continental sources. Here, we present measurements of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5
content: Year-round observations of aerosol characteristics remain scarce over the equatorial Indian Ocean, particularly at receptor locations far from South Asian continental sources. Here, we present measurements of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) chemical composition, aerosol optical properties, meteorology, air-mass transport, and five supporting dual-carbon isotope measurements from the Maldives Climate Observatory at Gan (MCOG; 0.69° S, 73.15° E) during the 2022 seasonal cycle. During the northeast monsoon (NEM), continental influence from South and Southeast Asia coincided with higher PM 2.5 concentrations (5.6±2.7µgm-3), aerosol optical depth at 500 nm (AOD 500; 0.17±0.09), black carbon (BC), organic carbon (OC), and non-sea-salt sulfate. In the southwest monsoon (SWM), PM 2.5 and AOD 500 were approximately 41 % and 35 % lower, respectively, while the relative contribution of marine aerosol increased. These differences likely reflect the combined influence of changes in air-mass origin and monsoon meteorology, including increased precipitation and wet scavenging during the SWM. Despite pronounced changes in aerosol abundance and composition, the BC mass absorption cross-section at 658 nm (BC-MAC 658) differed only modestly between the NEM (8.8±2.9m2g-1) and SWM (10.2±3.2m2g-1), with no statistically significant seasonal difference. The isotope measurements showed substantial sample-to-sample variability, with fossil-dominated and mixed fossil–contemporary signatures occurring within both monsoon regimes. These observations provide a year-round benchmark for aerosol transport, wet removal, composition, and BC absorption at a near-equatorial Indian Ocean receptor, complementary to previous measurements from the northern Maldives and useful for evaluating regional chemical-transport and Earth system models.

title: Magnesium Silicate Condensation in Sub-Neptune Envelopes: The Fundamental Link between Chemistry, Structure, and Observables
summary: Chemical interactions between the hydrogen-dominated envelopes and silicate-rich interiors of sub-Neptunes likely play a key role in shaping their atmospheric structure, mass–radius relations, and upper atmosphere composition. While atmosph
content: Chemical interactions between the hydrogen-dominated envelopes and silicate-rich interiors of sub-Neptunes likely play a key role in shaping their atmospheric structure, mass–radius relations, and upper atmosphere composition. While atmospheric abundances and structure deeply influence each other, many existing models have either considered the effects of chemical interactions without the structural implications or have modeled the envelope structure using oversimplified chemical networks. In this work, we introduce Rocky Raccoon, a coupled chemical equilibrium-atmospheric structure model. This model incorporates Mg, Si, O, C, and H species and produces self-consistent atmospheric chemical and thermal profiles for sub-Neptune envelopes, treating multispecies condensation for the first time. We find that the condensation sequence of magnesium silicates above a magma ocean is determined by the basal magma composition. We show that these condensation sequences drive the upper atmospheric composition to two endmembers: high oxygen abundances in the underlying melt produce compositions rich in oxygen-bearing volatiles (subsolar C/O) and higher mean molecular weight atmospheres with μ ∼ 4 amu, while oxygen-poor melts produce lower mean molecular weight atmospheres dominated by methane and silane (supersolar C/O). The transition between the two regimes is abrupt and depends on melt properties like Mg/Si ratios and oxygen abundances. The different condensation sequences also lead to different thermal profiles, as deep convection is inhibited over different regions due to varying molecular weight gradients. Further experiments and simulations are key to resolving critical uncertainties in the condensation sequences and the corresponding significant impacts on sub-Neptune composition and thermal structure.

title: Development of a one-step semi-homogeneous fluorescent method for multi-screening of sulfonamides in milk
summary: In this study, sulfamethoxypyridazine was used as template to synthesize a type of magnetic molecularly imprinted microsphere based on surface imprinting technique, and tetraphenylethylene was used as fluorophore to synthesize a fluorescent
content: In this study, sulfamethoxypyridazine was used as template to synthesize a type of magnetic molecularly imprinted microsphere based on surface imprinting technique, and tetraphenylethylene was used as fluorophore to synthesize a fluorescent tracer containing aggregation induced emission property. The two agents were combined to develop a semi-homogeneous fluorescent method for determination of sulfonamides. This method was simple (one sample-loading step) and rapid (7 min), its sensitivity was ultra-high (pg/mL level), and the microsphere could be reused for 6 times. Thanks to the ultra-high sensitivity, the milk sample could be assayed directly after 80-fold dilution, and the limits of detection for determination of the 21 SAs in milk were in the range of 0.08–3.98 ng/mL. Compared with fluorescein labeled fluorescent tracer, the sensitivities were improved for 19–671 folds. The analysis results for the unknown milk samples were consistent with a confirmational liquid chromatography mass spectrometry method. This is the first study reporting a semi-homogeneous competitive fluorescent method for determination of sulfonamides in food of animal origin based on magnetic molecularly imprinted microsphere and aggregation induced emission luminogen.

title: The Maxwell Mass Effect as a Model for the Venusian Atmosphere: Integrating the Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis, Radiative Opacity Lapse Rate and Polar-Vortex Energy Pathway
summary: The Maxwell Mass Effect treats the surface temperature of Venus as the dependent variable required to support atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy,
content: The Maxwell Mass Effect treats the surface temperature of Venus as the dependent variable required to support atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level acts as the thermodynamic anchor. A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate fixes the geometric separation between that level and the infrared emission altitude. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at 229 K, and a surface pressure of 91.5 bar. An energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within observed vortex descent speeds. Only this framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices.

title: Dual nicotine use as mixed combustion-aerosol exposure: a critical review of biomarker attribution and residual risk
summary: Combustible cigarettes, heated tobacco products (HTPs), and electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) generate chemically different exposure profiles, yet they are frequently used concurrently. This critical review evaluates dual nicotine
content: Combustible cigarettes, heated tobacco products (HTPs), and electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) generate chemically different exposure profiles, yet they are frequently used concurrently. This critical review evaluates dual nicotine use as a mixed combustion-aerosol exposure scenario and focuses on the practical problem of biomarker attribution. Complete switching from cigarettes to noncombustible products can reduce several biomarkers of combustion-derived toxicants, whereas dual use often preserves cigarette-related exposure and may sustain nicotine intake. Nicotine metabolites quantify systemic dose but do not identify the delivery source. Exhaled carbon monoxide, carboxyhemoglobin, nicotelline, urinary 2-cyanoethyl mercapturic acid, and its longer-window hemoglobin adduct cyanoethylvaline provide complementary information about recent or sustained combustion. NNAL and minor tobacco alkaloids identify tobacco-derived exposure but do not establish combustion, while propylene glycol in urine, plasma, or saliva may support recent attribution to PG-containing ENDS. Metals and carbonyl-related markers have limited product specificity. Biomarkers of oxidative stress, inflammation, DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and endothelial injury indicate biological response rather than exposure source. We therefore propose a tiered attribution framework that interprets biomarkers along two axes: source specificity and temporal resolution. The framework combines product-use history with markers of nicotine intake, recent and longer-window combustion, tobacco substrate, recent vaping, device-associated constituents, and early biological effects. Cutoff-based verification panels are incorporated as a complementary compliance layer rather than as substitutes for source attribution. Dual use should not be treated as a uniform category or as evidence of harm reduction by default. Toxicological assessment should classify use patterns, document cigarette displacement, and distinguish reduced emissions, reduced internal exposure, and reduced disease risk.

title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE – II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500–5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators (vsin i ≤ 30 km
content: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500–5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators (vsin i ≤ 30 km s−1) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and λ Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with TONALLI, and the BACCHUS code. We obtained median abundances of ε(C) = 8.37±0.10, ε(N) = 7.35±0.16, ε(O) = 8.63±0.08, ε(S) = 7.19±0.18, and ε(Fe) = 7.45±0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] =−0.48), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1–0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.

title: УСТОЙЧИВОЕ РАЗВИТИЕ ГОРОДОВ И НАСЕЛЁННЫХ ПУНКТОВ: РЕАЛИЗАЦИЯ ЦУР 11 ПОСРЕДСТВОМ ПРОСТРАНСТВЕННОГО ПЛАНИРОВАНИЯ, РАЗВИТИЯ ТРАНСПОРТА И ЭКОЛОГИЧЕСКОЙ ПОЛИТИКИ.
source: Central Asian Journal of Academic Research
summary: Maqolada Barqaror rivojlanish maqsadlari (BRM) 11 “Shaharlar va aholi punktlarini inklyuziv, xavfsiz, barqaror (rezilyent) va ekologik jihatdan barqaror qilish”ni fazoviy rejalashtirish, transportni rivojlantirish hamda ekologik siyosat orq
content: Maqolada Barqaror rivojlanish maqsadlari (BRM) 11 “Shaharlar va aholi punktlarini inklyuziv, xavfsiz, barqaror (rezilyent) va ekologik jihatdan barqaror qilish”ni fazoviy rejalashtirish, transportni rivojlantirish hamda ekologik siyosat orqali amalga oshirish yondashuvlari tahlil qilinadi. BRM 11ga erishish kompleks va tarmoqlararo yondashuvni talab etishi, shaharsozlikdagi qarorlar transport yuklamasi va ekologik cheklovlar bilan o‘zaro muvofiqlashtirilishi zarurligi asoslanadi. Tadqiqot nazariy va huquqiy asoslarni o‘rganish, shuningdek xalqaro va milliy amaliyotni umumlashtirish orqali muammoli jihatlar (jumladan, transport tarmog‘ining ortiqcha yuklanishi, kelishilgan strategiyalar yetishmasligi va mahalliy monitoring imkoniyatlarining cheklanganligi) aniqlanadi hamda davlat siyosatini yagona konsepsiya asosida shakllantirish zarurligi asoslanadi. Ish umumilmiy metodlar (tahlil, sintez, mantiqiy tahlil) va maxsus yondashuvlarni (huquqiy tahlil, qiyosiy tahlil, кейс-стadi) qo‘llash orqali amalga oshirilgan. Amaliy yo‘nalish sifatida Hindistonning Surat shahri tajribasi ko‘rib chiqiladi; boshqaruv mexanizmlarini takomillashtirish uchun esa mahalliy darajada monitoringni kuchaytirish hamda ekologik me’yorlarga muvofiq rejalashtirish va transport qarorlarini qo‘llab-quvvatlashda raqamli vositalar, jumladan sun’iy intellekt (AI)dan foydalanish bo‘yicha takliflar ilgari suriladi.

title: The science and culture of meat consumption: Traditional meanings of meat and their modern reinterpretation
summary: Meat has played a central role in human diets throughout history, serving not only as a dense source of high-quality protein and essential micronutrients but also as a symbol of cultural identity, social status, and communal tradition. From
content: Meat has played a central role in human diets throughout history, serving not only as a dense source of high-quality protein and essential micronutrients but also as a symbol of cultural identity, social status, and communal tradition. From prehistoric hunting societies to modern industrial food systems, meat consumption has shaped and reflected economic development, religious practices, and culinary customs across civilizations. In particular, meat occupies a significant place in traditional Korean food culture, where it has been incorporated into ritual foods, festive dishes, and socially meaningful dining practices. This review explores meat consumption from interdisciplinary perspectives encompassing meat science, nutrition, anthropology, and food culture. The nutritional and biological significance of meat is examined, highlighting its contributions to human health and physiological function. The role of meat in Korean traditional food culture is also analyzed to illustrate how culinary practices embody cultural values and collective identity. Finally, this review addresses the modern reinterpretation of meat consumption in response to concerns regarding health, animal welfare, and environmental sustainability. By integrating scientific and cultural perspectives, this review provides a comprehensive understanding of the past, present, and future significance of meat in human diets and food systems.

title: Preliminary evaluation of carbon and nitrogen stable isotopes for discriminating Korean native black goat meat from Australian Boer goat meat
summary: This study evaluated the potential of carbon and nitrogen stable isotope profiles for discriminating Korean native black goat (KNBG) meat from Australian Boer goat (AG) meat. Longissimus thoracis et lumborum muscles from KNBG and AG (n = 5
content: This study evaluated the potential of carbon and nitrogen stable isotope profiles for discriminating Korean native black goat (KNBG) meat from Australian Boer goat (AG) meat. Longissimus thoracis et lumborum muscles from KNBG and AG (n = 5 per group) were analyzed for Total carbon (C), δ¹³C, Total nitrogen (N), and δ¹⁵N using an elemental analyzer–isotope ratio mass spectrometry. KNBG showed significantly higher Total C and δ¹³C values but lower Total N and δ¹⁵N values than AG (adjusted p < 0.05). Principal component analysis clearly separated the two groups along PC1, which explained 82.8% of the total variance. Within this preliminary dataset (n = 5 per group), linear discriminant analysis using δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N correctly classified all samples under leave-one-out cross-validation. These results provide preliminary evidence that carbon and nitrogen stable isotope profiles may be useful for discriminating KNBG from AG meat. However, larger and more diverse sample sets and independent validation are required to establish a robust origin authentication approach.

title: Modern Paradigms in Rational Drug Design: A Comprehensive Review
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Pharmaceutical drug discovery has undergone a paradigm shift over the past century, evolving from phenotypic screening and serendipitous discovery to structural, computational, and molecularly targeted paradigms. Early drug discovery relied
content: Pharmaceutical drug discovery has undergone a paradigm shift over the past century, evolving from phenotypic screening and serendipitous discovery to structural, computational, and molecularly targeted paradigms. Early drug discovery relied heavily on natural product isolation and empirical observation, which, while yielding foundational pharmacotherapies, lacked mechanistic precision and carried high failure rates. The modern era of rational drug design integrates high-resolution structural biology—specifically X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM)—with computational modeling, quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) analyses, and artificial intelligence (AI) to systematically engineer therapeutics with high affinity, exquisite selectivity, and optimal pharmacokinetic profiles. This comprehensive review synthesizes the methodological framework of contemporary drug discovery. We trace the continuum of target identification and validation across multi-omics platforms, functional genomics (CRISPR/Cas9), and chemical probes, detailing the physical and thermodynamic parameters that define druggable binding pockets. We examine lead discovery strategies, contrasting High-Throughput Screening (HTS) with Fragment-Based Drug Design (FBDD), and delineate structure-based (SBDD) and ligand-based (LBDD) approaches. Furthermore, we address the biophysical optimization of lead compounds through physicochemical parameterization, Lipinski's Rule of Five, in silico ADMET prediction, and targeted prodrug or nanoparticle delivery systems. Finally, we explore frontier therapeutic modalities, including proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), covalent inhibitors, allosteric modulators, and deep generative AI models. Through detailed clinical case studies of imatinib, oseltamivir, and sofosbuvir, this manuscript demonstrates the real-world application of rational design, while providing a critical analysis of clinical attrition causes and future automated closed-loop discovery paradigms

title: Reactivating retired wind turbines as distributed sources of physical inertia for resilient power systems
summary: The transition towards renewable energy systems introduces a dual challenge, with declining system inertia and the growing accumulation of end-of-life infrastructure. While inverter-based generation reduces the physical inertia required for
content: The transition towards renewable energy systems introduces a dual challenge, with declining system inertia and the growing accumulation of end-of-life infrastructure. While inverter-based generation reduces the physical inertia required for frequency stability, large numbers of wind turbine generators are reaching retirement despite retaining substantial electromechanical capability. This creates a mismatch between emerging system needs and underutilised resources. We show that retired wind turbine generators can be reactivated as distributed sources of physical inertia, enabling electromechanical energy exchange with the grid through the controlled release and recovery of stored rotor kinetic energy. By linking frequency-responsive activation to rotor dynamics, these assets provide support during disturbances. System-level analysis indicates that reactivated generators improve frequency response across a range of operating conditions, increasing frequency nadir and reducing cumulative frequency deviation. Beyond the improvement in dynamic performance, this approach offers a pathway for the functional reuse of renewable infrastructure. By extending the operational role of existing assets, it connects system stability with circular resource utilisation. These results suggest that renewable technologies may evolve from single-purpose generation units into persistent system resources, offering a scalable route towards more resilient and sustainable low-carbon power systems.

title: Can a green agricultural policy reconcile grain production and ecological protection? Evidence from China's National Agricultural Green Development Pilot Zone
summary: Introduction Safeguarding grain supply while reducing the ecological pressures generated by agricultural production is a major challenge for the green transition of agriculture. However, county-level evidence remains limited on whether comp
content: Introduction Safeguarding grain supply while reducing the ecological pressures generated by agricultural production is a major challenge for the green transition of agriculture. However, county-level evidence remains limited on whether comprehensive green agricultural policies can simultaneously improve grain production and the ecological environment. This study examines the National Agricultural Green Development Pilot Zone (NAGDPZ) and evaluates its effect on the grain-ecology coupling coordination degree (GECCD) and the trade-offs involved. Methods Using a balanced panel of 1626 Chinese counties from 2000 to 2025, we measure GECCD with a coupling coordination model and exploit the staggered implementation of NAGDPZ in a difference-in-differences framework. We decompose the policy effects into grain production and ecological performance and examine how baseline conditions and grain-related firm development (GRF) modify them. Results NAGDPZ increases GECCD by 0.0090 index points. The result is robust to parallel-trends and placebo tests, alternative model specifications, a delayed policy-effective year, and controls for concurrent policies. Effect decomposition shows that this increase does not arise from simultaneous improvements in grain production and the ecological environment: NAGDPZ increases ecological performance by 0.0360 index points but reduces grain production performance by 0.0216 index points. Conditional-effect analysis shows that greater chemical input dependence and stronger ecological endowment enhance the ecological effect of NAGDPZ. By contrast, the effects of mechanization intensity and chemical input dependence on grain production are not statistically robust. GRF strengthens the effect of NAGDPZ on GECCD and mitigates its adverse effect on grain production, although it attenuates ecological improvement. Further analysis shows that the average ecological policy effect remains positive in both the high- and low-GRF groups. Discussion NAGDPZ improves GECCD overall, but the improvement is driven primarily by ecological gains and is accompanied by adjustment pressure on grain production. This finding indicates a transition-related trade-off when conventional inputs are withdrawn before green technologies and production organizations can fully replace them. By facilitating technology adoption, factor integration, and specialized services, grain-related firms can strengthen producers' adaptive capacity and help shift green agricultural development from constraint-driven improvement based on input reduction toward synergy-driven improvement based on technological progress and efficiency gains.

title: Post-Project Institutional Longevity in Ethiopian Community Forestry: A Systematic Review of Enforcement and Compliance
summary: Community-based forest governance has been promoted in Ethiopia since the mid-1990s, yet the durability of Participatory Forest Management (PFM) institutions after external project exit remains poorly understood. This systematic review exam
content: Community-based forest governance has been promoted in Ethiopia since the mid-1990s, yet the durability of Participatory Forest Management (PFM) institutions after external project exit remains poorly understood. This systematic review examined why some forest user groups (FUGs) persist after donor withdrawal while others decay. Following PRISMA 2020, seven databases and university repositories were searched for studies published. Of 1,007 records, 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and the 60% quality threshold of the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Evidence was synthesized narratively, guided by Ostrom’s Institutional Analysis and Development framework and the Schlager and Ostrom property rights hierarchy. Forest condition frequently outlasted the institutions established to protect it: an estimated 35–67% of groups were non-functional or impaired, although only one site reported direct counts. Patrol enforcement declined once subsidies ended, owing to uncompensated opportunity costs, risk, equipment depreciation, and large forest blocks. Compliance eroded because kebele and woreda courts rarely upheld informal bylaws, leaving the exclusion right the least secure of five property rights. Inequitable distribution of costs and benefits and elite capture undermined support for the rules. Durable governance appeared to rest on four pillars: customary–statutory legal hybridity, statutory judicial backstopping, high-value commercial incentives, and nested governance unions, most effective in combination. Evidence is constrained by short-term, cross-sectional designs, concentration in NGO-supported sites, and inconsistent definitions of institutional survival. Policy should formalize bylaws and strengthen judicial backing, while programs should plan exit strategies and incentivize guards. Future research should adopt standardized survival metrics and longitudinal designs.

title: AI-powered electronic noses: advances in machine learning for food quality and sensory assessment
summary: Electronic noses (e-noses) are devices that mimic the human olfactory system through arrays of gas sensors associated with pattern recognition algorithms to detect, identify, and quantify volatile organic compounds (VOCs) for food quality a
content: Electronic noses (e-noses) are devices that mimic the human olfactory system through arrays of gas sensors associated with pattern recognition algorithms to detect, identify, and quantify volatile organic compounds (VOCs) for food quality assessment. Despite the growing application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to enhance e-nose systems, there is limited understanding of how they perform across different food categories. This review summarizes findings from 106 studies published between 2010 and 2026, investigating AI-driven e-nose systems for quality and sensory assessment across dairy, meat, seafood, beverages, fruits, and processed foods. We evaluate the performance of supervised algorithms such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) alongside Deep Learning (DL) approaches such as transfer learning (TL), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), focusing on classification accuracy, spoilage detection, authenticity testing, and flavor profiling. The reviewed literature consistently shows that ML integration significantly improves odor pattern recognition and reduces reliance on human sensory panels, with deep learning models showing particular strengths in handling high-dimensional sensor data. However, challenges like sensor drift, dataset variability, and limited model generalization remain barriers to wider development. This review highlights the need for standardized datasets and more robust TL approaches to advance e-nose technology toward reliable real-world food safety applications.

title: From Farm to Fashion: Transforming Vegetable Waste Into Sustainable Leather Alternatives
summary: The global leather industry faces mounting pressure due to its environmental, ethical, and resource challenges. Conventional leather production consumes large quantities of water and chemicals, while synthetic alternatives rely on petroleum
content: The global leather industry faces mounting pressure due to its environmental, ethical, and resource challenges. Conventional leather production consumes large quantities of water and chemicals, while synthetic alternatives rely on petroleum-based polymers. In this context, the conversion of vegetable waste into sustainable leather substitutes represents a promising and eco-conscious innovation. This chapter explores the scientific foundations, material engineering, and sustainability perspectives of vegetable waste-derived leather alternatives. It discusses the biochemical composition of agricultural residues, extraction of biopolymers, fabrication techniques, and characterization methods. Further, it examines environmental benefits, cost feasibility, and market adoption trends within the fashion industry. By bridging the gap between agricultural waste management and sustainable design, this chapter outlines a circular model that supports ethical fashion, resource efficiency, and carbon reduction.

title: Phenological Patterns and Bud-rank-dependent Fruit Weights in Three Korean Strawberry Cultivars
summary: The relative contributions of the flower bud order within an inflorescence (bud rank), cultivar, and intensive environmental variables to flowering-to-harvest days (FHD) and fruit weight were quantified at the plant level (n = 219) for thre
content: The relative contributions of the flower bud order within an inflorescence (bud rank), cultivar, and intensive environmental variables to flowering-to-harvest days (FHD) and fruit weight were quantified at the plant level (n = 219) for three Korean strawberry cultivars: forcing types 'Sulhyang' and 'Kuemsil' and the semi-forcing type 'Jukhyang'.Plants were cultivated in a tunnel-type plastic greenhouse from September of 2023 to March of 2024, with flowering dates, harvest dates, and fresh fruit weights recorded for primary, secondary, and tertiary buds in the first and second inflorescences.Days to first flowering exhibited clear cultivar-dependent separation (56.5-87.5 d), whereas FHD displayed substantial within-group variation, with a three-way ANOVA accounting for only 24.2% of the total variance.In contrast, bud rank exerted a dominant effect on fruit weight (p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.54).The mean fresh weights of primary-, secondary-, and tertiary-budderived fruits were 26.8, 21.5, and 14.1 g, respectively, exhibiting a 47% reduction in fruit weight from primary-to tertiary-bud-derived fruits.Within-bud-rank Pearson correlations between FHD and fruit weight were negligible (|r| ≤ 0.15), indicating that an apparent size-time trade-off observed in the pooled data reflected bud-rank stratification rather than within-plant developmental coupling.Leave-one-out cross-validation of FHD prediction models constructed exclusively from intensive environmental variables yielded R 2 values ranging from -1.41 to 0.50, providing insufficient precision for practical use in management decision-making.Collectively, these results demonstrate that bud-rank monitoring provides a more reliable basis for harvest scheduling than environmentbased regression and that removing later-differentiating buds may enhance marketable fruit weight.

title: Impact of organic farming schemes on soil health, economic viability and farmer adoption in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu, India
summary: This study was conducted to evaluate the comprehensive impact of organic farming schemes implemented in the Nilgiris district, India through systematic assessment of 200 farmers. The research examined bio-input adoption patterns, soil healt
content: This study was conducted to evaluate the comprehensive impact of organic farming schemes implemented in the Nilgiris district, India through systematic assessment of 200 farmers. The research examined bio-input adoption patterns, soil health transformations, economic viability and implementation constraints using advanced statistical methods including logistic regression analysis. Results revealed a 65.5 % adoption rate with vermicompost showing the highest preference at 77 %, followed by biofertilisers at 67.5 % and biopesticides at 59 %. Soil analysis demonstrated statistically significant improvements in all parameters: pH increased by 0.34 units, organic carbon content increased by 0.22 % (42.3 % increase) and electrical conductivity (EC) decreased by 0.10 dS m-1 (all p < 0.001). Economic analysis yielded exceptional results with a 14.7 % reduction in production costs, 137 % increase in farmer income and a benefit-cost (B : C) ratio of 2.31. Organic farmers achieved 37.51 % price premium compared to 5.38 % for non-adopters. Logistic regression identified three critical adoption barriers: lack of technical knowledge (odds ratio (OR) = 0.466, 53 % reduction in adoption odds), high input costs (OR = 0.395, 60 % reduction) and pest management difficulties (OR = 0.391, 61 % reduction), all significant at p < 0.001. Despite pest management being the top constraint, farmers achieved a 20.3 % yield increase, demonstrating economic viability when combined with improved soil health and market access. The study validates both environmental sustainability and economic profitability of organic farming in the Nilgiris while providing evidence-based recommendations for program enhancement.

title: Linkage, dependence and ripple effects in China’s logistics industry: A disaggregated input–output baseline for sustainable supply chain analysis along the Belt and Road, 2014
summary: Standard input–output tables bury logistics inside a wider transport and postal category, which hides how a national logistics system is tied into cross-border production. We separate logistics into seven freight sub-sectors in the 2014 Wor
