content: Standard input–output tables bury logistics inside a wider transport and postal category, which hides how a national logistics system is tied into cross-border production. We separate logistics into seven freight sub-sectors in the 2014 World Input–Output Database, using China’s 2018 national table for the separation ratios, and measure backward and forward linkages, external dependence and ripple effects. The Belt and Road (B&R) sample is the 23 partner economies WIOD reports separately, so the land corridor is covered only in part. Backward linkages run mainly to petroleum, coking and mining inputs in East and South Asia; forward linkages reach construction and electronics manufacturing as far as Central and Eastern Europe. External dependence of the logistics sector is 26.27% of value added, but the 23 B&R economies account for only 3.03 percentage points of it, or 11.6%, and within that subset five economies supply 76%. The share stays between 9% and 12% across alternative sample definitions, and the 26.27% total stays between 22.9% and 30.8% under a 20% error in the separation ratios. Air cargo is the most exposed sub-sector at 53.54%. Air cargo, waterborne cargo and warehousing sit above the economy-wide mean on both ripple coefficients; road, rail, pipeline and express delivery sit below it on influence. As 2014 is the initiative’s first full year, the estimates are a structural baseline against which later tables can be read.

title: Transition to Holacracy and Digital Supply Chain Management
summary: Digitalization offers great opportunities for improving supply chain management. However, its full potential is limited by the tendency of managers in these chains to rely on hierarchical organizational structures, which prevent the full ut
content: Digitalization offers great opportunities for improving supply chain management. However, its full potential is limited by the tendency of managers in these chains to rely on hierarchical organizational structures, which prevent the full utilization of employees’ competencies. These competencies are necessary for the creation and use of artificial intelligence that operates on both physical and non-physical management objects. The solution to this problem can be achieved through holacracy, which creates conditions for employees in supply chain links to act as “sensors” and “actuators”. These roles are essential for the development and implementation of a digital twin that can help manage these chains. The purpose of this article is to create theoretical and methodological prerequisites for the use of holacracy in digital supply chain management.To achieve the purpose of this article, we used terminological analysis, descriptive and faceted methods, or a TDF methodology. The article explains the essence of holacracy and the digitalization of supply chain management. It discusses digitized options for supply chains, as well as developed technologies for the interaction of persons involved in digital supply chain management in a holacratic environment. The article also justifies the approach to developing digital management solutions for supply chains based on holacracy.

title: Technology Impact Indicators for Ecosystem-Based Fisheries Management
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This report presents three reviews of performance measures and indicators from three distinct fields of technology development under study within Infinifish, and contributes to Work Package 6, Task 2. The first review examines literature re
content: This report presents three reviews of performance measures and indicators from three distinct fields of technology development under study within Infinifish, and contributes to Work Package 6, Task 2. The first review examines literature related to energy efficiency measures in capture fisheries, the second examines literature related to seabed impact quantification, and the third addresses the diverse field of valorization efforts to reduce biomass waste generated from capture fisheries bycatch and processing activities. The aim of these reviews is to present the state of the art in measuring and recording utility of individual fishing/processing technology, to clarify how this utility can then be scaled up to inform or promote uptake, and finally how impact at higher scales of societal or environmental impact can be measured, within the broader topics of seabed disturbance, carbon footprint, and waste utilization in capture fisheries. Because the first two topics relate to direct physical impacts of capture fisheries activities, indicators are evaluated with regards to being measurable during operations, sensitive to technological change, and scalable from vessels to ecosystems. The framework builds on existing regulatory structures including the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD) and addresses gaps in current electronic monitoring (EM) adoption. Seabed impact indicators, for instance, are well developed for spatial extent (swept-area ratio) and benthic state (relative benthic status). On the other hand, tow-resolved disturbance intensity, and routine vessel-monitoring polling can be too coarse to resolve accurate gear foot printing. This can leave a gap between mechanistic understanding and operational measurementsensor-based indicators are positioned to close. Because the last topic lies further down the value chain, it is intended to inform compliance with Waste Management Directives, inform pathways societal resilience, and support transitions toward a blue circular economy. Recommendations are made for what and how measures could be recorded in future studies or technological development, including Infinifish technologies, within these distinct fields, thereby providing bases from which the best-practice methodologies found in reviews can be further developed. For fuel efficiency studies, there is a need for greater documentation of confounding factors, more explicit decomposition of catch efficiency versus fuel efficiency when reporting fuel use intensity (FUI), and more haul and trip resolution data demonstrating methods to better support technological benefits of increases fuel efficiency. For seabed impacts, there is a need for electronic monitoring to develop such that benthic impacts can be quantified at the haul or trip level, while the linkage between an individual haul event and its impact on state indicators need further development. title: The effect of science-based targets on corporate emissions trajectories
summary: Voluntary corporate climate targets are intended to reduce emissions, but their effects may depend on how those emissions are accounted for. Using CDP disclosures for 4,186 firms between 2016 and 2025 and a staggered difference-in-differenc
content: Voluntary corporate climate targets are intended to reduce emissions, but their effects may depend on how those emissions are accounted for. Using CDP disclosures for 4,186 firms between 2016 and 2025 and a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that science-based target approval lowers market-based Scope 2 emissions by about 27%, while Scope 1 and location-based Scope 2 remain unchanged. The renewable share of purchased electricity rises by 7.8 percentage points, with no change in electricity consumption or grid carbon intensity. The shift runs through contractual sourcing, with the largest response in unbundled energy attribute certificates, which are bought separately from electricity supply, without necessarily adding new generation. Market-based accounting can therefore register reductions without a corresponding change in physical emissions. Contractual sourcing can support decarbonization, but assessing progress toward corporate climate goals requires distinguishing it from changes in energy use and the electricity system.

title: Consumer response to a multi-channel promotional campaign for local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq: a mixed-methods evaluation
summary: Introduction This study looked at how a multi-channel promotional campaign, affected what people know, how they feel, and whether they actually bought local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Methods A single cohort of 400 consumers
content: Introduction This study looked at how a multi-channel promotional campaign, affected what people know, how they feel, and whether they actually bought local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Methods A single cohort of 400 consumers was surveyed before the campaign (September–October 2025) and re-contacted after campaign implementation (July–August 2026). After matching respondents, we were able to compare 165 individuals with confidence. Our questionnaire covered knowledge, attitudes, buying habits, campaign exposure and recognition (distinguishing visibility, engagement, and message recall), message quality, barriers to purchase, and willingness to pay. We used a mix of statistical tools, from simple comparisons to more advanced techniques like regression analysis and clustering. Results Knowledge increased significantly from pre-campaign (2.621 ± 0.904) to post-campaign (2.903 ± 0.992; Δ = +0.282, p = 0.003, Cohen’s dz. = 0.236). No statistically significant overall changes were detected in attitudes (Δ = +0.074, p = 0.328) or purchasing behavior (Δ = −0.012, p = 0.872). Overall campaign exposure was moderate (2.653/5), with social media exposure higher than traditional media. Barriers to purchasing included insufficient label information (3.313), difficulty finding the product (3.275), and weak packaging/branding (3.258). PCA identified eight underlying dimensions explaining 63.3% of variance, and K-means clustering produced five exploratory consumer profiles: “Informed but barrier-constrained engaged consumers” (21.0%); “Low-engagement/low-response consumers” (17.0%); “Committed local-olive-oil advocates” (29.5%); “Under-reached but potentially receptive consumers” (8.2%); and “Positive but underinformed consumers” (24.2%). Discussion The big takeaway is that awareness alone is not enough. People need to actually find the product, trust what is on the label, and feel good about the packaging and price. The wide regional differences also tell us that one-size-fits-all does not work, because local context matters a lot. Our consumer profiles offer a helpful roadmap for tailoring future efforts, rather than using a blanket approach. Conclusion Promotional campaigns can effectively increase consumer knowledge about local olive oil, but translating awareness into positive attitudes and purchasing behavior requires integrated interventions addressing quality assurance, traceability, packaging, distribution, and consumer trust. In addition, differentiated marketing strategies based on consumer segments offer a practical pathway for strengthening the local olive oil.

title: A gravity-based framework for the spatial allocation and distribution of storage capacity to facilitate reuse of construction and demolition waste
summary: This study examines how the location and capacity of intermediary storage hubs affect reuse of construction and demolition waste in the built environment. A gravity-based framework is developed to investigate how varying number, location, a
content: This study examines how the location and capacity of intermediary storage hubs affect reuse of construction and demolition waste in the built environment. A gravity-based framework is developed to investigate how varying number, location, and size of storage capacities affect material flows across a hypothetical network under various constraint conditions. Travel deterrence is applied to the model, presented in a case study of Great Britain’s road-transport network, to study the impacts of distance cutoff thresholds on material flows and the effects of the spatial distribution of storage capacity scaled by supply, demand and node centrality. The results show that under flow-constrained conditions in a homogeneous network, maximum reuse is achieved by maximising recovery efficiency when supply is limited. The study also investigates spatial allocation of storage infrastructure when total capacity is fixed, then determines the spatial agglomeration of more centralised or distributed storage network under different material and transport limitations.

title: Direct-from-Wood Fibrillation for Self-Binding Porous Materials: a novel valorization pathway for residual wood and coarse wool waste
summary: Identifying viable valorization pathways for biogenic waste streams has become increasingly important in the context of the climate crisis. In this work, forestry waste, in combination with industrial waste wool, was processed through simpl
content: Identifying viable valorization pathways for biogenic waste streams has become increasingly important in the context of the climate crisis. In this work, forestry waste, in combination with industrial waste wool, was processed through simple and direct methods in order to achieve a foam-like material. Different energy inputs were explored for direct-from-source fibrillation. \qty{5}{\fibrillation} resulted in a multiscale mix of wood particles and fibrils, here defined as wood fibrils, providing the porous material with sufficient stability and preventing significant shrinkage during drying. When incorporating industrial waste wool, samples with $\uplambda$-values as low as \qty{64}{\thermal} were achieved. Additionally, the incorporation of waste wool increased hygroscopic and fire-retardant properties. Wood fibrils were combined with guanidine phosphate and aluminum hydroxide (\qty{20}{\wtpct}). Guanidine phosphate enabled self-extinguishing behavior, while both routes showed improved thermal degradation management, supporting development towards practical applications. This work demonstrates that the inherent binding properties of low-energy fibrillated residual wood enable the development of bio-based, porous material systems. The mechanical, thermal and fire-performance of these systems can be tailored by incorporating different components, such as organic and inorganic flame-retardants, as well as industrial waste wool, creating new opportunities for waste valorization.

title: Exploring the challenges facing landscape management in smart city studies with the approach of artificial intelligence
source: Journal of Environmental Engineering and Landscape Management
summary: This applied study analyzes the components and development challenges of smart cities in Sanandaj using a descriptive-analytical approach. The main objective of the research is to identify the challenges and key components of the smart city
content: This applied study analyzes the components and development challenges of smart cities in Sanandaj using a descriptive-analytical approach. The main objective of the research is to identify the challenges and key components of the smart city development process, and to assess the performance of these components to pinpoint areas for improvement. Data were collected through documentary sources, organizational records, and a researcher-designed questionnaire distributed to 60 experts and officials across different districts of the city. The study employed several analytical methods, including Fuzzy TOPSIS, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network to rank, assess, and predict the performance of the components. The results showed that the Smart Economy (0.872) and Smart People (0.843) were the most influential components, while Smart Services (0.643) and Smart Transportation ranked lowest, reflecting infrastructural weaknesses in these areas. Correlation analysis revealed a weak link between Smart People and overall smart city realization, highlighting a gap between digital readiness and technological needs. The Smart Environment performed relatively well but had low predictive potential (0.392) in the MLP model. The findings stress the need for stronger digital infrastructure, enhanced digital literacy among citizens, integrated transportation systems, and participatory governance as key factors guiding Sanandaj’s transition to a sustainable, smart city.

title: Appendix S1. Supplementary Materials: Search Protocol, PRISMA Flow, Characteristics of Included Studies, and Full-Text Exclusions
summary: My research focuses on agricultural economics, sustainable agriculture, and rural development, with particular interests in the socio-economic dimensions of agricultural sustainability in developing countries. My work examines smallholder l
content: My research focuses on agricultural economics, sustainable agriculture, and rural development, with particular interests in the socio-economic dimensions of agricultural sustainability in developing countries. My work examines smallholder livelihoods, agricultural value chains, land-use practices, environmental governance, and the institutional arrangements shaping farmers' participation in sustainable agricultural initiatives. I am particularly interested in agricultural carbon markets, carbon farming, agroforestry, sustainability standards, benefit-sharing mechanisms, and the distribution of responsibilities, costs, benefits, and risks among farmers and other stakeholders. My research also addresses agricultural policy, rural institutions, farmer organisations, and the implications of environmental and market-based interventions for household welfare and livelihood resilience. My methodological interests include systematic literature reviews, household surveys, quantitative socio-economic analysis, and mixed-method research.

title: Industrial heat coupling as a conditional driver of the system value of fusion energy in weather-resolved global energy systems
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This archive contains the model, input data and results for the manuscript "Industrial heat coupling as a conditional driver of the system value of fusion energy in weather-resolved global energy systems" by Hung Vo Thanh and Baehyun Min (E
content: This archive contains the model, input data and results for the manuscript "Industrial heat coupling as a conditional driver of the system value of fusion energy in weather-resolved global energy systems" by Hung Vo Thanh and Baehyun Min (Energy, manuscript EGY-D-26-20831, revised version). The study asks how much of the system value of fusion energy comes from selling industrial heat as well as electricity. It uses a nine-region capacity-expansion model for 2030–2050 with annual energy balances, linked to a chronological dispatch model of the same system. Fusion competes with geothermal energy, gas with carbon capture, hydrogen storage, solar, wind, batteries and interregional transmission. The heat market is represented in two ways: an avoided gas-boiler credit, and an industrial heat sector by region and temperature grade in which gas boilers, electric boilers and heat pumps compete with fusion heat. What the archive contains - The capacity-expansion model and the dispatch model (Python, SciPy/HiGHS and PyPSA), with the planning–operations feedback loop.- All curated input data. Every techno-economic value carries a source identifier that is resolved in data/processed/sources.csv.- The 45 hourly solar and wind

title: Thinking the pathologies of infrastructural Europe through Rotterdam
summary: This article explores what the everyday reveals about the regulation of global supply chains by EU law. Taking the story of a dockworker in the Port of Rotterdam as its point of departure, it examines the legal and compliance mechanisms thr
content: This article explores what the everyday reveals about the regulation of global supply chains by EU law. Taking the story of a dockworker in the Port of Rotterdam as its point of departure, it examines the legal and compliance mechanisms through which the European Union increasingly seeks to govern transnational supply chains, from subcontracting arrangements and environmental regulation to corporate human rights commitments, all encompassed in emerging mandatory due diligence frameworks in EU law and some Member States. Rotterdam’s story is approached as a diagnostic site of infrastructural Europe, where the promises of European legality encounter the material infrastructures through which goods, labour, resources and legal responsibility circulate across and beyond Europe. Read from this standpoint, the EU law for global supply chains appears to be only partially attuned to the distributed and relational forms of harm it seeks to govern. This article argues that it not only reflects failure of implementation, but a deeper crisis of attunement, whereby contemporary due diligence mechanisms struggle to perceive the socio-material conditions through which harm is produced and dispersed. It concludes by proposing the everyday as an epistemic standpoint for EU law, examining in concrete cases how, in the port of Rotterdam, trade unions, NGOs and affected communities seek to reconfigure responsibility from below and, in doing so, push EU law beyond procedural abstraction towards a more structural engagement with the realities of global supply chains.

title: Elemental and biochemical responses of Cantharellus cibarius to peri-urban environmental conditions
summary: Aim: This study aimed to characterise and compare the elemental and biochemical composition of Cantharellus cibarius fruiting bodies obtained from traders and reported to originate from six peri-urban forest areas, and to assess differences
content: Aim: This study aimed to characterise and compare the elemental and biochemical composition of Cantharellus cibarius fruiting bodies obtained from traders and reported to originate from six peri-urban forest areas, and to assess differences in their chemical profiles across the reported sampling locations. Methods: Proximate composition, macro- and trace elements, fatty acids (FA), free sterols, water-soluble B-group vitamins, ascorbic acid, total phenolic content, and 2,2’-azinobis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) radical-scavenging activity were determined using gravimetric, ICP-OES, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), and liquid chromatographic methods. Multiple factor analysis was used to integrate the metal, fatty-acid, sterol, and vitamin data blocks. Results: Moisture and protein contents were relatively stable across locations, whereas crude fat, fatty-acid composition, sterols, vitamins, and several elements showed pronounced site-dependent variation. Unsaturated FA predominated, and samples from the central-southern region contained the highest levels of acetylenic and polyunsaturated FA, ergosterol, and fungisterol. Site-related differences were observed in several elements, particularly Fe, Mn, Ni, and Zn. The first two dimensions of multiple-factor analysis explained 56.7% of the total variation and revealed clear geographical differentiation. Central-southern samples were distinguished mainly by fatty-acid and sterol profiles, whereas coastal samples occupied a contrasting position, particularly associated with fatty-acid and metal contributions. Samples from western, east-northern, and north-eastern locations were differentiated by varying contributions of the four chemical data blocks. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance confirmed significant differences among locations for all four data blocks and for the integrated multiple-factor analysis space. Conclusions: C. cibarius showed clear site-dependent chemical variation across peri-urban locations. Multiple factor analysis (MFA) confirmed that this differentiation reflected coordinated changes across elements, FA, sterols, and vitamins. The observed patterns may relate to local environmental conditions, but cannot be attributed solely to anthropogenic pressure.

title: Effects of fine-granular electricity procurement for renewable and low-carbon hydrogen production - a comparative analysis of production strategies
summary: Renewable hydrogen is an integral part of managing the energy transition due to its potential to drive the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. However, the market uptake of renewable hydrogen produced via electrolysis is impeded by hi
content: Renewable hydrogen is an integral part of managing the energy transition due to its potential to drive the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. However, the market uptake of renewable hydrogen produced via electrolysis is impeded by high costs and risks across the hydrogen value chain. Additionally, within the European Union (EU), strict regulatory requirements on renewable hydrogen affect the economic viability of electrolysis projects. In the transition phase towards a renewable hydrogen economy, expanding electrolyzer operations beyond renewable hydrogen production to include low-carbon hydrogen may increase economic performance and attract investment in electrolysis projects. In our study, we assess the economic impact of supplementing renewable hydrogen with low-carbon hydrogen production in compliance with the EU regulatory framework, utilizing fine-granular electricity procurement across five exemplary bidding zones (BZs). For BZs exhibiting high potential for grid-connected low-carbon hydrogen production, Levelized Cost of Hydrogen for a renewable hydrogen production strategy including non-oversized long-term PV-, wind- and hydropower Power Purchase Agreements may be reduced by up to 78.7 % through additional short-term low-carbon hydrogen production. However, significant variations in electricity generation across BZs result in numerous BZs not meeting the regulatory requirements, limiting the overall potential of electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen production. In less decarbonized BZs, establishing low-carbon hydrogen entails the risk of ongoing investments in natural gas infrastructure, counteracting the role of low-carbon hydrogen as a transitional solution. To advance the energy transition supported by hydrogen, we recommend that policymakers align hydrogen regulation with long-term decarbonization objectives by integrating financial subsidies for electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen.

title: Leaf primary metabolomic profiling of autochthonous grapevine varieties under Douro Superior terroir
summary: Introduction Vitis vinifera L. is one of the most widely grown worldwide fruit crop being considered a high-value and economically important fruit-producing perennial trailing crop. Understanding the metabolic mechanisms underlying inter-va
content: Introduction Vitis vinifera L. is one of the most widely grown worldwide fruit crop being considered a high-value and economically important fruit-producing perennial trailing crop. Understanding the metabolic mechanisms underlying inter-varietal diversity and adaptability to summer stress constitutes a valuable resource toward more resilient viticulture. Methods This study aimed to characterize and compare the primary metabolomic profiles of six grapevine varieties (‘Alicante Bouschet’, ‘Donzelinho Tinto’, ‘Malvasia Preta’, ‘Tinto Cão’, ‘Touriga Franca’ and ‘Touriga Nacional’) over two consecutive growing seasons (2023 and 2024). Results and Discussion A total of 56 primary metabolites were annotated, comprising sugars, amino acids, organic acids, polyphenols, and other functional groups. Multivariate statistical analyses (PCA and HCA) showed that sampling year was the major driver of leaf metabolome variation. Two-way ANOVA revealed that 45 metabolites were significantly affected by year and/or variety. Furthermore, five metabolites (pyruvic acid, myo -inositol, phenylalanine, quercetin, and dehydroascorbic acid dimer) displayed a significant year × variety interaction, demonstrating distinct, variety-specific plasticity across growing seasons. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the environmental inter-annual conditions are broadly related with the global leaf metabolomic profile, while the variety-specific profiling remain evident, particularly in organic acid regulation and key protective stress-related metabolites.

title: CEO environmentally responsible leadership and ambidextrous green innovation: the roles of organizational climate for psychological safety and environmental dynamism
summary: Introduction While firms increasingly articulate environmental commitments, many still struggle to translate these commitments into substantive environmental outcomes. Drawing on upper echelons, organizational climate, and ambidexterity the
content: Introduction While firms increasingly articulate environmental commitments, many still struggle to translate these commitments into substantive environmental outcomes. Drawing on upper echelons, organizational climate, and ambidexterity theories, this study examines the relationship between CEO environmentally responsible leadership (CERL) and ambidextrous green innovation (AGI), focusing on the indirect role of organizational climate for psychological safety (OCPS) and the conditional role of environmental dynamism (ED). Methods Using survey data from 334 Chinese manufacturing firms, partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) is applied to test the hypothesized relationships. Various robustness analyses addressing nonlinearity, endogeneity, and unobserved heterogeneity are performed to assess the stability of the findings. Results The results show that CERL is positively associated with both OCPS and AGI, while OCPS is positively associated with AGI. The indirect association between CERL and AGI through OCPS is positive and significant. Moreover, both the positive association between OCPS and AGI and the indirect association between CERL and AGI via OCPS are stronger at higher ED. The robustness analyses support the stability of these results. Discussion The findings contribute to theoretical understanding by showing how environmentally responsible leadership is associated with green innovation through a psychologically safe organizational climate and how environmental dynamism conditions this relationship. Practically, the findings suggest that firms may complement environmentally responsible leadership with a psychologically safe climate in which employees can challenge established practices and pursue new green solutions, particularly under dynamic environmental conditions. Overall, the study provides theoretical and managerial insights into how firms can achieve substantive environmental outcomes through leadership and organizational conditions that support green innovation.

title: Climate-Induced Environmental Change and Human Well-Being in the Transboundary Sundarbans: A Systematic Review
summary: The world’s largest contiguous mangrove forest and among the most climate-vulnerable social-ecological systems, the transboundary Sundarbans is shared by Bangladesh and India. Overdependence on its ecosystem resources, along with accelerati
content: The world’s largest contiguous mangrove forest and among the most climate-vulnerable social-ecological systems, the transboundary Sundarbans is shared by Bangladesh and India. Overdependence on its ecosystem resources, along with accelerating sea-level rise, salinity intrusion from seawater, tropical cyclones, riverbank erosion, and mangrove degradation, increasingly threatens the integrity of its ecosystem and livelihoods for millions. In this systematic review, we synthesise the latest evidence on climate-related environmental change and its impact on human welfare across the transboundary Sundarbans. A systematic search of the literature from January 2010 to July 2026 was conducted using the Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed databases, and grey literature sources were selected following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Of the 535 previous articles references identified in the search, 23 studies met our pre-established inclusion criteria and were analyzed using a narrative thematic synthesis. Results highlight salinity intrusion, sea-level rise, repetitive hits of tropical cyclones, shoreline erosion, and mangrove degradation as key climate-change-related drivers of the region. The new stressors compromise agricultural productivity, fisheries production, and ecosystem services, while concomitantly raising drinking-water salinity and the incidence of food insecurity. Climate-related diseases (e.g., gender inequalities, livelihood dependence, and poor adaptive capacity) lead to higher vulnerability to climate change impacts for women, children, and forest- and fishery-dependent households. The review also points to ongoing gaps in transboundary governance, alignment of environmental monitoring, climate finance, and integrated adaptation planning between Bangladesh and India. You need to strengthen ecosystem-based adaptation, climate-resilient livelihoods, public health interventions, gender-responsive policies, and bilateral governance mechanisms to increase robustness against the long-term effects of disease outbreaks. This review also offers an inclusive evidence base to assist policymakers, researchers, and development practitioners in designing climate adaptation and integrated climate-smart management strategies specific to the transboundary Sundarbans, as well as similar at-risk UES, using the delineated key themes.

title: The illusion of predictability in carbon price forecasting and look-ahead bias
summary: Machine learning studies report large gains in forecasting EU Allowance (EUA) prices, but their designs rarely rule out leakage of future data. EUA futures returns are forecast one, five and twenty-two trading days ahead over 2022 to 2026 w
content: Machine learning studies report large gains in forecasting EU Allowance (EUA) prices, but their designs rarely rule out leakage of future data. EUA futures returns are forecast one, five and twenty-two trading days ahead over 2022 to 2026 with nine models: a random walk, an autoregressive model with exogenous inputs, an elastic net, Extra Trees, XGBoost, k-nearest neighbours, support vector regression, a feed-forward network and an LSTM. Nineteen daily series enter in four economically motivated blocks: energy fundamentals, including the coal-to-gas switching price, financial markets, bond yields, and uncertainty and market activity. Every predictor is observable at the forecast origin, hyperparameters are fixed on 2018 to 2021 data, and models are refitted monthly with a purge between training targets and the origin. No model beats a random walk at any horizon; Clark and West tests, Holm-adjusted Diebold and Mariano tests and the model confidence set agree. Most long-horizon loss reflects drift learned during the 2018 to 2021 rally. Past EUA returns and policy uncertainty carry small but consistent OOS information, whereas the renewable share and the switching gap, prominent in in-sample rankings, impair forecasts. Measuring predictors on the target day would have produced spurious gains of up to ten percent.

title: Strengthening Agri-Food Systems Through Sustainable Logistics in Low-Income Settings
summary: Agricultural systems in Low-Income Countries (LICs) such as agri-food systems can be improved through sustainable logistics to address significant gaps in poverty reduction, food security and climate resilience as small-scale producers make
content: Agricultural systems in Low-Income Countries (LICs) such as agri-food systems can be improved through sustainable logistics to address significant gaps in poverty reduction, food security and climate resilience as small-scale producers make up a majority of those in the low-income regions. This increases malnutrition and economic instability. Sustainable logistics enhances the use of environmentally friendly methods such as digital tracking, solar powered storage and cold chain optimization to minimize waste, cut down on carbon emissions, as well as to improve the resilience of supply chains in the event of shocks such as disasters or a collapse in the market. Aggression strategies such as last-mile delivery using cheap electric vehicles or bicycles, aggregation facilities, and infrastructure investments on rural roads according to resource constraints are important.

title: Taste Work and Evaluative Knowledge: Specialty Coffee and the Production of Discerning Bodies
summary: The sociological analysis of gourmet and high-quality foods is primarily based on three research programs. From the perspective of economic sociology, the value of gourmet goods is inferred from the conventions and practices of the worlds o
content: The sociological analysis of gourmet and high-quality foods is primarily based on three research programs. From the perspective of economic sociology, the value of gourmet goods is inferred from the conventions and practices of the worlds of consumption and production. In contrast, cultural sociology examines gourmet foods as objects of status-related consumption, which indicate the social position and thus the symbolic value of the consumer. Finally, from an ethnomethodological perspective, the application and elaboration of vocabularies of valuation, connoisseurship, and taste are highlighted. We bring these three approaches together around a blind spot they share—taste work and the sensory socialization of customers. Empirically, we draw on field observations of coffee tastings and coffee packaging. Tastings as a form of taste work are based on the explicit linking of sensory experience (tasting the coffee) and discursive communication of evaluation categories. This not only cultivates bodies that are able to taste and evaluate, but also produces the customers on which roasteries depend. Coffee packages work as intermediary objects: they stabilize customers’ expectations and carry the evaluative categories and taste notes of professional tastings into everyday consumption.

title: Urban New-Energy Innovation in China: Spatiotemporal Dynamics, Collaboration Networks, and Associated Factors
summary: New-energy technology innovation is an important driver of the low-carbon energy transition, with increasingly pronounced spatial clustering and inter-city collaboration. Yet the co-evolution of innovation output and collaboration networks
content: New-energy technology innovation is an important driver of the low-carbon energy transition, with increasingly pronounced spatial clustering and inter-city collaboration. Yet the co-evolution of innovation output and collaboration networks and the factors associated with network evolution remain unclear. Using city-level patent data from China for 2020–2024, we combine geospatial analysis, social network analysis, and zero-modified valued exponential random graph models to examine the spatiotemporal patterns, network evolution, and factors associated with collaboration. The results show that urban new-energy innovation output increased from 19,379 to 38,904 patent applications, remaining concentrated in the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, and Bei-jing–Tianjin–Hebei region while gaining strength in central and western China. Intercity collaboration also expanded, with collaboration ties increasing from 502 to 1,227 and collaboration intensity rising, alongside persistent concentration in 1 eastern core cities and growing interregional linkages. Further analysis shows that endogenous network effects and collaboration persistence were consistently positively associated with intercity collaboration. Administrative proximity also showed a strong positive association: the conditional odds of collaboration for city pairs within the same province were 3.14–5.45 times those for cross-province pairs. Technological proximity and the innovation resource base showed significant positive associations in most years, whereas associations with geographical proximity and policy factors varied. These findings provide empirical evidence to inform the spatial configuration of regional innovation and support interregional collaborative innovation.

title: Vintage identification of aged Kinmen Kaoliang liquor using a low-cost multichannel gas-sensor electronic nose and edge machine learning
source: International Conference on Information Technology and Computer Communications (ITCC)
summary: Kinmen Kaoliang liquor is Taiwan's flagship sorghum spirit, holding roughly 80% of the domestic white-spirit market. Its sensory quality and vintage are today described almost exclusively by expert panellists, a subjective and low-throughpu
content: Kinmen Kaoliang liquor is Taiwan's flagship sorghum spirit, holding roughly 80% of the domestic white-spirit market. Its sensory quality and vintage are today described almost exclusively by expert panellists, a subjective and low-throughput process that ordinary consumers cannot reproduce. This study investigates whether an affordable, consumer-grade electronic nose combined with edge machine learning can objectively discriminate the vintage of aged Kinmen Kaoliang liquor. A Grove Multichannel Gas Sensor v2, which simultaneously measures nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), ethanol (C2H5OH) and volatile organic compounds (VOC), was used to sample the headspace of liquors bottled in 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023 at two alcoholic strengths (38% and 58% ABV), together with two non-liquor control substances (American coffee and 75% disinfectant alcohol). A total of 238 ten-second acquisitions were collected through the Edge Impulse tinyML platform, cleaned, calibrated and normalized, and used to train a neural-network classifier. Using maximum-value spectral features, the model reached an overall validation accuracy of 92.1% (per-class F1 scores of 0.84- 0.97), and live classification of randomly selected samples returned similarity scores of 9-10 out of 10. The measured gas signatures showed no monotonic trend with bottling year, which is consistent with the strict process control of the distillery and indicates that each vintage carries a distinct but stable multi-channel fingerprint. Each measurement required only ten seconds, demonstrating that a sub-US$100 electronic nose can serve as a rapid, objective and portable tool for spirit authentication and quality control. Limitations regarding sample size, sensor drift and single-instrument calibration are discussed, and directions for cross-validation against human panels and counterfeit detection are proposed.

title: Energy–Financial Market Linkages: Oil and Global Equity Exposure in Saudi Equities
summary: Saudi Arabia provides a distinctive setting for examining financial resilience during economic diversification and the transition towards a lower-carbon economy. Accordingly, this study examines whether Brent crude oil price changes remain
content: Saudi Arabia provides a distinctive setting for examining financial resilience during economic diversification and the transition towards a lower-carbon economy. Accordingly, this study examines whether Brent crude oil price changes remain associated with Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) returns after global equity conditions are considered, while also assessing asymmetry, structural change, sectoral heterogeneity, and volatility. Using 227 monthly observations from February 2007 to December 2025, the study applies Newey–West HAC regressions using month-end TASI and Brent returns, asymmetric oil-price models, HAC-robust structural-stability tests, sector analysis, lagged robustness tests, and auxiliary GARCH(1, 1) estimation. Developed ex-US returns serve as the principal global benchmark, with the Shiller S&P 500 price series used for sensitivity analysis. Consistent with this design, Brent returns are positively associated with TASI returns unconditionally (β = 0.1998, p < 0.001). After controlling for global equity conditions, the Brent coefficient decreases to 0.1177 but remains significant (p = 0.0066), while the global coefficient remains positive and significant (β = 0.4937, p < 0.001). The full-sample test supports asymmetry, although the finding is sensitive to specification. Global-control candidate-date tests do not reject stability at the 5% level, while oil-only evidence is bandwidth-sensitive. Materials and Energy exhibit positive conditional oil associations, while evidence of sector differences depends on the covariance estimator. Overall, Saudi equities reflect continued oil exposure alongside global equity influence. The findings describe contemporaneous associations rather than causal oil-shock or reform effects, with asymmetry and sector differences requiring qualified interpretation.

title: Impacts of Closures of Critical Maritime Chokepoints on China’s Trade and the Global Supply Chain
summary: China is deeply integrated into global supply chains, yet the dependence of China-related trade on critical maritime chokepoints, and the cascading impacts of their closure, remain unquantified. Here, we combine trade flows, maritime transp
content: China is deeply integrated into global supply chains, yet the dependence of China-related trade on critical maritime chokepoints, and the cascading impacts of their closure, remain unquantified. Here, we combine trade flows, maritime transport networks and multi-regional input–output linkages to assess closures at ten major maritime chokepoints. We find that closures of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal would substantially increase shipping costs and reduce trade flows, whereas closures of the Strait of Hormuz and the Bosporus Strait would interrupt trade because no viable alternative routes exist. These direct effects propagate through global supply chains: through backward and forward production linkages, every USD 1 of disrupted trade is associated with approximately USD 4.7 of gross output worldwide. Import disruptions propagate mainly upstream, with economies outside China bearing a disproportionate share of the effects. Export disruptions, in contrast, generate larger effects within China because export production is closely tied to domestic industries. Our results indicate that resilience strategies should focus on reducing closure probability and duration, while distinguishing between import- and export-side risks, to safeguard China-related trade and strengthen global supply-chain resilience.

title: Pricing and Carbon-Reduction Decisions in a Subsidized Steel Slag Road-Material Supply Chain: A Stackelberg Game Approach
summary: Road infrastructure is a carbon-intensive segment of the transport sector, while steel slag remains substantially underutilized despite its potential to substitute natural aggregates and reduce emissions. Distorted pricing, spatial transpor
content: Road infrastructure is a carbon-intensive segment of the transport sector, while steel slag remains substantially underutilized despite its potential to substitute natural aggregates and reduce emissions. Distorted pricing, spatial transport costs, and information asymmetry constrain its large-scale deployment. This study develops a government-subsidized two-echelon Stackelberg game comprising a steel producer as the leader and a road contractor as the follower. The carbon-reduction coefficient is calibrated using published life-cycle assessment results, yielding approximately 2.18 kg CO2e per tonne of steel slag. Equilibrium pricing, procurement, carbon reduction, supply chain profits, and social welfare are derived under no-subsidy and per-unit-subsidy regimes, and the model is extended to an incomplete-information setting with Bayesian conjugate learning. The results show that a per-unit subsidy simultaneously raises the equilibrium steel slag price and procurement quantity, with gains shared between upstream and downstream firms but disproportionately favoring the leader. The subsidy enhances carbon reduction and extends the economically viable transport radius, and the economic critical distance is close to the LCA-based environmental critical distance. Carbon price and technology adaptation cost substantially moderate subsidy effectiveness. When environmental value is fully internalized through carbon markets, the welfare-maximizing subsidy may be small or even negative; when carbon markets are incomplete, subsidies remain a necessary corrective instrument. Under incomplete information, an initial overestimation of hidden costs suppresses procurement and abatement, but Bayesian learning converges to the complete-information equilibrium within about 5–10 periods, reducing belief variance by approximately 96.9%. These findings provide a quantitative framework for designing subsidy, carbon-pricing, information-disclosure, and supply chain coordination policies for low-carbon road materials.

title: Determinants of trade in renewable energy equipment: an extended gravity model for Belt and Road countries
summary: International trade in renewable energy equipment plays an important role in the diffusion of technologies supporting the global energy transition, yet the economic, energy-sector, and institutional factors associated with this trade across
content: International trade in renewable energy equipment plays an important role in the diffusion of technologies supporting the global energy transition, yet the economic, energy-sector, and institutional factors associated with this trade across Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) countries remain insufficiently examined. This study investigates China’s exports of renewable energy equipment to 63 BRI countries over 2010–2019 using an extended gravity model that combines conventional economic and geographical determinants with renewable energy capacity indicators and measures of institutional integration. The panel was compiled from UN Comtrade, World Bank, and IRENA data. Specification tests support a random-effects estimator (Breusch–Pagan LM χ 2 (1) = 849.2, p < 0.001; Hausman χ 2 (5) = 6.09, p = 0.297; Mundlak χ 2 (5) = 3.99, p = 0.551; N = 536). Geographical distance is negatively associated with exports (elasticity −1.42), while importer GDP per capita (1.21), population (1.11), and annual renewable capacity additions in partner countries (0.05) are positively associated with export values. WTO membership is conditionally associated with exports that are about 63% higher, other factors held constant, and this association is robust to cluster-robust and Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, PPML estimation, alternative estimation windows, and identification from accessions alone; SCO and APEC membership show no statistically significant association. China’s installed renewable capacity is not separately identified from the common time trend of exports. A supplementary, descriptive comparison of actual and model-predicted trade for 2021–2023 identifies substantial cross-country differences in unrealized export potential, including for Kazakhstan and other Central Asian economies. The results indicate that renewable energy equipment trade is associated not only with conventional gravity factors but also with the expansion of destination renewable energy markets and the multilateral institutional conditions governing trade.

title: Coupling NO Activation with CO–Driven Site Regeneration: Oxygen-Tolerant CO-SCR over Ru–Pt/Al2O3 Catalysts
summary: Low-temperature CO-assisted selective catalytic reduction of NOx under oxygen-rich conditions remains limited by competitive CO oxidation, oxygen-induced active-site blocking, and the high noble-metal demand of conventional Pt-based catalys
content: Low-temperature CO-assisted selective catalytic reduction of NOx under oxygen-rich conditions remains limited by competitive CO oxidation, oxygen-induced active-site blocking, and the high noble-metal demand of conventional Pt-based catalysts. Here, a Ru@Pt/Al2O3 catalyst comprising partially alloyed Pt–Ru nanoparticles was developed to couple efficient NO activation with rapid regeneration of oxygen-covered active sites. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization, temperature-programmed measurements, kinetic analysis, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the Ru@Pt interfacial interaction modifies the electronic structure of the surface Pt sites, shifts the d-band center, and optimizes the adsorption energies of NO*, CO*, and O* intermediates. The partially alloyed architecture consequently enhances low-temperature NOx conversion and N2 selectivity (95% NOx conversion at 179 °C; 88–89% N2 selectivity between 179 and 210 °C) over a broad operating window while improving resistance to oxidative deactivation under lean conditions. This behavior is attributed to the combined effects of an electronically modified Ru-enriched shell region, uniform nanoparticle dispersion, porous Al2O3 support architecture, and rapid interfacial redox cycling. The Ru@Pt interface promotes NO activation while CO facilitates the removal of adsorbed oxygen species, thereby continuously regenerating catalytically accessible sites. The reported activation free-energy barriers on Ru@Pt/Al2O3 are 0.70 eV for NO dissociation and 0.64 eV for CO-mediated oxygen removal, compared with 1.16 and 1.57 eV on Pt and 0.88 and 1.79 eV on Ru, respectively. N-assisted NO reduction has a lower barrier than direct N–N recombination on all three surfaces, supporting a proposed sequence of NO activation, N2 formation, and CO-assisted site regeneration. Compared with conventional monometallic or randomly distributed bimetallic catalysts, the Ru@Pt configuration provides a confined interfacial environment that simultaneously regulates intermediate adsorption, suppresses oxygen poisoning, and reduces excessive Pt utilization. These findings establish Ru@Pt/Al2O3 as a promising oxygen-tolerant catalyst for low-temperature de-NOx applications in lean-burn exhaust purification.

title: The permanence paradox in forest carbon markets: Institutional risk transmission and financial exposure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository provides the supplementary materials and computational reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript entitled “The Permanence Paradox in Forest Carbon Markets: Institutional Risk Transmission and Financial Exposure.” T
content: This repository provides the supplementary materials and computational reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript entitled “The Permanence Paradox in Forest Carbon Markets: Institutional Risk Transmission and Financial Exposure.” The package includes supplementary materials (S1–S12), structured evidence datasets, critical appraisal records, claim–evidence mapping, thematic coding protocols, AI-assisted review documentation, financial exposure scenarios, executable Python scripts, a Jupyter Notebook, and computational validation results. These materials support the development of the Carbon Integrity Resilience (CIR) framework and illustrate how ecological disturbances, institutional recognition, compensation mechanisms, and contractual liability allocation shape financial exposure in forest carbon markets. The repository facilitates methodological transparency, evidence traceability, independent examination, and reproducibility of the documented computational analyses.

title: How third-party assurance changes corporate emissions reporting and firm behavior
summary: Mandatory third-party assurance of corporate emissions is spreading, but it is unclear whether verification changes emissions themselves or only the figures firms report. We estimate the causal effect of third-party verification of corporat
content: Mandatory third-party assurance of corporate emissions is spreading, but it is unclear whether verification changes emissions themselves or only the figures firms report. We estimate the causal effect of third-party verification of corporate emissions using staggered adoption among CDP-reporting firms from 2018 to 2025. Verification produces two distinct effects on how firms report and how they operate. A reporting effect appears immediately in the extensive and intensive margins of Scope 3 value-chain categories, changing category coverage and reported emissions. A behavioral effect operates through Scope 1, as emissions fall gradually in the years after adoption, driven by a shift away from fuel consumption. Scope 2 emissions, both location-based and market-based, show no robust change. These findings suggest that third-party verification can improve emissions inventories, influence subsequent operational decisions and guide the design of mandatory assurance requirements for corporate climate reporting.

title: Sources of ore-forming fluids and components of calcite, barite, and fluorite deposits in the Changyang–Songzi area, Hubei Province, central China: constraints from fluid inclusions and H–O–C–S isotopes
summary: The Changyang-Songzi area, southwestern Hubei Province, central China, hosts numerous carbonate-hosted calcite, barite, and fluorite deposits, but the sources of their ore-forming fluids and components remain poorly constrained. We report f
content: The Changyang-Songzi area, southwestern Hubei Province, central China, hosts numerous carbonate-hosted calcite, barite, and fluorite deposits, but the sources of their ore-forming fluids and components remain poorly constrained. We report fluid inclusion microthermometry and H–O–C–S isotope data for these deposits. The results show that two-phase aqueous (liquid + vapor) inclusions homogenize at 127 °C–239 °C (sample means 149 °C–197 °C) and have salinities of 8.7–23.2 wt% NaCl equiv. Barite-hosted inclusions record the hottest and most saline fluids (sample means 177 °C–197 °C and 17.1–18.5 wt%), fluorite-hosted inclusions the coolest and least saline (149 °C–165 °C and 11.9–12.3 wt%), and calcite-hosted inclusions intermediate values. Inclusion water in calcite and barite (δ 18 O = +1.3‰ to +11.5‰; δD = −70‰ to −52‰) is strongly 18 O-shifted relative to the meteoric water line, as is typical of evolved basinal brines, consistent with water calculated to be in equilibrium with the mineral grains (+7.0‰ to +9.1‰), whereas inclusion water in fluorite (δ 18 O = −11.2‰ to −8.9‰; δD = −49‰ to −42‰) plots close to the meteoric water line, indicating a larger share of little-evolved meteoric-derived water. Barite δ 34 S values (+31.7‰ to +35.1‰) match Cambrian–Early Ordovician seawater sulfate, consistent with sulfate derived from marine evaporites, and calcite δ 13 C values (−8.8‰ to −0.8‰) indicate carbon derived mainly from marine carbonate wall rocks with a variable organic contribution. We infer that saline basinal brines, which probably acquired Ba, F, and sulfate from Ediacaran–Cambrian strata, ascended along faults and deposited barite, fluorite, and calcite in NW-trending fractures as they cooled and mixed with dilute meteoric-derived water. The deposits are best classified as fault-controlled, carbonate-hosted hydrothermal vein deposits comparable to the Ba–F and Mississippi Valley-type (MVT) Pb–Zn deposits of the western Hubei–western Hunan–eastern Guizhou region. NW-trending faults that cut Lower Ordovician limestones (barite–fluorite) and Upper Cambrian dolostones (calcite) above Lower Cambrian black shales and evaporite-bearing strata are the most prospective targets. Fluid inclusion homogenization temperatures of ∼150 °C–200 °C, salinities of ∼12–19 wt% NaCl equiv. and barite δ 34 S values of +31‰ to +35‰ provide practical exploration criteria.

title: The Digital Paradox: Why Does the Digitalisation of Industries in Western China Suppress China-Malaysia Trade?
source: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
summary: This study investigates whether industrial digitalisation in western China promotes or paradoxically inhibits China-Malaysia bilateral trade, and examines the mediating role of government digital attention. Using panel data (2013-2023) from
content: This study investigates whether industrial digitalisation in western China promotes or paradoxically inhibits China-Malaysia bilateral trade, and examines the mediating role of government digital attention. Using panel data (2013-2023) from four western Chinese provinces (Chongqing, Guizhou, Guangxi and Yunnan), Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) is employed to test a moderated mediation model. Results reveal a significant “digital paradox”: whilst digital industrialisation promotes trade, industrial digitalisation exerts a considerable negative effect on bilateral flows. Government digital attention positively moderates the innovation-to-digitalisation relationship, generating a net beneficial synergistic effect. The small sample size (41 observations) and provincial-level aggregation limit generalisability. Future research should extend to firm-level data and additional ASEAN partners. Policymakers should prioritise digital industrialisation over mere process digitisation, establish China-ASEAN digital trade pilot zones, and harmonise cross-border data governance to convert efficiency gains into trade expansion. This research offers theoretical perspective on digital trade friction by demonstrating that digitalisation can reduce trade when institutional coordination lags and regional competitiveness restructuring occurs.
