title: AI-Mediated Care-Washing: Discourse, Cognition, and Dual-Layer Decoupling in China’s Elderly Companion Product Sector
source: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
summary: This study examines how enterprises in China’s AI companion product sector publicly construct their products as legitimate care solutions for elderly users, and whether practitioners privately understand that discourse’s relationship to com
content: This study examines how enterprises in China’s AI companion product sector publicly construct their products as legitimate care solutions for elderly users, and whether practitioners privately understand that discourse’s relationship to commercial and technical realities. A two-phase sequential qualitative design was employed. Study 1 conducted qualitative content analysis of twelve enterprise-affiliated texts through hybrid deductive-inductive coding; Study 2 conducted semi-structured interviews with eight practitioners in mainland China and Hong Kong, analyzed through thematic analysis. Study 1 identified two discourse patterns: emotional equivalence claims constructing AI interaction as equivalent to human companionship, and vulnerability erasure replacing elderly vulnerability with technological empowerment. Study 2 found that practitioners acknowledged a gap between promotional claims and technical capability, maintained different communicative registers for internal and external audiences, and were privately aware of the vulnerability enterprise discourse suppresses. This study proposes AI-mediated care-washing as a dual-layer decoupling construct extending care-washing theory, contributes to institutional decoupling theory by documenting communicative register bifurcation, and advances vulnerable consumer research by identifying filial obligation as the mechanism converting elderly vulnerability into purchasing behaviour.

title: The Digital-Green Development Nexus: Integrating Technological Transformation, Clean Energy, and Sustainable Industrialization
summary: Twentieth-century catch-up industrialization relied on cheap fossil electricity, high energy intensity, and delayed environmental cleanup. That sequential pathway is now structurally foreclosed by tightening carbon border regimes, falling r
content: Twentieth-century catch-up industrialization relied on cheap fossil electricity, high energy intensity, and delayed environmental cleanup. That sequential pathway is now structurally foreclosed by tightening carbon border regimes, falling renewable and storage costs, and AI-driven global manufacturing standards. Drawing on eleven live empirical datasets across twenty-four economies (2000–2025)—spanning World Bank WDI manufacturing, high-tech export, R&D, and energy-intensity series alongside Ember/OWID grid carbon-intensity and low-carbon electricity data—this monograph exposes a stark Twin-Transition Asymmetry. Clean-grid developing economies (Ethiopia at 100% low-carbon power, Kenya at 90%, Brazil at 89%, Chile at 66%) remain under-industrialized, while fast-growing manufacturing hubs (China, Vietnam, Malaysia, India, Indonesia, Bangladesh) remain heavily exposed to coal-and-gas grids (461–696 gCO2/kWh) and imminent carbon-border trade barriers. Operationalizing a Polycrisis Resilience and Intersectional Engineering framework, this study synthesizes how digital intelligence and clean energy co-evolve to drive sustainable industrialization. It evaluates AI-enabled smart grids, factory digital twins, Digital Product Passports, green-electron eco-industrial parks, circular bio-economy IoT, and dual-use regional clean-tech manufacturing—while auditing digital energy rebound, unmanaged AI data-center loads, and green-protectionist exclusion. Scenario modeling to 2050 indicates that synchronized digital-green leapfrogging lifts emerging-market carbon-adjusted manufacturing productivity to 268 (2024=100), compared with 158 under fragmented efficiency and 89 under carbon lock-in and polycrisis erosion. Series: Optimizing Humanity's Outlook This Century (No. 46) · Institution: H Heuristics · ORCID: 0009-0002-6161-9387

title: GREEN ECONOMY IN ECONOMIC THOUGHT: ORIGINS, FRAMEWORKS, AND DEBATES
summary: Purpose of the Research.The article aims to trace the conceptual lineage of the green economy -from Pigou's theory of externalities and Georgescu-Roegen's thermodynamic critique to current debates over decoupling and post-growth thinking an
content: Purpose of the Research.The article aims to trace the conceptual lineage of the green economy -from Pigou's theory of externalities and Georgescu-Roegen's thermodynamic critique to current debates over decoupling and post-growth thinking and to provide a critical appraisal of the principal policy instruments advanced under this framework, evaluating their theoretical coherence and empirical track record. Methodology of the Research.The study employs a systematic literature review and criticalanalytical methodology, synthesising seminal theoretical works, peer-reviewed empirical studies, institutional reports, and policy documents.Comparative case study analysis (EU, Costa Rica, China, Nordic countries) is used to assess real-world policy outcomes.The author integrates insights from neoclassical welfare economics, ecological economics, and post-Keynesian macroeconomics to construct a multi-framework assessment. Applied Significance of the Research.The research offers policymakers, economists, and development practitioners a structured guide to the strengths and limitations of green economy instruments -carbon pricing, green public investment, and nature-based finance -enabling more informed design of sustainability transitions. Results of the Research.The research finds that: (1) the EU ETS, Nordic carbon taxes, and China's renewable energy industrialisation demonstrate that policy can drive meaningful decarbonisation; (2) absolute decoupling of material throughput from GDP growth has not been achieved at the required scale; (3) carbon pricing is regressive without careful revenue recycling; (4) nature-based finance instruments are theoretically contested and empirically mixed; and (5) justice and political economy dimensions remain insufficiently addressed in mainstream green economy discourse.Originality and Scientific Novelty of the Research.The article's originality lies in its integrative approach: rather than advocating for one theoretical school, it positions the green economy as a productively contested field and maps the full spectrum of analytical traditionsfrom Pigouvian welfare economics to degrowth -within a unified critical framework.

title: De novo production of pelargonidin 3-O-glucoside from glucose by metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli
summary: Anthocyanins are natural colorants responsible for the diverse, vibrant hues of many fruits and flowers, and are valued for health-promoting effects including antioxidant, anticancer, anti-diabetic, and anti-inflammatory activities. However
content: Anthocyanins are natural colorants responsible for the diverse, vibrant hues of many fruits and flowers, and are valued for health-promoting effects including antioxidant, anticancer, anti-diabetic, and anti-inflammatory activities. However, low yields from direct extraction of natural sources have limited commercial-scale production. To address this, metabolic engineering of model microorganisms has been explored for anthocyanin biosynthesis, but production levels still fall short of industrial demand. Here, we report the development of engineered Escherichia coli strains capable of efficiently producing pelargonidin 3- O -glucoside (P3G) from glucose. Through selection of superior enzyme candidates, gene expression optimization, and pathway modularization and optimization, the engineered E. coli strain produced 3.0 mg/L P3G from L-tyrosine in shake flask culture. Notably, 1.4 mg/L P3G was also achieved from glucose alone, demonstrating the strain’s capability for complete de novo biosynthesis without exogenous precursor supplementation. This work demonstrates that E. coli can serve as an efficient microbial cell factory for the one-step, de novo biosynthesis of anthocyanins from simple carbon sources, providing a scalable and sustainable alternative to the conventional plant-based extraction.

title: Challenging the balance of power: The imposing capacity of social movements in climate and environmental justice struggles
summary: Studies of climate and environmental movements have largely relied on media reporting as a proxy for political influence, yet this proxy cannot account for how movements interfere with the vested economic interests that underpin the existin
content: Studies of climate and environmental movements have largely relied on media reporting as a proxy for political influence, yet this proxy cannot account for how movements interfere with the vested economic interests that underpin the existing balance of power. Starting from the premise that movements have been learning to strategise beyond particular issues and sites of struggle, we develop a framework that conceptualises a set of advanced aspects of movement strength as what we call imposing capacity. This term refers to the strategic and organisational capacity to limit the terrain of struggle and persistently shape it without being contained or fully repressed. Imposing capacity sits at the boundary between what is currently empirically observable and what history has shown to be possible. The framework draws on dynamics of contention theory and Marxist perspectives on social movements and enables empirical analysis of movement strength at the meso level of society. It treats the balance of power as dynamic rather than fixed: a contingent outcome of conflict between social movements from above and below. Applying the framework to study imposing capacity across contexts allows for sharper theorisations of movement struggle and of its possible role in larger-scale transformation in the environmental justice and degrowth literatures.

title: Microplastic accumulation in blue carbon ecosystems and its potential consequences for carbon sequestration and climate policy
summary: Blue Carbon Ecosystems (BCEs) sit at the receiving end of land-based plastic inputs, and the same trapping that builds these stores also concentrates microplastics (MPs). In this synthesis of 196 sources, vegetated coastal sediments hold ab
content: Blue Carbon Ecosystems (BCEs) sit at the receiving end of land-based plastic inputs, and the same trapping that builds these stores also concentrates microplastics (MPs). In this synthesis of 196 sources, vegetated coastal sediments hold about 1.7 times, and locally up to 8.5 times, as many particles as adjacent bare substrates. Reported abundances span 15 to 12,852 items kg⁻¹ dry sediment in mangroves and 17.7 to 1,000 items kg⁻¹ in seagrass sediments, with 0.75 to 4.25 items blade⁻¹ on seagrass leaves. We organised the evidence around three pathways by which MPs could reduce sequestration: light attenuation at leaf and thallus surfaces, which lowers photosynthetic carbon fixation; changes in sediment bulk density, porosity and redox, which govern whether buried carbon is remineralised; and restructuring of rhizosphere and sediment microbial communities, which sets decomposition rates. Evidence is strongest for particle retention and for microbially mediated carbon loss in microcosms, where microplastics with nitrogen raised seagrass soil CO₂ efflux by 195%. It is weakest where accounting needs it, since no field study has linked MP loading to a measured change in carbon burial. The relationship is mechanistically supported but not yet quantified in situ, and field validation is the central research priority. Two precautionary steps are nonetheless warranted. MP load should be reported as a site-condition variable in blue carbon measurement, reporting and verification under the 2013 IPCC Wetlands Supplement, so that it enters Nationally Determined Contribution accounting. It should also become a site-selection and permanence-risk criterion in blue carbon crediting standards and in the Global Plastics Treaty monitoring provisions.

title: Green Hydrogen Corridors, Value Capture, and SDG Trade-offs in the Global South
summary: Background. Green hydrogen is promoted as an export commodity for the Global South, yet analyses rarely examine how its economic rents are divided among host states, foreign developers and importing offtakers. Objective. We ask whether expo
content: Background. Green hydrogen is promoted as an export commodity for the Global South, yet analyses rarely examine how its economic rents are divided among host states, foreign developers and importing offtakers. Objective. We ask whether export corridors enable sustainable industrialisation or reproduce resource dependence. Method. A comparative multiple-case design covers six corridors (Morocco, Egypt, Namibia, the Gulf, India and Chile/Latin America) using public evidence graded in four tiers to November 2026. A six-rent taxonomy and a six-dimension, 0–3 host-capture scorecard are tested against five hypotheses derived from FDI theory, MNC bargaining, global value chain governance and institutional theory. Robustness is assessed with four weighting schemes, leave-one-dimension-out analysis and a 10,000-run score-perturbation simulation. Results. Green ammonia prices observed in India’s auctions carry premiums of 11–44% over grey ammonia, and the 2024 H2Global tender settled 124% above it; bankability depends on aggregated or long-term buyers, while about 78 African projects lack firm offtake. India (13 of 18 points) and the Gulf (11) lead. India ranks first under all four weighting schemes and in 93% of perturbation runs (80% without ties); the order of the middle tier depends on weighting. Conclusions. Host capture is associated with state demand aggregation, equity and domestic use rather than resource quality. Corridors advance SDGs 7, 9 and 13 but risk costs to SDGs 10 and 17 where exports remain molecule-only enclaves. We offer stakeholder guidance and testable propositions for empirical follow-up. JEL CLASSIFICATION: F23; O13; Q42; Q56

title: Posted-Price Parity of Certified Green Building Materials Under Taiwan’s Mandatory Usage-Rate Regime: An Exploratory Case Study of Three Suppliers’ List Prices and Quotations
summary: Green building material (GBM) certification is intended to reduce information asymmetry, but its price effect under mandatory-use rules is unclear. This exploratory multi-material case study examined whether Taiwan’s GBM label was associate
content: Green building material (GBM) certification is intended to reduce information asymmetry, but its price effect under mandatory-use rules is unclear. This exploratory multi-material case study examined whether Taiwan’s GBM label was associated with posted price differentials in the list prices and quotations of three purposively selected suppliers. Tiles (primary evidence): for recycled-label ceramic tiles counted toward the usage-rate requirement (206 stock-keeping units), 27 of 28 within-series matched pairs had identical list prices; the cross-sectional hedonic label premium was −0.95% (90% confidence interval: −4.02% to 2.26%), against quality-grade premiums of 11.0–60.3%, whereas a series fixed-effects model gave +2.75% (0.11% to 5.49%), consistent with selective certification of larger formats. Concrete (descriptive only): recycled-label low-carbon concrete, which is not counted toward the requirement, was priced identically to Portland cement concrete under a supplier-set promotional quotation. Coatings (exploratory): healthy-label coatings with recycled silica powder, also counted toward the requirement, were not priced higher. No substantial label premium was found in these suppliers’ listed prices and promotional quotations; this posted-price parity does not imply transaction-price or total procurement-cost parity and cannot be extrapolated to the Taiwan market. The design cannot distinguish a pooling equilibrium from low certification costs, input-cost savings, uniform pricing, or buyer indifference.

title: Electrochemical Discharge of End-of-Life Lithium-Ion Batteries in Organic Electrolyte for Safe Recycling
summary: The growing demand for electric vehicles is increasing the production and use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), leading to a higher volume of end-of-life cells entering recycling plants. Current European Union regulations require high recove
content: The growing demand for electric vehicles is increasing the production and use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), leading to a higher volume of end-of-life cells entering recycling plants. Current European Union regulations require high recovery rates of critical raw materials (Ni, Co, Mn, Li), which necessitate safe, scalable battery discharge. Electrochemical discharge, achieved by immersing cells in a conductive electrolyte, is attractive because it is easily scalable and largely independent of cell design. However, early aqueous approaches using sodium chloride resulted in severe battery casing corrosion and the evolution of hydrogen and oxygen gases. To overcome these issues, we explore the use of a nonaqueous redox medium for the first time. Using manganese acetylacetonate (Mn(acac)3) and tetrabutylammonium tetrafluoroborate (TBA-BF4) in propylene carbonate (PC), the cell was discharged to 1.5 V and rebounded to 2.3 V within the safe limit for industrial battery crushing processing for recycling. The organic electrolyte extracted 59% of the nominal energy, comparable to the value obtained from potassium carbonate salt (best known) in an aqueous medium. Postdischarge analysis showed intact ligands, indicating that the redox mediator remained in solution and there were no signs of corrosion or damage to the battery casing. Therefore, this is a promising alternative for large-scale battery discharge in industry.

title: Acrylamide and Endocrine–Metabolic Disruption: Evidence from Human and Animal Studies – A Narrative Review
summary: Purpose of the review This review compiles and analyzes the scientific evidence of the effects of acrylamide on the endocrine system in animals and humans. We review the potential pathways of exposure, metabolism, mechanisms of action, and
content: Purpose of the review This review compiles and analyzes the scientific evidence of the effects of acrylamide on the endocrine system in animals and humans. We review the potential pathways of exposure, metabolism, mechanisms of action, and metabolic implications. Recent findings Acrylamide affects the endocrine and reproductive systems and is correlated with changes in sex hormones, puberty and menopause. In addition, maternal acrylamide exposure can affect the endocrine and metabolic features of offspring. Therefore, direct or indirect acrylamide exposure can interfere with sex hormones, thyroid function and glycemic homeostasis, with potential implications for infertility, thyroid tumors and the development of metabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes and obesity. Summary Acrylamide, a toxic compound present in many foods, affects redox balance and cellular processes, such as signaling pathways, and induces neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity and genotoxic effects. These effects are associated with oxidative stress, DNA damage and protein dysfunction, and affect physiological systems, such as the endocrine system.

title: Beyond Disclosure: Board Gender Diversity, Climate Risk Communication, and Environmental Performance
summary: In this study, we examine the intersection of corporate governance and sustainability by investigating how women's representation on corporate boards influences firms' climate risk disclosure. Employing textual analysis, we find that firms
content: In this study, we examine the intersection of corporate governance and sustainability by investigating how women's representation on corporate boards influences firms' climate risk disclosure. Employing textual analysis, we find that firms with greater female representation on their boards have significantly lower volume but higher quality of climate risk‐related disclosure in their regulatory filings. This relationship is reinforced using a quasi‐natural experiment based on California Senate Bill No. 826 (2018), which mandates female board representation. Further analysis reveals that the reduction in extensive climate‐related disclosures stems from superior environmental performance, rather than from information withholding or greenwashing. Overall, our findings highlight the influence of board composition on climate risk communication and the critical role of gender diversity in enhancing the clarity, credibility, and effectiveness of such disclosures.

title: Bamboo as a sustainable alternative to plastic in a drip irrigation system
summary: Bamboo’s potential as an alternative to polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is primarily for use in pipes in drip irrigation systems. From a sustainability perspective, this research investigates the environmental benefits of bamboo relative to plasti
content: Bamboo’s potential as an alternative to polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is primarily for use in pipes in drip irrigation systems. From a sustainability perspective, this research investigates the environmental benefits of bamboo relative to plastics. Compared with PVC, which causes contamination such as soil degradation and water pollution, bamboo can be an alternative; compared with other materials, it might be lighter, and its compressive strength is excellent. Therefore, it could become a sustainable material for various uses in the future, primarily in construction and farming, given its large market. Some countries, such as China, India, and Ghana, have been pushing its adoption globally. This study compares bamboo’s performance with plastic and examines the technical traits that make bamboo suitable for irrigation systems. Several challenges appear during field trials, such as rough inner surfaces and uneven diameters. However, when pre-treatment and proper maintenance are emphasised, bamboo has been shown to hold its own in both urban and rural settings. During the field trial, leaks were discovered in most union accessories. On the other hand, in the laboratory, the bamboo tube achieved pressures around 30 PSI. While hydraulic performance was between 75 and 85 per cent, it was not far from PVC's. Bamboo presents an alternative in zones where it grows abundantly; it’s an ecological choice with a reduced carbon footprint.

title: Mitigating Lahore's Urban Heat Island: Satellite Derived Thermal Stress Assessment, Priority Urban Forestry Zoning, and Climate Adaptive Species Planning
summary: Replacing irrigated farmland and riverine woodland with paved surfaces has intensified the surface urban heat island (SUHI) across Lahore, Pakistan, increasing heat exposure during pre-monsoon summer months (Nasar-U-Minallah et al., 2023; S
content: Replacing irrigated farmland and riverine woodland with paved surfaces has intensified the surface urban heat island (SUHI) across Lahore, Pakistan, increasing heat exposure during pre-monsoon summer months (Nasar-U-Minallah et al., 2023; Shah et al., 2026). Most satellite thermal studies of Lahore track historical warming without turning pixel-level temperature patterns into priority planting maps or checking whether proposed trees fit local soils, groundwater decline, and forest regulations. In this study, Landsat 9 Collection 2 Level-2 thermal (TIRS-2) and optical (OLI-2) imagery from June 15, 2026 (LC09_L2SP_149038_20260615_20260617_02_T1; 30 m resolution; WGS 1984 UTM Zone 43N / EPSG:32643) was processed in ArcGIS Pro to map Land Surface Temperature (LST), the Urban Thermal Field Variance Index (UTFVI), and a five-class Urban Forestry Priority Zoning raster across the full WRS-2 Path 149 / Row 038 Lahore-Ravi alluvial plain (34,089.30 km²; 37,876,999 valid pixels). Cleaned scene-wide LST averaged 38.43 °C (standard deviation 8.75 °C), separating built-up cores exceeding 47 °C from cooler refugia over the Ravi River (27.57 °C sampled pixel, >19 °C cooler) and Shahdara Reserve Forest (33.99 °C sampled interior pixel, >13 °C cooler, with canopy cores at ≤32 °C). A calibration check of the raster equations identified two scaling sensitivities that are reported transparently: computing NDVI on unscaled Landsat Collection 2 surface reflectance digital numbers compresses canopy NDVI toward 0.14-0.20 (explaining why Shahdara Reserve Forest initially registered 0.144 before temperature-assisted correction restored it to the protected green class), and evaluating UTFVI with a degrees-Celsius mean denominator (38.4263 °C) instead of Kelvin (311.5763 K) amplifies positive UTFVI ratios by 8.11 times. Across the full analyzed scene, 3,015.58 km² (8.85%) fall in Priority 1 (Critical Planting Zone, LST > 47 °C) and 8,222.77 km² (24.12%) in Priority 2 (High Planting Need, 42-47 °C), while 10,486.34 km² (30.76%) represent existing cool green cover requiring protection. Linking these spatial zones with Lahore's hot semi-arid (BSh) climate normals, alkaline calcareous soils (pH 7.2-8.4), declining groundwater levels (0.78-1.0 m/year), and high particulate loads yields a tiered native urban forestry strategy built around Azadirachta indica, Pongamia pinnata, and Cassia fistula, expanded with Terminalia arjuna, Ficus religiosa, Ficus benghalensis, Ficus virens, Syzygium cumini, Vachellia nilotica, and mixed-stand Dalbergia sissoo, paired with phased replacement of maladapted or invasive exotics (Broussonetia papyrifera, Eucalyptus camaldulensis, Prosopis juliflora, and monoculture Conocarpus erectus) in line with Lahore's 2024 Green Master Plan and Punjab's 2025 Forest Act amendments.

title: AI‑generated advertising and the trust deficit: a qualitative exploration of authenticity, empathy, and resistance among Bangladeshi consumers
source: Journal of Intelligent Digital Media and Communication
summary: Existing research has examined consumer responses to AI-generated advertising across individual dimensions such as trust, authenticity, product involvement, and brand value, but their combined interpretation in emerging-market contexts rema
content: Existing research has examined consumer responses to AI-generated advertising across individual dimensions such as trust, authenticity, product involvement, and brand value, but their combined interpretation in emerging-market contexts remains insufficiently understood. This study also explores the influencing factors affecting perception and behavioural outcomes through the lens of the Consumer Perception and Response to AI Advertising Framework (CPRAIF). A qualitative research design was employed. Data were collected through 22 semi-structured interviews with Bangladeshi consumers recruited using purposive and snowball sampling and analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. The findings indicate that participants are reluctant to adopt AI advertisements, although this differs according to brand value, product involvement, and AI literacy among the participants. Furthermore, respondents appreciate the human-assisted advertisements, and they are unable to connect emotionally with AI-generated advertisements. Because of information utility, unrealistic visual elements, and poor production quality, respondents are reluctant to AI-generated advertisements. Moreover, they are concerned about environmental and ethical issues. In general, respondents oppose AI-generated ads more than they oppose artificial intelligence itself. Their acceptance depends on whether they think the use of artificial intelligence is helpful, realistic, and clear and has proper help from humans.

title: Entrepreneurship, Technology, Sustainable Practices in The Bioeconomic Transition of Southeast Asia: A Systematic Literature Review of Empirical Studies for Furniture Producer
source: Drewno Prace Naukowe Doniesienia Komunikaty = Wood Research Papers Reports Announcements
summary: This research investigates the prospects of furniture producers in the context of the bioeconomic transition, focusing on Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia). As the global economy increasingly shifts towards sustainable pract
content: This research investigates the prospects of furniture producers in the context of the bioeconomic transition, focusing on Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia). As the global economy increasingly shifts towards sustainable practices and technological advances, furniture producers must be resilient in facing these increasingly rapid and diverse changes. This paper presented a combination of a bibliometric analysis approach and a systematic literature review of empirical studies utilising the PRISMA analysis framework to synthesise existing knowledge on the dimensions encountered by furniture industries and their strategic responses during the bioeconomic transition. This bibliometric study analyses the evolving landscape of entrepreneurship, technology, and sustainable practices by furniture producers in the evolving global bioeconomic transition. A systematic literature review was conducted using the PRISMA analysis framework to examine the challenges encountered by Southeast Asian furniture industries, emphasising the importance of entrepreneurial aspects in the bioeconomic transition and the necessity for further research on political strategies. There is a knowledge gap in technology, particularly in the innovation of new materials from biological sources and technologies for commercialisation to enhance efficiency in the bioeconomic shift, with an emphasis on sustainable practices to promote sustainable consumption habits among manufacturers. The analysis points out the changing connection among entrepreneurship, technology, and sustainable practices in the furniture domain, emphasising the critical role of collaboration for ecological and economic resilience.

title: Short- and long-term effects of exchange rates on CO2 emissions
summary: We investigated the effects of exchange rate movements on CO2 emissions in a Global Vector Autoregressive model. We constructed a model of the world economy and international CO2 emissions using 34 economies, equivalent to 77% of the world
content: We investigated the effects of exchange rate movements on CO2 emissions in a Global Vector Autoregressive model. We constructed a model of the world economy and international CO2 emissions using 34 economies, equivalent to 77% of the world GDP and 80% of world CO2 emissions. Our analysis concentrated on six major CO2 emitters (China, the U.S., India, Russia, Japan, and Germany). Our findings are: (i) a domestic currency depreciation is related to increasing CO2 emissions; (ii) exchange rates are associated with CO2 through industrial production and stock markets; (iii) fluctuations in exchange rates are associated with changes in CO2 emissions in the long term; (iv) the U.S. dollar is related to international CO2 emissions (spillover effect); (v) changes in trade integration are associated with changes in the relationship between exchange rates and CO2, but the effect is small. An SVAR model for the U.S. provided additional evidence for the link between the exchange rate and carbon emissions. Finally, the responses of carbon emissions in Germany and Russia to exchange rate shocks lose statistical significance when using the producer price index to deflate their variables. These results indicate linkages between exchange rates and economic and environmental variables in the short and long term.

title: A review of bio-based adhesives for engineered wood products: current status, challenges, and future outlook
summary: Engineered wood products (EWPs) are central to sustainable low-carbon construction, yet their manufacture depends on synthetic formaldehyde adhesives with significant health and environmental concerns and whose regulatory position is now na
content: Engineered wood products (EWPs) are central to sustainable low-carbon construction, yet their manufacture depends on synthetic formaldehyde adhesives with significant health and environmental concerns and whose regulatory position is now narrowing; from August 2026, the European Union has been reducing its permissible formaldehyde emission limit for wood-based articles. This has driven a global research effort to develop viable bio-based alternatives with potentially reduced environmental and health impacts. However, safety depends on the complete formulation, including crosslinkers and additives, and cannot be assumed solely from a bio-based origin. This review assesses whether bio-adhesives derived from proteins, lignin, tannins, and carbohydrates can meet this growing demand. Rather than cataloguing chemistry in isolation, each binder family is evaluated against the constraints that an operating plant could face: such as press factor, feedstock volume and batch consistency, cost parity, emissions certification, and structural qualification. These constraints are mapped onto specific products, ranging from structural glulam and cross-laminated timber to plywood and oriented strand board. Commercial deployment has already occurred, with lignin and soy binders bonding industrial plywood and particleboard today, but only in interior service and only where partially bio-based hybrids operate inside conventional resin architectures rather than as fully bio-based adhesives.

title: Green Engineering of Chlorella vulgaris -Based Waste-to-Resource Biorefineries: A PRISMA-ScR Scoping Review of Circularity Metrics and Scale-Up Barriers
summary: This scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) maps and synthesizes evidence on Chlorella vulgaris-based waste-to-value systems, focusing on resource recovery, circularity benefits, process integration, sustainability metrics, and scale-up barriers. A sy
content: This scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) maps and synthesizes evidence on Chlorella vulgaris-based waste-to-value systems, focusing on resource recovery, circularity benefits, process integration, sustainability metrics, and scale-up barriers. A systematic search of scientific databases and gray literature identified 40 studies (2010–2025) that underwent a complete re-audit of the extraction process. The evidence base is dominated by laboratory-scale investigations (TRL 3–4; n = 31; 77.5%) using real waste streams (agroindustrial, municipal, industrial, food, aquaculture, and mixed), while pilot and demonstration studies remain limited (TRL 5–6; n = 6; 15%), with a geographic bias toward Asia (n = 18; 45%). Chlorella vulgaris consistently contributes to nitrogen (22/40; 55.0%) and phosphorus (19/40; 47.5%) recovery, improved effluent quality, carbon utilization, and biomass generation for biodiesel, biogas, animal feed, biofertilizers, lipids, and other value-added products. Despite these advances, implementation remains constrained by variable waste composition, energy-intensive harvesting and downstream processing, insufficient standardization of performance and circularity indicators, and limited integration of technoeconomic analysis and life cycle assessment (LCA was applied in only 1 of 40 studies, whereas TEA, MCI, and exergy/emergy assessments were absent). Accordingly, an integrated framework and scale-up roadmap coupling technology readiness with prospective LCA and TEA are proposed to advance Chlorella vulgaris-based platforms toward scalable circular waste-to-resource systems.

title: Fostering Green Café Image in the Culinary Sector: A PLS-SEM and NCA Approach on Employee Achievement Motivation and Green Skills
summary: This research aims to investigate the causal mechanisms and absolute prerequisites of Achievement Motivation and Green Skills on the formulation of Work Environmental Behavior among employees in eco-friendly cafes. The study adopted a quant
content: This research aims to investigate the causal mechanisms and absolute prerequisites of Achievement Motivation and Green Skills on the formulation of Work Environmental Behavior among employees in eco-friendly cafes. The study adopted a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, involving 229 employees from five eco-friendly cafes in Bandung City, Indonesia. Empirical data were evaluated using a complementary dual-analytical approach: Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine sufficient logic and mediation effects, and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) to evaluate necessity logic and bottleneck thresholds. The PLS-SEM results confirm that achievement motivation has a positive and significant effect on both green skills and work environmental behavior, with green skills acting as a valid partial mediator. Interestingly, the NCA evaluation unveiled a new dimension: achievement motivation acts as an absolute necessary condition; its absence will immediately obstruct the implementation of pro-environmental behavior. Conversely, green skill serves only as a performance-optimizing catalyst and becomes an essential prerequisite only when the company targets flawless absolute environmental behavior (100%). The originality of this research rests on the methodological integration of PLS-SEM and NCA within the Green Human Resource Management discourse in the sustainable culinary sector. This study offers theoretical novelty by deconstructing previous assumptions; proving that eco-friendly initiatives in the workplace do not merely require technical expertise (green skills) as a facilitator, but are fundamentally bounded (acting as a bottleneck) by the magnitude of the workers' internal achievement motivation. Cafe management is advised to restructure recruitment strategies by prioritizing achievement-oriented candidates, which must be subsequently refined through targeted green skills training.

title: India's Role in the Geopolitics of the Global South
summary: This book investigates India’s contribution to the geopolitical landscape of the Global South, highlighting its increasing impact in shaping both regional and global dynamics. Since the formation of the United Nations, India has supported i
content: This book investigates India’s contribution to the geopolitical landscape of the Global South, highlighting its increasing impact in shaping both regional and global dynamics. Since the formation of the United Nations, India has supported international organizations, while also backing non-alignment initiatives that aim to protect economically weaker countries from subordination to big powers. This has placed India in a unique position to act both as an advocate for developing countries and as a bridge between the Global North and the Global South. This book investigates India’s increasing influence across a range of historical, cultural, economic, political, and strategic perspectives. The book encompasses India’s diplomatic strategies and soft power influence in the Global South, its green diplomacy, its role as a strategic counterweight to China, and its strategic engagement with Latin America and Africa. In particular, the book brings out India’s role as an advocate for a more inclusive and equitable global order that better represents the aspirations and priorities of the Global South. Based on in-depth, up-to-date insights, this book will be an important reference for researchers working across the fields of international relations, global politics, Indian foreign policy, and the geopolitics of the Global South.

title: Ecological Conflict Resolution in Forest Fire Governance; Local Wisdom and Human Security in Merauke, Papua Selatan
summary: Forest and land fires generate interacting ecological risks, governance tensions, and threats to human security. In Merauke, South Papua, their management requires attention to landscape variation and to the legitimacy of decisions affectin
content: Forest and land fires generate interacting ecological risks, governance tensions, and threats to human security. In Merauke, South Papua, their management requires attention to landscape variation and to the legitimacy of decisions affecting communities. This article examines how locally grounded knowledge and ecological conflict resolution can inform collaborative fire governance and protect human security. It applies a qualitative integrative narrative review of research published in 2017–2026, distinguishing direct evidence from Merauke and Wasur National Park from comparative findings elsewhere. Published Merauke observations show 2,671 MODIS hotspots in 2015 and 534 in 2019, with approximately 98% of burned areas on non-peatland in both years. Recent Wasur research additionally documents seasonality and Indigenous Kanume fire-use knowledge, without establishing uniform practices throughout the regency. The synthesis finds that local ecological observations, inclusive deliberation, reliable attribution procedures, and feasible livelihood alternatives can complement scientific monitoring. It proposes an evidence-sensitive governance framework connecting fire-risk identification, knowledge validation, negotiated responsibilities, grievance review, and human-security evaluation. These mechanisms are propositions rather than empirically established programme outcomes in Merauke. Effective fire governance should therefore combine ecological risk reduction with procedural recognition, accountable participation, and protection of health and livelihoods, while future field research tests the model's implementation and effects.

title: Added mass offset half of the efficiency gains in Europe’s electric vehicles
summary: I estimate technological progress in battery-electric vehicles from every battery-electric vehicle registered in the European Union, Iceland, and Norway from 2019 to 2025. The trade-off between energy consumption and vehicle attributes take
content: I estimate technological progress in battery-electric vehicles from every battery-electric vehicle registered in the European Union, Iceland, and Norway from 2019 to 2025. The trade-off between energy consumption and vehicle attributes takes the functional form implied by the physics of energy consumption, and the estimated mass and drag coefficients are close to the values implied by the test cycle. At fixed attributes, technological progress reduced consumption by 14.3 percent. Fleet-average consumption fell by only 7.5 percent, because the average new vehicle became 271 kilograms heavier. The added mass offset 53 percent of the technological progress, and the mass of larger batteries alone offset 29 percent. Range rose 45 percent, mainly because battery capacity became cheaper. The longer range likely raised electric vehicle sales enough to offset the emissions from the added electricity. Motor power, which carries a large energy cost in internal combustion vehicles, does not affect electric vehicle consumption.

title: Situational Teleworking and Employee Contextual Performance of Telecommunication Firms in South-South, Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: The study examined the relationship between situational teleworking and employee contextual performance of telecommunication firms in South-South, Nigeria. The specific objectives of the study were to determine the impact of situational tel
content: The study examined the relationship between situational teleworking and employee contextual performance of telecommunication firms in South-South, Nigeria. The specific objectives of the study were to determine the impact of situational teleworking on the measures of employee contextual performance. three research questions and hypotheses were formulated for this study. Relevant literatures were reviewed from the study. This study anchored on two theories which are institutional theory and organizational system theory. This study employed a descriptive correlational research design. The population of the study was forty-five thousand five hundred and eighty-four (45,584) from the entire staff of the four telecommunication firms in South-South, Nigeria with a sample size of 394 using Taro Yemene to determine it. Structured questionnaire was the only source of data collection. Inferential statistics and Spearman rank order correlation coefficient statistical tools were used to analyze the data with the aid of SPSS. The findings of the study, uncovered that situational teleworking was highly positive and statistically significant with the criterion measures. This study concluded that behaviours designed to facilitate work systems or formats that support teleworking features, like situational teleworking, improve the nature and content of employee relationships and help to close any social gaps or differences that may exist. Therefore, this study recommended among others that situational teleworking activities should be structured to allow for significant emotional balance, stress management and relief in a way that help employees effectively handle and manage work pressure as well as perform better in accordance with their responsibilities.

title: Generative AI-Enabled Digital Platforms for Sustainability: Understanding SME Adoption in the Sharing Economy
summary: This paper examines the perceptions of small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers toward the use of sharing economy (SE) platforms supported by generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool of resource sharing, with a focus on ho
content: This paper examines the perceptions of small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers toward the use of sharing economy (SE) platforms supported by generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool of resource sharing, with a focus on how they contribute to improvements in sustainability. We have used a mixed-method technique; the study has used narrative inquiry to obtain the lived experience of SME managers who utilize SE platforms to optimize resources actively. These narratives provided qualitative insights into managerial decision-making, platform trust perceptions, and digital sharing services' perceived environmental value. On these results, a quantitative survey produced 502 valid answers from SME managers in various fields. These findings can provide practical information to policymakers in order to facilitate the SE services to assist the SMEs through promoting access. Lastly, this research contributes to the growing evidence on scaling sustainable practices in SMEs through generative AI sharing platforms. The research indicates that technological competence prevails over environmental awareness, which demonstrates the necessity of SMEs to increase sustainability reporting by organized digital skill advancement, data analysis, and interpretation capabilities to impel the adoption of the SE.

title: Polymers of Intrinsic Microporosity Tailored Screen Printed Electrodes for Humidity Detection
summary: This work reports the development of an innovative resistive humidity sensor based on a Polymer of Intrinsic Microporosity (PIM) deposited onto a screen‐printed electrode. PIMs are characterized by an intrinsic microporous network that prov
content: This work reports the development of an innovative resistive humidity sensor based on a Polymer of Intrinsic Microporosity (PIM) deposited onto a screen‐printed electrode. PIMs are characterized by an intrinsic microporous network that provides high surface area and tunable gas permeability, making them attractive materials for electrochemical applications. Here, the synthesis of a carboxylated PIM (cPIM) is presented, together with sensor fabrication, material characterization, and evaluation of relative humidity (RH%) sensing performance. The PIM‐based sensor exhibits sensitivity from 27 RH%, reaching a response of R = 184 and a response time of 67s at 95 RH%. Reversibility was evaluated at 50 RH%, showing stable and reproducible responses over multiple cycles and a recovery time of 56 s, without compromising the structural integrity of cPIM4h during operation. The combination of suitable response and recovery times with a broad dynamic range enables reliable humidity detection across different environmental conditions. These results highlight the potential of PIM‐based materials for the development of advanced and sustainable gas sensing platforms for industrial and environmental applications.

title: The nonnative species biomass problem: despite lower numbers, the biomass of nonnative fish and snails equals that of native species in a Florida spring
summary: Invasions by nonnative species pose a major threat to freshwater ecosystem function and integrity. Freshwater springs, particularly those in Florida, are threatened by loss of water quantity, degradation of water quality, and invasions of n
content: Invasions by nonnative species pose a major threat to freshwater ecosystem function and integrity. Freshwater springs, particularly those in Florida, are threatened by loss of water quantity, degradation of water quality, and invasions of nonnative species, the last of which exacerbate the other problems. Most studies quantify the abundance of nonnative species by numbers of individuals, but the average size of species also is important as large species may have greater impacts on systems than small species. Therefore, we evaluated the biomass of native and nonnative fish and snails in a first magnitude spring in Florida. We used seine, snorkel, and video surveys to sample fish and random substrate quadrat samples to sample snails. We measured individuals of all species and calculated biomasses from weights estimated from length measurements. For both fish and snails, the native species outnumbered the nonnative species. Small poeciliids and killifish were the most numerous fish, whereas tiny hydrobiid snails were the most numerous snails. In contrast, most of the nonnative fish and snails were as large or larger than the largest native fish and snails, producing aggregate biomasses of nonnative species that were roughly equivalent to those for fish and snails. Given the greater impact of large-bodied organisms on ecosystem processes, these nonnative species likely have a much greater impact on this spring than their numbers would suggest.

title: Long-term performance and end-of-life pathways of silica aerogel-latex composites
summary: End-of-life (EoL) considerations are crucial for achieving circularity in the construction materials sector. Production-oriented developments in this field often involve evaluating sustainability in the manufacturing process. However, resea
content: End-of-life (EoL) considerations are crucial for achieving circularity in the construction materials sector. Production-oriented developments in this field often involve evaluating sustainability in the manufacturing process. However, research on disposal scenarios remains a challenge due to the scarcity of long-term data. This work aims to examine the durability of silica aerogel-latex composites by subjecting them to hydrothermal conditions (T of 35-55 °C, RH of 70-80%), estimating the equivalent of 24 years of normal use as building insulation based on the adopted aging model. The performance changes caused by the accelerated aging were analyzed, and the protocols for several EoL pathways were proposed. Chemical and mechanical recycling approaches were developed to produce a composite with properties suitable for an insulation material. Combining virgin and aged material at different ratios (15-50%) was shown to preserve the insulating and mechanical quality of the composite. Life cycle assessment (LCA) was used to quantify the sustainability of each laboratory-scale method over two use cycles, with a boundary set as cradle-to-cradle and cradle-to-grave, depending on the disposal scenario. Mechanical recycling showed the lowest environmental impact due to minimal processing requirements, demonstrating the feasibility of a circular EoL approach for silica aerogel-based insulation.

title: ROLE OF HR ANALYTICS IN IMPROVING EMPLOYEE RETENTION AND WORKFORCE PLANNING IN ORGANISATIONS
summary: Human Resource (HR) Analytics, also known as people analytics or workforce analytics, involves the systematic use of employee-related data and analytical methods to support human resource decisions. This paper examines how HR Analytics can
content: Human Resource (HR) Analytics, also known as people analytics or workforce analytics, involves the systematic use of employee-related data and analytical methods to support human resource decisions. This paper examines how HR Analytics can contribute to employee retention and workforce planning. Employee turnover creates direct and indirect costs, while ineffective workforce planning can lead to skill shortages, overstaffing, workload imbalance and disruption to organisational performance. Drawing on published research and established human resource management theories, the paper discusses how descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive analytics can help organisations understand workforce patterns, identify retention risks, forecast staffing requirements and evaluate HR interventions. The literature indicates that analytics can strengthen evidence-based decision-making when reliable data, appropriate analytical skills, managerial support and employee trust are present. However, predictive models cannot fully explain an employee’s decision to stay or leave, and careless use of employee data may create privacy, fairness and surveillance concerns. The paper recommends a gradual, transparent and human-centred approach in which analytics informs, rather than replaces, professional judgement. The study is based entirely on secondary sources and does not claim to have collected original survey or interview data. Keywords: HR Analytics, people analytics, employee retention, employee turnover, workforce planning, predictive analytics, human resource management.

title: Climate insecurity as economic achilles’ heel of dental practice owners
summary: Human-introduced climate change, pollution and biodiversity loss are interconnected crises that threaten livelihoods and (oral) health. Climate change, which is often the most visible and publicly recognised of the nine planetary boundaries
content: Human-introduced climate change, pollution and biodiversity loss are interconnected crises that threaten livelihoods and (oral) health. Climate change, which is often the most visible and publicly recognised of the nine planetary boundaries, represents only one dimension of wider ecological instability. Dental practice owners are increasingly facing the economic, social and health consequences of the overstepping planetary boundaries on their businesses and in their local communities. This article examines how exceeding planetary boundaries translates into financial and operational consequences for dental practice, exposing both short and long-term vulnerabilities of current dental business models. The authors argue that dental practice owners will need to adopt anticipatory, forward-looking strategies that reduce opportunity costs and strengthen long-term economic planning and operational viability.

title: From lab to market: Statistical optimization, techno-economic feasibility, and circular bioeconomy integration of a Wrightia tinctoria herbal oil for scalp psoriasis
summary: The present study proposes a business model canvas highlighting a formulation-to-commercialization strategy for an herbal oil formulation targeting scalp psoriasis. Considering the limitations of prolonged use of corticosteroids, this work
content: The present study proposes a business model canvas highlighting a formulation-to-commercialization strategy for an herbal oil formulation targeting scalp psoriasis. Considering the limitations of prolonged use of corticosteroids, this work presents a green, steroid-free topical alternative leveraging conventional blends of coconut, sesame and castor oils enriched with an aqueous extract of Wrightia tinctoria . An I-optimal mixture design was adopted to statistically optimize critical responses with prime concern on its rheological, physico-chemical and pharmacological properties. The optimized formulation comprising coconut oil (15.68%), castor oil (23.10%), sesame oil (40.00%) and W. tinctoria extract (21.22%) yielded favorable outcomes, including viscosity (191.92 cP), spreadability (7.38 cm), anti-inflammatory activity (246.13%), antioxidant activity (236.50%), clarity index (0.672), low peroxide value (4.53 meq/kg) and microbial load (4.30 log CFU/mL) with a global desirability index of 0.551. Model validation confirmed the robustness and reliability of the optimized models and further demonstrated an excellent stability over 60–90 days of storage. A comprehensive techno-economic analysis indicated a minimal production cost (₹36.19 per 100 mL), a 70% gross profit margin, break-even feasibility within the first 6 months of operation, with a sustainable profitability exceeding ₹48 lakh in 3-year financial projection. Beyond its commercial viability, the product aligns strongly with key United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) – SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) – highlighting its significance in green therapeutics and rural entrepreneurship. Importantly, the product production phase integrates the circular bioeconomy principles characterized by low energy consumption, zero solvent usage, reduced carbon footprint and effective biomass valorization. A cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA), compliant with ISO 14040/44 standards, reinforced the environmental sustainability of the formulation. In summary, this manuscript translates a statistically robust, scientifically validated and clinically relevant lab-scale formulation into a sustainable, economically feasible and commercially scalable business canvas model in the area of dermatological applications.

title: Sustainable Beauty: A Critical Analysis of Sustainability Discourse and Framing Strategies in Shiseido’s and Weleda’s Corporate Reports (2018-2024)
source: Lingue Culture Mediazioni - Languages Cultures Mediation (LCM Journal)
summary: In the beauty sector, sustainability discourse is not limited to describing environmental or management practices; it also shapes meanings, values, and forms of corporate legitimation. This study analyses, from a Critical Discourse Analysis
content: In the beauty sector, sustainability discourse is not limited to describing environmental or management practices; it also shapes meanings, values, and forms of corporate legitimation. This study analyses, from a Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) perspective (Fairclough 2003; Wodak and Meyer 2015), the discursive construction of sustainability in Shiseido’s and Weleda’s sustainability reports published between 2018 and 2024. With corpus-assisted tools used as heuristic support, the study highlights two discursive constructions of corporate sustainability: an ecological-relational configuration, centred on nature, supply chain, care and interdependence; and an institutional-transformative configuration, oriented towards governance, targets, innovation and empowerment. The analysis also suggests that framing, legitimation and representation of social actors contribute to making sustainability plausible and coherent with corporate identity (Entman 1993; van Leeuwen 2007, 2008). The study is situated within the debate on sustainability discourse and corporate sustainability reporting, showing that the reports examined do not simply reflect sustainability but construct it discursively as a practice of responsibility, accountability and corporate identity within the beauty sector.

title: Financial Flexibility and Firm Resilience Under Macroeconomic Policy Uncertainty
source: Academic Journal of Finance and Accounting
summary: Macroeconomic policy uncertainty raises the cost of external finance and the option value of waiting, which turns a firm’s financial slack into a potential source of resilience. This paper examines whether, and in which form, financial flex
content: Macroeconomic policy uncertainty raises the cost of external finance and the option value of waiting, which turns a firm’s financial slack into a potential source of resilience. This paper examines whether, and in which form, financial flexibility helps firms withstand policy uncertainty. Financial flexibility is decomposed into cash flexibility, measured by cash holdings relative to industry peers, and debt flexibility, measured by unused debt capacity relative to the industry leverage benchmark. Using an annual panel of 12,970 firm-year observations for 2,831 U.S. non-financial listed firms over 2014–2018 and a monthly panel of 338 S&P 500 constituents over 2015–2018, combined with the news-based economic policy uncertainty (EPU) index, three results emerge. First, cash flexibility predicts stronger subsequent sales growth and investment, whereas debt flexibility predicts investment continuity and a markedly lower probability of a severe stock-price decline. Second, the stock returns of firms with greater debt flexibility respond less adversely to EPU shocks: a one-standard-deviation increase in debt flexibility adds about 0.20 percentage points to the monthly return for each one-standard-deviation rise in EPU, whereas cash flexibility provides no comparable cushion. Third, the cushioning effect is concentrated among smaller firms, consistent with a financing-constraint channel. The evidence indicates that unused borrowing capacity, rather than accumulated cash, is the form of flexibility that insulates firm value from policy shocks.

title: An all-solid-state PVC-membrane microsensor for potentiometric and voltammetric determination of paroxetine in pharmaceutical samples
summary: In the present work, a new all-solid-state microsensor built on a polyvinyl chloride (PVC) membrane was fabricated to quantify paroxetine (PRX) in pharmaceutical formulations through both potentiometric and voltammetric approaches. An ion-p
content: In the present work, a new all-solid-state microsensor built on a polyvinyl chloride (PVC) membrane was fabricated to quantify paroxetine (PRX) in pharmaceutical formulations through both potentiometric and voltammetric approaches. An ion-pair complex between paroxetine and tetraphenylborate (PRX–TPB) was synthesized and incorporated as the ionophore within the PVC membrane. Detailed potentiometric characterization showed that the sensor followed Nernstian behavior, yielding a slope of 59.1 ± 0.8 mV per decade (R 2 = 0.9998) across paroxetine hydrochloride concentrations spanning 10 –6 to 10 –2 mol.L -1 . The microsensor reached a detection limit of 3.71 × 10 –7 mol.L −1 , combined with a response time below 10 s and roughly seven weeks of usable working life without loss of potentiometric behavior. Best performance fell within the pH window of 4.0 to 8.0. The same PRX-selective device was further characterized voltammetrically and successfully applied to paroxetine assay in marketed tablets by both electrochemical routes, with outcomes matching UV–Vis spectrophotometry at 95% confidence level, providing evidence that the microsensor is a dependable, uncomplicated, and low-cost option for pharmaceutical quality control.

title: Fluorescent carbon dot-based nanoprobes for antibiotic sensing in environmental and food matrices
summary: The use of antibiotics at an increasing rate is considered an emerging contaminant in the environment. Excessive use of this class of drugs can cause environmental pollution and severe health risks in humans. Antibiotics used in farming lea
content: The use of antibiotics at an increasing rate is considered an emerging contaminant in the environment. Excessive use of this class of drugs can cause environmental pollution and severe health risks in humans. Antibiotics used in farming leave residue in edible animal products. Animal products consumed by humans can have antibiotic residues. Not following suitable dosage protocols has left an increasing residual amount of antibiotics in food samples and in the environment. The presence of residual antibiotics in the environment causes bacteria to develop antibiotic resistance. Hence, low-level detection of these residual drugs is of utmost need. Carbon dots (CDs) have gained huge attention because of their exceptional optoelectronic behavior, high water dispersibility, excellent biocompatibility, and facile availability. Thus, research studies on the design of CD-based fluorometric sensing systems for fast and accurate identification of antibiotics in aqueous media and food samples are very impactful. However, a detailed analysis concerning the application of CDs in antibiotic sensing is required. Herein, a detailed introduction and classification of antibiotics are discussed. Moreover, different fluorescence mechanisms of these probes for sensing various antibiotics are reported. This review describes the recently reported CD-based probes for the effective sensing of different classes of antibiotics. This review may be helpful for researchers developing new CD-based systems for more selective and low-level recognition of antibiotics.

title: An Exploratory Assessment of Behavioral Green Supply Chain Management Practices in Indonesian Halal Foodservice: A Two-Stage PLS-SEM Approach
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: The sustainability trend has emerged as a pivotal issue amid rising global awareness of intensifying climate change, the need for effective resource management, and pressing social disparities. To promote sustainability, it is crucial to ad
content: The sustainability trend has emerged as a pivotal issue amid rising global awareness of intensifying climate change, the need for effective resource management, and pressing social disparities. To promote sustainability, it is crucial to adopt Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) practices as essential strategies by reforming operational practices from behavioral perspectives in accordance with environmental management principles. This study presents a conceptual framework to provide an exploratory assessment of how behavioral GSCM practices influence sustainability performance. This research employs a quantitative design, using cross-sectional surveys to gather data from Indonesian halal foodservice managers in the hospitality and tourism industry, yielding 40 responses. The collected data were analyzed through model evaluation and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using SmartPLS4, following the higher-order embedded two-stage approach. This preliminary empirical assessment found that behavioral GSCM practices significantly influence sustainability performance. As a result, it enhances the understanding of behavioral GSCM practices in the Indonesian halal foodservice sector. Moreover, further research with larger, more diverse samples will offer valuable insights for policymakers, businesses, customers, and communities, thereby promoting green initiatives that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Market behavior in climate-exposed sectors: Evidence from Indonesia
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleNovi Swandari Budiarso - Corresponding author, email: novi.sbudiarso@unsrat.ac.idAbstractClimate change has heightened interest in financial market behavior, particularly in sectors exposed to environmen
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleNovi Swandari Budiarso - Corresponding author, email: novi.sbudiarso@unsrat.ac.idAbstractClimate change has heightened interest in financial market behavior, particularly in sectors exposed to environmental and transition risks. This study examines market behavior in climate-exposed sectors by analyzing weak-form market efficiency, bubble dynamics, herding behavior, regime shifts, and volatility asymmetry in stocks from the Indonesia Stock Exchange over the period January 2, 2020 to December 30, 2025, covering 260 firms across energy, industrials, consumer non-cyclicals, and basic materials sectors. The analysis employs variance ratio tests, Hurst analysis, Bai–Perron structural break tests, SADF/GSADF bubble detection, CSAD regressions, and AR(1)-EGARCH modeling. The results indicate systematic deviations from weak-form market efficiency across all sectors, with variance ratio statistics significantly exceeding unity and Hurst exponents ranging from 0.58 to 0.69, indicating persistent long-memory behavior. Structural break analysis identifies three distinct regimes in the industrials sector, while other sectors remain relatively stable. Bubble detection reveals 22 explosive episodes in the energy sector, including a prolonged 141-day bubble, and eight bubble periods in the industrials sector, whereas no bubbles are observed in the consumer non-cyclicals and basic materials sectors. Herding behavior is weak, conditional, and not robust across specifications. Volatility dynamics exhibit strong persistence, fat-tailed distributions, and good-news dominance, with regime-dependent asymmetry particularly evident in industrials. The findings should be interpreted in the context of climate-exposed sectors, as the analysis does not directly incorporate explicit climate-risk measures. Overall, the study reveals pronounced heterogeneity in market behavior across climate-exposed sectors, highlighting regime-dependent financial dynamics and sectoral heterogeneity in emerging markets, with implications for investors and policymakers.AcknowledgmentsThe authors gratefully acknowledge Sam Ratulangi University for the provision of facilities and resources that enabled this study.

title: CHAPTER 7. CONTEMPORARY APPROACHES TO PHYSICAL REHABILITATION OF ADULTS WITH SCOLIOSIS: TRADITIONAL AND INNOVATIVE METHODS

content: Scoliosis in adulthood is a complex structural and functional spinal disorder characterized by three-dimensional deformity of the spinal alignment, impaired trunk biomechanics, changes in muscle balance, and limitations in the functional capacity of the musculoskeletal system.Unlike scoliotic deformities occurring during the growth period, the clinical presentation in adults is often complicated by degenerative changes in the intervertebral discs and facet joints, reduced soft tissue elasticity, chronic pain, and impaired sagittal balance.These changes may adversely affect physical activity, the ability to perform activities of daily living, occupational functioning, and quality of life.In contemporary clinical practice, adult scoliosis is regarded not merely as a deviation of the spine in the frontal plane but as a multidimensional deformity requiring assessment of coronal and sagittal balance, the rotational component, and the patient's functional status [5, 10].It is important to distinguish between idiopathic scoliosis, which develops during childhood or adolescence and persists after skeletal maturity, and adult degenerative scoliosis, which develops as a result of age-related changes in spinal structures.Primary idiopathic scoliosis may affect an individual throughout their lifetime, whereas the degenerative form is more commonly associated with asymmetric degeneration of intervertebral discs, articular surfaces, and ligamentous structures, as well as changes in the mechanical loading of individual spinal 5. title: The thermal density paradox: evaluating rooftop solar options for net-zero high-density buildings
summary: Urban densification reduces the amount of rooftop collection area available per dwelling, creating a potential mismatch between building energy demand and on-site solar generation. This policy perspective examines this spatial constraint us
content: Urban densification reduces the amount of rooftop collection area available per dwelling, creating a potential mismatch between building energy demand and on-site solar generation. This policy perspective examines this spatial constraint using California’s 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Title 24, Part 6) as a regulatory case study. It distinguishes the electrical input required by heat pump water heaters (HPWHs) from the thermal energy delivered as domestic hot water (DHW), and compares photovoltaic (PV) and hybrid photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) options on a common roof area basis. A transparent, illustrative 600 m² multifamily-building scenario estimates annual PV electricity, PVT electricity, and the electricity-equivalent value of useful PVT heat under stated assumptions. Under the central assumptions, PV produces 172,800 kWhₑ yr⁻¹. In comparison, PVT produces approximately 190,000 kWhₑ yr⁻¹ plus a theoretical 140,000 kWhₑ-equivalent yr⁻¹ from 420,000 kWhₜₕ yr⁻¹ of captured heat if all heat can be usefully stored and delivered. The combined 330,000 kWhₑ-equivalent yr⁻¹ is an upper-bound service-equivalent estimate, not measured net-electricity output or a prediction of annual net-zero performance. The paper defines Return on Surface Area (ROSA) as annual useful energy service yield per unit of constrained roof area. It proposes performance-based code evaluation, workforce development, and incentives for verified thermal load displacement. The analysis identifies a potential spatial advantage for PVT while recognizing that code compliance and lifecycle economics depend on climate, building form, storage, load coincidence, and system design.

title: Phases, Techniques and Tools of Negotiation
summary: The previous chapters have explained what is at stake in a negotiation, where power comes from and how strategic interaction can be analysed. Negotiators, however, must also act: they must open the talks, make offers, respond to the other s
content: The previous chapters have explained what is at stake in a negotiation, where power comes from and how strategic interaction can be analysed. Negotiators, however, must also act: they must open the talks, make offers, respond to the other side’s proposals, decide when and how much to concede, close an agreement and then live with it. This chapter turns from analysis to practice. It examines the phases through which negotiations pass, the techniques most useful in each phase and the practical tools helping negotiators to manage complex talks.

title: Operational data disclosure shapes satellite verification of power-plant CO2 emissions
summary: Spaceborne CO2 plume imaging is widely proposed to verify power-plant inventories, yet sparse daytime snapshots measure instantaneous flux whereas annual accountability must detect subtle carbon-intensity shifts beyond existing records. Com
content: Spaceborne CO2 plume imaging is widely proposed to verify power-plant inventories, yet sparse daytime snapshots measure instantaneous flux whereas annual accountability must detect subtle carbon-intensity shifts beyond existing records. Combining US satellite benchmarks, US and European generation and emissions fleets, Sentinel-5P NO2 matchups and simulations across 11,543 stations, we define when satellites cut annual emission-change error. Over routine US generation records, archived EMIT retrievals yield no gain (-3.3%, 95% upper bound +0.4%; ground references beat satellites by +14–32 percentage points), and neither regional grids nor NO2 replace hourly plant load. Without hourly load, idealized sensors (10% error, zero bias) detect single-plant misreporting only above 70% at 80% power, versus 6.3% with hourly load. Globally, eligible emissions span 19% over Climate TRACE inventories to 67% over provincial thermal-fuel statistics and 71% over no-change baselines, while disclosure quadruples gains under improved sensors.

title: Beyond supply-chain risk: a three-tier social life cycle assessment of wood-based aviation fuel in Japan
summary: Japanese policy promotes domestic feedstocks, including wood, for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), partly to revitalize feedstock-producing regions. We apply a three-tier social life cycle assessment to Fischer–Tropsch SAF from sawmill resi
content: Japanese policy promotes domestic feedstocks, including wood, for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), partly to revitalize feedstock-producing regions. We apply a three-tier social life cycle assessment to Fischer–Tropsch SAF from sawmill residue: supply-chain risk screening, regional feasibility to 2120 and six companies’ documented conduct. The route places more of its work in Japan than fossil jet, yet most screened risk lies overseas. Comparisons with fossil jet and used-cooking-oil SAF depend on the activity basis and residue mapping. Under business as usual, attributed forestry work gains weight in all 47 prefectures as labor forces contract, while the route’s added value falls relative to regional output. Companies document supplier governance, most clearly for forced labor, yet feedstock companies hold no assessable evidence on forestry safety. The domestic work thus gains weight while remaining the least evidenced part of the route. Its social performance depends on input procurement, host-region planning and supplier evidence.
