title: Powering the Transition: What Drives Renewable Energy Consumption Across Developed and Developing Economies?
summary: As the world faces climate change and energy security challenges, the transition to renewable energy has become essential for global sustainability. The factors influencing renewable energy adoption vary between developed and developing cou
content: As the world faces climate change and energy security challenges, the transition to renewable energy has become essential for global sustainability. The factors influencing renewable energy adoption vary between developed and developing countries due to differences in their economic, political, and social contexts. This study investigates the key drivers of renewable energy consumption, focusing on environmental taxes, research and development (R&D) funding, institutional quality, and economic growth. Using panel data from 40 countries, including 20 developed and 20 developing countries, over the period from 1995 to 2021, the study applies fixed effects regression and one year lagged panel regression specifications. The results indicate that, in developing countries, the main determinants are positively associated with renewable energy consumption in the same year fixed effects models and remain positive in the one year lagged specifications. In developed countries, environmental taxes and R&D are positively associated with renewable energy consumption in the same year fixed effects models, whereas in the one year lagged specifications, R&D, institutional quality, and GDP per capita are positively associated with renewable energy consumption, while environmental taxes are negatively associated with it. These findings highlight the complexity of energy transitions and the need for policies tailored to different economic contexts and levels of institutional capacity. The study contributes to the literature by providing a comparative perspective and practical insights for policymakers and investors seeking to support sustainable energy transitions.

title: Local Imperfect Feedback Control in Nonequilibrium Biophysical Systems Enabled by Response Constraints
summary: How biological networks achieve robust control despite relying on imperfect, local information remains an important open question. Here, we identify constraints that can limit nonequilibrium steady-state responses so severely that even crud
content: How biological networks achieve robust control despite relying on imperfect, local information remains an important open question. Here, we identify constraints that can limit nonequilibrium steady-state responses so severely that even crude, local feedback rules can achieve globally stable control without requiring precise network design or global information. Specifically, using Markov jump processes as a framework for biophysical dynamics, we derive general nonequilibrium constraints showing that, for many classes of rate perturbations, steady-state responses have fixed signs across all perturbation strengths, so that near-equilibrium responses predict far-from-equilibrium behavior regardless of system complexity. These constraints clarify several biological phenomena: monotonicity is guaranteed whenever a perturbation acts on a single rate parameter, and nonmonotonic responses, as observed, for example, in transcription factor regulation, arise only when an input simultaneously modulates multiple rates. Even in this case, we identify a graph-theoretic concept termed “coherence” that allows for a restoration of monotonicity. We show how coherence naturally and generally emerges in classic biophysical models of adaptation, including chemotaxis and transcription factor regulation. We next show that, within a control-theoretic framework, these constraints guarantee that simple linear feedback on small subsets of kinetic rates achieves globally stable tracking and adaptation without coordinated manipulation of many regulated variables. For systems with one regulator, local stability implies global stability for arbitrary network topologies without fine-tuning. For multiple regulators, the response constraints restrict the allowed nullcline geometry in ways that preclude unstable dynamical structures. Together, these results reveal that nonequilibrium statistical mechanics fundamentally constrains biochemical network responses, explaining when and why responses are monotonic or nonmonotonic and guaranteeing the effectiveness of minimal, local feedback for robust control in complex reaction networks.

title: Proximity-induced unconventional superconductivity and chiral topological phases in twisted graphene/NbSe 2 van der Waals heterostructure
summary: We study proximity-induced unconventional superconductivity in a twisted graphene/NbSe2 van der Waals heterostructure using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism. The normal-state parameters of proximitized graphene are extracted from ab initi
content: We study proximity-induced unconventional superconductivity in a twisted graphene/NbSe2 van der Waals heterostructure using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism. The normal-state parameters of proximitized graphene are extracted from ab initio calculations at a twist angle of 23.4 degrees, which reduces the common symmetry of the heterostructure to C3. We construct symmetry-allowed superconducting gap functions of the graphene layer according to the irreducible representations of the C3 group, containing singlet and triplet pairing channels and their mixtures. Computing the topological invariants as a function of the mixing parameters, we find a rich phase diagram of chiral topological superconducting phases, characterized by nonzero Chern numbers C. While the nature of the superconducting order parameter of NbSe 2 remains debated, the formation of the van der Waals heterostructure can alter the relative stability of competing pairing channels, potentially stabilizing a chiral pairing that is proximity-induced into graphene and triggers the topological phases identified here, making the twisted graphene/NbSe 2 heterostructure a promising platform for chiral topological superconductivity detectable via quasiparticle interference imaging and transport measurements.

title: Layer-selective chirality switch in bilayer graphene intercalated by Janus monolayers
summary: We predict that intercalating bilayer graphene with nonmagnetic WSSe or magnetic MnSSe Janus monolayers induces a layer-selective switch of the in-plane Rashba spin texture, resulting in opposite spin current directions in the top and botto
content: We predict that intercalating bilayer graphene with nonmagnetic WSSe or magnetic MnSSe Janus monolayers induces a layer-selective switch of the in-plane Rashba spin texture, resulting in opposite spin current directions in the top and bottom graphene layers. First-principles calculations reveal that both Janus monolayers shift the Dirac cones of the two graphene layers to different energies, decoupling their low-energy states, while simultaneously inducing opposite signs of the proximity-induced Rashba spin-orbit coupling in each. Tight-binding modeling of the proximitized layers, combined with Rashba-Edelstein charge-to-spin conversion calculations, confirms that the spin current direction can be independently controlled by gating the top or bottom graphene layer. Bilayer graphene intercalated by Janus monolayers thus represents a promising platform for gate-tunable, layer-selective spintronic devices.

title: Temperature coefficient of potential of LixC6 for thermorechargeable battery
summary: The thermorechargeable battery (TB) can convert environmental temperature change into electric energy with use of difference in the temperature coefficient α of the potential E between the positive and negative electrodes. Here, we investig
content: The thermorechargeable battery (TB) can convert environmental temperature change into electric energy with use of difference in the temperature coefficient α of the potential E between the positive and negative electrodes. Here, we investigated α for Li x C 6 against the Li + concentration x during delithiation. Li x C 6 exhibits successive phase transition from 1, 2, 2L, 3L, 4L, to 1L phases during delithiation. In the 2L-2 and 2-1 regions (large- x region), solid component α C 6 for Li x C 6 is almost constant except near the edges of the regions. In the 1L-4L, 4L-3L and 3L-2L regions (small- x region), however, α C 6 rather continuously decreases with x . The x -dependence of α C 6 is discussed with a phenomenological model incorporating the stage structure.

title: Genome-wide fitness profiling reveals flagellar rotation as an energetic liability during anaerobic maintenance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
summary: Bacteria in nature and disease frequently spend time in non-growing states, yet the genes that allow cells to survive without growing are poorly understood. Using Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain PA14 as a model system in which to study non-gr
content: Bacteria in nature and disease frequently spend time in non-growing states, yet the genes that allow cells to survive without growing are poorly understood. Using Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain PA14 as a model system in which to study non-growth powered by anaerobic phenazine cycling, we employed randomly barcoded transposon-insertion sequencing (RB-TnSeq) to identify the genes required for this maintenance state using a platform that sustains anaerobic survival via continuous phenazine reoxidation. We found 167 genes whose disruption altered survival, including genes involved in transcription, translation, protein quality control, and cell envelope integrity. Comparing our results to published TnSeq data from other forms of energy-limited growth arrest (conditions where electron acceptor or carbon availability constrains energy conservation below that required for cell growth/division) in PA14 revealed that while a subset of genes are fitness determinants across distinct growth-arrested states, most are condition-specific. Notably, genes involved in flagellar regulation and assembly were broadly detrimental to survival. Leveraging a high-throughput electrochemical system that allows for quantitative and mechanistic dissection of the phenazine cycling-dependent maintenance state, we found that flagellar abundance influences cells’ survival, metabolic rate, and ATP levels. Moreover, removing the flagellar stator proteins MotA and MotC, which are required for flagellar rotation but not assembly, reversed these defects, indicating that the energetic cost of flagella comes from their rotation rather than construction. These results show that in a low-powered maintenance state, limiting energy-dissipating processes, such as proton-motive force loss through flagellar rotation, supports cell survival. IMPORTANCE The genetic landscape governing non-growth survival under energy limitation, and the cellular processes that help or hinder it, remain largely uncharacterized. What does a cell need to do, and what must it avoid, to survive when growth-arrested? Answering this question is clinically important because non-growing bacteria are often antibiotic tolerant. Here, we used a genome-wide screen of Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain PA14, an opportunistic pathogen, to identify fitness determinants of viability during a non-growth state powered by anaerobic phenazine-cycling, a state mimicking the anoxic cores of biofilms. Our findings suggest that growth-arrested cells live at a bioenergetic knife's edge, where an energy-dissipating process, like a rotating flagellum, can tip the balance between vitality and death, providing a bioenergetic rationale for the known repression of flagellar expression in mature biofilm cores.

title: Polariton-Polariton Coherent Coupling in a Molecular Spin-Superconductor Chip
summary: The ability to establish coherent communication channels is key for scaling up quantum devices. Here, we engineer interactions between distant polaritons, hybrid spin-photon excitations formed at different lumped-element superconducting res
content: The ability to establish coherent communication channels is key for scaling up quantum devices. Here, we engineer interactions between distant polaritons, hybrid spin-photon excitations formed at different lumped-element superconducting resonators within a chip. The chip consists of several resonator pairs, slightly detuned in frequency to make them addressable, capacitively coupled within each pair and inductively coupled to a common readout line. They interact locally with samples of PTMr and Tripak − organic free radicals, deposited onto their inductors, which provide model S = 1 / 2, g ≃ 2 spin ensembles. Frequency-dependent microwave transmission experiments, performed at very low temperatures, measure polariton frequencies as a function of magnetic field in different scenarios. When only one resonator within a pair hosts a molecular sample, the results evidence that spins couple remotely to the empty LER as well as to the local cavity mode. If both resonators interact with a spin ensemble, the magnetic field tunes the polariton frequencies relative to each other, on account of the different spin-photon interactions at each LER. When polaritons are brought into mutual resonance, the microwave transmission spectroscopically resolves an avoided level crossing that evidences a polariton-polariton interaction mediated by the circuit. Then, pump-probe experiments reveal that the excitation of a polariton within a connected pair is indeed felt, thus it can be read out, by the other one. Model calculations, compatible with the experimental parameters and results, suggest that the system excitation eigenstates show photon-photon and spin-spin correlations and entanglement near the polariton-polariton anticrossing.

title: Latent developmental-arrest burden after cleavage-stage transfer: a counterfactual reanalysis of a published IVF cohort
source: Journal of Assisted Reproduction and Genetics
summary: Purpose To estimate how many cleavage-stage (day-3) transfers in low-zygote IVF cycles occur where extended culture would have yielded no transferable blastocyst, and to compare clinical pregnancy after day-5 transfer with that in day-3 cyc
content: Purpose To estimate how many cleavage-stage (day-3) transfers in low-zygote IVF cycles occur where extended culture would have yielded no transferable blastocyst, and to compare clinical pregnancy after day-5 transfer with that in day-3 cycles inferred to be progressable. Methods Counterfactual secondary analysis of a published single-center cohort of 1116 first fresh cycles in which transfer day was assigned by the weekday of oocyte retrieval (584 day 3; 532 day 5, including 70 extended-culture cancellations). Zygote-specific day-5 cancellation rates were applied to the day-3 arm to estimate a latent-arrest fraction, and the day-5 per-protocol clinical pregnancy rate was compared with the implied day-3 progressable rate. The published arm-level comparison is not repeated as a finding. Results With ≤ 5 zygotes, an estimated 104 of 471 day-3 cycles (22.1%; 95% CI 17.3–26.8) were putatively futile transfers, falling from 37.3% at one zygote to 4.5% at five; 85% of this burden arose in cycles with one or two zygotes. The implied day-3 progressable rate was 32.7%, against 31.3% after day-5 per-protocol transfer (residual difference − 1.3 percentage points; 95% CI − 8.6 to 5.7). With ≥ 6 zygotes the residual difference was 23.6 points (95% CI 11.7–35.4). Covariate-adjusted g-computation gave similar estimates; the transfer-day-by-zygote-number interaction was significant (continuous model, P = 0.004). Conclusions About one in five cleavage-stage transfers in low-zygote cycles, concentrated in one- and two-zygote cycles, was estimated to occur where extended culture would have found no transferable blastocyst. These assumption-dependent estimates support counseling and prospective evaluation of cumulative live birth, not a universal transfer policy.

title: A semi-infinite hydraulic fracture propagating in a poroelastic medium
summary: We solve the near-tip coupled hydromechanical problem of a hydraulic fracture propagating in a permeable poroelastic medium, represented locally as a semi-infinite crack moving at constant velocity. In the moving tip frame, all fracture fie
content: We solve the near-tip coupled hydromechanical problem of a hydraulic fracture propagating in a permeable poroelastic medium, represented locally as a semi-infinite crack moving at constant velocity. In the moving tip frame, all fracture fields are steady. The porous solid obeys linear poroelasticity, fracture propagation follows linear elastic fracture mechanics, fluid flow within the tensile fracture is governed by lubrication theory, and the fracturing and pore fluids are treated as identical Newtonian liquids. The primary unknowns are the fracture opening and the fluid displacement function along the fracture, determined from the resulting nonlinear system of equations. In a viscosity–toughness scaling, the problem depends on four dimensionless parameters: a dimensionless permeability rho ϱ $\varrho$ (associated with the intensity of fluid leak-in), a dimensionless effective confining stress upper Sigma prime 0 Σ 0 ′ $\varSigma _0'$ (measuring the relative importance of fluid leak-off and leak-in), the drained–undrained Poisson’s ratio contrast beta β $\beta$ and the poroelastic stress coefficient eta η $\eta$. The solution evolves from a drained, toughness-dominated near-tip asymptote with uniform net pressure to an undrained, storage-viscosity-dominated far-field asymptote. Numerical solutions are obtained over parameter ranges representative of various rock types. The fully coupled model is compared with simplified models, namely uncoupled and one-way coupled formulations, over distances from the fracture front spanning laboratory-to-field scales. The resulting relative difference maps in the left parenthesis rho comma upper Sigma prime 0 right parenthesis (ϱ, Σ 0 ′) $(\varrho ,\varSigma _0')$ parameter space identify four characteristic regimes: negligible poroelastic effects, dominance of the direct mechanical poroelastic response, importance of the poroelastic backstress and a fully coupled regime. The latter occurs mainly at large rho ϱ $\varrho$ and small upper Sigma prime 0 Σ 0 ′ $\varSigma _0'$, corresponding to strong leak-in relative to leak-off.

title: WOVEN IDENTITY: TRADITIONAL ARBËRESH COSTUMES OF SICILY (PIANA DEGLI ALBANESI AND SANTA CRISTINA GELA): HISTORICAL RESEARCH FOR APPLIED VALORIZATION
source: International Congress From Research to Application
summary: This paper examines the textile heritage of the Arbëreshë communities in Sicily, specifically in the towns of Piana degli Albanesi (Hora e Arbwreshwvet) and Santa Cristina Gela (Swndahstina), within the broader historical context of the isl
content: This paper examines the textile heritage of the Arbëreshë communities in Sicily, specifically in the towns of Piana degli Albanesi (Hora e Arbwreshwvet) and Santa Cristina Gela (Swndahstina), within the broader historical context of the island’s Albanian-speaking settlements, which also include Palazzo Adriano (Palac Adriano), Contessa Entellina (Kundisa), and Mezzojuso (Munxifsi). Established from the 15th century onwards, following the diaspora triggered by Ottoman expansion in the Balkans, these Arbëresh centers in Sicily have preserved a remarkable ethno-linguistic and liturgical identity over the centuries. The study demonstrates how this identity finds its most profound visual and semiotic expression in the art of traditional costume, interpreted not as a static relic, but as a dynamic cultural device and a historical "text" to be decoded. The research is based on a rigorous philological investigation, conducted through the cataloging and analysis of documentary and historical photographic sources. This survey has made it possible to map the morphological evolution of the garments and to develop a systematic typological classification. The study defines the transitions and social stratifications that distinguish everyday attire, "semi-festive" (or intermediate) dress, formal festive wear, and wedding attire. For each type, the following are examined: structural elements and historical models to be preserved; decorative motifs, which provide a stylistic and artistic overview of the attire, a cultural background essential for determining the date of manufacture and the stylistic influences that have shaped the garment into its present form; accessories and jewelry, which facilitate a semiotic and symbolic decoding of the attire. Particular attention is devoted to the tailoring craftsmanship and the micro-technological excellence of the embroidery techniques. The research delves into the material dimension of the artifacts, describing the use of exceptionally high-quality yarns and raw materials, most notably 24-karat gold, employed in intricate, hand-stitched embroidery on fine fabrics. 6This level of mastery is examined in relation to the variations and enduring features found in the traditional attire of other historical Sicilian-Arbëresh communities, namely Palazzo Adriano, Contessa Entellina, and Mezzojuso, thereby highlighting both shared identity markers and distinct local characteristics. The second part of the work shifts from historiographical theory to the contemporary practice of heritage preservation. It addresses the critical subject of modern textile restoration and preventive conservation techniques, essential for halting the biological and structural degradation of centuries-old artifacts and ensuring their physical survival. Finally, the study presents an operational model for outreach and regeneration, centered on the implementation of specialized vocational training courses within the local area.

title: Hierarchical heterostructure engineering for strength–ductility synergy in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys
summary: Additive manufacturing creates high-entropy alloys under thermal conditions that are difficult to reproduce by conventional routes. Rapid solidification, directional heat flow, and repeated reheating generate cellular substructures, melt-po
content: Additive manufacturing creates high-entropy alloys under thermal conditions that are difficult to reproduce by conventional routes. Rapid solidification, directional heat flow, and repeated reheating generate cellular substructures, melt-pool boundaries, solute-partitioned interfaces, metastable phases, and nanoscale precipitates. These features are often treated separately, although their mechanical effect depends on how they interact across length scales. This Mini Review examines additive manufacturing as a route for constructing hierarchical heterostructures that coordinate strength and plasticity. Emphasis is placed on the conversion of solidification-derived heterogeneity into useful deformation architecture rather than on a process-by-process comparison. Cellular and subgrain structures, lamellar eutectics, coherent or semi-coherent precipitates, metastable phase transformation, ceramic reinforcement, and post-processing are discussed as connected design tools. Recent studies on laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and directed energy deposition (DED) show that high strength can coexist with substantial tensile ductility when hard regions carry load while softer or transformable regions maintain strain accommodation and when interfaces delay rather than trigger localization. The key challenge is therefore not simply maximizing phase complexity or defect-free density, but controlling the spatial continuity, stability, and mechanical contrast of heterogeneities. Design principles and remaining limitations for microstructure-oriented development of additively manufactured high-entropy alloys are summarized.

title: Environmental procuratorial public interest litigation under the ecological and environmental code: institutional design and operational logic
summary: Promulgated in 2026, the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China introduces the concept of ‘ecological and environmental procuratorial work’ into legislation for the first time and systematically sets out procura
content: Promulgated in 2026, the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China introduces the concept of ‘ecological and environmental procuratorial work’ into legislation for the first time and systematically sets out procuratorial responsibilities for ecological and environmental public interest litigation in nine provisions. Article 1074 establishes special rules for damage to the marine ecological environment. Through an examination of institutional evolution, analysis of legal norms, and comparative inquiry, this article addresses how the Code consolidates and restructures environmental procuratorial public interest litigation and what distinctive indigenous characteristics emerge in the marine context. It argues that China’s system is not a transplant of US citizen suits, but a structural institutional innovation grounded in China’s own constitutional system. The Code establishes four basic forms: procuratorial involvement in compensation for non-marine ecological and environmental damage; procuratorial public interest litigation concerning compensation for marine ecological and environmental damage; environmental civil public interest litigation; and environmental administrative public interest litigation. The system is both compliance-inducing and collaborative. It differs fundamentally from US citizen suits in the source of authority, the identity of plaintiffs, procedural logic, and institutional functions. US citizen suits originate in private rights, operate subject to judicial review constraints, and pursue punishment and deterrence; China’s system originates in legal supervision, prioritizes pre-litigation measures to secure compliance, and seeks ecological restoration. The marine framework illustrates these indigenous characteristics particularly clearly. Article 1074 establishes a dual structure in which regulatory authorities have priority in seeking compensation and procuratorial organs bring proceedings as a backstop. The Bohai Sea special case initiative demonstrates institutional capacities in cross-regional marine governance that private litigation lacks. The Code marks a transition from dispersed rules to an integrated system, whose underlying logic continues to be shaped by China’s constitutional framework.

title: Testing the urban environmental transition hypothesis in Somalia
summary: Rapid urbanization is reshaping the environmental trajectory of Sub-Saharan Africa, yet existing evidence for Somalia models urbanization only in linear form and therefore cannot detect whether its effect on emissions eventually reverses. T
content: Rapid urbanization is reshaping the environmental trajectory of Sub-Saharan Africa, yet existing evidence for Somalia models urbanization only in linear form and therefore cannot detect whether its effect on emissions eventually reverses. This study examines the drivers of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in Somalia over 1990–2024, focusing on whether urbanization affects emissions non-linearly. Within an extended STIRPAT framework, the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds-testing approach is applied to annual data, with urbanization entered in linear and quadratic form alongside energy intensity, per-capita income, and urban agglomeration. Unit root tests that allow for structural breaks confirm that no series is integrated of order two, and the bounds test establishes a stable long-run relationship. The results reveal an inverted-U relationship between urbanization and CO₂ emissions: emissions rise in the early stages of urban expansion and decline once urbanization exceeds an estimated turning point of approximately 47.2%, a threshold that lies within the sample range and that Somalia crossed in 2017. Energy intensity and per-capita income raise emissions significantly in the long run, indicating that growth has not yet decoupled from environmental pressure, whereas urban agglomeration is statistically insignificant. The error-correction term shows that roughly 73% of any deviation from equilibrium is corrected within a year, and fully modified OLS and canonical cointegrating regression estimates corroborate the inverted-U relationship. The findings imply that Somalia’s climate and development planning should integrate low-carbon urban design into the management of its rapidly growing, displacement-driven cities, expand solar and other renewable electricity to replace diesel generation and charcoal, and pursue energy-efficiency gains, so that continued urban and economic growth is associated with lower rather than higher emissions.

title: TRIP13 as a key potential biomarker of ovarian cancer: screening, validation and targeted inhibition
summary: Background Among gynecological malignancies, ovarian cancer (OC) which ranks first in mortality rate, often presents no typical clinical manifestations in its early stages and lacks effective means for early diagnosis. Therefore, it is impe
content: Background Among gynecological malignancies, ovarian cancer (OC) which ranks first in mortality rate, often presents no typical clinical manifestations in its early stages and lacks effective means for early diagnosis. Therefore, it is imperative to screen out key genes for early diagnosis and prognostic analysis of OC, and to identify the correctness of the screened key genes for OC through experimental methods. Methods The dataset GSE54388, GSE26712 and GSE18520 in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database was collected. To select hub genes, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network were used. At the same time, machine learning techniques (LASSO, SVM-RFE and Boruta) were used to further screen the core genes. Differential expression level analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and survival analysis were employed to screen for key genes related to OC. Clinical specimens, SKOV3 cells and subcutaneous transplanted tumor models were used to evaluate the importance of key genes in the occurrence and development of OC through biological experiments. Results Two core genes (TK1 and TRIP13) were screened through WGCNA analysis, PPI network and machine learning algorithms. Through gene differential expression analysis, ROC analysis, and survival analysis, thyroid hormone receptor interactor 13 (TRIP13) was selected as the key gene in OC. The immunohistochemical staining results of clinical specimens from 23 OC patients showed that compared with normal ovarian epithelial tissues, the TRIP13 protein expression was progressively upregulated with the degree of OC malignancy. DCZ0415, a potent TRIP13 inhibitor, could significantly inhibit the proliferation and migration of SKOV3 cells, reduce TRIP13 protein expression in tumor of subcutaneous transplant tumor models, and inhibit tumor growth. Conclusion TRIP13 may be a key potential biomarker for the development and prognosis of OC. It also may be an action target of the diagnosis and treatment for OC.

title: Biomedical applications of gallic acid–metal assemblies
summary: Gallic acid (GA) is a naturally occurring polyphenolic monomer with metal-chelating and redox-active properties; however, free GA is limited by poor bioavailability, susceptibility to oxidative metabolism, and potential pro-oxidant toxicity
content: Gallic acid (GA) is a naturally occurring polyphenolic monomer with metal-chelating and redox-active properties; however, free GA is limited by poor bioavailability, susceptibility to oxidative metabolism, and potential pro-oxidant toxicity at high concentrations. The construction of GA–metal assemblies through coordination with metal ions can modulate the reactivity of phenolic hydroxyl groups, enhance in vivo stability and delivery efficiency, and confer distinctive nanoscale redox duality with tunable antioxidant and pro-oxidant behaviors. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in the application of GA–metal assemblies in precision cancer therapy, tissue repair and anti-inflammatory intervention, antibacterial and anti-infective treatment, and the management of metabolic and neurological disorders, while also outlining the molecular basis of cell-death pathways such as ferroptosis and cuproptosis, as well as immune microenvironment remodeling. Finally, perspectives are provided on key challenges, including long-term biosafety assessment, in vivo metabolic tracking, and quality standards for clinical translation.

title: Butyrate-Assisted Electrofermentation Enhances NADH Availability and Regulates Gene Expression for Improved Butanol Selectivity
summary: Sustainable biofuel production offers a pathway to reduce fossil fuel dependence while minimizing environmental impact. Low yields and competing by-products limit the industrial viability of acetone–butanol–ethanol (ABE) fermentation. This
content: Sustainable biofuel production offers a pathway to reduce fossil fuel dependence while minimizing environmental impact. Low yields and competing by-products limit the industrial viability of acetone–butanol–ethanol (ABE) fermentation. This study demonstrates precursor-assisted electrofermentation (EF) as a non-genetic strategy for redox-driven, precursor-specific control of carbon flux in Clostridium acetobutylicum ATCC-824, enabling selective butanol production via butyrate supplementation and acetone/ethanol production via acetate supplementation. Under the applied potential (–0.4 V vs. Ag/AgCl), butyrate supplementation (8 g/L) achieved a maximum butanol titer of 9.75 g/L, a 66.7% improvement over the best conventional butyrate condition (5.85 g/L), with a glucose-based yield of 0.203 g/g, productivity of 0.135 g/L/h, and 37.2% carbon recovery as solvent products. Acetate supplementation instead favored the production of acetone (2.01 g/L) and ethanol (1.88 g/L). EF enhanced intracellular reducing power, with butyrate conditions achieving an 85.8% NADH increase and a NAD+/NADH ratio reduction from 2.01 to 0.93, consistent with an accelerated acidogenic-to-solventogenic transition. Gene expression analysis showed that butyrate-EF upregulated solvent-committing and pathway genes (bdh 28.5-fold, hbd 1.94-fold, and crt 7.81-fold) while suppressing the acid-forming marker ack (0.187-fold of control). In contrast, acetate feeding instead induced adc (8.41-fold) and ack (19.21-fold), reflecting divergent metabolic commitment driven by precursor identity. Electrochemical characterization revealed distinct electron-transfer characteristics between the two precursor-supplemented systems. These findings establish precursor-specific electrofermentation as a non-genetic bioprocess intensification strategy for tunable solvent selectivity in sustainable biofuel production.

title: Forest net primary productivity responses to compound temperature–moisture anomalies vary along a hydroclimatic gradient in Northeast China
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Forest productivity responses to compound temperature–moisture anomalies vary markedly across hydroclimatic settings, revealing a clear mismatch between the climate states most commonly experienced by forests and those most strongly associa
content: Forest productivity responses to compound temperature–moisture anomalies vary markedly across hydroclimatic settings, revealing a clear mismatch between the climate states most commonly experienced by forests and those most strongly associated with negative productivity anomalies. Using a multi-source net primary productivity (NPP) record on an approximately 1-km geographic grid in Northeast China during 1985–2024, we evaluated compound climate states across a pronounced hydroclimatic gradient by distinguishing historical occurrence, conditional NPP response, backward composition, and joint occurrence. Hot–dry (HD) and cold–wet (CW) were the most frequent historical corner states based on non-detrended climate indices, with mean occurrence frequencies of 13.71% and 12.06%, respectively. In the detrended analysis, cold–dry (CD) had the highest full-domain conditional-probability point estimate for a negative NPP anomaly (58.88%), followed by CW (57.70%). Hydroclimatic background further differentiated these responses: the conditional probability of a negative NPP anomaly under HD was higher in semi-arid and semi-humid forests than in humid forests, whereas CW showed the opposite zonal ordering. Severity dependence was also state-specific: under CW, the probability of a negative NPP anomaly increased more consistently with moisture severity, whereas the severe negative tail was less uniformly ordered. HD exhibited a non-monotonic severity response. As NPP anomalies became increasingly negative, the combined backward representation of the four corner states increased from 40.62% at SNPI * < 0 to 47.66% at SNPI * < −1, with CW showing the largest joint probability in the severe negative tail (2.51%). Here, negative NPP anomalies represent low ranks of detrended residuals rather than fixed absolute productivity losses. The opposing HD/CW gradients and increasing corner-state shares recurred across the CASA-only 1985–2015 and 30- and 35-year records, although leading states and some local responses differed. Annual cross-product agreement remained weak, leaving uncertainty in the harmonized NPP record. By separating occurrence, conditional response, backward composition, and joint occurrence, these results reveal hydroclimatic contrasts in forest productivity associations that climate-state frequency alone cannot capture.

title: 2-Ferrocenyl-Phosphinine: Synthesis, Coordination Chemistry, and Properties
summary: A novel 2-ferrocenyl-phosphinine was synthesized via the [4 + 2] cycloaddition reaction between 2-pyrone and an in situ generated ferrocenyl-substituted phosphaalkyne (Fc–C≡P) under release of CO2. Comprehensive spectroscopic, crystallograp
content: A novel 2-ferrocenyl-phosphinine was synthesized via the [4 + 2] cycloaddition reaction between 2-pyrone and an in situ generated ferrocenyl-substituted phosphaalkyne (Fc–C≡P) under release of CO2. Comprehensive spectroscopic, crystallographic, electrochemical, and DFT studies establish the new phosphinine as a sterically demanding, redox-active ligand. %Vbur calculations demonstrate greater steric encumbrance compared to previously reported 2-substituted phosphinines, while coordination to Au(I), Cu(I), Rh(I), and group 6 metal precursors highlights its broad coordination versatility. The ferrocenyl substituent provides a handle for fine-tuning the electronic properties of the ligand, making this compound a promising platform for the construction of redox-switchable coordination compounds, materials, and catalysts.

title: Effect of filler geometry on the residual cure kinetics and thermal degradation of epoxy bifiller nanocomposites
summary: This study investigates the synergistic effects of SiN and MoS 2 on the mechanical and thermal behaviour stability of epoxy (EP). The hybrid nanocomposite with 0.25 wt% SiN/ 0.75 wt% MoS 2 (ESD3) exhibited increase in tensile strength, Youn
content: This study investigates the synergistic effects of SiN and MoS 2 on the mechanical and thermal behaviour stability of epoxy (EP). The hybrid nanocomposite with 0.25 wt% SiN/ 0.75 wt% MoS 2 (ESD3) exhibited increase in tensile strength, Young’s modulus, and elongation at break by 149%, 155%, and 111%, respectively, compared to the neat matrix, credited to the synergism between the nanofillers. The nanocomposite containing 0.5 wt% SiN (ES2) showed near-complete curing due to the “hotball” mechanism. In contrast, the corresponding epoxy-MoS 2 nanocomposite (ED2) displayed dual curing peaks at higher heating rates, arising from delayed curing of trapped remnants between nanosheets. The hybrid ESD3 system demonstrated improved curing over ED2, dominated by SiN. Curing kinetics analyzed using various models revealed lower residual curing in ES2. Thermal stability assessed via TGA using model-fitting and model-free approaches showed that ESD3 possessed the highest stability, confirming enhanced resistance to thermal degradation. HR-TEM confirmed uniform nanofiller dispersion and strong interfacial interaction with the matrix. The formation of ramified SiN networks may reduce Kapitza resistance, while SiN-MoS 2 synergy enhances heat transfer, thermal stability, and overall conductivity. These findings demonstrate the potential of these nanocomposites in applications requiring high-performance and thermally stable materials.

title: Europe Returns to Nuclear Power: Why Brussels Is Changing Its Energy Strategy
summary: The European Union is reconsidering the place of nuclear power in its energy strategy. The shift is driven not by a retreat from renewable energy, but by the growing importance of energy security, affordability and system reliability alongs
content: The European Union is reconsidering the place of nuclear power in its energy strategy. The shift is driven not by a retreat from renewable energy, but by the growing importance of energy security, affordability and system reliability alongside decarbonisation. This viewpoint traces the political and economic background to Europe’s earlier nuclear decline, examines the vulnerabilities revealed by the current model of the energy transition and considers the European Commission’s renewed support for nuclear power, particularly small modular reactors (SMRs). It argues that the emerging European approach is moving away from a binary choice between nuclear and renewables towards a more pragmatic combination of low-carbon technologies, grids, storage and flexible generation. At the same time, SMRs remain a technology whose economics, standardisation and waste-management implications have yet to be demonstrated at scale. Europe’s nuclear revival should therefore be understood not as a reversal of the energy transition, but as an attempt to make it more resilient. Европейский союз пересматривает место атомной энергетики в своей энергетической стратегии. Этот сдвиг связан не с отказом от возобновляемой энергетики, а с растущим значением энергетической безопасности, доступности энергии и надёжности энергосистемы наряду с декарбонизацией. В статье рассматриваются политические и экономические причины предшествующего сокращения роли атомной генерации в Европе, уязвимости нынешней модели энергоперехода и новый курс Еврокомиссии на поддержку атомной энергетики, прежде всего малых модульных реакторов (SMR). Основной тезис состоит в том, что европейский подход постепенно уходит от противопоставления атома и ВИЭ и движется к более прагматичному сочетанию низкоуглеродных технологий, сетей, накопителей и гибкой генерации. При этом экономическая эффективность, серийность и особенности обращения с отходами SMR ещё не доказаны в промышленном масштабе. Поэтому возвращение атома следует рассматривать не как отказ от энергоперехода, а как попытку сделать его более устойчивым.

title: Two-Step Chronoamperometric Sensing of Extracellular Hydrogen Peroxide from Living Cells Using a Pt Nanoparticle/ITO Electrode
summary: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is one of the most extensively studied reactive oxygen species (ROS), serving as a key redox signaling molecule involved in diverse redox-regulated cellular processes. For scalable electrochemical monitoring of extr
content: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is one of the most extensively studied reactive oxygen species (ROS), serving as a key redox signaling molecule involved in diverse redox-regulated cellular processes. For scalable electrochemical monitoring of extracellular H2O2, a submicromolar limit of detection (LOD) is required but remains challenging because background redox currents originating from the culture medium obscure the H2O2-dependent current response. Herein, we report an electrochemical H2O2 monitoring technique using a PtNP-modified indium tin oxide (ITO) electrode operated by two-step potential chronoamperometry (TCA). An anodic pretreatment step forms platinum surface oxide, which is subsequently reduced during the cathodic measurement step. This modulation of the surface oxide state enhances the H2O2-dependent response, yielding an enhanced reduction current that increases linearly with H2O2 concentration. The two-step potential modulation strategy provides robust signal amplification, achieving an LOD of 0.12 μM, which is applicable to extracellular H2O2 monitoring. The TCA-operated PtNP/ITO electrode is further applied to incubation media collected from NOX4-expressing living cells, where it reliably resolves inhibitor-dependent modulation of extracellular H2O2 levels. This work demonstrates the potential of TCA-operated PtNP/ITO electrodes for measuring extracellular H2O2 and evaluating pharmacological modulation of hydrogen peroxide secretion.

title: Geochronology and petrogenesis of high-Nb alkaline volcanic rocks from NW Neyshabour, Iran: evidence for incipient slab tearing in the Eocene
summary: K-rich alkaline volcanic rocks from northwest of Neyshabour city represent a small but important part of the Cenozoic magmatism in the Sabzevar structural zone, NE Iran. They vary in composition from trachyandesites to alkali rhyolites with
content: K-rich alkaline volcanic rocks from northwest of Neyshabour city represent a small but important part of the Cenozoic magmatism in the Sabzevar structural zone, NE Iran. They vary in composition from trachyandesites to alkali rhyolites with a dominance of trachytes. New whole-rock Ar–Ar geochronology suggests that this episode of volcanism occurred in the Middle Eocene (∼44.2 Ma) rather than Miocene as generally assumed. These volcanic rocks can be divided into three groups based on their elemental compositions: (1) the P-suite with the least differentiated trace element patterns among studied samples; (2) the A-suite with signatures of amphibole fractionation based on their low Dy/Dy* as well as decreasing Dy/Yb with SiO 2; and (3) the F-suite with signatures of feldspar fractionation based on their elevated rare earth element in addition to negative Sr and Eu anomalies. The most primitive P-suite lavas show relative enrichment in incompatible elements, such as high large-ion lithophile element and high field strength element contents and elevated Nb/Zr ratios. These characteristics and their relatively flat middle rare earth elements to heavy rare earth elements (MREE–HREE) patterns suggest that the parental magma of the P-suite likely originated from an enriched shallow lithospheric mantle source. Fractional crystallization of amphibole, feldspar and Fe–Ti oxides can account for the evolution of the A-suite lavas, whereas fractionation of a mineral assemblage dominated by feldspar and Fe-Ti oxides explains the evolution of the F-suite. Considering their close spatial and temporal association with calc-alkaline lavas and adakites in the region, we propose that this episode of alkaline volcanism could be related to the initial development of a slab window in the downgoing Neo-Tethyan Sabzevar Ocean plate in the Eocene, which induced the upwelling of the underlying asthenospheric mantle and the subsequent melting of the overlying shallow subcontinental lithospheric mantle due to heating and decompression.

title: Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: 77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic
content: 77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.

title: The Growth and Biochemical Responses of Capsicum frutescens L. (Chilli Pepper) in Soil Obtained from a Coal Mining Environment in Ugiamwen Community, Edo State, Nigeria
summary: Ugiamwen, a fertile region in Edo State, relies heavily on agriculture, and Capsicum frutescens L. (pepper) is a key economic crop. However, coal mining near farmlands has raised concerns about soil contamination and its effects on crop gro
content: Ugiamwen, a fertile region in Edo State, relies heavily on agriculture, and Capsicum frutescens L. (pepper) is a key economic crop. However, coal mining near farmlands has raised concerns about soil contamination and its effects on crop growth. This study assessed heavy metal concentrations in soils and evaluated the metal induced stress responses of C. frutescens grown under contaminated conditions. Soil samples were collected from two primary sites: coal mining soil (CMS) and adjacent farmland soil (FS), while control soil (CS) was obtained 160 m away from the mining activities. Soil physical properties and concentrations of copper (Cu), chromium (Cr), arsenic (As), and lead (Pb) were analyzed; cadmium was below the detection limit. To assess plant responses, percentage germination, plant height, leaf number, chlorophyll content, antioxidant enzyme activities, and metal accumulation in roots, stems, and leaves were determined. Results showed significantly elevated Cu concentrations in CMS and FS soils. Although, Cu was elevated, Pb, Cr, and As remained below the permissible limits established by the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment (CCME) agricultural soil quality guidelines. Lead and Cr accumulated predominantly in leaves, while Cu was higher in roots and As in stems. Germination, growth, and leaf production were markedly reduced in contaminated soils, and plants failed to fruit, unlike control plants, which flowered at 72 days after planting. Visible symptoms included chlorosis and stunted growth. Reduced chlorophyll content and increased antioxidant enzyme activities further indicated oxidative stress. Overall, mining-derived soil contamination significantly impaired the growth and productivity of C. frutescens.

title: Cost of Flexibility in NGCC-CCS Plants: Thermal Energy Storage versus Grid-Scale Battery Storage
source: University of Hertfordshire Research Archive (University of Hertfordshire)
summary: Great Britain’s transition towards a low-carbon electricity system increases the need for flexibility alongside variable renewable generation. In natural gas combined-cycle (NGCC) plants equipped with post-combustion carbon capture and stor
content: Great Britain’s transition towards a low-carbon electricity system increases the need for flexibility alongside variable renewable generation. In natural gas combined-cycle (NGCC) plants equipped with post-combustion carbon capture and storage (CCS), steam extraction for solvent regeneration couples heat demand with electrical output. This thesis compares plant-integrated thermal energy storage (TES) supplying the CCS reboiler with grid-scale lithium-ion battery energy storage systems (BESS) operating at the electrical interface. The analysis uses marginal cost of flexibility (MCF), defined as average incremental net cost per credited MWh-flex. TES flexibility is calculated from useful reboiler heat through an electrical-equivalent conversion factor; BESS flexibility is measured as AC electrical output. The study combines existing HOMER operating records with chronological storage calculations and financial assessment on an 8% real discount-rate basis over 25 years. Under the four-hour TES reference case, p40/p60 dispatch thresholds and an installed-cost assumption of £40/kWh-th, TES provides 12,776.80 MWh-flex annually at £42.91/MWh-flex. This cost includes charging opportunity cost and useful-discharge electricity value. The 100 MWh and 200 MWh headline BESS cases, each with a 50 MW converter, yield £54.41 and £58.49/MWh-flex, respectively. A separate SOC-constrained, price-responsive BESS sensitivity yields £50.13 and £59.85/MWh-flex under its own operating and accounting assumptions. With the headline BESS assumptions held fixed, TES installed-cost parity occurs at approximately £46.52/kWh-th and £48.83/kWh-th against the two respective BESS cases. TES therefore has the lower calculated reference MCF under the specified screening assumptions. The comparison remains conditional on physical integration, electrical headroom, dispatch, accounting scope and the retained price–thermal alignment limitation. An illustrative headroom restriction reverses the headline ordering. The study contributes an application of chronological storage accounting to CCS reboiler heat shifting, an installed-cost parity analysis and a comparison of the specified storage cases within explicit physical and economic boundaries.

title: Geometry-controlled meridional transport as a physical interpretation of threshold deglaciations: A 1-ODE Conceptual Model of Glacial–Interglacial Cycles
summary: We present a one-equation conceptual model of Late Pleistocene glacial–interglacial cycles, in which the position of the Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet margin evolves under orbital forcing through the competing effects of snowfall, local ins
content: We present a one-equation conceptual model of Late Pleistocene glacial–interglacial cycles, in which the position of the Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet margin evolves under orbital forcing through the competing effects of snowfall, local insolation-driven ablation, and meridional heat and moisture transport. Rather than being prescribed as jumps between discrete states, the size dependence of the deglaciation threshold emerges from the interaction between orbital forcing and a transport term that strengthens as the ice sheet expands towards lower latitudes, providing a physical interpretation of the threshold behaviour introduced phenomenologically by Paillard (1998). The moisture and heat transport terms depend on the meridional temperature gradient between the tropics and the ice-sheet margin, thereby controlling how the deglaciation threshold varies with ice-sheet size. Additional nonlinear feedbacks associated with ice-sheet retreat are represented through a history-dependent instability amplifier, reproducing the observed asymmetry between slow glaciations and rapid terminations. After calibration against the LR04 benthic oxygen-isotope stack over the last million years, the model reproduces the timing, amplitude, and irregularity of glacial cycles during the last 800 kyr, with an accuracy comparable to that of Paillard's model while providing an explicit physical interpretation of its switching mechanism. A simple time dependence of two parameters further extends the model to the last two million years and improves its representation of the Mid-Pleistocene Transition. The results suggest that enhanced meridional heat transport, driven by the amplification of the meridional temperature gradient as the ice sheet expands, may precondition glacial terminations. This mechanism could explain why even relatively weak orbital insolation peaks can trigger deglaciations when Northern Hemisphere ice sheets approach their maximum extent. Further research should focus on a deeper analytical investigation of the model equation, the separation of atmospheric and oceanic transport contributions, its coupling with simplified energy-balance and carbon-cycle equations, and the replacement of phenomenological switches with explicit physical processes. If confirmed, the proposed mechanism would provide a minimal and physically interpretable link between orbital forcing, meridional transport, and nonlinear ice-sheet dynamics throughout Quaternary glacial cycles.

title: Distance‐ and Direction‐Dependent Effects of Macroalgae on Early Epilithic Bacterial Assemblages and Coral Settlement Processes
summary: While the expansion of macroalgae on coral reefs is a global concern, the spatial scales and mechanisms through which macroalgae inhibit coral recruitment processes and the role of epilithic bacteria in coral settlement remain inadequately
content: While the expansion of macroalgae on coral reefs is a global concern, the spatial scales and mechanisms through which macroalgae inhibit coral recruitment processes and the role of epilithic bacteria in coral settlement remain inadequately understood. Using tiles preconditioned at three distances of two algal species in both up and down-current directions, we show that macroalgae shape early epilithic bacterial assemblages, with strong effects 1 cm downstream of both algae. When exposing the tiles to larvae of two coral species in ex situ settlement experiments, the coral Acropora pulchra showed reduced larval settlement on cryptic surfaces of tiles conditioned 1 cm up and downstream of the alga Dictyota bartayresiana, whereas the coral Pocillopora acuta showed the opposite pattern. Specific bacterial taxa within the families Bdellovibrionaceae, Pirellulaceae, Flavobacteriaceae and Rhodobacteraceae were associated with P. acuta settlement with differences across algal species. When tiles with coral spat were returned to their initial positions on the reef, spat survival was consistently reduced closer to, and particularly 1 cm downstream of, D. bartayresiana. These results demonstrate that macroalgae influence coral settlement and post-settlement survival at centimetre scales through distance- and flow-dependent effects and indicate that these effects may be mediated by epilithic bacterial assemblages.

title: Beyond natriuresis: NAPE-PLD as an emerging molecular target of NCC-inhibiting diuretics—mechanistic hypothesis and translational agenda in Hypertension
summary: Natriuresis through inhibition of the renal sodium-chloride cotransporter (NCC) is the established initiating mechanism of hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, and indapamide, but chronic blood-pressure lowering also reflects reduced system
content: Natriuresis through inhibition of the renal sodium-chloride cotransporter (NCC) is the established initiating mechanism of hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, and indapamide, but chronic blood-pressure lowering also reflects reduced systemic vascular resistance and drug-specific extrarenal actions. Recent structural and preclinical work identified N-acyl phosphatidylethanolamine phospholipase D (NAPE-PLD), a membrane zinc hydrolase that generates anandamide and other N-acylethanolamines, as a binding target of hydrochlorothiazide and of the chemically distinct NCC-inhibiting diuretics chlorthalidone and indapamide. Importantly, this evidence does not yet establish that clinically used doses increase anandamide in humans or that NAPE-PLD explains cardiovascular outcome benefits. Rather, it provides a testable molecular hypothesis that can be integrated with established renal and vascular mechanisms. We therefore distinguish three evidence layers: (i) clinically established NCC inhibition and natriuresis; (ii) experimentally supported drug-specific vascular effects involving potassium channels, calcium handling and Rho/Rho-kinase signaling; and (iii) the emerging NAPE-PLD/endocannabinoid hypothesis. We review the molecular architecture of NAPE-PLD, its regulation by membrane substrates and bile acids, the drug-binding interface described for hydrochlorothiazide, and the downstream biology of anandamide at CB1, CB2, TRPV1 and PPAR-related pathways. Particular attention is given to endothelial nitric oxide signaling, blood-brain barrier biology, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress and sympathetic regulation. We also propose a precision-pharmacology research framework based on drug structure, low-renin/salt-sensitive phenotype, kidney function, lipidomic endocannabinoid signatures and NAPE-PLD pharmacodynamic biomarkers. The central conclusion is deliberately conservative: NAPE-PLD is a credible newly identified molecular target of NCC-inhibiting diuretics, but the clinical importance of this interaction remains unproven and requires independent replication, human pharmacodynamic studies and prospective outcome-oriented investigation. Clinical trial registration: Not applicable.

title: Bioactive Electrospun Poly(L‐Lactic Acid) Nonwovens Enriched With Basil Essential Oil for Potential Wound‐Dressing Applications
summary: The need to improve wound management has increased interest in incorporating natural bioactive compounds into wound dressing materials. Electrospun fibers loaded with essential oils show strong potential for functional dressings, although t
content: The need to improve wound management has increased interest in incorporating natural bioactive compounds into wound dressing materials. Electrospun fibers loaded with essential oils show strong potential for functional dressings, although the use of basil essential oil (BEO) in these systems remains limited. In this study, PLLA/BEO nonwovens are produced by electrospinning, and their physicochemical properties relevant to wound dressing applications are evaluated. Incorporating BEO into PLLA increases thermal stability (up to +16°C), promotes crystal reorganization, and improves the ductility of the material. The randomly distributed nanofibers successfully encapsulate the BEO, with average diameters from 534 to 690 nm and exhibit mechanical performance comparable to or higher than that reported for commercial fibrous wound dressings. The membranes show high porosity (80%–82%), water vapor transmission rates of 741.84–960.66 g m −2 day −1, and hydrophobicity above 110°, limiting their water absorption (< 6.30%). Additionally, they display elevated surface roughness (> 0.6 μm) and adhesion forces below 1 N. The matrix maintains strong evaporative retention of BEO at 37°C (~80% at 116 h) and enables a sustained release of approximately 40%–63% in PBS during the monitored period. These findings position PLLA/BEO as a promising material for advanced wound dressings.

title: JWST NIRSpec G395H Transmission Spectra of Two Similar Sub-Neptunes in the TOI-125 System
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has enabled the first in-depth characterizations of sub-Neptune atmospheres, revealing a diversity of chemical compositions and cloud properties that challenge current models. Multiplanet systems provid
content: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has enabled the first in-depth characterizations of sub-Neptune atmospheres, revealing a diversity of chemical compositions and cloud properties that challenge current models. Multiplanet systems provide an opportunity to compare planetary atmospheres while controlling for formation conditions within the same protoplanetary disk. We present JWST NIRSpec G395H 3–5 μ m observations of two similarly sized sub-Neptunes orbiting a Sun-like star within the TOI-125 system: TOI-125 b (P = 4.65 days, R p = 2.73 R ⊕, M p = 9.5 M ⊕, T eq = 1040 K) and TOI-125 c (P = 9.15 days, R p = 2.76 R ⊕, M p = 6.7 M ⊕, T eq = 830 K), comprising one full transit of TOI-125 b but only 70% of the transit of TOI-125 c due to larger than predicted transit timing variations. We obtain precise R ∼ 100 transmission spectra for both planets, with median error bars of 50 ppm for TOI-125 b and 85 ppm for TOI-125 c. Atmospheric retrievals are compatible with a ∼150× solar metallicity atmosphere or clouds above ∼3 mbar for TOI-125 b and a ∼100× solar metallicity atmosphere or clouds above ∼10 mbar for TOI-125 c. Our results may support recent evidence for metal enrichment in sub-Neptunes, while also further complicating the proposed trend in atmospheric feature size with planet temperature. However, shorter-wavelength follow-up observations of both planets are needed to establish whether their spectra are truly muted or feature rich, with implications for the nature of sub-Neptunes around Sun-like stars.

title: Full-Length Transcriptome Profiling of Wheat to Spot Blotch across Tissues and Genotypes
summary: Background Spot blotch, caused by the hemibiotrophic fungus Bipolaris sorokiniana, is a major constraint on global wheat production. Although several resistance genes and QTLs have been identified, the transcriptional architecture of both r
content: Background Spot blotch, caused by the hemibiotrophic fungus Bipolaris sorokiniana, is a major constraint on global wheat production. Although several resistance genes and QTLs have been identified, the transcriptional architecture of both resistance and susceptibility-particularly its organ specificity and post-transcriptional complexity-remains poorly resolved. Full-length transcriptome profiling across multiple tissues and genetic backgrounds carrying different resistance loci is therefore required to distinguish passive failure of defence from active, pathogen-exploitable susceptibility programmes. Results In this study, we generated the first multi-tissue Oxford Nanopore full-length transcriptome atlas of the wheat- B. sorokiniana interaction by sequencing leaves, leaf sheaths and glumes of the resistant-susceptible pair ZS54 (R)/ZS57 (S) and integrating an independent leaf transcriptome dataset from a second pair (ZS31/ZS3, R/S) that carries different resistance loci. High-quality long-read data identified 6,996 novel genes and 11,072 novel isoforms, many of which were enriched in plant-pathogen interaction pathways. Differential expression analysis revealed a conserved susceptibility signature characterised by systemic down-regulation of photosynthesis (Calvin cycle, antenna proteins and chloroplast components) accompanied by hyperactivation of Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signalling, plant-pathogen interaction, phenylpropanoid and glutathione metabolism, and cell-wall catabolism. Tissue-resolved responses were distinct: sheaths emphasised cell-wall reinforcement and redox processes, leaves showed carbon mobilisation and lipid degradation, and glumes activated secondary metabolism and energy pathways. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified organ-specific modules tightly correlated with disease severity and nominated hub genes encoding a xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase, a pentatricopeptide-repeat protein and a PPPDE thiol peptidase. Comparison confirmed that, despite the different chromosomal locations of the resistance loci, both resistant lines (ZS54 and ZS31) exhibited coordinated transcriptional reinforcement of chloroplast structure, photosynthetic machinery and related stress-response processes under fungal challenge. In contrast, photosynthetic collapse and unproductive defence hyperactivation, including HR/ROS programmes that benefit the necrotroph, were shared susceptibility features, while residual flavonoid and structural capacity modulated quantitative disease severity. Conclusions Although the resistance loci of these two pairs of materials are located on different chromosomes, the core transcriptional programmes are largely shared. Resistant genotypes maintain coordinated reinforcement of chloroplast structure and photosynthetic machinery, consistent with a protective acclimation that preserves tissue integrity, whereas susceptible genotypes exhibit photosynthetic collapse accompani

title: Source‐Sink Structures Shape Global Drought Propagation
summary: The spatial propagation of drought plays a critical role in shaping synchronized global drought occurrences. As hubs (sources and sinks) for drought propagation, the global role of sources and sinks has not been thoroughly assessed. Identif
content: The spatial propagation of drought plays a critical role in shaping synchronized global drought occurrences. As hubs (sources and sinks) for drought propagation, the global role of sources and sinks has not been thoroughly assessed. Identifying key propagation hotspots and tracing their global pathways is essential for understanding how droughts evolve over time and space. Here, five paired drought source (location that droughts move from)‐sink (region where droughts are more likely to propagate to) systems at the continental scale are identified: western Congo Basin‐eastern Congo Basin, Sahel and savanna regions‐Sahara Desert, Labrador Peninsula‐Great Plains, Amazon Plain‐Brazilian Plateau, Tarim Basin and Tianshan Mountain‐Central Siberian Plateau, Stanovoy Range, Yangtze River Basin, Middle East. Analyzing water vapor budget between sources and sinks reveals a pattern of drought propagation from sources to sinks, contrasting with water vapor moving in the opposite path. This exacerbates drought severity in drought sinks, a trend likely to intensify under future scenarios with increased radiative forcing. This study identifies a drought source‐sink structure, providing a new perspective on large‐scale drought spatial propagation. These offer critical insights for drought early warning and mitigation strategies across regions.
