title: Nationwide mapping of mangrove EWT and LMA in China using universal sensitive subdomains and Bayesian-optimized machine learning models
summary: Mangroves support global carbon cycling and biodiversity. Leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) and leaf mass per area (LMA), core functional traits, are vital ecological monitoring indicators. Yet vague spectral response mechanisms hamper
content: Mangroves support global carbon cycling and biodiversity. Leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) and leaf mass per area (LMA), core functional traits, are vital ecological monitoring indicators. Yet vague spectral response mechanisms hamper precise, stable large-scale remote sensing inversion. This study constructed a national sensitive spectral screening framework based on 1023 plots and 102,300 full-spectrum field data across China’s mangrove zones. Combining spectral clustering and cross-regional meta-analysis, we used group-differential gradient perturbation two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (GDGP-2D-COS) and Bayesian optimization to extract sensitive bands and identify regional optimal wavelengths and universal sensitive subdomains. We further developed 120 inversion strategies to generate high-resolution national maps of mangrove EWT and LMA across China. Our results reveal universal sensitive subdomains cover 795–878 nm, 968–975 nm, 1735–1765 nm, and 2021–2050 nm; LMA lies in the red edge and SWIR regions: 729–765 nm, 1564–1672 nm, and 1978–1990 nm. Four machine-learning verifications prove that regional and universal bands yield robust accuracy: EWT R 2 = 0.620–0.965, LMA R 2 = 0.504–0.908. Tested on Sentinel-2 and ZY-1 02E data, universal sensitive spectral subdomains remain steady (EWT R 2 = 0.506–0.965; LMA R 2 = 0.444–0.848). China’s mangrove EWT is 0.205–0.550 kg/m2 and LMA 0.06–0.214 kg/m2, matching ecological benchmarks. This work supplies scientific and technical support for mangrove carbon sink assessment, targeted ecosystem management and sustainable conservation.

title: Rehabilitasi Ekosistem Pesisir melalui Penanaman Mangrove dan Kegiatan Bersih Pantai di Pantai Pasir Jambak, Kota Padang
source: Agrokreatif Jurnal Ilmiah Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat
summary: Pasir Jambak Beach, Padang City, is facing increasing environmental degradation due to coastal erosion, mangrove ecosystem deterioration, and the accumulation of coastal waste. A preliminary field assessment conducted over an area of approx
content: Pasir Jambak Beach, Padang City, is facing increasing environmental degradation due to coastal erosion, mangrove ecosystem deterioration, and the accumulation of coastal waste. A preliminary field assessment conducted over an area of approximately 5,000 m² identified around 540 kg of coastal waste, predominantly consisting of wood debris (52%) and plastic waste (17%). In addition, the pre-test results indicated that community knowledge regarding the ecological functions of mangroves, coastal waste management, and environmental conservation was at a moderate level, with an average score of approximately 50%. This community service program aimed to enhance community knowledge and participation while supporting coastal ecosystem rehabilitation through an integrated approach combining environmental education, beach clean-up activities, mangrove planting, and collaboration among higher education institutions, local communities, and the private sector through a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program. The program involved 75 participants and consisted of environmental awareness sessions, mangrove planting training, beach clean-up activities, the planting of 1,230 Rhizophora spp. seedlings, and a three-month monitoring program. Program effectiveness was evaluated using pre-test and post-test assessments, field observations, and seedling survival analysis. The results demonstrated improvements across all knowledge indicators following the educational activities. A total of 540 kg of coastal waste was collected, while monitoring revealed that 960 out of 1,230 planted seedlings survived, resulting in a seedling survival rate of 78.05%. The integrated approach, which combines ecosystem rehabilitation with community empowerment through environmental education and multi-stakeholder collaboration, effectively strengthened community participation in coastal conservation while supporting sustainable mangrove rehabilitation.

title: Canopy morphology and plant biomass exert decoupled seasonal control over sediment organic carbon storage in tropical seagrass meadows
summary: Introduction Seagrass meadows are among the most effective blue carbon sinks globally; however, the relationships between plant functional traits and sediment organic carbon (SOC) storage remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, we
content: Introduction Seagrass meadows are among the most effective blue carbon sinks globally; however, the relationships between plant functional traits and sediment organic carbon (SOC) storage remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, we quantified plant biomass and canopy morphological traits in two Enhalus acoroides meadows on Hainan Island, China, during the dry and rainy seasons, and assessed their associations with SOC density using partial correlation, variance partitioning and partial least squares path modeling. Results Plant biomass showed a net negative association with SOC density (standardized total associations of -0.75 and -0.63 in the rainy and dry seasons), whereas canopy morphological traits, specifically shoot density and leaf length, were positively associated with SOC storage (0.57 and 0.59). These opposing associations followed seasonally differing pathways: biomass was consistently associated with SOC through sediment redox properties, whereas morphology was associated with SOC through sediment properties in the rainy season and through the organic carbon deposition rate in the dry season. Discussion These patterns are consistent with enhanced mineralization associated with high biomass and with particle trapping associated with dense canopies, although the underlying mechanisms were not directly measured and remain to be tested experimentally. Our findings indicate that canopy morphological traits, rather than biomass, are the principal statistical predictors of SOC storage in these meadows, and suggest that incorporating such traits may improve blue carbon assessment.

title: Biofilms, persistence and reservoirs: interconnected drivers of antibiotic resistance, with a focus on Enterobacterales and other Gram-negative pathogens
source: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
summary: Antibiotic resistance and bacterial survival during treatment in Enterobacterales and other Gram-negative pathogens are shaped by interconnected genetic, physiological, community, and ecological processes. In this review, we examine biofilm
content: Antibiotic resistance and bacterial survival during treatment in Enterobacterales and other Gram-negative pathogens are shaped by interconnected genetic, physiological, community, and ecological processes. In this review, we examine biofilms as structured communities that combine growth limitation, matrix-mediated protection, and enhanced horizontal gene transfer, thereby increasing tolerance and facilitating the selection and maintenance of resistance determinants. We then discuss bacterial persistence and stress-response networks, including toxin-antitoxin systems, the (p)ppGpp stringent response, SOS signaling, and envelope stress pathways, that contribute to phenotypic heterogeneity and the survival of non-growing or slow-growing subpopulations during bactericidal treatment without classical resistance mutations. Building on these foundations, we synthesize emerging metabolic, regulatory, structural, and non-canonical mechanisms that extend beyond canonical efflux, target modification, and enzymatic drug inactivation, including metabolic and redox rewiring, proteostasis-linked stress management, small regulatory RNAs and global transcriptional regulators, peptidoglycan remodeling, L-form switching, de novo resistance-conferring peptides arising from non-coding DNA, and the effects of abiotic and physical factors such as pollutants, microplastics, and microgravity. Finally, we place these processes within a One Health framework by highlighting environmental, animal, and host-associated reservoirs that maintain and disseminate resistant organisms and resistance determinants. Together, the evidence reviewed indicates that resistance gene acquisition, physiological heterogeneity, community architecture, and ecological context jointly shape antimicrobial responses and the long-term maintenance of multidrug-resistant populations, underscoring the need to integrate resistance, tolerance, and persistence into surveillance, diagnostics, and therapeutic design.

title: Estimated potential soil CO₂ and N₂O emission dynamics along a narrow elevational gradient in a warm- temperate coastal forest
summary: Soil greenhouse gas emissions may vary across short elevational gradients, but their controls remain unclear in humid coastal forests. We investigated soils from three elevations in a warm-temperate forest of Kunyu Mountain, China (217, 302
content: Soil greenhouse gas emissions may vary across short elevational gradients, but their controls remain unclear in humid coastal forests. We investigated soils from three elevations in a warm-temperate forest of Kunyu Mountain, China (217, 302 and 411 m). Laboratory incubations were used to derive Q 10 values for CO 2 and N 2 O emissions, which were combined with field meteorological data and moisture correction functions to estimate monthly, seasonal and annual emissions. Redundancy analysis was then used to identify soil factors associated with emission variation. Annual mean potential CO 2 emission rates declined significantly with elevation, with rates at the low-elevation site 83.8% and 241.0% higher than those at the middle- and high-elevation sites, respectively. CO 2 emissions were higher in the growing season than in the non-growing season at all elevations, and the seasonal increase was strongest at the high-elevation site. In contrast, annual mean N 2 O emission rates did not differ significantly among elevations, although high-elevation soils emitted more N 2 O than middle-elevation soils during the middle and late growing season. Carbon-normalized CO 2 -C emission intensity decreased with elevation, whereas nitrogen-normalized N 2 O-N loss intensity was highest at high elevation, about four times that at middle elevation. Redundancy analysis identified soil pH as the strongest independent explanatory factor for CO 2 emissions (65.9%, P = 0.01) and soil total nitrogen stock as the main factor for N 2 O emissions (50.2%, P = 0.02). These findings suggest that soil properties, substrate availability, stand characteristics and microclimate, rather than temperature alone, shape soil greenhouse gas emissions along narrow elevational gradients.

title: The multidimensional roles of branched-chain amino acids in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a precision medicine perspective from metabolic imprint to effect amplifier
summary: The global epidemic of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has prompted the academic community to continually explore early-warning biomarkers and core pathogenic mechanisms. In recent years, elevated circulating levels of branched-chain amino
content: The global epidemic of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has prompted the academic community to continually explore early-warning biomarkers and core pathogenic mechanisms. In recent years, elevated circulating levels of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and their metabolic intermediates were demonstrated to show an independent and robust positive correlation with the risk of developing T2DM. Following the logical thread of “phenotypic association–mechanistic exploration–causal interrogation–repositioning–translational application,” this review summarizes relevant prospective cohort studies and molecular mechanistic investigations. BCAAs and their metabolic derivatives (such as branched-chain α-keto acids and acylcarnitines) not only exhibit superior early-warning value, but also may actively contribute to the pathological progression of T2DM by hyperactivating the mTORC1 pathway to block insulin signaling, inducing mitochondrial dysfunction and ectopic lipid deposition, disrupting the gut microbiota barrier, and perturbing one-carbon metabolism–mediated epigenetic modifications. Facing recent conflicts regarding the causal relationship between the two, this review breaks away from traditional unidirectional or bidirectional parallel etiologic paradigms. It proposes an integrative conceptual framework that repositions the role of BCAAs in T2DM as both a “metabolic imprint” that integrates diverse upstream metabolic impairments and a potential “effect amplifier” that may aggravate downstream metabolic dysfunction under specific conditions. Based on this new conceptual framework, we further evaluate recent progress and clinical bottlenecks in moderate dietary BCAA restriction and pharmacological interventions targeting BCAA catabolism. Finally, from the dimensions of tissue-specific metabolism, microbiota–host interactions, potential epigenetic regulatory mechanisms, and multi-dimensional real-time monitoring, this review outlines future directions for personalized precision nutrition and intervention management in T2DM.

title: Hydrodynamic compartmentalization of a late Ediacaran mixed carbonate–siliciclastic ramp in the Tamengo Formation, Brazil
summary: Mixed carbonate–siliciclastic ramps preserve pronounced environmental heterogeneity generated by interactions among carbonate production, siliciclastic input, storm reworking, and microbial stabilization. However, how changes in relative ac
content: Mixed carbonate–siliciclastic ramps preserve pronounced environmental heterogeneity generated by interactions among carbonate production, siliciclastic input, storm reworking, and microbial stabilization. However, how changes in relative accommodation shaped lateral facies variability, and how depositional and stratigraphic processes controlled the preservation of terminal Ediacaran benthic assemblages, remain poorly constrained. The upper Ediacaran Tamengo Formation of west-central Brazil offers an opportunity to investigate these relationships through its record of Cloudina, microbialites, and regionally documented Corumbella within a storm-influenced mixed carbonate–siliciclastic succession. We integrate microfacies analysis, sedimentary structures, facies architecture, and stratigraphic relationships from key outcrops and two drill cores to reconstruct its depositional evolution. Fifteen microfacies, grouped into four facies associations, record muddy and microbial carbonate deposition, oolitic accumulation, storm reworking, and fine-grained mixed sedimentation. Their vertical and lateral distribution supports a low-gradient ramp with recurrent ooid-rich complexes, lower-energy sectors, and storm-generated event beds. Within a broader transgressive–regressive succession, transgressive erosion and migration of depositional belts reworked earlier deposits; a laterally variable maximum flooding interval expanded shale-rich and other fine-grained facies; and subsequent progradation brought renewed oolitic accumulation and storm-generated shell-rich beds. Sheltered, lower-energy settings likely developed through the combined influence of inherited paleotopography, coastal embayment geometry, accommodation, sediment supply, and fair-weather circulation. At the same time, ooid-rich complexes may have locally accentuated hydrodynamic gradients and facies partitioning. Storms redistributed intraclasts, ooids, and skeletal debris, producing tempestites with reworked Cloudina. Original occurrence, transport, burial, and preservation therefore followed partly independent pathways. Microbial accretion depended on substrate stability and remained susceptible to erosion before early lithification, whereas biomineralized Cloudina skeletons could remain recognizable after storm reworking. As depositional environments shifted through successive systems tracts, stratigraphic evolution created distinct preservation windows: transgressive erosion reworked earlier deposits, maximum flooding expanded fine-grained settings favorable to burial and preservation, and subsequent progradation renewed storm reworking and the accumulation of shell-rich deposits. The Tamengo succession thus illustrates how facies heterogeneity and stratigraphic architecture jointly controlled where benthic remains were recorded and how they were preserved within terminal Ediacaran mixed carbonate–siliciclastic systems.

title: Sources and Apportionment of Organic Matter in Former Spartina alterniflora Wetlands of Jiaozhou Bay, China: Evidence from n-Alkanes and Carbon Isotopes
source: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
summary: Coastal wetlands are long-term carbon sinks, and the eradication of the invasive C4 cordgrass Spartina alterniflora is reshaping carbon cycling in these ecosystems, yet the present-day sources of sedimentary organic matter (OM) after eradic
content: Coastal wetlands are long-term carbon sinks, and the eradication of the invasive C4 cordgrass Spartina alterniflora is reshaping carbon cycling in these ecosystems, yet the present-day sources of sedimentary organic matter (OM) after eradication remain poorly resolved. In a wetland of Jiaozhou Bay, China, we collected 21 surface-sediment samples along seven land-to-sea transects one year after eradication and combined n-alkane biomarkers with TOC/TN, C/N and δ13C to apportion OM sources. A δ13C two-end-member model conditional on a negligible C4 (Spartina-type) input, supported by all δ13C values lying far from the C4 signature, attributes 76.3~91.1% (mean 85.9%) of bulk OM to marine phytoplankton and 8.9~23.7% (mean 14.1%) to C3 plants. A Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis shows that this marine dominance is robust within the assumed end-member distributions and model structure, conditional on the assumed absence of a C4 contribution (marine fraction > 50% in 96% of accepted scenarios), but the precise fraction depends on the assumed end-members; an assumed 10% C4 input would lower the marine estimate to ~67%. An n-alkane three-end-member model resolves the modeled n-alkane pool into terrestrial leaf waxes (mean 67.6%), marine sources (mean 31.3%) and aquatic plants (mean 1.1%). These results establish the present-day spatial organization of OM sources rather than a temporal trajectory; repeated sampling is needed to quantify change attributable to eradication.

title: A Process-Based Model of Individual Leaf Development and Storage Root Growth in Autumn-Sown Radish (Raphanus sativus L.)
summary: Radish (Raphanus sativus L.) is one of the major vegetables supporting a stable food supply in Korea, yet process-based crop models for this crop remain scarce.We developed an autumn-sown radish model in Cropbox that links individual leaf d
content: Radish (Raphanus sativus L.) is one of the major vegetables supporting a stable food supply in Korea, yet process-based crop models for this crop remain scarce.We developed an autumn-sown radish model in Cropbox that links individual leaf development in response to temperature with canopy assimilation, dry matter production, and allocation between the shoot and a combined root pool.Observations of individual processes collected in walk-in chambers and temperature gradient houses from 2018 to 2024 supported parameter estimation and component evaluation.Leaf number and total leaf area were evaluated with observations excluded from their respective fitting objectives, and shoot and root dry weights were calibrated with two autumn sowings from 2020 and evaluated with a 2024 crop.Agreement was stronger for total leaf area than for its distribution among ranks, while aggregate dry weight errors were lower in the cross-year evaluation than in calibration.These results support simulations of leaf development and biomass accumulation in autumn radish, with broader yield and environmental response applications requiring evaluation under additional growing conditions.

title: Effects of rootstock and biochar-based soil amendments on soil-plant carbon and water dynamics in a mediterranean vineyard
summary: In this study, a field trial was conducted on Malvazija istarska grafted onto SO4 and 420A rootstocks, over two growing seasons, 2021 and 2022. Five treatments were evaluated as soil amendments: biochar produced from grapevine pruning resid
content: In this study, a field trial was conducted on Malvazija istarska grafted onto SO4 and 420A rootstocks, over two growing seasons, 2021 and 2022. Five treatments were evaluated as soil amendments: biochar produced from grapevine pruning residues by Kon-Tiki flame-curtain pyrolysis (B), urea-enriched biochar produced the same way but quenched with 5% urea solution (BU), shredded pruning residues (R), organic fertilizer (O), and unamended control (C). B was applied at a rate of 1.2 t ha -1, corresponding to the amount obtainable from the vineyard’s own annual pruning residues. This approach aligned the application rate with on-site biomass availability, in contrast to the substantially higher rates (9–50 t ha -1) used in many previous studies. In a circular economy context, such rates present a major constraint, as internal vineyard pruning residues are insufficient, requiring external biomass that disrupts the closed-loop principle and increases the carbon footprint. Treatment and rootstock effects on soil CO 2 flux, soil volumetric water content, leaf net CO 2 assimilation, leaf water potential, and yield per vine were assessed across seven phenological stages. Responses at both soil and leaf levels were strongly dependent on rootstock and phenological stage, with treatment effects on soil CO 2 flux, soil volumetric water content, and leaf water potential frequently differing between years. Despite this variability, B application resulted in the highest yield per vine for both rootstocks in both seasons, while SO4 generally outyielded 420A. These findings indicate that the effects of B on soil and plant water relations are contingent on rootstock type and seasonal conditions, whereas the positive effect of grapevine-pruning-residue B on yield was consistent across contrasting seasons. In a rainfed Terra Rossa vineyard in Istria, biochar applied at 1.2 t ha - ¹, a rate achievable using the vineyard’s own pruning residues, consistently increased total yield in Malvazija istarska grafted onto SO4 and 420A rootstocks during the 2021 and 2022 growing seasons. As yield components and fruit composition were not measured, the implications of this increase for yield formation and fruit quality should be further investigated. Multi-site and longer-term trials are therefore needed before broader recommendations can be made.

title: Burn Severity Shapes Post‐Fire Methane Uptake in European Boreal Forest Soils
summary: Forest fires are increasing in frequency and severity across boreal regions, yet their long‐term impact on soil methane (CH 4) fluxes remains uncertain. Understanding the conditions that govern post‐fire CH 4 dynamics is critical for projec
content: Forest fires are increasing in frequency and severity across boreal regions, yet their long‐term impact on soil methane (CH 4) fluxes remains uncertain. Understanding the conditions that govern post‐fire CH 4 dynamics is critical for projecting fire‐climate feedbacks in northern forest ecosystems. Fire severity alters soil microclimate, organic horizons, physiochemistry, and microbial function, yet severity‐resolved evidence from European boreal forests remains scarce. We measured CH 4 fluxes over 28 months following prescribed burns in Scots pine‐dominated forests in Finland. Fire severity, quantified via field assessments and remote sensing, emerged as a key driver of post‐fire CH 4 uptake. Low‐severity burns had greater CH 4 uptake than unburned areas, resulting in an estimated 46% higher cumulative uptake over the first two growing seasons. In contrast, uptake in higher‐severity burns was comparable to that in unburned areas. Maximum uptake occurred after approximately 0.3–0.4 cm of organic‐horizon consumption, consistent with improved gas transport following limited removal of the surface organic layer, whereas uptake declined with greater organic‐horizon consumption. Across the severity gradient, warmer and drier soils increased CH 4 uptake. Hierarchical partitioning showed that soil moisture and temperature together accounted for 81.5% of the variance explained by model predictors, whereas residual organic‐horizon depth and canopy mortality accounted for 17% and time since fire for 1.5%. Our findings demonstrate that post‐fire CH 4 uptake depends on fire severity and associated soil environmental conditions rather than on fire occurrence alone. Accounting for fire severity and soil environmental responses should improve predictions of post‐fire CH 4 dynamics in boreal ecosystems.

title: Mowing shifts the late-season carbon trajectory without changing the atmospheric control of mid-summer uptake in a temperate meadow steppe
summary: Background Temperate grasslands are widely mown for hay, yet it is unclear whether mowing changes only the seasonal trajectory of their carbon exchange or also the environmental controls that shape it. We compared an annually mowed meadow s
content: Background Temperate grasslands are widely mown for hay, yet it is unclear whether mowing changes only the seasonal trajectory of their carbon exchange or also the environmental controls that shape it. We compared an annually mowed meadow steppe with a fenced control, using one eddy covariance tower per treatment, over 2019–2022. Results Both meadow steppes showed a mid-summer depression of gross primary production (GPP) that coincided with the annual maximum in vapour pressure deficit (VPD). Path models gave negative VPD coefficients on GPP in both treatments (-0.35 mowed and − 0.29 fenced) and negligible direct coefficients of soil water content, even though the mowed meadow steppe held 14.5–22 percentage points more surface soil water in every year. The fenced meadow steppe was unimodal in all four years, whereas the mowed meadow steppe produced a second late-season maximum in two of four years, in both cases before the harvest date. Growing-season GPP was 31–71% higher in the fenced meadow steppe, and its growing-season carbon sink was 1.3–2.1 times larger; the contrast persisted annually, with a fenced annual sink 1.3–2.9 times that of the mowed meadow steppe in 2019–2022. Soil temperature was the strongest positive control on both GPP and respiration. Conclusions Mowing shifted the late-season trajectory and reduced the growing-season carbon sink, but it did not change the atmospheric control of mid-summer uptake or impose a soil-water constraint at this site. Because each treatment is monitored by one tower, these are site-level contrasts without formal treatment inference, but the annual sink was consistently larger in the fenced meadow steppe in all four years.

title: Modelling reversible sorption as a mechanism for contaminant release from resuspended sediment
summary: The contamination of lake and river beds is partially driven by sorption, a process in which contaminants adhere to sediment. In this paper, a coupled sediment-contaminant transport model is developed in which sorption is modelled with a fi
content: The contamination of lake and river beds is partially driven by sorption, a process in which contaminants adhere to sediment. In this paper, a coupled sediment-contaminant transport model is developed in which sorption is modelled with a first-order kinetic reaction term. The model accounts for exchanges between surface water and an underlying sediment bed through turbulent diffusive fluxes and is validated against laboratory experiments. The model introduces two key dimensionless parameters: the ratio of sorption to sediment suspension time scales (upper Gamma Γ $\operatorname {\varGamma }$), and the ratio of the contaminant and sediment diffusivities (upper D D $\operatorname {\mathit{D}}$). One-dimensional numerical simulations of the erosion of a contaminated sediment layer are used to investigate the influence of the dimensionless parameters, the initial conditions and the volume of eroded sediment. The value of upper Gamma Γ $\operatorname {\varGamma }$ is found to determine the relative importance of desorption and fluxes across the sediment–water interface to increasing the dissolved contaminant concentration in the surface water. The proportion of the dissolved contaminant concentration released into the surface water via desorption is found to depend on the contaminant concentrations in the underlying sediment bed in addition to upper Gamma Γ $\operatorname {\varGamma }$. A three-dimensional simulation of channel flow over bedforms illustrates the applicability of our one-dimensional results to higher-dimensional systems. This work concludes with a demonstration of the model applicability to a broad range of problems.

title: Mild spring frost compromise subsequent dehydration tolerance in more tolerant subtropical forestry species
summary: East Asian forests increasingly face combined spring frost and autumn drought within a single growing season, yet spring frost effects on subsequent drought responses remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that spring frost would negativ
content: East Asian forests increasingly face combined spring frost and autumn drought within a single growing season, yet spring frost effects on subsequent drought responses remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that spring frost would negatively affect subsequent dehydration tolerance (indicated by stem water potential at stomatal closure, Ψstem-close), and that this negative effect would be more pronounced in species with greater baseline dehydration tolerance (more negative baseline Ψstem-close). To test these hypotheses, we subjected seven subtropical evergreen woody species to simulated spring frost followed by extreme autumn drought. We examined hydraulic and carbon-related traits relative to frost-induced deviation in autumn Ψstem-close to uncover underlying mechanisms. Our results showed that mild spring frost, even without visible defoliation, significantly elevated autumn Ψstem-close across the seven species overall. At the species level, this effect was significant in three out of the four dehydration-tolerant species studied. Counterintuitively, while greater non-structural carbohydrate (NSC) reserves and less strict stomatal regulation were typically associated with greater dehydration tolerance, these same adaptive traits rendered plants more susceptible to frost-induced elevation in autumn Ψstem-close and thus more vulnerable to autumn drought. This increased vulnerability was likely associated with slow NSC mobilization, and was manifested through delayed post-frost root biomass accumulation and accelerated chlorophyll degradation during drought. Collectively, our findings demonstrated that mild spring frost can selectively undermine the hydraulic advantages of dehydration-tolerant species. Planting schedules that decouple frost and drought exposure, such as outplanting in November-December after the summer-autumn drought period has passed, may help mitigate this vulnerability.

title: Anaerobic Oxidation of Methane Couples Sulfide Generation Promotes Mercury Sequestration in Gas Hydrate Sediments
summary: The deep sea constitutes the largest marine mercury (Hg) reservoir on Earth, with gas hydrate‐cold seep systems emerging as critical, yet poorly constrained, hotspots for Hg cycling. While these systems host intense microbial activity and s
content: The deep sea constitutes the largest marine mercury (Hg) reservoir on Earth, with gas hydrate‐cold seep systems emerging as critical, yet poorly constrained, hotspots for Hg cycling. While these systems host intense microbial activity and sulfide production that drive Hg methylation, demethylation and sequestration, the specific migration, transformation, and speciation of Hg within gas hydrate sediments remain elusive. Here, we present a systematic geochemical analysis of W19 drill core during the GMGS3 expedition from the Shenhu area, South China Sea to address this gap. The results reveal pronounced Hg enrichment (up to 122.0 ng/g) at the fossil sulfate‐methane transition (SMT), tightly coupled with enrichments of sulfur and sulfophilic trace elements (e.g., Mo, Sb, and As). Sequential leaching demonstrates that Hg is predominantly sequestered as highly insoluble Hg‐sulfide precipitation derived from anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM), with this authigenic sulfide fraction accounting for up to 94.1% of the total Hg pool. Additionally, elevated Fe/Al ratio, Hg content, and Mo enrichment factor (Mo EF) indicate Hg release driven by the reductive dissolution of iron‐manganese oxyhydroxides. Crucially, this sulfide‐mediated sequestration effectively arrests Hg(II) migration, and may simultaneously suppress microbial mercury methylation, identifying gas hydrate‐cold seep systems as previously unrecognized geochemical Hg barriers in the deep sea. These finding fundamentally advances the understanding of geogenic Hg fate in marine sediments and anticipating how climate driven destabilization of hydrate reservoirs may alter deep‐sea Hg mobilization pathways under future warming scenarios.

title: Unmanaged waste as an outcome of expanding sub-Saharan cities
summary: Unmanaged waste poses growing environmental and public health risks across rapidly urbanising cities, yet its drivers remain poorly understood. In this study, we undertake a multi-scale spatial analysis of unmanaged waste across ten cities
content: Unmanaged waste poses growing environmental and public health risks across rapidly urbanising cities, yet its drivers remain poorly understood. In this study, we undertake a multi-scale spatial analysis of unmanaged waste across ten cities in sub-Saharan Africa. We show that unmanaged waste consistently concentrates at infrastructure-deficit urban stress points. Population density, economic gradients and urban morphology establish the broad conditions for waste presence, whereas service accessibility, road hierarchy and settlement informality determine where waste accumulates locally. Urban morphology remains influential across scales, shaping both the likelihood of waste presence and accumulation size. We find that growth trajectories, coupled with infrastructure-deficit, produce distinct spatial patterns of waste. High-growth cities exhibit small and fragmented waste sites, whereas more established systems exhibit fewer, larger and spatially consolidated sites. Our results suggest that waste management interventions should prioritise dense urban peripheries characterised by small building footprints and narrow spacing. Expanding waste service provision within these areas could help address persistent unmanaged waste.

title: Low overlap between bacterial and viral communities in meltwater and sediments of ice rise cryoconites
summary: Cryoconite microbial communities are regulated by viruses and a wide range of functional genes linked to cold adaptation, yet interactions between sediment- and water-associated communities remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the
content: Cryoconite microbial communities are regulated by viruses and a wide range of functional genes linked to cold adaptation, yet interactions between sediment- and water-associated communities remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the microbial, viral, and functional diversity of meltwater and sediments from cryoconites on the Ward Hunt Ice Rise of the Last Ice Area. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed to assess microbial and viral biodiversity, while antibiotic resistance genes, virus-host matching and antiviral defense systems served as proxies for microbial interactions. Cryoconite holes host strongly compartmentalized microbial assemblages with contrasting diversity patterns. Bacteria, including filamentous Cyanobacteria and Actinomycetes, were more diverse in sediment, whereas eukaryotes such as dinophytes, green algae and rotifers were more diverse in meltwater. Viruses followed host patterns, with bacteriophages (Caudoviricetes) dominating sediment and giant viruses (Nucleocytoviricota) more prevalent in meltwater. Sediment communities also exhibited greater diversity of antibiotic resistance genes. These results demonstrate that meltwater and sediment aggregates from cryoconites support distinct biological communities and provide an initial baseline for future spatial and temporal comparisons.

title: A Comparative Chemical Evaluation of Immune modulation Nutritional Components in Commercial Broiler Finisher Feeds in Al-Bayda City, Libya
summary: The Eastern Libyan coast features a unique convergence of hyper-arid desert solar irradiance and the cooler thermodynamic sink of the Mediterranean Sea. This paper presents a novel thermodynamic configuration leveraging a closed-loop superc
content: The Eastern Libyan coast features a unique convergence of hyper-arid desert solar irradiance and the cooler thermodynamic sink of the Mediterranean Sea. This paper presents a novel thermodynamic configuration leveraging a closed-loop supercritical Ammonia Gas Cycle (AGC) integrated with Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) and concentrated solar-thermal power (CSP). Ammonia (NH3) presents exceptional thermodynamic properties, including a low boiling point (-33.34°C) and high latent heat, making it an ideal working fluid for low-to-medium temperature differential harvesting. This study models an optimized multi-stage organic Rankine cycle using ammonia to bridge the diurnal thermal delta of the Tobruk-Derna maritime corridor. The proposed framework demonstrates a net efficiency enhancement of 14.2% compared to conventional steam-rankine systems under identical coastal atmospheric constraints, while providing a zero-carbon pathway for regional grid stabilization and co-generated desalinated water

title: Alterations of microbial life footprint enhance carbon stabilization under pH amelioration
summary: Abstract1. Amelioration of soil pH extremes is widely recognized as a foundational intervention for promoting soil organic carbon stabilization; however, the underlying mechanisms by which pH amelioration enhances stabilized soil organic ca
content: Abstract1. Amelioration of soil pH extremes is widely recognized as a foundational intervention for promoting soil organic carbon stabilization; however, the underlying mechanisms by which pH amelioration enhances stabilized soil organic carbon remain unclear.2. Using a 7-year field trial conducted on plots with a homogenized soil background (initial soil pH 8.44) and four organic amendment treatments (biochar, chicken manure, kitchen waste-derived organic material, and straw), we statistically adjusted for differences in inorganic nitrogen inputs and tracked the temporal trajectories of soil organic carbon responses to pH amelioration. All effect sizes were calculated relative to the chicken manure treatment, as soil pH changed relatively slowly under this treatment.3. Soil pH amelioration was accompanied by a 10.6% increase in mineral-associated organic carbon and a 55.5% increase in microbial necromass carbon. These carbon responses were underpinned by a reconstructed microbial life footprint: bacterial and fungal biomass increased by 66.5% and 95.2%, respectively, the Gram-positive:Gram-negative bacteria ratio decreased by 40.9%, and the microbial stress indicator was attenuated by 87.1%. Enzymatic activities also showed a functional shift, with cellobiohydrolase activity increasing but β-glucosidase activity decreased under pH amelioration. These microbial and enzymatic alterations were further accompanied by increases in microaggregate proportion (3.0%) and microaggregate-associated carbon (5.9%), suggestive of local coupling between microbial processes and physical carbon protection. Over the course of the trial, the pH amelioration-shared effect on particulate organic carbon gradually weakened, whereas that on mineral-associated organic carbon initially weakened and subsequently strengthened.4. Synthesis and applications: Soil pH amelioration can partly reconfigure the microbial life footprint and carbon deposition pathways. Proactively adopting measures that ameliorate soil pH may therefore favor the deposition and storage of stabilized organic carbon and could serve as a complementary strategy for enhancing soil carbon sinks in croplands.

title: Quantitative palaeohydrology reveals fluvial response to early‐mid Triassic climate change
summary: Anthropogenic climate change represents the greatest modern forcing on global river dynamics. Investigating the sensitivity of rivers to past climate change is thus crucial in understanding future landscapes in a warming world. The Sherwood
content: Anthropogenic climate change represents the greatest modern forcing on global river dynamics. Investigating the sensitivity of rivers to past climate change is thus crucial in understanding future landscapes in a warming world. The Sherwood Sandstone Group, UK, a unit of early‐middle Triassic (c. 248 to 239 Ma) dryland fluvial deposits, records the protracted climatic‐biotic recovery period following the Permo‐Triassic Mass Extinction. We quantify the evolution of this fluvial system, exposed in the southwest UK, by combining facies‐scale sedimentology with a numerical palaeohydraulic workflow. We reconstruct key hydraulic and geomorphic characteristics, showing that gravel‐bed lower Triassic rivers had palaeoslopes between 1.0 × 10 −3 and 2.0 × 10 −3 m/m and bankfull water discharges of c. 600 m 3 /s. During the middle Triassic, rivers were sand‐bedded, with palaeoslopes between 8 × 10 −2 and 5 × 10 −2 m/m. Bankfull water discharges ranged between 290 and 360 m 3 /s: half those of the lower Triassic. This halving of bankfull discharge occurs despite an inferred eightfold increase in catchment area in the mid‐Triassic and stable levels of long‐term precipitation, and is attributed to lower Triassic catchments generating highly intermittent, disproportionately large bankfull flow events. Coupled with the very coarse grain size recorded in the Lower Triassic and regional stratigraphic correlations to similar conglomerate sheets across NW Europe, we attribute this to a global hyperthermal event: the Late Smithian Thermal Maximum (c. 248 Ma). Rapid warming during a greenhouse interval triggered widespread landscape devegetation, bedrock erosion and extreme, infrequent monsoonal precipitation. Our results demonstrate the ability of quantitative palaeohydrology to produce numerically informed depositional models and to identify the impacts of extreme global warming.

title: Multi-responsive biopolymer–lipid hybrid nanocarriers for controlled doxorubicin delivery
summary: release studies under different conditions demonstrated pH-, enzyme-, and short-term temperature-dependent drug release. Compared with conventionally surfactant-stabilized nanoparticles, the developed HNPs exhibited significantly improved c
content: release studies under different conditions demonstrated pH-, enzyme-, and short-term temperature-dependent drug release. Compared with conventionally surfactant-stabilized nanoparticles, the developed HNPs exhibited significantly improved cytocompatibility toward mouse fibroblast (L929) cells. Additionally, DOX-loaded HNPs exhibited significant anticancer activity against human breast cancer (MCF-7) cells. Overall, the developed HNP system combines a surfactant-free formulation, enhanced cytocompatibility, and multi-stimuli-responsive drug release, making it a promising platform for controlled cancer drug delivery.

title: Antidepressants in water: the overlooked contamination and how a NiCo₂O₄@rGO nanophotocatalyst removes trazodone
source: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A Chemistry
summary: Trazodone is an antidepressant increasingly detected in aquatic environments and thus poses risks to ecosystems and human health. We report the synthesis of a NiCo₂O₄/reduced graphene oxide (NC@rGO) nanocomposite and its application as a vi
content: Trazodone is an antidepressant increasingly detected in aquatic environments and thus poses risks to ecosystems and human health. We report the synthesis of a NiCo₂O₄/reduced graphene oxide (NC@rGO) nanocomposite and its application as a visible-light-driven photocatalyst for the degradation of trazodone. The composite was characterized by TEM, SEM, XRD, Raman, FT-IR, BET, zeta potential, magnetic studies, EIS, Mott–Schottky, and XPS analyses. NC@rGO achieved 95% degradation efficiency with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.031 min −1 . It was a 6.6-fold improvement over bare NC. We attribute this enhancement mainly to rGO-mediated electron transfer, which favors charge separation. Scavenger experiments indicated superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes as the dominant reactive species. LC-MS/MS analysis identified the photodegradation products of trazodone and revealed a complex transformation pathway involving hydroxylation, dechlorination, and cleavage of the piperazine ring. Cytotoxicity tests in three organ-relevant human cell models (CCD-1079Sk, HepG2, H9c2(2–1)) showed that the photocatalytic transformation of trazodone does not yield highly toxic products, indicating both the efficacy and environmental safety of the proposed remediation strategy.

title: Residential built-environment typologies and ecological quality in a high-density city: spatial heterogeneity and evidence from Shanghai
source: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
summary: Rapid urbanization in high-density cities has intensified conflicts between residential development and ecological quality. However, previous studies have often focused on individual built-environment indicators, while the relationships bet
content: Rapid urbanization in high-density cities has intensified conflicts between residential development and ecological quality. However, previous studies have often focused on individual built-environment indicators, while the relationships between residential built-environment typologies and vegetation greenness, as well as their spatial heterogeneity, have received limited attention. To address these questions, this study analyzed 8,035 residential AOIs in Shanghai by integrating remote sensing, building, and water-network data. The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) was used to characterize vegetation greenness, while Height, building coverage ratio (BCR), floor area ratio (FAR), and Distance to Water characterized the built environment. K-means clustering identified four residential typologies, among which Low-rise Sparse Development had the highest NDVI and High BCR–High FAR the lowest. NDVI exhibited significant spatial clustering (Moran’s I = 0.823, p < 0.001). OLS showed that Height was positively associated with NDVI, whereas BCR, FAR, and Distance to Water were negatively associated, with BCR having the strongest negative effect (β = −0.1047, p < 0.001). GWR improved explanatory power over OLS (R2 = 0.642 vs. 0.130), revealing spatial non-stationarity. These findings highlight the associations of residential typology and spatial context with vegetation greenness, with FAR exhibiting the strongest negative association based on standardized OLS coefficients (β = −0.2784), providing evidence for differentiated vegetation-oriented planning in high-density cities.

title: TPMS-based reformer for ammonia decomposition: Effect of Ni/Al2O3 catalyst thickness on heat and mass transfer for Schwarz-P topology
summary: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures as a catalyst carrier are a perspective solution for compact reformers due to their high surface to volume ratio. In this work, the ammonia decomposition process is numerically investigated
content: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures as a catalyst carrier are a perspective solution for compact reformers due to their high surface to volume ratio. In this work, the ammonia decomposition process is numerically investigated in a Schwarz-P TPMS-based reformer (10 mm unit cell) coated with a Ni / Al 2 O 3 catalyst. Catalyst layer thicknesses from 125 to 1000 μ m were analyzed across 623–923 K. The numerical predictions of ammonia conversion were validated against reference experimental data for a Ni / Al 2 O 3 catalyst from the references, demonstrating strong agreement with a mean absolute percentage deviation of less than 7%. The results show that catalyst layer thickness significantly influences reformer performance, particularly up to 500 μ m . However, further increases in thickness yield minimal improvements in ammonia decomposition process. This behavior indicates that for thicknesses greater than 500 μ m , the process becomes limited by internal mass transfer resistance, preventing the effective utilization of the additional catalyst volume.

title: Methyl Jasmonate and Spermine Modulate Distinct Ionic, Metabolic, and Photochemical Responses in Salt-Stressed Lemon Basil
summary: Salinity impairs crops through two chemically distinct processes: competition between Na+ and K+ for transport and binding sites and accumulation of Cl–. Exogenous signaling molecules can modulate these processes, but most studies have test
content: Salinity impairs crops through two chemically distinct processes: competition between Na+ and K+ for transport and binding sites and accumulation of Cl–. Exogenous signaling molecules can modulate these processes, but most studies have tested a single molecule in soil-grown plants, and whether molecules with different chemical properties affect the same or different response components in recirculating hydroponics is unclear. This study aimed to determine whether foliar methyl jasmonate (MeJA, 100 μM), a volatile oxylipin ester, and spermine (Spm, 500 μM), a polyamine with four protonatable amino groups, applied alone or combined, modulate the same or distinct components of the salinity response of lemon basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) grown with 40 mM NaCl in a recirculating nutrient film technique system. Concentrations of Na+, K+, and Cl– were measured in roots, stems, leaves, and inflorescences, together with organic osmolytes, phenylpropanoids, photosynthetic pigments, and in vivo chlorophyll fluorescence and electrochromic shift parameters. Salinity increased leaf Cl– more than 5-fold and reduced leaf and stem dry mass by 32% and 43%. MeJA primarily altered leaf cation balance: relative to the saline control, it lowered leaf Na+ by 57% and the leaf Na+/K+ ratio by 61% and increased free amino acids by 216% and proline by 34%, but it also increased leaf Cl– by 15% and decreased chlorophyll a by 30% and carotenoids by 26%. Spermine was associated with higher measured flavonoid (36%) and anthocyanin (47%) concentrations. The combination produced the largest photochemical response: linear electron flow increased by 164%, accompanied by a 38% increase in relative thylakoid proton flux. No regulator restored vegetative dry mass. The responses associated with MeJA and spermine therefore differed across the measured traits, and their use in saline hydroponics should be matched to the intended outcome: cation homeostasis, accumulation of bioactive compounds, or photochemical performance. Future studies should address dose–response combinations, full production cycles, and essential oil composition and should combine these regulators with nutrient solution management that limits Cl– accumulation.

title: Iron-Photocatalysed Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Coupled with Nickel-Catalysed SH2 for Decarboxylative sp3–sp3 Coupling of Free Carboxylic Acids and NHPI Esters
summary: Decarboxylative cross-coupling of two alkyl fragments without precious-metal catalysts, external oxidants, or stoichiometric base remains a central challenge in synthetic chemistry. Here we show that near-UV (395 nm) excitation of an Fe(III
content: Decarboxylative cross-coupling of two alkyl fragments without precious-metal catalysts, external oxidants, or stoichiometric base remains a central challenge in synthetic chemistry. Here we show that near-UV (395 nm) excitation of an Fe(III)–carboxylate complex initiates decarboxylative sp3–sp3 coupling of free carboxylic acids with N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) redox-active esters by ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT), in cooperation with a nickel catalyst that closes the cycle through bimolecular homolytic substitution (SH2). A single loading of trifluoroethanol (≈0.55 equiv, 4 µL at 0.1 mmol scale) replaces the external base by acting as a proton shuttle between the iron and nickel cycles. Turnover depends on a β-carbonyl handle on at least one coupling partner: the carbonyl chelates nickel in a five-membered ring and stabilises the Ni(III)–alkyl intermediate against β-hydride elimination and hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) quenching. The platform engages unactivated, long-chain primary alkyl groups at 27–44% (NHPI-ester side) and 14–37% (free-acid side), a regime that remains difficult to reach under purely photochemical, base-free conditions, delivers 39 unique products (41 entries) at 14–96% yield overall, and provides a working hypothesis for the cooperative iron/nickel cycle that remains subject to further mechanistic validation.

title: Future Phenology of Chinese Vegetation Is Mediated by Hot Drought Extremes
summary: Climate warming is expected to lengthen vegetation growing seasons, but increasing drought and heat may constrain this potential. We derived daily gross primary productivity from a light‐use‐efficiency model driven by multi‐source Coupled M
content: Climate warming is expected to lengthen vegetation growing seasons, but increasing drought and heat may constrain this potential. We derived daily gross primary productivity from a light‐use‐efficiency model driven by multi‐source Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 inputs and projected functional phenology across China under four emissions scenarios. Under SSP5‐8.5, the start of the growing season (SGS) advanced 13.8 days, the end of the growing season (EGS) was delayed 10.9 days, and growing‐season length increased 24.7 days in 2081–2100 relative to 1995–2014. The Joint Drought Indicator (JDI), representing compound soil‐moisture‐temperature exposure, had larger absolute grid‐cell time‐mean coefficients than the Standardized Precipitation‐Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) in 53.06%–63.09% of cells for SGS and 62.97%–69.41% for EGS. However, direct climate variables explained more pooled phenological variation, with temperature and soil moisture contributing most to the pooled SGS and EGS models, respectively. Projected growing‐season extension should be interpreted alongside increasing hot‐drought exposure, particularly in autumn.

title: Light, Sugar and Phytohormone Crosstalk in Shoot Branching: Mechanisms and Perspectives
summary: Shoot branching is a fundamental determinant of plant architecture, critically influencing biomass accumulation, crop yield and adaptability to high-density planting. The precise regulation of axillary bud outgrowth is essential for optimis
content: Shoot branching is a fundamental determinant of plant architecture, critically influencing biomass accumulation, crop yield and adaptability to high-density planting. The precise regulation of axillary bud outgrowth is essential for optimising the trade-off between vegetative growth and reproductive output. This complex developmental process is orchestrated by a dynamic interplay between environmental cues and endogenous signals, including phytohormones and metabolic sugars. Here, we synthesise current understanding of shoot branching control within a unified hierarchical framework: light acts as the upstream environmental cue that drives photosynthetic carbon assimilation and simultaneously activates photoreceptor-mediated signalling; sugar and trehalose-6-phosphate (Tre6P) then function as the metabolic gate that sets bud competence; and hormones (auxin, cytokinin, strigolactone, abscisic acid, brassinosteroid and gibberellin) act as the downstream executive layer that converts this competence into a specific bud fate. We highlight how sugar signalling integrates with hormonal transport and sensitivity to regulate bud fate, and we critically distinguish well-established regulatory relationships from hypotheses awaiting experimental validation. Finally, we discuss the potential of manipulating these signalling nodes-through molecular design breeding, controlled-environment agriculture and high-density planting-to engineer ideal plant architectures, providing theoretical insights and breeding strategies for developing horticultural varieties adapted to modern, sustainable agricultural systems.

title: Preparation and In Vitro Evaluation of Paclitaxel‐Loaded Lipid‐Shelled Nanobubbles for Ultrasound‐Triggered Drug Delivery
summary: This study developed paclitaxel (PTX)‐loaded lipid‐shelled nanobubbles (NBs) for ultrasound‐triggered drug delivery. The PTX‐NBs were prepared using thin‐film hydration combined with perfluoropropane gas exchange and mechanical agitation. P
content: This study developed paclitaxel (PTX)‐loaded lipid‐shelled nanobubbles (NBs) for ultrasound‐triggered drug delivery. The PTX‐NBs were prepared using thin‐film hydration combined with perfluoropropane gas exchange and mechanical agitation. Particle size, zeta potential, morphology, drug loading, etc., were characterized. Drug release was evaluated under acidic tumor‐associated and physiological pH conditions. Free PTX and a 1,2‐distearoyl‐sn‐glycero‐3‐phosphocholine–based control formulation were included to assess formulation‐dependent pH behavior. Ultrasound‐triggered release was examined at different intensities and exposure durations. In vitro cytotoxicity, apoptosis and haemolytic activity were also evaluated. The PTX‐NBs had a mean particle size of 390.5 ± 45.2 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.182 ± 0.023 and a zeta potential of −22.97 ± 3.4 mV. Scanning electron microscopy showed sphericalsubmicron structures. Drug loading and encapsulation efficiency were 8.7% ± 1.1% and 71.3% ± 4.8%, respectively. After 84 h, cumulative PTX release was 81.5% ± 5.2% at pH 5.0 and 20.7% ± 2.3% at pH 7.4. Ultrasound exposure resulted in 60.5% ± 5.7% release within 2 h. At 48 h, the half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values were 3.2 ± 0.4 µg/mL for PTX‐NBs and 8.9 ± 1.2 µg/mL for free PTX; the IC50 decreased to 1.8 ± 0.3 µg/mL when PTX‐NBs were combined with ultrasound. The PTX‐NBs showed nanoscale size, pH‐dependent release, increased release after ultrasound exposure, enhanced in vitro cytotoxicity and acceptable preliminary hemocompatibility. Direct confirmation of the gas‐filled core and acoustic behavior is required before the formulation can be described as acoustically responsive.

title: Ionization, Latitude, and Altitude Dependence of Particle Formation in Stratospheric SO 2 and H 2 S Injection Plumes
summary: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) has received increasing attention as a potential temporary climate intervention strategy. A critical source of uncertainty involves subgrid processes within injection plumes─specifically new particle fo
content: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) has received increasing attention as a potential temporary climate intervention strategy. A critical source of uncertainty involves subgrid processes within injection plumes─specifically new particle formation (NPF)─which influence particle size distribution and overall SAI efficacy. This work provides the first comprehensive modeling study of NPF and size distribution evolution within subgrid aircraft plumes at tropical and subpolar sites for both sulfur dioxide (SO2) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) SAI. Results indicate that H2S SAI generally produces new particles as effectively as SO2 SAI when the precursor mass injection rate is the same. Notably, due to a much higher ionization rate, subpolar regions exhibit higher particle formation efficiency and less condensation on background aerosols compared to tropical areas. Without considering the ionization effect, NPF in the subpolar SO2 and H2S SAI plumes is negligible. Furthermore, NPF efficacy diminishes sharply with increasing injection altitude, a trend driven by changing ionization rates and other parameters at higher elevations. The analysis also highlights that particle creation efficiency is strongly affected by other factors. The insights gained contribute to more informed decision-making regarding climate intervention strategies and governance.

title: Forest reserves as sources or sinks? Untangling the role of protected areas in spruce bark beetle dynamics
summary: Forest reserves are often perceived as sources of Ips typographus outbreaks due to high volumes of mature host trees and limited intervention, yet empirical evidence for this assumption remains inconsistent. This chapter reviews pathways of
content: Forest reserves are often perceived as sources of Ips typographus outbreaks due to high volumes of mature host trees and limited intervention, yet empirical evidence for this assumption remains inconsistent. This chapter reviews pathways of potential spread from protected areas to surrounding forests and synthesizes recent literature on bark beetle dynamics, natural enemies, and ecological functions. Evidence indicates that protected areas can, under certain conditions, act as local sources of beetles, particularly following large disturbances. However, managed forests may equally contribute to infestations within reserves. Outbreak dynamics are primarily driven by disturbance regimes, forest composition, and landscape structure rather than protection status. Mixed-species and structurally diverse forests consistently show lower infestation risk than spruce-dominated monocultures. Evidence for enhanced control by natural enemies in protected areas remains inconclusive. We conclude that landscape-level diversification, rather than intensified control at reserve boundaries, is key to reducing bark beetle risk.

title: Influence of CO2/CH4 production ratios on the isotope signature of methane
summary: Stable carbon isotopes are often used to infer dominant methanogenic pathways in wetland ecosystems. We performed closed system incubations with Sphagnum bog peat, monitoring CO2 and CH4 production and isotopic composition across incubation
content: Stable carbon isotopes are often used to infer dominant methanogenic pathways in wetland ecosystems. We performed closed system incubations with Sphagnum bog peat, monitoring CO2 and CH4 production and isotopic composition across incubation temperatures and over time. We observed higher CO2 production relative to CH4 production (CO2/CH4 > 1). Whereas for closed methanogenic systems one would typically expect the CO2 pool and resultant CH4 to become increasingly enriched as 13C-depleted carbon is transformed to CH4, we saw the stable carbon isotopic composition of both gases became increasingly 13C-depleted in parallel over the course of the incubations. We hypothesized that these unusual trends were due to CO2 with organic matter isotopic composition (‑25 ‰) being added by non-fractionating catabolic processes at a higher rate than CO2 reduction to CH4, resulting in increasing 13C depletion in the CO2 pool over time. Methane was formed from that increasingly depleted CO2 pool at a relatively constant apparent fractionation factor and thus its δ13C became more depleted over time as well. We developed an explanatory mass balance model which reproduced our observations and was consistent with our hypothesis. The isotope mass balance model accurately reproduced changes in δ13C-CO2 and δ13C-CH4 under conditions consistent with hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis drawing from a progressively 13C-depleted CO2 pool. These results show the CO2/CH4 production ratio strongly influences δ13C-CH4 by controlling the δ13C-CO2. Small shifts in CO2-dominated versus CH4-dominated metabolism can substantially alter δ13C-CH4 even in the absence of major changes in methanogenic pathway, potentially leading to misinterpretation of isotope signals from incubations, porewaters, or emissions if not considered.

title: Marine Heatwaves in Polar Regions
summary: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly reported in polar oceans, where sea ice, salinity-controlled stratification, and strong seasonality shape these extremes. This work synthesizes knowledge of Arctic and Antarctic MHWs, from existing l
content: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly reported in polar oceans, where sea ice, salinity-controlled stratification, and strong seasonality shape these extremes. This work synthesizes knowledge of Arctic and Antarctic MHWs, from existing literature and new analyses. Surface MHWs are more intense and regionally diverse in the Arctic than around Antarctica. Mooring records provide the first observational evidence that subsurface Arctic MHWs can be as intense as shallower events. Surface heat fluxes dominate MHW onset and decline at both poles, but their effect is modulated by sea ice, which insulates the ocean, constrains SST variability, and sustains events through a melt–stratification–SST feedback. With warm water in the subsurface, vertical processes also contribute more at both poles than at lower latitudes. Around Antarctica, vertical processes even rank second after surface heat flux, whereas in the Arctic, advection is the second-largest contribution. Arctic MHWs have intensified rapidly and are projected to increase more than anywhere else, whereas Antarctic trends remain weak. Ecosystem impacts are documented mainly in the Arctic, where MHWs also affect Indigenous communities. Finally, polar-specific challenges for MHW definitions, observations, and models are discussed.

title: Comment on "Assessment of Modeling Tree Stem Methane Fluxes Using Gridded Environmental Data Sets" by Zhao et al. (2026)
summary: Zhao et al. (2026) assess whether tree stem CH₄ fluxes can be modeled from gridded environmental data, using a compilation of 13,547 flux observations and a random-forest model; their model gives a global upland stem flux of −32.2 Tg CH₄ yr
content: Zhao et al. (2026) assess whether tree stem CH₄ fluxes can be modeled from gridded environmental data, using a compilation of 13,547 flux observations and a random-forest model; their model gives a global upland stem flux of −32.2 Tg CH₄ yr⁻¹ (uptake). We checked the 12,366 deposited entries against their sources. Half contain factual errors, including soil, branch and canopy fluxes entered as stem fluxes, reversed signs and unconverted units, and these errors create most of the apparent uptake at height. Our reconstruction gives a net upland source with both the deposited data (+9.8 Tg CH₄ yr⁻¹) and the corrected data (+3.2 Tg CH₄ yr⁻¹). Zhao et al. attribute 81 % of their estimated sink to heights above 6 m, where all 46 corrected upland measurements show emission. The reconstructed model has no skill at sites it was not trained on. The corrections also raise Zhao et al.'s Amazon Basin estimate. We release the corrected compilation to support the next steps the authors propose.

title: Evaluating energy and nutrient recovery from onion waste: A simulated biorefinery optimized system
summary: This study presents an integrated anaerobic digestion (AD)- hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) biorefinery, simulated in Aspen Plus® V14, for sustainably converting onion waste into biomethane, biocrude, biochar, and biofertilizers. Model vali
content: This study presents an integrated anaerobic digestion (AD)- hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) biorefinery, simulated in Aspen Plus® V14, for sustainably converting onion waste into biomethane, biocrude, biochar, and biofertilizers. Model validation demonstrated excellent predictive accuracy across diverse feedstocks, with methane composition predictions showing low relative errors ranging from 0.10% to 2.03%. The thermophilic AD system (55 °C) generated 550 L kg⁻¹ VS biogas with 65% CH₄ and an energy content of 12.5 MJ kg⁻¹ VS, with upgraded biomethane exceeding 95% purity. Using an Aspen Plus®–RSM framework, the optimal AD conditions were identified as 37.02 °C mesophilic temperature, 50.04 °C thermophilic temperature, 2.69 kg VS m⁻³ day⁻¹ OLR, and 21.95 days HRT, achieving 0.57 m³ kg⁻¹ VS methane and 130.19 m³ day⁻¹ biogas. For the HTL–composting subsystem, optimal conditions of 291.48 °C, 16 MPa, and 60 °C produced 40.67 wt % biocrude, 14.21 wt % biochar, 7.25 wt % NPK, 22.64 wt % liquid fertilizer, and 87% nutrient recovery. Overall, the integrated optimized biorefinery demonstrates a highly efficient circular bioeconomy pathway for onion waste valorization through simultaneous recovery of renewable energy, carbon-rich products, and nutrients.

title: Isotopic fractionation patterns during heterotrophic nitrification by Alcaligenes faecalis
summary: The observation of nitrification by heterotrophic bacteria indicates that chemolithoautotrophs are not the only microorganisms with this capability, but the environmental relevance of heterotrophic nitrification remains unclear. Stable nitr
content: The observation of nitrification by heterotrophic bacteria indicates that chemolithoautotrophs are not the only microorganisms with this capability, but the environmental relevance of heterotrophic nitrification remains unclear. Stable nitrogen (N) isotope ratios can reveal underlying biochemical pathways. We investigated the N isotope effects of the heterotrophic nitrifier Alcaligenes faecalis, which converted ammonium (NH4+) into hydroxylamine (20%, NH2OH), nitrite (5%, NO2-), and nitrous oxide (0.6%, N2O); the remainder of NH4+ was attributed to incorporation into biomass, confirming NH4+ assimilation as the primary consumption pathway. The net N isotope effect for total NH4+ consumption was 13.8 ± 0.4‰, which is within the reported range for bacterial NH4+ assimilation and generally lower than values reported for ammonia oxidation. Along with low-δ15N biomass, NH4+ conversion produced 15N-depleted NH2OH, NO2-, and N2O, which became progressively enriched in 15N over time as NH4+ consumption proceeded. With a time-resolved isotope-mass balance model, we estimated similar isotope effects for NH2OH and biomass formation (16.2 ± 0.6‰ and 14.5 ± 1.5‰, respectively). NO2- showed an inverse isotope effect with respect to NH2OH, its closest measured precursor, ending up as the most 15N-enriched product pool. The N2O exhibited an elevated site preference (24‰ to 38‰), indicating contributions from NH2OH decomposition and its reaction with nitric oxide. More broadly, heterotrophic nitrification may represent an underappreciated link between N assimilation and the production of reactive N intermediates and N2O with potential implications for N cycling in natural ecosystems.

title: Exposome Wide Associations, DNA adduct and eGFR Dynamics: Evaluation of oxidative stress in CKDu pathogenesis
summary: Background Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown Etiology (CKDu) is a growing public health concern in agricultural regions, where environmental exposures are implicated as potential etiological agents. However, the combined nephrotoxic effects
content: Background Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown Etiology (CKDu) is a growing public health concern in agricultural regions, where environmental exposures are implicated as potential etiological agents. However, the combined nephrotoxic effects of complex heavy metal and pesticide mixtures remain poorly elucidated. Methods We conducted a population-based case-control study including 215 CKDu cases and 215 age- and sex-matched community controls without symptoms of CKDu. Serum concentrations of exposomes, including heavy metals (Al, Ni, As, Cd, Hg, and Pb) and pesticide residues (organochlorines, organophosphates, and pyrethroids), were measured using mass spectrometry, while oxidative DNA damage was estimated as urinary 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG). A series of univariate, multivariate linear regression and mediation analyses were performed to explore independent exposure-outcome associations and identify underlying mechanistic pathways connecting environmental toxicants to estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline. Results CKDu cases had significantly higher serum body burdens of heavy metals, most notably Al (32.32 vs. 13.43 µg/L, p < 0.001), Hg (16.17 vs. 7.55 µg/L, p = 0.001), and Cd (3.17 vs. 0.10 µg/L, p < 0.001), as well as elevated levels of several pesticides, including cyfluthrin (11.33 µg/L vs <LLOQ, p < 0.001) and transfluthrin (6.03 vs. 0.83 µg/L, p = 0.012). In multivariate analysis adjusting for co-exposures, a significant inverse association was observed with eGFR for Cd (β=-0.382, As β=-0.332, Pb β=-0.254, Hg β=-0.250, and Al β=-0.222) with p < 0.05. Using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, we identified a toxic threshold of 8-OHdG DNA adducts at 9.5 µg/L (AUC = 0.690, p < 0.001). Finally, mediation analysis revealed that oxidative DNA damage significantly mediated the effect of Pb (16.89%, parathion 15.24%, Hg 12.22%, Al 11.82%, As 9.86% and Cd 8.75% on eGFR decline(p < 0.001). Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that multi-pollutant exposome profiling can effectively capture complex interactions between environmental heavy metals and pesticides, which are critically involved in the pathogenesis of CKDu. title: Strain selection determines the morphology and silver loading of supernatant-mediated silver nanoparticles: evidence from bacteria isolated from an urban lake
source: Kristu Jayanti Journal of Core and Applied Biology (KJCAB)
summary: Urban lakes in expanding Indian cities receive mixed domestic and agricultural inputs, and their culturable bacteria are of interest both as indicators of sanitary status and as a source of strains for applied biotechnology. A surface water
content: Urban lakes in expanding Indian cities receive mixed domestic and agricultural inputs, and their culturable bacteria are of interest both as indicators of sanitary status and as a source of strains for applied biotechnology. A surface water sample from Doddagubbi Lake, Bengaluru, India, was examined by culture-dependent methods. The heterotrophic plate count on nutrient agar was 8.0 × 103 CFU mL-1. Presumptive coliforms were detected on eosin methylene blue agar, whereas Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Salmonella spp. and actinobacteria were not recovered. Three Gram-negative, motile, aerobic isolates (KJU0088, KJU0089 and KJU0090) were purified and characterised by colony morphology, staining, biochemical tests, UV–visible profiling of cell-free spent broth, antibiotic susceptibility and cross-streak assay. Two representative strains were identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing as Citrobacter freundii KJU0088 (GenBank PZ682701) and Comamonas testosteroni KJU0089 (GenBank PZ682702). All three isolates were susceptible to ofloxacin, kanamycin and azithromycin and showed no mutual antagonism. Cell-free supernatants of all three isolates reduced 1 mM AgNO3 to a black colloid within 24 h. Field emission scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (FESEM–EDS) showed that, under an identical synthesis protocol, particle morphology and silver content differed between preparations: silver accounted for 40.1 ± 0.4, 23.1 ± 0.3 and 13.3 ± 0.3 wt% for KJU0088, KJU0089 and KJU0090, respectively, with the residual carbon and oxygen fraction rising as the silver fraction fell. The study provides baseline culturable-bacteria data for Doddagubbi Lake and shows that the morphology and silver loading of supernatant-mediated silver nanoparticles depend on the isolate used.

title: Analysis of Source‐to‐Sink Pollutant Transport in Porous Surface Using Lie Symmetry and Perturbation Method
source: International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics
summary: This study presents semi‐analytical investigation of the coupled transport of momentum, heat, and pollutant concentration in a porous ground surface, incorporating advective, diffusive, and reactive mechanisms. Unlike conventional analytica
content: This study presents semi‐analytical investigation of the coupled transport of momentum, heat, and pollutant concentration in a porous ground surface, incorporating advective, diffusive, and reactive mechanisms. Unlike conventional analytical approaches that often neglect coupling effects or rely purely on numerical approximations, the present model integrates the incompressible Navier‐Stokes equations with nonlinear heat transfer and advection‐diffusion‐reaction formulations to capture the multiphysics nature of subsurface transport processes. Using Lie symmetry analysis, the governing nonlinear system of partial differential equations is reduced to ordinary differential equations, which are then solved using a perturbation‐based approach that linearises the system into a solvable set of linear equations, allowing direct integration under defined validity conditions. The combined use of Lie symmetry analysis and the perturbation method is adopted because the reduced equations remain strongly coupled and nonlinear, and therefore do not readily admit solutions through standard special‐function or Green's function techniques, while still preserving explicit dependence on the governing physical parameters. Parametric analysis shows that increased decay reduces pollutant penetration depth, higher Reynolds numbers enhance advective dominance and steepen concentration gradients, and thermal effects influence velocity profiles and contaminant dispersion. These findings provide additional physical insights into the interplay among flow, heat, and reactive transport in porous media, offering a simpler, more reproducible integration framework for predicting pollutant fate. The proposed model has practical relevance in groundwater contamination assessment and environmental remediation planning, particularly in scenarios where rapid yet reliable analytical approximations are required.

title: Ground-to-Canopy Tree Methane Fluxes: Implications for Scaling and Forest Budgets
summary: Most existing measurements of tree methane (CH₄) exchange are concentrated near the ground, leaving the contribution of upper stems, branches, and leaves to methane budgets poorly resolved. We measured CH₄ fluxes on stems, branches, and lea
content: Most existing measurements of tree methane (CH₄) exchange are concentrated near the ground, leaving the contribution of upper stems, branches, and leaves to methane budgets poorly resolved. We measured CH₄ fluxes on stems, branches, and leaves of seven temperate trees up to 22 m and tested whether basal measurements predicted upper-stem exchange. Stem fluxes were predominantly emissions to the atmosphere, with hotspots at height and negative fluxes in only 5% of measurements at or above 2 m. Basal extrapolations over- or underestimated upper-stem exchange and sometimes predicted net uptake where measured profiles showed net emission. Illustrative scaling showed that branches and leaves, because of their large surface areas, could dominate total tree-surface flux despite low per-area rates.
