Ground-to-canopy observations are therefore needed to resolve the magnitude and direction of whole-tree methane exchange and its contribution to forest budgets.

title: Deciphering Heteroatom Migration Mechanisms: A Multi‐Scale Analysis Model at the Solid‐Liquid Interface
summary: Ultra‐high‐purity (UHP) metals underpin advanced microelectronics, aerospace, cryogenic physics, and emerging energy technologies, yet their production is limited by the nonlinear migration, segregation, and trapping of trace impurities at
content: Ultra‐high‐purity (UHP) metals underpin advanced microelectronics, aerospace, cryogenic physics, and emerging energy technologies, yet their production is limited by the nonlinear migration, segregation, and trapping of trace impurities at the solid–liquid (S–L) interface. Conventional experiments cannot resolve these dynamic interfacial processes with sufficient spatial and temporal precision, which leaves a persistent gap between empirical observation and predictive control. This review examines how multiscale computational methods can be combined to clarify impurity migration at S–L interfaces during directional solidification and zone‐refining purification. We discuss first‐principles calculations for electronic interactions and segregation thermodynamics, molecular dynamics simulations for transient evolution and solute kinetics at the solid–liquid interface, phase‐field modeling for mesoscale dendrite morphology and solute redistribution, and finite element modeling for process‐scale transport and optimization. Together, these methods provide a cross‐scale framework that connects atomic mechanisms with manufacturing conditions. We further highlight machine‐learning‐assisted parameter optimization, multifield coupled simulation, and operando validation as priorities for moving UHP metal fabrication from empirical adjustment toward predictive design.

title: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merr.) pod dimension under varying assimilate availability
summary: Pod dimension traits, such as pod length, pod width, and pod volume, influence seed size and yield in soybean (Glycine max L. Merr.), but how these traits respond to changes in assimilate availability during seed filling remains unclear. Th
content: Pod dimension traits, such as pod length, pod width, and pod volume, influence seed size and yield in soybean (Glycine max L. Merr.), but how these traits respond to changes in assimilate availability during seed filling remains unclear. Thus, this study investigated these responses using depodding and defoliation, applied weekly from growth stage R5 through R5 + 4 weeks in two cultivars from different maturity groups (MGII and MGIV). Pod length remained unchanged (p > 0.05) under all assimilate supply conditions, but pod width and volume increased significantly (p < 0.001) with increased assimilate supply and were positively correlated with unit pod weight (width: r = 0.16–0.81 in MGII, 0.37–0.79 in MGIV; volume: 0.34–0.86 in MGII, 0.33–0.77 in MGIV) and unit seed weight (width: r = 0.15–0.77 in MGII, 0.22–0.84 in MGIV; volume: r = 0.29–0.65 in MGII, 0.20–0.83 in MGIV). Conversely, pod width and volume showed no significant response to decreased assimilate supply. These findings suggest that pod length is relatively insensitive, while pod width and volume are more sensitive to assimilate availability during early seed filling, and may serve as phenotypic metrics for evaluating assimilate-responsive pod expansion and final pod size under source-sink manipulation.

title: An Electrically Gated Solid‐State Thermal Transistor for Energy‐Efficient Thermal Management
summary: Vapor‐compression heating and cooling systems dominate modern thermal management, yet their efficiency and scalability remain constrained by mechanical complexity and refrigerant‐based operation. Solid‐state approaches offer an attractive a
content: Vapor‐compression heating and cooling systems dominate modern thermal management, yet their efficiency and scalability remain constrained by mechanical complexity and refrigerant‐based operation. Solid‐state approaches offer an attractive alternative, with recent demonstrations showing the potential for highly efficient, compact thermal control. Here we demonstrate an electrically gated solid‐state thermal transistor based on bulk single‐crystal barium titanate, achieving a switching ratio of 1.6, among the highest reported for bulk ferroelectrics. We further introduce switching efficiency as a figure of merit, reaching ∼8.52 cm 3 J −1, more than two orders of magnitude higher than that of the highest‐performing reported thermal switch, PbZrO 3. Unlike previous thermal switches that operate between two discrete states, this device provides continuously tunable thermal‐conductivity states, enabling transistor‐like modulation and amplification of heat flow. In situ x‐ray diffraction combined with first‐principles calculations shows that switching originates from anisotropic phonon transport between ferroelectric domains. Integrated into a proof‐of‐concept thermal‐management system, the device shifts the baseline temperature of a miniature human analog by ∼0.6°C at a cycle‐averaged power input of 33 µW cm −2, approximately ninefold lower than a vapor‐compression heat pump performing the same task. These results establish ferroelectric thermal transistors as a programmable, energy‐efficient platform for solid‐state thermal management.

title: Impacts of Explicit Oxalate Chemistry on Dust Iron Dissolution and Soluble Iron Deposition in a Global Model
summary: Atmospheric iron deposition is a crucial nutrient source for marine ecosystems, yet the mechanisms that generate secondary soluble iron from dust remain poorly constrained. Here, we implement an explicit, observation‐constrained aqueous oxa
content: Atmospheric iron deposition is a crucial nutrient source for marine ecosystems, yet the mechanisms that generate secondary soluble iron from dust remain poorly constrained. Here, we implement an explicit, observation‐constrained aqueous oxalate chemistry scheme within the global model CAM6‐Chem to quantify its impact on dust iron dissolution. Since glyoxal (GLY) is a key precursor of oxalate, we evaluate GLY and find a large low bias in the default model. We correct this by applying an empirical scaling factor to GLY‐driven oxalate production. With this constraint, the model reproduces the observed variability of aerosol and in‐cloud oxalate, although aerosol oxalate remains underestimated. The simulation predicts a global oxalate production of 12.3 Tg yr −1 and a lifetime of about 2.3 days. Oxalate forms mainly in cloud water, and the oxidation of GLY by OH provides about 70% of the global source. Relative to the original simplified parameterized scheme, the explicit chemistry increases in‐cloud oxalate concentrations by more than an order of magnitude, improving agreement with cloud‐water observations and enhancing dust iron dissolution. Consequently, global oxalate‐promoted dust soluble iron production triples from 266 to 780 Gg yr −1, raising the dust soluble iron deposition from 1.3 to 1.8 Tg yr −1. A multi‐source iron budget indicates that dust supplies about 88% of soluble iron deposition to the ocean and that oxalate‐promoted dissolution accounts for nearly half of dust soluble iron. These results highlight the importance of explicit oxalate chemistry for representing atmospheric iron dissolution processing and its impact on marine biogeochemistry.

title: Evolutionary Crosslinking‐Driven 3D Printing of Silicone Elastomers
summary: Flexible functional systems require materials that combine mechanical compliance, structural stability, and long-term reliability. Silicone elastomers satisfy these requirements through their low modulus, large recoverable deformation, envi
content: Flexible functional systems require materials that combine mechanical compliance, structural stability, and long-term reliability. Silicone elastomers satisfy these requirements through their low modulus, large recoverable deformation, environmental stability, and chemically crosslinked networks. Among them, platinum-catalyzed addition-cure silicones are particularly attractive because of their low curing shrinkage, uniform networks, and stable properties. However, increasing structural complexity and functional integration challenge conventional mold-based fabrication and motivate additive manufacturing of complex silicone architectures. A central challenge in silicone 3D printing is to move beyond tailoring materials for printability toward designing printing processes around their intrinsic material behavior, thereby enabling precise control over both geometry and properties. Unlike thermoplastics or photocurable elastomers, addition-cure silicones undergo continuous, time- and temperature-dependent crosslinking after mixing, leading to concurrent evolution of crosslinking state, rheology, and mechanical stability during shaping. This Review defines this process as evolutionary crosslinking and introduces "crosslinking-in-shaping" to describe manufacturing in which structure generation is intrinsically coupled with crosslinking evolution. This Review establishes a five-step framework for extrusion-based silicone additive manufacturing, reorganizing existing studies from a manufacturing-science perspective. The framework is also applicable to other thermosetting material systems governed by irreversible crosslinking and thermal regulation.

title: Interpretable Forecasting of Basic Oxygen Furnace Steam Recovery With Energy‐Equivalent Error Metric and Shapley Additive Explanations Attribution
summary: Basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steam recovery is an important but less systematically studied secondary‐energy process in steelmaking. Its heat‐to‐heat variability affects recovered‐energy assessment, steam‐system balance, and waste‐heat utiliz
content: Basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steam recovery is an important but less systematically studied secondary‐energy process in steelmaking. Its heat‐to‐heat variability affects recovered‐energy assessment, steam‐system balance, and waste‐heat utilization. This study develops an interpretable forecasting framework for BOF steam recovery using industrial production data from a 300‐t converter. A backpropagation (BP) neural network optimized by fivefold cross‐validated chaotic particle swarm optimization (CPSO), denoted as 5‐CV‐CPSO‐BP, is used to improve forecasting robustness. To strengthen the engineering relevance of model evaluation, an energy‐equivalent error metric, , is introduced to convert steam‐mass prediction errors into recovered‐energy deviations. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) are employed to quantify variable‐level attributions and support process interpretation. Based on 785 heats and 10 independent runs, the proposed model achieved an average test‐set mean absolute percentage error of 5.37%, a mean absolute error of 1.63 t, an R 2 of 0.912, and a of 3.75 GJ, outperforming BP, CPSO‐BP, gray wolf optimization‐backpropagation, random forest, and least‐squares support vector machine. SHAP results identify annular gap opening, hood height, oxygen blowing volume, molten steel temperature, and total scrap weight as dominant variables, corresponding to flow control, reaction intensity, and thermal balance.

title: Mapping and Monitoring Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide From NASA's OCO ‐2 Satellite
summary: Carbon dioxide (CO 2) is a leading greenhouse gas (GHG) and a principal driver of climate change. There is now an acceptance by almost all sectors of society that our planet's future climate is becoming hotter and more extreme, caused by GH
content: Carbon dioxide (CO 2) is a leading greenhouse gas (GHG) and a principal driver of climate change. There is now an acceptance by almost all sectors of society that our planet's future climate is becoming hotter and more extreme, caused by GHGs in the atmosphere, particularly CO 2. Since 2014, the NASA satellite Orbiting Carbon Observatory‐2 (OCO‐2) has been continuously sensing CO 2 concentrations over the globe. Mapping and monitoring CO 2 at small‐scale spatial and temporal resolutions allow carbon‐cycle scientists to locate unusual behaviors, hypothesize causes, and revise climate projections. Aggregations of the satellite data to coarse yearly or large regional scales can limit answers to the “Where?” and “When?” questions needed for GHG mitigation. This article starts with OCO‐2 retrievals on orbit tracks and demonstrates how to aggregate and filter them to display temporal and spatial signals, based on more than 7 years of OCO‐2 data. One of the filters monitors the planet's progress toward “net zero by 2050.” Resampling‐based inference highlights places in the space–time “cube” where the inter‐annual and inter‐regional variability of the carbon cycle is being disrupted, such as during El Niño/La Niña periods and the deceleration/acceleration of industrial activity as a result of the 2020–2021 COVID‐19 pandemic.

title: BRICS+ and the Future of Industrial Decarbonisation: Advancing Cooperation in Hard-to-Abate Sectors
summary: For BRICS+ economies, these developments present both risks and opportunities. Carbon-intensive production could face rising compliance costs and barriers to market access, while early investment in low-emission technologies could strengthe
content: For BRICS+ economies, these developments present both risks and opportunities. Carbon-intensive production could face rising compliance costs and barriers to market access, while early investment in low-emission technologies could strengthen competitiveness, attract investment, and create new industrial capabilities.

title: Hydrological setting and legacy phosphorus decouple algal recovery from catchment nitrogen decline
summary: Nitrogen reductions do not necessarily indicate lake recovery when phosphorus and chlorophyll respond differently. We analyzed 5,421 sampling records from 268 monitoring sites in Latvian lakes and reservoirs (1990–2022), combining long-term
content: Nitrogen reductions do not necessarily indicate lake recovery when phosphorus and chlorophyll respond differently. We analyzed 5,421 sampling records from 268 monitoring sites in Latvian lakes and reservoirs (1990–2022), combining long-term trends, paired period contrasts, and mixed-effects models. In five core waterbodies, ammonium nitrogen and total nitrogen (TN) declined by 70 % and 51 %, respectively, whereas total phosphorus (TP) showed no significant trend (+41 %; Mann–Kendall P = 0.085). Across 238 waterbodies, paired comparisons between 2007 and 2013 and 2016–2022 showed a 16 % decline in TP, robust to alternative windows. Chlorophyll a (Chl- a ) records began in 2002, after most of the nitrogen decline had occurred, so they document conditions after the nitrogen reduction, not algal responses during it. Across 2,252 concurrent samples, TP was more strongly associated with Chl- a than TN (standardized mixed-effects coefficients: 0.252 and 0.003, respectively; at most 0.060 for TN after seasonal adjustment). Site-level Chl- a trends correlated with TP trends (Spearman’s ρ = 0.62; n = 31). The log–log Chl- a –TP slope was 0.98 in 259 natural lakes but −0.17 (not significant) in nine reservoirs. The contrast persisted even after excluding each reservoir in turn or the Daugava cascade. In three run-of-river reservoirs, phosphate accounted for more than half of TP during the growing season. Within sites, TP increased in wetter years (precipitation elasticity 0.21; P = 0.011), whereas TN did not show a detectable response. These results indicate that phosphorus availability and hydrological setting are central to interpreting changes in nutrients and chlorophyll following nitrogen decline.

title: Deforestation in the Legal Amazon and the Tocantins-Araguaia River Basin and the Loss of Ecosystem Services: An Analysis of the 2020–2025 Period
source: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies
summary: This study analyzed the relationship between deforestation in the Legal Amazon and the loss of ecosystem services in the Tocantins-Araguaia River Basin between 2020 and 2025. It was an applied research study that combined a quantitative ana
content: This study analyzed the relationship between deforestation in the Legal Amazon and the loss of ecosystem services in the Tocantins-Araguaia River Basin between 2020 and 2025. It was an applied research study that combined a quantitative analysis of official vegetation monitoring time series with a qualitative reading of scientific literature and institutional documents from the water and energy sectors. The data showed that the Legal Amazon lost 56,796 km² of primary forest during this period, peaking at 13,038 km² in 2021 and dropping to 5,731 km² in 2025. While deforestation rates in the Amazon declined, the clearing of native vegetation remained high in the Cerrado portion of the basin, particularly in the state of Tocantins, which lost 230,255 hectares in 2023 and 153,311 hectares the following year. The analysis identified losses in climate regulation, carbon storage, water regulation, water quality, and biodiversity services, and examined the nexus between land use, water availability, and energy. The literature on hydrological responses to deforestation presents mixed results; long-term studies within the Tocantins-Araguaia system itself point to increased river flows, indicating that seasonal distribution—rather than annual volume—should be the focus of the problem. Monetary valuation was used strictly as an exploratory exercise, without measuring actual economic damage. It is concluded that the reduction of deforestation in the Amazon cannot be analyzed in isolation; an integrated approach is required that considers the Amazon-Cerrado transition and the river basin as complementary planning units.

title: Flow-topography interactions modulate zooplankton abundance and vertical carbon flux along the Vitória-Trindade Seamount Chain (Southwestern Atlantic)
source: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
summary: Interactions between mesoscale eddies and seamounts strongly modify local circulation, nutrient transport, and planktonic communities. This study investigates the hydrodynamic-zooplankton coupling along the Vitória–Trindade Seamount Chain (
content: Interactions between mesoscale eddies and seamounts strongly modify local circulation, nutrient transport, and planktonic communities. This study investigates the hydrodynamic-zooplankton coupling along the Vitória–Trindade Seamount Chain (VTC) in the southwestern Atlantic, using CTD and Underwater Vision Profiler (UVP5) observations along two transects crossing and south of the chain. Flow–topography interactions involving the Vitória Eddy (VE) and regional seamounts modulated chlorophyll- a distributions and zooplankton abundance, which was eightfold higher at stations under combined eddy-seamount influence (236.9 ind L −1 ) than at oceanic stations, whereas seamount proximity alone produced only a modest increase over oceanic conditions. Although classical seamount-induced upwelling was not detected, elevated chlorophyll- a within the thermocline and downstream of Davis Bank indicates enhanced vertical mixing linked to flow–seamount interactions and eddy deformation. Rhizaria numerically dominated the UVP5-resolved zooplankton assemblage (organisms ≥ 600 μ m ESD), accounting for 79.4% of total abundance, particularly within the euphotic zone and thermocline layers. The normalized biovolume size spectrum (NBSS) showed flatter slopes and higher intercepts near the shelf and in VE-influenced regions versus steeper slopes and lower intercepts offshore and at seamount-only stations, consistent with greater trophic transfer efficiency under eddy influence and energy-limited, oligotrophic conditions elsewhere. Estimated particulate organic carbon (POC) fluxes were highest at stations influenced by the VE (up to 185 mg POC m −2 d −1 ), roughly an order of magnitude above oceanic stations, reflecting lateral shelf inputs and particle retention. These patterns highlight the joint role of mesoscale eddies and seamounts in regulating carbon export along the VTC.

title: On the number of roots of linearised polynomial and classes of cubic Boolean functions with good nonlinearity of order two
summary: It is widely recognised that determining a precise lower bound for the nonlinearity of order two for a general class of cubic monomial Boolean functions is a challenging problem. This paper explores for a given integer n ≥ 4, some values of
content: It is widely recognised that determining a precise lower bound for the nonlinearity of order two for a general class of cubic monomial Boolean functions is a challenging problem. This paper explores for a given integer n ≥ 4, some values of integers s, t where n > s > t ≥ 1 for which cubic monomial Boolean functions having the form Tr1n(μx2s+2t+1), μ ∈ 𝔽2n* possess sharper lower bounds on their nonlinearity of order two. The functions obtained are worth considering for securing symmetric cryptosystems against various quadratic approximation attacks and fast algebraic attacks. The paper also explicitly characterises the parameter configurations (n, s, t, μ) under which the first-order derivative of the function Tr1n(μx2s+2t+1) collapses into an affine mapping. In addition, it is shown that the subclass given by the form Tr13t(μx22t+2t+1) has zero nonlinearity of order two when μ ∈ 𝔽23t* satisfies the condition μ22t + μ2t + μ = 0.

title: AI-assisted design and control of a landsman converter for electric vehicle charging applications with advanced power factor correction
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: The burgeoning electric vehicle (EV) industry necessitates cutting-edge solutions to improve the efficiency and sustainability of EV charging systems. This paper presents an innovative Landsman converter design tailored for EV charging appl
content: The burgeoning electric vehicle (EV) industry necessitates cutting-edge solutions to improve the efficiency and sustainability of EV charging systems. This paper presents an innovative Landsman converter design tailored for EV charging applications, incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) to achieve effective power factor correction (PFC). The integration of AI into the converter's control strategy enhances its ability to optimize operational performance, ensuring a high-power factor, minimizing harmonic distortion, and boosting energy efficiency throughout the charging process. The study develops a sophisticated simulation model of the Landsman converter using MATLAB/Simulink, wherein AI algorithms are employed to dynamically adjust the converter's operation. This approach enables the system to adapt to varying load conditions and input voltages, demonstrating superior performance in terms of power factor correction and overall efficiency. The simulation results underscore the potential of combining AI with power electronics to elevate EV charging technology, offering significant advancements in creating smarter, more reliable, and efficient charging infrastructures. This research highlights the transformative impact of AI on enhancing power electronics designs, paving the way for more sustainable and effective solutions in the rapidly evolving EV sector.

title: An IoT-based approach for real-time fault detection and localization in electrical distribution networks using ThingSpeak
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This paper presents a real-time monitoring, fault detection, and localization system for electrical distribution networks based on the ThingSpeak internet of things (IoT) platform. The proposed approach enables continuous acquisition and an
content: This paper presents a real-time monitoring, fault detection, and localization system for electrical distribution networks based on the ThingSpeak internet of things (IoT) platform. The proposed approach enables continuous acquisition and analysis of key electrical parameters, such as voltage and current. A MATLAB/Simulink model of the IEEE 33-bus distribution network is developed to simulate both normal operating conditions and fault scenarios. The generated data are transmitted to the ThingSpeak cloud platform for real-time visualization and analysis. The system enables rapid fault detection and accurate localization by analyzing variations in electrical signals. The results demonstrate that the proposed solution improves system reliability, reduces fault detection time, and provides an efficient and cost-effective tool for smart grid monitoring and supervision.

title: A 17-level switched-capacitor inverter with asymmetric voltage distribution and inherent balancing: design and experimental verification
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This paper proposes a 17-level switched-capacitor multilevel inverter (SC-MLI) whose four capacitors are deliberately held at unequal voltages: two at the full input voltage and two at half of it. Halving the smallest synthesizable step is
content: This paper proposes a 17-level switched-capacitor multilevel inverter (SC-MLI) whose four capacitors are deliberately held at unequal voltages: two at the full input voltage and two at half of it. Halving the smallest synthesizable step is the novelty of the work, because it doubles the number of levels obtainable from a given set of capacitors and therefore yields seventeen equidistant levels and a fourfold voltage gain from fourteen switches, four capacitors, two diodes, and a single DC source, with no voltage sensor and no balancing controller. Self-balancing is proven analytically for both capacitor groups; the capacitors and a single soft-charging inductor are sized from the maximum discharge duration, and two modulation strategies are implemented on the same FPGA. The design was validated by simulation and on a laboratory prototype driving a 180 W single-phase induction motor. The measured output reaches 186.4 V from a 47.175 V input, a gain of 3.95, with a voltage total harmonic distortion of 1.12% and capacitor ripples between 2.3% and 4.5%, and the measured efficiency is 94.6%. Against eleven recent SC-MLI topologies, the converter attains the highest gain per component count and the lowest cost function 2.38.

title: Analysis of novel cubature Kalman filter based DVR control for mitigating power quality issues in electrical distribution systems
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Power quality (PQ) is a critical concern in modern distribution networks due to voltage disturbances caused by excessive load tapping at the Point of common coupling (PCC) and nonlinear loads. Voltage sag and swell conditions adversely affe
content: Power quality (PQ) is a critical concern in modern distribution networks due to voltage disturbances caused by excessive load tapping at the Point of common coupling (PCC) and nonlinear loads. Voltage sag and swell conditions adversely affect sensitive electrical equipment and system stability. The dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) is an effective power-electronic device for mitigating these disturbances. However, its compensation performance largely depends on the accuracy and response speed of the control algorithm. This paper proposes a cubature Kalman Filter (CKF)-based voltage estimation technique to improve the detection and mitigation of voltage swell disturbances in distribution systems. The proposed CKF algorithm accurately estimates system voltage and generates reference signals for controlling the voltage source converter (VSC) of the DVR. Based on these reference signals, the DVR injects an appropriate compensating voltage into the distribution line, restoring the load voltage to its desired value. The proposed technique improves disturbance detection accuracy, estimation reliability, and dynamic compensation performance. The effectiveness of the CKF-based DVR control strategy is implemented and evaluated using MATLAB/Simulink. Furthermore, its performance is compared with extended Kalman filter (EKF) and linear Kalman filter (LKF) techniques to demonstrate its improved estimation accuracy, faster response, and effectiveness in mitigating voltage swell disturbances in sensitive load-connected distribution systems.

title: Assessing learning progress and teaching effectiveness in the era of generative AI: a dual bibliometric analysis and systematic review
source: International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE)
summary: Despite the rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education, educators and policymakers face a critical challenge: the absence of a comprehensive synthesis identifying how GenAI tools affect the evaluat
content: Despite the rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education, educators and policymakers face a critical challenge: the absence of a comprehensive synthesis identifying how GenAI tools affect the evaluation of learning progress and teaching effectiveness. Existing studies remain fragmented and lack systematic mapping of research trends, dominant methodologies, and research gaps. To address this, the present study adopts a dual methodological approach combining bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review. A bibliometric analysis of 363 Scopus-indexed publications (2015–2025) was conducted using VOSviewer to map publication trends, influential authors, productive countries, and dominant themes. This was complemented by a systematic review of 35 high-quality empirical studies. Findings reveal an exponential surge in publications post-2022, driven by the democratization of large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT. GenAI enhances personalized feedback, self-regulated learning (SRL), and formative assessment at scale, while raising substantive concerns about academic integrity, algorithmic bias, and the erosion of outcome-based evaluation frameworks. The study concludes that sustainable GenAI integration requires human-centered pedagogical designs, institutional governance, and equity-focused policy, offering a structured evidence base for researchers, educators, and policymakers.

title: High-gain multi-stage interleaved DC–DC converter with fuzzy logic control for electric vehicle applications
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: High-gain DC-DC converters are essential for interfacing low-voltage batteries with high-voltage DC buses in electric vehicles (EVs). This study proposes a three-stage cascaded interleaved high-gain DC-DC converter with a dual-floating-outp
content: High-gain DC-DC converters are essential for interfacing low-voltage batteries with high-voltage DC buses in electric vehicles (EVs). This study proposes a three-stage cascaded interleaved high-gain DC-DC converter with a dual-floating-output configuration for battery-powered EV applications. The converter increases a 24 V battery input to approximately 600 V, achieving an overall voltage gain of 25. A Mamdani-type fuzzy logic controller regulates the duty cycle based on output-voltage error and its rate of change. MATLAB/Simulink simulations evaluate voltage conversion, transient response, current behavior, and voltage stability. The results demonstrate stable 24 V-to-600 V conversion with coordinated operation of the three cascaded stages. The proposed configuration provides a modular approach to high-gain DC-DC conversion for EV applications and a basis for future studies on bidirectional operation and hybrid energy sources.

title: Effect of load distribution strategy on the performance and sizing of standalone photovoltaic systems
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Accurate load representation is important for dependable sizing of standalone photovoltaic systems, mainly for healthcare facilities with seasonally varying equipment use. This study estimates the effect of load profile representation on th
content: Accurate load representation is important for dependable sizing of standalone photovoltaic systems, mainly for healthcare facilities with seasonally varying equipment use. This study estimates the effect of load profile representation on the sizing and simulated performance of a standalone photovoltaic system for a rural healthcare center in Al-Musayab District, Babil, Iraq. Two load-modeling approaches were analyzed using PVsyst software V 7.2.11 under the same working schedule of 08:00–15:00, five days per week a conventional daily-load profile with weekly inflection and a seasonally adjusted monthly-load profile based on devices operating months and monthly working days. The monthly load model reduced the estimated yearly demand from 9847.5 to 7805.5 kWh. Consequently, the required PV-array capacity decreased from 9.45 to 6.75 kWp, while the nominal battery-storage capacity decreased from 39.6 to 31.7 kWh. Case 1 supplied 99.71% of its modeled demand and recorded 28.24 kWh of annual missing energy, whereas case 2 achieved complete modeled load coverage with zero missing energy. Yearly unused energy decreased from 5803.6 to 3416.1 kWh, and the performance ratio increased from 50.96% to 56.72%. Nevertheless, the smaller battery bank in case 2 showed greater use and a shorter estimated lifetime, indicating a storage sizing trade off. For the investigated facility and adopted PVsyst software conditions, the results demonstrate that device level, month-dependent load representation provides a more operationally representative basis for system sizing. Further validation using measured load data and additional locations is required before broader generality.

title: Lecturers’ perspectives on the use of AR filters in higher education in Kazakhstan
source: International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE)
summary: This article presents the results of a qualitative study analyzing the readiness of lecturers at Kazakhstani universities to use augmented reality (AR) filters on social media as a pedagogical tool. The theoretical framework was provided by
content: This article presents the results of a qualitative study analyzing the readiness of lecturers at Kazakhstani universities to use augmented reality (AR) filters on social media as a pedagogical tool. The theoretical framework was provided by the European digital competence framework for educators (DigCompEdu). Empirical data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 13 lecturers teaching ‘information and communication technologies’ (ICT), representing four universities with varying statuses and teaching experience ranging from one to thirty-seven years. The analysis was carried out using thematic coding based on the conceptual domains of DigCompEdu. It was found that teachers perceive AR filters primarily as an effective means of increasing student motivation and engagement, as well as a tool for formative feedback. This study is the first to examine AR filters on social media and aims to identify the discrepancy between teachers’ pedagogical intuition and their underdeveloped capacity to adapt resources and plan assessments. The study highlights the need for support for institutional systems, targeted training in AR content creation, and the establishment of communities.

title: Smart grid optimization: AI and machine learning approaches for energy management and load forecasting
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: In contemporary energy systems, smart grids make a significant contribution to generating efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy. Smart grids are crucial to the performance optimization of energy systems, accurate load forecasting, and
content: In contemporary energy systems, smart grids make a significant contribution to generating efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy. Smart grids are crucial to the performance optimization of energy systems, accurate load forecasting, and effective energy management. To find a solution to the condition related to energy management and load forecasting, in the current study we demonstrate a novel hybrid optimization technique that can be used to eliminate the barriers to optimization: a combination of multi-strategy particle swarm optimization (MPSO) with the gazelle optimization algorithm (MPSOGOA) along with artificial neural networks (ANN). By allowing the MPSOGOA algorithm to exploit the exploration power of a multi-strategy particle swarm optimization, as well as the converging nature of gazelle optimization, these algorithms are successful in training ANN models, which dramatically improves the accuracy of the prediction. The evaluation of the proposed hybrid approach that was performed on real-life smart grid datasets shows that the hybrid method effectively outperforms standard algorithms and significantly improves the precision of the forecasts, the operational cost, as well as the reliability. Application of this enhanced hybrid solution offers a reliable and effective smart grid technology architecture in the energy management system for intelligent decision-making.

title: Fuzzy logic controller-based bidirectional DC-DC converter for regenerative braking in electric vehicle applications
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Advanced power conversion and control techniques are required to improve performance and energy recovery, given the growing need for energy-efficient electric vehicles (EVs). This paper presents the design of a bidirectional DC-DC converter
content: Advanced power conversion and control techniques are required to improve performance and energy recovery, given the growing need for energy-efficient electric vehicles (EVs). This paper presents the design of a bidirectional DC-DC converter based on a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) for regenerative braking applications in electric vehicles. The suggested converter operates in two modes: regenerative mode, which recovers braking energy and feeds it back into the battery to improve overall energy efficiency, and driving mode, which uses the battery to power the motor. To ensure optimal voltage and current regulation across a range of load and speed conditions, FLC is trained to dynamically adjust the duty cycle of the converter switches. FLC is more flexible, responds more quickly in transient situations, and is more effective during mode changes than traditional PI control. According to the simulation results, system robustness, battery-charging stability, and energy-recovery efficiency have all significantly improved. The suggested method offers a clever and practical way to regulate EV power sustainably, thereby increasing driving range and reducing energy losses.

title: Stacked Bi-LSTM architecture for precise SOC prediction and power control in electric vehicle BMS
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Accurate state of charge (SOC) estimation and effective power management are essential functions of battery management systems (BMS) for electric vehicles (EVs). This study proposes an integrated BMS framework that combines a stacked bidire
content: Accurate state of charge (SOC) estimation and effective power management are essential functions of battery management systems (BMS) for electric vehicles (EVs). This study proposes an integrated BMS framework that combines a stacked bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network for SOC estimation with a prediction-informed rule-based strategy for dynamic power distribution. Battery voltage, current, temperature, and SOC data are processed using normalization, noise filtering, and a sliding-window technique before being provided to the stacked Bi-LSTM network. The predicted SOC is subsequently used to support dynamic power balancing among battery cells or modules. The reported results show that the proposed model achieves an SOC estimation root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.98%, mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.75%, and R² of 0.985, while the associated power distribution strategy achieves a reported power distribution efficiency (PDE) of 96.82%. The electrical performance analysis also reports reduced voltage ripple and peak cell temperature, together with improved charge/discharge efficiency. These results demonstrate the potential of integrating deep temporal SOC prediction with prediction-informed power distribution for intelligent EV BMS applications. Further validation using fully characterized datasets and operating conditions is required to establish broader applicability.

title: Simulink-based powertrain validation of an archetype-driven electric motorcycle retrofit recommendation framework
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Retrofitting internal combustion engine (ICE) motorcycles into electric motorcycles offers a scalable pathway for transport electrification in motorcycle-dependent regions. A data-driven retrofit-as-a-service (RaaS) decision framework was p
content: Retrofitting internal combustion engine (ICE) motorcycles into electric motorcycles offers a scalable pathway for transport electrification in motorcycle-dependent regions. A data-driven retrofit-as-a-service (RaaS) decision framework was previously developed that clusters motorcycles into five retrofit archetypes and maps each to electric vehicle component tiers, with feasibility assessed through a conservative steady-state lower-bound range estimate. That estimate, however, had not been validated against dynamic driving conditions, leaving its conservatism unverified. This paper presents a drive-cycle validation of the framework using a longitudinal powertrain model implemented in MATLAB and Simulink over a representative world motorcycle test cycle (WMTC). The simulation reproduces the transient acceleration and braking energy that the steady-state model omits. Results show that the original steady-state estimate was not conservative for lightweight archetypes, where simulated energy demand exceeded the analytical prediction. To address this, a speed-dependent transient correction factor is derived and frozen, restoring the lower-bound range to a true conservative floor across all five archetypes. The MATLAB and Simulink implementations agree to within 0.2 percent. The corrected lower bound remains below the simulated range in every case, with feasibility margins from 3.6 to 34 percent. The validated framework provides a defensible early-stage planning tool, with conversational decision support identified as future work.

title: Dynamic behavior and control of a fixed-gain LLC resonant converter in grid-connected photovoltaic systems
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems increasingly employ LLC resonant converters for their soft-switching capability and high efficiency. However, traditional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) needs wide-range frequency control, which
content: Grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems increasingly employ LLC resonant converters for their soft-switching capability and high efficiency. However, traditional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) needs wide-range frequency control, which leads to deviation from resonance and results in the loss of these benefits. This paper presents a fixed-gain control strategy in which the LLC converter is constrained to operate near its resonant frequency with approximately constant voltage gain, while MPPT is achieved by regulating the PV array voltage rather than the DC link voltage. Unlike predictive and hybrid MPPT methods, it adds no hardware or control degrees of freedom; the same perturb-and-observe algorithm, proportional-integral controller, and voltage-controlled oscillator are used, and only the regulated quantity changes. The complete system, comprising a 126.1 kW PV array, LLC converter, and grid-side inverter, is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink under stepped irradiance (300-1000 W/m²). Results show that fixed-gain operation confines the switching frequency to 76-84 kHz, preserves zero-voltage and zero-current switching across all irradiance levels, and results in reduced distortion of resonant current to 6.8% as compared to 14.5% using wide-range control. The PV-to-grid efficiency rises from 89.7% to 92.4% at 300 W/m² and from 93.6% to 95.1% at 700 W/m², while the DC-link voltage remains within ±6.5% without degrading grid-current quality.

title: Hardware implementation of low-frequency selective harmonic elimination on multilevel inverter
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are widely used in medium- and high-power applications due to their improved output waveform quality and reduced voltage stress on semiconductor switches. However, low-order harmonics remain a significant challen
content: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are widely used in medium- and high-power applications due to their improved output waveform quality and reduced voltage stress on semiconductor switches. However, low-order harmonics remain a significant challenge, particularly when low switching frequencies are employed. This research presents the hardware implementation of low-frequency selective harmonic elimination (SHE) for a multilevel inverter to improve output power quality while reducing switching losses. The nonlinear SHE equations are solved to determine appropriate switching angles for eliminating selected low-order harmonics while maintaining the required fundamental voltage. The obtained switching angles are implemented using a digital controller and gate-drive circuit, and the performance is validated through simulation and experimental hardware results. The simulation results achieve an overall total harmonic distortion (THD) of 17.23%, while the experimental prototype records a THD of 18.39%, showing a close correspondence between the simulated and practical results. The targeted 5th-order harmonic is effectively eliminated, and the measured fundamental voltage exhibits reduced deviation from the reference value. The close agreement between simulation and experimental results confirms the effectiveness of the proposed low-frequency SHE technique for improving harmonic performance while maintaining reduced switching activity and associated switching losses.

title: Real-time battery parameter estimation using an advanced Kalman filter integrated with a DALY BMS controller
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive MATLAB/Simulink model for simulating the charge and discharge characteristics of a battery. The model incorporates key electrical parameters such as internal resistance, open-circuit voltage, and capacity
content: This paper presents a comprehensive MATLAB/Simulink model for simulating the charge and discharge characteristics of a battery. The model incorporates key electrical parameters such as internal resistance, open-circuit voltage, and capacity, allowing for accurate prediction of battery behavior under various operating conditions. The simulation framework enables the analysis of different charging algorithms, discharge profiles, and the impact of temperature on battery performance. Furthermore, the modular design facilitates the integration of this battery model into large power system simulations, enabling the evaluation of energy storage system performance in diverse applications. Simulation results demonstrate the model’s ability to accurately replicate real-world battery behavior, providing a valuable tool for design, analysis, and optimization of battery-based systems.

title: Hybrid PSC-aware ANN-incremental conductance MPPT strategy using P-V curve probing for photovoltaic systems
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This work introduces a hybrid maximum power point tracking (MPPT) strategy for photovoltaic (PV) systems under partial shading conditions (PSCs), combining a PSC-aware artificial neural network (ANN) with adaptive incremental conductance (I
content: This work introduces a hybrid maximum power point tracking (MPPT) strategy for photovoltaic (PV) systems under partial shading conditions (PSCs), combining a PSC-aware artificial neural network (ANN) with adaptive incremental conductance (INC) refinement. A power-voltage (P-V) curve probing mechanism samples the PV output at five predefined voltage levels scaled by the open-circuit voltage. A multilayer perceptron processes the resulting normalized power features to estimate the global maximum power point (GMPP) voltage. The ANN provides global estimation, while INC performs local refinement to compensate for residual prediction errors. A finite-state supervisory mechanism coordinates both stages and reactivates global prediction following significant operating changes. MATLAB/Simulink simulations are conducted under uniform irradiance, temperature variations, and several partial shading scenarios. Compared with the standalone PSC-aware ANN, the hybrid strategy increases MPPT efficiency from 96.30% to 97.04% under static PSC, from 90.84% to 93.15% under severe PSC, and from 94.17% to 96.40% under dynamic PSC. The results confirm the benefit of combining ANN-based global GMPP voltage estimation with adaptive INC local refinement under complex shading conditions. Experimental/HIL validation remains for future work.

title: Long range-based smart vehicle safety and control system
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: The increasing demand for intelligent transportation systems has led to the development of advanced vehicle safety solutions. This paper presents an automotive vehicle control safety system based on long range (LoRa) sensor technology for r
content: The increasing demand for intelligent transportation systems has led to the development of advanced vehicle safety solutions. This paper presents an automotive vehicle control safety system based on long range (LoRa) sensor technology for reliable, LoRa, and low-power communication. The proposed system integrates multiple sensors to monitor critical parameters such as obstacle distance, vehicle condition, and environmental factors. Using LoRa communication, real-time data is transmitted between vehicles or to a monitoring unit to support timely decision-making and accident prevention. The system ensures secure and energy-efficient data transmission while maintaining extended coverage. Experimental analysis demonstrates that the proposed LoRa-based safety framework enhances vehicle control, improves situational awareness, and contributes to safer and smarter transportation systems.

title: Modified DC-DC converter for BLDC motor drives: Technical overview and commutation torque ripple reduction
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Brushless DC motors (BLDCMs) have emerged as a preferred alternative to conventional motors across a wide range of applications, including household appliances, industrial systems, and electric vehicles. Their growing adoption stems not onl
content: Brushless DC motors (BLDCMs) have emerged as a preferred alternative to conventional motors across a wide range of applications, including household appliances, industrial systems, and electric vehicles. Their growing adoption stems not only from strong performance in position and speed regulation, but also from advantages such as high-power density, low-noise operation, and compatibility with electronic control. However, a persistent challenge in BLDC drives is torque ripple, which remains a key limitation of the technology. This paper presents a concise review of the different factors contributing to torque ripple in BLDCMs. Since reducing torque ripple is essential for achieving energy-efficient operation in BLDC drives, this work proposes a novel switched-capacitor-based ZETA hybrid converter as a means of suppressing it. In addition, the paper surveys various modified converter topologies currently used for this purpose. Findings indicate that the drive achieves minimal torque ripple at a specific converter duty ratio, and that both the ripple magnitude and commutation time vary as the duty ratio is adjusted.

title: Acoustic condition prediction of electrical engine
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Nowadays, modern industry relies heavily on condition-based maintenance (CBM) and fault diagnosis (FD) for rotating equipment (RM). In addition, monitoring and timely repair of machinery require knowledge of its remaining useful life (RUL).
content: Nowadays, modern industry relies heavily on condition-based maintenance (CBM) and fault diagnosis (FD) for rotating equipment (RM). In addition, monitoring and timely repair of machinery require knowledge of its remaining useful life (RUL). Furthermore, high-efficiency electric transportation systems are based on electric motors. The increasing demand for efficiency, availability, and reliability has led to extensive research in this field. In particular, the analysis of electric motor sound data using artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a significant advancement. This paper presents the mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) features of the array of a recurrent machine learning (ML) model that can learn and classify a wide variety of electric motor voice signals with robust performance. Moreover, new electric motor diagnostic tools are more accurate and efficient thanks to rotor signals from Kaggle's IDMT-ISA-ELECTRIC-ENGINE dataset and AI defect detection methods that enhancing their flexibility and efficiency. In this study, MFCC demonstrates strong performance in identifying operating modes, even in the presence of background noise. Additionally, recurrent models improve performances by increasing the robustness and reduce the time complexity associated with monitoring low-level motors. The proposed MFCC-based deep recurrent neural network (DRNN) model on the test dataset, achieving an exceptional overall accuracy of 99.83%.

title: Student ambition and national needs: an evidence-based student allocation model
source: International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE)
summary: Student choice in university majors is largely influenced by their preference and not the demand in the labor market. This is indicative of poor alignment of Ministries of Higher Education, Education and Planning that creates surplus supply
content: Student choice in university majors is largely influenced by their preference and not the demand in the labor market. This is indicative of poor alignment of Ministries of Higher Education, Education and Planning that creates surplus supply of graduates in traditional areas and deficit in priority areas. This imbalance leads to unemployment and shortage of skills in the labor market. This paper constructs a student allocation model based on evidence that meets labor market forecasting and national development objectives. The research is an integrated multimodal student allocation model based on labor market expectation, institutional capacity and governance mechanisms and industry feedback in the post-conflict countries such as Iraq. Herein lies the uniqueness and novelty of this study. The research was based on a quantitative cross-sectional design, which involved 153 stakeholders, such as policymakers, administrators, planners, and industry experts in Iraq. Results showed that the impacts of all the predictors were statistically significant, with economic forecasting and career guidance having the largest impacts on the effectiveness of the strategic student allocation system. The outcomes are used to support the evidence-based student allocation system to meet the needs of national workforce in Iraq at the output of higher education. The model provides practical policy recommendations to stakeholders on gradient mismatch and on the way the country’s higher education system can be better aligned with the needs of the labor market.

title: High-gain single-switch DC-DC converter with incremental conductance MPPT control for fuel cell applications
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: An ultra-high-step-up single-switch DC-DC converter is presented for proton exchange membrane fuel cell interfaces that require a regulated high-voltage DC bus from a low and load-dependent source voltage. Its distinguishing feature is the
content: An ultra-high-step-up single-switch DC-DC converter is presented for proton exchange membrane fuel cell interfaces that require a regulated high-voltage DC bus from a low and load-dependent source voltage. Its distinguishing feature is the combination of an LCL-type switched-inductor input network and an enhanced quadratic boost stage in a single-switch topology, integrated with incremental-conductance maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and DC-bus regulation. Simulations using a 1.26 kW proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) model show conversion from 20 V to a regulated 300 V at approximately 80% efficiency. Under the same source, load, and MPPT conditions, the high-gain single-switch (HGSS) converter delivers about 25% more output power than a conventional boost converter, reduces root mean square (RMS) and peak-to-peak output ripple by approximately 85%, and operates at a duty cycle of 0.52 rather than 0.9. These results identify the topology-control combination as a candidate for high-gain PEMFC interfaces, subject to experimental verification of losses and long-term operation.

title: Real-time hardware validation of an improved grey wolf optimizer MPPT with adaptive re-initialization for PV systems under partial shading
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Under dynamic environmental conditions and partial shading, photovoltaic systems exhibit multimodal power–voltage characteristics, causing conventional maximum power point tracker algorithms to get trapped at local maxima, resulting in osci
content: Under dynamic environmental conditions and partial shading, photovoltaic systems exhibit multimodal power–voltage characteristics, causing conventional maximum power point tracker algorithms to get trapped at local maxima, resulting in oscillations, energy losses, and slow tracking. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved grey wolf optimizer (IGWO) with four key enhancements: quasi-random Sobol sequence for initialization, a non-linear exponential decay of the coefficient, dynamic adaptive partial re-initialization, and a stagnation-based early-stopping rule. The algorithm was put into practice in real time on an 8-bit ATmega328P microcontroller and experimentally validated using a 50 kHz Boost converter connected to a 36 W PV array under both uniform and severe multi-peak shading conditions. The results show a tracking efficiency of 99.0 ± 0.5% and an average convergence time of 0.35 ± 0.08 s for the multi-peak PSC. The IGWO achieved efficiency improvements of 2.5%, 2%, and 3.2%, compared with the grey wolf optimizer variants, particle swarm optimization, and perturb and observe, while maintaining stable GMPP operation with only negligible oscillations. This study offers a computationally efficient, oscillation-free MPPT solution suitable for embedded PV systems in electric vehicles and satellite applications.

title: Ion motion algorithm-based MPPT for photovoltaic systems using a SEPIC converter under partial shading conditions
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Solar photovoltaic (PV) output depends heavily on the prevailing irradiance, and once shading becomes non-uniform, the power-voltage (P-V) curve can break into several local peaks alongside a single true maximum, a situation that frequently
content: Solar photovoltaic (PV) output depends heavily on the prevailing irradiance, and once shading becomes non-uniform, the power-voltage (P-V) curve can break into several local peaks alongside a single true maximum, a situation that frequently defeats conventional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) schemes searching for the global maximum power point (GMPP). To address this limitation, this paper presents an MPPT strategy built on the Ion motion optimization algorithm (IMOA) and paired with a SEPIC DC-DC converter for stand-alone (off-grid) PV systems. The controller was assessed through closed-loop simulations in PSIM across four irradiance levels: 1000 W/m², 750 W/m², 500 W/m², and 250 W/m². Under uniform, full irradiance, the algorithm delivered an output power of 95.08 W, a tracking accuracy of 99.77%, and a tracking time of 0.98 s; under partial shading, it sustained an accuracy above 99% while converging faster than a benchmark particle swarm optimization (PSO) controller. These findings indicate that the proposed IMOA-based approach reliably and effectively locates the GMPP across changing irradiance conditions.

title: Characteristic improvement of maximum power point tracker using DC-DC buck converter based on genetic algorithm-tuned GPID controller
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Effective maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is crucial for preserving steady power output since photovoltaic (PV) systems undergo substantial characteristic degradation under changing solar irradiation conditions. In order to enhance the
content: Effective maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is crucial for preserving steady power output since photovoltaic (PV) systems undergo substantial characteristic degradation under changing solar irradiation conditions. In order to enhance the dynamic characteristics of a DC-DC buck converter utilized as an MPPT system for photovoltaic applications, this work suggests a genetic algorithm (GA)- tuned proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. Finding the ideal controller parameters that reduce steady-state error, settling time, rise time, and overshoot while preserving the required output voltage is the goal. Based on a fitness function obtained from the converter's closed-loop response, the GA was used to maximize the controller gains. According to simulation results, Kp = 100, Ki = 12.84, and Kd = 100 were found to be the ideal controller parameters. A very quick rise time of 4.07×10-10 s and a settling time of 7.25×10-10 s were attained using the suggested controller. In comparison to 0.01 s without GA tweaking, the converter achieved the required output power of 150 W and output voltage of 14.7 V in 0.005 s under standard test conditions. Additionally, the suggested system maintained a steady output voltage of 14.68 V and output power of 149.64 W when solar irradiance dropped from 1000 W/m² to 300 W/m², exhibiting greater robustness and tracking characteristics.

title: Self-healing smart grid: how automation reduces blackouts and power failures
source: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
summary: Modern societies depend heavily on a continuous and reliable supply of electricity, yet traditional power grids are increasingly vulnerable to outages caused by equipment failures, extreme weather, cyber threats, and rising demand. Blackout
content: Modern societies depend heavily on a continuous and reliable supply of electricity, yet traditional power grids are increasingly vulnerable to outages caused by equipment failures, extreme weather, cyber threats, and rising demand. Blackouts and power failures not only disrupt daily life but also lead to significant economic losses and safety risks. In response to these challenges, self-healing smart grids have emerged as a transformative solution. By integrating advanced automation, sensors, real-time data analytics, and intelligent control systems, self-healing smart grids can detect, isolate, and respond to faults automatically—often within seconds. This capability greatly reduces the frequency, duration, and impact of power outages. As automation becomes more sophisticated, self-healing smart grids are redefining how electrical networks operate, shifting from reactive systems to proactive and resilient infrastructures that ensure greater reliability and efficiency in power delivery.

title: Reducing complexity for predictive current control for PMSM created on a developed target function
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: When requesting a definite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) for mobility weakening control of permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSM), issues arose related to the limit-strength standard. To address these issues, we propo
content: When requesting a definite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) for mobility weakening control of permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSM), issues arose related to the limit-strength standard. To address these issues, we propose a proportional-integral-derivative (PID)-type cost function specifically designed for FCS-MPC in this framework. This cost function comprises three parts: an equivalent error cost that focuses on current following, a basic error cost to reduce steady-state control errors, and a characteristic wrong cost proposed to reduce ripple errors. In this group, the cost function is used to implement delay compensation to improve prediction accuracy in the control system. Simulation results show that when the PMSM limits are misaligned and with on-diluting control, the FCS-MPC establishes a type cost function that forces the control system's robustness to engine limits and load-force disturbances, while maintaining attractive dynamic characteristics. Notably, this control strategy reduces the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the three-phase current from 13.09% to 4.79% and reduces the ripple force by 50% to 5.75%.

title: Design of an adaptive super-twisting sliding mode controller with extended state observer for robot manipulator trajectory tracking
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: Sliding mode controllers often trade chattering suppression against rapid recovery from large initial tracking errors, yet the combined effect of severe initial offsets, high-bandwidth commands, and unmeasured disturbances remains insuffici
content: Sliding mode controllers often trade chattering suppression against rapid recovery from large initial tracking errors, yet the combined effect of severe initial offsets, high-bandwidth commands, and unmeasured disturbances remains insufficiently characterized within a single reproducible benchmark. This study compares classical SMC, fractional-order SMC (FOSMC), adaptive SMC, and a proposed adaptive super-twisting SMC with an extended state observer (AST-SMC+ESO) on a common two-degree-of-freedom planar manipulator under identical initial conditions, solver settings, and disturbances. The novelty of the proposed design is its combination of a leakage-regularized adaptive super-twisting gain with a third-order observer. Simulations show that AST-SMC+ESO achieves the lowest RMSE of the four controllers, 0.5958 rad and 0.5288 rad for joints 1 and 2, with peak torques of 260.03 N m and 86.48 N m. These peaks are below those of adaptive SMC and FOSMC but above those of classical SMC, which tracks far less accurately. FOSMC exhibits a persistent tracking offset and a torque peak exceeding 5.1 kN m, impractical for most actuators. AST-SMC+ESO thus offers a favorable compromise among robustness, tracking precision, and peak actuation demand for torque-limited drives such as collaborative robot joints. These results, obtained on an idealized rigid-body plant, motivate hardware-in-the-loop validation.

title: Forecasting solar panel using SARIMA integrated with filtering enhancement
source: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
summary: This study aims to improve short-term photovoltaic DC power forecasting as a predictive information layer for PV energy management and power electronic applications by integrating the seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIM
content: This study aims to improve short-term photovoltaic DC power forecasting as a predictive information layer for PV energy management and power electronic applications by integrating the seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) model with three filtering techniques: the Savitzky–Golay filter (SGF), exponential smoothing filter (ESF), and adaptive Kalman filter (AKF). The SARIMA model was developed as a baseline forecasting approach, while the filtering techniques were applied as post-processing methods to reduce residual fluctuations and improve prediction stability. The dataset was obtained from a photovoltaic system installed at Universitas Negeri Surabaya (UNESA), Indonesia, with DC power measurements recorded at 15-minute intervals over 31 consecutive days. The forecasting performance of the proposed approaches was evaluated using the mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R²) metrics. The results demonstrate that integrating filtering techniques improves the forecasting performance compared with the baseline SARIMA model. Among the evaluated approaches, the SARIMA-SGF framework achieved the best performance, followed by SARIMA-ESF and SARIMA-AKF, indicating that filtering-based post-processing can effectively enhance SARIMA forecasting accuracy for short-term photovoltaic direct current (DC) power prediction. The findings highlight the potential of combining statistical forecasting models with filtering techniques, particularly for photovoltaic (PV) systems with limited historical data availability.

title: Modelling custom: Large language models and customary international law between scarcity and abundance
summary: The identification of customary international law has long been shaped by a narrative of scarcity with respect to evidence, access, and analytical capacity. This scarcity has contributed, among other things, to a persistent Global North bia
content: The identification of customary international law has long been shaped by a narrative of scarcity with respect to evidence, access, and analytical capacity. This scarcity has contributed, among other things, to a persistent Global North bias in the identification and formation of custom. However, recent legal and technological developments have ushered in an era of abundance, marked by both unprecedented access to data and powerful tools for its analysis. Extensive information on states’ actions and legal positions – across a broader range of jurisdictions, languages, and formats – is now accessible, and large-scale computational analysis is increasingly feasible. This article explores the implications of these developments for the study of customary international law. It argues that a data-driven approach, leveraging large language models to analyse state practice and opinio juris from carefully constructed datasets that account for diversity, offers significant promise for overcoming traditional challenges in the identification of custom and may transform how customary norms are identified and studied.

title: Mitigation technologies for wellbore blockage caused by coal powder ejection from surface wells in mining-disturbed areas: a case study
source: Geomechanics and Geophysics for Geo-Energy and Geo-Resources
summary: Surface wells drilled in mining-disturbed areas are an effective means for pressure-relief gas drainage. In soft, outburst-prone coal seams, however, high-pressure gas can carry coal powder into the wellbore, causing severe plugging and a c
content: Surface wells drilled in mining-disturbed areas are an effective means for pressure-relief gas drainage. In soft, outburst-prone coal seams, however, high-pressure gas can carry coal powder into the wellbore, causing severe plugging and a consequent decline in drainage efficiency. Intense mining disturbance, low coal strength, and high gas pressure were identified as the primary contributing factors. High-pressure gas flushing was applied to alleviate the blockage. Results show that flushing is most effective when the working face is positioned directly beneath the well, yielding an average peak gas flow rate of 30.9 m 3 /min and sustaining a rate above 10 m 3 /min for 57.5 days. A standpipe installed inside the slotted pipe was also tested, but coal powder continued to enter through the drain holes, rendering this approach ineffective. A third alternative—fitting a metal mesh filter around the slotted pipe—was subsequently proposed. Laboratory tests indicated that while the mesh effectively retained coal powder, it also reduced gas flow; a 1.0 mm mesh size was identified as optimal for the surface wells in this test. In field applications, wells 1024-2 and 1024-3, equipped with the 1.0 mm mesh, achieved an average peak flow rate of 27.29 m 3 /min and maintained a flow above 10 m 3 /min for 45.5 days, confirming satisfactory performance in mitigating wellbore plugging.

title: Green consumption and sustainable behaviors among university students
summary: This research aims to examine the green consumer behaviors of university students and to reveal the underlying structure and tendencies of these behaviors. The research data were collected through a survey administered to students at Ondoku
content: This research aims to examine the green consumer behaviors of university students and to reveal the underlying structure and tendencies of these behaviors. The research data were collected through a survey administered to students at Ondokuz Mayıs University (OMU), Türkiye. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), correlation analysis, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) were employed to analyze the data. The findings indicate that students strongly adopt environmentally friendly behaviors associated with daily life routines, such as energy and water conservation. In contrast, behaviors requiring greater cognitive evaluation and economic sacrifice, such as recycling practices and the preference for environmentally friendly products, were found to be less prevalent. The factor analysis revealed that green consumption behavior consists of four main dimensions: Green purchase attitude, curtailment behaviors, sustainable behaviors, and interpersonal environmental influence. The structural model results showed that green purchase attitude and interpersonal environmental influence have positive and significant effects on sustainable behaviors, while the effect of curtailment behaviors was found to be marginally significant. The findings highlight the complexity of the relationship between favorable environmental evaluations and actual environmentally responsible practices, suggesting that attitudes alone may not fully explain sustainable behaviors. Accordingly, the study highlights the importance of integrating environmental courses into all academic programs and supporting them with practical projects, strengthening recycling infrastructure, and developing social initiatives that encourage environmentally responsible practices in order to promote green consumption and sustainable behaviors.

title: Restoring global forest canopy structure complexity for potential local warming mitigation
summary: Forests are natural coolers of Earth’s land surface temperatures. However, the local biophysical cooling provided by forest is often constrained by trade-off between expanding forest areas and competing land uses, which has challenged both
content: Forests are natural coolers of Earth’s land surface temperatures. However, the local biophysical cooling provided by forest is often constrained by trade-off between expanding forest areas and competing land uses, which has challenged both policymakers and scientists for decades. Restoring forest canopy structural complexity has long been viewed as a promising nature-based strategy to alleviate this constrain, yet its effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood at the global scale. Using satellite-derived land surface temperature and LiDAR-based measurements of canopy structures, we show that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances local land surface cooling across most global forests (90.0%). The cooling potential of vertical canopy complexity consistently exceeds that of horizontal crown cover density, which has been long overlooked. By aligning canopy structure complexity of managed forests with that of nearby intact forests, we estimate a potential reduction of 0.25 ± 0.001 °C in local land surface temperature globally. Our findings provide insights into strengthening the climate regulation of existing forests through the ecological restoration of forest canopy structure complexity and suggest a space-efficient management strategy that complements, rather than substitutes for, forest conservation and afforestation.

title: Women, Climate Conflict and Environmental Peacebuilding: Lessons from The Niger Delta
source: International Journal of Social and Economic Development
summary: The resource-rich Niger Delta is home to crude oil, which is the major export source, accounting for over eighty per cent of Nigeria’s revenue, but remains one of the most environmentally polluted and conflict-ridden zones in sub-Saharan Af
content: The resource-rich Niger Delta is home to crude oil, which is the major export source, accounting for over eighty per cent of Nigeria’s revenue, but remains one of the most environmentally polluted and conflict-ridden zones in sub-Saharan Africa. Against this backdrop, this paper examines the intersection of gender, climate-induced conflict, and environmental peacebuilding in the region, focusing on the contributions of women to development and conflict transformation.
